Title: Governor's Interview - Vision
text: Governor's Interview -Vision Governor's Interview -Vision 27 Dec. 2001 * Published in Visao magazine on 12/27/2001 Vision: The physical circulation of the euro begins within days. What is the balance sheet that makes these three years of single currency? Vitor Constancio: The introduction of the euro took place in January 1999. Since that date, the shield does not exist as currency, it exists only as a unit of account, which we use in the notes and coins. The economic impact of the euro occurred at that time and has been a success story. Although the exchange rate against the dollar has been falling, over these two Years? This is not where you can assess the success of this project. This is not even where you can assess the strong nature of the euro. What are the great achievements of the euro? It was a success, because from day one a huge money market in euros was created, which worked without problems. This contributed very quickly to the emergence of a large debt market, so that in 1999 international bonds were issues in euros of a value higher than that of the dollar. And in 2000 almost the same thing happened. There has been a huge increase in the role of the euro in capital markets, which has enabled large companies to rely on another means of financing and to make major acquisition and internationalisation operations. Including Portuguese companies, which had lower costs and easier to issue debt to be able to invest in Latin America and elsewhere. Is this success visible only in the debt market? Which would be very important. But even in terms of instruments such as stocks, with the denomination of all of them in euros, there was also an increase in the importance of the euro compared to the one that had the currencies that integrated it. It was also a success, as European monetary policy since January 1999 has been well adjusted to Europe's economic situation. More than in the years that immediately preceded the entry into the euro. The euro has thus made a good contribution to the economy... In fact, the euro started its life in a period of relative economic slowdown, and at a time when inflation was very low. Interest rates declined to unseen values, reaching 2.5 percent. And that contributed greatly to the recovery that took place in late 1999 and 2000, when the European economy grew by 3.4 percent. The biggest growth in the last ten years. The contribution of the existence of a European Central Bank... Interest rates are, in real terms, at historically low values. For example, the average real interest rate in the euro area between 1990 and 1998 was around 4.5%; short-term real interest rates are now around 2% and long-term interest rates range from 2% to 3% by country. Monetary policy has been appropriate for the European climate. This is a set of facts that let us say that the euro was a success. Moreover, the President of the US Federal Reserve has acknowledged that the euro, in addition to being the currency of one of the most powerful areas in the world, has achieved all these aspects of operation which, in fact, make the importance of a currency. Has the euro proven to be a strong currency? The exchange rate between the euro and the dollar is not a criterion for assessing whether or not the euro is a strong currency. Firstly, because these fluctuations between the various European currencies that once existed and the dollar have happened for decades. Going only to the 1980s and 1990s, the milestone was estimated to be about 50%, between 1980 and 1985; then, in two years, it was valued almost 100%, fell 26% and rose 27%... Therefore, this depreciation of 20-something stakes, since the euro was created, has to be seen in this context of very sharp fluctuations and with great variation in recent decades. Will the euro rise against the dollar? Not to say it will rise already, quickly, but the historical experience shows well what is this dance between the coins. How do you assess the strength of a coin? It is evaluated according to various criteria. Firstly, a stable low inflation regime has been contributed, i.e. the internal value of the currency is guaranteed. This is, above all, important for a relatively closed economic area such as the euro area, which only imports from abroad 12% to 15%. Secondly, it is a strong currency if it has diversified and deep money and financial markets in order to offer a whole full range of implementing instruments to investors at low costs. This is a little less about the stock market, but sharply on the money market and the debt instruments market. Third, the currency is strong if it reveals that markets have confidence in maintaining a low long-term inflation regime. And that is reflected in the long-term interest rates, which are determined by the markets. This is a market test. Since the euro exists, interest rates on European treasuries have been systematically below US rates. This reflects long-term confidence that the euro guarantees macroeconomic stability in a low inflation regime. And it's a sign of euro fortitude. For example, ten-year debt costs the U.S. State less than the Us State Portuguese at the moment. Which is only possible because we are in the euro. Will it be the world's first currency? That's not even a goal. You don't get much money flowing in other parts of the world. It is convenient for companies not to have foreign exchange risk problems when trading with other countries, which has a certain economic value. And it certainly has a certain geopolitical value. But economic value, in the strict sense, is less important than one sometimes imagines. It's not a goal, although it may exist. I am convinced that the importance of the euro will continue to increase in the various areas of use as an international currency. But we're still in a preliminary phase. What is the real role of the euro? The main objective of the euro is to give Europe autonomy in its monetary policy. Give independence. That is, to give greater control over the conjuncture and, in essence, over its destiny. As a relatively closed area, it means that it can manage monetary policy, taking into account almost exclusively its needs for macroeconomic stability, without worrying excessively about external problems. Giving priority to the internal objectives of the economic environment, either to control inflation or to mitigate the risks of a recession. Which is very important, as we are not obliged to follow what other economies are doing, when that is not best suited to ours. This greater autonomy, that greater independence, that greater control over the fate of Europe is the main aspect of this project. The current policy difference in interest rates between the ECB and the Fed is a example of this? In the sense that we understand that, in relation to the conditions of the European economy, our rates are adequate. Does the euro dispense with political union? It is a fact that these three years of the euro show that it can function without political union in the strictest sense. But it is good to say that this is the only way to say that this is the case because a set of rules and institutions that involve a huge sharing of sovereignty has been defined. And that this whole project is in itself a project of political union. That is, when the countries opted for the euro, they decided that they needed to share sovereignties to preserve their interests. And they did. A European system of central banks with great independence of operation has been decided... ... with the Model of the Bundesbank, the German central bank... ... the most independent in the world. With operating rules that involve the participation of the governors of the different central banks, the decentralized functioning of the system. The rules determined a great deal of political union. Some consider this independence excessive... I don't see any discussion around her, at least in official terms. But it comes out, every once in a while... In terms of jeopardising the principle of independence, I have not seen it. It is a recent choice of countries, it has been made and it is in the treaties, in the constitutional texts. In this field, is there already a real political union? We are already in political union in this respect. The euro proves, moreover, like other things that are happening in Europe, that the European project is not as crisis-only as it is often if it reads. There are always, at every moment, and particularly at this stage, reasons for frustration with the European project. In particular, when defence and foreign policy problems have now been raised, there have been some frustrations in this area. But it's good to look back and see the importance of what has already been achieved. Things that would have seemed impossible ten or twenty years ago. The euro was one of those impossible projects... Many people in the world, and in Europe too, almost until the eve of the euro, did not believe that this project was possible. And it was. It's a fundamental historical change. It's one of those moments when the great story goes under our eyes - appearances would be modest, but the consequences are of enormous scope. With the significance that the euro has for the evolution and overcoming of nation states in Europe, this is one of those moments. Three years ago, he said that the euro had two sides, one as a catalyst for liberalisation and another advocate of the European social model. Which one are you winning? The two sides coexist, have their role and should have their influence, to different degrees, at different times. At the stage we are at, the euro and monetary union have boosted liberalising trends. At the same time, and to the extent that the current independence of macroeconomic management makes it possible to better respond to shocks, it also makes it easier to defend the European social model, if that is the choice of governments. This role of the euro is also there and is very important. Can the crisis affect the euro at this stage of the transition to physical currency? The political crisis? The economy... first (see box). It would be preferable for the physical introduction of the euro to take place at a time of greater euphoria. It would have a greater psychological impact. But the fact that we are in a period of slowdown and economic uncertainty does not create difficulties in the physical introduction of the euro. Everything is going as planned. Europe is growing much lower, but it has not gone into recession. It can also be thought that the successful introduction of specimens in euro will have a positive psychological effect on the General European population. And about the economy... The psychological aspect is very important. The impact it has on people, from the moment they can move around the 12 countries with the same currency, gives a sense of belonging, of sharing destiny. I think that this contributes to greater economic optimism in the euro area. On the other hand, the fact that it happens in a period of relative deceleration helps to remove the idea that the introduction of specimens into the euro could contribute to increasing inflation. And you can't, despite the unfavorable situation? It's the wrong idea. There is no conjuncture that anyone can take advantage of to raise prices; the change to euro specimens does not affect the market power of undertakings, which are subject to the same competition; and when it comes to rounding and conversions, everything indicates that the impact is small. But can there be an impact? We came to the conclusion that, at worst, the impact it would have on the price index, and would be at once, would not exceed 0.23 per cent. So we're looking at normal year-end increases? There have been previous price hits. I think it has been a good decision to impose double pricing since 1 October, when it was only mandatory for the period of double movement. Doing so before had the double advantage of taking awareness of this operation earlier and allowing to control the conversion during this period. And it also caused some rounding eventually made up to have diluted, in this period, without much impact on inflation. I think that will be visible in January and February. Do you believe in a 15-euro zone? In the medium term I believe. Five years seems like a realistic horizon to me. UK included? It is curious, in the polls conducted in the United Kingdom, to have a majority against entry into the euro, but at the same time 70% of the population say that they are convinced that, in the long term, the euro will replace the pound. It's an interesting dichotomy. And it basically means understanding that the euro is an inevitable historical trend. What about the impact of the three countries on the euro? The impact is positive. Because it strengthens the economic area of the euro. In the case of England, strengthens it with Europe's largest financial market. That would be very positive for the euro. We are in the process of transition. Is everything going as planned? We supplied the coins to the banks in September. The notes were delivered in October. In this pre-supply phase, everything went well and on schedule. In December, we entered the phase of banks supplying trade. This is going slower than you'd expect, but with normality. There are some costs involved in this operation, as there are for banks, and there are some larger companies in the sector that, perhaps looking to have less costs, have postponed the process a bit. But the meetings we have had with the associations reveal that everything will be ready in the first days of January. Do the costs pass to the end customer? We are talking about very low figures in relation to the turnover of the sectors concerned, with very little effect on price policy. Does the average level of knowledge about the euro meet? As a result of the polls, Portugal has higher levels of knowledge than the European average, which is positive. But in the polls, the Portuguese appear in the last places ... I'm talking about the Eurobarometer, about the date knowledge and the conversion rate. These are the main aspects for the general population, and then we are above the European average. What about the companies? The surveys of the National Commission of the Euro show very good results. The overwhelming majority of companies have done the operations they had to do and are prepared for the euro. But there are a lot of people who still have no information about this process... There will be problems, especially with some segments of the population, and the media will have many stories in the first few weeks. But I hope there aren't any big problems. a name"box"/aPolitical crisis H2The current political crisis will bring problems to the economy?/h2 pAs all crises, has some costs. It's good that the crisis is resolved quickly, but it's a crisis normal in democracy./p h2Which comes at a bad time... /h2 p Appears in a economic slowdown, which is not the best. But I also believe I can say, with security, that it will not significantly affect the growth in 2002. The institutions operate, although some more significant decisions do not can be taken. Fortunately, we have the Budget approved. The central aspect of the life of the Public Administration has been secured since the beginning of the year, and the rest of the economy has a stable framework to be able to function. That is, the costs that result from this political crisis, and of course there are some, are relatively small. /p h2Prepare elections, form a government , approve a new Budget... /h2 pNo doubt, and that has its cost. But I don't think it will affect the rate of growthof the economy significantly. The fact that we are in the euro helps. The whole legal and institutional framework resulting from being members of the European european union helps to have a fundamental stability that the political situation does not causa./p h2does not aggravate years that would already be of great requirement and difficulty policy, in terms of the balance of public accounts and compliance with the Stability?/h2 pThe next few years are of great demand in these areas, but the current situation does not add new difficulties./p h2We are in the end of the large volume of community aid,unrecoverable?/h2 pNot necessarily. This impasse can bring costsWho has access to funds can continue to do your projects./p h2But not the big projects... /h2 pBig decisions of course not./p h2And that doesn't worry you?/h2 pIt's a cost. But no major project will suffer irremediably for three months delay./p h2Should there be early elections as soon as possible?/h2 pI don't speak up about it. What I'm saying is, whatever the decision, should be taken as soon as possible./p h2Is there any solution, better for the economy, that early elections?/h2 pA this does not answer. Mean i do not want to do /p h2Was appointed as one of the chances to lead the Socialist Party... /h2 pI'm already removed from life politics for many years. And I'm in a public service position, which implies a posture of total political independence. Which I think I've kept and I'm going to continue to maintain. Entrevista do Governador -Viso Entrevista do Governador -Viso 27 dez. 2001 * Publicada na revista Viso em 27/12/2001 Viso: A circulao fsica do euro comea dentro de dias. Qual o balano que faz destes trs anos de moeda nica? Vtor Constncio: A introduo do euro deu-se em Janeiro de 1999. Desde essa data, o escudo no existe como moeda, existe apenas como unidade de conta, que ns usamos nas notas e moedas. O impacto econmico do euro deu-se nessa altura e tem sido uma histria de sucesso. Apesar de a taxa de cmbio em relao ao dlar ter vindo a descer, ao longo destes dois anos? No por a que se pode avaliar o sucesso deste projecto. Nem sequer por a que se pode avaliar o carcter forte do euro. Quais so os grandes feitos do euro? Foi um sucesso, porque desde o primeiro dia se criou um enorme mercado monetrio em euros, que funcionou sem problemas. O que contribuiu, muito rapidamente, para o surgimento de um grande mercado de dvida, de tal maneira que, em 1999, foram feitas emisses de obrigaes internacionais em euros de valor superior ao do dlar. E em 2000 quase aconteceu o mesmo. Houve um enorme aumento do papel do euro nos mercados de capitais, o que permitiu a grandes empresas contar com outro meio de financiamento e fazerem grandes operaes de aquisio e internacionalizao. Incluindo empresas portuguesas, que tiveram custos mais baixos e maior facilidade em emitir dvida para poderem investir na Amrica Latina e noutros stios. Esse sucesso visvel apenas no mercado de dvida? O que j seria muito importante. Mas mesmo em termos de instrumentos como as aces, com a denominao de todas elas em euros, houve tambm um aumento da importncia do euro em comparao com a que tinham as moedas que o integraram. E foi tambm um sucesso, na medida em que a poltica monetria europeia, desde Janeiro de 1999, foi bastante ajustada situao econmica da Europa. Mais do que nos anos que imediatamente precederam a entrada no euro. O euro deu, assim, um bom contributo economia... Na verdade, o euro iniciou a sua vida num perodo de relativa desacelerao econmica, e num perodo em que a inflao era muito baixa. As taxas de juro diminuram para valores nunca vistos, atingindo os 2,5 por cento. E isso contribuiu muito para a recuperao que se deu no final de 1999 e em 2000, ano em que a economia europeia cresceu 3,4 por cento. O maior crescimento dos ltimos dez anos. O contributo da existncia de um Banco Central Europeu... As taxas de juro esto, em termos reais, em valores historicamente baixos. Por exemplo, a mdia das taxas de juro reais da zona do euro, entre 1990 e 1998, foi da ordem dos 4,5%; neste momento as taxas de juro reais de curto prazo andam volta dos 2% e as de longo prazo variam entre 2% e 3%, consoante os pases. A poltica monetria tem sido adequada conjuntura europeia. Trata-se de um conjunto de factos que nos deixam afirmar que o euro foi um sucesso. Alis, o presidente da Reserva Federal norteamericana reconheceu que o euro, alm de ser a moeda de uma das zonas mais poderosas do mundo, conseguiu todos estes aspectos de funcionamento que fazem, de facto, a importncia de uma moeda. O euro provou ser uma moeda forte? A taxa de cmbio entre o euro e o dlar no um critrio para avaliar se o euro ou no uma moeda forte. Em primeiro lugar, porque essas flutuaes entre as vrias moedas europeias que antes existiam e o dlar aconteceram durante dcadas. Indo apenas aos anos 80 e 90, o marco desvalorizou-se cerca de 50%, entre 1980 e 1985; depois, em dois anos, valorizou-se quase 100%, desceu 26% e subiu 27%... Portanto, esta depreciao de 20 e poucos por cento, desde que o euro foi criado, tem de ser vista nesse quadro de flutuaes muito acentuadas e com grande variao, nas ltimas dcadas. O euro vai valorizar-se face ao dlar? No quer dizer que vai subir j, rapidamente, mas a experincia histrica mostra bem o que esta dana entre as moedas. Como avalia a fora de uma moeda? Avalia-se de acordo com vrios critrios. Em primeiro lugar, se contribuiu para um regime estvel de inflao baixa, ou seja, se assegura o valor interno da moeda. Isso , sobretudo, importante para uma zona econmica relativamente fechada como a zona do euro, que apenas importa do exterior 12% a 15%. Em segundo lugar, uma moeda forte se dispuser de mercados monetrios e financeiros diversificados e profundos, de forma a oferecer toda uma panplia completa de instrumentos de aplicao aos investidores, com baixos custos. Com o euro acontece isso, um pouco menos no que respeita ao mercado de aces, mas acentuadamente no mercado monetrio e no mercado de instrumentos de dvida. Em terceiro lugar, a moeda forte se revelar que os mercados tm confiana na manuteno de um regime de inflao baixa a longo prazo. E isso se reflectir nas taxas de juro de longo prazo, que so determinadas pelos mercados. Este um teste de mercado. Ora, desde que o euro existe, as taxas de juro dos ttulos dos tesouros europeus tm estado sistematicamente abaixo das taxas americanas. Isso reflecte uma confiana a prazo, de que o euro garante estabilidade macroeconmica num regime de inflao baixa. E um sinal de fortaleza do euro. A ttulo de exemplo, neste momento, a dvida a dez anos custa menos 0,3% ao Estado portugus que ao Estado americano. O que s possvel porque estamos no euro. Ser a primeira moeda mundial? Isso no sequer um objectivo. No se ganha muito em ter moeda a circular noutras zonas do mundo. conveniente para as empresas no terem problemas de risco cambial quando transaccionam com outros pases, o que tem um certo valor econmico. E, seguramente, tem um certo valor geopoltico. Mas o valor econmico, em sentido estrito, menos importante do que por vezes se imagina. No um objectivo, embora possa vir a existir. Estou convencido de que a importncia do euro vai continuar a aumentar, nos vrios domnios de utilizao, como moeda internacional. Mas estamos ainda numa fase preliminar. Qual o verdadeiro papel do euro? O objectivo principal do euro o de dar Europa autonomia na sua poltica monetria. Dar independncia. Isto , dar maior domnio sobre a conjuntura e, no fundo, sobre o seu destino. Como zona relativamente fechada, significa que pode gerir a poltica monetria, tendo em conta quase exclusivamente as suas necessidades de estabilidade macroeconmica, sem se preocupar excessivamente com problemas externos. Dando prioridade aos objectivos internos de conjuntura econmica, seja para controlar a inflao seja para minorar os riscos de uma recesso. O que muito importante, na medida em que no somos obrigados a seguir o que outras economias esto a fazer, quando isso no o mais adequado nossa. Essa maior autonomia, essa maior independncia, esse maior controlo sobre o destino da Europa o principal aspecto deste projecto. A actual diferena de polticas em matria de taxas de juro entre o BCE e a Fed um exemplo disso? . No sentido em que ns entendemos que, em relao s condies da economia europeia, as nossas taxas esto adequadas. O euro dispensa a unio poltica? um facto que estes trs anos do euro demonstram que pode funcionar sem haver uma unio poltica, no sentido mais estrito. Mas bom dizer que s assim porque se definiu um conjunto de regras e de instituies que implicam uma enorme partilha de soberanias. E que todo este projecto , em si mesmo, um projecto de unio poltica. Ou seja, quando os pases optaram pelo euro, decidiram que precisavam de partilhar soberanias para preservar os seus interesses. E fizeram-no. Foi decidido um sistema europeu de bancos centrais com grande independncia de funcionamento... ... com o modelo do Bundesbank, o banco central alemo... ... o mais independente do mundo. Com regras de funcionamento que implicam a participao dos governadores dos diferentes bancos centrais, o funcionamento descentralizado do sistema. As regras determinaram uma grande dose de unio poltica. H quem considere essa independncia excessiva... No vejo discusso em torno dela, pelo menos em termos oficiais. Mas surge, de vez em quando... Em termos de pr em causa o princpio da independncia, no tenho visto. uma escolha recente dos pases, foi feita e est nos tratados, nos textos constitucionais. Neste campo, j existe uma verdadeira unio poltica? Nesta matria j estamos na unio poltica. O euro prova, alis, como outras coisas que se passam na Europa, que o projecto europeu no est to em crise como muitas vezes se l. H sempre, em cada momento, e em particular nesta fase, motivos de frustrao com o projecto europeu. Nomeadamente, quando se colocaram agora problemas de defesa e poltica externa, houve algumas frustraes nesse domnio. Mas bom olharmos para trs e vermos a importncia do que j foi conseguido. Coisas que pareceriam impossveis h dez ou vinte anos. O euro era um desses projectos impossveis... Muita gente no mundo, e na Europa tambm, quase at s vsperas do euro, no acreditou que este projecto fosse possvel. E foi. uma alterao histrica fundamental. daqueles momentos em que a grande Histria nos passa por debaixo dos olhos -as aparncias dir-se-iam modestas, mas as consequncias so de enorme alcance. Com o significado que o euro tem para a evoluo e para a superao dos Estados-naes na Europa, este um desses momentos. H trs anos, disse que o euro tinha duas faces, uma de catalisador da liberalizao e outra de defensor do modelo social europeu. Qual est a ganhar? As duas faces coexistem, tm o seu papel e devero ter a sua influncia, em graus diferentes, em diferentes momentos. Na fase em que estamos, o euro e a Unio Monetria tm potenciado as tendncias liberalizantes. Ao mesmo tempo, e na medida em que a actual independncia de gesto macroeconmica possibilita uma melhor resposta a choques, permite tambm defender mais facilmente o modelo social europeu, se for essa a escolha dos governos. Esse papel do euro tambm est l e muito importante. A crise pode afectar o euro, nesta fase de transio para a moeda fsica? A crise poltica? A econmica... primeiro (ver caixa). Era prefervel que a introduo fsica do euro se fizesse num momento de maior euforia. Teria um impacto psicolgico maior. Mas o facto de estarmos num perodo de desacelerao e de incerteza econmica no cria dificuldades introduo fsica do euro. Tudo est a caminhar como previsto. A Europa est com um crescimento muito mais baixo, mas no entrou em recesso. Inclusive, pode pensar-se que a introduo bem sucedida dos espcimes em euros ter um efeito psicolgico positivo sobre a populao europeia em geral. E sobre a economia... O aspecto psicolgico muito importante. O impacto que tem nas pessoas, a partir do momento em que podem circular nos 12 pases com a mesma moeda, d um sentimento de pertena, de partilha de destino. Penso que isso contribui para um maior optimismo econmico na zona do euro. Por outro lado, o facto de acontecer num perodo de relativa desacelerao ajuda a afastar a ideia de que a introduo dos espcimes em euro poder contribuir para aumentar a inflao. E no poder, apesar da conjuntura desfavorvel? uma ideia errada. No h conjuntura que algum possa aproveitar para aumentar preos; a mudana para os espcimes em euro no afecta em nada o poder de mercado das empresas, que esto sujeitas mesma concorrncia; e, no que diz respeito aos arredondamentos e converses, tudo indica que o impacto diminuto. Mas pode haver impacto? Chegamos concluso que, na pior das hipteses, o impacto que teria no ndice de preos, e seria de uma vez s, no ultrapassaria 0,23 por cento. Estamos ento perante aumentos normais de final de ano? J houve acertos de preos anteriores. Penso que foi uma boa deciso impor a dupla afixao de preos desde 1 de Outubro, quando era apenas obrigatria para o perodo da dupla circulao. Faz-lo antes teve a dupla vantagem de tomar-se mais cedo conscincia desta operao e de permitir controlar a converso durante este perodo. E tambm fez com que alguns arredondamentos eventualmente feitos para cima se tenham diludo, neste perodo, sem grande impacto na inflao. Penso que isso ser visvel em Janeiro e Fevereiro. Acredita numa zona euro a 15? No mdio prazo acredito. Cinco anos parece-me um horizonte realista. Reino Unido includo? curioso, nas sondagens feitas no Reino Unido, existir uma maioria contra a entrada no euro, mas, simultaneamente, 70% da populao dizer que est convencida de que, a prazo, o euro substituir a libra. uma dicotomia interessante. E significa, no fundo, a compreenso de que o euro uma tendncia histrica inevitvel. E o impacto dos trs pases no euro? O impacto positivo. Porque refora o espao econmico do euro. No caso da Inglaterra, refora-o com a maior praa financeira europeia. Isso seria muito positivo para o euro. Estamos em plena fase de transio. Est tudo a decorrer como previsto? Fizemos o fornecimento das moedas aos bancos, em Setembro. As notas foram entregues em Outubro. Nesta fase de pr-abastecimento, tudo correu bem e dentro do previsto. Em Dezembro, entrmos na fase de os bancos fazerem o fornecimento ao comrcio. Isso est a decorrer mais devagar do que seria de prever, mas com normalidade. H alguns custos envolvidos nessa operao, tal como h para os bancos, e h algumas empresas maiores do sector que, talvez procurando ter menos custos, adiaram um pouco o processo. Mas as reunies que temos tido com as associaes revelam que acabar por estar tudo pronto nos primeiros dias de Janeiro. Os custos passam para o cliente final? Estamos a falar de valores muito reduzidos em relao ao volume de negcios dos sectores em causa, com efeitos muito diminutos na poltica de preos. O nvel de conhecimento mdio sobre o euro satisfaz? A avaliar pelas sondagens, Portugal est com nveis de conhecimento superiores mdia europeia, o que positivo. Mas, nas sondagens, os portugueses surgem nos ltimos lugares... Estou a falar do eurobarmetro, sobre o conhecimento da data e a taxa de converso. Esses so os aspectos principais para a populao em geral, e, a, estamos acima da mdia europeia. E quanto s empresas? Os inquritos da Comisso Nacional do Euro revelam muito bons resultados. A esmagadora maioria das empresas fez as operaes que tinha a fazer e est preparada para o euro. Mas h muita gente que continua sem informao sobre este processo... Haver problemas, sobretudo com alguns segmentos da populao, e a comunicao social ter muitas histrias nas primeiras semanas. Mas espero que no haja grandes problemas. Crise poltica

A actual crise poltica vai trazer problemas para a economia?

Como todas as crises, tem alguns custos. bom que a crise se resolva depressa, mas uma crise normal em democracia.

Que surge numa altura m...

Aparece numa altura de desacelerao econmica, o que no o melhor. Mas tambm creio poder dizer, com segurana, que no vai afectar de forma significativa o crescimento em 2002. As instituies funcionam, embora algumas decises mais significativas no possam ser tomadas. Felizmente, temos o Oramento aprovado. O aspecto central da vida da Administrao Pblica est assegurado desde o princpio do ano, e o resto da economia tem um quadro estvel para poder funcionar. Ou seja, os custos que resultam desta crise poltica, e evidente que h alguns, so relativamente pequenos.

Preparar eleies, formar um Governo, aprovar um novo Oramento...

Sem dvida, e isso tem o seu custo. Mas no creio que v afectar a taxa de crescimento da economia de forma significativa. O facto de estarmos no euro ajuda. Todo o enquadramento legal e institucional que resulta de sermos membros da Unio Europeia ajuda a uma estabilidade fundamental que a situao poltica no pe em causa.

No vem agravar anos que j seriam de grande exigncia e dificuldade poltica, ao nvel do equilbrio das contas pblicas e do cumprimento do Pacto de Estabilidade?

Os prximos anos so de grande exigncia nesses domnios, mas a situao actual no acrescenta novas dificuldades.

Estamos na fase final do grande volume de ajudas comunitrias.irrecuperveis?

No necessariamente. Este impasse pode trazer custosQuem tem acesso aos fundos pode continuar a fazer os seus projectos.

Mas no os grandes projectos...

As grandes decises claro que no.

E isso no o preocupa?

um custo. Mas nenhum grande projecto sofrer, de forma irremedivel, por trs meses de atraso.

Deve haver eleies antecipadas o mais rpido possvel?

Sobre isso no me pronuncio. O que eu digo que, qualquer que seja a deciso, deve ser tomada o mais rpido possvel.

H alguma soluo, melhor para a economia, que as eleies antecipadas?

A isso no respondo. Significaria pronunciar-me sobre matria poltica e no quero faz-lo.

Foi apontado como uma das hipteses para liderar o Partido Socialista...

J estou retirado da vida poltica h muitos anos. E estou num cargo de servio pblico, o que implica uma postura de total independncia poltica. Que acho que tenho mantido e vou continuar a manter. Estou retirado da vida poltica.

Em definitivo?

No tenho qualquer inteno, de qualquer espcie, de regressar vida poltica.

text: Interview of the Governor - Semanari... Interview of the Governor -Economic Weekly 28 Dec. 2001 *Published in the Economic Weekly on 12/28/2001 Economic Weekly - We are just days from the entry into circulation of the euro. Is confident in the success of the operation? Vitor Constancio - I think all conditions are met. The changes that were planned in recent months were made without problems. Banks have been supplied since September with coins and, since October, with banknotes. Therefore, everything is ready as expected. Still, can something go wrong? Of course, minor problems can always occur in such an operation. But I do not think they can be substantial, as banknotes and coins are distributed throughout the country, including the Autonomous Regions. The success of the operation will depend on the behaviour of economic agents. Than advice would give them? In relation to the general public, the essential aspect is the use of a new unit of account and that leads to the need for adaptation. It is important that people earn referrals and try to fix certain amounts that are important in their daily lives, such as their salary or the cost of the things they most often buy. Because having two or three references as a comparison term makes it easier to understand what the use of a new currency is. Although I admit that there are segments of the population that will have more difficulty, I believe that at the end of a while people will adapt to the new reality. Are you not afraid that with the introduction of the euro, inflation will skyrocket? Banco de Portugal carried out a study, together with THE INE, with simulations with various hypotheses associated with conversion and rounding, taking into account the attractive prices that companies want to present, and, at most, if all rounding were made upwards, there could be a one-off impact on the price index of 0.23 percentage points, which is very low. Some consumer associations have doubts about the results of this study... It must not be forgotten that the physical introduction of the euro does not alter the market power of companies in any way. In most markets there is competition, so companies will have great difficulty taking advantage of to raise prices. On the other hand, we are in a phase of economic slowdown across the euro area and this is not a climate that favours price increases. In Portugal there are some complaints regarding the distribution of the costs of the operation. No should Banco de Portugal have been responsible for these costs? A currency change operation has costs and the company has to assume those costs in general. There are clearly advantages to the economy, particularly for companies that have been benefiting from low interest rates and who without the euro would not have had it. So I think it is normal for these costs to be shared by the various economic actors. The decision that was taken at the general level of the euro countries was not to enter into a general scheme of subsidies and payments of this operation. There have been different practices in supply operations between countries and between banks within the same country, but no country has imposed rules on banks for this operation. Banks have costs and, in a way that depends on their trade policy, they have done the supply operation to retailers, with practices that are different according to their business relationships. Three years ago the European economic situation was not expected to deteriorate as it happened. Is this a good timing for the introduction of the euro? It would be preferable if the physical introduction of the euro were in a period of greater economic euphoria, because then everything is easier. In any case, this period of lower growth - and that's what we're talking about, because we're not in recession - doesn't make the operation any harder. And it may even happen that the psychological effect of the introduction of the euro can create a period of greater optimism in people. Although the great economic effects of the creation of the euro have taken on since January 1999, the psychological effects are enormous and sectors such as tourism or e-commerce can benefit greatly. What about political instability? Could it somehow affect this operation? No. The institutions operate and the Government has the capacity to manage it. Some say that the euro can encourage consumption and others that it may retract. Or which is more likely? Either possibility will be very temporary. There may be a first moment of adaptation that can retract consumption, but it will be very fast. From there there there may be phenomena of monetary illusion, since, for all countries, the introduction of the euro represents a division and therefore an apparent reduction in prices. I believe, however, that such effects will never be very significant and only temporary. The euro as a currency has been around for three years. Has the effect been positive for the economy? The great economic impact of the euro began even before January 1999 and was linked to the drop in interest rates and capital costs for businesses, which manifested itself more intensely after January 1999. One of the great achievements of the euro was the very rapid creation of a money market and debt instruments in euros cheaper and deeper than they existed before. This allowed European and Portuguese companies access to financing at a lower cost of capital. This greatly facilitated all the internationalization operations of the companies. Individuals also felt this ease in accessing credit... Which is natural. At the beginning of the 1990s, housing interest was around 20% and now, in nominal terms, they are between 5% and 6%. And in nominal terms wages have gone up a lot compared to what they were at the beginning of the decade, so the financial effort to access credit is much smaller. This caused households, which had at the beginning of the decade a total indebtedness of 18.5% of their disposable income and paid 4.7% interest at that time, at the end of the decade have an indebtedness level of 83% and pay 4.1% in interest. The improvement in the standard of living of the population as a result of this was indeed impressive. But do you recognize the existence of cases of excessive indebtedness? Excessive indebtedness is difficult to qualify. Firstly, when the comparison is made, there are European countries with higher levels. Secondly, the financial effort with interest charges has even been reduced. Now, of course, indebtedness has limits and that is why we have seen a slowdown in demand for housing and durable consumer goods. This does not allow us to say that indebtedness is excessive. For example, uneven credit values continue to fall. And the indebtedness of the bank abroad, also not worries you? Portuguese banks are careful and, in fact, when we look at the ratings and solvency ratios of our banks, we see that they are at perfectly adequate values. We have followed liquidity management closely and it has been found throughout 2001 that banks have issued more medium-term debt instruments and greatly reduced dependence on credit growth this year in relation to short-term interbank financing. The existing situation is normal. The possibility of securitisation operations could help banking in its financing... We have recently issued a notice regulating prudential aspects related to securitisation. We have also submitted a draft decree on securitisation to the Government some time ago which, if approved, will facilitate the creation of vehicle institutions for securitisation operations and hopefully that can come out. What about the introduction of countercyclical provisions? Are you ready to move? This issue, which we have been looking at for some time now, is being discussed in Europe as dynamic provisions, because it has been found that the regime that normally exists is pro-cyclical. Thus, we discuss the change of this system for structural reasons and that have nothing to do with a particular conjuncture. What was the downperformance of the euro in the foreign exchange markets? Judging one currency from the evolution of the exchange rate against another is a bad evaluation criterion. In the last 20 years there have been greater fluctuations between European currencies against the dollar. It is possible to reconstitute a synthetic euro from the currencies that constitute it and, if we look at exchange rates backwards, we see that in 1985 the euro was at much lower values than it is today. But the ECB would certainly like to see the euro at a higher level... The exchange rate is not an objective of European monetary policy. It's just an element we look at to see what impact it can have on inflation. But as the euro zone is a relatively closed space that imports 12% to 15% from abroad, exchange rates have a relatively low impact on domestic inflation. There are many temporary factors that have affected the evolution of the euro, without, however, putting at risk what is essential, which is the internal value of the currency. Domestic inflation has been falling and falling into figures that are the objective of European monetary policy, which is to be below 2%. This is the essential aspect, because if almost 90% of what is used for consumption or investment in the euro area is produced internally, what must prevail is the problem of the internal value of the currency, that is, low inflation, and this is ensured. Do you therefore believe that the euro is, following these criteria, a strong currency? Yes. In addition, assessing a currency for a large economic zone, such as the euro area, must first be done on the basis of the internal value of the currency, secondly, the depth and efficiency of the money and financial markets and, thirdly, the level of medium and long-term interest rates, which are entirely determined by the markets. In this case, the rates are low, which corresponds to the confidence that, in the long run, the currency ensures a low inflation regime. The medium and long-term interest rates of the euro have been systematically lower than the dollar's interest rates. Markets believe that, on a 10-year scale, the euro will ensure a lower inflation regime than the United States and this is a criterion for a strong currency. Budget policy h2With the euro, our monetary policy came to be decided in Frankfurt... /h2 pIn Frankfurt, but with our participation. /p h2Still, there are serious implications for the Portuguese economy of monetary decisions taken for the whole euro area... /h2 pWith its participation in the European Union, a commitment to ensure full freedom of movement of capital. For a economy such as Portugal, the use of exchange rates as an instrument has limitations and is not efficient. The choice that Portugal made was the right one and from there we Benefits. Of course, there are consequences for having to respect certain disciplines. Benefit from an inflation regime and low interest rates also implies that there is an appropriate income policy. That is, we cannot have a cost evolution that is far removed from the evolution of average inflation european union because, if not, we will lose competitiveness and have problems. /p h2I mean, without productivity increases can there be no wage increases? /h2 pThis is always true whatever the monetary and exchange rate regime. Or average living level of a population only increases if it increases real productivity. That means being aware that there is and cannot be monetary illusion. Live in a scheme that, in the long term, will always be low inflation and we have to realize that increases in purchasing power and standard of living have to be accompanied by productivity increases. We have been evolving in this respect and in the 1990s possible to deflate without large costs./p h2Our inflation has been above the European average. Is this sustainable?/h2 pA member country of the Union monetary policy cannot permanently and systematically have an inflation rate above partners. This will not happen, because if, by an internal behavior costs and prices, we start to have higher inflation for a very long time. time, we lose competitiveness, we will have more unemployment and the economy will adjust to inflation rate. However, it is not necessary for inflation rates to be the same. Is possible to live with a differential such as what we have had on average since January 1999. We must understand that a single monetary policy involves convergence for the European area by all member countries.there will be an internalization of new rules of operation and regulation of the economy, which has not yet fully happened in Portugal. /p h2E level budgetary, is there discipline? /h2 pNo. The new rules here were also not fully internalized. Living in monetary union leaves countries as internal regulatory instrument for the use of budgetary policy, in particular automatic stabilizers. Which means that it is absolutely essential to any member of monetary union has an anticyclical fiscal policy and, therefore, to have a loose situation in periods of economic expansion in order to be able to automatic stabilizers in periods of deceleration. This is an absolutely indispensable rule. It was also a rule that was not fully fulfilled, but anyway... We will, as in all countries, learn from the experience, because we will now have to make a difficult adjustment in the field of budget in the next two to three years. Something we're going to have to do that's going to require great courage, great realism and great consensus, but that will allow all we understand better that, in fact, fiscal policy has to have a anticyclic behavior./p Glossary FAQ Site map Useful links Legal notices Csirt contacts

Entrevista do Governador -Semanrio Econmico 28 dez. 2001 *Publicada no Semanrio Econmico em 28/12/2001 Semanrio Econmico -Estamos a poucos dias da entrada em circulao do euro. Est confiante no sucesso da operao? Vtor Constncio -Penso que todas as condies esto reunidas. As alteraes que estavam previstas nos ltimos meses foram realizadas sem problemas. Os bancos foram abastecidos, desde Setembro, com as moedas e, desde Outubro, com as notas. Portanto, tudo est pronto conforme o previsto. Ainda assim, pode alguma coisa correr mal? Como evidente, podem sempre acontecer pequenos problemas numa operao desta envergadura. Mas no creio que possam ser substanciais, visto que as notas e as moedas esto distribudas por todo o pas, incluindo as Regies Autnomas. O sucesso da operao vai depender do comportamento dos agentes econmicos. Que conselhos lhes daria? Em relao ao pblico em geral, o aspecto essencial a utilizao de uma nova unidade de conta e que leva necessidade de uma adaptao. importante que as pessoas ganhem referncias e que procurem fixar certos montantes que so importantes na sua vida quotidiana, tal como os seu salrio ou o custo das coisas que mais frequentemente compram. Porque ter duas ou trs referncias como termo de comparao facilita compreender o que a utilizao de uma nova moeda. Embora admita que haja segmentos da populao que vo ter mais dificuldade, acredito que ao final de um tempo as pessoas se vo adaptar nova realidade. No receia que com a introduo do euro a inflao dispare? O Banco de Portugal realizou um estudo, em conjunto com o INE, com simulaes com hipteses vrias associadas converso e aos arredondamentos, tendo em conta os preos atractivos que as empresas queiram apresentar, e, no mximo, se todos os arredondamentos fossem feitos para cima, poderia haver um impacto pontual no ndice de preos de 0,23 pontos percentuais, o que muito baixo. Algumas associaes de consumidores tm dvidas quanto aos resultados desse estudo... preciso no esquecer que a introduo fsica do euro no altera em nada o poder de mercado das empresas. Na maior parte dos mercados h concorrncia, portanto as empresas tero grandes dificuldades em aproveitar para aumentar os preos. Por outro lado, estamos numa fase de abrandamento econmico em toda a zona euro e esta no uma conjuntura que favorea aumentos de preos. Em Portugal h algumas queixas em relao repartio dos custos da operao. No deveria ter sido o Banco de Portugal a responsabilizar-se por esses custos? Uma operao de mudana de moeda tem custos e a sociedade tem de assumir esses custos de forma geral. H claramente vantagens para a economia, nomeadamente para as empresas que tm estado a beneficiar de taxas de juro baixas e que sem o euro no teriam tido. Por isso, penso que normal que esses custos sejam partilhados pelos vrios agentes econmicos. A deciso que foi tomada a nvel geral dos pases do euro foi de no entrar num esquema geral de subsdios e de pagamentos desta operao. Tm existido, sim, prticas diferentes nas operaes de abastecimento entre pases e entre bancos dentro do mesmo pas, mas nenhum pas imps regras aos bancos para esta operao. Os bancos tm custos e, de uma forma que depende da sua poltica comercial, fizeram a operao de abastecimento aos retalhistas, com prticas que so diferentes de acordo com as relaes comerciais que tm. H trs anos no se esperava que a conjuntura econmica europeia se deteriorasse como aconteceu. Este um bom timing para a introduo do euro? Era prefervel se a introduo fsica do euro fosse num perodo de maior euforia econmica, porque a tudo mais fcil. Em todo o caso, este perodo de menor crescimento -e disso que estamos a falar, pois no estamos em recesso -no dificulta em nada a operao. E pode at acontecer que o efeito psicolgico da introduo do euro possa criar um perodo de maior optimismo nas pessoas. Embora os grandes efeitos econmicos da criao do euro se tenham dado desde Janeiro de 1999, os efeitos psicolgicos so enormes e sectores como o turismo ou o e-commerce podem beneficiar muito. E a instabilidade poltica? Pode, de alguma maneira, afectar esta operao? No. As instituies funcionam e o Governo tem capacidade de gesto corrente. H quem diga que o euro pode incentivar o consumo e outros que o pode vir a retrair. O que mais provvel? Qualquer das hipteses ser muito temporria. Poder haver um primeiro momento de adaptao que pode retrair o consumo, mas ser muito rpido. A partir da pode haver fenmenos de iluso monetria, j que, para todos os pases, a introduo do euro representa uma diviso e, portanto, uma reduo aparente de preos. Creio, no entanto, que efeitos deste tipo nunca sero muito significativos e apenas temporrios. O euro como divisa j existe h trs anos. O efeito tem sido positivo para a economia? O grande impacto econmico do euro comeou ainda antes de Janeiro de 1999 e esteve associado quebra das taxas de juro e dos custos do capital para as empresas, o que se manifestou com maior intensidade depois de Janeiro de 1999. Uma das grandes realizaes do euro foi a criao muito rpida de um mercado monetrio e de instrumentos de dvida em euros mais baratos e mais profundos do que existiam antes. O que permitiu s empresas europeias e portuguesas acesso a financiamento com um custo de capital inferior. Isso facilitou imenso todas as operaes de internacionalizao das empresas. Os particulares tambm sentiram essa facilidade no acesso ao crdito... O que natural. No incio da dcada de 90 os juros para habitao andavam nos 20% e agora, em termos nominais, esto entre os 5% e os 6%. E em termos nominais os salrios subiram muito em relao ao que eram no incio da dcada, pelo que o esforo financeiro para aceder ao crdito muito menor. O que fez que as famlias, que tinham no incio da dcada um endividamento total de 18,5% do seu rendimento disponvel e pagavam nessa altura de juros 4,7% deste, no fim da dcada tm um nvel de endividamento de 83% e pagam 4,1% em juros. A melhoria do nvel de vida da populao em resultado disto foi de facto impressionante. Mas reconhece a existncia de casos de excessivo endividamento? O excessivo endividamento difcil de qualificar. Em primeiro lugar, quando se faz a comparao verifica-se que existem pases europeus com nveis superiores. Em segundo lugar, o esforo financeiro com encargos com juros at se reduziu. Agora, claro que o endividamento tem limites e por isso que temos assistido a uma desacelerao da procura de habitao e de bens de consumo duradouros. O que no permite dizer que o endividamento excessivo. Por exemplo, os valores do crdito mal parado continuam a descer. E o endividamento da banca no exterior, tambm no o preocupa? Os bancos portugueses so cuidadosos e, de facto, quando olhamos para os ratings e para os rcios de solvabilidade dos nossos bancos, vemos que esto em valores perfeitamente adequados. Temos seguido de perto a gesto da liquidez e verificou-se, ao longo de 2001, que os bancos emitiram mais instrumentos de dvida de mdio prazo e reduziram bastante a dependncia para o crescimento do crdito deste ano em relao ao financiamento interbancrio de curto prazo. A situao existente normal. A possibilidade de realizar operaes de titularizao poderia ajudar a banca no seu financiamento... Publicmos recentemente um aviso a regular os aspectos prudenciais ligados titularizao. Apresentmos tambm h j algum tempo ao Governo um projecto de decreto sobre titularizao que, a ser aprovado, facilitar a criao de instituies de veculo para a realizao de operaes de titularizao e esperemos que isso possa vir a sair. E a introduo de provises anticclicas? Est pronta a avanar? Esta questo, que estamos a analisar h j algum tempo, discute-se na Europa com o nome de provises dinmicas, porque se verificou que o regime que normalmente existe pr-cclico. Assim, discute-se a alterao deste sistema por razes estruturais e que nada tm a haver com uma conjuntura particular. A que se deveu o mau desempenho do euro nos mercados cambiais? Julgar uma moeda a partir da evoluo da taxa de cmbio em relao a outra um mau critrio de avaliao. Nos ltimos 20 anos houve maiores flutuaes entre as moedas europeias em relao ao dlar. possvel reconstituir um euro sinttico a partir das moedas que o constituem e, se formos ver a taxas de cmbio para trs, verificamos que, em 1985, o euro estava em valores muito inferiores aos que est hoje. Mas o BCE gostaria certamente de ver o euro a um nvel mais elevado... A taxa de cmbio no um objectivo da poltica monetria europeia. apenas um elemento que analisamos para ver qual o impacto que pode ter na inflao. Mas, como a zona euro um espao relativamente fechado que importa 12% a 15% do exterior, as taxas de cmbio tm um impacto relativamente reduzido na inflao interna. H muitos factores temporrios que afectaram a evoluo do euro, sem, no entanto, terem posto em risco aquilo que essencial, que o valor interno da moeda. A inflao interna tem vindo a descer e a situar-se em valores que constituem o objectivo da poltica monetria europeia, que ficar abaixo dos 2%. Este que o aspecto essencial, porque se quase 90% daquilo que utilizado em consumo ou investimento na zona do euro produzido internamente, o que deve predominar o problema do valor interno da moeda, ou seja, uma baixa inflao, e essa assegurada. Acredita, portanto, que o euro , seguindo esses critrios, uma moeda forte? Sim. Alm disso, avaliar uma moeda para uma grande zona econmica, como a zona do euro, deve ser feito, primeiro, em funo do valor interno da moeda, em segundo lugar, da profundidade e eficincia dos mercados monetrios e financeiros e, em terceiro lugar, do nvel de taxas de juros de mdio e longo prazo, que so totalmente determinadas pelos mercados. Neste caso, as taxas so baixas, o que corresponde confiana que, a longo prazo, a moeda assegura um regime de inflao baixa. As taxas de juro de mdio e longo prazo do euro tm sistematicamente sido inferiores s taxas de juro do dlar. Os mercados acreditam que, numa escala de 10 anos, o euro assegurar um regime de inflao mais baixa que os Estados Unidos e isso um critrio de uma moeda forte. Poltica oramental

Com o euro, a nossa poltica monetria passou a ser decidida em Frankfurt...

Em Frankfurt, mas com a nossa participao.

Ainda assim, existem srias implicaes para a economia portuguesa das decises monetrias tomadas para toda a zona euro...

Com a sua participao na Unio Europeia, tomou-se um compromisso de assegurar a total liberdade de circulao de capitais. Para uma pequena economia como Portugal, o uso das taxas de cmbio como instrumento tem limitaes e no eficiente. A escolha que Portugal fez foi a adequada e da tirarmos benefcios. Claro que da decorrem consequncias no sentido de termos de respeitar certas disciplinas. Beneficiar de um regime de inflao e taxas de juro baixas tambm implica que se verifique uma poltica de rendimentos adequada. Ou seja, no podemos ter uma evoluo dos custos que seja muito afastada da evoluo da inflao mdia europeia porque, se no, perderemos competitividade e teremos problemas.

Ou seja, sem aumentos de produtividade no pode haver aumentos salariais?

Isso sempre verdade qualquer que seja o regime monetrio e cambial. O nvel de vida mdio de uma populao s aumenta se aumentar a produtividade real. Isso significa ter conscincia que no h e no podemos ter iluso monetria. Vivemos num regime que, a prazo, ser sempre de inflao baixa e temos que perceber que aumentos de poder de compra e de nvel de vida tm de ser acompanhados por aumentos de produtividade. Temos vindo a evoluir neste aspecto e na dcada de 90 foi possvel desinflacionar sem grandes custos.

A nossa inflao tem estado acima da mdia europeia. Isso sustentvel?

Um pas membro da Unio Monetria no pode ter de forma permanente e sistemtica uma taxa de inflao acima dos seus parceiros. Isso no acontecer, pois se, por um comportamento interno errado de custos e preos, comearmos a ter uma inflao mais alta durante muito tempo, perdemos competitividade, teremos mais desemprego e a economia ajustar a taxa de inflao. No necessrio, contudo, que as taxas de inflao sejam iguais. possvel viver com um diferencial tal como o que temos tido em mdia desde Janeiro de 1999. Temos de compreender que uma s poltica monetria implica comportamentos de convergncia para a rea europeia por parte de todos os pases membros.haver uma interiorizaro de novas regras de funcionamento e de regulao daTem de economia, coisa que ainda no aconteceu totalmente em Portugal.

E a nvel oramental, h disciplina?

No. As novas regras, aqui, tambm no foram totalmente interiorizadas. Viver em Unio Monetria deixa aos pases como instrumento de regulao interna a utilizao da poltica oramental, nomeadamente os estabilizadores automticos. O que significa que absolutamente essencial a qualquer membro da Unio Monetria ter uma poltica oramental anticclica e, portanto, ter uma situao folgada em perodos de expanso econmica para poder deixar funcionar os estabilizadores automticos em perodos de desacelerao. Esta uma regra absolutamente imprescindvel. Tambm foi uma regra que no foi totalmente cumprida, mas enfim... Iremos, como em todos os pases, aprender com a experincia, porque vamos ter agora de fazer um ajustamento difcil em matria oramental nos prximos dois a trs anos. Algo vamos ter de fazer que vai exigir grande coragem, grande realismo e grandes consensos, mas que vai permitir que todos compreendamos melhor que, de facto, a poltica oramental tem que ter um comportamento anticclico.

Title: Governor's Interview - Express
text: Governor's Interview - Express 29 Dec. 2001 * Published in expresso weekly on 12/29/2001 Express - There are studies that point to small variations in consumer prices resulting from the introduction of the euro. What's your opinion? Vitor Constancio - In addition to the, say, mechanical aspect of conversion and small adjustments for companies to present so-called attractive prices (below a rounded number), the simulations made by Banco de Portugal, with the goods and services integrated in the purchasing basket and the price index, give, in a pessimistic scenario, an effect of a small increase in prices of 0.23, and, in an optimistic scenario, make downward adjustments (due to the need to present psychological prices), with a reduction of 0.26. But what is the impact on prices? Firstly, the physical introduction of the euro does not create a situation in which companies could really take advantage of rising prices, because they were always at risk of competitors not doing so. Secondly, the euro will be introduced in a period of economic slowdown in Europe, and this is not a favourable environment for price increases by businesses. So everything is a factor that leads me to be quite optimistic about a very small impact of the euro on the inflation rate, as we will see in January. But there is already knowledge of some cases of rounding up. Can't they influence the inflation rate? No. This would have occurred since 1 October, when the double display was imposed. I would remind you, however, that the inflation rate fell from October to November. Do you admit that the period of double circulation does not last more than 15 days? You can. I think that process will be quick. I don't know if it's going to be 15 days, but it's going to be quick. I wouldn't be surprised if the replacement took place in the first two weeks. People tend to keep memories of both coins and banknotes. Is this marginal in the process of collecting the shields in circulation or does it have any meaning? Our prediction is that in the currencies it will not be marginal. We think that there will indeed be many coins that will not be exchanged. As for the notes, I admit that some people keep them from remembrance, but there will not be many, and there will be many per person, so this will not have much meaning. But for 20 years Banco de Portugal will exchange any of the shield notes that are currently in circulation. The 20-year period that Banco de Portugal gives for this exchange is also longer than that granted in other countries... yes, but there are also countries that have bigger ones. There are countries that have an infinite deadline. In Germany, for example, a citizen can exchange milestone notes at any time. As long as the Bundesbank exists, they will honor your grades. Other countries are five or ten years old. What will happen to the collected notes and coins? Will they be destroyed? Completely. The coins repaid pass to the new coin, and the banknotes will be made into tiny pieces and compacted into bricks on their own machines. How many notes and coins will be collected? Some 1500 million coins and about 320 million banknotes will be collected. This is what's in circulation. As I say, in the coins we predict that there will be a big break. Not in the notes. Will the euro change the habits of the Portuguese, forcing us to walk with a higher number of coins? Of course i do. In a first phase, conversions do give, in fact, cents, and you have to have penny coins to make the change, without forgetting that a penny is approximately two escudos. Why doesn't Portugal make 500 euro banknotes? Because the quantities that will certainly be sought in Portugal of notes of these amounts are very small, which meant making plates and preparing the equipment for a mini-production. It would be very expensive to produce small quantities. It would be uneconomic. Returning to prices, a trend that exists is to make the price comparison at the level of the different countries of Europe of the euro. Do you think this might introduce some hits or some variations? As the famous James Tobin said, "coins are like languages, if there was only one better understanding." With the euro the comparations will be easier and this will have an effect on price transparency. It will be a slow process, not necessarily a process of absolute convergence, because there are goods more transacted than others and there are specific distribution conditions that make the costs may be different here or there, so there are always economic reasons for some differences. All this means that there are, even in monetary unions in a single country, price differences between different regions, and this will continue to exist in Europe, but there will be a slow trend towards some convergences. Will taxation be a differentiating element? Taxation will in fact introduce elements of differentiation, as is the case between the various US states, to give the example of a large existing monetary union; like wage differences, for example in distribution, they also lead to different costs, and this legitimately allows prices to be different. But the pressure will exist in the low direction. Increased competition will dictate this law, which is in favour of a fall in inflation. That will also require some tax cuts? It may happen, but there are also studies, done at the time of the preparation of the reports for monetary union, which show that between the US states there are indirect tax differences of five and six points and remain so. That is, differences of this order do not lead to changes and are compatible with the functioning of the economy without problems. There will be limits, of course. If there are differences of 10 or 20 points, this will lead to adjustments, but one can live with significant differences, as the experience of the United States demonstrates. And will there be a tendency to converge on wages? In that case, it would be on the rise, of course. But I hope not, because I think there is already sufficient understanding that mere monetary conversion does not change economic conditions, namely does not alter the productivity relations of economies. In the long run, as we know, wages are conditional and tend to align with the relative productivity levels of the different countries. If they try not to comply with this law, the result will of course be unemployment. That consciousness exists. People are informed. Trade unionists are aware of these phenomena, and I therefore believe that there will be no great pressure to do so. There will be some influence, it is indisputable, especially in the analysis of less informed people. But we will have to fight this trend, and I think that business and trade union leaders are well aware of this problem. How long will it take Portugal to reach European level? We have been less developed than Europe for centuries and in recent decades we have been growing at a rate higher than the European average, so we are converging. When we entered the European Union in '85, we had an income per inhabitant, in purchasing power parities, which was 53% or 54% of the European average, and now we have 74%. We are the country that has had the fastest progression in these 15 years since the outing. More: if we look at the last few decades, we are among the countries in the world that have had a higher growth rate. For example, with comparable statistical data on purchasing power parities for all countries from 1950 to 1992, we are among the ten countries that grew faster at an average annual rate.. I do not think we should be discouraged from this process of convergence. It can be concluded that it considers that the Portuguese economy is not as bad as it is said... The last thing I'd like to look like was optimistic. I am aware of our vulnerabilities and the difficulties to overcome. On the other hand, I do not believe that the climate of self-flagellation that we have been going through is justified. There is a slowdown in the growth of the Portuguese economy, which was to be expected and even, I would say, after the previous strong growth, inevitable, because we have to understand that there was a phase in which we had a period of very strong growth in domestic demand. We continue to maintain an investment rate that is the highest in Europe, and this was made possible by the substantial decrease in financing costs and the cost of capital in general for businesses. The fall in interest rates has rationally led individuals and businesses to higher levels of indebtedness, because they are now solvent to do so, but obviously this has limits. Domestic spending had to start to slow and began to slow last year in the second half. That was desirable and has to be understood. Even so we have grown, both last year and this year, marginally above Europe's average growth rate, so we are not in a very anomalous situation. What we are facing is a very difficult budgetary situation and structural problems that condition our development and are slow ly resolving. In terms of public spending? Yes, that will require major adjustments in the next two or three years, requiring big decisions. And I think that will require a greater national consensus. I stress, however, that there is not exactly a situation of technical unsustainability of Portuguese public finances. We have, for example, a debt ratio that is lower than the European average (that is not what this is about). We have international commitments in the context of the European Union and the Stability Pact, which we must respect. And this imposes certain targets, which are, in the long term, useful for the Portuguese economy, because it is necessary to make fiscal policy a countercyclical policy instrument permanently. We have to realise that living in monetary union, fiscal policy must always have that characteristic. That hasn't happened in the last few years. We also have structural problems that concern our decades-long or even secular delay. The main thing is at the educational level which, although in the process of correction, progresses at too slow a pace. The indicator that impressed me most in recent times was the percentage of the population that has completed secondary education. We have 21% in the population aged 25 to 65 with secondary education, and we could imagine that we would be correcting this very quickly in the new generations, which unfortunately does not happen at the desirable rate, because even in the population aged 25 to 29 the percentage is only 35%, when the European average is above 70%. Portuguese society will have to harden because we need greater financial responsibility, greater discipline and culture of effort and to accept, with the coldness of historical processes, the changes in the productive structures that await us.

Penso que no nos devemos desencorajar em relao  continuao desse processo de convergncia. Pode concluir-se que considera que a economia portuguesa no est assim to mal quanto se diz... A descida das taxas de juro conduziu racionalmente os particulares e as empresas a nveis de endividamento mais elevados, porque agora so solventes para o fazer, mas obviamente que isso tem limites. A despesa interna tinha de comear a desacelerar e comeou a desacelerar o ano passado, no segundo semestre. Isso era desejvel e tem de ser compreendido. Mesmo assim ns crescemos, quer no ano passado quer este ano, marginalmente acima da taxa mdia de crescimento da Europa, portanto no estamos numa situao muito anmala. O que temos pela frente  uma situao oramental muito difcil e problemas estruturais que condicionam o nosso desenvolvimento e so de resoluo lenta. Em termos da despesa pblica?
