Title: Declaration of the Governor Vitor Constncio - News conference related to the entry into circulation of the euro banknotes and coins
text: Declaration of the Governor Vitor C... Declaration of the Governor Vitor Constancio -News conference related to the entry into circulation of the euro banknotes and coins 31 Dec. 2001 31 December 2001 Tomorrow the euro banknotes and coins will enter into circulation. This is a unique moment in the world and in the European monetary history. Twelve countries renounce their monetary symbols and share sovereignty in such a relevant domain. In a globalised world, the euro will enable the European Union and its participating Member States to better control their own destiny. The European unity project becomes now particularly strengthened. The existence of a single currency is a key factor to guarantee the peace and prosperity of a continent, which suffered in the past the torments of wars and conflicts. The euro will change Europe and it has changed Portugal. The preparations for participation in the euro took a decade and involved two governments, to whose converging activity I would like to pay tribute today. There was foresight and discipline in the accomplishment of the strategy. The country meets its obligations when it has clear objectives and well-defined targets. This decade witnessed a first adjustment stage in which inflation was brought down to European levels and a second stage in which we have already enjoyed the benefits of a new low inflation regime. It was also a decade in which the Portuguese financial system gained increased strength and saw a modernisation. Without our participation in the euro there would not have been room for the structural fall in interest rates, which paved the way for thousands of households to have access to credit and to a wide range of durable consumer goods, thus improving their standard of living. Likewise, companies also started to benefit from lower financial charges and, with the lower cost of capital, they could more easily invest and modernise themselves. History will record the changes undertaken by the country in the last decade as extraordinary and it will also report the impressive improvement recorded in the standard of living in such a short period. Like any good currency, the euro has thus two sides: the one that makes us benefit from low inflation and low interest rates and the demanding side, which imposes discipline in the income policy and financial responsibility in the fiscal policy. We cannot ignore the new operating rules imposed by the euro. The lowest cost is the one related to the adjustment that needs to be currently made to a new currency unit. Getting used to a new currency is what our emigrants usually do, without great difficulty, as well as all those who have had the opportunity of travelling abroad. We shall not therefore exaggerate the effort that we shall have to make to get used to the new monetary species. For a period of two months, i.e. until the end of February, banknotes and coins denominated in escudos will continue to be legal tender. Afterwards, the escudo will forever cease to circulate; it will be possible however to exchange escudo banknotes at banks until June and at the Banco de Portugal during the next twenty years. Banknotes shall preferably be exchanged at banks. All ATMs will start to dispense only euro banknotes at the end of four days. There is no need to rush or to be afraid of not being prepared in the first day. During the first days, mixed payments should be avoided, i.e. the payment of an amount partly in euro and partly in escudo. As far as possible, payments of small amounts should be made using the exact money. Retailers shall endeavour to give the exchange only in euro. These are some simple rules for a smooth and effective changeover. Let me take this opportunity to extend my thanks to the trade and banking sectors for the excellent co-operation given to all the preparation process of this huge logistic operation. The country is counting on both sectors to contribute to a smooth physical introduction of the euro. I would also like to thank the media for the excellent work they have done in the disclosure of all the aspects related to the introduction of the new banknotes and coins. Along with the remarkable work of Comissao Nacional do Euro, and without the effort of the media, the population would not have been as prepared as it is today. Every detail was planned with the required lead time and care. The dual circulation period will enable a smooth adjustment. With serenity, we are going to overcome the remaining resistance and difficulties associated with the entry into circulation of the new currency, so that we can build a better future for the new generations.

Title: Governor's Article - Public
text: Article of the Governor -Public Article of the Governor -Public 31 Dec. 2001 By Vitor Constancio "In this place and today, a time is opened in the history of the world and we can say that we saw its origin" (Goethe) The euro has existed for three years as a real currency. However, as the famous Moliere's character who proseed without knowing it, also all used it without realizing what they were doing. Truly as a currency, the shield has disappeared since January 1999 and has continued to exist merely as a fraction of the euro, that is, as a unit of account. Since that date the euro is our currency, but a fraction of the euro we have continued to call shield and the circulation of banknotes and coins has been done in that unit of account to which we are accustomed. The great economic and historical scope of the creation of the euro took place three years ago and many did not realize it. Here applies to what Jorge Luis Borges called the modesty of the story that passes through us "demure", because "its essential dates, for a long time, can be equally secret". It is, moreover, Borges who uses the quote of Goethe that I put in the epigraph, said symptomatically about the defeat of the German army in Valmy in 1792 as he prepared to take Paris and stifle the French Revolution. In a fundamental contrast, the date we are now celebrating is, on the contrary, the realisation of the project of European unity aimed at ensuring the peace and prosperity of the continent. Conceived by Jean Monnet after The Second World War, with the aim, among others, of installing permanent peace between Germany and France, the European project comes to a high point with the creation of the euro, now finally visible to all in the banknotes and coins that begin its circulation. On the subject of the European project Monnet used to say that "more than uniting states sought to unite peoples". The common currency is an important vehicle for achieving this objective, since, as the famous James Tobin says with the rationalism proper to economists: "the currency is like languages, if there were only one better understanding". The creation of the euro is a unique moment in the history of Europe and the world. Other attempts at partial monetary integration in Europe, such as the Latin Monetary Union (1865-1927) or its Scandinavian counterpart (1873-1931), did not have a single currency or a Common Central Bank. The current project of the euro corresponds to an extraordinary sharing of sovereignty between old nations that thus subsume themselves in order to better survive. In a globalized world, with free movement of capital, even the average nations have full monetary sovereignty. That is why the euro now arises and, at this stage of human history, it fully corresponds to the Hegelian "spirit of the world". European history in recent decades proves that only Germany had monetary sovereignty because it alone defined its interest rate policy according to its own economic situation. For the other countries, the game consisted of trying to follow German politics. It is understood that their leaders preferred to participate in Frankfurt in the definition of European monetary policy rather than merely following what the Bundesbank alone decided. Giving up the symbolic power of your own currencies has become a condition to better defend your interests. As Toqueville already reminded us: "Nations are like men, they love what satisfies their passions, but they like even more than they assure their interests." Endorsing with an integrated economic and monetary area, the European Union and all the nations that integrate it are now stronger to control their own destiny. In fact, the economic benefits of the euro are particularly realised internally in the functioning of the European economy itself and do not depend much on the global role of the euro. From an international perspective, the benefits are essentially political power and independence. The US has always set an example with its policy of 'benign negligence' towards the dollar exchange rate, prioritising its domestic objectives. In '71 and '72, on the eve of presidential elections, they preferred to let the dollar depreciate and sink the Bretton-Woods system, to take action with internal recessive effects to defend it. Nixon's finance minister then told his European colleagues: "The dollar is our currency, but it is your problem." The great advantage of having a currency of global importance lies in the freedom to pursue its own internal policies. With its own currency, Europe can have an autonomous economic policy. Above all, the importance of the euro makes it possible to defend the European economic and social model. Europe now has the means to choose the model of society it deems best suited to its civilizational values. Like all good currencies, however, the euro has two sides: that of catalyst of liberalisation or that of defender of the European social model. Monetary union and the consequent full integration of the European economic area can be seen as another instrument of liberalisation globalisation or, on the contrary, as the only viable way for Europe to defend its economic model. Moreover, only the existence of these alternative views can explain the remarkable convergence of political positions that have made it possible to share sovereignty that the creation of the euro entails. For some, the euro, by depriving countries of traditional instruments of intervention in the economic environment, would lead to adjustments falling exclusively on the labour market, thus forcing their full liberalisation. The Stability Pact, by severely conditioning fiscal policy, would hasten the dismantling of the welfare state, making its reform more urgent. There is, however, another vision of things. The euro Europe will be a relatively closed monetary area in relation to the outside world and will thus be able to maintain autonomous policies that defend its own social model. Importing only about 12% of what it produces, it is the conditions and internal policies that determine almost 90% of what is produced and consumed in Europe. Europe thus has the possibility of pursuing an independent macroeconomic policy, geared to domestic objectives without being overly distressed by the euro exchange rate, in addition to what conditions internal price stability, the predominant objective of European monetary policy. It is not true that Europe must completely destroy social protections because of globalisation. A relatively closed economic area with its own currency has the capacity to maintain different levels of redistribution than those in force in other parts of the world. The necessary reform of the Welfare State has foundations beyond those related to globalization. It is not true, moreover, that Europe is not competitive just because it has higher wage and social costs than the US. The proof that it is competitive is that it sells more than it buys abroad, despite the almost lack of customs protections, exactly the opposite of the US which still has a loss-making trade balance. Like Janus, ancient two-faced Roman god, alleged inventor of coins and present in the oldest minted in Rome, the euro confronts us with its two faces. In practice, as always happens, both will coexist and, to different degrees, will influence the course of history. We are far, however, from the convenience of a single thought. Ambiguous as everything that has historical scope, also for us Portuguese, the euro has two sides: the sympathetic face that provides us low inflation and low interest rates and the demanding face that imposes discipline on us in income policy and financial responsibility in fiscal policy. The largely permanent nature of the fall in interest rates has resulted in an increase in the wealth and indebtedness of private economic operators. Many households and businesses have increased their ability to access credit and rationally, in the face of the new low inflation and interest rate regime, have decided to use it to increase their consumption and investment expenditures. Companies took advantage of expanding and modernizing their production capacity and their indebtedness grew to 83 percent of GDP in 2000. Households in 1990 had an indebtedness of less than 20 percent of Disposable Income and interest charges accounted for about 4.7 percent. In 2000, the debt ratio rose to about 86 percent, but interest charges were only at 4.1 percent of Disposable Income. This increase in indebtedness had its counterpart in access to goods and services, housing and other durable consumer goods, which substantially improved the quality of life of the Portuguese far beyond what results from the real increase in Disposable Income. History will record as extraordinary the transformations that the country has undergone in the last decade and will mark as unprecedented the improvement of the standard of living in such a short period. As we know, the growth rate of the potential product is in Portugal of about 3%. Well, if income per inhabitant grew by 3% per year, in parity of purchasing powers, in another 10 years we would reach the average income that today has the inhabitants of the European Union, a value so coveted in so many impatient comparations. I know that it is very difficult to maintain this pace of growth for ten consecutive years and that the phase in which we are in a strong economic slowdown makes it impossible for the time being. I do not recall, therefore, what we have recently achieved or that aritmetic possibility to instill any displaced optimism, which I do not feel, but so simply to recall some factors of hope and collective self-esteem so necessary in this fog of crisis and self-flagellation in which the country seems to have plunged. Only two years ago, in a critical essay, our Eduardo Lourenco portrayed us: "For the first time, our country lives itself and begins to be seen by others, who know where we are and who we are, as an insogranily happy people.... Rather than masochism, an all nothing hypocritical, with which we were the poor Lusitanians." Looking back, we can have further proof of the eternal divorce between historical time and political or media time. We had, of course, forgotten the other demanding side of the euro. Packed with the justified consumerist euphoria of cheap credit, we have exaggerate and ignored the demands of discipline in public deficits and rigour in adjusting wage cost growth to the progress of internal productivity and inflation of our European partners. We have to internalize new rules of operation of the economy. Fiscal policy must be used countercyclically to absorb shocks, which means having zero balances or even budget surpluses in the prosperity phases. There must be increases in costs, salaries and profit margins, which are related to those of our European partners. With the discipline of a common currency, wages, more than local inflation, determine competitiveness and unemployment. Wage realism guarantees employment and this is a social objective of absolute priority. If there is systematically faster progression of our income than is allowed by the productivity differential between Portugal and our partners, if there are illusions about this, we will obviously pay with unemployment and recession. One cannot also jump over this arithmetic reality that says that the real average incomes of a population only grow which grows its real productivity on average. The internalisation of new rules implies recognizing a paradigm shift which, by caricature a little, we can characterize this: the world has gone from a regime in which macroeconomic policy ensured full employment and income policy should control inflation, to a new regime in which macroeconomic policy, in particular monetary, controls inflation and income policy conditions unemployment. In 1997, he wrote: "The essential part of the necessary adjustments will be for companies that will have to find new comparative advantages as they slowly disappear those resulting from lower wage costs. The answer lies, as we know, in a strategy to increase productivity, qualityand product diversification. Many traditional companies will disappear in the medium term. Others will have to emerge to sustain new growth. Participation in monetary union given the investment climate it creates and the possibility of giving rise to investimentos that truly modernize the Portuguese productive structure will be the only way to respond to the challenge of competitiveness in the European context. Foreign investment will make a significant contribution to this process, but the effort of Portuguese companies will be the decisive factor. .... That is why the process carries risks and has the size of a bet. It is the only possible way, but we must quickly change the reality of our productive structures." At the present time, however, they are mainly faced with a difficult budgetary situation in the face of the commitments we have made on the medium-term evolution of the budget deficit. The recent Council of Finance Ministers of the European Union confirmed the objective of ating a zerodeficit in 2004, which from more than 2% this year is extremely demanding. Even if the economic growth scenario is fully reproduced from the very end of next year, difficult tax and expenditure decisions are awaiting us to try to achieve that objective. The country will need broad consensus and a solid political solution to deal with what awaits us. We have to understand that fiscal policy has to be used in a monetary union differently from what we have experienced in recent years. Unfortunately it seems that we only learn from experience, but the cost of the next adjustment will have the compensation of putting us back on the path of an anticyclical use of the fiscal policy that is in our interest to keep permanently. The phase of strong synchronised slowdown in the world economy deepens the factors of concern that have affected the expectations of economic operators. However, the pessimism should notbe overstated because in 2001 and 2002 Portugal continues to grow more than the European average. Without the euro, the consequences of this situation would be far worse for Europe and Portugal. Finally concrete from now on, the euro can even awakenin vo optimism throughout Europe. Recent polls in Denmark and Sweden now give euro-friendly majorities and in England, despite the majority oot, more than 70% of respondents say they are convinced that the euro will eventually replace the pound. How canthe euro influence the future of the European project? The evidence has been in existence for three years that it did not need a prior political union to exist, although it can be said that the euro is itself a decisive element of the possible European political union. In the theater of history nothing, however, is played. From the existence of the single currency does not necessarily result from the Federation of Sovereign States or even less the Federal State with which some dream. We are no longer in time to believe in the cunning hegeliana of reason that led humanity, by unplanned paths, towards the rationality of the historical process. History is not only "the biography of great men" as Carlyle intended, but it is also not the consequence ofvast impersonal things in men are mere "labels that give name to events" (Tolstoy). In the High Middle Ages there was a lingua franca in Europe and gold ensured that coins circulated throughout Europe existed. This resulted in the unity of Europe with which, in the context of the idea of empire, some dreamed, but rather the subsequent fragmentation into powerful states. It is certain that this time the creation of the euro reflects the historical need for greater European unity, based on a partilhada culture with common values that precede the formation of modern European nations. As a powerful tool for rationalising and re-reifying social life (Simmel), the common currency will contribute to strengthening European identity. The psychological impactof using the same currency and the same monetary species in 12 European countries will be considerable. However, the clarification of European destiny will depend essentially on the choices that European leaders, with full democratic participation, will decide in the near future. The euro is, however, a great moment and a huge achievement. Along side great frustrations and healing hopes, the European project is continuing its march. text_original: Artigo do Governador -Pblico Artigo do Governador -Pblico 31 dez. 2001 Por Vtor Constncio Neste lugar e no dia de hoje, inaugura-se uma poca na histria do mundo e podemos dizer que assistimos  sua origem (Goethe) O euro existe h trs anos como verdadeira moeda. No entanto, como a famosa personagem de Molire que fazia prosa sem o saber, tambm todos o usaram sem perceber o que faziam. Verdadeiramente como moeda, o escudo desapareceu desde Janeiro de 1999, tendo continuado a existir meramente como uma fraco do euro, ou seja, como unidade de conta. Desde aquela data que o euro  a nossa moeda, mas a uma fraco do euro continumos a chamar escudo e a circulao de notas e moedas tem sido feita nessa unidade de conta a que estamos habituados. O grande alcance econmico e histrico da criao do euro deu-se h trs anos e muitos no deram por ele. Aqui se aplica aquilo a que Jorge Luis Borges chamava o pudor da histria que passa por ns recatada, porque as suas datas essenciais, durante muito tempo, podem ser igualmente secretas. , alis, Borges que usa a citao de Goethe que coloquei em epgrafe, dita sintomaticamente a propsito da derrota do exrcito alemo em Valmy em 1792 quando se preparava para tomar Paris e abafar a Revoluo Francesa. Em fundamental contraponto, a data que agora celebramos constitui, pelo contrrio, a concretizao do projecto de unidade europeia destinado a garantir a paz e a prosperidade do continente. Concebido por Jean Monnet, aps a Segunda Guerra Mundial, com o objectivo, entre outros, de instalar a paz permanente entre a Alemanha e a Frana, o projecto europeu chega a um momento cimeiro com a criao do euro, agora finalmente visvel para todos nas notas e moedas que iniciam a sua circulao. A propsito do projecto europeu Monnet costumava dizer que mais que unir Estados procurava unir os povos. A moeda comum constitui um importante veculo para a realizao desse objectivo, j que, como afirma o clebre James Tobin com o racionalismo prprio dos economistas:  a moeda  como as lnguas, se houvesse s uma entendamo-nos todos melhor. A criao do euro  um momento nico na histria da Europa e do mundo. Outras tentativas de integrao monetria parcial na Europa, como a Unio Monetria Latina (1865-1927) ou a sua congnere Escandinava (1873-1931), no dispuseram de uma moeda nica nem de um Banco Central Comum. O projecto actual do euro corresponde a uma extraordinria partilha de soberanias entre velhos Estados-Naes que assim se subsumem para melhor sobreviver. Num mundo globalizado, com livre circulao de capitais, nem as mdias naes dispem de plena soberania monetria. Por isso o euro surge agora e, nesta fase da histria da humanidade, corresponde plenamente ao hegeliano esprito do mundo. A histria europeia das ltimas dcadas prova que apenas a Alemanha dispunha de soberania monetria porque s ela definia a sua poltica de taxas de juro em funo da sua prpria situao econmica. Para os restantes pases, o jogo consistia em tentar seguir a poltica alem. Compreende-se que os seus dirigentes tenham preferido participar em Frankfurt na definio da poltica monetria europeia em vez de se limitarem a seguir o que, sozinho, decidia o Bundesbank. Desistir do poder simblico das suas moedas prprias passou a ser condio de defender melhor os seus interesses. Como nos recordava j Toqueville: As naes so como os homens, amam o que satisfaz as suas paixes, mas gostam ainda mais do que assegura os seus interesses. Dotada de um espao econmico e monetrio integrado, a Unio Europeia e todas as naes que a integram so agora mais fortes para controlar o seu prprio destino. Na verdade, as vantagens econmicas do euro concretizam-se sobretudo no plano interno do funcionamento da prpria economia europeia e no dependem muito do papel mundial do euro. Na perspectiva internacional, os benefcios so essencialmente de poder poltico e de independncia. Os EUA sempre deram o exemplo com a sua poltica de negligncia benigna em relao  taxa de cmbio do dlar, dando prioridade aos seus objectivos domsticos. Em 71 e 72, em vsperas de eleies presidenciais, preferiram deixar desvalorizar o dlar e afundar o sistema de Bretton-Woods, a tomar medidas com efeitos recessivos internos para o defender. O ministro das Finanas de Nixon disse ento aos seus colegas europeus: O dlar  a nossa moeda, mas  o vosso problema. A grande vantagem de ter uma moeda com importncia mundial reside na liberdade de prosseguir as suas prprias polticas internas. Com moeda prpria a Europa pode ter uma poltica econmica autnoma. Acima de tudo a importncia do euro permite defender o modelo econmico e social europeu. A Europa passa a ter os meios para escolher o modelo de sociedade que entender mais adequado aos seus valores civilizacionais. Como todas as boas moedas, porm, o euro tem duas faces: a de catalisador da liberalizao ou a de defensor do modelo social europeu. A Unio Monetria e a consequente integrao plena do espao econmico europeu podem ser vistos como mais um instrumento da globalizao liberalizante ou, pelo contrrio, como a nica forma vivel da Europa defender o seu modelo econmico. Alis, s a existncia destas vises alternativas poder explicar a notvel convergncia de posies polticas que tornou possvel a partilha de soberania que a criao do euro implica. Para uns, o euro, ao privar os pases dos instrumentos tradicionais de interveno na conjuntura econmica, levaria a que os ajustamentos caiam exclusivamente no mercado de trabalho forando assim a sua liberalizao total. O Pacto de Estabilidade, ao condicionar fortemente a poltica oramental, apressaria o desmantelamento da Estado-Providncia, tornando a sua reforma mais urgente. Existe, porm, uma outra viso das coisas. A Europa do euro ser uma zona monetria relativamente fechada em relao ao exterior e poder assim manter polticas autnomas que defendam o seu prprio modelo social. Importando apenas cerca de 12% do que produz, so as condies e as polticas internas que determinam quase 90% do que se produz e consome no espao europeu. A Europa tem assim a possibilidade de prosseguir uma poltica macroeconmica independente, virada para objectivos internos sem se angustiar excessivamente com a taxa de cmbio do euro, para alm do que esta condiciona a estabilidade interna dos preos, objectivo predominante da poltica monetria europeia. No  verdade que a Europa tenha de destruir totalmente proteces sociais por causa da globalizao. Um espao econmico relativamente fechado, dotado de moeda prpria, tem capacidade para manter nveis de redistribuio diferentes dos que vigoram noutras partes do mundo. A necessria reforma do Estado-Providncia tem fundamentos para alm dos que esto relacionados com a mundializao. No , alis, verdade que a Europa no seja competitiva apenas por ter custos salariais e sociais mais elevados que os EUA. A prova de que  competitiva  que vende mais do que compra ao exterior, apesar da quase inexistncia de proteces aduaneiras, exactamente o contrrio dos EUA que continuam a ter uma balana comercial deficitria. Como Janus, antigo deus romano de duas caras, alegado inventor das moedas e presente nas mais antigas cunhadas em Roma, o euro confronta-nos com as suas duas faces. Na prtica, como sempre acontece, ambas vo coexistir e, em graus diferentes, influenciaro o curso da histria. Estamos longe, porm, da comodidade de um pensamento nico. Ambguo como tudo o que tem alcance histrico, tambm para ns, portugueses, o euro apresenta duas faces: a face simptica que nos proporciona baixa inflao e baixas taxas de juro e a face exigente que nos impe disciplina na poltica de rendimentos e responsabilidade financeira na poltica oramental. O carcter em larga medida permanente da descida das taxas de juro implicou um aumento da riqueza e da capacidade de endividamento dos agentes econmicos privados. Muitas famlias e empresas aumentaram a sua capacidade para aceder ao crdito e, racionalmente, em face do novo regime de inflao e juros baixos, decidiram us-lo para aumentar as suas despesas de consumo e investimento. As empresas aproveitaram para expandir e modernizar a sua capacidade produtiva e o seu endividamento cresceu at 83 por cento do PIB em 2000. As famlias em 1990 tinham um endividamento inferior a 20 por cento do Rendimento Disponvel e os encargos com juros representavam cerca de 4,7 por cento. Em 2000, o rcio da dvida subiu para cerca de 86% por cento, mas os encargos com juros eram apenas em 4.1 por cento do Rendimento Disponvel. Este aumento do endividamento teve a sua contrapartida no acesso a bens e servios,  habitao e a outros bens de consumo duradouro, que melhoraram substancialmente a qualidade de vida dos portugueses muito para alm do que resulta do aumento real do Rendimento Disponvel. A histria registar como extraordinrias as transformaes que o pas operou na ltima dcada e assinalar como sem precedentes a melhoria do nvel de vida em to curto perodo. Como se sabe, a taxa de crescimento do produto potencial  em Portugal de cerca de 3%. Pois bem, se o rendimento por habitante crescesse a 3% ao ano, em paridade de poderes de compra, em outros 10 anos atingiramos o rendimento mdio que hoje tm os habitantes da Unio Europeia, valor to cobiado em tantas impacientes comparaes. Bem sei que  muito difcil manter durante dez anos consecutivos esse ritmo de crescimento e que a fase em que estamos de forte desacelerao econmica o inviabiliza para j. No recordo, assim, o que recentemente conseguimos nem aquela possibilidade aritmtica para instilar qualquer optimismo deslocado, que alis no sinto, mas to simplesmente para recordar alguns factores de esperana e de auto-estima colectiva to necessrios neste nevoeiro de crise e auto-flagelao em que o pas parece ter mergulhado. H apenas dois anos, em ensaio crtico, ainda nos retratava assim o nosso Eduardo Loureno:  Pela primeira vez, o nosso pas vive-se a si mesmo e comea at a ser visto pelos outros, que sabem onde ficamos e quem somos, como um povo insolentemente feliz.... Antes isso que o masoquismo, um tudo nada hipcrita, com que ramos os lusitanos coitados. Olhando para trs, podemos ter mais uma prova do eterno divrcio entre o tempo histrico e o tempo poltico ou meditico. Havamos,  certo, esquecido a outra face exigente do euro. Embalados na justificada euforia consumista do crdito barato, exagermos e ignormos as exigncias de disciplina nos dfices pblicos e de rigor na adequao do crescimento de custos salariais ao andamento da produtividade interna e da inflao dos nossos parceiros europeus. Temos que interiorizar novas regras de funcionamento da economia. Tem que se usar a poltica oramental de forma anticclica para absorver choques, o que implica ter saldos nulos ou mesmo excedentes oramentais nas fases de prosperidade. Tem que haver aumentos de custos, de salrios e de margens de lucro, que estejam referenciados aos dos nossos parceiros europeus. Com a disciplina de uma moeda comum, os salrios, mais do que a inflao local, determinam a competitividade e o desemprego. O realismo salarial garante o emprego e esse  um objectivo social de absoluta prioridade. Se houver sistematicamente progresso mais rpida dos nossos rendimentos do que  permitido pelo diferencial de produtividade entre Portugal e os nossos parceiros, se houver iluses sobre essa matria, pagaremos, obviamente, com desemprego e com recesso. No se pode tambm saltar por cima dessa realidade aritmtica que diz que os rendimentos mdios reais de uma populao s crescem o que cresce a sua produtividade real em mdia. A interiorizao de novas regras implica reconhecer um alterao de paradigma que, caricaturando um pouco, podemos caracterizar assim: o mundo passou de um regime em que a poltica macroeconmica assegurava o pleno emprego e a poltica de rendimentos devia controlar a inflao, para um novo regime em que a poltica macroeconmica, em particular a monetria, controla a inflao e a poltica de rendimentos condiciona o desemprego. Neste sentido, escrevia j em 1997 o seguinte: O essencial dos indispensveis ajustamentos passar pelas empresas que tero de encontrar novas vantagens comparativas  medida que lentamente forem desaparecendo as que resultam de custos salariais mais baixos. A resposta est, como se sabe, numa estratgia de aumento da produtividade, da qualidade e da diversificao do produto. Muitas empresas tradicionais iro desaparecer a mdio prazo. Outras tero que surgir para sustentar o novo crescimento. A participao na unio monetria dado o clima de investimento que cria e a possibilidade de originar investimentos que verdadeiramente modernizem a estrutura produtiva portuguesa ser a nica forma de responder ao desafio da competitividade no contexto europeu. O investimento estrangeiro dar uma contribuio significativa para esse processo, mas o esforo das empresas portuguesas ser o factor decisivo. ....  por isso que o processo comporta riscos e tem a dimenso de uma aposta.  o nico caminho possvel, mas temos que mudar rapidamente a realidade das nossas estruturas produtivas. No momento actual estamos, porm, confrontados sobretudo com uma dificlima situao oramental face aos compromissos que assumimos sobre a evoluo a mdio prazo do dfice oramental. Recente Conselho de Ministros das Finanas da Unio Europeia confirmou o objectivo de se atingir um dfice nulo em 2004, o que a partir dos mais de 2% deste ano  extremamente exigente. Mesmo que se verifique plenamente o cenrio de crescimento econmico com recuperao significativa a partir de meados do prximo ano, aguardam-nos difceis decises em matria de impostos e despesas para tentar cumprir aquele objectivo. O pas vai precisar de vastos consensos e de uma slida soluo poltica para fazer face ao que nos espera. Temos de compreender que a poltica oramental tem que ser usada numa unio monetria de forma diferente daquela que experimentmos nos ltimos anos. Infelizmente parece que s aprendemos com a experincia, mas o custo do prximo ajustamento ter a compensao de nos colocar de novo no caminho de uma utilizao anticclica da poltica oramental que  do nosso interesse manter em permanncia. A fase de forte desacelerao sincronizada da economia mundial adensa os factores de preocupao que tm afectado as expectativas dos agentes econmicos. Convm, porm, no exagerar o pessimismo porque em 2001 e 2002 Portugal continua a crescer mais do que a mdia europeia. Sem o euro as consequncias desta conjuntura seriam, alis, bem piores para a Europa e para Portugal. Finalmente concreto a partir de agora, o euro pode mesmo despertar novo optimismo por toda a Europa. Recentes sondagens na Dinamarca e na Sucia do agora maiorias favorveis ao euro e na Inglaterra, apesar da maioria se opor, mais de 70% dos inquiridos afirma-se convencido de que o euro acabar por substituir a libra. De que forma poder o euro influenciar o futuro do projecto europeu? Existindo h j trs anos ficou feita a prova de que no requeria uma prvia unio poltica para existir, embora se possa dizer que o euro  ele prprio um elemento decisivo da possvel unio poltica europeia. No teatro da histria nada, porm, est jogado. Da existncia da moeda nica no decorre necessariamente a Federao de Estados Soberanos ou ainda menos o Estado Federal com que alguns sonham. J no estamos em tempo de acreditar na hegeliana astcia da razo que conduzia a humanidade, por caminhos no planeados, na direco da racionalidade do processo histrico. A histria no  apenas a biografia dos grandes homens como pretendia Carlyle, mas tambm no  a consequncia de vastas foras impessoais em os homens so meras etiquetas que do nome aos acontecimentos (Tolstoy). Na Alta Idade Mdia existia na Europa uma lingua francae o ouro assegurava a existncia de moedas que circulavam por toda a Europa. No resultou da a unidade da Europa com que, no contexto da ideia de imprio, alguns sonhavam, mas antes a fragmentao posterior em poderosos Estados.  certo que, desta vez, a criao do euro reflecte a necessidade histrica de uma maior unidade europeia, baseada numa cultura partilhada com valores comuns que antecedem a formao das naes europeias modernas. Tratando-se de um instrumento poderoso de racionalizao e reificao da vida social (Simmel), a moeda comum contribuir para o reforo da identidade europeia. O impacto psicolgico de usarmos a mesma moeda e as mesmas espcies monetrias em 12 pases europeus, ser considervel. No entanto, a clarificao do destino europeu depender essencialmente das escolhas que os leaders europeus, com plena participao democrtica, vierem a decidir no prximo futuro. O euro , porm, um grande momento e uma enorme realizao. A par de grandes frustraes e de esperanas empoladas, o projecto europeu prossegue a sua marcha. Aos cpticos que periodicamente anunciam a sua morte podemos responder como Galileu: Eppur, si muove ! * Publicado no jornal Pblico em 31/12/2001 p ,

Governor's Interview -Daily News 31 Dec. 2001 *Published in the Daily News on 12/31/2001 Daily News - What is the main concern with the physical arrival of the euro? Vitor Constancio - The desire for everything to go smoothly is our main concern. I think that will be the case, since the preparation has been long. Everything is prepared so that from the first day the process takes place with normality. The main difficulty for the population is the adaptation to a new unit of account, but deep down this is what our emigrants did, relatively quickly and without major problems. In the early days there will surely be incidents. But I don't think they're going to be significant. Does Banco de Portugal have any concrete supervisory action at this time? Since the end of December we have set up a permanent communication system with the banks and SIBS, which will continue during January, so that we have permanent information on everything that is going on and we can respond to legal difficulties and clarifications that may arise. We also report daily to the European Central Bank (ECB) and the European Commission. But many changes have already occurred before the 31st. For example, in relation to the use of cheques, since 20 December, around 40% of these payments were already in euro. In electronic transfers, more than 60% have been in euros since mid-December. These are high levels of habituation to the euro. There are data, in relation to other countries, which place the Portuguese above of average habituation values. Doesn't it surprise you? No, because we have had a modern banking sector for many years. The degree of use by the population of modern means of payment is above many European countries. We have a very modern payment system that surprises many foreigners. What is no longer the case for businesses, in adapting to the euro, where we are always to lose. Why? There is a huge network of small and medium-sized enterprises and it is natural that things happen more slowly there. Companies only start operating in euros from the moment there is a requirement. But since 1 October, we have imposed double pricing, a very positive initiative which most European countries have not adopted. Worked. We saw many small traders, who were not obliged to do the double posting and who did. It's been a very important few months of preparation. But there were some problems, notably with the large distribution, which Banco de Portugal the non-payment of some costs of the physical change to the euro. How was the question? Some companies didn't pre-eat... Right now, everyone's pre-feeding. There was a dialogue with Banco de Portugal and the opportunity to clarify that some costs they did not really have to bear. It was a problem that didn't exist. As far as consumers are, the only resource they have is commercial banks... But it's only natural that it should be. We're talking about money. The banking system is the great vehicle for the introduction of a new currency. But that could lead banks to pass the costs on to customers... It is clear that the physical introduction of the euro has costs for everyone, which is more than offset by the advantages. There are small logistical costs to be borne by all of us. But, all in all, they are very small and easily absorbed. The two sectors that bear the most direct costs are banking and distribution. Ultimately, it's always the whole economy, but it all depends on the competition. We want the sectors that are making the greatest effort so far to continue to be profitable. The fact that the euro enters an economically less favourable period cannot distrust of the European currency? I don't think so. Evidently everything is easier in periods of euphoria and prosperity. We are not in recession, just in economic slowdown. I do not believe that this prevents the population from understanding that the euro has been beneficial. Take look at the events of 9/11 and the crisis that has intensified in the world. If we were not in the euro the instability would have been greater. One of the measures he advocates is wage restraint... Salary realism. But you're not the only one. It also criticises a certain financial haemorrhage, caused by the budgeting of many expenditures... The use of funding of public projects in project finance is used by many countries. It is not reprehensible, provided that all the multiannual commitments that the State takes are known, transparent and have limits, so as not to compromise future budgets. Just this precaution? Budgetary restraint is not enough. We must internalise that fiscal policy has to be used in an anticyclical way. Unfortunately, our fiscal policy has not followed this standard and now we have to make an adjustment. The Stability Pact states that by 2004 countries must have a balanced budget. They all presented programs with this goal and we also have to meet. From this year's deficit, it is a very demanding target. From wage restraint to spending restraint in public services, everything will have to happen. Is Portugal able to meet this goal? We have a great synchronised economic developments with the rest of Europe, which has been increasing. If there really is a European and global recovery from the very end of next year, the Portuguese economy will follow this movement, which will facilitate fiscal adjustment. But we start from a high imbalance, above 2% this year, which makes it difficult to balance in 2004. Given the current political instability, is Portugal on the knife edge? No, we don't have a situation of unsustainability of public finances. There are commitments that impose discipline. Being in the euro is not just about benefiting from what it provides us with. It imposes certain rules to be complied with in the field of costs and budgetary policy. There is no economic and financial problem with dramatic contours. There is a very demanding objective that involves difficult measures. And are these measures possible in the current political landscape? I don't know about that. It is desirable that there are political solutions capable of making these decisions. Is budgetary policy currently being used in this countercyclical context? At the moment, it is, as it has set out for this year with the target of a deficit of 1.1% of GDP and will be over 2%. There's been a run of automatic stabilizers. We just didn't have enough leeway to be able to do that without making a difficult correction. That's the problem. Isn't the countercyclical reading of the budget very goodwill on your part? No. The increase in the deficit is largely explained by the drop in revenues, but not entirely. Also due to the slowdown in the economy. The problem is our starting situation. Is it possible to take these measures without a party pact? Portugal would benefit if it could carry out a vast social pact at this stage, involving political forces and the social partners. We have not yet fully internalised the rules of operation within monetary union and this would benefit greatly from the achievement of a broad social pact. We have been used to unemployment rates much lower than Europe for decades. But for this to be possible in the framework of monetary union, realism in wage policy and a good use of fiscal policy is necessary. Are the rules fundamental? These are two fundamental rules. If we are wrong, what will happen is that we lose competitiveness and have unemployment. It's the most penalizing situation of all. European monetary policy currently determines inflation, with the various countries converging on this average European rate. And income policy conditions unemployment, which has changed the paradigm to which the world has been accustomed. What is the risk of no containment? The variable that adjusts from now on is unemployment. That's what we should avoid. Hence the appeals I make to be realistic. Entrevista do Governador -Dirio de Notcias 31 dez. 2001 *Publicada no Dirio de Notcias em 31/12/2001 Dirio de Notcias -Qual a principal preocupao com a chegada fsica do euro? Vtor Constncio -O desejo de que tudo corra sem problemas, a nossa principal preocupao. Penso que assim ser, uma vez que a preparao foi longa. Tudo est preparado para que desde o primeiro dia o processo decorra com normalidade. A principal dificuldade para a populao a adaptao a uma nova unidade de conta, mas no fundo isso foi o que fizeram os nossos emigrantes, com relativa rapidez e sem grandes problemas. Nos primeiros dias haver seguramente incidentes. Mas creio que no sero significativos. O Banco de Portugal tem alguma aco concreta de superviso nesta altura? Desde finais de Dezembro que montmos um sistema de comunicao permanente com os bancos e com a SIBS, que prosseguir durante Janeiro, para termos uma informao permanente sobre tudo o que se passa e podermos responder a dificuldades e esclarecimentos legais que possam surgir. Fazemos ainda um reporte dirio para o Banco Central Europeu (BCE) e para a Comisso Europeia. Mas muitas mudanas j ocorreram antes do dia 31. Por exemplo, em relao utilizao dos cheques, desde o dia 20 de Dezembro que cerca de 40% destes pagamentos j eram em euros. Nas transferncias electrnicas, mais de 60% j eram em euros desde meados de Dezembro. So nveis elevados de habituao ao euro. Existem dados, em relao a outros pases, que colocam o consumidor portugus acima de valores mdios de habituao. No o surpreende? No, porque desde h muitos anos que temos um sector bancrio moderno. O grau de utilizao pela populao dos modernos meios de pagamento est acima de muitos pases europeus. Temos um sistema de pagamentos bastante moderno e que surpreende muitos estrangeiros. O que j no acontece em relao s empresas, na adaptao ao euro, onde estamos sempre a perder. Porqu? Existe uma enorme rede de pequenas e mdias empresas e natural que a as coisas se passem mais lentamente. As empresas s passam a funcionar em euros a partir do momento em que exista a obrigatoriedade. Mas impusemos, desde o dia 1 de Outubro, a dupla afixao de preos, uma iniciativa muito positiva e que a maior parte dos pases europeus no adoptou. Funcionou. Vimos muitos pequenos comerciantes, que no eram obrigados a fazer a dupla afixao e que a fizeram. Foram meses de preparao muito importantes. Mas houve alguns problemas, nomeadamente com a grande distribuio, que pediu ao Banco de Portugal o no pagamento de alguns custos da mudana fsica para o euro. Como ficou a questo? Algumas empresas no fizeram pr-alimentao... Neste momento, todos fizeram pr-alimentao. Houve um dilogo com o Banco de Portugal e a oportunidade de esclarecer que alguns custos eles no tinham realmente que suportar. Foi um problema que no chegou a existir. Em relao aos consumidores, o nico recurso que tm so os bancos comerciais... Mas natural que assim seja. Estamos a falar de dinheiro. O sistema bancrio o grande veculo para a introduo de uma nova moeda. Mas que poder levar os bancos a passar os custos para os clientes... evidente que a introduo fsica do euro tem custos para todos, que so mais do que compensados pelas vantagens. H pequenos custos de natureza logstica a suportar por todos ns. Mas, todos somados, so muito pequenos e facilmente absorvidos. Os dois sectores que suportam mais custos directos so a banca e a distribuio. Em ltima anlise, sempre toda a economia, mas tudo depende da concorrncia. Queremos que os sectores que fazem agora o maior esforo continuem a ser rentveis. O facto do euro entrar num perodo economicamente menos favorvel no poder provocar alguma desconfiana em relao moeda europeia? Creio que no. Evidentemente tudo mais fcil em perodos de euforia e prosperidade. No estamos em recesso, apenas em desacelerao econmica. No creio que tal impea a populao de compreender que o euro tem sido algo de benfico. Veja-se os acontecimentos do 11 de Setembro e a crise que acentuaram no mundo. Se no estivssemos no euro a instabilidade teria sido maior. Uma das medidas que defende a conteno salarial... Realismo salarial. Mas no a nica. Critica igualmente uma certa hemorragia financeira, feita pela no oramentao de muitas despesas... O recurso a financiamento de projectos pblicos em project finance utilizado por muitos pases. No condenvel, desde que todos os compromissos plurianuais que o Estado assume sejam conhecidos, transparentes e tenham limites, para no se comprometer oramentos futuros. Basta apenas esta precauo? No basta apenas a conteno oramental. Temos de interiorizar que a poltica oramental tem que ser usada de forma anticclica. Infelizmente, a nossa poltica oramental no seguiu este padro e agora temos de fazer um ajustamento. No Pacto de Estabilidade est definido que at 2004 os pases tm de ter o oramento equilibrado. Todos eles apresentaram programas com essa meta e ns tambm temos de cumprir. A partir do dfice deste ano, um objectivo muito exigente. Desde a conteno salarial conteno de despesas nos servios pblicos, tudo vai ter de acontecer. Portugal tem condies de cumprir essa meta? Possumos uma grande sincronizao de evoluo econmica com o resto da Europa, que tem vindo a acentuar-se. Se realmente houver uma recuperao europeia e mundial a partir de meados do prximo ano, a economia portuguesa acompanhar esse movimento, o que facilitar o ajustamento oramental. Mas partimos de um desequilbrio elevado, acima de 2% este ano, que torna difcil o equilbrio em 2004. Tendo em conta a actual instabilidade poltica, Portugal est no fio da navalha? No, no temos uma situao de insustentabilidade das finanas pblicas. Existem compromissos que impem disciplina. Estar no euro no s beneficiarmos daquilo que ele nos proporciona. Impe certas regras a cumprir no domnio dos custos e da poltica oramental. No existe um problema econmico-financeiro com contornos dramticos. H um objectivo muito exigente que implica medidas difceis. E essas medidas so possveis, no actual cenrio poltico? Isso no sei. desejvel que haja solues polticas com capacidade de tomar essas decises. Neste momento a poltica oramental est a ser usada neste contexto anticclico? Neste momento, est, uma vez que se partiu para este ano com o objectivo de um dfice de 1,1% do PIB e vai ser superior a 2%. Houve um funcionamento dos estabilizadores automticos. S que no tnhamos margem de manobra suficiente para poder fazer isso sem a seguir fazermos uma correco difcil. Esse o problema. A leitura anticclica que faz do oramento no muito boa vontade da sua parte? No. O aumento do dfice explicado em grande parte pela quebra de receitas, mas no totalmente. Tambm devido desacelerao da economia. O problema a nossa situao de partida. possvel tomar essas medidas sem um pacto de partidos? Portugal beneficiaria se pudesse realizar nesta fase um vasto pacto social, que envolva foras polticas e os parceiros sociais. No interiorizmos ainda totalmente as regras de funcionamento dentro da Unio Monetria e isso beneficiaria muito com a realizao de um vasto pacto social. Estamos habituados, h dcadas, a taxas de desemprego muito inferiores s europeias. Mas para isto ser possvel no quadro da Unio Monetria, necessrio realismo na poltica salarial e uma boa utilizao da poltica oramental. So as regras fundamentais? So duas regras fundamentais. Se tivermos um comportamento errado, o que acontecer que perdemos competitividade e teremos desemprego. a situao mais penalizadora de todas. Actualmente a poltica monetria europeia determina a inflao, com os vrios pases a convergirem para essa taxa mdia europeia. E a politica de rendimentos condiciona o desemprego, o que mudou o paradigma a que o mundo esteve habituado. Qual o risco de no haver conteno? A varivel que ajusta a partir de agora o desemprego. o que devemos evitar. Da os apelos que fao para que haja realismo. Descida das taxas de juro Descida das taxas de juro

A descida das taxas de juro foi o principal benefcio da moeda nica para as famlias portuguesas?

Sim, para particulares e empresas. O importante que se trata de uma mudana permanente. Vamos continuar a viver num regime de inflao e de taxas de juro baixas. essa a reputao da Europa e os objectivos da poltica monetria. E esse facto tornou possvel que, de uma forma racional, as famlias e as empresas se tivessem endividado mais, porque passaram a ser solventes. Se as taxas de juro continuassem como no incio dos anos 90, na ordem dos 20% para a compra de habitao, nada disto seria possvel. Ou se houvesse o receio, por parte das famlias e bancos, de que as taxas poderiam voltar a ter esses valores, no teria havido este recurso ao crdito.

Mas os portugueses endividaram-se muito...

As famlias portuguesas tinham em 1990 uma dvida que representava 18,5% do seu rendimento disponvel. E pagavam de juros por essa pequena dvida 4,7% do rendimento disponvel. Dez anos depois, tm uma dvida mais de dez vezes maior, em valor absoluto, que representa 86% do seu rendimento disponvel. Mas s pagam 4,1% em juros. Ou seja, o peso dos juros agora menor apesar da dvida ser maior. Significam muito milhes de contos, que as famlias souberam utilizar de uma forma racional para comprarem bens de consumo duradouros e com isso melhorarem substancialmente o seu nvel de vida, muito para alm daquilo que medido pela evoluo dos salrios reais e do rendimento disponvel, como indicadores de bem estar.

As empresas tambm aproveitaram esta descida?

As empresas viram, de sbito, os seus encargos financeiros reduzirem-se. No s resolveram muitos problemas, como tambm puderam fazer investimentos, modernizar-se e internacionalizar-se. O movimento de internacionalizao das empresas portuguesas no teria a escala que teve se no tivessem recorrido a um grande mercado de capitais europeu, podendo endividar-se em euros a taxas de juro baixas. Outra vantagem do euro o facto das empresas agora poderem contar com o acesso ao grande mercado europeu sem risco cambial e numa situao de estabilidade, que lhes permite planear a sua actividade a mdio e longo prazo.

O euro j est estvel?

Sim, mas esse no um objectivo da poltica monetria europeia. A rea do euro economicamente muito vasta e relativamente fechada ao exterior, pelo que a poltica monetria tem como objectivo essencial a estabilidade interna dos preos. evidente que a taxa de cmbio influencia-a, mas o efeito reduzido, embora o consideremos. O euro uma moeda forte porque assegura a estabilidade interna dos preos.

Inflao

E isso tem sido alcanado?

Sim e vai acentuar-se no prximo ano. A inflao tem estado acima dos 2% e para o ano vai estabilizar, na zona do euro, abaixodos 2%.vincada.Essa desacelerao tambm acontecer em Portugal, de uma forma muito

Mas poder haver inflao em Portugal devido questo do preo dos transportes pblicos, perfeitamente insustentveis para as empresas. Adiamos este ajustamento ou aproveitamos o euro para o fazer?

O euro no ser aproveitado. H decises a tomar em relao a alguns preos que so controlados e que devem ser ajustados. O problema oramental vai exigir decises difceis e corajosas nos prximos trs anos. Os transportes so um dos domnios onde essas decises vo ter de surgir, pensadas e ajustadas necessidade de consolidao oramental.

A inflao vai desacelerar?

Sim. Foi relativamente elevada em 2001 -4,3% / 4,4% -tendo chegado a 5,1% em Maro. Nos trs primeiros meses do ano houve razes para um aumento artificial da inflao. Esses efeitos j comearam a diluir-se. Obviamente que os valores mdios de 2002 vo depender muito do que for o resultado das negociaes salariais. fundamental que estas sejam feitas a pensar na inflao futura e no na passada.

Arredondamentos

Existem riscos de subida da inflao, por via do arredondamento dos preos na passagem para o euro?

um risco marginal. Fizemos um estudo simulando arredondamentos para baixo e para cima. Em relao aos bens e servios que integram o cabaz de compras do nosso ndice de preos, as concluses so que, no pior cenrio, o ndice de preos subiria 0,23 pontos. Num cenrio mais optimista, em que as empresas arredondassem sistematicamente para baixo, o ndice de preos desceria 0,26. So valores negligenciveis.

J existem sinais de que so negligenciveis?

Desde Outubro que temos a dupla afixao de preos. Se existisse a tentao de aproveitar a entrada do euro, seria a partir dessa altura que teriam comeado a faz-lo. Ora, a inflao em Portugal desceu em Novembro em relao a Outubro e essa desacelerao vai prosseguir, devendo ser muito visvel em Janeiro e Fevereiro. A entrada do euro no altera o poder de mercado das empresas. Uma empresa no pode, pelo facto de haver a introduo do euro, aumentar os seus preos porque no tem garantia que as outras tambm o fazem. E estamos num perodo de desacelerao econmica, que no a melhor conjuntura para tal.

Mas tem havido alguns incidentes, com arredondamentos mal feitos...

Houve alguns maus exemplos, no quero referir nomes, que podiam ter sido evitados. Mas tambm no exageremos, tudo isso foi em quantidades muito pequenas, na procura dos chamados preos atractivos, que so mais certos e exigem menos trocos. Mas continuo confiante que no haver nenhum efeito visvel na inflao em Portugal.

Governor's Interview -Economic Diary 02 jan. 2002 Published in the Economic Journal on 02/01/2002 Economic Diary - What advantages can be attributed to the euro? Vitor Constancio - The main economic effects of the euro were when it was created in January 1999, when it began to be our currency. In the Portuguese case, the effects were even before 1999. In fact, the main effect for the Portuguese economy was the lowercost of capital in general, with unprecedented benefits in our history. An advantage that is becoming a disadvantage due to indebtedness families. Disadvantage, no. This process has to be seen together. On the whole, the fall in interest rates, seen as persistent in the future, made people realize that their wealth had increased and that they were solvent to use credit. During these years there was a spectacular increase in the standard of living of the Portuguese which is beyond what were the increases in wages and disposable income. This is not measured directly in the most current statistics. What has also happened for companies and the state, he too, owes. In the case of companies, for example, the permanent reduction in the cost of financing has made it easier for them to expand, modernise and internationalise. Of course, all of this has limits. What about that limit? No, it hasn't been outdone. So far, although the economic slowdown has been occurring since 2000, non-credit has not increased. Since last year [2000] it has been felt that in particular individuals have begun to brake, as seen by the slowdown in the progression of consumption and credit. Will the slowdown be the test to assess whether the debt limit has been exceeded? It would all depend on the degree of shock that would exist. In what is normal cyclical evolution, nothing points to complicated situations. Portugal, with the level of indebtedness it has, is now more fragile than in the past to face a recession? We're not in recession. And there is no prediction that points to a recession, neither in the Portuguese economy nor in the European economy. It's a scenario that's not worth thinking about. Do you believe that Portugal, in 2002, will grow more than predicted by the IMF? This month we will publish the Economic Bulletin with our forecasts. What should be the profile of Portuguese economic policy? A country, in order to live in monetary union, must respect certain rules of operation so that, in times of economic slowdown, it has responsiveness. The single currency requires fiscal policy to be countercyclical (slowdown in spending in times of high economic growth). Unfortunately, that didn't happen between us. Fiscal policy has created great difficulties in meeting the commitments made in the context of the Stability Pact. This will determine that the next two to three years will be extraordinarily difficult for fiscal policy, requiring big decisions, realism and consensus. Budgetary policy will, in the short term, also contribute to the worsening of economic situation. It is the price of politics not having always been and at all times countercyclical during the last four years. What do you mean, the need to make big decisions? At European level, the budgetary balance target remains in 2004. If that's the rule, Portugal has to comply. And in the process of being done, in the face of the current deficit, it will have to make a number of difficult decisions, including containing the growth in public spending. Is freezing civil service salaries one of those difficult decisions? I will not comment on specific measures. Besides fiscal policy, are there other policies that deserve more attention? A country living in monetary union must know that it cannot systematically diverge from the levels of cost and price increases of its partners. Because if it does, it will have recessionary consequences and increased unemployment, adjusting in this way to cost growth and inflation similar to that of its partners. With the euro, there are two essential rules for regulating the economy that need to be internalised. One is that fiscal policy must be countercyclical, since it is the only instrument that allows action on economic developments. And the second rule is alignment in the evolution of wage costs and prices, classically designated as income and price policy. What is the contribution to be made by the Government to moderate wage costs and prices? It depends on the institutional framework of each country. But there is always an element that is what governments do to civil service salaries. In the context of the ECB's calls for structural reforms, the labour market work Portuguese need to be more flexible? The reaction of wages in Portugal to the evolution of the economic situation has been greater than that of the countries of the Union. Our unemployment rate has also been systematically lower, even today this is happening. This shows that, in practical operation, there has been flexibility in the labour market. Where we have then in fact a problem is in public finances. Right now it's really our big problem. And that has repercussions on important sectoral policies, such as health. Regardless of the governments, the next few years will be budgetary adjustment. In view of the situation, it would be advantageous to postpone the budgetary balance target set for countries for 2004? It's too early to tell. If a significant economic recovery is confirmed from the second quarter of next year, as is now planned, the maintenance of the target corresponds to what was foreseen. Decisions need to be taken with the most likely economic scenario. The doctrine that the ECB says it follows does not seem to be the one that follows. For example, the ECB stands for price stability understood as 2% inflation but ends up interest rates with inflation above that figure. A change in interest rates takes from one year to 18 months to have an effect on the economy. A monetary policy cannot therefore be decided on the basis of the observed inflation rate, but its forecast. Decisions are made using all available information to predict what may turn out to be the level of inflation. It turned out that energy and food price shocks led to temporary effects, which we did not foresee, which eventually drove inflation above 2% in the last year. In the set of information that the ECB uses to make its decision, the evolution of the monetary mass (M3) is being voted to oblivion, disappeared? It's not gone. The evolution of monetary aggregates is part of the whole set of information that is used by all central banks. M3 is not an intermediate monetary policy objective as it was for other central banks. How was it possible for the ECB to consider that the European economy would be immune to the slowdown in the U.S. economy? We never said we'd be immune. I recognise that there was excessive optimism when we considered that the effects of the American situation would be minor in Europe. We thought that, with the euro zone economically very closed, where trade with the US accounts for about 2% of European product, the effects would not be very large. However, a much larger, accelerated and psychological contagion effect was produced through the capital market. There was a certain error of evaluation. This error of assessment had consequences at the level of monetary policy, which eventually be more restrictive than desirable? If there is one thing that cannot be said of the monetary policy of the euro zone, it is that it has been restrictive or restrictive. Over this three-year period, real interest rates in Europe were much lower than when there were several currencies. For various reasons, such as differences in the situation between countries and, in the early 1990s, the effects of German unification, Europe experienced 91 to 98 with real interest rates of 4.5 to 5% on average. Since the creation of the euro this average is between 2 and 3%. At present, real interest rates are, moreover, below that average. And in 2000 Europe grew by 3.4%, the highest rate in the last ten years. But under-assessing the negative effects of the U.S. slowdown decision to lower interest rates? The assessment of the effects of the slowdown in the US economy in Europe did not have much consequence, because the indicators quickly showed that the contagion was ultimately significant. It turns out that the rate of inflation, for temporary reasons, was at that time well above 2% and there was a risk of creating an inflationary inertia. But the fact is that we lowered interest rates four times in 2001 to levels that put real interest rates below those at the beginning of 1999. The price stability target, understood as inflation below 2%, acted as a constraint to the adoption of rapid measures to react to the situation? The objective of price stability is structuring. If this objective were less demanding, the ECB could be more agile in reacting to the changing the situation, as did the U.S.? I'm not going to speculate on that. But the economic slowdown in the US was much faster than in Europe and that alone justifies different reactions. And our view of monetary policy does not lead us to an attitude of great activism. In view of what happened in 2001, the ECB should reflect on the existence of some deflationary bias in the objectives of euro area monetary policy? I don't think you can talk in those terms. We are forecasting higher growth in the euro area than the US economy and lower inflation. In the context of these forecasts, and with the current level of interest rates, I do not believe that there can be talk of deflationary bias. In 1999 it took more than a dollar to buy a euro. Since then the euro was deaparting with. How do you explain this weakness of the euro? We cannot talk about the fragility of the euro. The euro is a strong currency. For a relatively closed area, such as the euro area, the exchange rate is not an economic policy objective. It is an element to consider in predicting inflation. Moreover, if we look at the last 20 years, we see that the fluctuations between the European currencies and the dollar have been huge and permanent. For example, between 80 and 85, the milestone was almost 50% against the dollar. Then, from 85 to 87 it was valued almost one hundred percent... That is, this movement of the euro since 99 fits perfectly into what has been this fluctuation. The physical introduction of banknotes and coins may not also be translated into an assessment of the to the euro? These phenomena will not have a sufficient quantitative effect to move the exchange rate. The effect you can have is more psychological. The moment of physical introduction is a test of the success of this project. The way they look at the euro will also change in the positive direction. Does the entry of the euro involve costs? The costs are very low. The entire assessment of costs, in particular in the banking and distribution sectors - the most involved - are small as a percentage of GDP. There are costs that are impossible to measure, such as those of psychological adaptation to the euro. There are psychological costs that will be temporary. The Portuguese, when they emigrated or went abroad, did and make the experience of adapting very quickly to a new unit of account. Countries with populations with much lower level of formal education than Portugal have had changes in monetary units several times during the last years and have not suffered any trauma. There may be some initial psychological resistance, which will dissipate rapidly. In addition to the positive aspects. Today, a very large proportion of the European population travels. When you do this you will have the advantage of walking in twelve countries with the same currency, which will have positive effects for tourist and cultural activity. Price transparency itself will strengthen competition. Does the immediate resistance to the new currency prospect any downtime in consumption? In the first few days people will take more time to shop, because they have to do math, they have to adapt... But it is extraordinarily temporary and will not affect consumption. It is not because of the introduction of the euro that people will consume less throughout the year. And the fact that banknotes and coins enter into circulation at a time when the economy is slowing down... It was nicer than it was in a period of euphoria. In a phase of economic euphoria everything is better absorbed. But this new reality may even introduce a tone of optimism in the European population, because of the advantages that people will feel. This is a change that transcends purely economic aspects. It's a completely unique experience, having a currency without political union. In 19th-century Germany, monetary union preceded political union. But the creation of the euro, with this aspect of historical originality, is in itself a strong example of political union. To the extent that the currency is traditionally associated with the sovereignty of states, there is a sharing of sovereignty to better defend their interests. As Tocqueville said, "nations are like men, they like what satisfies their passions, but even more than they assure their interests." The euro itself represents a dimension of political union. The European Union is a totally original construction. In addition to some of the frustrations and disappointments that many Europeans feel about european construction, the euro is a very strong sign that it continues and deepens. It is a very positive sign that we are building conditions in Europe that better guarantee peace and prosperity. And can the euro catalyze other elements of political union? As these three years prove, the functioning of the euro does not have as a precondition the existence of political union. Of course it could be a catalyst. Nothing's thrown. And it is clear that sharing the same monetary specimens helps to create a sense of belonging to a community among Europeans, on a scale that would not happen without it. Will this result in consequences? They could work. I wouldn't say it's necessarily a catalyst, but it's certainly a facilitator. And the euro does not require a full political union, as its first three years show. But it obviously requires a strong dose of political collaboration between countries. Is that enough? I think so, yes. There is a capacity for dialogue and coordination in the economic area that has made the euro possible.

Entrevista do Governador -Dirio Econmico 02 jan. 2002 Publicada no Dirio Econmico em 02/01/2002 Dirio Econmico -Que vantagens  possvel atribuir ao euro? Vtor Constncio -Os principais efeitos econmicos do euro deram-se na altura em que foi criado, em Janeiro de 1999, altura em que comeou a ser a nossa moeda. No caso portugus, os efeitos deram-se ainda antes de 1999. De facto, o principal efeito para a economia portuguesa foi a descida do custo do capital em geral, com benefcios sem precedentes na nossa histria.
