Title: Governor's Speech - Conference on "Economics and Management"
text: Speech of the Governor - Conference... Governor's Speech - Conference on "Economics and Management" 29 jan. 2002 Lisbon, 29 January 2002 I want to begin by thanking you for inviting me to participate in this meeting on "Economics and Management", organized by PWC, and thus have the opportunity to address an important auditorium of business cadres. The title of this session speaks of 'a critical moment for the global economy', while the theme proposed to me mentions 'stability and prosperity'. The two messages seem to be difficult to reconcile, although I know that the world has become accustomed to expecting too much from the Central Banks. Fortunately, reality seems to want to help. Like the USA, the signs of the economic recovery planned for this year are also multiplying in Europe. The confidence indicators published in recent days for Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands and the German IFO for January, released yesterday, all reveal an acceleration of good augury. Although a slow recovery is expected in the first part of the year, the European economy is expected to be growing in the second half of the year near the rate of potential product around 2.5%, even if our forecast for the average annual rate in the euro area is only around 1.2%. If we add this figure to the 1.6% that occurred last year after the 3.4% of 2000, we confirm the perilof economic cycles and the instability that always threatens the world economy. Many factors contribute to this greater instability: economies are more open, interdependent and volatile than before. Markets are more liquid and globalized. Financial globalisation has accentuated the synchronisation of asset price developments, even when key data do not justify it in certain parts of the globe. The relocation facilities of productive activities aggravate the vulnerability of many economies. In this context, and for a small open economy like ours, participation in the European Union is an invaluable factor of stability. I am not referring to the stability of economic developments, but to the profound stability resulting from the sharing of rules and the convergence of institutions that membership of the European Union entails. Our participation in monetary union ensures the monetary stability of a low inflation regime. In the long run, inflation in the various regions that are members of a monetary union will eventually tend to converge towards an average value. In fact, member countries that maintain systematically higher price increases will eventually stop being competitive and suffer a recessionary process with unemployment that will eventually moderate inflation. Monetary stability also includes exchange rate stability with an economic area to which we allocate the overwhelming majority of our exports of goods and services. In short, for the first time in decades Portuguese companies can count on reduced interest rates, a low cost of capital and access to a vast market without foreign exchange risk. Without these conditions, they could not have internationalised as they have in recent years. The benefit of that fundamental macroeconomic stability also allows for investment and production planning with safer horizons than in the past. Finally, the requirements of the Stability Pact require that public finances must remain on a solvency path, which ensures financial stability. All this means that our participation in the European Union guarantees the stability of rules and principles of operation that theory and historical evidence point to as indispensable to the growth and prosperity of countries: low inflation, prudent and sustainable fiscal policy, opening up the economy and markets without distortions. Of course, this is not enough to avoid periods of greater uncertainty or perplexity such as the one we are now going through and which I do not intend to conceal. We are in the middle of a prolonged electoral period, which although normal in democracy has inevitable costs and, above all, we are going through a phase of pessimism about the prospects for the future of the country. One of those phases proper to the cyclothymic and unsafe countries that easily go from euphoria to depression. The electoral fog further complicates the task of trying to clearly discern where we are and what our real problems are. We cannot be mistaken for diagnosis and the most dangerous illusion is to assume that all diagnoses are made. In my view, and in general terms, the economy faces the following three problems: 1. difficult budgetary situation which requires a significant reduction of the deficit in little time; 2. a slowdown in economic growth, which we share with the rest of the europe, but which has its own internal factors; 3. a structural deficit of competitiveness that we have to deal with new business solutions, which alter the supply side of the economy, in order to overcome the challenges posed to us the enlargement of the European Union. The most serious and immediate issue is the state of public finances. In July last year I recalled with appropriate emphasis the need to comply with the Stability Pact and then stated that: "This requirement means that, rather than with an economic crisis, the country is facing a budgetary crisis." What is at stake is the commitments we have made on the medium-term evolution of the budget deficit. A recent Council of Finance Ministers of the European Union confirmed the target of achieving a zero deficit in 2004. There will therefore have to be some difficult decisions, probably on the revenue side and on the expenditure side, to reduce the deficit. The country will need broad consensus and a solid political solution to deal with what awaits us. If the timetable approved by ECOFIN is maintained, it is a question of reducing the deficit from 2.2% to zero in three years, which is difficult and does not constitute a dramatic situation. There is, moreover, no technical problem of sustainability of Portuguese public finances. We have a debt ratio to GDP of 55%, much lower than the European average and the rules of the Deficit Stability Pact ensure that it will have to continue to decline. Respect for the great guidelines contained in the Stability Programme presented is essential to the international credibility of our economic policy, a decisive aspect for a small economy vulnerable by recent imbalances and in need of attracting capital. What makes fiscal consolidation more difficult is that it has to be achieved in a period of slowing economic growth, the second problem I mentioned. This slowdown results from the impact of developments in the European economy, but has endogenous factors associated with the indebtedness of economic agents accumulated in recent years. During this period, growth was sustained in the excessive dynamism of domestic expenditure that grew far above the increase in domestic product, thus being associated with a growing indebtedness of private economic agents. Of course, this evolution could not continue indefinitely. As for the state, although public debt has been falling as a percentage of GDP, the increase in public consumption has stimulated domestic demand and contributed to a pro-cyclique fiscal policy from 98. It should be noted that the evolution of domestic expenditure, consumption and investment was largely inevitable as a result of the shock of the permanent fall in interest rates since the preparatory period for our participation in the euro. Even a more restrictive fiscal policy would not have prevented the significant progression of private spending and indebtedness. The economy has undergone a change in the 'economic regime' and has gone through a phase of forcibly adjusting to the new situation. The fall in interest rates during the second half of the decade and, after the guarantee of our entry into monetary union, the permanent nature of this fall, implied an increase in the wealth and indebtedness of private economic agents. Many households and businesses have suddenly become solvent to access credit and rationally, in the face of the new inflation and low interest rate regime, they decided to use it to increase their spending. Companies have taken advantage of expanding and modernizing their productive capacity and internationalizing. Such a process naturally has limits, precisely those which stem from the credit worthiness of economic operators. With high levels of indebtedness increases vulnerability to future economic shocks and from a certain moment begins a natural process of moderation of increased expenditure. Indebtedness of economic actors associated with a level of domestic demand higher than GDP leads to a deficit with the outside world. However, for a country without its own currency as is now our case, the external deficit limits result only from the aggregation of the indebtedness capacity of its agents, including banks. They have mediated between domestic and foreign agents, indebted to the interbank markets of the euro zone to finance the expansion of credit. Foreign banks have provided these resources because they positively assess the soundness of Portuguese banks. This point deserves some further research because it is always difficult to free ourselves from old ways of thinking created during previous episodes of external imbalance when we had our own currency. The problem of the external deficit for a region of a monetary union is obviously no longer a question of a lack of foreign exchange or a possible currency crisis. There is therefore no need for the same type of rapid adjustment as in past experience, which is a first difference to be noted. The indebtedness of the agents is all in euros, that is, in our own currency. The availability of financing therefore depends exclusively on the micro-economic solvency of private economic operators. The normal evolution of the economy, even in temporary slowdown, allows households and businesses to obtain the income in euros needed to meet the debt service contracted. In this new economic regime, in which we are macroeconomically a region of European monetary union, the issue of balance of payments is not an autonomous issue, but is only a reflection of the budgetary constraint faced by economic operators  families, companies and financial institutions. The second significant difference from past experience is that this time the deficit is not the result of public deficits and its financing has been secured by the market after the filter of an adequate analysis of the credit risks involved. This does not mean that the economy has ceased to have external restrictions and can continue to spend much higher than it produces. In the coming years, the deficit in the balance of goods and services will have to be significantly reduced. Deficit and debt limits are, however, introduced by private actors themselves or by markets that thus ensure the functioning of self-correction mechanisms for deficit slacks, mechanisms which are naturally restrictive in nature. In fact, either agents start moderating expenses and increasing their savings levels or start banks to tighten their risk analysis criteria and reduce the supply of credit as a result. The later this slowdown process began, the more abrupt the stop could be and the greater the risks of a real recession. For this reason, the slowdown in domestic expenditure can be considered positive, since this means the path of a "soft landing" of the Portuguese economy. Since the second half of 2000, the slowdown in domestic spending has occurred in the context of full employment, an increase in real wages and an increase in the disposable income of individuals. The latter's growth, being higher than consumption, means that there has been an increase in the savings rate, which shows that households have begun to correct excess expenditure growth. Of course, this may, and has implied, a slowdown in economic growth, but the inevitable slowdown in domestic spending does not have to translate linearly into the reduction of product growth, as there is always the possibility that companies, in the face of slowing domestic demand, will divert more production to export. Perhaps this has already happened last year, a period in which exports have grown more than demand from our client countries, which means that there has been a gain in market share, including in traditional exports. This process needs to continue in the coming years. In short, what all this means is that we need another pattern of growth, less based on domestic demand and more based on productivity increases that give greater strength to our external competitiveness. Which brings us to the third problem I set out behind. We need a profound structural shock on the supply side, which depends on some public policies but which will have to result, above all, from more business initiative. Unfortunately, neither the majority of private agents nor the State seem to have sufficiently internalised the new rules for the functioning of the economy of a member country of a monetary union. These rules are the other side of the euro, demanding and discipable, which we have unfortunately ignored. These are rules that require changing behaviour, some structural reforms and a new macroeconomic regulation regime. This implies the recognition of a paradigm shift: the world has moved from a regime in which macroeconomic policy ensured full employment and income policy should control inflation, to a new regime in which macroeconomic policy, in particular monetary policy, controls inflation and income policy conditions unemployment. In view of these new operating rules, our situation shows some signs of vulnerability, such as the existence of a fragmented and short-term wage negotiation system, the weight of stifling bureaucracy and an ineffective judicial system, a poor budget framework regime and weaknesses in the political system, with the difficulty of obtaining government majorities and the need for a state with more prestige and authority. There are profound reforms to be made in the public and private spheres, with urgency proportional to the challenges we will have to overcome with our own effort in the coming years. We will not benefit from substantial declines in interest rates, no exchange rate devaluations will be possible to temporarily re-finance the competitiveness of domestic production, and finally transfers from the European Union will tend to decrease as a percentage of GDP. As I said recently: "In a word, we are out of the easy remedies that in the past have alleviated our delays and compensated for our mistakes. We have to rely mainly on ourselves to ensure our development. This requires a culture of effort, work and rigour.  The improvement of our competitiveconditions involves multiple aspects of the Portuguese economy and society. Increasing productivity is the only way to consistently improve living standard without causing inflationary pressures. Productivity is, however, a resulting one and not an instrument that is easily manipulated. Its increase takes time and involves a complex process involving a wide range of factors. Among them, the absorption capacity of technical progress; rationalisation of production; the change in the sectoral composition of the product; the use of external production economies, dependent on the infrastructure network and the educational level of human resources. The more general institutional environment that conditions a society's ability to modernize is also important. Portugal has all the potential to successfully continue a process of real convergence with its European partners. From 1985 to now, Portugal grew at an average rate of 3.8 percent, well above the European average and went from 53 percent of the average European income to a value of 74 percent. We are now in a phase of adjustment and reduction of imbalances generated by the previous period of strong growth. This correction is necessary to create conditions of sustainability for the development process, and should therefore not be a factor of displaced pessimism. Some doubt the country's ability to operate the necessary transformations in the production structure and gain new comparative advantages. They wanted to be able to predict and perhaps plan this process by identifying priorities on what we should produce in the future, which is manifestly impossible. After the appropriate framework conditions, it will be up to the business initiative, Portuguese and foreign, to lead this transformation process. The current situation only makes it more important that public intervention contributes to creating conditions for modernising and liberalising product and capital markets, encouraging innovation and a business culture stimulated by a good investment climate. Public policies for the construction of infrastructure with guaranteed social profitability and, above all, the improvement of the qualification of human resources, remain indispensable contributions. The overall productivity of an economy does not jump short with reforms of immediate effect, but Portugal, ensuring macroeconomic stability, absence of exchange risk and low costs compared to other member countries of the European Union, has all the conditions to ensure a more favorable investment climate. And this is decisive for the objective of convergence and adjustment over the coming years. The essential scan so many adjustments will be for companies. Companies will have to find new comparative advantages as they slowly disappear those resulting from lower wage costs. Many traditional companies will disappear in the medium term. Others will have to emerge to sustain new growth. From this perspective it is necessary to attract more foreign investment, but the decisive contribution will have to come from Portuguese companies. In fact, the only possible way is to rapidly change the reality of our productive structures. Only in this way, and for once, will Jean Monnet be right when he stated that "men only act in a state of need and only recognize the need in times of crisis."

Discurso do Governador -Conferncia sobre "Economia e Gesto" 29 jan. 2002 Lisboa, 29 de Janeiro de 2002 Quero comear por agradecer o convite para participar nesta reunio sobre "Economia e Gesto", organizada pela PWC, e ter, assim, oportunidade de me dirigir a um importante auditrio de quadros empresariais. O ttulo desta sesso fala de momento crtico para a economia global, enquanto que o tema que me foi proposto menciona estabilidade e prosperidade. As duas mensagens parecem ser difceis de conciliar, embora eu saiba que o mundo se habituou a esperar muito dos Bancos Centrais. Felizmente que a realidade parece querer dar uma ajuda.  semelhana dos USA, tambm se multiplicam na Europa os sinais da recuperao econmica prevista para este ano. Os indicadores de confiana publicados nos ltimos dias para a Itlia, a Blgica, a Holanda e o IFO alemo para Janeiro, ontem divulgado, todos revelam uma acelerao de bom augrio. Embora se preveja uma retoma lenta na primeira parte do ano, a economia europeia dever estar a crescer na segunda metade do ano perto da taxa do produto potencial que se situa em torno de 2,5%, mesmo se a nossa previso para a taxa mdia anual na zona euro se situa apenas em torno de 1,2%. Se juntarmos este nmero aos 1,6% verificados no ano passado aps os 3,4% de 2000, confirmamos a perenidade dos ciclos econmicos e da instabilidade que sempre ameaa a economia mundial. Muitos factores contribuem para esta maior instabilidade: as economias so mais abertas, interdependentes e volteis do que antes. Os mercados so mais lquidos e globalizados. A globalizao financeira acentuou a sincronizao da evoluo do preo de activos, mesmo quando os dados fundamentais o no justificam em certas partes do globo. As facilidades de deslocalizao de actividades produtivas agravam a vulnerabilidade de muitas economias. Neste contexto, e para uma pequena economia aberta como a nossa, a participao na Unio Europeia  um factor de estabilidade inestimvel. No me refiro a estabilidade da evoluo econmica, mas  estabilidade profunda que resulta da partilha de regras e da convergncia de instituies que a pertena  Unio Europeia implica. A nossa participao na unio monetria assegura a estabilidade monetria de um regime de inflao baixa. Com efeito, a longo prazo, a inflao das vrias regies integrantes de uma unio monetria acabar por tender a convergir para um valor mdio. Na verdade, os pases membros que mantiverem aumentos de preos sistematicamente superiores acabaro por deixar de ser competitivos e sofrer um processo recessivo, com desemprego, que acabar por moderar a inflao. Na estabilidade monetria referida inclui-se tambm a estabilidade cambial com uma rea econmica para onde destinamos a esmagadora maioria das nossas exportaes de bens e servios. Em resumo, pela primeira vez em dcadas as empresas portuguesas podem contar com reduzidas taxas de juro, um baixo custo de capital e acesso a um vasto mercado sem risco cambial. Sem essas condies no poderiam, alis, ter-se internacionalizado como o fizeram nos ltimos anos. O benefcio daquela estabilidade macroeconmica fundamental permite tambm o planeamento dos investimentos e da produo com horizontes mais seguros que no passado. Finalmente, as exigncias do Pacto de Estabilidade impem que as finanas pblicas tenham que se manter numa trajectria de solvabilidade, o que assegura a estabilidade financeira. Tudo isto significa que a nossa participao na Unio Europeia garante a estabilidade de regras e princpios de funcionamento que a teoria e a evidncia histrica apontam como indispensveis ao crescimento e  prosperidade dos pases: inflao baixa, poltica oramental prudente e sustentvel, abertura da economia e mercados sem distores. Evidentemente que isso no basta para evitar perodos de maior incerteza ou perplexidade como aquele que agora atravessamos e que no pretendo escamotear. Estamos no meio de um perodo eleitoral prolongado, que embora normal em democracia tem inevitveis custos e, sobretudo, atravessamos uma fase de pessimismo sobre as perspectivas para o futuro do pas. Uma daquelas fases prprias dos pases ciclotmicos e inseguros que passam facilmente da euforia  depresso. O nevoeiro eleitoral complica ainda mais a tarefa de tentar discernir com clareza onde estamos e quais so os nossos reais problemas. No nos podemos enganar de diagnstico e a iluso mais perigosa consiste em supor que todos os diagnsticos esto feitos. Em meu entender, e em termos genricos, a economia defronta-se com os seguintes trs problemas: 1. uma difcil situao oramental que requer uma reduo significativa do dfice em pouco tempo; 2. uma desacelerao do crescimento econmico, que partilhamos com o resto da Europa, mas que tem factores internos prprios; 3. um dfice estrutural de competitividade a que temos que fazer face com novas solues empresariais, que alterem o lado da oferta da economia, por forma a vencer os desafios que nos coloca o alargamento da Unio Europeia. A questo mais sria e imediata  a situao das finanas pblicas. Em Julho do ano passado recordei com apropriado nfase a necessidade de cumprir o Pacto de Estabilidade e afirmei ento que : Esta exigncia significa que, mais do que com uma crise econmica, o pas est confrontado com uma crise oramental. O que est em causa so os compromissos que assumimos sobre a evoluo a mdio prazo do dfice oramental. Recente Conselho de Ministros das Finanas da Unio Europeia confirmou o objectivo de se atingir um dfice nulo em 2004. Tero, assim, que ser tomadas algumas decises difceis, provavelmente quer do lado das receitas quer do lado das despesas, para reduzir o dfice. O pas vai precisar de consensos alargados e de uma slida soluo poltica para fazer face ao que nos espera. Se se mantiverem os calendrios aprovados pelo ECOFIN, est em causa reduzir o dfice de 2,2% para zero em trs anos, o que sendo difcil no configura uma situao dramtica. No existe, alis, um problema tcnico de sustentabilidade das finanas pblicas portuguesas. Temos um ratio da dvida em relao ao PIB de 55%, muito inferior  media europeia e as regras do Pacto de Estabilidade quanto aos dfices asseguram que ter que continuar a diminuir. O respeito pelas grandes orientaes contidas no Programa de Estabilidade apresentado  essencial  credibilidade internacional da nossa poltica econmica, aspecto decisivo para uma pequena economia vulnerabilizada por desequilbrios recentes e com necessidade de atrair capitais. O que torna mais difcil a consolidao oramental  que ela tem que ser concretizada num perodo de desacelerao do crescimento econmico, o segundo problema que mencionei. Esta desacelerao resulta do impacto da evoluo da economia europeia, mas tem factores endgenos associados ao endividamento dos agentes econmicos acumulado nos ltimos anos. Neste perodo o crescimento esteve sustentado no excessivo dinamismo da despesa interna que cresceu muito acima do aumento do produto interno, estando assim associada a um endividamento crescente dos agentes econmicos privados. Como  bvio, essa evoluo no poderia continuar indefinidamente. Quanto ao Estado, embora a dvida pblica tenha vindo a diminuir em percentagem do PIB, o aumento do consumo pblico estimulou a procura interna e contribuiu para uma poltica oramental pr-ciclica a partir de 98. Note-se que a evoluo da despesa interna, consumo e investimento, era em grande medida inevitvel em resultado do choque da descida permanente das taxas de juro desde o perodo preparatrio para a nossa participao no euro. Mesmo uma poltica oramental mais restritiva no teria evitado a progresso significativa da despesa e do endividamento privado. A economia sofreu uma alterao de regime econmico e atravessou uma fase de foroso ajustamento  nova situao. A queda das taxas de juro durante a segunda metade da dcada e, aps a garantia da nossa entrada na unio monetria, o carcter permanente dessa descida, implicou um aumento da riqueza e da capacidade de endividamento dos agentes econmicos privados. Muitas famlias e empresas tornaram-se de sbito solventes para aceder ao crdito e, racionalmente, em face do novo regime de inflao e juros baixos, decidiram us-lo para aumentar as suas despesas. As empresas aproveitaram para expandir e modernizar a sua capacidade produtiva e internacionalizar-se. Um processo deste tipo tem naturalmente limites, precisamente os que decorrem da capacidade creditcia dos agentes econmicos. Com nveis elevados de endividamento aumenta a vulnerabilidade a choques econmicos futuros e a partir de certo momento inicia-se um processo natural de moderao do aumento da despesa. Um endividamento dos agentes econmicos associado a um nvel de procura interna superior ao PIB conduz a um dfice com o exterior. No entanto, para um pas sem moeda prpria como  agora o nosso caso, os limites do dfice externo resultam apenas da agregao da capacidade de endividamento dos seus agentes, incluindo os bancos. Estes tm intermediado entre os agentes domsticos e o exterior, endividando-se junto dos mercados interbancrios da zona euro para financiar a expanso do crdito. Os bancos estrangeiros tm proporcionado estes recursos porque avaliam de forma positiva a solidez dos bancos portugueses. Este ponto merece algum aprofundamento porque  sempre difcil libertarmo-nos de antigos modos de pensamento criados durante anteriores episdios de desequilbrio externo -quando tnhamos moeda prpria. O problema do dfice externo para uma regio de uma unio monetria deixa de ser, obviamente, uma questo de falta de divisas ou de uma possvel crise cambial. No se verifica, pois, a necessidade do mesmo tipo de ajustamento rpido como nas experincias passadas, o que constitui uma primeira diferena a assinalar. O endividamento dos agentes  todo em euros, ou seja, na nossa prpria moeda. A disponibilidade do financiamento depende, pois, exclusivamente da solvabilidade microeconmica dos agentes econmicos privados. O evoluir normal da economia, mesmo que em desacelerao temporria, permite s famlias e s empresas obterem o rendimento em euros necessrio para satisfazer o servio da dvida contrada. Neste novo regime econmico, em que somos macroeconomicamente uma regio da unio monetria europeia, a questo da balana de pagamentos no  uma questo autnoma, mas  apenas o reflexo da restrio oramental que defrontam os agentes econmicos  famlias, empresas e instituies financeiras. A segunda diferena significativa relativamente a experincias passadas reside no facto que, desta vez, o dfice no resulta de dfices pblicos e o seu financiamento tem sido assegurado pelo mercado aps o filtro de uma adequada anlise dos riscos de crdito envolvidos. Isto no significa que a economia tenha deixado de ter restrio externa e possa continuar a gastar muito acima do que produz. Nos prximos anos vai ter que reduzir-se significativamente o dfice da balana de bens e servios. Os limites ao dfice e ao endividamento so, porm, introduzidos pelos prprios agentes privados ou pelos mercados que asseguram, assim, o funcionamento de mecanismos de auto-correco dos dfices, mecanismos que so naturalmente de natureza restritiva. Na verdade, ou os agentes comeam a moderar despesas e a aumentar os seus nveis de poupana ou comeam os bancos a apertar os seus critrios de anlise de risco e a reduzir em consequncia a oferta de crdito. Quanto mais tarde comeasse este processo de desacelerao, mais abrupta poderia ser a paragem e maiores os riscos de uma verdadeira recesso. Por essa razo se pode considerar como positiva a desacelerao que se comeou a verificar na despesa interna, uma vez que isso significa o caminho de uma aterragem suave da economia portuguesa. Desde a segunda metade de 2000 a desacelerao da despesa interna deu-se no contexto de uma situao de pleno emprego, de uma subida dos salrios reais e de um aumento do Rendimento Disponvel dos particulares. O crescimento deste ltimo, sendo superior ao do consumo, significa que houve uma subida na taxa de poupana, o que revela que as famlias comearam a corrigir os excessos de crescimento da despesa. Evidentemente que isso pode implicar, e tem implicado, uma quebra do crescimento da economia, mas a inevitvel desacelerao da despesa interna no tem que se traduzir linearmente na reduo do crescimento do produto, visto que h sempre a possibilidade das empresas, perante a desacelerao da procura interna, desviarem mais produo para a exportao. Talvez isso j tenha acontecido o ano passado, perodo em que as exportaes cresceram mais do que a procura dos nossos pases clientes, o que significa que houve ganho de quota de mercado, incluindo nas exportaes tradicionais.  necessrio que esse processo continue nos prximos anos. Em suma, o que tudo isto significa  que necessitamos de um outro padro de crescimento, menos assente na procura interna e mais baseado em aumentos de produtividade que dem maior solidez  nossa competitividade externa. O que nos remete para o terceiro problema que enunciei atrs. Precisamos de um profundo choque estrutural do lado da oferta, que depende de algumas polticas pblicas mas que ter que resultar, sobretudo, de mais iniciativa empresarial. Infelizmente, nem a generalidade dos agentes privados nem o Estado parecem ter interiorizado suficientemente as novas regras de funcionamento da economia de um pas membro de uma unio monetria. Essas regras so a outra face do euro, exigente e disciplinadora, que temos infelizmente ignorado. So regras que requerem a alterao de comportamentos, algumas reformas estruturais e um novo regime de regulao macroeconmica. Isto implica o reconhecimento de uma alterao de paradigma: o mundo passou de um regime em que a poltica macroeconmica assegurava o pleno emprego e a poltica de rendimentos devia controlar a inflao, para um novo regime em que a poltica macroeconmica, em particular a monetria, controla a inflao e a poltica de rendimentos condiciona o desemprego. Na perspectiva destas novas regras de funcionamento, a nossa situao apresenta alguns sinais de vulnerabilidade, como seja, a existncia de um sistema de negociao salarial fragmentado e de curto horizonte, o peso de uma burocracia asfixiante e um sistema judicial ineficaz, um regime deficiente de enquadramento oramental e insuficincias no sistema poltico, com a dificuldade de obter maiorias de governo e com a necessidade de um Estado com mais prestgio e autoridade. H reformas profundas a fazer na esfera pblica e na esfera privada, com a urgncia proporcional aos desafios que teremos que vencer com o nosso prprio esforo nos prximos anos. No voltaremos a beneficiar de descidas substancias das taxas de juro, no sero possveis desvalorizaes cambiais para repor temporariamente a competitividade das produes nacionais e, finalmente, as transferncias da Unio Europeia tendero a diminuir em percentagem do PIB. Como afirmei recentemente: Numa palavra, acabaram-se os remdios fceis que no passado aliviaram os nossos atrasos e compensaram os nossos erros. Temos que contar sobretudo com ns prprios para garantir o nosso desenvolvimento. Isso requer uma cultura de esforo, de trabalho e de rigor.  A melhoria das nossas condies de competitividade envolve mltiplos aspectos da economia e da sociedade portuguesa. Aumentar a produtividade  a nica forma de melhorar consistentemente o nvel de vida sem causar presses inflacionistas. A produtividade , porm, uma resultante e no um instrumento que se deixe facilmente manipular. O seu aumento requer tempo e implica um processo complexo que envolve um vasto leque de factores. Entre eles, a capacidade de absoro do progresso tcnico; a racionalizao da produo; a alterao da composio sectorial do produto; o aproveitamento das economias externas de produo, dependentes da rede de infraestruturas e do nvel educativo dos recursos humanos. Assume tambm importncia a envolvente institucional mais geral que condiciona a capacidade de uma sociedade se modernizar. Portugal dispe de todas as potencialidades para continuar com sucesso um processo de convergncia real com os seus parceiros europeus. De 1985 para c, Portugal cresceu a uma taxa mdia de 3.8 por cento, bem acima da mdia europeia e passou de 53 por cento do rendimento mdio europeu para um valor de 74 por cento. Estamos agora numa fase de ajustamento e reduo dos desequilbrios gerados pelo anterior perodo de forte crescimento. Esta correco  necessria para criar condies de sustentabilidade ao processo de desenvolvimento, e no deve, por isso, constituir factor de deslocado pessimismo. Alguns duvidam da capacidade do pas para operar as necessrias transformaes na estrutura produtiva e ganhar novas vantagens comparativas. Queriam poder prever e porventura planear esse processo, identificando prioridades sobre o que devemos produzir no futuro, o que  manifestamente impossvel. Garantidas as condies de enquadramento apropriadas, caber  iniciativa empresarial, portuguesa e estrangeira, comandar esse processo de transformao. A situao actual apenas torna mais importante que a interveno pblica contribua para criar condies de modernizao e liberalizao dos mercados de produtos e de capitais, de encorajamento da inovao e de uma cultura empresarial estimulada por um bom clima de investimento. As polticas pblicas de construo de infra-estruturas com assegurada rendibilidade social e, acima de tudo, a melhoria da qualificao dos recursos humanos, continuam a ser contributos indispensveis. A produtividade global de uma economia no salta de patamar com reformas de efeitos imediatos, mas Portugal, garantindo estabilidade macro-econmica, ausncia de risco cambial e custos baixos comparando com os outros pases membros da Unio Europeia, tem todas as condies para assegurar um clima de investimento mais favorvel. E isso  decisivo para o objectivo de convergncia e de ajustamento durante os prximos anos. O essencial desses ajustamentos passar pelas empresas. As empresas tero que encontrar novas vantagens comparativas  medida que lentamente forem desaparecendo as que resultam de custos salariais mais baixos. Muitas empresas tradicionais iro desaparecer a mdio prazo. Outras tero que surgir para sustentar o novo crescimento. Nessa perspectiva  necessrio atrair mais investimento estrangeiro, mas o contributo decisivo ter que provir das empresas portuguesas. Na verdade, o nico caminho possvel implica mudar rapidamente a realidade das nossas estruturas produtivas. Apenas dessa forma, e por uma vez, no ter razo Jean Monnet quando afirmava que  os homens s agem em estado de necessidade e s reconhecem a necessidade em momentos de crise.

Title: Foreword by the Governor Vitor Constncio - Economic Bulletin March 2002
text: Foreword by the Governor Vitor Constancio - Economic Bulletin March 2002 30 Apr. 2002 The publication of this Economic Bulletin is an opportunity to do a first assessment of the behaviour of Portuguese economy over the past year. The recent evolution of the economy indicates the existence of three groups of problems: 1. a deceleration of economic activity, that we share with the rest of Europe, but which has its own endogenous factors; 2. a difficult budgetary position that requires a significant reduction of the deficit at a very short notice; 3. a structural deficit of competitiveness, that we must face with new solutions intended to change the supply side of the economy, in order to meet the challenges posed by European Union enlargement. 2001 was marked by a significant decrease in the growth rate of output from 3.6% in 2000 to 1.8%, a value nonetheless still higher than the European average. This behaviour evolved in line with the world economy, that also characterised by a strong reduction in growth and by a deterioration of international trade that implied, in our case, a deceleration of demand in our external markets from 11.8 % in 2000 to only 1.2% in 2001. In addition to this, however, the slowdown of growth in Portugal was also due to the behaviour of domestic demand that went up by only 0.9%, after an increase of 3.0% in 2000. This deceleration of both consumption and investment, already initiated in 2000, reflects the adjustment of the economy, following a period of strong growth that implied a higher indebtedness of the economic agents. Therefore, since the second half of 2000, households have increased their savings rate and contained consumption, that grew by only 0.8% in 2001 compared with 2.8% in 2000. This behaviour, despite the continued increase in Disposable Income (1.9%) and the maintenance of the full employment situation, is a normal reaction to the indebtedness level attained and to the negative expectations generated in the meantime regarding the future of the economy. Likewise, firms also reduced investment that registered a global negative rate of 0.8%, in spite of the increase in public investment. The deceleration of domestic demand, in turn, was offset by an increase in the contribution of exports net of imports to the growth of the economy. Indeed, exports grew more than international demand, meaning that our exports had a gain in market share. As a result, the deficit of the balance of goods and services declined significantly by 2 percentage points. In turn, the combined balance of the current and capital accounts (equivalent to the former balance of current transactions) declined to 8.1%. The deceleration in domestic demand was behind this improvement of the external balance and is expected to continue this year. In effect, the factors behind the recent trend of domestic demand continue to be present, and are possibly more pronounced due to the inevitable budget consolidation measures. Therefore, it is only natural that this year the Portuguese economy will grow below the European average. Over the coming years, the deficit of the balance of goods and services will have to decrease further. The limits on the deficit and on indebtedness are introduced by the private agents themselves or by the markets, thereby ensuring the operation of deficit autocorrection mechanisms, which are naturally of a restrictive nature. The later this deceleration process is started, the more abrupt could be the slowdown and the higher would be the recessive risks. For this reason, the deceleration in domestic demand may be considered positive, since that corresponds o a path towards a smooth adjustment of the Portuguese economy. Since the second half of 2000, domestic expenditure decelerated in spite of a full employment situation, an improvement in real wages and an increase in the disposable income of households. This income increased more than the growth in consumption, which means that there was an increase in the household savings rate, which indicates that households have started on their own initiative to correct excessive expenditure growth. This has therefore implied a fall in economic growth. However, the deceleration of domestic expenditure does not linearly translate into a reduction in output growth, since firms may always channel more production to exports. This seems to have happened last year, since, as I mentioned above, there was a gain in market share, including in traditional exports. It is necessary to maintain this development over the coming years. This should be taken into account in managing the expectations of economic agents, in order to avoid an excessive and unjustified pessimism about the future of the economy. On balance, this means that we need a different growth pattern, less centred on domestic demand and more based on productivity increases, that improve our external competitiveness. This leads me to address the third problem mentioned at the beginning. A profound structural shock is necessary on the supply side, dependent on some public policies, but which will chiefly be the result of more business initiative. Unfortunately, neither most private agents nor the State seem to have adequately realised the new operating rules of the economy for a country that is member of a monetary union. These rules require a change in behaviour, some structural reforms and a new macroeconomic regulatory system. The most serious and immediate issue is the situation of public finance. Last year, I recalled the need to comply with the Stability Pact and I said then: This requirement means that the country faces a budget crisis, rather than an economic crisis. The issues at stake are the commitments assumed on the medium-term development of the budget deficit. As it is known, there is no technical problem of sustainability of Portuguese public finances. Our debt to GDP ratio is 55%, below the European average and the deficitrelated regulations laid down in the Stability Pact ensure that it will have to decrease further. Compliance with the major guidelines contained in the Stability Programme is essential for the international credibility of our economic policy. The deterioration of the budget deficit in 2001 makes the task more difficult. A high level of national consensus is required as regards the objectives to be attained, without any drama, but in line with a sense of responsibility usually shared by everyone regarding the interests of the country. In particular, this external credibility requires the maintenance of the objective of a budgetary position close to balance by 2004, given the need to show serious efforts of budget consolidation. In order to reduce the deficit, some tough decisions will have to be taken, including containing expenditure and avoiding any measures that may reduce tax receipts. The situation may even justify an increase in some indirect taxes with more immediate effects on the recovery of current revenues. In the short run, all these measures have restrictive consequences that must be offset by a higher buoyancy of exports, boosted by an international economic recovery and by a rechannelling of production to external markets. In order to make this development possible, it is necessary to reverse the trend observed in recent years of wage increases above output growth. This would not necessarily correspond to a freezing of wages, but to more moderation in wage increases. We must all realise that, under the present situation, this is an essential condition to maintain high employment levels and thus avoid the deterioration of exclusion factors and more inequalities in Portuguese society. A last word to the recent creation of the Commission led by the Banco de Portugal, with the participation of the Ministry of Finance and the Instituto Nacional de Estatistica, with a view to analysing and updating the accounts utilised in the notification of the Excessive Deficit Procedure reported in late February. It should be stressed that part of the problems related to the assessment of the final value of the deficit are associated with issues known for quite a long time, but that require final clarification with the Eurostat. These issues are related, firstly, to the treatment of equity increases in some public companies. This is particularly controversial, since they can be considered as financial asset operations or as capital transfers with an influence on the deficit. Secondly, they are related to the problem of the values of taxes and social contributions considered in National Accounts when compared with those registered in Public Accounts. On the other hand, there are still some issues related to the application of the specialisation principle of the fiscal year in the translation from Public Accounts concepts, which are mainly on a cash basis, to National Accounts standards. In addition, many Autonomous Funds and Services only have to present their final accounts by 15 May. It should be stressed, however, that the work of the Commission do not cover an audit to public accounts, in the technical sense of the term, since there are neither the time nor the means required to carry out such audit, nor should we interfere with the competences of the Court of Auditors. The Commission will present its conclusions up to August, in time for the preparation by the Instituto Nacional de Estatistica of the forthcoming notification of the Excessive Deficits Procedure, to be reported in early September.

Title: Introduction by the Governor of the Commission's Report for the Analysis of Public Accounts
text: Introduction by the Governor of The Report... Introduction by the Governor of the Commission's Report for the Analysis of Public Accounts 23 jul. 2002 1. Following Eurostat's non-certification of the General Government deficit for 2001 and reported in February, it requested the Government that Banco de Portugal lead a Commission for the Analysis of Public Accounts. Although the matter is not included in the normal competences of Banco de Portugal, the government's advisory functions that its Organic Law specifies justify the acceptance of the mission in question. From the outset there was an understanding that it was not a question of carrying out an audit in the technical sense of the term, but fundamentally of evaluating and quantifying some methodological decisions of Eurostat and of dealing with information not available in February. On the other hand, it was important for the defence of the institutions that the Commission should also include the National Institute of Statistics and the Directorate-General for Budget, since these two entities are the main responsible for reporting to Eurostat. The revision carried out is essentially the result of methodological changes and theva information, since the Report prepared for the Excessive Deficit Procedure, normally carried out in February, constitutes a precarious estimate without final account data of any of the subsectors and, in particular, of the accounts of the Funds and Autonomous Services (including the National Health Service) and the Regional and Local Administration. This is a situation that needs to be changed, as this year there has been a significant and greater deviation than was usual between the February Reporte and the value now determined. To this end, the Commission presents a set of recommendations on the submission of data by different services in order to improve the preparation of the Report in future years. 2. The deficit reported in February was2.2% of GDP, but still in March and on the basis of new provisional information on local government accounts, the Government sent Eurostat a review of the public deficit from 2001 to 2.4% of GDP. This figure was the startingpoint for the Commission's work. In the meantime, in its communique at the end of March announcing the non-certification of the public accounts of some Member States, Eurostat referred as justification for the case Portuguese the existence of two problems. The first referred to the need to revise the accounting of taxes and social contributions in accordance with Regulation 2516 of November 2000 for which Portugal obtained a valid derogation until June 2002. The second problem related to capital increases for several public companies that were regarded as operations on financial assets and, as such, did not count on the budget deficit. However, as companies have systematic losses, Eurostat believes that it should treat that form of financing as transfers that go into the determination of the budget deficit. These two problems have been common knowledge for some time and, of course, either of them could lead to an increasein public deficits in recent years. The correction of taxes recorded on a commitment basis had been foreseen since November 2000 and research into the financing of public enterprises had begun in the course of 2001. In fact, the Portuguese Government adopted a transparent attitude on these points and had already provided Eurostat in early 2002 with the information needed for the calculations on the correction of tax revenues and last year had already been available for all the information on the accounts of public undertakings relevant to the analysis of the issue of capital increases. On the latter, Eurostat indicated to the Portuguese authorities in early April that its first estimate involved an increase in the 2001 deficit by 0.25% of GDP. It should be stressed that, as stated below in the text of the Report (page 19), "... a European survey of the actual way of recording these transactions remains undisclosed, so that only one situationremains to be taken..., the decision may constitute non-equivalent treatment in the other Member States and is therefore discriminatory for Portugal'. In the meantime, the Commissionfor the Analysis of Public Accounts has developed its own methodology for addressing this problem, focusing, given its relevance, on transport companies. According to this method, capital increases should continue to be treated as financial transactions that do not enter the deficit,but in return for the amount of compensatory compensation due to undertakings to ensure an adequate ratio of financial autonomy. This method seems more correct and for 2001 results in a negligible difference from eurostat's estimate (0.23% versus 0.25%). The divergence becomes more significant for other years and, above all, allows better framing of the financing of public companies that are investing and lack higher equity. 3. As regards the correction of tax revenues and social contributions, the problem stems from the amendment of the national accounting rules of the European System of Accounts (ESA 95) which was introduced by Regulation 2516. The esa 95 has the principle of economic specialisation which implies that the register of revenue or expenditure must relate to the year in which they were economically carried out and become due and not when they were settled. As regards revenue, the difference between revenue staked and revenue collected should not, however, be systematically significant and should even be annulled when the average of several years is made. The fact that this is not happening in several countries has led Eurostat to amend the processesthrough that Regulation of November 2000 which requires the use of one of two new methods: either to calculate and apply an unchargeability rate or to adopt a cash logic with small adjustments to the actual revenue sums collected. The Commissionrecommends this second method and consequently calculated a difference of 0.6% of GDP in 2001 which represents a reduction in tax revenues compared to the amounts previously used. However, for the application of that Regulationsome countries obtained derogations. In our case the derogation was valid until June of this year. In this context, the Portuguese government has maintained to the European Commission, with the support of a legal opinion, that this derogation means that the new method should only be applied to revenue data from 2002 and that using it for 2001 and previous years would constitute an improper retroactive application of the Regulation. The alternative interpretation, which seems to be that of Eurostat, is that the derogation isonly to give countries more time to gather data and to decide which method they prefer, which will then be applied for several years retroactively. The issue is expected to be resolved at the next Excessive Deficit Procedure Report in early September. The Commission for the Analysis of Public Accounts has not considered that it should not comment on this legal problem. Thus, the final result reached by the Commission for the Public Accounts deficit in 2001 presents dois figures: without the correction of revenues calculated on a compromise basis the deficit was 3.5% of GDP and, if this correction is applied, the deficit was 4.1 % (see Annex B). 4. In addition to the two methodological changes referred to, the amendment to the State Budget for 2002, presented in May, introduced a new criterion by inquiring all administration services on outstanding amounts from previous years, including supplier credit. The revised Budget thereforeincludes the payment of all these debts this year, which increases the respective deficit from the point of view of Public Accounting, which uses a cash criterion. In the national accounting perspective, however, these expenditures, since they have actually been realised in previous years, have to be added to the deficit of those same years, according to a criterion of commitments or economic specialisation. In the past and with regard to expenditure, only those relating to the National Health Service and the interest on publicdebt were the subject of this treatment, all others recorded in the year in which they were paid. Excluding those two types of expenditure, the Revised Budget for 2002 identifies an amount to be paid this year and allocated to previous years dand about 1% of GDP. For the preparation of the budget review carried out in May, services had not been asked to distribute this amount for years, which of course did not refer only to 2001. The Commission therefore had to ask the publicservices that had contributed the most to that amount of 1% of expenditure for years ended (see Annex D) for the following additional information: (a) distribution of the expenditure mentioned by the different years to which they relate and which, in some cases, date back to periods prior to 1999; (b) clearance of amounts which had been paid in 2001 but which were related to expenditure from previous years. Only with this information was it possible to have a comparable number of public deficits, according to the newc riterio introduced. Otherwise the deficits of each year would appear distorted, since the figure for 2002 would be completely purged of expenditure attributable to other years while the accounts of recent years would continue to contain expenditure that does notcorrespond to expenditures committed in previous years. Despite the excellent collaboration provided by the Directorate-General for budget and the services involved, the final answers to these questions were not fully available until the end ofJune. This was one of the main factors in the Commission's work. As a result of the clearances on this point, the final figure to be added to the 2001 deficit is 0.3% of GDP. 5. One final methodological change concerns the dealing ofrevenues and expenses related to Community Funds and processed by various Autonomous Funds and Services. The Commission for the Analysis of Public Accounts considers that revenue stemming from Community funds should be recorded in the last period in which expenditure takes place, thereby ensuring that revenue stowe off the deficit is guaranteed. This implies that advances made by the European Union or the Portuguese Treasury must be recorded as a financial transaction (Financial Assets or Liabilities) until they are realised in actual expenditure or revenue, at which time the active or passive situation should be cancelled. This procedure alone ensures that each year's deficit reflects expenditure incurred that year and isnot artificially affected by the entry of revenue recorded on a purely cash basis, i.e. allocated to the time when they enter regardless of their use. This methodological change led to the considering ofthe available balances in fsa units in the amount of 0.1% of GDP which reduces the deficit in National Accounting by the same amount. This problem was also raised by the problems caused by the revenue stemming from Autonomous Funds and Services which were one of the factors in the review of budget implementation drawn up by the Directorate-General for budget and to which I will refer to the following point. Rather, however, it should be recalled that the four methodological change points already mentioned have contributed to a worsening deficit of 2001 by 1.0% of GDP. The application of all these methodological changes for years prior to 2001, as defined by Eurostat, will be the responsibility of the INE as the statistical authority responsible for the definitive accounts of publicadministrations. 6. Putting aside the methodological changes referenced, the provision of new information led the Directorate-General for Budget to re-estimate budget implementation in 2001. In this context, it was decided to continue the work of the Comission until it had the final accounts of Autonomous Funds and Services, the Regional and Local Administration, and the Social Security and the Tax Administration itself. This objective, in addition to the point already indicated on the distribution of expenditure for years ended,and that the Commission's work should only now be concluded, however, within the planned timetable. It was intended to ensure that, as far as possible, the figures calculated by the Commission were no longer subject to revisions on the basis of further training until data were sent to Eurostat atthe end of August in the context of the next Excessive Deficit Procedure. From this point of view, it should be noted that the latest figures on tax revenues were not finalised until 15 July. Algsome Autonomous Funds and Services that by law only have to deliver final accounts on 15 May, only later came to do so. The final accounts of the NHS were made available in early July and those of Social Security on 17 this month. 7. The Frameworksummarises the deficit corrections resulting from the Commission's work: The revision of the budget implementation estimate reaches a high value (0.7%) that had never occurred in previous years, revealing problems of precarious informationand budgetary control that is necessary to correct. On this and other problems the Commission has considered to make a set of 5 Recommendations which seek to draw from the problems examined useful conclusions for the future. 8. In addition to thefull understanding of the factors leading to the high deficit of 2001, it is also important to compare the evolution of revenue and expenditure compared to the initial budget which provided for a deficit of only 1.1 % of GDP. Assuming, for the purposes of analysis, the worst-case scenario for the 2001 deficit, the Commission's estimates make it possible to build the following comparative table: As can be seen, the worsening of the deficit compared to the initial budget resulted mainly from a fall in revenues (-2.8%) which, in addition to the methodological correction referred to, can be attributed to the economic downturn and to some fiscal change measures adopted for 2001. Total expenditure only increased by 0.2% of GDP compared to the initial budget, albeitwith a substanci al change in composition. However, whatever its origin, the increase in the deficit last year means that fiscal policy was expansionary, having caused an increase in the primary deficit adjusted to the cycle. The high deficit atinggone also has the seriousness of not respecting the Stability Pact by exceeding the 3% limit. In order to avoid the most serious consequences associated with a possible excessive deficit declaration by the Council of the European Union, it is essential to correct the situation as early as this year. Several of the factors identified as responsible for the worsening of the deficit indicate that 2001 was a very particular year that will not be easily repeated. The desired correction therefore seems possible, especially after the measures already adopted by the Government and taking into account budgetary implementation so far. The country has now started a demanding adjustment period which must be collectively assumed. The objectives set out in the context of the Stability Pact require that the deficit be significantly reduced in 2003 and 2004 in a fiscal consolidation effort that all those responsible have a duty to support in order for Portugal to respect its commitments and, above all, to build the foundations of a properly anti-cyclical fiscal policy as it is essential for a member country of a monetary union. Lisbon, 23 July 2002 Vitor Constancio Governor of Banco de Portugal
text_original: Introduo pelo Governador do Relat... Introduo pelo Governador do Relatrio da Comisso para a Anlise das Contas Pblicas 23 jul. 2002 1. Na sequncia da no certificao pelo Eurostat do dfice do Sector Pblico Administrativo referente ao ano de 2001 e reportado em Fevereiro, solicitou o Governo que o Banco de Portugal liderasse uma Comisso para Anlise das Contas Pblicas. Embora o assunto no se inclua nas competncias normais do Banco de Portugal, as funes de aconselhamento do Governo que a sua Lei Orgnica especifica, justificam a aceitao da misso em causa. Desde o incio houve o entendimento de que no se tratava de realizar uma auditoria no sentido tcnico do termo, mas fundamentalmente de avaliar e quantificar algumas decises metodolgicas do Eurostat e de tratar informao no disponvel em Fevereiro. Por outro lado, foi importante para a defesa das instituies que a Comisso integrasse tambm o Instituto Nacional de Estatstica e a Direco-Geral do Oramento, uma vez que estas duas entidades so as principais responsveis pelo Reporte ao Eurostat. A reviso efectuada resulta, no essencial, de alteraes metodolgicas e de nova informao, uma vez que o Reporte preparado para o Procedimento de Dfices Excessivos, normalmente realizado em Fevereiro, constitui uma estimativa precria sem dados finais das contas de qualquer dos subsectores e, em especial, das contas dos Fundos e Servios Autnomos (incluindo do Servio Nacional de Sade) e da Administrao Regional e Local. Esta  uma situao que  necessrio alterar, uma vez que se verificou este ano um desvio significativo e superior ao que era habitual verificar-se entre o Reporte de Fevereiro e o valor agora determinado. Nesse sentido, a Comisso apresenta um conjunto de recomendaes sobre a apresentao de dados pelos diferentes servios por forma a melhorar a preparao do Reporte em anos futuros. 2. O dfice reportado inicialmente em Fevereiro era de 2,2% do PIB, mas ainda em Maro e com base em nova informao provisria sobre as contas da Administrao Local, o Governo enviou ao Eurostat uma reviso do dfice pblico de 2001 para 2.4% do PIB. Este valor constituiu o ponto de partida dos trabalhos da Comisso. Entretanto, no seu comunicado de finais de Maro em que anunciava a no certificao das contas pblicas de alguns Estados membros, o Eurostat referia como justificao para o caso portugus a existncia de dois problemas. O primeiro referia-se  necessidade de reviso da contabilizao dos impostos e contribuies sociais de acordo com o Regulamento 2516 de Novembro de 2000 para o qual Portugal obtivera uma derrogao vlida at Junho de 2002. O segundo problema relacionava-se com os aumentos de capital para diversas empresas pblicas que foram considerados como operaes sobre activos financeiros e, como tal, no contavam para o dfice oramental. No entanto, como as empresas registam prejuzos sistemticos, o Eurostat entende dever tratar aquela forma de financiamento como transferncias que entram na determinao do dfice oramental. Estes dois problemas eram do conhecimento geral desde h algum tempo e, naturalmente, qualquer deles poderia conduzir a um aumento dos dfices pblicos dos ltimos anos. A correco dos impostos registados numa base de compromissos estava prevista desde Novembro de 2000 e a investigao sobre o financiamento das empresas pblicas havia sido iniciada no decurso de 2001. Na verdade, o Governo portugus adoptou uma atitude transparente sobres esses pontos e havia j fornecido ao Eurostat no incio de 2002 a informao necessria para os clculos relativos  correco das receitas dos impostos e no ano passado haviam sido j disponibilizados todos os elementos sobre as contas das empresas pblicas relevantes para a anlise da questo dos aumentos de capital. Sobre estes ltimos, o Eurostat indicou s autoridades portuguesas no princpio de Abril que a sua primeira estimativa implicava um aumento do dfice de 2001 em 0,25% do PIB. Sublinhe-se que, conforme se refere adiante no texto do Relatrio (pgina 19), ...continua por fazer  ou por divulgar um levantamento europeu do efectivo modo de registo destas operaes, pelo que, ao identificar apenas uma situao..., a deciso pode configurar um tratamento no equivalente nos restantes Estados-membros, sendo, portanto, discriminatria para Portugal . Entretanto, a Comisso para a Anlise das Contas Pblicas desenvolveu uma metodologia prpria para tratar este problema, incidindo, dada a sua relevncia, nas empresas de transporte. De acordo com este mtodo os aumentos de capital devem continuar a ser tratados como operaes financeiras que no entram no dfice, mas em contrapartida este deve ser aumentado pelo montante das indemnizaes compensatrias devidas s empresas para lhes assegurar um adequado ratio de autonomia financeira. Este mtodo parece mais correcto e para 2001 resulta numa diferena negligencivel relativamente  estimativa do Eurostat (0,23% contra 0,25%). A divergncia torna-se mais significativa para outros anos e, sobretudo, permita enquadrar melhor no futuro o financiamento de empresas pblicas que estejam a investir e caream de capitais prprios mais elevados. 3. No que se refere  correco das receitas de impostos e contribuies sociais, o problema tem origem na alterao das regras de contabilidade nacional do Sistema Europeu de Contas (SEC 95) que foi introduzida pelo referido Regulamento 2516. No SEC 95 vigora o princpio da especializao econmica que implica que o registo de receitas ou despesas deve reportar-se ao ano em que as mesmas foram economicamente realizadas e se tornaram devidas e no quando foram liquidadas. No que se refere s receitas, a diferena entre receitas devidas e receitas cobradas no deveria, porm, ser sistematicamente significativa e deveria mesmo anular-se quando feita a mdia de vrios anos. O facto disso no estar a acontecer em vrios pases levou o Eurostat a alterar os procedimentos atravs do referido Regulamento de Novembro de 2000 que impe a utilizao de um de dois novos mtodos: ou calcular e aplicar uma taxa de incobrabilidade ou adoptar uma lgica de caixa com pequenos ajustamentos s receitas efectivamente cobradas. A Comisso recomenda este segundo mtodo e em consequncia calculou uma diferena de 0,6% do PIB em 2001 que representa uma reduo de receitas de impostos relativamente aos valores anteriormente utilizados. Entretanto, para a aplicao daquele Regulamento alguns pases obtiveram derrogaes. No nosso caso a derrogao era vlida at Junho deste ano. Nesse contexto, o Governo Portugus sustentou junto da Comisso Europeia, com apoio em parecer jurdico, que essa derrogao significa que o novo mtodo s dever ser aplicado aos dados das receitas a partir de 2002 e que utiliz-lo para valores de 2001 e anos anteriores constituiria uma indevida aplicao retroactiva do Regulamento. A interpretao alternativa, que parece ser a do Eurostat,  a de que a derrogao serve apenas para dar mais tempo aos pases para reunirem dados e para decidirem qual o mtodo que preferem, o qual passar ento a ser aplicado a vrios anos retroactivamente. A questo dever ficar resolvida por ocasio do prximo Reporte do Procedimento de Dfices Excessivos no incio de Setembro. A Comisso para a Anlise das Contas Pblicas entendeu no se pronunciar sobre este problema jurdico. Deste modo, o resultado final a que chegou a Comisso para o dfice das Contas Pblicas em 2001 apresenta dois valores: sem a correco das receitas apuradas numa base de compromissos o dfice foi de 3,5% do PIB e, no caso de se aplicar essa correco, o dfice foi de 4,1 % (ver Anexo B). 4. Para alm das duas alteraes metodolgicas referidas, a alterao ao Oramento de Estado para 2002, apresentada em Maio, veio introduzir um novo critrio ao inquirir todos os servios da Administrao sobre os montantes em dvida com origem em anos anteriores, incluindo crdito de fornecedores. O Oramento revisto contempla, assim, o pagamento de todas essas dvidas este ano, o que faz aumentar o respectivo dfice na ptica da Contabilidade Pblica que usa um critrio de caixa. Na ptica da Contabilidade Nacional, porm, essas despesas, uma vez que foram efectivamente realizadas em anos anteriores, tm que se adicionar ao dfice desses mesmos anos, de acordo com um critrio de compromissos ou de especializao econmica. No passado e no que se refere a despesas, apenas as referentes ao Servio Nacional de Sade e aos juros da dvida pblica eram objecto deste tratamento, sendo todas as outras registadas no ano em que eram pagas. Excluindo aqueles dois tipos de despesas, o Oramento revisto para 2002 identifica um montante para ser pago este ano e atribudo a anos anteriores de cerca de 1% do PIB. Para a elaborao da reviso do Oramento realizada em Maio no se tinha solicitado aos servios a distribuio por anos desse montante, que naturalmente no se referia apenas a 2001. A Comisso teve assim que solicitar aos servios pblicos que mais tinham contribudo para aquele valor de 1% de despesas de anos findos (ver Anexo D) as seguintes informaes adicionais: a) Distribuio das despesas mencionadas pelos diferentes anos a que dizem respeito e que, nalguns casos, remontam a perodos anteriores a 1999; b) Apuramento dos montantes que tivessem sido pagos em 2001, mas que se referiam a despesas de anos anteriores. Unicamente com essa informao era possvel ter uma srie comparvel de dfices pblicos, de acordo com o novo critrio introduzido. De outra forma os dfices de cada ano apareceriam distorcidos, uma vez que o valor para 2002 ficaria completamente expurgado de despesas atribuveis a outros anos enquanto as contas dos ltimos anos continuariam a conter despesas que na verdade correspondem a despesas comprometidas em anos anteriores. Apesar da excelente colaborao prestada pela Direco Geral do Oramento e pelos servios envolvidos, as respostas finais a estas questes s ficaram completamente disponveis em finais de Junho. Este foi um dos principais factores de demora dos trabalhos da Comisso. Em resultado dos apuramentos referentes a este ponto, o valor final a adicionar ao dfice de 2001  de 0,3% do PIB. 5. Uma ltima alterao metodolgica refere-se ao tratamento das receitas e despesas relacionadas com os Fundos Comunitrios e processadas por diversos Fundos e Servios Autnomos. Entende a Comisso para a Anlise das Contas Pblicas que as receitas provenientes de Fundos Comunitrios devem ser registadas no mesmo perodo em que ocorrem as despesas, garantindo-se, assim, a neutralidade das receitas face ao dfice. Isto implica que os adiantamentos realizados pela Unio Europeia ou pelo Tesouro portugus devem ser registados como operao financeira (Activos ou Passivos Financeiros) enquanto no se concretizarem em despesa ou receita efectiva, momento em que a situao activa ou passiva deve ser cancelada. Apenas este procedimento garante que o dfice de cada ano reflecte as despesas realizadas nesse ano e no est artificialmente afectado por entrada de receitas registadas numa base puramente de caixa, ou seja, atribudas ao momento em que do entrada independentemente da sua utilizao. Esta alterao metodolgica conduziu a considerar os saldos disponveis em vrios FSA no valor de +0,1% do PIB o que reduz o dfice em Contabilidade Nacional no mesmo montante. Esta problemtica foi tambm suscitada pelos problemas ocorridos com as receitas de Fundos e Servios Autnomos que constituram um dos factores da reviso da execuo oramental elaborada pela Direco Geral do Oramento e a que farei referncia no ponto seguinte. Antes, porm,  conveniente recordar que os quatro pontos de alterao metodolgica j referidos contriburam para um agravamento do dfice de 2001 em 1,0% do PIB. A aplicao de todas estas alteraes metodolgicas para anos anteriores a 2001, nos termos que vierem a ser definidos pelo Eurostat, caber ao INE como autoridade estatstica responsvel pelas contas definitivas das Administraes Pblicas. 6. Pondo de lado as alteraes metodolgicas referenciadas, a disponibilizao de nova informao conduziu a que a Direco Geral do Oramento procedesse a nova estimativa da execuo oramental em 2001. Nesse contexto, decidiu-se continuar os trabalhos da Comisso at se dispor das contas finais de Fundos e Servios Autnomos, da Administrao Regional e Local, e da Segurana Social e da prpria Administrao Fiscal. Este objectivo, alm do ponto j indicado sobre a distribuio das despesas de anos findos, explica que os trabalhos da Comisso s agora se tivessem podido concluir, dentro, porm, do calendrio previsto. Pretendeu-se assegurar que, tanto quanto possvel, os valores apurados pela Comisso j no fossem susceptveis de revises com base em nova informao at ao envio de dados ao Eurostat no final de Agosto no contexto do prximo Procedimento de Dfices Excessivos. Nesta perspectiva, importa sublinhar que os ltimos nmeros relativos s receitas de impostos s ficaram concludos em 15 de Julho. Alguns Fundos e Servios Autnomos que por lei s tm de entregar contas definitivas em 15 de Maio, s mais tarde o vieram a fazer. As contas finais do SNS foram disponibilizadas no princpio de Julho e as da Segurana Social a 17 deste ms. 7. O Quadro seguinte resume as correces ao dfice que resultaram do trabalho da Comisso: A reviso da estimativa da execuo oramental atinge uma valor elevado (0,7%) que nunca se tinha verificado em anos anteriores, revelando problemas de precariedade de informao e de controle oramental que se torna necessrio corrigir. Sobre este e outros problemas a Comisso entendeu fazer um conjunto de 5 Recomendaes que procuram extrair dos problemas analisados concluses teis para o futuro. 8. Para uma completa compreenso dos factores que conduziram ao elevado dfice de 2001, importa tambm comparar a evoluo de receitas e despesas relativamente ao oramento inicial que previa um dfice de apenas 1,1 % do PIB. Admitindo, para efeitos de anlise, o pior dos cenrios para o dfice de 2001, as estimativas realizadas pela Comisso permitem construir o seguinte quadro comparativo: Como se pode verificar, o agravamento do dfice em relao ao oramento inicial resultou sobretudo de uma quebra de receitas (-2,8%) que, para alm da correco metodolgica referida, se pode atribuir  desacelerao econmica e a algumas medidas de alterao fiscal adoptadas para 2001. As despesas totais apenas aumentaram 0,2% do PIB em relao ao oramento inicial, embora com uma substancial alterao de composio. No entanto, qualquer que tenha sido a sua origem, o aumento do dfice no ano passado significa que a poltica oramental foi expansionista, tendo provocado um aumento do dfice primrio ajustado ao ciclo. O elevado dfice atingido tem tambm a gravidade de no respeitar o Pacto de Estabilidade ao exceder o limite de 3%. Para evitar as consequncias mais graves associadas a uma eventual declarao de dfice excessivo por parte do Conselho da Unio Europeia,  essencial corrigir a situao j este ano. Vrios dos factores identificados como responsveis do agravamento do dfice, indicam que 2001 foi um ano muito particular que no se repetir facilmente. A correco desejada parece, assim, possvel, sobretudo depois das medidas j adoptadas pelo Governo e tendo em conta a execuo oramental at este momento. O pas iniciou agora um exigente perodo de ajustamento que tem de ser colectivamente assumido. Os objectivos definidos no contexto do Pacto de Estabilidade impem que o dfice se reduza significativamente em 2003 e 2004 num esforo de consolidao oramental que todos os responsveis tm o dever de apoiar para que Portugal respeite os seus compromissos e, acima de tudo, construa as bases de uma poltica oramental correctamente anti-cclica como  essencial para um pas membro de uma Unio Monetria. Lisboa, 23 de Julho de 2002 Vtor Constncio Governador do Banco de Portugal

Title: Statement by the Governor at the Joint Annual Discussion - IMF/WB
text: Statement by the Governor at the Joint Annual Discussion - IMF/WB 29 Sep. 2002 Mr. Chairman, Ladies and Gentlemen, I begin by welcoming Timor-Leste as a new member of our Institutions. Over the years Portugal has supported the emergence of Timor-Leste as an independent and democratic nation and we will continue to support its future development. The world economy is going through an hesitant recovery that is still being threatened by several additional risks. Nevertheless, it should be pointed out that, in view of last year shocks and the correction of equity prices, the world economy has shown considerable flexibility and resilience. This has been particularly true so far of the financial sector. The overall performance benefited from the proper response of macroeconomic policies. In Europe, both monetary and fiscal policies have been used to help stabilize the situation. Interest rates have been reduced since last year and stay now at historically low levels in real terms. Fiscal policy has also played its role by allowing automatic stabilizers to operate. Monetary and fiscal policies are therefore not restrictive and stand ready to help economic agents to overcome the effects of a post-bubble economic environment. In the European Union, several countries allowed the fiscal position to deteriorate beyond what was foreseen in the context of the Stability and Growth Pact. My own country breached the 3% limit to the budget deficit. More recently, the date foreseen for several countries to achieve a budgetary position close to balance was postponed to 2006. These developments, regretful as one may consider them, do not put into question the basic objectives of the Stability and Growth Pact. Countries that do not respect the 3% limit to the deficit have to quickly correct the situation. The Portuguese Government is committed to do so and is applying difficult measures required to reduce the deficit which only proves that the Pact is working. The extension of the timetable to 2006, in order to avoid an excessively pro-cyclical stance of fiscal policy, was accompanied by the adoption of targeted annual deficit reductions that ensure the credible maintenance of the final objective of balanced budgets.
