Title: Governor's Interview - Public, Renaissance Radio, A Dois
text: Governor's Interview,... Interview of the Governor -Public, Radio Renaissance, The Two 19 jan. 2004 January 19, 2004 What's it going to be like in 2004? From an economic point of view it will be better than the last two years. We come from a period when we had until a recession, with a one percent drop in product, and in 2004 we're going to have some growth. It is a moderate recovery that is accompanied, in essence, by the moderate recovery of the European economy, but it is in any case the reversal of a cycle, which will have greater expression in 2005. In 2004 the economy will grow again and the Portuguese will consume more. But with these meagre 0.75 percent in 2004 and 1.75 percent in 2005, how do we can be optimistic? One can be optimistic if we look at the stage in which the economy is today. This was a period of inevitable adjustment after many years of strong growth, of strong expansion of household and business expenditure, associated with a growth in indebtedness, and 19-01-2004 this period had to be interrupted. We had to go through a phase of containment and adjustment. That is what has happened and now we are getting out of this phase, so the reversal is in itself positive. On the other hand, if we exclude from the evolution of the economy the variables that depend directly on the State Budget - consumption and public investment - which will have negative developments in 2004, we will see that we will essentially have a growth in productive, private economic activity of about 1.5 in 2004 and almost three percent in 2005. These figures reflect the fact that Portuguese companies have installed capacity and can take advantage of the dynamism of the European economy that will pull the Portuguese economy. For most people salaries are the essential part of their income and yet a drop in real wages is expected in 2004, but Banco de Portugal expects a increase in household disposable income. How is that possible? In 2004 disposable income fell, but for this year we anticipate positive growth because this income not only depends on wage developments, it also depends on state transfers, and these transfers have been increasing significantly. With growth rates predicted, all indications are that unemployment will continue to rise. That's something that doesn't leave anyone too quiet. Of course you won't. That is the most negative aspect and that is why the current situation is not a good situation. I never said otherwise. What I stressed was the need to look at this reversal of the cycle with some optimism. It is important to say that nothing has happened about our ability to converge with Europe now or in the future... But let's diverge... We will diverge this year and next, but that does not mean that we will not return to a path of convergence because the potential growth of the Portuguese economy has not suddenly gone to just one percent. We'il be three years late. For three essential reasons. First, because we live in what I call the prodigious decade of the Portuguese economy - which unfortunately will not be repeated again or has historical precedent - during which time, with the fall in interest rates, the Portuguese had an exceptional improvement in the standard of living. This period was accompanied by indebtedness of households and companies, but a rational indebtedness, because with interest rates so low people became solvent to buy certain goods... Is there no risk today that interest rates will rise again? It is clear that interest rates will not remain forever at current levels 19-01-2004. With the recovery of the European economy there may be an increase and so I have said that households and banks must be prudent. Moreover, we have made it mandatory for banks to provide people with a simulation of the charges they would incur if interest rates were two points above current levels, to see what this would mean in terms of effort for households. It's a precautionary measure. But the truth is that today the financial burden snares of our higher indebtedness are similar to those that households had in the early 1990s, when their debt was only 20 percent of disposable income. This debt expansion could not continue at the same pace. It was impossible and so we always had to go through a period of slowdown, a break, which was compounded by two factors: the global slowdown after 2001 and a very serious budgetary problem. We must also reduce the budget deficit and this weighs negatively on our ability to grow again faster, as I have already said. For civil servants, with the current proposal for wage increases, there will be no certainly resumes. Could the government have made a different proposal? Since the adoption of the Budget we knew that the funds provided were these and would not give for more. It is two years, 2003 and 2004, in which there will be a strong restraint of the salaries of civil servants which, I think, will not be able to continue in the following years. But was it necessary or not? This restraint has become inevitable, not least because in the last 12 years the salaries of civil servants have grown more than the average salary in the economy as a whole. We may consider these two years as a correction to what these previous increases were. But as such restraint will be difficult to maintain from 2005 on, this poses problems with the continued reduction of the public deficit. It has argued that it is necessary to change the payment rules in the not least because it is not enough to contain wage increases. What changes? In order to be able to contain the growth of the wage bill in the public administration, there must be an automatic and gradual reduction in staff. There are a lot of people who retire every year, if they're not all replaced... Wouldn't redundancies also be necessary? Redundancies are not possible and are not foreseen. If the State is reduced to hiring only a part of the people it loses because of reform, will it be able to hire new people, with another capacity, another formation, another mentality, which you need to better serve the country? If there are admissions, it is clear that they should be of people with a more modern background and attitude, and this will ensure a renewal of the pictures, it is certainly slow. Even so, fiscal consolidation is very difficult when we look at the coming years. Why? Because economic growth will be moderate and therefore will not generate a recovery in tax revenues that relieves pressure on state accounts. Then because it will not be possible to continue to contain wages. And finally because there will be no availability for new extraordinary, legitimate but not repeatable measures, such as those we have had. This means that we are facing several years of difficulties in consolidating public accounts, which requires spending-side measures and revenue-side measures. Why is this fiscal consolidation so important? For many Portuguese it appears only as a way for us to fasten our belts... There are several reasons. First, we have a very unbalanced situation, especially if we do not count on the extraordinary measures... Do we reduce the deficit just because we have a commitment to Europe? We have this commitment, which remains despite the problems with the Stability Pact. In a monetary union there is an absolute need for budgetary discipline rules, because elsea a country could have an overly expansionary policy and there needs to be coherence when we have a single monetary policy and twelve budgetary policies. When the Stability Pact was discussed, it was very critical, he even called it the " instability." Why do you now consider him so important? I have always said that it is essential to have rules of budgetary discipline in a monetary union. Rules can be discussed from the perspective of Europe, but from the moment they exist, a country like Portugal has to comply with them. A small, vulnerable country with a large budgetary imbalance has to make a special effort, especially since the Pact is not over. The big countries, France and Germany, will reduce their deficits and in 2005 will be within the limits set out in the Treaty, so if at that time a country like Portugal is not complying will certainly suffer consequences on the financial markets. If we're careless, we may have to pay a little higher interest rates. But there are more reasons to abide by the rules. One of them is that we have to prepare the Budget to cope with future burdens of an ageing population. Spending on health and pensions will increase. He has argued that we should have a more open immigration policy. How is that compatible with unemployment to be increased at least until 2005? They're two distinct things in time. One thing is the conjuncture situation, another the structural needs of the country. He criticized "the difficulties that manifest themselves in welcoming more immigrants". What is it that Did you mean by this sentence? The difficulties are the derived from a survey, conducted in several European countries, which revealed, to my surprise, that Portugal was the country where the rejection of immigrants was the largest. It was a surprise to me. Now thinking about our structural problems - ours and Europeans - one of the problems that arises for the future, when we look at the potential growth of Europe and Portugal, is that this potential growth is affected by demographics, population growth. A big difference between Europe and the United States is that while they have a population growing one percent a year, Europe has a declining population. In the 1990s the United States grew at a rate one percent above the European pace, but if you consider the growth rate per inhabitant, it was almost equal. This means that the potential growth rate of an economy depends heavily on job supply, demographic growth. What is in Europe is a declining population that does not guarantee the long-term progression of labour supply. If we do not solve this problem, we will have lower growth rates and less chance of addressing the consequences of an ageing population. This implies the willingness of European countries to accept more immigrants, means that Europeans have to work more years than today and also implies an increase in birth rate. The three things will be necessary if we want Europe not to go into decline and have increasing difficulties in solving its social problems. The truth is that the trend has been to decrease the number of years that work and the number of children per couple. What can one do to reverse this trend? There are public policies... Policies like the one now announced in the U.S. to promote birth? I do not know the details of this new policy, but I would remind you that in Europe there are well-achieved public policies in countries as different as France or Sweden. Is the left prepared to defend these kinds of policies? I do not answer that question which is not in my domain. It is necessary to react and, at the moment, in Europe, several countries are discussing proposals to extend the number of years of work: Germany, Italy, France. The spectacular increase in people's life expectancy means that attitudes towards work have to keep up with this change. Things are not static, so if Europe wants to defend its culture, its civilisation, and wants to have the economic means to do so by maintaining its social model, it is necessary to ensure stronger economic growth in the future, which requires structural measures. Measures such as the revision of the retiring regime for civil servants go within the correct sense? Is that enough? I do not know if they are enough, but it is clear that it stems from what I said that we cannot encourage an early retirement policy. Banco de Portugal predicts that, in order to meet the targets that are proposed, the Government will have further cut in spending and investment. There is no divergence here with the message from Jorge Sampaio to the Assembly of the Republic, which, advocating the consolidation of budget, also advocates more public investment and more transfers? It proposes the President the "squaring of the circle"? You're going to have to ask the president. I'm not going to comment on your message. I would like to point out that it was a year after Jorge Sampaio contributed to a resolution adopted in the House in which the main parties committed themselves to deficit reduction and compliance with our European commitments. In essence it has made an appeal in this regard. That is the reading I am reading: the President has called for a renewal of consensus on these objectives. But such objectives are achievable without less State, better State and fiscal consolidation? I can't and shouldn't be in this debate. You've argued that there should be fewer civil servants... In the introduction I wrote for the Bank's last economic bulletin I made a distinction between what are the current needs of reducing the deficit - and there are 36 different ways of doing so - and what is the most fundamental, more fundamental debate about the desirable dimension of the State. This debate is a political debate in which neither the Bank nor I enter. What is written about economic matters always has debatable political consequences, but the perspective in which the Bank and its Governor intervene must be as neutral as possible. So the recommendations I have made have only to do with the short-term problems that we are facing. For example, if we want to reduce the budget deficit, we have to act on revenue and expenditure, and so I have spoken against reducing THE IRC. Not that I think that this reduction should or should not happen, but because in the short term, in technical terms, it is estimated that in 2005 this decrease represents a loss of revenue of 0.4 percent of GDP, which is significant. In the face of the current horizon, we hardly have room for manoeuvre to lower taxes in the immediate future. And may it be necessary to raise taxes? I don't know, i don't know I do not have complete control of the budgetary data to be able to respond. It's not even my job. The duty of a central bank is to draw attention to the needs of macroeconomic policy, not to rule on taxes that should rise or fall. If I spoke about the IRC it was only to stress that I believe that there is no room for tax to go down, this or any other. Whether there should be more or less state is a debate that is in the area of politics, where at the moment I am not at all. He considered that there is some success in containing expenditure but also said that further to ensure genuine fiscal consolidation. In his perspective, to what extent has the effort of these two years already secured some fiscal consolidation? Without extraordinary revenues, the 2003 deficit would be greater than than the one in 2001... The point is that in the meantime the economy has gone through a recession and this has had the consequence that the state has collected less taxes. The extraordinary measures have the advantage of offsetting the loss of revenue associated with this recession. When the economy recovers, revenues will rise... Taking the effect of the economic cycle and extraordinary revenues, what remains? Is there budgetary restraint or not? There is, of course, and when I mentioned the restraint in expenditure that is what I was referring to. This restraint has set a lower level for current public spending that will have effects in the future. Even if from 2005 onto wage growth closer to normal, it will be from a lower level, so there has been fiscal consolidation in this area. Aren't you afraid of the next election cycles? Do not fear that there will be the temptation to open the purse strings? I hope that will not happen, not least because we have a more demanding European framework. I would like to stress again: we need to have a balanced budget for the reasons I have already mentioned, but also to be able to cope better with fluctuations in the economy, which has not happened in recent years, and because we must be aware that we cannot have budget deficits that undermine the future growth of the economy and wealth. There are four reasons for weight - European rules, an ageing population, the ability to react to economic cycles and to have healthier growth - on which we must reflect. Just think that if we had a more balanced budget, in the recession situation we are in, politics should have been more expansionary. But since we didn't... After the decisions of finance ministers on france's excessive deficits and germany, the Stability Pact is dead? The Pact is not dead, which was difficult to approve and impose the fines he provided for. That part will be affected by what happened in November, but the rest is not gone. The very resolution that ministers adopted, which was different from that of the Commission, reaffirms the objectives of the Pact and that the countries that are now in excess will be again within the rules of the Treaty in 2005. So the Commission was wrong to take the matter to court? What Commissioner Solbes explained was that the decision to go to court had to do with matters of procedure that are very important. It is a question of whether, if there is a regulation for which the Commission is responsible, at any time a Council of Ministers may adopt resolutions not based on Commission proposals. And this is a point of procedure which has to do with the existence or of a Community method in european operation, or its replacement by an intergovernmental method. This question of procedure refers to a very important one, the question of whether we are evolving into a "directory" solution in which countries such as France and Germany end up taking its lead even against the Commission's view... We are not moving in that direction because there has been no change in the treaties. Wouldn't there be with the proposed Constitution? No, there wouldn't be. It was foreseen there that the Commission kept the exclusive of the legislative initiative, so that the Commission's role in this matter would not be touched. As is the constitution proposal, did you vote yes? Without any hesitation. And i do not understand some of the speakers in the debate since, if we think about Portugal's interests, we would see that they would be enormously affected if we had an opinion that would put us outside the European consensus. What is the great danger that is now hanging over the world economy? There are still some doubts about the sustainability of the recovery. It is happening, the European Commission has just reviewed its estimates for the fourth quarter on the rise, but consumers are still heavily indebted, companies still need further restructuring and there is a situation of major imbalance in the American economy, fiscal imbalance and balance of payments. This can put great pressure on exchange rates and require measures to reduce these deficits that affect economic growth. Caixa Geral de Depositos's attempt to strengthen its position in Spain was important? This is another matter on which Banco de Portugal does not have to comment. The Bank only had to make sure, and did so, that if caixa wanted to expand it had the capital needed to do so. That would require a capital boost. From there it was a business decision that was up to management and the shareholder. Isn't it important for Portuguese companies to expand abroad? Yes, but I never shared any excessive enthusiasm at one point. And I explain: it is clear that Portuguese companies that have competence, know-how and available capital should seek to expand where this is economically profitable, which sometimes implies internationalization. This has happened with several important Portuguese companies and it is good, for example, portuguese companies to be operating and investing in the countries that will join the European Union and there are no companies from these countries operating in Portugal, which is a sign that enlargement is also an opportunity for us. From the point of view of companies, internationalisation is justified in some cases what is not justified is that there is public support for such internationalisation. It doesn't worry foreign companies to buy Portuguese companies, banks foreigners to buy Portuguese banks? It is generally desirable that important companies be owned by Portuguese, even for reasons of national cohesion, but this has limits. It has the limits that stem from international commitments, because we are in an integrated European market, and those that stem from economic efficiency. We should not defend situations that are not the best in terms of efficiency if others are able to come here and do better. Foreigners operating in Portugal also contribute to the growth of our economy. This year Banco de Portugal imposed a very heavy sanction on an old Governor, also deputy and psd spokesman for economic issues, Dr. Tavares Moreira, apparently accusing him of damaging management in an institution Bank. As such a penalty may also affect national self-esteem and has it already appealed, was it not justified for the Bank to explain it better? I'm not going to talk about it. This process has its guarantees of secrecy and the Bank has not given any news about this case. This isn't where I'm going to do it. There's a feature... But is there no duty to inform depositors and shareholders? They were informed and their situation was completely safeguarded. The fundamental concern of banking supervision is to ensure the interests of banks' customers, to ensure that they have no losses, and this has happened in the case under review. Everything was handled so that no depositor sandant or no client would be harmed.
text_original: Entrevista do Governador -Pblico,... Entrevista do Governador -Pblico, Rdio Renascena, A Dois 19 jan. 2004 19 de Janeiro de 2004 Como  que vai ser 2004? Do ponto de vista econmico vai ser melhor do que os ltimos dois anos. Vimos de um perodo em que tivemos at uma recesso, com uma queda do produto de um por cento, e em 2004 vamos ter algum crescimento.  uma retoma moderada que acompanha, no fundo, a recuperao tambm moderada da economia europeia, mas  em todo o caso a inverso de um ciclo, o que ter maior expresso em 2005. Em 2004 a economia vai voltar a crescer e os portugueses vo consumir mais. Mas com estes escassos 0,75 por cento em 2004 e 1,75 por cento em 2005, como  que se pode ser optimista? Pode-se ser optimista se olharmos para a fase em que hoje se encontra a economia. Este foi um perodo de inevitvel ajustamento aps muitos anos de forte crescimento, de forte expanso das despesas das famlias e empresas, associada a um crescimento do endividamento, e 19-01-2004 esse perodo tinha de interromper-se. Tnhamos de passar por uma fase de conteno e ajustamento.  isso que tem ocorrido e agora estamos a sair dessa fase, pelo que a inverso  em si mesma positiva. Por outro lado, se excluirmos da evoluo da economia as variveis que dependem directamente do Oramento de Estado -o consumo e o investimento pblico -, que tero evoluo negativa em 2004, veremos que teremos essencialmente um crescimento da actividade econmica produtiva, privada, de cerca de 1,5 em 2004 e quase trs por cento em 2005. Estes nmeros reflectem o facto de as empresas portuguesas terem capacidade instalada e poderem aproveitar o dinamismo da economia europeia que puxar pela economia portuguesa. Para a maioria das pessoas os salrios so a parte essencial do seu rendimento e ainda se antev para 2004 uma quebra dos salrios reais, mas o Banco de Portugal prev um aumento do rendimento disponvel das famlias. Como  isso possvel? Em 2004 o rendimento disponvel caiu, mas para este ano prevemos um crescimento positivo porque esse rendimento no depende apenas da evoluo dos salrios, depende tambm das transferncias do Estado, e essas transferncias tm vindo a aumentar de forma significativa. Com as taxas de crescimento previstas, tudo indica que o desemprego continuar a subir. Isso  algo que no deixa ningum muito sossegado. Claro que no deixa. Esse  o aspecto mais negativo e  por isso que actual situao no  uma boa situao. Nunca disse o contrrio. Aquilo que sublinhei foi a necessidade de olhar para esta inverso do ciclo com algum optimismo.  importante dizer que nada aconteceu quanto  nossa capacidade de convergir com a Europa agora ou no futuro... Mas vamos divergir... Vamos divergir este ano e no prximo, mas isso no significa que no voltemos a um caminho de convergncia porque o crescimento potencial da economia portuguesa no passou de sbito para apenas um por cento. Teremos trs anos de atraso... Por trs razes essenciais. Primeiro, porque vivemos aquilo a que chamo a dcada prodigiosa da economia portuguesa -que infelizmente no se voltar a repetir nem tem precedente histrico -, perodo durante o qual, com a queda das taxas de juro, os portugueses tiveram uma excepcional melhoria do nvel de vida. Esse perodo foi acompanhado de um endividamento das famlias e das empresas, mas um endividamento racional, porque com as taxas de juro to baixas as pessoas passaram a ser solventes para comprarem certos bens... No h hoje nenhum risco de as taxas de juro voltarem a aumentar?  evidente que as taxas de juro no ficaro para sempre nos nveis 19-01-2004 actuais. Com a recuperao da economia europeia poder haver um aumento e por isso tenho dito que as famlias e os bancos tm de ser prudentes. Mais: tornmos obrigatrio que os bancos apresentem s pessoas uma simulao dos encargos que contrairiam caso as taxas de juro estivessem dois pontos acima dos nveis actuais, para se ver o que isso representaria em termos de esforo para as famlias.  uma medida de cautela. Mas a verdade  que hoje os encargos financeiros do nosso maior endividamento so semelhantes aos que as famlias tinham no incio dos anos 90, quando a sua dvida era apenas 20 por cento do rendimento disponvel. Esta expanso da dvida no podia continuar ao mesmo ritmo. Era impossvel e por isso tnhamos sempre de passar por um perodo de desacelerao, de quebra, o que foi agravado por dois factores: a desacelerao a nvel mundial aps 2001 e um problema oramental muito srio. Temos tambm de reduzir o dfice do oramento e isso pesa negativamente na nossa capacidade de voltar a crescer mais depressa, como j referi. Para os funcionrios pblicos, com a actual proposta de aumentos salariais, no haver certamente retoma. O Governo poderia ter feito uma proposta diferente? Desde a aprovao do Oramento que sabamos que as verbas previstas eram estas e no dariam para mais. So dois anos, 2003 e 2004, em que haver uma conteno forte dos vencimentos dos funcionrios pblicos que, penso, no poder manter-se nos anos seguintes. Mas era ou no necessria? Essa conteno tornou-se inevitvel, at porque nos ltimos 12 anos os vencimentos dos funcionrios pblicos cresceram mais do que a mdia dos vencimentos na economia em geral. Poderemos considerar estes dois anos como uma correco do que foram esses aumentos anteriores. Mas como tal conteno ser difcil de manter a partir de 2005, isso pe problemas  continuao da reduo do dfice pblico. Tem defendido que  necessrio alterar as regras de pagamento na administrao pblica, at porque no basta conter os aumentos salariais. Que alteraes? Para conseguir conter o crescimento da massa salarial na administrao pblica  necessrio que haja, de forma automtica e gradual, uma reduo de efectivos. H muita gente que se reforma todos os anos, se no forem todos substitudos... No seriam necessrios tambm despedimentos? Os despedimentos no so possveis nem esto previstos. Se o Estado fica reduzido a contratar apenas uma parte das pessoas que perde por se reformarem, ser que consegue contratar as pessoas novas, com outra capacidade, outra formao, outra mentalidade, que lhe fazem falta para servir melhor o pas? Havendo admisses,  evidente que devero ser de pessoas com uma formao e uma atitude mais moderna, e isso assegurar uma renovao dos quadros,  certo que lenta. Mesmo assim a consolidao oramental  muito difcil quando olhamos para os prximos anos. Porqu? Porque o crescimento econmico ser moderado e, por isso, no gerar uma recuperao de receitas fiscais que alivie a presso sobre as contas do Estado. Depois, porque no ser possvel continuar a conter os salrios. E finalmente porque no haver disponibilidade para novas medidas extraordinrias, legtimas mas no repetveis, como as que temos tido. Isto significa que estamos perante vrios anos de dificuldades para consolidar as contas pblicas, o que exige medidas do lado da despesa e medidas do lado das receitas. Porque  to importante essa consolidao oramental? Para muitos portugueses ela surge apenas como uma forma de apertarmos o cinto... H vrias razes. Primeiro, temos uma situao muito desequilibrada, sobretudo se no contarmos com as medidas extraordinrias... Reduzimos o dfice apenas porque temos um compromisso com a Europa? Temos esse compromisso, que se mantm apesar dos problemas com o Pacto de Estabilidade. Numa unio monetria h a necessidade absoluta de haver regras de disciplina oramental, porque seno um pas podia ter uma poltica demasiado expansionista e  necessrio haver coerncia quando temos uma s poltica monetria e doze polticas oramentais. Quando se discutiu o Pacto de Estabilidade foi muito crtico, chamou-lhe at "pacto de instabilidade". Porque  que agora o considera to importante? Sempre disse que  essencial haver regras de disciplina oramental numa unio monetria. Podem-se discutir as regras na perspectiva da Europa, mas a partir do momento que existem, um pas como Portugal tem que as cumprir. Um pas pequeno, vulnervel e com um desequilbrio oramental grande tem de fazer um esforo especial, tanto mais que o Pacto no acabou. Os pases grandes, a Frana e a Alemanha, iro reduzir os seus dfices e em 2005 estaro dentro dos limites definidos no Tratado, pelo que se nessa altura um pas como Portugal no estiver a cumprir sofrer certamente consequncias nos mercados financeiros. Se nos descuidarmos poderemos ter de vir a pagar taxas de juro um pouco mais altas. Mas h mais razes para cumprirmos as regras. Uma delas  que temos de preparar o Oramento para fazermos face a encargos futuros decorrentes do envelhecimento da populao. As despesas com a sade e com as penses de reforma vo aumentar. Tem defendido que devemos ter uma poltica de imigrao mais aberta. Como  isso compatvel com o desemprego a aumentar pelo menos at 2005? So duas coisas distintas no tempo. Uma coisa  a situao conjuntural, outra as necessidades estruturais do pas. Criticou "as dificuldades que se manifestam em acolher mais imigrantes". O que  que queria dizer com esta frase? As dificuldades so as derivadas de uma sondagem, feita em vrios pases europeus, que revelou, para minha surpresa, que Portugal era o pas onde era maior a rejeio  entrada de imigrantes. Para mim foi uma surpresa. Ora pensando nos nossos problemas estruturais -nossos e europeus -, um dos problemas que se coloca para o futuro, quando olhamos para o crescimento potencial da Europa e de Portugal,  que esse crescimento potencial  afectado pela demografia, pelo crescimento da populao. Uma diferena grande entre a Europa e os Estados Unidos  que enquanto estes tm uma populao a crescer um por cento ao ano, a Europa est com uma populao declinante. Na dcada de 90 os Estados Unidos cresceram a um ritmo um por cento acima do ritmo europeu, mas se considerarmos a taxa de crescimento por habitante, foi quase igual. Isto quer dizer que a taxa de crescimento potencial de uma economia depende muito da oferta de trabalho, do crescimento demogrfico. O que h na Europa  uma populao em declnio que no garante a progresso a prazo da oferta de trabalho. Se no resolvermos este problema teremos menores taxas de crescimento e menores possibilidades de fazer face s consequncias do envelhecimento da populao. Isto implica disponibilidade dos pases europeus para aceitarem mais imigrantes, implica que os europeus tenham de trabalhar mais anos do que hoje e supe tambm um aumento da natalidade. As trs coisas vo ser necessrias se quisermos que a Europa no entre em declnio e tenha dificuldades crescentes para resolver os seus problemas sociais. A verdade  que a tendncia tem sido para diminuir o nmero de anos que se trabalha e o nmero de filhos por casal. O que  que se pode fazer para inverter essa tendncia? H polticas pblicas... Polticas como a agora anunciada nos EUA para promover a natalidade? No conheo os pormenores dessa nova poltica, mas recordo que na Europa h polticas pblicas bem conseguidas em pases to diferentes como a Frana ou a Sucia. A esquerda est preparada para defender esse tipo de polticas? No respondo a essa questo que no  do meu domnio.  necessrio  reagir e, neste momento, na Europa, vrios pases discutem propostas no sentido de estender o nmero de anos de trabalho: a Alemanha, a Itlia, a Frana. O aumento espectacular da esperana de vida das pessoas faz com que as atitudes perante o trabalho tenham que acompanhar essa mudana. As coisas no ficam estticas, pelo que se a Europa quer defender a sua cultura, a sua civilizao, e quer ter os meios econmicos para o fazer mantendo o seu modelo social,  necessrio garantir um crescimento econmico mais forte no futuro, o que exige medidas estruturais. Medidas como a reviso do regime de aposentao dos funcionrios pblicos vo no sentido correcto? So suficientes? No sei se so suficientes, mas  evidente que decorre do que eu disse que no podemos encorajar uma poltica de reformas antecipadas. O Banco de Portugal prev que, para cumprir as metas que se prope, o Governo vai ter de cortar ainda mais na despesa e no investimento. No h aqui uma divergncia com a mensagem de Jorge Sampaio  Assembleia da Repblica que, defendendo a consolidao oramental, tambm defende mais investimento pblico e mais transferncias? Prope o Presidente a "quadratura do crculo"? Tero de perguntar ao Presidente. No vou comentar a sua mensagem. Assinalo que foi feita um ano depois de Jorge Sampaio ter contribudo para uma resoluo, aprovada na Assembleia, em que os principais partidos se comprometeram com objectivos de reduo do dfice e de cumprimento dos nossos compromissos europeus. No essencial fez um apelo nesse sentido.  essa a leitura que fao: o Presidente apelou a uma renovao do consenso em torno desses objectivos. Mas tais objectivos so realizveis sem haver menos Estado, melhor Estado e consolidao oramental? No posso nem devo entrar nesse debate. J defendeu que devia haver menos funcionrios pblicos... Na introduo que escrevi para o ltimo boletim econmico do Banco fiz uma distino entre o que so as necessidades actuais de reduzirmos o dfice -e no h 36 maneiras diferentes de o fazer -e o que  o debate mais estrutural, mais de fundo, sobre a dimenso desejvel do Estado. Esse debate  um debate poltico no qual nem o Banco, nem eu entramos. O que se escreve sobre matria econmica tem sempre consequncias polticas discutveis, mas a perspectiva em que o Banco e o seu Governador intervm deve ser a mais neutra possvel. Por isso, as recomendaes que tenho feito tm exclusivamente a ver com os problemas de curto prazo com que estamos confrontados. Por exemplo: se se quer reduzir o dfice oramental tem de se actuar nas receitas e nas despesas e, por isso, falei contra a reduo do IRC. No que pense que essa reduo deva ou no acontecer, mas porque no curto prazo, em termos tcnicos, se calcula que em 2005 essa descida represente uma perda de receita de 0,4 por cento do PIB, o que  significativo. Perante o actual horizonte dificilmente temos margem de manobra para, no futuro imediato, descer impostos. E poder ser necessrio subir impostos? No sei. No tenho o domnio completo dos dados oramentais para poder responder. Nem me compete. O dever de um banco central  chamar a ateno para as necessidades da poltica macroeconmica, no pronunciar-se sobre os impostos que devem subir ou descer. Se me pronunciei sobre o IRC foi apenas para sublinhar que considero que no h margem para descer impostos, este ou outro qualquer. Saber se deve haver mais ou menos Estado  um debate que se situa na rea da poltica, onde neste momento no estou de maneira nenhuma. Considerou que existe algum sucesso na conteno das despesas mas tambm disse que  necessrio ir mais longe para garantir uma verdadeira consolidao oramental. Na sua perspectiva, at que ponto  que o esforo destes dois anos j garantiu alguma consolidao oramental? Sem receitas extraordinrias, o dfice de 2003 seria maior do que o de 2001... O ponto  que entretanto a economia atravessou uma recesso e isso teve como consequncia que o Estado cobrou menos impostos. As medidas extraordinrias tm a vantagem de compensarem a perda de receitas associada a essa recesso. Quando a economia recuperar, as receitas vo subir... Descontando o efeito do ciclo econmico e das receitas extraordinrias, o que  que fica? H ou no conteno oramental? H, claro que h, e quando referi a conteno nas despesas era a isso que me referia. Essa conteno definiu um patamar mais baixo para a despesa pblica corrente que ter efeitos no futuro. Mesmo que a partir de 2005 haja um crescimento salarial mais perto do normal, far-se- a partir de um patamar inferior, pelo que houve nesse domnio consolidao oramental. No receia os prximos ciclos eleitorais? No teme que haja a tentao de abrir os cordes  bolsa? Espero que isso no acontea, at porque temos um enquadramento europeu mais exigente. Volto a insistir: necessitamos de ter um oramento equilibrado pelas razes que j referi mas tambm para podermos enfrentar melhor as flutuaes da economia, coisa que no tem acontecido neste anos, e porque temos de ter a conscincia de que no podemos ter dfices oramentais que comprometam o crescimento futuro da economia e da riqueza. So quatro razes de peso -regras europeias, envelhecimento da populao, capacidade de reagir aos ciclos econmicos e de ter um crescimento mais saudvel -sobre as quais devemos reflectir. Basta pensar que se tivssemos um oramento mais equilibrado, na situao de recesso em que nos encontramos, a poltica devia ter sido mais expansionista. Mas como no tnhamos... Depois das decises dos ministros das Finanas sobre os dfices excessivos da Frana e da Alemanha, o Pacto de Estabilidade est morto? O Pacto no est morto, o que era difcil era aprovar e aplicar as multas que ele previa. Essa parte estar afectada pelo que aconteceu em Novembro, mas o resto no desapareceu. A prpria resoluo que os ministros aprovaram, que era diferente da da Comisso, reafirma os objectivos do Pacto e que os pases que agora esto em excesso estaro, em 2005, de novo dentro das regras do Tratado. Ento a Comisso fez mal em levar o assunto para tribunal? O que o comissrio Solbes explicou foi que a deciso de ir para tribunal teve a ver com questes de procedimento que so muito importantes. Trata-se de saber se, havendo um regulamento pelo qual a Comisso  responsvel, a qualquer momento um Conselho de Ministros pode aprovar resolues no baseadas em propostas da Comisso. E este  um ponto de procedimento que tem a ver com a existncia ou de um mtodo comunitrio no funcionamento europeu, ou pela sua substituio por um mtodo intergovernamental. Essa questo de procedimento remete para outra muito importante, a de saber se estamos a evoluir para uma soluo de "directrio" em que pases como a Frana e a Alemanha acabam por levar a sua avante mesmo contra a opinio da Comisso... No estamos a evoluir nesse sentido porque no houve qualquer mudana nos tratados. No haveria com a proposta de Constituio? No, no haveria. Estava l previsto que a Comisso conservava o exclusivo da iniciativa legislativa, pelo que o papel da Comisso nessa matria no seria tocado. Tal como est a proposta de Constituio, votava sim? Sem qualquer hesitao. E no compreendendo alguns dos intervenientes no debate j que, se pensarmos nos interesses de Portugal, veramos que eles seriam enormemente afectados se ns tivssemos uma opinio que nos colocasse fora do consenso europeu. Qual o grande perigo que paira neste momento sobre a economia mundial? H ainda algumas dvidas sobre a sustentabilidade da retoma. Ela est a acontecer, a Comisso Europeia acaba de rever as suas estimativas para o quarto trimestre em alta, mas os consumidores ainda esto muito endividados, as empresas ainda necessitam de mais reestruturao e h uma situao de grande desequilbrio na economia americana, desequilbrio oramental e na balana de pagamentos. Isso pode colocar grande presso sobre as taxas de cmbio e requerer medidas de reduo desses dfices que afectem o crescimento econmico. A tentativa da Caixa Geral de Depsitos de reforar a sua posio em Espanha era importante? Essa  outra matria sobre a qual o Banco de Portugal no tem de pronunciar-se. O Banco s tinha de garantir, e f-lo, que se a Caixa quisesse expandir-se tivesse os capitais necessrios para o fazer. Isso exigiria um reforo de capital. A partir da era uma deciso empresarial que competia  gesto e ao accionista. No  importante as empresas portuguesas expandirem-se para o exterior? Sim, mas nunca partilhei de algum entusiasmo excessivo que houve em certa altura. E explico:  evidente que as empresas portuguesas que tm competncia, know-how e capitais disponveis devem procurar expandir-se onde isso  economicamente rentvel, o que implica por vezes a internacionalizao. Isso sucedeu com vrias empresas portuguesas importantes e  bom, por exemplo, empresas portuguesas estarem a operar e a investir nos pases que vo aderir  Unio Europeia e no haver empresas desses pases a operar em Portugal, o que  um sinal de que o alargamento  tambm uma oportunidade para ns. Do ponto de vista das empresas, a internacionalizao justifica-se -nalguns casos o que no se justifica  existirem apoios pblicos a essa internacionalizao. No o preocupa empresas estrangeiras comprarem empresas portuguesas, bancos estrangeiros comprarem bancos portugueses?  desejvel em geral que as empresas importantes sejam detidas por portugueses, at por motivos de coeso nacional, mas isso tem limites. Tem os limites que decorrem de compromissos internacionais, pois estamos num mercado europeu integrado, e os que decorrem da eficincia econmica. No devemos defender situaes que no sejam as melhores em termos de eficincia se outros forem capazes de vir para c e fazer melhor. Estrangeiros a operarem em Portugal tambm contribuem para o crescimento da nossa economia. Este ano o Banco de Portugal aplicou uma sano muito pesada sobre um seu antigo Governador, tambm deputado e porta-voz do PSD para as questes econmicas, o dr. Tavares Moreira, acusando-o aparentemente de gesto danosa numa instituio bancria. Uma vez que tal penalidade tambm pode afectar a auto-estima nacional e o prprio j recorreu, no se justificava que o Banco a explicasse melhor? No vou falar sobre esse assunto. Esse processo tem as suas garantias de sigilo e o Banco no deu nenhuma notcia sobre esse caso. No  agora que o farei. H um recurso... Mas no h o dever de informar os depositantes e accionistas? Foram informados e a sua situao foi completamente salvaguardada. A preocupao fundamental da superviso bancria  garantir os interesses dos clientes dos bancos, garantir que no tenham perdas, e isso aconteceu no caso em anlise. Tudo foi tratado para que nenhum depositante nem nenhum cliente sassem lesados.

Title: Speech of the Governor at the opening of the 14th Lisbon Meeting with the PALOP and Timor-Leste delegations to the IMF/BM Annual Assembly
text: Intervention of the Governor in the abertu... Speech of the Governor at the opening of the 14th Lisbon Meeting with the PALOP and Timor-Leste delegations to the IMF/BM Annual Assembly 28 set. 2004 September 28, 2004 Ambassadors, Governors, Ladies and Gentlemen 1. I begin by thanking everyone for their presence at this 14th Meeting of Central Banks of the PALOP and East Timor. The number already reached is the happy reflection of a tradition of cooperation that has been consolidated. We actually maintain strong cooperation in many areas of central bank activity: payment systems, accounting systems, IT plans or money market development. In February of this year, we held another Meeting of Governors in Cape Verde to discuss the conduct of monetary policy in which representatives of Brazil and Macau also participated. During the year, Banco de Portugal also continued its participation in various initiatives in the context of the efforts made by the PALOP and Timor-Leste to modernize their financial systems and institutionally strengthen their Central Banks. Among these initiatives, we highlight the continuation of the process of institutional consolidation in Timor-Leste, which led to the maintenance of cooperation with the Monetary and Payments Authority of that country at a relatively high level, covering virtually all the main areas of intervention of a central bank. It is also worth noting the Bank's involvement, at the request of the IMF, in two exercises in support of the monitoring activity of that institution, with a view to increasing transparency and the adoption of universal codes and standards of good conduct. During 2005 we will continue the cooperation efforts that have been developed in the areas already mentioned, through technical missions, training courses or thematic seminars. 2. This Lisbon Meeting usually takes place on the eve of the annual meeting of the IMF and the World Bank, which means that the international economic situation will be examined at the working meeting of our delegations yesterday. The world economy has evolved very favorably in 2004. The recovery gradually expanded and was widespread in all major regions, although with different rhythms. The US, along with Asia, are the main drivers of growth. Economic expansion has been supported by the continued accommodating tassum of macroeconomic policies. The global economic situation presents some vulnerabilities and, in terms of future prospects, a slowdown in the pace of growth is expected. In recent months, as a result of the sharp rise in oil prices and geopolitical uncertainties, short-term risks have been aggravated in terms of future developments in both inflation and economic activity reflecting financial markets. On the other hand, significant vulnerabilities persist, associated with macroeconomic imbalances in the public and external sectors, in particular in the US, as well as structural weaknesses that condition sustained growth, especially in Europe. Concerns are also the way in which the markets for financial and real estate assets will react to a new cycle of more restrictive macroeconomic policies and the consequences of a possible abrupt slowdown in growth in China and Asia. Inflationary pressures, although increasing, remain relatively contained. This stems from the maintenance of significant levels of overcapacity in many countries, together with moderate wage developments in relation to productivity. From a policy point of view, progress in the credibility and independence of monetary authorities has made it possible to improve the inflationary expectations of economic operators. However, protectionist pressures and the fragility of structural fiscal positions pose medium-term risks. Moreover, as a result of the soundness of demand and the sharp rise in prices of primary goods, inflationary pressures are expected to rise somewhat. 3. After a year of severe recession, the Portuguese economy can take advantage of the international recovery to also begin an economic recovery, which will remain below the European average this year and next. In fact, developments so far confirm BP's forecast of 1.25% growth this year. However, it should be noted that the growth composition will be significantly different from that originally forecast, following the figures released for the second quarter of the year. There will be more domestic expenditure, especially private and public consumption, and a more negative contribution from the external sector as a result of an unexpected increase in imports. This contributes to substantially aggravating the external trade imbalance, also affected by a loss of terms of exchange due to rising oil prices. Households and the state are increasing their indebtedness again and the private savings rate is down slightly. Nevertheless, this development was not accompanied by the increase in indebtedness of Portuguese banks, particularly in interbank markets, a variable that has been a sharp reduction since last year. This development is explained by the growing securitisation of credits that reduces the balance sheet and financing needs of banks, the use of higher maturity securities and the increase in equity in the system. This change in the growth pattern reflects the weaknesses of domestic supply in the face of the dynamism of demand and reveals how the main problems of the Portuguese economy are structural in nature: low productivity for the levels of income achieved and loss of competitiveness of our productions from years to this part. Portugal has not yet internalized what it means to live in monetary union. From this situation has taken away the benefit of low interest rates, which have allowed the explosion of access to durable consumer goods and housing itself, developments that have undeniably represented a substantial improvement in the quality of life. However, the necessary consequences on the necessary structural adaptations or the indispensable disciplines in the field of wage costs and public finances have not been taken away from, which the new framework makes imperative to ensure the competitiveness of our productions. In particular, we continue to have a difficult budgetary problem to solve. For the deficit in 2003, 2.8% of GDP contributed decisively to several extraordinary measures which accounted for about 2.5 percentage points of GDP and without which the deficit figure would have a level of 5.3% of GDP. As I said in the presentation of our June Economic Bulletin: "Of course, the extraordinary revenue-making measures are legitimate and accepted by Eurostat for the purpose of excessive deficit reporting. In addition, they have the justification of partly replacing the revenues that temporarily caused the recession to decrease. Considering the deficit without its inclusion is, however, necessary to draw attention to the difficulties we will still face in achieving the objective of full fiscal consolidation. It is important not to feed illusions because the expected moderate economic growth, while making a significant contribution, will not be enough to automatically generate a significant recovery in tax revenues. The success achieved by containing current expenditure must therefore be continued in the coming years. In the immediate future, however, further measures will be needed on the expenditure and revenue side, in particular by achieving better results in combating tax evasion." Meanwhile, the European Commission continues to predict that Portugal will exceed a deficit of 3% this year and the Minister of Finance recently announced that, in order to avoid this, extraordinary revenues amounting to EUR 2 billion would be needed. This shows how difficult the 2005 Budget will be, given the starting point and the need to respect the 3% limit, in a year that will already see significant growth and when the existing recognition of public debt has made its ratio to GDP noticeably exceed the 60% provided for in the Treaty on Union. Last year we would have had more justification to exceed the 3% deficit, since, as I drew attention at the time, the Excessive Deficit Regulation provides for the presumption of a justified excess when a recession reaches above  0.75%. It is also clear that the intensity of the 2003 recession affects public accounts in 2004, when economic growth will also be moderate. These arguments will not be made next year, however. The situation requires, as I said, measures on the revenue side and on the expenditure side. In 2005, the decrease in revenue stemming from the reduction in the IRC rate, which I had occasion to disagree with, will account for about 0.4% of GDP. As the Minister of Finance has recently acknowledged, there is therefore no room for further tax cuts that are not properly offset in revenue or expenditure and it is necessary to combat tax evasion, including some changes to the banking secrecy regime. The necessary and effective fiscal consolidation is not yet complete and must continue in the coming years. Several commentators have conveyed in the media the idea that the proposals for revision of the Stability Pact presented by the Commission would entail the significant relaxation of its disciplinary function. This is a miseye on what is at stake. A monetary union requires, as we know, a strong budgetary rule and, as such, the proposals under discussion do not alter the Treaty or the essence of the Pact. That does not mean that these are not significant proposals. As is also known, the ECB has recommended that the review does not imply text changes in the current Regulations. However, it should be stressed that several of the Commission's proposals do not imply a change in the wording of the Regulations and may, in my opinion, be positive. In addition to the obvious and consensual proposal on the need to step up monitoring of compliance with the Pact in periods of good economic growth, I would like to stress two others: firstly, with regard to the proper interpretation of what the expression, not defined in the Regulations, means, on the objective of the medium-term budget being 'close to balance or in surplus'. The application of this principle has been somewhat confusing over time and only in March 2003 ECOFIN and the European Council clearly recognised that 'Compliance with the Stability and Growth Pact requirement on the near-equilibrium or surplus position should be assessed in cycle-adjusted terms'. I believe that a clever application of this principle of the preventive arm of the Pact should also take into account the country's specific conditions with regard, in particular, to the level of the government debt ratio and the potential growth rate. I would remind you, in order to avoid confusion, that this has nothing to do with the nominal limit of 3% contained in the Treaty itself and that it is not under review. The second point I stress is precisely the proposal to give greater importance in the supervision of the Pact to the criterion of the limit of the public debt ratio which is directly departing from the Treaty, but which has not been properly considered. The importance of this criterion is fundamental for monetary policy, since it can fulfill its mission at lower costs if there are no problems of unsustainability of public finances, of which the evolution of the level of indebtedness is a privileged indicator. The emphasis given by the Commission to this criterion is a sign that there are no important foundations of monetary union. The fact that any amendments have to be voted unanimously in the Council is also a guarantee that acts in the same direction. On the other hand, it should not be forgotten that monetary policy alone is sufficient to ensure price stability and the soundness of the currency. In the meantime, the Pact will continue to exist as a disciplinary rule and to be a reference for financial markets, so we should not take lightly the possibility of exceeding its limits. Moreover, as I have pointed out, even without the Pact, it is still in our interest to reduce the actual budget deficit, especially now that higher economic growth is announced. Indeed, this objective of consolidation is essential for us to recover for the future the anti-cyclical function of fiscal policy and to address the budgetary consequences of an ageing population. Immediately, we note that the Portuguese economy has begun to emerge from the recessionary environment that has recently passed through and that the resumption of growth will help reduce the budget deficit. On the other hand, the Bank's forecasts imply that the unemployment rate will start to decline next year and that Disposable Income will increase in real terms this year and next. We must therefore not feed exaggerated pessimism. 4. It is time to refer now to the developments of african economies and the prospects for international cooperation. Progress in macroeconomic and political stability, lower debt burdens following the HIPC initiative and better agricultural conditions, as well as rising oil production in some countries, have enabled growth in the region to increase, with further acceleration in 2005. Higher demand and rising prices of primary goods have had positive effects on trade balances in many countries. The biggest gains come naturally for oil exporting countries. But also for most oil importing countries, the gains associated with higher exports, in value, of primary goods outweigh the losses resulting from the oil bill. There is, however, a minority of countries that could suffer substantial loss of terms of trade. There are still significant risks for sub-Saharan Africa in the event of a sharp slowdown in the Chinese economy, as this has been the main driver of price hikes for non-energy primary goods. Having already seen substantial improvements in the field of macroeconomic stability, sub-Saharan Africa is now facing significant challenges in infrastructure development, and in strengthening institutions and governance, as well as in the areas of health and education. The Millennium Development Goals are still far from being achieved. As for African countries, NEPAD can make an important contribution to better governance, including the quality of public institutions, transparency, accountability and the fight against corruption. The international community also has a relevant role to play, either by reducing barriers to exports in developing countries and by committed to increasing development aid flows. Meeting the Millennium Development Goals requires additional resources and greater efficiency of available aid. The EU, in the context of the Monterrey Conference commitments, continues to increase Official Development Assistance (ODA) at a pace consistent with the 0.7% of GDP target. In addition to ODA, a number of proposals have emerged from innovative sources of additional funding, including the International Financial Facility and global tax suggestions, in particular the taxation of carbon emissions in energy production or international monetary transactions. The International Monetary and Financial Committee has put this issue of mobilising international aid on the agenda of its next meeting, following the previous call for the International Monetary Fund, in cooperation with the World Bank, to further the issue of aid effectiveness, absorption capacity and additional financing modalities for the achievement of the Millennium Development Goals. This subject is one of the themes of our Meeting this year and will be developed in the intervention of Professor Braga de Macedo, which we are pleased to have with us today. The Millennium Goals today seem difficult to achieve, but the effort and resources mobilised to meet them are, in addition to a moral requirement, the expression of self-interest well understood. The deep interdependence in which the peoples of the planet live today serve as the basis for cooperation and the imperative of higher transfers of resources that are indispensable for the correction of current imbalances. Let us think of some of the root causes of violence and terrorism. Let us think about the social displacements and potential conflicts that may emerge in the context of an intense demographic transformation that will cause developed countries, which now account for only 18% of the world's total population, and which in 1950 still represented 32%, to have a weight of only 12% in 2050, with Europe representing only 4%. The coming decades will certainly present very complex problems and the truth is that no one knows whether the greater complexity of the world system tends towards a self-organization with stability or if we are facing the spectrum of recurrent crises: financial, environmental or socio-political. It is only known that the trend towards globalization is technologically inexorable and that the inherent risks associated with it "make the utopia of a world society a little more real or, at least, more urgent" (Ulrich Beck). Navigating uncertainty and without mirrors in the future, we know, however, as Francis Bacon said, that "he who does not apply new remedies must expect new evils". Lisbon, 28 September 2004
