Sntese de declaraes  imprensa do Governador Vtor Constncio a propsito da crise do crdito hipotecrio de alto risco (subprime) nos Estados Unidos 13 set. 2007 Razes e consequncias da crise do subprime A crise do crdito hipotecrio de alto risco ( subprime) nos Estados Unidos no tem assumido propores maiores do que se previa, mas os excessos cometidos e a distribuio do risco por muitos agentes em vrios pases que compraram ttulos e instrumentos derivados associados a esse crdito criaram um problema de falta de informao sobre quem  que vai suportar as perdas do incumprimento desse crdito imobilirio e sobre a dimenso dessas perdas.  isso que explica a quebra de liquidez em vrios mercados. A falta de liquidez de mercado, que no se deve confundir com liquidez monetria, consiste em no existirem ou serem escassas as transaces por falta de agentes financeiros dispostos a transaccionar a um determinado preo. A falta de liquidez neste sentido est ligada a uma quebra de confiana que se gerou essencialmente por faltar o tipo de informao referida. Existe tambm um efeito de contgio para outros tipos de instrumentos no contexto de um processo geral de reviso da avaliao do risco. Isto tem afectado segmentos importantes do mercado de ttulos de dvida privada (a pblica tem continuado a ter muita procura), desde o de papel comercial at vrios tipos de obrigaes. A superao da falta de liquidez de mercado em todos estes casos depende dos agentes financeiros envolvidos na crise do crdito subprime americano comearem a divulgar as perdas que vo suportar e, em geral, recomearem as transaces aps uma reviso do valor de activos e instrumentos financeiros. A confiana de ambos os lados do mercado tem que voltar a restabelecer-se, ainda que a outros preos. A situao acabar por normalizar, mas pode levar algum tempo. Actuao do BCE As intervenes iniciais do BCE normalizaram o mercado monetrio interbancrio at uma semana, tendo sempre conseguido trazer a taxa do overnight para valores prximos da taxa definida pela poltica monetria. Mas, visto que no tem existido uma transmisso para prazos mais longos, por no existirem agentes financeiros dispostos a transaccionar para essas maturidades, o Conselho de Governadores do BCE decidiu fazer uma interveno extraordinria a 3 meses de 40 mil milhes de euros, realizada no final de Agosto, e no dia 6 de Setembro decidiu realizar outra na semana seguinte, sem fixar previamente quer a quantidade quer a taxa. O objectivo foi introduzir liquidez a prazos mais longos, de forma a estimular os agentes a recomear a transaccionar nesses prazos. A responsabilidade de um Banco Central  manter em funcionamento o mercado monetrio de curto prazo e temos feito o necessrio para normalizar o segmento interbancrio. Tendo em conta a turbulncia dos mercados e a grande incerteza existente, o Conselho de Governadores do BCE, rgo que decide a poltica monetria, deliberou manter o nvel das taxas de juro e recolher informao adicional e examinar novos dados antes de tirar outras concluses para a poltica monetria. Isto tambm contribui para assegurar aos mercados que o BCE no ignora as dificuldades da situao actual, sem prejudicar o cumprimento do objectivo, que lhe  definido pelo Tratado, de garantir a estabilidade dos preos na rea do euro. Em qualquer caso, a reviso em curso da avaliao do risco j implica um aumento do custo do financiamento e significa que acabou o ciclo do crdito fcil para agentes e instrumentos de mais alto risco. Situao do sistema financeiro portugus De acordo com o levantamento que o Banco de Portugal fez junto das instituies bancrias, a exposio, directa e indirecta, aos instrumentos associados ao mercado americano subprime no tem praticamente expresso no total do balano do sistema bancrio. O Banco de Portugal analisou tambm com as instituies bancrias a situao de liquidez, actual e previsional, bem como a dos respectivos mecanismos de gesto. Estes eram os aspectos imediatamente mais importantes a analisar. Evidentemente, a evoluo dos mercados em geral e para alm dos associados ao problema do mercado subprime poder vir a revelar outros problemas de valorizao de activos. De qualquer forma, as avaliaes internacionais feitas recentemente aos bancos portugueses confirmam a sua robustez e capacidade de resistir a choques.  certamente isso que justifica que desde o incio da turbulncia actual os preos dos ttulos emitidos pelos bancos portugueses tenham acompanhado estritamente a evoluo dos ndices mdios do sector bancrio europeu. Temos insistido bastante na necessidade de manter a estabilidade financeira e a rentabilidade e solidez do sistema bancrio. Momentos como este provam a importncia desse objectivo. Felizmente podemos dizer que no existem outros factores especficos de preocupao no sistema bancrio portugus que justificassem agora novas iniciativas. Impactos nas economias portuguesa e europeia As previses que o Conselho de Governadores analisou na sua reunio de 6 de Setembro revelam um cenrio central em que o crescimento da rea do euro em 2007 e 2008  revisto em baixa em apenas 0,1%. Os dados fundamentais que tm alimentado a recuperao econmica europeia e portuguesa mantm-se ainda. Ao contrrio dos Estados Unidos, a Europa no tem um problema geral de incumprimentos e queda de preos no mercado imobilirio. Naquele cenrio central, que implica a normalizao do funcionamento dos mercados financeiros a curto prazo, a reduo do crescimento seria, pois, muito ligeira e pouco relevante tambm para Portugal. No entanto,  importante sublinhar que se acentuaram os riscos em torno do cenrio de base, porque a normalizao dos mercados pode levar mais tempo, ou porque a desacelerao econmica americana pode revelar-se mais acentuada, com efeitos negativos no crescimento mundial, ou ainda porque o aumento da averso ao risco pode exceder o previsto e conduzir a condies financeiras menos favorveis ao crescimento. Portugal est muito dependente do que ocorrer na economia mundial e, em particular, na europeia, no existindo factores especficos da economia portuguesa que levem o Banco de Portugal a rever as previses actuais, includas nas que o BCE divulgou em 6 de Setembro. A regulao e superviso de instituies e mercados financeiros  preciso repensar os sistemas de regulao e superviso de instituies e mercados financeiros. Isso pode envolver aspectos como o papel das agncias de rating; as normas sobre a transparncia de divulgao de exposies de vrios tipos de instituies, incluindo hedge-funds e outros veculos financeiros (SIV -structured investment vehicles); os regulamentos sobre exigncia de rcios de capital; as regras sobre a comercializao de produtos financeiros, de forma a torn-los menos complexos e opacos junto de clientes e investidores, etc. A actual situao revelou tambm que muito se espera da interveno dos Bancos Centrais, mas estes, para desempenharem a sua misso de normalizar o funcionamento dos mercados, sem compensar os que cometeram excessos, tm de ter acesso fcil e imediato  informao sobre a situao das instituies financeiras, o que justifica que estejam envolvidos ou sejam responsveis directos pela respectiva superviso. Houve pases que evoluram recentemente em sentido contrrio sem vantagem aparente. Em resumo, haver muita coisa a repensar serenamente sobre regulao e superviso uma vez passada esta turbulncia. 13 Setembro 2007

Title: Intervention of The Administrator Dr. Vitor Pessoa in the III International Seminar promoted by IFB on the use of Cash in SEPA
text: Intervention of the Administrator Dr. Vi... Intervention of The Administrator Dr. Vitor Pessoa in the III International Seminar promoted by IFB on the use of Cash in SEPA Feb. 1, 2014 2008 The role of Banco de Portugal and the Eurosystem in the management of cash Vitor Pessoa Administrator of Banco de Portugal Speech at the III International Seminar promoted by the IFB on 1 February 2008 on the use of Cash in SEPA This intervention aims primarily to place Banco de Portugal in the context of an innovative Eurosystem strategy aimed at streamlining and improving management processes and making money available to credit institutions and the general public. SEPA focuses only on three payment instruments: credit transfers, direct debits and card payments. However, there needs to be a good articulation between the various existing instruments, including cash. The Eurosystem takes a position of neutrality in view of its use, without prejudice to pursuing efficiency-generating policies. At the end of 2007, cash circulation in the Eurosystem has increased by more than 12 billion banknotes, in a figure of more than EUR 600 billion. The annual growth rate (in number of notes) has been on average 8% per year. In this development, it is also not strange the growing role that the Euro plays at international level. It is undeniable that, even if there is a progressive change in payment behaviour, with greater use of electronic means, cash will tend to remain, in the medium term, as the most widely used retail payment instrument in the Eurosystem. In Portugal too, despite the trend towards greater use of electronic payment instruments, cash has maintained its importance to be assessed by the number of withdrawals made at IC's counters and ATMs. In fact, cash is the payment instrument i) with less associated costs for low-value transactions; (ii) which serves as a contingency payment instrument; iii) that has a social role, avoiding the exclusion of people without bank account and electronic payment instruments, iv) which best allows monitoring and avoiding expenses above the possibilities, v) which is safer in terms of fraud. The fact that cash continues to be widely used does not mean that its management remains unchanged. In fact, there has been significant developments in the distribution and treatment of cash in Portugal, with direct impacts on the activity of the Central Bank, commercial banks and other actors in that sector. This development was mainly motivated by the fact that the banking system has given private companies operating in the cash area (Securities Transport Companies -ETV) the responsibility for managing their cash flows. In this process, ETV act with a view to fully streamlining their activity in the field of operational cash management. Another major development, begun in the 1980s, is related to the increasing use of ATMs. These are effectively the main channel of distribution of banknotes by the public -90% of withdrawals are carried out in ATM and only 10% at the counter of credit institutions (CI). Portugal, after Spain, is the country with the highest ATM per 1000 inhabitants, about 1.07 (when the European average is 0.74). The massive use of ATMs has enabled IC's to free up labour, and therefore has functioned as a generating element of cost reduction and increased efficiency in cash management. Finally, there is now a new technological development, with the introduction of recirculating equipment, in particular over the counter, which will allow, among other benefits, to reduce the execution time of operations and cash closing, human errors and the number of cash transports by ETV; increase the security and level of service provided to the customer; and also ensure a dynamic and permanent management of cash. Banco de Portugal has been monitoring all these developments, assuming a position of pro-active cooperation with the banking system itself in order to enhance efficiency gains in the cash management process. In this sense, the Bank has been establishing an increasingly close dialogue with cash operators  IC's and ETV's. Thus, in 2004, it created an Interbank Working Group for Cash (GTIN), integrated by APB and the main Portuguese IC's, as well as a Working Subgroup for Cash Recirculation (SGRN), with representatives of all ETV operating in Portugal. The creation of a specific and autonomous Cash EG has taken into account that this is a payment instrument involving unique aspects which require differentiated treatment and in respect of which central banks are issuing authorities. As is common knowledge, the European Central Bank has the exclusive right to authorise the issue of banknotes in the Euro Area, and the National Central Banks are entitled to issue those banknotes. The activities of these working groups have revolved around two major projects: Common Framework for the Recirculation of Euro Banknotes (QC) Single Euro Cash Area (SECA) -"Roadmap" for greater convergence of services provided by central banks in the field of cash. THE QC is a project which, assuming that the cash recirculation activity is no longer exclusive to NCBs, aims to create conditions to ensure compliance by CI and other cash professionals with appropriate standards in the treatment of euro banknotes in order to contribute to the maintenance of quality and ensure the authenticity of banknotes in circulation. Obviously all this in a context of proper level playing field. The model adopted by Banco de Portugal was based on two pillars: one of a legal nature, with the publication of a Decree-Law (DL No. 195/2007 of 15 May) and regulatory regulations that granted Banco de Portugal the powers and instruments inherent to its status as regulator; and another, of a contractual nature, making the exercise of the activity of recirculation of the conclusion of contract dependent, which operates, thus, as a enabling title, in place of heavier mechanisms, such as authorization and registration or issuance of authorisation or permit. This model has been appropriate, having created a framework that allowed Banco de Portugal, on the one hand, to have counter-ordenational power and, on the other hand, to adopt a contractual solution in the relationship with the recirculating entities, which resulted in a light mechanism, but at the same time safe and able to accommodate the changes that the evolution of the activity might dictate. So far the balance sheet is highly positive and the objective of concluding contracts with the main market players has been achieved. With regard to the SECA project, it emerged from a wish list produced by the European Payments Council (EPC), noting the main aspects that could be improved by the Eurosystem. The European Central Bank (ECB) responded with the Roadmap, which provided for a set of measures for harmonisation and progressive convergence of services provided by NCBs in the cash area: 1) free access to cash services provided by ncBs; 2) acceptance of currency deposits by NCBs without restrictions; 3) extension of service hours and/or adoption of measures of similar effect; 4) installation of electronic interfaces for the communication of deposits/withdrawals; 5) acceptance of unfaced and non-oriented notes free of charge; 6) common packaging standards for deposits and cash withdrawals. Banco de Portugal aligned itself with this project, and even took some measures in advance, such as the revision of the service periods and the conditions of receipt of deposits. On the other hand, it started to accept deposits of metallic currency as early as 2004 and the installation of electronic interfaces for the communication of deposits and withdrawals is under study. Finally, the technological modernization of the area of sanitation of banknotes was started, through an investment program with a view to the acquisition of equipment adaptable to the choice of multiorientation and multidenomination. In addition and in a way that can be considered innovative, Banco de Portugal has bet on the training of professionals who handle cash as a way to better combat counterfeiting. More than restricting itself to face-to-face training  which has been carried out  the Bank has bet on the e-learning system, soon providing an application with which it intends to reach thousands of professionals. In conclusion, we are sure that there is a way to go and the potential for rationalisation. Banco de Portugal has been receptive and remains open to dialogue with banks and ETV, which has proved to be an excellent way to find structured solutions to promote efficiency in cash management. Thank you very much.
text_original: Interveno do Administrador Dr. V... Interveno do Administrador Dr. Vtor Pessoa no III Seminrio Internacional promovido pelo IFB sobre a utilizao do Numerrio na SEPA 01 fev. 2008 O papel do Banco de Portugal e do Eurosistema na gesto do numerrio Vtor Pessoa Administrador do Banco de Portugal Interveno no III Seminrio Internacional promovido pelo IFB em 1 de Fevereiro de 2008 sobre a utilizao do Numerrio na SEPA Esta interveno pretende fundamentalmente situar o Banco de Portugal no contexto de uma estratgia inovadora do Eurosistema visando a racionalizao e a melhoria de processos de gesto e de disponibilizao do numerrio s Instituies de Crdito e ao Pblico em geral. A SEPA foca-se apenas em trs instrumentos de pagamento: transferncias a crdito, dbitos directos e pagamentos com carto.  necessrio, contudo, que haja uma boa articulao entre os diversos instrumentos existentes, entre os quais figura tambm o numerrio. O Eurosistema assume uma posio de neutralidade face  utilizao deste, sem prejuzo de prosseguir polticas geradoras de eficincia. A circulao de numerrio no Eurosistema tem vindo a aumentar, totalizando, no final de 2007, mais de 12 mil milhes de notas, num valor que ultrapassa os 600 mil milhes de euros. A taxa anual de crescimento (em quantidade de notas) tem sido em mdia de 8% ao ano. Nesta evoluo no  estranho tambm o crescente papel que o Euro desempenha a nvel internacional.  inegvel que, mesmo ocorrendo uma alterao progressiva no comportamento associado aos pagamentos, com maior utilizao dos meios electrnicos, o numerrio tender a manter-se, a mdio prazo, como o instrumento de pagamento a retalho mais usado no Eurosistema. Tambm em Portugal, no obstante a tendncia para uma maior utilizao de instrumentos de pagamento electrnicos, o numerrio tem mantido a sua importncia relativa, a avaliar pelo nmero de levantamentos efectuados aos balces das ICs e nos caixas automticos (ATMs). Na realidade, o numerrio  o instrumento de pagamento i) com menos custos associados para transaces de baixo valor; ii) que serve de instrumento de pagamento de contingncia; iii) que tem um papel social, evitando a excluso de pessoas sem conta bancria e instrumentos de pagamento electrnico, iv) que melhor permite monitorizar e evitar gastos acima das possibilidades, v) que  mais seguro em termos de fraude. O facto do numerrio continuar a ser muito utilizado, no significa que a sua gesto permanea inalterada. Tem-se assistido, com efeito, a uma evoluo significativa no domnio da distribuio e tratamento do numerrio em Portugal, com impactos directos na actividade do Banco Central, dos bancos comerciais e ainda de outros intervenientes naquele sector. Esta evoluo foi sobretudo motivada pelo facto de o sistema bancrio ter atribudo s empresas privadas que operam na rea do numerrio (Empresas de Transporte de Valores -ETV) a responsabilidade pela gesto dos seus fluxos tesouraria. Nesse processo, as ETV actuam numa perspectiva de racionalizao plena da sua actividade em matria de gesto operacional do numerrio. Outra evoluo de relevo, iniciada na dcada de 80, prende-se com a utilizao crescente dos caixas automticos. Estes so efectivamente o principal canal de distribuio de notas pelo pblico -90% dos levantamentos so realizados em ATM e apenas 10% ao balco das Instituies de Crdito (IC). Portugal, a seguir a Espanha,  o pas com mais ATM por 1000 habitantes, cerca de 1.07 (quando a mdia europeia  de 0.74). A utilizao massiva dos ATM permitiu s ICs libertar mo-de-obra, tendo por isso funcionado como elemento gerador de reduo de custos e de aumento de eficincia na gesto do numerrio. Por ltimo, assiste-se neste momento a uma nova evoluo tecnolgica, com a introduo dos equipamentos recirculadores, designadamente ao balco, que permitiro, entre outros benefcios, reduzir o tempo de execuo das operaes e de fecho de caixa, os erros humanos e o nmero de transportes de numerrio pelas ETV; aumentar a segurana e o nvel de servio prestado ao cliente; e ainda assegurar uma gesto dinmica e permanente do numerrio. O Banco de Portugal tem vindo a acompanhar todas estas evolues, assumindo uma posio de cooperao pro-activa com o prprio sistema bancrio no sentido de potenciar ganhos de eficincia no processo de gesto de numerrio. Nesse sentido, o Banco tem vindo a estabelecer um dilogo cada vez mais estreito com os operadores de numerrio  ICs e ETVs. Assim, em 2004, criou um Grupo de Trabalho Interbancrio para o Numerrio (GTIN), integrado pela APB e as principais ICs portuguesas, bem como um Subgrupo de Trabalho para a Recirculao de Numerrio (SGRN), com representantes de todas as ETV a operar em Portugal. A criao de um GT especfico e autnomo para o numerrio teve em considerao que este  um instrumento de pagamento envolvendo aspectos nicos que obrigam a um tratamento diferenciado e em relao ao qual os Bancos Centrais so autoridades emissoras. Com efeito, como  do conhecimento geral, o Banco Central Europeu detm o direito exclusivo de autorizar a emisso de notas na rea do Euro, competindo aos Bancos Centrais Nacionais a emisso dessas mesmas notas. As actividades destes grupos de trabalho tm girado em torno de dois grandes projectos: Quadro Comum para a Recirculao de Notas Euro (QC) Single Euro Cash Area (SECA) -Roadmap para uma maior convergncia de servios prestados pelos Bancos Centrais no domnio do numerrio. O QC  um projecto que, assumindo efectivamente que a actividade de recirculao de numerrio deixou de ser exclusiva dos BCN, visa criar condies para garantir a observncia da aplicao, por parte das IC e de outros profissionais que operam com numerrio, de normas apropriadas no tratamento de notas de euro, por forma a contribuir para a manuteno da qualidade e garantir a autenticidade das notas em circulao. Obviamente que tudo isto num contexto de adequado level playing field. O modelo adoptado pelo Banco de Portugal assentou em dois pilares: um de natureza legal, com a publicao de um Decreto-Lei (DL n. 195/2007, de 15 de Maio) e de normativos regulamentares que outorgaram ao Banco de Portugal os poderes e instrumentos inerentes  sua qualidade de regulador; e um outro, de cariz contratual, fazendo depender o exerccio da actividade de recirculao da celebrao de contrato, o qual opera, assim, como ttulo habilitante, em substituio de mecanismos mais pesados, como seja o de autorizao e registo ou de emisso de autorizao ou alvar. Este modelo tem vindo a mostrar-se adequado, por ter criado um enquadramento que permitiu ao Banco de Portugal, por um lado, dispor de poder contra-ordenacional e, por outro, adoptar uma soluo contratual no relacionamento com as entidades recirculadoras, o que resultou num mecanismo leve, mas simultaneamente seguro e apto a acomodar as alteraes que a evoluo da actividade vier a ditar. At ao momento o balano  altamente positivo, tendo sido atingido o objectivo de celebrao de contratos com os principais agentes do mercado. Relativamente ao projecto SECA, este surgiu de uma wish list produzida pelo European Payments Council (EPC), dando nota dos principais aspectos eventualmente a melhorar pelo Eurosistema. O Banco Central Europeu (BCE) respondeu com o Roadmap, onde previu um conjunto de medidas com vista  harmonizao e  progressiva convergncia de servios prestados pelos BCN, na rea do numerrio: 1) livre acesso aos servios de numerrio prestado pelos BCN; 2) aceitao de depsitos de moeda pelos BCN sem restries; 3) alargamento dos horrios de atendimento e/ou adopo de medidas de efeito similar; 4) instalao de interfaces electrnicos para a comunicao de depsitos/levantamentos; 5) aceitao de notas no faceadas e no orientadas livre de encargos; 6) standards de embalamento comum para os depsitos e levantamentos de numerrio. O Banco de Portugal alinhou-se com este projecto, tendo inclusivamente tomado algumas medidas antecipadamente, como foi a da reviso dos perodos de atendimento e das condies de recepo dos depsitos. Por outro lado, passou a aceitar depsitos de moeda metlica logo a partir de 2004 e encontra-se em estudo a instalao de interfaces electrnicos para a comunicao de depsitos e levantamentos. Finalmente, deu-se nicio  modernizao tecnolgica da rea do saneamento de notas, atravs de um programa de investimentos com vista  aquisio de equipamentos adaptveis  escolha multiorientao e multidenominao. Complementarmente e de uma forma que pode considerar-se inovadora, o Banco de Portugal apostou na formao de profissionais que manuseiam numerrio como forma de melhor combater a contrafaco. Mais do que restringir-se  formao presencial  que tem sido realizada -, o Banco apostou no sistema de e-learning, disponibilizando em breve uma aplicao com a qual se pretende chegar a milhares de profissionais. Em concluso, estamos certos de que h caminho a percorrer e potencial de racionalizao. O Banco de Portugal tem sido receptivo e mantm-se aberto ao dilogo com os Bancos e as ETV, o que se tem revelado uma excelente forma de encontrar solues estruturadas para a promoo da eficincia na gesto do numerrio. Muito obrigado.

Title: Speech by Deputy Governor Jos Agostinho Martins de Matos at the Conference "10 years of the European System of Central Banks"
text: Speech by Deputy Governor Jose Ag... Speech by Deputy Governor Jose Agostinho Martins de Matos at the Conference "10 years of the European System of Central Banks" 06 jul. 2009 6 July 2009 "Banco de Portugal's experience in the Eurosystem" ( 1) Jose Agostinho Martins de Matos Deputy Governor of Banco de Portugal I would like to begin by thanking me for the invitation i have been invited to speak at this Conference. One point I find interesting is that, in the title of the conference, it is mentioned "ten years" but, in fact, eleven have passed. This additional year, of which I will highlight some aspects, is particularly important in the eurosystem's experience, constituting a very significant test of the eurosystem's activity. Before moving on to the scheme of my presentation, I would also like to thank the Governor, Professor Vitor Constancio, for sharing with him the experience of having been his "Alternate" over the course of these years in the Governing Council. With regard to this particular presentation, I would also like to thank Dr. Silvia Luz for helping me prepare, that she discussed with me several of the aspects contained herein. Moreover, from this point of view, Dr. Silvia Luz is the symbol of a vast set of paintings and old paintings of Banco de Portugal and other institutions of the Eurosystem, some of which are present here today, which have made possible this adventure of sharing a single currency over this time and of having made a very refined preparation, very detailed over the several years. The topics I will address include, firstly, the mandate and organisation of the ESCB and the Eurosystem and, secondly, monetary policy. These are two topics to which I will make a very brief reference, because they are better known of all, although sometimes and surprisingly not completely known. The third topic, Banco de Portugal and the Eurosystem, will be a point where I will try to be more detailed because there has been a lack of information here that it may be useful to try to address in a conference of this nature. In the fourth topic I will sum up the results in the first 10-11 years of Eurosystem and monetary union. I will mention these aspects very briefly, because the fourth session talks about the Portuguese economy in the last 10 years and will certainly develop this theme much more. On the point of the Eurosystem in the face of the global crisis I will make some references to these aspects, together with the challenges for the coming years. I won't look at the next 10 years, not the next 20 years. At the moment, we are very concerned and very busy with the next 1, 2 or 3 years and therefore I will mention some of the aspects for this shorter term. Finally, I will make some final conclusions. There is not much to be known about the mandate and organisation of the Eurosystem. Its primary objective is to maintain price stability in the euro area. That is why the ECB and the Eurosystem were set up. At a hearing where there will be many lawyers, it must be said that the Eurosystem is not yet an official expression. However, it is foreseen in the Treaty of Lisbon, which we hope will finally be adopted. But from the outset, since 1998, it has been perceived the need to have a specific brand to separate and identify the central bank that would issue the new currency of the euro. That central bank would be the ECB and the national central banks of the countries that would be part of the euro area. The Eurosystem is run by the Governing Council, and the decision-making bodies of the Eurosystem are therefore the decision-making bodies of the ECB. The ECB has legal personality, with decision-making capacity, just as the national central banks that are part of the Eurosystem have legal personality. I mentioned the main objective, but I would not like to forget the secondary objective. As the Treaty says, "without prejudice to the objective of price stability", the system also aims at "supporting the general economic policies of the European Community". The primary objective outsplants all others, but we are aware in the Eurosystem that there is also a secondary objective set out in the Treaty. The Treaty identifies the basic tasks of the Eurosystem: the definition of monetary policy; the carrying out of foreign exchange operations; the holding and management of the official reserves of the Member States; promoting the proper functioning of the payment system. It then mentions a number of other tasks: the authorisation of monetary issue, i.e. putting banknotes into circulation; consultative tasks in which the ECB and the system have the functions of consulting and issuing opinions, in some cases mandatory, on Community or national legislative initiatives of interest to the Eurosystem; and collaboration with the other national central banks and other national and Community authorities in the field of prudential supervision and in the statistical field, for example. The organization of the Eurosystem is well known. I would only mention here that the Governing Council is the eurosystem's highest decision-making body. It is a body that meets every two weeks, so it has a high-frequency activity in terms of EU organisations, the first meeting of each month dedicated to deliberating on monetary policy. At the second meeting, the Council deliberates on all the other activities of the Eurosystem. The General Council includes the President and Vice-President of the ECB and all the Governors of the central banks of all Member States (currently 27) who are part of the European System of Central Banks (ESCB). There are several Community policies that are considered of common interest to the whole system: the coordination of monetary policies, the evaluation of the exchange rate mechanism in its second version, erm2, and, to great prominence, also the discussion of the European international agenda. There are many aspects where the fact that the ECB is the issuer of the euro reserves it, as well as the Eurosystem, the exclusive of some angles of international activity and in the international monetary cooperation of the euro area. But there are other aspects, particularly within the IMF, where the position of banks not participating in the euro area is also relevant, and it is important to have a coordinated position. Therefore, the General Council is the right point to exchange views at the level of the supreme organs of the system. Moving on to monetary policy, the main aspects are also relatively well known. I will just remind you that the Governing Council defines monetary policy with the aim of maintaining price stability. The Council established its own operational definition of price stability, a quantitative definition in the medium term, according to which the growth of the harmonised consumer price index in the euro area should be less than, but close to, 2%. With regard to the monetary policy strategy, the so-called "two-pillar strategy", the Governing Council takes decisions taking into account, on the one hand, all elements of the analysis of the economy and, on the other hand, the analysis of monetary aspects. The Bank has this double look at the economy as a whole, cross-checking this information and it is on the basis of this integrated set of information and analysis that it makes its decisions on official interest rates. As for transmission mechanisms, central banks basically act in the economy by setting very short-term interest rates. Under normal conditions, it is through the spread of these interest rates to other segments of the money market, the financial market and the economy as a whole that monetary policy materialises. Under less normal conditions, such as the one we now live in, the transmission mechanism may be affected. In other words, the actions of the authorities on official interest rates may not be reflected immediately, or not even reflected in interest rates, in the various segments of the various markets and in the level of bank rates. Banking rates, in the specific case of the European economic system, have a decisive weight, because we have a very bank based system, rather than being more market based, as in the USA. The financing conditions of the banking system are decisive for the financing of the economy in the euro area. The transmission of monetary policy has been somewhat affected for some time, but we can say that the conditions for the transmission of monetary policy have been restored in the meantime, especially since the ECB decided to lower rates more aggressively and, as risk aversion has been reduced, interest rates in monetary markets have adjusted, following the fall in official rates. In monetary policy, we have, on the one hand, the decision and, on the other, the implementation. I will now refer more to aspects of the monetary policy operational framework. Monetary policy decisions are fundamentally the decisions that the Council takes in terms of the level of official rates, with the rate of the main refinancing operations being the most important, at least under normal conditions. The implementation of monetary policy is the responsibility of the Executive Board of the ECB and is implemented in a decentralised manner throughout the Eurosystem. For monetary policy operations, we have, under normal conditions, a permanent liquidity-supply facility and a deposit facility. They're both overnight facilities. Any bank that has excess liquidity at the end of the day can put it in the ECB's deposit facility. If, on the contrary, it needs liquidity you can use the system to finance itself through the liquidity-provided facility. The interest rates of these facilities define a corridor within which, in principle, the overnight rates practiced in the interbank market will be. For obvious reasons, there would be no reason for the rates on this market to be lower than the deposit facility rates, because banks always have the alternative of depositing in the Eurosystem. There would also be no need to finance themselves more expensively in the interbank market, because they could obtain liquidity from the Eurosystem at the rate of ease of lending. In addition to facility operations, so-called core refinancing operations are crucial under normal conditions. Transactions are carried out weekly, for a period of one week, in the form of repurchase agreements with the interest rate formed at auction. The minimum rate of this auction is announced by the ECB and is the eurosystem's main official interest rate under normal conditions. In addition to one-week forward operations, the Eurosystem predicted from the outset long-term refinancing operations, which were generally three-month transactions, held every month in auctions with fixed quantities offered, in which the Eurosystem is a "price taker" of market conditions, yielding liquidity to the prevailing rates in the money markets for that period. This normal way of acting is greatly altered in the crisis situation in which we have been living and, in particular, it has changed a lot since October last year. We will see further ahead the huge financial market turmoil following the bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers. There were very important changes in the implementation of monetary policy at the time, in particular the fact that unlimited transfers of fixed-rate liquidity were made, both for the main refinancing operations and for the longer-term refinancing operations. The only limit to the amount of liquidity transferred is dependent on the amount of eligible collateral that banks have or are willing to deliver to the system for liquidity. In addition, the system successively extended the long-term period of these operations. It has carried out operations on irregular terms, operations for six months and, more recently, even announced operations a year ago, of which it has already made one recently and two more operations are planned by the end of 2009. It is not decided what the conditions are for putting these operations into the future, but in any case we are talking about a great certainty and confidence given to the entire banking system regarding the willingness to obtain financing from the central bank for a relatively long period. One aspect I would like to highlight is that the operational framework of monetary policy is almost the same as that adopted and adopted in the Governing Council at the beginning of monetary union. The possibility of carrying out structural transactions, with outright outright or outright assets, has always been accepted in order to permanently affect liquidity conditions. The Eurosystem recently announced a programme to buy covered bonds, mortgage bonds issued by banks, up to a maximum of 60 billion to be completed within a year. Operations of this kind have never been carried out in the past, but they will start now, exactly from today, and their technical preparation has been facilitated by the scope of the initial operational framework. After the introduction of the mandate and monetary policy, i would now enter the most specific point about Banco de Portugal's experience in the Eurosystem. We must first of all recall that the monetary policy decision is a centralised decision in the Council. Each Governor of the national central bank, in addition to the members of the Executive Board, participates, on a personal and independent basis, in these decisions, according to the rule, provided for in the Treaty, of "to every man or woman, one vote". The Council is therefore an independent body that makes monetary policy decisions, thinking about Europe, thinking about the conditions of the euro area globally and not on the terms of any individual country, nor those countries of whose central banks are governors. But the implementation of monetary policy is decentralised, taking place through and under the responsibility of national central banks. This is provided for in the Treaty and has been done from the outset. Of course, national central banks contribute to monetary policy decisions by helping to technically prepare decisions. Both the national central banks and the ECB, through their staffs, support the members of the Governing Council and technically contribute to the preparation of decisions. Of the activities of Banco de Portugal that we can include in the eurosystem sphere, in addition to the preparation and implementation of monetary policy (which is very important, but which is not even the most significant amount of resources, although it occupies very qualified resources), we have, first of all, the management of the ECB's reserves. The national central banks have handed the ECB part of their reserves, in accordance with certain rules, to constitute the ECB's external reserves, which are however managed decentralisedby by the national central banks. Secondly, we have the functioning of domestic and transnational payment and settlement systems  an area absolutely crucial for the efficient functioning of the single money market and the integrated financial market  which was already central banks before the Eurosystem and which continued. On the other hand, national central banks are also fundamental in the production and issue of banknotes and in the compilation and dissemination of statistics, the latter being an area where decentralised character is very important, despite very strong coordination, and also a very resource-intensive area of the Eurosystem with very good quality human resources. We also have several other activities (international relations and cooperation, legal advice, accounting and budgetary control, internal audit, information systems, external communication, etc.) that fall under the Eurosystem and are carried out by the national central banks and Banco de Portugal in Portugal. In addition, there are other activities that central banks carry out outside the Eurosystem, but conditioned and coordinated to some extent with the activities of the Eurosystem, such as the management of external reserves and other financial assets of the national central banks themselves. The operation of Banco de Portugal in the Eurosystem has fundamentally meant a new paradigm. We were a central bank over 150 years old (of the oldest in the world) when monetary union began. We were doing all the usual activities of a central bank, but preparing for the euro before 1998 and realising it after 1998. What has happened is that the Bank continues to do all the activity it was doing, but the frame of reference has become the euro area and all the institutions and decision-making mechanisms governing the euro area central bank, namely the Eurosystem. Banco de Portugal had, before the adoption of the single currency, an operational monetary policy framework that was very close to what came to be the system adopted by the ECB. Very close because, in the late 1980s, the transition from monetary control to credit limits and administrative setting of interest rates for the conduct of monetary policy through indirect instruments was prepared, Banco de Portugal studied all the methods available in Europe and had the perception, which was confirmed to be correct, that any future European central bank, if and when it were to settle, would most likely adopt an operational scheme that would not depart significantly from what was then used in the Deutsche Bundesbank. Moreover, several other central banks in Europe had an operational scheme that was very close and, therefore, from that point of view, the transition from our operational framework to that of the ECB was relatively smooth and without difficulties. In the management of reserves, the Bank had to manage the ECB's reserves and its own. It had to adapt the functioning of the payment system and continue to produce statistics, but according to an even tighter harmonisation and coordination scheme than it already existed (the production of statistics in the field of central banks was reasonably codified, but the fact that in the eurosystem has made it even more precise). In terms of legislative action, the opinions and instructions that we must implement must comply with aspects of coherence and compatibility with the rules that are laid down at Eurosystem level. In the production of banknotes, Banco de Portugal was one of the banks that did not produce banknotes when it had its own currency. It had the finishing phase and the banknote ing phase, but had no complete and autonomous production of banknotes and decided to equip itself with a factory and with its own capacity to produce banknotes. It has done so in the context of the decentralised pooling that has been adopted in the Eurosystem to produce banknotes, which involves an overall amount that is decided at Eurosystem level. The composition of this set by denominations is also defined at Eurosystem level and each central bank is responsible for producing part of that total quantity of banknotes. Each national central bank shall put into circulation, through the banking system, banknotes produced by itself or by other central banks, to which it also supplies notes of those it produces. As monetary policy is centralised, the aspects of communication and "speaking with one voice" are absolutely crucial in the Eurosystem. But this, as the President of the ECB has said several times, is a multicultural, multilingual system with different histories. It is therefore very important the ability to speak in the local space, in the local language, in a different way, for local audiences. Communication policy must therefore be very coordinated at central level, but it must be sufficiently diverse at the level of the various countries. For a medium-sized country like Portugal and for a central bank such as Banco de Portugal (which had some international activity), the fact that it became part of the Eurosystem has qualitatively changed the way it operates in international relations. Banco de Portugal is the agent of the State and is the shareholder of the IMF, for example. It has such activities and normal holdings of national central banks. But for a bank of our size, it is completely different to do so in isolation or to do so within the framework of the Eurosystem, one of the two most important central banks in the world. The type of obligations and responsibilities, but also the kind of attention, it's different. Banco de Portugal has more voice now, even in this area, which we could consider as distant, because it has the opportunity to know what is happening at the level of the intervention of the Eurosystem and the ECB in all international "outs" of discussion, formal or formal, and to contribute its opinion to the formation of the collective opinion of the Eurosystem. Banco de Portugal, as a central bank (not as a supervisory authority, whose demands also increased) has not lost any of its operational responsibilities or any of the work it had and probably increased them. We cannot therefore reduce the resources we use, and this is a finding that other central banks also make. We have the ECB, but we still have the decentralised implementation of the eurosystem's policy and many other activities, which means that resource consumption cannot be significantly lower and, on the contrary, in some cases, increased. Banco de Portugal is a reasonably efficient bank with about 1700 employees. Its overall dimension, including supervision (which some central banks do not have), is reasonable and has not grown, at least not in the strict area of central bank. It has recently grown in supervisory activity, where more resources are needed, but not in its activity as a central bank. It has continued to try to manage its resources well in terms of quality, without increasing them quantitatively. The decentralised participation of the central Portuguese in the Eurosystem is not a disorganised participation. The ECB (and the Eurosystem) is an extremely organised and highly coordinated European entity. Nothing is improvised and cannot be improvised. You have to have a very careful job. This participation and this care is also done because the national central banks are part of the technical structures and committees  there are Eurosystem committees for all areas of the bank's activity  for technical support for meetings and decisions, including monetary policy decisions, the prior analysis of initiatives and the monitoring of all initiatives that are taken, implementation of the decentralised monetary policy and other activities of the ESCB. The Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal defined that excellence within the Eurosystem should be one of its strategic objectives, which has always been internalised in the Bank's life. Excellent being is something that is achieved to a greater or lesser extent, but it could be said that Banco de Portugal does have several good examples of excellence in the eurosystem's participation, such as economic analysis, asset management, the payment system, among others. To make this transformation at Banco de Portugal, a 150-year-old bank that has been preparing for the last two decades to participate in the euro area, it took a great deal of capacity for its staff  and I take this opportunity to publicly praise the work of Banco de Portugal's staff. The people who enter the Bank at the moment and the younger staff cannot imagine the activity of the central bank only in this way: to participate in the committees, to know what is discussed in the committees, to "brief" the Governor, to know the decisions that are relevant to his activity in the Governing Council. This is the way to work on a day-to-day basis of any framework within Banco de Portugal, in a world completely different from what we lived 25 years ago, when we had exchange controls, quantitative credit control, administrative interest rate setting, etc. and the internal functioning of Banco de Portugal was different. The Bank was able, had the necessary and able staff to make this preparation to live in the Eurosystem. The entire activity of Banco de Portugal at the moment also reflects, also in its balance sheet, the activity in the Eurosystem. All the most important items and accounts of our balance sheet are related to or conditioned by the eurosystem's activity. Firstly, we have transactions related to monetary policy, both active liquidity-easing transactions or, in passive transactions, liabilities to credit institutions, primarily deposits that constitute the minimum availabilities required of commercial banks. Secondly, in transactions linked to participation in the ECB, we have, in assets, equity participation and the value of assets (external reserves) transferred to the ECB. Thirdly, transactions associated with the operation of the European payment system, the TARGET system. In the Portuguese, in particular  in other central banks it will be different  we have, in liabilities, responsibilities towards the Eurosystem, corresponding to our responsibilities in relation to the whole system for the functioning of the trans-European payment system. This balance constitutes automatic financing, without conditionality and remunerated at the "repo" rate, which the Bank obtains from abroad and which is reflected in its balance sheet by transactions resulting from the mere exogenous operation of the payment system. When a bank orders us a payment abroad or when we originate a payment abroad, we automatically create that liability in relation to the outside. The whole system is financed "jointly and severally" by the mere functioning of the payment system. As is well known, the operation of these operations is regulated by ECB instructions and guidelines. These balances are not settled, which, under normal conditions, represents a great source of flexibility in the external financing of the Portuguese economy through Banco de Portugal. As for the transactions associated with the issue of banknotes, we have, in liabilities, the banknotes in circulation recorded in our balance sheet, for a value which is merely accounting. When issuing banknotes, the Eurosystem knows the overall value of banknotes put into circulation and each national central bank is assigned a calculated part corresponding to its capital key. It is not possible, in monetary union, where banknotes circulate throughout all countries, to know what the national monetary circulation is, we no longer know how many banknotes and coins portuguese economic agents have in their power to finance expenditures. We don't know, we can't know. We know how much was issued by the whole system and which part is responsible for us. We also know what part we put into circulation. This is an activity in which Banco de Portugal receives and delivers to the national commercial banks the notes they want to deliver or need to receive. It is a totally exogenous mechanism for the central bank, there is no decision from us on the amount of notes that the public and banks want to have. The difference between the banknotes assigned to us by the capital key and the banknotes we put into circulation is currently a very significant remunerated asset value. All four of these groups of operations are indispensable and inseparable from the eurosystem's activity. A fifth type of transaction stems from our management of our own external assets, gold and reserve assets (which we call reserve assets in the Bank's publications, for convenience and to be better understood by our readers), the foreign currency, the euros in the trading portfolio, the euros of a medium-term investment portfolio that the Bank has. In this area of our balance sheet, we have greater management autonomy; even so, this greater autonomy is not absolute freedom to manage these assets. In the case of gold, with the Eurosystem and with all other central banks, we are signatories to the so-called Central Bank Gold Agreement, in which we commit ourselves, with other central banks, to only make a certain volume of gold transactions, obviously to protect the conditions of this market and the value of assets. At the moment, under the current conditions of the gold market, this agreement represents a less active restriction, but it was already important, in particular, when it was born as early as 1998, at a time when gold prices were much lower. In addition, there are other constraints to all the assets that we can manage, because central banks need to coordinate within the Eurosystem to contribute to the so-called "system liquidity deficit". Therefore, there are limitations to the overall amount that we can have as assets, so that the primacy of the conduct of monetary policy is verified throughout the system and, jointly and severally, the contribution of each central bank to that liquidity deficit is determined. With regard to the results in the first ten years, I can be relatively brief. I can say that the euro was a success. Many expected the euro to be a failure or imagined immense difficulties for the euro to assert itself and function. The euro worked very well both in book-entry terms and in terms of banknotes and coins when cash changeover occurred. The euro has been a success and the central bank issuing the euro, i.e. the ECB (and the Eurosystem), is now one of the two most important monetary authorities in the world economy. It's something significant. The fact that Banco de Portugal participates in this project and, through Banco de Portugal, the Portuguese economy, is not a fact of somenos. It is often undervalued, but it is very important that Banco de Portugal and the country, through the Bank, are part of the Eurosystem. As far as monetary policy is about monetary policy, the result was price stability in the euro area. We can say that we had a space for price stability during the first ten years. There was a successful financial integration and adaptation of the payment system. We had TARGET, we moved to TARGET 2 and we're launching TARGET 2 Securities to allow for proper settlement of central bank securities. We have sepa ("Single Euro Payments Area") for the retail payment system (of which the Eurosystem has been a very active promoter) and we have had stability of the financial system. The Eurosystem has fulfilled its objectives in these ten years and has performed its tasks well. I would then mention some results for Portugal. These points will be dealt with at the last session of this Conference, more dedicated to the Portuguese economy, I will therefore be very synthetic and only illustrative. There was a very strong disinflation process in the case of Portuguese: we had an inflation rate of 17.7% before the euro area participation. There were other countries with also very high inflation rates. We have lowered to a rate of 6.1% immediately before entering the euro and we have an average rate of 2.9% after entering the euro. It's a low inflation rate and very close to stability for a country like ours. If we look at the most recent data from 2008 and 2009 we see that the inflation rate in Portugal is much lower, is the second lowest in the euro area and is much lower than the area average. Portugal has had good results in terms of inflation. In terms of growth, the results are not so famous. This is also the case in other countries. The results have been unsatisfactory, especially in recent years, not because of participation in the euro, but for other reasons that have been discussed. If we were outside the euro, we would probably be much worse off, even from a growth point of view. With regard to public accounts, we have made a very large adjustment effort to participate in the euro area and, when it was necessary in 1998 to assess the countries, we were below the 3% reference value for the public accounts deficit, like several other countries, moreover. Only Greece was not, but it did soon after. There has been a great deal of effort with regard to the quality of economic fundamentals. We then had some problems in good periods: we were able to tighten up and consolidate when we had to, but we had some problems with the management of public finances. And the fact that we have had problems with public finances in good times has forced us to adopt pro-cyclical policies at other times. We have lived in recent years on this shuttle of budgetary policies that have had to be very tight and pro-cyclical at certain times, as opposed to what should be possible. In terms of public debt, we had a relatively comfortable position compared to the euro area average  and we still do. Our deficit is a reasonable deficit even after 2007 and despite the large increase compared to the euro average. The problem is that the conditions of the area as a whole have also deteriorated. In terms of current account balance, it is true that Portugal is one of the countries that has a relatively high deterioration of external accounts, and there has an indicator of loss of competitiveness that is important. I would like to point out that some of the measures of loss and gain of competitiveness are quite debatable. There are several other measures besides this actual exchange rate calculated based on the Consumer Price Index (CPI). In the Bank's report, published relatively recently, it can be seen that there was some deterioration in Portuguese competitiveness, but this loss occurred fundamentally until 2001-2002. Since then, the loss of competitiveness has been virtually nil. We have had a reasonable development in terms of competitiveness in the context of relatively weak overall economic performance. It is also important to mention in this context that the external imbalance (which in monetary union does not have the same meaning as it would have, for example, in previous balance of payments crisis situations) partly reflects the spontaneous indebtedness of autonomous economic agents resulting from their own activity, both households and businesses. This indebtedness is endogenously corrected: at some times we realize that this indebtedness has limits and has been corrected. We do not have our own currency and we do not have a risk of a currency crisis and therefore the competitiveness and the balance of payments problem looks different. I am not saying that it is not a problem to have a cumulative imbalance in the external balance. This means that we have, in some way, with more or less problems of measurement, a problem of competitiveness. The difficulty (and that is what I wanted to highlight) is that the problem of competitiveness is not solved with exchange rate policy, it is also not manifested in any kind of exchange rate difficulties. Rather, it requires other budgetary policy instruments and structural policies and appropriate behaviour on the part of economic actors. I would draw an interim conclusion here which is important because, in the case of our participation in the euro area, it is important to realise that without autonomous monetary and exchange rate policy (we have a policy that serves the euro area as a whole), the quality of other national policies, fiscal policy and structural policies is decisive. In addition to these policies, the very attitudes that are internalised by economic agents are also decisive. Businesses, workers, families, the state need to incorporate the constraints of living in a single currency. It has been noticed that for some time some of the economic actors I mentioned have not completely internalised these constraints, even though they all benefit from living in the single currency. In order to benefit from the single currency, we must follow the rules and accept the constraints that this change in economic and monetary policy regime brings associated. A few short words about the Eurosystem in the face of the global crisis. We are celebrating the ten years of monetary union, but the eleventh year has been a particularly important year because the Eurosystem has faced a global crisis. And this global, economic and financial crisis has required monetary, budgetary and fiscal response capabilities and other support policies to stabilise the financial system. This year, with this crisis, the Eurosystem has been tested. It could be said that the ECB and the Eurosystem had worked in a relatively benign system, but it has now been tested and very hard and the ECB has done very well from that test. The bis 'annual report), published eight days ago in Basel, includes a graph with summary indicators of "stress" in financial markets and setting out five phases in this crisis so far. I would point here to key moments when the capacity of the ECB and the Eurosystem has been demonstrated. The first date, which is worth all in a certain way, despite the misunderstanding it generated at the time, is August 9, 2007. On that day, money markets were "dry", there was no liquidity and there was a situation of great tension in the markets. The ECB ran the risk, which at the time was poorly understood and even criticised by many people, of giving up liquidity unlimitedly. It seemed, however, that he had a capacity for foreknowledge and to realize what was to follow greater than that of others. The immediate reaction capacity was extremely strong and noted in all markets. The second date is 8 October 2008 in the most complicated period of the crisis  which is relatively short but of great stress, started from mid-September with the bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers  when lack of confidence and risk aversion reached levels never seen before and it was necessary to have very intense and very coordinated policy responses. On 8 October 2008, the big central banks (I am talking about the ECB here together with other central banks) began a process of aggressive and coordinated interest rate cuts. I would remind you that during the first half of the year, when inflation risks were not removed, the ECB even increased interest rates in the summer. However, as of October, in the face of the worsening crisis and the risk of a deep recession, the ECB has also adopted a very aggressive response towards falling interest rates. The ECB has since lowered its repo rate by 325 basis points. The setting of rates at this time is quite low, with the ease of deposit at 0.25%, the repo rate at 1% and the marginal liquidity-in-the-liquidity facility rate at 1.75%. Even with these levels of fees, the ECB remains very attentive to the situation. I would remind you that at last Thursday's press conference in Luxembourg, at one of those semiannual Council meetings outside Frankfurt, President Trichet again said: "I do not change the message I gave two months ago, one month ago. We didn't decide today that this was the lowest level we could ever retain in any circumstances". The President of the ECB acknowledges, on behalf of the Governing Council, that the crisis and recession requires the Eurosystem and the ECB, despite the low levels of the current rates, open ness to any decision that is necessary in the light of developments, particularly if they become more negative. This was obviously said on the same day that it was said, and well, that the level of rates was appropriate. This means that the Eurosystem is extremely attentive to the potential risks of worsening the crisis and therefore does not exclude anything at this time. Fiscal policy also had a very aggressive response to the crisis, with high budget deficits in 2009, and in some countries also in 2010. We are dealing with a very strong, expansionary response to budgetary policy and we must recognise that this very strong response is absolutely indispensable. In the short term, no one questions this absolute need in the recession situation in which we have experienced. But the Eurosystem and several of its leaders  the Governor of Banco de Portugal, for example, have already said this publicly  have said that it is essential to have exit and correction strategies for this fiscal expansionism as soon as it is perceived that the exit from the recession in the economy is relatively clear and firm. There is therefore a long-term sustainability problem of public finances in Europe and around the world. In Portugal too, given the level of budget deficit ratios that we have been forced to have with the response to the crisis, but, as has been said by the authorities, there is a real need to have an exit strategy as soon as possible. In addition to monetary and budgetary policies, there were also policies to directly support the financial system. I would like to refer to this point for one reason: in measures at European level on guarantees to bank debt and on recapitalisation projects, the Eurosystem intervened at European and national level, i.e. through Banco de Portugal, to contribute to the definition of pricing of collateral financing operations or some debt instruments associated with recapitalisation processes. It is interesting to see how the Eurosystem was the entity that, at that time, was considered the most independent and the most capable of contributing quickly to avoid one of the serious problems that could be faced with more direct government intervention in the banking system, that is, to prevent each country from supporting its banking systems with completely misaligned prices and, therefore with a greater risk of breaching the basic rules of State aid in the Community. Of course, the main measures in this area were not from the Eurosystem, they were from the Member States and the European Commission, because it is essential that the single market and the single market for financial services are not called into question by this intervention. Returning to monetary policy, in addition to the downward trend in official interest rates, there was also a significant increase in the balance sheets of the various central banks as a percentage of the GDP of the various countries, reflecting quantitative measures to expand liquidity. In the case of the Eurosystem, the size of the balance sheet before the crisis was already much larger than that of the other central banks. With the crisis, it increased again and, as we can see from the evolution of the balance sheet of the various central banks, the growth of these balance sheets was very fast in the case of the Fed and other central banks. In the Eurosystem the growth was lower, because there was already much more intermediation activity done by the Eurosystem, and even then there was an additional growth of this quite large intervention from October 2008. At the Fed we have a more explosive situation of balance sheet growth also from the same height, but from a level that was extremely stable and relatively low before the crisis. Several liquidity management measures taken by the Eurosystem in this area, including the extension of the list of eligible assets as collateral, which occurred at a time when the system had now received and also accepted bank loans as collateral. Over a relatively prolonged period of time there was much emphasis in the ECB's communication to the so-called "separation principle", i.e. the Eurosystem made a distinction between the direction/stance of monetary policy and liquidity management measures. For example, during the first half of 2008, there had been very large growth in oil prices and monetary policy was still little concerned about the signs of crisis and recession, which were less evident. The level of inflation measured by consumer prices in early summer was the highest since the beginning of monetary union. There was, therefore, some concern not to relieve the monetary policy orientation, but at the same time to normalise the functioning of markets by liquidity management measures. Since the fall in rates and since October, we have lived in perfect combination, there is no distinction between the relief of policies by the way of rates and the relief of policies through the measures of "enhanced credit suport", aiming at the restoration of operating conditions of the various markets, which, in this case, has an additional effect of signalling very important policies, especially because the level of rates is already very low. When the level of rates is too low, central banks can always lower them a little more, but there is a limit, which is zero. I will not enter into theoretical discussions on this matter, but there are other ways to continue, in these cases, to have expansionist policies, through the quantitative route, thus signaling the support of the recovery until there is any risk of a general increase in the price level. We had a brutal increase in risk aversion in September/October, evidenced by the increase in the gap between rates of non-co-lateralised and co-related operations three months ago in the money markets, which it has been correcting in recent months. Indeed, there are some positive signs in terms of reducing risk aversion and further standardising the functioning of markets. But with regard to risk and normalisation, there is a complicated problem that I will only state. When we talk about normalizing, it's because we have some idea of what's normal. However, for example, the BIS report draws very well, we will have a new normal again, which at the moment we do not know exactly what it is. We all knew and all complained in various reports that the levels of risk aversion before the crisis were extraordinarily low, too low, with very little caution in the functioning of the financial system. It is therefore natural that the new normal ity is not similar or equal to the one we had before the crisis. During its eleventh year of life, the ECB had to manage a very difficult crisis situation. I think it was reassuring to see that, in conditions of great stress in the markets, in financial institutions and in the economy, the Eurosystem was able to respond and respond well. Its institutional framework, its analytical framework, its structures were prepared and responded in crisis situations. The Eurosystem showed that it was not just another European bureaucracy. On the contrary, it has shown that it is a European institution up to the circumstances. I think that Banco de Portugal has also been up to what needs to be done in our country. In terms of the European institutions, I would venture to conclude that, at certain times, it was even the only European institution that was up to the circumstances. However, other Community institutions have provided adequate responses to the demands of the crisis. The coming years will be discussed here in other sessions, as well as the future and the problems related to the ecb's role in financial stability. The Heads of State and Government approved Ecofin's proposals and confirmed the idea of creating a European Systemic Risk Board. It will be an entity without legal personality, which will be dedicated to macro-prudential supervision, i.e. to the financial stability of the system as a whole (the financial system, the institutions, the market, infrastructure) and where all the governors of the Central Banks of the ESCB will be added. Support and technical support will be provided by the ECB. We will also have on this Board the top officials of the so-called "level 3 committees", which will be called European supervisory authorities or "agencies" for banks, insurance and financial markets. This is an extremely important step, parallel to others that are being taken in other parts of the world. On the part of macro-prudential supervision, the recognition of the responsibilities that central banks have always had in this area will crystallize into an increased importance and responsibility for the ECB and the ESCB. On the other hand, in the so-called micro-prudential supervision, i.e. of the institutions, there will be the said transformation of the "level 3 committees" into authorities with responsibilities for the development of a "Single European Rule Book", which is applicable in all Member States  which is an absolutely indispensable step and which we have supported  and the need for supervisory colleges to operate for cross-border groups. There are more controversial aspects there, which are not completely resolved. The European Commission was left to make legislative proposals. What exists so far are political agreements on the configuration of supervision in the coming years, the idea and political pressure to start operating in 2010. But the European Commission has its own responsibility to convert these proposals into legislative projects. In the future of the Eurosystem there is one aspect that will be addressed at another session of this Conference and on which I would also like to leave a word. This is the legal problem, which has been resolved at legal level, of the rotation of voting rights in the Governing Council as a result of the enlargement of the euro area. It has always been made to ensure that monetary policy should be decided by as small a body as possible and, at the same time, representative of the euro area as a whole, which could pose difficulties when the euro area had a very large enlargement and the principle of "a man (woman) a vote" remained. The issue has already been legally resolved and there has been no talk of this in recent times. I do not think that there will be any problem from a practical point of view, even if there is enlargement. When the number of Governors of national central banks is 18 or more, governors who have the right to vote will vote, but the important thing is that all Governors, even during short periods in which they do not have the right to vote, are still able to participate in the activities of the Council and, therefore, to be able to influence with their analysis the decisions that may be taken. I would finally conclude on four topics, saying, first, that Banco de Portugal and the country were well prepared for the single currency and the Eurosystem. Secondly, the results in the first 10 years of the Eurosystem were generally positive and positive for Portugal. Thirdly, participation in the single currency is not a panacea: the fundamentals, structural conditions and quality of policies and attitudes of economic actors are decisive. Finally, in the coming years, the requirements will not be lower. The crisis isn't over yet. We need to manage and emerge from the crisis and the economic downturn in the near future. The ECB and the Eurosystem will therefore continue to be involved. On the other hand, lessons will need to be learned from the crisis  for banks, the financial system and the authorities. Thank you so much for your attention. (1) This text constitutes an edited version of the oral presentation made with the support of a set of slides, which are reproduced in the annex.
