Title: Address by Mr. Carlos Costa on the occasion of his taking office as Governor of Banco de Portugal
text: Address by Mr. Carlos Costa on the... Address by Mr. Carlos Costa on the occasion of his taking office as Governor of Banco de Portugal 07 Jun. 2010 7 June 2010 Minister of State and Finance, Secretaries of State, Chairman of the Board of Auditors of Banco de Portugal, Members of the Advisory Board of Banco de Portugal, Vice-President of the European Central Bank, Dear colleagues, Members of the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal, Ladies and Gentlemen, I am truly grateful for the Governments trust in me, expressed through the invitation to become Governor of Banco de Portugal, the central bank of the Portuguese Republic and member of the European System of Central Banks and the Eurosystem. This independent and much respected Portuguese institution has long served the country and it is a great honour for me to become its Governor. Today, the Banks main concern is the maintenance of stability  that of prices and of the national financial system, through its capacity as supervisor of credit institutions, financial companies and payment institutions, and as a member of the National Council of Financial Supervisors. I am all the more honoured by this appointment since it has come at a particularly demanding time for both the country and the institution itself. We are currently facing challenges which the international financial crisis is posing for central banks in general, and for the European System of Central Banks and Banco de Portugal in particular. The international financial crisis that broke out in August 2007 was to become the severest crisis of the last 75 years and has recently taken on a particularly virulent form in the euro area, where it brought about a sudden disruption in the balance and in the principles established just two months ago. The Portuguese economy and its banking system then bore the brunt. There are lessons to be drawn from the way events have unfolded, though it is too early to foresee just how extensive the fallout will be. The international crisis has highlighted many things. Firstly, it is that a successful price stability policy is crucial for sustained economic growth, but it does not alone ensure financial stability; secondly, it has demonstrated that financial instability may lead to severe macroeconomic imbalances, and it is for this reason that financial stability must be the second major objective of a central bank; thirdly, it has shown that financial stability requires a range of macro-prudential instruments that take into account the fact that systemic effects cannot be detected by prudential supervision of each financial intermediary as a separate entity; and finally, it has illustrated how safeguarding the stability of a financial system in a context of globalisation and cross-border financial integration requires concerted international action by supervisory authorities in the countries involved, and this covers defining prudential rules, monitoring compliance by financial institutions, and solving the problems that emerge. We stand therefore in the midst of an international financial crisis which has underlined and strengthened the role played by central banks in creating the conditions essential to underpin sustained development: price stability and financial stability. These conditions are indeed necessary but they are not sufficient: their impact on sustained development hinges on other economic policies, budgetary and structural among them, and on their consistent articulation with monetary and financial stability policies. In short, the international financial crisis has reminded us how important central bank functions are for the fostering of sustained development. Firstly, it is the task of central banks  and in our case the Eurosystem  to ensure the price stability necessary for guaranteeing the real value of income and savings, for minimising financing costs, with the variations of risk premia in mind, and for setting the compass to optimal resource allocation. Since their establishment, the ECB and the Eurosystem, which includes Banco de Portugal, have fulfilled their mandate, which has been to ensure that the annual average inflation rate holds firm below 2%. For Member States which, like Portugal, adopted the euro after a long period of much higher inflation, integration within a monetary area enjoying price stability has been instrumental in improving financing conditions for corporations and households, in terms of both price and volume. This has brought in its wake the capacity to take on more debt. The economic and social players, however, were in general quicker to take up the benefits of participation in the euro than they were to respect the rules on wage and price formation consistent with price stability. On the back of this has come an economy slacker on competitiveness and with an added drawback  the emergence of new players with wage cost advantages. A start has indeed been made on addressing this problem, but a solution for the Portuguese economy has yet to be found. Restoring competitiveness in the tradable goods sector is indispensable for ensuring sustainable economic growth and job creation. This means that price stability, which is a prerequisite for deconstructing the uncertainty of savers and investors, also requires economic agents (corporations and households) to come more quickly to an understanding of the need for curbs on the wage and price formation process; in parallel, it requires greater reliance on the increase in value added per unit of output, either by raising productivity or by rapidly transforming the tradable goods productive sectors and racking up efficiency in non-tradable sectors. The current account balance deteriorated as a result of a specific combination: on the one hand, easier access to financing and greater exposure to debt among economic agents; and on the other, faltering competitiveness. The result was an economy with higher external public and private indebtedness. On top of this, there was another factor: the structural shortfall in domestic savings, where the situation has in fact worsened, as a result of the fact that the public accounts have leeched with the impact of the international financial crisis and of the budgetary measures introduced to stem the crisis and shore up economic recovery. The great challenge now facing the euro area in general and the Portuguese economy in particular is the combination of deteriorating external financing requirements in some of the areas Member States, above all those posting a structural shortage of domestic savings, with financial markets more focused on and concerned with the sustainability of mounting indebtedness  especially, though not exclusively, for public agents  as well as tighter conditions for external financing. It is urgent to make it clear to external financing agents that the countrys indebtedness is sustainable. This requires gradual but determined adjustment of external financing requirements to the severe restrictions now being faced, and as the trust that financial agents have in the country ebbs away, so will these restrictions be tightened. A guarantee needs to be flagged to the markets, and this necessarily involves a more solid bedrock of domestic savings, both private and public, and an economy showing improved competitiveness. The cornerstones of sustained growth in the Portuguese economy are consistent and credible public deficit cuts, increased private savings and buoyant exports. It therefore follows that the great advantages of price stability and participation in the euro area, so quickly taken on board by economic agents, must perforce be matched by an adjustment in the behaviour of wage formation and income distribution. The pace of this adjustment, in the current international crisis, must be decisively and credibly ratcheted up, since otherwise Portuguese economic recovery will be jeopardised. Secondly, as I mentioned at the start, the present international financial crisis has shown that financial stability is a prerequisite for price stability, with central banks responsible for monitoring the stability and efficiency of the financial system, which is the cornerstone of a modern economy. An efficient and stable financial system is a necessary condition for fostering domestic savings and ensuring they are channelled into financing economic agents and rationalising investment. The credibility and efficiency of the financial system are two key features in proper financing for corporate and household requirements, ensuring volumes and maturities that mesh with the nature of the investments; they are also key features in promoting the optimal allocation of resources and thereby the returns on savings. And so it is that the international financial crisis has drawn our attention again to the fact that financial system stability has an impact on other sectors. It is a public good that cannot be left to self-regulation by financial institutions; nor does it simply happen as a result of supervision that focuses on individual institutions as separate entities. In economies where financing comes chiefly via credit operations through the banking system, two of the factors that enhance the capacity to attract and channel savings are a pro-active approach and quality from the financial system supervisor. This is particularly important for those agents that do not have access to capital markets or international financing, such as small and medium-sized companies and it is all the more relevant in economies like the Portuguese, where the banking system plays a fundamental role, not only in funding investment but also in attracting external savings that make up for the structural deficit in domestic savings. As I mentioned earlier, the stability of the Portuguese financial system is the second main objective of Banco de Portugal. The issue can be broken down into various tiers: microprudential, macro-prudential and European supervision, along with participation in the provision of new prudential rules. With regard to the first level  micro-prudential supervision  I need only say that the Portuguese financial system is sound. It was not directly exposed to the so-called subprime crisis and it took advantage of an initiative stemming from Banco de Portugal to increase its own funds to what is, in international terms, a very acceptable cushion. Be that as it may, there is room for improvement in the accuracy and the quality of the supervision applied to each and every institution in the system. First and foremost, therefore, the supervision of financial institutions must be reinforced and carried through as an ongoing process, using teams already set up on site in some institutions, with the broadening of this practice to the main institutions in the financial system. This will make it possible to acquire a more direct and profound knowledge of the supervised entity and of its risk profile. Close ongoing supervision analyses the nature of business lines and the risks in various financial products; it covers the process of identifying, assessing and managing the different types of risk (among them credit, market, liquidity, interest rate, exchange rate and operational risk); and it provides an appraisal of the organisation and management model. A thorough assessment of all the implications for the institution has to be made, in particular as regards the taking on of risk, complex vehicles, and securitisation and re-securitisation transactions, the aim being to ensure that such risks are correctly reflected in the institutions balance sheets and adequately covered by own funds. Finally, it is necessary to check whether the institutions remuneration schemes do not hamper its very sustainability. Secondly, micro-prudential supervision has to apply the principle of systematic doubt, so that it can, among other things, carry out a role that is counter-cyclical. The fact that a financial institution is coming in with good performance does not mean that permanent oversight of that institution can be dispensed with: a constant check is needed on the soundness of its fundamentals, its future risks and the way these are recorded on its balance sheet. Thirdly, it is important to take into account that the more thorough the internal auditing, control and compliance mechanisms of each institution, the better the quality and reliability of micro-prudential supervision; and the same is true the more adequate the governance model of the supervised financial institution, both from the perspective of risk assessment, acceptance and monitoring, and also that of its accountability; and the same is also true, as recent experience bears witness, the more competent and responsible the external audit. The micro-prudential supervision carried out by Banco de Portugal must include a clear definition of the competences and responsibilities of the various control levels of financial institutions. Finally, the confidence of savers and investors in the banking system must be bolstered, through clear characterisation of the financial products on offer, including withdrawal conditions, the risks involved and the method used to calculate return. The current international financial crisis has shown that the information supplied to savers or investors has not always been complete or suitable to their level of financial literacy; moreover, investors sometimes select a financial product and either ignore the risk involved, or assume that the risk is covered by insurance mechanisms that do not in fact exist. With regard to the second level of supervision  systemic or macro-prudential  it should be noted, as I mentioned earlier, that developments are occurring in this area all round the globe. The international crisis that began in 2007 brought an awareness that the decision-making processes in financial institutions do not take into account the externalities that result from their actions; therefore, supervision must assess the resilience of the system, i.e. its capacity to absorb such externalities while keeping on an even keel. Thus, for instance, in August 2007, there were default and volatility rates, risk premia and asset ratings which, if considered in isolation in specific financial institutions, would make it impossible to anticipate subsequent developments, as a self-amplifying chain reaction took hold. In this context, where Portugal is concerned, the work undertaken by the National Council of Financial Supervisors must continue and be further developed. As for the third level  European and international supervision  it is necessary to bear in mind that systemic risk has a cross-border nature and that, as a consequence, it requires a concerted response at both European and international levels. This has already given rise to an array of institutional innovations and proposals for new prudential rules. Banco de Portugal has addressed these developments, which are part of a process under way that must continue to be carefully monitored, with the sustained credibility of domestic financial institutions hinging on it. The cumulative effect of the proposals under discussion must be duly examined, with consideration, among other things, of the role of banks in financial intermediation, and therefore the overall impact on the economy. What must be ensured is a level playing field, taking into account the specific nature of business models and the nature of associated risks. On the one hand, there must be the guarantee that the increase in banking intermediation costs is in line with the nature and the assessment of the risks to be covered and, on the other, that the emergence of nonregulated financial intermediation is not being encouraged, giving rise to a new systemic problem. It needs to be understood that supervision may involve costs, but it produces a public good. Finally, as regards the reformulation of prudential regulations, Banco de Portugal will continue to monitor the existing legal framework, building on the information gathered in the exercise of both micro-and macro-prudential supervision, ensuring in particular that the scope of supervision covers all banking institutions and products and that the prudential treatment involved is commensurate with the associated risks, and a level playing field guaranteed. This means that in the coming years Banco de Portugal will have to face major challenges in the field of prudential supervision, not only at a domestic and European level, but also more generally at an international level. Therefore, Banco de Portugal will continue to acquire the skills and the organisation models required to guarantee timely, effective and independent micro-prudential supervision (while questioning preconceived ideas where necessary); it will continue with its ongoing assessment of systemic risks; and it will continue to play an active part in domestic macro-prudential supervisory mechanisms. At the same time, its capacity to dissect and discuss the new prudential supervisory rules and models must be further enhanced, in order to maximise its influence in the various European fora in which the Bank participates. Banco de Portugal not only watches over the stability of the financial system, but also over the smooth operation of payment systems. This is an important component of the transaction costs borne by economic agents, and is particularly relevant in an open economy like the Portuguese. In fact, it is impossible to conceive today of a modern economy without electronic payment systems, and the Portuguese system is widely acknowledged as excellent. In this field, Banco de Portugal and the institutions participating in Portuguese payment systems are currently facing a number of challenges that require special attention. Firstly, there are the effects of the transposition of the Payment Services Directive  in particular greater competition in the provision of payment services  and this has given rise to new areas which have brought increased responsibility for Banco de Portugal. Secondly, there is the implementation of the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA), with public authorities specifically urged by the ECOFIN Council to prove that they fully intend to push the migration process forward by drawing up integrated and coordinated national plans for the full migration of domestic public administrations to SEPA rules, products and services. Thirdly, there is the launch of the TARGET2 Securities platform, which will significantly change the role of the national central banks of the Eurosystem in the area of post-trade settlement services for securities transactions, bringing about European harmonisation unprecedented in this type of markets. Finally, I would like to mention the implementation of new payment processors, the new payment technologies (such as the Internet and mobile phones) and increasing innovation in the retail payments market, particularly with the development of the e-Payments Framework. This will require a considerable increase in the role played by Banco de Portugal in payment systems oversight, especially regarding the risk control mechanisms in these systems and the production of relevant statistical information. Minister of State and Finance, Secretaries of State, Chairman of the Board of Auditors of Banco de Portugal, Members of the Advisory Board of Banco de Portugal, Vice-President of the European Central Bank, Ladies and Gentlemen, In short, Banco de Portugal is now facing a number of challenges that will test the capacity of both its Board of Directors and staff, but I firmly believe that these challenges will continue to be successfully met. My belief is based on three factors: the culture of Banco de Portugal and the levels of excellence and reputation achieved within the Eurosystem; the work carried out by Professor Vitor Constancio and the other members of the Board of Directors in addressing current challenges; and, last but not least, the quality and commitment that have always been displayed by the staff of the Bank. Firstly, Banco de Portugal is an institution with unparalleled reputation and credibility. These two features have proved to be invaluable at times when the country was confronted with change and even turbulence. For over 160 years, Banco de Portugal has never failed to make a decisive contribution to the countrys stability and prosperity. Secondly, Professor Vitor Constancios further enhancement of prudential supervision is either already in place or in the pipeline. I would like to take this opportunity to congratulate our outgoing Governor and current Vice-President of the European Central Bank, wishing him every success in his new post. Professor Constancio, it is really an honour for our country that you have taken on this important position at the ECB. Finally and no less important for that, I would like to mention the quality and commitment of the Banks staff. All organisations must adapt to the challenges around them, by acquiring new skills and reshaping work organisation matrices. Throughout its history, Banco de Portugal has more than proved its capacity to respond effectively to challenges. Its adaptation to the demanding criteria for participation in the Eurosystem was particularly noteworthy. In the space of a few years, there were many departments in Banco de Portugal deemed to be among those with the best quality and reputation in the Eurosystem  from support areas, such as IT, and traditional activities, such as treasury and issue, to more specialised departments, such as economic research, markets and statistics, which are directly involved in monetary policy definition, implementation, monitoring and analysis. This is what leads me to believe that Banco de Portugal will once again prove that it is an agile and responsive institution, living up to its commitments, enjoying prestige both at home and internationally and attracting the most talented professionals. Both I and fellow members of the Board of Directors count on the dedication of all staff to achieve this aim. As a final note, I would like to stress that it is a pleasure to chair a Board comprising members with the highest moral and professional standards, as is the case of the current members of the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal. Carlos da Silva Costa Lisbon, 7 June 2010

Title: Statement to the press by the Governor of Banco de Portugal on the results of the stress testing exercise undertaken by Portuguese banks
text: Statement to the press by the Gover... Statement to the press by the Governor of Banco de Portugal on the results of the stress testing exercise undertaken by Portuguese banks 23 Jul. 2010 Banco de Portugal and the Committee of European Banking Supervisors (CEBS) published today, on the respective websites, the results of a stress testing exercise carried out on four Portuguese banking groups (Caixa Geral de Depositos, Banco Comercial Portugues, Espirito Santo Financial Group and Banco BPI). This EU-wide exercise was coordinated by CEBS, in cooperation with the European Central Bank (ECB) and with the direct participation of the national supervisory authorities of each EU country. The aim of the exercise was to assess the resilience of a representative group of EU banks to an extremely adverse, but plausible, scenario. As a whole, the Portuguese banking groups that were tested, directly or indirectly represent approximately three quarters of the total assets of the Portuguese banking system in 2009, of which two thirds are directly covered by Banco de Portugal. The results published today confirm the soundness of the Portuguese banking system under a very adverse scenario, confirming the conclusions of the stress testing exercises conducted by Banco de Portugal on a periodic basis. It can therefore be concluded that: First and despite the impact of the extremely adverse scenario on the profitability and solvency levels of the institutions subject to the tests, the four Portuguese banking groups met a Tier 1 target capital ratio of more than 6%, both in 2010 and 2011 (for the purposes of the exercise, this figure was considered the benchmark ratio that ensures financial soundness). Consequently, there is no need to reinforce the capital position of Portuguese banks. With regard to the adverse scenario, this stress test was developed assuming the materialisation of a large number of risk factors that I will now describe. Hence, significant falls in stock prices were considered, which translated into devaluations of the banks share portfolios. Second, an interest rate risk was introduced by applying haircuts to the sovereign debt in the trading book of banks. This means that the assessment of sovereign risk by the market was factored into the exercise, but not the possibility of default of EU countries. Hence, the sovereign debt held in the trading book was reassessed taking as a basis the maximum levels of government bond spreads of each EU country compared to Germany since 7 May 2010. It should be recalled that European sovereign debt markets experienced strong turbulence in this period, which was particularly acute in some countries. In addition, the deterioration of sovereign exposures, mirrored in the significant rise in the interest rates of Treasury bonds over this two-year horizon, was also indirectly reflected in estimates of the private sectors loan losses. Third, a fall in real estate prices was also considered. This hypothesis, which was assumed by Banco de Portugal although the evidence available points to the non-existence of an overvaluation in the housing market in Portugal, confirms the severity of the scenario used for Portuguese banks. Four, the exercise assumed an increase in the probability of default of the private sector, which would result from the impact of faltering economic activity, increasing unemployment and rising interest rates. Finally and according to the usual practice in the stress tests conducted by Banco de Portugal, account was also taken of the impact of the adverse scenario on the financial position of the pension funds of bank employees, which is a specific feature of the Portuguese banking system. In sum, taking on board all the above mentioned risk factors, the results obtained confirm that the four Portuguese banks subject to this stress testing exercise  accounting for a very considerable share of total banking system assets  would withstand a severe additional materialisation of risks, at both global and national level. Even in such an adverse scenario, the four Portuguese banks that were involved in the tests would continue to show adequate solvency levels, measured in particular by the respective Tier 1 ratios. Carlos da Silva Costa Lisbon, 23 July 2010

Title: Speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the 1st Conference of the Central Balance Sheet: "Companies and Economic Growth"
text: Speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the 1st Conference of the Central Balance Sheet: "Companies and Economic Growth" 10 jan. 2011 Intervention by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at 1st Conference of the Banco de Portugal Balance Sheet Center Lisbon, 10 January 2011 The assessment of the Portuguese economic situation and the understanding of the need for adjustment with which we are faced cannot and should not be subsumed as mere implications of the international financial crisis. To do so would be reductive and misleading. It would mean losing sight of the unsustainable trajectory of both public debt and the trajectories of our country's foreign debt and international investment position. The international financial crisis only anticipated the inevitable: the need for fiscal consolidation and reduction of the external imbalance of the Portuguese economy, with the inherent implications in macro and microeconomic terms. On the other hand, summarizing the country's economic problems to the need for fiscal consolidation and reducing the external imbalance would also be reducing. It would mean losing sight of the Portuguese economic problem resulting from the lack of a sustained development process, i.e. a development process that determines the increase in value added per asset, job creation and the reduction of the unemployment rate, within a framework of sustainability of public finances and the international investment position. A macroeconomic adjustment process that is limited to fiscal consolidation and the reduction of the external imbalance, and thus does not include a process of re-emptive of the Portuguese economy on a path of sustained development, is an ephemeral response. It does not attack the background issues that determine imbalances and therefore tends to be an episode of a stop-and-go cycle. I therefore believe that it is imperative to look at the immediate challenges of the Portuguese economy against the background of a sustained development strategy, i.e. in a consistent framework of economic policies that has the need to continue to increase value added by asset, job creation and the sustainability of public finances and external debt at the same time. An increase in value added by assets that is not accompanied by job creation and reduced unemployment is not sustainable: it creates socio-economic imbalances that put pressure on public finances and social cohesion and end up determining political unsustainability. An increase in value added by asset and employment that is not accompanied by the sustainability of public finances and/or external debt is also not sustainable: the increase in future taxation or the difficulty of external financing end up determining a reduction in domestic demand and, consequently, the reversal of the job creation process and the increase in the unemployment rate. Finally, the sustainability of public finances and the net external position is a function not only of the levels of public deficits and the external deficit but also of the trajectory of potential growth, i.e. the evolution of value added by asset and the level of employment. This means that we must keep in mind that the Portuguese economy is now facing a wider problem than fiscal consolidation and the external deficit, even though these restrictions are more active and therefore more visible. The Portuguese economy is faced with five imperatives: 1. Sustainability of public finances; 2. Increased the savings rate of households and the self-financing rate of companies; 3. Strengthening the marketable goods sector; 4. Rationality in resource allocation and investment decisions; 5. Safeguarding and strengthening the stability of the financial system. I have already had the opportunity to refer to issues relating to the sustainability of public finances, the increase in the savings rate of households and the safeguarding and strengthening of the stability of the financial system. Therefore, in view of the theme of this seminar, Today I will focus on the need to strengthen the rate of self-financing of enterprises, strengthen the sector producing transactionable goods and more rationality in the allocation of resources and investment decisions. In general with the understanding of the matter, the following three points should be made in mind. Firstly, Portuguese companies now have levels of indebtedness that are much higher than the European average and make them very vulnerable to both cyclical fluctuations and the cost of financing. This vulnerability is accentuated in a serious way when companies are confronted with a reduction in the credit supply of the financial system. This situation is a reflection of results distribution practices that do not favour self-financing and credit policies that do not sufficiently take into account debt levels. The liquidity constraint that the sovereign risk crisis has induced in the Portuguese financial system and the new prudential models of risk assessment impose a change in the indebtedness practices of Portuguese companies. They need to increase their levels of self-financing and increase equity. Secondly, the Portuguese business structure is today a reflection of an internal, public and private demand, which favored the expansion of the supply of non-transferable goods. This development was a reflection, on the one hand, of the volume of public investment in the area of infrastructure and the modernization and development of utilities services, following the privatization process; and, on the other hand, it was a reflection of the ease of access of households to mortgage credit, both in terms of volume and price, induced by the integration of the Portuguese economy into EMU. This development has created an imbalance between the transactionable goods sector and the non-transactionable goods sector, which has been aggravated by the external deficit. The unsustainability of the international investment position of the Portuguese economy today imposes a rebalancing between the sectors producing non-transactionable goods and transactionable goods. The non-transactionable goods sector will suffer from the adjustment of domestic demand, both public and private. The response of the transactionable goods sector is not mechanical. It depends not only on external demand but also on the supply available and its competitiveness, both in terms of cost and quality. That is, it depends on the response of companies and, in particular, on the entrepreneurial capacity of the country. It is therefore important to understand what this dependence on available supply and entrepreneurial capacity means. The efficiency of the combination of inputs depends on the vision of those who organize them and gives them purpose, that is, of companies. It is a reality where values, behavioral patterns and knowledge are crossed, both tacit and formal. A changing reality, depending on the internal balances and their surroundings. That is, depending on the nature and quality of the contract that binds the actors that make up the organisation and depending on the perception of threats or opportunities resulting from the evolution of markets, technological developments and the emergence of new competitors. This means that seeking only the rebalancing between the sectors producing non-transactionable goods and producing transactionable goods as a result of the adjustment of domestic demand would not guarantee the replacement of a sustained development path. In the absence of a proportionate response from companies, stimulating the production of transactionable goods and services, we can see an unsustainable path of reducing the external deficit with worsening unemployment and income. Therefore, the behavior and strategy of companies take on a critical nature in solving the structural problems of the Portuguese economy. This is the key theme of my intervention: business and economic growth. We need to review the obstacles and idiosyncrasies of organization that limit the ability to respond to the threats and opportunities of the environment: the ability to absorb knowledge and technologies and to capture and process relevant information. Some of these factors are specific to the company, reflect its culture, the personality of the entrepreneur, in particular its entrepreneurial sense and aggregation of wills, the perception of the objectives of the organization by its members and the formal and tacit qualifications of these. The other part depends on the environment in which the company operates: values and patterns of behavior; quality of public institutions and policies; quality of physical infrastructure; nature and efficiency of the financial system; nature and purpose of associative mechanisms; availability of services and information relevant to the decision-making process of companies, among others. In this area, two areas are particularly relevant. The first area relates to the system of resolving emerging economic and financial conflicts, such as those related to the protection of intellectual property, the resolution of insolvency situations and, more generally, the guarantee of compliance with contracts. It is worth mentioning the conflicts resulting from the labor area, where it is necessary to find ways to reconcile the flexibility and metamorphosis of the organization, condition of its survival in the market, and the protection of the worker, which implies the ability of the company to adjust to changes in the respective framework. The second area has to do with the nature, quality and purpose of the so-called national innovation system, that is, the triangle formed by the subsystems of education, vocational training and research and technological development. It is demonstrated that a country's national innovation system should take into account that country's distance from the technological frontier; whereas the link between the three subsystems determines the efficiency of their financing; that the purpose of the system and the three subsystems (the answer to the question to educate, train and investigate for what?) and the agenda that commands them determines the intensity and nature of the innovation process and that the latter commands the speed of adjustment to competition and market developments as well as the anticipation of opportunities. Thus, the quality of the national innovation system is a fundamental factor in the sustained development process, as it determines the creation of value and the extent of job creation. An innovation system exclusively focused on incremental innovation tends to generate productivity increases in progressively more mature sectors and, by the maturity of markets, reduce the incorporation of the work factor. Thus, the quality of the development process is determined not only by the nature of the allocation of the investment of companies but also by the quality and nature of the national innovation system. Education, vocational training and professional research are such critical factors for the sustained development process that they cannot be given to themselves. They are a matter of national interest that, in particular, is of interest to the business fabric, the future of which determines. The availability of macroeconomic and sectoral statistical information is also one of the factors that decisively affect the quality and opportunity of business decisions. Banco de Portugal's provision of statistical information tailored to the needs of companies is thus part of creating conditions conducive to the development of companies and, in particular, to better substantiate decisions. In this context, the information from Banco de Portugal's Balance Sheet Center is a very useful tool for companies. It allows them to be situated in relation to their peers, surpassing the opacity inherent in the aggregation of statistics. It allows them to be situated in relation to the distribution for each of the indicators. Given the exhaustive coverage that characterizes the statistics of banco de Portugal's Central Balance Sheet, the information they transmit is even more relevant. It induces a dynamic of strategic review of each company according to its position in each of the indicators and thus creates a virtuous dynamics at the level of the sector or subsector, with a perimeter that can be adjusted according to the nature and relevance of the issue. In a view, the path of sustained development requires more than the expansion of the marketable goods sector to compensate for the contraction of the non-transactionable goods sector. It requires mobility in terms of products, technologies and markets that overcomes the threat of new competitors or the obsolescence of technologies. Part of this momentum results from the company's own strategy, namely from investment options and its organization to absorb technologies and detect opportunities. However, a significant part depends on the environment in which the company operates, in particular on the incentives and the quality of the tangible and intangible factors within its reach. It depends, in particular, on the nature, quality of the institutions and public goods provided to it. Lisbon, 10 January 2011 Carlos da Silva Costa
text_original: Interveno do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa na 1 Conferncia da Central de Balanos: "As Empresas e o Crescimento Econmico" 10 jan. 2011 Interveno do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa na 1 Conferncia da Central de Balanos do Banco de Portugal Lisboa, 10 de Janeiro de 2011 A avaliao da situao econmica portuguesa e a compreenso da necessidade de ajustamento com que estamos confrontados no podem nem devem ser subsumidas como meras implicaes da crise financeira internacional. Faz-lo seria redutor e enganador. Significaria perder de vista que so insustentveis tanto a trajectria da dvida pblica como as trajectrias da dvida externa e da posio de investimento internacional do nosso pas. A crise financeira internacional apenas antecipou o inevitvel: a necessidade de consolidao oramental e de reduo do desequilbrio externo da economia portuguesa, com as inerentes implicaes em termos macro e microeconmicos. Por outro lado, resumir os problemas econmicos do pas  necessidade de consolidao oramental e de reduo do desequilbrio externo tambm seria redutor. Significaria perder de vista que o problema econmico portugus resulta da falta de um processo de desenvolvimento sustentado, isto , um processo de desenvolvimento que determine o aumento do valor acrescentado por activo, a criao de emprego e a reduo da taxa de desemprego, num quadro de sustentabilidade das finanas pblicas e da posio de investimento internacional. Um processo de ajustamento macroeconmico que se limite  consolidao oramental e  reduo do desequilbrio externo, e que, assim, no se inscreva num processo de reposio da economia portuguesa numa trajectria de desenvolvimento sustentado, constitui uma resposta efmera. No ataca as questes de fundo que determinam os desequilbrios e, por isso, tende a ser um episdio de um ciclo stop-and-go. Por isso, considero que  imperativo perspectivar os desafios imediatos da economia portuguesa tendo como pano de fundo uma estratgia de desenvolvimento sustentado, isto , num quadro consistente de polticas econmicas que tenha presente a necessidade de prosseguir simultaneamente o aumento do valor acrescentado por activo, a criao de emprego e a sustentabilidade das finanas pblicas e da dvida externa. Um aumento do valor acrescentado por activo que no seja acompanhado de criao de emprego e da reduo do desemprego no  sustentvel: gera desequilbrios socioeconmicos que exercem presso sobre as finanas pblicas e a coeso social e acabam por determinar a insustentabilidade poltica. Um aumento do valor acrescentado por activo e do emprego que no seja acompanhado da sustentabilidade das finanas pblicas e/ou da dvida externa tambm no  sustentvel: o aumento da tributao futura ou a dificuldade de financiamento externo acabam por determinar a reduo da procura interna e, por consequncia, a reverso do processo de criao de emprego e o aumento da taxa de desemprego. Por ltimo, a sustentabilidade das finanas pblicas e da posio externa lquida  funo no s dos nveis dos dfices pblicos e do dfice externo mas tambm da trajectria do crescimento potencial, isto , da evoluo do valor acrescentado por activo e do nvel de emprego. Isso significa que temos de ter presente que a economia portuguesa est hoje confrontada com um problema mais vasto do que a consolidao oramental e o dfice externo, no obstante serem essas as restries mais activas e, por isso, mais visveis. A economia portuguesa est confrontada com cinco imperativos: 1. Sustentabilidade das finanas pblicas; 2. Aumento da taxa de poupana das famlias e da taxa de auto-financiamento das empresas; 3. Reforo do sector dos bens transaccionveis; 4. Racionalidade na afectao de recursos e nas decises de investimento; 5. Salvaguarda e reforo da estabilidade do sistema financeiro. Tive j oportunidade de me referir s questes relacionadas com a sustentabilidade das finanas pblicas, o aumento da taxa de poupana das famlias e a salvaguarda e o reforo da estabilidade do sistema financeiro. Por isso, e tendo em conta o tema deste seminrio, vou hoje concentrar-me na necessidade de reforo da taxa de autofinanciamento das empresas, de reforo do sector produtor de bens transaccionveis e de maior racionalidade na afectao dos recursos e nas decises de investimento. Para se entender o que est em causa, importa ter presentes os seguintes trs pontos. Em primeiro lugar, as empresas portuguesas tm hoje nveis de endividamento que so muito superiores  mdia europeia e que as tornam muito vulnerveis tanto s flutuaes cclicas como ao custo de financiamento. Esta vulnerabilidade acentua-se de forma grave sempre que as empresas so confrontadas com uma reduo da oferta de crdito do sistema financeiro. Esta situao  o reflexo de prticas de distribuio de resultados que no privilegiam o auto-financiamento e de polticas de crdito que no tm suficientemente em conta os nveis de endividamento. A restrio de liquidez que a crise do risco soberano induziu no sistema financeiro portugus e os novos modelos prudenciais de avaliao de risco impem uma alterao das prticas de endividamento das empresas portuguesas. Estas tm de aumentar os seus nveis de auto-financiamento e reforar os capitais prprios. Em segundo lugar, a estrutura empresarial portuguesa  hoje o reflexo de uma procura interna, pblica e privada, que favoreceu a expanso da oferta de bens no transaccionveis. Este desenvolvimento foi o reflexo, por um lado, do volume de investimento pblico na rea das infra-estruturas e da modernizao e do desenvolvimento de servios da rea das utilities, no seguimento do processo de privatizao; e, por outro lado, foi o reflexo da facilidade de acesso das famlias ao crdito hipotecrio, tanto em termos de volume como de preo, induzida pela integrao da economia portuguesa na UEM. Este desenvolvimento gerou um desequilbrio entre o sector de bens transaccionveis e o sector de bens no transaccionveis, que teve como contrapartida um agravamento do dfice externo. A insustentabilidade da posio de investimento internacional da economia portuguesa impe hoje o reequilbrio entre os sectores produtores de bens no transaccionveis e de bens transaccionveis. O sector de bens no transaccionveis sofrer com o ajustamento da procura interna, tanto pblica como privada. A resposta do sector de bens transaccionveis no  mecnica. Depende no s da procura externa como da oferta disponvel e da respectiva competitividade, tanto em termos de custo como de qualidade. Isto , depende da resposta das empresas e, em particular, da capacidade empreendedora do pas. Importa, por isso, entender o que significa esta dependncia da oferta disponvel e da capacidade empreendedora. A eficincia da combinao dos factores de produo depende da viso de quem os organiza e lhes d finalidade, isto , das empresas. Trata-se de uma realidade onde se cruzam valores, padres comportamentais e conhecimentos quer tcitos quer formais. Uma realidade mutante, em funo dos equilbrios internos e da sua envolvente. Isto , em funo da natureza e da qualidade do contrato que vincula os actores que integram a organizao e em funo da percepo das ameaas ou das oportunidades que resultam da evoluo dos mercados, dos desenvolvimentos tecnolgicos e da emergncia de novos concorrentes. Isto significa que procurar apenas o reequilbrio entre os sectores produtores de bens no transaccionveis e produtores de bens transaccionveis, em resultado do ajustamento da procura interna, no garantiria a reposio de uma trajectria de desenvolvimento sustentado. Na ausncia de uma resposta proporcionada das empresas, estimulando a produo de bens e servios transaccionveis, podemos assistir a uma trajectria insustentvel de reduo do dfice externo com agravamento do desemprego e do rendimento. Por isso, o comportamento e a estratgia das empresas assumem uma natureza crtica na resoluo dos problemas estruturais da economia portuguesa.  este o tema-chave da minha interveno: as empresas e o crescimento econmico. Temos de rever os obstculos e as idiossincrasias de organizao que limitam a capacidade de resposta s ameaas e s oportunidades da envolvente: a capacidade para absorver conhecimentos e tecnologias e para captar e processar informao relevante. Parte destes factores so especficos da empresa, reflectem a sua cultura, a personalidade do empresrio, nomeadamente o seu sentido empreendedor e de agregao de vontades, a percepo dos objectivos da organizao por parte dos seus membros e as qualificaes formais e tcitas destes. A outra parte depende do meio em que a empresa opera: valores e padres de comportamento; qualidade das instituies e polticas pblicas; qualidade das infraestruturas fsicas; natureza e eficincia do sistema financeiro; natureza e finalidade dos mecanismos associativos; disponibilidade de servios e de informao relevante para o processo de deciso das empresas, entre outros. Neste domnio, so particularmente relevantes duas reas. A primeira rea tem a ver com o sistema de resoluo dos conflitos econmicos e financeiros emergentes, como, por exemplo, os relacionados com a proteco da propriedade intelectual, com a resoluo de situaes de insolvncia e, mais geralmente, com a garantia de cumprimento dos contratos. So de destacar os conflitos resultantes da rea laboral, onde se torna necessrio encontrar formas de conciliar a flexibilidade e a metamorfose da organizao, condio da respectiva sobrevivncia no mercado, e a proteco do trabalhador, que implica a capacidade da empresa para se ajustar s mudanas do respectivo enquadramento. A segunda rea tem a ver com a natureza, qualidade e finalidade do chamado sistema nacional de inovao, isto , o tringulo formado pelos subsistemas da educao, formao profissional e da investigao e desenvolvimento tecnolgico. Est demonstrado que o sistema nacional de inovao de um pas dever ter em conta a distncia desse pas relativamente  fronteira tecnolgica; que a articulao entre os trs subsistemas determina a eficincia do respectivo financiamento; que a finalidade do sistema e dos trs subsistemas (a resposta  questo educar, formar e investigar para qu?) e a agenda que os comanda determina a intensidade e a natureza do processo de inovao e que este ltimo comanda a rapidez de ajustamento  concorrncia e  evoluo dos mercados bem como a antecipao de oportunidades. Desse modo, a qualidade do sistema nacional de inovao constitui um factor fundamental do processo de desenvolvimento sustentado, na medida em que determina a criao de valor e a extenso da criao de emprego. Um sistema de inovao exclusivamente voltado para a inovao incremental tende a gerar acrscimos de produtividade em sectores progressivamente mais maduros e, por fora da maturidade dos mercados, reduzir a incorporao do factor trabalho. Assim, a qualidade do processo de desenvolvimento  determinada no s pela natureza da alocao do investimento das empresas como pela qualidade e natureza do sistema nacional de inovao. Educao, formao profissional e investigao profissional so factores to crticos para o processo de desenvolvimento sustentado que no podem ficar entregues a si prprios. So uma matria de interesse nacional que, em particular, interessa ao tecido empresarial, cujo futuro determina. A disponibilidade de informao estatstica macroeconmica e sectorial constitui igualmente um dos factores que condicionam decisivamente a qualidade e a oportunidade das decises empresariais. A disponibilizao por parte do Banco de Portugal de informao estatstica ajustada s necessidades das empresas faz assim parte da criao de condies propcias para o desenvolvimento das empresas e, em particular, de uma melhor fundamentao das decises. Neste contexto, a informao da Central de Balanos do Banco de Portugal constitui uma ferramenta muito til para as empresas. Permite-lhes situarem-se relativamente aos seus pares, ultrapassando a opacidade inerente  agregao das estatsticas. Permite-lhes situarem-se relativamente  distribuio para cada um dos indicadores. Tendo em conta a cobertura exaustiva que caracteriza as estatsticas da Central de Balanos do Banco de Portugal, a informao que transmitem  ainda mais relevante. Induz uma dinmica de reviso estratgica de cada empresa em funo do seu posicionamento em cada um dos indicadores e, desse modo, cria uma dinmica virtuosa ao nvel do sector ou de subsector, com um permetro que pode ser ajustado em funo da natureza e da pertinncia da questo. Em suma, a trajectria de desenvolvimento sustentado requer mais do que a expanso do sector de bens transaccionveis que compense a contraco do sector de bens no transaccionveis. Requer a mobilidade em termos de produtos, tecnologias e de mercados que supere a ameaa de novos concorrentes ou a obsolescncia de tecnologias. Parte desta dinmica resulta da prpria estratgia da empresa, nomeadamente das opes de investimento e da sua organizao para absorver tecnologias e detectar oportunidades. Todavia, uma parte significativa depende do meio em que a empresa opera, nomeadamente dos incentivos e da qualidade dos factores tangveis e intangveis que esto ao seu alcance. Depende, em particular, da natureza, da qualidade das instituies e dos bens pblicos que lhe so proporcionados. Lisboa, 10 de Janeiro de 2011 Carlos da Silva Costa

Title: Intervention of Administrator Teodora Cardoso at the Conference "Portugal 2011: Come the Fund or Go to the bottom?": "Economic and Monetary Union  Still crazy after all these years?"
text: Intervention of Administrator Teod... Intervention of Administrator Teodora Cardoso at the Conference "Portugal 2011: Come the Fund or Go to the bottom?": "Economic and Monetary Union  Still crazy after all these years?" 31 jan. 2011 Previous point: the title of the conference (See the Fund, or go to the bottom?) If we want to be taken seriously, we should be careful with the sound bites. This can be interpreted as revealing a dangerous and media-recurring attitude, but it reflects much more the weakness of political institutions than the country's real ability to define and accept the measures necessary to correct imbalances and promote development. In fact, whatever resource we have to make to international support, only what we ourselves are able to take on and carry out can defend us from "going to the bottom". To claim that the measures we must take are imposed on us only denotes political weakness and leads to rapid reversal of policies as soon as the situation changes, even when the fundamental interest of the country requires their maintenance. It was not the intention of the conference organisers to defend such an interpretation, but there is always the risk that (second) meaning of the titles will eventually overlap with the content and, in this case, it is important to avoid it. EMU: A crazy passion? The origins Here we have another sound bite to demystify. EMU was indeed a visionary idea, but it was also an idea based on great realism. When Tommaso Padoa-Schioppa published in 1987 the report entitled Efficiency, Stability and Equity: Strategy for the Evolution of the Economic System of the European Community, it made clear the point (which had already been proven) of the impossible coexistence between freedom of trade, capital mobility, the independence of monetary policies and the maintenance of exchange rate stability, ensured by the European Monetary System (EMS). Given the importance of exchange rate stability for the completion of the single market and its relevance to ensuring Europe a position in the global context afforded to its economic and political weight, the factor to be sacrificed would have to be the independence of national monetary policies. Underlining the reasonableness of that conclusion was the fact that that independence was already virtually non-existent, even in the circumstances then prevailing. The SME crisis of the early 1990s would then prove it. It was, however, clear that moving to the single currency meant much more than the loss of independence of monetary policies. In addition, strong coordination of fiscal policies and the adoption of structural policies compatible with the new macroeconomic framework were required. All this was widely discussed in time. The Stability and Growth Pact was adopted to discipline fiscal policies, while successive initiatives were being taken in structural matters, with emphasis on the malograde "Lisbon Strategy". Adopted in 2000, with the stated objective of "making Europe the most competitive and competitive knowledge-based economy in the world" by 2010, it would eventually become a symbol of the ineffectiveness of European policies in this area. As for the Stability Pact, it did not have much better luck, although progress on budgetary discipline was greater than that achieved in the structural area. Political misconceptions But if the idea was not crazy and if its constraints were recognized, why were they not obeyed? A political explanation was widely discussed from the outset: the need to make a monetary union work, a much greater degree of political union is needed. The defence of a federalist solution never managed, however, to gain sufficient traction and, when the Amsterdam Treaty was discussed(2), it had become taboo to simply mention the term "federal". The historical, sociological and political foundations of such evolution have been addressed in thousands of pages. Another reason, more accidental but well known to the social sciences, deserves, however, a prominent place: it results from the unintended consequences to which the adoption of the single currency gave rise. In contradiction with its own objectives, it has resulted in reducing the pressure on acceding countries, both in terms of budgetary discipline  due to flaws in the design and implementation of the Stability Pact  and in relation to the structural policies necessary to ensure their competitiveness in a framework where the use of exchange rate devaluations would no longer be possible. Of course, the importance of these two factors was largely due to the inability of financial markets to distinguish the implied risk in the debts of the different euro area countries, aggravated throughout the 2000s by the widespread tendency towards undervaluation of financial risks. The low level of interest rates and risk premiums, on the one hand, and the growing competitiveness demands on the international market have thus accommodated strategies that based economic growth, employment and budgetary discipline itself (seen through the prism of the Stability Pact) on the expansion of domestic demand. The housing booms in Ireland and Spain are testament to this and show how those indicators (including the government debt ratios themselves (3)) can be volatile when they are not accompanied by a broader and more in-depth analysis of the factors that are at their origin. In the light of this experience, Europe is now seeking to improve its governance methods, particularly in the budgetary field. Better coordination in this area is certainly necessary, but the same is true of better coordination of economic policies themselves and none of them exempts each country from taking responsibility for its own policies, respecting the framework in which it is part, both at European and global level. Portugal In the case Portuguese, it is clear that the problem is not only budgetary. Unlike Ireland and Spain, it is also not the result of a housing boom: the demand for fiscal adjustment, which became clear in 2001 and led to a decade of almost economic stagnation, has prevented this problem. However, we have persisted for too long in ignoring the structural shortcomings of the economy and, above all, in not making the pedagogy indispensable to address them. Even when we made important reforms, we were sure not to give them too much to highlight, aware of their unpopularity and choosing not to fight it. We therefore continue not only to see politicians, commentators and market analysts demanding the reforms we have already made, but also  which is more serious  backing away from the obstacle of completing them and giving them the coherence and visibility they need, not only to convince markets, but above all to stimulate job and productivity growth. Budgetary problems have largely resulted from this, with budgetary stimulus for internal demand being the role of securing growth, ignoring productivity and thus reinforcing the undesirable side of the effects of the sudden fall in interest rates resulting from integration into the single currency. It is therefore up to us that it is our greatest responsibility to solve the problems that directly affect us. Participation in EMU has enormous advantages in this context. It gives us some time to make the necessary adjustment: in its absence, the loss of access to debt markets in 2010 would have had catastrophic consequences. We must, however, recognise that we have already lost most of the time  and the capacity for funding  that we had and, therefore, we must now accept the difficulties and see how to overcome them. The stability of the currency also assures us that the value of the debt  public and private  is not subject to the foreign exchange risk that, outside EMU, would throw it to unaffordable levels. The essential issue that remains unresolved is to promote the allocation of the country's resources to competitive activities at the global level, attracting for them both national and foreign investment. This means that it is necessary to assume once and for all the opening up of the economy, which makes a coherent reform programme indispensable, capable of motivating the country  and especially the most qualified young people  to attract international investors and to convince nationals to bet on openness and competition, instead of protecting and capturing regulatory power. Such a programme must include promoting competition in non-transactional sectors, continuing and extending administrative simplification efforts, tax and labour policies, improving public finance management, strengthening public administration, etc. But above all it must reveal coherence of purpose and conviction as to its usefulness. Programmes of measures attributed to pressure from external entities may, as with imf stabilisation programmes, solve financing crises in the in the short term but, if they are not prepared and firmly promoted internally, they cannot solve the problems we now face and which combine the need to simultaneously reduce the indebtedness of all sectors of the economy  not just the State  and foster their sustained growth. Lisbon, 31 January 2011 Teodora Cardoso (1) Presentation on the panel under this title integrated in the IDEFF Conference, Portugal 2011: Come the Fund or Go to the bottom? The opinions expressed do not hold Banco de Portugal responsible. (2) Signed in 1997, the Amsterdam Treaty replaced the Maastricht Treaty which in 1992 introduced the single currency. (3) In 2007, the government debt ratios of Ireland and Spain were 25% and 36% of GDP respectively, compared with 65% for Germany. The European Commission's most recent forecasts for 2011 amount to 107% for Ireland and 70% for Spain (76% for Germany).

Interveno da Administradora Teodora Cardoso na Conferncia "Portugal 2011: Vir o Fundo ou Ir ao fundo?": Unio Econmica e Monetria  Still crazy after all these years?" 31 jan. 2011 Ponto prvio: o ttulo da conferncia (Vir o Fundo, ou ir ao fundo?) Se queremos ser levados a srio, devemos ter cuidado com os sound bites. Este pode ser interpretado como revelando uma atitude perigosa e recorrente em termos mediticos, mas que reflecte muito mais a fraqueza das instituies polticas do que a capacidade real do pas para definir e aceitar as medidas necessrias para corrigir os desequilbrios e promover o desenvolvimento. Na verdade, seja qual for o recurso que tenhamos de fazer ao apoio internacional, s aquilo que ns prprios formos capazes de assumir e de levar a cabo nos poder defender de ir ao fundo. Alegar que as medidas que devemos tomar nos so impostas apenas denota fraqueza poltica e conduz  rpida reverso das polticas logo que a conjuntura muda, mesmo quando o interesse fundamental do pas exige a sua manuteno. No era inteno dos organizadores da Conferncia defender tal interpretao, mas h sempre o risco do (segundo) sentido dos ttulos acabar por sobrepor-se ao contedo e, neste caso, importa evit-lo. A UEM: Uma paixo louca? As origens Aqui temos um outro sound bite a desmistificar. A UEM foi, de facto, uma ideia visionria, mas foi tambm uma ideia assente num grande realismo. Quando Tommaso Padoa-Schioppa publicou, em 1987, o relatrio intitulado Efficiency, Stability and Equity: Strategy for the Evolution of the Economic System of the European Community, tornou claro o ponto (que j antes tinha provado) da impossvel coexistncia entre a liberdade de trocas comerciais, a mobilidade dos capitais, a independncia das polticas monetrias e a manuteno da estabilidade cambial, at a assegurada pelo Sistema Monetrio Europeu (SME). Dada a importncia da estabilidade cambial para a realizao do mercado nico e a relevncia deste para assegurar  Europa uma posio no contexto global proporcionada ao seu peso econmico e poltico, o factor a sacrificar teria de ser a independncia das polticas monetrias nacionais. A sublinhar a razoabilidade desta concluso estava o facto de essa independncia ser j praticamente inexistente, mesmo nas circunstncias ento prevalecentes. A crise do SME do incio da dcada de 1990 viria depois a comprov-la. Era, porm, claro que avanar para a moeda nica implicava muito mais que a perda de independncia das polticas monetrias. A par delas, exigia-se uma forte coordenao das polticas oramentais e a adopo de polticas estruturais compatveis com o novo enquadramento macroeconmico. Tudo isto foi amplamente discutido a seu tempo. O Pacto de Estabilidade e Crescimento foi adoptado com vista a disciplinar as polticas oramentais, enquanto sucessivas iniciativas foram sendo tomadas em matria estrutural, com destaque para a malograda Estratgia de Lisboa. Adoptada em 2000, com o objectivo declarado de, at 2010, tornar a Europa a economia baseada no conhecimento mais dinmica e competitiva do mundo, acabaria por tornar-se no smbolo da ineficcia das polticas europeias nesta rea. Quanto ao Pacto de Estabilidade, no teve muito melhor sorte, embora o progresso em matria de disciplina oramental fosse superior ao conseguido na rea estrutural. Os equvocos polticos Mas, se a ideia no era louca e se as suas condicionantes foram reconhecidas, porque razo no foram elas obedecidas? Uma explicao poltica foi largamente discutida desde o incio: a necessidade de, para fazer funcionar uma unio monetria, ser necessrio um muito maior grau de unio poltica. A defesa de uma soluo federalista nunca conseguiu, porm, ganhar suficiente traco e, aquando da discusso do Tratado de Amsterdo (2), tornara-se j tabu a simples meno do termo federal. Os fundamentos histricos, sociolgicos e polticos de tal evoluo j foram tratados em milhares de pginas. Uma outra razo, mais acidental, mas bem conhecida das cincias sociais, merece, todavia, um lugar de destaque: resulta ela das consequncias no desejadas a que a adopo da moeda nica deu origem. Com efeito, em contradio com os seus prprios objectivos, esta teve como resultado reduzir a presso sobre os pases aderentes, tanto em matria de disciplina oramental  devido a falhas de concepo e de implementao do Pacto de Estabilidade  como em relao s polticas estruturais necessrias para assegurar a sua competitividade num enquadramento em que deixara de ser possvel o recurso s desvalorizaes cambiais.  claro que a importncia destes dois factores deveu muito  incapacidade dos mercados financeiros para distinguir o risco implcito nas dvidas dos diferentes pases da rea do Euro, agravada ao longo da dcada de 2000 pela generalizada tendncia para a subvalorizao dos riscos financeiros. O baixo nvel das taxas de juro e dos prmios de risco, por um lado, e as exigncias crescentes em matria de competitividade no mercado internacional vieram, assim, a acomodar estratgias que assentavam o crescimento econmico, o emprego e a prpria disciplina oramental (vista pelo prisma do Pacto de Estabilidade) na expanso da procura interna. Os booms imobilirios da Irlanda e da Espanha so disso testemunho e mostram como aqueles indicadores (incluindo os prprios rcios de dvida pblica (3)) podem ser volteis, quando no so acompanhados de uma anlise mais alargada e aprofundada dos factores que esto na sua origem. Face a essa experincia, a Europa procura agora melhorar os seus mtodos de governncia, em particular no domnio oramental. A melhor coordenao nessa rea  certamente necessria, mas o mesmo  verdade da melhor coordenao das prprias polticas econmicas e nenhuma delas dispensa que cada pas assuma a responsabilidade pelas suas prprias polticas, respeitando o enquadramento em que se insere, tanto no plano europeu como global. Portugal No caso portugus,  evidente que o problema no  s oramental. Ao contrrio da Irlanda e da Espanha, tambm no  o resultado de um boom imobilirio: a exigncia de ajustamento oramental, que se tornou clara em 2001 e conduziu a uma dcada de quase estagnao econmica, evitou-nos esse problema. Persistimos, todavia, por demasiado tempo, em ignorar as deficincias estruturais da economia e sobretudo em no fazer a pedagogia indispensvel para as resolver. Mesmo quando fizemos reformas importantes, preocupmo-nos em no lhes dar muito realce, conscientes da sua impopularidade e optando por no a combater. Continuamos, por isso, no s a ver polticos, comentadores e analistas de mercados a exigir nos reformas que j fizemos, como  o que  mais grave  a recuar perante o obstculo de as completar e lhes dar a coerncia e visibilidade necessrias, no s para convencer os mercados, mas sobretudo para estimular o crescimento do emprego e da produtividade. Os problemas oramentais resultaram em boa parte da, tendo cabido aos estmulos oramentais  procura interna o papel de garantir o crescimento, ignorando a produtividade e reforando assim o lado indesejvel dos efeitos da descida sbita das taxas de juro resultante da integrao na moeda nica. , por isso, a ns que compete a maior responsabilidade na soluo dos problemas que directamente nos atingem. A participao na UEM apresenta, neste contexto, enormes vantagens. Proporciona-nos algum tempo para levar a cabo o ajustamento necessrio: na sua ausncia, a perda de acesso aos mercados da dvida em 2010 teria tido consequncias catastrficas. Temos, no entanto, de reconhecer que j perdemos a maior parte do tempo  e da capacidade de financiamento  de que dispnhamos e, por isso, agora h mesmo que aceitar as dificuldades e que ver como ultrapass-las. A estabilidade da moeda garante-nos, alm disso, que o valor da dvida  pblica e privada  no est sujeito ao risco cambial que, fora da UEM, a atiraria para nveis incomportveis. A questo essencial que continua por resolver  a de promover a atribuio dos recursos do Pas a actividades competitivas no plano global, atraindo para elas tanto o investimento nacional como o estrangeiro. Para isso  necessrio assumir, de uma vez por todas, a abertura da economia, o que torna indispensvel um programa coerente de reformas, capaz de motivar o Pas  e sobretudo os jovens mais qualificados , de atrair os investidores internacionais e de convencer os nacionais a apostarem na abertura e na concorrncia, em lugar da proteco e da captura do poder regulatrio. Um tal programa tem de incluir a promoo da concorrncia nos sectores no transaccionveis, a continuao e extenso dos esforos de simplificao administrativa, as polticas fiscal e laboral, a melhoria de gesto das finanas pblicas, o reforo da administrao pblica, etc. Mas tem sobretudo de revelar coerncia de propsitos e convico quanto  sua utilidade. Programas de medidas atribudas  presso de entidades externas podem, como sucedeu com os programas de estabilizao do FMI, resolver crises de financiamento no curto prazo mas, se no forem preparados e convictamente promovidos a nvel interno, no podem resolver os problemas que agora enfrentamos e que combinam a necessidade de simultaneamente reduzir o endividamento de todos os sectores da economia  no apenas do Estado  e fomentar o seu crescimento sustentado.
