Title: Interview with Governor Carlos da Silva Costa - Daily Economic and Economic TV
text: Interview with Governor Carlos da... Interview with Governador Carlos da Silva Costa -Daily Economic and Economic TV Feb. 16. 2011 Daily Economic and Economic TV February 16, 2011 Maria Joao Avillez (MJA) - What is the situation today of our banking? What are your main weaknesses, what are the biggest defenses? Carlos Costa (CC) - The bankis solid. It's good news and a good entry into our conversation. Which means you have the capital you need for the risk you have on the balance sheet. There is a dynamic, there are risks that enter the balance sheet and others that come out... MJA -Like the tides... CC - Like the tides. These risks are very much depending on the economic situation and, therefore, in a less favourable situation, resistance must be increased. Taking the example of the tides, "who goes to sea, he is adhering ashore". In other words, banking is solid, capitalised, but it is prudent and desirable to strengthen its capital. That is why Banco de Portugal recommended that, in the case of the distribution of dividends, there should be a concern about the strengthening of capital. This is a year to strengthen capital. MJA -A welcome suggestion... CC - It was a recommendation. But she was very welcome. MJA - Advocates then the strengthening of capital? CC - Why strengthen capital? To continue to support the economy and prevent any deterioration of the situation, which delimits the scope for action, weakens it. But none of these recommendations is more than the application of such a principle of prudence: "those who go to sea, they are on shore." MJA  So when the governor of Banco de Portugal falls asleep or wakes up looking at the map of the bank, he has no chills of distress... CC - I hope I never get to the shiver of distress. We are watching, monitoring and dialoguing with the financial system. The dialogue has been good and the system is attentive to the needs that arise in a particularly adverse environment. The strategies followed by the different banks - both from the point of view of disposal of assets and the strengthening of capital, or from the point of view of selectivity/credit - shows that this fruitful dialogue, as well as the concern of Banco de Portugal in anticipating events, have had results. MJA - And how concerned are you about funding? Where and how to seek financing if deposits are weak, bearing in mind that one day there may be a limit to the "generosity" of the European Central Bank? CC - The question is very pertinent. And it is necessary to understand this: by reason of the benefits of adhering to the single currency - in particular, the fall in interest rates - the Portuguese economy has been characterised, in the last ten years, by a movement of the reduction of the savings rate of households - halved - and, at the same time, the public sector increased its deficit, especially in the final phase of the decade. This means that the internal savings rate is not enough to fund those in need of funding. Banks thus served as a pipeline, between foreign savings from capital markets and domestic financing needs. The Portuguese economy relied not only on the savings of households, but also on the financing that banks brought from capital markets, which, of course, is contingent on the evolution of the markets. As it was unfavorable it made it more difficult for banks to access the capital market... MJA -Hence the Eurosystem... CC -... which comes to support the banking system by yielding liquidity, a measure with a temporary component. And as it is not desirable for the financial system to remain indefinitely dependent on the eurosystem's liquidity-making, banks have followed guidelines to adapt credit to available financing, while also taking these liquidity needs. But none of this is done overnight. In the Nordic economies, which went through something similar in the early 1990s, this process of balancing domestic savings with financing needs took four/five years. There is to be systematic, persistent and rational, with a view to two things: to minimise the impact on the economy - the reduction of funding means a limitation of credit - and at the same time to strengthen the savings rate of households. If it increases, and if public sector funding needs diminish, obviously the impact on the business sector and the economy is less. MJA - Would you advise our Bankto go through a mergers and acquisitions process? Looking at BCP, BES, BPI, Caixa, Santander, Banif, Montepio, what does the governor of Banco de Portugal advocate? CC-The governor does not have to give advice on this matter. This is part of the strategy of each of the institutions... MJA - But should the Bank go through this process now? CC-Not necessarily, but depends on the strategy of each of the institutions. The important thing is that each of them, when launched in a merger or acquisition strategy, checks whether it has the necessary capital, generates synergies and creates enough value to remunerate shareholders. They need to remain interested in monitoring the institutions, it will be necessary to strengthen capital in order to meet the Basel requirements III. And it is still necessary to know that a consolidation process is more than the sum of balance sheets. MJA - A piece of advice, a warning, a determination? CC-In aritmetics, more with more, gives more, but in processes of this nature, can give less. Here, the only concern of the governor of Banco de Portugal is that when doing such an operation, one has to be very aware of all the difficulties of the route. And with every difficulty... your answer. The ultimate goal will be to show that "more with more, gives more", and that the probability of there being a 'less' is completely eliminated from the beginning of the operation. However, it is up to each of the financial institutions to decide what they want; it is up to shareholders to look at the value creation resulting from such an operation. If an institution decides to proceed with an acquisition process, or two institutions decide to start a merger process, there is only one major concern of Banco de Portugal: look at the business model underlying the process, verify that the new entity is solid, if it complies with all the requirements and if the business model is a model that generates more. MJA -Has been in office since June 2010. Your main concern was to give banco de Portugal all credibility again, possibly affected by the recent past? CC - I put the question in another way. My concern is not to strengthen banco de Portugal's credibility, because I do not think it had been pinched. Banco de Portugal is a very qualified machine, very capable. She faced circumstances she was not used to confronting... MJA -... For instance? CC -... for example the LBW case. MJA - Weren't you used to it? Wasn't it about supervision? CC - But an institution is an institution and its circumstance. Which means that no institution can put itself out of the moment it operates. The paradigm of supervision that served during the years preceding the great crisis was based on the idea of self-regulation. However, it was conditioned by a set of legal frameworks and practices that were not necessarily the most intrusive. Moreover - and as good as the regulator is, even with the regulatory equipment it has today, and with the new philosophy of regulation - there is no zero risk. There's always risk. Financial innovation, the need to deliver results, the interest in standing out in relation to competition necessarily leads financial institutions to live by making the most of the regulatory framework. The relationship between the regulator and financial institutions is a permanent dialectic. What happened was that the equipment and tools we had were not fully suited to what was needed. MJA - Are you also "ilibar" your predecessor Vitor Constancio? CC - I am saying that Banco de Portugal has fulfilled its function according to a practice and a conception, which has since undergone a change of 180 degrees. I repeat, I cannot put the institution out of its circumstances and that was your circumstance. MJA - If you are a personal friend of the President of the ECB, Jean-Claude Trichet, which certainly facilitates your relations and the confidence in which they arise. How does he talk to you about Portugal? What's Trichet's biggest concern for us? CC-The same as mine: to ensure that the path of adjustment of public finances is consistent; ensuring medium-term sustainability; which is credible from a market point of view. And so all he wants to know when he talks to me is if we're taking the right steps... MJA -And if the route is good... CC -... Yes, and therefore Mr. Trichet is the first interested in demonstrating the portuguese's ability to follow a consistent, adjustment route and is also the first to worry if we move away from it. But that's what you have to say to me "officially." I was trying to go a little further: have you ever heard of Trichet's more impatient outbursts about our route? CC -As it is proper to a governor of a Central Bank, he has to keep the pressure on us, just as I hope to keep the pressure on those who have to decide on public finances. MJA - And these leaders welcome their pressures? CC-They will not be seen as pressures, but as warnings, advice, indications. There is a combination of efforts to move towards the sustainability of public finances. However, it must be realised that the sustainability we have set out to make means a great effort from the point of view of adjusting the structural balance of state accounts. In other words, political determination and capacity to meet the objectives set, in a word, is necessary to implement and supervise budget implementation. A question, moreover, on which Banco de Portugal has been very attentive and has intervened. MJA - Let's talk about BPN: brand new, new life, no one believes much... I also understand that having already examined all the 'dossiers' and reports, you will not be very inclined to believe that 'everything' is left to the announcement of the need for 500 million. That is, there will be fatally damages. The governor of Banco de Portugal has veto power. Are you going to use it on this issue? CC - Our relationship with the shareholder will be advice and, at the same time, regulator. The shareholder has every interest in our valuation. If we consider that the business model is not solid enough - which means future risk - and if we make observations in this regard, we are defending the interest of the shareholder.... MJA - But LBW not only does not have a solid model, but also lives in a kind of limbo. It is not known what its future will be, but in the meantime it is exerting a competition unfair at a time when there is no money, no trust... CC - In the Assembly ofThe Republic, I used the word "quarantine". When an institution is in the situation in which the LBW has been found, it is necessary to go through a phase... MJA - But how long the quarantine? Cc -Well, this has to do with two circumstances: the fact that some issues require clarification and audits that took a long time and, secondly, the process of reprivatisation that coincided with the most difficult moment of the capital market. That is, the time in which the reprivatization initiative took place played against the success of the process itself... No, I don't want to make a judgment, it's a matter where I'd have to look in detail at how the different agents who intervened in the processo operated. The agents are qualified, they will have the best of their interest and commitment. We have to look to the future. MJA -Precisely: what future? CC - There is a network of branches, a network of employees, a set of qualifications and we have institutions interested in installing or developing in the market Portuguese. Convergence of these factors is likely to produce a useful result. I imagine that the shareholder, when he talks with us, has in his own equation the possibility of recovering a bank that will then become interesting for a buyer. In essence, it was the idea behind the reprivatisation. MJA - What about competition with the other banks? CC -I would like to draw attention to the following: the fact that the bank's management was entrusted to Caixa Geral de Depositos, which was responsible for appointing the board of directors, and the fact that CGD is a conservative institution - in terms of prices and credit practices - led to the fact that, necessarily, there was a cultural transfusion from Caixa to LBW. That explains why lBW has not pursued aggressive practices in terms of interest rates, as it came from the past, and that it has not followed them in retaining customers either. In practice, LBW lost customers, both in the area of deposits and credit, which means that it was not aggressive about the system but that it gave it market share. And that is the side, let's say, that comforts us when we question possible unfair competition. The LBW has retracted to a level which, moreover, poses a problem to the shareholder. MJA - Why? CC - A downtime means that unit production costs have become higher, which in banking is the relationship between cost and income. Operating conditions have deteriorated, and one of the challenges of LBW is to adjust costs to turnover, or to reset turnover in relation to costs, in order to become a profitable bank. An unprofitable bank is an unsustainable bank. And an unsustainable bank is not in the interest of the shareholder. But there is a dialogue that is ongoing. MJA - How do you look at your powers? There is the idea that he has been an intervening, acting governor who comes out of the silent comfort of his cabinet to publicly use the word, warning the power and the various powers, public opinion etc. Is that what you had in mind when you took the job? CC - First of all, matches my profile. I believe that the obligation of the governor of Banco de Portugal is to put at the service of the bank and then, at the service of the financial community and the country, all the resources it has to anticipate problems... MJA - A big "tell-how"? CC -... Yes, we have a radar, it won't be perfect, but there is. The first thing to do is to put it at the service of our own capacity for intervention and then at the service of the financial community and the country. That's what we've been doing. I give you an example: in September 2010 - I only call it because it is public - we sent a letter to the banks, saying that it was necessary to start a process of reducing access to ecb financing, and a number of measures were put in place. I know that such a letter surprised some market players but today, looking back, I think you agree that the reason was with us. We have also released a financial stability report, in which we have called for the need to continue to strengthen capital, not only because an adverse economic situation was coming, but also because of the need to prepare for the new Basel III rules on banks' own funds. MJA -The bankers reacted... CC -... At the time there was some surprise, but today everyone understood that we were on the right track. We issue the recommendation of the retention of dividends - and the expression is this - in the amount compatible with the effective strengthening of equity. The actors in the financial system realized that it was in everyone's interest to do that. That is, we issue recommendations that benefit everyone, benefit each one: everyone must be on a path of great stability and great solidity... MJA- Are they? CC - They are on a trajectory both in anticipation of problems and their resolution... MJA - You know this because you want to talk a lot with the banks... CC - It is true: the attitude of the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal is also based on this very frequent and very intense dialogue. I am very happy to say that whenever I express interest in talking, this occurs immediately with great availability and great frankness. There is a working logic that consists of convincing our interlocutors of the goodness of our arguments so that it does not be mistakeed by an imposition. I'd say this is more of an act of seduction than command. MJA - Speaks a lot of his interlocutors of the banking system and little of the Government. What do you have to do with him? The new internal architecture that he set up at Banco de Portugal, speeding up the machine and taking it more actively in supervision, somehow contradicted what was the idea of the Government, which maintained prudential supervision at Banco de Portugal but transferred behavioral supervision to another entity. You avenged your choice. CC - Before my inauguration there was already a project with this configuration, called twin peaks. We have the responsibility of behavioral supervision which, until further adecision, will be performed by us in an irreprehensible, agile and capable way. If, then, who can decide to understand that it is necessary to revisit projects and review them, this issue goes beyond the governor of Banco de Portugal. I defend the current model: the coexistence of behavioral and prudential supervision, side by side, but with the so-called Chinese walls, that is, without mutual interference. It will then be up to the Board of Directors to make the arbitration, because it is a higher-level interest which is the stability of the financial system. As long as behavioral supervision is with us, Banco de Portugal will exercise this competence, with the utmost diligence, maximum panache. With the certainty that the coexistence of prudential supervision with behaviour is a "more with more" that produces even more. More financial stability, more customer protection, more... MJA - A message for the government? CC - It's not up to me to decide. MJA - What are your relations with the government, with the Prime Minister, for example? How do you analyze the politician Jose Socrates? Have you had several meetings with him, how do you work? CC- All right. I would even like to stress that it has fully respected the independence and autonomy of Banco de Portugal, even when we publish less pleasant figures such as those of the last Economic Bulletin... MJA - But not when you talked about recession... CC - We are not always the messengers that everyone would like to hear, but the messenger does not modify the message. What is to be withgiven is that when it is technically grounded and has an indisputable solidity, it is worth ignoring the message. Sooner or later your content hits us. If we are saying that we are going to have a period of lower economic growth, economic recession... MJA - Are we going or are we? CC - You could say we're in recession. The dynamics of the macroeconomic variables will produce what we have said, and that the international institutions have confirmed: an economic downturn during 2011, which is the counterpart of the adjustment process, of weight loss... MJA - What can create a vicious circle, or not? CC - It depends on the questions that arise in parallel. When I take a given stimulus to the economy, I have to have a dosage of compensation, and see where I go to get new stimuli for it. In this situation, they can only come from exports. When you ask me if this is going to cause a vicious circle, it will, if the answer from the marketable goods sectors, the exporting sector, is not up to what is going to happen. The evolution of exports was indeed positive. MJA - Gone? CC-The latest data are positive, but we must also be aware that there is a cap on the capacity of exporting companies. In other words, there is a time when they have to invest, which means that the resources available have to be directed to the marketable goods sector. It also means that you need to have skilled work, an organization, where you need to get into the plan of structural development factors. MJA -Tantos "ses"... CC-But it's the "ifs" that make the policy. Doing politics is nothing but articulating and organizing the different vertices. The less they are, the less effective the result. MJA - Says that he works well with the Prime Minister and that he accepts well the guidelines of Banco de Portugal. But do you feel, or not, more comfortable working with someone with the age, characteristics and profile of finance minister Teixeira dos Santos? CC - These are different statutes and dialogue plans. With the Minister of Finance work in detail. MJA - And well, what doI know? CC- All right. MJA - Is this the government's safety peg? CC - It is someone indispensable to continue a policy of adjustment and consolidation of public finances: it was he who gave the face, who did a part of the work, until 2007. The period 2008/2009, only the Minister will be able to explain it. It is finally he who has to take - I think with great personal cost - this boat to good port. No one is more aware of what needs to be done, and of our difficulties. MJA - Can't then leave office? CC - I would say that you are a person with an awareness of the problems and the notion of what needs to be done and that, therefore, it is indispensable to the process of fiscal consolidation of the country. MJA - That's what's called a safety pin. CC - Making the appropriate declaration of interests, it is known that I have a lot of personal appreciation for Professor Fernando Teixeira dos Santos and that he is a friend, but I think I am able to distinguish the two facets. MJA - When you work with him you find someone exhausted or acabrunhado or on the contrary, a firm ruler and... CC - I frankly admire the resistance of our Finance Minister. Yes, I mean it frankly. Although I am the kind of person who when he gets up in the morning is as if he gets up on the first day, even if the day was of great concern, I think the minister overcomes me! You have to have a great animic strength to be, every day, with that energy and determination. He will perhaps do so with some weariness, but that is natural. What we have to recognize is that, from an animic point of view, he has shown a resistance that surprises me. MJA - But I have to go back: I know that the governor of Banco de Portugal was critical of the 2010 budget implementation. If it wasn't for pt's pension fund... I ask: what happened to your friend, Fernando Teixeira dos Santos, from 2007 here? CC - I leave it to him to explain. The Finance Minister is capable of a good explanation. What I want to say is that I am very much looking forward to portuguese society being able to make great progress in the adjustment processes. In other words, political, economic and social actors have to incorporate that there are no free lunches! And that this budgetary adjustment is the consequence of less discipline in the past. Sooner or later, this indiscipline would have to be paid for. MJA -But it was Teixeira dos Santos who "there" was when the "mayonnaise began to deslassar", was the conductor. If the violin or strings go off, the conductor has to have a different conduct. CC- It's true. Unless the assistance values more of an out-of-tune orchestra than tuned. And sometimes the detuning of the orchestra is induced by the indiscipline of the spectators. MJA -From the spectators? What about the drop in VAT in May 2009? What about the increases in the civil service before the latest legislative ones? CC - As you know, I advocated the creation of a Budgetary Council or an independent tax agency. We must recognise the good practices followed by Sweden, Austria, Denmark, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, and adapt them to us. And they consisted of an independent and non-politicised body that could send signals on the implications of certain proposals - on revenue and expenditure - on the balance of the budget and the sustainability of public finances. In the expectation that economic agents will be able to realize that there are no free lunches. What today seems free in the future has a price. The Minister of Finance thus takes, on the one hand, the comfort of the opinion of an independent agency on measures that have this effect of unsustainability and, on the other hand, the beacon of the macroeconomic pre-economic pre-empressives of preparing the Budget. I think your job will become easier. MJA - The institution didn't come late? CC - It should have been set up in 2000 so that macroeconomic supervision could have taken place within the European framework. It was in this sense that stability and growth programmes had been planned. But excessive confidence in the ability to continue to finance deficits has led everyone to allow themselves to be dragged into a situation where debt has grown... That is why I argue that this is an important moment in Portuguese civic culture: we are not talking about fiscal consolidation but of a change in values. And mentalities. We have to be responsible today for what's going to happen tomorrow. What we have decided today is neither innocuous nor indifferent, neither for us nor for the next generations. This adjustment process must lead to an appropriation by the Portuguese of the notion that they are responsible for their future. MJA - We have no indication at the moment that this may turn out to be so... CC - We look at resources and consider that our problem is financing, but first is values, then institutions, and thirdly, it is policies. Funding comes in last. If we look at the problem of financing in isolation from institutions, values and policies, we merely continue to do badly what we were already doing wrong. This isn't A, B or C, it's a society problem. It's ours. MJA - Is there a problem with the institutions? CC - It is necessary that Portuguese society realizes that this problem exists, that we have institutional gaps and, that is why I proposed the Budgetary Council. Today institutions are weakened, particularly in the public sector. We have a lack of staff in senior management and we have to dignify and honor it at the same time that we have to slim down the administration. And why is that? Because we must be aware that some tasks, which in the past were performed by less qualified, today, with new technologies, administration can be organized differently: with a new model of management and organization. Which isn't easy. MJA - Why is there no strength or political will to do so? CC - There are no reforms of the administration that do not involve costs: financial, political, social. It is a long-term project on which consensus must be built because without a prestigious, qualified and sized administration, public goods will not be produced or the general interest safeguarded. It is up to this administration to produce the thinking about the public goods to be produced, the general interests to be pursued, the options which will then be transformed into policies. Strong and qualified institutions reinforce the quality of dialogue between the State and civil society. The better your thinking production capacity, the better the paintings, the better the policy will be. MJA - Have we already got rid of the IMF or, fatally, will it have to come, whatever will be the model of your intervention? CC -I prefer to ask like this: do we still have the animic strength and the ability to convince the markets that we will do what we commit to? The evolution of interest is being determined by exogenous and endogenous factors. These have to do with budget implementation, the programme for consolidating public finances, growth prospects. Exogenous factors have to do with public statements, with expectations for the next European Council... MJA -Two paths? CC -Two trains. Ours, which is the path of adjustment and reduction of the budget deficit; and the European, which is what goes through the decisions of the European Council, the revision of the Stability Pact, the revision of the European governance model. If a great synchronised between our train and the European train operates, obviously we are talking from a different perspective. But we cannot just concentrate on the European train and forget that ours has to arrive at the station in time! And then we have to wait for those who run the European train to realize that there is a time to get to that station. MJA - What does it mean? CC - Means the need to reshape economic governance, to ensure greater cohesion between EU countries, proposals that have also been systematically advocated by the central banks of the euro area and the ECB. We have said that we need to the political model is up to the monetary model, and that economic policy is accompanied by the unity of monetary policy in terms of coordination. I would stress that monetary policy and central banks and the ECB have played their part in a way that probably very few observers would expect! And in a way that, when history is made, it will be considered exemplary. MJA - What can happen in March? CC - What I would like is for there to be clear results on our side in terms of budget implementation, and on the European side clear results in reaffirming the economic governance model. In view of the creation, on the part of the different observers of the European Union, the feeling that the group is cohesive and supportive and that, moreover, countries with a sustainable trajectory can be sure that any liquidity problems will not jeopardise this sustainable trajectory of public finances. MJA - How can the country face budget implementation in 2011, which involves a commitment to reduce the deficit from more than 8% to 4.6%? Do you think it's possible? CC - The governor of Banco de Portugal is there to verify, in the numbers, that it is possible to meet these objectives. We announce much more ambitious objectives than those of other Member States, and we must send the message - to partners and markets - that we are in a process of adjustment on a single and ambitious scale. But the fact that we are doing this high-risk exercise cannot serve as an excuse for not doing so. From the moment we commit, we will have to. We must therefore pay increased attention: all forces must be aware that no one takes any advantage if we do not meet the budgetary objectives. MJA -Implied: these "other forces" can not wave with instability, no motions, nor ghosts of political crises... CC - Everyone knows what the political market is, what is political logic, that is not what worries me, but the consensus that underlies this political struggle. What counts is this strong consensus that the various actors convey to the population and abroad, that there is a country and there are national objectives that must be shared. Take brazil's example: the markets did not doubt that whoever was elected President would continue to be followed a determined and firm trajectory in terms of economic policy! We must, in a word, be capable of it and fortunately there have already been signs of this, with agreements and consensus. We need to know that there are restrictions that we have to understand. It's the same thing as a family budget and its sustainability. If, then, we have differences between going to the movies or going to the theater, that's what distinguishes the options of one and the other. Now, what one and the other have to pass on to the lender is the idea of being able to fulfill a commitment. MJA - Are our banks ready for the second stress tests coming? The truth is that after the first tests - and Portugal did well - there was the Irish case. CC -Well... what is "to be prepared"? Being prepared means this: if the worst is produced, do I have an answer to this situation or not? MJA - What's the worst? CC - It is obviously a situation of a drop in gross domestic product (GDP). Therefore, a drop in significant growth, an increase in the unemployment rate and a decrease in disposable income that will affect the ability of banks' customers to honour their commitments. The worst will certainly be a stock market crash and a situation in which fixed income markets are also breaking down. MJA -But the "worst" gets closer... CC - In previous tests, the worst-case scenario was likely to occur at 5%... In the coming years, the economic crisis scenario is expected to be even more extreme, which will have a greater impact on the results of banks and their capital. I am, however, convinced that we will have the mechanisms available to say: if the worst is produced, we have an answer to this scenario. The question is not to say "if the worst is produced, there are no effects" - by definition, if it does, there will be negative effects. The question is: if the negative effects occur, are the banks able to ensure solvency, business continuity, the soundness of the system? MJA- Are they? CC - I am convinced that there will be conditions to demonstrate that we have the mechanisms available to solve an extreme situation... But watch out! We cannot rule out the worst case scenario even if there is a very low probability of it being produced! In a context where investors are suspicious of the European financial system -not Portuguese - and when capital markets are important for the continuation of the financial system's activity, it is normal for confidence requirements to be met and for the system to show that it is in a position to meet them. That's what we have to demonstrate. MJA - From the governor of Banco de Portugal one should not hear words of extreme pessimism that lead to defeatism or disbelief. But beyond what you say "officially," are you, in your heart, worried? CC - In my heart? I am convinced of three things: first, the financial system has already assumed the need to prepare and is doing so. Then the Portuguese authorities, and particularly the Ministry of Finance, are aware of the possible need for new support mechanisms. Thirdly, I am convinced that the business model and the nature of the Portuguese financial system puts it in a relatively less unfavorable situation than most international financial systems. MJA - Why? CC - Because it was not hit by the subprime crisis. It had no toxic assets, unlike other... Northern European financial systems have applied excess savings to toxic assets. Portugal, because it did not have excess savings, did not have these luxuries and passed the test. And we have passed another, very important one: our financial system is not conditioned by a housing bubble, unlike in third countries. Finally, about 80% of the financial system Portuguese is made up of institutions of comparable size. The other institutions have their own characteristics, but they are not today a cause for concern from the point of view of the adequacy of capital and from the point of view of the business model. The only Achilles heel is a reflection of the insufficiency of internal savings, is the need to resort to the outside to access funding. It is through the way of obtaining funding that we have a very active restriction today, and it is by this way that there can be the transmission to the Portuguese economy of a difficulty in financing. But banks are conducting their strategy to minimise the impact on credit, especially On SMEs.

Entrevista ao Governador Carlos da Silva Costa -Dirio Econmico e Econmico TV 16 fev. 2011 Dirio Econmico e Econmico TV 16 de Fevereiro de 2011 Maria Joo Avillez (MJA) -Qual a situao, hoje, da nossa banca? As estratgias seguidas pelos diferentes bancos -quer do ponto de vista de alienao de activos e do reforo de capitais, quer do ponto de vista da selectividade/crdito -mostra que esse frutfero dilogo, bem como a preocupao do Banco de Portugal em antecipar os acontecimentos, tm tido resultados. MJA -E qual o seu grau de preocupao com o funding? Onde e como buscar financiamentos se os depsitos esto fracos, tendo em ateno que um dia poder haver um limite para a "generosidade" do Banco Central Europeu? CC -A questo  muito pertinente. E  preciso perceber o seguinte: por fora dos benefcios da adeso  moeda nica -em particular, a descida das taxas de juro -a economia portuguesa caracterizou-se, nos ltimos dez anos, por um movimento da reduo da taxa de poupana das famlias -passou para metade -e, ao mesmo tempo, o sector pblico incrementou o seu dfice, sobretudo, na fase final da dcada. O que significa que a taxa da poupana interna no chega para financiar os que tm necessidade de financiamento. Os bancos serviram assim de pipeline, entre a poupana externa vinda dos mercados de capitais e as necessidades de financiamento interno. A economia portuguesa contou no s com as poupanas das famlias, mas com o financiamento que os bancos trouxeram dos mercados de capitais, o qual, obviamente, est contingente  evoluo dos mercados. Como ela foi desfavorvel tornou mais difcil o acesso dos bancos ao mercado de capitais... MJA -Da o Eurosistema... CC -... que surge a apoiar o sistema bancrio cedendo liquidez, uma medida com uma componente temporria. Nas economias nrdicas, que passaram por algo idntico no incio dos anos noventa, esse processo de balanceamento da poupana interna com as necessidades de financiamento levou quatro/cinco anos. MJA -Aconselharia que a nossa Banca passasse por um processo de fuses e aquisies? Olhando para o BCP, BES, BPI, Caixa, Santander, Banif, Montepio, o que advoga o governador do Banco de Portugal? MJA -No estava habituado? No se tratava de superviso? CC -Mas uma instituio  uma instituio e a sua circunstncia. O que significa que nenhuma instituio se pode colocar fora do momento em que actua. O que sucedeu foi que os equipamentos e as ferramentas de que dispnhamos no estavam totalmente adequados quilo que era necessrio. MJA -Est tambm a " ilibar" o seu antecessor Vtor Constncio? CC -Estou a dizer que o Banco de Portugal preencheu a sua funo de acordo com uma prtica e com uma concepo, a qual sofreu entretanto uma alterao de 180 graus. Repito: no posso pr a instituio fora da sua circunstncia e a sua circunstncia era essa. MJA -Sei que  amigo pessoal do presidente do BCE, Jean-Claude Trichet, o que certamente facilita as vossas relaes e a confiana em que elas decorrem. Como  que ele dialoga consigo sobre Portugal? Qual a maior preocupao de Trichet em relao a ns? CC-A mesma que a minha: assegurar que a trajectria de ajustamento das finanas pblicas  consistente; que garante a sustentabilidade a mdio prazo; que  credvel do ponto de vista dos mercados. CC -Como  prprio de um governador de um Banco Central, ele tem de manter a presso sobre ns, da mesma forma que eu espero manter a presso sobre quem tem de decidir em matria de finanas pblicas. MJA -E esses responsveis acolhem bem as suas presses? CC-No sero vistas como presses, mas como avisos, conselhos, indicaes. MJA -Mas, o BPN no s no tem um modelo slido, como vive numa espcie de limbo. CC -Na Assembleia da Repblica, utilizei a palavra "quarentena". Quando uma instituio se encontra na situao em que se encontrou o BPN,  necessrio passar por uma fase... MJA -Mas at quando a quarentena? Temos a responsabilidade da superviso comportamental que, at nova deciso, ser por ns desempenhada de forma irrepreensvel, gil e capaz. MJA -Um recado para o Governo? CC -No me cabe a mim decidir. MJA -Quais so as suas relaes com o Governo, com o primeiro-ministro, por exemplo? Como analisa o poltico Jos Scrates? MJA -Tenho porm de voltar atrs: sei que o governador do Banco de Portugal foi crtico da execuo oramental de 2010. Se no fosse o fundo de penses da PT... Pergunto: que  que aconteceu ao seu amigo, Fernando Teixeira dos Santos, de 2007 para c? CC -Deixo para ele explicar. O ministro das Finanas  capaz de uma boa explicao. E os aumentos na funo pblica antes das ltimas legislativas? CC -Como sabe, defendi a criao de um Conselho Oramental ou uma agncia fiscal independente. H que reconhecer as boas prticas seguidas pela Sucia, ustria, Dinamarca, Holanda, Reino Unido, e adapt-las a ns. Ns anunciamos objectivos muito mais ambiciosos do que os de outros Estados-membros, e temos de passar a mensagem -a parceiros e mercados  de que estamos num processo de ajustamento de uma escala singular e tambm ambiciosa. H que ter, por isso, ateno redobrada: todas as foras tm de estar conscientes de que ningum tira nenhuma vantagem se no cumprirmos os objectivos oramentais. MJA -Subentendido: essas "outras foras" no podem acenar com instabilidade, nem moes, nem fantasmas de crises polticas... CC -Toda a gente sabe o que  o mercado poltico, o que  a lgica poltica, no  isso que me preocupa, mas sim o consenso que est subjacente a essa luta poltica. O que conta  esse forte consenso que os diversos actores transmitem para a populao e para o exterior, de que h um pas e h objectivos nacionais que devem ser partilhados. Olhe o exemplo do Brasil: os mercados no duvidaram que, quem quer que fosse eleito Presidente, continuaria a ser seguida uma determinada e firme trajectria, em termos de poltica econmica! Temos, numa palavra, de ser capazes do mesmo e felizmente j houve sinais disso, com acordos e consensos.  preciso saber que h restries sobre as quais nos temos que entender.  a mesma coisa que um oramento familiar e a sua sustentabilidade. Agora, o que uns e outros tm que passar para o credor  a ideia de ser capaz de cumprir um compromisso. MJA -Os nossos bancos esto preparados para os segundos testes de stress que a vm? Estar preparado significa isto: se o pior se produzir, tenho ou no resposta para essa situao? MJA -O que  o pior? CC - obviamente uma situao de quebra do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB). Portanto, uma quebra do crescimento significativa, o aumento da taxa de desemprego e uma diminuio do rendimento disponvel que afectar a capacidade dos clientes dos bancos para honrarem os seus compromissos. O pior ser, seguramente, uma quebra das bolsas e uma situao em que os mercados de rendimento fixo tambm registassem uma quebra. MJA -Mas o "pior" vai ficando mais perto...
