Nos prximos, o cenrio de crise econmica dever ser ainda mais extremo, o que significar um maior impacto nos resultados dos bancos e dos seus capitais. Estou, porm, convencido de que teremos os mecanismos disponveis para dizer: se o pior se produzir, temos resposta para esse cenrio. A questo no  dizer "se o pior se produzir, no h efeitos" -por definio, se ele se produzir, haver efeitos negativos. A questo : se os efeitos negativos se produzirem, os bancos esto em condies de assegurar a solvncia, a continuidade de negcio, a solidez do sistema? MJA -Esto? CC -Estou convencido que haver condies para demonstrar que dispomos dos mecanismos disponveis para resolver uma situao extrema... Mas ateno! No podemos excluir o pior cenrio mesmo que haja uma probabilidade muito baixa de ele se produzir! Num quadro onde existe desconfiana dos investidores relativamente ao sistema financeiro europeu -no em relao ao portugus -e quando os mercados de capitais so importantes para a continuao da actividade do sistema financeiro,  normal que se verifiquem requisitos de confiana e que o sistema demonstre que est em condies de os satisfazer.  isso que temos de demonstrar. MJA -Da parte do governador do Banco de Portugal no se devem ouvir palavras de extremo pessimismo que conduzam ao derrotismo ou  descrena. Mas, para alm do que diz "oficialmente", est, no seu ntimo, preocupado? CC -No meu ntimo? Estou convencido de trs coisas: primeiro, o sistema financeiro j assumiu a necessidade de se preparar e est a faz-lo. Depois as autoridades portuguesas, e particularmente o Ministrio das Finanas, esto atentas  eventual necessidade de novos mecanismos de apoio. Terceiro: estou convencido de que o modelo de negcio e a natureza do sistema financeiro portugus o coloca em situao relativamente menos desfavorvel do que a maioria dos sistemas financeiros internacionais. MJA -Porqu? CC -Porque no foi atingido pela crise do subprime. No tinha activos txicos, ao contrrio de outros... Os sistemas financeiros do Norte da Europa aplicaram os excessos de poupana em activos txicos. Portugal, pelo facto de no ter excesso de poupana, no tinha esses luxos e passou a prova. E passmos outra, muito importante: o nosso sistema financeiro no est condicionado por uma bolha imobiliria, ao contrrio do que sucedeu em pases terceiros. Finalmente: cerca de 80% do sistema financeiro portugus  formado por instituies de dimenso equiparvel. As outras instituies tm caractersticas prprias, mas no so, hoje, motivo de preocupao do ponto de vista da adequao dos capitais e do ponto de vista do modelo de negcio. O nico calcanhar de Aquiles  o reflexo da insuficincia da poupana interna,  a necessidade de recorrer ao exterior para aceder a funding.  pela via de obteno do funding que temos hoje uma restrio muito activa, e  por esta via que pode haver a transmisso  economia portuguesa de uma dificuldade de financiamento. Mas os bancos esto a conduzir a sua estratgia no sentido de minimizar o impacto sobre o crdito, sobretudo s PME.

Title: Intervention of Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the Seminar: "Behavioral Standards in Retail Banking"
text: Intervention of Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the Seminar: "Behavioral Standards in Retail Banking" Feb. 23. 2011 February 30, 2011 Increasing importance of retail banking behavioural supervision It is relatively recent to recognize the importance of regulating and supervising the conduct of credit institutions in the marketing of retail banking products and services, and their reporting duties towards customers. Following the international financial crisis, it was recognised that financial stability also depends on the balance between the interests of institutions and those of customers and on the sustainability of the relations between the two in retail banking markets. Behavioural supervision promotes these two elements necessary for the proper functioning and stability of the financial system, which are essential for confidence in it. The importance of behavioural supervision has increased as citizens step up their relationship with banks and other credit institutions, increasingly accessing credit and different means of payment, while making savings products available to them with different risks. The range of products marketed in these markets has expanded and become more complex, incorporating characteristics that increase your risk, make it more difficult to understand and evaluate and accentuate the asymmetry of information between customers and institutions. The relationship between clients and credit institutions is tended to be asymmetric. In general, customers have incomplete and imperfect information about the banking products they purchase and also have less financial knowledge: this limits their ability to understand the products and assess their suitability. That is why, in the absence of regulation and supervision, the non-convergence of interests between customers and institutions tends to resolve themselves, at the limit, in an unfavorable manner to the client. In the wake of the international financial crisis, it is known that the uninformed action of bank customers may jeopardise financial stability; uninformed choices can accentuate flaws in the functioning of these markets, as has happened in the subprime credit market in the USA. In this context, legislators and regulatory and supervisory authorities have been structuring systematic action based on the requirement for more transparent and accurate information on marketed products, the definition of rules for the functioning of these markets and the promotion of financial training. National legislators and the European Union itself have developed a number of regulatory initiatives in the field of consumer protection of financial products and services. Regulators have been given responsibility for the supervision of rules of conduct and principles of action, to which credit institutions must be subordinated in the marketing of their products and services, and for compliance with the legal and regulatory standards that structure the functioning of these markets. In 2010, as part of the reform of the architecture of European financial supervision, responsibilities for supervising the actions of credit institutions in their relationship with their clients were expressly assigned to the European Banking Authority (EBA) for supervising the actions of credit institutions in their relationship with their clients, confirming the importance these matters have assumed. Its supervisory powers have been conferred on it alongside prudential supervision powers, thus implicitly recognising the complementarity between these two aspects of banking supervision which contribute to the same objective: ensuring the stability of the financial system. Financial stability is an essential element of the sustained development process, taking into account the role that the financial system plays in channeling the savings accumulated by surplus agents, allocated it to productive investment. Functions assigned to Banco de Portugal In Portugal, the responsibility for supervising the performance of credit institutions in the relationship with their clients (behavioral supervision) was assigned to Banco de Portugal in the field of markets for banking products and services by Decree-Law No. 1/2008 of 3 January. This legal document revised the General Regime of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations, introducing Title VI, called "Behavioral Supervision", which provides that Banco de Portugal, in the exercise of its regulatory power, issues to credit institutions guidelines for compliance with principles of transparency of information and for the adoption of codes of conduct. In addition, banco de Portugal's supervisory and sanctioning powers have been strengthened. The current powers focus not only on the application of the regulatory standards that the Bank issues, but also on compliance with the legislation that frames the functioning of retail banking markets. Throughout 2008, the reporting duties of credit institutions defined in the General Regime and banco de Portugal's powers in the field of behavioural supervision were also strengthened, in particular in the fields of advertising; pre-contractual information, especially consumer credit; transparency of contracts and complaint management. The management of bank customer complaints is an essential element of Banco de Portugal's behavioral supervision strategy. In this matter, the Bank, an independent entity that exercises an arbitration power, today functions as an adecence body for the assessment of complaints, involving important resources in its function. Institutions should understand bank customer complaints as an opportunity to improve the quality of service provided. They should therefore analyse them in a balanced and proportionate manner, thus contributing to ensuring customer confidence in the banking system, an intangible and volatile asset which is one of the cornerstones of financial stability. The strengthening of Banco de Portugal's powers and competences has been complemented and expanded through important legislative action, in the framework of the regulation of retail banking markets, in particular in housing and consumer credit, but also in bank deposits and payment services. In most cases, these legislative initiatives have expressly given Banco de Portugal responsibility for overmonitoring the application of these same diplomas, in addition to the preparation of impact assessment reports. It is, moreover, in this context that Banco de Portugal has been asising banks and other credit institutions to report various information, and the entities supervised, in general, responded quickly. Banco de Portugal's strategy of action Banco de Portugal's strategy of action in the behavioral supervision of retail banking covers the different areas of the relationship between credit institutions and bank customers. It embodies itself around three major vectors: 1. Definition of information transparency regulations and codes of conduct in the marketing of banking products and services; 2. Supervision of compliance with the legal and regulatory system in force; 3. Information and financial training. This strategy aims at the smooth functioning of retail banking markets, promoting consumer protection, but also by stimulating greater competition between institutions, favourable to both customers and the institutions themselves. As part of this strategy, principles have been defined to comply with information transparency (accuracy, timeliness, proportionality between advantages and costs and conditions of access to those products); at the same time, in sectoral, rules have been laid down in compliance with those same principles. A set of good practice guidelines has also been structuring and shaping the actions of credit institutions in these markets. The supervision of the actions of credit institutions is also an essential component of Banco de Portugal's strategy of action, including all institutions operating in national territory  be they Portuguese, subsidiaries or branches of foreign credit institutions  all branches of institutions, all its internet sites, potentially all its over-the-counter employees. The supervisory instruments range from carrying out inspections in the institutions to verify their way of acting to the analysis of reports sent to the Bank and to the assessment of complaints and requests for information received daily by Banco de Portugal. At the same time, financial information and training have become components of Banco de Portugal's strategy of action, following the recognition of the decisive role of information and financial training in the efficient functioning of retail banking markets and in the protection of banking customers. Financial information concerns the explicitness of the characteristics and risks of these products, while financial training allows customers to improve their understanding and have a better perception of possible risks, allowing them to adapt their behaviors accordingly. But the accuracy and transparency of the information provided by institutions to their clients is not enough. It is also necessary that those who sell, in particular the banking employees who provide services to the branches, have the capacity to inform and assist the customer properly, explaining to him with accuracy and transparency the characteristics and risks of the financial products marketed by the respective institutions. Adequate information and financial training are not only payable to bank customers. First, it is a requirement that the banks of credit institutions is made, as the General Regime of Credit Institutions explains. In this way, business training and ethics are fundamental elements in the development of credit institutions' activity in retail banking. Financial training values the instruments for regulating transparency and the reporting duties of credit institutions. More informed and higher-trained clients help monitor markets and, by promoting choices better tailored to their risk profile and needs, contribute to greater stability of the financial system as a whole. The strategy and the various regulatory initiatives and projects developed by Banco de Portugal under these functions are the subject of regular public reports. Since 2008, annual reports on behavioural supervision have been published and, since 2009, interim summaries of activities have been published. The behavioral supervision of retail banking is entrusted to Banco de Portugal, which has exercised it competently and diligently. Following the recent internal reorganization of banking supervision functions, Banco de Portugal created the Department of Behavioral Supervision, in addition to the Department of Prudential Supervision and the Department of Investigation and Sanctioning Action. This model of organization ensures the coexistence of behavioral and prudential supervision, but without mutual interference. In this model, it is up to the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal that the arbitration is responsible, because it is a higher level interest: the stability of the financial system. Challenges for behavioral supervision In the current economic and financial context, it has now been recognised that behavioural supervision contributes strategically to the solvency of the banking system and to the stability of the financial system, in addition to protecting the interests of banking customers. It is in this context that banco de Portugal faces important challenges in the behavioral supervision of retail banking. The promotion of responsible conduct in access and lending and the promotion of financial literacy are increasingly important on the agenda of national and international authorities, in the context of policies to promote savings and prevent excessive credit use. This is a matter that also worries Banco de Portugal, which is therefore looking at issuing guidelines to credit institutions on the granting of responsible credit. Individual credit institutions have no incentive to adopt and continue such measures, but their implementation through the intervention of the supervisory authority generates positive externalities for each of the institutions and for the stability of the financial system as a whole, assuming characteristics of the public good. Other important projects that Banco de Portugal is preparing in the field of behavioural supervision involve the extension of regulations on reporting duties to companies, the definition of good practices to be met by credit institutions at the close of accounts, the implementation of the new payment services regime, the transposition of the electronic money directive and the revision of the cheque scheme. At the same time, Banco de Portugal, together with CMVM and ISP, within the framework of the National Council of Financial Supervisors, is implementing the National Financial Training Plan. It is also important to mention a recent initiative of Banco de Portugal: the creation of the "Forum for Behavioral Supervision", which will make known the concerns of the various agents of retail banking markets, thus involving them in the definition of the Bank's options and lines of action. This forum will include banking associations, credit institutions, consumer protection associations, business associations and relevant public entities. Banco de Portugal thus attaches great importance to the role of behavioural supervision of retail banking, considering that it contributes decisively to strengthening customer confidence in the financial system and, consequently, to ensuring its stability.
text_original: Interveno do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa no Seminrio: "Normas Comportamentais na Banca de Retalho" 23 fev. 2011 23 de Fevereiro de 2011 Importncia crescente da superviso comportamental da banca de retalho  relativamente recente o reconhecimento da importncia da regulao e fiscalizao da conduta das instituies de crdito na comercializao dos produtos e servios bancrios de retalho, e dos seus deveres de informao para com os clientes. Na sequncia da crise financeira internacional, reconheceu-se que a estabilidade financeira tambm depende do equilbrio entre os interesses das instituies e os dos clientes e da sustentabilidade das relaes que se estabelecem entre ambos nos mercados bancrios de retalho. A superviso comportamental promove estes dois elementos necessrios ao bom funcionamento e  estabilidade do sistema financeiro, essenciais para a confiana no mesmo. A importncia da superviso comportamental tem aumentado  medida que os cidados intensificam a sua relao com os bancos e com outras instituies de crdito, acedendo cada vez mais ao crdito e aos diferentes meios de pagamento, ao mesmo tempo que lhes so disponibilizados produtos de poupana com diferentes riscos. A gama de produtos comercializados nestes mercados alargou-se e tornou-se mais complexa, incorporando caractersticas que aumentam o seu risco, tornam mais difcil a sua compreenso e avaliao e acentuam a assimetria de informao entre clientes e instituies. A relao entre clientes e instituies de crdito  tendencialmente assimtrica. Em geral, os clientes possuem informao incompleta e imperfeita sobre os produtos bancrios que adquirem e tambm tm menos conhecimentos financeiros: isto limita a sua capacidade para entender os produtos e avaliar a sua adequabilidade.  por isso que, na ausncia de regulao e superviso, a no convergncia de interesses entre clientes e instituies tende a resolver-se, no limite, de forma desfavorvel ao cliente. Na sequncia da crise financeira internacional, sabe-se que a actuao no informada dos clientes bancrios pode pr em risco a estabilidade financeira; as escolhas no informadas podem acentuar falhas no funcionamento destes mercados, como sucedeu no mercado do crdito subprime nos EUA. Neste contexto, legisladores e autoridades reguladoras e de superviso tm vindo a estruturar uma actuao sistemtica, baseada na exigncia de uma informao mais transparente e rigorosa sobre os produtos comercializados, na definio de regras de funcionamento destes mercados e na promoo de aces de formao financeira. Legisladores nacionais e a prpria Unio Europeia tm desenvolvido diversas iniciativas normativas no domnio da proteco dos consumidores de produtos e servios financeiros. Aos reguladores tm vindo a ser atribudas responsabilidades pela fiscalizao de regras de conduta e de princpios de actuao, a que as instituies de crdito se devem subordinar na comercializao dos seus produtos e servios, e pelo cumprimento das normas legais e regulamentares que estruturam o funcionamento destes mercados. Em 2010, no mbito da reforma da arquitectura da superviso financeira europeia, foram expressamente atribudas  Autoridade Bancria Europeia (EBA, o novo rgo de superviso bancria) responsabilidades pela superviso da actuao das instituies de crdito na relao com os seus clientes, confirmando a importncia que estas matrias passaram a assumir. As suas competncias de superviso comportamental foram lhe atribudas a par das competncias de superviso prudencial, reconhecendo-se, assim, implicitamente, a complementaridade entre estas duas vertentes da superviso bancria que concorrem para o mesmo objectivo: a garantia da estabilidade do sistema financeiro. A estabilidade financeira constitui um elemento essencial do processo de desenvolvimento sustentado, tendo em conta o papel que o sistema financeiro desempenha na canalizao da poupana acumulada pelos agentes excedentrios, alocando-a ao investimento produtivo. Funes atribudas ao Banco de Portugal Em Portugal, a responsabilidade de superviso da actuao das instituies de crdito na relao com os seus clientes (superviso comportamental) foi atribuda ao Banco de Portugal no domnio dos mercados de produtos e servios bancrios pelo Decreto-Lei n. 1/2008, de 3 de Janeiro. Este diploma legal procedeu  reviso do Regime Geral das Instituies de Crdito e Sociedades Financeiras, introduzindo o Ttulo VI, designado de Superviso Comportamental, que prev que o Banco de Portugal, no mbito do exerccio do seu poder regulamentar, emita para as instituies de crdito normas orientadoras para o cumprimento de princpios de transparncia de informao e para a adopo de cdigos de conduta. Complementarmente, os poderes, fiscalizador e sancionatrio, do Banco de Portugal foram reforados. Os actuais poderes incidem, no s sobre a aplicao das normas regulamentares que o Banco emite, mas tambm sobre o cumprimento da legislao que enquadra o funcionamento dos mercados bancrios de retalho. Ao longo de 2008, foram ainda reforados os deveres de informao das instituies de crdito definidos no Regime Geral e os poderes do Banco de Portugal em matria de superviso comportamental, designadamente nos domnios da publicidade; da informao pr-contratual, sobretudo do crdito aos consumidores; da transparncia dos contratos e na gesto de reclamaes. A gesto das reclamaes dos clientes bancrios  um elemento essencial da estratgia de superviso comportamental do Banco de Portugal. Nesta matria, o Banco, entidade independente que exerce um poder de arbitragem, funciona hoje como instncia de recurso para a apreciao de reclamaes, envolvendo importantes recursos nesta sua funo. As instituies devem entender as reclamaes dos clientes bancrios como uma oportunidade para melhorarem a qualidade de servio prestada. Devem, por esse motivo, analis-las de forma equilibrada e proporcional, contribuindo, assim, para assegurar a confiana dos clientes no sistema bancrio, um bem intangvel e voltil que  uma das pedras angulares da estabilidade financeira. O reforo dos poderes e competncias do Banco de Portugal tem sido complementado e alargado atravs de importante actuao legislativa, no quadro da regulao dos mercados bancrios de retalho, em particular no crdito a habitao e aos consumidores, mas tambm nos depsitos bancrios e servios de pagamento. Na generalidade dos casos, essas iniciativas legislativas tm atribudo expressamente ao Banco de Portugal a responsabilidade pela fiscalizao da aplicao desses mesmos diplomas, alm da elaborao de relatrios de avaliao de impacto. , alis, neste quadro que o Banco de Portugal tem solicitado aos bancos e a outras instituies de crdito o reporte de informao diversa, tendo as entidades supervisionadas, em geral, respondido de forma clere. Estratgia de actuao do Banco de Portugal A estratgia de actuao do Banco de Portugal na superviso comportamental da banca de retalho abrange as diferentes reas da relao das instituies de crdito com os clientes bancrios. Ela corporiza-se em torno de trs grandes vectores: 1. Definio de normativos de transparncia de informao e de cdigos de conduta na comercializao de produtos e servios bancrios; 2. Fiscalizao do cumprimento do ordenamento jurdico e regulamentar em vigor; 3. Informao e formao financeira. Esta estratgia tem como objectivo o bom funcionamento dos mercados bancrios de retalho, promovendo a proteco dos consumidores, mas tambm estimulando uma maior concorrncia entre as instituies, favorvel quer aos clientes quer s prprias instituies. No mbito desta estratgia de actuao, definiram-se princpios a que deve obedecer a transparncia de informao (rigor, actualidade, proporcionalidade entre vantagens e custos e condies de acesso a esses mesmos produtos); ao mesmo tempo, sectorialmente, foram estabelecidas regras a cumprir no respeito por esses mesmos princpios. Um conjunto de orientaes de boas prticas tem tambm vindo a estruturar e a moldar a actuao das instituies de crdito nestes mercados. A fiscalizao da actuao das instituies de crdito  tambm uma componente essencial da estratgia de actuao do Banco de Portugal, abarcando todas as instituies a operar em territrio nacional  sejam elas portuguesas, filiais ou sucursais de instituies de crdito estrangeiras , todos os balces das instituies, todos os seus sites na Internet, potencialmente, todos os seus funcionrios de balco. Os instrumentos de fiscalizao vo desde a realizao de inspeces nas instituies para verificao da sua forma de actuao  anlise de reportes remetidos ao Banco e  apreciao das reclamaes e dos pedidos de informao recebidos diariamente pelo Banco de Portugal. Paralelamente, a informao e formao financeira passaram a ser componentes da estratgia de actuao do Banco de Portugal, acompanhando o reconhecimento do papel decisivo da informao e da formao financeira no funcionamento eficiente dos mercados bancrios de retalho e na proteco dos clientes bancrios. A informao financeira diz respeito  explicitao das caractersticas e dos riscos destes produtos, enquanto a formao financeira permite que os clientes melhorem a compreenso dos mesmos e tenham uma melhor percepo de eventuais riscos, permitindo-lhes adequar em conformidade os seus comportamentos. Mas o rigor e a transparncia da informao prestada pelas instituies aos seus clientes no so suficientes.  tambm necessrio que quem vende, designadamente os funcionrios bancrios que prestam servio aos balces, tenha capacidade para informar e assistir devidamente o cliente, explicando-lhe com rigor e transparncia as caractersticas e riscos dos produtos financeiros comercializados pelas respectivas instituies. A adequada informao e formao financeira no so exigveis apenas aos clientes bancrios. Trata-se, em primeiro lugar, de uma exigncia que se coloca aos quadros das instituies de crdito, como explicita, alis, o Regime Geral das Instituies de Crdito. Desta forma, a formao e a tica dos negcios so elementos fundamentais no desenvolvimento da actividade das instituies de crdito na banca de retalho. A formao financeira valoriza os instrumentos de regulao da transparncia e dos deveres de informao das instituies de crdito. Clientes mais informados e com nvel de formao mais elevado ajudam a monitorizar os mercados e, ao promoverem escolhas mais ajustadas ao seu perfil de risco e s suas necessidades, contribuem para a maior estabilidade do sistema financeiro no seu todo. A estratgia e as diversas iniciativas regulamentares e projectos desenvolvidos pelo Banco de Portugal no mbito destas funes so objecto de relatrios pblicos regulares. Desde 2008, foram publicados relatrios anuais de superviso comportamental e, desde 2009, snteses intercalares de actividades. A superviso comportamental da banca de retalho est confiada ao Banco de Portugal, que a tem exercido com competncia e diligncia. Na sequncia da recente reorganizao interna das funes de superviso bancria, o Banco de Portugal criou o Departamento de Superviso Comportamental, alm do Departamento de Superviso Prudencial e do Departamento de Averiguao e Aco Sancionatria. Este modelo de organizao assegura a coexistncia da superviso comportamental e da prudencial, mas sem interferncias mtuas. Neste modelo,  ao Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Portugal que cabe fazer a arbitragem, porque est em causa um interesse de nvel superior: a estabilidade do sistema financeiro. Desafios para a superviso comportamental No actual contexto econmico e financeiro, passou a reconhecer-se que a superviso comportamental contribui estrategicamente para a solvabilidade do sistema bancrio e para a estabilidade do sistema financeiro, para alm da proteco dos interesses dos clientes bancrios.  neste quadro que se perspectivam para o Banco de Portugal importantes desafios na superviso comportamental da banca de retalho. A promoo de condutas responsveis no acesso e na concesso de crdito e a promoo da literacia financeira assumem importncia crescente na agenda das autoridades nacionais e internacionais, no mbito de polticas de promoo da poupana e de preveno do recurso excessivo ao crdito. Esta  uma matria que tambm preocupa o Banco de Portugal, que, deste modo, est a perspectivar a emisso de orientaes para as instituies de crdito sobre a concesso de crdito responsvel. As instituies de crdito, individualmente, no tm incentivo para a adopo e prossecuo deste tipo de medidas, mas a sua implementao atravs da interveno da autoridade de superviso gera externalidades positivas para cada uma das instituies e para a estabilidade do sistema financeiro como um todo, assumindo caractersticas de bem pblico. Outros projectos importantes que o Banco de Portugal est a preparar no domnio da superviso comportamental envolvem a extenso da regulamentao sobre deveres de informao ao crdito s empresas, a definio de boas prticas a cumprir pelas instituies de crdito no encerramento de contas, a implementao do novo regime dos servios de pagamento, a transposio da directiva da moeda electrnica e a reviso do regime do cheque. Paralelamente, o Banco de Portugal, em conjunto com a CMVM e o ISP, no mbito do Conselho Nacional dos Supervisores Financeiros, est a implementar o Plano Nacional de Formao Financeira.  tambm importante referir uma iniciativa recente do Banco de Portugal: a criao do Frum para a Superviso Comportamental, que dar a conhecer as preocupaes dos diversos agentes dos mercados bancrios de retalho, envolvendo-os, deste modo, na definio das opes e linhas de actuao do Banco. Este frum integrar associaes do sector bancrio, instituies de crdito, associaes de defesa dos consumidores, associaes empresariais e entidades pblicas relevantes. O Banco de Portugal atribui, assim, grande importncia  funo de superviso comportamental da banca de retalho, considerando que contribui decisivamente para reforar a confiana dos clientes no sistema financeiro e, consequentemente, para assegurar a sua estabilidade.

Title: Summary of the address by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the debate organised by the Frum de Administradores de Empresas on the "Financing Model for the Portuguese Economy"
text: Summary of the address by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the debate organised by the Forum de Administradores de Empresas on the "Financing Model for the Portuguese Economy" 15 Jun. 2011 The Governor of Banco de Portugal, Carlos da Silva Costa, participated today, as guest speaker, in a debate organised by the Forum dos Administradores de Empresas on the Financing model for the Portuguese economy. The Governor discussed the problems of the Portuguese economy in the context of the international financial crisis, the global economic crisis and the sovereign debt crisis that affects the euro area economies. The current situation of the Portuguese economy results from major structural weaknesses and unsustainable fiscal policies, whose effects were exacerbated and magnified by the international crisis and by an incomplete economic governance model in the euro area. Globalisation and excess liquidity, resulting to a large extent from an accommodative monetary policy in the United States, translated into credit expansion without adequate risk assessment. These developments were at the origin of the sub-prime crisis and its repercussions for the banking system in northern Europe in 2007-2008, of the subsequent fiscal expansion and of the sovereign debt crisis witnessed today in the euro area peripheral economies. The euro area economic governance model proved inadequate to address the situation. This model relies on four fundamental assumptions: (i) fiscal sovereignty of the Member States; (ii) no bail-out  Member States are prohibited to assume the liabilities of other Member States; (iii) no-default  there is no mechanism in place for orderly debt restructuring; and (iv) no-exit  the possibility of leaving the Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) is not foreseen. The Stability and Growth Pact, which aimed at supplementing the governance model by imposing vigilance mechanisms and financial discipline, turned out to be insufficiently robust. This setting has brought to light the weaknesses of the Portuguese economy. These structural weaknesses are evident in the continued accumulation of debt by households, firms and the public sector, and are the counterpart to an economic development and job creation model relying on the expansion of the nontradable goods sector. In Portugal, in a context of higher risk aversion in the financial markets and an incomplete economic governance model in the euro area, the indebtedness level, low output growth and the territorial coincidence between the sovereign and the banking business resulted in the interruption of market financing to the Portuguese economy, rendering the request for financial assistance from the European Union and the International Monetary Fund inevitable. The adjustment of the Portuguese economy implies the deleveraging of the financial sector, stronger domestic savings and the rebalance of public accounts, which will necessarily translate into a contraction of domestic demand. Establishing a sustainable growth path requires the development of the tradable goods sector, which in turn calls for the implementation of reforms aimed at improving the quality of public policies and institutions, as well as at diversifying the financing sources of the economy. On the other hand, at the European level, it is crucial to strengthen the economic governance model through the creation of effective mechanisms to control financial discipline and to preserve competitiveness, guaranteeing the sustainable development of the euro area economies. These mechanisms should be supplemented by others providing liquidity to EMU countries, while coping with confidence crises in international financial markets and preventing liquidity constraints from becoming solvency problems. Lisbon, 15 June 2011

Title: Statement by the Governor of Banco de Portugal on Stress-testing exercise in the European Union: Main results for Portuguese banks
text: Statement by Governor Carlos da... Statement by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa on stress test exercise in the European Union and the main results for Portuguese banks 15 jul. 2011 The European Banking Authority (EBA), in cooperation with the European Systemic Risk Board (ESRB) and national supervisory authorities, coordinated a stress test exercise carried out by financial institutions  called a bottom-up exercise. The purpose of this exercise is to assess the resilience of financial institutions to adverse market conditions and to contribute to the overall assessment of systemic risk in the Financial System of the European Union. The exercise in question was carried out using consistent methodologies, with scenarios and assumptions developed by the EBA in cooperation with the ESRB, the European Central Bank (ECB) and the European Commission. The methodology and assumptions were established to assess the capital adequacy of banks against a core tier 1 core capital ratio of 5%. The adverse scenario was defined by the ECB and covers a two-year time horizon (2011-2012). The exercise was carried out on the assumption of static balance sheet at the level of December 2010. The financial year did not take into account either the business strategies planned by the banks or the management acts after that date and does not correspond to a forecast of the banks' results. In the Portuguese, the exercise was carried out by the four largest banking groups, and also covered the respective pension funds of bank employees. These banking groups as a whole accounted for about two-thirds of the total assets of the banking system Portuguese in 2010. It should be reported that Banco Santander Totta, which represents about 8.5 percent of the total assets of the banking system, was not included, since, being a subsidiary of Banco Santander, it was integrated into the stress test exercise carried out by Banco de Espana. This means that, overall, this exercise stress test covered about three quarters of the banking system Portuguese. Despite the particularly adverse environment in which Portuguese banks have been developing their activity and the severity of the scenario used for stress test, the results show that the Portuguese banks concerned exceed the minimum capital set for the financial year (i.e., the Core Tier 1 capital ratio of 5%), which demonstrates the resilience of the banking sector Portuguese. Nevertheless, given the importance of strengthening capital adequacy for stability and confidence in the Portuguese banking system, Banco de Portugal decided that banks should strengthen basic capital in order to overcome even more loosely the minimum that served as the basis for the exercise. In this way, all banks will be able to face adverse scenarios more safely. Finally, I would like to stress that Banco de Portugal continues to set more stringent standards, which certainly represents an additional factor of confidence in the soundness of the banking system Portuguese. Lisbon, 15 July 2011
text_original: Declarao do Governador Carlos da... Declarao do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa sobre o exerccio de stress test na Unio Europeia e os principais resultados para os bancos portugueses 15 jul. 2011 A Autoridade Bancria Europeia (EBA), em cooperao com o Comit Europeu de Risco Sistmico (ESRB) e as autoridades nacionais de superviso, coordenou um exerccio de stress test realizado pelas instituies financeiras  designado por exerccio bottom-up. Este exerccio tem por objectivo avaliar a resistncia das instituies financeiras a condies de mercado adversas, assim como contribuir para a avaliao global do risco sistmico no sistema financeiro da Unio Europeia. O exerccio em causa foi realizado usando metodologias consistentes, com cenrios e pressupostos desenvolvidos pela EBA em cooperao com o ESRB, o Banco Central Europeu (BCE) e a Comisso Europeia. A metodologia e os pressupostos foram estabelecidos para avaliar a adequao de capital dos bancos face a um rcio de capital de base, Core Tier 1, de 5%. O cenrio adverso foi definido pelo BCE e abrange um horizonte temporal de dois anos (2011-2012). O exerccio foi realizado no pressuposto de balano esttico ao nvel de Dezembro de 2010. O exerccio no tomou em considerao nem as estratgias de negcios planeadas pelos bancos nem os actos de gesto posteriores quela data e no corresponde a uma previso de resultados dos bancos. No caso portugus, o exerccio foi realizado pelos quatro maiores grupos bancrios, tendo contemplado igualmente os respectivos fundos de penses dos empregados bancrios. Estes grupos bancrios, no seu conjunto, representavam cerca de dois teros do total do activo do sistema bancrio portugus em 2010. Refira-se que o Banco Santander Totta, que representa cerca de 8.5 por cento do total do activo do sistema bancrio, no foi includo, dado que, sendo uma filial do Banco Santander, foi integrado no exerccio de stress test realizado pelo Banco de Espaa. Isto significa que, globalmente, este exerccio de stress test abrangeu cerca de trs quartos do sistema bancrio portugus. Apesar do enquadramento particularmente adverso em que os bancos portugueses tm vindo a desenvolver a sua actividade e da severidade do cenrio usado de stress test, os resultados evidenciam que os bancos portugueses em causa superam o mnimo de capital fixado para o exerccio (isto , o rcio de capital Core Tier 1 de 5%), o que demonstra a resilincia do sector bancrio portugus. No obstante, dada a importncia do reforo da adequao de capital para a estabilidade e confiana no sistema bancrio portugus, o Banco de Portugal decidiu que os bancos deviam reforar o capital de base, de forma a superar ainda mais folgadamente o mnimo que serviu de base ao exerccio. Deste modo, todos os bancos estaro em condies de afrontar com maior segurana cenrios adversos. Por ltimo, gostaria de sublinhar que o Banco de Portugal continua assim a estabelecer padres mais exigentes, o que, decerto, representa um factor adicional de confiana na solidez do sistema bancrio portugus. Lisboa, 15 Julho 2011

Title: Interview with Governor Carlos da Silva Costa - Hour H of the Business Journal
text: Interview with Governor Carlos da... Interview with Governor Carlos da Silva Costa -Hora H of jornal de Negocios 14 set. 2011 Business Journal Hour H September 14, 2011 Pedro Santos Guerreiro (PSG) -Defends a "cleanliness" of the balance sheets of banks. But that means using the state's capitalisation fund, nationalisation of banking." When we asked in this room whether some banks could be nationalised, the answer was unanimous: yes. Carlos Costa (CC) - They're totally wrong. PSG - There will be no nationalizations? CC -What will be is a participation through... First thing, there's nothing imposed here. It depends on the bank's strategy, unless there was an emergency situation, which I don't see. What will be there is a strategic option for each of the banks, namely: do I want to use the capitalization fund and position myself better for the future? Or would I rather live with a small tumor, not knowing if it's carcinogenic? PSG - No one wants to lose control of the bank to the state. CC - The recapitalisation fund does not change the shareholder control of the entities where it enters, they are merely preferred holdings. It does not alienate existing shareholders or any future investors. PSG - Bankers don't believe that. CC - This is going to come out in the law, it's going to get out in the law. PSG - The stock market capitalization of banks is so low that an intake of capital takes the state easily majority. CC - Can't. Wait for the diploma to be published by the Ministry of Finance. PSG - Politicians won't run the banks, no matter what? Cc - You are here distinguished jurists, ask them if through preferred shares someone can intervene in a bank. This was not the initial position of our interlocutors. I said and I take it: with me governor, it is not possible to have a model of participation in which the structure of shareholder control is changed or the interest of future shareholders is removed. Otherwise we would be nationalising and the aim is not to relaunch the financial system. And so there's no doubt about it, he's fine. PSG - So why the troika exam? CC - The discussion is not Portuguese. Stress tests were done and we're still suspicious in the air. To address this suspicion, there are two key issues: showing that we have the capital needed for any surprises - and that does not mean that you are waiting for surprises; and show that we have risk management and assessment models that allow us to evaluate what is in the balance sheets. In fact, there is a first information: we have accepted a second indicator on credit quality, the credit indicator at risk. We have the first information about the system and the quality of the portfolio of the financial system Portuguese, by the sample of the eight largest banks, compared with the European average. Credit coverage at risk is above the European average Banks have a problem that results from funding, which results from insufficient savings. Portuguese banks, generally speaking, have the capital they need for the business they do. However, it is natural that with a negative evolution of the economy there will be an increase in credit at risk. To address this, the BdP has insisted that capital needs to be strengthened. This corresponds to creating conditions to return to the international market. PSG - Says that with you at Banco de Portugal there will be no nationalization. It's Martim Moniz from Portuguese banking. Cc - But I don't want to die! (laughs) PSG - Is the troika's examination of the banks' credit portfolio being done a statement of no confidence in the BdP in exercising its regulatory role? Don't you feel unauthorized? CC - Our borrowers and markets have a doubt about the health of the financial system. The BdP doesn't share that doubt Doesn't mean there can be no problems here and there. Just as the market shares a doubt about the health of the European financial system. Markets have the idea that there are assets in the books that are not worth what is in accounting. The question that was posed in the assistance plans was: how are we going to eliminate this doubt? In the case of Greece and Ireland, an entity was called completely on the sidelines of the supervisor, who entered through the banks and did the exercise. That's not the case here. In Portugal, the property of the process is the BdP, which leads the steering committee that monitors the audits. If the troika had doubts about the BdP, we wouldn't trust the presidency. The first fiscal year corresponds to the auditors saying whether what is raised in the accounts corresponds to the equity situation, that is, if the photograph is right... PSG - Whether there are skeletons in the closet or not... CC - I don't think there is. Let's see, let's see. PSG - What are the risk factors? PPP's? Real estate credit? Big shareholders too indebted? CC - The question that arises is the dynamics of photography. I take the picture and then I ask how this animal will run if a thunderstorm is triggered? Is it fast? Right? Are you lame? Aren't you? It is the part relating to the stress test, the assessment of assets in stress conditions, which has to do fundamentally with the evolution of the Portuguese economy in the near future. If the evolution is very negative it is clear that the balance sheets will suffer. It is inherent in the nature of the banking business. PSG - The troika plan provides 35 billion for state guarantees to banking. What is the value used? CC - Some have been used as a precaution. As we are dependent on exogenous factors that condition the rating, we are not under a surprise. Those who are not under a surprise beware. PSG - Is the troika money enough? CC -Banks have to reduce the ratios between credit and deposits, have the economy to increase their savings rate, have the state to do the exercise of "debt de-indebtedness", and companies too. One of the variables of the process is the disposal of assets by individuals, private companies, the ESS, the State. Are we going to adjust the status quo? Let's go. How? De-indebteding the economy, de-leveraging. There are two opportunities: one, to reduce credit to the economy, and the other through the disposal of assets. What is assumed in the 78 billion is the disposal of assets that will allow to accommodate the financing of the economy and deleveraging. If the economic agents resist, we will have a problem closing the equation. PSG -The bank says it has no one to sell credit portfolios other than such discounts that gets a very large oddity and capital needs. The equation is getting insoluble... CC - It is a strategic issue of each of the institutions, which is facing a dilemma: either cuts in credit, and this will mean losing size in terms of economy, harming the efficiency ratio, and in the long term, compromising its presence in the market, or alienating assets. By alienating assets, in some cases, you will have to recognise in the present, oddities that, whether you like it or not, you will have to recognise in the future. The current dilemma facing a board today is to take over today and clean up today the balance sheet of this, I would say, a problem inherited from a more favourable economic environment, or, on the contrary, continue to live with it for a few years, harming its future profitability. The dilemma for Portuguese banks is: do we want to have bad news today and a lot of good news in the future, or do we want to continue with bad news in the future, especially with the suspicion about the reality of what is on the balance sheet? The existence of a capitalization fund is an opportunity to solve a problem, put the counters to zero and enter a sequence of interesting stories. From the point of view of the economy it is the best solution, because in the solution where the adjustment is made through financing to the economy everyone loses in a negative spiral, because the credit that I cut here is reflected in the ability to repay another credit there. PSG - Is there a risk of a credit crunch? CC - We will have to adopt measures that necessarily involve adjustments by all actors. Complacency with the absence of adjustment of one actor is paid by others. It is important to make rapid progress in streamlining businesses, particularly in the public sector, because resources will be freed up and adjustment facilitated. It is crucial to consolidate the budget. All these are pieces of a puzzle, and if one of the pieces doesn't make the move they're supposed to make, there's another one that's going to have to suffer the corresponding impact. PSG - Three years ago lehman brothers went bankrupt. A month later, then-Finance Minister Portuguese said that, "whatever happens, the Deposits of the Portuguese are guaranteed." Do you repeat this phrase today? CC- Of course. And indeed, as you know, legislation will come out to strengthen that protection. When the BdP requires banks to reinforce a core tier one, it is nothing but thinking about two things. In the interests of customers and in the stability of the financial system. Because the core tier one exists as an absorption pad in case of shock. And that's what it's for. It's just like airbags. The airbags aren't in the cars to fire every day. The purpose of capital is to prevent the shock from being transmitted to third parties. Because this is a shock with real impact on the economy. Unlike a car producer, which opens bankruptcy what remains is more market for other car producers. If in a financial system someone has difficulties, they get difficult for everyone else. So the system's interest is stability. By the way, Lehman Brothers was the best demonstration. Lehman didn't set up a business for anyone, he destroyed business for everyone. A sound financial institution is in everyone else's interest, because everyone pays the price for the lack of system soundness. When we ask for a strengthening of core tier one, risk analysis, compliance and control functions, we are thinking about customers, starting with depositors. And we're thinking of shareholders, who don't like to see capital evaporate because of any accident. Everyone has an interest in the stability of the financial system. PSG -25 years after Portugal's integration into the EEC, are we living a moment of European disintegration? CC - We're not living in any moment of disintegration. What is foreseen in the Maastricht Treaty, which was taken over by the Treaty of Lisbon, is that economic and monetary union is built on clear principles: "no exit", "no bail out", "no default" and the principle of national sovereignty in tax matters. This constriction worked very well for ten years. There is currently a deficiency in the economic arm of EMU. The only thing compatible with the Treaty is the increase in the integration process, which must be done at the point where there is a weakness: economic government. PSG - That is, the measures of the European Council for economic government. CC-The resolution of the problems we are facing will only be found if we move towards the process of further integration and revision of the economic pillar of EMU. We need to continue the decisions of 21 July of the European Council, we must realise that no mechanism had been envisaged to deal with the liquidity difficulties of an EMU member, that the mechanism that is now envisaged is essential, must intervene at an early stage, because a liquidity problem can become a solvency problem. A country is solvent with a spread of 300 basis points, is insolvent with spreads of 500 basis points. PSG -He is optimistic... CC -Auguro a great future. I don't think the integration process can stop. The process of globalization requires it. In a few years, there will be those who say that in 1985 there was a group of Portuguese who had the audacity to take the last train that departed from the Western gare of Europe for European integration We caught it in the stirrup, but we managed to catch it. Three years later there would have been a change in geopolitical circumstances such that our position in terms of European integration would have been entirely different. After the fall of the Berlin Wall it would have been different. Fortunate those who have taken the initiative to fight for European integration, fortunate the date we entered... PSG - Lucky the date of emu's joined? CC - No doubt. It was a great opportunity for the country. But you have to realize that when you're part of a club there are rules, when you don't respect the rules there are consequences. The consequences did not become visible immediately because the markets were very condescending. PSG -Can Greece exit the euro? CC-If EMU is not designed to fragment, it is unthinkable, in the context of the current treaty, an exit. The EU is in the position of a large oil tanker on the high seas that has to repair some damage and at the same time navigate. To navigate we will need a new route, which goes through the integration; to repair damage, we need instruments, will and perception, by all economic and political actors, including the Greeks, that the opportunity cost of not being part of the integration process is so high that they would be the first to hit. PSG - Is the orderly restructuring of Greece's debt possible? CC - Central banks have always been against any idea of debt restructuring. The reaction of the markets to a restructuring is certainly limitless. A company can go bankrupt - the lender knows what assets it will take possession of. But on the sovereign level, there are no prisons for states for economic crimes and there is no way to seed assets. So a creditor's reaction to a sovereign risk, if by chance an idea of "default" presents itself, is of uncertainty Before which court will I claim rights? How much will I get paid? PSG - What is the escape to the Greek situation? CC -It is to return to the decisions of 21 July of the European Council, to implement them as soon as possible, a matter which has been addressed insistently by the ECB: to ask governments to implement them; explain to national public opinion that the opportunity cost of not doing so is too high; that there is a short-sighted exercise in which the short-term advantage is strongly nullified by the long-term disadvantage. PSG - How far should federalism go? Do you agree with eurobonds? CC - We should not focus on modalities, but on principles, objectives and forms. If we want to give the markets an idea that the whole is cohesive and secure, and that each member is not at risk of default, there has to be a group guarantee for each member. The motto is simple: "one for all and all for one". PSG - How do you do that? CC - They can be "eurobonds", they can be guarantees... A model must be found in which when one Member State goes to the market, the others function as guarantors of compliance. Why? Because there are government structures at European level that ensure efficient supervision, because there are reciprocal obligations and sanctionmechanisms. PSG -Sanctions? CC - Yes, it is the mechanism that gives credibility to good behavior. I am much more in favour of a premium system than a system of sanctions, which is very easy to manage. PSG - With the creation of a permanent financial aid mechanism it is not an illusion to believe in sovereignty. CC -The "vestaphian" illusion of each one doing what he wants in his territory and not being accountable... it's an illusion. Everyone is dependent on everyone. What there are is different levels of interdependence. In a game of interdependencies, we have every advantage of being part of the hard core, which has strength, because we benefit from group logic. Outside a context of European integration, outside a context of monetary integration, we are much less important. And of course good solutions will depend heavily on Europe's institutional models. We must strive to ensure that Europe's institutional model continues to have the European Commission as a central element from the point of view of European dynamics, and that the balance between large and small Member States is high, and that the logic of operation is always that of the common interest. PSG - What's going wrong so there are more tax increases this year and more spending cuts next year than was anticipated? CC - To produce services is like in a company: there is an organization. The first thing I have to do in restructuring is get to know the organization well. Because I have to ensure that the production process follows; I have to know where the fats are; whether there are alternative production processes; if the product is required. It's a job you can't do in two weeks. PSG Is giving the Government a teaspoon... CC - It is necessary to do so. That is, it is necessary to analyze. The problem is that we are faced with two completely alikeised times, which is the time for reducing expenditure and the time for reducing the deficit. In the very short term, and we have to do justice to the Minister of Finance, it was illusory to think that without a plan an appropriate intervention was made on reducing public spending and efficiency If there is no identification of priorities, if there is no good analysis of processes, what happens is that precipitation becomes friendly to inertia. I think some things that have happened in the last two months show how the lack of precision becomes extremely friendly to inertia PSG - Want to give an example? CC - No, I'm not going. BUT Aren't we killing the economy with so many taxes? CC - The economy cannot continue with the level of taxation it has. The effort has to be on the expense side. We have a State that has been aggregating functions, of a social nature and other natures, such as economic, without having reorganized itself. We certainly have too much expenses and less administration. Administration in the sense of quality of organization, quality of management, clear definition of what needs to be done. And we have, at the same time, a product that has not accompanied the accumulation of tasks that have been given to the State. That is, we were assuming functions without at the same time having developed the potential product. The process of external indebtedness that we have been witnessing, in which we went from about 35% to 108% of GDP, was at the same time that the potential product of the Portuguese economy was decreasing. PSG - Why did this happen? CC - Because it was made for investments that have no direct effect on the productive capacity of the country. Today we have to deal with the numerator and the denominator at the same time. We have to deal with the numerator, which means external debt, which means the deficit. We have to get them under control. But at the same time, we have to deal with the denominator, which is the product. And the product means growth. And then we have to get an idea of the desirable sequence of management of this adjustment process. And it goes through a rapid increase in the area of the commercialisable goods, by a rapid increase in the area of exports. This implies financing that leads to economic growth, economic growth that will comfort the effort that, in parallel, we will have to make on the side of public spending. So we have two convergent processes, but both have to work in a synchronized way: the fiscal adjustment process and the economic growth process. The process of economic growth will depend heavily on how to process deleveraging and reorganization of the financial system, the transfer of credit to the economy, and how companies react to that credit. PSG -The IMF advocates a strong reduction ofthe single social t axa. What's your opinion? CC - It is important to ensure three things. First, strengthening the competitiveness of exports. And strengthening the competitiveness of exports is not just the result of price. It also results from the installed capacity to continue exporting. Secondly, any advantage that is transferred to companies must materialise in a real increase in competitiveness and not just an increase in rents. Thirdly, we must realise that it is important that the increase in exports and the use of installed capacity of exporting companies must also materialise in terms of increased employment. This means that barriers to hiring workers need to be reduced in a logic of stable bonding. Why? Because if we move on to the logic of overtime and other models, deep down, we are in a logic of containment and not growth. PSG - Are you giving a message to the Government that this change that is happening in labor laws includes an incentive to hire? CC -I would say that anything that favors the stability of the working relationship, and that is said in the MoU, is important to the economy. Workers need to have a stable relationship with the company, because that is the only way they invest in the skills required of them. And the company must not have to permanently rotate workers who do not have a stable relationship, because otherwise they cannot invest in training and human capital either. And we have a generation that today has to be the subject of investment, which itself has TO self-invest to ensure that we will have a new layer of workers who, in the long term, will replace existing ones. PSG - Are you concerned about human resources in the economy? CC - We must urgently think about the organization of the transition from school to company. We have to learn from the Swiss, we have to learn from the Germans, we have to learn from Singapore, because this is a point where there is a huge waste of human capital. We are at a permanent mismatch between necessary skills and available competencies. It is a key area for social concertation. PSG - Is this external intervention an opportunity for Portugal? CC - It's a great opportunity. I used an enigmatic term, said it was the opportunity to break with the "ancien regime". Breaking with the idea that civil society captures the State and the State captures civil society. It must also lead to a break from the point of view of business culture. I am very concerned about a point which is the transition of companies to the second and third generation and, in particular, from the third to the fourth generation in the fabric of SMEs. I was recently talking to one of the most successful industrialists in the footwear industry and asked if you've ever thought about how you're going to continue the company. We have no governance models, transmission models, models to support the assumption of the company when the family group takes itself so heavy that the company transforms from a productive center into a distribution center, which can not continue when there is no business capacity or when the heirs themselves are not interested in continuing, because they have other professional lives. There are sectors that have been victims, but I just make a note: Inditex was born when the Ave Valley was already in crisis. Inditex today is what it is, which means that there was no fatality in the clothing sector. I leave this only for reflexion.

Title: Speech given by Deputy Governor Pedro Duarte Neves at the inauguration ceremony of the new members of the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal
text: Speech given by the Vice-Govern... Speech given by Deputy Governor Pedro Duarte Neves at the inauguration ceremony of the new members of the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal 14 set. 2011 Mr Minister of State and Finance, Mr Secretaries of State, Governor of Banco de Portugal, Ladies and gentlemen, On behalf of me and my colleagues now sworn in, I thank the government for its confidence in us to join the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal. It is a great honor, because we are invited to perform functions in an institution with a long history of service to the country, and a great responsibility, to take place at a time when Portugal and Banco de Portugal are facing extremely demanding and unprecedented challenges in recent decades. Allow me, Minister, to use this opportunity to refer to the Strategic Guidelines defined by the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal for 2011-2013 and which constitute the reference for the strategic planning of the activities to be carried out by the institution in this period. The first line of guidance  known as Financial Stability in the European Context  stems from the recognition of the crucial role of central banks in the field of financial stability, which is particularly demanding in cases such as that of the Bank of Portugal, where there is simultaneous responsibility for the micro and macroprudential supervision of credit institutions. In this respect, the need for effective implementation in Portugal, as in the other European countries, of the reforms resulting from the international response to the financial crisis, in particular the regulatory proposals referred to as Basel III, is now mentioned. In the field of microprudential supervision  and in line with the option taken by Banco de Portugal in 2009 to install permanent inspection teams in the main banking groups  the on-site inspective component will continue to be strengthened, with a more direct and deeper understanding of the institution's activity and its risk profile, through a more intrusive and early-targeted approach to situations that could endanger the solvency or liquidity of institutions. In the context of macroprudential supervision  in which Banco de Portugal has increased responsibilities through its participation in the European Systemic Risk Board  it is important to continue to strengthen the capacity to identify and analyse the main systemic risks with a view to its timely prevention. In the area of supervising the conduct of credit institutions in retail banking markets, Banco de Portugal will continue to extend the regulatory framework for the various market segments, deepening transparency rules and standards of conduct, also giving greater importance to financial literacy projects. In order to investigate and implement deterrent and sanctioning measures that prevent and suppress irregular practices by supervised entities, Banco de Portugal will continue to strengthen its capacity for intervention. Finally, it is important to continue to ensure the high standards of efficiency of payment systems, in the context of implementation of the Single Euro PaymentArea. Also within the scope of this first guideline, there are currently and in the immediate future demanding responsibilities for monitoring the Financial Assistance Program to Portugal and the development of the actions necessary for its successful implementation, involving various areas of activity of Banco de Portugal. The second strategic guideline corresponds to a full and effective contribution to the performance of monetary authority functions within the Framework of the Eurosystem in its various aspects, such as economic advice, monetary policy implementation, financial asset management, payment systems, monetary issuance and statistical production. Thus, as part of its participation in the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks, Banco de Portugal should continue to contribute to maintaining price stability in the euro area. The third guideline is a strengthening of the procedures for ensuring the efficient organisation and management of the resources available to Banco de Portugal, in particular with regard to the qualification and career management of human resources. Banco de Portugal will also intensify ongoing work on operational risk management and compliance with its internal processes. Finally, the fourth strategic guideline aims to strengthen Banco de Portugal's communication mechanisms in order to contribute to a closer, transparent and affirming relationship with Portuguese society - as well as optimising the quality of services provided to the community, in particular in the areas of promoting economic and financial literacy and producing relevant economic and statistical information for economic actors. This year, the 165th anniversary of the founding of Banco de Portugal is completed. I can assure you of your that the Board of Directors, now renewed, and all the employees of the institution will do everything - now as in the past - to honor the history of Banco de Portugal, marked by the rigor and independence of its performance and by the enormous dedication to the public cause. Lisbon, 14 September 2011 Intervention of the Minister of State and Finance, Vitor Gaspar, in the inauguration of the members of the Board of Directors of the Bank

Discurso proferido pelo Vice-Governador Pedro Duarte Neves na cerimnia da tomada de posse dos novos membros do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Portugal 14 set. 2011 Senhor Ministro de Estado e das Finanas, Senhores Secretrios de Estado, Senhor Governador do Banco de Portugal, Minhas Senhoras e meus Senhores, Em meu nome e dos meus colegas agora empossados agradeo a confiana que o Governo em ns depositou para integrarmos o Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Portugal. Trata-se de uma grande honra, por sermos convidados a desempenhar funes numa instituio com uma longa histria de servio ao Pas, e de uma grande responsabilidade, por ter lugar num momento em que se colocam a Portugal e ao Banco de Portugal desafios extremamente exigentes e sem precedentes nas ltimas dcadas.
