Title: Speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa of Banco de Portugal at the XXI Lisbon Meeting
text: Speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa of Banco de Portugal at the XXI Lisbon Meeting 19 set. 2011 Financial stability as a necessary condition for the sustainability of the economic growth Ambassadors, Governors, Ladies and Gentlemen About three years ago, the collapse of investment bank Lehman Brothers triggered the biggest financial and economic crisis since the Great Recession, with very marked repercussions on the world economy, international trade flows and the financial system. This financial crisis, which began in the United States and then migrated to Europe, has morphed over time. Moving from a crisis of financial institutions to a sovereign debt crisis, the importance of financial stability has been put back on the agenda. In the case of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), the crisis also revealed: (i) the importance of the sustainability of public finances in emu; (ii) the need to strengthen the economic arm of EMU; iii) the need to adapt the integration model between financial systems and the structural and institutional frameworks that determine income distribution and price formation and iv) the limits of tolerance to divergences of structural dynamics. Like this: 1. The financial crisis has put the importance of financial stability on the agenda for the functioning of the economy, given the negative impact on economic growth difficulties in accessing finance, and the persistent failures of the financial infrastructure or financial markets. As a corollary, it has also been the specifics of the functioning of the economy and the need to review the risks, the perimeter and the levels that are subject to specific regulation, as well as the practices supervision conditions. As a consequence, not only has the self-regulation model been at stake, but also insufficient supervision limited to the micro dimension, with contempt or subalternization of macro and systemic dimensions. 2. In the case of EMU, the financial crisis through the sovereign debt crisis: the. It revealed the critical importance of the sustainability of public finances for the fundraising by financial institutions and, in this way, for the stability of the financial system and for the financing of the real economy. b. It revealed shortcomings, both in terms of rules and institutions as well as mechanisms that ensure the balance between the economic arm and the monetary policy of EMU, i.e. revealed flaws in the model of economic c. Demonstrated that an economy whose financial system depends on a single sovereign has a greater systemic vulnerability or risk than another in a diversity of dependencies and, therefore, a greater increase in the mitigation of risk (a situation similar to that which is being produced in a territory where a economic agent has a decisive role in the evolution of its activity). d. And finally, the financial crisis has demonstrated the conditioning nature (at the limit, structural divergences and institutional mechanisms that determine the dynamics of income distribution and price formation and, in the the metamorphosis of the productive structures This factor, which, in synthetic form, is the economic competitiveness, tends to be all the more the lower the degree of political integration of the monetary area. I will focus today on the importance of the stability of the financial system, bearing in mind that it depends on three fundamental components: 1. financial institutions (where banks and insurance companies assume the 2. financial infrastructures (which allow the transfer of payments, as well as 3. financial markets (encompassing the money market and the labour market) relay role), such as trading, clearing and liquidation of financial instruments) capital funds, which have as their main function to channel excess funds into sectors for sectors with financing needs). 1 - The role of the financial system In continental Europe's financing model, banks play a crucial role in the functioning of the economy. 1.1. Banks first channel resources from economic agents with savings to agents in need of financial resources. Through the intermediation of monetary financial institutions, agents with savings can optimise the profitability of their assets by managing the degree of risk assumed in its financial investments, and agents in need of financial resources can, through loans banks, finance their investment projects or smooth their consumer profile throughout life. In this context, banks play a very important role in the selection and monitoring of projects to be financed. Banks seek to minimise the risks of information asymmetry underlying customer relationships, both in the selection of projects (minimising the risk of adverse selection) and in their ongoing assessment (minimising the moral risk that debtors will not take all the effort necessary to ensure the success of the project). The mechanisms for selecting and monitoring banks, in addition to mitigating the level of risk assumed, allow to increase the efficiency in the allocation of resources in the economy, ensuring that only projects with greater economic viability are financed. These benefits are relevant mainly for small and medium-sized enterprises, more susceptible to information opacity problems and with greater difficulties in accessing other sources of funding. 1.2. Secondly, the financial intermediation function underlies a maturity transformation mechanism. Deposits raised by banks generally assume a short-term maturity, and these resources are channelled into lending, which usually assumes a longer average maturity. Banks have since been responsible for creating liquidity in the economy, allowing agents with financial constraints to ensure their financing needs. 1.3. Finally, banks perform critical functions in the payment system, enabling the execution of financial transactions between agents and enhancing the optimization of costs and transaction times, while ensuring the security required in these types of transactions. 2. The need to regulate the financial system The raising of funds with short maturities and the granting of credit with longer maturities lead to an imbalance of maturities in the banks' balance sheet, making them inherently unliquid institutions and subject to refinancing risk. On the other hand, they expose the holders of the funds raised to the risk of recovery of the granted credit. The stability of a bank and the financial system depends on liquidity risk and solvency risk. Both determine the system's ability to mediate savings and, as a result, the financial system's ability to secure financing adjusted to the development stage of the economy. The stability of institutions and the financial system is therefore a public good that must be ensured through institutional rules and frameworks that materialise in industry practices and in the prudential supervision architecture. Financial institutions are the first line of defense of financial stability. They must adopt sound and prudent management that allows them to be profitable and solvent at all times. This implies the adoption of effective internal control systems, ensuring the effective management of the risks inherent in the activity carried out. A governance model that ensures that stakeholders directly concerned control the institution and ensures the autonomy of internal audit, compliance and risk management functions in relation to the executive area is an essential pillar of the soundness of institutions and, consequently, of financial stability. However, successive financial crises have shown that self-regulation does not in itself guarantee the stability of the financial system. A second line of defence of financial stability is essential, based on the adoption of mandatory measures aimed at: -Control access to the activity, in order to prevent entities of dubious reputation or that do not have technical, human and material resources suitable for the operations they propose to carry out in the system; -ensure adequate and prudent risk management in each institution, based on a capital base sufficiently sound to accommodate losses incurred without harming the normal development of the activity and also based on liquidity cushions that allow to fill any constraints on the institution's financing capacity; -impose capital requirements on the basis of risks arising from the activity carried out, in particular credit, market (including minimum capital requirements for foreign exchange and trading book risks) and operational risks; -Control the risks assumed by an institution by imposing limits on the concentration of the creditor positions assumed before a client or group of clients "linked to each other" (i.e. group of clients who are so connected to each other that, in the event that one of the elements encounters financial problems, one or more of the other elements will probably have difficulties in fulfilling their obligations). In particular, all risks to a client (or group of linked clients) may not exceed a certain percentage of the institution's own funds. -Set limits on holdings in other companies and, in order to prevent conflicts of interest, set limits on the granting of credit to shareholders holding qualifying holdings and prohibit the granting of loans (except for purposes specified in law) to members of the administrative or supervisory bodies of the institution. -Safeguard the appropriate balance between the financial flows associated with the balance sheet items to ensure that they have liquid funds to meet their financial obligations on reasonable terms as they expire (liquidity risk). The rules assume another important line of defense of the stability/soundness of the bank: An external audit model that protects the general interest (i.e. all stakeholders who do not intervene in the governance of the institution, starting with the depositors and customers). External auditors should take over and be understood as those responsible for ensuring the reliability and quality of the financial information provided to third parties, in particular to market players in general, which also play an important role in monitoring the activity carried out by the institutions. In addition, the establishment of minimum prudential rules is to create a uniform framework for the institutions' market action. They are therefore simplified and preventive instruments, which is why they must be understood as a complement to sound and prudent management, and can never replace effective risk assessment, management and internal control systems. These prudential rules of a preventive nature must be supplemented by other corrective rules, such as the requirement of minimum levels of provision of overdue claims (i.e. claims which, on the contracted maturity date, were not paid by the debtor), which represent the recognition, in the institution's accounts, of a reduction in the amount to be recovered in respect of that credit. However, it is not enough to have a consistent framework of instruments of a preventive and corrective nature. Instruments are needed to deal with possible cases of serious disturbance under the normal operating conditions of the institution and in order to prevent the spread of these situations to the rest of the system (prevention of the risk of contagion), which may impose sanitation measures. These extraordinary measures are very diverse (from restrictions on the exercise of certain activities to direct intervention measures in management, such as the appointment of provisional directors), Their concrete adoption depends on the size and severity of the existing problems. In extreme cases, it is necessary to trigger the liquidation process of an institution. In the supervision of financial institutions, two risk elements have gained particular acuity: liquidity risk, and the sufficiency and quality of equity. First, an international consensus was generated on the need to improve the regulation of the liquidity risk of the banking system. In the context of Basel III, limits will be set on two new liquidity ratios. On the one hand, on the liquidity coverage ratio , to ensure that banks are in permanent condition to withstand a very adverse financial shock for at least a month. To do so, they must have a buffer of high liquidity assets. On the other hand, prudential limits on the net stable financing ratio will be defined. This requirement is more structural in nature and aims to define the incentives necessary for banks to reduce the structural gap in balance sheet deadlines and to use more stable sources of financing to ensure resilience in the medium and long term. Although the imbalance of maturities is perhaps the one that most easily justifies the need for financial regulation, the main pillar of bank regulation is based, at least since the first Basel Agreement, on regulating the capital of banks. By imposing minimum regulatory ratios between the capital and the assets (risk-weighted) of banks, incentives are given to mitigate the level of risk assumed. In fact, banks may take risks considered excessive in order to maximise profitability in the short term. For example, banks can assume an excessive leverage degree by significantly expanding their assets over available capital. Another possibility relates to the type of risk assumed, as banks can invest available resources in assets with potentially high yields but with significant risks (exposure to the subprime sector is a recent example of such a situation). Thus, the imposition of minimum capital and leverage ratios is another pillar of financial system regulation and has undergone some improvements following the global financial crisis. A strong capital base not only increases the banks' ability to cope with unanticipated losses: it also contributes to aligning shareholder incentives with the optimal social, as the risks assumed will be borne by them in the event of losses. In addition, the imposition of minimum capital requirements is a way of mitigating negative externalities arising from excessive risk-taking, which can lead to appreciable economic costs. Some incentives for risk-taking are pro-cyclical: in phases of strong economic growth, prevailing optimism can give rise to some "myopia" in risk assessment, assuming that "this time is different". At these stages, it is common to see excessive credit growth, insufficient risk discrimination and pressure to achieve results that may be reflected in deteriorating risks. On the other hand, in recessive periods, it is common to see a higher than desirable contraction in credit because banks are more risk-averse, undermining the recovery of economic activity. To mitigate this cyclical dimension of banking system risk, the Basel III regulatory package imposes countercyclical capital buffers. The need for regulation can also be paradoxically justified by the existence of the function of last resort lender. Some banks (commonly referred to as too-big-to-fail) are too large for them to fail without causing catastrophic damage to the economy and payment system. Other banks, although not particularly large, may be so linked to other banks that their bankruptcy would result in contagion effects comparable to those caused by the big banks. In these situations, there is a strong likelihood that these banks will have easy access to lender of last resort functions or other forms of aid, possibly through the injection of public funds. The recognition of this implied guarantee gives incentives for banks to become "too big" or to take systemic risks that could jeopardise the stability of the financial system. The regulation of systemic banks therefore requires particular attention, as recognised in the wake of the last financial crisis. As such, there are proposals for these banks to be subject to even more demanding regulation. The recent proposals of the Basel Committee on this subject and the Vickers report for the United Kingdom are an important contribution in this area. Prudential supervision rules and practices aim to ensure the stability of the financial system. However, they are not always enough. Therefore, there are two complementary mechanisms that, by the confidence they induce, minimize the risk of contagion between institutions. In most advanced economies and partly in emerging economies, deposit guarantee schemes have been set up over the last decades, the aim of which is to minimise the likelihood of deposit runs by small depositors. However, these systems do not protect large depositors or other creditors, who continue to play an important role in monitoring banks, as more sophisticated investors with better risk management and assessment capabilities. Moreover, the role of lender of last resort assumed by central banks is an important intervention mechanism in the event of an invalidity situation of a banking institution. Since Walter Bagehot published the book Lombard Street in 1837, there is some consensus that the central bank should be available to recount assets held by banks, providing the liquidity necessary for the continuation of the activity of banks that, although solvent, are in serious liquidity problems. This is a complement to the requirements on minimum amounts of liquid assets that banks have to have, usually defined as a percentage of deposits collected from customers. These assets allow banks to have a minimum level of liquidity to cope with a sudden increase in deposit withdrawals. During the global financial crisis, central banks in advanced economies have actively played this role, in particular by adopting unconventional monetary policy measures which, in a context of paralysis in interbank money markets and other segments of wholesale debt markets, have allowed banks to refinance their short-term liabilities without threatening their solvency. In summary, several market failures justify the regulation of the financial system. During the 1970s, 1970s and 1990s, deregulation and gradual financial liberalisation were seen. However, recent episodes of financial crises can be found (e.g. the savings and loans crisis in the United States, the turbulence that followed the ltcm bankruptcy, the crisis in Russia, the banking crisis in the Nordic countries and, more recently, the subprime crisis and the financial crisis that arose following the collapse of Lehman Brothers). Following these crises it has been recognised that the costs of financial liberalisation can be too high when there are market failures and problems aligning incentives. Thus, a progressive strengthening of financial regulation, i.e. a process of re-regulation, in recent years this advance has been even more significant. The implementation of Basel III will strengthen the soundness of the global banking system and reduce the incidence and magnitude of financial crises. 3. Financial stability and the role of central banks Central banks play a crucial role in maintaining financial stability. In many countries, this mission is explicitly defined in its mandates, alongside the responsibilities relating to monetary policy and price stability. Central banks traditionally play the role of lender of last resort and, as such, have responsibilities in the analysis and monitoring of risks on financial stability, with a view to avoiding the materialisation of systemic risks. Before the financial crisis, it could be thought that price stability and financial stability are essentially complementary objectives. In fact, price stability enhances the stability of the economy by enabling economic operators to anchor their expectations in a context of low uncertainty. In turn, the absence of volatility contributes positively to financial stability. However, there may be conflicts between these two objectives. For example, if interest rates remain low for a relatively long period, incentives may be created to increase risk in the banking system, in particular through excessive credit expansion. Although the price stability objective may require interest rates to remain low for a possibly long period, there must be other instruments, of a micro and/or macroprudential nature, that take risks to the banking system. The stability of the financial system as a whole requires sound and strong supervision of the financial system at the microprudential level. Institutional structures vary between countries and in some cases microprudential supervision is an integral part of the mission of central banks; in other cases, there is an autonomous supervisory authority. Despite the institutional model, it is essential that banks and other financial institutions are monitored rigorously and permanently, ensuring that the strategies and risks assumed are compatible with their financial soundness in the short, medium and long term. In other words, it is necessary to ensure that each bank, individually considered, has the liquidity and capital levels appropriate to the risks assumed. But the financial crisis has highlighted that monetary policy and microprudential supervision are not enough to ensure the stability of the financial system. It has become clear that a complementary set of appropriate instruments is needed to address the main risks to financial stability. In this context, macroprudential policy is now being defined, and it is agreed that central banks should play a key role in implementing this policy. Some currents of thought consider that the desirable situation implies greater policy coordination between the authorities with responsibilities in macroprudential policy and monetary policy, even in cases where these functions are not exercised simultaneously by the central bank. 4. Macroprudential policy as a systemic risk management tool in the financial system The debate on macroprudential policy arose essentially during the global financial crisis. The Larosiere report, published in early 2009, helped launch this discussion, as well as various initiatives by the G20, the IMF and the Financial Stability Board. According to this report, the aim of macroprudential supervision is to limit disruptions to the entire financial system to protect the economy from significant losses in real product. Meeting this objective requires monitoring of potentially systemic financial institutions, in close coordination with microprudential supervision, and, above all, systemic risks that may affect several institutions at the same time, due to common exposures or with high correlation. Thus, macroprudential policy is essentially concerned with containing the systemic risk that may result inter alia from: -shocks affecting at the same time a large number of institutions with similar exposures; -contagion effects associated with bouts of confidence involving a sudden non-renewal of liabilities; -negative externalities on the financial system as a whole and on the economy originated by the behaviour of each bank in scenarios of excessive risk increase. An essential point in the definition of macroprudential policy is the need to avoid an excessive breadth of the credit cycle. It is common to observe, throughout history, periods of excessive credit growth, followed by periods of strong restrictions in this activity. These fluctuations contribute to increasing the breadth of the economic cycle: strong credit growth underlies an acceleration in economic activity; retraction has serious recessive effects. In many situations, these cyclical movements are accompanied by fluctuations in asset prices, in particular those that can be used as collateral. For this reason, the excessive expansion of credit is often accompanied by a marked overvaluation in the real estate markets. In situations of abrupt credit slowdown, the materialization of credit risk is stronger and not fully anticipated by banks. In extreme situations, banking crises are more widespread, with a marked interruption of financing of the economy and high economic costs, making it virtually inevitable to mobilise public funds to absorb losses and to keep banks adequately capitalised. In this sense, it is relatively agreed that mechanisms should be set up to provide incentives to moderate the breadth of the credit cycle, particularly in the period when market incentives lead to rapid and unsustainable credit growth. The countercyclical capital buffers defined under Basel III will be one of the most important instruments for achieving this objective. Banks will therefore be required to accumulate more capital during periods of strong credit growth, which could subsequently be released in periods of economic slowdown to avoid abrupt contractions in lending. In addition to this countercyclical instrument, macroprudential authorities may use a complementary set of instruments such as dynamic provisions, limits (countercyclical) to leverage ratios, limits to the ratio between the value of the loan and the value of the guarantee, among many others. In addition, macroprudential policy should have tools to manage other systemic risks, including: -maturity imbalance and refinancing risk (listing as possible countercyclical limit instruments to liquidity ratios, or taxes on financing in wholesale debt markets); -direct and indirect exposures to common or correlated risks (e.g. imposing limits on large exposures); -incentives for excessive risk-taking (it is essential to define specific regulation for systemic institutions and to define credible and effective resolution mechanisms). Most of these instruments are not a recent innovation. In fact, there is extensive international experience in the use of these instruments, in particular by authorities from emerging economies who have often had to implement mechanisms to contain demand pressures that could lead to an overheating of the economy and the financial system. We therefore have much to learn: not only with the recent global financial crisis, which has more directly affected advanced economies, but also with all the experiences of emerging market economies. 5. The measures taken by Banco de Portugal in a context of pressure stemming from the financial stability Overall, the Portuguese banking system has maintained a significant capacity for adaptation and resilience since the beginning of the international financial and economic crisis, ensuring, without significant disruption, the financing of the economy in a very adverse environment. Portuguese banks have developed their activities on the basis of a relatively traditional financial intermediation model and with regulatory capital levels globally appropriate to the risks assumed. Nevertheless, the framework in which banks carry out their activities implies that they will have to face a period of significant risks and challenges. In the event that Portuguese banks maintain an adequate capacity to resist adverse shocks, Since the summer of 2010 Banco de Portugal has taken several measures that reinforce stability and confidence in the banking system Portuguese. These measures have been strengthened in the context of the economic and financial adjustment programme defined following the request for financial assistance to the European Union, euro area countries and the IMF. In this context, I would like to highlight the following measures: -Banks have been advised to promote the gradual deleveraging of their balance sheets in order to converge on a more stable financing structure and to reduce their dependence on financing with the ECB. The economic and financial adjustment programme provides that the gradual and orderly process of deleveraging the financial system does not jeopardise the financing of the most productive sectors of the economy. As part of this process, the credit-deposit ratio is expected to gradually converge to a maximum of around 120 per cent by mid-2014; -Recommendations were made for the adoption of prudent policies for the distribution of results and improvement of operational efficiency; -Monitoring, regulation and supervision of the banking system has been intensified; -Regulatory requirements have been increased in terms of solvency ratios. Initially a Minimum Core Tier 1 ratio of 8 percent was imposed from the end of 2011. However, under the programme, these requirements have been strengthened, with a Minimum Core Tier 1 ratio of 9 per cent from the end of 2011 and 10 per cent at the latest by the end of 2012. This measure implies that part of the recommendations set out in Basel III are implemented with significant anticipation, going far beyond the minimum requirements required by this international agreement. Measures taken over the past few years to ensure the liquidity of the financial system have also recently been strengthened under the international financial assistance programme. These measures include strengthening the available collateral and the possibility of issuing state-guaranteed debt amounting to an overall amount of up to EUR 35 billion. A 12 billion bank recapitalisation support fund has also been made available, ensuring that all banks, if necessary, can access essential funds to meet new regulatory requirements. However, it is desirable for banks to meet the new capital requirements through the use of private market solutions, favouring strategies to strengthen the capital base and sell credits and non-strategic assets. These requirements aim to ensure that banks are able to withstand any additional shocks and strengthen confidence in the soundness of the banking system Portuguese. The results obtained in the European stress test exercise conducted by the European Banking Authority (EBA) are a sign of this resilience. Despite the particularly adverse environment and the severity of the scenario used in the year, the Portuguese banks that participated in the year exceed the minimum capital ratio set for the year. Despite the positive results, it was defined that two of the participating banks, in agreement with Banco de Portugal, would strengthen their balance sheets through capital increases or asset disposals. This difficult framework illustrates the importance of the central bank in maintaining financial stability, especially when it is both responsible for macro and micro prudential supervision. In the Strategic Guidelines for 2011-2013, recently defined by the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal, the first strategic line relates precisely to financial stability. In this context, Banco de Portugal plans to step up monitoring, regulation and supervision of the banking system. In addition, the Bank will strengthen the capacity to analyse and discuss the new rules and new models of macro and micro prudential supervision to enhance influence on the different European outside countries in which it participates. 6. Conclusion Ambassadors, Governors, Ladies and Gentlemen Despite the troubled times we are experiencing, the devastating consequences of the recent economic and global crisis should be seen as an opportunity to prepare ourselves to better address risks on financial stability. While it is impossible to guarantee that we will be able to avoid any future crisis, as mentioned in the Larosiere report itself, we can do our best not to repeat the mistakes of the past, always being aware that our actions in the present will be decisive for what may happen in the future. Carlos da Silva Costa Lisbon, 19 September 2011 BCPLP portal Lisbon Meetings 2011
text_original: Interveno do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa do Banco de Portugal no XXI Encontro de Lisboa 19 set. 2011 A estabilidade financeira como condio necessria para a sustentabilidade do crescimento econmico Senhores Embaixadores, Senhores Governadores, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores H cerca de trs anos, o colapso do banco de investimento Lehman Brothers desencadeou a maior crise financeira e econmica desde a Grande Recesso, com repercusses muito acentuadas na economia mundial, nos fluxos de comrcio internacional e no sistema financeiro. Esta crise financeira, que teve incio nos Estados Unidos e que migrou depois para a Europa, metamorfoseou-se ao longo do tempo. Ao passar de uma crise das instituies financeiras para uma crise da dvida soberana, veio repor na ordem do dia a importncia da estabilidade financeira. No caso da Unio Econmica e Monetria (UEM), a crise veio ainda revelar: i) a importncia da sustentabilidade das finanas pblicas no quadro da UEM; ii) a necessidade de reforar o brao econmico da UEM; iii) a necessidade de adequar o modelo de integrao entre sistemas financeiros e os quadros estruturais e institucionais que determinam a distribuio de rendimento e a formao de preos e iv) os limites de tolerncia a divergncias das dinmicas estruturais. Assim: 1. A crise financeira reps na ordem do dia a importncia da estabilidade financeira para o funcionamento da economia, dado o impacto negativo sobre o crescimento econmico das dificuldades de acesso ao financiamento, e das falhas persistentes nas infra-estruturas financeiras ou nos mercados financeiros. Como corolrio, veio tambm repor na ordem do dia a especificidade do sector financeiro no funcionamento da economia e a necessidade de rever os riscos, o permetro e os nveis que so objecto de regulao especfica, bem como as prticas de superviso aplicveis. Como consequncia, no s ficou em causa o modelo de auto-regulao como se revelou insuficiente uma superviso circunscrita  dimenso micro, com desprezo ou subalternizao das dimenses macro e sistmica. 2. No caso da UEM, a crise financeira, atravs da crise da dvida soberana: a. Revelou a importncia crtica da sustentabilidade das finanas pblicas para a captao de recursos por parte das instituies financeiras e, por essa via, para a estabilidade do sistema financeiro e para o financiamento da economia real. b. Revelou lacunas, tanto em termos de regras como de instituies bem como de mecanismos que garantam o equilbrio entre o brao econmico e o brao monetrio da UEM, ou seja, revelou falhas no modelo de governo econmico c. Demonstrou que uma economia cujo sistema financeiro dependa de um nico soberano tem uma vulnerabilidade ou risco sistmico maior do que uma outra em que se registe uma diversidade de dependncias e, por conseguinte, uma maior mitigao do risco (situao semelhante  que se produz num territrio em que um nico agente econmico tem um peso determinante na evoluo da respectiva actividade). d. E, por ltimo, a crise financeira demonstrou a natureza condicionante (no limite, determinante) das divergncias estruturais e dos mecanismos institucionais que determinam a dinmica da distribuio de rendimento e da formao de preos e, no mais longo prazo, a metamorfose das estruturas produtivas Este factor, que, de forma sinttica, se designa por competitividade da economia, tende a ser tanto mais determinante quanto menor for o grau de integrao poltica da rea monetria. Vou concentrar-me hoje sobre a importncia da estabilidade do sistema financeiro, tendo presente que ela depende de trs componentes fundamentais: 1. das instituies financeiras (onde os bancos e as companhias de seguros assumem o 2. das infra-estruturas financeiras (que permitem a transferncia dos pagamentos, bem 3. e dos mercados financeiros (englobando o mercado monetrio e o mercado de papel de relevo), como a negociao, compensao e liquidao de instrumentos financeiros) capitais, que tm como principal funo canalizar os fundos em excesso nuns sectores para os sectores com necessidades de financiamento). 1  O papel do sistema financeiro No modelo de financiamento da Europa continental, os bancos desempenham um papel crucial no funcionamento da economia. 1.1. Em primeiro lugar, os bancos canalizam recursos de agentes econmicos com poupanas para agentes que necessitam de recursos financeiros. Atravs da intermediao das instituies financeiras monetrias, os agentes com poupanas podem optimizar a rendibilidade dos seus activos, gerindo o grau de risco assumido nas suas aplicaes financeiras, e os agentes que necessitam de recursos financeiros podem, atravs de emprstimos bancrios, financiar os seus projectos de investimento ou alisar o seu perfil de consumo ao longo da vida. Neste contexto, os bancos tm um papel muito importante na seleco e monitorizao dos projectos a financiar. Os bancos procuram minimizar os riscos de assimetria de informao subjacentes s relaes com clientes, quer na seleco dos projectos (minimizando o risco de seleco adversa), quer na sua avaliao permanente (minimizando o risco moral de que os devedores no assumam todo o esforo necessrio para assegurar o sucesso do projecto). Os mecanismos de seleco e monitorizao dos bancos, alm de mitigarem o nvel de risco assumido, permitem aumentar a eficincia na alocao de recursos na economia, assegurando que so financiados apenas os projectos com maior viabilidade econmica. Estes benefcios so relevantes sobretudo para as pequenas e mdias empresas, mais susceptveis a problemas de opacidade de informao e com maiores dificuldades no acesso a outras fontes de financiamento. 1.2. Em segundo lugar, a funo de intermediao financeira tem subjacente um mecanismo de transformao de maturidades. Os depsitos captados pelos bancos assumem geralmente uma maturidade de curto prazo, sendo estes recursos canalizados para a concesso de emprstimos que, habitualmente, assumem uma maturidade mdia mais longa. Desde modo, os bancos so responsveis pela criao de liquidez na economia, permitindo que agentes com restries financeiras assegurem as suas necessidades de financiamento. 1.3. Por ltimo, os bancos desempenham funes crticas no sistema de pagamentos , permitindo a execuo de transaces financeiras entre agentes e potenciando a optimizao dos custos e tempos de transaco, garantindo simultaneamente a segurana exigida neste tipo de operaes. 2. A necessidade de regulao do sistema financeiro A captao de recursos com maturidades curtas e a concesso de crdito com maturidades mais longas originam um desequilbrio de maturidades no balano dos bancos, tornando-os instituies inerentemente ilquidas e sujeitas a risco de refinanciamento. Por outro lado, expem os detentores dos recursos captados ao risco de recuperao do crdito concedido. A estabilidade de um banco e do sistema financeiro depende do risco de liquidez e, do risco de solvncia. Tanto um como o outro determinam a capacidade do sistema para intermediar a poupana e, em consequncia, a capacidade do sistema financeiro assegurar o financiamento ajustado ao estdio de desenvolvimento da economia. Por isso, a estabilidade das instituies e do sistema financeiro constitui um bem pblico que tem de ser assegurado atravs de regras e quadros institucionais que se materializem nas prticas da indstria e na arquitectura de superviso prudencial. As instituies financeiras so a primeira linha de defesa da estabilidade financeira. Elas devem adoptar uma gesto s e prudente que lhes permita serem rentveis e solventes a cada momento. Tal implica a adopo de sistemas de controlo interno eficazes, que garantam a gesto efectiva dos riscos inerentes  actividade desenvolvida. Um modelo de governao que garanta que os stakeholders directamente interessados controlam a instituio e que assegure a autonomia das funes de auditoria interna, de conformidade e de gesto de riscos relativamente  rea executiva  um pilar essencial da solidez das instituies e, consequentemente, da estabilidade financeira. Todavia, as sucessivas crises financeiras tm demonstrado que a auto-regulao no garante por si s a estabilidade do sistema financeiro.  imprescindvel uma segunda linha de defesa da estabilidade financeira, assente na adopo de medidas de carcter impositivo, destinadas a: -Controlar o acesso  actividade, para evitar que actuem no sistema entidades de reputao duvidosa ou que no disponham de meios tcnicos, humanos e materiais adequados s operaes que se propem executar; -Garantir uma gesto adequada e prudente dos riscos em cada instituio, assente numa base de capital suficientemente slida para acomodar perdas incorridas sem prejudicar o desenvolvimento normal da actividade e tambm assente em almofadas de liquidez que permitam suprir eventuais constrangimentos  capacidade de financiamento da instituio; -Impor requisitos de fundos prprios em funo dos riscos decorrentes da actividade desenvolvida, designadamente dos riscos de crdito, de mercado (incluindo requisitos mnimos de fundos prprios quanto aos riscos cambial e da carteira de negociao) e operacional; -Controlar os riscos assumidos por uma instituio, impondo limites  concentrao das posies credoras assumidas perante um cliente ou grupo de clientes ligados entre si (isto , grupo de clientes que estejam de tal forma ligados entre si que, na eventualidade de um dos elementos se deparar com problemas financeiros, um ou mais dos restantes elementos tero provavelmente dificuldades em cumprir as suas obrigaes). Em concreto, o conjunto dos riscos perante um cliente (ou grupo de clientes ligados entre si) no pode exceder determinada percentagem dos fundos prprios da instituio. -Fixar limites s participaes em outras sociedades e, para prevenir conflitos de interesses, fixar limites  concesso de crdito a accionistas detentores de participaes qualificadas e proibir a concesso de emprstimos (salvo com finalidades especificadas na lei) a membros dos rgos de administrao ou fiscalizao da instituio. -Salvaguardar o equilbrio adequado entre os fluxos financeiros associados s rubricas do balano, para assegurar que dispem de fundos lquidos para cumprir, em condies razoveis, as suas obrigaes financeiras  medida que as mesmas vencem (risco de liquidez). As regras pressupem uma outra importante linha de defesa da estabilidade/solidez do banco: Um modelo de auditoria externa que proteja o interesse geral (ou seja, todos os stakeholders que no intervm na governao da instituio, a comear pelos depositantes e pelos clientes). Os auditores externos devem assumir-se e serem entendidos como os responsveis pela garantia da fiabilidade e da qualidade da informao financeira fornecida a terceiros, nomeadamente aos agentes do mercado em geral, que desempenham igualmente uma funo importante de vigilncia da actividade desenvolvida pelas instituies. Alm disso, o estabelecimento de regras prudenciais mnimas tem em vista criar um enquadramento uniforme da actuao das instituies no mercado. So, por isso, instrumentos simplificados e de carcter preventivo, motivo pelo qual tm de ser entendidos como complemento de uma gesto s e prudente, nunca podendo substituir sistemas eficazes de avaliao, gesto e controlo interno dos riscos. Estas regras prudenciais de natureza preventiva tm de ser complementadas por outras, de carcter correctivo, como a exigncia de nveis mnimos de provisionamento de crditos vencidos (isto , crditos que, na data de vencimento contratada, no foram pagos pelo devedor), que representam o reconhecimento, nas contas da instituio, de uma reduo do valor a recuperar relativamente a esse crdito. Todavia, no basta dispor de um quadro consistente de instrumentos de natureza preventiva e correctiva. So necessrios instrumentos para fazer face a eventuais casos de perturbao grave nas condies normais de funcionamento da instituio e de modo a evitar a propagao dessas situaes ao resto do sistema (preveno dos riscos de contgio), o que pode impor medidas de saneamento. Essas providncias extraordinrias so muito diversificadas (desde restries ao exerccio de determinadas actividades at medidas de interveno directa na gesto, como a designao de administradores provisrios), A sua adopo concreta depende da dimenso e gravidade dos problemas existentes. Em casos extremos, torna-se necessrio accionar o processo de liquidao de uma instituio. No superviso das instituies financeiras, dois elementos de risco ganharam particular acuidade: o risco de liquidez, e a suficincia e a qualidade dos capitais prprios. Em primeiro lugar, gerou-se um consenso internacional sobre a necessidade de aperfeioar a regulao do risco de liquidez do sistema bancrio. No contexto de Basileia III, sero estabelecidos limites sobre dois novos rcios de liquidez. Por um lado, sobre o rcio de cobertura de liquidez , para garantir que os bancos esto em condies permanentes de resistir a um choque financeiro muito adverso durante, pelo menos, um ms. Para tal, devem dispor de um buffer de activos de elevada liquidez. Por outro lado, sero definidos limites prudenciais sobre o rcio de financiamento estvel lquido. Este requisito tem uma natureza mais estrutural e pretende definir os incentivos necessrios para que os bancos reduzam o desfasamento estrutural de prazos no balano e recorram a fontes de financiamento mais estveis, de modo a assegurar a resistncia a choques a mdio e longo prazos. Apesar de o desequilbrio de maturidades ser porventura o que mais facilmente justifica a necessidade de regulao financeira, o principal pilar da regulao dos bancos assenta, pelo menos desde o primeiro Acordo de Basileia, na regulao do capital dos bancos. Atravs da imposio de rcios regulamentares mnimos entre o capital e os activos (ponderados pelo risco) dos bancos, so dados incentivos para mitigar o nvel de risco assumido. De facto, os bancos podem assumir riscos considerados excessivos com o objectivo de maximizar a rendibilidade no curto prazo. Por exemplo, os bancos podem assumir um grau de alavancagem (leverage) excessivo, expandindo os seus activos de forma significativa face ao capital disponvel. Outra possibilidade prende-se com o tipo de risco assumido, dado que os bancos podem investir os recursos disponveis em activos com rendibilidades potencialmente elevadas, mas com riscos significativos (a exposio ao sector subprime constitui um exemplo recente de tal situao). Deste modo, a imposio de rcios mnimos de capital e de alavancagem constitui outro dos pilares da regulao do sistema financeiro, tendo sido alvo de alguns aperfeioamentos na sequncia da crise financeira global. Uma forte base de capital no permite apenas aumentar a capacidade dos bancos para fazer face a perdas no esperadas: contribui tambm para alinhar os incentivos dos accionistas com o ptimo social, dado que os riscos assumidos sero suportados por eles em caso de perdas. Adicionalmente, a imposio de requisitos mnimos de capital  uma forma de mitigar as externalidades negativas originadas pela excessiva assumpo de riscos, que podem originar custos econmicos apreciveis. Alguns incentivos para a tomada de riscos so pr-cclicos: em fases de forte crescimento econmico, o optimismo prevalecente pode dar origem a alguma miopia na avaliao dos riscos, assumindo-se que desta vez tudo ser diferente (this time is different). Nestas fases,  comum observar-se um crescimento excessivo do crdito, uma insuficiente discriminao de riscos e uma presso para a obteno de resultados que pode reflectir-se na deteriorao dos riscos. Em contrapartida, em perodos recessivos,  comum observar-se uma contraco do crdito superior ao desejvel, pelo facto de os bancos se encontrarem mais avessos ao risco, prejudicando a recuperao da actividade econmica. Para mitigar esta dimenso cclica do risco do sistema bancrio, o pacote regulamentar Basileia III impe buffers de capital contra-cclicos. A necessidade de regulao tambm pode ser justificada, paradoxalmente, pela existncia da funo de prestamista de ltima instncia. Alguns bancos (habitualmente designados por too-big-to-fail) so grandes demais para que possam falir sem originar danos catastrficos na economia e no sistema de pagamentos. Outros bancos, embora no sejam particularmente grandes, podem estar de tal forma ligados a outros bancos que a sua falncia originaria efeitos de contgio comparveis aos causados pelos grandes bancos. Nestas situaes, existem fortes probabilidades de que estes bancos tenham acesso facilitado a funes de prestamista de ltima instncia (lender of last resort) ou a outras formas de auxlio, eventualmente atravs da injeco de fundos pblicos. O reconhecimento desta garantia implcita d incentivos aos bancos para que se tornem grandes demais ou que assumam riscos sistmicos, passveis de pr em causa a estabilidade do sistema financeiro. A regulao de bancos sistmicos exige, por isso, particular ateno, conforme foi reconhecido na sequncia da ltima crise financeira. Como tal, existem propostas para que estes bancos sejam sujeitos a uma regulao ainda mais exigente. As recentes propostas do Comit de Basileia sobre este tema e o relatrio Vickers para o Reino Unido constituem um contributo importante neste domnio. As regras e as prticas da superviso prudencial visam assegurar a estabilidade do sistema financeiro. Todavia, nem sempre bastam. Por isso, h dois mecanismos complementares que, pela confiana que induzem, minimizam o risco de contgio entre instituies. Na generalidade das economias avanadas e em parte significativa das economias emergentes, foram institudos ao longo das ltimas dcadas sistemas de garantia de depsitos, cujo objectivo  minimizar a probabilidade de ocorrerem corridas aos depsitos por parte dos pequenos depositantes. Contudo, estes sistemas no protegem os grandes depositantes nem os restantes credores, que continuam a desempenhar um papel importante na monitorizao dos bancos, tratando-se de investidores mais sofisticados e com melhores capacidades de gesto e avaliao de risco. Alm disso, a funo de prestamista de ltima instncia assumida pelos bancos centrais  um mecanismo de interveno importante no caso de uma situao de iliquidez de uma instituio bancria. Desde que Walter Bagehot publicou o livro Lombard Street, em 1837, que existe algum consenso de que o banco central deve estar disponvel para redescontar activos na posse dos bancos, providenciando a liquidez necessria  continuao da actividade de bancos que, apesar de solventes, se encontrem com problemas graves de liquidez. Trata-se de um complemento s exigncias sobre montantes mnimos de activos lquidos que os bancos tm de possuir, geralmente definido em percentagem dos depsitos captados junto de clientes. Estes activos permitem aos bancos dispor de um nvel mnimo de liquidez para fazer face a um eventual aumento repentino dos levantamentos de depsitos. Durante a crise financeira global, os bancos centrais das economias avanadas tm desempenhado activamente este papel, em particular atravs da adopo de medidas no convencionais de poltica monetria que, num contexto de paralisia nos mercados monetrios interbancrios e noutros segmentos dos mercados de dvida por grosso, permitiram aos bancos refinanciar os seus passivos de curto prazo sem ameaar a sua solvabilidade. Em sntese, diversas falhas de mercado justificam a regulao do sistema financeiro. Durante as dcadas de 70, 80 e 90 assistiu-se a movimentos de desregulao e gradual liberalizao financeira. Contudo,  possvel encontrar episdios recentes de crises financeiras (por exemplo, a crise savings and loans nos Estados Unidos, a turbulncia que se seguiu  falncia do LTCM, a crise na Rssia, a crise bancria nos pases nrdicos e, mais recentemente, a crise do subprime e a crise financeira que surgiu na sequncia do colapso da Lehman Brothers). Na sequncia destas crises reconheceu-se que os custos da liberalizao financeira podem ser demasiado elevados quando existem falhas de mercado e problemas de alinhamento de incentivos. Voltou-se, assim, a um reforo progressivo da regulao financeira, ou seja, a um processo de re-regulao, Nos ltimos anos, este avano foi ainda mais significativo. A implementao de Basileia III permitir reforar a solidez do sistema bancrio mundial e diminuir a incidncia e magnitude de crises financeiras. 3. A estabilidade financeira e o papel dos bancos centrais Os bancos centrais desempenham um papel crucial na manuteno da estabilidade financeira. Em muitos pases, esta misso est explicitamente definida nos seus mandatos, a par com as responsabilidades relativas  poltica monetria e  estabilidade de preos. Tradicionalmente, os bancos centrais desempenham a funo de prestamista de ltima instncia e, como tal, tm responsabilidades na anlise e monitorizao de riscos sobre a estabilidade financeira, tendo em vista evitar a materializao de riscos sistmicos. Antes da crise financeira poderia pensar-se que a estabilidade de preos e a estabilidade financeira so objectivos essencialmente complementares. De facto, a estabilidade de preos potencia a estabilidade da economia, permitindo aos agentes econmicos ancorar as suas expectativas num contexto de reduzida incerteza. Por seu turno, a ausncia de volatilidade contribui de forma positiva para a estabilidade financeira. Contudo, podem existir conflitos entre estes dois objectivos. Por exemplo, no caso de as taxas de juro permanecerem reduzidas durante um perodo relativamente prolongado, podem ser criados incentivos para aumentar o risco no sistema bancrio, designadamente atravs da expanso excessiva do crdito. Apesar de o objectivo de estabilidade de preos poder exigir que as taxas de juro se mantenham reduzidas durante um perodo possivelmente longo,  necessrio que existam outros instrumentos, de natureza micro e/ou macroprudencial, que mitiguem os riscos sobre o sistema bancrio. A estabilidade do sistema financeiro, no seu conjunto, requer uma slida e forte superviso do sistema financeiro ao nvel microprudencial. As estruturas institucionais variam entre pases e nalguns casos a superviso microprudencial  parte integrante da misso dos bancos centrais; noutros casos, existe uma autoridade de superviso autnoma. No obstante o modelo institucional,  essencial que os bancos e as restantes instituies financeiras sejam acompanhados de forma rigorosa e permanente, assegurando que as estratgias e os riscos assumidos so compatveis com a sua solidez financeira no curto, mdio e longo prazos. Por outras palavras,  necessrio garantir que cada banco, individualmente considerado, dispe dos nveis de liquidez e de capital adequados aos riscos assumidos. Mas a crise financeira evidenciou que a poltica monetria e a superviso microprudencial no so suficientes para assegurar a estabilidade do sistema financeiro. Tornou-se claro que  necessrio um conjunto complementar de instrumentos adequados para fazer face aos principais riscos sobre a estabilidade financeira. Neste contexto, comea agora a definir-se a poltica macroprudencial, os e a tornar-se consensual que os bancos centrais devero assumir um papel primordial na implementao desta poltica. Algumas correntes de pensamento consideram que a situao desejvel implica uma maior coordenao de polticas entre as autoridades com responsabilidades na poltica macroprudencial e na poltica monetria, mesmo nos casos em que estas funes no so exercidas simultaneamente pelo banco central. 4. A poltica macroprudencial como instrumento de gesto de riscos sistmicos no sistema financeiro O debate sobre a poltica macroprudencial surgiu essencialmente durante a crise financeira global. O relatrio Larosire, publicado no incio de 2009, contribuiu para lanar esta discusso, assim como diversas iniciativas do G20, do FMI e do Financial Stability Board. De acordo com este relatrio, o objectivo da superviso macroprudencial  limitar as perturbaes sobre o conjunto do sistema financeiro para proteger a economia de perdas significativas no produto real. O cumprimento deste objectivo exige o acompanhamento de instituies financeiras potencialmente sistmicas, em estreita articulao com a superviso microprudencial, e, sobretudo, de riscos sistmicos que possam afectar simultaneamente vrias instituies, devido a exposies comuns ou com elevada correlao. Deste modo, a poltica macroprudencial tem como preocupao essencial conter o risco sistmico que pode resultar inter alia de: -choques que afectem simultaneamente um elevado nmero de instituies com exposies semelhantes; -efeitos de contgio associados a quebras de confiana que impliquem uma no renovao sbita de passivos; -externalidades negativas sobre o conjunto do sistema financeiro e sobre a economia originadas pelo comportamento de cada banco em cenrios de aumento excessivo do risco. Um ponto essencial na definio da poltica macroprudencial prende-se com a necessidade de evitar uma amplitude excessiva do ciclo de crdito.  comum observar-se, ao longo da histria, perodos de crescimento excessivo de crdito, seguidos de perodos de fortes restries nesta actividade. Estas flutuaes contribuem para aumentar a amplitude do ciclo econmico: o crescimento forte do crdito est subjacente a uma acelerao da actividade econmica; enquanto a sua retraco tem graves efeitos recessivos. Em muitas situaes, estes movimentos cclicos so acompanhados por flutuaes nos preos dos activos, em particular dos que podem ser utilizados como colateral. Por esse motivo, a expanso excessiva do crdito  muitas vezes acompanhada por uma marcada sobrevalorizao nos mercados imobilirios. Nas situaes de abrandamento abrupto do crdito, a materializao do risco de crdito  mais forte e no totalmente antecipada pelos bancos. Em situaes extremas, as crises bancrias so mais generalizadas, com interrupo vincada do financiamento da economia e custos econmicos elevados, tornando-se praticamente inevitvel a mobilizao de fundos pblicos para absoro de perdas e para manter os bancos adequadamente capitalizados. Neste sentido,  relativamente consensual que devem ser criados mecanismos que providenciem os incentivos para moderar a amplitude do ciclo de crdito, muito em particular no perodo em que os incentivos de mercado conduzem a um crescimento rpido e no sustentvel do crdito. Os buffers de capital contracclicos definidos no mbito de Basileia III sero um dos instrumentos mais importantes para atingir este objectivo. Ser, assim, exigido aos bancos que acumulem mais capital durante perodos de forte crescimento do crdito, que poder posteriormente ser libertado em perodos de abrandamento econmico para evitar contraces abruptas na concesso de crdito. Alm deste instrumento contra-cclico, as autoridades macroprudenciais podero utilizar um conjunto complementar de instrumentos como provises dinmicas, limites (contra-cclicos) a rcios de alavancagem, limites ao rcio entre o valor do emprstimo e o valor da garantia, entre muitos outros. Adicionalmente, a poltica macroprudencial deve dispor de instrumentos que permitam gerir outros riscos sistmicos, nomeadamente: -o desequilbrio de maturidades e o risco de refinanciamento (enumerando-se como possveis instrumentos limites contra-cclicos a rcios de liquidez, ou impostos sobre o financiamento nos mercados de dvida por grosso); -exposies, directas e indirectas, a riscos comuns ou correlacionados (impondo, por exemplo, limites a grandes exposies); -incentivos para tomada de risco excessivo (sendo essencial definir regulao especfica para instituies sistmicas e definir mecanismos de resoluo credveis e eficazes). A maior parte destes instrumentos no constitui uma inovao recente. De facto, existe uma ampla experincia internacional na utilizao destes instrumentos, em particular por autoridades de economias emergentes que, em muitas ocasies, tiveram de implementar mecanismos para conter presses sobre a procura, passveis de originar um sobreaquecimento da economia e do sistema financeiro. Temos, portanto, muito a aprender: no apenas com a recente crise financeira global, que afectou de forma mais directa as economias avanadas, mas tambm com todas as experincias vividas em economias de mercado emergentes. 5. As medidas tomadas pelo Banco de Portugal num contexto de presses sobre a estabilidade financeira Em termos globais, o sistema bancrio portugus tem mantido uma assinalvel capacidade de adaptao e resistncia desde o incio da crise financeira e econmica internacional, assegurando, sem perturbaes significativas, o financiamento da economia num enquadramento muito adverso. Os bancos portugueses tm desenvolvido a sua actividade com base num modelo de intermediao financeira relativamente tradicional e com nveis de capital regulamentar globalmente adequados aos riscos assumidos. No obstante, o enquadramento em que os bancos desenvolvem a sua actividade implica que estes tero de enfrentar um perodo de assinalveis riscos e desafios. Para que os bancos portugueses mantenham uma adequada capacidade de resistncia a choques adversos, o Banco de Portugal tomou, desde o Vero de 2010, diversas medidas que reforam a estabilidade e a confiana no sistema bancrio portugus. Estas medidas foram reforadas no contexto do programa de ajustamento econmico e financeiro definido na sequncia do pedido de assistncia financeira  Unio Europeia, aos pases da rea do euro e ao FMI. Neste contexto, gostaria de destacar as seguintes medidas: -Os bancos foram aconselhados a promover a desalavancagem gradual dos respectivos balanos, de modo a convergir para uma estrutura de financiamento mais estvel e a diminuir a sua dependncia do financiamento junto do BCE. O programa de ajustamento econmico e financeiro prev que o processo gradual e ordenado de desalavancagem do sistema financeiro no comprometa o financiamento dos sectores mais produtivos da economia. No mbito deste processo, o rcio entre crdito e depsitos dever convergir gradualmente para um valor mximo de cerca de 120 por cento em meados de 2014; -Foram transmitidas recomendaes para a adopo de polticas prudentes de distribuio de resultados e de melhoria da eficincia operacional; -Foi intensificado o acompanhamento, a regulao e a superviso do sistema bancrio; -Foram aumentadas as exigncias regulamentares em termos de rcios de solvabilidade. Inicialmente foi imposto um rcio Core Tier 1 mnimo de 8 por cento a partir do final de 2011. Contudo, no mbito do programa, estas exigncias foram reforadas, impondo-se um rcio Core Tier 1 mnimo de 9 por cento a partir do final de 2011 e de 10 por cento o mais tardar at ao final de 2012. Esta medida implica que parte das recomendaes definidas em Basileia III sejam implementadas com uma antecipao significativa, indo muito alm dos requisitos mnimos exigidos por este acordo internacional. As medidas tomadas ao longo dos ltimos anos para assegurar a liquidez do sistema financeiro foram tambm recentemente reforadas no mbito do programa de assistncia financeira internacional. Estas medidas incluem o reforo do colateral disponvel e a possibilidade de emisso de dvida com garantia estatal num montante global at 35 mil milhes de euros. Foi tambm disponibilizado um fundo de apoio  recapitalizao dos bancos de 12 mil milhes de euros, assegurando que todos os bancos, se necessrio, podero ter acesso aos fundos essenciais para satisfazer as novas exigncias regulamentares. Contudo,  desejvel que os bancos cumpram as novas exigncias de capital atravs do recurso a solues privadas de mercado, privilegiando estratgias de reforo da base de capital e de venda de crditos e activos no estratgicos. Estas exigncias tm como objectivo assegurar que os bancos tm capacidade para resistir a eventuais choques adicionais e reforar a confiana na solidez do sistema bancrio portugus. Os resultados obtidos no exerccio de stress test europeu conduzido pela European Banking Authority (EBA) so um sinal desta resilincia. Apesar do enquadramento particularmente adverso e da severidade do cenrio utilizado no exerccio, os bancos portugueses que participaram no exerccio superam o rcio mnimo de capital fixado para o exerccio. No obstante os resultados positivos, ficou definido que dois dos bancos participantes, em acordo com o Banco de Portugal, reforariam os seus balanos atravs de aumentos de capital ou de alienaes de activos. Este enquadramento difcil ilustra a importncia do banco central na manuteno da estabilidade financeira, sobretudo quando  simultaneamente responsvel pela superviso macro e micro prudencial. Nas Linhas Gerais de Orientao Estratgica para 2011-2013, definidas recentemente pelo Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Portugal, , a primeira linha estratgica prende-se precisamente com a estabilidade financeira. Neste mbito, o Banco de Portugal prev intensificar o acompanhamento, a regulao e a superviso do sistema bancrio. Adicionalmente, o Banco reforar as capacidades de anlise e de discusso das novas regras e dos novos modelos de superviso macro e micro prudencial para potenciar a influncia nos diferentes fora europeus em que participa. 6. Concluso Senhores Embaixadores, Senhores Governadores, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores Apesar dos tempos conturbados que vivemos, as consequncias devastadoras da recente crise econmica e global devem ser encaradas como uma oportunidade para nos prepararmos para melhor enfrentar riscos sobre a estabilidade financeira. Embora seja impossvel garantir que teremos condies para evitar qualquer crise futura, conforme referido no prprio relatrio de Larosire, podemos fazer o nosso melhor para no repetirmos os erros do passado, tendo sempre a conscincia de que as nossas aces no presente sero determinantes para o que possa acontecer no futuro. Carlos da Silva Costa Lisboa, 19 de Setembro de 2011 Portal BCPLP > Encontros de Lisboa > 2011

Title: Intervention of Deputy Governor Pedro Duarte Neves at the opening session of the 1st National Conference on Financial Education (ASFAC)
text: Intervention by Deputy Governor Pedr... Intervention of Deputy Governor Pedro Duarte Neves at the opening session of the 1st National Conference on Financial Education (ASFAC) 27 set. 2011 27 September 2011 I am happy to take part in this Financial Literacy Conference  an increasingly topical and relevant theme, in the face of the profound changes in financial systems around the world and the priorities arising from the current economic climate. 1. Framing Alongside citizens' increasingly widespread access to financial products and services, over the past few years has seen a transformation of the framework in which people make financial decisions. These changes naturally have implications for the levels of literacy that are now needed for citizens so that they can act confidently and responsibly in financial markets. Technological advances and increased globalisation and financial integration have contributed to the considerable increase in the range of products available to the common consumer. The high credit expansion that preceded the outbreak of the international financial crisis and increased competition among banks in the creation of innovative and attractive products have led to the emergence of products with greater complexity and a degree of risk not always easy to perceive, even for the most sophisticated consumer. This greater complexity and diversity of products, which characterize retail banking markets today, in addition to hindering a selection based on strict criteria, enhance the asymmetry of information between financial institutions and their customers, thus harming market competition. In addition to these changes in supply and demand conditions in financial markets, demographic change also gives greater demand to citizens' levels of financial literacy. In fact, low birth rates in most countries including Portugal, the highest life expectancy and the consequent trend towards the ageing of the population undermine the long-term sustainability of social security systems. This development has already led, in several countries, to a reduction in the benefits associated with social security, a trend that is expected to continue in the future and which will imply a greater transfer of responsibility and risk from the State to the individual in the formulation of reform plans. In addition, the low national savings rates, the level of external indebtedness of the Portuguese economy and the current situation of public accounts make the Portuguese economy very vulnerable to market sentiment and other factors that determine its financing capacity. In an economic environment characterised by increased uncertainty, greater restrictions on access to credit and higher levels of unemployment, the personal consequences of inadequate financial decisions can be considerably aggravated. It is therefore particularly relevant, at the present juncture, to raise public awareness of the need for savings, for timely planning of reform and for the responsible use of credit. 2. Involvement of central banks and financial regulators In view of this framework, Banco de Portugal, since it was given specific competences in the field of behavioural supervision in 2008, has been intervening in the markets for retail banking products and services with various initiatives to promote consumer protection, an essential aspect of financial stability. The promotion of financial literacy has been a key pillar of this strategy, while functioning as a reinforcement and complement to these measures. In fact, consumers' greater ability to understand and become aware of their rights enhance the effects and efficiency of regulatory and supervisory measures, such as the duties of providing information by credit institutions, or the provision of complaints reception mechanisms. Banco de Portugal's concern with the promotion of financial literacy, manifested at various levels of action, has been shared with several central banks, financial regulators and international organisations. In particular, the OECD, which  through the International Financial Education Network (INFE), created in 2008, with Banco de Portugal as a founding member , has played an important role in reflecting on the themes associated with financial literacy and in defining guiding principles and good practices. Also relevant is the fact that the EBA, the new European Banking Authority established in 2011, explicitly defines, within its competences, behavioural supervision and accountability functions in promoting financial literacy. The actions of central banks and financial regulators in this area are generally through the development of national financial training plans or strategies, which are an instrument for the framework of projects promoting literacy in a coordinated and integrated manner. These strategies normally include: identifying needs and priorities for action; the main areas and target audiences to be reached; and, furthermore, the definition of objectives and methods of evaluation of the various projects and the strategy that integrates them. The National Financial Literacy Plan, recently published by the National Council for Financial Supervision and submitted to public consultation, places Portugal among the pioneer countries in this area. 3. Survey as a tool for diagnosing needs and priorities In order to enable the identification of needs and priorities in terms of financial literacy, it is essential to make a diagnosis prior to the literacy levels of the population. This examination was carried out through the Survey on the Financial Literacy of the Portuguese Population, conducted by Banco de Portugal in 2010, whose first results have already been released and which will also be mentioned today by Professor Susana Narciso, in aspects related to consumer credit. Although the final conclusions of this diagnosis are still being worked on  they will be released shortly at the Banco de Portugal Financial Literacy Conference at the beginning of November  I can already say that the survey has made it possible to characterize in an unprecedented way the knowledge and financial habits of the population. In fact, the stratification of the sample and the distribution of questions by thematic areas have made it possible to identify the segments of the population and the themes where the most significant gaps in terms of understanding by citizens on financial issues are possible. The fact that the survey focuses on the various dimensions of the concept of financial literacy, which cover not only knowledge but also how the perception of concepts is likely to affect citizens' attitudes and behaviour, has enabled information to be obtained on aspects that are very relevant to financial decision-making and generally difficult to assess in another way. Examples of these are the criteria underlying the choice between financial products, the importance attached to family planning and savings, as well as the motivations underlying the use of credit. Thus, this survey is an indispensable tool for defining work to be carried out in the future, not only in the field of financial literacy but also in the regulation of markets and other functions carried out by Banco de Portugal in the field of behavioural supervision. In particular, by allowing a better definition of the debt profile, the survey will facilitate the orientation of Banco de Portugal's actions in the field of responsible credit, with a view to preventing over-indebtedness and the risk of default. 4. The National Financial Training Plan The implementation of a National Financial Training Plan with the scope and objectives intended presents numerous challenges. First, the success of a National Financial Training Plan depends on the participation of a large number of partners in the implementation of projects, in the development of training materials, in the training of trainers and in the dissemination and promotion of the various initiatives to its target audience. Indeed, given the importance of literacy in the management of personal finances, there are several institutions which, even before the definition of a plan or strategy at national level, already carry out such actions. Examples of this are credit institutions, government agencies, consumer associations, foundations and other public or private bodies. This diversity of initiatives, promoted by entities with different objectives and competences, usually provides duplication of effort and the existence of gaps in some areas or segments of the population which, not being targeted by the promoters of the various projects, can, however, be national priorities. Thus, one of the first functions of the Plan is to survey existing initiatives and potential partners to be involved, in their integration, taking into account the objectives and guidelines defined, and in their coordination in order to ensure greater resource efficiency, through the use of existing complementarities and synergies. Another challenge of particular importance is the need for monitoring and evaluation of the Plan, as well as the various projects that integrate it. In fact, the definition of evaluation criteria when formulating the guidelines of the plan  as was done in Portugal, in accordance with international good practice  allows both better clarification of the objectives sought and confers accountability to its promoters. However, the evaluation of financial literacy plans still presents some practical difficulties, related to the measurement or quantification of the various components of the concept of financial literacy and the correct identification of their impact. The innovative nature of these evaluations implies that there is still no widely tested methodology that can serve as a model, so this is an issue on which research and debate are far from complete. Another important topic of reflection at international for a is the involvement of credit institutions in financial training. In view of their experience and knowledge of the markets, the participation of these institutions in the promotion of financial literacy is of particular importance and there are several of them already developing such projects. However, in the recognition that the commercial activity of banking entities and their performance as trainers may give rise to conflicts of interest, this debate has mainly focused on the definition of an appropriate framework for their participation  an issue also very relevant in Portugal, especially with regard to the direct participation of these institutions, as trainers in school spaces. In conclusion, I would therefore like to point out that, despite the various financial training initiatives already in Place in Portugal, the theme of financial literacy continues to merit in-depth reflection. The holding of conferences, such as the one in which we are taking part today, by promoting the analysis and debate on these matters, makes a very significant contribution to promoting and raising awareness of the importance of financial literacy.
