Title: Speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the II Antena 1/Jornal de Negcios Conference: The Adjustment Process and the "New Normality" of the Portuguese Economy
text: Speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the II Antena 1/Jornal de Negocios Conference: The Adjustment Process and the "New Normality" of the Portuguese Economy 18 out. 2011 I begin by thanking you for the invitation to be present at this II Antena 1/Jornal de Negocios Conference on "The State and the Competitiveness of the Portuguese Economy". The theme of the Conference, the current part of which is unquestionable, invites us to reflect on the period of adjustment that we are experiencing today and on the reality that will follow it. We really ask ourselves questions like: Where are we going? What is the "new normal" and in what "world" we will live it? Under what conditions will we reach "destination"? By "new normality" I mean the situation that we can expect to live in a country that has successfully implemented the financial assistance programme and which fits into an international context very different from the one that has characterized the last decades. The levels of indebtedness of the Portuguese economy in the post-adjustment The Portuguese economy is in an adjustment process resulting from the accumulation of imbalances. Although the correction of these imbalances was precipitated by the triggering of the international financial crisis, it must be acknowledged that the path of increasing public and private indebtedness was not sustainable, even in a more benevolent international financial framework, so adjustment would always be inevitable. Of course, in an adverse international context such as the one we live in, this adjustment becomes more difficult and more urgent. At the end of the financial assistance programme and, assuming  as is imperative  that this will be successfully applied, the levels of indebtedness and, consequently, the financing needs of the Portuguese economy will remain very high. In fact, the current projections indicate that: Net external indebtedness, assessed by investment position around 124% of GDP in 2014, which is compared to a value, 129% of GDP; the government debt ratio is around 108% of GDP; Household indebtedness remains slightly higher than 100% of the disposable income (compared to 116% at the start of the programme). The indebtedness of non-financial corporations still reaches about 114% of GDP. The new funding context The reality of international financial markets in the coming years will be substantially different from the one that preceded the international financial crisis. Much more scrutiny is expected of the risk involved in financing operations in both the private and public sectors. Similarly, the banking sector will not be tolerated by the leverage levels seen in the past. The return to market financing under normal conditions, that is, involving "bearable" risk premiums, implies a significant change in the perception of the risk of the Portuguese economy. All sectors of the Portuguese economy will therefore be obliged to maintain enormous discipline, because only in this way will it be possible to continue to reduce debt ratios and, at the same time, refinance the existing debt stock. The return to a sustainable financing path, which presupposes access to normal financial markets, thus requires not only strict compliance with the ongoing adjustment programme, but also the incorporation of a new paradigm in the definition of macroeconomic and budgetary policy and the behaviour of economic actors. In particular, it is essential that intertemporal budgetary constraint sits on the premise of all economic decisions. In fact, the stability of debt ratios as a percentage of GDP implies an aritmetic ratio between primary balances, nominal interest rates, product growth and initial debt levels. This unavoidable ratio becomes clear with some examples: Consider an average nominal interest rate of 3.7%, an inflation rate of 1.5% and a real product growth rate of 2%. In this case, the stabilisation of the international investment position of the Portuguese economy around 120% of the gdp requires a positive balance of the current and capital account, excluding the payment of 0.24% of GDP. With GDP growth of only 1%, and maintaining in other cases, the surplus of the balance will have to be 1.44% of GDP. An average nominal interest rate on public debt of 3.7% is considered, a inflation of 1.5% and a 2% revenue growth. The stabilisation of the government debt at 110% of GDP requires a positive primary budget balance of 0.22% gdp. With GDP growth of 1%, and maintaining the other assumptions, the balance 1.32% of GDP. These examples illustrate well that the return to normality will not be a return to the past. The components of the adjustment The consolidation of public finances is a priority and should be seen as a factor that boosts product growth in the short term either through the release of resources to the private sector or through the reduction of sovereign risk on financing. Reducing household indebtedness through amortisations in excess of new credit is also essential. This reduction in indebtedness is particularly difficult in a context of falling activity, reduced disposable income and unemployment. However, the reduction in levels of private consumption is unavoidable and must be understood as indispensable to the very financial sustainability of families. The reduction of household indebtedness involves three fundamental elements: greater sensitivity to savings to safeguard the future, greater clairvoyance in the decision of investments and greater responsibility for access to credit. Like households, non-financial corporations should also pursue a deleveraging process. However, this process must be judicious in order to maintain investments that prove indispensable to sustain market share gains on international markets. Policies leading to the reduction of non-financial corporations' indebtedness should preserve long-term competitive capacity as well as operational capacity. In the long run, maintaining capital levels per worker is essential to keep up with the process of technological development and increase productivity. In operational terms, the existence of short-term financing for current operations is very important, particularly for exporting companies. In this context, the increased involvement of international banking institutions in the financing of Portuguese companies would be a very positive development. The recapitalisation of the banking system is a very important fourth adjustment factor, and is in line with the deleveraging of households and businesses. This recapitalisation will have to translate into the medium-term maintenance of a ratio of deposit transformation into sustainable credit and compatible with international standards. The banking system will also have to comply with the prudential requirements underlying the Basel III Agreement. Requirements to ensure the sustainability of the adjustment In the adjustment period and in the "new normal" that will follow it, it is therefore necessary to reduce the indebtedness of the various institutional sectors, safeguarding viable companies and mitigating the effects on GDP growth. If the adjustment of external accounts and public accounts is not accompanied  and this is the real challenge  by a qualitative transformation of the Portuguese economy, the stabilisation of debt levels will necessarily be transitory. This qualitative transformation aims to aim at greater productivity, greater employment and greater efficiency in the public sector. It follows that the durable consolidation of public accounts is an essential component of the sustained development process that must follow the adjustment process. Thus, it is not by chance that the theme  I repeat, very timely  chosen for this conference is "The State and the competitiveness of the Portuguese economy". The sustainability of public finances implies a reduction in the weight of public expenditure on the product. In a first phase, of greater urgency, it is understood that the consolidation of expenditure is done through cross-cutting scans because they are the ones that ensure effectiveness in meeting the targets. In a second phase, the approach will have to be different, judicious and qualitative. Sustainable consolidation requires the proper maintenance and functioning of public services vital to the functioning of the economy and society at large. An indiscriminate reduction in public spending, based on the widespread weakening of production levels and the quality of public goods and services, would strongly weaken the sustainable development process. This second phase will have to be a phase of qualitative evaluation and process reengineering. The choice of state functions to be performed as a priority will have to reflect the preferences revealed by society and the levels of taxation that it is willing to tolerate. Services must be prioritised and choices should be made, favouring those who, from the point of view of revealed preferences and the importance for economic development, are vital. This is a process that requires time. Reducing the cost of producing the public goods and services necessary for the functioning of a modern economy contributes decisively to the make this economy, as a whole, more efficient and more competitive at international level. There should therefore be an effort to increase the productivity of public administration in general and an effort to rationally use the resources allocated to each objective, mitigating the effects of reducing expenditure on the level and quality of services provided. Aspects such as process analysis, human resources management and the corresponding incentive systems and the development of systems for the permanent monitoring of expenditure and activity of the various services are part of this concern. The innovation and adoption effort of new technologies and the improvement of human capital are, in a country such as Portugal, critical elements to be taken into account in the context of a qualitative scrutiny of public expenditure. In particular, the quality, coherence and productivity of trinomial education, vocational training and research, also known as the national innovation system, are crucial for the quality of the allocation of public resources and the potential growth of the economy. Indeed, the ability to provide the economy with knowledge, frameworks and lifelong learning is crucial for it to be transformed. It is therefore important to build bridges between university and business, between the vocational training system and businesses and between the research system and businesses. Save more, invest better and use credit more responsibly In short, the "new normal" corresponds to a reality in which the levels of external indebtedness, public indebtedness and indebtedness of households and companies will remain very high. In this context, it will be necessary to trust the markets in so that the financing of the economy is at the lowest cost and in the best conditions. The sustainability of public accounts, household savings capacity, the quality of corporate indebtedness and the recapitalisation of banks will be decisive in restoring and maintaining that confidence. I will therefore end by taking up three key ideas of my intervention: saving more, investing better and using credit in a much more responsible way. Thank you very much. Carlos da Silva Costa Lisbon, 18 October 2011
text_original: Interveno do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa na II Conferncia Antena 1/Jornal de Negcios: O Processo de Ajustamento e a Nova Normalidade da Economia Portuguesa 18 out. 2011 Comeo por agradecer o convite para estar presente nesta II Conferncia Antena 1/Jornal de Negcios sobre O Estado e a competitividade da economia portuguesa. O tema da Conferncia, cuja actualidade  inquestionvel, convida-nos a reflectir sobre o perodo de ajustamento que hoje vivemos e sobre a realidade que lhe suceder. Efectivamente colocam-se-nos questes como: Para onde vamos? Qual a nova normalidade e em que mundo a viveremos? Em que condies chegaremos ao destino? Por nova normalidade refiro-me  situao que podemos esperar viver num pas que aplicou com sucesso o programa de assistncia financeira e que se enquadra num contexto internacional muito diferente daquele que caracterizou as ltimas dcadas. Os nveis de endividamento da economia portuguesa no ps-ajustamento A economia portuguesa encontra-se num processo de ajustamento que resulta da acumulao de desequilbrios. Ainda que a correco destes desequilbrios tenha sido precipitada pelo desencadear da crise financeira internacional, h que reconhecer que a trajectria de crescente endividamento pblico e privado no era sustentvel, mesmo num quadro financeiro internacional mais benvolo, pelo que o ajustamento seria sempre inevitvel. Naturalmente, num contexto internacional adverso como aquele em que vivemos, este ajustamento torna-se mais difcil e mais urgente. No final do programa de assistncia financeira e, supondo  como  imperioso  que este ser aplicado com sucesso, os nveis de endividamento e, consequentemente, as necessidades de financiamento da economia portuguesa permanecero muito elevados. Com efeito, as actuais projeces apontam para que: O endividamento externo lquido, avaliado pela posio de investimento internacional, se situe em cerca de 124% do PIB em 2014, o que compara com um valor, em 2011, de 129% do PIB; O rcio da dvida pblica seja da ordem de 108% do PIB; O endividamento das famlias permanea ligeiramente superior a 100% do rendimento disponvel (face a 116% no incio do programa). O endividamento das sociedades no financeiras atinja ainda cerca de 114% do PIB. O novo contexto de financiamento A realidade dos mercados financeiros internacionais nos prximos anos ser substancialmente diferente da que precedeu a crise financeira internacional.  de esperar um muito maior escrutnio do risco envolvido nas operaes de financiamento tanto do sector privado como do sector pblico. De igual forma, no sero tolerados ao sector bancrio os nveis de alavancagem observados no passado. O retorno a um financiamento de mercado em condies de normalidade, isto , envolvendo prmios de risco suportveis, implica uma alterao significativa da percepo do risco da economia portuguesa. Todos os sectores da economia portuguesa estaro, assim, obrigados a manter uma enorme disciplina, pois s assim ser possvel continuar a reduzir os rcios de endividamento e, ao mesmo tempo, proceder ao refinanciamento do stock de dvida existente. O retorno a uma trajectria sustentvel de financiamento, que pressupe o acesso aos mercados financeiros em condies de normalidade, exige, assim, no apenas o cumprimento rigoroso do programa de ajustamento em curso, como tambm a incorporao de um novo paradigma na definio da poltica macroeconmica e oramental e no comportamento dos agentes econmicos. Em particular,  fundamental que a restrio oramental intertemporal seja premissa de todas as decises econmicas. De facto, a estabilidade dos rcios da dvida em percentagem do PIB implica uma relao aritmtica entre os saldos primrios, as taxas de juro nominais, o crescimento do produto e os nveis iniciais da dvida. Esta relao incontornvel torna-se clara com alguns exemplos: Considerem-se uma taxa de juro nominal mdia de 3,7%, uma taxa de inflao de 1,5% e uma taxa de crescimento real do produto de 2%. Neste caso, a estabilizao da posio de investimento internacional da economia portuguesa em torno dos 120% do PIB requer um saldo positivo da balana corrente e de capitais, excluindo o pagamento de juros, de 0,24% do PIB. Com um crescimento do PIB de apenas 1%, e mantendo as outras hipteses, o excedente da balana ter de ser de 1,44% do PIB. Considerem-se uma taxa de juro nominal mdia da dvida pblica de 3,7%, uma taxa de inflao de 1,5% e um crescimento do produto de 2%. A estabilizao do rcio da dvida pblica em 110% do PIB requer um saldo oramental primrio positivo de 0,22% do PIB. Com um crescimento do PIB de 1%, e mantendo as demais hipteses, o saldo primrio ter de ser de 1,32% do PIB. Estes exemplos ilustram bem que o retorno  normalidade no ser um retorno ao passado. As componentes do ajustamento A consolidao das finanas pblicas  uma prioridade e deve ser encarada como um factor que potencia o crescimento do produto no curto prazo quer pela via da libertao de recursos para o sector privado quer pela via da reduo do risco soberano que incide sobre o financiamento. A reduo do endividamento das famlias, atravs de amortizaes superiores  obteno de novo crdito,  tambm essencial. Esta reduo do endividamento  particularmente difcil num contexto de queda da actividade, de reduo do rendimento disponvel e de desemprego. No entanto, a reduo dos nveis de consumo privado  incontornvel e ter de ser entendida como indispensvel  prpria sustentabilidade financeira das famlias. A reduo do endividamento das famlias passa por trs elementos fundamentais: maior sensibilidade  poupana para acautelar o futuro, maior clarividncia na deciso das aplicaes e maior responsabilidade no acesso ao crdito. Tal como as famlias, as sociedades no financeiras devem tambm prosseguir um processo de desalavancagem. No entanto, este processo deve ser criterioso, de forma a manter os investimentos que se revelem indispensveis para sustentar os ganhos de quota de mercado nos mercados internacionais. As polticas conducentes  reduo do endividamento das sociedades no financeiras devem preservar a capacidade competitiva a longo prazo, bem como a capacidade operacional. A longo prazo, a manuteno de nveis de capital por trabalhador  fundamental para acompanhar o processo de desenvolvimento tecnolgico e aumentar a produtividade. Em termos operacionais, a existncia de financiamento de curto prazo para operaes correntes  muito importante, designadamente para as empresas exportadoras. Neste contexto, o acrescido envolvimento das instituies bancrias internacionais no financiamento de empresas portuguesas seria um desenvolvimento muito positivo. A recapitalizao do sistema bancrio  um quarto factor de ajustamento muito importante, e est em consonncia com a desalavancagem das famlias e das empresas. Esta recapitalizao ter de traduzir-se na manuteno a mdio prazo de um rcio de transformao de depsitos em crdito sustentvel e compatvel com os padres internacionais. O sistema bancrio ter ainda de dar cumprimento aos requisitos prudenciais subjacentes ao Acordo de Basileia III. A recapitalizao bancria vai permitir uma reduo da exposio ao risco, uma percepo mais favorvel dos mercados financeiros relativamente  economia portuguesa e, por conseguinte, uma reduo dos prmios de risco no financiamento da economia portuguesa. Requisitos para garantir a sustentabilidade do ajustamento No perodo de ajustamento e na nova normalidade que se lhe seguir , portanto, necessrio reduzir o endividamento dos diversos sectores institucionais, salvaguardando as empresas viveis e mitigando os efeitos sobre o crescimento do PIB. Se o ajustamento das contas externas e das contas pblicas no for acompanhado  e este  o verdadeiro desafio  por uma transformao qualitativa da economia portuguesa, a estabilizao dos nveis de endividamento ser necessariamente transitria. Esta transformao qualitativa tem de visar maior produtividade, maior emprego e maior eficincia do sector pblico. Daqui decorre que a consolidao durvel das contas pblicas  uma componente essencial do processo de desenvolvimento sustentado que deve suceder ao processo de ajustamento. Assim, no  por acaso que o tema  repito, muito oportuno  escolhido para esta conferncia  O Estado e a competitividade da economia portuguesa. A sustentabilidade das finanas pblicas implica uma reduo do peso da despesa pblica no produto. Numa primeira fase, de maior urgncia, compreende-se que a consolidao da despesa se faa atravs de cortes transversais porque so estes que garantem eficcia no cumprimento das metas. Numa segunda fase, a abordagem ter de ser diferente, criteriosa e qualitativa. Uma consolidao sustentvel requer a manuteno e o funcionamento adequado de servios pblicos vitais ao funcionamento da economia e da sociedade em geral. Uma reduo indiscriminada da despesa pblica, assente no enfraquecimento generalizado dos nveis de produo e da qualidade de bens e servios pblicos, debilitaria fortemente o processo de desenvolvimento sustentvel. Esta segunda fase ter de ser uma fase de avaliao qualitativa e de reengenharia de processos. A escolha das funes do Estado a desempenhar de forma prioritria ter de reflectir as preferncias reveladas pela sociedade e os nveis de tributao que esta est disposta a tolerar. H que hierarquizar servios e fazer escolhas, privilegiando os que, do ponto de vista das preferncias reveladas e da importncia para o desenvolvimento econmico, so vitais. Este  um processo que exige tempo. Reduzir o custo da produo dos bens e servios pblicos necessrios ao funcionamento de uma economia moderna contribui decisivamente para que essa economia se torne, no seu conjunto, mais eficiente e mais competitiva no plano internacional. Deve, por isso, existir um esforo para aumentar a produtividade da administrao pblica em geral e um esforo para utilizar racionalmente os recursos afectos a cada objectivo, mitigando os efeitos da reduo da despesa sobre o nvel e a qualidade dos servios prestados. Aspectos como a anlise de processos, a gesto de recursos humanos e dos correspondentes sistemas de incentivos e o desenvolvimento de sistemas de acompanhamento permanente da despesa e da actividade dos diversos servios enquadram-se nesta preocupao. O esforo de inovao e de adopo de novas tecnologias e a melhoria de capital humano so, num pas como Portugal, elementos crticos a ter em conta no quadro de um escrutnio qualitativo da despesa pblica. Em particular, a qualidade, a coerncia e a produtividade do trinmio educao, formao profissional e investigao, tambm conhecido como sistema nacional de inovao, so determinantes para a qualidade da afectao dos recursos pblicos e para o crescimento potencial da economia. Com efeito, a capacidade de fornecer  economia conhecimento, quadros e formao ao longo da vida  determinante para que esta possa transformar-se. , por isso, importante construir pontes entre a universidade e as empresas, entre o sistema de formao profissional e as empresas e entre o sistema de investigao e as empresas. Poupar mais, investir melhor e usar o crdito de forma mais responsvel Em resumo, a nova normalidade corresponde a uma realidade em que os nveis de endividamento externo, de endividamento pblico e de endividamento das famlias e das empresas permanecero muito elevados. Neste contexto, ser necessria a confiana dos mercados para que o financiamento da economia se faa ao menor custo e nas melhores condies. A sustentabilidade das contas pblicas, a capacidade de poupana das famlias, a qualidade do endividamento das empresas e a recapitalizao dos bancos sero decisivas para restabelecer e manter essa confiana. Termino, assim, retomando trs ideias-chave da minha interveno: poupar mais, investir melhor e usar o crdito de forma muito mais responsvel. Muito obrigado. Carlos da Silva Costa Lisboa, 18 de Outubro de 2011

Title: Speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the 4th National Congress of Economists
text: Speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the 4th National Congress of Economists 21 out. 2011 October 30, 2011 Ladies and gentlemen, I begin by congratulating the Order of Economists for holding another edition of this Congress, which is extremely important to promote reflection among economists. There is therefore one of the order's tasks, which is precisely to safeguard the space of economists as opinion makers in economic matters. Next week, the European Council will meet twice in the interval of just three days, which denotes the urgency of the situation in Europe. As already mentioned by the President of the European Central Bank, the European Union has become the epicenter of the international crisis and on Europeans today is under enormous pressure. Given that we are facing a critical week for Europe, it is important that we understand how the European Union has become the epicenter of a crisis that has arisen in the United States, and how the international crisis, the European crisis and the Portuguese crisis have come together. This will be the focus of the first part of my speech. The second part will be dedicated to the future and, more specifically, to the medium-term challenges facing the Portuguese economy under the current conditions. I. THE EU AS THE EPICENTER OF THE INTERNATIONAL CRISIS The current global crisis arises in three successive vacancies, which have been partially overlapping: At first, we have a crisis that is a reflection of the need to structural adjustment of advanced economies and, in particular, of the northern economy the impact of globalization. Secondly, we have the sub-prime crisis, which originates in the affecting in particular the banking sector in Northern Europe. In a third moment, and this is the stage in which we find ourselves, we have the crisis of sovereign debt. This crisis began by affecting Greece, Ireland and Portugal and threatens extend to other economies, and has become a real systemic crisis of euro area. The financial system has functioned as the transmission shaft of this crisis and its changes, first, until 2007, contributing to the postponement of the adjustment of economies; promoting global transmission and amplification of the effects of the crisis. Globalization and the U.S. crisis As I said, the current crisis has its origin in the need for structural adjustment of advanced economies, and in particular the US economy, to the phenomenon of globalisation and the emergence of new low-cost production centres. The increase in supply from Asian economies has had two important consequences. On the one hand, it promoted "deindustrialisation" and, consequently, a massive reduction in employment in the marketable goods sector, mainly affecting the United States. On the other hand, it favored very benign macroeconomic conditions for more than a decade. The low levels of inflation and sustained growth, starting in the mid-1990s, created the illusion that we would be facing a "new paradigm" in the world economy, inducing an attitude of less vigilance, particularly on the part of the Us Federal Reserve. The accommodative monetary policy allowed so-called "ninjas" citizens without income, without jobs and without assets (no income, no job, no assets)  to access credit and encouraged a large-scale investment in the construction sector, generating jobs that replaced the destroyed employment in the area of the transmarketers. Strong demand in the area of non-tradeable goods offset the drop in transactions, while imports from Asian economies allowed price growth to be contained. This was a period when financial stability concerns were overresuming. Indeed, significant growth in the price of assets has been tolerated, especially in the housing market, fuelled by the ease of access to credit. At the same time, and taking advantage of the end of the so-called Glass-Steagall Act, a financial business model based on strong leverage in the banking sector was developed. Through structured products, sometimes very complex, this model allowed the transfer of banking risk to third parties with little perception of the transferred risk. The current credit rating model has contributed decisively to fueling this phenomenon. The international financial crisis and its transmission to Europe The "bursting" of the US housing market bubble and the inability of many mortgage lenders to honour their claims, the so-called subprime crisis, was at the root of the current international financial crisis. This crisis was almost instantly transmitted to financial institutions in Northern Europe  this was the case with Fortis, the Royal Bank of Scotland, ABN Amro and several German banks. These institutions, coming from richer and more demographically aged countries (and therefore with a higher volume of savings to apply), had invested heavily in structured products, which suddenly suffered a very strong devaluation. The bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers was the key moment of this stage. Fears of contagion have triggered large-scale aid interventions to northern European banks. For Portugal, this was both a near crisis and a distant crisis, as the Portuguese financial system, being a savings importing system, did not have relevant investments in this type of assets. Events in Northern Europe have caused a drop in demand, calling into question the productive fabric, particularly because of the difficulties in obtaining credit from companies (of which the automotive sector was, due to its economic relevance, a paradigmatic example). In this context, the European Council decided to launch a programme to expand public spending, which should, in the terms announced, be "timely, targeted and temporary". There has therefore been a general stimulus to increased public spending in the European Union. The same thing happened on the American side. In a short period of time, there has been a widespread and very significant increase in deficits and public debt. The problem, which at this stage was still a northern European problem, has become a problem for Europe in general. The sovereign debt crisis in the euro area The worsening public accounts situation occurred at a time when markets began to be much more rigorous in scrutinising the economies, debt and sustainability conditions of each individual country's public debt. In the case of the European Union, despite the widespread increase in deficits and public debt, there has not been a general increase in external indebtedness, because the external positions of the Member States are very different. This heterogeneity produced a curious situation. Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) presented the best indicators among advanced economies: it had a lower debt ratio, a more balanced current account and a lower inflation rate than, for example, the United Kingdom, Japan or the United States. The euro area would therefore be better able to build confidence than any other area. How then was it possible that the euro area became the epicentre of the crisis? The answer lies precisely in the internal heterogeneity of its members, combined with the absence of a coherent model of economic government in EMU. The combination, in several euro area countries, of very high levels of external debt and public debt with insufficient growth has become the focus of market attention, transporting the crisis to southern Europe. Indeed, even though the situations are very different, at the origin of the Greek, Irish and Portuguese crises there was doubt about the capacity of these countries to generate the income necessary to cope with the service of public debt and external debt. The difficulties in obtaining funding from these countries have revealed a major flaw in the model of economic and monetary union: the lack of a mechanism to deal with temporary liquidity problems in a Member State. In a context where euro area states do not hold their own currency, this lack of model creates a situation where liquidity problems can easily turn into solvency problems. The response from euro area policy makers has been late, insufficient and "several voices", undermining the effectiveness of the measures announced. This lack of effective response has put a huge weight on the European Central Bank. Since the European Central Bank is prevented from financing public debt, it has become necessary to create a mechanism that would allow transitional liquidity-free situations to be resolved without the sovereign being at risk of insolvency (the so-called "Securities Market Program"). In addition, and within its statutory limits, the Eurosystem has guaranteed to all credit institutions that have the collateral required access to the necessary liquidity. Liquidity has been transferred at a fixed rate, i.e. without any price discrimination on the basis of amounts sought, or the geographical location of the institutions. Finally, there has been concern on the part of the Eurosystem to communicate with one voice at all:00 at all, through the President of the European Central Bank, thereby avoiding exacerbating market instability. In a context of strong nervousness in the financial markets, the Deauville meeting introduced an additional uncertainty factor, as it was first admitted that a euro area state could default. By admitting that sovereigns may default, States are jeopardising the banks' risk calculation convention by implicitly assuming that institutions have to have the capital to deal with that risk. Banks are thus faced with the requirement to calculate the oddities implicit in the public debt portfolios and to assess the corresponding capital shortfall. We are therefore in a vicious cycle, in which the financial system has given rise to a political problem and the inadequacy of the political response has created new problems for the financial system. At the moment, markets are demanding the strengthening of banks' capital to address sovereign risk. For their part, banks are dependent on policy decisions that are decisive for how this risk should be addressed. In this context, the increase in the volume and eligibility of the European Stability Fund will not be sufficient. In parallel, a set of rules must be adopted which everyone will have to subscribe to, with injunctive value, and comply under the principle of enhanced cooperation laid down in the Treaty of Lisbon. Group cohesion requires stronger mechanisms that promote financial discipline, combat moral hazard and ensure contractual security. The Portuguese crisis in the euro area sovereign debt The Portuguese crisis is a reflection of an unusable trajectory of indebtedness of the State, families and companies. This debt path resulted from the international financial environment characterised by excess liquidity, as well as the effects associated with the adoption of the euro. The convergence of interest rates in Portugal to the significantly lower levels prevailing in European countries with a greater tradition of macroeconomic stability, alongside access to a financial market that would meet all credit demand at reduced costs, led to a sharp expansion of private spending from the mid-1990s onto the 1990s, consumption and real estate investment expenditure. The public sector followed a similar path of indebtedness, when it should have adopted a countercyclical strategy to counter the overheating of the economy. This action by the public sector contributed to the explosion of external indebtedness measured by the international investment position. In the last decade, domestic savings have fallen to historic lows and the allocation of resources, which favoured the non-transactionable sector, was not the best. The growth rate of the potential product has decreased, which means that investment expenses did not have the expected return. Thus, Portugal was, in any case, faced with an adjustment problem. The international financial crisis has only precipitated the adjustment, which is thus being done under more adverse conditions. Today, the crisis is a crisis in Europe and is no longer just a crisis in southern Europe. But this finding does not cancel out the need for adjustment of the Portuguese economy, because although the crisis can be resolved in the centre of Europe, the problem of Portuguese will not cease to exist. Similarly, the resolution of the European problem  which is fundamentally a political problem  will once again make the American problem clear, which persists and which, being a structural problem, is more difficult to solve. II. PORTUGAL AND THE CHALLENGES OF THE "NEW NORMAL" As I said initially, I would like to focus the second part of this intervention on the medium-term challenges facing the Portuguese economy. The adjustment programme and its implications for the contraction of public spending and the increase in the tax burden are already well known. It is now important to know how we will get to the end of the programme and what reality we will face. In other words, what is the "new normal" of the Portuguese economy in the post-adjustment program? Debt levels remain very high The successful implementation of the adjustment programme, which implies, in addition to reducing domestic expenditure, a strong growth in exports over the next three years, will make it possible to put the indebtedness of the various institutional sectors on a downward trajectory. However, debt levels will remain very high, and in 2015 external indebtedness, public indebtedness, household indebtedness and corporate indebtedness are expected to all exceed 100% of GDP. This means that the Portuguese economy will continue to rely largely on international financial markets. At the end of the adjustment programme, the economy's ability to re-obtain market financing will depend on maintaining a sustainable path of external debt and public debt. The financial discipline of the public sector and the other players in the economy is not exhausted, so during the period of implementation of the adjustment programme - it will have to be part of the "new normal". This is even more relevant given that international financial markets will be much more attentive to risk, deleveraging processes and debt ratios, penalising any deviations from expectations. The consolidation of public finances does not end in 2014 The process of consolidating public accounts will not be completed in 2014. The emergency situation we are experiencing implies, in the short term, cross-cutting public spending and very significant tax increases. However, the sustainability of public accounts will only be guaranteed if, in a second phase, the supply of public goods and services is adapted to the preferences of society and the levels of taxation that it is willing to tolerate. This is a fundamental debate that must be done publicly and openly. In addition to adjusting the level of production, it is also necessary to ensure efficiency in the provision of goods and services by the public sector. Efficiency gains are crucial not only to facilitate fiscal consolidation but also because they contribute to increased productivity in the economy as a whole. It must, however, be aware that the efficiency of the State is not obtained by decree. Thus, although the margin for efficiency gains is very significant, the realization of these gains implies profound changes in the organizational model, management rules and processes of public administration. Finally, it is crucial to ensure that the State, as a formatter of the environment in which the economy develops, creates an institutional framework, a framework of rules and a framework of values that are in line with the interests of those who innovate, those who risk, those who gamble, those who create wealth. It is imperative to continue to reduce the indebtedness of businesses and households Companies have to start a deleveraging process and invest in self-financing. It is necessary to understand the motivations underlying the choice of financing modality and the reasons why entrepreneurs distribute profits rather than investing in the company itself. At the same time, we must also learn from past mistakes and to make much more demanding scrutiny of investment projects. This is an absolutely crucial aspect in a context where funding is scarce. Households will also have to continue to reduce their debt levels. This reduction will naturally happen if families take a responsible attitude, save more to guard the future, if they invest more clearly and access credit more responsibly. If, during the coming years, Portuguese households write off real estate credit in net terms, this process will in itself generate a dynamic of debt. The challenges of the banking sector We also need a stronger financial system. The financial system will have to remain, even after 2014, a vital nerve of the Portuguese economy. It is he who transforms savings into financing capacity, thereby promoting economic development. We therefore need a financial system that has even improved risk management and analysis capability and can meet the needs of the economy, both in terms of maturity and risk profiles. The financial system will face two important difficulties, which are both two strategic challenges. On the one hand, the decrease in turnover inherent in the ongoing deleveraging process immediately implies a deterioration in efficiency ratios. On the other hand, banks face a disparity between active rates, inherited from times when credit was cheap, and passive fees, funding, which are more expensive. It is up to banks to define the best strategies to combat these difficulties by seeking efficiency gains by streamlining resources and making the most of replacing less well-paid credit with higher paid credit. Conclusion In conclusion, the "new normal" entails challenges for all sectors of the economy. They are different, but no less demanding than those we now live in. How we deal with these challenges will determine our ability to reach a new level of development of the Portuguese economy and society. Thank you very much. Carlos da Silva Costa October 30 , 2011
text_original: Interveno do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa no 4 Congresso Nacional dos Economistas 21 out. 2011 21 de Outubro de 2011 Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, Comeo por felicitar a Ordem dos Economistas por realizar mais uma edio deste Congresso, que  de extrema importncia para promover a reflexo entre economistas. Cumpre-se, assim, uma das misses da Ordem, que  precisamente salvaguardar o espao dos economistas enquanto formadores de opinio em matria econmica. Na prxima semana, o Conselho Europeu reunir-se- duas vezes no intervalo de apenas trs dias, o que denota bem a urgncia da situao que se vive na Europa. Como j referido pelo Presidente do Banco Central Europeu, a Unio Europeia tornou-se o epicentro da crise internacional e sobre os europeus incide hoje uma enorme presso. Tendo em conta que estamos diante de uma semana crtica para a Europa,  importante que percebamos como  que a Unio Europeia se tornou o epicentro de uma crise que surgiu nos Estados Unidos, e como  que a crise internacional, a crise europeia e a crise portuguesa se conjugaram. Este ser o foco da primeira parte da minha interveno. A segunda parte ser dedicada ao futuro e, mais concretamente, aos desafios de mdioprazo que se colocam  economia portuguesa nas actuais condies. I. A UNIO EUROPEIA ENQUANTO EPICENTRO DA CRISE INTERNACIONAL A actual crise global surge em trs vagas sucessivas, que se foram parcialmente sobrepondo: Num primeiro momento, temos uma crise que  reflexo da necessidade de ajustamento estrutural das economias avanadas e, em particular, da economia norte americana, ao impacto da globalizao. Num segundo momento, temos a crise do sub-prime, com origem nos Estados Unidos, mas afectando em particular o sector bancrio do Norte da Europa. Num terceiro momento, e esta  a fase em que nos encontramos, temos a crise da dvida soberana. Esta crise comeou por afectar a Grcia, Irlanda e Portugal e ameaa estender-se a outras economias, tendo-se tornado numa verdadeira crise sistmica da rea do euro. O sistema financeiro tem funcionado como o veio de transmisso desta crise e das suas mutaes, primeiro, at 2007, contribuindo para o adiamento do ajustamento das economias; subsequentemente, promovendo a transmisso global e a amplificao dos efeitos da crise. A globalizao e a crise norte-americana Como referi, a actual crise tem a sua gnese na necessidade de ajustamento estrutural das economias avanadas e, em particular da economia norte-americana, ao fenmeno da globalizao e ao surgimento de novos centros de produo de baixos custos. O aumento da oferta proveniente das economias asiticas teve duas consequncias importantes. Por um lado, promoveu a desindustrializao e, consequentemente, uma reduo macia de emprego no sector de bens transaccionveis, afectando sobretudo os Estados Unidos. Por outro lado, favoreceu condies macroeconmicas muito benignas durante mais de uma dcada. Os reduzidos nveis de inflao e o crescimento sustentado, a partir de meados de 90, criaram a iluso de que estaramos perante um novo paradigma na economia mundial, induzindo uma atitude de menor vigilncia, nomeadamente por parte da Reserva Federal norte-americana. A poltica monetria acomodatcia praticada permitiu que os chamados ninjas cidados sem rendimento, sem emprego e sem activos (no income, no job, no assets)  pudessem aceder ao crdito e incentivou um investimento em larga escala no sector da construo, gerando emprego que substituiu o emprego destrudo na rea dos transaccionveis. A forte procura na rea dos bens no transaccionveis compensou a quebra nos transaccionveis, ao mesmo tempo que as importaes provenientes das economias asiticas permitiam conter o crescimento dos preos. Este foi um perodo em que as preocupaes com a estabilidade financeira foram descuradas. Com efeito, foi tolerado um crescimento significativo do preo dos activos, com destaque para o mercado imobilirio, alimentado pela facilidade de acesso a crdito. Ao mesmo tempo, e tirando partido do fim do chamado Glass-Steagall Act, desenvolveuse um modelo de negcio financeiro assente numa forte alavancagem do sector bancrio. Atravs de produtos estruturados, por vezes muito complexos, este modelo permitiu transferir o risco bancrio para terceiros com pouca percepo do risco transferido. O modelo vigente de notao do risco contribuiu decisivamente para alimentar este fenmeno. A crise financeira internacional e a sua transmisso  Europa O rebentamento da bolha do mercado imobilirio norte-americano e a incapacidade de muitos credores hipotecrios para honrarem os seus crditos, a chamada crise do subprime, esteve na origem da actual crise financeira internacional. Esta crise transmitiu-se quase instantaneamente s instituies financeiras do Norte da Europa  foi o caso do Fortis, do Royal Bank of Scotland, do ABN Amro e de diversos bancos alemes. Estas instituies, oriundas de pases mais ricos e demograficamente envelhecidos (e, portanto, com maior volume de poupanas para aplicar), haviam investido fortemente nos produtos estruturados, que subitamente sofreram uma fortssima desvalorizao. A falncia do Lehman Brothers foi o momento-chave desta etapa. Os receios de contgio desencadearam intervenes em larga escala de ajuda aos bancos do Norte da Europa. Para Portugal, esta era, simultaneamente, uma crise prxima e uma crise longnqua, na medida em que o sistema financeiro portugus, sendo um sistema importador de poupana, no detinha aplicaes relevantes neste tipo de activos. Os acontecimentos no Norte da Europa geraram uma quebra da procura, pondo em causa o tecido produtivo, designadamente em virtude das dificuldades de obteno de crdito por parte das empresas (de que o sector automvel foi, pela sua relevncia econmica, um exemplo paradigmtico). Neste contexto, o Conselho Europeu decidiu lanar um programa de expanso da despesa pblica, programa esse que deveria ser, nos termos anunciados, oportuno, focado e transitrio (timely, targeted and temporary). Houve, portanto, um estmulo generalizado ao aumento da despesa pblica na Unio Europeia. O mesmo aconteceu do lado norte-americano. Num curto espao de tempo, verificou-se um agravamento generalizado e muito significativo dos dfices e da dvida pblica. O problema, que nesta fase era ainda um problema do Norte da Europa, tornou-se um problema da Europa em geral. A crise da dvida soberana na rea do euro O agravamento da situao das contas pblicas ocorreu num momento em que os mercados comearam a ser muito mais rigorosos no escrutnio das economias, do endividamento e das condies de sustentabilidade da dvida pblica de cada pas individual. No caso da Unio Europeia, no obstante o aumento generalizado dos dfices e da dvida pblica, no houve um aumento generalizado do endividamento externo, porque as posies externas dos Estados-Membros so muito diferentes. Esta heterogeneidade produziu uma situao curiosa. A Unio Econmica e Monetria (UEM) apresentava os melhores indicadores entre as economias avanadas: tinha um rcio de dvida mais baixo, uma balana de transaces correntes mais equilibrada e uma taxa de inflao mais baixa do que, por exemplo, o Reino Unido, o Japo ou os Estados Unidos. A rea do euro estaria, por isso, mais apta a gerar confiana do que qualquer outra rea. Como foi ento possvel que a rea do euro se tenha tornado o epicentro da crise? A resposta encontra-se precisamente na heterogeneidade interna dos seus membros, conjugada com a ausncia de um modelo de governo econmico coerente na UEM. A conjugao, em diversos pases da rea do euro, de nveis de endividamento externo e de dvida pblica muito elevados com crescimento insuficiente tornou-se o foco da ateno dos mercados, transportando a crise para o Sul da Europa. Efectivamente, e ainda que as situaes sejam muito diferentes, na origem das crises grega, irlandesa e portuguesa esteve uma dvida acerca da capacidade destes pases para gerar o rendimento necessrio para fazer face ao servio da dvida pblica e da dvida externa. As dificuldades de obteno de financiamento por parte destes pases revelaram uma falha importante no modelo da Unio Econmica e Monetria: a ausncia de um mecanismo para fazer face a problemas temporrios de liquidez de um Estado-Membro. Num contexto em que os Estados da rea do euro no detm moeda prpria, esta insuficincia do modelo cria uma situao em que problemas de liquidez se podem facilmente transformar em problemas de solvncia. A resposta por parte dos decisores polticos da rea do euro tem sido tardia, insuficiente e a vrias vozes, prejudicando a eficcia das medidas anunciadas. Esta ausncia de resposta eficaz tem colocado um enorme peso sobre o Banco Central Europeu. Uma vez que o Banco Central Europeu est impedido de financiar dvida pblica, tornouse necessrio criar um mecanismo que permitisse que as situaes transitrias de falta de liquidez pudessem ser resolvidas sem que o soberano ficasse em risco de insolvncia (o chamado Securities Market Program). Adicionalmente, e dentro dos limites estatutrios que lhe competem, o Eurosistema tem garantido a todas as instituies de crdito que dispem do colateral exigido o acesso  liquidez necessria. A liquidez tem sido cedida a taxa fixa, ou seja, sem qualquer discriminao de preo em funo de montantes procurados, ou da localizao geogrfica das instituies. Por ltimo, tem havido uma preocupao por parte do Eurosistema de comunicar sempre a uma s voz, atravs do presidente do Banco Central Europeu, evitando desta forma exacerbar a instabilidade nos mercados. Num contexto de forte nervosismo nos mercados financeiros, a reunio de Deauville veio introduzir um factor de incerteza adicional, na medida em que se admitiu, pela primeira vez, que um Estado da rea do euro poderia entrar em incumprimento. Ao admitir que os soberanos podem entrar em incumprimento, os Estados esto a pr em causa a conveno de clculo de risco dos bancos, admitindo implicitamente que as instituies tm de ter capital para fazer face a esse risco. Os bancos ficam assim confrontados com a exigncia de calcular as imparidades implcitas nas carteiras de dvida pblica e de apurar as correspondentes insuficincias de capital. Estamos, assim, num ciclo vicioso, em que o sistema financeiro deu origem a um problema poltico e a inadequao da resposta poltica criou novos problemas ao sistema financeiro. Neste momento, os mercados exigem o reforo do capital dos bancos para fazer face ao risco soberano. Por seu turno, os bancos esto dependentes de decises polticas determinantes para a forma como esse risco deve ser encarado. Neste quadro, no ser suficiente o aumento do volume e da elegibilidade do Fundo Europeu de Estabilidade.  necessrio adoptar, em paralelo, um conjunto de regras que todos tero de subscrever, com valor injuntivo, e cumprir ao abrigo do princpio da cooperao reforada previsto no Tratado de Lisboa. A coeso de grupo requer mecanismos mais fortes que promovam a disciplina financeira, combatam o moral hazard e garantam a segurana contratual. A crise portuguesa no quadro da dvida soberana da rea do euro A crise portuguesa  reflexo de uma trajectria insustententvel de endividamento do Estado, das famlias e das empresas. Esta trajectria de endividamento resultou do ambiente financeiro internacional caracterizado por excesso de liquidez, bem como dos efeitos associados  adopo do euro. A convergncia das taxas de juro em Portugal para os nveis significativamente mais baixos prevalecentes nos pases europeus com maior tradio de estabilidade macroeconmica, a par do acesso a um mercado financeiro que permitia satisfazer a totalidade da procura de crdito a custos reduzidos, induziram uma forte expanso da despesa privada a partir de meados da dcada de 90, em particular das despesas de consumo e de investimento imobilirio. O sector pblico seguiu um caminho idntico de endividamento, quando deveria ter adoptado uma estratgia contra-cclica que contrariasse o sobreaquecimento da economia. Esta actuao do sector pblico contribuiu para a exploso do endividamento externo medido pela posio de investimento internacional. Na ltima dcada, a poupana interna caiu para mnimos histricos e a alocao dos recursos, que privilegiou o sector no transaccionvel, no foi a melhor. A taxa de crescimento do produto potencial reduziu-se, o que significa que as despesas de investimento no tiveram o retorno esperado. Assim, Portugal estava, em qualquer caso, confrontado com um problema de ajustamento. A crise financeira internacional apenas precipitou o ajustamento, que, desta forma, est a ser feito em condies mais adversas. Hoje, a crise  uma crise da Europa e j no  apenas uma crise do Sul da Europa. Mas esta constatao no anula a necessidade de ajustamento da economia portuguesa, porque embora a crise possa ser resolvida no centro da Europa, nem por isso o problema portugus deixar de existir. Da mesma forma, a resoluo do problema europeu  que  fundamentalmente um problema poltico  voltar a tornar evidente o problema americano, que subsiste e que, sendo um problema estrutural,  mais difcil de resolver. II. PORTUGAL E OS DESAFIOS DA NOVA NORMALIDADE Como inicialmente referi, gostaria de centrar a segunda parte desta interveno nos desafios de mdio-prazo que se colocam  economia portuguesa. O programa de ajustamento e as suas implicaes em matria de contraco da despesa pblica e de aumento da carga tributria so j bem conhecidos. Importa agora saber como chegaremos ao final do programa e que realidade enfrentaremos. Por outras palavras, qual a nova normalidade da economia portuguesa no ps-programa de ajustamento? Os nveis de endividamento mantm-se muito elevados A execuo bem sucedida do programa de ajustamento, que implica, alm da reduo da despesa interna, um forte crescimento das exportaes nos prximos trs anos, permitir colocar o endividamento dos diversos sectores institucionais numa trajectria descendente. No entanto, os nveis de endividamento permanecero muito elevados, prevendo-se que, em 2015, o endividamento externo, o endividamento pblico, o endividamento das famlias e o endividamento das empresas continuem todos a exceder 100% do PIB. Isto significa que a economia portuguesa continuar a depender largamente dos mercados financeiros internacionais. No final do programa de ajustamento, a capacidade da economia para voltar a obter financiamento de mercado depender da manuteno de uma trajectria sustentvel do endividamento externo e da dvida pblica. A disciplina financeira do sector pblico e dos restantes actores da economia no se esgota, assim, no perodo de implementao do programa de ajustamento -ter de ser parte da nova normalidade. Este aspecto  ainda mais relevante tendo em conta que os mercados financeiros internacionais estaro muito mais atentos ao risco, aos processos de desalavancagem e aos rcios de endividamento, penalizando quaisquer desvios em relao s expectativas. A consolidao das finanas pblicas no termina em 2014 O processo de consolidao das contas pblicas no estar concludo em 2014. A situao de emergncia que vivemos implica, no curto-prazo, cortes transversais da despesa pblica e aumentos de tributao muito significativos. No entanto, a sustentabilidade das contas pblicas s ser garantida se, numa segunda fase, se adequar a oferta de bens e servios pblicos s preferncias da sociedade e aos nveis de tributao que esta est disposta a tolerar. Este  um debate fundamental que deve ser feito publicamente e de modo aberto. Alm de ajustar o nvel de produo,  tambm necessrio garantir a eficincia na proviso de bens e servios pelo sector pblico. Os ganhos de eficincia so cruciais no apenas para facilitar a consolidao oramental mas tambm porque contribuem para o aumento da produtividade no conjunto da economia. H, no entanto, que ter conscincia de que a eficincia do Estado no se obtm por decreto. Assim, ainda que a margem para ganhos de eficincia seja muito significativa, a concretizao desses ganhos implica profundas mudanas no modelo organizativo, nas regras de gesto e nos processos da administrao pblica. Por ltimo,  crucial assegurar que o Estado, enquanto elemento formatador do ambiente em que se desenvolve a economia, crie um quadro institucional, um quadro de regras e um quadro de valores que convirjam com os interesses dos que inovam, dos que arriscam, dos que apostam, dos que criam riqueza.  imperativo continuar a reduzir o endividamento das empresas e das famlias As empresas tm de iniciar um processo de desalavancagem e apostar no autofinanciamento. H que perceber as motivaes subjacentes  escolha da modalidade de financiamento e as razes que levam os empresrios a distribuir os lucros em vez de investirem na prpria empresa. Paralelamente, h tambm que aprender com os erros passados e fazer um escrutnio muito mais exigente dos projectos de investimento. Este  um aspecto absolutamente crucial num contexto em que o financiamento  escasso. As famlias tambm tero de continuar a reduzir os seus nveis de endividamento. Esta reduo acontecer naturalmente se as famlias adoptarem uma atitude responsvel, se pouparem mais para acautelar o futuro, se investirem de forma mais esclarecida e se acederem ao crdito de forma mais responsvel. Se, durante os prximos anos, as famlias portuguesas amortizarem crdito imobilirio em termos lquidos, esse processo gerar por si s uma dinmica de desendividamento. Os desafios do sector bancrio Precisamos tambm de um sistema financeiro mais forte. O sistema financeiro ter de continuar a ser, mesmo aps 2014, um nervo vital da economia portuguesa.  ele que transforma a poupana em capacidade de financiamento, promovendo, por esta via, o desenvolvimento econmico. Precisamos, por isso, de um sistema financeiro que tenha capacidade de anlise e de gesto de risco ainda mais aperfeioada e que consiga responder s necessidades da economia, quer em termos de maturidades quer em termos de perfis de risco. O sistema financeiro ir deparar-se com duas dificuldades importantes, que constituem, simultaneamente, dois desafios estratgicos. Por um lado, a diminuio do volume de negcios inerente ao processo de desalavancagem em curso implica, no imediato, uma deteriorao dos rcios de eficincia. Por outro lado, os bancos enfrentam uma disparidade entre as taxas activas, herdadas de tempos em que o crdito era barato, e as taxas passivas, de funding, que so mais caras. Cabe aos bancos definir as melhores estratgias para combater estas dificuldades, procurando ganhos de eficincia atravs da racionalizao de recursos e tirando o melhor partido da substituio de crdito menos bem pago por crdito mais bem pago. Concluso Em concluso, a nova normalidade comporta desafios para todos os sectores da economia. Eles so diferentes, mas no menos exigentes do que aqueles que agora vivemos. A forma como lidarmos com esses desafios determinar a nossa capacidade para alcanar um novo patamar de desenvolvimento da economia e da sociedade portuguesas. Muito obrigado. Carlos da Silva Costa 21 de Outubro de 2011

Title: Intervention of the Governor of Carlos da Silva Costa at the Lunch-Colloquium of the Portuguese Spanish Industry Office - Madrid (only in Castilian)
text: Intervention of the Governor of Carlos... Intervention of the Governor of Carlos da Silva Costa at the Lunch-Colloquium of the Portuguese Spanish Industry And Trade Association -Madrid (only in Castilian) 30 nov. 2011 Good afternoon, Mr. Ambassador, ladies and gentlemen, I would like to thank the Spanish-Portuguese Chamber and the other institutions involved in this Organization and tell you, sincerely, that it is a pleasure to be here with you. My speech today will deal with the immediate challenges and medium-term challenges facing the Portuguese economy. It is important that we bear in mind that we cannot assess and respond to the immediate challenges without reflecting, first of all, on the medium-term challenges facing the Portuguese economy. Baltic sailors say there are no storms for sailors who know the ports they are heading towards; there are only storms for those who don't know where they're going. In the same way, we need to know what the reality is and what are the challenges that Portugal is going to encounter at the end of the "Financial Assistance Programme", so that we can define and order our priorities. The Portuguese economy is in a process of adjustment that cannot and should not be considered as a mere consequence of the international financial crisis. The Portuguese crisis is the result of an accumulation of imbalances and reflects, in particular, the unsustainable trajectory of public and private indebtedness. The Portuguese economic problem also reflects, on the other hand, the absence of a sustainable development process. Although the correction of these imbalances has been triggered by the effects of the international financial crisis, it is necessary to bear in mind that the growing indebtedness of the Portuguese State, families and companies would not have been sustainable, even in a more favourable international financial context. The adjustment would be, in any case, a non-negotiable imperative. The unsustainable trajectory of indebtedness, public and private, is the result of an international financial scenario that allowed interest rates in Portugal not to diverge significantly from the rates of European countries with a greater tradition of macroeconomic stability. At the same time, the country benefited from access to a financial market that made it possible to meet the obtaining of credit at low cost. From the mid-90s, there was a period of strong expansion of private spending, related, in particular, to consumption and real estate investment. The public sector followed a similar trajectory of indebtedness and a strategy to mitigate the warming of the economy was not adopted as necessary. Domestic savings reached historic lows and the placement of available resources promoted the development of the non-tradable goods sector. External indebtedness, as measured by international investment position, increased significantly. The trajectory of public indebtedness and private indebtedness was not sustainable, although, in an unfavorable international context such as the one in which we live today, adjustment becomes even more difficult and more urgent. And the Portuguese problem is not only a problem of budgetary consolidation and external imbalance. The Portuguese crisis reflects the absence of a sustainable development process that requires the implementation of economic policies that guarantee the stability of public finances and external debt and, at the same time, increase the added value per worker while generating employment. The medium-term challenge to improving the Portuguese economy is precisely that: to make Portugal a more productive country and, at the same time, capable of providing its population with a higher per capita income, well-being and level of employment. And it is not possible to place the country on a sustainable growth trajectory by neglecting the stability of public finances and the stability of external debt. The stability of public finances and external debt are, like the increase in productivity and employment, fundamental variables of the sustainable development process. The "new normal" It is important to reflect now on the reality that will follow the adjustment period and on the challenges that, in this "new normal", will be presented to it in the Portuguese economy. If the implementation of the adjustment programme is adequate, the indebtedness of the various institutional sectors will enter a downward trajectory, forced by the reduction in domestic expenditure and the significant increase in exports. In the meantime  and it is important to underline this  the levels of public and private indebtedness will remain very high. According to projections: Net external indebtedness, as measured by the international investment position, should be close to 124% of GDP in 2014; The public debt ratio should be close to 108% of GDP; Household indebtedness will remain above 100 percent of the disposable income; The indebtedness of non-financial corporations will be in the order of 114% of GDP. If the levels of public and private indebtedness remain high, the financing needs of the economy will also remain high. Thus, the Portuguese economy will continue to rely heavily on international financial markets. However, access to international financial markets will not be as easy as in the past. There will be significantly greater scrutiny of the risk associated with financing operations, both in the public and private sectors, and less tolerance for leverage levels. In the "new normal" of international financial markets, it will only be possible to refinance existing debt at relatively low risk premiums if there is a significant change in the Portuguese economy's perception of risk. And the perception of the risk of the Portuguese economy will only change if the current adjustment programme is scrupulously complied with and if, simultaneously, a new paradigm is adopted in the definition of macroeconomic and budgetary policy as well as in the behaviour of all economic agents. For these reasons, the financial discipline of the public sector and the other economic agents is a challenge that will be present in the "new normal". Consolidation of public finances The stability of public finances is an essential condition of the sustainable development process that should follow the adjustment. In a first phase, of greater urgency, it is understood that the consolidation of public accounts must be materialized from generalized cuts in spending. However, in a second phase, the approach will have to be different, because the general reduction of public spending would compromise the process of sustainable development. The sustainable growth of the Portuguese economy depends on the quality of the goods and public services provided. In this second phase, we will therefore have to reflect on the functions that the State must perform. This choice should reflect the preferences revealed by the company and, simultaneously, the levels of taxation that the company is willing to tolerate in order to benefit from those functions. This weighting will take time and will have to be accompanied by an assessment of the cost of producing goods and providing public services. Only in this way will we have a more efficient and more competitive economy at the international level. It is necessary to reformulate and centralize the decision model of public investments, prioritizing investment according to the expected economic return. On the other hand, it is important to highlight the regulatory functions of the State. The essential function of a modern state is not to produce. The State must supervise the functioning of productive and labor markets, eliminating existing obstacles to the effective reallocation of productive resources to the most competitive sectors, only having to interfere in the logic of supply and demand to correct market failures or to assess recognized investment results. The challenges of families and businesses The scarcity of domestic savings is a structural feature and a major vulnerability of the Portuguese economy. In order for us to mitigate the external imbalance of the Portuguese economy, it is therefore essential that families increase their savings rate, saving more, investing more clearly and accessing credit more responsibly. It is also necessary for companies to start a process of deleveraging, putting self-financing before the distribution of results. However  and this is an important aspect  deleveraging must be cautious and preserve those investments that guarantee market share gains in international markets. In the absence of a response from firms, stimulating the production of tradable goods and services, the objective of reducing the external deficit will be seriously compromised and we will see a deterioration in employment and a decline in incomes. And the increase in tradable goods and services has to start from the existing business fabric. It is with the companies we have, with the social capital and human capital available that we have to move forward. It is necessary to review the factors that limit the responsiveness of companies to the opportunities and threats of the context in which they find themselves. In particular, we need to promote professionalised management of companies, with a clear separation between management functions and ownership. Capital, in order to be remunerated, does not have to be accompanied by management, as a result of a logic of control of said management, which is associated with a perverse incentive scheme. On the other hand, it is particularly important to act in the system of resolution of economic and financial conflicts of companies, finding ways to reconcile the flexibility of the organization and the protection of the worker. In Portugal, there is a tendency to protect the worker by immobilizing his job. It is necessary to differentiate between the two and the faster we do it, the easier it will be to readjust the productive fabric. Another particularly relevant aspect is the national innovation system, made up of the education, vocational training and research subsystems. The national innovation system determines the creation of value and its extension towards job creation. There is no innovation without education, without vocational training and without research. But education, research and vocational training do not guarantee development without a clear bridge between the productive fabric, the needs of the economy and the national innovation system. Soundness and efficiency of the financial system The soundness and efficiency of the Portuguese financial system are key elements for the sustainable development of the Portuguese economy, given the critical role that the financial system plays in financing the economy. The Portuguese financial system is sound, but we must bear in mind the need to strengthen this solidity, an objective that, in fact, is in line with the deleveraging effort required of families and companies. The Portuguese financial system must prepare to respond to the new prudential rules resulting from basel III by strengthening the quality of its own funds (in particular those of first quality), mitigating leverage and improving the management and supervision of liquidity risk. Only in this way will it be possible to reduce risk exposure and only in this way will it be possible to achieve a more favourable perception of the financial markets in relation to the Portuguese economy and the consequent decrease in the risk premiums associated with the financing of the economy. Conclusion In short, the "new normal" corresponds to a reality in which the levels of external indebtedness, public indebtedness and indebtedness of families and companies will remain very high. In this context, the confidence of the markets will be necessary so that the financing of the economy is done at the lowest cost and under the best conditions. The stability of public accounts, the saving capacity of families, the quality of corporate indebtedness and the strengthening of banks' capital will be decisive in restoring and maintain that trust. Thanks a lot. Madrid, November 30 , 2011
