A meu ver, h trs instituies que favorecem a transformao no sentido de tornar as sociedades mais inclusivas: a educao, o bom funcionamento do mercado de trabalho e a existncia de um contexto que premeia a iniciativa e o sucesso individual.  necessrio que quem tem competncias nestes trs domnios seja responsabilizado por criar condies que favoream a mobilidade social. Quando o capital social est desajustado,  importante que o ajustamento seja construdo com base num compromisso, que tem de ser mais virtuoso que o anterior, permitindo transformar as instituies presentes em instituies mais inclusivas, abertas e que favoream o desenvolvimento econmico. O consenso deve ser legitimado e apropriado pelos agentes econmicos e sociais e utilizar as instituies vigentes como ponto de partida. Construir o consenso significa definir o campo onde se desenvolve a interao entre os membros do grupo e qual  o comportamento legtimo e expectvel de cada um. No significa anular interesses prprios ou conflitos de interesses, nem to pouco eliminar a perceo individual de qual  o comportamento mais interessante para cada elemento do grupo. O consenso , sim, um instrumento que permite transpor preferncias individuais para preferncias coletivas e torna compatvel o interesse de cada elemento do grupo com o interesse comum. Numa sociedade moderna, a transformao das preferncias individuais em coletivas expressa-se sob a forma da valorizao dada aos seguintes fatores: Estabilidade nominal; Capacidade de antecipao e resoluo de restries financeiras coletivas (de origem pblica e externa); Resposta ao processo de globalizao da economia mundial. Todavia, a construo do consenso no garante necessariamente uma dinmica virtuosa de revitalizao institucional. Esta depende da capacidade de as regras sob as quais se forma o consenso responderem a problemas resultantes da interao com a envolvente e gerarem dinmicas de desenvolvimento. O consenso institucional que favorea a inflao, o dfice oramental e o endividamento externo como mecanismos de resposta aos conflitos em torno da disputa pela distribuio do rendimento de uma sociedade  necessariamente um consenso subptimo ou limitativo. Na verdade, trata-se de uma soluo que, mais cedo ou mais tarde, conduzir a uma perda da dinmica de desenvolvimento. Tambm  limitativo o consenso que ignore as condies de concorrncia  escala global e as alteraes tecnolgicas atravs da cristalizao dos modelos de relacionamento interpessoal e de proteo dos mercados locais, pois acabar por gerar a sua prpria autodestruio. O consenso que conduza  acumulao de capital social  o que permite passar para um patamar superior de resoluo de problemas imanentes do prprio grupo ou originrios do exterior do grupo. O consenso  um instrumento fundamental do processo de autoregenerao das sociedades inclusivas. Se a confiana entre agentes for elevada e as normas e as redes de relaes sociais forem suficientemente flexveis, as instituies tendero a gerar endogenamente a sua prpria reforma. O capital social garante que cada participante na sociedade incorpora as regras do jogo, no apenas como constrangimento, mas tambm como oportunidade de afirmao e progresso social, assente na educao, no mrito e no empreendedorismo. A importncia do consenso na transformao da economia portuguesa A gerao de dinmicas virtuosas na economia e sociedade portuguesas requer que se alcance consenso alargado relativamente  necessidade de: 1. Salvaguardar o equilbrio das contas pblicas e externas; 2. Implementar uma poltica de distribuio de rendimentos assente em regras que assegurem a mobilidade social e a manuteno da competitividade da economia; 3. Salvaguardar o espao econmico portugus no espao econmico global. Neste contexto,  fundamental que todos percebam as regras do jogo e as restries que se impem ao pas de forma absoluta. A quantidade de propostas que ignoram estes limites  excessiva para uma sociedade que faz parte de uma unio monetria; mas tambm seria excessiva para uma sociedade com moeda prpria num contexto globalizado.  importante que a sociedade portuguesa compreenda que todos os atores legitimamente tm interesses conflituantes, legitimamente discutem e defendem os seus interesses e que o compromisso no  uma manifestao de fraqueza. As restries impem-se mesmo que tentemos esquec-las. O ajustamento do quadro normativo e institucional deve procurar reforar a confiana entre os agentes econmicos, estimular a iniciativa de cada agente dentro desse quadro e fazer a mediao dos interesses em conflito, de forma a criar solues win-win. Em suma, o debate que temos de fazer deve procurar responder s seguintes perguntas: Quais as restries que,  partida, resultam do campo histrico, cultural e institucional de onde viemos? Quais os conflitos que emanam e que tm de ser legitimamente geridos dentro deste contexto? Quais as restries que resultam da envolvente? Qual  a capacidade de compromisso dos agentes econmicos, sociais e polticos? Muito obrigado.

Title: Address by the Governor of Banco de Portugal at the 3rd Reuters-TSF Conference
text: Address by the Governor of Banco de... 30 May. 2013 AddressbytheGovernorofBancodePortugalatthe3rdReuters-TSFConferencePortugalPost-Troika:RisksandOpportunities Theroleofbankinginfinancingthe -Iwouldliketostartbythankingyoufortheinvitationtotakepartintheopeningofthis3rdConferencepromotedbyReutersandTSF.AroundtwoandahalfyearsagoIhadthechancetotakepartinthe2ndoftheseconferences. Atthattime,withtheeuroarea'ssovereigndebtcrisisinfullprogress, we economy Good morning. watched the wholesale capital markets close to Portugal's banks. Today our banking system is more robust and in a better position to finance a sustained recovery of the Portuguese economy. It is worth remembering the steps taken since then and to outline the challenges -no less demanding -that we now face. This is the purpose of my address. I. THE STEPS TAKEN Thus I would like to start with the steps taken so far. We now have more capitalised, more transparent banks, in a more comfortable liquidity position. We benefit from increased supervision and a stronger regulatory framework. Solvency levels in the Portuguese banking institutions have been strengthened and now compare well with those of the main European banking institutions quoted on the stock markets. At the end of 2010, the Portuguese banking system had a core Tier 1 ratio of 8.1%. By the end of 2012, it reached 11.5%, clearly above the lower limit of 10% set in the Economic and Financial Assistance Programme to Portugal (EFAP). The recapitalisation operations undertaken by the main banking institutions in 2012 -financed largely by the facility proposed in the EFAP -made a key contribution to boosting solvency in the system. Besides solvency, the liquidity position of the main banking institutions has improved considerably. The loan-to-deposit ratio of the eight major banks fell from around 150% at the end of 2010 to around 120% in 2012. Thus there was a gradual convergence towards a more sustainable financing structure that was less sensitive to changes in risk perception among international investors. This positive trend in the loan-to-deposit ratio on the one hand reflects the behaviour of private individuals' deposits -which, after growing sharply in 2011, was very stable in 2012 -and on the other hand, a fall in credit granted by banks. Two large Portuguese banking institutions have returned to the bond markets in the interim. This is also an encouraging sign, although the cost and volume of bond issues held do not yet allow these operations to be seen as a relevant alternative to financing. With a more comfortable liquidity situation, the banks have managed to reduce their dependence on Eurosystem financing. Furthermore, the non-standard monetary policy measures adopted by the European Central Bank have led to significant increases in assets eligible for use in monetary policy operations, bringing available collateral to levels that are now comfortable. To encourage the distribution of liquidity among the Portuguese banks, Banco de Portugal has also launched a new platform for processing secured and unsecured interbank money market operations. The improvement in the banks' solvency and liquidity levels coincided with a very large boost in banking system supervision. In 2011, Banco de Portugal launched a wide-ranging inspection programme under the EFAP, which came to be known as the SIP (Special Inspections Programme). This involved an external assessment of the banks' credit portfolios, verification of the risk assessment methods used by the institutions and assessment of the methodologies used in the stress tests. The SIP provided a snapshot of the quality of the banks' assets. As the situation is dynamic, Banco de Portugal included cross-cutting periodic monitoring of the overall credit portfolio as part of regular banking system supervision, or of specific asset classes which were particularly exposed to macroeconomic or market developments. Thus the goal is to ensure that at any given moment the balance sheets of the banks accurately reflect the reality of their assets. Thus, in 2012, Banco de Portugal ran a detailed assessment of the building and real estate sectors' credit portfolios. In 2013, two special audits will be carried out to confirm the prudence level used for the credit portfolio impairments among the main banking groups. There will also be two audits on the institutions' credit risk management procedures, including the processes for restructuring problematic credit. Banco de Portugal also intensified its macro-supervision of the financial system. The traditional monitoring of banking institutions, which was by nature fundamentally static and case-by-case, is now complemented by a forward-looking, systemic approach, based on financing and capital plans submitted by the banks each quarter, and stress-testing. The legal and regulatory instruments available to the authorities to maintain financial system stability have also been greatly reinforced over the last two years. In this area I would like to refer to the following: The change to the banks' access to capitalisation through public investment; The new framework for preventive, early intervention and resolution mechanisms; The changes to the deposit guarantee system; And the initiatives relating to prevention and management of arrears situations. The legislative framework will be strengthened in the near future, through the approval of the EU Directive on bank recovery and resolution and the corresponding transposition into domestic law. In this regard, please allow me a brief aside to emphasise that despite what is commonly believed, deposits that are not covered by the guarantee funds are now more protected than in the past. Deposits are protected through: the requirement to have adequate capital ratios; the stress-testing, that allows the resilience of the banks' balance sheets in specific scenarios to be assessed; and the creation of forcible capitalisation mechanisms for the use of institutions' shareholders, where deemed necessary. This means that Banco de Portugal's activity in increasing equity capital requirements and running stress-tests and cross-cutting audits of banks' balance sheets aims not only to strengthen financial system stability, but also to boost confidence among depositors and Treasury bond-holders. Financial stability and confidence go hand-in-hand in other words. II. CHALLENGES The results I have just mentioned are encouraging and reveal that significant progress has already been made in tackling the crisis; however this does not mean that the difficulties are behind us, or that the challenges that we face are less tough. Domestically the main challenge to the banking system is profitability. As we know, the banks' profitability has been under great pressure. This is due to a variety of factors. Firstly, default in the credit portfolio has been increasing, because of the recession we are facing. Secondly, spreads have narrowed due to various circumstances, of which I would like to pick out five: The low level of short-term interest rates, which reduces spreads on demand deposits; High financing costs, as a result of the deposit base and hybrid instruments; Decreasing activity in the credit market; Increasing defaults in the credit portfolio; The low profitability of the mortgage credit granted in the past. Thirdly, despite the adjustment made to-date, the banks currently bear operating costs that are out of step with the "new normal", in which the economy will have much lower leverage levels than those of before the international financial crisis. This low profitability, coupled with the increasing application of Basel III rules, will continue to force institutions to manage their capital levels with particular care and proactivity. To respond to these challenges, the institutions must take action on various fronts. On the one hand, they need to find ways to reduce the proportion of mortgage credit agreed in the past with low spreads, thereby freeing liquidity for new activity. On the other hand, they need to execute their resource rationalisation plans with determination, in order to bring about structural cost reduction. Lastly, they need to actively seek out strategic investors that can bring new capital to the institutions. At European level, the negative interaction between the financing of the sovereigns and that of the banking system must be broken credibly and effectively, and the normal functioning of the money and debt markets in the euro area must be re-established. The creation of the Banking Union is the key to this process. With the Banking Union, the European Central Bank becomes responsible for the prudential supervision of euro area credit institutions, doing so through the so-called Single Supervisory Mechanism, which brings together the ECB and the national supervisory authorities. From the middle of 2014, the ECB will take on responsibility for the functioning of the integrated supervision system, through the Single Supervisory Mechanism. The ECB will be responsible for direct supervision of the most important credit institutions and the national supervisory authorities will directly supervise all the other institutions, always following a common framework. Over the past few months, detailed preparatory work has been undertaken to put the Single Supervisory Mechanism into operation. Banco de Portugal has taken an active role in this process. In this regard, I would like to make an important point: the technical work is being carried out with complete commitment and rigour to ensure that the transition of the Portuguese systems to the new European system goes smoothly, with the aim of building a solid, effective and homogeneous supervisory model for European banking. I have no doubt that the Single Supervisory Mechanism will allow a common set of norms to be applied to banking and will result in standardised supervisory procedures and practices aligned with demanding benchmarks. It will thereby contribute to increasing the solidity of the euro area banks, promoting depositor confidence and stability in the European financial system as a whole. However, the Banking Union structure will only be complete with two additional pillars. I of course refer to the need within Europe to have common instruments to resolve institutions and a deposit guarantee mechanism, that can act as a safety net for the whole integrated supervisory system. This is the only way to ensure confidence levels are identical across the Banking Union. We are aware of the challenges and obstacles we face in this process. We know that building a common safety net that on the one hand minimises losses to taxpayers and on the other hand conserves investor and depositor confidence in the banking system and institutions is a complex exercise that is not free of risk. In this regard I would like to leave you with three messages. Firstly, I want to give you a message of determination. Banco de Portugal will not give up the fight for a European solution for these safety instruments for the system and will contribute proposals and arguments so that the solution may be introduced quickly, ensuring an appropriate balance between the considerations at stake. Secondly, I want to issue a warning. We cannot lose our way on the journey towards the new model. Today, Portugal is still more vulnerable than other countries to facts or developments that lead to a deterioration of risk perceptions over the banking system, even where these are unfounded. This situation warrants redoubled prudence and good sense in managing the transition process towards full banking union. And it is on this basis that I want to leave you with a final message on the Banking Union, a message of confidence. As a result of the assessment exercises on banks' assets, the recapitalisation of the institutions and the enhancing of the regulatory instruments and supervisory tools, which began in 2011, we are now better prepared to face the challenges of the Banking Union. I am sure that the good practices that we have developed since the end of 2010 will facilitate the integration of our supervision and our institutions into the Single Supervisory Mechanism. Thus we may have legitimate hope and a reasonable expectation that in the medium term the Banking Union will bring effective and material benefits to our institutions and citizens. III. FINAL NOTES: FINANCING THE ECONOMY I would like to turn now to the "other side of the mirror", the manufacturing base and the companies that make it up. Financing the economy does not only depend on the solvency and liquidity of the banks; it also depends on a large set of factors that affect the perception and appetite for risk among banking institutions. In other words, credit to firms does not only depend on there being demand for financing, but also on that demand for financing being interesting to the banks, meaning that there is a high chance of recovering the credit granted. Factors such as firms demand prospects or their leverage greatly influence the banks decision to grant credit. Demand prospects have deteriorated considerably with the recession, which leads to increased risk aversion, both for investors and for banks. Worsening demand prospects are also related to the structural adjustment of the Portuguese economy. This adjustment involves: On the one hand, a structural reduction in domestic spending, with the consequent downsizing of the non-tradable sector and thus falling credit to this sector due to a lack of solvent demand; On the other hand, better prospects for the sectors working with the external market, which will tend to increase their demand for credit both for working capital and for investment. These circumstances have therefore influenced not only the cost of credit, but also its distribution across the sectors; the construction, real estate and trade sectors, more exposed to domestic demand fluctuations, are those registering a sharper fall in credit; in contrast, credit to exporters is behaving more positively. These trends should not change greatly in the near future, as high levels of indebtedness of both firms and households imply that the stimulus to economic growth will have to come from external demand. Even so, it is possible to reduce risk perception among banks and improve the supply conditions of credit to the economy. We may adopt measures to reduce the asymmetry of information and make firms financial situation (in particular SMEs) more transparent. We may also consider creating risk-sharing mechanisms and promoting the increase of firms capital. Portuguese firms low levels of equity s when compared to firms in most mainland European countries imply a double fragility in our case: financial fragility, as companies are particularly vulnerable to changes in financing conditions, both in terms of volumes and interest rates; and strategic fragility, given that high leverage is inconsistent with safeguarding the ability to respond to changes in the environment, and thus jeopardises the company's sustained growth. This situation is the result of a careless attitude on the part of many companies, which bet on a short-sighted strategy of maximum leverage and profit distribution. It is also the result of a tax system that favours debt financing over capital. Lastly, it results from the general complacency that typifies the period before the financial crisis and which led to an expansion in credit, not always after a suitable consideration of the risk involved. To give an idea of the order of magnitude involved, over a third of Portuguese companies showed profits in 2010 and 2011, and -I emphasise that I am only referring to companies that presented profits -they had a capital adequacy ratio below 30%. The capital needed to boost capital adequacy up to that 30% level would be in the order of 18.4 billion, equivalent to 11% of GDP. To bring capital adequacy levels among profitable companies to 50% would require capitalisation of 55.6 billion, 32% of GDP. Thus we need to find solutions to boost capital levels in the Portuguese manufacturing base significantly. Different options should be considered and combined: To recalibrate taxation to ensure neutrality between debt and equity financing; To consider subordinated capital increase mechanisms as part of the new European multiannual financial framework in conjunction with a reduction in indebtedness of the companies in the financial system; To open up companies' equity to new investors. Of course, these matters do not belong within the remit of Banco de Portugal. For our part, we will continue to strengthen supervision, with the goal of ensuring sufficient capital and liquidity in the banks and to promote sound management practices. This is the best contribution that Banco de Portugal can make to maintain confidence, safeguard savings and ensure that the banking system continues to finance the economy based on a prudent assessment of the risks. Thank you very much. Lisbon, 30 May 2013

Title: Opening speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the Seminar: "Social Economy, Employment and Local Development"
text: Intervention of opening of the Government... Opening speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the Seminar: "Social Economy, Employment and Local Development" 18 Jun 2013 I begin by expressing my satisfaction at the fact that Banco de Portugal welcomes in its facilities this seminar promoted by Caritas Portuguesa, together with the National Center of Culture and IPI Consulting Newtork. These facilities, which correspond to the old church of Sao Juliao, were subject to important requalification works and should be understood as a living space open to the city. I also appreciate the opportunity i have been given to open this seminar. The social economy takes on a particularly important significance in the current context of the Portuguese economy, evidencing the irreplaceable contribution that civil society can make to social cohesion. The social economy, also known as the "third sector", includes private public utility activities from civil society. The organizations of this sector are characterized by (i) being formally institutionalized with their own management bodies; (ii) have a private origin; (iii) non-profit-making in the sense that profits are not distributed by the owners or by management; (iv) typically involve voluntary labour. When talking about the third sector, there is a tendency to question whether social objectives and the absence of profit-making in these institutions are compatible with the generation of economic surpluses or efficiency concerns. This attitude reflects an incorrect view. The institutions of the third sector should generate the surpluses necessary to strengthen their resilience and expand their activity, as these are determining factors in their sustainability. These institutions must be efficient, i.e. they must pursue their objectives without wasting or underusing the resources at their disposal. The weight of the third sector Although sometimes not very noticeable by public opinion, the weight of the third sector in Portugal is not at all negligible. The importance of this sector is even greater at times marked by socio-economic difficulties and, in particular, by very high levels of unemployment, such as those currently experienced by Portuguese society. According to the National Institute of Statistics (INE), we are talking about 55,000 organizations, which employ (with contract) about 260,000 people and have a contribution to GDP of 2.8 percent. If we count voluntary work, the contribution of the social economy to GDP will be around 3.8 percent. Whatever the evaluation criterion, the third sector is very relevant in the Portuguese economy. The importance of this sector, however, goes beyond the mere economic dimension: it is also very relevant in the congregation of wills, through volunteering. The number of people working on a voluntary basis is higher than many imagine. In Portugal, it reaches about one million people. According to the information provided by the INE, in the third sector, about 40 percent of working hours are provided by volunteers. We can think, from the outset, that voluntary work is mostly carried out by people without occupation. In Portugal, this idea does not correspond to reality. Here, voluntary work is mostly carried out by people in employment, a fact which in itself should be a matter for reflection. It means, from the outset, that there is still a vast field for the development of volunteering in Portugal. People without occupation can also volunteer, contributing to the general interest and personal appreciation. The INE data also show that, in the third sector, the percentage of volunteers with higher education is very significant. In fact, the average profile of the volunteer is of someone with higher education and professional activity. We need to create conditions to attract people who do not fit this profile, especially those who have more time available for this process of civic affirmation. In addition, international indicators also confirm that there is scope to make progress on volunteering in Portugal. According to a 2012 European Commission report in Portugal, employment in the third sector accounted for about 5 per cent of total employment; in Sweden, for example, was around 12 percent. The difference is even more evident when we find that only 10 percent of Portuguese volunteer; in the Netherlands, for example, this figure reaches 60 per cent. This concludes that, although there are one million Portuguese involved in volunteer ing, we are still a long way from the European average. We certainly have a great way to go. The importance of efficiency Despite the importance of the third sector, many institutions do not have an adequate organisational and management model, i.e. a model that aims at an optimal use of the resources they have at their disposal or which they have the possibility to mobilise. The implementation of appropriate models of organization and management is essential to increase the efficiency of these institutions and, consequently, the benefit of their recipients. In other words, the better organised the third sector is, the easier it will be able to achieve the social objectives it pursues. The efficient use of resources and the quality of the organization are two particularly relevant factors in the current context of adjustment of the Portuguese economy and are determinant for the satisfaction of the agents involved. One of the major challenges of the management of these institutions is to ensure the moral compensation of those who work on a voluntary basis. Volunteers will only feel effectively satisfied and motivated if the host organisations operate efficiently. That is, if organisations give them the feeling that they are part of a team that seeks to achieve common goals, making the most of each other's skills and efforts. The organisation is particularly relevant for the third sector. When dealing with social objectives and managing human resources on a voluntary basis we tend to indulge in organization failures and be less attentive to the proper use of resources. This attitude is not desirable or acceptable. On the contrary, the nature of the institutions of the third sector has implied a moral obligation to use the resources available in the best possible way, so that each of the people who participate in them feel useful, satisfied and motivated to continue collaborating. The quality of the organisation and management of these entities is even more relevant if we take into account that the third sector has a very significant asset that will have to be managed in order to ensure its sustainability and pursue new objectives. In this regard, it should be forgotten that many institutions have a long history, sometimes secular, and that over time they have accumulated successive layers of routines that tend to generate inefficiencies or to compromise with their manifestations. It is necessary to change this reality. Third sector institutions have to professionalise their management and organisation because only then will they be able to involve and attract more citizens available to work voluntarily for society. Increased importance of the sector in the current adjustment process The importance of the third sector in Portuguese history has never been greater than at the moment we are going through. The enormous socio-economic impact of the adjustment process has two dimensions: a cyclical and a structural dimension. The cyclical dimension corresponds to unemployment resulting from the unfavorable evolution of external demand, which will tend to be reabsorbed with the recovery of the international economy. The structural dimension of unemployment did not result from the evolution of external demand but from the permanent destruction of jobs associated with the adjustment of the supply of non-tradable goods in the face of reduced domestic demand for these goods, in particular demand based on household and public sector indebtedness. To understand this phenomenon, it is enough to take into account sectors that were dependent on public investment, public demand or private demand financed by indebtedness. The sectors producing non-tradable goods are now facing a lasting contraction in demand (domestic, by definition) and are therefore in a process of adjusting production and employment that will not be recoverable only at a higher stage of development. In contrast, the sectors producing tradable goods are redirecting their production to external markets, optimising the use of installed capacity and increasing market shares. It is these sectors that are particularly market-oriented that will have the opportunity to expand their production capacity and create new jobs by absorbing workers who have been laid off by companies producing non-tradable goods. This means that the reduction in structural unemployment is dependent on the ongoing process of rebalancing the country's productive structure by reallocating resources, including labour, between the non-tradable sector, in contraction, and the tradable sector. This is a process based on the expansion of the production capacity of tradable goods that will determine the creation of job opportunities for workers who have lost their jobs in non-tradable goods producing companies. It is not worth feeding illusions as to the inexorability of this process or about the need to reallocate human resources between sectors. This is an inevitable and painful process for Portuguese society. This means that the current level of unemployment has a strong structural component, affecting both those who worked in the non-tradable goods sectors and those who had not yet entered the labour market, i.e. people over the age of 45 and young people. The management horizon of this adjustment process, as I said, will not be short. The redeployment of workers between sectors obviously implies the recovery of the European economy, but it also involves new investments, which requires entrepreneurial capacity and time. In addition, it is necessary for workers to acquire new qualifications, as long-term unemployment can lead to the obsolescence of previously acquired knowledge. It is therefore urgent to accelerate the expansion of the marketable goods producing sector by increasing its capacity through new investments, and to strengthen or create mechanisms to mitt the effects of this adjustment on social cohesion. From an economic point of view, it is important to avoid a loss of the productive potential of the economy. The unemployed resulting from the structural adjustment process must be permanently excluded from production and therefore from the labour market. To this end, it is necessary to ensure that the requalification mechanisms of workers are efficient and that new jobs are economically sustainable. It is also necessary to ensure that the balance between income support mechanisms and the incentives to re-enter the labour market is safeguarded. That is, income support mechanisms cannot discourage the beneficiary from returning to the labour market. We must be aware that this process takes time, and that it will be more time consuming as the less clear or more misaligned the incentives of economic and social policy. With regard to social cohesion, it is necessary to avoid phenomena of exclusion resulting from the lack of means of subsistence, under penalty of generating a process of lasting destruction, both from the human point of view and from the point of view of productive potential. A balance must be ensured between income support mechanisms, incentives for professional requalification and availability, incentive and interest for re-entry into the labor market. That is, income support mechanisms cannot discourage their beneficiary from returning to the labour market and contribute to the productive potential of the society of which it is a member. Unfortunately, given the nature and size of the ongoing economic adjustment, the absorption of structural unemployment will entail social and personal costs that will be all the greater the longer this process is. Therefore, we must be able to manage this process within a framework that combines mechanisms of social cohesion and efficient mechanisms for redeployment and reuse of the productive potential of the Portuguese working population. It is up to the politically organised society, through the public authorities representing it, to need to establish or strengthen cohesion mechanisms that mitt the effects of exit from the labour market, including the risk of social exclusion by lack of income, and, at the same time, and in the general interest, to promote mechanisms that safeguard and enhance the productive potential incorporated in each worker who has lost his job. It is essential that the third sector and public authorities work in concert. The third sector also plays a very important role in this process of adjusting the Portuguese economy and society, both as a complementary mechanism to combat exclusion and as a determining element of the awakening and strengthening of social awareness of the problems resulting from the ongoing economic and social adjustment process. The third sector can and should play a central role in this bridge between the moment we are in and a near future that I am sure will be brighter, with the resorption of structural unemployment and the consequent contribution to the sustained growth of the Portuguese economy. Many thanks to all for your presence in this Seminar and in this Auditorium of Banco de Portugal. Lisbon, 18 June 2013
text_original: Interveno de abertura do Governad... Interveno de abertura do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa no Seminrio: "A Economia Social, o Emprego e o Desenvolvimento Local" 18 jun. 2013 Comeo por expressar a minha satisfao pelo facto de o Banco de Portugal acolher nas suas instalaes este seminrio promovido pela Critas Portuguesa, em conjunto com o Centro Nacional de Cultura e a IPI Consulting Newtork. Estas instalaes, que correspondem  antiga igreja de So Julio, foram sujeitas a importantes obras de requalificao e devem ser entendidas como um espao vivo e aberto  cidade. Agradeo igualmente a oportunidade que me foi dada para abrir este seminrio. A economia social assume um significado particularmente importante no atual contexto da economia portuguesa, evidenciando o insubstituvel contributo que a sociedade civil pode dar para a coeso social. A economia social, tambm designada por terceiro sector, contempla as atividades privadas de utilidade pblica com origem na sociedade civil. As organizaes deste sector caracterizam-se por (i) estarem formalmente institucionalizadas com rgos de gesto prprios; (ii) terem origem privada; (iii) no terem fins lucrativos, no sentido em que os lucros no so distribudos pelos donos ou pela gesto; (iv) envolverem tipicamente mode-obra em regime de voluntariado. Quando se fala do terceiro sector, h tendncia para questionar se os objetivos sociais e a ausncia de fins lucrativos nestas instituies so compatveis com a gerao de excedentes econmicos ou com preocupaes de eficincia. Esta atitude reflete uma viso incorreta. As instituies do terceiro sector devem gerar os excedentes necessrios ao reforo da sua resilincia e  expanso da sua atividade, pois estes so fatores determinantes da sua sustentabilidade. Estas instituies tm de ser eficientes, ou seja, devem prosseguir os seus objetivos sem desperdcio ou subaproveitamento dos recursos de que dispem. O peso do terceiro sector Apesar de, por vezes, no ser muito percetvel pela opinio pblica, o peso do terceiro sector em Portugal no  de todo negligencivel. A importncia deste sector  ainda maior em momentos marcados por dificuldades socioeconmicas e, em particular, por nveis de desemprego muito elevados, como os atualmente vividos pela sociedade portuguesa. De acordo com o Instituto Nacional de Estatstica (INE), estamos a falar de 55 mil organizaes, que empregam (com contrato) cerca de 260 mil pessoas e que tm um contributo para o PIB de 2,8 por cento. Se contabilizarmos o trabalho voluntrio, o contributo da economia social para o PIB ser da ordem dos 3,8 por cento. Qualquer que seja o critrio de avaliao, o terceiro sector  muito relevante na economia portuguesa. A importncia deste sector ultrapassa, contudo, a mera dimenso econmica: ele  tambm muito relevante na congregao de vontades, atravs do voluntariado. O nmero de pessoas que trabalham em regime de voluntariado  mais elevado do que muitos imaginam. Em Portugal, atinge cerca de um milho de pessoas. De acordo com a informao disponibilizada pelo INE, no terceiro sector, cerca de 40 por cento das horas de trabalho so asseguradas por voluntrios. Podemos pensar,  partida, que o trabalho voluntrio  maioritariamente efetuado por pessoas sem ocupao. Em Portugal, essa ideia no corresponde  realidade. Aqui, o trabalho voluntrio  maioritariamente realizado por pessoas com emprego, facto que, em si, deve constituir matria para reflexo. Significa, desde logo, que ainda h um vasto campo para o desenvolvimento do voluntariado em Portugal. As pessoas sem ocupao tambm podem fazer voluntariado, contribuindo para o interesse geral e para a sua valorizao pessoal. Os dados do INE permitem ainda constatar que, no terceiro sector, a percentagem de voluntrios com formao superior  muito significativa. De facto, o perfil mdio do voluntrio  de algum com formao superior e atividade profissional. Temos de criar condies para atrair as pessoas que no se enquadram neste perfil, sobretudo as que tm mais tempo disponvel para este processo de afirmao cvica.   Alm disso, os indicadores internacionais tambm confirmam que h margem para progredir no que diz respeito ao voluntariado em Portugal. Segundo um relatrio da Comisso Europeia de 2012, em Portugal, o emprego no terceiro sector correspondia a cerca de 5 por cento do emprego total; na Sucia, por exemplo, rondava os 12 por cento. A diferena ainda  mais evidente quando constatamos que apenas 10 por cento dos portugueses fazem voluntariado; nos Pases Baixos, por exemplo, esse nmero atinge 60 por cento. O que permite concluir que, apesar de haver um milho de portugueses envolvidos em servio de voluntariado, ainda estamos muito longe da mdia europeia. Temos, sem dvida, um grande caminho a percorrer. A importncia da eficincia Apesar da importncia do terceiro sector, muitas instituies no tm um modelo adequado de organizao e de gesto, isto , um modelo que vise uma utilizao otimizada dos recursos que tm ao seu dispor ou que tm a possibilidade de mobilizar. A implementao de modelos adequados de organizao e de gesto  fundamental para aumentar a eficincia destas instituies e, consequentemente, o benefcio dos seus destinatrios. Por outras palavras, quanto melhor organizado estiver o terceiro sector mais facilmente conseguir concretizar os objetivos sociais que prossegue. A utilizao eficiente de recursos e a qualidade da organizao constituem dois fatores particularmente relevantes no atual contexto de ajustamento da economia portuguesa e so determinantes para a satisfao dos agentes envolvidos. Um dos grandes desafios da gesto destas instituies consiste em garantir a compensao moral daqueles que nelas trabalham a ttulo voluntrio. Os voluntrios s se sentiro efetivamente satisfeitos e motivados se as organizaes que os acolhem funcionarem de forma eficiente. Isto , se as organizaes lhes transmitirem o sentimento de que fazem parte de uma equipa que procura alcanar objetivos comuns, tirando o melhor partido das competncias e dos esforos de cada um. A organizao  particularmente relevante para o terceiro sector. Quando lidamos com objetivos de natureza social e gerimos recursos humanos em regime de voluntariado tendemos a condescender com falhas de organizao e estar menos atentos  boa utilizao dos recursos. Esta atitude no  desejvel ou aceitvel. Pelo contrrio, a natureza das instituies do terceiro setor tem implcita uma obrigao moral de utilizar os recursos disponveis da melhor maneira possvel, para que cada uma das pessoas que nelas participa se sinta til, satisfeita e motivada para continuar a colaborar. A qualidade da organizao e da gesto destas entidades  ainda mais relevante se tivermos em conta que o terceiro sector tem um patrimnio muito significativo que ter que ser gerido de forma a garantir a sua sustentabilidade e prosseguir novos objetivos. A este propsito, convm no esquecer que muitas instituies tm uma longa histria, por vezes secular, e que ao longo do tempo foram acumulando sucessivas camadas de rotinas que tendem a gerar ineficincias ou a transigir com as suas manifestaes.  necessrio mudar essa realidade. As instituies do terceiro sector tm de profissionalizar a sua gesto e a sua organizao porque s assim sero capazes de envolver e atrair mais cidados disponveis para trabalhar voluntariamente em prol da sociedade. Importncia redobrada do sector no atual processo de ajustamento A importncia do terceiro sector na histria portuguesa nunca foi to grande como no momento que estamos a atravessar. O enorme impacto socioeconmico do processo de ajustamento tem duas dimenses: uma dimenso cclica e uma estrutural. A dimenso cclica corresponde ao desemprego resultante da evoluo desfavorvel da procura externa, que tender a ser reabsorvido com a retoma da economia internacional. A dimenso estrutural do desemprego no resultou da evoluo da procura externa mas sim da destruio permanente dos postos de trabalho associada ao ajustamento da oferta de bens no transacionveis face  reduo da procura domstica desses bens, em particular da procura assente no endividamento das famlias e do sector pblico. Para entender este fenmeno basta ter presente os sectores que estavam dependentes do investimento pblico, da procura pblica ou da procura privada financiada por endividamento. Os sectores produtores de bens no transacionveis esto hoje confrontados com uma contrao duradoura da procura (domstica, por definio) e, por isso, esto num processo de ajustamento da produo e do emprego que no ser recupervel seno num estdio superior de desenvolvimento. Em contraste, os sectores produtores de bens transacionveis esto a redirecionar a sua produo para os mercados externos, otimizando a utilizao da capacidade instalada e aumentando quotas de mercado. So estes sectores especialmente orientados para os mercados externos que tero oportunidade de expandir a sua capacidade de produo e criar novos postos de trabalho, absorvendo os trabalhadores que foram dispensados pelas empresas produtoras de bens no transacionveis. O que significa que a reduo do desemprego estrutural est dependente do processo em curso de reequilbrio da estrutura produtiva do pas atravs da reafectao de recursos, nomeadamente do trabalho, entre o sector dos no transacionveis, em contrao, e o sector dos transacionveis. Este  um processo que assenta na expanso da capacidade de produo de bens transacionveis que determinar a criao de oportunidades de emprego para trabalhadores que perderam os postos de trabalho nas empresas produtoras de bens no transacionveis. No vale a pena alimentar iluses quanto  inexorabilidade deste processo ou quanto  necessidade de reafectar recursos humanos entre sectores. Trata-se de um processo inevitvel e doloroso para a sociedade portuguesa. Isto significa que o atual nvel de desemprego tem uma forte componente estrutural, afetando tanto os que trabalhavam nos sectores de bens no transacionveis como aqueles que no tinham ainda entrado no mercado do trabalho, isto  pessoas com idade superior a 45 anos e jovens. O horizonte de gesto deste processo de ajustamento, como disse, no ser curto. A reafectao de trabalhadores entre sectores implica, obviamente, a retoma da economia europeia, mas implica tambm novos investimentos, o que exige capacidade empreendedora e tempo. Adicionalmente,  necessrio que os trabalhadores adquiram novas qualificaes, pois o desemprego de longa durao pode levar  obsolescncia de conhecimentos anteriormente adquiridos. Urge, por isso, acelerar a expanso do sector produtor de bens transacionveis, aumentando a sua capacidade atravs de novos investimentos, e reforar ou criar mecanismos que mitiguem os efeitos deste ajustamento sobre a coeso social. Do ponto de vista econmico,  importante evitar que se produza uma perda do potencial produtivo da economia. H que evitar que os desempregados resultantes do processo de ajustamento estrutural fiquem definitivamente excludos da produo e, por conseguinte, do mercado de trabalho. Para tal,  necessrio garantir que os mecanismos de requalificao dos trabalhadores sejam eficientes e que os novos postos de trabalho sejam economicamente sustentveis. Tambm  necessrio assegurar que se salvaguarda o equilbrio entre os mecanismos de suporte ao rendimento e os estmulos para reingressar no mercado de trabalho. Isto , os mecanismos de apoio ao rendimento no podem desincentivar o beneficirio de regressar ao mercado de trabalho. Temos de ter conscincia de que este processo leva tempo, e que ser tanto mais demorado quanto menos claros ou mais desalinhados forem os incentivos da poltica econmica e social. Relativamente  coeso social,  necessrio evitar fenmenos de excluso que resultam da carncia de meios de subsistncia, sob pena de se gerar um processo de destruio duradoura, tanto do ponto de vista humano como do ponto de vista do potencial produtivo. H que assegurar o equilbrio entre os mecanismos de suporte ao rendimento, os estmulos para a requalificao profissional e a disponibilidade, incentivo e interesse para o reingresso no mercado de trabalho. Isto , os mecanismos de apoio ao rendimento no podem desincentivar o respetivo beneficirio de regressar ao mercado de trabalho e contribuir para o potencial produtivo da sociedade de que faz parte. Infelizmente, atendendo  natureza e  dimenso do ajustamento econmico em curso, a absoro do desemprego estrutural vai implicar custos sociais e pessoais que sero tanto maiores quanto mais prolongado for este processo. Assim sendo, temos de ser capazes de gerir este processo num quadro que combine mecanismos de coeso social e mecanismos eficientes de reafectao e de reutilizao do potencial produtivo da populao ativa portuguesa. Cabe  sociedade politicamente organizada, atravs dos poderes pblicos que a representam, o imperativo de estabelecer ou reforar mecanismos de coeso que mitiguem os efeitos da sada do mercado do trabalho, nomeadamente o risco de excluso social por ausncia de rendimento, e, simultaneamente, e em nome do interesse geral, promover mecanismos que salvaguardem e potenciem o potencial produtivo incorporado em cada trabalhador que perdeu o seu posto de trabalho.  fundamental que o terceiro sector e as entidades pblicas trabalhem de forma concertada. O terceiro sector tem tambm um papel importantssimo neste processo de ajustamento da economia e da sociedade portuguesas, quer como mecanismo complementar de combate  excluso quer como elemento determinante do despertar e do reforo da conscincia social dos problemas que resultam do processo de ajustamento econmico e social em curso. O terceiro sector pode e deve ter um papel central nesta ponte entre o momento em que nos encontramos e um futuro prximo que estou certo que ser mais risonho, com a reabsoro do desemprego estrutural e o consequente contributo para o crescimento sustentado da economia portuguesa. Muito obrigado a todos pela vossa presena neste Seminrio e neste Auditrio do Banco de Portugal. Lisboa, 18 de junho de 2013

Title: Initial intervention of Deputy Governor Pedro Duarte Neves in the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry into the Conclusion of Financial Risk Management Contracts by Public Sector Companies
text: Initial intervention of the Vice-Government... Initial intervention of Deputy Governor Pedro Duarte Neves in the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry into the Conclusion of Financial Risk Management Contracts by Public Sector Companies 09 jul. 2013 Mr President of the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry, ladies and gentlemen, The call sent to me, on behalf of Banco de Portugal, to participate in this session of the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry into the Conclusion of Financial Risk Management Contracts by Public Sector Companies - which I do with great pleasure - will have been due, I think, to the content of point c) referred to in Resolution of the Assembly of the Republic No. 68/2013 which is as follows: "To assess the degree of knowledge and possible intervention of entities with supervisory powers, in particular in relation to financial sector practices in these procedures". On this particular point I would like to make the following clarification. Swap contracts shall be regarded as financial instruments in accordance with point (i) of Article 2(1) (e) of the Securities Code. Consequently, and regardless of the purpose for which they are contracted, the issuance, marketing, trading and contracting of swaps have been explicitly regulated by this Code since 2007, in accordance with article 2(1) (h). Even in cases where such products are marketed by credit institutions in the retail and/or over-the-counter markets, institutions act as financial intermediaries, which is why the rules of conduct provided for in the Securities Code apply to them. Thus, the regulation, supervision and sanctioning of the rules applicable to swap contracts used, in particular in the management of interest rate risk, are excluded from the behavioral supervision powers of Banco de Portugal, and therefore not responsible for the verification of compliance with the obligations of information or other rules of conduct relating to the marketing and subscription of swap contracts. As far as the prudential supervision of Banco de Portugal is not, as far as Banco de Portugal is not, it does not cover, as is known, branches of banks based in the European Union and foreign banks. As regards national banks and subsidiaries of banks established in the European Union, Banco de Portugal's day-to-day monitoring did not identify, on the one hand, any significant negative impact on the results account of the institutions concerned, and, on the other hand, the risks incurred by these transactions were, in general, mitigated with risk hedging operations. Thus, from an accounting and prudential point of view, there was no concern for the solvency situation of these institutions. Finally, I would like to make a final clarification. As I believe you are aware of, the entities that are part of the state's business sector have no obligation to report to Banco de Portugal on their financing. Therefore, no information from public sector companies concerning the risk management contracts that are the subject of this Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry was sent to Banco de Portugal, as it did not have to be, as it did not have to be: that is, no information was sent by public sector companies on the date of commencing the contractual relationship, the amounts involved, procedures adopted, or on the terms of the contracts concluded. Thank you so much for your attention. Lisbon, 9 July 2013
text_original: Interveno inicial do Vice-Governa... Interveno inicial do Vice-Governador Pedro Duarte Neves na Comisso Parlamentar de Inqurito  Celebrao de Contratos de Gesto de Risco Financeiro por Empresas do Sector Pblico 09 jul. 2013 Senhor Presidente da Comisso Parlamentar de Inqurito, Senhoras e Senhores Deputados, A convocatria que me foi enviada para, em representao do Banco de Portugal, participar nesta sesso da Comisso Parlamentar de Inqurito  Celebrao de Contratos de Gesto de Risco Financeiro por Empresas do Sector Pblico -o que fao com muito gosto  ter ficado a dever-se, julgo, ao contedo da alnea c) referida na Resoluo da Assembleia da Repblica n 68/2013 que  o seguinte: Apurar o grau de conhecimento e eventual interveno das entidades com competncias de superviso, designadamente em relao s prticas do sector financeiro nestes procedimentos. Sobre este aspecto concreto gostava de fazer a seguinte clarificao. Os contratos de swap so considerados instrumentos financeiros, nos termos do ponto i) da alnea e) do n. 1 do artigo 2. do Cdigo dos Valores Mobilirios. Em consequncia, e independentemente da finalidade com que sejam contratados, a emisso, comercializao, negociao e contratao de swaps so, desde 2007, regulados explicitamente por este Cdigo, atento o disposto na alnea h) do n. 1 do referido artigo 2.. Mesmo nos casos em que tais produtos sejam comercializados por instituies de crdito no mercado de retalho e/ou ao balco, as instituies atuam na qualidade de intermedirios financeiros, razo pela qual se lhes aplicam as regras de conduta previstas no Cdigo dos Valores Mobilirios. Desta forma, a regulao, fiscalizao e sancionamento das normas aplicveis aos contratos de swap utilizados, nomeadamente, na gesto de risco de taxa de juro, esto excludos das competncias de superviso comportamental do Banco de Portugal, no lhe competindo por isso a verificao do cumprimento dos deveres de informao ou de outras regras de conduta relativas  comercializao e subscrio de contratos de swap. Quanto  superviso prudencial do Banco de Portugal, esta no abrange, como  sabido, sucursais de bancos com sede na Unio Europeia e bancos estrangeiros. No que se refere aos bancos nacionais e s filiais de bancos com sede na Unio Europeia, o acompanhamento corrente de superviso do Banco de Portugal no identificou, por um lado, qualquer impacto negativo com significado na conta de resultados das instituies em causa, e, por outro, os riscos incorridos com estas operaes estavam, na sua generalidade, mitigados com operaes de cobertura de risco. Assim, do ponto de vista contabilstico e prudencial, no resultou qualquer motivo de preocupao para a situao de solvabilidade destas instituies. Finalmente, gostava de fazer uma clarificao final. Como julgo ser do conhecimento dos Senhores Deputados, as entidades que integram o sector empresarial do Estado no tm qualquer obrigao de reporte ao Banco de Portugal sobre o seu financiamento. Por isso, no foi enviada ao Banco de Portugal, como alis no tinha que ser, qualquer informao proveniente de empresas do sector pblico referente aos Contratos de Gesto de Risco que so o objecto de apreciao desta Comisso Parlamentar de Inqurito: isto , no foi remetida pelas empresas do sector pblico qualquer informao sobre a data de incio da relao contratual, os montantes envolvidos, procedimentos adoptados, ou sobre os termos dos contratos celebrados. Muito obrigado pela vossa ateno. Lisboa, 9 de julho de 2013

Title: Message from Governor Carlos da Silva Costa to the President of APICCAPS
text: Message from Governor Carlos da Si... Message from Governor Carlos da Silva Costa to the President of APICCAPS Dec 4, 2013 Dear President of APICCAPS Fortunato Frederico, I thank you for your kind invitation to participate in the presentation of the new Strategic Plan of the Footwear Industry for the period 2014-2020. With great pity for me, I cannot be present because I am in Frankfurt today at the meeting of the Governing Council of the European Central Bank. The footwear sector has a special meaning for me. In my professional life I have met people from this sector with whom I have established a lasting friendship. Additionally, footwear is an example of success for the Portuguese economy, which has demystified two ideas that are often referred to as obstacles to development. Firstly, the footwear sector has shown that there is no dichotomy between modern and traditional sectors. Portuguese footwear was able to create new production processes, promoting a strong link between companies, and demonstrated that not only is it indispensable but also possible to improve the standard of intrasectoral specialization, by betting not only on improving product quality but also in anticipating demand trends in the upper market segments, moving from the condition of suppliers of products to the condition of producers of demand trends, that is, fashion, and the corresponding products. This demonstration of intrasectoral mobility for higher market segments, with greater added value and greater control of the value chain, is the best demonstration that there is a future for companies in traditional sectors and that this future does not depend on the persistence of a competitiveness model based on low wages, but on consistent dynamics, combining management capacity, technology, knowledge absorption, market knowledge and demand dynamics. Secondly, the footwear sector stresses the importance of exposure to competition in the process of improving intrasectoral specialisation when accompanied by entrepreneurial spirit and an appropriate entrepreneurial attitude. Unlike other sectors, the footwear sector has responded to or even anticipated aggressive and growing international competition by improving efficiency levels and repositioning in the market. The footwear sector has converted two major threats into two great opportunities. I am referring to European integration, with the consequent opening up of the domestic market which was until then captive; and the opening up of the European Community market in the context of globalisation and the emergence of competition in low-wage Asian countries. The success of the answers was not the result of chance or the result of improvisation. It was the result of sharing a strategic feeling among the actors in this process, which had as its pillars an awareness of the objectives to be achieved and of the means to be mobilised and of the ways forward. Among these and other factors, the role of APICCAPS was decisive, not only because it promoted associativism but, above all, because it promoted associativism around the broad sharing of a diagnosis of the situation of the sector and the evolution of the markets, a vision of the future and the means to achieve it, that is, by sharing a strategic concept that guided the multiplicity of the actions and actors that determined the successful trajectory of the sector. The recent achievement of the European Business Promotion Award in the "Support for Internationalisation" category is a recognition of all the work done by APICCAPS, and is also a guarantee of renewal of the successes achieved in the past. This entrepreneurial capacity of APICCAPS is not only a case worthy of study by all those who today are dedicated to the study of the concept of collective entrepreneurship, in the path of Schumpeter's work, but also constitutes a reference for the response of other tradable sectors where SMEs predominate. Congratulations to the footwear sector and its association, APICCAPS. Frankfurt, 4 December 2013 Carlos da Silva Costa Governador Banco de Portugal
text_original: Mensagem do Governador Carlos da Si... Mensagem do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa ao Presidente da APICCAPS 04 dez. 2013 Caro Presidente da APICCAPS Fortunato Frederico, Agradeo o amvel convite que me dirigiu para participar na apresentao do novo Plano Estratgico da Indstria de Calado para o perodo 2014-2020.
