Title: Speech by the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the XXV Lisbon Meeting on Governance of credit institutions and financial stability
text: Intervention of the Governor of the Bank... Speech by the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the XXV Lisbon Meeting on Governance of credit institutions and financial stability 25 Jun 2015 Mr Secretary of State, Ambassadors, Governors, Ladies and Gentlemen, In this speech I will begin by mentioning the importance of the governance models of financial institutions and the lines of defence of their financial soundness, then addressing issues relating to the international framework of banking regulation and supervision schemes and the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing. The governance of institutions and the defence of financial soundness Financial stability is a very valuable public good, a key factor for: (i) preserving the confidence of economic operators; (ii) Ensure adequate allocation of savings to the economy; and (iii) Promoting sustainable economic growth. Increased volatility and increased uncertainty make it difficult to finance the real economy, negatively affecting investment, long-term economic prospects and the well-being of citizens in general. Safeguarding financial stability and efficient functioning of markets require robust and effective rules and institutions to support economic activity. The existence of a sound financial system capable of facing adverse situations, with adequate solvency and liquidity levels, with an appropriate incentive system, with adequate governance and management models and properly regulated and supervised is essential for the proper functioning of any economy. No country is the same as another and each is the bearer of its own culture that is reflected in the governance models and the quality of its financial institutions, as well as on the values that animate them. These factors are critical to ensure their financial soundness and preserve the relationship of trust with their counterparts. The adequacy of credit institutions' corporate governance models is a support for their soundness and, consequently, of safeguarding financial stability. It is essential that governance models ensure: (i) segregation of functions; (ii) the autonomy and independence of internal audit, compliance and risk management functions; (iii) that the interests of stakeholders and the general interest of the institution are properly taken care of. There are several lines of defense of financial soundness and stability. Two of them are within the financial institutions themselves: they are the supervisory and internal control bodies and their administration. The third line of defence is external auditors, who play a central role in verifying and assessing the quality of information. Supervisors, such as Banco de Portugal, are on a fourth line of defense. These various lines of defence imply that financial stability depends critically on the production of information, the various levels of verification and the use of such information, in particular for the purposes of stakeholder information and supervision. It should also be kept in mind that, in the globalised world in which we live, with a growing interdependence of financial institutions, supervisors cannot focus their assessment on an institution of themselves, they must grasp the interactions it has with all others. As they say, it is necessary to be very attentive to the tree and, at the same time, very attentive to the forest. This approach, which goes beyond the individual situation and contextualizes it in a broader framework, has been finding a reflection on the evolution of supervisory models. In fact, in the wake of the international financial crisis, supervisory models have been undergoing significant changes, becoming more intrusive and, at the same time, having a more transversal and foresighted approach. However, despite all the progress and improvements made in recent years, these models obviously continue to have limitations and constraints. As stated in the Financial Stability Board report submitted to the G20 in November 2012: "No supervisory system can catch everything." The difficulties faced by a supervisor are magnified by the fact that financial institutions often operate in multiple jurisdictions, requiring very close cooperation with multiple supervisors, with different practices and attitudes. If institutions operate in more "opaque" and less cooperative jurisdictions, the risks to conducting supervisory activity are obviously enhanced. The intensification of the international activity of Portuguese banks, particularly in Portuguese-speaking countries, and the increasing involvement of their banking systems, make it essential to promote close cooperation between the various regulatory and supervisory authorities. Banco de Portugal attaches particular importance to joint reflection on issues relating to the regulation and supervision of credit institutions and the safeguarding of financial stability. These considerations lead me to the second part of my speech, which is about aligning regulatory and supervisory arrangements. Alignment of regulatory and supervisory arrangements The international financial crisis showed the existence of several vulnerabilities and regulatory failures, affecting the very foundations of the global financial system. In particular, it made visible the misalignment between the globalization of markets and the institutional and normative framework of regulation and supervision, as well as the expressive role of an unregulated sector. The institutional and regulatory changes that have been introduced, with emphasis on the implementation of Basel III and the European banking union construction project, will not cease to have an impact on all Portuguese-speaking countries and the financial institutions operating in them. Banco de Portugal, as part of the European financial system, is naturally very committed to working together with its counterparts on this matter. As a reflection of this commitment, Banco de Portugal's cooperation activity with the other Central Banks of portuguese-speaking countries (BCPLP) has increasing focus on supervision and safeguarding financial stability in its various dimensions: macroprudential, microprudential and behavioural supervision, sanctioning action and prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing. It is important that the supervisory regimes of the various countries pursue the objective of aligning with the international regulatory framework for banking supervision. In the specific context of the European Union, the fulfilment of conditions allowing the recognition of the equivalence of supervisory schemes in third countries induces potential benefits, as it influences the determination of capital requirements related to the activity of subsidiaries of the European institutions and thus the volume and cost of financing local economies. I would like to highlight in this regard the draft cooperation between the BCPLP on the regimes for the regulation and supervision of banking systems, the basis of which was launched at the XXII Lisbon Meeting in November 2012. In this context, the importance of identifying the conditions in banking legislation and in the regulatory and supervisory procedures of the various countries could undermine the equivalence between regimes and between them and the European Union regime was undermined. To give body to this project, a Working Group composed of representatives of bcplp was constituted. This group has already produced a preliminary report, in which a comparative analysis of the legal and regulatory regimes of the different countries involved is carried out, based on a previous exercise of self-assessment, with the aim of enabling the identification of good practices and possible lines of convergence. To this end, the regulatory framework for supervised activity and supervisory mechanisms in the various systems was carried out, the organisation of their supervisory systems was examined and important supervisory issues such as access to the activity and conditions of exercise, the prudential supervision process and the fight against capital raising and terrorist financing were also addressed. The first conclusions of this work were presented at the III BCPLP Banking Supervision Meeting, held in Brasilia, on June 17 and 18, with the aim of promoting the debate and establishing a timetable for the conclusion of the final report, which is expected to take place in 2015. The conclusions of the preliminary report and subsequent debate should contribute to a growing rapprochement between the regulatory and supervisory systems of Portuguese-speaking countries and the international legal and regulatory framework. Promoting convergence between these schemes will enhance compliance with the conditions necessary for the recognition of the equivalence of these countries' supervisory systems in relation to the existing EU regime. It should be noted that, with the entry into force of the European Prudential Requirements Regulation, which introduced Basel III into the sphere of the European Union, the process of recognition of equivalence of third country supervisory regimes, leaving the national supervisory authorities to have the power to carry out such recognition on a bilateral basis. The process now is the exclusive competence of the European Commission, which has now carried out recognition on a multilateral basis. In this new framework, the Commission has already adopted an equivalence decision in December 2014 identifying a number of third countries considered equivalent, and a new equivalence assessment process is currently underway, with the collaboration of the European Banking Authority (EBA). As with the methodology adopted by the Working Group set up among the BCPLP to which I have already referred, the work of the EBA-led Group will be based on the responses to a questionnaire to which the countries whose schemes will be examined should respond. Thus, the exercise carried out at BCPLP level may also prove useful for Portuguese-speaking countries that will be the subject of such evaluation. At the same time, the EBA assessed the equivalence of professional secrecy schemes in a number of countries, giving rise to a recommendation from that Authority on the third countries assessed as equivalent to join colleges of supervisors in the European Union. Banco de Portugal considers it of the utmost importance to boost and strengthen initiatives that enhance an approximation between regulatory and supervisory regimes in the global financial market. The issue of alignment with the international regulatory framework for banking supervision becomes even more critical when associated with other dimensions, such as preventing and combating money laundering practices, as these may, in particular, derail correspondence between banks, with the consequent risk of financial exclusion for some countries. Prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing The soundness, integrity and stability of financial institutions and confidence in the financial system can be severely undermined through money laundering practices that often take on a transnational dimension. Important efforts have been made globally to prevent and combat this type of practice, notably through the Financial Action Group (FATF). A new Directive (the fourth) on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing has recently been adopted at European Union level, introducing new requirements, in particular in the light of the revised FATF recommendations. The new European regulations will obviously have an impact on the relationship with third-country institutions. There are multiple changes introduced by the Directive. By way of example I mark only four: (i) the creation of a centralised register of beneficial owners of entities companies and other legal persons incorporated in national territory, with access to for competent authorities and financial institutions; (ii) changes in the definition of risk jurisdictions, with the the European Commission is not to issue a list of third-party jurisdictions with strategic deficiencies in this area; (iii) the permission of the unrestricted and direct exchange of information between the parent home of a transnational banking group and its subsidiaries and subsidiaries calls for the removal of obstacles to exchanges of information in the banking groups; (iv) Innovations in correspondence relationships with institutions third-country financial institutions, with the implementation of enhanced surveillance measures that go beyond traditional banking correspondence relationships (e.g. in the context of transfer of funds or securities settlement). These developments, aimed at strengthening the anti-money laundering devices, presenting in themselves a clear rationality, do not fail to place important challenges with regard to the adaptation of the various banking systems to the new European regulations in an increasingly interdependent world. We will all have to make an effort to improve not only the mechanisms for preventing money laundering, specific to credit institutions and their effective supervision, but also the mechanisms for exchanging information in this area, together with the transparency-enhancing mechanisms to identify the ultimate control of the various collective structures operating in our financial systems. I am sure that through the continued committed and articulated effort of all, which has been characteristic of these 25 years of cooperation, it will be possible to contribute to the identification and reduction of obstacles and blockades, to a closer approximation between regulatory and supervisory regimes and, ultimately, to the promotion of the confidence of economic operators, stability and sustained growth of our economies. Thank you very much [1] Ready for presentation.
text_original: Interveno do Governador do Banco... Interveno do Governador do Banco de Portugal, Carlos da Silva Costa, no XXV Encontro de Lisboa sobre Governao das instituies de crdito e estabilidade financeira 25 jun. 2015 Senhor Secretrio de Estado, Senhores Embaixadores, Senhores Governadores, Minhas Senhoras e meus Senhores, Nesta interveno comearei por referir a importncia dos modelos de governao das instituies financeiras e as linhas de defesa da respetiva solidez financeira, abordando em seguida questes relativas ao enquadramento internacional dos regimes de regulao e superviso bancria e  preveno do branqueamento de capitais e do financiamento do terrorismo. A governao das instituies e a defesa da solidez financeira A estabilidade financeira  um bem pblico valiosssimo, um fator-chave para: (i) Preservar a confiana dos agentes econmicos; (ii) Assegurar uma adequada afetao da poupana na economia; e (iii) Promover o crescimento econmico sustentvel. Maior volatilidade e acrescida incerteza dificultam o financiamento da economia real , afetando negativamente o investimento, as perspetivas econmicas de longo prazo e o bem-estar dos cidados em geral. A salvaguarda da estabilidade financeira, bem como o funcionamento eficiente dos mercados exigem regras e instituies robustas e eficazes que apoiem a atividade econmica. A existncia de um sistema financeiro slido , capaz de enfrentar situaes adversas, com nveis de solvabilidade e de liquidez adequados, com um sistema de incentivos apropriado, com modelos de governao e de gesto adequados e devidamente regulado e supervisionado  essencial para o bom funcionamento de qualquer economia. Nenhum pas  igual a outro e cada um  portador de uma cultura prpria que se repercute nos modelos de governao e na qualidade das suas instituies financeiras , bem como nos valores que as animam. Estes fatores so crticos para garantir a sua solidez financeira e preservar a relao de confiana com as suas contrapartes. A adequao dos modelos de governao corporativa das instituies de crdito  um sustentculo da sua solidez e, consequentemente, da salvaguarda da estabilidade financeira.  fundamental que os modelos de governao garantam: (i) a segregao de funes; (ii) a autonomia e independncia das funes de auditoria interna, de compliance e de gesto de riscos; (iii) que os interesses dos stakeholders e o interesse geral da instituio so devidamente acautelados. So vrias as linhas de defesa da solidez financeira e da estabilidade. Duas delas situamse dentro das prprias instituies financeiras : so os rgos de fiscalizao e de controlo interno e a respetiva Administrao. A terceira linha de defesa so os auditores externos, que desempenham um papel central na verificao e avaliao da qualidade da informao. Os supervisores, como o Banco de Portugal, situam-se numa quarta linha de defesa. Estas vrias linhas de defesa implicam que a estabilidade financeira depende, de forma crtica, da produo de informao, dos vrios nveis de verificao e da utilizao dessa informao, nomeadamente para efeitos de informao dos stakeholders e de superviso. Importa tambm ter presente que, no mundo globalizado em que vivemos, com uma crescente interdependncia das instituies financeiras, os supervisores no podem centrar a sua avaliao numa instituio de per si, tm de apreender as interaes que esta mantm com todas as outras. Como se costuma dizer,  necessrio estar muito atento  rvore e, simultaneamente, muito atento  floresta. Esta abordagem, que vai alm da situao individual e a contextualiza num quadro mais amplo , tem vindo a encontrar reflexo na evoluo dos modelos de superviso.De facto, na sequncia da crise financeira internacional, os modelos de superviso tm vindo a sofrer alteraes significativas, tornando-se mais intrusivos e, em paralelo, passando a ter um enfoque mais transversal e mais prospetivo. Todavia, apesar de todos os progressos e aperfeioamentos introduzidos nos ltimos anos, estes modelos continuam a ter, obviamente, limitaes e condicionantes . Conforme refere o relatrio do Financial Stability Board apresentado ao G20 em novembro de 2012: No supervisory system can catch everything. As dificuldades com que um supervisor se defronta so ampliadas pelo facto de as instituies financeiras atuarem com frequncia em mltiplas jurisdies , exigindo uma cooperao muito estreita com mltiplos supervisores, com diferentes prticas e atitudes. Caso as instituies operem em jurisdies mais opacas e menos cooperantes, os riscos para a conduo da atividade de superviso so obviamente potenciados. A intensificao da atividade internacional dos bancos portugueses , designadamente em Pases de Lngua Portuguesa, e o envolvimento crescente dos respetivos sistemas bancrios, tornam essencial a promoo de uma cooperao estreita entre as diversas autoridades de regulao e de superviso. O Banco de Portugal atribui particular relevncia  reflexo conjunta sobre as questes relativas  regulao e superviso das instituies de crdito e  salvaguarda da estabilidade financeira. Estas consideraes conduzem-me  segunda parte da minha interveno, que tem a ver com o alinhamento dos regimes de regulao e de superviso . Alinhamento dos regimes de regulao e de superviso A crise financeira internacional veio mostrar a existncia de diversas vulnerabilidades e falhas regulamentares, atingindo as prprias fundaes do sistema financeiro global. Em especial, tornou visvel o desalinhamento entre a globalizao dos mercados e o quadro institucional e normativo de regulao e superviso, bem como o expressivo papel de um setor no regulamentado. As alteraes institucionais e regulamentares que tm vindo a ser introduzidas , com destaque para a implementao de Basileia III e para o projeto europeu de construo da Unio Bancria, no deixaro de ter impacto em todos os Pases de Lngua Portuguesa e nas instituies financeiras que neles operam. O Banco de Portugal, enquanto integrante do sistema financeiro europeu, est naturalmente muito empenhado em trabalhar conjuntamente com os seus homlogos nesta matria. Como reflexo deste empenho, a atividade de cooperao do Banco de Portugal com os restantes Bancos Centrais dos Pases de Lngua Portuguesa (BCPLP) tem atribudo um enfoque crescente  superviso e  salvaguarda da estabilidade financeira nas suas vrias dimenses: superviso macroprudencial, microprudencial e comportamental, ao sancionatria e preveno do branqueamento de capitais e do financiamento do terrorismo.  importante que os regimes de superviso dos vrios pases prossigam o objetivo de alinhamento com o enquadramento regulamentar internacional em matria de superviso bancria. No contexto especfico da Unio Europeia, o preenchimento de condies que permitam o reconhecimento da equivalncia dos regimes de superviso em pases terceiros induz potenciais benefcios, na medida em que influencia a determinao dos requisitos de fundos prprios relacionados com a atividade das filiais das instituies europeias e, dessa forma, o volume e o custo de financiamento s economias locais. Gostaria de destacar a este propsito o projeto de cooperao entre os BCPLP relativo aos regimes de regulao e superviso dos sistemas bancrios, cujas bases foram lanadas no XXII Encontro de Lisboa, em novembro de 2012. Assumiu-se, neste mbito, a importncia de identificar os condicionamentos existentes na legislao bancria e nos procedimentos de regulao e superviso dos diversos pases que pudessem prejudicar a equivalncia entre regimes e entre estes e o regime da Unio Europeia. Para dar corpo a este projeto, foi constitudo um Grupo de Trabalho composto por representantes dos BCPLP. Este grupo produziu j um relatrio preliminar, no qual se procede a uma anlise comparativa dos regimes legais e regulamentares dos diferentes pases envolvidos, baseada num exerccio prvio de autoavaliao, com o intuito de permitir a identificao de boas prticas e possveis linhas de convergncia. Para o efeito, procedeu-se ao enquadramento normativo da atividade supervisionada e dos mecanismos de superviso nos vrios ordenamentos, foi analisada a organizao dos respetivos sistemas de superviso e foram ainda abordados temas importantes em matria de superviso, como sejam o acesso  atividade e condies de exerccio, o processo de superviso prudencial e o combate ao braqueamento de capitais e ao financiamento do terrorismo. As primeiras concluses deste trabalho foram apresentadas no III Encontro de Superviso Bancria dos BCPLP, realizado em Braslia, nos passados dias 17 e 18 de junho, com o objetivo de promover o debate e estabelecer um calendrio para concluso do relatrio final, que dever ter lugar ainda em 2015. As concluses do relatrio preliminar e o debate subsequente devero contribuir para uma aproximao crescente entre os sistemas de regulao e superviso dos Pases de Lngua Portuguesa e o enquadramento legal e regulatrio internacional. A promoo da convergncia entre estes regimes permitir potenciar o cumprimento das condies necessrias para o reconhecimento da equivalncia dos regimes de superviso destes pases face ao regime vigente na UE. Importa notar que, com a entrada em vigor do Regulamento Europeu relativo aos requisitos prudenciais, que introduziu Basileia III na esfera da Unio Europeia, alterou-se o processo de reconhecimento de equivalncia dos regimes de superviso de pases terceiros, deixando as autoridades de superviso nacionais de ter a faculdade do proceder a esse reconhecimento, numa base bilateral. O processo  agora da competncia exclusiva da Comisso Europeia que passou a realizar o reconhecimento numa base multilateral. Neste novo enquadramento, a Comisso j adotou uma deciso de equivalncia, em dezembro de 2014, identificando um conjunto de pases terceiros considerados equivalentes, encontrando-se atualmente em curso um novo processo de avaliao de equivalncia, com a colaborao da Autoridade Bancria Europeia (EBA).  semelhana da metodologia adotada pelo Grupo de Trabalho constitudo entre os BCPLP a que j aludi, o trabalho do Grupo liderado pela EBA ter por base as respostas a um questionrio a que os pases cujos regimes sero analisados devero responder. Deste modo, o exerccio efetuado ao nvel dos BCPLP poder igualmente revelar-se til para os Pases de Lngua Portuguesa que venham a ser objeto da referida avaliao. Paralelamente, a EBA avaliou a equivalncia dos regimes de segredo profissional de um conjunto de pases, dando origem a uma recomendao daquela Autoridade, sobre a possibilidade de os pases terceiros avaliados como equivalentes integrarem colgios de supervisores na Unio Europeia. O Banco de Portugal considera da maior importncia a dinamizao e fortalecimento das iniciativas que potenciem uma aproximao entre regimes de regulao e superviso no mercado financeiro global. A questo do alinhamento com o enquadramento regulamentar internacional em matria de superviso bancria torna-se ainda mais crtica quando associada a outras dimenses, como, por exemplo, a preveno e combate s prticas de branqueamento de capitais, uma vez que estas podem, nomeadamente, inviabilizar relaes de correspondncia entre bancos, com o consequente risco de excluso financeira para alguns pases. Preveno do branqueamento de capitais e do financiamento do terrorismo A solidez, integridade e estabilidade das instituies financeiras e a confiana no sistema financeiro podem ser gravemente comprometidas atravs de prticas de branqueamento de capitais que assumem, com frequncia, dimenso transnacional. Importantes esforos tm vindo a ser desenvolvidos a nvel global para prevenir e combater este tipo de prticas, designadamente atravs do Grupo de Ao Financeira (GAFI). A nvel da Unio Europeia foi recentemente aprovada uma nova Diretiva (a quarta) sobre a preveno do branqueamento de capitais e do financiamento do terrorismo que introduz novas exigncias, designadamente  luz das recomendaes revistas do GAFI. A nova regulamentao europeia ter obviamente impacto no relacionamento com instituies de pases terceiros. So mltiplas as alteraes introduzidas pela diretiva. A ttulo de exemplo assinalo apenas quatro: (i) A criao de um registo centralizado de beneficirios efetivos de entidades societrias e de outras pessoas coletivas constitudas em territrio nacional, de acesso irrestrito para as autoridades competentes e instituies financeiras; (ii) As alteraes em matria de definio de jurisdies de risco, passando a competir  Comisso Europeia a emisso de uma lista de jurisdies terceiras com deficincias estratgicas nesta matria; (iii) A permisso da troca irrestrita e direta de informaes entre a casa-me de um grupo bancrio transnacional e as suas sucursais e filiais participadas maioritariamente, apelando  remoo dos obstculos s trocas de informao no mbito dos grupos bancrios; (iv) As inovaes em matria de relaes de correspondncia com instituies financeiras de pases terceiros, com aplicao de medidas de vigilncia reforadas que vo alm das tradicionais relaes de correspondncia bancria (e.g. no mbito de operaes de transferncia de fundos ou de liquidao de valores mobilirios). Estes desenvolvimentos, destinados a robustecer os dispositivos de preveno do branqueamento de capitais, apresentando em si mesmos uma racionalidade clara, no deixam de colocar importantes desafios no que concerne  adaptao dos vrios sistemas bancrios  nova regulamentao europeia, num mundo cada vez mais interdependente. Todos teremos de fazer um esforo para melhorar no s os dispositivos de preveno do branqueamento de capitais, prprios das instituies de crdito e a sua efetiva superviso, como tambm os mecanismos de troca de informaes relativamente a esta matria, a par dos dispositivos de reforo da transparncia que permitam identificar o controlo ltimo das diversas estruturas coletivas que atuam nos nossos sistemas financeiros. Estou certo de que atravs da continuao do esforo empenhado e articulado de todos, que tem caraterizado estes 25 anos de cooperao, ser possvel contribuir para a identificao e reduo de obstculos e bloqueios, para uma maior aproximao entre regimes de regulao e superviso e, em ltima instncia, para a promoo da confiana dos agentes econmicos, da estabilidade financeira e do crescimento sustentado das nossas economias. Title: Inauguration speech of the Governor of Banco de Portugal
text: Gove's swearing-in speech... Inauguration speech of the Governor of Banco de Portugal 10 jul. 2015 Madam Minister of State and Finance, Minister for Internal Affairs, Minister for the Presidency and Parliamentary Affairs, Minister for the Economy, Secretaries of State, President of the Audit Board of Banco de Portugal, Members of the Advisory Board of Banco de Portugal, Ladies and Gentlemen, Members of the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal, Ladies and gentlemen, I begin by thanking me for the confidence i have placed to continue to lead Banco de Portugal for the next five years. Banco de Portugal's activity in the last five years has developed in a particularly adverse and demanding context, characteristic: -By the implementation of the Economic and Financial Assistance Program to Portugal; -By tensions in international financial markets, by the financial fragmentation of the euro area and by the subsequent and desirable decision to create the Banking Union. During this period, the Bank was called upon to assume broad and complex responsibilities, of which it would highlight the following: -Under the Economic and Financial Assistance Program, Banco de Portugal assumed several functions related to its mandate to safeguard the stability of the financial system Portuguese. It also provided economic and financial advice to the Government, provided extensive statistical information and processed the financial flows of the assistance programme; -As a member of the Eurosystem and co-responsible for monetary policy in the euro area, Banco de Portugal: or Actively participated in the design and implementation of monetary policy measures aimed at combating financial fragmentation; or Successfully secured the migration to the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) and completed in good time work on linking the European central bank currency securities settlement (T2S) platform, which came into operation recently (in June 2015); or Participated in the development of the second series of euro banknotes and produced a share of the new 20 euro banknotes; -In the field of economic studies, the Bank continued to have its work published in leading scientific journals and confirmed, in the Eurosystem, a reputation for excellence in research; -In the field of statistics, the Bank maintained high quality standards in statistical production and dissemination, as is acknowledged by the recent adhering to the imf's most demanding standard (under the so-called Special Data Dissemination Standard Plus); -In the field of behavioural supervision, the Bank has invested heavily in financial literacy and inclusion, in parallel with safeguarding the balance of banks' relationship with their clients; -Finally, in the framework of the new powers assigned to it, Banco de Portugal applied a resolution measure to Banco Espirito Santo, the third largest banking group Portuguese. This period was marked by a particularly difficult challenge that consisted of maintaining financial stability in a context of severe restrictions on public indebtedness, and in which the national banking system had accumulated underprovisioned risk and insufficient undue ness. The situation of the banking system in 2010 was the culmination of a policy pursued over more than a decade of: -Underestimation of risk; -Sector credit concentration; -Financing of highly leveraged takeovers; -Tolerance towards unsustainable levels of household and business indebtedness. This approach - which I repeat has been pursued over more than a decade - reflected in an allocation of resources that did not take due account of the optimization of return on investment or, at the very least, the ability to recover the credit granted through the generation of adequate cash-flows. The consequence was, as you would expect, a mediocre evolution of the potential product, with a loss of the volume and quality of employment created. In the context of the crisis, the banking system was forced to recognise a high level of comparades, with a negative impact on results and, consequently, the need to strengthen capital. The total number of odd jobs amounted to almost EUR 40 billion in the period 2008-2014. Compared to other countries in an imbalance, it should be stressed that, in the case of Portuguese, the management of the rebalancing process was done with the safeguarding of financial stability and the protection of the public and the "cotton test" is: -On the one hand, the benign evolution of deposits, which mirrors the confidence of bank customers (in the period between 2008 and 2014, deposits of residents to the banking system grew by about 11 percent); -And, on the other hand, the impact of aid to the financial system on public debt, which has been lower than in many other economies, including the euro area. According to data from the European Commission, in the period 2008-2013, public support measures for the financial sector in Portugal totalled 6.6 percent of GDP (compared with about 40 percent in Ireland, 22 percent in Greece and 9.3 percent in Spain). When, in 2010, I started my first term as Governor I was well aware of the large scale of this challenge. At that time, I stressed the need to strengthen the supervision of financial institutions, following an approach of proximity, intrusive, and subordinated to the principle of systematic doubt. To this end, I established that Banco de Portugal would need to be embletin competences and organisational models to ensure: -Timely, effective and independent microprudential supervision; -A permanent assessment of systemic risks; -strengthening the capacity to review and discuss new rules and new models of prudential supervision; -An active and influential participation in national and international macroprudential supervision mechanisms. These guidelines were well present in the activity and performance of Banco de Portugal throughout my first term. In fact, significant changes were made at the level of the organizational and government structure of Banco de Portugal, new competencies and analysis instruments were developed and human resources were strengthened, according to a logic of adequacy of competence profiles to the functions performed and obeying principles of meritocracy. However, this task is not yet completed and future challenges will not be less demanding. Building on the experience and lessons of the past, I intend to deepen these guidelines during my second term of office, now within the framework of the european banking union in consolidation. Significant progress has been made in the last few years in correcting these imbalances, but the task is yet to be completed. Thus: -Banks have significantly reduced their leverage, measured by the relationship between credit and deposits, but still have low levels of profitability that are reflective of: -Lower efficiency ratios than competitors, -Low financial margins, -Significant amounts of credit at risk, -High concentration of risk in certain assets and sectors, such as real estate; -Companies have low degrees of financial autonomy, reflecting low capital levels and low propensity for self-financing (debt as a percentage of non-financial companies' GDP in Portugal was around 124 per cent at the end of 2013, compared with an average of 87 per cent in the euro area), to the detriment of their ability to invest and innovate and their resilience to changing economic conditions and the emergence of new competitors; -Households still have high levels of indebtedness (around 91 per cent of GDP in 2013, compared to 61 per cent in the euro area), making them vulnerable to income declines - particularly those resulting from increases in unemployment, or the persistence of structural unemployment - and adjustments in interest rates. There is therefore a priority agenda, which consists of: -Strengthening the capitalisation of banks to ensure adequate coverage of the risks they are or may be exposed to, in particular in adverse economic scenarios; furthermore, the necessary capitalization will have to take into account the specificity of each institution in terms of balance sheet, risk, business model, and the ability of shareholders to respond to a capital increase if necessary; -ensure the sustainability of banks' business models, including through the adoption of a cost structure appropriate to their ability to generate revenue, and taking into account the prospects of a single supervisory and regulatory framework and new forms of interaction between banks and customers; -Anticipate movements of rationalisation and consolidation of the banking system at European level, the necessary consequence of the creation of a banking union with single supervision, a single resolution mechanism and, as expected, a single deposit guarantee mechanism; -Strengthen the governance model of institutions by reference to best practices, with a particular focus on: (i) The competence, capacity and autonomy of risk assessment and management, control and compliance and internal audit functions; (ii) transparency of strategic decisions and the off-balance sheet situation, in order to protect unrepresented interests, whether minority shareholders or depositors or the general public; -Adopt mechanisms that prevent unsustainable indebtedness of individuals and businesses and not feed unsustainable demand levels that generally give rise to sectoral bubbles (as happened in some countries with the construction and real estate promotion sectors). The aim is to avoid painful adjustments by debtors, significant demand breakdowns, bankruptcies, unemployment and uncollectables in the financial system; -Ensure the continued controlled deleveraging of the non-financial business sector, based on an increase in corporate own capital, in particular through the development of risk-sharing savings instruments (e.g. by taking equity or subordinated loans). In this context, banks will be encouraged to: (i) Adopt an active attitude of credit risk management once critical levels of financial dependence on the part of each company have been exceeded; for example by requiring capital gains, ceding debt to investors interested in participating in company capital or converting debt into equity. Of course, this presupposes a legal framework favourable to the conversion into equity or subordinated debt of the party exceeding the acceptable levels of corporate indebtedness; (ii) apply higher risk weights, and consequently capital consumption, to exposures considered excessive, in order to discourage unsustainable leverage; -Ensure a reallocation of resources that promote sustainable growth of potential product and job creation, including through viable investment in the tradable sector. To this end, banks need to take a new step towards the implementation of the savings they are in. But it's not enough. Lessons must be learned from the interdependencies between financial institutions and between them and the non-financial area. A proactive approach to safeguarding financial stability needs to be taken by using macroprudential measures and adapting legal frameworks, in particular the tax regime. The solidity of each tree does not guarantee the sustainability of the forest. This means that supervision has to go beyond the activation of risk containment measures at the level of each institution, i.e. it has to adopt macroprudential measures that define and maintain fire lines that misunderstand the risk of contagion. All in all: -We had to limit the risks of a forest in which the trees grew less guarded, with weakened trunks that undermined the solidity of the tree itself; -We had to avoid the domino effect on the financial system that resulted from the risk of a large institution being reduced. Effectively, a large tree with a disproportionate canopy and, on top of that, with a weakened trunk can determine the destruction of the surrounding forest. I refer to the cases of oversized institutions with own funds that did not not only take into account the oddities of the assets contained in the balance sheet, but also reflected inappropriate value-taking practices; -We had to review our own methods of surveillance and supervision which, as in the case of all other supervisors, were based on values and incentives that did not match reality (an illusion of values and behaviors that fueled another illusion that proved deadly: that of self-regulation). Today, the challenge of supervision is not to fall into the illusion that institutions are virtuous and based on values and principles aimed at balancing the different interests in presence and, above all, the general interest. Values, principles and institutions are specific to a particular society, so the supervisory model cannot ignore this specificity. In fact, and in general, supervision today has a lack of institutional values and frameworks that oblige it not only to be vigilant about compliance with the rules and principles, but also on the quality of the information provided to it and the models of government that produce it. This means that it is necessary to strengthen the mechanisms for auditing the quality and integrity of information and to significantly strengthen the sanctions applicable to fraud and failures in these areas. We are talking about the foundations of public trust in the information provided to the different stakeholders and those who care for the general interest, that is to say the supervisors. In this increasingly complex environment, Banco de Portugal's active and influential participation in the European decision-making process implies an increased demand in terms of competences, resources and the quality and robustness of its processes and its model of government. Contrary to what many will think, the responsibilities and functions entrusted today to Banco de Portugal are not only much higher, but even more complex than those assigned to it when Portugal had its own currency. Participation in monetary union since 1999 and, more recently, in the banking union, require Banco de Portugal to have multiple knowledge and skills and, above all, a technical and operational capacity never before exercised, in order to influence the formulation of solutions and decision-making with relevance at European level. An influential country presupposes an influential and active central bank in the different European forums in which it participates. The truth is that in this context of great demand, Banco de Portugal has been able to assert itself among its peers based on the quality of the analyses it produces and the skills it has available, having earned a high reputation in various areas of shared responsibility. This is the result of the bank's excellent technical quality of human resources, as well as its effort and a proactive attitude of problem-making and solution formulation. In this sense, Banco de Portugal will continue to invest in its greatest asset, which are the employees, through the enhancement of internal talent, the promotion of policies of differentiation and recognition of merit, promoting the strengthening of its technical independence and its corporate culture. With the rejuvenation of the Bank's staff, special attention will also be paid to strengthening cohesion between different generations of workers, in order to ensure a full alignment of all with the values and ethical standards of the Institution. In this regard, I would like to point out that the Bank will soon complete the revision of the Codes of Conduct which had already been strengthened during my first term of office. These apply to both members of the Board of Directors and employees in general, following best practices in this area and the framework emanating from the Eurosystem. In the context of internal management, the Bank will continue its policy of cost containment and internal efficiency, based on more collaborative, more results-oriented management practices and with greater flexibility in the use of its human and material resources. Internal governance support mechanisms, in particular for risk management, compliance and internal audit, will also be strengthened, alongside the deepening of strategic planning exercises and management monitoring and control tools. Therefore, I am sure that Banco de Portugal will successfully overcome future challenges, demonstrating that it is an agile organization, able to constantly review the working methods and instruments and to make improvements to its operation in the face of the rapid and permanent change in the reality that accompanies it. In this context, the Bank will continue to deepen institutional cooperation with other authorities, in particular with other regulators and political powers, in all initiatives contributing to the improvement of the financial system and to the development of the Portuguese economy and society - naturally respecting the specific competences of each and its institutional independence. For the task entrusted to me now, I am sure that I will count on the competence, availability and solidarity of my colleagues on the Board of Directors, whom I take this opportunity to thank for the support provided in the last five years, as well as all the employees of Banco de Portugal. Thank you very much. Carlos da Silva Costa Lisbon, 10 July 2015
text_original: Discurso de tomada de posse do Gove... Discurso de tomada de posse do Governador do Banco de Portugal 10 jul. 2015 Senhora Ministra de Estado e das Finanas, Senhora Ministra da Administrao Interna, Senhor Ministro da Presidncia e Assuntos Parlamentares, Senhor Ministro da Economia, Senhores Secretrios de Estado, Senhor Presidente do Conselho de Auditoria do Banco de Portugal, Senhores Membros do Conselho Consultivo do Banco de Portugal, Caros Colegas, Membros do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Portugal, Minhas Senhoras e meus Senhores, Comeo por agradecer a confiana que me  depositada para continuar a liderar o Banco de Portugal nos prximos cinco anos. A atividade do Banco de Portugal nos ltimos cinco anos desenvolveu-se num contexto particularmente adverso e exigente, caraterizado: -Pela execuo do Programa de Assistncia Econmica e Financeira a Portugal; -Por tenses nos mercados financeiros internacionais, pela fragmentao financeira da rea do euro e pela subsequente, e desejvel, deciso de criar a Unio Bancria. Durante este perodo, o Banco foi chamado a assumir amplas e complexas responsabilidades, de que destacaria as seguintes: -No mbito do Programa de Assistncia Econmica e Financeira, o Banco de Portugal assumiu diversas funes relacionadas com o seu mandato de salvaguarda da estabilidade do sistema financeiro portugus. Adicionalmente prestou aconselhamento econmico e financeiro ao Governo, forneceu vasta informao estatstica e processou os fluxos financeiros do programa de assistncia; -Enquanto membro do Eurosistema e corresponsvel pela poltica monetria na rea do euro, o Banco de Portugal: o Participou ativamente no desenho e na implementao das medidas de poltica monetria destinadas a combater a fragmentao financeira; o Assegurou com sucesso a migrao para a rea nica de Pagamentos em Euros (SEPA) e concluiu em tempo til os trabalhos de ligao  plataforma europeia de liquidao de ttulos em moeda de banco central (T2S), que entrou em funcionamento recentemente (em junho de 2015); o Participou no desenvolvimento da segunda srie de notas euro, tendo produzido uma parcela das novas notas de 20 euros; -No domnio dos estudos econmicos, o Banco continuou a ter os seus trabalhos publicados em revistas cientficas de topo, tendo confirmado, no Eurosistema, uma reputao de excelncia na investigao; -No domnio das estatsticas, o Banco manteve elevados padres de qualidade na produo e disseminao estatstica, como  alis reconhecido pela recente adeso ao padro mais exigente do FMI (no mbito do chamado Special Data Dissemination Standard Plus); -No domnio da superviso comportamental, o Banco apostou fortemente na literacia e incluso financeiras, em paralelo com a salvaguarda do equilbrio da relao dos bancos com os seus clientes; -Finalmente, no quadro dos novos poderes que lhe foram atribudos, o Banco de Portugal aplicou uma medida de resoluo ao Banco Esprito Santo, o terceiro maior grupo bancrio portugus. Este perodo ficou marcado por um desafio particularmente difcil que consistiu na manuteno da estabilidade financeira num contexto de fortes restries ao endividamento pblico, e em que o sistema bancrio nacional acumulara risco subprovisionado e imparidades insuficientes. A situao do sistema bancrio em 2010 foi o culminar de uma poltica prosseguida ao longo de mais de uma dcada de: -Subestimao do risco; -Concentrao setorial do crdito; -Financiamento de tomadas de participaes altamente alavancadas; -Tolerncia perante nveis insustentveis de endividamento das famlias e das empresas. Esta abordagem  que repito foi prosseguida ao longo de mais de uma dcada -refletiuse numa afetao de recursos que no teve em devida conta a otimizao do retorno do investimento ou, no mnimo, a capacidade de recuperao do crdito concedido atravs da gerao de cash-flows adequados. A consequncia foi, como seria de esperar, uma evoluo medocre do produto potencial, com prejuzo do volume e qualidade do emprego criado. No contexto da crise, o sistema bancrio foi forado a reconhecer um nvel elevado de imparidades, com impacto negativo nos resultados e, consequente, necessidade de reforo do capital. O total de imparidades ascendeu, no perodo 2008-2014, a praticamente 40 mil milhes de euros. Comparando com outros pases em situao de desequilbrio, h que sublinhar que, no caso portugus, a gesto do processo de reequilbrio foi feita com a salvaguarda da estabilidade financeira e a proteo do errio pblico -o teste do algodo : -Por um lado, a evoluo benigna dos depsitos, que espelha a confiana dos clientes bancrios (no perodo entre 2008 e 2014, os depsitos de residentes junto do sistema bancrio cresceram cerca de 11 por cento); -E, por outro lado, o impacto das ajudas ao sistema financeiro sobre a dvida pblica, que foi inferior ao verificado em muitas outras economias, incluindo da rea do euro. De acordo com dados da Comisso Europeia, no perodo 2008-2013, as medidas de apoio pblico ao setor financeiro em Portugal totalizaram 6,6 por cento do PIB (o que compara com cerca de 40 por cento na Irlanda, 22 por cento na Grcia e 9,3 por cento em Espanha). Quando, em 2010, iniciei o meu primeiro mandato como Governador estava bem ciente da grande escala deste desafio. Nessa altura, sublinhei a necessidade de reforar a superviso das instituies financeiras, seguindo uma abordagem de proximidade, intrusiva, e subordinada ao princpio de dvida sistemtica. Para tal, estabeleci que seria necessrio o Banco de Portugal dotar-se de competncias e de modelos de organizao que permitissem assegurar: -Uma superviso microprudencial oportuna, eficaz e independente; -Uma avaliao permanente dos riscos sistmicos; -O reforo da capacidade de anlise e de discusso das novas regras e dos novos modelos de superviso prudencial; -Uma participao ativa e influente nos mecanismos nacionais e internacionais de superviso macroprudencial. Estas orientaes estiveram bem presentes na atividade e atuao do Banco de Portugal ao longo do meu primeiro mandato. Efetivamente, foram introduzidas significativas alteraes ao nvel da estrutura organizacional e de governo do Banco de Portugal, foram desenvolvidas novas competncias e instrumentos de anlise e os recursos humanos foram reforados, segundo uma lgica de adequao de perfis de competncia s funes exercidas e obedecendo a princpios de meritocracia. Todavia, esta tarefa no est ainda concluda e os desafios futuros no sero menos exigentes. Beneficiando da experincia e das lies do passado,  minha inteno aprofundar estas orientaes durante o meu segundo mandato, agora no quadro da Unio Bancria europeia em consolidao. Nos ltimos anos foram feitos progressos significativos na correo destes desequilbrios, mas a tarefa est por concluir. Assim: -Os bancos reduziram significativamente a sua alavancagem, medida pela relao entre crdito e depsitos, mas apresentam ainda baixos nveis de rendibilidade que so reflexo de: -Rcios de eficincia inferiores aos concorrentes, -Baixas margens financeiras, -Montantes significativos de crdito em risco, -Elevada concentrao do risco em determinados ativos e setores, como seja o imobilirio; -As empresas tm baixos graus de autonomia financeira , reflexo dos reduzidos nveis de capital e baixa propenso ao autofinanciamento (a dvida em percentagem do PIB das empresas no financeiras em Portugal era de cerca de 124 por cento no final de 2013, o que compara com uma mdia de 87 por cento na rea do euro), com prejuzo da sua capacidade para investir e inovar e da sua resilincia s alteraes das condies conjunturais e ao aparecimento de novos concorrentes; -As famlias tm ainda nveis de endividamento elevados (cerca de 91 por cento do PIB em 2013, o que compara com 61 por cento na rea do euro), tornando-as vulnerveis a quebras de rendimento -nomeadamente as que resultam de aumentos do desemprego, ou da persistncia do desemprego estrutural  e a ajustamentos no nvel das taxas de juro. H, assim, uma agenda prioritria, que consiste em: -Reforar a capitalizao dos bancos para garantir adequada cobertura dos riscos a que estes esto ou podero vir a estar expostos, nomeadamente em cenrios econmicos adversos; mais, a capitalizao necessria ter que ter em considerao a especificidade de cada instituio em termos de balano, risco, modelo de negcio, e a capacidade dos acionistas para responder a um aumento de capital se necessrio; -Assegurar a sustentabilidade dos modelos de negcio dos bancos , nomeadamente atravs da adoo de uma estrutura de custos adequada  sua capacidade de gerar receita, e tendo em conta as perspetivas de um quadro de superviso e regulao nico e as novas formas de interao entre os bancos e os clientes; -Antecipar movimentos de racionalizao e consolidao do sistema bancrio  escala europeia, consequncia necessria da criao de uma unio bancria com superviso nica, um mecanismo nico de resoluo e, como esperado, um mecanismo nico de garantia de depsitos; -Reforar o modelo de governo das instituies tomando como referncia as melhores prticas, com particular incidncia sobre: (i) A competncia, capacidade e autonomia das funes de avaliao e gesto do risco, de controlo e de compliance e auditoria interna; (ii) A transparncia das decises estratgicas e da situao extrapatrimonial, de forma a proteger os interesses no representados, sejam os acionistas minoritrios, sejam os depositantes, seja o pblico em geral; -Adotar mecanismos que previnam fenmenos de endividamento insustentvel dos particulares e empresas e no alimentar nveis de procura insustentveis que geralmente do lugar a bolhas setoriais (como aconteceu em alguns pases com os setores da construo e da promoo imobiliria). Pretende-se, desta forma, evitar ajustamentos dolorosos dos devedores, quebras significativas de procura, falncias, desemprego e incobrveis no sistema financeiro; -Garantir a continuao da desalavancagem controlada do setor empresarial no financeiro, assente num aumento dos capitais prprios das empresas, nomeadamente atravs do desenvolvimento de instrumentos de captao de poupana com partilha de risco (por exemplo, atravs da tomada de participaes no capital ou de emprstimos subordinados). Neste contexto, os bancos sero incentivados a: (i) Adotar uma atitude ativa de gesto do risco de crdito uma vez sempre que ultrapassados nveis crticos de dependncia financeira por parte de cada empresa; por exemplo exigindo reforo dos capitais prprios, cedendo a dvida a investidores interessados em participar no capital das empresas ou convertendo a dvida em capital prprio. Naturalmente, tal pressupe um quadro legal favorvel  converso em capital prprio ou dvida subordinada da parte que exceda os nveis aceitveis de endividamento das empresas; (ii) Aplicar maiores ponderadores de risco, e por consequncia, de consumo de capital, para exposies consideradas excessivas, de forma a desincentivar uma alavancagem insustentvel; -Assegurar uma reafetao de recursos que promova o crescimento sustentvel do produto potencial e a gerao de emprego, nomeadamente atravs do investimento vivel no setor transacionvel. Para o efeito,  necessrio que os bancos adotem uma nova atitude na aplicao da poupana que intermedeiam. Mas no basta. H que tirar lies das interdependncias entre as instituies financeiras e entre estas e a rea no financeira.  necessrio adotar uma atitude proactiva de salvaguarda da estabilidade financeira atravs do recurso a medidas macroprudenciais e de adaptaes dos quadros legais, nomeadamente do regime fiscal. A solidez de cada rvore no garante a sustentabilidade da floresta. O que significa que a superviso tem que ir para l do acionamento de medidas de conteno do risco ao nvel de cada instituio, isto , tem de adotar medidas macroprudenciais que definam e mantenham linhas de corta-fogo que mitiguem o risco de contgio. Em suma: -Tivemos que limitar os riscos de uma floresta em que as rvores cresceram de forma menos vigiada, com troncos enfraquecidos que minavam a solidez da prpria rvore; -Tivemos necessidade de evitar o efeito domin sobre o sistema financeiro que resultou do risco de queda de uma grande instituio. Efetivamente, uma grande rvore com uma copa desproporcionada e, ainda por cima, com um tronco enfraquecido pode determinar a destruio da floresta envolvente. Refiro-me aos casos de instituies sobredimensionadas, com fundos prprios que no tinham em conta no s as imparidades dos ativos constantes do balano, como refletiam prticas valorimtricas desadequadas; -Tivemos que rever os nossos prprios mtodos de vigilncia e superviso que, como no caso de todos os outros supervisores, assentavam em valores e incentivos que no tinham correspondncia com a realidade (uma iluso de valores e comportamentos que alimentou outra iluso que se revelou mortfera: a da autorregulao). Hoje, o desafio da superviso  o de no cair na iluso de que as instituies so virtuosas e assentam em valores e princpios que visam o equilbrio dos diferentes interesses em presena e, sobretudo, o interesse geral. Os valores, os princpios e as instituies so especficos de determinada sociedade, pelo que o modelo de superviso no pode ignorar essa especificidade. Com efeito, e de uma forma geral, a superviso tem hoje pela frente uma insuficincia de valores e quadros institucionais que a obrigam no s a ser vigilante sobre o cumprimento das regras e dos princpios, como tambm sobre a qualidade da informao que lhe  fornecida e dos modelos de governo que a produzem. Tal significa que  necessrio fortalecer os mecanismos de auditoria da qualidade e da integridade da informao e reforar significativamente as sanes aplicveis s fraudes e s falhas nestas reas. Estamos a falar dos alicerces da confiana pblica na informao fornecida aos diferentes interessados e queles que zelam pelo interesse geral, isto  aos supervisores. Neste enquadramento crescentemente complexo, uma participao ativa e influente do Banco de Portugal no processo de deciso europeu implica uma exigncia acrescida em termos de competncias, de recursos e da qualidade e robustez dos seus processos e do seu modelo de governo. Ao contrrio do que muitos pensaro, as responsabilidades e funes que esto hoje confiadas ao Banco de Portugal so no s muito superiores, como ainda mais complexas do que aquelas que lhe estavam atribudas quando Portugal tinha a sua prpria moeda. A participao na unio monetria desde 1999 e, mais recentemente, na unio bancria, exigem ao Banco de Portugal mltiplos conhecimentos e competncias e, sobretudo, uma capacidade tcnica e operacional nunca antes exercida, de forma a influenciar a formulao de solues e a tomada de decises com relevncia  escala europeia. Um pas influente pressupe um banco central influente e ativo nos diferentes fruns europeus em que participa. A verdade  que neste quadro de grande exigncia, o Banco de Portugal tem sido capaz de se afirmar entre os seus pares com base na qualidade das anlises que produz e das competncias de que dispe, tendo granjeado uma elevada reputao em diversas reas da responsabilidade partilhada. Isto  o resultado da excelente qualidade tcnica dos recursos humanos do Banco, bem como do seu esforo e de uma atitude pr-ativa de anteviso de problemas e de formulao de solues. Nesse sentido, o Banco de Portugal continuar a apostar no seu maior ativo, que so os colaboradores, atravs da potenciao do talento interno, da promoo de polticas de diferenciao e de reconhecimento do mrito, promotoras do reforo da sua independncia tcnica e da sua cultura corporativa. Com o rejuvenescimento dos quadros do Banco, ser tambm dada especial ateno ao reforo da coeso entre as diferentes geraes de trabalhadores, no sentido de garantir um pleno alinhamento de todos com os valores e os padres ticos da Instituio. A este propsito, refiro que o Banco concluir, em breve, a reviso dos Cdigos de Conduta que j tinham sido reforados durante o meu primeiro mandato. Estes so aplicveis quer aos membros do Conselho de Administrao quer aos colaboradores em geral, seguindo as melhores prticas neste domnio e o enquadramento que emana do Eurosistema. No mbito da gesto interna, o Banco continuar a poltica de conteno de custos e de eficincia interna, assente em prticas de gesto mais colaborativas, mais orientadas para os resultados e com maior flexibilidade na utilizao dos seus recursos humanos e materiais. Sero tambm reforados os mecanismos de suporte  governao interna , designadamente em matria de gesto de risco, da compliance e da auditoria interna, a par do aprofundamento dos exerccios de planeamento estratgico e dos instrumentos de acompanhamento e de controlo de gesto. Por isso, estou certo que o Banco de Portugal ultrapassar os desafios futuros com sucesso, demonstrando ser uma organizao gil, capaz de permanentemente rever os mtodos e instrumentos de trabalho e de introduzir melhorias ao seu funcionamento em face da rpida e permanente alterao da realidade que acompanha. Neste contexto, o Banco continuar a aprofundar a cooperao institucional com outras autoridades, designadamente com outros reguladores e com os poderes polticos, em todas as iniciativas que contribuam para a melhoria do sistema financeiro e para o desenvolvimento da economia e da sociedade portuguesa -naturalmente dentro do respeito das competncias especficas de cada um e da sua independncia institucional. Para a tarefa que agora me  confiada, estou certo de que contarei com a competncia, disponibilidade e solidariedade dos meus colegas do Conselho de Administrao, a quem aproveito para agradecer o apoio prestado nos ltimos cinco anos, bem como de todos os colaboradores do Banco de Portugal. Muito obrigado. Carlos da Silva Costa Lisboa, 10 de julho de 2015

Title: Opening speech by Administrator Hlder Rosalino at the International Conference "The Earthquake of 1755 - Resilient Lisbon"
text: Opening speech by Administrator Helder Rosalino at the International Conference "The Earthquake of 1755 - Resilient Lisbon" 02 nov. 2015 Mr Ambassador of Japan in Portugal Ladies And Gentlemen of the City Council of Lisbon Mr President of the Civil Protection Authority Mr President of the Institute Portuguese of the Sea and atmosphere Dear Guests Ladies and Gentlemen It is with great satisfaction that Banco de Portugal joins and welcomes in the Central Nave of its headquarters building this important International Conference, evocative of the Earthquake of 1755 (which yesterday turned 260 years old) and promoter of reflection on the dangers, vulnerabilities and risks associated with the seismic phenomenon, thus contributing so that Lisbon can be a city increasingly prepared and resilient to this type of natural disaster. The debate on issues related to planning, organisation and response to large-scale seismic events, along with the discussion of public policies that contribute to strengthening the security of populations and to a greater awareness of citizenship around phenomena of this nature, is a very useful contribution and institutional significance. I congratulate the City Council of Lisbon for such a relevant initiative, which brings together so many prestigious national and international experts in relevant and transversal areas for the discussion of this topic. This will certainly be a conference that will leave a valuable legacy for future developments in this area, which will take advantage of all those who work and take responsibility in this area. On this occasion and in the presence of the Councillors of CM Lisboa, I would like to to mark the contribution that Banco de Portugal has been giving to the city from the space in which we are, which was once one of the most important Churches of Lisbon, the Church of St. Julian, whose history is closely linked to the Earthquake of 1755. The Bank completed about 3 years ago a profound rehabilitation of this Building, which functions as its Institutional Office, rehabilitation that was integrated in the revitalization project of the Baixa/Chiado area, promoted by the Lisbon City Council and which obtained important results for the city. The rehabilitation project at Banco de Portugal Headquarters had, along with functional and safety objectives, the central concern of increasing the resilience and responsiveness of this building to natural disasters and in particular seismic events. However, Banco de Portugal wanted to go further and proposed to offer the city and its visitors this space in which we are, and that will be very soon enriched with the opening of the Money Museum. This ship was, not many years ago, a space used for technical and support areas, for the installation of forts and for storage in general. This rehabilitation project has made it possible to transform this space into what we can see here today. In April 2014, and still without having completed the money museum project, the Bank decided to open this building to the public, creating the Interpretation Center of the Wall of D. Dinis, which streamlines interpretive visits to the wall dating back to the reign of D. Dinis, about 700 years old, and which is on the lower floor of this Nave. The wall of D. Dinis, classified as a national heritage, was an important archaeological discovery resulting from the rehabilitation works of this building, which is why the Bank decided to insert it in the money museum project and, in this sense, make it available to the city and its visitors, creating an Interpretation Center for this purpose. In addition to visits to the Wall, the Bank has been boosting in this space for a year and a half, an intense cultural, educational and scientific program, including thematic exhibitions, cultural extension activities in various domains, educational and representation activities and multiple thematic visits. This Nave has also hosted important seminars, conferences and national and international meetings, related to economic, financial, legal and social issues, among others. This is currently an open space, with growing demand and which has been affirmed in the city of Lisbon, not only for the excellence of the conditions it offers and for its architectural beauty, but also for the importance and relevance of the space and for the cultural and educational offer that has been promoted by Banco de Portugal and which is addressed to the city and to all who visit it. I would like to mention that in the first 12 months of opening to the public of this space, and still without the Money Museum operating, more than 30,000 visitors were registered, with great relevance to the segment of domestic and foreign tourists. The number of visitors has been increasing successively and the levels of satisfaction determined are in the order of 90%. I believe that these figures attest, in itself, to the success of this project, which had from the first hour with the enthusiastic support and very close to the City Council of Lisbon, not only in the context of the rehabilitation of this building, but also in the context of the cultural mission that the Bank proposed to develop. But Banco de Portugal's main objective is to open in the first quarter of next year the Money Museum, which will have 10 exhibition and interactive tour centers. This will, we are sure, be one of the most innovative and interesting museums in Europe alusing the history of money and the themes of economics and financial education. It will be a Museum of large audiences and that will greatly contribute to the cultural offer of the city of Lisbon. It will also be a business card for Banco de Portugal in the context of its insertion in the European System of Central Banks. An additional note, to mention that currently takes place in this space, and until December, a vast set of cultural initiatives evocative of the Earthquake of 1755, with emphasis on the temporary exhibition: (Re)Foundations of Lisbon. This exhibition shows us a significant set of pombaline stake, found in the context of archaeological excavation works associated with the rehabilitation works of this building. It is an exhibition that should be visited, to the extent that leads us to the imaginary of the reconstruction and reconstruction of Lisbon after the Earthquake of 1755, and that allows us to understand how, at the time, the city prepared for this type of natural phenomena. Finally, I would like to re-mark the excellence of the institutional relationship and cooperation in various areas that the Lisbon City Council and Banco de Portugal have been maintaining for the benefit of the city and its inhabitants and visitors, of which the organization of this conference is a good example. I hope that the work of the conference will live up to your best expectations. Thank you very much Exhibition (Re)Foundations of Lisbon Money Museum Website
text_original: Interveno de abertura do Administrador Hlder Rosalino na Conferncia Internacional O Terramoto de 1755  Lisboa Resiliente 02 nov. 2015 Senhor Embaixador do Japo em Portugal Senhores Vereadores da Cmara Municipal de Lisboa Senhor Presidente da Autoridade de Proteo Civil Senhor Presidente do Instituto Portugus do Mar e da Atmosfera Caros Convidados Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores  com grande satisfao que o Banco de Portugal se associa e acolhe na Nave Central do seu edifcio sede esta importante Conferncia Internacional, evocativa do Terramoto de 1755 (que ontem fez 260 anos) e promotora de reflexo em torno dos perigos, vulnerabilidades e riscos associados ao fenmeno ssmico, contribuindo assim para que Lisboa possa ser uma cidade cada vez mais preparada e resiliente a este tipo de desastre natural. O debate em torno das problemticas relacionadas com o planeamento, organizao e resposta a eventos ssmicos de grande dimenso, a par da discusso das polticas pblicas que contribuem para o reforo da segurana das populaes e para uma maior conscincia de cidadania em torno de fenmenos desta natureza, constitui um contributo de grande utilidade e significado institucional. Felicito a Cmara Municipal de Lisboa por to relevante iniciativa, que junta tantos e to prestigiados especialistas nacionais e internacionais em domnios relevantes e transversais para a discusso deste tema. Esta ser seguramente uma conferncia que deixar um legado valioso para desenvolvimentos futuros neste domnio, que aproveitar a todos os que trabalham e assumem responsabilidades nesta rea. Nesta ocasio e na presena dos Senhores Vereadores da CM Lisboa, gostaria de assinalar o contributo que o Banco de Portugal tem vindo a dar  cidade a partir do espao em que nos encontramos, que outrora era uma das mais importantes Igrejas de Lisboa, a Igreja de So Julio, cuja histria est intimamente ligada ao Terramoto de 1755. O Banco terminou h cerca de 3 anos uma profunda reabilitao deste Edifcio, que funciona como a sua Sede Institucional, reabilitao que se integrou no projeto de revitalizao da zona Baixa/Chiado, promovido pela Cmara Municipal de Lisboa e que obteve importantes resultados para a cidade. O projeto de reabilitao da Sede do Banco de Portugal teve, a par de objetivos funcionais e de segurana, subjacente a preocupao central de aumentar a resilincia e a capacidade de resposta deste edifcio a catstrofes naturais e em particular a eventos ssmicos. Porm, o Banco de Portugal quis ir mais longe e props-se oferecer  cidade e aos seus visitantes este espao em que nos encontramos, e que ser muito em breve enriquecido com a abertura do Museu do Dinheiro. Esta Nave era, no h muitos anos, um espao usado para reas tcnicas e de apoio, para instalao de casas-fortes e para arrumos em geral. Esse projeto de reabilitao permitiu transformar esse espao no que aqui hoje podemos ver. Em abril de 2014, e ainda sem ter concludo o projeto do Museu do Dinheiro, o Banco decidiu abrir este edifcio ao pblico, criando o Ncleo de Interpretao da Muralha de D. Dinis, que dinamiza visitas interpretativas  muralha que remonta ao reinado de D. Dinis, com cerca de 700 anos, e que se encontra no piso inferior ao desta Nave. A muralha de D. Dinis, classificada como patrimnio nacional, foi uma importante descoberta arqueolgica decorrente das obras de reabilitao deste edifcio, razo pela qual o Banco resolveu inseri-la no projeto do Museu do Dinheiro e, nesse sentido, disponibiliz-la  cidade e aos seus visitantes, criando um Ncleo de Interpretao para o efeito. Para alm das visitas  Muralha, o Banco tem vindo a dinamizar neste espao, desde h um ano e meio, um intenso programa cultural, educativo e cientfico, incluindo exposies temticas, atividades de extenso cultural em vrios domnios, atividades educativas e de representao e mltiplas visitas temticas. Esta Nave tem igualmente acolhido importantes seminrios, conferncias e reunies nacionais e internacionais, ligadas a temas econmicos, financeiros, jurdicos e sociais, entre outros. Este , atualmente, um espao aberto, com crescente procura e que se tem afirmado na cidade de Lisboa, no s pela excelncia das condies que oferece e pela sua beleza arquitetnica, mas tambm pela importncia e relevncia histria do espao e pela oferta cultural e educativa que tem vindo a ser promovida pelo Banco de Portugal e que  dirigida  cidade e a todos os que a visitam. Gostaria de referir que nos primeiros 12 meses de abertura ao pblico deste espao, e ainda sem o Museu do Dinheiro a funcionar, foram registados mais de 30 mil visitantes, com grande relevncia para o segmento dos turistas nacionais e estrangeiros. O nmero de visitantes tem vindo a aumentar sucessivamente e os nveis de satisfao apurados situam-se na ordem dos 90%. Julgo que estes nmeros atestam, s por si, o sucesso deste projeto, que contou desde a primeira hora com o apoio entusistico e muito prximo da Cmara Municipal de Lisboa, no s no quadro da reabilitao deste edifcio, mas tambm no contexto da misso cultural que o Banco se props desenvolver. Mas o principal objetivo do Banco de Portugal passa por abrir no primeiro trimestre do prximo ano o Museu do Dinheiro, que contar com 10 ncleos de exposio e de visita interativa. Este ser, estamos certos, um dos Museus mais inovadores e interessantes da Europa alusivos  histria do dinheiro e aos temas da economia e da educao financeira. Ser um Museu de grandes pblicos e que em muito contribuir para a oferta cultural da cidade de Lisboa. Ser igualmente um carto-de-visita para o Banco de Portugal, no contexto da sua insero no Sistema Europeu de Bancos Centrais. Uma nota adicional, para referir que decorre atualmente neste espao, e at dezembro, um conjunto vasto de iniciativas culturais evocativas do Terramoto de 1755, com destaque para a exposio temporria: (Re)Fundaes de Lisboa. Esta exposio mostra-nos um significativo conjunto de estacaria pombalina, encontrada no mbito dos trabalhos de escavao arqueolgica associados s obras de reabilitao deste edifcio.  uma exposio que deve ser visitada, na medida em que nos conduz ao imaginrio da reconstruo e refundao de Lisboa aps o Terramoto de 1755, e que nos permite perceber como,  poca, a cidade se preparou para este tipo de fenmenos naturais. Gostaria, para finalizar, de voltar a assinalar a excelncia da relao institucional e da cooperao em vrios domnios que a Cmara Municipal de Lisboa e o Banco de Portugal vm mantendo em benefcio da cidade e dos seus habitantes e visitantes, de que a organizao desta conferncia  um bom exemplo. Espero que os trabalhos da conferncia correspondam s vossas melhores expectativas. Muito obrigado Exposio (Re)Fundaes de Lisboa Stio do Museu do Dinheiro

Title: Intervention of The Administrator Joo Amaral Tomaz in the session on the new 20 banknote - Europa Series
text: Intervention of Administrator John A... Intervention of The Administrator Joao Amaral Tomaz in the session on the new 20 banknote -Europa Series 24 nov. 2015 From tomorrow, November 25, the new 20 banknote enters circulation in Portugal and the other 18 euro area countries. The new 20 banknote is the third denomination of the second series of euro banknotes  the Europa series  to enter circulation after the new 5 banknotes in May 2013 and 10 in September 2014. The Europe series results from a compromise between continuity and innovation, two characteristics considered indispensable to strengthen confidence in a currency. Visually, the new 20 banknote bears some similarities to that of the first series, maintaining the dominant color (blue), the architectural style (Gothic) and the dimensions. In addition to the security features already known, such as the hologram and watermark, the new 20 banknote features the emerald number, introduced in the new 5 and 10 banknotes and which will be present throughout the Europe series, and an innovative security element  the window with portrait  which makes it even more resistant to contrapartation. The 20 banknote is the most widely used banknote in Portugal. It is also the one with the highest number of infighting seized, both in Portugal and in the entire euro area. While counterfeit banknote levels in Portugal and the euro area remain very low, it is essential that the public and cash professionals know how to assess the authenticity of a banknote at the time they receive it. The reason is very simple: a defaulted note cannot be exchanged for a genuine note, which means that those who accept a defaulted note, deeming it to be an authentic note, will not be able to recover its value. In this regard, I would like to express my thanks to all entities contributing to the safety of fiduciary movement in Portugal, where the number of seized incontract accounts for only 1% of the total contraptics seized in the euro area. This result is due not only to the performance of Banco de Portugal, but also to the relevant role that the banking system, entities operating in the areas of cash management and distribution and police authorities (in particular the Judicial Police, our partner in this area) have been playing in this area. There are other very relevant messages that need to be transmitted to the public regarding the release of this new note. With the entry into circulation of the new 20 banknote, the Portuguese will not have to exchange any banknotes. The 20 first series banknote will remain in circulation and may continue to be used to make payments without any restrictions. The new 20 banknote and the 20 banknote from the first series will circulate simultaneously, as is the case with 5 and 10 banknotes from the first and second series.
