The date on which the first grade grades will no longer be legal course has not yet been set, but I can assure you that it will be announced well in advance. In any case, it should be made clear: the first grade notes will never lose their value. There is no prescription after 20 years as it was for the shield. In other words, the euro banknotes of the first series, even after they have lost their legal status, may be exchanged, for an unlimited period of time, at Banco de Portugal and the other national central banks of the Eurosystem. For the launch of the new 20 banknote, around 4.3 billion banknotes were produced in several euro area countries. At VALORA, S.A.  a company 100% owned by Banco de Portugal  44 million banknotes were produced, marking the beginning of the production of second series banknotes in Portugal. Since the beginning of this year, Banco de Portugal has developed a wide range of information and training, communication and technical support initiatives for professionals and the general public to prepare for the launch of the new banknote. The European Central Bank and the national central banks of the euro area have joined forces to promote timely adaptation of all types of equipment operating with cash. Although the responsibility for adapting the equipment is ultimately the responsibility of its owners, the Eurosystem and, in particular, Banco de Portugal have taken all the measures that were within its power to achieve this adaptation as soon as possible. However, although we now have information that the main public transport and motorway management companies will be prepared now, we cannot guarantee that all the equipment of the other economic operators will be able to accept the new 20 banknote as of tomorrow. I would also like to point out that, in addition to the communication and information initiatives that Banco de Portugal has promoted for professionals and the general public, we are aware that other institutions are also doing so. It should be highlighted the relevant initiative of the police authorities, namely gnr, which has developed awareness campaigns among the populations with less access to information and which, as such, are more exposed to possible attempts at fraud. Confidence in the euro  our currency  is an asset that we all have a duty to preserve. I would remind you again that no one is required to exchange notes on behalf of Banco de Portugal or on behalf of credit institutions. I end my speech by saying that the euro is now certainly the most visible symbol of the Process of European Integration. This was once again confirmed and reinforced by the European Commission's latest Eurobarometer, the results of which were released a few weeks ago, according to which 61% of citizens surveyed in the 19 euro zone countries see the euro as positive for their country, the highest since the introduction of the euro in 2002. In the case of Portugal, the share is now perfectly identical to the euro area average, and it was even the country where satisfaction with the single currency grew the most (from 50% to 61%). Next, Antonio Garcia, Director of the Department of Issuance and Treasury of Banco de Portugal, and Celia Amado, specialist in analysis of contraparts, will start a brief training/information action on cash in general and on the new 20 banknote, in particular, after which we will all be at your disposal for clarification of any issues. Thank you all so much. Legal Notices CSIRT Contacts
text_original: Interveno do Administrador Joo A... Interveno do Administrador Joo Amaral Tomaz na sesso sobre a nova nota de 20 -Srie Europa 24 nov. 2015 A partir de amanh, dia 25 de novembro, entra em circulao, em Portugal e nos outros 18 pases da rea do euro, a nova nota de 20. A nova nota de 20  a terceira denominao da segunda srie de notas de euro  a srie Europa  a entrar em circulao, depois das novas notas de 5, em maio de 2013, e de 10, em setembro de 2014. A srie Europa resulta de um compromisso entre a continuidade ea inovao, duas caratersticas consideradas indispensveis para reforar a confiana numa moeda. Visualmente, a nova nota de 20 apresenta algumas semelhanas face  da primeira srie, mantendo a cor dominante (azul), o estilo arquitetnico (Gtico) e as dimenses. Alm dos elementos de segurana j conhecidos, como o holograma e a marca de gua, a nova nota de 20 apresenta o nmero esmeralda, introduzido nas novas notas de 5 e 10 e que estar presente em toda a srie Europa, e um elemento de segurana inovador  a janela com retrato  que a torna ainda mais resistente  contrafao. A nota de 20  a nota mais utilizada em Portugal. E  tambm aquela que regista o maior nmero de contrafaes apreendidas, tanto em Portugal, como em toda a rea do euro. Embora os nveis de contrafao de notas em Portugal e na rea do euro permaneam muito baixos,  fundamental que o pblico e os profissionais que lidam com numerrio saibam avaliar a autenticidade de uma nota no momento em que a recebem. A razo  muito simples: uma nota contrafeita no pode ser trocada por uma nota genuna, tal significa que quem aceitar uma nota contrafeita, julgando tratar-se de uma nota autntica, no poder recuperar o seu valor. A este propsito, gostaria de expressar o meu agradecimento a todas as entidades que contribuem para a segurana da circulao fiduciria em Portugal, onde o nmero de contrafaes apreendidas representa somente 1% do total de contrafaes apreendidas na rea do euro. Este resultado deve-se, no apenas ao desempenho do Banco de Portugal, mas tambm ao relevante papel que o sistema bancrio, as entidades que operam nas reas da gesto e da distribuio de numerrio e as autoridades policiais (em particular a Polcia Judiciria, nosso parceiro nesta rea) tm vindo a desempenhar neste domnio. Existem outras mensagens muito relevantes que  necessrio transmitir ao pblico a propsito do lanamento desta nova nota. Com a entrada em circulao da nova nota de 20, os portugueses no tero de trocar quaisquer notas. A nota de 20 da primeira srie continuar em circulao e poder continuar a ser utilizada para efetuar pagamentos, sem quaisquer restries. A nova nota de 20 e a nota de 20 da primeira srie vo circular em simultneo, como j se verifica, de resto, relativamente s notas de 5 e de 10 da primeira e da segunda srie. A data em que as notas da primeira srie deixaro de ter curso legal ainda no foi definida, mas posso garantir-vos que ser anunciada com bastante antecedncia. Em qualquer caso, convm deixar claro o seguinte: as notas da primeira srie nunca perdero o seu valor. No existe prescrio ao fim de 20 anos como se verificava para o escudo. Ou seja, as notas de euro da primeira srie, mesmo depois de perderem o curso legal, podero ser trocadas, por um perodo de tempo ilimitado, no Banco de Portugal e nos restantes bancos centrais nacionais do Eurosistema. Para o lanamento da nova nota de 20, foram produzidos cerca de 4,3 mil milhes de notas em diversos pases da zona euro. Na VALORA, S.A.  empresa detida a 100% pelo Banco de Portugal , foram produzidas 44 milhes de notas, marcando o incio da produo de notas da segunda srie em Portugal. O Banco de Portugal desenvolveu, desde o incio deste ano, um conjunto alargado de iniciativas de informao e de formao, de comunicao e de apoio tcnico, para profissionais e para o pblico em geral, para preparar o lanamento da nova nota. O Banco Central Europeu e os bancos centrais nacionais da rea do euro uniram esforos para promover a adaptao atempada de todos os tipos de equipamentos que operam com numerrio. Embora a responsabilidade pela adaptao dos equipamentos seja, em ltima anlise, dos respetivos proprietrios, o Eurosistema e, em particular, o Banco de Portugal tomaram todas as medidas que estavam ao seu alcance para que essa adaptao fosse concretizada o mais atempadamente possvel. Contudo, e apesar de termos hoje informao de que as principais empresas de transportes pblicos e de gesto de autoestradas estaro desde j preparadas, no podemos garantir que todos os equipamentos, dos demais agentes econmicos, estejam aptos a aceitar a nova nota de 20 j a partir de amanh. Gostaria tambm de assinalar que, para alm das iniciativas de comunicao e de informao que o Banco de Portugal tem promovido para os profissionais e para o pblico em geral, temos conhecimento de que outras instituies tambm o esto a fazer.  de realar a relevante iniciativa das autoridades policiais, designadamente a GNR, que tem desenvolvido campanhas de sensibilizao junto das populaes com menor acesso  informao e que, como tal, esto mais expostas a eventuais tentativas de burla. A confiana no euro  a nossa moeda   um ativo que todos temos o dever de preservar. Volto a recordar que ningum est mandatado para trocar notas em nome do Banco de Portugal ou em nome das instituies de crdito. Termino a minha interveno referindo que o euro  hoje, seguramente, o smbolo mais visvel do processo de integrao europeia. Este facto foi, uma vez mais, confirmado e reforado pelo ltimo Eurobarmetro da Comisso Europeia, cujos resultados foram divulgados h algumas semanas atrs, segundo o qual 61% dos cidados inquiridos nos 19 pases da zona euro consideram o euro como positivo para o seu pas, sendo este o valor mais elevado desde a introduo do euro em 2002. No caso de Portugal, a percentagem  agora perfeitamente idntica  mdia da zona euro, tendo sido inclusivamente o pas onde a satisfao com a moeda nica mais cresceu (de 50% para 61%). De seguida, Antnio Garcia, Diretor do Departamento de Emisso e Tesouraria do Banco de Portugal, e Clia Amado, especialista em anlise de contrafaes, vo iniciar uma breve ao de formao/informao sobre o numerrio, em geral, e sobre a nova nota de 20, em particular, aps a qual estaremos todos  vossa disposio para o esclarecimento de quaisquer questes. Muito obrigado a todos. Avisos legais Contactos CSIRT

Title: Opening speech of Deputy Governor Pedro Duarte Neves at the 5th Conference of the Balance Sheet Center in Coimbra
text: Opening speech of the Vice-Gov... Opening speech of Deputy Governor Pedro Duarte Neves at the 5th Conference of the Balance Sheet Center in Coimbra Feb. 23. 2016 Good afternoon, everyone. To open this 5th Conference of the Central Balance Sheet, I decided to focus this presentation on three main aspects: (i) illustration of the success of the export ing sector in the recent adjustment period of the Portuguese economy; (ii) main characteristics of the change in the structure of the export sector; and, finally, (iii) future challenges and recent teachings for Portuguese entrepreneurs and, in particular, for exporting companies. 1) Illustration of the success of the exporting sector in the adjustment period To illustrate the success of the export sector, during the recent adjustment period of the Portuguese economy, I will mention three indicators.  Firstly, the nominal change in exports from 2010 to 2015, a five-year period corresponding to the recent adjustment process of the Portuguese economy. This indicator jointly reflects the variation in exported quantities and their unit prices and, therefore, the change in the total revenues of exporting companies. The growth in this five-year period is, in all its own way, remarkable: growth in exports of goods: 32.8 percent; Growth in service exports: 38.7 percent; Growth in tourism exports: 52.6 percent. These figures thus clearly illustrate the success of export activity in this adjustment period.  The second indicator is market share gains in foreign markets. The robust growth of exports in the most recent period reflects, on the one hand, the evolution of external demand directed to the Portuguese economy and, on the other hand, the existence of significant gains in market share. Between 2008 and 2015, demand towards the Portuguese economy grew by 11.2 per cent in real terms, highlighting the performance of economies outside the euro area, particularly emerging economies, which until very recently proved more dynamic than the euro area. In the same period, the cumulative change in market share stood at about 14.5 percent. That is, the growth in volume recorded in this period by Portuguese exports  about 27 percent  about 40 percent corresponded to an increase in external demand; 60 percent of the actual expansion of exports reflected a gain in our penetration into foreign markets.  The third indicator corresponds to the weight of exports in gross domestic product, which increased by about 9 percentage points between 2008 and 2015, from about 31 to about 40 percent of GDP. On average, in the period from 1995 to 2007 exports accounted for only about 28 percent of GDP. This development reinforces the perspective that there is a significant recomposition of the structure of the Portuguese economy in the most recent period, towards a growing orientation of productive resources to sectors with greater exposure to international competition. This favorable development was associated not only with the performance of companies traditionally exposed to foreign markets, but also with companies that started their export activity.  These three indicators clearly illustrate the success of the behaviour of the export sector in recent years. This success was one of the most striking characteristics of the recent adjustment of the Portuguese economy, having been reflected in a marked way in two very important aspects: Redeployment of productive resources from sectors not exposed to international competition to sectors exposed to international competition; Financing capacity of the Portuguese economy (which translates the adjustment capacity of households and non-financial enterprises, following the adjustment process of these institutional sectors) reflected in current and capital surpluses. The sectors represented here today -Sectors of Madeira, Cork and Paper  are good examples of sectors of the economy that, in a very marked way, have contributed to the growth of exports in the last four years. 2) Changes in the structure of the exporting sector: main characteristics I then identify some very important changes in the structure of the exporting sector Portuguese:  Nature of shocks - Structural export developments stem in part from the adjustment to shocks that occurred in the late 1990s, with the enlargement of the EU to the countries of Central and Eastern Europe and the growth of China as a participant in international trade. On the other hand, the severe contraction of domestic demand during the Economic and Financial Adjustment Programme period is an additional factor for the structural adjustment of exports.  Greater weight of the export component in the business model - Portuguese exports have performed well in recent years, characterized by an increase in the proportion of companies involved in export activity and an increase in the average weight of exports in sales.  Renewal of exporting companies - There is a very relevant contribution on the part of exporters who started the activity more recently. Considering the average for the period 2010-2012, companies that started the activity less than 10 years ago accounted for about one third of the nominal average growth of exports in this period. This reflects an important export dynamic in younger companies. Additionally, when assessing the weight of these companies in total exports, it is concluded that about a quarter of exports in 2012 resulted from companies that started the activity after the year 2000. This development reflects the progressive reorientation of national productive factors to export activity, which is an essential element of the adjustment process currently underway.  Nature of exported goods - The fact that 70 per cent of Portuguese trade now corresponds to trade within each sector means that the nature of trade and competitiveconditions has changed. Companies located in Portugal compete mainly in sectors where the country is both an exporter and importer, and this competition is determined by a set of factors that goes far beyond salary, such as technological capacity, innovation or differentiation of production from international competitors.  Technological content of exports - The increase in exports of the last 12 years has not followed either the line of strengthening of specialization observed in the first years of integration or a softer adjustment line marked by an expansion of exports and imports from the same sectors. The expansion of trade occurred with strong sectoral and specialization changes. The change in the sector structure corresponded to a change in the technological profile of product exports, with a sharp reduction in the weight of low-tech goods and an affirmation of exports of medium and high-tech goods.  Characteristics of export expansion from 2005 on: sustained growth on a broad basis of product types -After 2005, a period of export expansion was opened different from the previous ones. In this period, a strong growth in exports coincided with the continued change in the sectoral structure, i.e., Portuguese exports are growing again, but this growth was not led either by the so-called traditional sectors or by a limited set of large projects in well-defined sectors.  Thus, between 2005 and 2012 Portuguese exports grew  as already mentioned above the European average, highlighting the contributions of sectors as diverse as agriculture and food industry, pulp and paper, furniture, metal products, plastics, petroleum products, chemical and pharmaceutical industry. At the same time, exports of clothing and footwear have recovered, reinsing the downward trend, and those of automobiles and machinery continue to grow, remaining as two of the most important exporting sectors in the country.  Destination of Exports: In the adjustment period, the trend of increasing the weight of exports to non-EU countries, which began in the mid-2000s, continued. The weight of extra EU trade rose from 25.6/25.1 percent in 2008 to 27.3/31.2 percent in 2015 for exports of goods/services.  The vast majority of Portuguese exports are intended, as is well known, to intra-EU markets. The main partners are Spain, Germany, France, the United Kingdom and the Netherlands, with these 5 countries systematically present in the top 10 destination countries of Portuguese exports since 2008.  Among the extra EU countries are the United States of America, China, Morocco, Algeria, Mozambique and Canada where exports have doubled or more than doubled in the last five years.  Characteristics of exporting companies - Portuguese exporting companies have distinctive characteristics of those that sell exclusively to the internal market, namely because they are larger, more productive, because they practice higher average wages and because they have a higher capital ratio per worker. These stylised facts are, moreover, similar to those found for other countries. 3) Future perspectives and challenges -Maintaining the financing capacity of the Portuguese economy is an indispensable feature for sustained growth of the Portuguese economy; -Recent developments have clearly illustrated the clear advantages of diversifying the destination of production (between the internal market and the external market between Community destinations and extra-Community destinations); it is therefore important that, in a scenario of a foreseeable continuation of the recovery of domestic demand, efforts are continued to increase exports and diversify their destinations (the benefits of diversification are an important focus of the recent crisis); -Recent experience has also shown the difficulties faced by (or cease to exist) financially fragile companies: thus, companies should increase their own capital and reduce their level of indebtedness, in particular in situations where indebtedness may be a risk element in the face of changing exogenous conditions for the company (sudden reductions in demand or increases in access to finance rates); -Recent experience has also shown that there are no successful models based on low wage costs: innovation, enhanced technological content and increased commercial strength have been  since the mid-last decade  key elements for several companies to successfully adapt to changes in competition globally; and, from this point of view, here is the suggestion of a greater connection of the business structure to universities. In conclusion,  The behavior of Portuguese exports is undoubtedly one of the most positive developments of the recent period of the Portuguese economy;  The export growth model  which results from individual business choices  was characterized by a very significant diversification in terms of composition (goods and services) and in terms of geographical destination, which is an important element of resilience of the Portuguese economy in the face of adverse shocks. I would therefore like to leave here my public recognition for the enormous contribution of several companies to the exportsector Portuguese in the recent past  in particular for the sectors represented here today, Wood, Cork and Paper  as well as the notes of reflection on future teachings and challenges. 4) Thanks Finally, I would like to leave my thanks: first of all, to the Bissaya Barreto Foundation for their collaboration in the preparation of this event; then to the Banco de Portugal Balance Sheet Center team that has been the main promoter of these conferences (we will on thursday) and all banco de Portugal services involved in the preparation and realization of this conference. Coimbra, February 23, 2016
text_original: Interveno de abertura do Vice-Gov... Interveno de abertura do Vice-Governador Pedro Duarte Neves na 5. Conferncia da Central de Balanos em Coimbra 23 fev. 2016 Boa tarde a todos. Para abertura desta 5 Conferncia da Central de Balanos, decidi focar esta apresentao em trs aspetos principais: (i) ilustrao do sucesso do setor exportador no recente perodo de ajustamento da economia portuguesa; (ii) principais caractersticas da alterao de estrutura do setor exportador; e, finalmente, (iii) desafios futuros e ensinamentos recentes para os empresrios portugueses e, em particular, para as empresas exportadoras. 1) Ilustrao do sucesso do setor exportador no perodo de ajustamento Para ilustrar o sucesso do setor exportador, no decurso do recente perodo de ajustamento da economia portuguesa, vou referir trs indicadores.  Em primeiro lugar a variao nominal das exportaes de 2010 a 2015, perodo de cinco anos que corresponde ao processo de ajustamento recente da economia portuguesa. Este indicador reflete, conjuntamente, a variao das quantidades exportadas e dos respetivos preos unitrios e, por isso, a variao das receitas totais das empresas exportadoras. Os crescimentos verificados neste perodo de cinco anos so, a todo o ttulo, notveis: crescimento das exportaes de bens: 32,8 por cento; Crescimento das exportaes de servios: 38,7 por cento; Crescimento das exportaes de turismo: 52,6 por cento. Estes nmeros ilustram, assim, de uma forma muito clara o sucesso da atividade exportadora neste perodo de ajustamento.  O segundo indicador so os ganhos de quota de mercado nos mercados externos. O crescimento robusto das exportaes no perodo mais recente reflete, por um lado, a evoluo da procura externa dirigida  economia portuguesa e, por outro lado, a existncia de ganhos significativos de quota de mercado. Entre 2008 e 2015, a procura externa dirigida  economia portuguesa cresceu, em termos reais, 11,2 por cento, destacando-se o desempenho das economias fora da rea do euro, nomeadamente das economias emergentes, que se revelaram, at muito recentemente, mais dinmicas do que a rea do euro. No mesmo perodo, a variao acumulada da quota de mercado situou-se em cerca de 14,5 por cento. Ou seja, do crescimento em volume registado neste perodo pelas exportaes portuguesas  cerca de 27 por cento  cerca de 40 por cento correspondeu a um aumento da procura externa; 60 por cento da expanso real das exportaes refletiu um ganho da nossa penetrao nos mercados externos.  O terceiro indicador corresponde ao peso das exportaes no produto interno bruto, que aumentou cerca de 9 pontos percentuais entre 2008 e 2015, passando de cerca de 31 para cerca de 40 por cento do PIB. Em mdia, no perodo de 1995 a 2007 as exportaes representavam apenas cerca de 28 por cento do PIB. Esta evoluo refora a perspetiva de que se est a assistir no perodo mais recente a uma recomposio significativa da estrutura da economia portuguesa, no sentido de uma crescente orientao de recursos produtivos para setores com maior exposio  concorrncia internacional. Esta evoluo favorvel esteve associada no s ao desempenho de empresas tradicionalmente expostas aos mercados externos, mas tambm de empresas que iniciaram a sua atividade exportadora.  Estes trs indicadores ilustram, de uma forma clara, o sucesso do comportamento do setor exportador nestes ltimos anos. Este sucesso constituiu uma das caractersticas mais marcantes do ajustamento recente da economia portuguesa, tendo tido reflexo de uma forma marcada em dois aspetos muito importantes: Reafectao de recursos produtivos de setores no expostos  concorrncia internacional para setores expostos  concorrncia internacional; Capacidade de financiamento da economia portuguesa (que traduz capacidade de ajustamento das famlias e das empresas no financeiras, na sequncia do processo de ajustamento destes setores institucionais) refletido em excedentes da balana corrente e de capital. Os setores aqui hoje representados -Setores da Madeira, da Cortia e do Papel  constituem bons exemplos de setores da economia que, de uma forma muito marcada, contriburam para o crescimento das exportaes nestes ltimos quatro anos. 2) Alteraes na estrutura do setor exportador: principais caractersticas Identifico, de seguida, algumas alteraes muito importantes na estrutura do setor exportador portugus:  Natureza dos choques -A evoluo estrutural das exportaes decorre, em parte, do ajustamento a choques ocorridos no final da dcada de noventa, com o alargamento da EU aos pases do Centro e Leste da Europa e com o crescimento da China como participante no comrcio internacional. Por outro lado, a severa contrao da procura interna no perodo do Programa de Ajustamento Econmico e Financeiro constitui um fator adicional para o ajustamento estrutural das exportaes.  Maior peso da componente de exportaes no modelo de negcio -As exportaes portuguesas tm registado um bom desempenho nos ltimos anos, caracterizado por um aumento da proporo de empresas envolvidas na atividade exportadora e por um aumento do peso mdio das exportaes nas vendas.  Renovao das empresas exportadoras -Existe um contributo muito relevante por parte dos exportadores que iniciaram a atividade mais recentemente. Considerando a mdia do perodo 2010-2012, as empresas que iniciaram a atividade h menos de 10 anos foram responsveis por cerca de um tero do crescimento mdio nominal das exportaes nesse perodo. Este facto traduz uma importante dinmica exportadora nas empresas mais jovens. Adicionalmente, quando se avalia o peso destas empresas no total de exportaes, conclui-se que cerca de um quarto das exportaes em 2012 resultou de empresas que iniciaram a atividade aps o ano 2000. Esta evoluo traduz a progressiva reorientao dos fatores produtivos nacionais para a atividade exportadora, o que constitui um elemento essencial do processo de ajustamento atualmente em curso.  Natureza dos bens exportados -O facto de 70 por cento do comrcio portugus corresponder hoje a trocas dentro de cada setor significa que a natureza do comrcio e das condies de competitividade se alterou. As empresas localizadas em Portugal concorrem maioritariamente em setores em que o pas  simultaneamente exportador e importador, sendo esta concorrncia determinada por um conjunto de fatores que vai muito para alm do salrio, tais como a capacidade tecnolgica, a inovao ou a diferenciao da produo face aos concorrentes internacionais.  Contedo tecnolgico das exportaes -O aumento das exportaes dos ltimos 12 anos no seguiu nem a linha de reforo da especializao verificada nos primeiros anos da integrao nem uma linha de ajustamento mais suave marcada por uma expanso das exportaes e importaes dos mesmos setores. A expanso do comrcio deu-se com fortes alteraes setoriais e da especializao.  alterao da estrutura setorial correspondeu uma mudana do perfil tecnolgico das exportaes de produtos, com uma forte reduo do peso dos bens de baixa tecnologia e uma afirmao das exportaes de bens de mdia e alta tecnologia.  Caractersticas da expanso das exportaes a partir de 2005: crescimento sustentado numa base alargada de tipos de produtos -Depois de 2005, abriu-se um perodo de expanso das exportaes diferente dos anteriores. Neste perodo, coincidiu um crescimento forte das exportaes com a continuao da alterao da estrutura setorial, ou seja, as exportaes portuguesas voltam a crescer, mas tal crescimento no foi liderado nem pelos designados setores tradicionais nem por um conjunto limitado de grandes projetos em setores bem definidos.  Assim, entre 2005 e 2012 as exportaes portuguesas cresceram  como j referido acima da mdia europeia, destacando-se os contributos de setores to diversificados como a agricultura e indstria alimentar, a pasta e papel, mobilirio, produtos metlicos, plsticos, produtos petrolferos, indstria qumica e farmacutica. Ao mesmo tempo, as exportaes de vesturio e calado recuperaram, invertendo a tendncia de queda, e as de automveis e mquinas continuam a crescer, mantendo-se como dois dos mais importantes setores exportadores do pas.  Destino das Exportaes: No perodo de ajustamento manteve-se a tendncia de aumento do peso das exportaes para pases extra UE, iniciada em meados da dcada de 2000. O peso das trocas extra UE passou de 25,6 / 25,1 por cento em 2008 para 27,3 / 31,2 por cento em 2015 no caso das exportaes de bens / servios.  A larga maioria das exportaes portuguesas destina-se, como  bem sabido, a mercados intra UE. Os principais parceiros so Espanha, Alemanha, Frana, Reino Unido e Pases Baixos, encontrando-se estes 5 pases sistematicamente presentes nos 10 principais pases de destino das exportaes portuguesas desde 2008.  Entre os pases extra UE, destacam-se os Estados Unidos da Amrica, China, Marrocos, Arglia, Moambique e Canad onde as exportaes duplicaram ou mais do que duplicaram nos ltimos cinco anos.  Caractersticas das empresas exportadoras -As empresas exportadoras portuguesas apresentam caractersticas distintivas daquelas que vendem exclusivamente para o mercado interno, designadamente pelo facto de serem maiores, mais produtivas, por praticarem salrios mdios mais altos e por apresentam um rcio de capital por trabalhador mais elevado. Estes factos estilizados so, alis, semelhantes aos encontrados para outros pases. 3) Perspetivas e desafios futuros -A manuteno da capacidade de financiamento da economia portuguesa constitui uma caracterstica indispensvel para um crescimento sustentado da economia portuguesa; -A evoluo recente ilustrou de forma muito clara as claras vantagens da diversificao do destino da produo (entre mercado interno e mercado externo, entre destinos comunitrios e destinos extra-comunitrios);  importante, por isso, que num cenrio de previsvel continuao da recuperao da procura interna se continuem a verificar esforos para aumentar as exportaes e diversificar os respetivos destinos (as vantagens de diversificao constituem um importante ensinamento da recente crise); -A experincia recente mostrou tambm as dificuldades por que podem passar (ou deixar de existir) empresas frgeis do ponto de vista financeiro: assim, as empresas devero reforar os seus capitais prprios e reduzir o seu nvel de endividamento, em especial em situaes em que o endividamento possa constituir um elemento de risco em face de alterao de condies exgenas  empresa (redues sbitas da procura ou subidas das taxas de acesso a financiamento); -A experincia recente mostrou tambm que no h modelos de sucesso baseados em baixos custos salariais: a inovao, o reforo do contedo tecnolgico e o aumento da fora comercial constituram  a partir de meados da dcada passada -elementos determinantes para vrias empresas se conseguirem adaptar com sucesso s alteraes da concorrncia a nvel global; e, sob esse ponto de vista, fica aqui a sugesto de uma maior ligao da estrutura empresarial s universidades. Em concluso,  O comportamento das exportaes portuguesas constitui, sem margem para dvidas, um dos desenvolvimentos mais positivos do perodo recente da economia portuguesa;  O modelo de crescimento das exportaes  que resulta de escolhas individuais de empresas  caracterizou-se por uma diversificao muito significativa em termos de composio (bens e servios) e em termos de destino geogrfico, o que constitui um importante elemento de resilincia da economia portuguesa face a choques adversos. Gostava, assim, de deixar aqui o meu reconhecimento pblico pelo enorme contributo de vrias empresas para o setor exportador portugus no passado recente  em particular para os setores hoje aqui representados, Madeira, Cortia e Papel  bem como as notas de reflexo sobre ensinamentos e desafios futuros. 4) Agradecimentos Finalmente, gostava de deixar os meus agradecimentos: antes de mais,  Fundao Bissaya Barreto pela colaborao na preparao deste evento; depois  equipa da rea da Central de Balanos do Banco de Portugal que tem sido a principal promotora destas conferncias (vamos na quinta) e a todos os servios do Banco de Portugal envolvidos na preparao e realizao desta conferncia. Title: Interview of the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Carlos da Silva Costa, to Expresso
text: Interview of the Governor of the Bank of... Interview of the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Carlos da Silva Costa, to Expresso 05 mar. 2016 Do you know that the portuguese's image of the governor of Banco de Portugal has changed radically? Instead of a figure that emanativesecurity and solidity, it is the one who has responsibility for the banks but can do little. This problem is not exclusive to Portugal. It happened in the United Kingdom, Belgium, France, Germany... At a time when there is a problem in the banking system there is a question to the governors about the exercise of the function and what should have been guaranteed. The governors' mission is two objectives: to ensure nominal stability and financial stability. What we need to assess is whether there has been continuity of financing of the economy, safeguarding depositors' confidence and protecting deposits. I believe that financial stability has been guaranteed. It's one thing to be this, it's another to make sure that financial institutions don't have problems. The financial system looks like a property that has alarm, electric fence and a sign saying "watch out for the dog". But the alarm doesn't work, the fence isn't electrified and there's no dog. The property can be robbed and no one gives up in time. That's just not true. It is the cases that consume the most resources and attention that produce the biggest problems. What we must ask ourselves is why, despite this attention and resources, the questions arise. And this is because the facts that produce the difficulties of banks are accumulated problems that only become visible when the difficulties manifest themselves. But Banco de Portugal (BdP) has been overseeing banks for a long time. Yes, but the BdP has to secure three things. First, that banks are able to provide capital to absorb the losses that may occur in the balance sheets; second whereas they have risk management and control adapted to that risk absorption capacity; third, that they have government models capable of ensuring this function and who have audits capable of giving guarantees. It turns out that there is a pro-cyclique nature in this activity: in periods when everything is fine there is greater availability to take risk and there is a grantof credit above the availability of reimbursement by those who take credit. Usually crises are not caused by periods of crises, but by periods of expansion. Does that explain that the financial system Portuguese has destroyed almost EUR 40 billion in these years [the value of accumulated impairments]? The financial crisis has had an impact on almost every country in Europe. The only difference was time and how the impact was transmitted. The first countries to suffer were those that had to make nationalizations or capitalizations as early as 2009, The United Kingdom, Belgium, France, Holland, Denmark, Germany... Then there is a second wave covering Ireland and Greece. The third takes portugal and Spain. This is because the modes of transmission are different, either through funding [bank funds] or by applications. The countries of Northern Europe, which are surplus to savings, have been hit mainly through the applications they have made on paper that has proved toxic. Southern European countries, which are not surplus in savings, have been hit by funding because the capital market has closed. The closing of markets has had a very negative impact on banks. This impact was offset by the ECB's liquidity, which operated very well and with very high values. When we make the story of this first impact of the crisis, let's see that it has been well managed. People don't have that opinion. By 2011, banks were able to manage the problem of the need for alternative sources of funding without disrupting the financing of the economy. But the banks at the time were remunerating their shareholders on the basis of profits that we now know are artificial. That's the essential question... But we must first see what happened in the second phase of the process, when the sovereign [the state] lost access to the market. This has immediate effects on the sovereign's rating and, consequently, on the rating of the instruments available to the banks. The financing of the economy only continued because there was an adjustment programme that allowed the rating to be waived to gain access to the ECB. When there is a crisis, it is transmitted by three ways: through companies, families and the sovereign. Companies have a drop in demand, greater financial difficulties and cases of non-compliance begin to arise... In the Portuguese, it wasn't just financial difficulties. Many companies had business models that did not work and the one sands lent without discretion. The BdP wasn't able to see that. That's going to be the big question for the future. In a period of expansion, central banks have to have instruments to control the effect of credit and the self-feeding of euphoria on underestimation of risk and credit growth. Whenever there is economic growth there is an underestimation of risk. That is why the macroprudential function has been introduced. That is, despite the bank's ratios being in line with and the risk is properly assessed, there must be the capacity to anticipate what may be produced. During the adjustment period we were pioneers in this area, we introduced instruments that were generalized: the need to have three-year capital projections in banks, assessing how banks calculate risk. Are you recognizing that before the BdP had no tools to do this oversight? No, I am recognizing that all supervisors, including the BdP, have to learn lessons from the crisis. But there are specificities in Portugal... That's what I wanted to get to... ... too much credit of cyclical activities, real estate and construction, conflicts of interest between shareholders and creditors, excessive indebtedness... The problems of the economy are later problems in the financial system. A country where companies have a preference for indebtedness over capitalization is a country much more exposed to cyclical fluctuation. We cannot solve our financial problems if we do not establish policies and criteria that limit corporate indebtedness. Moreover, there was no concern to capture good business, facilitating credit to these companies, bet on business with a model that based on the indefinite continuation of household indebtedness and public demand. When it fails, you know what happens. It was like this here, in Spain or Ireland... Hitting Totobola on Monday is easy. Institutions such as the BdP exist to watch out for these situations. And countries like Ireland or Spain came out much better out of the crisis than we did. The problem is identical and in some cases more serious. The solution is always the same, recapitalize the banks, absorb the losses and, if there is no capacity of the shareholders to do so, the state and the taxpayer intervene. But that depends on the state's debt capacity and the situation in Ireland and Spain was very different. They were able to face losses using public debt, without shooting it to levels beyond desirable. In the Portuguese, the issue is very different, companies, families and the state were heavily indebted and had limited funding, which resulted from external assistance. What you are saying is that in 2011, faced with the alternative of an Irish solution  taking over the debt of the banks at once  we consciously and deliberately assumed that the bank clean-up process would take years? It was a bank clean-up process that would require capacity to mobilise capital, would require the use of the program's 12 billion line. Only half was used. Why? But that was an option of the banks!... What would have happened if we had opted for the Irish frontloading model? First, we would clash with the limitation of external financing, with an impact on the definition of the rescue program; secondly, we would certainly lead to almost all banks being public capital, which was not the best at the time, regardless of ideological options. And it would certainly hinder the rationalization process. In 2011, there was a meeting in the BdP with the presidents of the banks, which resulted in pressure to call for external intervention. Today, it seems clear that the bailout has resolved not only state financing but also that of banks. The rescue also served to save the banks. At that time, the only thing that was posed was whether we were able to ensure that The months of May and June were not critical from the point of view of the state's compliance with debt repayment and payments. And what the banks were told was that they could not feed the illusion that they could finance the bonds they were going to win, there was no way to do so. In other words, the banks would also run out of money. Let us imagine that in May there was a non-fulfillment of the obligations. There are several versions and theories about what happened at that time... This question must be addressed to Professor Teixeira dos Santos. But he will explain to them that he made the announcement of the ransom request within the permissible limit, the deadlines for the approval of an assistance program were longer than the deadlines we had to observe in matters of state guarantees. On that day [of the ransom request] Professor Teixeira dos Santos took the initiative knowing, with a great sense of responsibility, that if we did not, we would hardly be able to have a program of assistance in time. Did Teixeira dos Santos warn you before announcing it publicly? You didn't warn me. But we were both perfectly aware that we had a problem. More people had a conscience. What he did was safeguard within the time limit the possibility of approving a program that avoided default. This is not a matter of ideology or opinion, it is a matter of fact. What Teixeira dos Santos did was very important. He did so against the prime minister, Jose Socrates. I don't pronounce it about that. He did so in the public interest. We must be aware that the programme was necessary, in order to avoid a much greater risk, that of the republic's cessation of payments, which would have chain consequences. Are you saying that the approval of Pec IV would not have prevented the ransom? It is a framework that cannot be developed today. What was at the time was a desire to rehearse an alternative route to the programmes that had been implemented in Greece and Ireland. But this implied a great willingness of the Member State to make the corresponding adjustment. It would be good if one day the then President of the European Commission, Barroso, explained to history what happened. This explains why the ECB and the European Commission have worked so hard to approve such a plan. And it explains the german chancellor's goodwill towards SGP IV. This was not unanimous in European countries, notably northern Europe. I am not in the secret of these discussions, what I say is external observation, but it should not be forgotten that it was perhaps the only time that there was a joint statement by the Commission and the ECB, with the sympathy of other actors, on the need to move forward with a different adjustment programme. Different doesn't mean less costs. Was it different because it wasn't by external imposition? It was different from the point of view of the property. Political autonomy? Yes, we would make the adjustments we had to make, but under another condition. Would we be what Paulo Portas later called a protectorate? This alternative route did not reach its end, the drawing was not made. Without knowing the drawing I can not anticipate what would be the result. What I can say is that there was a willingness to follow paths that were not exactly followed until then, but this implied great internal cohesion around the programme, a determination to achieve the goals - which would be the same - and certainly the European consensus that has not been tested. The profitability of banks is still miserable or does not even exist today. That poses a serious problem. Sure. When you are in the middle of a process of great transformation, you always run the risk of a relapse, but you can not lose sight of the way forward to achieve the sustainability of the business model. We must look at the current result of bank exploitation, purging from the effects of the past. That's what an investor wants. Then we have to look at what is the core of the bank, disparading assets that do not generate income: doubtful debt credits, real estate assets received in payment and other assets that consume capital and do not generate income. These types of assets do not exist only in Portugal, but everywhere... Are the Portuguese banks doomed to be swallowed by the European giants? The basic question is this: are banks able to complete the ongoing transformation process and make core activity a profitable activity while at the same time disdoing the assets that penalize them? It is the same problem that portuguese, Italian or european banks have. What would be desirable was to find solutions to remove punitive assets from the banks' balance sheet, by placing them in vehicles that would then allow them to be sold to final investors. This has not happened systematically. It cannot happen systematically as long as banks have to bear significant capital loss to do this type of operation. Because they have to sell below the value on the balance sheet. The values in the balance sheet are correct, in business continuation logic. Only those who come to buy, buy below these values. Unless there is the possibility of building a system of guarantees that allows the securitisation of these assets, and thus interest investors with a long-term vision and able to keep these assets on their balance sheets. That is, create a bad bank? You don't have to call it bad bank. You can create a vehicle, as was done in Spain, where assets that are not core of banks, that do not generate income or that need a lot of time to generate it are placed. Do you still defend the need for this mechanism? Yes, but it must be a European solution or with European support. Have you talked to the current government about this? yes, but that's in the offices. Is it important that caixa geral de depositos remains 100% public? It is important that there is an entity that can cover market failures if they occur. Under market and competitive conditions. And without any kind of public advantage because it's public ly. Should the state have a public bank? I don't see any reason why I shouldn't have it. 100% public? The percentage question would leave it open, but it's not for me to talk. Now, I do not see that from the point of view of good repute, nor from the point of view of alignment with the interests of the institution, the State shareholder is inferior to a private shareholder. It is now necessary to ensure that the administration is guided by reasons of sustainability of the institution and that it has all the freedom to make decisions on risk and rationalisation of the institution. It seems that the ecb is Portuguese the ECB and that Portugal is going to be a Spanish colony. Ownership of banks will depend on the strategy they pursue. The completion of the ongoing restructuring. This will determine your profitability and the ability to diversify the shareholder base. And also the price of banks, the relationship between the market price and the balance sheet value ( price to book value). A value that in Europe is generally at a discount. It's too big. 30 a 40%. Across Europe, it's not just in Portugal. When there are signs of a return on profitability, there will be a valuation of the banks. A bank's best defense is market interest in its bonds. But is there or is there not a 'Spanishization' of Portuguese banking, which emanades from a Frankfurt strategy? No. There is a risk that, being banks with a market value far below the balance sheet value, someone buys ahead of the market. If I were in the management of a bank or a shareholder I would be pushing to return to positive results and an ROE [return on capital] above 10%. This is the institution's best defense against any attempted purchase. You're running away from the question. Is there a vision in the ECB that favours Iberian consolidation or not? There is a different view of wanting European banks to have shareholder structures that ensure the ability to absorb losses. And to increase capital if necessary. Does that mean having big banks? It doesn't mean big. It means profitable, with capital cushions and ability to go to market. Portuguese, there's no... When you're in a situation of weakness, what you have to do is figure out how to get out. This takes time and until then there may be purchase attempts. That is why it is urgent to move forward and continue in this persevering effort. If the financial system Portuguese is dominated by Spanish banks, are you worried? No. The issue that worries me is the financing of the economy. It is to ensure that the banking system channels savings to agents in need of financing and to ensure that that savings are allocated in risky conditions to ensure that in the end there is a flow of return that allows the investor and depositor to recover their money. Will Santander, La Caixa or BBVA give you these guarantees? I cannot comment on BBVA, it is not present on the Portuguese, or it is only residually. La Caixa has been a very important partner in BPI and I hope it will continue to be important given the importance bpi has in the financial system Portuguese. He expects La Caixa to continue in Portugal. What solution do you see for the bpi impasse? I don't talk about specific situations. I think there is interest in a reference shareholder being kept in Portugal, Portuguese banks need foreign shareholders. Has your Angolan colleague called you about these changes? I never talk about relationships between colleagues, even when they're intense. Do you agree with the end of bpi voting limitations? It's a question for the legislator. In regulated sectors where an entity has to take care of the public interest, it is up to that entity to ensure the conditions that ensure that the shareholder structure is aligned with the last objectives, which are the soundness of the institution and financial stability. Until the crisis, no one cared about this. At the limit there was a concern with the administrators. We must now scrutinise not only the directors but the shareholders. And ask if a bank has a shareholder structure that allows it to respond to a capital requirement or a difficulty if it does. Mario Centeno is Finance Minister and Ricardo Mourinho Felix secretary of state. Before they were at Banco de Portugal, now they are next to those who criticize or even criticize the BdP. None. There may be differences of opinion, but it doesn't put me in any trouble. Regarding Professor Mario Centeno, he was in charge by me as a consultant to the governor to promote a conference that took place in May 2015, a sign that we have an easy working relationship. Regarding Dr. Ricardo Felix, I have a lot of appreciation, he was concerned with modeling within the Department of Studies. With you, Mario Centeno was considered as not having a profile to head the Department of Studies of the BdP. Now, has the profile to be Minister of Finance? I'm not talking about any specific case. Appointments to management positions at this bank, since I took office, have been made by open invitation and applications. They have also come to be evaluated by a jury in which the governor does not participate or influence. In this case, the jury report was very clear. Viewed from the outside, his proximity to the previous minister Vitor Gaspar was incredibly superior to what he has with Mario Centeno. I don't know why. You don't know why? I think all The Portuguese know... My relationship is merely institutional, committed, cooperative. And if we take stock of the three months of this Government and the relations I had with Vitor Gaspar in the first three months of his term of office, I would say that there is more interaction at this stage. In this short time he had to solve banif, in which he was criticized, and make a decision on the senior debt of Novo Banco, which was criticized by Ricardo Mourinho Felix. And he appointed Sergio Monteiro, which was also not well received in the Government. I'll explain everything. In the Banif resolution, the cooperation between the BdP and the Government was good and only then has a major problem been avoided. We must be aware that there has been a frank, loyal, institutional interaction with me and my teams. I am very grateful for the work that has been done by the members of the Government. With regard to the retransfer of senior issues to institutional [novo banco], we limit to apply the law in terms of loss sharing with previous stakeholders. If we did not, we would be disobeying the hierarchy of creditors provided for by law. If anyone today thinks this hierarchy is not appropriate, then they have to change the law. On the appointment of Sergio Monteiro, it was already planned yet it was not imagined that there would be a XXI Government. If the BdP did not follow up on that contract, it would obviously have to compensate it. Did you have to compensate him? Have you ever hired him? Of course, right after completing his duties in the 20th Government and before the start of the XXI. But the appointment of Sergio Monteiro already happens with this Government in office. The conclusion of the hiring process takes place at this stage, but all the legal acts that required the BdP are earlier. No one calls into question the technical capacity of Dr. Sergio Monteiro and no one also calls into question that the BdP is not designed to perform this function. He said this at the Assembly of the Republic in October 2014, long before this issue was put; he said it was not desirable for the BdP to be the resolution authority because there is a conflict between supervision and resolution. And secondly, the resolution authority must necessarily have the presence of those who have the power to decide on behalf of the State. If it wasn't desirable, why did it stay that way? Because at the time the resolution authority was created and the resolution fund there was a concern about media savings and the BdP sometimes serves as a surrogate. Why don't you change that now? I very much wish that it would change. It is your wish that the resolution background will come out of the purview of the BdP. My wish is that the BdP does not perform the functions of resolution authority, that is the important one. The resolution fund is merely instrumental. In this respect I agree with the Prime Minister. Did you be strange at the time that BES was the only big bank not to resort to the troika's capitalisation line? What is provided for in the law is that the institution is the one who takes the initiative to ask for access to recapitalisation. The data contained in the presentation of accounts did not allow us to assume that there was falsification of information. Why didn't you ask Ricardo Salgado to leave in January 2014, when KPMG delivered the report that showed that ESI's accounts were not right? KPMG doesn't say there's a fake of accounts. He says there's a bankrupt entity, it's something else. If she was broke, the accounts weren't right. Look at the law at the time and check if there was a way to make a process of goodre in the face of law and jurisprudence. Today, retrospectively, it's easy, but with the data of the time we couldn't do it. Therefore, it was for legal reasons. The legal framework is what it is. Notice, already after the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry (CPI), the BdP saw a decision to withdraw suitability be annulled by a court. In this case, it was a small financial company, but it's the same thing. Imagine the care and legal certainty that you need to have in the case of a large institution. At what point did you stop trusting Ricardo Salgado? At the end of May [2014], the day I received the information that showed that there was forgery of accounts. Doesn't there have to be powers that will allow the governor of Banco de Portugal to say that a banker cannot continue? If I had the powers of Mervyn King [governor of the Bank of England], I would have done it. Suitability seems a vague concept. If we arrive at Terreiro do Paco, in Lisbon, we can find everyone suitable. That's why the law's been amended. The concept of suitability was little densified, as legal experts say. It was perfectly possible to contradict the BdP's decision by arguing that we were assuming something that went against the elementary principles of presumption of good repute. Some have even written that good work is a kind of natural right. The law has been completely changed. Not to the point we would like, because there have been constitutional considerations, but the densification of the concept of suitability goes far beyond being a person with a life without incident. Today, suitability is moral, professional suitability and, in addition, ability to be part of a team consistently. We're in a different chapter. Did you receive a lot of pressure at the time not to act on the BES case? I don't talk about it. What I am saying is that the first entity to act in the case of BES was Banco de Portugal. A posteriori everyone had ideas about whether to do. The BES case was not the first case. Before there had been the LBW... The LBW is not mine! But how is it possible for this to happen a second time in a much larger bank? There is a case of a Spanish bank in which the Bank of Spain had more than twenty inspectors long inside the bank and despite this could not see operations of the same nature. So, as Dr. Artur Santos Silva says, "is it possible to systematically deceive the regulator"? That is why I said in my swearing-in speech that one of the fundamental conditions for exercising the supervisory function is that all other rings that support supervision work, if not the supervisor runs the risk of not being able to gather the information he needs. The bank's internal control mechanisms... Were you surprised when you realized what was going on at BES? [pause] As I was an actor in the very close monitoring process, I would say that I was surprised by the bankruptcy of companies in the non-financial area, very concerned about contamination to the financial area and obviously very surprised by the problem of counterfeiting accounts. Did you ever feel frustrated that you hadn't seen it before? I always feel that way. It's the same frustration a cop has when he arrives late at the scene of the murder. We're here to prevent it from happening. During that period, you didn't get in trouble? It did, but my main concern is about the moral foundations of Portuguese society. This can only happen if the moral foundations of Portuguese society are not strong enough to prevent the occurrence. And they're not? I don't know, i don't know Each one draws his conclusions. He said that many people only had opinions about bes after it fell and, it is said, was silent during the process. Were you referring to politicians? If the governor was surprised, it is natural that many people were surprised and had surely the best of opinions and were convinced that nothing would happen. When on July 10 [2014] we asked BES to communicate to the market authority that it had a capital cushion to address exposure to the group companies that were going bankrupt, we did so because we were concerned about protecting the bank. In this process, we adjusted our perception of the problem as we were getting new elements. If we had all the elements at the outset, the strategy would have been naturally different. Did you do it in isolation? I did it with Banco de Portugal. Inside Banco de Portugal, were there times when you were alone? No. Banco de Portugal is a consistent team. There may be discussion and divergence of opinions but decisions have always been taken by consensus. Why did you fail the first attempt to sell the New Bank? We had two years to sell and we had a duty to show diligence. Two years and elections on the doorstep. It has nothing to do with it. How can people believe that? The process accelerated upon the elections. It has nothing to do with it. In fact, the sale would have an ambivalent [electoral] effect, depended on the price. It had to do with the Directorate General for Competition (DGCom). We wouldn't be able to get an additional deadline if we hadn't shown diligence. And by the way, the circumstances in which this process was done had risks that we were aware of, and had advantages. The advantages was to show that we were diligent, create in the bank the obligation to organize for a sale process, make the bank known to several interested parties. But we knew we had risks: the risk that resulted from the bank's balance sheet was still being closed; the risk that resulted from the capital required of the bank is not yet defined (today it is already); the risk of having assets with contingencies that could scare buyers; the risk that potential European buyers themselves have a sword of Damocles on their heads which resulted from being subject to a capital assessment process. And then there was an accident we weren't expecting, the Shanghai Stock Exchange. With the Shanghai crisis, one of the candidates surely thought twice before raising money in the market and the other of the candidates must have thought that, to make investment, it would be on the Shanghai stock exchange, to hold the market. Is it important that this sale is made by consolidation, that is, with Novo Banco being bought by a bank that is already in Portugal? What is fundamental is that Novo Banco has an owner who print a strategy, that owner has capital and capacity to support the bank and that ensures the ability to provide services and its role in the business fabric Portuguese. Then, it is essential that it guarantees an interesting price, because it reduces losses, knowing that market conditions are very adverse. This is if the option is for sale. If the option is different, then it is necessary to restructure the bank to ensure that it is efficient and continues to provide services at the lowest cost, in an aggressive competitive framework. You admit to selling the bank on the stock exchange? It's not excluded. But the BdP is not the owner of the process, it is the trustee. As such, we must have all roads open. We should also have flexibility in relation to the amount to be sold. What is crucial is to ensure, if that is the goal, the ownership of the bank. But the basic question is this: do we want to sell or not? This is not a Question of BdP. When you transferred senior debt from Novo Banco to bad BES, did you get the notion that you made a decision that international investors only expect from countries like Venezuela? No. If you read the Financial Times editorial, you see it's not like that. We read this and many others. From a market point of view, it was a radical decision. This was the first time the resolution directive was applied. Do you know that it has affected the risk of Portugal? I am convinced that we have not done so and the proof of this is that some investors have returned to the Portuguese. Were you forced to sell Banif to Santander? No. [To say this] is a total ignorance. We were called upon to make a sale on the resolution board, which means selling the banking business to an entity that has to have a banking license. It had to be a bank operating in Portugal. Then there are conditions that were established by DGCom: it had to be a bank that ensured the viability of the business. If Banif had failed to make a separation between a good bank and a side bank [to the letter, "side bank"], it could not be an entity that came to redo the exercise. DGCom put us before some parameters and there were two buyers who had come forward, Banco Popular and Santander. The two had been hierarchized by the consulting company hired by Banif's management for the voluntary sale process, N1, first Santander, according to Popular. We invited you both to make proposals. They had until 8 am on Sunday to submit a proposal, Santander submitted and Popular gave up. Only Santander met the sales requirements. If the sale to Santander failed by midnight on Sunday, the left over was the settlement and there we were creating a much higher cost and a systemic problem in the archipelagos. Everybody'd love to buy things like that. In the short hour for the seller. There are facts that are produced in an advertised way, the actors have to do everything to make sure they don't happen. It was the chronicle of an announced sale. Exactly. The Board of Directors and [Banif's] shareholders had to take the necessary measures to ensure that the limit situation did not take place. But it did. Why did you leave for midnight on the last day? And there is a political issue: the push of the Banif issue facilitated the clean exit and that the issue was not discussed in the election campaign. The resolution process can only be triggered from the moment public aid is not accepted. Public aid to Banif had been in place for a long time. It is dg competition that has the power to decide whether or not public aid is illegal. And DG Competition let the process drag on. The State Portuguese also left and was inside the bank. The State Portuguese and the administration would not decree that the aid was invalid. At most, they could sell the bank. I insist, unlike the BES or the LBW, in banif the state was inside. The BdP had to look at the bank as a bank that respected prudential ratios and was awaiting validation of the public aid process. As long as she wasn't declared legal or illegal, she had to treat him fairly. What puts uncertainty for taxpayers is that there is a silo-based system where everyone is responsible for their area  and Banco de Portugal, CMVM, government and administrations do everything they have to do  but there is no whole vision. The Banif case is evident in this. I don't want to make any sense about any of the actors, because I believe that each of them has been diligent. What they have to go looking for is at every moment who is the determining actor and whether he at that moment anticipates the risk and acts in accordance with that risk and if he has the incentives for it. And I'm going to stay here. When an administration puts eight plans on DGCom and they're all bad, something's wrong. There were four banks recapitalized. Three  BPI, Caixa and BCP  were able to negotiate restructuring plans with DG Competition that it validated. And one didn't make it, Banif. The question is what interests prevented the parties from converging. And you don't have the BdP obligation to realize that something's going on in the bank? When it is revealed the correspondence exchanged in this regard in the framework of the CPI will realize what was the attitude of the BdP. What's that? I can't say more. Taxpayers are going to pay "a lot of money." The common interest has not been defended. It is normal for there to be minority interests in a bank, majority interests, for agency problems... Are you saying that it was the interests of minority shareholders that stopped the resolution of the problem? As one sociologist i value very much, [Pierre] Bourdieu, a bench is a field of forces. We try to look at human groups as if they were homogeneous, but each person carries their interest. Bourdieu was an anthropologist, did not study finance or economics. Also the Pessoa said that the country had not studied [laughs]. We have to hire an anthropologist for Banco de Portugal... No, we don't. I don't need an anthropologist to figure that out. I need to understand what my skills limits are and understand what's going on. I have no doubt that, throughout the history of the banking system since 1989/90, there is a dynamic interpersonal relationship and field of forces that explains failures and successes of the banking system. There is a basic question: those who enter a force field cannot be neutral, because if they stay neutral, they stay away. And you need to know what interests you stand for. Has Banif's management defended the interests of minority shareholders? Each one was diligent in defending the interests, what happens is that the bank should have submitted a restructuring plan and did not present. Banif's CPI is going to start. Are you going with a clear conscience? Undoubtedly. The BdP did what it had to do, warned when it had to warn, performed its supervisory function as it had to supervise. Can the Portuguese trust the financial system and Portuguese there are still skeletons in the closet? Portuguese banks now have much higher levels of capital and liquidity than they had in 2010. The identification of risks is done and the only thing that can bring surprise is the continuation of an economic crisis. At the end of his second term, will the financial system be stronger than when he entered? Surely. Do the Portuguese have reason to trust that? That's what we're working for. And to trust you? What the BdP did in the cases that are in the public square was what any central bank would do if it were dealing with the same problems and with a sovereign with the same conditions. A central bank of a country with a very strong treasure can manage problems probably with more waste but less noise. During his term, he never happened to him as the character of Jo Soares who said "what else will happen to me?!" [Laughs] There's one characteristic that people who work with me, and to whom I'm very grateful, know i have, is that every morning is a new day. I'm not looking back, I'm looking forward. Haven't you ever lost a night's sleep? I've lost nights of sleep working here. Do you feel destituous or a victim? It's not in my way of victimizing myself. I regard the function as an independent function, with the risks of displeasing some, now others; as a function that has to be exercised autonomously, and therefore without receiving instructions from one or the other, with the aim of pursuing the public interest  and the public interest in the BdP is financial stability and monetary stability. Did it cross your mind to come out, "I'm sick of this, I'm going to play golf"? No [laughs]. Listen, if I wanted to have a quiet life, I wouldn't have agreed to come to this place and i'd let go of being vice president of the EIB. But I didn't know what was coming. I knew it, I knew it. I didn't know that much, but I did. I was vice-president of the EIB, I had the privilege of having responsibilities that fill me with contentment. I left with my high price and with many more advantages than I had in Lisbon. When I came here, I can say i knew how to have a difficult task ahead of me. One of these days my wife reminded me of this, "I still remember when you said to me: I hope you don't invite me..."
