Title: Opening speech of Administrator Hlder Rosalino at the Finance Innovation Day Conference
text: Opening speech of Administrator Helder Rosalino at the Finance Innovation Day Conference 30 jan. 2017 Welcome to Banco de Portugal and the Money Museum. It is with satisfaction that Banco de Portugal welcomes in its facilities a very significant set of representatives of the financial system and other entities for the discussion of innovation and digital transformation in banking. I begin by thanking Microsoft for the initiative of this conference and for the value proposition it presented to Banco de Portugal in order to make it truly useful, not only for the financial system, but also for Banco de Portugal in view of its responsibilities as monetary authority and regulator of the financial system. This was, moreover, the condition for Banco de Portugal to be able to host and join the holding of this conference. It is, in fact, an initiative that has as its central purpose the promotion of the debate around the challenges facing the banking sector and its regulation, as a result of innovation and the profound digital transformation underway. This conference has important speakers, covering the areas of strategic consulting and human resources management, as well as the international financial system itself, who will make known their experience in addressing innovation and the digital business. It also has an intervention by Banco de Portugal, which will have the opportunity to present the essential lines of its own digital transformation process, as well as its vision, as a regulator, on some of the expected impacts on the banking sector resulting from the innovations that are being anticipated. This is not the first initiative that Banco de Portugal welcomes or organises on this subject, seeking to boost, at national level, the debate on the major challenges digital innovation puts to the financial system and its regulation. Banco de Portugal organized, in October last year, an important international conference dedicated to the theme of Digital Banking and FinTech, which allowed us to discuss the challenges and threats posed to the banking system in these areas. This Conference was attended by reputable international speakers from some of Europe's largest central banks, the EDF, the IMF and international consultants. At the same time, Banco de Portugal has set up an internal and multidisciplinary think tank, with the aim of studying the evolution of Digital Banking and FinTech and to look at, in 2020, the challenges that arise in the broader context of its mission and in the specific framework of its regulatory and supervisory responsibilities. As has been acknowledged by several experts, the banking system is currently facing a certain "existential crisis", which does not clearly predict how they will be and how banks will work in the not too distant future. This crisis stems, on the one hand, from the significant change in the economic conditions underlying its business model and the growing regulatory pressure and, on the other hand, from the profound digital transformation of the economy and society to which we are witnessing. The effects of the financial crisis in recent years, linked to a Banking Union with a still incomplete institutional framework, pose major challenges for European and national banks. The consequences of low levels of economic growth on business volume and defaulting credit, the effects of very low interest rates and high regulatory requirements are currently very active restrictions on banking system activity. In this context, the effects of ongoing technological changes that will be accentuated, whether in the field of Digital Banking or FinTech, in addition to presenting themselves as an increasingly demanding challenge, can be a great opportunity for the banking sector, but also for businesses and consumers. Digital Banking and FinTech have common traits. Both phenomena are technological shocks that are changing the architecture and business models of the banking system in all geographies on a large scale. But there are differences between these two technological movements, regarding the timing and uncertainty of their effects. The effects of Digital Banking are already significantly altering the relationship between banks and their customers, with the evolution of the offer of technology-based products and services. This phenomenon will be reinforced over the next few years, considering that the new generations (especially the "Millennium" and "Digital Natives") generations are increasingly apprehendable by the use of new technologies and for the provision of services customized to their real needs. Therefore, it is not surprising that there is a decrease in the physical presence of banks, both in number of branches and employees. All the countries of the European Union have seen a reduction of around 40,000 branches in the last five years. In the case of employees this reduction was 250,000. However, this reduction process is far from over, as they have been heralded by the majority of new banks and significant adjustments in the coming years, largely as a result of ongoing digital developments. As far as FinTech is said, the degree of uncertainty about their impacts is much higher. Many of the new technology-based financial services offerings have been developed outside the banking system by startups and cover diverse areas such as payment systems, credit operations, management and financial mobility. For its promoters, this wave of innovation and digital transformation promises a technological revolution that will democratize financial services, with the following immediate benefits: Consumers will have more options, services more targeted to their needs and more attractive prices, Small and medium-sized enterprises will have access to new credit facilities and better market conditions; Banks will become more productive, with lower transaction costs, higher capital efficiency and increased operational resilience; The financial system itself will become more resilient, with greater diversity, redundancy and depth; And, above all, financial services will be more inclusive, with better people connected, more informed and increasingly empowered. However, it is not certain that most of the startups that are boosting these innovations will survive, just as it is not yet clear which business areas will thrive in the FinTech universe. Nor is the level of response that the banking system will give to this phenomenon yet. Therefore, it is still particularly difficult to anticipate the evolution of the banking system as a result of technological innovation associated with the provision of new financial services based on FinTech. Although the levels of uncertainty are still very high, the challenges facing the financial system are enormous in the field of innovation and digital transformation. They require a vision and strategy, an innovative attitude, the openness to introduce new business approaches, new partnerships and, not least, investment capacity and strengthening the internal skills of banks. The consequences of these developments, which can be quite disruptive on banks' business models, also pose major challenges for supervisors, both in the micro and macroprudential areas and in the behavioural area. Banks' new architecture and new business models will require a multidisciplinary response from central banks, posing challenges to several of their core functions, such as monetary policy implementation, reserve asset management, banking supervision and financial stability assurance. As the Governor of the Bank of England recently said: "In the face of these new challenges, central banks must have consistent approaches to similar activities carried out by different institutions, which can lead to the same risks to financial stability. Just because something is new doesn't necessarily mean it should be treated differently. Similarly, just because it's outside the regulatory perimeter doesn't necessarily mean it needs to be brought in." In short, the message of the Governor of the Bank of England is that it is necessary to know to act. And it is necessary to be close to or even within technological innovation, to understand and guide it in the interest of financial stability. That was why the Bank of England created the FinTech Accelerator, which in addition to the goal of accelerating the FinTech ecosystem, aims to reflect on how the supervisor can monitor and benefit from technological innovation in these areas. There are new times for the banking system, but also for central banks, which require new approaches, new resources and new skills. I hope that this conference will become a valuable contribution to help build as much shared a vision as possible on the challenges and benefits that digital transformation can bring to the functioning of the entire financial system. And I hope that you will enjoy this space as much as possible and that you can benefit from the guided tour of our magnificent Money Museum, which tells the story of the evolution of money and also of the financial system. This is the ideal space to connect the past, translated by the Museum, with the future we try to anticipate with this conference. I wish you all a good conference. Thank you very much.
text_original: Interveno de abertura do Administrador Hlder Rosalino na Conferncia "Finance Innovation Day" 30 jan. 2017 Bem-vindos ao Banco de Portugal e ao Museu do Dinheiro.  com satisfao que o Banco de Portugal acolhe nas suas instalaes um conjunto muito significativo de representantes do sistema financeiro e de outras entidades para a discusso da inovao e da transformao digital na banca. Comeo por enderear um agradecimento  Microsoft pela iniciativa desta conferncia e pela proposta de valor que apresentou ao Banco de Portugal no sentido de a tornar verdadeiramente til, no s para o sistema financeiro, mas tambm para o Banco de Portugal na perspetiva das suas responsabilidades enquanto autoridade monetria e regulador do sistema financeiro. Essa foi, alis, a condio para que o Banco de Portugal pudesse acolher e associar-se  realizao desta conferncia. Trata-se, efetivamente, de uma iniciativa que tem como propsito central a promoo do debate em torno dos desafios que se colocam ao setor bancrio e  sua regulao, em resultado da inovao e da profunda transformao digital em curso. Esta conferncia conta com importantes oradores, que cobrem as reas da consultoria estratgica e da gesto dos recursos humanos, bem como do prprio sistema financeiro internacional, que nos daro a conhecer a sua experincia na abordagem  inovao e ao negcio digital. Conta tambm com uma interveno do Banco de Portugal, que ter oportunidade de apresentar as linhas essenciais do seu prprio processo de transformao digital, bem como a sua viso, enquanto regulador, sobre alguns dos impactos esperados para o setor bancrio resultantes das inovaes que se perspetivam. Esta no  a primeira iniciativa que o Banco de Portugal acolhe ou organiza sobre este tema, procurando dinamizar, ao nvel nacional, o debate em torno dos grandes desafios que a inovao digital coloca ao sistema financeiro e  sua regulao. O Banco de Portugal organizou, em outubro do ano passado, uma importante Conferncia internacional dedicada ao tema da Banca Digital e das FinTech, que permitiu debater os desafios e as ameaas que se lhe colocam ao sistema bancrio nestes domnios. Essa Conferncia mereceu a presena de reputados oradores internacionais, vindos de alguns dos maiores bancos centrais da Europa, do FED, do FMI e tambm de consultoras internacionais. Paralelamente, o Banco de Portugal criou um grupo de reflexo interno e multidisciplinar, com o objetivo de estudar a evoluo da Banca Digital e das FinTech e de perspetivar, no horizonte 2020, os desafios que se lhe colocam no contexto alargado da sua misso e no quadro especfico das suas responsabilidades de regulao e superviso. Como tem vindo a ser reconhecido por vrios especialistas, o sistema bancrio vive atualmente confrontado com uma certa crise existencial, que no deixa antecipar com clareza como iro ser e como vo funcionar os bancos num futuro no muito longnquo. Esta crise resulta, por um lado, da significativa alterao das condies econmicas subjacentes ao seu modelo de negcio e  crescente presso regulatria e, por outro, da profunda transformao digital da economia e da sociedade a que estamos a assistir. Os efeitos da crise financeira vivida nos ltimos anos, associados a uma Unio Bancria com um quadro institucional ainda incompleto, colocam grandes desafios aos bancos europeus e nacionais. As consequncias dos baixos nveis de crescimento econmico sobre o volume de negcio e sobre o crdito em incumprimento, os efeitos das muito baixas taxas de juro e as elevadas exigncias regulatrias so atualmente restries muito ativas  atividade do sistema bancrio. Neste contexto, os efeitos das alteraes tecnolgicas em curso e que se iro acentuar, sejam no domnio da Banca Digital ou das FinTech, para alm de se apresentarem como um desafio cada vez mais exigente, podem constituir uma grande oportunidade para o setor bancrio, mas tambm para as empresas e para os consumidores. A Banca Digital e as FinTech tm traos comuns. Ambos os fenmenos constituem choques tecnolgicos que esto a mudar em grande escala a arquitetura e os modelos de negcio do sistema bancrio em todas as geografias. Mas existem diferenas entre estes dois movimentos tecnolgicos, relativamente ao momento e  incerteza dos seus efeitos. Os efeitos da Banca Digital j esto a alterar, de forma muito significativa, a relao entre os Bancos e os seus clientes, com a evoluo da oferta de produtos e servios de base tecnolgica. Este fenmeno ser reforado ao longo dos prximos anos, considerando que as novas geraes (sobretudo as geraes Millennium e Digital Natives) tm cada vez maior apetncia pela utilizao de novas tecnologias e pela oferta de servios customizados s suas reais necessidades. Por isso, no  surpreendente que esteja a ocorrer uma diminuio da presena fsica dos bancos, tanto em nmero de balces, como de colaboradores. No conjunto dos pases da Unio Europeia observou-se uma reduo de cerca de 40 mil agncias nos ltimos cinco anos. No caso de colaboradores essa reduo foi de 250 mil. No entanto, este processo de reduo est longe de estar terminado, na medida em que tm sido anunciados pela generalidade dos bancos novos e expressivos ajustamentos nos prximos anos, em grande parte como resultado da evoluo digital em curso. No que se refere s FinTech o grau de incerteza sobre os seus impactos  bastante superior. Muitas das novas ofertas de servios financeiros de base tecnolgica foram desenvolvidas fora do sistema bancrio por startups e cobrem reas diversificadas, como os sistemas de pagamento, as operaes de crdito, a gesto e a mobilidade financeira. Para os seus promotores, esta onda de inovao e transformao digital promete uma revoluo tecnolgica que ir democratizar os servios financeiros, com os seguintes benefcios imediatos: Os consumidores tero mais opes, servios mais direcionados s suas necessidades e preos mais atrativos, As pequenas e mdias empresas tero acesso a novas facilidades de crditos e a melhores condies de mercado; Os bancos tornar-se-o mais produtivos, com menores custos de transao, maior eficincia de capital e maior resilincia operacional; O prprio sistema financeiro tornar-se- mais resiliente, com maior diversidade, redundncia e profundidade; E, principalmente, os servios financeiros sero mais inclusivos, com pessoas melhor conectadas, mais informadas e cada vez mais capacitadas. Porm, no  certo que a maior parte das startups que esto dinamizar estas inovaes venha a sobreviver, do mesmo modo que ainda no  claro quais sero s reas de negcio que iro prosperar no universo das FinTech. Tambm no  ainda certo o nvel de resposta que o sistema bancrio ir dar a este fenmeno. Por isso,  ainda particularmente difcil antecipar a evoluo do sistema bancrio em resultado da inovao tecnolgica associada a proviso de novos servios financeiros baseados nas FinTech. No obstante os nveis de incerteza serem ainda muito grandes, o certo  que os desafios que se colocam ao sistema financeiro so enormes no domnio da inovao e da transformao digital. Exigem uma viso e uma estratgia, uma atitude inovadora, a abertura para introduzir novas abordagens de negcio, novas parcerias e, no menos importante, capacidade de investimento e de reforo das competncias interna dos bancos. As consequncias destas evolues, que podem ser bastante disruptivas sobre os modelos de negcios dos bancos, colocam igualmente grandes desafios s autoridades de superviso, tanto nas reas micro e macroprudencial, como na rea comportamental. A nova arquitetura e os novos modelos de negcios dos Bancos obrigaro a uma resposta multidisciplinar dos bancos centrais, colocando desafios a vrias das suas funes core, tais como a implementao da poltica monetria, a gesto de ativos de reserva, a superviso bancria e a garantia da estabilidade financeira. Como dizia recentemente o Governador do Banco de Inglaterra: Face a estes novos desafios, os bancos centrais devem ter abordagens consistentes para atividades semelhantes levadas a cabo por diferentes instituies, que podem conduzir aos mesmos riscos para a estabilidade financeira. S porque algo  novo no significa necessariamente que deva ser tratado de forma diferente. Da mesma forma, apenas porque est fora do permetro regulatrio no significa necessariamente que precise de ser trazido para dentro. Em suma, a mensagem do Governador do Banco de Inglaterra  a de que  preciso conhecer para atuar. E  preciso estar perto ou mesmo dentro da inovao tecnolgica, para a compreender e orientar no interesse da estabilidade financeira. Essa foi a razo pela qual o Banco de Inglaterra criou o  FinTech Accelerator, que para alm do objetivo de acelerar o ecossistema das FinTech, pretende refletir sobre a forma como o supervisor pode acompanhar e beneficiar da inovao tecnolgica nestas reas. Vivem-se tempos novos para o sistema bancrio, mas tambm para os bancos centrais, que exigem novas abordagens, novos recursos e novas competncias. Espero que esta conferncia se transforme num valioso contributo para ajudar  construo de uma viso tanto quanto possvel partilhada sobre os desafios e os benefcios que a transformao digital pode introduzir no funcionamento de todo o sistema financeiro. E espero que desfrutem o mais possvel deste espao e que possam beneficiar da visita guiada ao nosso magnifico Museu do Dinheiro, que conta a histria da evoluo do dinheiro e tambm do sistema financeiro. Este  o espao ideal para ligar o passado, traduzido pelo Museu, com o futuro que tentamos antecipar com esta conferncia. Desejo a todos uma boa conferncia. Muito obrigado. Title: Interview of the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Carlos da Silva Costa, to the Public
text: Interview of the Governor of the Bank of... Interview of the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Carlos da Silva Costa, to the Public 08 mar. 2017 There are documents that did not deliver in the parliamentary committee of inquiry (CPI) to the case Banco Espirito Santo (BES). From the outset, an internal document of November 8, 2013 that advocated a timely performance in relation to Ricardo Salgado. Why didn't you turn them in? They are working documents and as was transmitted to the CPI, the working documents are not covered by the duty of disclosure. The document in question is part of a series of internal reflections which began on my initiative in February 2013 on news published in the press to determine whether there was a rationale for what was published and how serious it was. Between February 2013 and November a lot happened and between November and April 2014 when D . Ricardo Salgado accepted that he would not continue to lead the bank also much happened. Wasn't that an important document? What is important to say is that what the document suggested, which was to continue the reflection, was exactly what was done: first, to continue to reflect on the facts that were being indicted, second, to confront the people concerned with those same facts and, thirdly, to build the evidence and then on the basis of the evidence to know what consequences should be taken from that evidence. This was done, it was clearly transmitted to the CPI. Subsequent investigations led the bank to conclude that there was no reason for ricardo salgado's loss of suitability... No. No, no, no, no, no, no The note was duly taken into account and what the subsequent findings led to the conclusion was that there were sufficient reasons, first, not to allow the taking of office in cases where applications for authorisation were pending. And secondly, there were enough reasons that were consecrated in April 2014, to demand from Dr. Ricardo Salgado a succession plan and to demand that the family move away from the management of BES. And this is expressed in documentation that was delivered to the CPI. We are talking about an internal note from the end of 2013, but the process of withdrawal of suitability only came to fruition until later why? The suitability assessment process began in February 2013. In September, early October 2013, we started an investigation into some administrators of the Espirito Santo Group, because it was in the domain of the non-financial group that the questions were raised. Third, on November 5, 2013, Banco de Portugal questioned Dr. Ricardo Salgado, both about the payment of Mr. Jose Conceicao Guilherme in 2011 in the amount of 8.5 million, and about the relationship maintained with Akoya. This letter was answered by Dr. Ricardo Salgado on November 21, 2013 and from there began a process of correspondence, with successive accumulation of information that leads us to that on April 16, 2014 Dr. Ricardo Salgado to Banco de Portugal the letters of resignation of the positions whose records were pending with the Bank. But why didn't they take the suit and have to wait for the resignation? I couldn't do it. There are two judgments, the first, of the Supreme Administrative Court in 2005 and the second of the Central Administrative Court of the South, in 2012, and then a third of the Central Administrative Court of the North, already after the Resolution, on 23 September 2015, which clearly said that the withdrawal of the suitability depended on the existence of previous judicial convictions. And it was necessary that they had become final. Had Banco de Portugal had no way of removing the suitability of a banker if he had not been convicted and the conviction had not become final? Until 24 October 2015 it was like this. Meanwhile, the law has been amended, giving Banco de Portugal the possibility to intervene and remove the suitability of someone on whom there are well-founded reasons to doubt their ability to continue ahead of an institution. In any case, even in this case, they can always appeal the decision of Banco de Portugal. And so it is very important the letter that Dr. Ricardo Salgado wrote to Banco de Portugal at the time, to give up, in essence, the possibility of asking for a new registration. Under pressure from Banco de Portugal... We could put pressure on it and we made it to the point where people agreed to come up with a succession plan and accept that they would not be part of the governing bodies and more, accept that the whole family would move away from the management of the bank. And we did everything on the edge of what was allowed and maintaining a lot of pressure. As you imagine, in October, November 2013 or January 2014, having with me the Espirito Santo family, as I once had, or Dr. Ricardo Salgado, or all the others and telling them face to face, you do not have the suitability to continue ahead of an institution, it was a great novelty for themselves and it was also an act of great affirmation of the independence and capacity of Banco de Portugal to interpret strictly by law. Only the law didn't allow it to go beyond a certain point. From what he says, until the law was achanged in October 2014, he had his hands tied to remove the suit ability from a banker. Did you push for the law to be changed? When did you put pressure on it? Did. It would have to make the history, but a legislative change is not born and consummated on the day it is approved, it is born well in advance and was the subject of internal reflection, first, and the competent entities to demonstrate that there was a need to create a legislative framework that gave the supervisor powers ... In this period of 2013/2014, he was giving an account of what was happening to the Government. We certainly exchanged information. And if the legislative process was triggered, it is certainly because our argument was convincing. And the law did not fully accept our intention. But it gives us a margin of manoeuvre that we didn't have at all at the time. Would it change anything about what you did? Necessarily, with the knowledge that one has afterwards, it would be much more... I wouldn't say more aggressive, because the law wouldn't allow me. But it would have at least a much greater anguish, because it would be limited by law... But couldn't you do more? What we did was what we could do, in a fair assessment of the information we had available, with the common sense that demanded the situation. It's very easy today, with the information we have, to make sense of that time. Now, how many commentators have censured me for not having authorized a successor to Dr. Ricardo Salgado to take over? How many? Are you still able to be governor of Banco de Portugal? Of course i do. When you are governor of an institution such as Banco de Portugal, which has by statute, by organic law and for public knowledge an important role and a recognition of its independence, independence also involves the ability to carry out the mission entrusted to it and the fulfillment of mandates. Do you feel that the government is somehow pushing for your exit? The relations I have had with the Government are normal, institutional and there are a number of issues on which we have been very closely involved - and which have been the subject of statements by the Prime Minister, on which I hope to succeed as soon as possible, for the sake of the country's financial stability. But it does not ignore that there are people within the PS with political responsibilities, or in the parties that support the Government, who make public attacks on it. All my colleagues who are central bank governors, starting with the Fed and passing through the ECB and the Bank of England, all of them have, in the name of independence and in the name of their equidistance, that accepting that their action is scrutinised, is the subject of criticism. But also in the name of independence and in the name of defending the institution's mission they must fulfil their mandate and continue what is the mission entrusted to the institution. It's a little more than a review. Some say openly that the governor is unable to continue to exercise his mandate. I would only not be able to exercise my mandate if I were not able to guarantee the independence of Banco de Portugal and to ensure the fulfilment of the mission entrusted to it. As I think I can guarantee the independence of Banco de Portugal... Moreover, there are public statements that recognize this same independence. I have a very strong commitment to the mission and the objectives - and we are achieving them, in particular the objective of financial stability - I do not see why I should not go on. On the contrary. There is no independence of an institution without strong commitment to the fulfillment of mandates. He was with the President of the Republic for days, it was the President who suggested that he go to Parliament to explain this latest controversy. I do not comment on conversations with any of the public entities with whom I have meetings, be it mr President, mr. Prime Minister or Mr Minister of Finance. With regard to the decisions I make, I take those decisions with the autonomy of those who believe that at some point it is appropriate to explain, especially if these explanations are relevant for eliminating misunderstandings. You're afraid that once the New Bank is settled, the government will say no? First, Banco de Portugal is an independent entity. Secondly, it has rules, including those relating to the mandate of its governor. And thirdly, the relations I have with the Government from an institutional point of view do not in any way allow me to imagine such a situation. In any case, the question is whether or not I want to fulfill my mandate and whether or not I want to be the guardian of banco de Portugal's independence. And you want to serve your term to the end? If I do not fulfil my mandate, I do not fulfil my obligation to safeguard the independence of Banco de Portugal. Fernando Ulrich handed him a document in 2013, warning him of ges' gigantic debt. What did you do to the document? The document was delivered in August 2013. At that time, GES had already been identified as one of the large debtors of the system. And we were already preparing ETRIC 2, which is a request to the auditors to, in an area that was not our supervisor, issue their opinions on the financial soundness of the institutions what was done in a first preliminary report in February 2014 and which was delivered in the final report in May 2014. Then Banco de Portugal found that the value of ESI's liabilities did not correspond to the real value - and this forced an in-depth investigation. The BPI delivered a document that was duly taken into account, although it did not add to what we already knew. What was transmitted to the troika? In the assistance program what was followed by the BdP and the troika was the financial system. The companies were only followed to the extent that they were debtors of the financial system. That's why we've done ETRIC 2, which is a completely exceptional action, where we ask auditors to audit companies that are not subject to our supervision, in order to understand what the risk results from them for banks. But we had already completed two-thirds of the assistance program. And within those two-thirds we did extremely important actions. First, and contrary to what was said in the public square, we carried out a programme of external and independent audits of all the banks, which were promoted by the auditors under the control of the BdP and the troika, which to this end constituted a monitoring committee where the troika, the BdP and three central bank experts from Belgium were, France and Spain. At what point in this process do you realize that there is a very big problem in BES? There are two distinct moments. One in which I have the indication of a large indebtedness of GES, which is October 2013, after ETRIC 1, which leads to the realization that there was part of the debt of ESI that was not based in Portugal, nor supervised by the BdP, which was not registered. It means ges clearly gets on our radar. And that's why we determined the ring fencing - the bank armor. However, BES will not default on solvency ratios until 27 July when it presents the accounts for the second quarter of 2014. And that's the only time there's a moment of bes collapse. The first moment you realize everything is at stake is October 2013? It's not that everything is at risk, what's at stake is bes's non-financial area. If you tell me that when Ulrich gives you a letter and you wouldn't add much information to him. The document given to me by Dr. Fernando Ulrich was produced in a different context, which I admit was advisory in a conflict between parties. Portugal was about to finish the assistance program. Were you afraid that Portugal would not be able to finish it if the fall of BES had been sooner? The problem did not occur, because the fall of bes only manifested itself on 27 July, in which the bank presented the quarterly accounts - and a capital shortfall, below the minimum required. And it failed to demonstrate that it would be able to re-operate in a timely manner. Never before the exit of the memo did it cross your mind that BES could be dragged with GES? Everything was done so that ges did not drag the BES, to avoid contagion. And it wasn't through contagion that the problem happened. It was through other operations that, in time, they will be clarified. It seems that only on the day of the presentation of results the BdP realized the situation in which the BES accounts were. No, a week earlier the auditor started alerting us to strange situations that affected the soundness of the bank. At the moment it is in secret of justice, but it was only human hand that caused the BES, from one moment to the next and surprising everyone (including bank staff), to present a loss of a dimension that we could never anticipate. So two, three weeks earlier, it didn't occur to you that that could happen? Clear. Moreover, in July there was a communication from the BES board of directors to the CMVM where they referred to what was the capital radio and the cushion they had to deal with risks in the non-financial area. Nothing would suppose such a situation, as is the result of all the testimonies [of the time]. There are sufficient reasons to think that the bank had a decapitalisation process that only turned out at the end of the second quarter. Today, can we be assured that a BES case will not happen again? We can be assured today that there are much more powerful follow-up mechanisms than there were at that time. We are assured that today there is great attention to the effects of euphoria in the expansion phases, in order to limit credit bubbles and real estate bubbles. We can be assured that there are instruments of intervention if the issue is found in time. No one can think that he anticipates the act before it is produced - that is, it is only known that a credit was badly granted after it was granted. And that's why banks have the capital to absorb losses, which is why banks are asked to have it because the supervisor's ultimate goal is to ensure two things: financial stability and deposit security. Evaluated our action by these two criteria, we can say that, despite the great problem we had, there was never capital flight, there are no depositors who have lost their deposits, nor was there interruption of financing of the economy. And if we want to understand what this means, it is to look at what happened in Cyprus, Ireland, Greece, Belgium. In all of them or depositors suffered, or taxpayers suffered much more than in Portugal. Montepio is a case with similarities with BES, with regard to the news that is coming out in the newspapers about who leads, not the bank, but the shareholder. How's Montepio? Caixa Economica is stabilized, is in a process of reformulation of the government model, has a professionalized administration, is taking serious steps towards becoming a financial pillar of the third sector. What about the stockholder? It is an entity that is not supervised by the BdP. And don't you worry that the sole shareholder of a bank is not supervised in practice by anyone? It is supervised by a public entity [Ministry of Labor, Solidarity and Social Security]. And I believe that the entity that oversees you is aware of the need to be diligent and attentive to the institution and certainly will be. Do you not worry that there are products from the mutual association, insurance, that are sold at the counters of Caixa Economica Montepio Geral? The products are not supervised by us. In any case, in order to separate the entities, we require the separation of marks. And don't you worry that there is excessive shareholder exposure to Caixa Economica? If the shareholder has a problem, how does the Cash Box look? That's not the point. What worries me is not that the shareholder has problems, it is to ensure that the bank is not exposed to the shareholder. That's the root of the contagion. If a shareholder has difficulties, he sells shares and his stake without affecting the bank. It only affects if it also benefits from credit. Credit between related entities cannot be accepted. Are you comfortable with the model in which the shareholder cannot be supervised by the BdP? Should it be rethought from a legislative point of view? I believe that the authorities are aware of the need to strengthen the quality of the relationship between the shareholder and Caixa Economica. We're interested in that ourselves. It's a conversation that's been around for a long time: everybody's very attentive, but... It is great that everyone is very attentive, because we are in a preliminary state which is the transition to the next stage, which is to take measures to ensure greater stability. And I think the steps go in this direction: clarification of the model of government, separation of entities and separation of the role of shareholder from the management of the financial institution. As for supervisory rules, has the Government spoken to the BdP about the changes it wants to make? And by the way, do you accept that the resolution power will come out of the BdP? The resolution has two dimensions: that of monitoring the banks, which is whether banks have plans to attack limit situations that can stay in the BdP or not. And the resolution situation itself, which implies the presence at the table of the political entity, because the options taken are not politically indifferent. Making a mandatory recapitalization, making a resolution with asset sales, making a resolution with a transition bank, or liquidating a bank has social and system policy implications. Moreover, some of these options can only be taken by those who have access to public money - either with a transitional loan or with direct financing. And the BdP cannot make any kind of financing of this nature, nor take part in capital. It makes no sense that an act of great importance and urgency should not be done with the presence and under the command of the entity that has the power, legitimacy and resources to decide it. In my opinion, this power must naturally be outside the BdP. Another issue is the architecture of the system: there are three supervisors, there is a board of financial supervisors and, above that, there is the financial stability board, which is chaired by the Finance Minister, which is a response to my concern to have a political agent at the critical time of a decision. We have to look at this architecture and ask if it has always worked efficiently. Your answer is? There are reasons for improvement, I have very clear ideas about strengthening the articulation between supervisors - and one is to create a permanent secretariat to share information. These 2016 budgetary and economic results show that there was an alternative to the politics of the troika times? No, these facts show that it will be possible to exit the excessive deficit procedure (EDP), which is very important, show that the tourism and tradable goods sector remains fundamental to the development of the Portuguese economy. Translating your answer: hasn't you changed a thing? As regards the alternative economic model? No, nothing like that. What I'm saying is that we're dependent on the tradable goods sector, like tourism. An economy is like a four-engine plane. Two are connected. One is the sector of tradable goods and exports, the other is private consumption, the other is public consumption and the other is investment. What I'm saying is that the tradable engine had the ability to handle the flight during the most difficult period and is revealing the same ability to continue to handle the flight, even with the other engines [in the economy] starting to work. The key is that the tradable engine does not slow down just because others get up and running. Is it predictable that the BdP will review its forecasts? It's too early to tell. Dr. Teodora Cardoso said last week that there was no sustainability in the way the deficit was obtained... The BdP has a treaty of Tordesilhas with the Council of Public Finance (CFP) - and was promoter of the same in 2010. I have great appreciation for the CFP, for its independence and I will never make a statement that is the responsibility... The BdP in its reports also analyses public finances. But what we are saying is that it is very important that we leave the EDP, it is very important to ensure a path of sustainability of public debt. And to do so, it is very important that policies are consistent with sustainability. And they're being? ... the composition of policies are not with the BdP. Looking at the public statements made by the political actors, who welcomed the results of the budget implementation, I believe that today we have a favourable context to defend the sustainability of public accounts. And based on the numbers? Execution is consistent with the Output of the PDE. And the next Budget must ensure the continuity of that consistency. The Bank of England acknowledged that it had made poor assessments of the impacts of the crisis (and the measures implemented in those years), the Bank of Spain also. Does Banco de Portugal make or make any assessment of its role and the estimates it has made during this period? Banco de Portugal has the humility and capacity for self-analysis to be able to recognize when the premises of its reasoning were under or overvalued and review its projections. Whenever we publish projections, we are in practice recognizing that we either make mistakes by excess or by default. The second aspect is to recognize that civic culture in Portugal is not exactly the civic culture of the United Kingdom. And therefore, having institutions capable of making a self-assessment is desirable, the BdP will always be in favor of this, but people must also know how to frame this exercise in a civic exercise that is not merely... public denunciation. The BdP will therefore not do this kind of analysis, as does the Bank of England or the Bank of Spain? Note: when I am talking to you, I am responding to a judgment without evaluation because the evaluation is already being made in public, without having been given the opportunity for us to present our argument and evaluation. But we imagine that their counterparts in England and Spain also give interviews... The circumstances of the Bank of Spain are completely different from ours. There has been much news about the appointments to the management of Banco de Portugal, with names that will have been rejected by the Government. Is it true you went back with your list of proposed names? I don't comment on dialogues that have to be fought at closed doors. And on that principle is: the governor presents a proposal and the government approves the names. It is natural that there is intense dialogue. As in any dialogue there is... points of view. And when will this dialogue come to an end? When the two parties converge. Is it natural, given the independence status of Banco de Portugal, that the Government systematically rejects a name that is proposed by the governor? I don't comment on that. Did you think it was right to appoint Francisco Louca to banco de Portugal's advisory board? The Advisory Board is by nature a reflection of civil society and economic means. It has a role that is to transmit in person what we sometimes read or hear. And we have a great opportunity to share, at closed doors, what we cannot share in the public square. Did it seem natural to you? I have no difficulty living with diversity. Would it do you think it would be right for the governor of Banco de Portugal to be appointed by the President of the Republic for the sake of his independence? In due course, in 2012, I submitted a proposal to the Finance Minister which was then not followed up (which had to do with having constitutional implications). If you get that proposal back, you'll understand what the governor's thinking was. Don't you want to explain to us what that proposal was? From what you tell me, if there is a constitutional limitation, it was for the appointment to be made by the President of the Republic. I defend, it is written in the Ministry of Finance and in the archives of banco de Portugal - a single term of eight years instead of two terms. Exactly in the name of independence. And I argue that the governor should be appointed by the President by the government's nominee. And that the chairman of the audit board should be appointed by the Assembly of the Republic, by the government's nominee - which means that I do not exclude, in any way, the government of the process. I would like to see a double legitimacy in order to strengthen independence. To the governor and the audit board. The PS has already ruled towards an appointment by the President, the PSD and CDS as well. Why do you think you've never advanced? I have no idea. In 2012 I made a proposal. At the moment, if we want to resume it, it will have to be reviewed on the basis of subsequent facts, namely the banking union which at the time was nowhere near or far on our horizon. Today we exercise a shared power.

O documento em causa faz parte de uma srie de reflexes internas que se iniciaram por minha iniciativa em Fevereiro de 2013 a propsito de notcias publicadas na imprensa que visavam determinar se havia fundamentao para aquilo que era publicado e qual a gravidade. Entre Fevereiro de 2013 e Novembro muita coisa se passou e entre Novembro e Abril de 2014 quando o dr. Ricardo Salgado aceitou que no continuaria  frente do banco tambm muita coisa se passou. E, em segundo lugar, que havia razes suficientes que, ficaram consagradas em Abril de 2014, para exigir ao dr. Ricardo Salgado um plano de sucesso e exigir  famlia que se afastasse da gesto do BES. Ricardo Salgado, tanto sobre o pagamento do Sr. Jos Conceio Guilherme no ano de 2011 no montante de 8,5 milhes, como sobre a relao mantida com a Akoya. Esta carta foi respondida pelo dr. Ricardo Salgado no dia 21 de Novembro de 2013 e a partir da iniciou-se um processo de correspondncia, com sucessiva acumulao de informao que nos leva a que em 16/17 de Abril de 2014 o dr. Ricardo Salgado remetesse ao Banco de Portugal as cartas de renncia aos cargos cujos registos se encontravam pendentes junto do Banco. H dois acrdos, o primeiro, do Supremo Tribunal Administrativo em 2005 e o segundo do Tribunal Central Administrativo do Sul, em 2012, e depois um terceiro do Tribunal Central Administrativo do Norte, j depois da Resoluo, em 23 de Setembro de 2015, que diziam claramente que a retirada da idoneidade dependia da existncia de prvias condenaes judiciais. E era necessrio que tivessem transitado em julgado. O Banco de Portugal no tinha forma de retirar a idoneidade a um banqueiro caso ele no tivesse sido condenado e a condenao no tivesse transitado em julgado? At 24 de Outubro de Outubro de 2015 era assim. Em qualquer caso, mesmo nessa hiptese, podem sempre recorrer da deciso do Banco de Portugal. E por isso  muito importante a carta que o dr. Ricardo Salgado escreveu ao Banco de Portugal na poca, a abdicar, no fundo, da possibilidade de pedir um novo registo. Por presso do Banco de Portugal... Podamos fazer presso e fizemos at ao ponto de as pessoas aceitarem apresentar um plano de sucesso e aceitarem que no fariam parte dos rgos da administrao e mais, aceitar que toda a famlia se afastaria da gesto do banco. Mas tambm em nome da independncia e em nome da defesa da misso da instituio tm de cumprir o seu mandato e prosseguir aquilo que  a misso confiada  instituio.  um pouco mais do que uma crtica. H quem diga abertamente que o governador no tem condies para continuar a exercer o seu mandato. S no teria condies para exercer o meu mandato se no fosse capaz de garantir a independncia do Banco de Portugal e de garantir o cumprimento da misso que lhe est confiada. No h independncia de uma instituio sem compromisso forte com o cumprimento dos mandatos. Esteve h dias com o Presidente da Repblica, foi o Presidente que lhe sugeriu que fosse ao Parlamento para explicar esta polmica mais recente. Relativamente s decises que tomo, tomo essas decises com autonomia prpria de quem entende que em determinado momento  oportuno explicar, sobretudo se essas explicaes so pertinentes para eliminar mal-entendidos. Teme que depois de resolvido o Novo Banco, o Governo o despea? Em primeiro lugar, o Banco de Portugal  uma entidade independente. Em segundo lugar, tem regras, incluindo as relativas ao mandato do seu governador. E, em terceiro lugar, as relaes que tenho com o Governo do ponto de vista institucional no me permitem, de forma nenhuma, imaginar uma situao dessas. De qualquer modo, a questo  saber se quero ou no cumprir o meu mandato e se quero, ou no, ser o guardio da independncia do Banco de Portugal. E quer cumprir o seu mandato at ao fim? Fernando Ulrich entregou-lhe em 2013 um documento, alertando-o para a dvida gigantesca do GES. O que fez ao documento? O documento foi entregue em Agosto de 2013. No o preocupa que haja produtos da associao mutualista, seguros, que so vendidos aos balces da Caixa Econmica Montepio Geral? Os produtos no so supervisionados por ns. Em qualquer caso, no sentido de separar as entidades, ns requeremos a separao de marcas. E no o preocupa que haja uma exposio excessiva do acionista  Caixa Econmica? Se o acionista tiver um problema, como  que fica a Caixa Econmica? A questo no  essa. O que me preocupa no  que o acionista tenha problemas,  assegurar que o banco no est exposto ao acionista. O PS j se pronunciou no sentido de uma nomeao pelo Presidente, o PSD e CDS tambm. Porque  que acha que nunca avanou? No fao ideia. Em 2012 eu fiz uma proposta. Neste momento, se a quisermos retomar, ter de ser revista em funo de factos posteriores, nomeadamente pela unio bancria que, na altura, no estava nem de perto, nem de longe, no nosso horizonte. Title: Opening speech of Administrator Hlder Rosalino at the "New Money" Conference
text: Opening speech of Administrator Helder Rosalino at the "New Money" Conference 03 Apr 2017 Good morning Welcome to Banco de Portugal and the Money Museum. I begin by greeting the Secretary of State for Industry, Dr. Joao Vasconcelos. It is a pleasure to welcome you here at Banco de Portugal. It is also with satisfaction that Banco de Portugal welcomes and joins the holding of the "New Money" Conference organized by the Online Eco Newspaper. I congratulate the Journal and its Director, Antonio Costa, for organizing this important initiative, and for bringing together, on this occasion, such a wide and relevant set of experts to talk about digital financial services and FinTechs. I thank, of course, also for the invitation i was addressed to participate in the opening of this conference, on behalf of Banco de Portugal. Banco de Portugal has been paying increasing attention to the theme of Digital Banking and especially to the evolution of FinTech, seeking to support and stimulate, at national level, the debate around the great challenges that digital innovation poses to the financial system and its regulation and supervision. To this end, Banco de Portugal organized, last October, an important international conference dedicated to the theme of Digital Banking and FinTechs, which allowed us to discuss the challenges and threats posed to the banking system in these areas. At the same time, Banco de Portugal has set up an internal, multidisciplinary think tank with the aim of studying the evolution of Digital Banking and FinTech and to look at, in the 2020 horizon, the challenges presented to it in the broader context of its mission. Banco de Portugal is, at the technical level, monitoring the digital innovation applied to the financial system in various dimensions: from the outset in the field of regulation and supervision, but also in the dimension of financial stability, payment systems and means, cybersecurity, and even reserve management and the conduct of monetary policy. It is a central and transversal theme in the Strategic Plan of Banco de Portugal for the next 4 years. In recent times, we have seen very significant changes in the financial services sector, induced by constant changes in the field of information technologies. However, the changes that are expected to happen by 2020 will be unprecedented. We have observed (and will continue to see) a progressive digitisation of financial services, the result of increasing technological development, the pressure to reduce costs, the change of behaviour by users of financial services and, not least, the entry of new entrants into this market, with emphasis on FinTech. FinTech is recognized that FinTech currently plays an active role in increasing the digital experience and financial innovation, outline ing many of the technological solutions that support the functioning of the digital financial market. FinTech is growing and has come to change the financial ecosystem. They have entered the markets and are competing and also cooperating with banks, at least in some parts of the value chain. Traditional financial institutions (incumbents) are currently challenged to build their offer of financial services and products with a perspective of constant improvement, adequacy and focus on the experience and expectations of consumers, which are increasingly sophisticated and based on positive digital experiences. It is indisputable that FinTech is already taking an important role in these transformations, causing some of them. The evolution in retail banking, following the introduction of new (and different) actors, offering new (and distinct) financial products and services, has been characteristic, by some authors, as the "uberization of financial services". The effects of Digital Banking are already significantly altering the relationship between banks and their customers, with the evolution of the offer of technology-based products and services. This phenomenon will be reinforced over the coming years, considering that the new generations are increasingly apprehendable by the use of new technologies and the provision of services tailored to their real needs. Therefore, it is not surprising that there is a decrease in the physical presence of banks, both in number of branches and employees. All the countries of the European Union have seen a reduction of around 40,000 branches in the last five years. In the case of employees this reduction was 250,000. However, this reduction process is far from over, as they have been heralded by the majority of new banks and significant adjustments in the coming years, largely as a result of ongoing digital developments. As far as FinTech is about the level of transformation it will generate and the degree of uncertainty about its impacts is still very high. For its promoters, this wave of innovation and digital transformation promises a technological revolution that will democratize financial services, with the following immediate benefits: 1. Consumers will have more options, services more targeted at their more attractive needs and prices. 2. Small and medium-sized enterprises will have access to new credit facilities and better market conditions. 3. Banks will become more productive, with lower transaction costs, higher capital efficiency and increased operational resilience. 4. The financial system itself will become more resilient, with greater diversity, redundancy and depth. 5. And, above all, financial services will be more inclusive, with better people connected, more informed and increasingly empowered. One of the areas where there is great growth potential for FinTechs lies at the level of payment services. There is already a great deal of appetite on the part of consumers for the use of digital payment services and the entry into force of the new European Payments Directive (PSD2), planned for 2018, should be another major stimulus, with regard to the emergence of new players in this area. The Directive extends the possibility of offering payment and bank account aggregation services to non-financial operators, making what was once exclusive to banks within the reach of FinTechs and even retail or telecommunications companies. There will be many opportunities, but there are also increasing risks and uncertainties that must be taken into account. Despite its growth and the financial resources it already uses, it is true that, in continental Europe, FinTechs still account for a small portion of the banking, payment services and asset management markets. We are still at an early stage of the process, with high uncertainty about the scope and sustainability of ongoing transformations. Many of the new technology-based financial services offerings have been developed outside the banking system by startups, covering areas as diverse as payment systems, lending, management and financial mobility, among others. However, it is not certain that most startups that are boosting these innovations will survive, as it is not yet clear which business areas will thrive in the FinTechs universe. Nor is the level of response that the banking system will give to this phenomenon yet. What strategies should they adopt? Competition; Cooperation; or even co-petition. The trend is still unclear. In this context, it is still particularly difficult to anticipate the evolution of the banking system as a result of technological innovation associated with the provision of new financial services based on FinTechs. The consequences of these developments, which can be quite disruptive on banks' business models, also pose major challenges for supervisors, both in the prudential area and in the behavioural area. Banks' new architecture and new business models will require a multidisciplinary response from central banks, posing challenges to several of their core functions, such as monetary policy implementation, reserve asset management, banking supervision and financial stability assurance. As one ECB official recently said: "Whatever direction we are heading, there is one fact that supervisors should take for granted: we are facing a growing risk and not yet clearly identified, now that FinTechs have come to stay and who often operate outside the regulated banking sector" There are, in fact, new times for the banking system, but also for regulators, which require new approaches, new resources and new competences. In recent years, European legislators have sought to create a regulatory framework for financial services that promotes greater competition, transparency, security and innovation. However, the challenge is to know the extent to which existing regulation, which is not yet harmonised, and the regulators' current practices are appropriate and in what respects they should be changed in view of the new emerging realities, which are largely still unknown. In the absence of a harmonised regulatory model, some jurisdictions are putting in place national legislation to frame some FinTechs activities, leading to different regulatory and supervisory models between the various countries. This creates cross-border distortions that operators tend to take advantage of through regulatory arbitrage. Monitoring and responding to this problem imposes a coordinated approach at national and European level between regulators, the financial system and FinTech themselves. Several countries are working to this end and there are good examples of ongoing initiatives bringing regulators closer to operators by creating innovation hubs and information and knowledge sharing processes. It is with this position of collaboration and sharing that Banco de Portugal is positioned, manifested as an openness to work with all stakeholders in the analysis and development of solutions in this area. In this regard, I hope that this conference will become a valuable contribution to helping build a shared vision of the challenges and benefits that digital transformation and FinTech can bring to the functioning of the entire financial system and its regulation. Thank you very much for what,
text_original: Interveno de abertura do Administrador Hlder Rosalino na Conferncia "New Money" 03 abr. 2017 Bom dia Bem-vindos ao Banco de Portugal e ao Museu do Dinheiro. O Banco de Portugal tem vindo a dedicar uma crescente ateno ao tema da Banca Digital e em especial  evoluo das FinTech, procurando apoiar e dinamizar, ao nvel nacional, o debate em torno dos grandes desafios que a inovao digital coloca ao sistema financeiro e  sua regulao e superviso. Este fenmeno ser reforado ao longo dos prximos anos, considerando que as novas geraes tm cada vez maior apetncia pela utilizao de novas tecnologias e pela oferta de servios customizados s suas reais necessidades. Por isso, no  surpreendente que esteja a ocorrer uma diminuio da presena fsica dos bancos, tanto em nmero de balces, como de colaboradores. No conjunto dos pases da Unio Europeia observou-se uma reduo de cerca de 40 mil agncias nos ltimos cinco anos. No caso de colaboradores essa reduo foi de 250 mil. No entanto, este processo de reduo est longe de estar terminado, na medida em que tm sido anunciados pela generalidade dos bancos novos e expressivos ajustamentos nos prximos anos, em grande parte como resultado da evoluo digital em curso. No que se refere s FinTech o nvel de transformao que ir gerar e o grau de incerteza sobre os seus impactos  ainda muito elevado. Para os seus promotores, esta onda de inovao e transformao digital promete uma revoluo tecnolgica que ir democratizar os servios financeiros, com os seguintes benefcios imediatos: 1. Os consumidores tero mais opes, servios mais direcionados s suas necessidades e preos mais atrativos. 2. As pequenas e mdias empresas tero acesso a novas facilidades de crditos e a melhores condies de mercado. 3. As oportunidades sero muitas, mas h tambm riscos e incertezas crescentes que devem ser tidas em considerao. Apesar do seu crescimento e dos recursos financeiros que j utiliza, a verdade que, na Europa continental, as FinTechs ainda representam uma pequena parcela dos mercados de servios bancrios, dos servios de pagamento e da gesto de ativos. Estamos ainda numa fase inicial do processo, com uma elevada incerteza relativamente ao alcance e  sustentabilidade das transformaes em curso. Muitas das novas ofertas de servios financeiros de base tecnolgica foram desenvolvidas fora do sistema bancrio por startups, cobrindo reas to diversificadas como os sistemas de pagamento, a concesso de crdito, a gesto e a mobilidade financeira, entre outras. Porm, no  certo que a maior parte das startups que esto dinamizar estas inovaes venha a sobreviver, como no  ainda claro quais sero s reas de negcio que iro prosperar no universo das FinTechs. Tambm no  ainda certo o nvel de resposta que o sistema bancrio ir dar a este fenmeno. Que estratgias devero adotar? De competio; De cooperao; ou mesmo de coopetio. A tendncia ainda no  clara. Neste quadro,  ainda particularmente difcil antecipar a evoluo do sistema bancrio em resultado da inovao tecnolgica associada a proviso de novos servios financeiros baseados nas FinTechs. As consequncias destas evolues, que podem ser bastante disruptivas sobre os modelos de negcios dos bancos, colocam igualmente grandes desafios s autoridades de superviso, tanto na rea prudencial, como na rea comportamental. A nova arquitetura e os novos modelos de negcios dos Bancos obrigaro a uma resposta multidisciplinar dos bancos centrais, colocando desafios a vrias das suas funes core, tais como a implementao da poltica monetria, a gesto de ativos de reserva, a superviso bancria e a garantia da estabilidade financeira. Como dizia recentemente uma responsvel do BCE: Seja qual for a direo em que nos dirigimos, h um facto que os supervisores devem ter como certo: estamos perante um risco crescente e ainda no claramente identificado, agora que as FinTechs vieram para ficar e que operam frequentemente fora do sector bancrio regulamentado Vivem-se, de facto, tempos novos para o sistema bancrio, mas tambm para os reguladores, que exigem novas abordagens, novos recursos e novas competncias. Nos ltimos anos, os legisladores europeus tm procurado criar um enquadramento regulamentar para os servios financeiros que seja promotor de maior concorrncia, transparncia, segurana e inovao. Contudo, o desafio  saber at que ponto a regulao existente, que no est ainda harmonizada, e as prticas atuais dos reguladores so adequadas e em que aspetos devero ser alteradas, face s novas realidades emergentes, em boa parte ainda desconhecidas. Na ausncia de um modelo regulatrio harmonizado, algumas jurisdies esto a colocar em prtica legislao nacional para enquadrar algumas atividades das FinTechs, originando modelos de regulao e superviso distintos entre os vrios pases. Esta situao cria distores ao nvel transfronteirio que os operadores tendem a aproveitar, atravs de arbitragem regulatria. O acompanhamento e a resposta a este problema impem a necessidade de ser assegurada uma abordagem coordenada ao nvel nacional e ao nvel europeu entre reguladores, o sistema financeiro e as prprias FinTech. Vrios pases esto a trabalhar nesse sentido e h bons exemplos de iniciativas em curso que aproximam os reguladores dos operadores, atravs da criao de hubs de inovao e de processos de partilha de informao e de conhecimento.  com essa postura de colaborao e partilha que o Banco de Portugal se posiciona, manifestado abertura para trabalhar com todas as partes interessadas na anlise e no desenvolvimento de solues neste domnio. Nesse sentido, espero que esta conferncia se transforme num valioso contributo para ajudar  construo de uma viso partilhada sobre os desafios e os benefcios que a transformao digital e as FinTech podem introduzir no funcionamento de todo o sistema financeiro e na sua regulao.
