Title: Article by Director Elisa Ferreira in the magazine of the Eurofi conference in Malta: "Financial Reform in the EU and Challenges still ahead"
text: Article by Director Elisa Ferreira... Article by Director Elisa Ferreira in the magazine of the Eurofi conference in Malta: "Financial Reform in the EU and Challenges still ahead" 13 Apr. 2017 The financial crisis that unfolded in 2007 and 2008 paved the way for significant reforms of the regulatory framework at EU level with the purpose of making the banking sector more resilient, with the ultimate goal of enhancing financial stability. One of the challenges faced by the EU legislators is how to strike the right balance between an increase in institutions resilience and the possible costs to economic growth resulting from new requirements, in particular when their impact flows through the lending channel. This requires a proper and well-substantiated calibration of the policies to be adopted. In this context, bearing in mind that Basel standards are originally designed to be applied to internationally active banks, it is of utmost importance that in their adoption at EU level the diversity of both the institutions for which policies are intended and the markets where they act is not overlooked, but never at the expense of fragmentation of the EU internal market. In this vein, proportionality appears as a principle of Better Regulation, placing responsibility on legislators to design proper frameworks with simpler rules to be applied to smaller, less complex and non-systemic institutions without compromising the robustness of the prudential regime and without creating different tiers of institutions competing in the single market. This can go beyond simpler reporting and disclosure requirements. This challenging task should not only fall to the EU legislators. The ESAs ought to be ready to leverage their experience and continue to advise on this matter. Additionally, while recognising that supervisors tasks require some degree of flexibility, the experience acquired with CRR/CRD IV has shown that discretion should be clearly framed in order to increase predictability for institutions and other stakeholders. This implies requiring supervisors judgment to follow transparent criteria leading to a consistent application of rules, considering not only the impact of decisions on institutions but also more broadly on the financial stability of a Member State or of the EU as a whole. In its recent proposal amending the CRR/CRD IV, the Commission suggests some important options to address these issues, such as the possibility of using simplified methods for computing certain capital requirements and, as regards Pillar 2, introducing proposals to better frame supervisors practices across the EU. The legislative process should aim at improving those proposals. This is an important step towards making international standards more commensurate to the EUs current diversity without compromising resilience and integration in the internal market. However, a resilient EU banking sector should also rely on other Pillars apart from a robust prudential framework. A fully-fledged banking union is yet to become a reality. The EDIS proposal was put forward by the Commission in 2015 and no agreement has been reached so far. The CRR/CRD IV legislative proposal should give a new impetus to this negotiation and allow it to come to a successful conclusion. Also, there is a clear need to strengthen the current EU safety nets as a last backstop resource. This goal should be achieved by giving more flexibility to existing instruments to be used within a resolution context. In order to provide resolution authorities with the necessary flexibility to ensure the successful implementation of a resolution strategy and the pursuit of the resolution objectives, the financing of resolution action, particularly the conditions for the use of resolution funds, must be revised at EU level. Lastly, a word on the Basel Committees work to finalise its post-crisis reforms, focusing on reducing the excessive variability in risk-weighted assets and on increasing comparability between institutions. It is crucial to ensure that this work is successfully completed and properly implemented in the EU in order to prevent attempts to weaken the achievements made in recent years. Ultimately, the merits of these reforms should be assessed, but a period of regulatory certainty and stability would then be necessary to allow these reforms to be properly implemented.

Title: Article by Director Elisa Ferreira in the magazine of the Eurofi conference in Malta: "Financial stability impact and considerations on MREL"
text: Article by Director Elisa Ferreira... Article by Director Elisa Ferreira in the magazine of the Eurofi conference in Malta: "Financial stability impact and considerations on MREL" 13 Apr. 2017 The Minimum Requirement for Own Funds and Eligible Liabilities (MREL) set out in the BRRD is an essential tool for resolution authorities, as it helps to ensure that banks have sufficient loss absorbency capacity under resolution without affecting liabilities that are key to the continuity of the banks business and without relying on taxpayers money. However, the design and implementation of the MREL framework was not without its faults. The problems were broadly identified by the European Commission in the legislative proposals presented in November 2016, but further work is still needed. Firstly, the BRRD failed to fully take into account the fact that banks would not be able to comply with MREL immediately after its entry into force. This is true for banks in general, but more so in the banking systems that are still recovering from the aftermath of the financial and sovereign debt crisis. Also, the criteria for setting the MREL laid down in the BRRD, and further developed in the Delegated Regulation, may lead to a significant amount of MREL shortfalls. This is especially the case if those criteria are applied mechanically, without taking into account the specific resolution strategy for each bank and national specificities regarding access to markets and debt issuance needs. These potential MREL shortfalls present significant risks, of a systemic nature. It is unlikely that markets will be able to absorb smoothly such large volumes of debt issuance. It could even be argued that the magnitude of the requirements being imposed on banks might cast doubts on the ability of banks to address them, which in turn would undermine the credibility of the whole MREL process. Moreover, it cannot be excluded that, if trapped between large MREL requirements and an inability to access financial markets, and given the current low interest rate environment, there might be a perverse incentive for banks to expand their balance sheets and aggravate their risk profile to offset higher funding costs, with riskier practices that would endanger financial stability. At international level, it also cannot be ignored that the scope of the MREL requirement goes beyond that of the TLAC. Whereas the TLAC applies only to G-SIBs, the MREL requirement applies to all credit institutions in the EU, regardless of their size. Proportionality is thus crucial, in order not to compromise the level playing field. Taking all of this into account along with the experience gathered so far, it is important that a proper transitional period is provided for, covering the compliance timeline, composition of MREL and location of loss absorbency capacity within the resolution group. In this way, banks would have enough flexibility to adapt their activity and funding structure in a manner that could be accommodated and would not promote unintended behaviours. This would allow systemic impacts arising from the MREL to be taken into account. In conclusion, the importance and benefits of MREL are indisputable. But, in its design and implementation we must weigh the possible negative spillovers arising from large MREL shortfalls and consider the overarching principles that presided over the creation of the resolution framework, with the ultimate goal of not endangering financial stability.

Title: Address by Director Elisa Ferreira at the Committee on Economic and Monetary Affairs - European Parliament
text: Address by Director Elisa Ferreira at the Committee on Economic and Monetary Affairs -European Parliament 25 Apr. 2017 Public Hearing on the new Banking Legislation Package I am very pleased to be back here at the ECON Committee to share with you some insights and personal views on my experience as a member of the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal responsible for prudential banking supervision, and as a Supervisory Board Member of the SSM (Single Supervisory Mechanism), for almost a year now. The setting up of the new institutional framework (Banking Union) within such a short period of time is a commendable success. The ECON Committee Members, Daniele Nouy, Andrea Enria, Elke Konig and Dominique Laboreix are, among others, to be congratulated for their valuable contributions for such success. Notwithstanding the immense achievements of the Banking Union, the on-going review of the legal acts represents a pivotal opportunity to reinforce some of its core elements. In fact, with the benefit of hindsight it is now clear that there are several missing links and stabilizing elements in this project -as many of us, in this Committee, have feared from the beginning  which one might compare to a car running with a flat tire, which leads to an unbalanced functioning, prone to accidents. Banking Union was anchored on a steady state assumption of an overall macroeconomic recovery, which we are far from having achieved collectively. Proof of that is the lengthy debate over how to address important crisis legacy issues for which the adequate tools are no longer available. In the present framework, the harsh conditions for any State intervention imposed by the BRRD (Bank Recovery and Resolution Directive) for Precautionary Recapitalization and by State Aid rules, accompanied by the supervisory and regulatory demands for extra capital and loss absorption instruments, amidst low profitability, low interest rates and high levels of NPLs (Non-Performing Loans) are conducive to significant transfers of wealth and the destruction of economic value, that may seriously jeopardize financial stability. This is all happening at a time when financial stability is still a national concern and responsibility, despite the much more limited ability for the usage of national tools to safeguard it. All of this speaks in favor of carefully but urgently fine-tuning the current legal framework and completing Banking Union or, at a minimum, ensuring a flexible application of the existing rules. The European Parliament and the ECON Committee, which were so engaged in the introduction of a review clause on the BRRD, have now the opportunity and responsibility to act decisively to preserve the purpose of the Banking Union project and to ensure financial stability, which are otherwise at risk. Missing elements encompass, firstly, and as was known from the beginning, a common safety net for depositors protection (EDIS) and a backstop for the Single Resolution Fund. Indeed, we need to work decisively both on risk sharing and risk reduction measures and not only on the later -in order to create a truly functioning Banking Union and to guarantee a decision process rightly balanced. The resolution framework may well function in a steady state when loss absorption capacity has been built up. However, the present legacy issues with a systemic nature call for the fine-tuning of important elements such as: (i) the conditions for the use of the precautionary recapitalization (article 32(4) of the BRRD), (ii) the conditions for the use of the Single Resolution Fund (articles 44(5) and 101(2) of the BRRD), and (iii) the MREL (Minimum Requirement for own funds and Eligible Liabilities) setting. The fact that the use of the Single Resolution Fund is conditional on a bail-in of 8% of total liabilities and own funds, and the amount to be drawn is limited to 5% of total liabilities and own funds, make its use virtually impossible. As a consequence, financial stability is endangered, particularly in the case of banks with insufficient loss absorption capacity -for example due to non-compliance with the MREL requirements in the current build up phase -or with liabilities based mainly on deposits, whose participation in loss absorption would dramatically endanger the continuity of critical functions in the bank but also adversely impact the whole financial system. Likewise, the design and implementation framework of MREL -which is an essential tool for the resolution authorities -are not without faults. BRRD failed to fully take into account the fact that banks would not be able to comply with MREL targets immediately after its entry into force. This is true for banks in general, but all the more so for traditional banking business models relying mostly on deposits  these banks will only be able to issue MREL-eligible instruments at a high cost amid severe market access constraints. I fully share the view that institutions losses must be borne by its shareholders and creditors, and not by public funds. However, in a context where we are still in a building up phase of loss absorption instruments eligible for MREL, it is important that a proper transitional period for the implementation of MREL targets is provided. Moreover, at the international level, it cannot be ignored that the scope of the MREL requirement goes beyond that of the TLAC (Total Loss Absorbing Capacity). Whereas TLAC applies only to G-SIBs (Global Sistemically Important Banks), MREL requirement applies to all credit institutions in the EU, regardless of their size. Proportionality and flexibility are thus crucial, in order not to compromise the level playing field. Additionally to the revision of the BRRD and CRD (Capital Requirements Directive), there are other stabilization elements, not necessarily foreseen in the initial project  which the ECON Committee, given its relevance for financial stability, must address. The most urgent one is, probably, the Non-Performing Loans (NPLs) situation in the Euro area, which remains a key priority. In this regard, I praise Andreas public call for an EU solution and also the work conduct by the SSM in this regard. It is crucial that this issue is tackled in a coordinated way, avoiding a fire-sale environment and negative spill-over effects. Other elements are also noteworthy, namely the need for a fast-tracking procedure with regard to the establishment of a transitional provision on the impacts arising from the application of IFRS9 (which will become mandatory in the EU as from 1 January 2018). I feel confident that the European institutions, and the European Parliament and the ECON members in particular, will contribute actively to ensure a safer and more resilient banking sector, completing and fine tuning Banking Union so that it delivers the expected results: protecting depositors and taxpayers, safeguarding financial stability and guaranteeing the conditions for appropriate lending to the real economy.

Title: Interveno do Vice-Governador Pedro Duarte Neves na Conferncia Meet the Market  The uses of LEI
text: Intervention by Deputy Governor Pedr... Intervencao do Vice-Governador Pedro Duarte Neves na Conferencia Meet the Market  The uses of LEI 21 Jun 2017 I would like to begin by welcoming all those who wished to participate in this joint initiative of Banco de Portugal and the Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation for clarification on the initiatives of the Legal Entity Identifier. I would like to take this opportunity to affirm the full commitment of the Portuguese authorities to support the adoption of the LEI. Banco de Portugal, the Securities Market Commission (CMVM), the Insurance and Pension Funds Supervisory Authority (ASF) and the National Council of Financial Supervisors have supported this initiative from the first hour. And they have done so in close partnership with the Institute of Records and Notary (IRN) that accepted the demanding responsibility to make this project operational in Portugal as a Local Operating Unit (LOU). The Legal Entity Identifier, commonly referred to as the LEI, resulted from an initiative of the heads of state and government of the G-20 countries who, as part of a broad set of measures to react to the financial crisis, advocated the establishment of a global identifier of legal entities that would allow the unique and unambiguous identification of the parties involved in financial transactions. Thus, on 5 November 2012, following the recommendations of the Finantial Stability Board, the Charter of the Regulatory Oversight Committee was approved, establishing the so-called Global LEI System, led by the LEI ROC. This body, established in January 2013, was initially made up of representatives of the national central banks and financial market regulators of the most developed countries worldwide and was then progressively open to new countries. The Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation (GLEIF) was established in June 2014 by the Financial Stability Board, with the mandate to ensure the implementation of the LEI, through the operational coordination of the different national agencies responsible for issuing LEI codes. It was in this context that the creation of a global LEI  i.e. a unique, unequivocal and internationally recognised identifier of entities involved in financial transactions  was promoted, which contributes to the achievement of various objectives from the point of view of financial stability. In addition to promoting better quality of information on financial transactions and therefore contributing to greater market integrity  thereby reducing the possibilities of market abuse and financial fraud  the existence of the LEI allows for better identification and assessment of microprudential, macroprudential risks and the creation of better conditions for the prevention of money laundering activities. This is why important adjustments have taken place in recent years in the European regulatory framework and in the process of collecting and compiling statistics. In this regard, it is important to highlight the pioneering role of European financial regulators in establishing the LEI as a mandatory identifier for supervised entities. In January 2014, the EBA issued a recommendation for the use of the LEI code as a supranational identifier for Credit Institutions and Investment Firms. This recommendation (EBA/REC/2014/01) was adopted by Banco de Portugal and published by Circular Letter in April 2014 (CC/003/2014/DSP), establishing the LEI as a mandatory identifier of all supervised entities covered by the CRR. ESMA and EIOPA also had initiatives of equivalent effect in their supervisory activities. The need for better information on financial transactions has, of course, had consequences for the activity of collecting and producing statistics. Indeed, the national and international statistical authorities have recognised the enormous importance of the LEI for the improvement of statistical compilation systems. These systems require the existence of statistical unit files, basic infrastructures of any statistical operation, which allow a unique and unique identification of economic agents. This identification is already available today in several countries for the purpose of identifying resident entities, such as Portugal, but it does not yet exist in a complete and easily accessible way in many countries, and the LEI can help overcome this gap. However, in identifying non-resident entities the difficulties are evident and statistical authorities will only be able to overcome the current difficulties through the existence of a unique identifier on a global scale. In an increasingly globalised world, where cross-border economic and financial transactions are increasingly important and where businesses are established in multiple countries, the LEI is a very useful tool for improving the quality of statistics, particularly in the area of balance of payments. Another example that the LEI can enhance is the definition of the perimeter of economic groups, notably through the second-level information that began this year to be incorporated into the LEI. This second level information goes beyond the mere identification of companies and also covers, for companies inserted in economic groups, the identification of the company that directly holds the applicant for the LEI code, as well as the parent company of each group. Obtaining information at consolidated level is certainly the most relevant development of the LEI, with various uses in terms of financial stability, such as risk aggregation and analysis of interconnections in the financial system. As regards the prudential area, the use of a single supranational code is essential for proper monitoring of the activities of the institutions, in particular as regards the ability to cross-reference information on counterparties. The unambiguous clearance of supranational exposure levels of entities to the financial sector is only truly possible with the existence of unique identification codes. In this sense, guidelines have been issued by both Banco de Portugal and European supervisors to prioritise the LEI as an identifier for the counterparties reported, for example in the context of reporting large exposures in the European context of reporting information for supervisory purposes. Cooperation between national and international authorities in supporting the LEI is therefore a priority that has also had the full support of Banco de Portugal Finally, the LEI codes are an important tool in the fulfilment of the preventive duties of Money Laundering and Prevention of Terrorism, facilitating, for example, the verification of the completeness and correction of the information that should accompany transfers of funds and obligations in respect of restrictive measures or international financial sanctions. The use of the LEI also enhances a risk-based supervisory exercise, enabling the identification  at entity level of a type of financial operator or, at the limit, of a country  exposure to specific economic agents, types of legal entities, or specific jurisdictions. In addition, it is desirable to strengthen the use of LEI codes for the prevention of BCFT as the collection and dissemination of data on the ownership and control structure of the entities holding an LEI code is generalised, in particular for better effective knowledge of the entity of last resort beneficial ultimate owner. However, it is reasonably clear that the potential benefits of the LEI will only materialise if there is widespread use of this global identifier. One of the obvious advantages of the generalisation of the LEI as a global identifier of companies will be the progressive reference of the economic and financial information available on companies, facilitating access to this information and allowing a more rigorous assessment of the risks associated with economic and financial transactions. It should also be said that the use of the LEI has benefits at various levels for financial institutions in terms of, for example, risk management, customer identification, operational efficiency gains in compliance with regulations on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, a better knowledge of their exposures and a simplification in the reporting process to supervisory authorities. At this conference we will have the opportunity to hear the main protagonists of the development of the LEI project on the evolution of the project and the future developments that anticipate, in particular on the importance that the LEI will have in the development of cross-border relations of collective entities. Joe Tracy, current chairman of the group that oversees and oversees and oversees the application of the principles defined for the LEI, will give us an overview of the principles that guide this project and the Global LEI System. We will also have an intervention by Gerard Hartsink, chairman of the GLEIF Board who will present the way in which the mission of the Global LEI System has been carried out. The importance of identifying the players and the operations in the market for their proper functioning will be presented by Jose Miguel Almeida of the Securities And Exchange Commission. We will also have the opportunity to hear from Stephan Wolf on future developments in the LEI, including business-oriented services. Irn has extensive experience in managing registration information for legal persons and managing electronic document certification. From IRN, Claudia Santos will present how this institute is developing the LEI service in Portugal and possible interconnections of the LEI with the services already provided by the IRN. text_original: Interveno do Vice-Governador Pedr... Interveno do Vice-Governador Pedro Duarte Neves na Conferncia Meet the Market  The uses of LEI 21 jun. 2017 Quero comear por dar as boas vindas a todos os que quiseram participar nesta iniciativa conjunta do Banco de Portugal e do Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation para esclarecimento sobre as iniciativas do Legal Entity Identifier. Gostaria de aproveitar esta oportunidade para afirmar o total compromisso das autoridades portuguesas de apoio  adoo do LEI. O Banco de Portugal, a Comisso do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios (CMVM), a Autoridade de Superviso de Seguros e Fundos de Penses (ASF) e o Conselho Nacional de Supervisores Financeiros tm apoiado esta iniciativa desde a primeira hora. E tm-no feito em estreita parceria com o Instituto dos Registos e Notariado (IRN) que aceitou a exigente responsabilidade de tornar operacional este projeto em Portugal na qualidade de Local Operating Unit (LOU). O Legal Entity Identifier, normalmente designado por LEI, resultou de uma iniciativa dos chefes de Estado e de governo dos pases do G-20 que, no mbito de um conjunto alargado de medidas de reao  crise financeira, defenderam o estabelecimento de um identificador global de entidades legais que permitisse a identificao nica e inequvoca das partes envolvidas em transaes financeiras. Assim, em 5 de Novembro de 2012, e seguindo as recomendaes do Finantial Stability Board, foi aprovado o Charter of the Regulatory Oversight Comitee que instituiu o chamado Global LEI System, liderado pelo LEI ROC. Este organismo, estabelecido em Janeiro de 2013, foi inicialmente constitudo por representantes dos Bancos centrais nacionais e de entidades reguladoras dos mercados financeiros dos pases mais desenvolvidos a nvel mundial, sendo depois progressivamente aberto a novos pases. A Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation (GLEIF) foi instituda em Junho de 2014, pelo Financial Stability Board, com o mandato de assegurar a implementao do LEI, atravs da coordenao operacional das diferentes agncias nacionais responsveis pela emisso de cdigos LEI. Foi neste contexto que foi promovida a criao de um LEI global  isto  um identificador nico, inequvoco e reconhecido internacionalmente de entidades envolvidas em transaes financeiras  que contribui para a obteno de vrios objetivos do ponto de vista da estabilidade financeira. Com efeito, para alm de promover uma melhor qualidade da informao sobre transaes financeiras e, por isso, contribuir para uma maior integridade do mercado  reduzindo assim as possibilidades de abuso de mercado e de fraude financeira -a existncia do LEI permite uma melhor identificao e avaliao de riscos microprudenciais, macroprudenciais, bem como a criao de melhores condies para a preveno de atividades de branqueamento de capitais. Por isso tiveram lugar, nos ltimos anos, importantes ajustamentos no enquadramento regulamentar europeu e no processo de recolha e de compilao das estatsticas. A este respeito,  importante salientar o papel pioneiro dos reguladores financeiros europeus no estabelecimento do LEI como identificador obrigatrio das entidades supervisionadas. Em janeiro de 2014, a EBA emitiu uma recomendao tendo em vista a utilizao do cdigo LEI como identificador supranacional para as Instituies de Crdito e Empresas de Investimento. Esta recomendao (EBA/REC/2014/01) foi adotada pelo Banco de Portugal e divulgada por Carta circular em abril de 2014 (CC/003/2014/DSP), estabelecendo o LEI como identificador obrigatrio de todas as entidades supervisionadas abrangidas pela CRR. Tambm a ESMA e a EIOPA tiveram iniciativas de efeito equivalente no mbito das suas atividades de superviso. A necessidade de uma melhor informao sobre transaes financeiras teve, naturalmente, consequncias na atividade da recolha e produo de estatsticas. Com efeito, foi reconhecido pelas autoridades estatsticas nacionais e internacionais a enorme importncia do LEI para a melhoria dos sistemas de compilao estatstica. Estes sistemas requerem a existncia de ficheiros de unidades estatsticas, infraestruturas bsicas de qualquer operao estatstica, que possibilitem uma identificao nica e unvoca dos agentes econmicos. Essa identificao est j hoje disponvel em vrios pases para efeitos da identificao das entidades residentes, como  o caso de Portugal, mas ainda no existe de forma completa e facilmente acessvel em muitos pases, podendo o LEI ajudar a superar essa lacuna. Contudo, na identificao de entidades no residentes as dificuldades so evidentes e as autoridades estatsticas s conseguiro ultrapassar as dificuldades atuais atravs da existncia de um identificador nico  escala mundial. Num mundo cada vez mais globalizado, em que as transaes econmicas e financeiras transfronteiras apresentam um peso cada vez mais importante e em que as empresas se estabelecem em mltiplos pases, o LEI constitui um instrumento muito til para a melhoria da qualidade das estatsticas, nomeadamente na rea da balana de pagamentos. Um outro exemplo que o LEI pode potenciar  a definio do permetro de grupos econmicos, nomeadamente atravs da informao de segundo nvel que comeou este ano a ser incorporada no LEI. Esta informao de segundo nvel ultrapassa a mera identificao das empresas, passando a abranger tambm, para as empresas inseridas em grupos econmicos, a identificao da empresa que diretamente detm a requerente do cdigo LEI, bem como da empresa-me de cada grupo. A obteno de informao ao nvel consolidado trata-se, com toda a certeza, do desenvolvimento mais relevante do LEI, com utilizaes vrias em termos de estabilidade financeira, como por exemplo a agregao de riscos e a anlise de interligaes no sistema financeiro. No que respeita  rea prudencial, a utilizao de um cdigo nico supranacional  fundamental para um acompanhamento adequado das atividades das instituies, nomeadamente no que respeita  capacidade de cruzamento de informao relativa a contrapartes. O apuramento inequvoco de nveis de exposio supranacional de entidades ao setor financeiro apenas se torna verdadeiramente possvel com a existncia de cdigos nicos de identificao. Neste sentido, tm sido emitidas orientaes quer pelo Banco de Portugal quer pelos supervisores europeus no sentido de privilegiar o LEI como identificador das contrapartes reportadas, como por exemplo no mbito do relato de grandes exposies no contexto europeu de reporte de informao para efeitos de superviso. A cooperao entre as autoridades nacionais e internacionais no apoio ao LEI constitui por isso uma prioridade que tem tambm contado com o total apoio do Banco de Portugal Finalmente, os cdigos LEI constituem uma ferramenta importante no cumprimento dos deveres preventivos do Branqueamento de Capitais e Preveno do Terrorismo, facilitando por exemplo a verificao da completude e correo da informao que deve acompanhar as transferncias de fundos e das obrigaes em matria de medidas restritivas ou sanes financeiras internacionais. A utilizao do LEI potencia tambm um exerccio de superviso baseado no risco, permitindo identificar  ao nvel da entidade, de um tipo de operadores financeiros ou, no limite, de um pas  a exposio a agentes econmicos especficos, a tipos de entidades legais, ou a jurisdies especficas. Adicionalmente,  desejvel que se reforce a utilizao dos cdigos LEI para a preveno do BCFT  medida que se for generalizando a recolha e divulgao de dados sobre a estrutura de propriedade e controlo das entidades titulares de um cdigo LEI, nomeadamente para melhor conhecimento efetivo da entidade de ltima instncia ultimate beneficial owner. Contudo,  razoavelmente claro que os potenciais benefcios do LEI s se materializaro se houver uma utilizao generalizada deste identificador global. Uma das vantagens bvias da generalizao do LEI como identificador global de empresas ser a referenciao progressiva da informao econmica e financeira disponvel sobre as empresas, facilitando o acesso a essa informao e permitindo uma avaliao mais rigorosa dos riscos associados s transaes econmicas e financeiras. Refira-se, tambm, que a utilizao do LEI tem benefcios a vrios nveis para as instituies financeiras em termos, por exemplo, da gesto de riscos, identificao de clientes, ganhos de eficincia operacional no cumprimento de regulamentao de preveno de branqueamento de capitais e financiamento do terrorismo, um melhor conhecimento das suas exposies e ainda uma simplificao no processo de reporte s autoridades de superviso. Nesta conferncia teremos a oportunidade de ouvir os principais protagonistas do desenvolvimento do projeto LEI sobre a evoluo do projeto e os desenvolvimentos futuros que antecipam, nomeadamente sobre a importncia que o LEI ter no desenvolvimento das relaes transfronteirias das entidades coletivas. Joe Tracy, atual chairman do grupo que superintende e vela pela aplicao dos princpios definidos para o LEI, dar-nos- uma perspetiva geral sobre os princpios que norteiam este projeto e sobre o Global LEI System. Teremos tambm uma interveno de Gerard Hartsink, chairman do Board do GLEIF que ir apresentar a forma como se tem desenvolvido a misso do Global LEI System. A importncia da identificao dos intervenientes e das operaes no mercado para o seu bom funcionamento ser apresentado por Jos Miguel Almeida, da Comisso de Mercado de Valores Mobilirios. Teremos tambm a oportunidade de ouvir Stephan Wolf sobre os desenvolvimentos futuros do LEI, nomeadamente dos servios direcionadas para as empresas. O IRN tem uma larga experincia na gesto da informao de registo relativa a pessoas coletivas e na gesto de certificao eletrnica de documentos. Do IRN, Cladia Santos ir apresentar a forma como este instituto est a desenvolver o servio LEI em Portugal e eventuais interligaes do LEI com os servios j providenciados pelo IRN. Title: Opinion article by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in the Public: "Conditions to accelerate development: innovation and quality of the management of organizations"
text: Governor Car's opinion piece... Opinion article by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in the Public: "Conditions to accelerate development: innovation and quality of the management of organizations" 04 set. 2017 "Conditions for accelerating economic development: innovation and quality ofmanagement organizations" Today we are witnessing the long-awaited cyclical recovery of the world economy. However, in many countries, the pace of economic growth remains moderate. The dominant concern of policy makers is therefore to understand the factors that maybe at the root of the poor performance of economies and to boost potential product growth in a sustainable and inclusive manner, ensuring social stability and the quality of public debate. This was evident in theematic st and discussions that took place in two important annual economic policy forums, which brought together central bankers, academics and other experts worldwide: the ECB Forum on Central Banking that took place in Sintra at the end of junho and the Jackson Hole Economic Symposium that took place in the State of Wyoming in the USA two weeks ago. The cross-cutting message to these two events was clear: productivity is a central factor in the growth of the potential product of an economy and is therefore a key determinant of the long-term standard of living of societies and the safeguarding of the preferences revealed by societies in terms of social equity; therefore, it is crucial to reverse the downward trend in production observed in major advanced economies. It should be noted that productivity growth was already slowing before the global financial crisis, but it increased in the context of it and is currently at very low levels. Recent economic studies suggest that the large productivity differences between companies and countries are explained by two types of factors: technological innovation and quality of management. As for technological innovation, the available results suggest that innovative economies have four keycharacteristics: 1) High competition -innovation is an effective way for companies to cope with competition; 2) High quality of education and predominance of a culture of merit and entrepreneurship; 3) Flexible labour market; (4) adequacy of financial systems to the financing needs of undertakings, in particular capital markets. To these four characteristics I would add two conditions which I consider important toretain in the economies the ideas generated there: 5) Access to a large market; 6) Society's ability to learn, surpassing itself, with failed initiatives. This means that policies for education and science must be at the top of countries' priorities. Public policies are also needed to support fundamental research, which, because it involves long periods of time, high uncertainty about the nature and the appropriation of its results, does not take place in companies. It should be taken into account, on the other hand, that productivity gains imply a lower incorporation of work. To compensate for this effect, an increase in the production scale of existing companies and new production units is necessary - which means that both quality of management is needed that ensures and enables the increase in the volume and value of production of existing companies, as well as entrepreneurial capacity to launch new companies, new products and enter new markets, redirectingworkers that technological advances sacrifice and giving jobs to new generations entering the labor market. Conditions should therefore be created to promote entrepreneurship, in particular by reducing context costs, ensuring the stability of the regulatory and fiscal framework and promoting financial risk-sharing mechanisms. Also according to recent studies, about 30% of the differences in productivity between countries are explained by differences in qualityand management in terms of efficiency and adjustment to technological and market dynamics. Innovation disqualifies products and reduces markets, but only destroys companies to the extent that they do not anticipate it and have a portfolio of products very exposed to radical innovation in progress, or do not have the capacity to absorb the knowledge and innovation necessary to adapt to new conditions of competition and new markets. Competition in markets, corporate governance practices, human capital and the quality of information are factors that influence the quality of management. This means that it is increasingly necessary to professionalise the management of companies, whose exercise must be legitimized by competence and not by the proprietyof -the quality of management is not an attribute inherent to the ownership of the company's capital. Policies are needed to combat barriers to entry and promote quality, reliability and access to information and, in particular, the dissemination and absorption ofinformation. In Portugal, the low productivity growth observed in recent decades is a limitation to the ability to sustain higher levels of consumption without incurring external imbalances. In order to have control over ourfuture we must be able to increase the margin of manoeuvre of our commercial and financial interdependencies. It is therefore, given the current level of indebtedness, it is essential to continue with the financial consolidation of public servants and deprive themand, at the same time, to create conditions that favour investment and increase productivity. Only this will allow us to gain the necessary leeway to grasp the future, freeing us from the shacklings of the past. The future is in our hands! P.S. -Over almost three decades, the Public has been able to adjust, renew and reinvent to respond to and follow the challenges of an ever-changing economy and society, never losing the ability to offer independent and quality information. The launch of the digital edition, which responds to the preferences of a new generation of readers, is an example of the audience's capacity for innovation. At a time when the media sector is experiencing a structural crisis, it is necessary to stress fromexhaustion that a free and independent imp rensa is fundamental to the creation of a public space of open debate and reasoned reflection, a necessary condition for the sustained development of a country. Congratulations to the Public for the journey taken and for becoming a referencepoint of public debate and reasoned reflection, fundamental pillars of our democracy.

Artigo de opinio do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa no Pblico: "Condies para acelerar o desenvolvimento: inovao e qualidade da gesto das organizaes" 04 set. 2017 Condies para acelerar o desenvolvimento econmico: inovao e qualidade da gesto das organizaes Estamos hoje a assistir  muito aguardada recuperao cclica da economia mundial. Contudo, em muitos pases, o ritmo de crescimento econmico permanece moderado. A preocupao dominante dos decisores de poltica , por isso, compreender os fatores que possam estar na origem do fraco desempenho das economias e impulsionar o crescimento do produto potencial, de forma sustentvel e inclusiva, assegurando a estabilidade social e a qualidade do debate pblico. Isso mesmo foi evidente na temtica e nas discusses ocorridas em dois importantes fruns anuais de poltica econmica recentes, que reuniram banqueiros centrais, acadmicos e outros especialistas a nvel mundial: o ECB Forum on Central Banking que teve lugar em Sintra no final de junho e o Jackson Hole Economic Symposium que teve lugar no Estado do Wyoming nos EUA h duas semanas atrs. A mensagem transversal a estes dois eventos foi clara: a produtividade  um fator central do crescimento do produto potencial de uma economia sendo, por conseguinte, um determinante fundamental do nvel de vida das sociedades no longo prazo e da salvaguarda das preferncias reveladas pelas sociedades em termos de equidade social; por isso,  crucial reverter a tendncia de desacelerao da produtividade observada nas principais economias avanadas. Importa notar que o crescimento da produtividade j estava a diminuir antes da crise financeira global, mas acentuou-se no contexto da mesma, estando atualmente em nveis muito reduzidos. Estudos econmicos recentes sugerem que as grandes diferenas de produtividade entre empresas e pases so explicadas por dois tipos de fatores: inovao tecnolgica e qualidade da gesto. Quanto  inovao tecnolgica, os resultados disponveis sugerem que as economias mais inovadoras apresentam quatro caractersticas fundamentais: 1) Elevada concorrncia -a inovao  uma forma eficaz de as empresas fazerem face  concorrncia; 2) Elevada qualidade da educao e predominncia de uma cultura de mrito e de empreendedorismo; 3) Mercado de trabalho flexvel; 4) Adequao dos sistemas financeiros s necessidades de financiamento das empresas, em particular dos mercados de capitais. A estas quatro caractersticas acrescentaria duas condies que considero importantes para reter nas economias as ideias que a so geradas: 5) O acesso a um mercado de grande dimenso; 6) Capacidade da sociedade para aprender, superando-se, com iniciativas fracassadas. Isto significa que as polticas para a educao e para a cincia devem estar no topo das prioridades dos pases. So tambm necessrias polticas pblicas de apoio  investigao fundamental, que por envolver longos perodos de tempo, elevada incerteza quanto  natureza e quanto  apropriao dos respetivos resultados, no tem lugar nas empresas. H que ter em conta, por outro lado, que os ganhos de produtividade implicam uma menor incorporao de trabalho. Para compensar este efeito  necessrio um aumento da escala de produo das empresas existentes e novas unidades produtivas -o que significa que  necessrio tanto qualidade de gesto que assegure e viabilize o aumento do volume e do valor da produo das empresas j existentes, como capacidade empreendedora para lanar novas empresas, novos produtos e entrar em novos mercados, permitindo redirecionar os trabalhadores que o avano tecnolgico sacrifica e dar emprego s novas geraes que entram no mercado do trabalho. Assim, devem ser criadas condies que favoream o empreendedorismo, designadamente reduzindo os custos de contexto, assegurando a estabilidade do quadro regulatrio e fiscal e promovendo mecanismos financeiros de partilha do risco. Ainda de acordo com estudos recentes, cerca de 30% das diferenas na produtividade entre pases so explicadas por diferenas na qualidade da gesto em termos de eficincia e de ajustamento s dinmicas tecnolgicas e de mercado. Com efeito, a inovao desqualifica produtos e reduz mercados, mas s destri empresas na medida em que estas no a antecipem e tenham uma carteira de produtos muito expostos  inovao radical em curso, ou no tenham capacidade para absorver o conhecimento e a inovao necessrios para se adaptarem s novas condies de concorrncia e a novos mercados. A concorrncia nos mercados, as prticas de governo societrio, o capital humano e a qualidade da informao so fatores que influenciam a qualidade da gesto. Isto significa que  necessrio cada vez mais profissionalizar a gesto das empresas, cujo exerccio deve ser legitimado pela competncia e no pela propriedade -a qualidade da gesto no  um atributo inerente  propriedade do capital da empresa. So necessrias polticas que combatam barreiras  entrada e que promovam a qualidade, fiabilidade e acesso a informao e, em particular, a difuso e absoro do conhecimento. Em Portugal, o reduzido crescimento da produtividade observado nas ltimas dcadas constitui uma limitao  capacidade de sustentar maiores nveis de consumo sem incorrer em desequilbrios externos. Para termos controlo sobre o nosso futuro temos que ser capazes de aumentar a margem de manobra de gesto das nossas interdependncias tanto comerciais como financeiras. , por isso, dado o atual nvel de endividamento, essencial prosseguir com a consolidao financeira dos agentes pblicos e privados e, paralelamente, criar condies que favoream o investimento e o aumento da produtividade. S isso nos permitir ganhar margem de manobra necessria para agarrar o futuro, libertando-nos das amarras do passado. O futuro est nas nossas mos! P.S. -Ao longo de quase trs dcadas, o Pblico foi capaz de se ajustar, renovar e reinventar para responder e acompanhar os desafios de uma economia e sociedade em constante mudana, nunca perdendo a capacidade de oferecer informao independente e de qualidade. O lanamento da edio digital, que responde s preferncias de uma nova gerao de leitores,  um exemplo da capacidade de inovao do Pblico. Numa altura em que o sector dos media vive uma crise estrutural,  necessrio sublinhar  exausto que uma imprensa livre e independente  fundamental para a criao de um espao pblico de debate aberto e de reflexo fundamentada, condio necessria do desenvolvimento sustentado de um pas. Title: Intervention of the Deputy Governor Elisa Ferreira at the inauguration ceremony of the members of the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal
text: In other words... Intervention of the Deputy Governor Elisa Ferreira at the inauguration ceremony of the members of the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal 08 set. 2017 Mr Minister for Finance Mr Deputy Secretary of State for Finance Mr Governor of Banco de Portugal Madam Chair of the Committee on Budget, Finance and Administrative Modernisation (COFMA) And I ask permission to greet, in this evocation, all the other personalities present here. Using the floor on behalf of the four elements that today assume functions (or new functions) as members of the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal is an act of great responsibility but i take with the greatest pleasure, for a fundamental reason: because we believe, all of us, that we will be able to constitute a cohesive, competent and dynamic Administration, at the height of what citizens have the right to expect from a central institution in the life of the country as is banco de Portugal. We share the four, several common feelings: First of all, the weight of responsibility, combined with a recognition of sincere for the trust in us placed by the Governor of the Bank of Portugal, from whom the initial proposal broke; then by the Budget Committee, Finance and Administrative Modernization of the Assembly of the Republic which carried out the corresponding hearings on 27 June and ruled in favour on 19 June 2010. July; and, finally, by the governmental designation achieved by resolving the Council of Ministers approved on August 24 and published today. Then, the conviction that, with experiences and experiences so rich and so different from each of its elements, this Board of Directors shall have the composition to find balanced, informed and capable summaries in the positions you will have to take. Allow me personally to stress the right gender parity - if not (yet) in the Council, at least among the new sworn in  parity that is often so scarce in top-level roles, particularly in the financial sector. In addition, the guarantee of a smooth transition conferred by the already long experience of the bank, including all the lessons arising from the crossing of such difficult times followed the 2007/08 crisis by the Governor and dr. Helder Rosalino, in addition to the experience of more than one year on the part of administrators now entrusted with greater responsibilities (Dr. Luis Maximo dos Saints and myself), aspects now enriched with the presence of two new members, Professor Ana Paula Serra and Dr. Luis Laginha de Sousa, both holders of robust academic and professional experience. A word also of recognition to the members who have ceased the duties we will assume, professor Pedro Duarte Neves and, until a few months ago, Dr. Jose Ramalho, of whom we expect continue to receive the benefit of your experienced advice. Finally, and perhaps this is the main link that unites us, I will refer to the enormous everyone's willingness to put our best attributes and efforts at the service of the Country. In this sense, we will continue the objectives adopted by the Board of Directors for banco de Portugal's Strategic Plan in the period 2017-2020, under the motto "always do better": an ambitious, demanding Bank, facing the future, aware of its past but not prisoner of it. We will develop the four main strategic guidelines defined: Affirm internally and externally the Bank's capabilities as a monetary currency; Participate in the definition of regulatory frameworks and in the application of supervisory system in order to ensure the robustness and stability of the financial system national and the confidence of economic operators; Promoting knowledge about the Portuguese economy and European integration, contributing to an enlightened and well-informed society; To be one of the most efficient banks in the Eurosystem. But the conviction with which we set out for the new phase of work that we are faced with will certainly not diminish our awareness or remove due clarity as to the difficulties that we will continue to have to overcome. In fact, and unlike some speeches in our view, the role of a national central bank in a country that integrates not only a monetary union but also a banking union does not become simpler or less relevant in view of the traditional model of purely national central banks. The defence of the national interest in a highly volatile external context (both in technological terms and in terms of regulation, in particular), amplified by all the risks and potentialities associated with so-called "globalisation", being already difficult, sees this difficulty aggravated when the margins of decisions and, often, their content, are largely defined in complex and invaluable negotiating frameworks, framework of the European Union. In fact, this problem is aggravated when the process of European construction itself  both in terms of institutional functioning, of legislation produced, of combined effect of regulatory standards and practices, or of the absence of finalisation of the global regulatory framework  may tend to leave, in practice, the objectives contained in the mandate of the Central Bank - and let me highlight in particular, the ultimate objective of national financial stability - in the hands of traditional entities while, on the other hand, greatly limits their scope for intervention. Given this complex framework, we have no doubt that adapting to this unstable and unfinished context, as well as the ability to influence it, require an increased level of technical and personal quality and a whole new degree of institutional sophistication. In the context of ambiguity and permanent change in which we live  particularly within the banking union  with the first tests of the articulation between European supervision and resolution to be carried out and producing results yet to be determined, with the main framework legislation to be reviewed (CRR, CRD IV, BRRD, etc.), it also seems indisputable that the defence of the national interest will undergo a detailed clarification of that same interest in each theme and the maximisation of the combined capacity for influence of all actors, in particular Government and Banco de Portugal, in close coordination with the other financial market supervisors in the markets, insurance and pension funds sectors (CMVM and ASF), and, where justified, even involving Members of the Assembly of the Republic and the European Parliament. Clairvoyance and determination are the strategic ingredients to be preserved in a process that should involve civil society and the business universe. It should be noted that some stabilisation of the national financial sector to which we have been witnessing has only been possible thanks to cooperation, in my view exemplary, among all public leaders, and a demanding but transparent and healthy relationship with industry. And if there are serious risks that persist, if there are past ballasts and practices to correct, there is an increasingly clear and defined path to tread safely and focusedly. I could not end without publicly explaining something that a year ago was a hope and which I have the enormous pleasure and obligation to confirm today through my personal testimony: I am referring to the enormous technical, professional and human quality of the vast majority of employees with whom I have had the privilege of working in this time that I already have in the administration of Banco de Portugal; the competence and unexceeded dedication with which they take on the difficult challenges we face are and will be the strongest guarantee of the collective success we pursue. On behalf of those sworn in, I end with a renewed thanks for the trust placed in us, reaffirming the full awareness of the difficulties that await us but assuming, individually and collectively, the solemn commitment to do our best to, through the reference institution that is Banco de Portugal, to contribute to the strengthening and stabilization of the national and European financial system and, in this way, the economy and national prosperity.
