Interveno da Vice-Governadora Elisa Ferreira na cerimnia da tomada de posse dos membros do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Portugal 08 set. 2017 Senhor Ministro das Finanas Senhor Secretrio de Estado Adjunto e das Finanas Senhor Governador do Banco de Portugal Senhora Presidente da Comisso de Oramento, Finanas e Modernizao Administrativa (COFMA) E peo licena para assim saudar, nesta evocao, todas as restantes personalidades aqui presentes. Usar da palavra em nome dos quatro elementos que hoje assumem funes (ou novas funes) enquanto membros do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Portugal  um ato de grande responsabilidade mas que assumo com o maior prazer, por um motivo fundamental: porque acreditamos, todos ns, que seremos capazes de constituir uma Administrao coesa, competente e dinmica,  altura do que os cidados tm o direito de esperar de uma instituio central na vida do Pas como  o Banco de Portugal. Partilhamos, os quatro, diversos sentimentos comuns: Antes de mais, o peso da responsabilidade, combinado com um reconhecimento sincero pela confiana em ns depositada pelo Senhor Governador do Banco de Portugal, de quem partiu a proposta inicial; depois pela Comisso de Oramento, Finanas e Modernizao Administrativa da Assembleia da Repblica que procedeu s audies correspondentes em 27 de junho e se pronunciou favoravelmente em 19 de julho; e, por fim, pela designao governamental concretizada atravs de resoluo do Conselho de Ministros aprovada em 24 de agosto e hoje publicada. Seguidamente, a convico de que, com experincias e vivncias to ricas e to distintas de cada um dos seus elementos, este Conselho de Administrao ter a composio adequada para encontrar snteses equilibradas, informadas e capazes nas posies que ter de vir a assumir. Permitam-me que pessoalmente sublinhe a bem vinda paridade de gnero  se no (ainda) no Conselho, pelo menos entre os novos empossados , paridade essa frequentemente to escassa em funes de topo, nomeadamente no setor financeiro. Acresce ainda a garantia de uma transio suave conferida pela j longa vivncia do Banco, incluindo todos os ensinamentos decorrentes da travessia de tempos to difceis como foram os que se seguiram  crise de 2007/08, por parte do Senhor Governador e do Dr. Hlder Rosalino, alm da experincia de j mais de um ano por parte dos administradores ora incumbidos de maiores responsabilidades (o Dr. Luis Mximo dos Santos e eu prpria), aspetos agora enriquecidos com a presena de dois novos membros, a Professora Ana Paula Serra e o Dr. Lus Laginha de Sousa, ambos detentores de robusta experincia acadmica e profissional. Uma palavra tambm de reconhecimento aos membros que cessaram as funes que assumiremos, o Professor Pedro Duarte Neves e, at h alguns meses, o Dr. Jos Ramalho, dos quais esperamos poder continuar a receber o benefcio do seu experiente conselho. Por ltimo, e talvez seja mesmo este o principal elo que nos une, referirei a enorme vontade de todos em colocar os nossos melhores atributos e esforos ao servio do Pas. Nesse sentido, prosseguiremos os objetivos adotados pelo Conselho de Administrao para o Plano Estratgico do Banco de Portugal no perodo de 2017-2020, sob o lema fazer sempre melhor: um Banco ambicioso, exigente, virado para o futuro, consciente do seu passado mas no prisioneiro dele. Desenvolveremos as quatro linhas principais de orientao estratgica definidas: Afirmar interna e externamente as capacidades do Banco enquanto autoridade monetria; Participar na definio dos enquadramentos regulatrios e na aplicao das prticas de superviso de forma a garantir a robustez e estabilidade do sistema financeiro nacional e a confiana dos agentes econmicos; Promover o conhecimento sobre a economia portuguesa e a integrao europeia, contribuindo para uma sociedade esclarecida e bem informada; Ser um dos bancos mais eficientes do Eurosistema. Mas a convico com que partimos para a nova fase de trabalho que se nos depara no nos ir certamente diminuir a conscincia nem retirar a devida lucidez quanto s dificuldades que vamos continuar a ter de vencer. De facto, e ao contrrio de alguns discursos a nosso ver pouco fundamentados, o papel de um Banco Central nacional num pas que integra no s uma Unio Monetria mas tambm uma Unio Bancria no se torna nem mais simples nem menos relevante face ao modelo tradicional dos Bancos Centrais puramente nacionais. A defesa do interesse nacional num contexto externo altamente voltil (quer em termos tecnolgicos quer em termos de regulao, designadamente), amplificado por todos os riscos e potencialidades associados  chamada globalizao, sendo j de si difcil, v essa dificuldade agravada quando as margens das decises e, frequentemente, o seu contedo, so em grande parte definidas em quadros negociais complexos e instveis, inclusivamente no quadro da Unio Europeia. De facto, este problema agrava-se quando o prprio processo de construo europeia  quer em matria de funcionamento institucional, quer de legislao produzida, quer de efeito combinado de normas e prticas regulamentares, quer ainda de ausncia de finalizao do quadro regulatrio global  pode tender a deixar, na prtica, os objetivos constantes do mandato do Banco Central -e permitam-me destacar em particular, o objetivo ltimo da estabilidade financeira nacional -nas mos das entidades tradicionais enquanto, por outro lado, lhes limita enormemente a margem de interveno. Perante este complexo quadro, no temos quaisquer dvidas de que a adaptao a este contexto instvel e inacabado, assim como a capacidade para o influenciar, exigem um acrescido nvel de qualidade tcnica e pessoal e um grau de sofisticao institucional totalmente novo. No contexto de ambiguidade e mutao permanente em que vivemos  nomeadamente no quadro da Unio Bancria , com os primeiros testes da articulao entre superviso e resoluo europeias a serem realizados e a produzirem resultados ainda por apurar, com a principal legislao de enquadramento a ser revista (CRR,CRD IV, BRRD, etc.), parece tambm incontestvel que a defesa do interesse nacional passar por uma clarificao detalhada desse mesmo interesse em cada tema e pela maximizao da capacidade de influncia combinada de todos os atores, em particular Governo e Banco de Portugal em articulao estreita com as restantes autoridades de superviso do mercado financeiro dos setores de mercados, seguros e fundos de penses (CMVM e ASF), e, nos casos em que tal se justifique, envolvendo mesmo deputados  Assembleia da Repblica e ao Parlamento Europeu. Clarividncia e determinao so os ingredientes estratgicos a preservar num processo que deve envolver a sociedade civil e o universo empresarial. Importa salientar que alguma estabilizao do setor financeiro nacional a que temos vindo a assistir s tem sido possvel graas a uma cooperao, a meu ver exemplar, entre todos os responsveis pblicos, e de um relacionamento exigente, mas transparente e so, com a indstria. E se existem riscos srios que persistem, se existem lastros do passado e prticas a corrigir, h um caminho cada vez mais claro e definido a trilhar com segurana e foco. No poderia terminar sem aqui explicitar publicamente algo que h um ano era uma esperana e que hoje tenho o enorme prazer e obrigao de confirmar atravs do meu testemunho pessoal: refiro-me  enorme qualidade tcnica, profissional e humana da grande maioria dos colaboradores com quem tive o privilgio de trabalhar neste tempo que j levo na administrao do Banco de Portugal; a competncia e a dedicao inexcedvel com que assumem os difceis desafios com que nos confrontamos so e sero a mais forte garantia do sucesso coletivo que perseguimos. Em nome dos empossados, termino com um renovado agradecimento pela confiana em ns depositada, reafirmando a conscincia plena das dificuldades que nos esperam mas assumindo, individual e coletivamente, o compromisso solene de dar o nosso melhor para, atravs da instituio de referncia que  o Banco de Portugal, contribuirmos para o robustecimento e estabilizao do sistema financeiro nacional e europeu e, por essa via, da economia e prosperidade nacional.

Title: Concluding remarks by Director Luis Laginha de Sousa at the Banco de Portugal Conference on Financial Stability
text: Concluding remarks by Director Luis... Concluding remarks by Director Luis Laginha de Sousa at the Banco de Portugal Conference on Financial Stability 17 Oct. 2017 We are facing a changing financial landscape, the fragilities that led to the recent crisis are not yet solved, and we now also have to deal with new challenges arising from several macroeconomic and regulatory developments that were put in practice to deal with it. The recent crisis left financial systems of many countries vulnerable to legacy assets, in some cases in a context of over-indebted economies. This vulnerability and the macroeconomic environment, characterized by very low interest rates and subdued economic growth, can significantly undermine the performance of the banking system. As we have seen this morning (Martinho, Oliveira, et. al), adverse economic conditions and interest rate shifts explain the large drop in average bank return on assets (ROA), that we have witnessed since 2008. Given the persistency of some of these conditions, they are likely to continue to exert a downward pressure on banks profitability for some time. This limits the capacity of banks to increase own funds via revenue generation, putting increased pressure on other forms of capitalization, which tend to be more costly. In response to the crisis, the regulatory and supervisory framework has been subject to extensive reforms. As a result, we have now a more robust and capitalized banking sector. These reforms, such as the minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities (MREL) and IFRS9, are still ongoing and I am convinced that, if properly implemented (and I will address this issue later on), the resilience of the financial system would be improved even further. However, it is important to keep in mind that these ongoing reforms put significant pressure on banks funding capacity, in an environment where this capacity is likely to be undermined. In order to achieve a successful steady state, it is important that the implementation of these reforms takes into account not only the benefits arising from higher funding requirements, but also its underlying macroeconomic costs. Although increasing banks resilience is extremely important to financial stability, we do not want to achieve the so-called stability of the graveyard. The cost of raising capital standards rely, to a great extent, both on the strategies pursued by banks in order to comply with these requirements and on the phase of the business cycle in which the banks operate. In a context where the capacity of banks to generate profits is constrained and the access to new equity is limited, the deleveraging of the banking sector seems, in some countries, the inevitable option. The effects of deleveraging can be more or less harmful depending on the channel through which credit is transmitted into the economy. As pointed out (in Mian, et al, 2017), the impact of credit supply shocks, depends on whether they contribute mostly to boost demand or, if by contrast, they affect the economy primarily by loosening firms borrowing constraints and, consequently, improving labour productivity. The first scenario leads to more amplified business cycles, combined with more severe recessions, since wages fail to provide the needed adjustment, given nominal downward rigidity. By contrast, the latest channel of transmission leads to more benign effects on economic growth and competitiveness. Regulation should, therefore, take into account which channel dominates and ideally try to incentivise the most appropriate transmission of credit into the economy. The interaction and substitutability between the regulated and non-regulated banking sector would also have to be taken into account by policy-makers. As pointed-out (in Martinez Miera and Repullo, 2017), an environment of low interest rates, especially when capital is scarce and costly, is particularly prone to the expansion of the shadow banking. In such situation, improving the resilience of regulated institutions may come at the expense of driving some financing activity outside the perimeter of regulation. In addition, when imposing capital standards, regulators should also consider the creation of mechanisms that incentivise banks to produce unbiased risk metrics. As discussed (by Joao Santos), capital standards make reported risk costly for institutions, and this encourages them to produce downward-biased estimations. Therefore, the main challenge of macroprudential policy at the current juncture can be summarized in a very simple sentence to say, but a very hard goal to achieve. The macroprudential policy has to be capable of improving the resilience of the financial system, while allowing an adequate level of financial intermediation to sustain economic recovery. As such, the implementation of macroprudential policy should consider not only the positive impact of its instruments on the mitigation of systemic risk but also the negative implications concerning their costs, and the unwanted effects and possible spillovers. However, there is considerably more research on analysing the impact of policy instruments in reducing the probability of a crisis than on assessing the costs or negative outcomes, resulting from their implementation. This can also be concluded by the presentation on the use and effectiveness of macroprudential policy (Stijn Claessens), which indicates that, the transmission mechanisms of policy instruments are not necessarily static, but rather evolving over time, with innovation, with reforms, and with the cycle of the financial system. The assessment of the effects I have just mentioned, should take into account the endogenous structure of the financial system and the non-linearities associated with policy effects. This clearly raises the boundaries of research required for risk and policy analysis Some of the presentations that we had today were great examples to highlight what Ive just said (Corbae; Mendoza). In addition (as discussed by John Fell) another important aspect to consider in policy implementation is the existent trade-offs between macroprudential policy instruments. Many of these instruments, although designed at targeting different sources of systemic risk, will impact on many of the same objectives. For example, borrower-based measures like loan-to-value (LTV) or loan-to-income (LTI) caps, even though more directed at taming the financial cycle, would also contribute to increase the resilience of the banking system, namely by reducing the borrowers probability of default and/or the losses, should such default occur. Along the same line of thought, different capital-based instruments, although targeted at specific intermediate objectives, will most likely be transmitted into the economy through the same channels. They may differ in the timing and scope of implementation, but they are essentially the same tool (i.e. capital ratios). The multiplicity of macroprudential policy goals and the relative similarity of policy instruments run the risk of an overload of policy measures if different sources of risk are targeted at separately. A global approach is needed in policymaking and the development of a concept of the stance of macroprudential policy would be very helpful to guide policy decisions. I would like to add a few remarks about the challenges that we still face today, as far as promoting financial stability is concerned. We cannot ignore that, despite the important steps taken, the Banking Union is still incomplete. Without a proper common deposit insurance scheme and the setting up of a backstop for the Single Resolution Fund, it simply cannot work properly. In fact, while supervisory and resolution decisions are taken at EU-level for the most relevant institutions, financial stability is still mostly a national concern and responsibility, despite the much more limited set of tools to safeguard it, particularly in a context where there is a clear misalignment between the responsibility of financial stability and risk control. Furthermore, the development of the Banking Union was anchored on a steady state assumption of a sustained macroeconomic recovery, which is still far from having been achieved. Proof of that is the debate that we had today on how to address important crisis legacy issues for which the adequate and effective tools are not available, at least under the current EU regulatory framework. The imposition of blind rules that do not take into account the heterogeneity of nonperforming loans (NPL) should be avoided. The NPL stock cannot be addressed in a way that triggers fire sales, potentially leading to a significant negative impact on the banking system and on the non-banking sectors of the economy as well. On the contrary, NPL should be addressed over an adequate period of time, taking into account the heterogeneity of NPL in banks balance sheet, in order to preserve financial stability. Additionally, in the development of European regulatory framework, greater attention should be given to transitional aspects. The entry into force of the Bank Recovery and Resolution Directive (BRRD) has occurred without a full recovery of the EU economies, and without banks having significantly strengthened their ability to absorb losses. The importance of MREL, within a harmonized bank resolution framework, is indisputable. It has clear benefits once the steady state situation has been achieved. The most important benefit is safeguarding financial stability in the long run, by promoting an orderly resolution of banks and protecting taxpayers, which contributes to mitigate the negative bank-sovereign feedback loop. However, in order to ensure such ultimate goal, its potential negative spillovers have to be taken into account, as they can undermine financial stability during the implementation phase, especially given the magnitude of the aggregate expected MREL shortfalls, vis-a-vis the current market capacity to absorb the necessary issuances. Following the crisis period, the European banking system is still on a challenging path towards a sustainable situation. The current context is still characterized by low profitability, by high stocks of legacy assets, and also by different market access conditions. As a consequence of such context, careful consideration must be given to the measures adopted by regulators and supervisors, whose responsibilities should be clearly distinguished, as those measures could actually create more risks for financial stability. The heterogeneous situation of banks across Europe cannot be neglected. Special attention should be paid to the specificities of each banking sector and to the impact of the supervisory and regulatory action, not only on the financial stability, but also on the overall economy. In particular, we should keep in mind that supervisory and regulatory measures, as well as the moment chosen for their adoption, may have significant implications on financial intermediaries and on their capacity to properly play their role in the economy. If those measures tend to favour the consolidation in the European banking sector, then we must take into account the potential disruptive and negative effects that such consolidation might have. Among such negative effects I would like to highlight two. One is a possible, and very likely, reduction of the services available to the business community of some member states, both in variety, in quality and in price, with this being particularly relevant for the member states which have their banks consolidated instead of being the consolidators. Another is the fact that we cannot neglect the risks underlying too-big-to-fail institutions, which we are actually trying to mitigate in the new regulatory context, nor can we neglect the negative consequences for the economy as a whole, associated with the lack of competition across banks. As it has already been said many times, but apparently we still need to say it many times more, and perhaps using loudspeakers, If a Bank is too big to fail, it is too big, period. The small is beautiful concept should probably be reinstated in the economic and financial jargon. The current environment clearly tests both the capacity of policymakers to mitigate systemic risks and of research to correctly identify such risks and assess the impact of policy measures. A global perspective in analysing risks and the impact of policy instruments is essential in order to pass this test. Let me finish as Ive started, by thanking all who made this Conference possible and to our Speakers in particular I hope youve had a fruitful time and that we can continue to meet, to discuss and to share information on topics that are key to our society as a whole.

Title: Interview of Vice Governor Luis Maximo dos Santos to Expresso: Sale of Novo Banco was achieved against winds and tides
text: Louis... Interview of Vice Governor Luis Maximo dos Santos to Expresso: Sale of Novo Banco was achieved against winds and tides 04 nov. 2017 Director of Banco de Portugal since July 2016 and deputy governor since September, Luis Maximo dos Santos chairs the Resolution Fund (FR) and has under his responsibility the departments of behavioral supervision and investigation and sanctioning action, among others. Unsurprisingly, he has an optimistic view of the sale of Novo Banco and the appreciation of the 25% with which the fund stayed. He confesses, however, that the coming years "will be a demand for the new shareholder," the Lone Star. It admits that it would have been preferable for the Resolution Fund to have a seat in the administration of Novo Banco, but that the means of supervision necessary to defend public interests were still taken care of. It acknowledges that "there are limits to the application of resolutions", but warns of the need for more flexibility so that this measure does not become a "universal panacea". He chaired the liquidation committee of BPP, 'bad' BES and, as chairman of the the Resolution, sold the Novo Banco and is taking care of the assets of the former Banif stayed at the bottom. Aren't you tired of taking care of the health of ex-banks? It gives me some satisfaction, in a country where so many people become famous in cutting public resources, that at least in the BPP has recovered the public resources applied by the State and also that other creditors have recovered something. In 2010, when the BPP's authorisation was revoked, I was chaired by the liquidation committee. It was a difficult challenge, because it was the first bank legally settled with the legislation that came from 2006. At the time, instead of congratulating me, they gave me their condolences. Would it be good ifyou thought the same thing about the 'bad' BES? It's a completely different situation. There is also some pioneering in the process. It was the first bank to be settled and remained until July 2016 with an unrevoked bank license, with a series of corrective measures that were withinthe scope of operations that could be done. Still, even in the bad BES it was possible to recover some value, but it is a drop of water for the responsibilities that the bank already in liquidation has. He did not participate in the BES resolution measure, but he knows what happened in these three Years. Could you have done differently for the better? The essential of ex-BES activity has been preserved and the stability of the system as well. That's really important. There has been much criticism of the intervention in the former BES, especially the banking, which will pay the invoice for decades... There are different perspectives. Only when faced with the urgency of the situation can a full assessment be made. What is a fact is that, after these three long years, Banco de Portugal fulfilled its duty, because it applied the resolution measure, finalized it, as it was supposed, selling the transitional bank, and this has a value that goes beyond Novo Banco and communicates to the whole system. It is clear that if we are faced with a global crisis in the system, the idea of resolution can hardly succeed if it challenges seven or eight banks. In this case it is difficult to apply resolution measures to them, because there would hardly be resources from other banks in the system to pay for it. And that's not what happened? The ex-BES case was private. It is true that there was a financial crisis, but in the other banks there were capitalizations and none was on the iinence of being able to stop operating. Portugal served as a guinea pig, was pushed by theEurop eias authorities into this resolution? I wouldn't take the point on that level. We already had legislation that would allow banks to be resolving since 2012. It's even curious. If we hadn't done it, we couldn't have solved BES in 2014. The principle underlying the idea of resolution is quiteattractive, because it directly responds to the losses to those who were in the bank, shareholders, subordinated bondholders and at the limit up to ordinary creditors, and all this financed by the system and not by taxpayers. I note that thereare limits to the application of these measures and some literature has emerged calling attention to a certain flexibility, because this of resolutions should not be a universal panacea. Unfortunately, the creation of the Banking Union took place without a real debate in the country. The solution to the collapse of Banco Popular in Spain was already different even from what happened to the former Banif, the banks of the Spanish system were safe, our No... I'm not supposed to comment on that because I wasn't involved in Banif's resolution. The bill to be paid by the banks is too high. It is not almost a tax on the system? It makes some sense that a bank that now enter Portugal has to do? It's true, it's true. But it is the model that has been created in the European Union to deal with banking crises. It was understood that a system with these characteristics was preferable, to be the other banks paying, than to be systematically convening public resources. Banking is very particular. For example, if an exemplary-managed bank is in the same system as a bank that collapsed it can be hit by a wave of mistrust. They'd lose them all. And trust costs a lot to gain, but it's lost veryeasily. This model, the contributions to the National and European Resolution Fund and the Deposit Guarantee Fund serve to enable people to feel, after all, that there is greater security. Every grain has its bran. If we do not wantto pay public resources, the invoice will have to be paid by the system. That's the rule. Why did the Resolution Fund have to take 25% of the bank? What I can say is that a sales procedure was organised that was considered open, transparente, competitive, non-discriminatory, but the final competitor only wanted to buy 75% of the capital. I see this 25% as a possibility for the Resolution Fund to value its position in the future. If it wasn't, wouldn't the New Bank have been sold? Wedon't necessarily have to be pessimistic. I also don't have an optimism that isn't based on reality. We're going to have to wait. We all recognise that the European Union's Directorate-General for Competition [DGComp] is a very demanding entity. The process complied with the requirements imposed. There is a conviction that there may be some value there. Certainly with a heavy legacy, so the business had these characteristics, but the whole process revealed a lot of maturity. You mean it was a complexbusiness action... Let's go in parts. Obtaining the ECB's authorisations, dealing with the Resolution Mechanism at the same time, always pressing, safeguarding the interests of the public waste, in terms of the taxpayer and the Portuguese State, having the authorisation of theGeneral Directorate of Competition and satisfying the buyer is no easy task. Only those who have really participated in this process, and I do not call it to me, is that they know in depth the difficulties that this has ended. What is a fact is that against winds and tides we get the essential objetivos. I don't mean by this that you open a path of ease. It will be a demanding path for the new shareholder and the Resolution Fund, but it is the first bank of transition to be sold in Europe, and still at a time of great crisis, with technological challenges ahead and a considerable regulatory burden. In the European context, there have been no major investments in banking since 2014. On the other hand, the buyer came from the USA, which is also, from the point of view of investment, interessante. The buyer, Lone Star, stays with Novo Banco, with a risk guarantee of the assets up to 3.89 billion, invests 1 billion in capitalisation and puts the other banks to pay what goes wrong. It would not be easier to break the bank and integrate it in other banks? The resolution is the framework that we have organised to deal with such cases. It would be more disruptive if the bank was broken. Surely if this possibility had appeared as feasible we would have had to obtain the necessaryauthorizations. That is, the BdP was limited in the performance of the sale that could do? Absolutely. We have to look at the rules we deal with. Keeping the Novo Banco as a unit was very important. The contingency mechanism is not a guarantee to the company, it is a guarantee to the bank's capital. Protects bank ratios. Can you say: more does this benefit shareholders? Sure, but only indirectly. There may be losses in the sale of assets and there is no need to inject capital on the part ofthe fund. It is a process that seems to me, within the difficulties, more balanced. And then there are no facilities: for eight years no dividends are distributed, and the Resolution Fund has a fundamental word on the management of those assets. How will the FR control that the new shareholders will protect your interests if they do not do you have a seat in the bank administration? There are concrete powers that do not actually translate into the presence in the administration, and that is a pity, but it was not because the buyerhad no rective. In the context of the negotiations between the Portuguese government and DGComp it was understood that the presence of the State was too intrusive. That is why the FR not only does not have a seat in the administration but cannot vote at the general meeting. But it has a commission of monitorization, which will have an important role and access to information that is not restricted to assets that are under the jurisdiction of the contingent capitalization mechanism. On the other hand, there are restrictions on transactions with re-lacionated parties and amechanism for monitoring credit policies and accounting policies. From what you know about Novo Banco and the buyer, which part is that of the 3.89 billion can be used? I should not express sensitivities about this matter. This iimitated didn't happen by chance. It's a ceiling. It will depend on many factors, nature of assets, market evolution, among others... In recent years, a number of bank managers have deceived everyone, including the supervisor. How do you guarantee that the person who bought Novo Banco will not act in a way that maximize losses to the FR? This problem has been identified. When the BdP had to proceed with the sale, it did not do so by ignoring the consequences it could have forthe competition. In fact, many international reports stressed as an embarrassment to our economy the absence of the sale of Novo Banco. It is very difficult to maintain a system in the uncertainty of what would happen to the bank. And that is why he fought himself to create mechanismfor those who eliminated a possible perversity of incentives and to have supervisory powers. We didn't just want to sell the New Bank. We were aware that with this solution some problems would arise, and the negotiation process had the maximum cautthem. Was it a business you can say: evil, the least? I'd say, well, least. "Resolution Fund must be close to the BdP" The deputy governor of Banco de Portugal (BdP) states that the net situation of the Resolution Fund (FR) is negative toface new responsibilities, that is, another resolution. But the revenues, through the contributions of the bank, ensure the payment of the loans of two resolutions (BES and Banif). Luis Maximo dos Santos argues that the FR must be with the BdP, but it does not shock him that it is autonomous from the BdP, as is the case in Spain. He confesses that the scale of actions against FR and BdP is large. And as for the Deposit Guarantee Fund (FGD), which it chairs, it says it is welloff and above the ceiling required for European banks. Will you continue to chair the Resolution Fund? I will continue until Banco de Portugal decides. Do you argue that the FR should be under the purview of the BdP or should it be an autonomous body? I defendwhat must be with the BdP, but the matter is complex. In Europe there are several models, because there are different dimensions. There is a preventive dimension of the resolution and an executive dimension, which concerns the determination of the resolution measure and its consequent execucao. Today, this problem cannot be put in the same terms as it was placed before 1 January 2016, when the Single Resolution Mechanism came into force. For example, the Central Bank of Spain has the preventive function of the resolution, and there is an institution  the FROB  that has an executive function. It is natural that the best way to organize this function will be discussed. It would no longer make sense to have an autonomous national resolution authority with the participation of BdP members? It can bea link mod. Like the Deposit Guarantee Fund, which works with the BdP but has its own legal personality. An authority that works with the central bank and reflects, depending on the matters you are deciding, different compositions maybe created. It's a debate that's open. Is fgd able to meet the payment of deposits if an institution goes bankrupt? The FGD is above the threshold that European rules require for its capitalisation. FGD is well capitalized. The space for the intervencao of the deposit guarantee decreased with the figure of the resolution. Only in the event of liquidation is the FGD triggered. Our fund is better capitalised on what is required by the ceiling vis-a-vis the European institutions. The relationship between the financial situationof the fund and the deposits covered by the guarantee is 1.19% , when the Directive imposes 0.8% by 2024. In Portugal we are above that level. How many actions are in place against the resolution of the old BES and the sale of Novo Banco and amounts may involve? Contesting the sale there aren't many. There is indeed a very significant dispute against the BdP and the FR challenging the resolution measure, the transfer of senior obligations and other claims. Is it possible to have an idea of how much fr may haveto pay under these? No. Only when the decisions are final. It is not correct to speak of values at this time. The BdP, in the processes it has, will be able to demonstrate its arguments. There were five precautionary measures against the sale. Any foi considered well-founded? No. He was amazed by bcp's action against RF because of the mechanism created to manage problem assets? Those who are in these roles should not be surprised by certain situations. Institutions are free to act on the terms they see fit best in defending what they think their interests are. I have no doubt that this operation benefits the financial system in multiple boards: in the perception of the country, in indirect effects on competitors and forthe effects of rating [credit rating]. As much as one might criticize, it is objectively positive for the financial system Portuguese. And BCP is part of it. Banco de Portugal is sure of the decisions it makes. Was BCP the only bank to takeaction of this nature? With these characteristics, yes. How are the FR accounts right now? The FR has about 250 million in revenue stemming from the contributions of banks and generates a positive cash flow. Annually, the fund is sustainable to pagar the loans it has to pay. But there's a negative net situation. If there is an incident with a bank under national supervision they would have to ask for more money? That's the truth. The advisory for the sale of Novo Banco has already cost more than 20,000by the end of 2016. Who pays? At one point there was doubt as to whether certain costs should be attributed to the BdP as a National Resolution Authority or the FR. The question was examined by the Court of Auditors, which considered that this should be attributed to the BdP. 85% of confirmedsanctions Maximo dos Santos says banking is prepared for new challenges. Success rate of convictions is around 85% The deputy governor of Banco de Portugal, which has two major departments - behavioral supervisionand the investigation and sanctioning processes of banking - says that there have been significant improvements in recent years in these two aspects. The strengthening of resources in the area of behavioral and sanctioning has revealed that nowadays "there is a moreeasy climate to comply by the institutions financial institutions," explains Luis Maximo dos Santos. On the other hand, he stresses that "the system is stronger today", even stating that "we all know several institutions that have eased their capitalization levels with these orthose measures and are making an effort to improve their internal organisational mechanisms". To that end, he says, it is not irrelevant that there is a deeper awareness that "the demand for financial stability is a permanent activity", that "one cannot let go". One of the most dynamic departments in the last 10 years has been that of investigation and sanctioning action, with several mega-lawsuits against banks that eventually disappeared from the map and under which seriousand very serious orders have fallen. Maximo dos Santos does not talk about them, but says that the department in question "is one of the most scrutinized". He explains: "Many of Banco de Portugal's convictions are appealed to the courts by the accused and convicted, and in these cases we have a success rate for convictions of around 85%." The deputy governor does not only refer to serious or very serious convictions, common in the mega-cases of the BpN or BPP and already confirmed by thetribunes, but also to the smaller ones, such as irregularities of price, interest rates or even collections of undue commissions. Challenges and supervision When asked about the low rates of profitability of Portuguese banking, the still problem of malparado and the challenges in terms of the digitization of the sector, Maximo dos Santos recognizes the weaknesses and the challenge of the paradigm shift. "We are on the threshold of a digital revolution that will change the way banks operate", but there have already been several changes desd andthe 80s and 90s and the sector "responded very well from the point of view of the diffusion of technology, there has even been a big qualitative leap". As for the supervisor's proper means of overtaking the revolution underway, he says: "Not only do you have them, but you are doing it. We must have a fit strategy and resources, listening to the market, ensuring levels of trust and protection of the rights of bank customers."

Entrevista do Vice-Governador Lus Mximo dos Santos ao Expresso: Venda do Novo Banco foi conseguida contra ventos e mars 04 nov. 2017 Administrador do Banco de Portugal desde julho de 2016 e vice-governador desde setembro, Lus Mximo dos Santos preside ao Fundo de Resoluo (FR) e tem sob a sua alada os departamentos de superviso comportamental e de averiguao e ao sancionatria, entre outros. Sem surpresas, tem uma viso otimista sobre a venda do Novo Banco e a valorizao dos 25% com que o fundo ficou. Confessa, contudo, que os prximos anos vo ser de exigncia para o novo acionista, o Lone Star. Admite que teria sido prefervel o Fundo de Resoluo ter assento na administrao do Novo Banco, mas que mesmo assim foram acautelados os meios de fiscalizao necessrios  defesa dos interesses pblicos. Reconhece que h limites  aplicao das resolues, mas alerta para a necessidade de mais flexibilidade para que esta medida no se torne uma panaceia universal. Presidiu  comisso liquidatria do BPP, do BES mau e, enquanto presidente do Fundo de Resoluo, vendeu o Novo Banco e est a tomar conta dos ativos do ex-Banif que ficaram no fundo. No est cansado de andar a tratar da sade de ex-bancos? D-me alguma satisfao, num pas onde tanta gente se torna clebre em lapidar recursos pblicos, que pelo menos no BPP se tenha recuperado os recursos pblicos aplicados pelo Estado e tambm que outros credores tenham recuperado alguma coisa. Em 2010, quando foi revogada a autorizao do BPP, convidaram-me a assumir a presidncia da comisso liquidatria. Foi um desafio difcil, porque foi o primeiro banco judicialmente liquidado com a legislao que vinha de 2006. Na altura, em vez de me darem os parabns, deram-me os psames. Era bom que acontecesse a mesma coisa no BES mau?  uma situao completamente diferente. Tambm h algum pioneirismo no processo. Foi o primeiro banco resolvido e ficou at julho de 2016 com uma licena bancria no revogada, com uma srie de medidas corretivas que limitavam o mbito de operaes que se podiam fazer. Ainda assim, mesmo no BES mau foi possvel recuperar algum valor, mas  uma gota de gua para as responsabilidades que o banco j em liquidao tem. No participou na medida de resoluo do BES, mas sabe o que se passou nestes trs anos. Podia ter-se feito diferente para melhor? O essencial da atividade do ex-BES foi preservada e a estabilidade do sistema tambm. Isso  mesmo muito importante. Tm sido muitas as crticas  interveno no ex-BES, sobretudo da banca, que vai pagar a fatura durante dcadas... H perspetivas diferentes. S quando se  confrontado com a urgncia da situao se pode fazer uma avaliao completa. O que  um facto  que, ao fim destes trs longos anos, o Banco de Portugal cumpriu o seu dever, porque aplicou a medida de resoluo, finalizou-a, como era suposto, vendendo o banco de transio, e isso tem um valor que vai alm do Novo Banco e se comunica a todo o sistema.  evidente que, se formos confrontados com uma crise global do sistema, a ideia de resoluo dificilmente consegue vingar, se esta colocar em causa sete ou oito bancos. Nesse caso  difcil aplicar-lhes medidas de resoluo, porque dificilmente haveria recursos de outros bancos do sistema para a pagar. E no foi isso que aconteceu? O caso do ex-BES foi particular.  verdade que havia uma crise financeira, mas nos outros bancos houve capitalizaes e nenhum esteve na iminncia de poder deixar de operar. Portugal serviu de cobaia, foi empurrado pelas autoridades europeias para esta resoluo? No poria a questo nesse patamar. J tnhamos legislao que permitisse a resoluo de bancos desde 2012.  at curioso. Se no a tivssemos feito no podamos ter resolvido o BES em 2014. O princpio subjacente  ideia de resoluo  bastante atrativo, porque faz responder diretamente os prejuzos queles que no fundo estavam no banco, acionistas, obrigacionistas subordinados e no limite at credores comuns, e tudo isso financiado pelo sistema e no pelos contribuintes. Reconheo que h limites  aplicao destas medidas e tem surgido alguma literatura a chamar a ateno para uma certa flexibilidade, porque isto das resolues no deve ser uma panaceia universal. Infelizmente, a criao da Unio Bancria fez-se sem um verdadeiro debate no pas. A soluo para o colapso do Banco Popular em Espanha j foi diferente mesmo do que aconteceu com o ex-Banif, os bancos do sistema espanhol ficaram a salvo, os nossos no... No devo comentar isso, porque no estive envolvido na resoluo do Banif. A fatura a pagar pelos bancos  demasiado elevada. No  quase um imposto sobre o sistema? Faz algum sentido que um banco que entre agora em Portugal tambm o tenha de fazer?  verdade. Mas  o modelo que se criou na Unio Europeia para se lidar com as crises bancrias. Entendeu-se que era prefervel um sistema com estas caractersticas, serem os outros bancos a pagar, do que estar sistematicamente a convocar recursos pblicos. A atividade bancria  muito particular. Por exemplo, se um banco exemplarmente gerido estiver no mesmo sistema de um banco que colapsou pode ser atingido pela vaga de desconfiana. Perderiam todos. E a confiana custa muito a ganhar, mas perde-se muito facilmente. Este modelo, as contribuies para o Fundo de Resoluo Nacional e Europeu e para o Fundo de Garantia de Depsitos servem para permitir que as pessoas sintam, apesar de tudo, que h uma maior segurana. No h bela sem seno. Se no queremos convocar recursos pblicos, a fatura ter de ser paga pelo sistema. Essa passou a ser a regra. Porque  que o Fundo de Resoluo teve de ficar com 25% do banco? O que posso dizer  que se organizou um procedimento de venda que foi considerado aberto, transparente, competitivo, no discriminatrio, mas o concorrente final s quis comprar 75% do capital. Vejo esses 25% como uma possibilidade de o Fundo de Resoluo valorizar a sua posio no futuro. Se no fosse assim, o Novo Banco no teria sido vendido? No temos de ser necessariamente pessimistas. Tambm no tenho um otimismo que no seja fundado na realidade. Teremos de aguardar. Todos reconhecemos que a Direo Geral da Concorrncia da Unio Europeia [DGComp]  uma entidade bastante exigente. O processo obedeceu aos requisitos impostos. H a convico de que poder estar ali [Novo Banco] algum valor. Com certeza com um legado pesado, por isso o negcio teve estas caractersticas, mas todo o processo revelou muita maturidade. Quer dizer que foi uma negociao complexa... Vamos por partes. Obter as autorizaes do BCE, lidar ao mesmo tempo com o Mecanismo de Resoluo, sempre a pressionar, acautelar os interesses do errio pblico, em termos do contribuinte e do Estado portugus, ter a autorizao da Direo Geral da Concorrncia e satisfazer o comprador no  tarefa fcil. S quem realmente participou neste processo, e no o chamo para mim,  que sabe a fundo as dificuldades que este encerrou. O que  um facto  que contra ventos e mars conseguimos os objetivos essenciais. No quero dizer com isto que se abre um caminho de facilidades. Vai ser um caminho de exigncia para o novo acionista e para o Fundo de Resoluo, mas  o primeiro banco de transio que se vende na Europa, e ainda num momento de grande crise, com desafios tecnolgicos pela frente e uma carga regulatria considervel. No contexto europeu, no existem grandes investimentos na banca desde 2014. Por outro lado, o comprador veio dos EUA, o que tambm , do ponto de vista do investimento, interessante. O comprador, o Lone Star, fica com o Novo Banco, com uma garantia de risco dos ativos mais problemticos at 3,89 mil milhes, investe 1000 milhes na capitalizao e pe os outros bancos a pagar o que correr mal. No seria mais fcil partir o banco e integr-lo em outros bancos? A resoluo  o quadro que temos organizado para lidar com casos deste gnero. Seria mais disruptivo se o banco fosse partido. Certamente se tivesse aparecido essa possibilidade como vivel teramos de obter as autorizaes necessrias. Ou seja, o BdP estava limitado na atuao da venda que podia fazer? Com certeza. Temos de observar as regras com que lidamos. Manter o Novo Banco como unidade foi muito importante. O mecanismo de contingncia no  uma garantia aos ativos,  uma garantia ao capital do banco. Protege os rcios do banco. Podero dizer: mais isso beneficia os acionistas? Com certeza, mas s indiretamente. Pode haver perdas na venda de ativos e no se verificar a necessidade de injetar capital por parte do fundo.  um processo que me parece, dentro das dificuldades, mais equilibrado. E depois no h facilidades: durante oito anos no se distribuem dividendos, e o Fundo de Resoluo tem uma palavra fundamental sobre a gesto daqueles ativos. Como vai o FR controlar que os novos acionistas vo proteger os vossos interesses se no tem assento na administrao do banco? H poderes concretos que de facto no se traduzem na presena na administrao, e isso  pena, mas no foi porque o comprador no tivesse recetivo. No contexto das negociaes entre o Governo portugus e a DGComp entendeu-se que a presena do Estado era demasiado intrusiva. Por isso, o FR no s no tem assento na administrao como no pode votar na assembleia-geral. Mas tem uma comisso de monitorizao, que ter um papel importante e acesso a informao que no se restringe aos ativos que esto sob a alada do mecanismo de capitalizao contingente. Por outro lado, existem para a gesto do banco restries relativas a transaes com partes relacionadas e um mecanismo de controlo das polticas de crdito e polticas contabilsticas. Do que conhece do Novo Banco e do comprador, que parte  que dos 3,89 mil milhes podero ser usados? No devo exprimir sensibilidades sobre essa matria. Este limite no aconteceu por acaso.  um limite mximo. Depender de muitos fatores, natureza dos ativos, evoluo do mercado, entre outros... Nos ltimos anos, uma srie de gestores bancrios enganou toda a gente, incluindo o supervisor. Como garante que quem comprou o Novo Banco no vai atuar de forma a maximizar as perdas para o FR? Esse problema foi identificado. Quando o BdP teve de proceder  venda, no o fez ignorando as consequncia que isso podia ter para os concorrentes. Alis, muitos relatrios internacionais sublinhavam como constrangimento  nossa economia a ausncia da venda do Novo Banco.  muito difcil manter um sistema na indefinio do que se iria passar com o banco. E por isso se batalhou para criar mecanismos que eliminassem uma eventual perversidade de incentivos e se munir de poderes de fiscalizao. No quisemos s vender o Novo Banco. Tivemos conscincia de que com esta soluo alguns problemas se iriam colocar, e o processo negocial teve as mximas cautelas. Foi um negcio sobre o qual se pode dizer: de mal, o menos? Eu diria: de bem, o menos. Fundo de Resoluo deve estar junto do BdP O vice-governador do Banco de Portugal (BdP) afirma que a situao lquida do Fundo de Resoluo (FR)  negativa para fazer face a novas responsabilidades, ou seja, outra resoluo. Mas as receitas, por via das contribuies da banca, asseguram o pagamento dos emprstimos de duas resolues (BES e Banif). Lus Mximo dos Santos defende que o FR deve estar junto do BdP, mas no o choca que este se autonomize do BdP, tal como acontece em Espanha. Confessa que a dimenso de aes contra o FR e o BdP  grande. E quanto ao Fundo de Garantia de Depsitos (FGD), ao qual preside, diz estar de boa sade e acima do limite mximo exigido para os bancos europeus. Vai continuar a presidir ao Fundo de Resoluo? Vou continuar at o Banco de Portugal o decidir. Defende que o FR deve estar sob a alada do BdP ou deve ser um organismo autnomo? Defendo que deve estar junto do BdP. Mas a matria  complexa. Na Europa h vrios modelos, porque h dimenses diferentes. H uma dimenso preventiva da resoluo e uma dimenso executiva, que diz respeito  determinao da medida de resoluo e sua consequente execuo. Hoje, este problema no se pode colocar nos mesmos termos em que se colocou antes de 1 de janeiro de 2016, data em que o Mecanismo nico de Resoluo entrou em vigor. Por exemplo, o Banco Central de Espanha tem a funo preventiva da resoluo, e h uma instituio  o FROB  que tem uma funo executiva.  natural que a melhor forma de organizar esta funo seja discutida. No faria mais sentido ter uma autoridade nacional de resoluo autnoma com a participao de membros do BdP? Pode ser um modelo. Tal como o Fundo de Garantia de Depsitos, que funciona junto do BdP mas tem personalidade jurdica prpria. Pode criar-se uma autoridade que funcione junto do banco central e que reflita, consoante as matrias que est a decidir, diferentes composies.  um debate que est em aberto. O FGD tem condies de fazer face ao pagamento de depsitos se uma instituio falir? O FGD est acima do limiar que as regras europeias exigem para a sua capitalizao. O FGD est bem capitalizado. O espao para a interveno da garantia de depsitos diminuiu com a figura da resoluo. S em caso de liquidao  que se aciona o FGD. O nosso fundo est mais bem capitalizado do que  exigido pelo limite mximo face s instituies europeias. A relao entre a situao lquida do fundo e os depsitos cobertos pela garantia  de 1,19% , quando a diretiva impe 0,8% at 2024. Em Portugal estamos acima desse patamar. Quantas aes existem contra a resoluo do antigo BES e a venda do Novo Banco e que montantes podem envolver? A contestar a venda no h muitas. H de facto um contencioso bastante relevante contra o BdP e o FR a contestar a medida de resoluo, a transferncia de obrigaes seniores e outros crditos.  possvel ter j uma ideia de quanto pode o FR ter de pagar no mbito destas? No. S quando as decises transitarem em julgado. No  correto falar de valores neste momento. O BdP, nos processos que tem, vai conseguir demonstrar os seus argumentos. Havia cinco providncias cautelares contra a venda. Alguma foi considerada procedente? No. Ficou espantado com a ao do BCP contra o FR por causa do mecanismo criado para gerir os ativos problemticos? Quem est nestas funes no se deve espantar com certas situaes. As instituies so livres de atuarem nos termos que entendam mais adequados na defesa do que acham ser os seus interesses. No me parece haver dvidas de que esta operao beneficia o sistema financeiro em mltiplos tabuleiros: na perceo sobre o pas, em efeitos indiretos nos concorrentes e para efeitos de rating [notao de risco]. Por muito que se possa criticar,  objetivamente positiva para o sistema financeiro portugus. E o BCP faz parte dele. O Banco de Portugal est seguro quanto s decises que toma. O BCP foi o nico banco a colocar uma ao desta natureza? Com estas caractersticas, sim. Como esto as contas do FR neste momento? O FR tem cerca de 250 milhes de receitas, por via das contribuies dos bancos, e gera um cash flow positivo. Anualmente, o fundo est sustentvel para pagar os emprstimos que tem para pagar. Mas tem uma situao lquida negativa. Se houver um incidente com um banco sob a superviso nacional teriam de pedir mais dinheiro? Isso  verdade. A assessoria para a venda do Novo Banco j custou mais de 20 milhes at ao final de 2016. Quem  que paga? A uma determinada altura houve uma dvida sobre se certos custos deviam ser imputados ao BdP enquanto Autoridade Nacional de Resoluo ou ao FR. A questo foi analisada pelo Tribunal de Contas, que entendeu que isso devia ser imputado ao BdP. 85% das sanes confirmadas Mximo dos Santos diz que banca est preparada para novos desafios. Taxa de sucesso das condenaes ronda os 85% O vice-governador do Banco de Portugal, que tem sob a sua alada dois departamentos de peso  a superviso comportamental e os processos de investigao e ao sancionatria  banca , afirma que houve melhorias significativas nos ltimos anos nestas duas vertentes. O reforo de meios na rea comportamental e sancionatria tem revelado que hoje em dia existe um clima mais favorvel ao cumprimento por parte das instituies financeiras, esclarece Lus Mximo dos Santos. Por outro lado, sublinha que o sistema est hoje mais slido, referindo mesmo que todos conhecemos diversas instituies que com estas ou aquelas medidas melhoraram os seus nveis de capitalizao e esto a fazer um esforo para melhorarem os seus mecanismos de organizao interna. Para isso, diz, no  irrelevante o facto de haver uma conscincia mais profunda de que a procura da estabilidade financeira  uma atividade permanente, que no se pode largar. Um dos departamentos mais dinmicos nos ltimos 10 anos tem sido o da investigao e ao sancionatria, com vrios megaprocessos a bancos que acabaram por desaparecer do mapa e sob os quais recaram contraordenaes graves e muito graves. Mximo dos Santos no fala sobre os mesmos, mas refere que o departamento em causa  um dos mais escrutinados. E explica: Muitas das condenaes do Banco de Portugal so objeto de recurso para os tribunais por parte dos acusados e condenados, e nestes casos temos uma taxa de sucesso relativa s condenaes que ronda os 85%. O vice-governador no se refere s s condenaes graves ou muito graves, comuns nos megaprocessos do BPN ou do BPP e j confirmadas pelos tribunais, mas tambm s mais pequenas, como irregularidades de prerio, taxas de juros ou mesmo cobranas de comisses indevidas. Desafios e superviso Quando questionado sobre as baixas taxas de rentabilidade da banca portuguesa, o ainda problema do malparado e os desafios em termos da digitalizao do sector, Mximo dos Santos reconhece as fraquezas e o desafio da mudana de paradigma. Estamos no limiar de uma revoluo digital que vai mudar o modo de atuao dos bancos, mas j houve vrias mudanas desde a dcada de 80 e 90 e o sector respondeu muito bem do ponto de vista da difuso da tecnologia, houve mesmo um salto qualitativo grande. Quanto aos meios adequados do supervisor para fiscalizar a revoluo em marcha, afirma: No s os tem como est a faz-lo. Temos de ter uma estratgia e recursos aptos, auscultando o mercado, garantindo nveis de confiana e proteo dos direitos dos clientes bancrios.

Title: Interview of Administrator Hlder Rosalino to ECO: BdP has an attitude of openness towards Fintech
text: Interview of Administrator Helder... Interview of Administrator Helder Rosalino to ECO: BdP has an attitude of openness towards Fintech 05 nov. 2017 Banco de Portugal has put Fintech into the strategic plan for 2017-2020 and has a attitude of openness, says the administrator. In 2018, it will create a single door of Fintech 'entry'. Banco de Portugal has put Fintech - the technology-based financial startups - in the 2017-2020 activity program. It is one of the priorities, now that the worst phase of the financial system, bank resolutions and their stabilisation is over. In the week of the Web Summit, Helder Rosalino, central bank administrator with the Fintech portfolio, explains in an interview what is at stake and what the objectives are. One of them, for 2018, is to create a single fintech gateway in contact with Banco de Portugal, "to understand the players and to be able to provide them with more aligned services". What is the starting point for technology-based financial enterprises in regulators' perspective? Firstly, the framework at European level must be made. This theme of Fintech and digital banking is on the agenda, both of the European Commission, which has been taking questionnaires on the subject and studies, is on the EBA agenda, is less, but it is on the ECB's agenda. But what has been felt, and I had the opportunity a month ago to have meetings in Brussels about it, is the idea of wait and see. That is... We are seeing a dynamic of Fintech, but they are startups and they do not yet have a very relevant dimension, we are not yet facing a risk to financial stability, a problem in the field of consumer protection. Therefore, there is a {European) understanding that premature intervention is not desirable because it can undermine innovation and new 'entrants', vital for the financial sector, and Europe is lagging behind the US. On the other hand, the European authorities recognise that they cannot remain indifferent to the movements that are taking place and that they promise such an eruption that they cannot put themselves in the position that this is a theme that passes on to them. What is being done in European terms? Working groups have been set up, both in the European Banking Authority (EBA) and in the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM or Mus in the Portuguese version), the European Commission is examining the results of a European questionnaire that had 226 responses, but the approach is still relatively 'soft', because [these entities] do not want to rush into creating mechanisms and regulations limiting innovation in the financial sector. Banks are also beginning to show discomfort at the entry of new players without a European regulatory framework... Nervousness. the banks are getting worried, but the banks will go through several phases, first the phase of indifference, then the phase of irritation and finally will move on to another stage, in which they realize themselves that Fintech have come to stay and have to understand them as entities that can complement their activity and will also be their competitors. And in Portugal, what is being done? Even before that, it is important to point out a European legislative intervention that will be relevant to Fintech, it is the transposition of the European Psd2 Directive, the revised payment services directive, which is due to enter into force on 13 January 2018. Why? Fintech's main area of activity is the payment area, i.e. Fintech covers many areas, but about 50% are in the payment area. Then there are others like crowdfunding, peer-to-peer lending, machine learning, but above all payments, because this is where the revenue is. And, recognizing this, the revised payments directive adapts to the new reality and brings significant opportunities for Fintech. In what sense? The revised Directive frames two new services: account information services and payment initiation services. What are these services? Especially in the first case, they allow a third party, a service provider that is not a bank, to be able to mediate the relationship with a financial institution by accessing accounts, obtaining information about customer accounts. These services are highly innovative and this directive allows Fintech to provide a technological solution that helps a customer manage the relationship with a bank, consolidating a customer's accounts and financial situation, budget management, payments... You can create a set of value-added services, provided by a third party, for individuals and even for companies. And in the case of payment initiation services, what is at stake? A customer, when going to a store, to any service provider such as Fnac or Worten, gives permission for him to himself to initiate his payment. You can allow that service provider to make payments for you by logging into the account without having to mark a code or make an ATM payment. That is, "you can initiate payments on behalf of the user in a convenient and expeditious manner without having to leave the website of the merchant to which you are purchasing a product or service". And we [Banco de Portugal], at PayChallenge - a conference that takes place this Monday afternoon in Lisbon - launched a challenge to startups to develop prototypes of services in these two areas. How will this directive be transposed to Portugal under what conditions? Banco de Portugal, at the request of the Ministry of Finance, submitted at the end of October a proposal to transpose the European Directive after a public consultation and discussion with the banks. And we have had, I think you can classify it that way, an attitude of openness towards Fintech. The options in the various areas were between a more protectionist and less protectionist attitude. In several dimensions, we have had an assessment that favours innovation, favours competition and an environment of flexibility and competitiveness in our payment system, which is the area covered in this Directive. In each country, the reality of Fintech can be seen at different levels... We have followed this topic over the past few years, but we have to say... ... that wasn't a priority? Exactly, it has not been a priority, because the country and Banco de Portugal faced very complicated challenges in relation to the financial system and, therefore, all efforts were few to focus on these issues. But we did not fail to follow the subject, we participated in international working groups, we did a study in 2014 and 2015 on cryptocurrencies and published some warnings... Banco de Portugal has followed this theme, but has not put it at the top of the agenda so far. Fintech and digital banking are central to Banco de Portugal's strategic plan 2017-2020, we have to follow this theme, we have to have a strategy and we have to be close to the sector. These are the three key dimensions and that is why a working group was set up to produce a report presented in April, a very thorough analysis of Fintech and digital banking and the way forward. This analysis involves realizing the dimensions of Fintech's impact on Banco de Portugal's responsibilities and also goes through our own organization in relation to the theme. What does that mean? It sounds simple, but it's complex. Banco de Portugal has multiple departments to monitor the banking sector and the issue of Fintech impacts on financial stability, prudential supervision and business models of banks, with behavioral supervision, even the conduct of monetary policy itself, the topic, moreover, that worries central banks the most despite being the most distant. But also with the sanctioning issues, because, at the limit, these Fintech can facilitate money laundering and terrorist financing. For example, one of the main concerns that critptomoedas bring is the possibility of making payments outside the financial circuit. We are increasingly strengthening the rules of preventing money laundering, politically exposed people, an almost Kafkaesque rendirated for banks that have to make a huge effort to prepare their compliance structures to meet the ever-increasing demands. But what has Banco de Portugal done? A permanent working group has been set up under a structure that already exists, the Specialized Commission for the System and Financial Stability, which has representatives of the various departments of Banco de Portugal and which I myself coordinate. We are now having internal debates and internal reflections on the impact of Fintech. At the same time, we are addressing the interlocutors... Are you talking to the Fintechs? Yes, one of the great initiatives we are going to do is the Pay Challenge conference, in partnership with Cionet, for which we invite Fintech to participate. We identified a set of key interlocutors, we have already had a meeting with the CEO of Easypay, Sebastiao Lancastre, there are already a set of other meetings scheduled, we want to realize the feeling towards the bank and the first interaction was very enlightening ... Fintech's assessment is that Banco de Portugal does not look at this theme. Yes, but they are surprised by the new dynamics of Banco de Portugal and the approach to this sector, the promotion of events. You see that Banco de Portugal is looking at Fintech, we want to do the Fintech Meetings next year. We have also been in a meeting with The Secretary of State for Industry, Ana Lehmann, and we want to develop joint initiatives. At the bottom, it is what some central banks are doing that have the most initiative in this area. What is the reference central bank? The Central Bank of the Netherlands is what lies ahead, has created an 'Inovation Hub', a 'sandbox' which basically what it does is to take these Fintech into the central bank and support them in addressing innovation taking into account the requirements that exist. In this work that we have developed, we also identified the Bank of England, created a Fintech Accelerator, but that does not serve as a comparison, because they have the 'City' and want to have the financial market, and are not in the euro zone and will leave the European Union. The Bank of holland is the one that is most developed, but there are two other relevant. The Bank of Spain has set up an internal group to assess the internal risks associated with Fintech, namely financial stability, which is basically what we have already done. The Bank of France has done something a little more interesting, created a single entry point for Fintech. What is the advantage of this model? Today, what happens? Fintech requests appear throughout departments. They need to liaise with the Department of Prudential Supervision to get a permit, then they relate to the Department of Behavioral Supervision because they want to provide a service, but then they need to talk to the Payments Department. Therefore, our plan for 2018 also goes around, by creating a single gateway, understanding the players to be able to provide them with more aligned services. What the Bank of France did was also a Fintech Forum. We at Banco de Portugal are also preparing a major payments conference, involving banks and fintech. And we want to do other initiatives like the one we did with ECO in April this year [New Money conference], where we sit the banks and the new 'entrants', to create an environment of sharing and reflection.
