text_original: Interveno do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa na Conferncia "Banking Summit | Leading into a new era" 06 fev. 2018 Interveno do Governador do Banco de Portugal, Carlos da Silva Costa [1]  para mim um grande prazer participar nesta edio do Banking Summit. O fenmeno da digitalizao nas economias e nas sociedades est a alterar, de forma irreversvel, os comportamentos e as expetativas dos agentes econmicos em vrios contextos. Conforme ilustraram as discusses desta tarde, o sistema financeiro no  exceo. O ano de 2018 , em muitos sentidos, um ano de verdadeiras transformaes com a entrada em vigor de um conjunto de novas diretivas e regulamentos cujo alcance promete revolucionar o sistema financeiro, e, em particular, o sector bancrio. Destacam se a DSP2[2], a MiFID II[3] e a IFRS9[4]. Na minha interveno de hoje partirei precisamente da introduo da nova Diretiva de Servios de Pagamento (DSP2) como ncora para o debate sobre as implicaes da digitalizao no sector bancrio. Muitos estudos tm apontado a DSP2 como o maior desafio  banca de retalho desde a inveno das ATM, vulgo multibanco, h cerca de 50 anos, ao colocar em risco entre 25% e 40% do produto lquido bancrio (net banking income)[5]. De facto, a DSP2 contribui para a criao de um mercado nico para os servios de pagamento promotor da concorrncia, que incentiva a inovao e a mudana, ao introduzir a possibilidade de criao dos servios de informao sobre contas e dos servios de iniciao de pagamentos por prestadores que se consideram terceiros na relao entre o utilizador e o seu banco. Esta abertura a prestadores de servios que se consideram terceiros na relao entre o utilizador e o seu banco abre o espao para a entrada de novos concorrentes que detm uma vantagem tecnolgica, como as FinTech, e se especializam em nichos de mercado ou que dispem e operam j com bases gigantes, como a Google, o Facebook, a Amazon e a Apple, e tm experincia na gesto de big data. Para os incumbentes, trata-se de um desafio mas tambm de uma oportunidade. As FinTech no devem ser vistas apenas como concorrentes dos prestadores tradicionais. Tambm podem ser instituies complementares ou parceiras. Em particular, podem ser instrumentais, ajudando os incumbentes a ultrapassar as condicionantes associadas ao baixo crescimento da atividade e  baixa rentabilidade e, ainda, a restabelecer e reforar os nveis de confiana e de reputao, postos em causa com a crise financeira de 2007. De facto, o acesso a novas tecnologias e a utilizao de inteligncia artificial vo determinar uma transformao do lado da oferta, na medida em que permitem extrair mais informao das bases de dados de que os bancos dispem. Desse modo, vo permitir uma melhor adequao da oferta das instituies financeiras s necessidades dos seus clientes, quer ao nvel do retalho (robo-advice) atravs da promoo de produtos de crdito ou poupana ajustados s preferncias dos financiados ou dos aforradores, quer atravs da conceo de propostas de investimento e de gesto de patrimnio que tiram partido da capacidade de operar com mais produtos e mais mercados e conceber produtos ajustados a perfis mais finos de preferncias reveladas pelos investidores (wealth management). Ao mesmo tempo, vo permitir uma maior adequao do risco do produto ao perfil do cliente e uma maior acuidade na avaliao do risco de crdito. E vo permitir, ainda, uma maior capacidade de gesto do risco e de determinao do correspondente preo, afinando e segmentando a avaliao do perfil de risco dos seus clientes, atravs do tratamento da informao socioeconmica e de uma viso precisa e atualizada da sua posio financeira com a utilizao em larga escala de modelos de credit scoring. Ao mesmo tempo, os bancos tm de se adaptar a uma nova realidade do lado da procura, confrontados com clientes que procuram solues flexveis, personalizadas, imediatas, em qualquer stio a qualquer momento  ATAWADAC (Any Time, Any Where, Any Device, Any Content) , reformulando a sua prpria oferta.  medida que novos players totalmente digitais entram no mercado providos de licenas para operar em livre prestao de servios, comea-se a questionar at quando ser necessria uma to vasta rede de balces como aquela que ainda caracteriza os sistemas bancrios de vrios pases Europeus. A resposta a esta questo vai depender do grau de literacia financeira e digital da populao, da forma como as diversas geraes valorizam a confidencialidade das suas informaes bancrias e da medida em que a proteo de dados seja assegurada. Na ausncia de literacia digital e, em particular, do entendimento das implicaes que a maior partilha de informao financeira comporta, os clientes bancrios ficam expostos a aes ilegais e fraudes. Importa, pois, que as diversas instituies, e em particular os bancos, promovam a consciencializao dos clientes bem como os nveis mnimos de literacia financeira e digital para que estes entendam que o aumento de opes e produtos traz consigo um maior grau de responsabilizao[6]. Simultaneamente, as novas possibilidades de tratamento e transmisso de informao vieram dar a oportunidade s entidades que, no sendo do setor bancrio, foram ao longo do tempo acumulando grandes bases de dados e experincia no respetivo tratamento automtico de grandes massas de informao. Essa experincia garante uma vantagem competitiva face aos incumbentes: as suas extensas bases de dados, capacidades analticas e de processamento de dados so fatores competitivos que lhes permitem explorar atividades financeiras ajustadas ao perfil de cada cliente. Embora os bancos tenham a seu favor o (re)conhecimento do pblico e a capacidade fiduciria acumulada, as suas bases de dados so limitadas geograficamente por comparao com as das empresas tecnolgicas  escala global. Passando o mass market a estar cada vez mais dependente da oferta dos grandes players, os bancos locais tendero a passar a ser redes complementares de colocao de produtos de marca branca e de recolha de fundos sem capacidades tecnolgicas nem de escala. Neste contexto, comeam a emergir dois cenrios[7] enquanto resultado dos desafios da digitalizao com que o sector bancrio se confronta: Um cenrio de inrcia, onde os bancos no respondem a estes desafios, e se confrontam com uma compresso das margens e limitao de cross-subsidiation, acabando por se tornar meras plataformas de captao de depsitos e de colocao de produtos, com a criao de valor a ocorrer fora da sua esfera, levando ou a uma progressiva perda de contacto com os clientes, ou a uma incapacidade de os trabalhar de forma autnoma. O conhecimento/contacto transfere-se para gigantes digitais que, j possuindo acesso a vastos conjuntos de informao dos clientes, comearo a focar se na cadeia de valor do sector bancrio, podendo, no limite, originar um efeito de crowding out dos bancos. E um segundo cenrio, de profunda transformao do sector, em que os bancos internalizam as novas tecnologias, atravs da aquisio ou do desenvolvimento interno de FinTechs e solues tecnolgicas afins. Neste cenrio, os bancos tiram partido da confiana e notoriedade histrica que tm junto dos seus clientes para promover solues cada vez mais focadas nas necessidades dos consumidores, que lhes permitem capturar novas fontes de receita ao mesmo tempo que reduzem vrios custos de funcionamento. Estes cenrios no so mutuamente exclusivos, e o resultado final poder bem ser uma combinao de ambos, originando um efeito de concentrao dentro do sector para criar sinergias. Assim, torna-se imperativo que a gesto dos bancos ao mais alto nvel possua competncias digitais suficientes[8] para enriquecer as discusses sobre as implicaes para o seu modelo de negcio e a forma de lhes dar resposta. Num contexto regulatrio ainda em mutao, e atento o estado de incompletude da Unio Bancria na Europa,  imperativo que o sector bancrio tenha uma viso holstica dos desafios com que se confronta, dando-lhe uma resposta atempada e consentnea com o papel que quer desempenhar na sociedade. Do ponto de vista de risco, importa notar que embora ainda no existam estudos empricos suficientes para aferir quais as implicaes da digitalizao do sector bancrio, h quem aponte para a existncia de menor volatilidade mas um aumento do risco sistmico (i.e. caudas mais largas) devido ao maior uso de inteligncia artificial[9]. Alm disso, a extenso da cobertura geogrfica promovida pela digitalizao e os diversos players em interao colocar desafios renovados  salvaguarda da estabilidade financeira que importar acautelar. A digitalizao comporta igualmente desafios para os bancos centrais e reguladores. A nova arquitetura e os novos modelos de negcio obrigam a uma resposta multidisciplinar dos bancos centrais e reguladores, exigem novas abordagens, recursos e competncias, de forma a maximizar as oportunidades e a minimizar os riscos para a sociedade. Desta forma,  muito importante que as autoridades competentes no interrompam a dinmica em curso, mas a enquadrem e assegurem, nomeadamente: A neutralidade da regulao, eliminando os fatores inibidores da adoo de tecnologias (seguras e eficientes) no desenvolvimento da atividade financeira. O tratamento justo e equilibrado entre incumbentes e novos entrantes, bem como entre jurisdies, no colocando em causa a confiana pblica na prestao de servios. A identificao de novos riscos e desafios colocados pela disponibilizao de servios financeiros de base tecnolgica e a adoo de iniciativas regulatrias e de superviso adequadas por forma a evitar zonas sombra com menores exigncias ao mesmo tempo que se garante a proteo de dados. Uma atuao coordenada entre reguladores e supervisores a nvel nacional e europeu. Neste sentido, espero que o Banking Summit se transforme num valioso contributo para ajudar  construo de uma viso tanto quanto possvel partilhada sobre os desafios e os benefcios que a transformao digital pode introduzir no funcionamento do setor bancrio. Title: Initial intervention by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in the Committee on Work and Social Security and in the Committee on Budget and Finance and Administrative Modernization
text: Initial Intervention of Governor C... Initial intervention by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in the Committee on Work and Social Security and in the Committee on Budget and Finance and Administrative Modernization Feb. 14. 2018 Initial Intervention of Governor Carlos da Silva Costa [1] Mr President, Ladies and gentlemen, Good morning In this brief initial speech I would like to leave some notes clarifying the role of Banco de Portugal in the issue that is the subject of my coming to this Commission, as well as on a number of related topics. 1. The possible entry of SCML into cemg's capital My presence in this Commission was requested in order to "provide all clarifications on the contours surrounding the hypothesis of the Santa Casa da Misericordia de Lisboa (SCML) entering the capital of Caixa Economica Montepio Geral, S.A. (CEMG)." On this topic it is important to me to point out that: Banco de Portugal (i) did not induce the conduct of any deal between SCML and The Montepio Geral - Mutual Association (MGAM), (ii) does not even have to comment decision to divest part of CEMG's capital to SCML. The decision to divest a shareholding by a shareholder is responsibility and not that of the supervisor. The terms of the implementation may, however, be subject to the supervisor's scrutiny and subsequent conditioning. Banco de Portugal values the diversification of the shareholder structure of any institution by itself supervised as an enabling mechanism for responding to prudential requirements. In this context, Banco de Portugal has assumed, in a generally, a position of principle in favour of the entry of a new shareholder into the CEMG. At the moment, Banco de Portugal does not have, nor would it have to have, concrete information on the terms of a possible transfer to the SCML on the part of the mgam has in CEMG. These are negotiations between two private entities (SCML and MGAM), not subject to the supervision of Banco de Portugal, whose financial decisions (rational and opportunity) are of their exclusive responsibility. 2. The provision of information by Banco de Portugal to this Commission On the provision of information by Banco de Portugal regarding CEMG, I would like to remind you that it is conditioned by the following factors: Firstly, CEMG is a bank in full operation, so that Banco de Portugal is bound by the duty of professional secrecy established in Article 80 of the General Regime of Credit Institutions and Financial. Secondly, the supervision of credit institutions is the responsibility of the Single Supervisory Mechanism, which delegates this responsibility to the national supervisory authorities in relation to institutions classified as Less Significant Institutions, maintaining their follow-up. 3. The transformation of CEMG into a Public Limited Company In the light of these limitations, the following should be highlighted. Until the end of 2015, CEMG operated as an economic cash that operated with its mutual association  MGAM  sharing with this its management body. With the entry into force of Decree-Law No. 190/2015, of September 10, the latest Legal Regime of Economic Boxes was approved in order to contribute to the robustness, autonomy and quality of government of the economic boxes. Under that scheme, CEMG is classified as a bank economy teller (as opposed to the attached cash registers). In November 2016, Banco de Portugal determined the transformation of CEMG into public limited liability company, after consulting the Securities Market Commission. CEMG then amended its statutes. Banco de Portugal authorized the transformation and the CEMG general meeting deliberated on the issue in April 2017. CEMG is today an autonomous legal entity organized in the form of a public limited company, clearly autonomous from the organic point of view and government model, in relation to its shareholder. As a bank economy cashier, it is treated as a bank and is subject to the General Regime of Credit Institutions and their related legislation. 4. Strengthening the identity of CEMG and separation of MGAM A path has been taken to strengthen CEMG's identity and effectively split the shareholder (MGAM). The process of separation/differentiation of brands, part of a wide range of actions that have been developed at the level of internal government, is motivated by the need for transparency about issuers and the nature of products placed over the counter of institutions. CEMG, like other institutions, is subject to the rules in force in order to provide all information to investors about who the issuers are and the characteristics of the products marketed by it. Such issuers and products may be subject to specifically applicable supervision depending on their nature. In the specific case of MGAM, it is an entity not subject to the supervision of Banco de Portugal, supervised by the Ministry of Labor, Solidarity and Social Security. It is not banco de Portugal's responsibility to monitor its operations, nor are the products issued by MGAM subject to the supervision of Banco de Portugal. However, because MGAM products are also marketed at CEMG branches, and in order to address the risks of an incorrect perception of the nature of products issued by MGAM by customers and the general public, in particular the possible confounding of these products with bank deposits, Banco de Portugal has been monitoring the issue, prudential perspective, so that each investor is properly informed. In this context, Banco de Portugal ordered CEMG to submit an action plan to ensure the separation between both brands, in order to make the differences between the two institutions publicly perceptible clearly and unequivocally. To comply with this determination, CEMG presented an ongoing action plan, with emphasis on: (i) the creation of our own mutual spaces and with own managers at CEMG branches, focused exclusively on the supply of MGAM products (called "Mutual Posts"); (ii) the renaming of CEMG products, reinforcing the name "Caixa Economica", and (iii) The change in the digital platforms used in interaction with customers, highlighting the redesign of cemg's website, which now has its own segregated page of the MGAM website. In addition, Banco de Portugal ordered CEMG to develop a conflict-of-interest prevention policy, which includes specific guidelines on relationships with related parties. It should be clarified that Banco de Portugal has not determined the creation of a new brand. Such a decision depends exclusively on the will of CEMG and its shareholder(s), who may take this option if they believe that it is essential to address the prudential concerns expressed by Banco de Portugal. I am at your disposal to answer any questions they consider relevant. Thank you very much. [1] Ready for presentation.

Interveno Inicial do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa na Comisso de Trabalho e Segurana Social e na Comisso de Oramento e Finanas e Modernizao Administrativa 14 fev. 2018 Interveno Inicial do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa [1] Senhor Presidente, Senhoras e Senhores Deputados, Bom dia, Nesta breve interveno inicial gostaria de deixar algumas notas de clarificao do papel do Banco de Portugal na questo que  objeto da minha vinda a esta Comisso, bem como sobre um conjunto de temas relacionados. 1. A possvel entrada da SCML no capital da CEMG A minha presena nesta Comisso foi solicitada a fim de prestar todos os esclarecimentos sobre os contornos que envolvem a hiptese da Santa Casa da Misericrdia de Lisboa (SCML) entrar no capital da Caixa Econmica Montepio Geral, S. A. (CEMG). Sobre esta temtica afigura-se-me importante salientar que: O Banco de Portugal (i) no induziu a realizao de qualquer negcio entre a SCML e o Montepio Geral  Associao Mutualista (MGAM), (ii) nem tem de se pronunciar sobre qualquer deciso de alienao de parte de capital da CEMG  SCML. A deciso de alienao de uma participao de capital por parte de um acionista  da sua responsabilidade e no do supervisor. Os termos da concretizao podem, contudo, estar sujeitos ao escrutnio do supervisor e seu subsequente condicionamento. O Banco de Portugal valoriza a diversificao da estrutura acionista de qualquer instituio por si supervisionada enquanto mecanismo habilitador de resposta s exigncias prudenciais. Neste contexto, o Banco de Portugal tem assumido, de uma forma geral, uma posio de princpio favorvel  entrada de um novo acionista na CEMG. Neste momento, o Banco de Portugal no dispe, nem teria de dispor, de informao concreta sobre os termos de uma eventual cedncia  SCML de parte da participao que o MGAM tem na CEMG. Tratam-se de negociaes entre duas entidades privadas (SCML e MGAM), no sujeitas  superviso do Banco de Portugal, cujas decises financeiras (racional e oportunidade) so da sua exclusiva responsabilidade. 2. A prestao de informao pelo Banco de Portugal a esta Comisso Sobre a prestao de informao pelo Banco de Portugal relativamente  CEMG, gostaria de recordar que esta se encontra condicionada pelos seguintes fatores: Em primeiro lugar, a CEMG  uma instituio bancria em plena atividade, pelo que o Banco de Portugal se encontra vinculado pelo dever de segredo profissional estabelecido no artigo 80. do Regime Geral das Instituies de Crdito e Sociedades Financeiras. Em segundo lugar, a superviso das instituies de crdito  da responsabilidade do Mecanismo nico de Superviso, o qual delega essa responsabilidade nas autoridades de superviso nacionais relativamente s instituies classificadas como Less Significant Institutions, mantendo o respetivo acompanhamento. 3. A transformao da CEMG em Sociedade Annima  luz das referidas limitaes, releva destacar o seguinte. At finais de 2015, a CEMG exerceu a atividade como uma caixa econmica que funcionava junto da respetiva associao mutualista  o MGAM , partilhando com esta o seu rgo de administrao. Com a entrada em vigor do Decreto-Lei n. 190/2015, de 10 de setembro, foi aprovado o mais recente Regime Jurdico das Caixas Econmicas no sentido de contribuir para a robustez, autonomia e qualidade de governo das caixas econmicas. Ao abrigo do referido regime, a CEMG  qualificada como caixa econmica bancria (por oposio s caixas econmicas anexas). Em novembro de 2016, o Banco de Portugal determinou a transformao da CEMG em sociedade annima, aps consulta  Comisso do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios. A CEMG alterou ento os seus estatutos. O Banco de Portugal autorizou a transformao e a assembleia geral da CEMG deliberou sobre a questo em abril de 2017.   A CEMG  hoje uma entidade jurdica autnoma organizada sob a forma de sociedade annima, claramente autonomizada do ponto de vista orgnico e de modelo de governo, em relao ao seu acionista. Enquanto caixa econmica bancria,  equiparada a um banco e encontra-se sujeita ao Regime Geral das Instituies de Crdito e respetiva legislao conexa. 4. Reforo da identidade da CEMG e separao do MGAM Tem sido trilhado um caminho de reforo da identidade da CEMG e de efetiva separao do acionista (o MGAM). O processo de separao/diferenciao de marcas, parte de um conjunto alargado de aes que tm vindo a ser desenvolvidas ao nvel do governo interno,  motivado pela necessidade de transparncia sobre os emitentes e a natureza dos produtos colocados ao balco das instituies. A CEMG,  semelhana de outras instituies, est sujeita s regras vigentes por forma a fornecer toda a informao aos investidores sobre quem so os emitentes e as caractersticas dos produtos por si comercializados. Tais emitentes e produtos podem estar sujeitos a superviso especificamente aplicvel consoante a sua natureza. No caso em concreto do MGAM, trata-se de uma entidade no sujeita  superviso do Banco de Portugal, tutelada pelo Ministrio do Trabalho, Solidariedade e Segurana Social. No compete ao Banco de Portugal fiscalizar a sua atuao, nem os produtos emitidos pelo MGAM se encontram sujeitos  superviso do Banco de Portugal. No entanto, em virtude de os produtos do MGAM tambm serem comercializados aos balces da CEMG, e tendo em vista acautelar os riscos de uma perceo incorreta da natureza dos produtos emitidos pelo MGAM por parte dos clientes e do pblico em geral, designadamente a eventual confundibilidade desses produtos com depsitos bancrios, o Banco de Portugal tem vindo a acompanhar a questo, numa perspetiva prudencial, para que cada investidor esteja devidamente esclarecido. Neste contexto, o Banco de Portugal determinou  CEMG a apresentao de um plano de ao que assegurasse a separao entre ambas as marcas, de modo a tornar publicamente percetvel, de forma clara e inequvoca, as diferenas entre as duas instituies. Para dar cumprimento a esta determinao, a CEMG apresentou um plano de ao que se encontra em curso, com destaque para: (i) A criao de espaos prprios mutualistas e com gestores prprios nos balces da CEMG, focados em exclusivo na oferta de produtos do MGAM (designados por Postos Mutualistas); (ii) A redenominao dos produtos da CEMG, reforando a denominao Caixa Econmica,e (iii) A alterao das plataformas digitais utilizadas na interao com os clientes , sendo de realar a reformulao do stio de Internet da CEMG, que passou a dispor de uma pgina prpria e segregada da pgina do MGAM. Adicionalmente, o Banco de Portugal determinou  CEMG a elaborao de uma poltica de preveno de conflito de interesses, que inclusse orientaes especficas em matria de relacionamento com partes relacionadas. Cumpre esclarecer que o Banco de Portugal no determinou a criao de uma nova marca. Tal deciso depende exclusivamente da vontade da CEMG e do(s) seu(s) acionista(s), os quais podero tomar essa opo se entenderem que a mesma  essencial para dar resposta s preocupaes prudenciais manifestadas pelo Banco de Portugal. Estou  disposio dos Senhores Deputados para responder s questes que considerem pertinentes. Muito obrigado. [1] Preparado para apresentao.

Title: Intervention of Deputy Governor Luis Maximo dos Santos in the opening of the Training Course for Trainers in Personal Finance Management organized by Banco de Portugal, Central Bank of Brazil and Alliance for Financial Inclusion
text: Intervention of The Deputy Governor Luis... Intervention of Deputy Governor Luis Maximo dos Santos in the opening of the Training Course for Trainers in Personal Finance Management organized by Banco de Portugal, Central Bank of Brazil and Alliance for Financial Inclusion Feb. 19. 2018 I. Welcome to Lisbon, welcome to Banco de Portugal. On behalf of Banco de Portugal, I would like to thank you for your presence and address a special greeting to the Central Bank of Brazil and the Alliance for Financial Inclusion (AFI, in the Acronym in English) for the joint organization of this course. This initiative is yet another testimony that cooperation between the Central Banks of Portuguese-speaking Countries (BCPLP), which already has a long history, is a good example at international level. The sharing of experiences among BCPLP in the context of inclusion and financial training took on a more permanent character, from 2013, with the I BCPLP Meeting on inclusion and financial training in Lisbon, followed by two more meetings in 2015 and 2017. These meetings have always had a very active participation on the part of all BCPLP, reflecting not only the importance that central banks attach to the theme of financial inclusion and training, but also of the wealth that this sharing has meant for all of us. Inclusion and financial training are essential for responsible financial citizenship and are important whatever the national context. In the contemporary world, the financial sector has taken on unprecedented prominence. This makes the themes of financial inclusion and literacy even more important. Financial inclusion is one of the dimensions of social inclusion and, to that extent, is a factor of inclusive economic development. Financial literacy, in turn, is not limited to people's knowledge of the characteristics and functioning of financial products and services. Includes also the way people deal with money, how they make their consumer decisions, what motivates them to save or borrow money  what we call financial attitudes and behaviours. International studies, in particular financial literacy surveys, show deficits in financial literacy (both in terms of knowledge and attitudes and behaviour) in all countries in which they are carried out. On the other hand, how to deal with these financial literacy deficits, priorities in terms of themes and audiences, the communication channels to be used depend on the economic, financial and institutional context of each country. This sharing between the central banks of Lusophony is therefore of enormous value, since it puts around the table a set of very diverse approaches, which, even if they cannot be directly transposed to other countries, allow us to know and reflect on how they can be adapted to each national context. It allows us not only to know the initiatives that have been successful in each country, but also to know what went least well. We are thus all in a better position to make the most correct choices in the implementation of inclusion and financial training policies. In the framework of the III BCPLP Meeting on Inclusion and Financial Training, which took place in Lisbon in July 2017, a Protocol of cooperation between the BCPLP and the AFI was signed, an initiative that provided us with another instrument to deepen our cooperation. This Protocol recognizes and frames the institutional collaboration between these entities, with a view to carrying out projects to strengthen competencies to promote inclusion and financial training in Portuguese-speaking countries. It deepens the mechanisms for sharing experience and technical support that have marked cooperation between BCPLP, as it joins a partner (the AFI) with knowledge and experience of implementing in the field of inclusion and financial training initiatives specifically targeted to increase access for the most disadvantaged populations to appropriate financial services. For Banco de Portugal it is an opportunity to collaborate with this international organization and - like the other BCPLP - to be able to benefit and be able to contribute to the sharing of knowledge and the identification of international best practices to promote inclusion and financial training. II. The training course for trainers in personal finance management that today we start is the first initiative developed under this Protocol, to which we hope that many others will follow. For the diversity of cultures that we have gathered here in this room and for the innovative character of the course, I am sure that this will be a very enriching experience for all present. On the one hand, here are technicians from four central banks, with experience in personal finance training in four countries (Angola, Brazil, Mozambique and Portugal) with different cultures, despite historical affinities, so the sharing of views will certainly be very interesting. On the other hand, it is a course with a singular structure, since the sessions are promoted by trainers of two central banks (Portugal and Brazil), thus promoting, from the outset, a greater diversity in the approach to the different themes. Let me highlight here the presence of employees of the Regional Network of Banco de Portugal who came from the Azores, evora, Faro and Viseu to be with us this week. The Banco de Portugal Regional Network has developed a fundamental work to bring financial training to local populations throughout the country and will have here an opportunity to contact with new approach methodologies, which can enrich the excellent work they already develop. I hope that this will be a well-spent week in Lisbon and that the sharing of experience and training methodologies will be useful to support the implementation of your own training initiatives in these areas.

Title: Speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the Launch Session of the Book of Homage to Jos da Silva Lopes
text: Speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the Launch Session of the Book of Homage to Jose da Silva Lopes 20 mar. 2018 Speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa [1] For Banco de Portugal it is an honor to join the launch of the book Estudos de Homenagem to Jose da Silva Lopes. This is a more than just tribute to a an economist who has been able to honor his profession and an exemplary man, both as a servant of the public cause and through his permanent civic intervention. The enormous appreciation and admiration that Banco de Portugal has for the unique figure of Dr. Jose da Silva Lopes has already been expressed on several occasions, which I note two conferences of tribute: i. In December 2003, the Conference organised jointly with other entities  including the Higher Institute of Economics and Management (ISEG)  in recognition of the outstanding and multifaceted career of Dr. Silva Lopes. We had, at the time, the privilege to also count on their presence, their informed opinions and their intellectual honesty and their proverbial and self-proclaimed pessimismo; ii. In December 2015, already after his death, the International Conference of the Bank, in which they bore witness to a number of national and international individualities who, in various capacities, have had the privilege to deprive with Dr. Silva Lopes. Dr. Jose da Silva Lopes was one of the most eminent and recognized Portuguese economists of the last fifty years, having been an attentive researcher of the national economy. As a professional, he was able to combine two important characteristics that made him a complete economist: i. A solid theoretical knowledge base; ii. A practical knowledge, destemming from the experience of those who were in the first and was the protagonist of the great transformations of the Portuguese economy in last decades. Although he did not opt for an academic career, his curriculum, both from an analytical and didactic point of view, is noteable. He was the author of a vast bibliography, including studies that are still a mandatory reference for students and researchers of the Portuguese economy, a subject he knew in depth, as very few. As an illustrative one, I would point out that the book The Portuguese Economy since 1960, which provides a systematized and detailed view of economic evolution from 1960 to the 1990s, without forgetting the institutional framework and economic regulation before and after 1974. Many other studies could refer to the vast legacy he has left us. He also dedicated much of his life to university teaching, with the conduction of several courses in various faculties. Throughout his professional career, he has held many prestigious positions, including those of Minister of Finance, Governor of Banco de Portugal, Member of the Assembly of the Republic, President of the Economic and Social Council and Administrator of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development. At the time of his death, in April 2015, he was a member, by inegency, of the Advisory Board of Banco de Portugal, with an assertive presence and constructive interpelacao that I have always greatly valued. At international level, we must not forget its very active involvement in the negotiations for Portugal's accession to EFTA (1959) and GATT (1961) and in the preparation of the Free Trade Agreement with the EEC (1972). He has also served on multiple occasions as a consultant to the World Bank and other international bodies. In the 1990s, he played a key role in the recast of the legislation applicable to the Portuguese financial system, as rapporteur of the Council for the Financial System, which I myself personally integrated. From the work carried out, the White Paper on the Financial System (1992) resulted, which served as the basis for the overall reform of the existing regulatory framework. Governor of Banco de Portugal between 1975 and 1980, Dr. Jose da Silva Lopes led the bank's management at a particularly difficult time in the country's recent economic and financial history. As Governor, he played a central role in overcoming the balance of payments crisis of 1977 that imposed a change in the priorities of Portuguese economic policy. In this capacity, he was responsible for the introduction in Portugal of the creeping-peg regime of the shield, which helped to overcome the period of great economic and financial instability experienced following the first oil shock and the profound political, economic and social changes in our country. As he later stated, "crawling-peg was one of the miracles of the Portuguese economy. Every time my historical pessimism didn't work was because of some miracle!" [2] The scale of the challenges it had to face becomes even more significant if it was seen in the light of Banco de Portugal's history and what was the reality of the Bank at the time it took office. After nationalization in September 1974, the Organic Law published in November 1975, granted Banco de Portugal the status of central bank and included, for the first time, the function of supervision of the banking system. On the other hand, the Bank's activity took place in a context where there was little access to sources of information and theoretical studies and the available statistics were very incomplete and unsophisticated. Perfectly aware of the difficulties and constraints that exist, Dr. Silva Lopes bet from an early age on the involvement of internationally renowned economists and an MIT team, who brought knowledge, strategic vision and new instruments. As Governor, he laid the foundations for a department of studies and statistics properly equipped in terms of knowledge and skills, contributing decisively to the affirmation of Banco de Portugal as a center of excellence in economic analysis. Its role has undoubtedly been decisive for strengthening the prestige of economic research carried out at the institution, also serving as an inducer of the quantitative and qualitative strengthening of economic research in Portugal. The legacy he left intact and is found in the Banco de Portugal Archive sits not only on the great challenges he had to face as Governor but also in his exemplary way of working. Thank you very much. [1] Ready for presentation. [2] Interview with Exame magazine in December 2004, republished by Expresso in April 2015.

Governador do Banco de Portugal entre 1975 e 1980, o Dr. Jos da Silva Lopes conduziu a gesto do Banco num momento particularmente difcil da histria econmica e financeira recente do Pas. Enquanto Governador, teve um papel central na superao da crise de balana de pagamentos de 1977 que imps uma alterao das prioridades da poltica econmica portuguesa. Nessa capacidade, foi responsvel pela introduo em Portugal do regime cambial de desvalorizao deslizante (crawling-peg) do escudo, que ajudou a ultrapassar o perodo de grande instabilidade econmica e financeira vivido na sequncia do primeiro choque petrolfero e das profundas alteraes polticas, econmicas e sociais no nosso Pas. Como o prprio declarou mais tarde, o crawling-peg foi um dos milagres da economia portuguesa. Todas as vezes que o meu pessimismo histrico no funcionou foi por causa de um milagre qualquer!. [2] A dimenso dos desafios que teve de enfrentar torna-se ainda mais significativa se perspetivada  luz da histria do Banco de Portugal e daquilo que era a realidade do Banco na altura em que assumiu funes. Depois da nacionalizao, em setembro de 1974, a Lei Orgnica publicada em novembro de 1975, atribua ao Banco de Portugal o estatuto de banco central e inclua, pela primeira vez, a funo de superviso do sistema bancrio. Por outro lado, a atividade do Banco decorria num quadro em que era escasso o acesso a fontes de informao e a estudos tericos e as estatsticas disponveis eram muito incompletas e pouco sofisticadas. Perfeitamente ciente das dificuldades e dos constrangimentos existentes, o Dr. Silva Lopes apostou desde cedo no envolvimento de economistas de renome internacional e de uma equipa do MIT, que trouxeram conhecimento, viso estratgica e novos instrumentos. Enquanto Governador, lanou as bases de um departamento de estudos e de estatsticas devidamente equipado em termos de conhecimento e de competncias, contribuindo decisivamente para a afirmao do Banco de Portugal como um centro de excelncia na anlise econmica. O seu papel foi, indubitavelmente, determinante para o reforo do prestgio da investigao econmica realizada na instituio, servindo tambm como indutor do reforo quantitativo e qualitativo da investigao econmica em Portugal. O legado que deixou intacto e se encontra no Arquivo do Banco de Portugal  testemunho no s dos grandes desafios que teve de enfrentar enquanto Governador mas tambm da sua forma exemplar de trabalhar. Muito obrigado. [1] Preparado para apresentao. [2] Entrevista  revista Exame em dezembro de 2004, republicada pelo Expresso em abril de 2015.

Title: Intervention of The Deputy Governor Elisa Ferreira at the hearing of Banco de Portugal in the Committee on Budget, Finance and Administrative Modernization: Bill No. 90/XIII/1st (BE)
text: In other words... Intervention of The Deputy Governor Elisa Ferreira at the hearing of Banco de Portugal in the Committee on Budget, Finance and Administrative Modernization: Bill No. 90/XIII/1st (BE) 06 Apr 2018 Madam President, Ladies and gentlemen, I would like to thank Banco de Portugal for its invitation to comment on Bill No. 90/XIII/1, which establishes the imposition of credit institutions reflecting negative interest rates on credit agreements granted to consumers for residential properties. Let me, ladies and gentlemen, begin by recalling that Banco de Portugal has previously had the opportunity to convey to this Commission its position on the subject of the bill under discussion. I would therefore like to recall and reiterate the understanding that was conveyed in the speeches of the Director of the Department of Behavioral Supervision and the Director of the Department of Prudential Supervision and the Bank of Portugal on 29 March 2016, and later at the hearing of the Governor which took place on 27 April of the same year. As has been pointed out then, the existing legal framework includes a rule according to which the interest rate of home loans  resulting from the sum of the spread of the interest rate with the indexer  must reflect the evolution of that same indexer. Indeed, it follows from article 21(2) of the new legal regime of mortgage credit, approved by Decree-Law No. 74-A/2017 of 23 June  which incorporated the rule previously provided for in Article 3 of Decree-Law No. 240/2006 of December 22  which, in situations where the interest rate of housing loan contracts is subject to a certain index, it shall result from the simple arithmetic average of the daily quotes of the index or reference rate observed in the month prior to the beginning of the interest counting period. Circular Letter No. 26/2015/DSC of 30 March 2015 reiterated this regulatory command and was transmitted to credit institutions that "(...) comply with the conditions laid down for determining the interest rate in credit and financing agreements concluded with their customers (...)", and "limits may be imposed on the variation of the indexer which prevent the full production of the effects arising from the application of this legal rule". However, this rule cannot fail to be interpreted in conjunction with other legally enshrined rules and principles. Thus, it has been argued by Banco de Portugal that the application of that provision should, inter alia, take into account the principle of the onerousness of the market loan, provided for in Article 395 of the Commercial Code, as well as the general principle of the balance between the contractual considerations in question. Banco de Portugal has also drawn attention to the function of financial intermediation of credit institutions, collecting investments (savings) from customers and applying them in the granting of credit, a function that is crucial for the functioning of the banking system and, consequently, an indispensable support for the development of the economy. This intermediation role has an inherent cost, not only financial (margin)  which implies the balanced treatment between the remuneration of customers' resources (it should be noted that the current legislation does not allow the application of negative rates on deposits) and the interest received as a result of the credit operations granted  but also of capital, since the granting of credit implies an allocation of funds that the credit institution has to carry out in the face of the risk inherent in this activity. The close relationship between credit and deposits is particularly relevant in the Portuguese financial system, where the relationship between credit and deposit amounts is now, and unlike the past, very close (transformation ratio of 93%), reinforcing the need to prevent asymmetries between assets and liabilities. It is more important that the Eurosystem's monetary policy operations only account for about 7% of the total financing of Portuguese banks, and only one of the types of refinancing operations  the so-called Targeted Long Term Refinancing Operations (TLTRO)  may have a negative rate (in the range of values between 0.0% and -0.40%). However, those requirements relate primarily to the granting of credit to banks, but only to the SME and consumer credit segment, and housing credit is not regarded for this purpose. This is not the case that the Portuguese banks are not able to finance themselves at negative rates. In this context, and as has been transmitted by Banco de Portugal, it is considered that only the legislature may, if it so chooses and after considering all the interests involved, clarify the rules applicable in cases where the interest rate on housing credit agreements reaches, as a result of the variation in the index, a negative value. The legislative initiative under discussion indicates that the legislator intends to intervene in this area. I would like to point out that the challenge posed to the national legislature is particularly complex, since we are not aware that, within the European Union, legislative or regulatory initiatives have been developed to establish express guidance on how negative interest rates are applied in housing credit agreements. It is, of course, up to the legislator to seek to find the solutions that best articulate the different interests in attendance, promoting the contractual balance between the parties and the sustainability of the financial system. Looking at the content of the legislative initiative under discussion, Banco de Portugal notes that, in its view, some of the proposed provisions would benefit from further clarification or precision, in order to remove any difficulties in its practical application and to ensure their implementation harmonised by credit institutions. Thus, for example, it may be appropriate to realise some aspects of the options given to credit institutions to reflect negative interest rates on contracts, in particular the definition of when institutions, if they choose this alternative, should deduct the amount of interest on outstanding capital. Another aspect of this initiative that may be considered is its entry into force and its application to ongoing credit agreements, and the possibility of such entry into force at a time when an interest counting period is underway does not seem to be safeguarded. Without prejudice to the possible clarification or accuracy of the aspects relating to the practical application of these new rules under discussion, it is understood to be noted that, regardless of their choice as to how to reflect negative interest rates in their contracts, institutions should, under the effective interest method, recognise interest in results over the period in which they are incurred, conditions in force during that same period, regardless of the time provided for settlement. Furthermore, the implementation of this initiative could entail costs of it developments for the institutions, which is likely to make the recovery of the profitability that the banking system has been recording. Banco de Portugal naturally remains committed to pursuing the tasks and powers that are or will be committed by law - safeguarding the duties of transparency and loyalty of credit institutions, from the outset as lenders, in relation to their borrowing clients. To this end, the legislator's consecration, in an unequivocal and fully coherent manner in the context of the relevant legal framework, of solutions which may be regarded by the Assembly of the Republic as the most appropriate is particularly important in order to ensure the effectiveness and efficiency of the supervision of the conduct of credit institutions. In this context, without prejudice to the opinion we have reiterated here today on this subject, you will like to include the full cooperation of Banco de Portugal in identifying the technical-legal aspects that may merit any improvement or clarification and, if so understood, in the presentation by Banco de Portugal of suggestions of a regulatory scope that continue, with regard to the project under consideration today, the objectives that will come to be taken over by the national legislature. Thank you so much. Lisbon, 6 April 2018
text_original: Eli... Interveno da Vice-Governadora Elisa Ferreira na audio do Banco de Portugal na Comisso de Oramento, Finanas e Modernizao Administrativa: Projeto de Lei n. 90/XIII/1. (BE) 06 abr. 2018 Senhora Presidente, Senhoras e Senhores Deputados, Gostaria de agradecer o convite dirigido ao Banco de Portugal para se pronunciar sobre o Projeto de Lei n. 90/XIII/1., que estabelece a imposio de as instituies de crdito refletirem as taxas de juro negativas nos contratos de crdito concedidos a consumidores para imveis destinados  habitao. Permitam-me, Senhoras e Senhores Deputados, que comece por recordar que o Banco de Portugal j teve anteriormente oportunidade de transmitir a esta Comisso a sua posio quanto ao tema que constitui o objeto do Projeto de Lei ora em discusso. Gostaria, portanto, de relembrar e de reiterar o entendimento que foi transmitido nas intervenes da Senhora Diretora do Departamento de Superviso Comportamental e do Senhor Diretor do Departamento de Superviso Prudencial e do Banco de Portugal, em 29 de maro de 2016, e, posteriormente, na audio do Senhor Governador que teve lugar em 27 de abril do mesmo ano. Conforme foi ento salientado, o quadro legal em vigor contempla uma regra segundo a qual a taxa de juro dos contratos de crdito  habitao  resultante da soma do spread da taxa de juro com o indexante  deve refletir a evoluo desse mesmo indexante. Com efeito, decorre do disposto no n. 2 do artigo 21. do novo regime jurdico do crdito hipotecrio, aprovado pelo Decreto-Lei n. 74-A/2017, de 23 de junho  que incorporou a regra anteriormente prevista no artigo 3. do Decreto-Lei n. 240/2006, de 22 de dezembro  que, nas situaes em que a taxa de juro dos contratos de crdito  habitao est sujeita a um determinado indexante, a mesma deve resultar da mdia aritmtica simples das cotaes dirias do ndice ou taxa de referncia observadas no ms anterior ao incio do perodo de contagem de juros. A Carta-Circular n. 26/2015/DSC, de 30 de maro de 2015, reiterou este comando normativo, tendo sido transmitido s instituies de crdito que () devem respeitar as condies estabelecidas para a determinao da taxa de juro nos contratos de crdito e de financiamento celebrados com os respetivos clientes (), no podendo ser introduzidos limites  variao do indexante que impeam a plena produo dos efeitos decorrentes da aplicao desta regra legal. Esta regra no poder, todavia, deixar de ser interpretada em conjugao com outras normas e princpios legalmente consagrados. Assim, tem sido defendido pelo Banco de Portugal que a aplicao do referido preceito dever, designadamente, ter em considerao o princpio da onerosidade do mtuo mercantil, previsto no artigo 395. do Cdigo Comercial, bem como o princpio geral do equilbrio entre as contraprestaes contratuais em causa. O Banco de Portugal tem ainda chamado a ateno para a funo de intermediao financeira das instituies de crdito, recolhendo aplicaes (poupanas) de clientes e aplicando-as na concesso de crdito, funo essa que  crucial para o funcionamento do sistema bancrio e, consequentemente, um suporte indispensvel ao desenvolvimento da economia. Este papel de intermediao tem um custo inerente, no s financeiro (de margem)  que implica o tratamento equilibrado entre a remunerao dos recursos dos clientes (salienta-se que a legislao vigente no admite a aplicao de taxas negativas nos depsitos) e os juros recebidos em resultado das operaes de crdito concedidas  mas tambm de capital, uma vez que a concesso de crdito implica uma alocao de fundos que a instituio de crdito tem de realizar face ao risco inerente a essa atividade. A estreita relao entre crdito e depsitos  particularmente relevante no sistema financeiro portugus, em que a relao entre os montantes de crdito e de depsito  agora, e ao contrrio do passado, muito prxima (rcio de transformao de 93%), reforando-se a necessidade de impedir assimetrias entre ativos e passivos. Mais se refira que as operaes de poltica monetria do Eurosistema apenas correspondem a cerca 7% do total do financiamento dos bancos portugueses, sendo que apenas um dos tipos de operaes de refinanciamento  os designados Targeted Long Term Refinancing Operations (TLTRO)  poder apresentar taxa negativa (no intervalo de valores compreendido entre 0.0% e -0.40%). Ora, estes requisitos prendem-se fundamentalmente com a concesso de crdito dos bancos, mas apenas para o segmento das PME e de crdito ao consumo, no sendo para este efeito, considerado o crdito  habitao. Verifica-se, deste modo, que os bancos portugueses no conseguem, na sua maioria, financiar-se a taxas negativas. Neste contexto, e como tem sido transmitido pelo Banco de Portugal, julga-se que apenas o legislador poder, se assim o entender e aps ponderar todos os interesses envolvidos, clarificar as regras aplicveis nos casos em que a taxa de juro dos contratos de crdito  habitao atinge, em resultado da variao do indexante, um valor negativo. A iniciativa legislativa em discusso indicia que o legislador pretende intervir neste domnio. Gostaria de salientar que o desafio colocado ao legislador nacional  particularmente complexo, uma vez que no temos conhecimento de que, no espao da Unio Europeia, tenham sido desenvolvidas iniciativas legislativas ou regulamentares destinadas a fixar orientaes expressas quanto  forma de aplicao das taxas de juro negativas nos contratos de crdito  habitao. Compete, naturalmente, ao legislador, procurar encontrar as solues que melhor articulem os diferentes interesses em presena, promovendo o equilbrio contratual entre as partes e a sustentabilidade do sistema financeiro. Analisando o contedo da iniciativa legislativa em discusso, o Banco de Portugal nota que, na sua perspetiva, algumas das disposies propostas beneficiariam de maior clarificao ou preciso, de modo a afastar eventuais dificuldades na sua aplicao prtica e a assegurar a sua implementao harmonizada pelas instituies de crdito. Assim, por exemplo, poder ser conveniente concretizar alguns aspetos relativos s opes conferidas s instituies de crdito para refletirem as taxas de juros negativas nos contratos, designadamente a definio do momento em que as instituies, caso optem por esta alternativa, devem proceder  deduo do montante de juros no capital em dvida. Outro aspeto desta iniciativa que poder ser eventualmente ponderado prende-se com a sua entrada em vigor e a respetiva aplicao aos contratos de crdito em curso, no parecendo estar salvaguardada a hiptese de essa entrada em vigor ocorrer num momento em que est em curso um perodo de contagem de juros. Sem prejuzo da eventual clarificao ou preciso dos aspetos relacionados com a aplicao prtica destas novas regras ora em discusso, entende-se ser de assinalar que, independentemente da sua opo quanto  forma de refletir as taxas de juro negativas nos respetivos contratos, as instituies devem, por fora do mtodo do juro efetivo, reconhecer os juros em resultados ao longo do perodo em que so incorridos, nas condies vigentes nesse mesmo perodo, independentemente do momento previsto para a respetiva liquidao. Acresce ainda que a implementao desta iniciativa poder acarretar custos de desenvolvimentos informticos para as instituies, o que  suscetvel de condicionar a recuperao da rendibilidade que o sistema bancrio tem vindo a registar. O Banco de Portugal mantm-se, naturalmente, empenhado em prosseguir -nos termos das atribuies e poderes que lhe so ou venham a ser cometidos por lei -a salvaguarda dos deveres de transparncia e de lealdade das instituies de crdito, desde logo enquanto mutuantes, em relao aos seus clientes-muturios. Para esse efeito, a consagrao pelo legislador, de modo inequvoco e plenamente coerente no contexto do enquadramento jurdico relevante, das solues que venham a ser consideradas pela Assembleia da Repblica como as mais adequadas  particularmente importante para assegurar a eficcia e a eficincia da superviso da conduta das instituies de crdito. Nesse contexto, sem prejuzo do parecer que hoje aqui reitermos a propsito desta temtica, contem, as Senhoras e Senhores Deputados, com toda a colaborao do Banco de Portugal na identificao dos aspetos de natureza tcnico-jurdica que possam merecer eventual aprimoramento ou clarificao e, se assim for entendido, na apresentao pelo Banco de Portugal de sugestes de mbito normativo que prossigam, desde logo no que respeita ao projeto hoje em apreciao, os objetivos que venham a ser assumidos pelo legislador nacional. Muito obrigada. Lisboa, 6 de abril de 2018

Title: Intervention of Administrator Hlder Rosalino at the opening session of the Interbank Meeting on Payment Systems
text: Intervention of the Administrator Helder... Intervention of Administrator Helder Rosalino at the opening session of the Interbank Meeting on Payment Systems 07 May. 2018 I would like to begin by welcoming everyone to this Interbank Meeting, in which Banco de Portugal wishes to share information on the latest developments in payment systems and the impacts of which are relevant to all participants in the national banking community. The generality of the agenda of this meeting takes up issues addressed, in its own way, at the previous interbank meeting, which took place just over seven months ago (28 September 2017). With regard to the Interbank Clearing System (SICOI), the recent revision of its Regulation, through Instruction 8/2018, published on 22 March 2018, deserves to be highlighted. This Instruction shall enter into force on June 5, revoking Instruction No. 3/2009 currently in force. This review has made some major changes: From the outset, the incorporation of the new immediate transfer subsystem, accommodating its specificities, clearing and real-time settlement, considerably different from the other SICOI subsystems (with compensation and deferred settlement); SICOI's own governance model has also been clarified and improved; just as an example, a SICOI Monitoring Committee (CAS) has been set up, which aims to enhance greater coordination between Banco de Portugal and SIBS, as processor entity, in the various activities related to the current operation and future evolution of the national retail payment system, always from a continuous promotion of safety and efficiency levels; The new risk management mechanisms of SICOI have also been framed, in this regulation the rules associated with the obligation to establish individual guarantee account by each of its direct participants. It should be noted that on this subject, and following the previous interbank meeting, it was extended consultation with participants in October 2017, from which the proposals to which Banco de Portugal has welcomed[1]. From in a brief manner, the individual guarantee account referred to will become effective on 2 July 2010. 2018 and the amendment of the individual amount limit in the Cheques subsystems, Transfers to Credit and Direct Debits will go from 100,000 to 500,000 and apply from 19 November 2018 (remaining at the current threshold for effects subsystems and ATMs). Also in the context of SICOI, the session held in September also indicated the dates of implementation of the new procedures for the suspension or urgent exclusion of participants in the different compensation subsystems. This implementation has already occurred in some subsystems: in Cheques, on October 30, 2017; SEPA Credit Transfers on 21 November 2017; and, more recently, in Direct Debits on May 4, 2018. For the other subsystems: in the Effects, they are expected to become effective from 29 October 2018; tei not SEPA in the first quarter of 2019; and finally, at the ATM, a final proposal for a timetable is expected, which is being finalised at the level of the CISP Interbank Card Working Group and which will be disseminated as soon as there is a decision in this context. As regards the state of the situation on the revised Payment Services Directive (DSP2), two main topics stand out at this time: on the one hand, the process of transposition into the national legal system and, on the other hand, the implementation of technical guidelines and requirements drawn up by the European Banking Authority (EBA). With regard to the transposition, I would remind you that, at the previous interbank meeting, Banco de Portugal was still preparing a proposal for a preliminary draft transposition diploma, which was submitted to the Ministry of Finance (on 27 October 2017). A number of interactions followed, in a dialogue that continued with the Bank's involvement, including the introduction of some adjustments aimed at extending the scope of the diploma and accommodating some rules for implementing other European Regulations relating to payment services. After consulting some entities, the Ministry has prepared a Law of legislative authorization, which will allow the transposition to be supported in Decree-Law. It should be noted that, from an enlarged European perspective, by the end of April the transposition was implemented in only 13 Member States[2]. In Portugal, in this there is now the expectation that the transposition process may be completed by the summer. With regard to the implementation of guidelines and technical requirements drawn up by the EBA, in compliance with mandates conferred on it by DSP2, the publication of the final version of the RTS on Strong Customer Authentication and Common Secure Communication on 13 March 2018 in the Official Journal of the EU stands out, 18 months (therefore until September 2019) for its adoption by market players. These RTS explain essential requirements to be observed by Payment Service Providers in terms of security and secure communication procedures with third-party service providers. Last ly and not least, in the point dedicated to immediate payments will be given indications about the design of the national solution, framed in the SICOI, as well as the TIPS solution (TARGET Instant Payments Settlement), of the Eurosystem, which is complementary to it. In particular, the evolution of the main implementation dates of these two outstanding projects will be shared and presented. The implementation of immediate payments in Portugal, and their availability to customers, are one of the main challenges for the Portuguese banking community in 2018. Even if these two solutions are optional, it is essential that both are correctly perceived by national banks, so they may involve in the retail payment services provision chapter. In this regard, I see that several European countries already have a significant number of members of the SCTinst[3] and that, for example, the Spanish community intends to join TIPS since its launch date in November 2018. I take this opportunity to mention that Banco de Portugal will hold next week  May 14  an important International Conference dedicated to Payment Systems, under the theme: "A new Era in Payments". This conference, in addition to promoting the debate on ongoing changes in the area of payments, will mark the relaunch of the Payment Systems Forum, an advisory structure aimed at promoting dialogue between the main national actors involved in retail payments. The Payment Systems Forum will bring together supply-side players (payment service providers, in particular banks) and demand (consumer associations, businesses, public administration bodies, among others), and will have as its central objective to monitor the issues that will mark, in the near future, what they call "the new era of payment systems". These topics include digital innovation in the area of payments (based on new technologies), the entry into the market of new payment service providers under DSP2, immediate payments, mobile payments, e-invoicing, among many other ongoing transformations. It will be possible, within the framework of this forum, to be more easily listened to by the different sensitivities and to collect contributions from the inescapable national stakeholder of payment systems, seeking to obtain a clearer and more complete view, to be expressed in common positions and recommendations, in particular, which can be assumed in the existing international outlaws and in which Banco de Portugal participates (notably in the Euro Retail Payments Board  ERPB; and the European Forum Forum Innovation In Payments (EFIP). The initiative to relaunch the Payment Systems Forum finds motivation in several factors: Adapt the Forum in line with the actions of THE NCBs of other European countries, in the to enable the sharing of information and to prepare national contributions within the Of topics under discussion at ERPB and EFIP level; Cover a wider range of topics now that migration to SEPA (Single Euro Payments Area) is completed; Integrate a wider range of stakeholders, with the emergence of new payment service providers, in particular in the fintech area; Respond in an integrated manner (providers and users) to the future challenges that regulatory aspects, security, innovation, etc. We naturally count on your participation in this initiative, which will have major national and international speakers in the area of payments. I thank you once again for your presence and interest in the topics proposed for this working session. Of course, there will be an opportunity to debate the presentations that will be made. Thank you very much Elder Rosalino [1] The final configuration of these mechanisms was communicated through a circular letter issued on 8 February 2018. [2] The European Commission maintains a website to monitor the process, ... [3] Based on the most recently published listing by the EPC (dated April 13, 2010) 2018), joined the SCTinst 949 institutions from 14 communities, the Austrian scheme being the most representative in this number (470 adherents). The German community includes 304 institutions, but for production starts only on July 10 next. This figure does not yet include the Portuguese market members: 10 institutions have formalised the process for the association in the window that will allow the start-up in early June.
