Conferncia do Frum para os Sistemas de Pagamentos 14 mai. 2018 Quero comear por agradecer a presena e a participao de todos neste importante evento. Deixo um especial agradecimento aos oradores e moderadores, nacionais e internacionais, que muito valorizaram esta Conferncia, que teve uma extraordinria adeso. Este magnfico espao foi exguo para corresponder ao interesse gerado por esta iniciativa. Esta primeira conferncia do Frum para os Sistemas de Pagamentos, hoje aqui realizada, constitui um momento de grande relevncia para o Banco de Portugal. Na realidade, na prossecuo da sua misso ao nvel dos sistemas de pagamentos, em particular enquanto catalisador e promotor do seu bom funcionamento, assume grande relevncia a cooperao e o dilogo com os diversos intervenientes deste mercado. O relanamento do Frum, que assim se concretiza,  um marco significativo, pois permite o envolvimento de mltiplas entidades, com preocupaes e perfis diversos em termos da oferta e procura de servios de pagamento. A abordagem abrangente e cooperante que o Frum proporciona s poder beneficiar o sistema de pagamentos nacional e, por conseguinte, a prpria economia e a sociedade, em geral. Na sesso de hoje tivemos oportunidade de testemunhar diferentes perspetivas, de mbito europeu e nacional, na tica do legislador (a Comisso Europeia), do Eurosistema (representado pelo BCE e pelo Banco de Portugal), dos prestadores de servios de pagamentos (atravs do EPC, de bancos nacionais e de instituies de pagamento e de moeda eletrnica), do principal operador tecnolgico dos sistemas de retalho nacionais (a SIBS) e, naturalmente, pela contribuio, interessada e atenta, dos utilizadores de servios de pagamento, desde empresas a organismos do setor pblico e consumidores. Como se constatou ao longo da conferncia, enfrentamos atualmente um conjunto significativo de desafios: desde um quadro regulamentar exigente  decorrente da DSP2, mas no s; at ao envolvimento de novos players neste mercado (Fintechs e outros); a um contexto de transformao digital resultante de uma continuada inovao tecnolgica; passando por preocupaes de preveno de fraude e de um papel ativo e atuante dos Bancos Centrais face a uma realidade em acelerada evoluo. O mundo est em grande transformao em todos os domnios, tendo por base a inovao tecnolgica, no sendo exceo na rea financeira. Caminhamos para o que alguns designam de Era de banca aberta, com todos os desafios e oportunidades que isso oferece. Hoje, como sempre, a existncia de sistemas de pagamentos modernos e resilientes, assentes em solues robustas que confiram a necessria confiana aos agentes,  fundamental a uma economia s. Os temas hoje lanados para discusso so abordados, a seu modo, no Relatrio dos Sistemas de Pagamentos, e constituem uma base alargada do debate que poder ser levado a cabo pelo novo Frum.  muito importante que a comunidade portuguesa firme posies conscientes e ponderadas face aos desafios referidos, no domnio das propostas de implementao de novas formas de realizao de pagamentos, com uma ateno especial ao quadro europeu em que estas discusses so habitualmente suscitadas. Um exemplo, entre outros focados na sesso de hoje,  o do suporte s solues de pagamentos imediatos. Caminhamos, no contexto pan-europeu, para um novo normal, em que os pagamentos at 15 mil euros so realizados com base em solues integradas, interoperveis, com liquidao em tempo real e disponibilizao de fundos ao beneficirio num prazo que no dever ultrapassar os 10 segundos. Este cenrio configura um paradigma diferente do que tem sido regra, traz consigo a necessidade de avaliar os (novos) riscos potencialmente associados e equacionar medidas de mitigao adequadas, ao mesmo tempo que exige um grau de robustez acrescido e maior capacidade de resposta das infraestruturas de suporte, face a uma disponibilidade 24/7/365. Em Portugal, dentro de algumas semanas passaremos a ter no Sistema de Compensao Interbancria (SICOI) um novo subsistema que permitir aos bancos oferecer solues de transferncias imediatas aos seus clientes. Ainda que se trate de um instrumento de pagamento que necessariamente crescer  medida que for sendo interiorizado pelos utilizadores, o seu lanamento no deixa de ser relevante e exprime o resultado do esforo dos vrios intervenientes do lado da oferta, que assim se alinha (e aproxima) como uma tendncia incontornvel. Mas no  apenas no desenho e no desenvolvimento destas solues que se encontram desafios. H tambm um potencial de alterao de comportamentos e de hbitos dos agentes econmicos quando se relacionam entre si, a partir do momento em que tais instrumentos passarem a estar disponveis numa base permanente e acessvel por mltiplos canais. Desde a gesto de tesouraria de uma empresa at s relaes entre particulares, passando pela realizao de transaes quer presenciais quer remotas [1], h um espectro alargado de possveis efeitos da adoo generalizada de solues desta natureza. Em Portugal no poderemos, naturalmente, ficar indiferentes a esta e outras realidades evolutivas. H no nosso pas uma tradio de solues de pagamento integradas, modernas, que vo de encontro aos interesses dos agentes. E precisamente por termos percorrido esse caminho, deveremos promover a necessria capacidade de adaptao no mercado portugus, de forma proactiva, atenta e  altura dos desafios. E neste sentido, volto a reforar, a cooperao assume um papel crucial. Atravs do Frum para os Sistemas de Pagamentos, a comunidade nacional dispor do local prprio para suscitar a discusso sobre os temas mais prementes, com vista a encontrar solues de consenso para problemas identificados, contribuindo simultaneamente e de uma forma efetiva para os fora europeus em que estes assuntos so trabalhados. Procurar-se- assim alicerar uma viso consistente entre a oferta e a procura de servios de pagamento, equilibrando adequadamente as diferentes perspetivas, numa demanda contnua das propostas e solues mais consensuais e de maior valia para o interesse pblico em jogo.  facto bem assente que no domnio dos pagamentos h uma constante necessidade de adaptao e melhoria. Como salientado pelo Senhor Governador, na sua interveno de abertura esta manh, o bom funcionamento destes sistemas  habitualmente percecionado como adquirido, situao que exige uma postura no s atenta como de abertura por parte dos reguladores. Face a este conjunto de fatores, concluo com uma palavra de confiana no modelo prosseguido. Temos fundadas expetativas quanto aos resultados que podero ser obtidos nesta nova fase, nas diferentes reas de trabalho que podero ser abrangidas pelo Frum. Da parte do Banco de Portugal, deixo a garantia de que sero dinamizados os trabalhos e fomentado o dilogo, de forma aberta e transparente, com vista a assegurar uma articulao equilibrada e construtiva entre todos os envolvidos perante os diferentes desafios. Assim prepararemos melhor o futuro dos sistemas de pagamentos em Portugal. Muito obrigado a todos pela vossa participao. [1] Aqui no sentido de comrcio eletrnico.

Title: Speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the Money Conference "Banking and Insurance: The Future of Money"
text: Speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the Money Conference "Banking and Insurance: The Future of Money" 18 May. 2018 Intervention of the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Carlos da Silva Costa [1] It is with great pleasure that I participate in this edition of the Money Conference dedicated to the "future of money". I believe that, as a starting point, we have to bear in mind that money isa necessary co-creation but not enough to generate development conditions, which contribute to the potentiation of its role as a facilitator of transactions and of reserve value. Institutions, intermediaries and financial markets and regulatory markets are also needed to optimize the role of money in the process of economic and financial development. So we have to ask ourselves so much about the future of money and on the trends of evolution of the mechanisms of financestry and the institutional and normative regulatory frameworks applicable to them. Given the vastness of the theme, I will limit myself to three notes: on the future of money, on the institutional and normative framework that determines its circulation and on developments in banking intermediation. First note: the future money. To talk about the future of money, we have to ask a seminal question: what is money? In the answer to this question, it is worth reviewingAdam Smith who, in his work the Wealth of Nations, identified the money as: A unit of account that serves as a measure of the value of a particular good, service, savings or loan; A means of exchange and release that serves to payfor goods and services and repay debts; A value reserve that allows you to retain purchasing power and transfer it from the present for the future. Three findings are immediately required. It was the introduction and generalisation of money that allowedus to tend and deepen the process of division of labour and economic specialisation, factors that formed the basis of the economic development process. It was the fact that money was a reserve of fungible value, which allowed economic agents holding surplusresources to transfer them, directly or through intermediaries, to the loss-making agents, that is to say thatthey lacked purchasing power, thus allowing them to anticipate consumer decisions or finance investment projections. And it was the need to reconcile the dematerialization of money with the safeguarding of the liberating power and reserve of value that imposed: First, the establishment of a legal obligation to accept money as a means of paying,the designated legal course, regardless of their support material; Second, a monopoly on issuing or creating a currency; And thirdly, the need for guidance on the issue or creation of currency, i.e. monetary policy orientation. This is because the liberating power of a dematerialised currency is based on the trust that it places on it who receives it in payment, in particular as to the possibility of using it for future payments; and, secondly, its value reserve attribute depends on the price stability which, in turn, depends on the guidance followed in issuing the u creation of currency, monetary policy. That is, the dematerialisation of the currency entailed the creation of a central bank while the stability of its value required the central bank to be given a mandate oriented towards nominal stability and the guarantee of independence of the central bank in the exercise of that mandate. Thus, in the euro area, where only euro banknotes and coins have legal status, the issuance of currency and the conduct of monetary policy are the tasks of the European Central Bank, in accordance with Article 128 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. According to the European Commission [2], the legal course of euro banknotes and coins must entail: (a) mandatory acceptance, (b) acceptance at the full nominal value ofthe collection of additional fees, and (c) legally recognised means of fulfilling payment obligations. Any other assets agreed or accepted as means of payment, such as so-called virtual currencies or crypto-currencies, are not legally entitled, as they are not legal requirements for this [3], and therefore cannot be considered money or designated as coins. They are assets whose agreed value depends on the underlying nature and/or the confidence of the agents operating in themarket respondent color. What means, first, that the material or digital support of a means of payment does not qualify it as currency  what qualifies it are the liberatory attributes resulting from the law; second, that the future of money will not be the multiplication of emitters devoid of the power that guarantees the legal course indispensable to the intertemporal liberatory power and, consequently, to the safeguarding of the reserve of value; and, finally, that the power underlying a dematerialized currency both underpins the papersupport, paper money, as a digital media, "digital central bank currency". Secondly, the role of money as a facilitator of trade and optimisation of the allocation of savings depends on the nature and quality ofthe institutional, regulatory and supervisory of the territory of the sovereign who assigns him a legal The introduction and dissemination of money was a necessary condition for optimizing the allocation of available savings but was not a suficient condition. Intermediation mechanisms, i.e. a financial system, were needed to inspire confidence in holders of monetary assets and guarantee the repayment of the brokered amounts. And, to this end, it was necessary to create and reproduce orestablish a relationship of trust between aphors and intermediaries, a relationship of trust that did not result from a process of spontaneous generation but before the creation, densification and deepening of acomplex institutional framework, comprising institutions or norms (regulation) and ability to verify compliance with the applicable regulatory framework (supervision). The rules, for reasons of legitimacy, are now a responsibility of the political/legislative power. Supervision, for reasons of efficiency, is a responsibility attributed to specialized institutions that the regulatory framework of each country designates. It is up to regulators to establish regulatory frameworks that minimise the risk of non-reimbursement of resources entrusted bypolicymakers to institutions for intermediation or non-compliance with future counterparts or obligations. In particular, it is for regulators to lay down the rules on the levels of capital that are necessary for financial intermediaries to cover or bear the risks of their financial or investment intermediation activity. For a given framework of social values, these rules are the cornerstone of trust in financial intermediaries. In turn, it is up to the supervisors to ensure, first, that the institutions that mediate the allocation of savings have the loss-absorbing capacity that is established in the prudential rules; second, that their risk appetite is aligned with their effective loss-absorbingcapacity; and third, that the risk is adequately measured and takes into account the economic cycle, in order to counter pro-cyclical behaviour, both in terms of assessment criteria, risk-taking and risk premium setting or in terms of andprovision and distribution of results; or, in the case of insurance companies and pension funds, to ensure that the reserves constituted and the nature of investments ensure compliance with future obligations. Cede thepointing: determining factors of the future evolution of the banking system Starting from the context of the European financial sector, I will identify the latest trends in the banking sector in Portugal and characterize some of the challenges it faces, namely the response to the legacy and the implications of the technological revolution and digitisation. First challenge: the legacy At European level, in 2017, the non-banking financial sector continued to grow, become more interconnected or less interconnectedand increase its risk exposure. For its part, the European banking sector has seen its profitability recover, driven by improved economic growth. In line with the European trend, in 2017, the Portuguese banking system has seen anumber of positive developments, including increased profitability, a significant reduction in the high stock of non-performing assets, improved efficiency, as measured by the cost-to-income ratio, strengthening the liquidity position and increasing capital ratios. However, the banking sector in Portugal still presents some vulnerabilities, with emphasis on the levels of non-productive assets, exposure to the sovereign and exposure to the real estate sector. These vulnerabilities generate mistrust about the robustness of banks' balance sheets, despite the valorimetry adopted to respect the accounting and prudential rules applicable in a logic of going concern. In this context, it is essential that Portuguese banks continue to comply with plans to reduce non-performing assets submitted to supervisory authorities, and in particular be able to respond to a possible worsening of prudentialrequirements. Portuguese banks cannot run the risk of being squeezed by a tenacious one resulting from a greater demand for a reduction in the volume of non-performing assets and a lower attractiveness of investors, such as the combined effects of a lower-than-Europeanaverage profitability and a higher volume of non-performing assets than the European average. The present improvement in the capitalization of the main institutions, together with the recovery of the Portuguese economy and the increase in real estate prices, create a favorable context for the further reduction of the level of non-productive assets, with positive consequences for obtaining financing in the international financial markets, at the very moment when they have to issue passive instrumentsto absorb losses (MREL). It is up to the management of the banks, in dialogue with their shareholders, to make strategic decisions regarding the dilemma they currently face: Or they reduce the level of non-productive assets in the balance sheet and, in this case, bankswill benefit from an upside of market valuation, determined by improved profitability, the reduction in capital consumption not and reducing investor mistrust; in return for registration loss or impairment in its results and of any possibleresults. the need to strengthen capital; Or adopt a gradual management of the value of the portfolio of non-performing assets that comply with the prudential and accounting requirements applicable at any given time and, in this in this case, banks will face less pressure on capital in return for the maintaining lower rates of profitability and distrust of market on the robustness of the balance sheets, which will determine a lower value of market in relation to thebook value and greater difficulty and higher cost attracting new investors, with a negative impact on the expansion of its activity Credit. The current framework should be seen by the institutions as an opportunity tocontinue to carry out structural actions, in particular at the level of operational costs, which increase their resilience and enable them to better respond to the challenges that are anticipated, such as the normalisation of monetary policy, the growing regulatory requirements supervision and increased competition from new companies specialising in the provision of digital financial services (FinTech). The second challenge: the impact of digital channel intermediation The phenomenon of digitisationin eco nomies and societies is irreversibly altering the behaviour and expectations of economic actors in various contexts. Technological change is an almost existential challenge for financial intermediary acuais. Paymentservices are the sector where the future is increasingly present. Financial system customers are increasingly looking for technological solutions with high availability, speed and convenience appropriate to our needs. And they areincreasingly exposed to the offer and attractiveness of service providers that gather these attributes. The first major test will take place in the area of payment services, where technological innovation will tend to be enhanced by the entry of newcompetitions and new models of service provision. In fact, the Revised Payment Services Directive (DSP2), by introducing the possibility of creating account information services and payment initiation services, by providers who consider'third parties' in the relationship between the user and its bank contributes to the creation of a single market for competitive payment services, which encourages innovation and change. Since commissions from d and payment services are one ofthe main sources of revenue in the banking system, the entry of new entrants and increased competition will limit overall revenue growth in the future and their sharing with new service providers. The successful adaptationof the banking system to this new technological and service delivery paradigm requires a high initial investment in technological infrastructure, but it also represents an opportunity for banks to structurally reduce their operating costs, including the size of their branch network. The dynamics generated by DSP2 and the continuous technological innovation make room for the entry of competitors: for the entry of so-called FinTech, which will specialize inniche markets u in partnerships with the incumbent entities; and for the entry of BigTechs, companies in the digital area, endorsed with large databases, cross-border, and with experience in their operation. These last entities, not from the banking sector, have over time gained a competitive advantage over incumbents. Its extensive databases and analytical and data processing capabilities are very relevant competitive factors as it allows them to adjust the purposeof financial products and services to each customer's profile and ensure their placement digitally. While banks have in their favor the (re)knowledge of the public and the accumulated fiduciary capacity, their databases are geographically limited by comparison with those of technology companies on a global scale. In turn, the design, cost of production and margin of financial products destined for the mass market will require scale to make possible a final segmentation of the mercado, for a diversification of risk and for a dilution of the technological cost. Therefore, it will be increasingly dependent on the offer of the big players. Local banks without technological capacity and scale will tend to work as complementarynetworks of financial product producers by placing products with the originators' brand or with their own brand (in a 'white mark' type distribution model), collecting and applying customer funds; and, secondly, as financing networks of companies whose size, being small, requires a proximity relationship in risk assessment and determines a greater weighting of the guarantee of continuity of financing, associated with the proximity relationship. Banks have to reinvent themselves. In retail banking they have to evolve from a product-centric business model to a customer-centric business model, in the use of information they have about them. Two scenarios are beginning to be outlined: [4] A scenario of inertia, where banks do not respond to these challenges, and face a margin squeeze and cross-subsidisation limitation, eventually becoming mere platforms for the distribution of financial products with the creation of value to occur outside your sphere. Your customer base will be exposed to competition from large digital operators who will naturally tend to focus on the banking sectorand may, at the limit, give rise to a crowding effect out of the banks. And a second scenario, of profound transformation of the banking sector, in which banks internalize new technologies, through the acquisition, establishment of or internal development of FinTechs and related technology solutions. Do use of trust and notoriety already acquired from its customers, in order to to foster solutions that are increasingly focused on the needs of consumers, which allowthem to capture new sources of revenue while reducing the costs of operation. These scenarios are not mutually exclusive, and the end result may well be a combination of both, resulting in a concentration effect within the sector determinedby the need to maximise the use of synergies. Digitisation also faces challenges for central banks and regulators. It is very important that the competent authorities do not interrupt the current dynamic,but to frame and ensure, in particular: (i) the neutrality of regulation, (ii) fair and balanced treatment between incumbents and new entrants, as well as between jurisdictions, (iii) the identification of new risks and challenges posed and the adoptionof appropriate regulatory and supervisory initiatives, and (iv) coordinated action between regulators and supervisors. On the other hand, the supervisory practice will have to be provided with new artificial intelligence tools so as not to waste the time of detecting and intervening in the provision of financial services by accredited operators and framing non-financial operators. Final considerations In a changing regulatory context, and in view of the fact that the Banking Union in Europe is still incomplete, it is imperative that the financial sector, especially the banking sector, take a holistic view of the problemsit is facing, giving it a timely and inline response to the role it wants to play in the economic and social system in which it operates and, ensuring the robustness of its balance sheet and the sustainability of its business model. Whateverthe organisation of the country's payment system or savings intermediation system, it is essential that the functioning of the financial system and capital market meets criteria of transparency, risk-taking, risk, efficiency and profitability premiums that ensure the sustainability of the business model and consequently the stability of the financial system, conditions for strengthening the confidence of policymakers. text_original: Interveno do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa na Conferncia Money Conference "Banca e Seguros: O Futuro do Dinheiro" 18 mai. 2018 Interveno do Governador do Banco de Portugal, Carlos da Silva Costa [1]  com grande gosto que participo nesta edio da Money Conference dedicada ao futuro do dinheiro. Penso que, como ponto de partida, temos que ter presente que o dinheiro  uma condio necessria mas no suficiente para gerar condies de desenvolvimento, que contribuem para a potenciao do seu papel de facilitador das transaes e de reserva de valor. Tambm so necessrias instituies, intermedirios e mercados financeiros e quadros normativos que permitam otimizar o papel do dinheiro no processo de desenvolvimento econmico e financeiro. Por isso, temos que nos interrogar tanto sobre o futuro do dinheiro como sobre as tendncias de evoluo dos mecanismos de intermediao financeira e dos quadros institucionais e normativos de regulao e de superviso que lhes so aplicveis. Dada a vastido do tema, limitar-me-ei a trs apontamentos: sobre o futuro do dinheiro, sobre o enquadramento institucional e normativo que determina a sua circulao e sobre os desenvolvimentos na intermediao bancria. Primeiro apontamento: o futuro dinheiro. Para falar do futuro do dinheiro, temos que colocar uma pergunta seminal: o que  o dinheiro? Na resposta a esta pergunta, vale a pena revisitar Adam Smith que, no seu trabalho a Riqueza das Naes, identificou o dinheiro como: Uma unidade de conta que serve de medida do valor de um determinado bem, servio, poupana ou emprstimo; Um meio de troca e liberatrio que serve para efetuar o pagamento de bens e servios e reembolsar dvidas; Uma reserva de valor que permite conservar poder de compra e transferi-lo do presente para o futuro. Trs constataes se impem de imediato. Foi a introduo e a generalizao do dinheiro que permitiu estender e aprofundar o processo de diviso de trabalho e de especializao econmica, fatores que constituram a base do processo de desenvolvimento econmico. Foi o facto de o dinheiro constituir uma reserva de valor fungvel, que permitiu que os agentes econmicos detentores de excedentes de recursos os pudessem ceder, diretamente ou atravs de intermedirios, aos agentes deficitrios, isto  que careciam de poder de compra, permitindo assim que estes antecipassem decises de consumo ou financiassem projetos de investimento. E foi a necessidade de conciliar a desmaterializao do dinheiro com a salvaguarda do poder liberatrio e de reserva de valor que imps: Primeiro, o estabelecimento de uma obrigao legal de aceitao do dinheiro como meio de pagamento, o designado curso legal, independentemente do respetivo suporte material; Segundo, um monoplio de emisso ou criao de moeda; E terceiro, a necessidade de uma orientao em matria de emisso ou criao de moeda, isto , de uma orientao em matria de poltica monetria. Isto porque, o poder liberatrio de uma moeda desmaterializada assenta na confiana que nela deposita quem a recebe em pagamento, em particular quanto  possibilidade de a usar para pagamentos futuros; e, em segundo lugar, o seu atributo de reserva de valor depende da estabilidade de preos que, por usa vez, depende da orientao seguida em matria de emisso ou criao de moeda, ou seja da poltica monetria. Isto , a desmaterializao da moeda implicou a criao de um banco central enquanto a estabilidade do seu valor requereu a atribuio ao banco central de um mandato orientado para a estabilidade nominal e a garantia de independncia do banco central no exerccio desse mesmo mandato. Assim, na zona euro, onde apenas as notas e moedas de euro tm curso legal, a emisso de moeda e a conduo da poltica monetria so atribuies do Banco Central Europeu, de acordo com o estabelecido no artigo 128. do Tratado sobre o Funcionamento da Unio Europeia. De acordo com a Comisso Europeia [2], o curso legal das notas e moedas em euros deve implicar: (a) aceitao obrigatria, (b) aceitao ao valor nominal total sem a cobrana de taxas adicionais, e (c) meio legalmente reconhecido para cumprir obrigaes de pagamento. Quaisquer outros ativos convencionados ou aceites como meios de pagamento, como as designadas moedas virtuais ou cripto-moedas, no tm curso legal, dado que no cumprem os requisitos legais para tal [3], e, por consequncia, no podem ser considerados dinheiro ou designados como moedas. So ativos cujo valor convencionado depende da natureza subjacente e/ou da confiana dos agentes que operam no correspondente mercado. O que significa, primeiro, que o suporte material ou digital de um meio de pagamento no o qualifica como moeda  o que o qualifica so os atributos liberatrios resultantes da lei; segundo, que o futuro do dinheiro no ser a multiplicao de emissores desprovidos do poder que garante o curso legal indispensvel ao poder liberatrio inter-temporal e, por consequncia,  salvaguarda da reserva de valor; e, por ltimo, que o poder subjacente a uma moeda desmaterializada tanto sustenta um suporte de papel, o papel-moeda, como um suporte digital, a designada moeda digital de banco central. Segundo apontamento: o papel do dinheiro enquanto facilitador das trocas e da otimizao da alocao da poupana depende da natureza e da qualidade do quadro institucional, regulatrio e de superviso do territrio do soberano que lhe atribui curso legal A introduo e difuso do dinheiro constituiu uma condio necessria para otimizao da alocao da poupana disponvel mas no foi uma condio suficiente. Foram necessrios mecanismos de intermediao, isto  um sistema financeiro, que inspirasse confiana aos detentores de ativos monetrios e garantisse o reembolso dos montantes intermediados. E, para tal, foi necessrio criar e reproduzir ou acentuar uma relao de confiana entre aforradores e intermedirios, relao de confiana que no resultou de um processo de gerao espontnea mas antes da criao, densificao e aprofundamento de um quadro institucional complexo, que compreende instituies, regras ou normas (regulao) e capacidade para verificar a observncia do quadro normativo aplicvel (superviso). As regras, por motivos de legitimao, so hoje uma responsabilidade do poder poltico/legislativo. A superviso, por motivos de eficincia,  uma responsabilidade atribuda a instituies especializadas que o quadro normativo de cada pas designa. Cabe aos reguladores estabelecer quadros normativos que minimizem o risco de no reembolso dos recursos confiados pelos aforradores s instituies de intermediao ou de no cumprimento da contrapartidas ou obrigaes futuras. Cabe nomeadamente aos reguladores estabelecer as regras relativas aos nveis de capital que so necessrios para os intermedirios financeiros cobrirem ou suportarem as perdas resultantes dos riscos da sua atividade de intermediao financeira ou de investimento. Para um dado quadro de valores sociais, estas regras so a pedra angular da confiana nos intermedirios financeiros. Por sua vez, cabe aos supervisores garantir, primeiro, que as instituies que fazem a intermediao da alocao da poupana tm a capacidade de absoro de perdas que est estabelecida nas regras prudenciais; segundo, que o seu o apetite de risco est alinhado com a sua capacidade efetiva de absoro de perdas; e terceiro, que o risco  adequadamente medido e tem em conta o ciclo econmico, de forma a contrariar comportamentos pr-cclicos, quer em termos de critrios de avaliao, de tomada de risco e de fixao de prmios de risco quer em termos de constituio de provises e de distribuio de resultados; ou, ainda, no caso das empresas seguradoras e dos fundos de penses, garantir que as reservas constitudas e a natureza dos investimentos asseguram o cumprimento das obrigaes futuras. Terceiro apontamento: fatores determinantes da evoluo futura do sistema bancrio Partindo do contexto do setor financeiro europeu, identificarei as mais recentes tendncias do setor bancrio em Portugal e caracterizarei alguns dos desafios com os quais este se confronta, nomeadamente a resposta ao legado e as implicaes da revoluo tecnolgica e digitalizao. Primeiro desafio: o legado Ao nvel europeu, em 2017, o setor financeiro no bancrio continuou a crescer, a tornarse mais interconectado ou menos fragmentado e a aumentar a sua exposio ao risco. Pelo seu lado, o sector bancrio europeu viu a sua rendibilidade recuperar, impulsionada pela melhoria do crescimento econmico. Em linha com a tendncia europeia, em 2017, o sistema bancrio portugus apresentou um conjunto de desenvolvimentos positivos, que incluram o aumento da rendibilidade, a reduo significativa do elevado stock de ativos no produtivos, a melhoria da sua eficincia, medida pelo rcio cost-to-income, o reforo da posio de liquidez e o aumento dos rcios de capital. Contudo, o setor bancrio em Portugal apresenta ainda algumas vulnerabilidades, com destaque para os nveis dos ativos no produtivos, de exposio ao soberano e de exposio ao setor imobilirio. Estas vulnerabilidades geram desconfiana sobre a robustez dos balanos dos bancos, no obstante a valorimetria adotada respeitar as regras contabilsticas e prudenciais aplicveis numa lgica de going concern. Neste contexto,  fundamental que os bancos portugueses continuem a cumprir os planos de reduo de ativos no produtivos submetidos s autoridades de superviso, e em particular tenham capacidade para responder a um eventual agravamento das exigncias prudenciais. Os bancos portugueses no podem correr o risco de ficarem apertados por uma tenaz que resulte de uma maior exigncia de reduo do volume de ativos no produtivos e de uma menor atratividade de investidores, como efeitos conjugados de uma rendibilidade inferior  mdia europeia e de um volume de ativos no produtivos superior  mdia europeia. A presente melhoria da capitalizao das principais instituies, aliada  recuperao da economia portuguesa e ao aumento dos preos do imobilirio, criam um contexto favorvel para a continuao da reduo do nvel de ativos no produtivos, com consequncias positivas para a obteno de financiamento nos mercados financeiros internacionais, isto no preciso momento em que tm de emitir instrumentos passiveis de absorver perdas (MREL). Compete  gesto dos bancos, em dilogo com os seus acionistas, tomar decises estratgicas quanto ao dilema que atualmente enfrentam: Ou procedem a uma reduo mais rpida do nvel de ativos no produtivos no balano e, nesse caso, os bancos beneficiaro de um upside de valorizao no mercado, determinado pela melhoria da rendibilidade, pela reduo de consumo de capital no produtivo e pela reduo da desconfiana dos investidores; por contrapartida do registo imediato de perdas ou imparidades na sua conta de resultados e de uma eventual necessidade de reforo de capital; Ou adotam uma gesto gradual do valor da carteira de ativos no produtivos que respeite os requisitos prudenciais e contabilsticos aplicveis a cada momento e, neste caso, os bancos enfrentaro menor presso sobre o capital por contrapartida da manuteno de menores taxas de rendibilidade e da desconfiana dos agentes de mercado sobre a robustez dos balanos, o que determinar um menor valor de mercado relativamente ao valor contabilstico e uma maior dificuldade e um maior custo na atrao de novos investidores, com reflexo negativo na expanso da sua atividade creditcia. O atual enquadramento deve ser encarado pelas instituies como uma oportunidade para continuarem a realizar ajustamentos de carter estrutural, nomeadamente ao nvel dos custos operacionais, que aumentem a sua resilincia e permitam responder melhor aos desafios que se antecipam, tais como, a normalizao da poltica monetria, as crescentes exigncias regulatrias e de superviso e o aumento da concorrncia por parte de novas empresas especializadas na prestao de servios financeiros por via digital (FinTech). O segundo desafio: o impacto da intermediao por canais digitais O fenmeno da digitalizao nas economias e nas sociedades est a alterar, de forma irreversvel, os comportamentos e as expetativas dos agentes econmicos em vrios contextos. A mutao tecnolgica constitui um desafio quase existencial para os acuais intermedirios financeiros. Os servios de pagamento so o sector onde o futuro  cada vez mais o presente. Os clientes do sistema financeiro procuram cada vez mais solues tecnolgicas com elevada disponibilidade, rapidez e convenincia adequadas s nossas necessidades. E esto cada vez mais exposto  oferta e  atratividade de prestadores de servios que renem estes atributos. O primeiro grande teste vai ocorrer na rea da prestao de servios de pagamento, onde a inovao tecnolgica tender a ser potenciada pela entrada de novos concorrentes e novos modelos de prestao de servios. De facto, a Diretiva de Servios de Pagamento revista (DSP2), ao introduzir a possibilidade de criao dos servios de informao sobre contas e dos servios de iniciao de pagamentos, por prestadores que se consideram terceiros na relao entre o utilizador e o seu banco, contribui para a criao de um mercado nico para os servios de pagamento promotor da concorrncia, que incentiva a inovao e a mudana. Sendo as comisses provenientes de servios de pagamentos uma das principais fontes de receitas do sistema bancrio, a entrada de novos operadores e o incremento da concorrncia vai limitar o crescimento global das comisses no futuro e a sua partilha com novos prestadores de servios. A adaptao bem-sucedida do sistema bancrio a este novo paradigma tecnolgico e de prestao de servios requer um elevado investimento inicial em infraestruturas tecnolgicas, mas representa tambm uma oportunidade para os bancos reduzirem de forma estrutural os seus custos operacionais, incluindo a dimenso da sua rede de balces. A dinmica gerada pela DSP2 e a contnua inovao tecnolgica abrem espao para a entrada de concorrentes: para a entrada das chamadas FinTech, que se especializaro em nichos de mercado ou em parcerias com as entidades incumbentes; e para a entrada das BigTechs, empresas da rea digital, dotadas de grandes bases de dados, transfronteirias, e com experincia na sua explorao. Estas ltimas entidades, no sendo do setor bancrio, foram ao longo do tempo adquirindo uma vantagem competitiva face aos incumbentes. As suas extensas bases de dados e as suas capacidades analticas e de processamento de dados, constituem fatores competitivos muito relevantes dado que lhes permite ajustar as propostas de produtos e servios financeiras ao perfil de cada cliente e assegurar a respetiva colocao por via digital. Embora os bancos tenham a seu favor o (re)conhecimento do pblico e a capacidade fiduciria acumulada, as suas bases de dados so limitadas geograficamente por comparao com as das empresas tecnolgicas  escala global. Por sua vez, a conceo, o custo de produo e a margem de produtos financeiros destinados ao mass market vai requerer escala para tornar possvel uma segmentao final do mercado, para uma diversificao do risco e para uma diluio do custo tecnolgico. Por isso, vai estar cada vez mais dependente da oferta dos grandes players. Os bancos locais sem capacidade tecnolgica e escala tendero a trabalhar como redes complementares dos produtores de produtos financeiros, atravs da colocao de produtos com a marca dos originadores ou com a sua prpria marca (num modelo de distribuio tipo de marca branca), recolhendo e aplicando os fundos de clientes; e, em segundo lugar, como redes de financiamento de empresas cuja dimenso, por ser pequena, requer uma relao de proximidade na avaliao do risco e determina uma maior ponderao da garantia de continuidade de financiamento, associada  relao de proximidade. Os bancos tm que se reinventar. Na banca de retalho tm que evoluir de um modelo de negcio centrado no produto para um modelo de negcio centrado no cliente, no uso efetivo da informao que tm a seu respeito. Comeam a esboar-se dois cenrios: [4] Um cenrio de inrcia, onde os bancos no respondem a estes desafios, e se confrontam com uma compresso das margens e limitao de subsidiao cruzada, acabando por se tornar meras plataformas de distribuio de produtos financeiros com a criao de valor a ocorrer fora da sua esfera. A sua base de clientes ficar exposta  concorrncia dos grandes operadores digitais que naturalmente tendero a focar-se na cadeia de valor do sector bancrio, podendo, no limite, originar um efeito de crowding out dos bancos. E um segundo cenrio, de profunda transformao do sector bancrio, em que os bancos internalizam as novas tecnologias, atravs da aquisio, estabelecimento de parcerias ou desenvolvimento interno de FinTechs e solues tecnolgicas afins. Fazem uso da confiana e notoriedade j adquirida junto dos seus clientes, de forma a fomentar solues cada vez mais focadas nas necessidades dos consumidores, que lhes permitam captar novas fontes de receita ao mesmo tempo que reduzem custos de funcionamento. Estes cenrios no so mutuamente exclusivos, e o resultado final poder bem ser uma combinao de ambos, originando um efeito de concentrao dentro do sector determinado pela necessidade de maximizar o aproveitamento de sinergias. A digitalizao comporta igualmente desafios para os bancos centrais e reguladores.  muito importante que as autoridades competentes no interrompam a dinmica em curso, mas a enquadrem e assegurem, nomeadamente: (i) a neutralidade da regulao, (ii) o tratamento justo e equilibrado entre incumbentes e novos entrantes, bem como entre jurisdies, (iii) a identificao de novos riscos e desafios colocados e a adoo de iniciativas regulatrias e de superviso adequadas, e (iv) uma atuao coordenada entre reguladores e supervisores. Por outro lado, a prtica de superviso ter que se dotar de novas ferramentas de inteligncia artificial para no perder o tempo de deteo e interveno na prestao de servios financeiros por operadores credenciados e de enquadramento de operadores no financeiros. Consideraes finais Num contexto regulatrio ainda em mutao, e atento o facto de a Unio Bancria na Europa estar ainda incompleta,  imperativo que o sector financeiro, especialmente o setor bancrio, tenha uma viso holstica dos desafios que est confrontado, dando-lhe uma resposta atempada e consentnea com o papel que quer desempenhar no sistema econmico e social em que opera e, desde logo, garantindo a robustez do seu balano e a sustentabilidade do respetivo modelo de negcio. Qualquer que seja a organizao do sistema de pagamentos ou de intermediao da poupana do pas  fundamental que o funcionamento do sistema financeiro e do mercado de capitais obedea a critrios de transparncia, de tomada de risco, de fixao de prmios de risco, de eficincia e de rentabilidade que garantam a sustentabilidade do modelo de negcio e por consequncia a estabilidade do sistema financeiro, condies determinantes do reforo da confiana dos aforradores. Title: Address by the Vice-Governor Luis Maximo dos Santos at the opening session of the Seminar on Bank Resolution with the Central Banks of Portuguese-speaking countries
text: Address by the Vice-Governor Luis Maximo dos Santos at the opening session of the Seminar on Bank Resolution with the Central Banks of Portuguese-speaking countries 24 May. 2018 1. Good morning. Welcome to Lisbon and to Banco de Portugal. Let me begin by thanking all the participants in the Seminar on Bank Resolution that takes place today and tomorrow morning. I extend a special welcome to our colleagues from the central banks of Angola, Brazil, Cabo Verde, Mozambique, Sao Tome and Principe and Timor-Leste, as well as Marc Dobler and Joao Leite, of the International Monetary Fund and European Central Bank, respectively, who work in crisis management. Allow me also to highlight that this Seminar is part of the close cooperation that we have with the Central Banks of the Portuguese-speaking countries (BCPLP), and has been a strategic priority for Banco de Portugal for a long time, permanently renewed for the greater good. In fact, this is the first initiative wholly dedicated to bank resolution in the context of BCPLP cooperation, thus bestowing it with a very special meaning. To all, our warmest thanks for your presence. Finally, allow me a word of thanks to those at Banco de Portugal who made this event possible, with particular emphasis on the Resolution and International Relations Departments, the heads of which I thank for the dedicated and meticulous way they committed themselves to the initiative. These reasons would be more than enough for me to gladly join you here, but I must add another: my personal enthusiasm for issues of resolution, for the themes we are going to discuss here in conceptual as well as in real terms. 2. The law governing bank resolution was introduced in Portugal in 2012 by way of Decree-Law 31-A/2012 of 10 February 2012, in compliance with the commitments made under the Economic and Financial Assistance Programme to Portugal, signed between the Government of Portugal on the one hand, and the European Union (Commission), the European Central Bank and the International Monetary Fund on the other, and was on the statute book from 17 May 2011 to 30 June 2014. The resolution regime was therefore created before the publication of Directive 2014/59/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 15 May 2014 establishing a framework for the recovery and resolution of credit institutions and investment firms, transposed into Portuguese law by Law No 23-A/2015 of 26 March 2015. In 2012, it had not been envisaged that the regime created would be applied as quickly and intensely as actually occurred. In fact, on 3 August 2014, Banco de Portugal was obliged to apply, in defence of financial stability, a resolution measure to Banco Espirito Santo S.A. and, on 20 December 2015, deliberated the application of resolution measures to Banif  Banco Internacional do Funchal, S.A., likewise to safeguard financial stability. They were very different resolution measures in their origin and conception, applied to banks with very different weights and roles in the context of the Portuguese financial system. The application of these measures meant an unprecedented effort for Banco de Portugal, which mobilised the whole bank, but the team of what is today the Resolution Department was a (if not the) fundamental pillar. One of the scheduled presentations will focus on these two cases, which will certainly come up as well during the discussion of other topics, such is the diversity and complexity of the problems they raised. It may well be said that in terms of bank resolution, Banco de Portugal  and particularly the Resolution Department  have certainly learned from experience. This Seminar is an occasion to share this learning and enrich ourselves through the diversity of your experiences and perspectives. 3. The creation of the banking union was a fundamental element in the European Unions strategy to respond to the succession of crises that began 10 years ago. But it is incomplete, and that creates serious asymmetries and risks. In fact, the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM) has operated since November 2014. The Single Resolution Mechanism (SRM) has operated fully since 1 January 2016. Banco de Portugal participates in both as national competent authority. However, the projected third pillar of the European banking union  the creation of a common deposit guarantee scheme  is in practice still waiting for a political agreement to enable it. Therefore, unless the banking union is completed, many of its advantages will be hampered. More than that: it will create perverse effects that jeopardise  at least in part  the reasons for its creation. The banking union is still not only incomplete, but also in need of consolidation, regardless of the form considered. Considering its newness and complexity, it is no surprise that it should be thus. But there are questions that need to be addressed: will we be able to suitably articulate the operation of the SSM and the SRM, without prejudice to the necessary separation of each mission? Will we be able to pay attention to detail  and we know well that the detail is often decisive  and be able to see problems in a comprehensive and coherent way, especially when we look at the issue of non-performing loans and MREL requirements? Are we all aware of how important it is to affirm the principle of the primacy of law regardless of the occasion? Will the European and national authorities articulate in the best way possible, considering their competences? Will they be able to interpret their missions without ever losing sight of the beacon of the great objectives of the European Union? We must never forget that behind the technicality of the questions are often hidden options of great importance and enormous impact. 4. In Portugal today, speaking about bank resolution is largely speaking about the European banking union. But the theme of resolution is as important for more developed economies as it is for emerging economies or less developed ones. The pursuit of financial stability is a permanent task. And it is crucial to promoting economic development. As bank resolution is an instrument used to, in certain conditions, guarantee financial stability, its relevance is unrelated to the level of economic development and sophistication of financial systems. The resolution of a bank is a measure to deal with financial institutions in serious crisis, and as a result, its impact cuts across financial systems. But a good legal framework for bank resolution cannot distance itself from the characteristics of the context in which it is applied. 5. The Seminar programme is very rich and diverse, covering a wide range of topics. I therefore believe that the conditions have been met for this Seminar to encourage excellent debate on a theme of interest to us all which has a long way to progress, be it in theoretical terms or its practical implementation. I am certain that these two days will be very beneficial to all. And I hope they will be two days well spent. Thank you very much for your attention.

Title: Interview of Administrator Hlder Rosalino to the Business Journal: "Bank accounts become a raw material"
text: Interview of Administrator Helder... Interview of Administrator Helder Rosalino to the Business Journal: "Bank accounts become a raw material" 04 Jun 2018 Parliament is already discussing the Government's proposal for the transposition of the new payments directive. These new rules pose challenges to banks and consumers, but they also represent opportunities, says Helder Rosalino. Payments will undergo profound changes in the coming months with the transposition of the new payments directive, PSD 2. Helder Rosalino, administrator of Banco de Portugal, believes that this directive "may be relatively equivalent to what happened to Uber, which has greatly changed what is the provision of services in the area of collective transport." National banks are preparingthem for the new payment rules will come into force with the new directive, PSD 2? This directive brings a requirement to banks, which is the requirement to allow access to customers' accounts. Bank accounts are no longer an exclusive of bancos, and access to the accounts by service providers is allowed. Banks have a technological requirement here, i.e. they have to create secure platforms. SIBS is developing a solution that covers the needs of the entirebanking system. Then there are banks that, of course, may themselves be developing technological solutions that can be complementary to this cooperative solution. But will this be a big challenge for banks? It will be because they will have to face thistechnological challenge. And this technological dimension is a dimension that is perhaps not the most complex to face. But the other dimension of changing the business model itself is the most pertinent issue. How will our banking system position itself in a context where access to its customers' accounts is given? And here the seats will not be with their arms crossed. What can they do? One of the most innovative services that PSD 2 brings is the aggregation service of information, i.e. enterour accounts and collect information, make a reading of our financial profile and, from there, add value. The fact that they are now available by other entities will make bank accounts a kind of raw material, so that they can develop value-added services and, in essence, create a set of complementary offers for customers. And banks admit themselves to function as information aggregators and do these services. What impact can this have on what is offered to customers? Some say that, in fact, this will change the value chain of financial services provision that today is very stable, because other entities will access our account, will have partnerships, have products complementares, information and will offer new services. Other offers will be created and other business models will flourish and this is where the banking system must naturally make a reflection. The banks won't want to miss this opportunity. In the case, the consumer is the one who ends up benefiting. In what way? The European Commission considered that it was important to change this paradigm of dominance of the big banks, which, in essence, did not allow competition and led to bankcustomers having to bear perhaps excessive costs in this dimension of payments. So the idea is for banks to share customer data to boost competitiveness. Of course, these new entities will be subject to scrutiny and a very demanding authorisation procedure. But consumers will be able to share their own data with other entities that will offer them more complete services, possibly at lower costs and who will naturally try to develop what is the user experience in the field of payments. In essence, will it transform the reality of payments? What will happen with PSD 2 may be relatively equivalent to what happened to Uber, which has transformed the logic of using collective transport, through a digital dimension, a great deal has changed what is the provision of services in the area of collective transport. Airbnb the same thing. In other words, access to information will allow a set of peopleto develop solutions that can transform the financial offer. "Immediate payments will be fully implemented this year" Two solutions are being developed in the context of immediate payments: a are national and the other is theresponsibility of the ECB. The degree of adhering to these payments will depend on the strategy followed by the banks in their promotion. In addition to the transposition of PSD 2, immediate payments will also bring transformations to the national market. Helder Rosalino acredita that these payments will be fully implemented in Portugal at the end of the year. Recently, the Competition Authority (AdC) published a study in which barriers to the entry of fintechs are detected. How does Banco de Portugal seeyou question? Firstly, it is very positive that the AdC has made this analysis, it is interesting that you look at this sector and that you assess it from the point of view of what the degree of competition is and the degree of openness. It is clear that the AdC does so in the perspective of the implementationof PSD 2 and this is not yet implemented. In general, I would say that the document produced is more of a warning document about the conditions that should be created in the future than what currently exists on the national market. How do you see themer cado these days? The national market must be understood from a long-term perspective in this area of payments. It is necessary to realize that a few decades ago an entity was created such as SIBS and was the promoter of a payment system in Portugal muito developed, very pioneering. We have payment services in Portugal that do not exist in other European countries and we have an ATM network that is a worldwide success story. Of course, our system is now faced with the need to reconsider itself and to reposition itself in a more pan-European perspective and that is what it is doing. National banks are currently preparing a solution for payments Immediate. When will it be available? There are two projects running in simultanand the for the introduction of immediate payments. There is one that is a national solution, developed by the banks and also by SIBS, with the characteristic of being a solution that must comply with European technical requirements. Immediate payment solutions already existed in several countries, including in Portugal we have an immediate payment solution, MBWay, the point is that the ECB wants an integrated European payment solution because we are in a SEPA area, a single area of payments in euros. Our expectation is that the national solution will be made available very soon, in June, July. Then there is another solution that is being developed by the ECB and that all countries can use. The ECB is somehow concerned that it may not have all the countries developing these solutions in time and has decided to create a solution of its own. It is a solution that will be available in November. These two solutions will co-exist. But why two solutions? Because the ECB's solution is asimple solution, it serves immediate payments of a basic logic in the sense that it has no associated value-added services. What does the national and other country solution add? It is a set of additional treasury management services, alerts, a whole set of added value. Our expectation is that immediate payments at the end of this year will be fully implemented in Portugal and that, in a while, they will be a solution with great relevancein retail payments, at national and European level. Is there an estimate of how much they might represent? It depends a lot on the promotion that banks make. If the banks have a business plan, they will put the immediate payments as an important offer. The support and level of implementation of immediate payment solutions will depend heavily on what the banks offer, everything that is the context surrounding. For example, the Netherlands is discontinuing everything that is direct debits and credit transfersbecause it wants to promote immediate payments as the basis of its payment system.
text_original: Entrevista do Administrador Hlder... Entrevista do Administrador Hlder Rosalino ao Jornal de Negcios: "Contas bancrias passam a ser uma matria-prima" 04 jun. 2018 O Parlamento j est a discutir a proposta do Governo para a transposio da nova directiva dos pagamentos. Estas novas regras colocam desafios a bancos e consumidores, mas representam tambm oportunidades, diz Hlder Rosalino. Os pagamentos vo sofrer transformaes profundas, nos prximos meses, com a transposio da nova directiva dos pagamentos, a PSD 2. Hlder Rosalino, administrador do Banco de Portugal, acredita que esta directiva "pode ser relativamente equivalente quilo que aconteceu com a Uber, que alterou muito aquilo que  a oferta de servios na rea dos transportes colectivos". Os bancos nacionais esto preparados para as novas regras dos pagamentos que entraro em vigor com a nova directiva, a PSD 2? Esta directiva traz uma exigncia aos bancos, que  a exigncia de permitir o acesso s contas dos clientes. As contas bancrias deixam de ser um exclusivo dos bancos, passando a ser permitido o acesso s contas por parte de prestadores de servios. Os bancos tm aqui uma exigncia tecnolgica, ou seja, tm que criar plataformas seguras. A SIBS est a desenvolver uma soluo que cobre as necessidades de todo o sistema bancrio. Depois h bancos que, naturalmente, podem eles prprios estar a desenvolver solues tecnolgicas que possam ser complementares desta soluo cooperativa. Mas este ser um grande desafio para os bancos? Ser porque vo ter que enfrentar, desde logo, este desafio tecnolgico. E esta dimenso tecnolgica  uma dimenso que talvez no seja a mais complexa de enfrentar. Mas a outra dimenso da alterao do prprio modelo de negcio  a questo mais pertinente. Como  que o nosso sistema bancrio se posicionar num contexto em que  dado acesso s contas dos seus clientes? E aqui os bancos no estaro de braos cruzados. O que podem fazer? Um dos servios mais inovadores que a PSD 2 traz  o servio de agregao da informao, ou seja, entrar nas nossas contas e recolher informao, fazer uma leitura do nosso perfil financeiro e, a partir da, acrescentar valor. O facto de passarem a ser acedveis por outras entidades vai fazer com que as contas bancrias sejam uma espcie de matria-prima, para em cima delas poder desenvolver servios de valor acrescentado e, no fundo, criar um conjunto de ofertas complementares aos clientes. E os bancos admitem eles prprios funcionar como agregadores de informao e fazer esses servios. Que impacto  que isso pode ter no que  oferecido aos clientes? H quem diga que, de facto, isto vai alterar a cadeia de valor da prestao de servios financeiros que hoje  muito estvel, porque outras entidades vo aceder  nossa conta, vo ter parcerias, ter produtos complementares, informaes e vo oferecer novos servios. Outras ofertas vo ser criadas e outros modelos de negcio vo florescer e  aqui que o sistema bancrio tem naturalmente de fazer uma reflexo. Os bancos no vo querer perder esta oportunidade. No final, quem acaba por beneficiar  o consumidor. De que forma? A Comisso Europeia entendeu que era importante alterar este paradigma de dominncia dos grandes bancos que, no fundo, no permitia uma concorrncia e levava a que os clientes bancrios tivessem que suportar talvez custos excessivos nesta dimenso de pagamentos. Assim, a ideia  que os bancos partilhem os dados dos clientes para impulsionar a competitividade. Naturalmente que estas novas entidades vo estar sujeitas a um escrutnio e a um processo de autorizao que tambm  exigente. Mas os consumidores vo poder partilhar os seus prprios dados com outras entidades que lhes vo oferecer servios mais completos, eventualmente a custos mais baixos e que vo naturalmente tentar desenvolver aquilo que  a experincia do utilizador no domnio dos pagamentos. No fundo, vai transformar a realidade dos pagamentos? Aquilo que se vai passar com a PSD 2 pode ser relativamente equivalente aquilo que aconteceu com a Uber que veio fazer uma transformao da lgica de utilizar transportes colectivos, atravs de uma dimenso digital alterou-se muito aquilo que  a oferta de servios na rea dos transportes colectivos.
