Title: Closing intervention of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, at the Conference on Banking Behavioral Supervision: new challenges ten years after the financial crisis
text: Closing intervention of the Vice... Closing intervention of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, at the Conference on Banking Behavioral Supervision: new challenges ten years after the financial crisis 25 set. 2018 Let me begin my speech by greeting and thanking the presence of the Deputy Minister, Dr. Pedro Siza Vieira; Madam President of the Committee on Budget, Finance and Administrative Modernization of the Assembly of the Republic, Dr. Teresa Leal Coelho; President of the Insurance and Pension Fund Supervisory Authority, Prof. Jose Almaca; Vice-President of the Securities Market Commission, Dr. Filomena Oliveira; and the presidents and directors of the financial institutions represented herein. To all the speakers I leave my thanks for accepting the invitation of Banco de Portugal to join us in this Conference and to enrich themselves with their excellent interventions. I would also like to leave a special greeting for participants from central banks, behavioral or government supervisory authorities from other countries, including: South Africa, Germany, Belarus, Brazil, Croatia, Spain, Italy and Malta. It was a pleasure for us to welcome you. I hope that the work of our Conference has lived up to your expectations, dare I assume that this has happened, so high has the quality of the speeches. Ten years ago the world plunged into a financial crisis of enormous proportions centered on the United States and Europe. It was recognized as the biggest financial and economic crisis since 1929. This time, international consultation and the action of public authorities, particularly central banks, prevented us from having a Great Depression like the one in the 1930s. But we have not escaped a Great Recession that has had tremendous economic and social consequences, seriously affecting the lives of many millions of people, and whose effects are still felt today. Ten years ago, the Portuguese  through Decree-Law No. 1/2008 of 3 January  acknowledged that the existing legal framework was clearly insufficient for adequate protection of the interests of bank customers. The supervisory authority was intended to intervene more actively, with the aim of strengthening its supervisory, decision-making and sanctioning powers. Citing the preamble to the decree-law, it was established "the behavioral supervision of credit institutions and financial corporations, within the framework of the duties of Banco de Portugal, giving the latter the powers to develop an effective action to ensure compliance with the standards of conduct, either by unofficial procedures or through customer complaints." But this Conference was not intended to signal ephemeris, however important they may be. As we can all see, your programme has been turned to the problems of the present and the near future and the new challenges they pose. Its fundamental purpose was to reflect together on these challenges, to obtain the contribution of protagonists of other experiences, at national and international level, some of them with interests and points of view not necessarily coincident, but which  I am sure  share the central objective of contributing to a market of retail banking products that is efficient and innovative, but also characterised by a high standard of compliance with consumer rights. If it is true that the purpose of this Conference was not to mark ephemeris, it would be very unfair not to provide, on this occasion, the recognition that is due to the teams that, since 2008, under the leadership of Dr. Lucia Leitao, assure banco de Portugal of the mission of behavioral supervision, which became autonomous as a department in 2011. It should be stressed that this is an allocation pursued exclusively at national level, which makes it even more important. As we know, the financial crisis has deeply shaken the confidence of society at large in banking institutions. To this extent, the essence of the banking business itself was reached. Restoring confidence in the financial sector has therefore become a public priority, taken on by political actors, regulators, supervisors and, of course, by the institutions themselves. A large part of the problems were precisely the existence of serious flaws in the institutions' conduct with their clients, the result of unsuitable or ineffective governance systems and a deeply wrong institutional culture. In fact, the crisis has made even clearer the risks to which bank customers, in particular credit, and the consequences of these risks for the financial system and economic activity in general may be subject. The acquisition of products that are unsuited to the risk profile and financial capacity of customers, in particular with regard to mortgage lending, has generated a significant number of defaults, with a strong negative impact on the economic situation of households and on the quality of the assets of credit institutions. Retail banking products, traditionally simple and easy to understand, have acquired increasing complexity, incorporating characteristics that increase their risk, make it more difficult to understand and evaluate, thus accentuating the asymmetry of information between customers and institutions. In a context of greater access to credit by households and managing their savings through banking markets, exposure to these risks and their effects becomes even more dangerous. The financial crisis and its consequences have made it inevitable that these issues will take on a major role on the agenda of legislators and supervisors. Its discussion at the level of the various international for a has intensified, leading to the systematization of recommendations on best practices to be adopted in the marketing of banking products and the preparation of regulatory initiatives. This increased regulation has led to the scope of intervention and the way the supervisor of retail banking markets is going through a process of change, and it is often talked about in the transition to a new paradigm of behavioral supervision. In this new paradigm, in addition to the traditional concerns related to the transparency of information and the duties of conduct that institutions are obliged to observe in the relationship with customers, banking behavioral supervision begins to intervene in new areas. The conduct supervisor starts to act upstream of the procurement process, through the assessment of the compliance of the internal procedures adopted by the institutions in the context of the creation and distribution of banking products and services, and must ensure the adequacy of these products and services, and the channels chosen for their distribution, the characteristics, needs and objectives of their target audiences. Rules have been created for institutions to implement mechanisms for approving and monitoring the remuneration policies of their workers involved in the preparation, marketing and granting of mortgage loans and the credit intermediaries with whom they maintain a binding contract, with a view to preventing conflicts of interest. In addition, specific knowledge and skills requirements have been established that such workers must have. It is sought, in this way, to ensure that, in addition to the information that is provided to bank customers, the employees of the institutions have a level of knowledge and skills that allows them to provide the necessary assistance to customers, in order to understand the characteristics and risks of the products they want to hire. In another plan, and in view of the impact of its role in the credit market, there was also the extension of the perimeter of supervision to credit intermediaries, through the regulation and supervision of the exercise of their activity, as it recognises its importance in ensuring responsible credit contracting. Credit intermediaries were now framed, as of January 1, 2018, by access and exercise requirements for the activity of credit intermediation, as well as for duties of conduct and mandatory information to consumers. At the same time, the promotion of financial training has been recognized as an essential component of the performance of behavioral supervision, with a view to ensuring, in the medium term, a public more qualified to make financial decisions. It is not enough to act on the supply side of the products. We also need to act on the demand side. Following this evolution, the behavioral supervision strategy adopted by Banco de Portugal is based on an action in three vectors, which constituted the themes of the panels of this conference: (i) the regulatory framework governing the conditions for the marketing of products and retail banking services; (ii) The requirement for the institutions to comply with this regulatory framework through a supervisory action, as well as the promotion of good practices; and (iii) The financial training of bank customers. Ten years after the financial crisis, it is necessary to conclude that the conditions for the exercise of banking behavioural supervision are profoundly altered. The regulatory framework has been greatly strengthened, requiring more intrusive and complex supervision. There is a new regulatory approach that gives supervisors greater discretion in their performance, which has as a counterpoint an even greater responsibility and demand. Public scrutiny is also more intense. More important, however, is the fact that all this is happening in a context of profound and accelerated transformation of retail banking markets, through technological innovation and the multiplication of new marketing channels. The progressive digitisation of retail banking channels and marketing channels has given rise to new products and services, often through new entities, and to new business models. A growing supply of financial products and services online or through applications, the entry of new players into the market (such as Fintech and social media companies), as well as the use of new technologies (Blockchain and Big Data), are not only changing the relationship that companies have with their customers but also pose new challenges to supervisors. It should be stressed that new technological tools can and should also be used as a facilitating instrument for regulatory compliance, thereby reducing their cost to institutions. In fact, supervisors have to provide themselves with human and technological resources in order to be able to carry out effective supervision in the digital environment. This is the only way to promote confidence in the use of digital channels and to contribute to a responsible offer on the part of the institutions. It is essential that the marketing of innovative banking products and services, or carried out in innovative way, does not compromise compliance with the regulatory framework and does not protect the banking customer. Ensuring safety is perhaps the biggest challenge, due to the difficulties it poses and because it is a decisive factor in generating confidence. It is not difficult to recognize that the current phase of development of the financial sector is extraordinarily demanding for banking institutions, so many are the challenges to overcome, some resulting from a past that we all want to overcome, others arising from a future that arrives every day. Whether the current measure of regulation is correct or if there are exaggerations is a legitimate discussion and will always be the subject of contradictory conclusions. According to a famous phrase, those who think that the cost of education is high should think of the price of ignorance. I believe that the same logic is beyond regulation: it is true that it has costs, sometimes very high, but the absence of it or its insufficiency can have a much higher cost, as the crisis of 2008 demonstrated, in the first place, for the banking institutions themselves. Is it preferable to pay the costs necessary to comply with more demanding regulation or to bear costs  not less high  with sanctions, litigation, loss of reputation and business? The biggest argument that the banking sector can give in favor of reducing the intensity of regulation is itself to assume, unequivocally, perceited by the clientele, a commitment to a culture oriented to regulatory compliance and customer satisfaction. The culture of an institution is rooted in the example of management, the valorization and reward of appropriate behaviors and the penalization of the incorrect ones. Simple things, but actually sometimes difficult to do. Institutional culture is an immaterial concept, which cannot be regulated. It has to be understood as a central priority and not as an adornment to impress. It has to be internalized and seen as something natural. It should be pursued in a systematic and coherent manner. It has to be implicit in the business plan. And it has to be extended  without exception  to all areas of the institutions, because we all know cases of inappropriate sectoral behavior that have led, by itself, to collapse. It should be designed for the specifics of the institution. Therefore, despite the similarities of the ultimate purposes, institutional cultures do not have to be mimetic. A strong institutional culture, based on sound values, protects banks, including governance failures. It can even be considered a risk reduction mechanism. The creation of an institutional culture is a task of the administrations of banks and not of regulators and supervisors, while the latter may play an adjunct role in creating an appropriate culture. Changing an institution's culture is a difficult and long-term task. An old Dutch saying says that trust gallops on a horse and returns on foot. Today, it's worse: confidence can be lost at digital speed, but the return remains very slow. Behavioral failures are, of course, not unique to the financial sector. The problem is that in the financial sector the consequences are more damaging. Ten years on the financial crisis, the most enlightened players in the banking sector have already realized how costly behavioral failures can be at various levels. And so they know that it is in their interest and that the institutions that manage to move decisively towards regaining confidence and breaking with the culture that undercame the 2008 crisis. We all hope that this will happen, because we all benefit. There is no economic development without a strong banking sector. The proof of this is exactly what happens when it fails. We are thus taking a common path from different positions. To be successful, everyone has to fulfill their mission. On the part of Banco de Portugal, I reaffirm the commitment of total commitment to the pursuit of the public mission committed to it. Thank you very much. Interveno de encerramento do Vice-Governador, Lus Mximo dos Santos, na Conferncia sobre Superviso Comportamental Bancria: novos desafios dez anos depois da crise financeira 25 set. 2018 Permitam-me que inicie a minha interveno saudando e agradecendo a presena do Senhor Ministro Adjunto, Dr. Pedro Siza Vieira; da Senhora Presidente da Comisso de Oramento, Finanas e Modernizao Administrativa da Assembleia da Repblica, Dra. Teresa Leal Coelho; do Senhor Presidente da Autoridade de Superviso de Seguros e Fundos de Penses, Prof. Jos Almaa; da Senhora Vice-Presidente da Comisso do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios, Dra. Filomena Oliveira; e dos presidentes e dos administradores das instituies financeiras aqui representadas. A todos os oradores deixo o meu muito obrigado por terem aceitado o convite do Banco de Portugal para se juntarem a ns nesta Conferncia e a enriquecerem com as suas excelentes intervenes. Gostaria ainda de deixar uma saudao especial para os participantes provenientes de bancos centrais, autoridades de superviso comportamental ou governamentais de outros pases, a saber: frica do Sul, Alemanha, Bielorrssia, Brasil, Crocia, Espanha, Itlia e Malta. Foi uma satisfao para ns acolher-vos. Espero que os trabalhos da nossa Conferncia tenham correspondido s vossas expetativas, atrevendo-me a supor que isso ter acontecido, to elevada foi a qualidade das intervenes. H dez anos o mundo mergulhou numa crise financeira de enormes propores centrada nos Estados Unidos e na Europa. Foi reconhecidamente a maior crise financeira e econmica desde 1929. Desta vez, a concertao internacional e a ao das autoridades pblicas, designadamente dos bancos centrais, impediram que tivssemos uma Grande Depresso como a dos anos 30 do sculo passado. Mas no escapmos a uma Grande Recesso que teve tremendas consequncias no plano econmico e social, afetando gravemente a vida de muitos milhes de pessoas, e cujos efeitos ainda hoje se fazem sentir. Tambm h dez anos, o legislador portugus  atravs do Decreto-Lei n. 1/2008, de 3 de janeiro  reconheceu que o quadro legal ento existente era claramente insuficiente para uma adequada proteo dos interesses dos clientes bancrios. Pretendia-se uma interveno mais ativa da autoridade de superviso, assumindo-se o objetivo de reforar os respetivos poderes de fiscalizao, deciso e sano. Citando o prembulo do referido decreto-lei, institua-se a superviso comportamental das instituies de crdito e das sociedades financeiras, no quadro das atribuies do Banco de Portugal, dando a este ltimo as competncias que lhe permitam desenvolver uma atuao efetiva para assegurar o cumprimento das normas de conduta, seja por procedimentos oficiosos, seja por via de reclamaes dos clientes. Mas esta Conferncia no teve por finalidade assinalar efemrides, por muito importantes que sejam. Como todos pudmos constatar, o seu programa foi virado para os problemas do presente e do futuro prximo e dos novos desafios que colocam. O seu propsito fundamental foi refletir em conjunto sobre esses desafios, obter o contributo de protagonistas de outras experincias, no plano nacional e internacional, alguns deles com interesses e pontos de vista no necessariamente coincidentes, mas que  estou certo  comungam do objetivo central de contribuir para um mercado de produtos bancrios de retalho que seja eficiente e inovador, mas tambm caracterizado por um elevado padro de cumprimento dos direitos dos consumidores. Se  verdade que o propsito desta Conferncia no foi assinalar efemrides, seria muito injusto no prestar, nesta ocasio, o reconhecimento que  devido s equipas que, desde 2008, sob a liderana da Dra. Lcia Leito, asseguram no Banco de Portugal a misso da superviso comportamental, que se autonomizou como departamento em 2011. Convm sublinhar que se trata de uma atribuio prosseguida exclusivamente no plano nacional, o que a torna ainda mais importante. Como sabemos, a crise financeira abalou profundamente a confiana da sociedade em geral nas instituies bancrias. Nessa medida, foi atingida a essncia do prprio negcio bancrio. Restaurar a confiana no setor financeiro tornou-se, por isso, uma prioridade pblica, assumida por atores polticos, reguladores, supervisores e, claro, pelas prprias instituies. Uma grande parte dos problemas residiu, precisamente, na existncia de graves falhas na conduta das instituies para com os seus clientes, fruto de sistemas de governao desadequados ou inoperantes e de uma cultura institucional profundamente errada. De facto, a crise veio expor de forma ainda mais clara os riscos a que podem estar sujeitos os clientes bancrios, em particular ao nvel do crdito, e as consequncias desses riscos para o sistema financeiro e a atividade econmica em geral. A aquisio de produtos desadequados ao perfil de risco e  capacidade financeira dos clientes, designadamente no que respeita ao crdito hipotecrio, veio gerar um nmero significativo de situaes de incumprimento, com um forte impacto negativo sobre a situao econmica das famlias e sobre a qualidade dos ativos das instituies de crdito. Os produtos bancrios de retalho, tradicionalmente simples e de fcil entendimento, foram adquirindo uma complexidade crescente, incorporando caractersticas que aumentam o seu risco, tornam mais difcil a sua compreenso e avaliao, acentuando assim a assimetria de informao entre clientes e instituies. Num contexto de maior acesso ao crdito pelas famlias e de gesto da sua poupana atravs dos mercados bancrios, a exposio a estes riscos e aos seus efeitos torna-se ainda mais perigosa. A crise financeira e as suas consequncias tornaram inevitvel que estas questes assumissem uma grande importncia na agenda de legisladores e supervisores. Intensificou-se a sua discusso a nvel dos diversos fora internacionais, conduzindo  sistematizao de recomendaes quanto s melhores prticas a adotar na comercializao de produtos bancrios e  preparao de iniciativas de regulao. Essa regulao acrescida tem conduzido a que o mbito de interveno e o modo de atuao do supervisor dos mercados bancrios de retalho esteja a passar por um processo de mudana, sendo frequente falar-se na transio para um novo paradigma de superviso comportamental. Neste novo paradigma, alm das tradicionais preocupaes relacionadas com a transparncia da informao e os deveres de conduta que as instituies esto obrigadas a observar na relao com os clientes, a superviso comportamental bancria passa a intervir em novas reas. O supervisor de conduta passa a atuar a montante do processo de contratao, atravs da avaliao da conformidade dos procedimentos internos adotados pelas instituies no mbito da criao e distribuio de produtos e servios bancrios, devendo garantir a adequao desses produtos e servios, e dos canais escolhidos para a sua distribuio, s caratersticas, necessidades e objetivos dos respetivos pblicos-alvo. Foram criadas regras para que as instituies implementem mecanismos de aprovao e monitorizao das polticas de remunerao dos seus trabalhadores envolvidos na elaborao, comercializao e concesso de crdito hipotecrio e dos intermedirios de crdito com os quais mantm contrato de vinculao, tendo em vista prevenir a ocorrncia de situaes de conflitos de interesses. Complementarmente, foram estabelecidos requisitos especficos de conhecimento e competncias que os referidos trabalhadores devem possuir. Procura-se, desde modo, assegurar que, para alm da informao que  prestada aos clientes bancrios, os trabalhadores das instituies possuem um nvel de conhecimento e competncias que lhes permita prestar a assistncia necessria aos clientes, com vista a que compreendam as caratersticas e os riscos dos produtos que pretendem contratar. Noutro plano, e atendendo ao impacto do seu papel no mercado do crdito, verificou-se tambm o alargamento do permetro da superviso aos intermedirios de crdito, atravs da regulao e superviso do exerccio da sua atividade, por se reconhecer a sua importncia para assegurar a contratao responsvel de crdito. Os intermedirios de crdito passaram a estar enquadrados, a partir de 1 de janeiro de 2018, por requisitos de acesso e de exerccio da atividade de intermediao de crdito, bem como por deveres de conduta e de prestao de informao obrigatria aos consumidores. Paralelamente, a promoo da formao financeira passou a ser reconhecida como uma componente essencial da atuao da superviso comportamental, tendo em vista garantir, a mdio prazo, um pblico mais capacitado para tomar decises financeiras. No basta atuar do lado da oferta dos produtos.  preciso tambm agir do lado da procura. Acompanhando esta evoluo, a estratgia de superviso comportamental adotada pelo Banco de Portugal assenta numa atuao em trs vetores, que constituram os temas dos painis desta conferncia: (i) O quadro normativo que regula as condies de comercializao dos produtos e servios bancrios de retalho; (ii) A exigncia do cumprimento pelas instituies desse quadro normativo, atravs de uma atuao fiscalizadora, bem como da promoo de boas prticas; e (iii) A formao financeira dos clientes bancrios. Dez anos depois da crise financeira, foroso  concluir que as condies do exerccio da superviso comportamental bancria esto profundamente alteradas. O quadro regulatrio foi bastante reforado, obrigando a uma superviso mais intrusiva e complexa. H uma nova abordagem regulatria que confere aos supervisores maior margem de discricionariedade na sua atuao, o que tem como contraponto uma ainda maior responsabilidade e exigncia. O escrutnio pblico  tambm mais intenso. Contudo, mais importante ainda  o facto de tudo isto acontecer num contexto de profunda e acelerada transformao dos mercados bancrios de retalho, por via da inovao tecnolgica e da multiplicao de novos canais de comercializao. A progressiva digitalizao dos canais de comercializao dos produtos e servios bancrios de retalho tem dado origem a novos produtos e servios, frequentemente atravs de novas entidades, e a novos modelos de negcio. Uma crescente oferta de produtos e servios financeiros online ou atravs de aplicaes, a entrada de novos atores no mercado (tais como as Fintech e as empresas dos media sociais), bem como a utilizao de novas tecnologias (Blockchain e Big Data), no s esto a alterar a relao que as empresas tm com os seus clientes como tambm colocam novos desafios aos supervisores. Importa sublinhar que as novas ferramentas tecnolgicas podem e devem ser aproveitadas tambm como um instrumento facilitador do cumprimento regulatrio, diminuindo assim o seu custo para as instituies. Na verdade, os supervisores tm de dotar-se de recursos humanos e tecnolgicos para poderem realizar uma eficaz superviso em ambiente digital. S assim ficaro habilitados a promover a confiana na utilizao dos canais digitais e a contribuir para uma oferta responsvel por parte das instituies.  fundamental que a comercializao de produtos e servios bancrios inovadores, ou efetuada em moldes inovadores, no comprometa o cumprimento do quadro normativo e no desproteja o cliente bancrio. A garantia da segurana  talvez o desafio maior, pelas dificuldades que coloca e por ser um fator decisivo para gerar confiana. No  difcil reconhecer que a atual fase de desenvolvimento do setor financeiro  extraordinariamente exigente para as instituies bancrias, tantos so os desafios a vencer, uns resultantes de um passado que todos queremos superar, outros decorrentes de um futuro que chega todos os dias. Saber se a medida atual de regulao  a correta ou se h exageros  uma discusso legtima e ser sempre objeto de concluses contraditrias. Segundo uma frase clebre, os que pensam que o custo da educao  elevado devem pensar no preo da ignorncia. Creio que a mesma lgica  extrapolvel para a regulao:  verdade que tem custos, por vezes muito altos, mas a ausncia dela ou a sua insuficincia pode ter um custo bem maior, como a crise de 2008 demonstrou, em primeiro lugar, para as prprias instituies bancrias.  prefervel pagar os custos necessrios ao cumprimento de uma regulao mais exigente ou suportar custos  no menos elevados  com sanes, litgios, perda de reputao e negcio? O maior argumento que o setor bancrio pode dar a favor da diminuio da intensidade da regulao  ele prprio assumir, de forma inequvoca, percecionada pela clientela, um compromisso com uma cultura orientada para o cumprimento regulatrio e a satisfao dos clientes. A cultura de uma instituio radica no exemplo da gesto, na valorizao e recompensa dos comportamentos adequados e na penalizao dos incorretos. Coisas simples, mas na verdade, por vezes, difceis de fazer. A cultura institucional  um conceito imaterial, que no pode ser objeto de regulao. Tem de ser entendida como uma prioridade central e no como um adorno para impressionar. Tem que ser interiorizada e vista como algo natural. Deve ser prosseguida de forma sistemtica e coerente. Tem de estar implcita no plano de negcios. E tem de ser estendida  sem exceo  a toda as reas das instituies, pois todos conhecemos casos de comportamentos setoriais inadequados que conduziram, s por si, ao colapso. Deve ser pensada para as especificidades da instituio. Por isso, apesar da similitude dos propsitos ltimos, as culturas institucionais no tm de ser mimticas. Uma cultura institucional forte, baseada em valores slidos, protege os bancos, inclusive das falhas de governao. Pode mesmo ser considerada um mecanismo de reduo do risco. A criao de uma cultura institucional  uma tarefa das administraes dos bancos e no dos reguladores e supervisores, conquanto estes ltimos possam ter um papel coadjuvante na criao de uma cultura adequada. Mudar a cultura de uma instituio  uma tarefa difcil e de longo prazo. Diz um antigo ditado holands que a confiana parte a galope num cavalo e regressa a p. Nos dias de hoje,  pior: a confiana pode perder-se  velocidade digital, mas o regresso continua a ser muito lento. As falhas comportamentais no so, evidentemente, um exclusivo do setor financeiro. O problema  que no setor financeiro as consequncias so mais danosas. Dez anos volvidos sobre a crise financeira os protagonistas mais esclarecidos do setor bancrio j perceberam bem como as falhas comportamentais podem ser custosas, a vrios nveis. E, por isso, sabem que  do seu interesse e das instituies que gerem caminhar decididamente no sentido da recuperao da confiana e romper com a cultura que esteve na base da crise de 2008. Todos esperamos que isso acontea, pois todos beneficiamos. No h desenvolvimento econmico sem um setor bancrio forte. A prova disso  justamente o que acontece quando falha. Estamos, assim, a percorrer um caminho comum, a partir de posies diferentes. Para sermos bem-sucedidos, cada um tem de cumprir a sua misso. Pela parte do Banco de Portugal, reafirmo o compromisso de empenho total na prossecuo da misso pblica que lhe est cometida. Muito obrigado. Title: Interview of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, to TSF/Dinheiro Vivo
text: Interview of the Deputy Governor, Luis... Interview of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, to TSF/Dinheiro Vivo 21 out. 2018 Your browser does not support the audio element. "It is time to reform the European Union" and "we must achieve that hope is overlay fear," Maximo dos Santos said in an interview, showing concern economic fragility of Italy and the European Union. But it was the financial landscape national that more minutes occupied in this conversation, where, says, about the New Bank, which "without the sale we would have an elephant in the room, no solution." The government reserves 800 million euros in this 2019 OE for Novo Banco. It's a reservation, but can we take a new injection into the New Bank for granted? In fact, the government is doing is complying with an agreement which is established to provide that up to a maximum value of EUR 850 million may be funded by the Resolution Fund so that, if necessary, it can make its commitments under the contingent capital mechanism, which was one of the essential parts for the sale of Novo Banco (NB). Whether it is right or not - and I am not shying away from the question - it is impossible to say, because, strictly speaking, this figure is estimated in relation to the accounts on 30 June and therefore only when the whole situation is assessed at the end of the year that we can know what will happen. Are we talking about 2019? Undoubtedly. The value is considerable, but there are variables that need to be taken into account to the final calculation and, without them, is premature. What would have to happen so there wasn't that injection? One of the elements has to do with the evolution of the bank, but also with the capital ratios and this is dependent on some assessments in the European context that then impact on the needs that may or may not occur. The mere intake of losses alone in no way justifies the activation of the mechanism, it is a combination of knowing (and we know at the moment) what is in the assets covered by the contingent capital mechanism and then seeing the bank's behaviour and capital ratios that occur. On the NB, I would like to stress an important point: I understand that one looks at these values and understands that they are values  and are  quite high. In any case, it should be stressed: the sale of the NB that Banco de Portugal, as a resolution authority, had the opportunity to make, was a very important milestone for the positive evolution of the Portuguese financial system, and I do not say so; this has been underlined in IMF reports, in rating agency reports, i.e. when we have to balance what we are paying, precisely the Resolution Fund, which is financed by contributions from the system. Only in the absence of resources is there this financing mechanism, which are state loans. But if this sale hadn't taken place, there would be other costs. If this hadn't happened, these rating hikes and the much more positive look at our entire financial system, certainly wouldn't have happened, because we would have an elephant in the room unsolved. And now, at least, we do have a bank that is making its way, albeit with a heavy legacy, and under regulatory pressure, in the sense that the Banco de Portugal authorities want to reduce the number of NPL, non-productive assets. This is a pressure on management, but the bank has made a way and especially the final accounts of this operation can only be considered when the participation in the Resolution Fund is also sold, because this participation will have a value and the better the bank is on that date, the higher the value of that participation. Therefore, this will mean that to these contributions we will have after deducting the default value that the Resolution Fund will have. The situation of the Fund may be of concern in the future, due to the guarantees provided and possible burdens, as it recorded a own resources shortfall of EUR 5.1 billion in 2017? It is obviously not the ideal situation. We all know the story of how the Resolution Fund started. In any event, the fulfilment of its obligations is ensured by planning the contributions being made and, in the case of the contingent capital mechanism, such financing. But the greater the burden of debt, the more it burdens the Fund. Can the Fund recover amounts from this sale? You can and you've done it. Did nb have the expected evolution? I am not the manager of nb, so it is only the management and its majority shareholder. Why? Because, first, the board administered, of course, and, as for the majority shareholder, it was established in the sale agreement that the Resolution Fund would not have a presence on the board of directors. It could have been, curiously, even the private shareholder who opposed it, it was in the context of the state's negotiations with the Directorate-General for Competition that it was understood that this would be a sign of a very intrusive presence of the State, and as there was a little fundamental idea of the bank ceasing the status of a transitional bank, this understanding prevailed. What I can tell you is that, following the strict limits of the powers that the Fund has, I believe that the NB situation has been a way of restructuring from a cost point of view... and, it is inevitable, we have to give some time, because at the end of the day the sale is only a year. In many other countries in Europe, large banks have only been able to recover after many years. How do you see the possibility of the State taking a share of the capital in banks due to the exercise of the conversion of rights into capital? Even under the tax credit slate? That's a question you have to ask the state. What I can say is that we have a public bank that is the largest in our system and, in many opinion, this is the appropriate position for the participation of public capital in the financial system. But doesn't it shock or surprise you? It will depend on the assessment of each situation and its framework, but in general I would say that the presence Credit is fundamental, even even consumer credit, which is no sin, we should not demend it, but we cannot fall into past mistakes, because the excess indebtedness of economic agents in general remains a great burden and we must be careful that there is prudence. financial system is well ensured by a bank with the size of CGD. New credit to families continues to grow. Will Banco de Portugal's recommendations and the increase in stamp duty provided for in the EO be sufficient to avoid a bubble scenario? At this point what is being done is really what it should be: we cannot be inattentive or rush. I believe that the macroprudential measure that has been in place since 1 July reflects this stance. That is, Banco de Portugal, noting that the level of household indebtedness is high compared to what is happening in international terms, noting that interest rates remain low, that credit has remained depressed for a long time  this is also a factor for people to become indebted  considered that even though there is no risk to financial stability in the short term, if these factors are growing we could see here a picture of an excessive reduction of some restriction in the criteria of lending, and that is not what is intended. Credit is fundamental, even consumer credit, which is no sin, we should not demonize it, but we cannot fall into past mistakes, because the excess indebtedness of economic agents in general remains a great burden and we must be careful that there is prudence. I believe that the institutions, even because of the poor results they have had, will also make this assessment, but deep down, sometimes there are competitive dynamics that can lose more sight to a medium-term dimension. And how is this check that there are no abuses? There's a dialogue. For now the institutions provide information to the bank and in accordance with the measure itself, in its monitoring, I believe that six months is a good period for this. And at the end of the year, a rigorous assessment will be made, because we have to detect and make a very accurate report.... According to what has reached the BdP so far, does it seem to you that there are many situations of abuse? It is not a question of abuse, the institutions themselves may, in certain cases, have the power to explain to the banco de Portugal institution why they do not follow the recommendation in this or that case. As I say, a rigorous picture of this after six months is a reasonable period. I believe that the fact that this issue has emerged for public debate has been very positive, because it is additional pressure to strictly comply with the regulation on solvency and the criteria that the measure itself contains. Was that the supervisor's intention to put the question on the agenda? No, this is not a media strategy. Pressure, so that behaviors are shaped? It is a typical measure of this type of situation and that other authorities have also followed, that is, preventively and taking into account the history and characteristics of our market we have advanced with these more restrictive criteria. It is not worth hiding that the measure is macro, but then can have micro effects on specific customers. But it's not about putting it on the agenda, it's about responding to a real problem. If these recommendations are not respected, Banco de Portugal admits to moving towards a new sanctioning instrument. Will we get to that point? That's anticipating something we don't know a little bit. The existence of sanctioning frameworks in the supervisory activity is very important, because it gives it credibility. The sanctions... I have the responsibility of the investigation and sanctioning action department. Now, the goal of supervision itself is not just to sanction. When we are sanctioning, we are already seeing that something has been wrong and what we want to do is to anticipate it, talk to the institutions, make them aware, listen to them and, deep down, to hold them accountable as well. At the bottom this anticipation goes through behavioral supervision, where Banco de Portugal wants to bet more? It is not typically behavioral domain. We're in an area that may be under certain circumstances, but we're not in that case yet. If there are specific determinations, which is one of the instruments that the bank has, and they are not complied with, it can give rise to sanctions. For now we are on a strictly macroprudential plan because, at the end of the day, what the measure is about is the prevention of systemic risks, preventing a softened lending, which is more vulnerable to economic developments, from putting institutions in difficulty. Could Banco de Portugal act better if it had more supervisory powers? It is difficult to answer this question for all kinds of supervision that is done in the bank. Today, the regulatory framework for prudential supervision is a European framework. In behavioural supervision there is also a set of directives that frame, the difference is that for behavioural purposes supervision is done on a national basis and in the prudential framework is done in a single supervisory mechanism. One must try to extract all the potential of the rules that exist, and there are many, I recognize that. The increase in fines for failures to communicate offshore transfers is foreseen in the OE. Agree? Is it really going to have an effect on the banks? Anything to increase transparency, particularly with these entities, is welcome, because we all know that they are entities where problems accumulate. It may be one of the cases where the existing sanctions were not sufficiently deterrent, but it is a matter of the OE and Banco de Portugal, by definition, it is not for him to comment on the OE Law. The Budget also provides for more dividends from Banco de Portugal. Do you think it's natural for the bank to give more and more money to the state? That's not necessarily the way. The thing is this: like any company, the bank has to have a risk provisioning policy, because it has and is a lot of them, and the purpose of Banco de Portugal is not to produce dividends. But if that goal is achieved, the better. Are the values reasonable? Values are always reasonable if they have correct measures. Is that the case? Let's be clear: this is the case in 2017 where the accounts have already been approved. As for the next... is premature, because the bank's accounts are not closed. Has the government already entered the amount of what it expects from Banco de Portugal? That's why I'm telling you I don't comment on The OE. What I can say is that we will have to wait for the year to evolve until the accounts close. The audit board will then give your opinion and only at that moment can we be right.... There may be instability factors that change the numbers. It's a matter that's just like that.... As for the national landscape, has the worst passed on to banks or could a new crisis throw some bank into a resolution situation? No one predicted the previous crisis, and allow me a slight tone  I am sometimes tempted to say that when everyone is predicting it, it is because it will not happen. Are you optimistic? That's not what this is about. There are of course a lot of risks because there are tectonic plates of the international economy that are moving. To say that there will be no more crises, this would not be at all reasonable because crises are inherent in the dynamics of economic activity. What would no longer be very normal is that, looking at the scale that the 2008 crisis had, which was the largest after 1929, it would be very strange for this crisis to be repeated in a relatively short period, because something would be really bad. Historical evidence shows that crises of this size only take place in long periods. But there are new risks, new realities, a new economy that is in motion, which is that of digital, and that we do not dominate at all levels, because non-stop credit does not arise only by mismanagement, often yes, but other times not.

Entrevista do Vice-Governador, Lus Mximo dos Santos,  TSF/Dinheiro Vivo 21 out. 2018 Your browser does not support the audio element.  tempo de reformar a Unio Europeia e temos de conseguir que a esperana se sobreponha ao medo, disse Mximo dos Santos, em entrevista, mostrando preocupao com a fragilidade econmica da Itlia e da Unio Europeia. Mas foi o panorama financeiro nacional que mais minutos ocupou nesta conversa, onde, diz, sobre o Novo Banco, que sem a venda teramos um elefante na sala, sem soluo. O governo reserva 800 milhes de euros neste OE 2019 para o Novo Banco.  uma reserva, mas podemos dar como certa uma nova injeo no Novo Banco? De facto, o governo o que faz  cumprir um acordo que est estabelecido no sentido de se prever que at um valor mximo de 850 milhes de euros possa haver um financiamento ao Fundo de Resoluo para que, se for necessrio, este possa assumir os seus compromissos no quadro do mecanismo de capital contingente, que foi uma das peas essenciais para a venda do Novo Banco (NB). Se  certo ou no  e no estou a fugir  pergunta -,  impossvel dizer, porque, em bom rigor, este valor  estimado relativamente s contas a 30 de junho e, portanto, s quando no final do ano se fizer a avaliao de toda a situao  que poderemos saber o que vai acontecer. Referimo-nos a 2019? Sem dvida. O valor  considervel, mas h variveis que tm de ser tidas em conta para o clculo final e, sem elas,  prematuro. O que teria de acontecer para que no houvesse essa injeo? Um dos elementos tem que ver com a evoluo do banco, mas tambm com os rcios de capital e isso est dependente de algumas avaliaes no contexto europeu que depois impactam nas necessidades que podem vir a verificar-se ou no. O mero incurso em perdas, s por si, de maneira nenhuma justifica o acionamento do mecanismo,  uma combinao de sabermos (e sabemos neste momento) o que est nos ativos abrangidos pelo mecanismo de capital contingente e depois vermos o comportamento do banco e os rcios do capital que se verificam. Sobre o NB, gostaria de sublinhar um ponto importante: percebo que se olhe para estes valores e se entenda que so valores  e so  bastante elevados. Em qualquer caso,  preciso sublinhar o seguinte: a venda do NB que o Banco de Portugal, enquanto autoridade de resoluo, teve ocasio de fazer, constituiu um marco importantssimo para a evoluo positiva do sistema financeiro portugus, e no sou eu que o digo; isso foi sublinhado em relatrios do FMI, em relatrios de agncias de rating, ou seja, quando temos de pr na balana o que estamos a pagar, em rigor  o Fundo de Resoluo, que  financiado por contribuies do sistema. Title: Opening speech of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, at the Annual Conference of the Association of Specialized Credit Institutions (ASFAC)
text: Opening speech of the Vice-Gov... Opening speech of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, at the Annual Conference of the Association of Specialized Credit Institutions (ASFAC) 22 out. 2018 1. Allow me a first word to greet, in the person of the President of the Board, Dr. Antonio Menezes Rodrigues, all the members of the governing bodies of the Association of Specialized Credit Institutions (ASFAC) and, as well, all the speakers and participants in this Conference. On the other hand, I would like to make a double congratulations: To Dr Antonio Menezes Rodrigues, for his recent election as Chairman of EUROFINAS  European Federation of Finance House Associations, and ASFAC, for holding another edition of this Conference. The importance and significance of the election are obvious and could therefore not be without the well-deserved record of congratulations; as far as the Conference is about the Conference, it is an initiative that has already been imposed in the calendar of events relating to the financial system, and is an excellent opportunity to identify trends in the consumer credit sector, to share and discuss problems, and congratulations are therefore also entirely justified. It is so with great pleasure that I participate in the Conference, being significant of the importance that Banco de Portugal attributes to the event the fact that, in addition to myself, we count on the presence, as speakers, of Dr. Lucia Leitao, director of the Department of Behavioral Supervision, and Dr. Joao Raposo, director of the Department of Investigation and Sanctioning Action. 2. Since its creation in 1991, ASFAC has filled an important space in a sector with very particular characteristics of the credit market and which has gained importance due to social developments and market dynamics. I consider it very important for the country and for regulatory and supervisory authorities that there is a strong associative movement of financial companies, endowed with the means and capacity to generate critical mass. We all have to win in that way. In fact, the more complex and dense the regulatory framework becomes, whether in the behavioral or prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, the more intrusive and principle-based supervision is, the more important the dialogue with industry representatives. It was precisely for this purpose that, in 2011, Banco de Portugal created the Forum for Behavioral Supervision, of which ASFAC is, from the beginning, an active participant. The path made since then clearer made the right of this decision. But our perspective is not that this dialogue is done only on the occasion of specific events, but in the day-to-day, because it is in this context that supervisors and supervised from it can extract all the usefulness. This willingness of Banco de Portugal to constantly engage in dialogue with the institutions, while strictly respecting the diversity of their roles, makes even more unacceptable practices that violate the regulatory framework and this is an aspect that cannot be further underlined. 3. The publication of Decree-Law No. 133/2009 of 2 June, which transposed the second European Directive on consumer credit agreements, was a milestone in consumer law in Portugal. Since then, a long way has come. As a result of the consequences of the financial crisis and increased awareness of how certain practices can be so harmful to consumers, institutions and the financial system, the regulatory framework and the demands of behavioural supervision have changed profoundly. The European impetus, in particular through the publication of several directives, was decisive. Ten years on the financial crisis it is possible to say that there is now greater transparency in retail banking markets, including in the important segment of consumer credit. Consumers are more protected in the sense that they are given more rights and some of the existing ones have been deepened. The duties of information were robused; consumer credit agreements have set ceilings for the annual overall effective charge rate (TAEG) and the nominal interest rate (NHS); the solvency assessment duty has been strengthened; the duty of assistance was created; certain bank fees have been banned or limited and, when associated with payment accounts, it has become much easier to compare them, especially after the format given to the commission comparator operating since 1 October; there is a regime for the prevention and management of non-compliance situations, to mention only a few examples. In another plan, changes recently introduced in the General Regime of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations have imposed on institutions new duties in the definition of the policy of remuneration and evaluation of workers who maintain contact with customers in the context of the marketing of retail banking products and services, with a view to minimizing the risk of conflicts of interest and avoiding potential harm to customers. It also established the need for institutions to establish specific procedures for the governance and monitoring of credit products, ensuring, in their design and distribution, the adequacy of these products to the interests, objectives and characteristics of consumers. It is also very important that on 1 January this year the legal regime for credit intermediaries came into force, which extended the perimeter of behavioural supervision. In fact, in order to access this activity, the prior authorization of Banco de Portugal, which is also responsible for supervising its exercise, is now necessary. The legislature established, however, a transitional period of one year during which it is accepted that natural and legal persons who already developed the activity of credit intermediary prior to the entry into force of the legal regime continue to develop it without obtaining authorization from Banco de Portugal. We are fully aware that the process of authorization of credit intermediaries is of significant importance for the sector of specialized credit institutions, taking into account the relevance of these entities in the distribution of consumer credit products. It is a challenge for the sector, but also for Banco de Portugal. Credit institutions play a decisive role in this process by providing the necessary information and support to the credit intermediaries with which they maintain or intend to establish binding contracts. Institutions should also ensure that the activity carried out by their partners observes the rules laid down by the legislator. I would like to make it clear that Banco de Portugal recognises the importance of the work that credit institutions and ASFAC have been developing in this area. We know that this is a transformation with multiple implications and considerable costs, especially in this transition phase. But the end result of this process will undoubtedly be a better functioning of the market, an objective that is beneficial for everyone. 4. The specialisation of supply according to demand needs is a source of efficiency gains and is also supposed to promote greater consumer satisfaction. The specialized grant ing of credit does not escape this general standard. A focused business model can bring several advantages. The characteristics of society and consumption habits are rapidly changing. From millennials to "generation Z", the specifics of consumer behavior are many and decisive. Companies, in general, need to understand them well to succeed in the market. The financial sector does not constitute  quite the contrary  exception to that rule. Without prejudice to the specificities of the sector, which  undoubtedly  there is currently the most relevant trend in the level of specialized credit is, in fact, common to all entities in the financial system: how to deal with the challenge of the economy and the digital society? Under the generic designation of "digital economy" there are different realities, which advance at different rates, but all with profound consequences in various planes and a common point to unite them: the technological revolution in production and consumption processes. Monitoring the process of marketing credit to consumers through digital channels is one of banco de Portugal's current priorities. On 17 January this year, Banco de Portugal issued a circular letter in which it requested the provision of information on credit products whose marketing process is initiated and completed through digital channels. The information obtained is essential to monitor and monitor the practices of credit institutions in the marketing of credit to consumers through digital channels, namely mobile devices (apps) and online platforms. This process has been developed in close coordination with credit institutions, being a good example of the dialogue between supervisors and supervised to which I mentioned above. 5. As has been reported and reported, consumer credit is experiencing high growth rates in Portugal, having already reached values corresponding to those before the financial crisis. It is essential to avoid incurring successive cycles of excessive and unjudicious credit granting that follows an abrupt and lasting fall. As it is known, Banco de Portugal adopted a macroprudential measure with the aim of preventing excessive risk accumulation in banks' balance sheets and ensuring that households obtain sustainable financing, minimizing the risk of default. Its objective is to contribute to adequate rigour in the criteria for granting credit. Consumer credit agreements concluded after 1 July 2018 are included in the scope of that measure, which will therefore also have an impact on the consumer credit market. The terms in which consumer credit is sometimes debated seems to me to be a real paradox of our time. In fact, the development and expansion of consumer credit is a direct consequence of powerful trends, in particular stagnation or lower wages, the fall in savings and the overdevelopment of the financial sector. Consumer credit is inextricably linked to a model of society that places consumption as a central value. It is a fundamental element of what we might call the "credit society" and, contrary to what is sometimes believed, it is a phenomenon that is present, even to different degrees, in all countries with developed financial systems. When things go wrong and the promised and sought-after paradise becomes a nightmare, moral judgments emerge in public debate. In their apparent uncontroversial character, they are, in fact, as a rule, superficial judgments, because they do not take due account of the root causes that feed the indebtedness and end  voluntarily or unintentionally  for diverting attention from the true roots of the issue. In fact, of course, there is nothing intrinsically reprehensible in the use of consumer credit; on the contrary, consumer credit has long corresponded to an economic and social need. What should not and cannot happen is the granting of credit irresponsibly, disrespecting consumer rights, with the purpose of taking economic advantage of the weaknesses and shortcomings of knowledge of banking customers. I therefore end by expressing a wish which is perfectly within our reach: for the benefit of bank customers, financial institutions, the functioning of the economy and society, responsible credit cannot be a mere objective  it must be a constant fact. Thank you so much for your attention. Presentation by the Director of the Department of Behavioral Supervision, LuciaLeitao, at the ASFAC Annual Conference

A concesso especializada de crdito no foge a esse padro geral. Um modelo de negcio focado pode trazer diversas vantagens. As caractersticas da sociedade e os hbitos de consumo esto em acelerada mutao. Dos millennials  gerao Z, so muitas e decisivas as especificidades do comportamento dos consumidores. As empresas, em geral, precisam de as compreender bem para ter sucesso no mercado. O setor financeiro no constitui  muito pelo contrrio  exceo a essa regra. Sem prejuzo das especificidades do setor, que  sem dvida  existem, atualmente a tendncia mais relevante no plano do crdito especializado , na verdade, comum a todas as entidades do sistema financeiro: como lidar com o desafio da economia e da sociedade digital? Sob a designao genrica de economia digital englobam-se realidades diversas, que avanam a ritmos diferentes, mas todas com profundas consequncias em diversos planos e um ponto comum a uni-las: a revoluo tecnolgica nos processos produtivo e de consumo. Acompanhar o processo de comercializao de crdito aos consumidores atravs de canais de digitais  uma das atuais prioridades do Banco de Portugal. Em 17 de janeiro deste ano, o Banco de Portugal emitiu uma carta circular nos termos da qual solicitou a prestao de informao sobre produtos de crdito cujo processo de comercializao seja iniciado e concludo atravs de canais digitais. A informao obtida  essencial para acompanhar e fiscalizar as prticas das instituies de crdito na comercializao de crdito aos consumidores atravs canais digitais, nomeadamente, dispositivos mveis (apps) e plataformas online. Este processo tem sido desenvolvido em estreita articulao com as instituies de crdito, sendo um bom exemplo do dilogo entre supervisores e supervisionados a que atrs me referi. 5. Como tem sido divulgado e noticiado, o crdito ao consumo est a registar elevadas taxas de crescimento em Portugal, tendo atingido j valores correspondentes aos anteriores  crise financeira.  fundamental evitar incorrer em sucessivos ciclos de concesso excessiva e pouco criteriosa de crdito a que se segue uma queda abrupta e duradoura. Como  conhecido, o Banco de Portugal adotou uma medida macroprudencial com o objetivo de evitar a acumulao de risco excessivo no balano dos bancos e garantir que as famlias obtm financiamento sustentvel, minimizando o risco de incumprimento. O seu objetivo  o de contribuir para que haja rigor adequado nos critrios de concesso de crdito. Os contratos de crdito ao consumo celebrados aps 1 de julho de 2018 esto compreendidos no mbito dessa medida, a qual, portanto, ter tambm impacto no domnio do mercado do crdito ao consumo. Os termos em que, por vezes, se debate o crdito ao consumo afiguram-se-me constituir um verdadeiro paradoxo do nosso tempo. Na verdade, o desenvolvimento e a expanso do crdito ao consumo so consequncia direta de poderosas tendncias, em especial a estagnao ou a reduo dos salrios, a queda da poupana e o hiperdesenvolvimento do setor financeiro. O crdito ao consumo est indissociavelmente ligado a um modelo de sociedade que coloca o consumo como valor central.  um elemento fundamental do que poderamos chamar a sociedade do crdito e, ao contrrio do que por vezes se quer fazer crer,  um fenmeno que est presente, ainda que em graus diferentes, em todos os pases com sistemas financeiros desenvolvidos. Quando as coisas correm mal e o paraso prometido e procurado se torna um pesadelo, emergem no debate pblico os juzos morais. No seu aparente carter incontroverso, so, na verdade, em regra, juzos superficiais, pois no levam em devida conta as causas profundas que alimentam o endividamento e acabam  voluntria ou involuntariamente  por desviar a ateno das verdadeiras razes da questo. Na verdade, como  evidente, nada h de intrinsecamente condenvel no recurso ao crdito ao consumo; pelo contrrio, o crdito ao consumo corresponde h muito a uma necessidade econmica e social. O que no deve nem pode acontecer  a concesso de crdito de modo irresponsvel, desrespeitando os direitos dos consumidores, com o propsito de tirar proveito econmico conjuntural das fragilidades e insuficincias de conhecimentos dos clientes bancrios. Termino, pois, exprimindo um desejo cuja concretizao est perfeitamente ao nosso alcance: em benefcio dos clientes bancrios, das instituies financeiras, do funcionamento da economia e da sociedade, o crdito responsvel no pode ser um mero objetivo  tem de ser um facto permanentemente praticado. Muito obrigado pela vossa ateno. Apresentao da Diretora do Departamento de Superviso Comportamental, LciaLeito, na Conferncia Anual da ASFAC

Title: Intervention of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, at the Conference "Corporate Governance: creation of value for society": "Corporate Governance: importance and limits"
text: Compatible... Intervention of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, at the Conference "Corporate Governance: creation of value for society": "Corporate Governance: importance and limits" 25 out. 2018 1. Let me begin by thanking you for inviting me to participate in this magnificent Conference and for greeting all the speakers and participants. In the person of the Presidents of the Board of Directors and the General Council, respectively Prof. Antonio Gomes Mota and Dr. Pedro Rebelo de Sousa, address my congratulations to the Portuguese Institute of Corporate Governance (IPCG) for its 15th anniversary, as well as for the timely realization of this event, and I also greet all the other members of the governing bodies. The creation of this Institute 15 years ago was a moment of inspiration, as it anticipated  at a time when the issue was still relatively marginal  the importance that the issue of corporate governance would gain. Portugal needs strong private institutions of associative nature, which promote the debate on topics that matter very much to the development of companies and the quality of management, in a broad sense, that are capable of generating critical mass on complex topics, such as corporate governance. A special reference is imposed on the implementation this year of the objective of approval of a Corporate Governance Code, long pursued by the IPCG, and which is undoubtedly a milestone in the private regulation plan in Portugal. 2. The theme of corporate governance is the subject of an already long theoretical reflection, with a particular focus on the USA, where some authors locate the first uses of the term in the 70s of the last century. In the United Kingdom, the so-called Cadbury Report, dated 1992 and produced by a committee set up to assess  already then  the root causes of a set of business collapses is considered a pioneer in the field. Since then, the attention paid to the theme of corporate governance  which has a multidisciplinary, because it convenes knowledge of economics, finance, accounting, law, management and behavior of organizations  it has not ceased to grow. The growing interest is of course no stranger to the succession of large-scale public corporate scandals, even before the financial crisis, as was the case with Banco Barings (1995), Enron (2002) and Parmalat (2003)  to name but a few of the best-known which in some way motivated the production of a set of codes of good corporate governance practices by international reference organisations such as the OECD, the World Bank and the Basel Committee, among others. But it was the financial crisis that began in 2007 and its tremendous consequences that brought to the foreground of public action, including in the regulatory field, corporate governance issues in all the most affected countries and the European Union. Without going into the analysis of the causes of the crisis  which are multiple  it can be said that it is widely accepted that one of the factors that originated and enhanced it was the clamorous failure of the internal government models of financial institutions. The occurrence of the crisis made clear what was already pointed out by the theory: banking activity has such particularities in relation to non-financial companies that it is indispensable that it has specific corporate governance rules. The security of the funds entrusted to banks requires that they be managed in a sound and prudent manner in order to maintain the trust of depositors, customers and investors, thus preserving financial stability. That is why the way these institutions manage their business is crucial to ensuring a model of sustainable economic growth. Problems in the management of banks  and it is enough that it is the isolated case of a bank  entail high risks to financial stability which, materialising, are negatively transmitted to other banks and, ultimately, can very materially affect the financing of the economy, as the financial crisis has shown. This therefore gives particular relevance to the theme of the internal government of banks. 3. The internal government shall consist of the system of organisation of functions, responsibilities, lines of reporting and control in financial institutions that supports their management and business model. In the internal government, the administrative and supervisory bodies of financial institutions are of particular importance, but also the holders of the essential functions that, among others, correspond to those responsible for the areas of risk management, compliance and internal audit. At issue are essentially: i. The decision-making process that makes it possible to define, at any moment, what should be combined with the interests of the various stakeholders, internal and banks; ii. The definition of a strategy to promote the pursuit of these interests, nor always coincident; and iii. The specific operationalisation of the strategy in question. The existence of a plurality of interests  from depositors, bondholders, customers, workers, shareholders and even the managers' own interests  inevitably causes them to conflict. A good system of corporate governance therefore involves the proper resolution of the problems listed: management of conflicts of interest and mitigation of the existence of information asymmetries. This allows us to realize the importance of corporate governance: to enable the composition of the various potentially divergent interests and to determine the performance of banks and the quality of their decision-making process. The internal government model will therefore have a decisive effect on the long-term sustainability of banks. This decisive importance of corporate governance for the activity of banks has become, especially after the crisis, intense regulatory treatment. 4. The evolution of regulation has been revealing an increasingly granular trend, a path that is not without difficulties. In fact, the initial phase in 2009 and 2010 revealed concern about one of the most salient aspects of the crisis  incentives misaligned with sustainable and prudent risk management. The practice of remunerative schemes based on variable components indexed to rapid expansions of the volume of transactions led to a culture of excessive risk. As a result, the initial reaction of regulators at international level was very much directed at remuneration policies and practices. Since 2011, the regulatory agenda has moved to a more comprehensive approach to corporate governance, and at this stage is concerned with regulating banks' corporate governance systems, especially in their organizational and control dimensions; and it is in the context of this broader regulatory vision that other aspects of government begin to be regulated: internal audit, external audit and adequacy of the members of the banks' management and oversight bodies, as well as the holders of essential functions. With the adoption of Directive 2013/36/EU of the European Parliament and the Council of 26 June 2013 on access to the activity of credit institutions and prudential supervision of credit institutions and investment firms, commonly known as 'CRD IV', corporate governance rules have become part of a comprehensive approach to organisation, control functions, persons and remuneration. An integrated view of the organisational structure at the level of responsibilities, the adequacy of the people who manage and oversee the institution and those responsible for essential functions, a sound and effective internal control framework, the autonomous design of the internal government of risk and remuneration policies aligned with a healthy and prudent risk culture were favoured. Ensure that the organizational structure of corporate governance of institutions is sound and the proper management and supervision has therefore become a central concern of banking regulation. From the outset, banks should define a profile for members of the administrative and supervisory bodies and seek candidates to bring together the knowledge, skills, experience, integrity and availability of the time necessary to fully carry out their duties. It is also indispensable the presence of an adequate number of formally independent members in the administrative and supervisory bodies, in order to promote adequate protection of the interests of the various stakeholders and the preservation of sound and prudent management and, ultimately, financial stability. Banks must also fully comply with the rules on incompatibilities (which differ from the rules on formal independence). In addition to formal independence, "independence of mind" is also required, a dimension that calls for the absence of conflicts of interest, even if potential. The management function within the banks cannot have ascending over the internal supervision function. On the contrary. Non-executive members of the management body and the supervisory body shall be empowered to fully carry out their surveillance duties. They should scrutinize the current management, taking into account the interests of the various stakeholders, internal and external, of the banks. The internal supervisory function, in turn, shall be provided with the information necessary for the full performance of its duties. It should be proactive in obtaining such information, and shall effectively carry out its tasks of assessing the internal control system, which is essential to ensure the reliability of the information made available during the decision-making process. Banks shall have an internal organisation based on a clear distribution of responsibilities between the various units and functions, as well as clear hierarchical and functional lines of reporting. Each employee shall be suitable for the functions he or she performs, in accordance with a recruitment and training policy that meets the specific needs of the banks. In particular, banks shall identify and assess holders of essential functions, i.e. persons performing functions which give them significant influence on management or whose functions may have a material impact on their risk profile. Internal control functions shall have the empowerment, independence and capacity for intervention necessary to achieve their objectives. The administrative and supervisory bodies shall act in such a way as to make clear the relevance of internal control functions, patent in internal regulations, and the evaluation, career progression and remuneration of employees assrelated to these functions shall comply with specific criteria, separate and distinct from the criteria relevant to employees assaffecting commercial areas. The evaluation and career progression policies and the remuneration practices and policies of the banks should promote the alignment of the interests of the members of the administrative and supervisory bodies, as well as the other employees, with the purpose of sound and prudent management. Banks should have a conflict-of-interest policy that allows them to identify and resolve them. And rules are also set to ensure that the statutory auditor fulfills his mission with effective independence. 5. This is only a brief summary of the regulatory requirements imposed by European and national legislation in this area. But even so, it is enough to recognize that the rules are many and demanding. The reality, however, has shown that they have become indispensable in view of the absence or ineffectiveness of adequate models of self-imposed internal government. With the financial crisis, it was politically inevitable, due to understandable social pressure, that the internal government of banks should move from the dominance of soft law to the hard law plan. Are the regulatory acquis and the monitoring of compliance by the authorities sufficient to prevent behavior of the kind that were at the origin of the financial crisis? Certainly, this regulatory strengthening, established and supervised uniformly at European Union level, allows us to say that we are now much better equipped with regard to corporate governance requirements to ensure financial stability, which cannot be welcomed. But organizations are made up of people and, to this extent, the behavioral dimension has been recognized as essential for the effectiveness of a good internal government model of banks and other companies. Even the best models may not resist the determination of who wants to sabotage them. But the more quality they have, the harder it will be to do so, and hence the extreme importance of banks being endowed with a robust model of government. Without an institutional culture oriented towards compliance with standards and good practices, based on values that guarantee reputation and, to that extent, are also a source of value for the company, the objectives of public regulation may not necessarily be achieved. In fact, institutional culture is an immaterial concept but it is decisive for the effectiveness of corporate governance. The exemplary behavior develops in a social environment and it becomes more difficult to obtain it if there is no inherent reward. If society does not value the ethical character of behaviors, it can hardly be expected that an organizational culture can emerge in companies that favors the effectiveness of good government and good practices. Therefore, ensuring the effectiveness of good corporate governance is not only the task of companies, regulators and supervisors; the effectiveness of good corporate governance also depends on our collective capacity to create a society that properly values ethics. Thank you so much for your attention.
text_original: Lu... Interveno do Vice-Governador, Lus Mximo dos Santos, na Conferncia Corporate Governance: criao de valor para a sociedade: "Corporate Governance: importncia e limites" 25 out. 2018 1. Permitam-me que comece por agradecer o convite para participar nesta magnfica Conferncia e por saudar todos os oradores e participantes. Na pessoa dos Presidentes da Direo e do Conselho Geral, respetivamente o Prof. Antnio Gomes Mota e o Dr. Pedro Rebelo de Sousa, endereo as minhas felicitaes ao Instituto Portugus de Corporate Governance (IPCG) pelo seu 15. aniversrio, bem como pela oportuna realizao deste evento, e sado igualmente todos os demais membros dos rgos sociais. A criao deste Instituto h 15 anos foi um momento de inspirao, pois antecipou  numa altura em que o tema era ainda relativamente marginal  a importncia que a questo do governo societrio viria a ganhar. Portugal precisa de instituies privadas fortes de cariz associativo, que promovam o debate sobre temas que muito importam ao desenvolvimento das empresas e da qualidade da gesto, em sentido amplo, que sejam capazes de gerar massa crtica sobre temas complexos, como  o caso do governo societrio. Uma referncia especial se impe relativamente  concretizao este ano do objetivo de aprovao de um Cdigo de Governo Societrio, h muito prosseguido pelo IPCG, e que constitui, sem dvida, um marco no plano da regulao privada em Portugal. 2. O tema do governo societrio  objeto de uma j longa reflexo terica, com particular foco nos EUA, onde alguns autores localizam as primeiras utilizaes do termo nos anos 70 do sculo passado. No Reino Unido,  considerado pioneiro na matria o chamado Relatrio Cadbury, datado de 1992 e produzido por uma comisso constituda para avaliar  j ento  as causas profundas de um conjunto de colapsos empresariais. Desde a, a ateno dada ao tema do governo societrio  que tem natureza multidisciplinar, pois convoca conhecimentos de economia, finanas, contabilidade, direito, gesto e comportamento das organizaes  no cessou de crescer. A esse crescente interesse no  estranha, evidentemente, a sucesso de escndalos empresariais de larga repercusso pblica, mesmo antes da crise financeira, como foi o caso do Banco Barings (1995), da Enron (2002) e da Parmalat (2003)  para s citar alguns dos mais conhecidos, que de algum modo motivou a produo de um conjunto de cdigos de boas prticas de governo societrio por parte de organizaes internacionais de referncia como a OCDE, o Banco Mundial e o Comit de Basileia, entre outras. Mas foi a crise financeira iniciada em 2007 e as suas tremendas consequncias que trouxeram para o primeiro plano da ao pblica, incluindo no domnio regulatrio, os temas de governo societrio em todos os pases mais afetados e na Unio Europeia. Sem entrar na anlise das causas da crise  que so mltiplas , pode dizer-se que  largamente aceite que um dos fatores que a originaram e potenciaram foi a clamorosa falha dos modelos de governo interno das instituies financeiras. A ocorrncia da crise tornou claro o que j era apontado pela teoria: a atividade bancria tem particularidades tais relativamente s empresas no financeiras que  indispensvel que tenha regras de governo societrio especficas.
