Title: Closing speech of the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the Dinner commemorating the 30th anniversary of Porto Business School
text: Gove's closing intervention... Closing speech of the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the Dinner commemorating the 30th anniversary of Porto Business School 25 nov. 2018 Closing intervention[1] Mr President of the Republic, Mr. Rector of the University of Porto, Former President of the General and Supervisory Board of Porto Business School Exmo. Dean da Porto Business School, Ladies and gentlemen, Very good night , everyone. It is with great pleasure that I join the celebration of the 30th anniversary of Porto Business School. The occasion and the place invite me to share with you brief reflections on the decisive and indispensable contribution that institutions like this can make to the development of our country. It is clear to everyone that the aspirations of individual well-being and collective equity of Portuguese society exceed the production capacity of the economy. Such misalignment can only be addressed with more and better economic growth. We also know that what is between the Portuguese economy and the front-line economy of advanced economies is the productivity of every hour worked and not the number of hours each person works. In addition,: First, the qualification of human resources, including the qualification of managers; And second, the adequacy, robustness and quality of management models are two of the most important productivity 'levers'. The relationship between management and productivity of companies is well documented. Widely known academic studies, notably by Professor John Van Reenen, who was in our country this week at the invitation of Banco de Portugal, estimate that about 30% of the differences in productivity between countries are explained by differences in the quality of management. Port'scontribution to business school is thus decisive in promoting the productivity of our economy, and, in this way, as indispensable for the development of our country. The qualification of human resources Portugal has in recent years seen considerable improvements in the qualification of human resources. However, there remain significant distances from European averages, so we need to continue to improve the formal education of our workers. In particular, older workers, who typically have fewer qualifications, can benefit greatly from lifelong vocational training strategies, which give them the tools they need to make the best use of jobs of the present and the future. This is a work that Porto Business School already proposes to develop in close partnership with companies, through its Future of Industry Strategy and Skills methodology. Of course, the promotion of the qualification of human resources cannot be limited to increasing the number of years of schooling of the population and promoting the quality of education from a static perspective. If the accumulated skills do not fit what the labor market seeks, social discontent, waste of resources and damage to public finances are generated. Inclusive growth therefore requires two conditions to be met: First, it is necessary to ensure that the education system anticipates and adjusts to the that the productive sector needs. The educational offer must promote the development of transversal competencies such as leadership, interpersonal relationships or problem-solving capacity, and must also respond to the requirements of technological development of the country; Secondly, we must ensure that the legislative framework, the administrative context and the own management of enterprises generate the ability to absorb the skills Developed. If this is not the case, we will be faced with unemployment, coupled with a mismatch between supply and demand in the labour market, brain drain, via emigration of specialized staff. The adequacy, robustness and quality of management models For the combination of capital and work to result in the production desired by the market, we need an entrepreneur, an organization and a management model. This should take into account the social, cultural, institutional and technological development stage of the country in which the company is part. The management model reflects the articulation that the manager prints to the triangle that unites environment, organization and strategy. That is, the management model defines an organization, which designs a strategy, in order to make the best advantage, and even influence, the environment that surrounds it. With regard to the quality of management models, our country still has good scope for progression to explore, as is evident in the latest edition of the Global Competitiveness Index, published by the World Economic Forum. In the list of indicators in which Portugal obtains the worst ranking, there are some related to the quality of management models, namely the attitude towards risk, in which we occupy the 80 position in 140 economies, a predisposition to delegate authority - position 70 out of 140 - and the integration of disruptive ideas - position 46 out of 140. We therefore need management models that open up to risk and dismay and that favour a decentralised decision. It is also important that management open itself up to the world. Studies show that the presence of a manager with export experience increases the likelihood that the company will start, maintain or intensify its export activity. Exposure to international markets offers valuable learning opportunities to managers, positively differentiating the quality of management models. This result is particularly relevant for Portugal, where there must continue to be a reorientation of resources to the tradable sector. Betting on the tradable sector is an indispensable condition for the sustained growth of economic activity in our country. Porto Business School recognizes the importance of this international openness, as is visible, for example, in the ambition placed at its annual Vertex conference or on its alumni platform. On the other hand, in a productive fabric like ours, very populated by family businesses in transition to the 3rd generation, it is also crucial to think how we can reconcile the professionalization of management with the family property of the company. In this context, it would be important to develop a standardized model of family holding companies with statutory and fiscal treatment: that induces the holding company's commitment to the companies and the territory where they are Located and that is easily accessible by smaller companies. Let me finish by paying a vivid tribute to Engineer Belmiro de Azevedo. Their determination and audacity have been instrumental in this School being what it is today and will certainly continue to inspire what the School will be in the future. I warmly thank you for the invitation to be here and I hope that Porto Business School can live many years, disseminating management models capable of catapulting Portugal to higher levels of productivity, development and well-being. Thank you very much. [1] Ready for presentation. References Artopoulos, A., D. Friel, J. C. Title: Opening speech by The Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the Conference "Four Years of Single Supervisory Mechanism: Lessons and Challenges Ahead"
text: Intervention of opening of the Government... Opening speech by the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the Conference "Four Years of Single Supervisory Mechanism: Lessons and Challenges Ahead" 27 nov. 2018 Opening intervention Good afternoon It is a great pleasure for me to welcome you all. Today's Conference marks daniele Nouy's last visit as Chair of the Supervisory Board. It thus serves as an excellent moment of reflection on what we have already achieved and what remains to be done in the process of building the Banking Union, which began in 2012. The challenges of creating the Single Supervisory Mechanism With the international reforms of the financial sector that followed the crisis, efforts were made to develop a regulatory framework harmonised with stricter capital, liquidity and (private) loss-absorbing requirements to protect taxpayers. In the European Union, the single rulebook and the European System of Financial Supervision have also been introduced. In June 2012, the former Governor of the Bank of France, Christian Noyer ii, and myselfiii, on the same date, called for the creation of a Banking Union with a common supervisory mechanism. On 4 November 2014, the start-up of the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM) constantiated the challenge we had launched years earlier. It is, therefore, with particular satisfaction that four years later I see a system in full operation, justifying, at the time of passing testimony of the Chair of the Supervisory Board, a thank you to Daniele Nouy for all the work that developed over the last few years and for its decisive contribution to the success of this project. Daniele Nouy has insisted over these four years on the need for the SSM to be "tough and fair", words that many of those present will recognize. His perseverance was essential to establishing the identity and credibility that we all recognize today with the SSM. Today, the relationship with the SSM is part of the day-to-day of the European banking system, but four years ago, Daniele Nouy and her team faced the herculean task of creating a new European institution from scratch  I would say, an almost miracle. Moreover, at the same time that the new supervisory teams were recruited and formed, a Comprehensive Assessment was carried out on the largest European banks  which would be subject to ssm supervision  embodied in an analysis of asset quality and effort testing. Today may seem easy, but four years ago the challenge was colossal and unparalleled. In addition to logistical challenges, the creation of the SSM faced organizational challenges: relationship level and the creation of trust links with the authorities of national supervision, and implementation of the legislation that was being produced and implemented at the same time, in particular related to prudential requirements; Powers instruments and supervisory exercise; and the framework for recovery and resolution of credit institutions. The SSM's first priority was to restore confidence in the European banking system deeply shaken by the various waves of crises europe has faced. This is an expression in a set of relevant metrics since the Comprehensive Assessment, of which i would highlight: increase in capital ratios: the CET1 ratio increased by 2.6 percentage points between the end of 2014 and the second quarter of 2018iv, and the reduction of non-performing loans (NPLs): from 958,000 eur 657 billion (between the end of 2014 and the second quarter 2018), which corresponds to an average NPL ratio of 4.4%v. As President Draghi recently pointed out, European supervision has brought a number of important benefits when compared to the fragmented system of national supervisors by: i. harmonising supervisory practices, ii. adopt a system-wide perspective by monitoring and mitigating risks, and iii. reduce the fragmentation of the operational supervisory framework vi. In this context, a number of SSM initiatives over the last few years related to: i. the harmonisation of the supervisory review and evaluation process (SREP)vii, ii. adequacy and suitability assessmentsviii, and iii. work related to non-performing loans ix. The initiatives I have identified are only a subset of extensive work already carried out by the SSM. A work manifestly positive for the increased rigour and increased degree of intrusion and the improvement of the governance it has imposed, by focusing on a cross-cutting risk culture, which systematically questions the sustainability of banking in the present and future in terms of procedures and business model. Future challenges Although we can say that in the euro area we are now better equipped to respond to future crises, there are still risks due to the incompleteness of the Banking Union. Today, supervisory and resolution decisions are mostly European, while the ultimate guarantor of financial stability remains national, with limited tools to act. Como referia recentemente Yves Mersch, What matters is that liability and control are aligned. When taxpayers money is involved at European level, a European control function is called for. x It is therefore essential that, in the shortest possible period, a mechanism for deposit guarantee, a backstop for the Single Resolution Fund (SIF) and liquidity supply capacity in resolution. In the transitional period, the equipping of European and national authorities to ensure the stability of national, regional and European financial systems is a critical and decisive factor in the public acceptance of the process of European integration and democratic legitimacy. Although it is always difficult to anticipate where new elements of stability disruption will arise, some are beginning to profile on the horizon, whether in shadow banking, in the areas of money laundering, or in the still unregulated world of FinTechs and digital development. The fact that some 'traditional' large banks, subject to intense regulation, are now worth less on the stock exchange than some FinTechs gives an idea of the new potential sources of risk. Moreover, digital is not the only major challenge. The management of non-performing loans in balance and compliance with much more demanding regulatory requirements (notably in MREL) remains on the agenda. Moreover, the disappearance of fragmentation in the European financial market entails a number of challenges that we cannot ignore. The current European debate focuses on further harmonisation of rules by removing remaining national options and discretion, as well as on the use of Direct-implementing Community Regulations rather than Directives requiring national transpositionxi. Such harmonisation is seen as necessary for cross-border financial integration, which enhances greater risk-sharing in Europe. The concomitant acceleration of cross-border banking mergers will in this context be a long-term reality. This concentration process will be as fast as the less prepared the banks are to compete in Europe. At national level, it will be important to assess what investment needs are and where to bet to compete in a market where the delimitation of the national border is less and less relevant, against the background of the discussion on the location of decision-making centres. These challenges are in the best place in the priorities that supervisory board chair candidate Andrea Enria identified at her hearing in Parliament European Last weekxii. Priorities which are a continue of the work of Daniele Nouy, and are in line with the priorities identified by the SSM for 2019xiii. With the benefit of the experience of recent years, I would suggest as a matter of additional reflection: a the need to densify the ssm's decision-making process, and a need to clearly separate regulatory supervision. Let me densify these ideas a little. Firstly, it is necessary to densify the s decision-making process in order to ensure shared ownership of problems and decisions, for example by setting up intermediate committees with due escalation to the Supervisory Board. Secondly, it is imperative to clearly separate regulatory supervision and, in addition, to ensure the application of the principle 'a responsibility for financial stability, a regulatory responsibility and a supervisory responsibility'. The separation of the functions of regulation of supervisory functions is a necessary condition of the political legitimation of the standard of regulation ensuring its correspondence with the preference revealed in terms of the organization of risk taking and the role of the financial system in the process of sustained development; and is therefore a guarantee of the independence of the supervisory function vis-a-vis political power. The coincidence between the regulatory and supervisory territories is a guarantee of compliance with the principle of central responsibility for financial stability. In this context it is necessary to evaluate: i. how can we ensure and safeguard this basic principle at the level of Banking Union, and ii. what mechanisms for coordination and convergence between the territorial authorities of regulation and supervision may establish between, on the one hand, the Banking Union and, on the other hand, the other Member States of the European Union. Furthermore, the SSM should refrain from being a market configuration body and not overriding developments resulting from the interaction of economic operators in a context of fair competition. I would conclude by thanking Daniele Nouy for her coming to Lisbon, making a vow of a fruitful discussion during the course of this afternoon. Interveno de abertura do Governador, Carlos da Silva Costa, na Conferncia"Quatro anos de Mecanismo nico de Superviso: lies e desafios futuros" 27 nov. 2018 Interveno de aberturai Boa tarde,  para mim um grande prazer dar as boas vindas a todos. A Conferncia de hoje marca a ltima visita que Danile Nouy nos faz enquanto Chair do Supervisory Board. Serve, assim, como um excelente momento de reflexo sobre aquilo que j atingimos e aquilo que ainda falta fazer no processo da construo da Unio Bancria, iniciado em 2012. Os desafios da criao do Mecanismo nico de Superviso Com as reformas internacionais do setor financeiro que se seguiram  crise, foram envidados esforos para desenvolver um quadro regulamentar harmonizado com requisitos mais rigorosos em termos de capital, liquidez e capacidade (privada) de absoro de perdas para proteger os contribuintes. Na Unio Europeia, introduziu-se, ainda, o conjunto nico de regras ( Single Rulebook) e o Sistema Europeu de Superviso Financeira. Em junho de 2012, o ex-Governador do Banco de Frana, Christian Noyer ii, e eu prprioiii, na mesma data, apelmos  criao de uma Unio Bancria dotada de um mecanismo de superviso comum. Em 4 novembro de 2014, a entrada em funcionamento do Mecanismo nico de Superviso (MUS) consubstanciou o repto que lanmos anos antes. , pois, com particular satisfao que quatro anos volvidos vejo um sistema em funcionamento pleno, justificando-se, no momento de passagem de testemunho da Chair do Supervisory Board, um agradecimento a Danile Nouy por todo o trabalho que desenvolveu ao longo dos ltimos anos e pelo seu contributo decisivo para o sucesso deste projeto. Danile Nouy tem insistido ao longo destes quatro anos na necessidade de o MUS ser tough and fair, palavras que muitos dos presentes reconhecero. A sua perseverana foi essencial ao estabelecimento da identidade e credibilidade que hoje todos reconhecemos ao MUS. Hoje, o relacionamento com o MUS faz parte do dia-a-dia do sistema bancrio europeu, mas h quatro anos, Danile Nouy e a sua equipa enfrentaram a tarefa herclea de criar de raiz uma nova instituio europeia  diria, um quase milagre. Mais ainda quando, ao mesmo tempo que se recrutavam e formavam as novas equipas de superviso, se efetuava uma Avaliao Completa (Comprehensive Assessment) aos maiores bancos europeus  que iriam ser sujeitos  superviso do MUS , consubstanciada numa anlise da qualidade dos ativos e na realizao de testes de esforo. Hoje pode parecer fcil, mas h quatro anos o desafio era colossal e sem paralelo. Alm dos desafios logsticos, a criao do MUS enfrentou desafios organizacionais: ao nvel de relacionamento e criao de elos de confiana com as autoridades de superviso nacionais, e ao nvel de implementao da legislao que estava a ser produzida e implementada ao mesmo tempo, designadamente relacionada com requisitos prudenciais; poderes, instrumentos e exerccio de superviso; e o enquadramento para a recuperao e resoluo de instituies de crdito. A primeira prioridade do MUS foi o restabelecimento da confiana no sistema bancrio europeu profundamente abalado com as vrias vagas de crises que a Europa enfrentou. Tal tem expresso num conjunto de mtricas relevantes desde o Comprehensive Assessment, das quais destacaria: o aumento dos rcios de capital: o rcio CET1 aumentou 2,6 pontos percentuais entre o fim de 2014 e o segundo trimestre de 2018iv, e a reduo dos crditos no produtivos ( non performing loans, NPLs): de 958 mil milhes de euros para 657 mil milhes de euros (entre o fim de 2014 e o segundo trimestre de 2018), o que corresponde a um rcio mdio de NPL de 4,4%v. Conforme referia recentemente o Presidente Draghi, a superviso europeia trouxe um conjunto de benefcios importantes quando comparada com o sistema fragmentado de supervisores nacionais ao: i. harmonizar as prticas de superviso, ii. adotar uma perspetiva de todo o sistema ao monitorizar e mitigar os riscos, e iii. reduzir a fragmentao do quadro operacional de superviso vi. Neste contexto,  de ressalvar um conjunto de iniciativas do MUS ao longo dos ltimos anos relacionadas com: i. a harmonizao do processo de anlise e avaliao para fins de superviso(Supervisory Review and Evaluation Process  SREP)vii, ii. as avaliaes da adequao e idoneidadeviii, e iii. os trabalhos relacionados com os crditos no produtivos ix. As iniciativas que identifiquei so apenas um subconjunto de um vasto trabalho j efetuado pelo MUS. Um trabalho manifestamente positivo pelo rigor acrescido e maior grau de intruso e pela melhoria da governao que imps, ao focar-se numa cultura de risco transversal, que questiona sistematicamente a sustentabilidade da banca no presente e no futuro em termos de procedimentos e de modelo de negcio. Os desafios futuros Embora possamos afirmar que na rea do euro estamos hoje mais bem equipados para dar resposta a crises futuras, subsistem ainda riscos devido  incompletude da Unio Bancria. Hoje, decises de superviso e resoluo so na sua maioria europeias, enquanto o garante ltimo da estabilidade financeira permanece nacional, com ferramentas limitadas para agir. Como referia recentemente Yves Mersch, What matters is that liability and control are aligned. When taxpayers money is involved at European level, a European control function is called for.x Assim,  fundamental que, no prazo mais curto possvel, se estabelea um mecanismo europeu de garantia de depsitos, uma backstop para o Fundo nico de Resoluo (FUR) e capacidade de fornecimento de liquidez em resoluo. No perodo transitrio, o apetrechamento das autoridades europeias e nacionais para garantir a estabilidade dos sistemas financeiros nacionais, regionais e europeu so um fator crtico e decisivo da aceitao pblica do processo de integrao europeia e de legitimao democrtica. Apesar de ser sempre difcil antecipar de onde vo surgir novos elementos de perturbao da estabilidade, alguns comeam a perfilar-se no horizonte, seja no shadow banking, nas reas do branqueamento de capitais, ou no mundo ainda desregulado das FinTechs e do desenvolvimento digital. O facto de alguns grandes bancos tradicionais, sujeitos a regulao intensa, valerem hoje menos em bolsa do que algumas FinTechs d uma ideia das novas potenciais fontes de risco. Acresce que o digital no  o nico grande desafio imediato. Permanece na agenda a gesto dos crditos no produtivos em balano e o cumprimento de requisitos regulatrios muito mais exigentes (designadamente em sede de MREL). Alm disso, o desaparecimento da fragmentao no mercado financeiro europeu comporta um conjunto de desafios que no podemos ignorar. O debate europeu atual centra-se na maior harmonizao de regras atravs da remoo de opes e discricionariedade nacional que ainda subsiste, bem como no recurso a Regulamentos Comunitrios de aplicao direta em vez de Diretivas que requerem transposio nacionalxi. Tal harmonizao  vista como necessria  integrao financeira transfronteiria, potenciadora de maior partilha de risco no espao europeu. A concomitante acelerao de movimentos de concentrao bancria transfronteiria ser neste contexto uma realidade a prazo. Esse processo de concentrao ser to mais rpido quanto menos preparados estiverem os bancos para concorrer no espao europeu. Ao nvel nacional, importar avaliar quais as necessidades de investimento e onde apostar para concorrer num mercado em que a delimitao da fronteira nacional  cada vez menos relevante, tendo como pano de fundo a discusso sobre a localizao dos centros de deciso. Estes desafios encontram expresso nas prioridades que o candidato a Chair do Supervisory Board, Andrea Enria, identificou, aquando da sua audio no Parlamento Europeu na semana passadaxii. Prioridades essas que so um continuar do trabalho de Danile Nouy, e esto em linha com as prioridades identificadas pelo MUS para 2019xiii. Com o benefcio da experincia dos ltimos anos, sugeriria como matria de reflexo adicional: a necessidade de densificar o processo decisrio do MUS, e a necessidade de se separar claramente superviso de regulao. Permitam-me densificar um pouco estas ideias. Em primeiro lugar,  necessrio densificar o processo decisrio do MUS para assegurar a ownership partilhada dos problemas e das decises, por exemplo atravs da constituio de Comits intermdios com o devido escalar para o Supervisory Board. Em segundo lugar,  imperioso separar claramente superviso de regulao e, adicionalmente, garantir a aplicao do princpio uma responsabilidade de estabilidade financeira, uma responsabilidade de regulao e uma responsabilidade de superviso. A separao das funes de regulao das funes de superviso  uma condio necessria da legitimao poltica do padro de regulao assegurando a sua correspondncia com a preferncia revelada em termos de organizao da tomada de risco e do papel do sistema financeiro no processo de desenvolvimento sustentado; e , por isso, uma garantia da independncia da funo de superviso face ao poder poltico. A coincidncia entre os territrios de regulao e superviso constitui uma garantia de observncia do princpio da responsabilidade central pela estabilidade financeira. Neste contexto  necessrio avaliar: i. de que forma poderemos assegurar e salvaguardar esse princpio bsico ao nvel da Unio Bancria, e ii. que mecanismos de coordenao e convergncia entre as autoridades territoriais de regulao e superviso poderemos estabelecer entre, por um lado, a Unio Bancria e, por outro lado, os restantes Estados Membros da Unio Europeia. Alm disso, o MUS dever-se- abster de ser uma a instncia de configurao de mercado, no se sobrepondo aos desenvolvimentos que resultam da interao dos agentes econmicos num contexto de concorrncia leal. Title: Opening speech by the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the Banca Forum 2018
text: Intervention of opening of the Government... Opening speech by the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the Banca Forum 2018 29 nov. 2018 Opening intervention i Good morning It is with pleasure that I participate in the 2018 edition of the Banking Forum. The intermediation of savings through deposit collection and lending is now undergoing a transformation process that poses a huge challenge for banks, regulators and supervisors. In my opening speech, I will try to set out the challenges that banking, supervisors and regulators have to face, particularly those resulting from technological development, strengthening the regulatory framework and reshaping supervisory practices, after having reviewed the remaining challenges, which are the legacy of the crisis. As a background, the need to ensure the public good that is the stability of the financial system, which requires the robustness of the institutions that are part of it, is always present. The challenges of legacy In recent years, the banking system Portuguese has been characterized by a number of positive developments, which include: i. the increase in capital ratios, ii. improving its efficiency, measured by the cost-to-income ratio, iii. strengthening the liquidity position, iv. increased profitability, and in. significant reduction in the high stock of non-performing assets resulting from the volume and quality of credit granted during the decade 2000 to 2010 and the effects of the financial crisis. However, the banking sector in Portugal still has some vulnerabilities: levels of non-performing assets, which are still high both in absolute terms and as in terms relating to other jurisdictions, and concentration of exposures to some classes of assets, in particular the debt real estate market and some developing economies. These vulnerabilities penalise profitability and tend to generate mistrust about the robustness of banks' balance sheets, despite the fact that the value-taken applies to the accounting and prudential rules applicable in a logic of concern going. This risk of mistrust tends to result in lower price-to-book-value, greater difficulty in capital increases and higher cost of placing debt instruments, particularly those likely to absorb losses. This makes it difficult to meet the minimum requirements of eligible capital and liabilities (MREL) and limits the ability to grant credit. It is therefore crucial that Portuguese banks continue to comply with the plans to reduce non-productive assets that they have submitted to supervisory authorities in due course. In particular, it is also crucial that they acquire the capacity to accommodate a possible worsening of prudential requirements. The reduction of non-performing assets will generate greater confidence in the robustness of the balance sheets, on profitability and on the sustainability of institutions, contributing to an improvement in their valuation by the markets. All stakeholders are gain: shareholders, employees, customers, depositors and, above all, the public interest. Cumulatively, it creates a favorable context for strengthening the recovery of the Portuguese economy, reducing credit risk and improving the profitability and sanitation of balance sheets. This will allow banks to increase resilience and respond better to the progressive normalisation of monetary policy and the regulatory requirements resulting from the cycle. And also to increased competition from digital platforms and the entry of new players providing services on a cross-border basis in a mature market with overcapacity installed. At the same time, banks must continue to make structural adjustments, in particular in terms of reducing operating costs. It will be necessary to continue with the reorganisation of institutions and the reduction of excess installed capacity. This is the only way to adjust to a mature market and the accelerated transformation of the business model in terms of both production and service delivery processes and demand-side preferences, particularly with regard to face-to-face and digital distribution channels. The challenges of transforming the business model arising from the digital age Portuguese banks are now faced with a problem of transforming their business model in order to respond to technological changes and the emergence of new types of competitors. After a significant reduction in investment in information systems in the last 10 years, these are characterized today by the little agility to treat large amounts of information in near real time. This is a challenge, but also an opportunity. There are new competitors who will certainly compete in the market taking advantage of the extensive databases and their analytical and information processing capabilities. And there are other competitors who can both compete for niche markets and can be complementary entities or partners. In this new framework, financial institutions will have to choose between scale or specialization, taking into account their ability to tailor products to a fine market segmentation. The scale allows the optimization of production costs and the safeguarding of the margin of financial products destined for the mass market. Institutions that do not have the capacity to achieve the required scale will have to consider a position in which they will operate: complementary distribution networks of financial products produced by third parties, in a 'white mark' distribution model, in which they collect and apply client funds. Your asset will be the proximity and trust of local customers whose savings will capture and invest in products made available by those who have scale dispersion and risk mitigation. and as small business financing networks that require a relationship proximity in risk assessment. Also the pressure to reduce costs and accompany technological development will tend to induce a new paradigm of organization based on the purchase of services from third parties (outsourcing), whenever banks do not have scale to ensure the monetization of the corresponding infrastructure or the mobilization and recycling of the required skills. It is an outsourcing of functions that results from the need to compress costs and ensure the appropriation of technological developments in areas of support, but determinant, of the provision of services. This outsourcing will occur with both large and small financial institutions. This means that banks will thus become dependent on a network of suppliers that will also contribute to systemic risk. That is, banks will be the visible face of a complex network of service providers. In this context, cybersecurity ii is already a critical element of the operation of the financial system, and is now one of the systemic risks with a high degree of criticism. From the banks' point of view, and with a view to ensuring adequate and sustainable levels of profitability, it is necessary to: i. reformulate the business model by moving to digital platforms with degrees of sophistication in order to ensure the attractiveness of the products and services provided and customer loyalty, ii. increase the capacity to segment the market by discrimination against the risk of of pricing operations and fine tuning, iii. ensure investments in technology, which at 'cruising speed' should correspond to 10/15% of the yield, iv. recruit skills appropriate to the new business model and risk management cybernetic, and v. have governance models that allow for an adequate response in terms of compliance and compliance with prudential rules. From the point of view of regulators, central banks and other financial supervisors, new business models and the new architecture of the financial system require new approaches, resources and skills and collaboration between jurisdictions in order to maximise functional efficiency and minimise risks to society. All this means that regulators and supervisors will have to keep in mind the complexity of the network to safeguard financial stability and efficient ly channel ing savings. It is very important that regulatory and supervisory authorities do not interrupt the ongoing dynamics, but frame them and ensure, in particular: i. the neutrality of regulation, ii. fair and balanced treatment between incumbents and new entrants, as well as between jurisdictions, iii. the identification of new risks and the consequent adoption of regulatory and adequate supervision, and iv. coordinated action between regulators and supervisors. It is up to regulatory authorities to strike an appropriate balance between society's risk preference and the efficiency of the financial intermediation function. They are also responsible for promoting the level playing field between the different financial intermediation agents, which implies adopting rules and supervisory practices based on the activity and not on the nature of the institution. In turn, supervisors will have to move from a reactive to a proactive model, which implies anticipating developments in financial intermediation processes and continuous access to the flow of financial transactions so that they can verify their regularity and compliance with prudential requirements. To this end, they will have to provide themselves with new tools, associated with the use of artificial intelligence, that allow them to accelerate the detectedness of irregularities or weaknesses and corresponding corrective intervention (a.k.a. SupTech)iii . Conclusion I'd finish with a few final notes. The challenges that are the legacy of the crisis and still persist add to the challenges  but also opportunities  of the digital age. These are many, varied, relevant and already put today and not in the distant future. The requirement of new regulation to ensure the level playing field, as well as the allocation of the supervision of appropriate technology and skills and in line with the new risks, are the best defence of financial stability, an essential condition for safeguarding trust in financial institutions and the normal performance of the intermediation function. In this 'new world', whatever the organisation of the payment system or the intermediation of savings, it is essential that the functioning of the financial system and the capital market be guided by strict criteria of transparency, taking and setting of risk premiums, efficiency, profitability and sustainability of the financial intermediation function. This requires that all interests in attendance be taken into account, and that the public interest associated with the role of intermediation of development savings prevail. In this regard, I hope that this year's Banking Forum will be a valuable contribution to helping build as much shared vision as possible on the challenges and opportunities we face. Thank you all so much. i Prepared for presentation. ii Central Banking (2018), The battle for cyber resilience, 20 August. iii Financial Stability Institute (2018), Innovative technology in financial supervision (suptech)  the experience of early users, FSI Insights on policy implementation No 9.
text_original: Interveno de abertura do Governad... Interveno de abertura do Governador, Carlos da Silva Costa, no Frum Banca 2018 29 nov. 2018 Interveno de abertura i Bom dia,  com todo o gosto que participo na edio de 2018 do Frum Banca. A intermediao da poupana atravs da captao de depsitos e da concesso de crdito est hoje a sofrer um processo de transformao que representa um enorme desafio para os bancos, para os reguladores e para os supervisores. Nesta minha interveno de abertura, procurarei enunciar os desafios que a banca, os supervisores e os reguladores tm de enfrentar, nomeadamente os que resultam do desenvolvimento tecnolgico, do reforo do quadro regulatrio e da reformulao das prticas de superviso, depois de ter passado em revista os desafios que subsistem, que so o legado da crise. Como pano de fundo est sempre presente a necessidade de garantir o bem pblico que  a estabilidade do sistema financeiro, que requer a robustez das instituies que dele fazem parte. Os desafios do legado Nos ltimos anos, o sistema bancrio portugus tem-se caracterizado por um conjunto de desenvolvimentos positivos, que incluem: i. o aumento dos rcios de capital, ii. a melhoria da sua eficincia, medida pelo rcio cost-to-income, iii. o reforo da posio de liquidez, iv. o aumento da rendibilidade, e v. a reduo significativa do elevado stock de ativos no produtivos resultantes do volume e da qualidade do crdito concedido durante a dcada de 2000 a 2010 e dos efeitos da crise financeira. Contudo, o setor bancrio em Portugal apresenta ainda algumas vulnerabilidades: os nveis de ativos no produtivos, que so ainda elevados tanto em termos absolutos como em termos relativos face a outras jurisdies, e a concentrao de exposies a algumas classes de ativos, designadamente a dvida pblica, ao mercado imobilirio e a algumas economias em desenvolvimento. Estas vulnerabilidades penalizam a rendibilidade e tendem a gerar desconfiana sobre a robustez dos balanos dos bancos, no obstante o facto de a valorimetria adotada respeitar as regras contabilsticas e prudenciais aplicveis numa lgica de going concern. Este risco de desconfiana tende a traduzir-se num menor price-to-book-value, numa maior dificuldade para proceder a aumentos de capital e num maior custo de colocao de instrumentos de dvida, nomeadamente os passveis de absorver perdas. Esta situao dificulta o cumprimento dos requisitos mnimos de fundos prprios e passivos elegveis (MREL) e limita a capacidade para conceder crdito. Por isso,  crucial que os bancos portugueses continuem a cumprir os planos de reduo de ativos no produtivos que oportunamente submeteram s autoridades de superviso. E, em particular,  tambm crucial que adquiram capacidade para acomodar um eventual agravamento das exigncias prudenciais. A reduo dos ativos no produtivos gerar maior confiana sobre a robustez dos balanos, sobre a rendibilidade e sobre a sustentabilidade das instituies, contribuindo para uma melhoria da sua valorizao pelos mercados. Ganham todas as partes interessadas: os acionistas, os colaboradores, os clientes, os depositantes e, acima de tudo, o interesse pblico. Cumulativamente, cria um contexto favorvel ao reforo da recuperao da economia portuguesa,  reduo do risco de crdito e  melhoria da rendibilidade e saneamento dos balanos. Tal permitir aos bancos aumentar a resilincia e responder melhor  progressiva normalizao da poltica monetria e s exigncias regulatrias resultantes do ciclo. E tambm ao aumento da concorrncia resultante de plataformas digitais e da entrada de novos players que prestam servios numa base transfronteiria num mercado maduro com excesso de capacidade instalada. Em paralelo, os bancos tm de continuar a realizar ajustamentos de carter estrutural, nomeadamente ao nvel da reduo dos custos operacionais. Ser necessrio prosseguir com a reorganizao das instituies e a reduo do excesso de capacidade instalada. S assim se podero ajustar a um mercado maduro e  acelerada transformao em curso do modelo de negcio no que toca tanto aos processos de produo e de prestao de servios como s preferncias reveladas do lado da procura, nomeadamente em matria de canais de distribuio presenciais e digitais. Os desafios da transformao do modelo de negcio decorrentes da era digital Os bancos portugueses esto hoje confrontados com um problema de transformao do seu modelo de negcio, de forma a responder s alteraes tecnolgicas e ao aparecimento de novos tipos de concorrentes. Depois de uma reduo significativa do investimento nos sistemas de informao nos ltimos 10 anos, estes caracterizam-se hoje pela pouca agilidade para tratar grandes quantidades de informao em tempo quase real. Trata-se de um desafio, mas tambm de uma oportunidade. H novos concorrentes que, seguramente, vo disputar o mercado tirando partido das extensas bases de dados e da sua capacidade analtica e de processamento de informao. E h outros concorrentes que tanto podem disputar nichos de mercado como podem ser entidades complementares ou parceiras. Neste novo enquadramento, as instituies financeiras tero que optar entre escala ou especializao, tendo em conta a respetiva capacidade para adequar os produtos a uma segmentao fina do mercado. A escala permite a optimizao dos custos de produo e a salvaguarda da margem de produtos financeiros destinados ao mass market. As instituies que no tenham capacidade para atingir a escala requerida tero que equacionar um posicionamento em que vo operar: como redes complementares de distribuio de produtos financeiros produzidos por terceiros, num modelo de distribuio tipo marca branca, em que recolhem e aplicam os fundos de clientes. O seu ativo ser a proximidade e a confiana dos clientes locais cuja poupana vo captar e investir em produtos disponibilizados por quem tem escala de produo e de disperso e mitigao do risco. e como redes de financiamento de pequenas empresas que requerem uma relao de proximidade na avaliao do risco. Tambm a presso para reduzir custos e acompanhar o desenvolvimento tecnolgico tender a induzir um novo paradigma de organizao assente na compra de servios a terceiros (outsourcing), sempre que os bancos no tenham escala para garantir a rentabilizao das correspondentes infraestruturas ou a mobilizao e reciclagem das competncias exigidas. Trata-se de uma externalizao de funes que decorre da necessidade de comprimir custos e garantir a apropriao dos desenvolvimentos tecnolgicos em reas de suporte, mas determinantes, da prestao de servios. Essa externalizao vai ocorrer tanto com as grandes como com as pequenas instituies financeiras. O que significa que os bancos passaro, assim, a ficar dependentes de uma rede de fornecedores que tambm iro contribuir para o risco sistmico. Ou seja, os bancos sero a face visvel de uma complexa malha de prestadores de servios. Neste contexto, a cibersegurana ii  j hoje um elemento crtico da operao do sistema financeiro, passando a constituir um dos riscos sistmicos com elevado grau de criticidade. Do ponto de vista dos bancos, e tendo em vista assegurar nveis adequados e sustentveis de rendibilidade,  necessrio: i. reformular o modelo de negcio transitando para plataformas digitais com graus de sofisticao elevados, de forma a garantir a atratividade dos produtos e servios fornecidos e a lealdade dos clientes, ii. aumentar a capacidade para segmentar o mercado, atravs da discriminao do risco das operaes e do fine tuning do pricing, iii. assegurar investimentos em tecnologia, que em velocidade cruzeiro devero corresponder a 10/15% do rendimento, iv. recrutar competncias adequadas ao novo modelo de negcio e  gesto do risco ciberntico, e v. ter modelos de governao que permitam uma resposta adequada em termos de compliance e de cumprimento das regras prudenciais. Do ponto de vista dos reguladores, dos bancos centrais e dos outros supervisores financeiros, os novos modelos de negcio e a nova arquitetura do sistema financeiro requerem novas abordagens, recursos e competncias e colaborao entre jurisdies, de forma a maximizar a eficincia funcional e a minimizar os riscos para a sociedade. Tudo isto significa que os reguladores e os supervisores tero que ter presente a complexidade da rede para salvaguardar a estabilidade financeira e a eficiente a canalizao da poupana.  muito importante que as autoridades de regulao e de superviso no interrompam as dinmicas em curso, mas as enquadrem e assegurem, nomeadamente: i. a neutralidade da regulao, ii. o tratamento justo e equilibrado entre incumbentes e novos participantes, bem como entre jurisdies, iii. a identificao de novos riscos e a consequente adoo de iniciativas regulatrias e de superviso adequadas, e iv. uma atuao coordenada tanto entre reguladores, como entre supervisores. Compete s autoridades regulatrias procurar um adequado equilbrio entre a preferncia de risco da sociedade e a eficincia da funo de intermediao financeira. Cabe-lhes, igualmente, promover o level playing field entre os diferentes agentes de intermediao financeira, o que implica adotar regras e prticas de superviso baseadas na atividade e no da natureza da instituio. Por sua vez, os supervisores tero de passar de um modo reativo para um modelo prativo, o que implica antecipar os desenvolvimentos dos processos de intermediao financeira e o acesso contnuo ao fluxo de operaes financeiras de forma a poderem verificar a sua regularidade e o respeito dos requisitos prudenciais. Para o efeito, tero que se dotar de novas ferramentas, associadas ao uso de inteligncia artificial, que lhes permitam acelerar a deteo de irregularidades ou fragilidades e correspondente interveno corretiva (vulgo SupTech)iii . Concluso Concluiria com algumas notas finais. Aos desafios que so legado da crise e ainda persistem, acrescem os desafios  mas tambm oportunidades  da era digital. Estes so muitos, variados, relevantes e colocamse j hoje e no num futuro distante. A exigncia de nova regulao que assegure o level playing field, bem como a dotao da superviso de tecnologia e competncias adequadas e consentneas com os novos riscos, so a melhor defesa da estabilidade financeira, condio essencial da salvaguarda da confiana nas instituies financeiras e do normal desempenho da funo de intermediao. Neste novo mundo, qualquer que venha a ser a organizao do sistema de pagamentos ou de intermediao da poupana,  fundamental que o funcionamento do sistema financeiro e do mercado de capitais seja guiado por rigorosos critrios de transparncia, de tomada e fixao de prmios de risco, de eficincia, de rendibilidade e de sustentabilidade da funo de intermediao financeira. Tal requer que sejam tidos em conta todos os interesses em presena, e que prevalea o interesse pblico associado ao papel de intermediao da poupana no desenvolvimento. Neste sentido, espero que o Frum Banca deste ano seja um valioso contributo para ajudar  construo de uma viso tanto quanto possvel partilhada sobre os desafios e as oportunidades com que nos defrontamos. Muito obrigado a todos. i Preparado para apresentao. ii Central Banking (2018), The battle for cyber resilience, 20 August. iii Financial Stability Institute (2018), Innovative technology in financial supervision (suptech)  the experience of early users, FSI Insights on policy implementation No 9.

Title: Speech of the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the Dinner-Debate in the Order of Engineers: "Determining Factors of a Sustained Model of Growth"
text: Speech of the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the Dinner-Debate in the Order of Engineers: "Determining Factors of a Sustained Model of Growth" 29 nov. 2018 Intervention 1 Good night. I begin by thanking Mr. Bastonario, Engineer Carlos Alberto Aires, for the invitation to participate in this dinner-debate. It's with great pleasure that I'm here. I chose as the theme for this session the "Determining factors of a sustained model of growth". I believe that this is a theme that is of the utmost relevance and timeliness for Portuguese society. Indeed, the phases of growth, such as the one we live in, are especially opportune to reflect on the priorities and challenges for the future of our country, without the pressure of cyclical emergencies or indeferred adjustments. The fact that we may already see signs of slowing economic activity makes this reflection even more pressing. 1. Unlimited needs vs. Scarce resources The reflection on the pathways of growth and economic development must take into account that the aspirations of individual well-being and collective equity of Portuguese society exceed the production capacity of the economy. The level of development that our society can aspire to is well mirrored in several indicators. Portugal ranks, for example, in the 41st position in the United Nations Human Development Index. In front of us are more than two dozen european economies, which attest stouts the margin of welfare progression that we still have in our country. Recent World Bank data for the Gini Index also show an improvement, revealing that more than 40% of the world's economies have lower levels of income inequality than in Portugal. The exploitation of this margin of progression in terms of well-being and equity is, however, seriously conditioned by the productive capacity of the economy. According to the available estimates, the potential growth of the Portuguese economy has decreased significantly over the last two decades, more recently observing a recovery that needs to be strengthened. The inability to grow faster is reflected in the level of gross domestic product per capita that we have achieved: over the last decade, GDP per capita Portuguese has remained 30 to 40% below the European Union average, without converging with the richest economies. It is therefore important to identify and implement conditions that promote the growth of the potential product  that is, that make the Portuguese economy structurally capable of growing at higher rates in the medium and long term. Without more robust growth, we will be forced to live with limited aspirations by our own inability to generate the income that satisfies them. 2. Hours worked vs. Labor productivity What is different from the Portuguese economy from the front-line oecd economies in terms of GDP per capita is the GDP generated per hour worked, i.e. labour productivity, not the number of hours each person works. The revitalisation of labour productivity becomes especially pressing in the face of the foreseeable loss of labour. The birth rate in Portugal fell from 9.2 births per 1,000 residents in 2011 to 8.4 per 1,000 in 2017. On the other hand, the our population is ageing: the number of senior citizens per 100 children increased from 128 in 2011 to 155 in 2017. It is therefore urgent to use the 'levers' that can expose the productivity of our workers. I will address four of these 'levers', which are certainly among the main ones, and which are, in particular: First, the skills of workers; Second, the levels of capital per worker, or capitalistic intensity; Third, the adequacy, quality and robustness of management models; And fourth, the innovation ecosystem. 3. Factors that promote the productivity of every hour worked 3.1. Level of skills of workers I then start with what is perhaps the most intuitive 'lever' to promote the productivity of every hour worked: the skills of workers. In this area, Portugal has seen considerable improvements in recent years. For example, the proportion of people aged 25 to 34 who completed secondary education increased in Portugal from 33% to 70% between 1995 and 2017, significantly approaching the EUROPEAN Union average of around 84% in 2017. There are still, however, a gap between European averages and we need to continue to improve the formal education of our workers. In particular, workers with more years of work, who have fewer qualifications, have much to benefit from lifelong learning, enabling them to make the best use of jobs in the present and the future. 3.2. Capitalintensity The capitalintensity is another  and one of the most relevant  'levers' of labor productivity. Portugal has historically low levels of capital per worker. The recent unfavorable evolution of business investment, which decreased by 34% between 2008 and 2013, has contributed to aggravate this capital shortage. It is therefore crucial to increase investment and take advantage of this recovery to learn from past mistakes and to make much more demanding scrutiny of investment projects. Infrastructure and support services are available, investments in the non-tradable sector have been made, they now need to monetise them, creating capacity in the tradable sector of the economy. The recovery of investment is, however, conditioned by the high level of indebtedness and the low rate of savings that the Portuguese economy shows. In 2017, Portugal was the fourth economy in the European Union with more leveraged non-financial companies. The savings rate for individuals was 4.7% in 2017, well below the 9.7% in the European Union. This means that the resumption of investment will necessarily have to be made by strengthening the companies' own capital, either by the current shareholders, or by the entry of new shareholders, national or foreign. 3.3. Adequacy, quality and robustness of management models For the combination of capital and work to result in desired production and valued by the market, we need an entrepreneur, an organization and a management model. The management model reflects the articulation that the manager prints between environment, organization and strategy. That is, the management model defines an organization, which designs a strategy, in order to make the best advantage, and even influence, the environment that surrounds it. Widely known academic studies, notably by Professor John Van Reenen, who has been in our country for days, at the invitation of Banco de Portugal, estimate that about 30% of the differences in productivity between countries are explained by differences in the quality of management. In this area, our country has a good margin of progression, as is evident in the latest edition of the Global Competitiveness Index, published by the World Economic Forum. In this index, there are still 15 economies of the European Union ahead of the Portugueseeconomy. In the list of indicators in which our country gets the worst ranking, some are closely related to management models, in particular the the attitude towards risk, in which we occupy the 80 position in 140 economies, a predisposition to delegate authority - position 70 out of 140 - and the integration of disruptive ideas - position 46 out of 140. We therefore need management models that promote openness to risk and promote decision decentralisation. Companies with more decentralized management will certainly be more open to diseruption and therefore more innovative. 3.4. Innovation ecosystem Promoting innovation is precisely the fourth and final 'lever' of productivity i would like to highlight. The innovation capacity of economies involves an entire ecosystem of factors, of which three would be highlighted. First, the culture of merit and entrepreneurship and society's ability to learn and deal with failure. Innovation is a continuous process, the fruits of which can take many years to emerge, with a high probability of failure at the end of this journey. The mistake is therefore an integral part of innovation  its role is to select the best ideas. Secondly, the dissemination of knowledge within the business fabric and the ability of companies to incorporate this knowledge, whether in the generation of new products or production processes  the so-called "radical innovation"  or in the improvement of existing products or processes  the so-called "incremental innovation". Finally, and thirdly, the innovation capacity of an economy also depends on the adequacy of the financial system, in particular the capital market, to the financing of innovative projects. This is a very important point, which I will take up next on the role that public policies can play. 4. Public intervention As is clear, it is possible to find numerous synergies between the different levers to promote productivity. Public policies have a relevant role to play precisely in stimulating such synergies. Productive investment can be stimulated by the adoption of a legal and institutional framework that induces an attractive business environment  that is, a business environment that facilitates a more efficient and flexible allocation of available resources and promotes a reduction in the levels of uncertainty with which economic agents operate. The attractiveness of the business environment depends, as is known, on numerous factors, including, and only to mention the most important ones: The functioning of the labour market; The tax framework, in particular its stability, predictability and incentives underlying; Levels of bureaucracy; Or justice system; The insolvency and recovery mechanisms; And functioning of the capital market. The Doing Business ranking, published by the World Bank, is a very useful indicator for assessing the relative attractiveness of our business environment, in that it commities the various savings in the quality of the regulatory infrastructure that frames the activity of companies. In this year's edition, Portugal dropped from 29th to 34th position, which indicates that it is less attractive in the eyes of international investors. Of the 27 remaining Member States of the European Union, 13 are better ranked than our country. The indicators that most contributed to this loss of attractiveness are related to licensing for construction and compliance with contracts. In addition, the qualification of human resources can benefit from a continuous evolution of the education system, which is not limited to the increase in the number of years of schooling of the population and the promotion of the quality of education from a static perspective. It is essential to permanently adapt skills to the labour market and extend some curricula to cross-cutting skills such as leadership, interpersonal relationships or problem solving. Promoting networks that bring companies closer to sources of competitiveness constitutes a third potential line for public policy intervention. These sources of competitiveness can be: Other companies with which they may have synergies; Universities from which they can receive scientific knowledge and labour; Or even foreign market outposts. There is also an important role to play in public policy as far as investment in innovation is concerned. On the one hand, investments in the form of venture capital, especially fruitful in generating innovation, present increasing returns with the scale and geographical aggregation of companies, since synergies and mutual learning are critical. Thus, public policies that promote, for example, hubs or clusters of companies benefiting from these investments allow not only to expose the success rate of the investments themselves, but also to generate important positive externalities. On the other hand, financing radical innovation or startups is far from adapting to the primary mission of the banking system because innovation processes have long maturities and present high risk and failure rates. The financing of innovation processes therefore requires specialised operators. In Portugal, these specialized operators are still underdeveloped and have limited possibilities to join larger foreign operators. All this makes it relevant that the State can guarantee persistent sources of financing, ideally involving private investors, always with tolerance to failure and always oriented to long-term financial return. It would finally highlight the very important role that public policies can play in promoting the aforementioned adequacy, quality and robustness of management models. In a productive fabric like ours, very populated by family businesses in transition to the 3rd generation, it is important to think how we can reconcile professionalization of management with family property of the company. Empirical studies indicate that, as a general rule, the quality of management practices is higher in cases where management is handed over to people outside the family that owns the company, or to people other than the company's founder. The professionalization of management is therefore a necessary condition to ensure the survival and long-term sustainability of family businesses and, thus, preserve their social capital. In addition, the separation between ownership and management allows to safeguard and find a fair balance between the legitimate interests of the different stakeholders of the company (holders of capital, other financiers, workers, suppliers, customers, etc.), contributing, also in this way, to the sustainability of the company. Public policies can encourage management in different ways in family businesses: First, revisiting the tax treatment of the distribution of results, to promote differentiation between ownership and management and foster an appropriate balance between distribution of results and reinvestment of profits; Second, generalizing the obligation to submit audited accounts by companies, guaranteeing the manager the immunity necessary to counterbalance the the interests of the various stakeholders in the most beneficial way for the company; Third, developing and making available the figure of the "family holding company", as legal typification of a model of centralised management of the shareholdings of members of a family, adjusted to the specificities of family businesses, still optional and supplementary, with statutory and tax treatment -which induces the holding company's commitment to its companies and the territory where are situated, -ensuring the indispensable legal certainty - and that is simple and easily accessible by smaller companies. Conclusion Let me end by reiterating my thanks for inviting you to be here. In times like today, marked by such strong heterogeneity and so low global dynamism in productivity, it is critical to realize, in particular, how the quality of business management and the ability to absorb knowledge can condition such dynamics. A comprehensive, informed and participated debate is crucial to find the best way to bridge the deviation that still parades our country from the richest and most developed economies. I therefore welcome the Order of Engineers for the initiative, which I greatly value, to foster this dialogue and I am naturally available to answer the questions or observations they wish to make.
