Title: Opinion article by the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, in Exame Magazine: "Our common currency, the euro"
text: Opinion article of the Governor, Ca... Opinion article by the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, in Exame Magazine: "Our common currency, the euro" 31 jan. 2019 The history of the European integration process reflects the need to respond to the growing interdependence resulting from the shift to higher levels of integration. The euro was one of those answers. The euro was inevitable in the logic of European integration from the moment the decision was taken to create the single market and put the productive structures of the different countries in a position of fair competition. The creation of a single currency and the adoption of a single monetary policy, managed by a European Central Bank, arise as a response to the need to ensure exchange rate stability in order to preserve the functioning and integrity of the internal market. Exchange variations  even when they result from the functioning of the market  constitute subsidies/penalties for economic operators and create uncertainty. They distort competition, generate trade transfer movements that are not based on economic fundamentals, cause social discontent and trigger breaking forces. The Crisis of the European Monetary System (EMS) in the early 1990s is a good example of this dynamic. The SME scheme was not compatible with the degree of openness of the economies participating in the internal market, nor with the existence of autonomous monetary policies. This inconsistency led to the currency crisis of 1992-1993, in which the magnitude of the fluctuations forced an extension to 15% of the exchange rate rate mechanism fluctuation bands, with direct implications for intra-European Union trade flows. This has clearly demonstrated, in practice, that the existence of an internal market without a single currency necessarily represents an unstable balance. The euro has safeguarded the integrity of the single market and resulted in two decades of price stability. The euro eliminated uncertainty and foreign exchange costs in the euro area and provided European businesses and households with a set of concrete and visible benefits: lower transaction costs; more transparent and competitive markets and increased trade; greater security in savings and investment decisions; easier to compare prices, make purchases and travel within Europe; easier access to other markets and new business opportunities. The single currency and the size of the euro area provide new opportunities on a global scale and give the European Union and the Member States a greater weight in the world economy. The euro is currently the second most widely used currency in the world. It is a secure reserve, is used for issuing debt worldwide and is widely accepted for international payments. The euro has also, of course, brought demands in terms of the behaviour of economic operators. From the outend of the no longer, mechanisms for clearing divergences between Member States in terms of wage and price formation, productivity developments and excessive leverage, including in the public sector. Before the introduction of the euro, whenever the economic part failed, it was the exchange rate "cane" that directly allowed foreign competitiveness to be re-achieved and, indirectly, a real depreciation of public and private debts, through inflation resulting from exchange rate devaluation. With the single currency and the single monetary policy it is no longer possible to resort to the devaluation of the currency to compensate for productivity differentials or real appreciations resulting from differences in inflation and to re-re-create the competitiveness and employment of a given economy. It is also no longer possible to make financial repression through debt devaluation, with the consequent transfer of wealth from creditors to debtors, in particular to the public sector. This means that, with the loss of the exchange rate "cane", price and wage deviations have an impact on the unemployment rate and productivity deviations accelerate the perception of the structural weaknesses of the economy and the need to carry out reforms. The euro makes more visible the importance of disciplining public finances and ensuring financial discipline of private actors. Excess leverage requires financial adjustment by debtors, not to be penalised by creditors. Therefore, the euro eliminates the anesthetising effect ofthe bio mother rate and, at the same time, the uncertainty associated with its variation. A single currency implies a single monetary policy. In a context where there are markedly different revealed national preferences, there is a risk of inconsistency between national economic and fiscal policies and the common monetary policy. It was therefore clear from the outset that it would be essential to create discipline, rules and institutions that would reduce that disparity in order to ensure stability. And that this would only be possible if each of the member countries took over and applied those rules. In the euro area, this discipline is tantamount to recognising and assuming that the conduct of national economic policies is a matter of common interest, as the Treaties predict. Without a single centre of power, the effectiveness of the policy depends on the effectiveness of the coordination of national policies and the adequacy of measures. The recent crisis has shown the need for stronger economic governance and better coordination of Member States' policies. In response, improvements have been made to coordination procedures (e.g. the creation of the European Semester) and the scope of monitoring/coordination has been extended beyond the budgetary area (e.g. external imbalances). Monitoring macroeconomic imbalances and coordinating economic and budgetary policies will need to continue to be strengthened so that there is an overall view of the impacts of national policies on the group. It only takes advantage of the euro who knows how to take over the rules, interpret them and apply them in a mutually advantageous way. We must, however, be aware that, even with appropriate rules and institutions, a monetary union is not immune to exogenous shocks and specific problems in any of its members. The problem of how to cope with asymmetric shocks that do not result from economic policy (or common shocks with asymmetric effects) remains, especially when they have a dimension that requires time to strike a new balance. The euro is good for those who know how to play the rules, it is risky for those who do not internalise these rules and only correspond to a steady state if it has credible mechanisms to respond to shocks not induced by politics. Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) must therefore have stabilisation mechanisms that can support Member States facing serious financial difficulties while safeguarding the stability and cohesion of the group. These mechanisms should be robust, equipped with adequate financial means and designed to enable a rapid and effective response, while promoting accountability and minimising moral hazard. EMU is based on mutual trust, where responsibility and solidarity are inextled. The need to provide EMU with such a mechanism was one of the lessons learned from the financial crisis and the reason for the creation of a permanent institution, the European Stability Mechanism (ESM). A reform of the ESM is underway to strengthen its role, its capacity to act and the effectiveness of its instruments. This reform needs to be ambitious. I have always argued that the ESM should move towards a genuine European Monetary Fund. An institution with a clear mandate, with adequate means and with independence of action from the Member States, which brings together the essential conditions for the creation of solutions in which everyone wins (win-win), a pillar of the cohesion of the whole. In short, the creation of the single currency 20 years ago was a crucial moment in the history of European integration. Since then, a long way has been taken and much has yet to go. In recent years, in response to the difficulties arising from the financial crisis, there have been profound changes in the rules and architecture of EMU, which have aimed to make it more balanced and more resistant to shocks. However, EMU still has significant weaknesses and remains incomplete in some key areas, such as the Banking Union and the Capital Markets Union. EMU results from a sharing of sovereignty between Member States. Its construction is based on the permanent negotiation and approximation of different positions from the outset, safeguarding national cultures and identities and, at the same time, ensuring a sense of belonging and group. This implies an institutional framework with great capacity to understand and manage differences and ensure the articulation between the interest of the whole and the specificities of the parties, in order to ensure that the whole is greater than the sum of the parties. It is therefore important that Member States continue to work together and in a spirit of commitment to complete the path begun in 1999, so that European citizens can benefit fully from the benefits of their common currency, or euros.
text_original: Artigo de opinio do Governador, Ca... Artigo de opinio do Governador, Carlos da Silva Costa, na Revista Exame: "A nossa moeda comum, o euro" 31 jan. 2019 A histria do processo de integrao europeia reflete a necessidade de responder  crescente interdependncia decorrente da passagem para patamares superiores de integrao. O euro foi uma dessas respostas. O euro era inevitvel na lgica da integrao europeia a partir do momento em que se tomou a deciso de criar o mercado nico e colocar as estruturas produtivas dos diferentes pases em condies de concorrncia leal. A criao de uma moeda nica e a adoo de uma poltica monetria nica, geridas por um Banco Central Europeu, surgem como resposta  necessidade de garantir estabilidade cambial , para preservar o funcionamento e a integridade do mercado interno. As variaes cambiais  mesmo quando resultam do funcionamento do mercado  constituem subsdios/penalizaes para os agentes econmicos e criam incerteza. Elas distorcem a concorrncia, geram movimentos de transferncia de comrcio que no tm por base os fundamentos econmicos, provocam descontentamento social e desencadeiam foras de rutura. A crise do Sistema Monetrio Europeu (SME) no incio dos anos 1990  um bom exemplo desta dinmica. O regime do SME no era compatvel com o grau de abertura das economias participantes no mercado interno, nem com a existncia de polticas monetrias autnomas. Essa inconsistncia conduziu  crise cambial de 1992-1993, na qual a magnitude das oscilaes forou um alargamento para 15% das bandas de flutuao do Mecanismo de Taxas de Cmbio, com implicaes diretas nos fluxos comerciais intra-Unio Europeia. Esta situao veio demonstrar claramente, na prtica, que a existncia de um mercado interno sem moeda nica representa necessariamente um equilbrio instvel. O euro salvaguardou a integridade do mercado nico e resultou em duas dcadas de estabilidade de preos. O euro eliminou a incerteza e os custos de natureza cambial na rea do euro e proporcionou s empresas e s famlias europeias um conjunto de benefcios concretos e visveis: custos de transao mais baixos; mercados mais transparentes e competitivos e aumento das trocas comerciais; maior segurana nas decises de poupana e de investimento; maior facilidade de comparao de preos, de efetuar compras e de viajar no espao europeu; acesso mais fcil a outros mercados e a novas oportunidades de negcio. A moeda nica e a dimenso da rea do euro proporcionam novas oportunidades  escala global e conferem  Unio Europeia e aos Estados-Membros um maior peso na economia mundial. O euro , atualmente, a segunda moeda mais utilizada no mundo . uma reserva segura,  utilizado para a emisso de dvida a nvel mundial e  amplamente aceite para pagamentos internacionais. O euro trouxe tambm, naturalmente, exigncias em termos do comportamento dos agentes econmicos. Desde logo porque deixaram de existir mecanismos de compensao de divergncias entre Estados-Membros ao nvel da formao de salrios e preos, da evoluo da produtividade e dos excessos de alavancagem, incluindo do setor pblico. Antes da introduo do euro, sempre que a parte econmica falhava, era a bengala cambial que permitia, de forma direta, repor a competitividade externa e, de forma indireta, uma depreciao real das dvidas pblicas e privadas, atravs da inflao que resultava da desvalorizao cambial. Com a moeda nica e a poltica monetria nica deixa de ser possvel recorrer  desvalorizao da moeda para compensar diferenciais de produtividade ou apreciaes reais resultantes de diferenas de inflao e repor a competitividade e o emprego de uma dada economia. Deixa tambm de ser possvel fazer represso financeira atravs da desvalorizao da dvida, com a consequente transferncia de riqueza dos credores para os devedores, em particular para o setor pblico. Isto significa que, com a perda da bengala cambial, os desvios de preos e salrios repercutem-se sobre a taxa de desemprego e os desvios de produtividade aceleram a perceo das fragilidades estruturais da economia e da necessidade de efetuar reformas. O euro torna mais visvel a importncia de disciplinar as finanas pblicas e de assegurar disciplina financeira dos agentes privados. Os excessos de alavancagem requerem ajustamento financeiro por parte dos devedores, sob pena de penalizarem os credores. Portanto, o euro elimina o efeito anestesiante da taxa de cmbio e, ao mesmo tempo, a incerteza associada  sua variao. Uma moeda nica implica uma poltica monetria nica. Num contexto em que existem preferncias nacionais reveladas marcadamente diferentes, existe um risco de inconsistncia entre as polticas econmicas e oramentais nacionais e a poltica monetria comum. Por isso, foi claro, desde o incio, que seria imprescindvel criar disciplina, regras e instituies que reduzissem aquela disparidade, de forma a garantir a estabilidade. E que tal s seria possvel se cada um dos pases membros assumisse e aplicasse essas regras. Na rea do euro, esta disciplina equivale a reconhecer e a assumir que a conduo das polticas econmicas nacionais  uma questo de interesse comum, como alis preveem os Tratados. No existindo um centro de poder nico, a eficcia da poltica est dependente da eficcia da coordenao das polticas nacionais e da adequao das medidas. A recente crise mostrou a necessidade de uma governao econmica mais forte e de uma melhor coordenao das polticas dos Estados-Membros. Como resposta, foram introduzidas melhorias nos procedimentos de coordenao (por exemplo, a criao do Semestre Europeu) e o mbito da monitorizao/coordenao foi alargado para alm do domnio oramental (passou a incluir, por exemplo, os desequilbrios externos). A monitorizao dos desequilbrios macroeconmicos e a coordenao das polticas econmicas e oramentais tero de continuar a ser reforadas para que exista uma viso de conjunto dos impactos das polticas nacionais sobre o grupo. S tira partido do euro quem sabe assumir as regras, interpret-las e aplic-las de forma mutuamente vantajosa. Devemos, todavia, estar cientes de que, mesmo com regras e instituies adequadas, uma unio monetria no  imune a choques exgenos e a problemas especficos em qualquer dos seus membros. Subsiste o problema de como fazer face a choques assimtricos que no resultem da poltica econmica (ou a choques comuns com efeitos assimtricos), sobretudo quando tm uma dimenso que requer tempo para alcanar um novo equilbrio. O euro  bom para quem sabe jogar as regras,  arriscado para quem no internaliza essas regras e s corresponde a um estado estacionrio se tiver mecanismos credveis que permitam responder a choques no induzidos pela poltica. Por conseguinte, a Unio Econmica e Monetria (UEM) tem de dispor de mecanismos de estabilizao que possam apoiar os Estados-Membros confrontados com graves dificuldades financeiras, salvaguardando a estabilidade e a coeso do grupo. Estes mecanismos devem ser robustos, dotados dos meios financeiros adequados e concebidos para permitir uma resposta rpida e eficaz, ao mesmo tempo que promovem a responsabilizao e minimizam o risco moral. A UEM assenta na confiana mtua, onde a responsabilidade e a solidariedade so indissociveis. A necessidade de dotar a UEM de um mecanismo desta natureza foi um dos ensinamentos da crise financeira e a razo da criao de uma instituio de carter permanente, o Mecanismo Europeu de Estabilidade (MEE). Est em curso uma reforma do MEE tendente a reforar o seu papel, a sua capacidade de atuao e a eficcia dos seus instrumentos. Esta reforma precisa de ser ambiciosa. Sempre defendi que o MEE deveria evoluir no sentido de um verdadeiro Fundo Monetrio Europeu. Uma instituio com um mandato claro, com meios adequados e com independncia de atuao em relao aos Estados-Membros, que rena as condies essenciais para a criao de solues em que todos ganham (win-win), pilar da coeso do todo. Em suma, a criao da moeda nica, h 20 anos, foi um momento crucial da histria da integrao europeia. Desde ento, um longo caminho foi j percorrido e muito h ainda para percorrer. Nos ltimos anos, como resposta s dificuldades decorrentes da crise financeira, registaram-se transformaes profundas nas regras e na arquitetura da UEM, que tiveram como objetivo torn-la mais equilibrada e mais resistente a choques. Todavia, a UEM apresenta ainda importantes debilidades e permanece incompleta em algumas reas-chave, como a Unio Bancria e a Unio dos Mercados de Capitais. A UEM resulta de uma partilha de soberania entre Estados-Membros. A sua construo assenta na permanente negociao e na aproximao de posies diferentes  partida, salvaguardando as culturas e as identidades nacionais e, ao mesmo tempo, garantindo o sentido de pertena e de grupo. Isto implica um quadro institucional com grande capacidade para entender e gerir diferenas e assegurar a articulao entre o interesse do todo e as especificidades das partes, de forma a garantir que o todo  superior  soma das partes. Importa, pois, que os Estados-Membros continuem a trabalhar, em conjunto e com esprito de compromisso, para completar o caminho iniciado em 1999, de modo que os cidados europeus possam beneficiar em pleno dos benefcios da sua moeda comum, o euro.

Title: Opening speech of the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the Conference "VIA BOLSA - Financing Through the Capital Market"
text: Intervention of opening of the Government... Opening speech of the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the Conference "VIA BOLSA -Financing Through the Capital Market" Feb. 19. 2019 Intervencao1 It is with great pleasure that Banco de Portugal is again hosting the Via Bolsa Conference promoted by Euronext. This edition of the initiative addresses a number of topics that are also very expensive for us, such as financing the real economy, the Capital Markets Union and innovation and the financial sector. The financial sector plays a critical role in efficiently affecting the resources of any economy. Their strength and efficiency are fundamental to sustained economic growth, promoting employment and inclusion. Efficient financing of the economy requires the adequacy of fundraising instruments and financing models to the risk preferences of policymakers and the nature of investments and investors. In this logic, it is necessary to distinguish between the investments made by existing companies  in which the project risk tends to be compensated by the lower risk of the promoter  and the investment made by nascent entities  in which there is a risk of the promoter and the project. And this risk will be all the greater the more innovative the product. Innovation is part of the process of metamorphosis of business structures and is an important lever for the productivity and competitiveness of companies and the economy as a whole. Innovation capacity depends to a large extent on the adequacy of the financial system, in particular the capital market, to the financing of innovative projects. The financial system Portuguese, in the image of what is happening in most countries of the European Union, is dominated by the banking sector. Banks play a crucial role in resources to finance investment and, consequently, the real economy. However, they are not designed to finance certain types of investment, particularly those related to radical innovation, usually associated with long maturities and high failure rates. It is not easy to find investors willing to finance disruptive technology innovation companies during the early stages of start-up and development. These companies are potentially excellent investments, but they also face great challenges and uncertainties, with no guarantee of success. Financing disruptive innovation processes thus requires investors with more risk appetite and the ability to build portfolios that allow a positive sum. Specialized or institutional operators, with the ability to manage higher risk portfolios and with knowledge of the technology and market adjusted to the risk they will assume. In capturing savings, the capital market is very dependent on how it competes with the banking system in the binomial risk/remuneration. This means that it must be able to mitigate risk through transparency and investment products that partly absorb risks from specific projects, such as investment funds. Investment funds are an important tool for channeling private savings into the economy and increasing the funding possibilities of businesses and projects  including innovators  contributing to economic growth. In this regard, in the context of the development of the Capital Markets Union, I welcome the political agreement reached earlier this month with the European Parliament on measures to improve the market for investment funds in the European Union, in particular their cross-border marketing. The business fabric Portuguese is dominated by small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), with insufficient equity and inability to absorb losses. It is therefore necessary to diversify the supply of financial products and promote more companies' access to the capital market. From the point of view of companies, the potential advantages come from higher volumes of equity, lower leverage ratios and greater resilience to the economic cycle. Currently, we have a banking system that tends to mitigate risk by obtaining collateral and, therefore, favors companies already established in relation to new investors. On the capital market side, there is a shortage of companies that meet the transparency and size requirements needed to generate confidence on the investor side, even those with the greatest appetite for risk. We also do not have structures dedicated to the financing of new entrepreneurs, especially when they start projects at greater risk. Specialist operators are still underdeveloped and have limited possibilities to partner with larger foreign operators. In the framework of an economy that has chronic savings insufficiency and that in the course of an investment surge needs external savings, it is necessary to: On the one hand, that Portuguese companies have the capacity to issue assets attractive to international investors; On the other hand, that banks have the capacity to securitise their credits and these securities with international institutional investors. I would like to point out the recent entry into force of the regulations that allow the constitution in Portugal  similar to what already exists in other countries  of the Real Estate Management and Investment Companies (SIGI). Sigi's main activity is the acquisition of real estate rights, for lease sandorifies or other forms of exploitation. In addition to promoting the approach of the real estate sector to the capital market, SIGI can enhance the uptake of investors (domestic and foreign) with a longer-term profile seeking a diversification of their portfolio. The emergence of this type of company is also a potentiator of greater liquidity of the real estate market and the boosting of the rental market. These conditions are particularly important in the case of the Portuguese economy  where the housing market is dominated by housing itself  because they can contribute to greater mobility of the work factor. Indeed, studies show that labour mobility is countries with a dynamic rental market. In a few, if: 1. ensure that the financial system is robust and efficient in capturing and affecting 2. promote transparency, depth, dynamism and integration of European capital markets; and 3. strengthen policies and financial instruments to fulfil the resources; gaps in the financing of the economy, in particular SMEs and businesses high growth, we will be creating sound financial foundations that enhance innovation, sustainable growth and jobs. Thank you very much and good wishes. 1 Prepared for presentation.
text_original: Interveno de abertura do Governad... Interveno de abertura do Governador, Carlos da Silva Costa, na Conferncia VIA BOLSA -Financiamento Atravs do Mercado de Capitais 19 fev. 2019 Interveno1  com enorme prazer que o Banco de Portugal volta a ser anfitrio da Conferncia Via Bolsa promovida pela Euronext. A presente edio da iniciativa aborda um conjunto de temas que tambm nos so muito caros, como o financiamento da economia real, a Unio dos Mercados de Capitais e a inovao e o setor financeiro. O setor financeiro desempenha um papel crtico na afetao eficiente dos recursos de qualquer economia. A sua solidez e eficincia so fundamentais para um crescimento econmico sustentado, promotor do emprego e da incluso. Um financiamento eficiente da economia requer uma adequao dos instrumentos de captao de recursos e dos modelos de financiamento s preferncias de risco dos aforradores e  natureza dos investimentos e dos investidores. Nesta lgica,  necessrio distinguir entre os investimentos realizados por empresas j existentes  em que o risco de projeto tende a ser compensado pelo menor risco do promotor  e o investimento realizado por entidades nascentes  em que existe um risco do promotor e do projeto. E este risco ser tanto maior quanto mais inovador for o produto. A inovao faz parte do processo de metamorfose das estruturas empresariais e constitui uma importante alavanca da produtividade e da competitividade das empresas e da economia no seu conjunto. A capacidade de inovao depende, em larga medida, da adequao do sistema financeiro, em particular do mercado de capitais, ao financiamento de projetos inovadores. O sistema financeiro portugus,  imagem do que sucede na generalidade dos pases da Unio Europeia,  dominado pelo setor bancrio. Os bancos tm um papel crucial na captao e canalizao de recursos para financiar o investimento e, consequentemente, a economia real. Todavia, no esto vocacionados para financiar certos tipos de investimento, particularmente os relacionados com a inovao radical, normalmente associados a maturidades longas e taxas de insucesso elevadas. No  fcil encontrar investidores dispostos a financiar empresas de inovao tecnolgica disruptiva durante as fases iniciais de arranque e desenvolvimento. Estas empresas constituem potencialmente excelentes investimentos, mas enfrentam tambm grandes desafios e incertezas, sem garantia de sucesso. O financiamento dos processos de inovao disruptivos requer, assim, investidores com mais apetite de risco e capacidade de constituir carteiras que permitam uma soma positiva. Operadores especializados ou institucionais, com capacidade de gerir carteiras de maior risco e com conhecimentos da tecnologia e do mercado ajustados ao risco que vo assumir. Na captao de poupanas, o mercado de capitais est muito dependente da forma como concorre com o sistema bancrio no binmio risco/remunerao. Isso significa que tem de ter capacidade para mitigar o risco atravs da transparncia e de produtos de investimento que absorvam em parte riscos de projetos especficos, como  o caso dos fundos de investimento. Os fundos de investimento so um instrumento importante para canalizar a poupana privada para a economia e aumentar as possibilidades de financiamento das empresas e dos projetos  designadamente os inovadores  contribuindo para o crescimento econmico. A este propsito, no contexto do desenvolvimento da Unio dos Mercados de Capitais, registo com agrado o acordo poltico alcanado j este ms com o Parlamento Europeu quanto s medidas de melhoria do mercado de fundos de investimento da Unio Europeia, designadamente da sua comercializao transfronteiras. O tecido empresarial portugus  dominado por empresas de pequena e mdia dimenso (PME), com insuficincia de capitais prprios e incapacidade de absoro de perdas. Por conseguinte,  necessrio diversificar a oferta de produtos financeiros e promover o acesso de mais empresas ao mercado de capitais. Do ponto de vista das empresas, as vantagens potenciais decorrem de maiores volumes de capitais prprios, menores rcios de alavancagem e maior resilincia ao ciclo econmico. Atualmente, temos um sistema bancrio que tende a mitigar o risco atravs da obteno de colateral e que, por isso, favorece as empresas j estabelecidas relativamente aos novos investidores. Do lado do mercado de capitais, h escassez de empresas que preencham os requisitos de transparncia e de dimenso necessrios para gerar confiana do lado dos investidores, mesmo os que tm maior apetite ao risco. Tambm no dispomos de estruturas vocacionadas para o financiamento de novos empreendedores, sobretudo quando iniciam projetos de maior risco. Os operadores especializados esto ainda pouco desenvolvidos e tm possibilidades limitadas de se associar a operadores estrangeiros de maior dimenso. No quadro de uma economia que tem insuficincia crnica de poupana e que para ter um surto de investimento precisa de poupana externa,  necessrio: Por um lado, que as empresas portuguesas tenham capacidade para emitir ativos atraentes para os investidores internacionais; Por outro lado, que os bancos tenham capacidade de titularizar os seus crditos e colocar esses ttulos junto de investidores institucionais internacionais. Assinalo a recente entrada em vigor da regulamentao que permite a constituio em Portugal   semelhana daquilo que j existe noutros pases  das Sociedades de Gesto e Investimento Imobilirio (SIGI). A atividade principal das SIGI consiste na aquisio de direitos reais sobre imveis, para arrendamento ou outras formas de explorao. Para alm de promoverem a aproximao do setor imobilirio ao mercado de capitais, as SIGI podem potenciar a captao de investidores (nacionais e estrangeiros) com perfil de mais longo prazo que procuram uma diversificao da sua carteira. O surgimento deste tipo de sociedade  tambm potenciador de uma maior liquidez do mercado imobilirio e da dinamizao do mercado de arrendamento. Estas condies so particularmente importantes no caso da economia portuguesa  em que o mercado de habitao  dominado pela habitao prpria  porque podem contribuir para uma maior mobilidade do fator trabalho. Efetivamente, estudos mostram que a mobilidade laboral  maior em pases com mercado de arrendamento dinmico. Em suma, se: 1. assegurarmos que o sistema financeiro  robusto e eficiente na captao e afetao 2. promovermos a transparncia, a profundidade, o dinamismo e a integrao dos mercados de capitais europeus; e 3. reforarmos as polticas e os instrumentos financeiros destinados a preencher as de recursos; lacunas de financiamento da economia, em especial das PME e das empresas de elevado crescimento, estaremos a criar bases financeiras slidas potenciadoras da inovao, do crescimento sustentvel e do emprego. Muito obrigado e votos de bom trabalho. 1 Preparado para apresentao.

Title: Intervention of The Administrator Luis Laginha de Sousa in the Meeting on Green Financing between Banco de Portugal and the Delegation of Representatives of the Pan-Delta of the Pearl River (China)
text: Intervention of The Administrator Luis L... Intervention of The Administrator Luis Laginha de Sousa in the Meeting on Green Financing between Banco de Portugal and the Delegation of Representatives of the Pan-Delta of the Pearl River (China) 07 mar. 2019 Mr. Executive Member of the Macao Trade and Investment Promotion Institute, Mr. Advisor to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology of the People's Republic of China, Mr. President of the Environmental Scientific Society of Sichuan Province, Exmos. Representatives of the Authorities of the Macao Special Autonomous Region, Exmos. Government Representatives of the Provinces and Regions of the Pan-Delta of the Pearl River, Guests On behalf of me and on behalf of Banco de Portugal, I am pleased to welcome the distinguished representatives of a region that has not only been well known by the Portuguese for several decades, but is also recognized throughout the world for several decades for its eco-nomic dynamism. I am sure that this visit, which we greatly honour and with which we are very pleased, will be a former opportunity to continue the deepening of mutual knowledge between Portugal and China. This visit can certainly open doors to future joint initiatives, with benefits for both sides. I am referring in particular to initiatives aimed at fostering sustainability in economies and societies worldwide. But also for the combination of efforts to combat the negative effects of climate change. Furthermore, and in particular, for the promotion of green finance, as a key contribution of the financial sector to the achievement of the overall objectives in the area of the environment. As we are in a Central Bank which is a place where economic thinking is produced and a lot is discussed, both the issues related to economic activity and financial activity, I would like to share with you a conviction that is also the basis of Banco de Portugal's actions on the themes of sustainability This conviction has to do with the fact that, if, on the one hand, the economy produces income, by or for example, the financial system plays a crucial role in preserving the wealth accumulated with the income generated by economic activity. However, no matter how much accumulated wealth, there is no financial system that will last if the economy is not resilient. It follows that sustainability, based on the three ESG (environmental, social and corporate governance) pillars, is effectively an indispensable element. An increasingly notorious phenomenon on a global scale in recent years is the widening of consensus on the need to accelerate the pace of transition of economies and societies towards greater sustainability. It is a visible phenomenon in relation to the generality of the challenges identified in the ESG domain. But it is, above all, a particularly serious phenomenon on the issue of climate change  and the objectives set out in this regard under the Paris Agreement, adopted in 1915. Climate change is indeed one of the main challenges facing both our pla-granddaughter as a whole and each of its countries, in particular a genuine global and shared responsibility. The potential impact of climate change that is underway on our planet is now recognised by a vast majority of the scientific community and public decision-makers. There is, however, a wide margin of uncertainty about aspects such as cadence, magnitu and the geographical distribution of that impact. In the long run, Portugal may be relatively less affected than most countries, according to analyses in a 2018 IMF study. Still, the impact on the Portuguese economy and society can be very significant  and also differentiated depending on the regions of the country. In fact, portugal's physical diversity, the extent of its exclusive maritime area and its special geographical location in the world determine that issues related to climate change take on an expression substantially greater than the strict size of its territory. This perspective, as well as the recognition of the need to contribute to the global effort, has led to the development of a diverse set of initials over the last decades, with the participation of authorities, businesses and citizens. These initiatives were combined with certain deep trends in the Portuguese economy and society  such as slowing the pace of economic growth or reducing the weight of industry in GDP  allowing for significant positive developments in the environmental field. Gross greenhouse gas emissions, for example, fell by about 22% between the peak reached in 2005 and the value recorded in 2017  allowing the average target set for 2020 to have already been reached. The incorporation of renewable sources in electricity production is another area in which the country has been among the most advanced in the European Union (third in 2015, for example). The current objectives seek to prolong these trends, with government authorities recently assido that they intend to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050. Results such as these have only been possible thanks to a combination of varied initiatives over decades  including temporary tax incentives, more permanent tax adjustments, various order regulatory regulations and society awareness campaigns, among others. I would like to end my first speech by recalling two unavoidable realities: the need to foster a timely transition towards sustainability and the scale of the financial needs associated with this process. It will therefore be essential to ensure that the management of the risks and opportunities of this transition is based on a broad involvement of the private sector  and in particular the financial system. The multiple initiatives that have been developed in the sphere of so-called green financing, at an increasing pace and on a global scale, are of this importance for which public authorities tend to be increasingly awake. Regional, national and supranational authorities have a crucial role to play in advancing sustainability, both as regulators and marketers and as examples of good practice to be adopted. I conclude by once again welcoming all of you to Banco de Portugal and to this message of exchange and joint reflection. Presentation of The Administrator Luis Laginha de Sousa: "Banco de Portugal's Perspective on Green Financing"

Title: Article by Director Ana Paula Serra in the "Gender Balance Index 2019": "Promoting a culture of social responsibility"
text: Article by Director Ana Paula Serra... Article by Director Ana Paula Serra in the "Gender Balance Index 2019": "Promoting a culture of social responsibility" 27 Mar. 2019 At the Banco de Portugal, we follow a set of core values promoting the full development and professional growth of our staff. We believe we must set an example in how we conduct ourselves. That is why we seek to ensure inclusiveness and equal opportunities for staff, regardless of gender, age, cultural background or disability. We value diversity and have several measures in place to promote well-being through the continuous development of our staff and upholding work-life balance. The Banco de Portugal promotes flexible working arrangements, including the option to work remotely three days per month. We strongly support staff taking parental leave. In addition to the rules laid down by Portuguese law governing maternity leave (five months with 80% pay plus a time allowance of two hours per day up to two years), staff members can take three to five days on top of holidays (according to staff members years of service). There are various child subsidies to support school studies, including a birth subsidy for every new child. The Banco de Portugal supports sports and leisure activities for staff, retired staff and their families. Among several initiatives, the central bank offers holiday camps for children during the Christmas, Easter and summer holidays. In 2018, more than 660 children attended these camps. Sharing best practice in Europe In 2015, the Banco de Portugal joined the iGen Forum, a project launched by Portugals Commission for Equality in Labour and Employment. Members commit to reinforcing and demonstrating a culture of social responsibility, incorporating the principles of equality between women and men into their strategies and management models. This includes a Community of Practice devoted to sharing the best examples of actions taken to achieve gender equality. Private and state-run organisations must present an annual plan that takes into account gender equality. Members of iGen participate as guest speakers in a dedicated session that is mandatory to newcomers and which is included in our yearly induction programme. This session is used to raise awareness of and discuss several real-life examples of gender-related issues that staff members may have to address in the office. The Banco de Portugal participates in a Eurosystem task force created to discuss, share and reflect on diversity issues. All national central banks in the euro area are invited to present certain initiatives within this group, promoting the topic internally, and offering networking and knowledge-sharing opportunities. At the end of 2018, 867 of the 1,755 positions at the Banco de Portugal were held by women. Of new hires between 2016-18, 53% were women. The share of women in top and middle management roles in 2018 was 30% and 51%, respectively. This compares to 22% and 34% in 2008. The central bank appointed its the first female member of the board of directors in 1979. In 2008, another woman got a seat on the board. Since 2017, women have held two of the six board posts: myself and Vice-Governor Elisa Ferreira.

Title: Initial intervention by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in the II Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry into the Recapitalization of Caixa Geral de Depsitos and the Bank's Management
text: Initial intervention by Governor C... Initial intervention by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in the II Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry into the Recapitalization of Caixa Geral de Depositos and the Bank's Management 27 mar. 2019 Mr President, Ladies and gentlemen, Good afternoon I thank you for inviting yourself to be heard in this Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry (IPC) and for the opportunity to provide clarification stemming from the subject-matter of the committee. My presence was requested as Governor of Banco de Portugal and former member of the Board of Directors of Caixa Geral de Depositos. As for the first, and in accordance with resolution of the Assembly of the Republic No. 24 A/2019, which constituted this IPC, I understand that my presence was requested in order to to "to]detain the performance of financial supervisors (...) with regard to the defence of the interest of taxpayers, the stability of the financial system and the interests of other creditors and employees of the institution (...)". As for the second, having been part of the board of directors of Caixa Geral between 2004 and 2006, I will answer all questions about credits approved at meetings in which it has participated, within the limits of the documentation to which I had access and my essoal p memory. In this initial intervention, I will briefly address five points. I will begin by recalling the change in the paradigm of supervision in the wake of the international financial crisis. I will then comment on Banco de Portugal's performance as supervisor of Caixa Geral de Depositos; the recapitalizations of Caixa Geral de Depositos, which occurred in 2012 and 2016; and the performance of Banco de Portugal following the results of ernst & young's audit. I will conclude with some considerations about what I consider to be relevant to retain these results. 1. The change in the supervisory paradigm following the international financial crisis Let me then begin by clarifying the objectives of prudential supervision and how this activity is carried out, and by recalling the profound paradigm shift that has occurred in the wake of the international financial crisis. Firstly, and in accordance with the principles of the Basel Committee, it should be bearing in mind that prudential supervision aims to promote the security and soundness of credit institutions and the financial system with a view to safeguarding financial stability. As is well known, the difficulties experienced since 2007 in the banking system in different Member States of the European Union have triggered multiple public interventions, which have involved vast injections of funds to contain, inter among others, the so-called 'too big to fail' risk and safeguard financial stability. Portugal was no exception, not standing out prominently when compared to other European countries. The international financial crisis of 2007-2008 revealed significant weaknesses, including several shortcomings in financial regulation and supervision at the global level. In response, international authorities have launched a comprehensive programme of regulatory initiatives covering prudential, accounting and behavioural matters. The paradigm of supervisory activity changed materially in the post-crisis period. Supervision has become more intrusive, skeptical, challenging, proactive, comprehensive, adaptable and conclusive. Portugal followed the paradigm shift of supervision. In this context, Banco de Portugal has introduced a broad set of changes, both in its internal organisation and in supervisory methods. Its legal powers have also been strengthened as supervisory authority and substantially revised the prudential requirements for credit institutions as a result of an articulated process at European level. In particular, it refers to this Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry, as regards the regulatory framework, the repeal of Notice No 3/2006 by Notice No 5/2008, which has significantly updated and deepened the requirements required of credit institutions and financial corporations in matters of internal control. To safeguard financial stability, and taking into account the first lessons of the international financial crisis, Banco de Portugal defined for the three-year 2011-2013 a strategy based on four fundamental axes: i. strengthening the solvency of banks; ii. in the protection of the liquidity of the system; iii. strengthening the monitoring and supervision of the banking system; and iv. improving the regulatory framework. In this context, since 2011, Banco de Portugal carried out a set of cross-cutting inspections to the eight largest banking groups in Portugal, on a consolidated basis, inspections that were known by the acronyms SIP, OIP, ETRICC, ETRICC2. The objective was to ensure that the levels of unevenness recognized for the credit portfolios were adequate and that the methodologies and procedures, including the valuation of collateralassociated with exposures, were sufficiently conservative and aligned with best practices. In 2014, as part of the transposition of the Capital Requirements Directive (CRD4), changes particularly relevant to corporate governance were introduced into the General Regime of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations. These changes introduced greater density, requirement and scrutiny in the assessment of the adequacy of the members of the governing bodies, first ly by the institution, and also by the supervisor, in the light of the criteria of suitability, professional qualification, independence and availability. At the same time, the obligation to define remuneration policies and practices in line with the effective risk management of institutions, their long-term policy and adequate levels of capital and liquidity was established. Finally, as regards the paradigm shift in supervision, it could not fail to highlight the creation of the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM) in November 2014, which structurally changed the way supervision became in the euro area. In short, it follows that the time horizon covered by ernst & Young  corresponding to the period 2000-2015  goes through two markedly different phases in terms of regulation and approach to the supervision of financial institutions. This change in context must, of course, be taken into account when analysing the audit findings. 2. The supervision of caixa geral de depositos After this framework note, allow me to briefly comment on Banco de Portugal's supervisory action on Caixa Geral de Depositos over the period covered by ernst & young's audit. Until 2010, several inspections and supervisory actions were carried out for particular topics. However, no supervisory actions have been developed specifically directed at the credit granting process, certainly for the following reasons: i. the lowest risk profile of Caixa Geral de Depositos compared to peers, ii. the successive evidence of adequate levels of unevenness for the coverage of the risk credit, and iii. the level of comfort of successive administrative and supervisory bodies and external auditors, according to the information then available. The intensity of supervision through the use of inspections has increased significantly since 2010 as the crisis intensified and the international and national regulatory framework has become more demanding. In the context of these inspections, the levels of the default of caixa geral de depositos did not show any anomalous behaviour towards the banking system. The conclusions obtained with the cross-cutting inspections carried out by Banco de Portugal between 2011 and 2013 and the European Central Bank (ECB) in 2014, when reviewing the quality of the credit portfolio of significant institutions (Asset Quality Review, AQR), also did not find any concealment or material underestimation of losses in the credit portfolio. Without prejudice to these results, recommendations were still issued to caixa Geral de Depositos to correct the weaknesses found and strengthen the internal control environment. It should also be noted that, during the cross-cutting years referred to, caixa Geral de Depositos was reinforcing the credit-related oddities identified in the "top 25" ernst & young audit. 3. Capital increases at Caixa Geral de Depositos During the period under analysis, Caixa Geral de Depositos was the subject of two recapitalizations, respectively in 2012 and 2016, the main contours of which should be recalled. In July 2012, the Portuguese, as the sole shareholder of Caixa Geral de Depositos, made a capital increase totaling EUR 1 650 million, which resulted in a capital increase of EUR 750 million and an issue of EUR 900 million of hybrid instruments (commonly referred to as "CoCos"). This capital strengthening was linked to the exercise then carried out by the European Banking Authority to the largest European banks, which had as main objectives to improve the robustness of the institutions through: (i) the strengthening of better quality capital (the so-called Core Tier 1); and (ii) the establishment of a temporary capital cushion to address the risks of exposure to sovereign debt, given the uncertainty associated with the sovereign debt crisis at that time. According to the assessment then carried out by Banco de Portugal, this capital increase of 1650 million euros, as described, sem sufficient to cover the projected needs, taking into account the assumptions of caixa geral de depositos' financing and capital plan and macroeconomic projections at the time. This capitalisation operation was considered State aid in the light of European rules, requiring Caixa Geral de Depositos to submit a restructuring plan for approval by the European Commission. It should be noted that Caixa Geral de Depositos implemented most of the commitments of the restructuring plan that would be approved, in particular with regard to cost reduction. Between 2012 and 2015, Caixa Geral de Depositos's activity was  as with other national banks  very affected by the adverse developments in the macroeconomic scenario. Developments in both economic activity and interest rates have moved significantly away from projections drawn up by national and international reference entities at the date of submission of recapitalisation and restructuring plans. This had a very material impact on the results of financial operations and the levels of credit default. For example, the projections underlying caixa Geral de Depositos's financing and capital plan for May 2012 were projected for the period 2012-2015: a cumulative GDP growth of 0.7%, which compared to -2.8% realized; an average of short-term interest rates in the euro area of 1.1%, which compared to with 0.2% realized. During the 2016 financial year, in the context of negative reference interest rates and increased supervisory and regulatory requirements in relation to capital requirements, Caixa Geral de Depositos's capital position continued to degrade, making a new capital increase. Thus, on August 31, 2016, the Portuguese Decided to increase the share capital under the new business plan to be implemented in the 2016-2019 mandate, which amounted to around EUR 3 900 million, including the conversion of the 900 million hybrid instruments issued and subscribed by the Portuguese in 2012. The business plan underlies an agreement in principle between the Portuguese State and the European Commission on the non-classification of the capital increase as State aid, provided that the following assumptions are verified: i. the performance of an asset valuation exercise (credit portfolio and others) with a criterion consistent with what would be applied by a private investor; ii. the rapid reduction of the volume of non-performing assets. It should be noted that the very significant value of the recapitalisation was ore about a change in the valuation of non-performing assets, which resulted in a significant increase in the oddities recorded by Caixa Geral de Depositos in 2016, in anticipation of the capital increase. Specifically, we moved from a perspective of maintaining the assets in the balance sheet to a perspective of accelerated reduction of these assets, which had relevant impacts, among others, on the valuation of credit collaterals and in the determination of the oddities of the assets for which a sales perspective was adopted. 4. Ernst & Young's audit and Banco de Portugal's subsequent performance Allow me now, and before concluding, to leave some notes on the audit carried out by Ernst & Young and the corresponding implications for the performance of Banco de Portugal, within the scope of its supervisory powers. On December 7, 2016, Caixa Geral de Depositos asked Banco de Portugal to coordinate an audit of the management acts carried out between 2000 and 2015, and the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal concluded that the subject-matter of this audit did not fall within the scope of its duties. As is known to this IPC, I requested shady at the time of this deliberation. Caixa Geral de Depositos hired auditor Ernst & Young to develop this work, whose final report was transmitted to Banco de Portugal on June 26, 2018. The work developed by Ernst & Young aimed to analyze the compliance of caixa geral de depositos management acts with internal standards and regulatory principles in force in the period 2000 to 2015, for a sample of credit operations, acquisition and disposal of assets and operations related to strategic decisions. In particular, the work developed has found the following three strands: Workstream 1 ("WS1") - Credit grant; Workstream 2 ("WS2") - Acquisition and disposal of assets; Workstream 3 ("WS3") - Strategic asset decisions. In the analysis of the approval procedures for the claims in which the greatest losses were in place, Ernst & Young identified several non-compliance with internal regulations or applicable legal and regulatory requirements; this in cases of credits originated in the pre-crisis period, a time period, which as I described earlier, revealed the need to increase the intensity and effectiveness of the supervisory activity. In the light of the conclusions of Ernst & Young's audit, Banco de Portugal is acting in two respects, depending on what the law provides for: on the one hand, assessing the existence of evidence of conduct likely to constitute illicit acts of a counter-national nature and, on the other hand, incorporating the information collected in the context of the audit into the evaluation and revaluation processes of the conditions for the exercise of functions in administrative or supervisory bodies. 5. Final considerations Ladies and gentlemen, let me conclude by saying that the Ernst & Young audit is an important opportunity to bring to the public debate two aspects which I consider critical. First, the need to frame the results of institutions in the time and macroeconomic and regulatory context in which these results were generated. This means that, in relation to the large exposures that have generated losses, it is important to distinguish: on the one hand, idiosyncratic factors that determined losses as a result of a risk assessment by the institution that granted the claims; on the other hand, factors of a transversal nature to the banking system, and here an additional distinction between: (i) losses resulting from the evolution of the economic economy; and (ii) losses associated with excessive sectoral concentration, resulting from a focus on sectors whose growth was not sustainable. Secondly, Ernst & Young's audit is making clear the need for credit institutions to: have a so-called risk appetite framework, i.e. a business model supported by shareholders and an appropriate volume of capital for the level of risk who decide to incur; provide for risk assessment and management models that allow (i) to assess the the risk taken and (ii) incorporate into the price of operations the corresponding risk, while ensuring an adequate level of risk of provisioning, so as not to distribute dividends corresponding to premiums risk; provide them with models of government that ensure (i) compliance with the regulatory and (ii) discourage behavior stemming from the risk appetite framework, ensuring consistency of activity with the business model. Thank you very much. I am available to you to answer the questions you are embeitant ly. text_original: Interveno inicial do Governador C... Interveno inicial do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa na II Comisso Parlamentar de Inqurito  Recapitalizao da Caixa Geral de Depsitos e  Gesto do Banco 27 mar. 2019 Senhor Presidente, Senhoras e Senhores Deputados, Boa tarde, Agradeo aos Senhores Deputados o convite para ser ouvido nesta Comisso Parlamentar de Inqurito (CPI) e a oportunidade para prestar esclarecimentos relacionados com o objeto da mesma. A minha presena foi solicitada na qualidade de Governador do Banco de Portugal e de ex-membro do Conselho de Administrao da Caixa Geral de Depsitos. Quanto  primeira, e de acordo com a Resoluo da Assembleia da Repblica n. 24 A/2019, que constituiu a presente CPI, entendo que a minha presena foi solicitada a fim de [a]preciar a atuao dos supervisores financeiros () no que respeita  defesa do interesse dos contribuintes, da estabilidade do sistema financeiro e dos interesses dos depositantes, demais credores e trabalhadores da instituio (). Quanto  segunda, tendo eu feito parte do conselho de administrao da Caixa Geral de Depsitos entre 2004 e 2006, responderei a todas as questes sobre crditos aprovados em reunies em que tenha participado, dentro dos limites da documentao a que tive acesso e da minha memria pessoal. Nesta interveno inicial, abordarei brevemente cinco pontos. Comearei por recordar a mudana do paradigma da superviso na sequncia da crise financeira internacional. Comentarei, de seguida, a atuao do Banco de Portugal enquanto supervisor da Caixa Geral de Depsitos; as recapitalizaes da Caixa Geral de Depsitos, ocorridas em 2012 e em 2016; e a atuao do Banco de Portugal na sequncia dos resultados da auditoria da Ernst & Young. Concluirei com algumas consideraes sobre o que considero ser relevante reter destes resultados. 1. A mudana do paradigma de superviso na sequncia da crise financeira internacional Permitam-me, ento, que comece por clarificar quais so os objetivos da superviso prudencial e como esta atividade  desenvolvida, e por recordar a profunda alterao de paradigma ocorrida na sequncia da crise financeira internacional. Em primeiro lugar, e em conformidade com os princpios do Comit de Basileia, importa ter presente que a superviso prudencial visa promover a segurana e a solidez das instituies de crdito e do sistema financeiro, tendo em vista a salvaguarda da estabilidade financeira. Como  bem conhecido, as dificuldades sentidas, a partir de 2007, no sistema bancrio em diferentes Estados-Membros da Unio Europeia desencadearam mltiplas intervenes pblicas, que envolveram vastas injees de fundos para conter, entre outros, o chamado risco too big to fail e salvaguardar a estabilidade financeira. Portugal no foi exceo, no se destacando de forma proeminente quando comparado com os restantes pases europeus. A crise financeira internacional de 2007-2008 revelou fragilidades importantes, incluindo vrias deficincias na regulao e na superviso financeiras ao nvel global. Em resposta, as autoridades internacionais lanaram um vasto programa de iniciativas regulatrias, abrangendo matrias de natureza prudencial, contabilstica e comportamental. O paradigma da atividade de superviso alterou-se materialmente no ps-crise. A superviso passou a ser mais intrusiva, ctica, desafiante, pr-ativa, abrangente, adaptvel e conclusiva. Portugal acompanhou a mudana de paradigma da superviso. Neste contexto, o Banco de Portugal introduziu um conjunto amplo de alteraes, quer na sua organizao interna, quer nos mtodos de superviso. Foram igualmente reforados os seus poderes legais enquanto autoridade de superviso e substancialmente revistos os requisitos prudenciais aplicveis s instituies de crdito em resultado de um processo articulado a nvel europeu. Em particular, releva para esta Comisso Parlamentar de Inqurito, no que se refere ao quadro regulamentar, a revogao do Aviso n. 3/2006 pelo Aviso n. 5/2008, que veio atualizar e aprofundar significativamente os requisitos exigidos s instituies de crdito e sociedades financeiras em matria de controlo interno. Para salvaguardar a estabilidade financeira, e atentas as primeiras lies da crise financeira internacional, o Banco de Portugal definiu para o trinio 2011-2013 uma estratgia assente em quatro eixos fundamentais: i. no reforo da solvabilidade dos bancos; ii. na proteo da liquidez do sistema; iii. no reforo do acompanhamento e superviso do sistema bancrio; e iv. na melhoria do quadro regulamentar. Neste mbito, a partir de 2011, o Banco de Portugal efetuou um conjunto de inspees transversais aos oito maiores grupos bancrios em Portugal, em base consolidada, inspees que ficaram conhecidas pelos acrnimos SIP, OIP, ETRICC, ETRICC2. O objetivo era o de assegurar que os nveis de imparidade reconhecidos para as carteiras de crdito eram adequados e que as metodologias e procedimentos, incluindo a valorizao dos colaterais associados s exposies, eram suficientemente conservadores e alinhados com as melhores prticas. Em 2014, no mbito da transposio da Diretiva sobre requisitos de fundos prprios (CRD4), foram introduzidas no Regime Geral das Instituies de Crdito e Sociedades Financeiras alteraes particularmente relevantes em matria do governo societrio. Estas alteraes introduziram maior densidade, exigncia e escrutnio na avaliao da adequao dos membros dos rgos sociais, em primeiro lugar pela instituio, e tambm pelo supervisor,  luz dos critrios de idoneidade, qualificao profissional, independncia e disponibilidade. Em paralelo, foi estabelecida a obrigatoriedade de definio de polticas e prticas remuneratrias consentneas com a gesto eficaz dos riscos pelas instituies, com a sua poltica de longo prazo e com adequados nveis de capital e liquidez. Por ltimo, e no que se refere  mudana de paradigma da superviso, no poderia deixar de realar a criao do Mecanismo nico de Superviso (MUS), em novembro de 2014, que alterou estruturalmente a forma como a superviso passou a ser efetuada na rea euro. Em suma, daqui resulta que o horizonte temporal coberto pela auditoria da Ernst & Young  correspondente ao perodo 2000-2015  atravessa duas fases marcadamente distintas em matria de regulao e abordagem  superviso das instituies financeiras. Esta alterao de contexto tem, naturalmente, de ser tida em conta na anlise das concluses da auditoria. 2. A superviso da Caixa Geral de Depsitos Feita esta nota de enquadramento, permitam-me que comente brevemente a ao de superviso do Banco de Portugal relativa  Caixa Geral de Depsitos ao longo do perodo coberto pela auditoria da Ernst & Young. At 2010, foram realizadas diversas inspees e aes de superviso visando temas particulares. No foram, contudo, desenvolvidas aes de superviso especificamente dirigidas ao processo de concesso de crdito, seguramente, pelas seguintes razes: i. o menor perfil de risco da Caixa Geral de Depsitos comparativamente aos pares, ii. a sucessiva evidncia de nveis de imparidade adequados para a cobertura do risco de crdito, e iii. o nvel de conforto dos sucessivos rgos de administrao e de fiscalizao e dos auditores externos, de acordo com as informaes ento disponveis. A intensidade da superviso atravs do recurso a inspees aumentou significativamente a partir de 2010,  medida que a crise se intensificou e o enquadramento regulatrio internacional e nacional se tornou mais exigente. No mbito destas inspees, os nveis de imparidade da Caixa Geral de Depsitos no revelavam qualquer comportamento anmalo relativamente ao sistema bancrio. As concluses obtidas com as inspees transversais realizadas pelo Banco de Portugal, entre 2011 e 2013, e pelo Banco Central Europeu (BCE), em 2014, aquando da reviso da qualidade da carteira de crdito das instituies significativas (Asset Quality Review, AQR), tambm no detetaram qualquer ocultao ou subestimao relevante de perdas na carteira de crdito. Sem prejuzo destes resultados, foram, ainda assim, emitidas recomendaes  Caixa Geral de Depsitos para corrigir as fragilidades detetadas e reforar o ambiente de controlo interno. Convm igualmente ressalvar que, ao longo dos exerccios transversais referidos, a Caixa Geral de Depsitos foi reforando as imparidades associadas a crditos identificados no top 25 da auditoria da Ernst & Young. 3. Os aumentos de capital da Caixa Geral de Depsitos Durante o perodo em anlise, a Caixa Geral de Depsitos foi objeto de duas recapitalizaes, respetivamente em 2012 e em 2016, cujos principais contornos importa aqui recordar. Em julho de 2012, o Estado Portugus, na qualidade de acionista nico da Caixa Geral de Depsitos, efetuou um reforo de capital no total de 1 650 milhes de euros, que se traduziu num aumento de capital de 750 milhes de euros e numa emisso de 900 milhes de euros de instrumentos hbridos (comummente designados por CoCos). Este reforo de capital esteve associado ao exerccio ento efetuado pela Autoridade Bancria Europeia aos maiores bancos europeus, que teve como principais objetivos melhorar a robustez das instituies atravs: (i) do reforo do capital de melhor qualidade (o chamado Core Tier 1); e (ii) da constituio de uma almofada temporria de capital para fazer face aos riscos de exposio a dvida soberana, dada a incerteza associada  crise da dvida soberana naquele perodo. De acordo com a avaliao ento realizada pelo Banco de Portugal, este aumento de capital de 1650 milhes de euros, nos termos descritos, afigurava-se suficiente para cobrir as necessidades projetadas, tendo em considerao os pressupostos do plano de financiamento e de capital da Caixa Geral de Depsitos e as projees macroeconmicas  poca. Esta operao de capitalizao foi considerada ajuda de Estado  luz das regras europeias, obrigando a Caixa Geral de Depsitos a submeter  aprovao da Comisso Europeia um plano de reestruturao.  de referir que a Caixa Geral de Depsitos implementou a maior parte dos compromissos do plano de reestruturao que viria a ser aprovado, em particular no que diz respeito  reduo de custos. Entre 2012 e 2015, a atividade da Caixa Geral de Depsitos foi   semelhana do verificado com os restantes bancos nacionais  muito afetada pela evoluo adversa do cenrio macroeconmico. Com efeito, a evoluo quer da atividade econmica quer das taxas de juro afastou-se significativamente das projees elaboradas pelas entidades nacionais e internacionais de referncia  data da submisso dos planos de recapitalizao e de reestruturao. Tal teve impacto muito material nos resultados de operaes financeiras e nos nveis de incumprimento do crdito. A ttulo de exemplo, as projees subjacentes ao plano de financiamento e de capital da Caixa Geral de Depsitos de maio de 2012 perspetivavam para o perodo de 2012 a 2015: um crescimento acumulado do PIB de 0.7%, que compara com -2.8% realizado; uma mdia das taxas de juro de curto prazo na rea do euro de 1.1%, que compara com 0.2% realizado. Durante o exerccio de 2016, num contexto de taxas de juro de referncia negativas e de maiores exigncias de superviso e regulatrias relativamente aos requisitos de capital, a posio de capital da Caixa Geral de Depsitos continuou a degradar-se tornando premente um novo reforo de capital. Assim, em 31 de agosto de 2016, o Estado Portugus deliberou um aumento de capital social no mbito do novo plano de negcios a ser implementado no mandato 2016-2019, o qual veio a ascender a cerca de 3 900 milhes de euros, incluindo-se neste caso a converso dos 900 milhes de instrumentos hbridos emitidos e subscritos pelo Estado Portugus em 2012. O plano de negcios tinha subjacente um acordo de princpio entre o Estado Portugus e a Comisso Europeia quanto  no qualificao do aumento de capital como auxlio de Estado, desde que verificados os seguintes pressupostos: i. a realizao de um exerccio de avaliao de ativos (carteira de crdito e outros) com um critrio consistente com o que seria aplicado por um investidor privado; ii. a reduo, de forma rpida, do volume de ativos no produtivos. Importa referir que o valor muito significativo da recapitalizao ficou a dever-se a uma alterao da perspetiva de valorizao dos ativos no produtivos, que se traduziu num aumento muito significativo das imparidades registadas pela Caixa Geral de Depsitos no exerccio de 2016, em antecipao do aumento de capital. Concretamente, passou-se de uma perspetiva de manuteno dos ativos no balano para uma perspetiva de reduo acelerada desses ativos, o que teve impactos relevantes, entre outros, na valorizao dos colaterais de crdito e na determinao das imparidades dos ativos para os quais foi adotada uma perspetiva de venda. 4. A auditoria da Ernst & Young e a atuao subsequente do Banco de Portugal Permitam-me agora, e antes de concluir, deixar algumas notas sobre a auditoria realizada pela Ernst & Young e as correspondentes implicaes para a atuao do Banco de Portugal, no mbito das suas competncias de superviso. Em 7 de dezembro de 2016, a Caixa Geral de Depsitos solicitou ao Banco de Portugal que coordenasse uma auditoria aos atos de gesto praticados entre 2000 e 2015, tendo o Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Portugal concludo que o objeto dessa auditoria no se enquadrava no mbito das suas atribuies. Como  do conhecimento desta CPI, solicitei escusa aquando desta deliberao. A Caixa Geral de Depsitos contratou a auditora Ernst & Young para desenvolver este trabalho, cujo relatrio final foi transmitido ao Banco de Portugal em 26 de junho de 2018. O trabalho desenvolvido pela Ernst & Young teve como objetivo a anlise da conformidade dos atos de gesto da Caixa Geral de Depsitos com as normas internas e os princpios regulamentares em vigor no perodo de 2000 a 2015, para uma amostra de operaes de crdito, aquisio e alienao de ativos e operaes relacionadas com decises estratgicas. Em concreto, o trabalho desenvolvido abarcou as seguintes trs vertentes: Workstream 1 (WS1)  Concesso de crdito; Workstream 2 (WS2)  Aquisio e alienao de ativos; Workstream 3 (WS3)  Decises estratgicas de ativos. Na anlise dos procedimentos de aprovao dos crditos em que se verificaram maiores perdas, a Ernst & Young identificou diversas desconformidades com os normativos internos ou requisitos legais e regulamentares aplicveis; isto nos casos de crditos originados no perodo pr-crise, perodo temporal, que conforme descrevi anteriormente, revelou a necessidade de aumentar a intensidade e a efetividade da atividade de superviso. Atentas as concluses da auditoria da Ernst & Young, o Banco de Portugal est a atuar em duas vertentes, em funo daquilo que a lei prev: por um lado, avaliando a existncia de indcios de condutas suscetveis de configurar ilcitos de natureza contraordenacional e, por outro lado, incorporando a informao recolhida no mbito da auditoria nos processos de avaliao e reavaliao das condies para o exerccio de funes em rgos de administrao ou fiscalizao. 5. Consideraes finais Senhores Deputados, permitam-me concluir referindo que a auditoria da Ernst & Young constitui uma importante oportunidade para trazer ao debate pblico dois aspetos que considero crticos. Em primeiro lugar, a necessidade de enquadrar os resultados das instituies no tempo e no contexto macroeconmico e regulatrio em que esses resultados foram gerados. Significa isto que, relativamente s grandes exposies que geraram perdas, importa distinguir: por um lado, fatores idiossincrticos que determinaram perdas em resultado de uma m avaliao de risco por parte da instituio que concedeu os crditos; por outro lado, fatores de natureza transversal ao sistema bancrio, cabendo aqui uma distino adicional entre: (i) perdas resultantes da evoluo da conjuntura econmica; e (ii) perdas associadas a uma concentrao setorial excessiva, resultado de uma aposta em setores cujo crescimento no era sustentvel. Em segundo lugar, a auditoria da Ernst & Young vem tornar muito clara a necessidade de as instituies de crdito: disporem de um chamado risk appetite framework, ou seja de um modelo de negcio suportado pelos acionistas e de um volume de capital adequado para o nvel de risco que decidem incorrer; se dotarem de modelos de avaliao e gesto de risco que permitam (i) avaliar prospectivamente o risco tomado e (ii) incorporar no preo das operaes o prmio de risco correspondente, ao mesmo tempo que asseguram um nvel adequado de provisionamento, por forma a no distribuir dividendos que correspondem a prmios de risco; se dotarem de modelos de governo que garantam (i) o cumprimento do quadro regulatrio e (ii) desincentivem comportamentos que contrariem o risk appetite framework, garantindo consistncia da atividade com o modelo de negcio. Muito obrigado. Fico  disposio dos Senhores Deputados para responder s questes que entendam colocar.
