Title: Article by Elisa Ferreira Vice-Governor of Banco de Portugal at the Eurofi Magazine: "Enabling the orderly management of failing locally systemic relevant banks"
text: Article by Elisa Ferreira Vice-Governor of Banco de Portugal at the Eurofi Magazine: "Enabling the orderly management of failing locally systemic relevant banks" 04 Apr. 2019 Remarkable progress has been made in the setting-up of the first pillars of Banking Union. However, its incompleteness poses renewed challenges that policymakers need to address. Absent stabilisation mechanisms  a fully-fledged EDIS, the provision of liquidity in resolution, etc.  in the short to medium term, banks will continue to be European in life but national in death. While supervisory and resolution decisions are mostly European, the ultimate guarantor of financial stability remains national. This unstable balance prevents economic agents from fully reaping the expected benefits of economic integration via a single market for wholesale and retail financial services. As stressed, among others, by Fernando Restoy, whereas MREL and bail-in requirements may work for larger banks, it is not clear whether such requirements are suited for a middle class of institutions that operate on a more traditional business model and which may be of no public interest at EU level but still have systemic relevance at local level. Solutions thus need to be found for the orderly exit of traditional medium-sized deposit- taking banks without disrupting financial stability. Otherwise, Member States will continue to be accused of circumventing the existing rules when adopting solutions whose ultimate objective is to safeguard financial stability and mitigate the economic impact of potential disorderly liquidations or resolution actions. Recent experience has shown the current framework might not be appropriate to address such cases. As an alternative, the topic of harmonising EU banks liquidation regimes has been put on the agenda. But what does bank liquidation mean? And do we have the tools to ensure its orderliness in the current context? Let us acknowledge that this is not a silver bullet. In the absence of an appropriate legal framework, liquidation might imply the immediate interruption of lending support, as well as the suspension of payments; it may have disruptive effects for creditors, depositors and other stakeholders, with the ensuing impact on the real economy, ultimately reinforcing the sovereign-bank doom loop. Instead of moving immediately towards the harmonisation of EU banks liquidation regimes, efforts must be made towards the establishment of an enabling framework for the orderly management of failing locally systemic relevant banks, combining elements of the resolution and liquidation frameworks  akin to the FDIC approach in the USA  while minimising losses and protecting relevant creditors and non-financial borrowers. Such enabling framework should include the definition of high level principles to be agreed by all Member States and applicable at national level. Possible paths might include: The establishment of special insolvency proceedings, with recourse to administrative options, assigning to a liquidating authority some of the instruments currently envisaged in the BRRD, as an alternative to the court-led liquidation regime. The liquidating authority and the funding sources available would need to be identified. The use of DGSs for deposit transfers abiding by the least cost principle. For that, a revision of the applicable State aid rules and of the national transpositions of the DGSD would be required. The liquidating authority having the option to offer guarantees or enter into profit and loss sharing regimes.

Title: Opinion article by Administrator Hlder Rosalino in the Business Journal: "Immediate transfers - opportunity (or threat) to the financial system"
text: Administrator opinion article... Opinion article by Administrator Helder Rosalino in the Business Journal: "Immediate transfers -opportunity (or threat) to the financial system" 02 May. 2019 In 2019, the 20th anniversary of the creation of the euro is marked. Over this period, payment systems in Portugal and the euro area have undergone a profound transformation and faced permanent challenges, creating unprecedented development opportunities. After these 20 years, with the increasing digitisation of economies and societies, regulatory changes in 2018 (via the Revised Payment Services Directive  DSP2), the emergence of new fintech operators and the ongoing technological upheae, opens a new era for payment service providers and their users, who increasingly value highly available services, speed and ease of use. In response to this new paradigm, several banking communities have developed immediate payment solutions, which ensure the continuous processing of bank transfers [24h/7d/365d], with the availability of funds in beneficiaries' accounts up to 10 seconds (real-time). These solutions are convenient, fast and efficient and can be gradually introduced as a preferred medium in various payment models. There are already European countries (The Netherlands, Finland and, to some extent Spain) assessing the advantages of migration from traditional credit transfers to immediate transfers. To this end, the definition by the European Authorities at the end of 2017 of a common standard (SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCTinst) scheme, as the basis for the creation of interoperable immediate transfer solutions in Europe, was an important milestone for the future evolution of payment services in Europe. Both the European Commission and the European Central Bank consider that the advent of immediate transfers  via a common scheme  support the development and evolution of retail payments in Europe, asserting itself as an alternative to purely national solutions or provided by a limited number of payment card brands (predominantly from the USA). In Portugal, the solution developed by the national community (SCTinst base) started in September 2018. Market aswelling exceeded the best expectations, reaching, by March 31, 2019, about 1.2 million transfers, with an average value of 1,000 euros per operation. There are many advantages of immediate transfers over other payment solutions. As a solution based solely on account movement, without the need for a bank card, immediate transfers lead to a simplification of the value chain and a decrease in the number of stakeholders involved in the payment cycle. In this sense, its adoption will lead to a reduction in costs and commissions, along with greater scope and efficiency in the processing of operations (in particular, in the face of immediate card-based transfers). State companies and bodies can benefit significantly from the widespread adoption of immediate transfers, as they allow, on the one hand, immediate confirmation and provision of funds and, on the other hand, to speed up accounting reconciliation and collection management, considerably reducing back-office costs. In terms of innovation, immediate transfers are the instrument par excellence for promoting the integration of digitisation processes, both in p2p and points of sale use. Immediate transfers are also the obvious tool to be used in the new payment services established by DSP2 and in the open banking platforms in the implementation phase. It has been assumed, by authorities and operators, that the increasing digitisation of the economy is enhancing immediate transfers as the instrument of payment that can best respond to the new habits and expectations of users, also contributing to the reduction of payment instruments that negatively affect the results and efficiency of the banking system. Both individuals and businesses and the State will be able to benefit from a gradually more intensive use of this instrument. The collective strategy should therefore point in this direction. It was, therefore, with surprise and concern that there was recently a decrease in the volume of immediate transfers, after a very significant and promising initial growth. This reversal has contributed greatly to the fact that banks have started to apply higher prices in immediate transfers (somewhat disproportionate to other instruments). This factor is critical to the success of immediate transfers, as it discourages their usual adoption by bank customers. The introduction of immediate transfers has resulted in a significant implementation and investment effort by the national banking community, which can only be monetised if conditions are created to create economies of scale in their use. In this sense, the financial system should remove barriers and implement practices, in particular in terms of pricing, which potentiate a widespread adoption of immediate transfers in remote payments and physical points of sale. Only in this way will it be possible to keep Portugal in the group of countries with the best payment systems, make room for innovation, strengthen the competitiveness of our financial system and, more importantly, provide solutions that support the development of the economy and facilitate the day-to-day lives of citizens.
text_original: Artigo de opinio do Administrador... Artigo de opinio do Administrador Hlder Rosalino no Jornal de Negcios: "As transferncias imediatas -oportunidade (ou ameaa) para o sistema financeiro" 02 mai. 2019 Em 2019, assinalam-se os 20 anos da criao do euro. Ao longo deste perodo, os sistemas de pagamentos, em Portugal e na rea do euro, sofreram uma profunda transformao e enfrentaram permanentes desafios, criando oportunidades de desenvolvimento sem precedentes. Passados estes 20 anos, com a crescente digitalizao das economias e das sociedades, as alteraes regulamentares ocorridas em 2018 (via Diretiva de Servios de Pagamento revista  DSP2), o aparecimento de novos operadores fintech e a disrupo tecnolgica em curso, abre-se uma nova era para os prestadores de servios de pagamento e para os seus utilizadores, que valorizam cada vez mais servios com elevada disponibilidade, rapidez e facilidade de utilizao. Como resposta a este novo paradigma, diversas comunidades bancrias desenvolveram solues de pagamentos imediatos, que asseguram o processamento contnuo de transferncias bancrias [24h/7d/365d], com disponibilizao dos fundos nas contas dos beneficirios at 10 segundos (real-time). Estas solues so cmodas, rpidas e eficientes, podendo ser gradualmente introduzidas como meio preferencial em diversos modelos de pagamento. H j pases europeus (Holanda, Finlndia e, em certa medida, Espanha) a avaliarem as vantagens de uma migrao das transferncias a crdito tradicionais para as transferncias imediatas. Nesse sentido, a definio pelas Autoridades Europeias, no final de 2017, de um standard comum (scheme SEPA Instant Credit Transfer -SCTinst), como base para a criao de solues de transferncias imediatas interoperveis no espao europeu, constituiu um marco importante para a evoluo futura da prestao de servios de pagamento na Europa. Quer a Comisso Europeia, quer o Banco Central Europeu consideram que o advento das transferncias imediatas  via scheme comum -vem suportar o desenvolvimento e a evoluo dos pagamentos de retalho na Europa, afirmando-se como alternativa a solues de mbito meramente nacional ou fornecidas por um nmero limitado de marcas de cartes de pagamento (predominantemente com origem nos EUA). Em Portugal, a soluo desenvolvida pela comunidade nacional (base SCTinst) arrancou em setembro de 2018. A adeso do mercado superou as melhores expetativas, atingindo, at 31 de maro de 2019, cerca de 1,2 milhes de transferncias, com um valor mdio de 1.000 euros por operao. So inmeras as vantagens das transferncias imediatas face a outras solues de pagamentos. Por ser uma soluo baseada apenas em movimentao de contas, sem necessidade de carto bancrio, as transferncias imediatas conduzem a uma simplificao da cadeia de valor e a uma diminuio do nmero de intervenientes envolvidos no ciclo de pagamento. Nesse sentido, a sua adoo originar uma reduo de custos e comisses, a par de maior abrangncia e eficincia no processamento das operaes (em especial, face s transferncias imediatas baseadas em carto). As empresas e os organismos do Estado podem beneficiar significativamente com a adoo generalizada das transferncias imediatas, na medida em que estas permitem, por um lado, a confirmao e a disponibilizao imediata dos fundos e, por outro, agilizar a reconciliao contabilstica e a gesto de cobranas, reduzindo consideravelmente os custos de back-office. Em termos de inovao, as transferncias imediatas so o instrumento por excelncia para promover a integrao de processos de digitalizao, quer na utilizao P2P, quer em pontos de venda. As transferncias imediatas so, tambm, o instrumento bvio a utilizar nos novos servios de pagamento estabelecidos pela DSP2 e nas plataformas de open banking em fase de implementao. Tem vindo a ser assumido, por autoridades e operadores, que a crescente digitalizao da economia vem potenciar as transferncias imediatas como o instrumento de pagamento que melhor pode responder aos novos hbitos e expetativas dos utilizadores, contribuindo, ainda, para a reduo dos instrumentos de pagamento que afetam negativamente os resultados e a eficincia do sistema bancrio. Tanto os particulares, como as empresas e o Estado podero beneficiar de uma utilizao gradualmente mais intensiva deste instrumento. A estratgia coletiva dever, pois, apontar nesse sentido. Foi, por isso, com surpresa e preocupao que se observou, recentemente, um decrscimo do volume de transferncias imediatas, aps um crescimento inicial muito significativo e promissor. Para esta inverso muito contribuiu o facto de os bancos terem passado a aplicar prerios mais elevados nas transferncias imediatas (de certa forma, desproporcionados face a outros instrumentos). Este fator  crtico para o sucesso das transferncias imediatas, porquanto desincentiva a sua adoo habitual pelos clientes bancrios. A introduo das transferncias imediatas implicou um esforo de implementao e de investimento significativo pela comunidade bancria nacional, que apenas poder ser rentabilizado se forem criadas condies que propiciem economias de escala na sua utilizao. Neste sentido, o sistema financeiro dever remover barreiras e implementar prticas, designadamente em termos de prerios, que potenciem uma adoo generalizada das transferncias imediatas nos pagamentos remotos e nos pontos de venda fsicos. S assim ser possvel manter Portugal no grupo dos pases com melhores sistemas de pagamentos, abrir espao  inovao, reforar a competitividade do nosso sistema financeiro e, mais importante, disponibilizar solues que apoiem o desenvolvimento da economia e facilitem o dia-a-dia dos cidados.

Title: Intervention of Administrator Hlder Rosalino at the opening session of the Interbank Meeting for Payment Systems
text: Intervention of the Administrator Helder... Intervention of Administrator Helder Rosalino at the opening session of the Interbank Meeting for Payment Systems 17 May. 2019 I would like to begin by welcoming everyone present at this first Interbank Meeting held in 2019. About four months after the entry into force of regulatory technical standards for strong customer authentication and common open reporting standards and safe1, Banco de Portugal intends, on the one hand, to reiterate, in the market, the need to implement the new requirements in a timely manner and, on the other hand, to launch a challenge for national payment service providers (PSP) to take advantage of this process to enhance their own digital transformation and provide their customers with safer and more innovative payment services. As we know, the revised Payment Services Directive has as one of the main objectives to promote financial innovation, efficiency, competition and security in payment services. This is the case, in a framework of new opportunities and challenges, that Banco de Portugal calls on everyone's effort to continue to have one of the most robust payment systems in all these dimensions. And Banco de Portugal, as it has always done, will be available to work with all institutions, in a posture of monitoring and sharing, promoting greater efficiency and innovation and safeguarding risk and security conditions. Today's Interbank Meeting welcomes, for the first time, national payment institutions and e-money institutions, to which I would especially like to thank them for their willingness to participate in these sessions for national payment service providers. Since the last Interbank Meeting held in May 2018, many new developments have been linked to the implementation of the Directive. From the outset, DSP2 was transposed for the legal system Portuguese through the publication of Decree-Law No. 91/2018 of November 12, which establishes the new legal regime for payment and electronic money services (RJSPME). As expected, Banco de Portugal was designated a National Competent Authority under DSP2, similar to what occurred at the time of the transposition of DSP1. In the meantime too, with the aim of promoting a harmonised implementation of the Directive, as well as clarifying some doubts about implementation to the market, the European Banking Authority (EBA) has published a set of guidelines, opinions and clarifications. So on today's agenda we have two pressing topics. The first, related to the implementation of technical requirements relating to strong customer authentication and common and secure open communication standards, which will come into force on 14 September 2019. The second, which focuses on the reporting of operational and security incidents of a severe nature, which has already entered into force on January 15, 2019. On the first topic  strong customer authentication and common and secure open communication standards  Banco de Portugal sent payment service providers, on March 26, 2016, to a Circular Letter requesting the completion of three questionnaires that will allow us to collect the information necessary to assess compliance: Of strong client authentication requirements; The requirements of the communication interfaces made available for access to third-party payment service providers (TPP); The conditions for them to benefit from an exemption from the contingency. In this regard, Banco de Portugal expects payment service providers to make all necessary adjustments and developments to comply with the provisions and that, once any non-conformities have been flagged in the coming months, they will be corrected in a timely manner. While the discussion is often focused on common and secure communication standards, the expected change and opportunity introduced by open banking (API), the reality is that the adoption of strong customer authentication mechanisms also entails significant challenges. The evolution of these mechanisms implies not only substantive changes in the internal processes of payment service providers, but also a change in the way users authenticate. This is perhaps one of the main challenges to be taken into account: the impact of these changes on the user experience and the time it takes for their habits to change and the new processes rooted in their day-to-day life. As far as the communication standards comply, Banco de Portugal expects payment service providers to implement interfaces that operate according to the defined requirements, allowing third party providers (TPP) to access payment accounts, initiate payment transactions and confirm the availability of funds, with the same ease and quality of service as if the user himself interacts with the bank through traditional channels. As of today, payment service providers must already make the technical specifications of their interface available free of charge to TPP and have a communication interface test device (be it a dedicated interface or the adapted user interface) so that TPP, in turn, can test their applications. This is the only way to comply with the regulatory requirements and take advantage of the opportunities created by DSP2 for the benefit of payment service providers and users. The second topic of the meeting  reporting on operational and security incidents of a severe nature  also results from DSP2. A few months after the entry into force of the reporting obligation, according to Bank Instruction No. 1/2019, the number of reported incidents is still very low. There have even been some situations in which payment service providers have even failed to comply with the reporting obligation, or where they have carried out the report after the expiry of the deadlines. Full compliance with this report obliges payment service providers to implement internal procedures to identify, record, evaluate and, if it is met in the criteria defined in the Instruction, report the incidents to Banco de Portugal. This is an especially important process to ensure the smooth functioning of payment systems and to ensure that user confidence in those systems is not affected. I finish this opening intervention by launching a challenge to those present. Given the reality of today, where the provision of financial services is increasingly supported by technological innovation, in which convenience and speed for the consumer are determining factors, in which the use of payment services is compared to sending emails or buying an airline ticket online, and where competition at European level is increasingly visible in the range of options for consumers, payment service providers should rethink their strategy. Such consideration should include the possibility of making new payment services available and the widespread adoption of immediate transfers. As regards the provision of new payment services, I would point out that banks themselves, payment institutions and electronic money institutions can also position themselves as providers of account information services and payment initiation service providers. With regard to immediate transfers, we believe that their adoption should be encouraged, both for remote payments and for payments at physical points of sale. Take a look at the movement of other European countries, which are strategically migrating so-called normal transfers to immediate transfers. Only with a proactive and open attitude will it be possible to keep Portugal in the group of countries with modern and innovative payment systems, strengthen the competitiveness of our financial system and, more importantly, provide solutions that support the development of the economy and facilitate the day-to-day life of citizens. We thank you once again for your presence and the interest shown in the topics proposed for this session. 1 Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/389 of 27 November 2017, applicable from 14 September 2019.
text_original: Interveno do Administrador Hlder... Interveno do Administrador Hlder Rosalino na sesso de abertura da Reunio Interbancria para os Sistemas de Pagamentos 17 mai. 2019 Gostaria de comear por dar as boas-vindas a todos os presentes nesta primeira Reunio Interbancria realizada em 2019. A cerca de quatro meses da entrada em vigor das normas tcnicas de regulamentao relativas  autenticao forte do cliente e s normas abertas de comunicao comuns e seguras1, o Banco de Portugal pretende, por um lado, reiterar, junto do mercado, a necessidade de procederem  implementao atempada dos novos requisitos e, por outro, lanar um desafio para que os prestadores de servios de pagamento (PSP) nacionais aproveitem este processo para potenciar a sua prpria transformao digital e disponibilizar aos seus clientes servios de pagamento mais seguros e inovadores. Como sabemos, a Diretiva dos Servios de Pagamento revista tem como um dos principais objetivos promover a inovao financeira, a eficincia, a concorrncia e a segurana nos servios de pagamento.  assim, num enquadramento de novas oportunidades e desafios, que o Banco de Portugal apela ao esforo de todos, para continuarmos a ter um dos sistemas de pagamentos mais robusto em todas essas dimenses. E o Banco de Portugal, como sempre tem feito, estar disponvel para trabalhar com todas as instituies, numa postura de acompanhamento e partilha, promovendo uma maior eficincia e inovao e salvaguardando as condies de risco e de segurana. A Reunio Interbancria de hoje acolhe, pela primeira vez, as instituies de pagamento e as instituies de moeda eletrnica nacionais, s quais gostaria especialmente de agradecer a disponibilidade para participarem nestas sesses dirigidas aos prestadores de servios de pagamento nacionais. Desde a ltima Reunio Interbancria, realizada em maio de 2018, muitas so as novidades associadas  implementao da Diretiva. Desde logo, a DSP2 foi transposta para o ordenamento jurdico portugus atravs da publicao do Decreto-Lei n. 91/2018, de 12 de novembro, que estabelece o novo regime jurdico dos servios de pagamento e de moeda eletrnica (RJSPME). Tal como era expectvel, o Banco de Portugal foi designado Autoridade Competente Nacional no mbito da DSP2, de forma similar ao que se verificou aquando da transposio da DSP1. Tambm entretanto, com o objetivo de promover uma implementao harmonizada da Diretiva, assim como de clarificar ao mercado algumas dvidas de implementao, a Autoridade Bancria Europeia (EBA) publicou um conjunto de orientaes, opinies e esclarecimentos. Por isso, na agenda de hoje temos dois tpicos prementes. O primeiro, relacionado com a implementao dos requisitos tcnicos relativos  autenticao forte do cliente e s normas abertas de comunicao comuns e seguras, que entraro em vigor em 14 de setembro de 2019. O segundo, que incide sobre o reporte de incidentes operacionais e de segurana de carter severo, que j entrou em vigor em 15 de janeiro de 2019. Sobre o primeiro tpico  autenticao forte do cliente e normas abertas de comunicao comuns e seguras  o Banco de Portugal enviou aos prestadores de servios de pagamento, em 26 de maro passado, uma Carta Circular solicitando o preenchimento de trs questionrios que permitiro recolher a informao necessria para avaliar o cumprimento: Dos requisitos de autenticao forte do cliente; Dos requisitos das interfaces de comunicao disponibilizadas para acesso de terceiros prestadores de servios de pagamento (TPP); Das condies para que possam beneficiar de uma iseno do mecanismo de contingncia. A este respeito, o Banco de Portugal espera que os prestadores de servios de pagamento efetuem todas as adaptaes e desenvolvimentos necessrios para dar cumprimento ao estipulado e que, uma vez sinalizadas eventuais desconformidades nos prximos meses, as mesmas sejam corrigidas atempadamente. Embora a discusso seja frequentemente centrada nas normas de comunicao comuns e seguras, pela expectvel mudana e oportunidade introduzida pelas API (open banking), a realidade  que a adoo de mecanismos de autenticao forte do cliente comporta tambm desafios significativos. A evoluo destes mecanismos implica no s alteraes substantivas nos processos internos dos prestadores de servios de pagamento, mas tambm uma mudana na forma como os utilizadores se autenticam. Este  talvez um dos principais desafios a ter em considerao: o impacto dessas alteraes na experincia dos utilizadores e o tempo necessrio para que os seus hbitos sejam alterados e os novos processos enraizados no seu dia-a-dia. No que s normas de comunicao respeita, o Banco de Portugal espera que os prestadores de servios de pagamento implementem interfaces que funcionem de acordo com os requisitos definidos, permitindo aos terceiros prestadores (TPP) aceder s contas de pagamento, iniciar operaes de pagamento e confirmar a disponibilidade de fundos, com a mesma facilidade e qualidade de servio como se fosse o prprio utilizador a interagir com o banco atravs dos canais tradicionais.  data de hoje, os prestadores de servios de pagamento devem j disponibilizar gratuitamente as especificaes tcnicas da sua interface aos TPP e ter um dispositivo de teste da interface de comunicao (seja ela uma interface dedicada ou a interface do utilizador adaptada) para que os TPP, por seu turno, possam testar as suas aplicaes. S assim se conseguir simultaneamente cumprir o estipulado regulamentarmente e tirar partido das oportunidades criadas pela DSP2, em benefcio dos prestadores e dos utilizadores de servios de pagamento. O segundo tpico da reunio  reporte de incidentes operacionais e de segurana de carter severo  resulta tambm da DSP2. Decorridos alguns meses desde a entrada em vigor da obrigao de reporte, de acordo com a Instruo do Banco n. 1/2019, o nmero de incidentes reportados  ainda muito reduzido. Inclusivamente existiram algumas situaes em que os prestadores de servios de pagamento incumpriram mesmo a obrigao de reporte, ou em que efetuaram o reporte depois de expirados os prazos estabelecidos. O cumprimento pleno deste reporte obriga os prestadores de servios de pagamento a implementar procedimentos internos para identificar, registar, avaliar e, caso seja enquadrado nos critrios definidos na Instruo, reportar os incidentes ao Banco de Portugal. Este  um processo especialmente importante para assegurar o bom funcionamento dos sistemas de pagamentos e garantir que a confiana dos utilizadores nesses sistemas no  afetada. Termino esta interveno de abertura lanando um desafio aos presentes. Perante a realidade dos dias de hoje, em que a prestao de servios financeiros  cada vez mais suportada pela inovao tecnolgica, em que a convenincia e rapidez para o consumidor so fatores determinantes, em que a utilizao de servios de pagamento  comparada ao envio de e-mails ou  compra online de uma passagem area, e em que a concorrncia a nvel europeu est cada vez mais visvel no leque de opes para os consumidores, os prestadores de servios de pagamento devem repensar a sua estratgia. Essa reflexo deve obrigatoriamente incluir a possibilidade de disponibilizao dos novos servios de pagamento e de adoo generalizada das transferncias imediatas. No que se refere  disponibilizao dos novos servios de pagamento, recordo que os prprios bancos, as instituies de pagamento e as instituies de moeda eletrnica, tambm se podem posicionar como prestadores de servios de informao sobre contas e prestadores de servios de iniciao de pagamentos. Relativamente s transferncias imediatas, consideramos que a sua adoo deve ser incentivada, quer para pagamentos remotos, quer para pagamentos nos pontos de venda fsicos. Veja-se o movimento de outros pases europeus, que se encontram estrategicamente a migrar as transferncias ditas normais para as transferncias imediatas. S com uma atitude proactiva e aberta ser possvel manter Portugal no grupo dos pases com sistemas de pagamentos modernos e inovadores, reforar a competitividade do nosso sistema financeiro e, mais importante, disponibilizar solues que apoiem o desenvolvimento da economia e facilitem o dia-a-dia dos cidados. Agradecemos mais uma vez a vossa presena e o interesse demonstrado nos temas propostos para esta sesso. 1 Regulamento Delegado (UE) 2018/389 da Comisso, de 27 de novembro de 2017, aplicvel a partir de 14 de setembro de 2019.

Title: Opening speech of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, in the 1st Dialogue on the planning of the resolution of Less Significant Institutions
text: Opening speech of the Vice-Gov... Opening speech of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, in the 1st Dialogue on the planning of the resolution of Less Significant Institutions 17 May. 2019 Good morning, everyone. Welcome to Banco de Portugal and, in particular, to the Resolution Department, which is today your host. 1. The European Union system on bank resolution and the Single Resolution Mechanism are the most innovative part of the European Banking Union, first of all because they institutionalise a process to prepare the institutions for settlement if the presuppositions of the implementation of a resolution measure are established. The figure of bank resolution is not in itself an innovation, but the overall terms of the European resolution regime are deeply innovative. As innovative, it will be said, as complex and full of consequences for the functioning of the banking system. 2. Today's session is the first structured and cross-cutting dialogue with the banking sector specifically dedicated to the planning of the resolution of less significant classified institutions and institutions that are not covered by the Single Resolution Mechanism. The institutions present here are called "less significant". This means, therefore, that  although less  they are significant. This designation reflects a comparative judgment vis-a-vis other larger institutions, but that does not mean, of course, that they are not also important for the banking system Portuguese. They're a lot of it. From the outset, because an efficient and agile banking system requires institutions of varying dimensions. Often what matters most is not the size of the institutions but the quality of the management and products offered, the productive efficiency, financial soundness, profitability and accuracy of regulatory compliance. "Small Is Beautiful" is the title of the famous book published by E. F. Schumacher, which reached a huge impact, especially in the seventies and eighties of the last century. You do not have to be adept at your theses in recognising the extreme importance, at various levels, of smaller financial institutions. 3. The action that Banco de Portugal is taking here today is by no means the first action taken by Banco de Portugal in the planning of the resolution of the least significant institutions, and, much less, is the first contact it promotes with this universe of institutions. In fact, this event follows internally developed work in the context of resolution planning and interactions that have been maintained bilaterally with several institutions present here, some of which are already aware of the information needs that this activity entails. Still, this event is an important milestone in this area of operation of Banco de Portugal, as a national resolution authority. In recent years, the resolution function has been especially dedicated to the implementation and finalization of resolution measures applied to Banco Espirito Santo, S.A., in 2014, and Banif  Banco Internacional do Funchal, S.A., in 2015, as well as, together with the Single Resolution Board, to the planning of the resolution for significant credit institutions. For the other institutions, a resolution plan will be prepared for all institutions in compliance with the law in a process which has already begun and will be continued gradually. This event is part of this context. It is therefore with great satisfaction that I note that the initiative promoted by Banco de Portugal deserved a great support from the institutions, which I interpret as the revelation that there is a special interest in knowing better the framework applicable to the planning of the resolution and an effective commitment to meet the requirements that it places on the institutions. 4. The resolution function occupies a decisive space in the construction of the Banking Union and is a central theme in the debate at European level on its deepening. The exercise of the resolution function is not limited to intervention with institutions which are in financial imbalance so severe that their continuity is threatened and insolvency appears imminent. On the contrary, in the current context, it is necessary to ensure  at all times  the existence of conditions at the level of banking groups and credit institutions that allow their possible resolution to take place effectively and can be carried out with the least possible disruption, as well as to ensure adequate levels of readiness for the implementation of resolution measures. This activity, which is continuous in nature, involves making judgments as to the feasibility of implementing resolution measures (which we might call "resolubility") and may even result in the determination of measures for the removal of any obstacles or obstacles to resolution. It is also in the context of this continuing activity that resolution authorities shall ascertain the amounts of own funds and liabilities that each institution must maintain in order to meet the necessary conditions for the absorption of losses to occur without diseruptions in the event of the imposition of losses. This exercise results in the fixing of the so-called MREL (Minimum Requirement for own funds and Eligible Liabilities) requirements. The promotion of the conditions so that  if necessary  the resolution of a credit institution can occur with the least possible disruption is a central objective in the Banking Union. But this objective can only be achieved with the active contribution of the credit institutions themselves. It is ultimately up to the institutions to ensure their own resolution. This initiative also aims to contribute to this purpose. Banco de Portugal, as a national resolution authority, must prepare resolution plans and set MREL requirements. However, such activity is only truly effective if the institutions are able, first of all, to provide the necessary information and, on the other hand, to implement the conclusions that may be drawn up in the context of resolution planning. That is why the word dialogue is indeed so true to designate this process. 5. The resolution function today operates, for the vast majority of the institutions present here today, in a uniform legal framework within the Banking Union and in an institutional framework which, to a large extent, concentrates the powers of resolution in a European authority, based in Brussels  the Single Resolution Council (SRB). It is therefore important to understand correctly the role of national resolution authorities in the current regulatory and institutional framework. Firstly, it is up to the national resolution authorities to integrate the Single Resolution Mechanism by participating in the Single Resolution Board. This participation is mainly carried out in three plans: (i) in the permanent work of planning the resolution on institutions considered significant, through participation in joint teams with the SRB; (ii) in horizontal work, related to policy-making, harmonisation of procedures and the design and improvement of methodologies; and yet yet (iii) participation in the decision-making process, either in the SRB Plenary or in its executive training, where measures are at stake specifically on groups or institutions in particular. Secondly  that is, in addition to participation in the work of the SRB  national resolution authorities are competent to perform resolution functions in relation to institutions which are not considered significant and which do not have a cross-border presence within the Banking Union. It is precisely within this concrete competence that Banco de Portugal promotes today's event. However  it should be stressed  even in relation to institutions classified as less significant, it should be worth noting that there is a superintendence of the SRB and that the decision-making capacity of national authorities, in the event of resolution, is limited to solutions that do not imply recourse to the Single Resolution Fund. Thirdly, it is also for the national resolution authorities to implement and implement the decisions adopted by the SRB, in particular through the practice of the acts which are necessary for the decisions of that country to take effect on the legal order of each country. As a second, it is ultimately the SRB sovereign as a resolution authority, active participation in the work of the single resolution mechanism by national authorities is of great relevance. It is essential to ensure that decisions in the field of resolution are properly framed at national level, on the basis of the banking system's own knowledge  which only national authorities have  and in the light of the best interests of preserving the financial stability of each country. The capacity to act in this area is not of a normative source; it depends on the influence that the national resolution authority can have on the work of the European authorities, which in turn depends on the recognition and credibility assigned to it by peers. From this point of view, Banco de Portugal is in a privileged position, given the experience accumulated in recent years and the external recognition of Banco de Portugal as a knowledge center in the field of resolution. 6. The work of this session is divided into five modules: (i) the general framework of the resolution regime; (ii) resolution planning; (iii) the simplified bond regime; (iv) Banco de Portugal's approach to the planning of the resolution of less significant institutions and (v) the minimum requirements for own funds and eligible liabilities. At the end of each module we will have a question and answer period. I am sure it will be a very useful session for clarifying the institutions represented here. Thank you so much for your attention.
