Conferncia de Cibersegurana: "A Ciber-resilincia no setor financeiro" 03 jun. 2019 Sejam bem-vindos ao Banco de Portugal e  nossa 2. Conferncia sobre Cibersegurana , este ano dedicada  "Ciber-resilincia no setor financeiro". Cumprimento todas as entidades presentes e os seus representantes, agradecendo a ampla participao registada, que  naturalmente um testemunho da importncia do tema que nos rene aqui no Museu do Dinheiro. Temos uma agenda muito ambiciosa, com reputados oradores, que espero que seja do interesse geral. Para nos falar da Estratgia Nacional para a Cibersegurana, teremos connosco o Eng. Lino Santos, Coordenador do Centro Nacional de Cibersegurana, que ser um dos principais keynote speakers deste evento. Para nos falar sobre a Cibersegurana na perspetiva da regulao e da superviso do Banco de Portugal, teremos o/a: Dr. Lus Costa Ferreira, Diretor do Departamento de Superviso Prudencial; Dra. Lcia Leito, Diretora do Departamento de Superviso Comportamental; Eng. Lus Gonalves, Coordenador do nosso Centro Operacional de Cibersegurana. Teremos, na segunda parte desta sesso, a perspetiva das autoridades de defesa do ciberespao o/a: Dr. Carlos Cabreiro, Diretor da Unidade Nacional de Combate ao Cibercrime e Criminalidade Tecnolgica da Polcia Judiciria; Dra. Vanda Jorge, Coordenadora da rea de Atividade Financeira Ilcita do Banco de Portugal. Encerraremos com uma viso transversal a nvel internacional sobre os desafios da cibersegurana, que nos ser transmitida pela Consultora Gartner, atravs do seu Executive Partner em Portugal, Eduardo Mastranza.  hoje uma realidade incontestada que o ambiente global em termos de ciberameaas se est a tornar progressivamente mais complexo, mais difcil de acompanhar e, sobretudo, de prevenir, com relevncia acrescida no setor financeiro, no qual se tem assistido, nos ltimos anos, a uma tendncia de crescimento do volume e da sofisticao dos ciberataques. De acordo com o Frum Econmico Mundial, o setor financeiro  claramente o setor mais visado pelo cibercrime, sendo alvo de nove em cada dez ataques realizados no ciberespao. Desses ataques, 40% so dirigidos a bancos centrais, 36% a bancos comerciais e 5% a entidades do setor de seguros. , portanto, uma ameaa transversal a todo o setor financeiro, com motivaes de vria ordem: desde financeiras, polticas, econmicas e at sociais. Estamos, neste contexto, todos sujeitos aos mesmos desafios, decorrentes de um sentimento crescente de insegurana no ciberespao, num mundo que  cada vez mais global e digital. O conjunto de desafios que hoje j conhecemos tender a multiplicar-se no futuro, especialmente potenciado pelos avanos tecnolgicos que estamos a viver (a chamada revoluo tecnolgica 4.0) e que sero tambm aproveitados por quem faz da prtica do crime no ciberespao a sua atividade principal. Citam-se, a ttulo de exemplo, a utilizao de tecnologias como o machine learning, que continuamente pode avaliar e testar novos mtodos de subverso dos sistemas de segurana (as mquinas podem aprender a melhorar cada vez mais os ataques); e a inteligncia artificial e a robtica , que podem ser utilizadas para o desenvolvimento de ferramentas para a realizao de ataques de elevada sofisticao e volume. As novas tecnologias no vieram s para melhorar os nossos nveis de desenvolvimento e de bem-estar, podem e esto tambm a ser utilizadas para explorar as nossas fragilidades. Se no houver uma atuao preventiva concertada, estas novas tecnologias tero a capacidade de exponenciar situaes de fraude no ciberespao, levando a que o crime, neste ambiente, assuma uma dimenso totalmente nova e se traduza num desafio permanente e constante no que respeita aos mecanismos de deteo, conteno e mitigao de um tipo de fraude cada vez mais complexo e escalvel. Seja do ponto de vista da utilizao abusiva de dados pessoais, da atividade financeira ilcita, da utilizao de solues de pagamento virtuais (e totalmente desintermediadas), ou at mesmo do branqueamento de capitais, podemos antecipar um crescimento sem precedentes das situaes de fraude econmica e financeira que podem ser realizadas no ciberespao. Isto, naturalmente, se os mecanismos de defesa no aumentarem na mesma dimenso.  este cenrio de fundo que nos levou a dirigir o tema desta conferncia para a Ciberresilincia no setor financeiro, que  no apenas um objetivo setorial, mas  sobretudo um objetivo nacional, dada a importncia que o sistema financeiro assume para o funcionamento de qualquer pas. A concretizao desse objetivo depende de uma viso comum, que devemos construir, e da combinao das vrias estratgias dos atores em presena. O propsito desta conferncia  precisamente o de ajudar  construo dessa viso comum e consequente articulao de estratgias, tendo o Banco de Portugal como catalisador de uma indispensvel cooperao intrassetorial. O Banco de Portugal iniciou a implementao da sua estratgia de cibersegurana em 2012, numa altura em que esta temtica no tinha ainda a centralidade que assume no presente. Desde essa altura desenvolveu um percurso de incremento de maturidade e de capacitao que o posiciona hoje na linha da frente em matria de cibersegurana, em termos nacionais e tambm internacionais. O reforo da capacitao do Banco de Portugal em termos de cibersegurana tem sido uma prioridade central do seu Conselho de Administrao nos ltimos anos e  uma das suas principais orientaes estratgicas para o futuro. O Banco de Portugal tem vindo a articular as diferentes componentes de segurana (tecnolgica, fsica e de informao) em alinhamento com as melhores prticas internacionais, dispondo de equipas especficas e dedicadas que no s asseguram a proteo da instituio, como tm como segunda misso apoiar e colaborar com outras entidades nacionais e internacionais. Nesse sentido, tem vindo a desenvolver uma postura de crescente ciber-resilincia, que lhe tem permitido enfrentar e suster importantes ameaas, sem qualquer interrupo da sua capacidade operacional e suportando adequadamente a sua misso institucional, do mesmo modo que lhe tem permitido apoiar outras entidades nacionais e internacionais em situaes de crise. O Centro Operacional de Cibersegurana do Banco de Portugal tem dinamizando redes de contacto, de cooperao e de estreita interao com mltiplas entidades (em Portugal e no Eurosistema), com o objetivo de partilhar informao em tempo real e de criar mecanismos de interajuda em situaes de crise, contribuindo assim para a partilha de experincias e para o desenvolvimento de um conceito de ciber-resilincia em rede. Estamos perfeitamente convictos de que o risco de contgio e o consequente impacto sistmico por ao de uma ou de um conjunto de ciberameaas nunca foram to grandes, pelo que se impe, mais do que nunca, o reforo de medidas de cooperao, interajuda e de partilha de informao entre todos os atores do setor financeiro nacional. Uma mesma ciberameaa pode afetar (em graus distintos) diferentes instituies independentemente da sua dimenso. Exemplos recentes a nvel mundial tm revelado essa realidade. No existe atualmente uma relao direta entre a dimenso de uma instituio financeira e a sua capacidade de suster um ciberataque. , por isso, essencial, colocar os diferentes organismos num plano horizontal, potenciando, dessa forma, que interajam entre si de forma equilibrada. Torna-se, de facto, necessrio apostar num paradigma de resposta em rede aos desafios que se colocam ao setor, devidamente coordenados centralmente, numa perspetiva de resposta federada aos ciberdesafios.  assim que hoje os bancos centrais nacionais do Eurosistema funcionam: h troca informao em tempo real, apoio mtuo entre instituies e cooperao centralizada. Na mesma linha, o Banco de Portugal, que j  uma referncia entre os seus pares europeus, pretende ser visto como um parceiro das instituies financeiras nacionais, primando pelo apoio, pela cooperao e pela disponibilizao das suas capacidades em prol do setor e das instituies que o compem. Nesse aspeto, o Banco no pode deixar de assumir o seu papel central e centralizador, promovendo a cooperao, a partilha de informao e conhecimento, a dinmica de grupo e interajuda, absolutamente necessrias para enfrentar as ameaas e os ataques. Para tal, o Banco de Portugal prope-se, no mbito da Estratgia Nacional para a Cibersegurana, criar e dinamizar um CSIRT setorial (Equipa de Resposta a Incidentes de Segurana) para o setor financeiro nacional. O Banco de Portugal possui laos de cooperao muito fortes a nvel internacional nesta vertente, promovendo frequentemente o estreitar de relaes e o estabelecimento de novos canais de cooperao e interajuda, que pretende colocar ao servio de todo o setor financeiro nacional. Atravs do Banco de Portugal, uma ciberameaa que se manifeste ao nvel do Eurosistema dever imediatamente ser partilhada no setor nacional, permitindo auxiliar as primeiras instituies afetadas e proteger as restantes de forma antecipada, por conhecimento prvio dos detalhes da ameaa.  precisamente com o propsito de apresentar esses objetivos, que no s so setoriais, como nacionais, contribuindo para um contexto de estabilidade financeira, que estamos aqui reunidos. Hoje, vamos poder assistir a intervenes que nos apresentaro estratgias e vises globais sobre esta temtica; mas tambm ser partilhado aquilo que de mais relevante o Banco est a desenvolver nesta temtica. Partilharemos medidas concretas em curso e a forma como o Banco tem vindo a integrar a cibersegurana na sua misso e nos seus processos. Para terminar, gostaria de reforar o compromisso do Banco de Portugal na promoo de uma cultura e de uma atuao que protejam o ciberespao financeiro nacional, baseadas na cooperao entre todos os intervenientes do setor e na definio de uma viso comum em matria de ciber-resilncia. Espero que esta conferncia nos ajude a caminhar nesse sentido. Muito obrigado 2. Conferncia de Cibersegurana: "A Ciber-resilincia no setor financeiro"

Title: Initial intervention of the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the annual hearing by the Committee on Budget, Finance and Administrative Modernization (COFMA) of the Assembly of the Republic under Article 54 of the Organic Law of banco de Portugal
text: Initial intervention of the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the annual hearing by the Committee on Budget, Finance and Administrative Modernization (COFMA) of the Assembly of the Republic under Article 54 of the Organic Law of Banco de Portugal 11 Jun 2019 Initial intervention[1] Madam President, Ladies and gentlemen, Good morning On May 10, Banco de Portugal released the Report of the Board of Directors - Activity and Accounts for 2018. On May 8, he had already released the Economic Bulletin with the analysis of the Portuguese economy in 2018. Also in May released the Reports on the Implementation of Monetary Policy, Monetary Issuance, Monitoring of the Macroprudential Measure on Consumer Credits and, more recently (June 5), published the Financial Stability Report. In April, the 2018 Behavioral Supervision, Payment Systems, Statistical Activity and Cooperation Activity Reports had already been made available. All these reports are available on Banco de Portugal's institutional website, giving expression to its policy of transparency and public accountability. Its reading allows not only to frame banco de Portugal's activity in 2018 in the national and international context, but also to obtain more detailed information on specific areas of its operations. In my initial speech  which, as usual, will also be available on the Internet  I will begin by very briefly detaining the internal and external context banco de Portugal's activity in 2018. Next I will make a balance sheet, necessarily not exhaustive, of this activity and end with some notes on the Balance Sheet and Accounts. As always, I will be happy to develop some of the points mentioned in response to the questions you want to ask. I. Framing In 2018, economic policy in the euro area remained oriented towards promoting price stability and sustained growth in an international context driven by less dynamism in global economic activity, rising trade and geopolitical tensions, greater uncertainty and more restrictive financial conditions. In Portugal, economic activity expanded for the fifth consecutive year, albeit at a more moderate pace. The real product surpassed, for the first time, the level reached before the international financial crisis and continued the reduction of indebtedness of the various sectors of the economy and, in this way, the correction of imbalances accumulated in the past. A decade after the outbreak of the international financial crisis, the European Union's financial system  including the Portuguese banking system  is more capitalised and scrutinised, following (i) the deep regulatory and institutional reforms introduced in the post-crisis (some still incomplete, such as the Banking Union) and (ii) new supervisory models and practices. However, there are still numerous challenges and uncertainties for which all actors in the decision-making process, including the Eurosystem's central banks, must be vigilant and prepared. Banco de Portugal is and will remain attentive and committed to responding to the challenges facing the national financial system. Its influence on decisions with impact on the Portuguese and euro area economies will depend on the mandate assigned to it and its ability to look at and respond to the challenges at national and European level. II. Activity in 2018 In 2018, Banco de Portugal remained faithful to the commitments of demand, improvement and self-overcoming, transversal to the various priorities defined in its Strategic Plan for 2017-2020. Banco de Portugal's activity took place in a context marked by multiple challenges. Let me highlight five: i. The evolution of the Eurosystem's monetary policy - in particular non-monetary measures preserving favourable financing conditions for the economy; ii. The sustainability challenges of the national banking system, which required a particular direction of supervisory action for government mechanisms and internal control, credit risk, capital and liquidity positions and models of business; iii. Safeguarding the stability of the national financial system, including the vulnerability and systemic risks and the adoption of a measure of macroprudential measures to mitigate the risks associated with granting new credit to the housing, mortgage or equivalent credit and consumer credit; iv. The extension of behavioural supervision responsibilities, resulting from the entry into force of new legislation; v. The impact of technological change and digital transformation on the activity of financial intermediation and payment systems and the necessary adjustment of competences and the organisational structure of Banco de Portugal. After this initial framework, I will briefly review the activity developed in 2018, structuring it around the four general lines of strategic orientation defined by the Board of Directors for the four-year period 2017-2020. Monetary authority As regards the functions of monetary authority, Banco de Portugal participated in monetary policy decisions within the Framework of the Governing Council of the European Central Bank (ECB). In 2018, the Eurosystem's monetary policy continued to be accommodative and continued to provide favourable financing conditions for euro area economies. In December, the Governing Council decided to cease monthly net purchases of the asset purchase programme, but announced that it would continue to reinvest all capital payments on securities over the long term after the first official interest rate rise. Banco de Portugal has ensured the implementation of the single monetary policy with the institutions and participated in the acquisition of financial assets under the asset purchase programs. In 2018, the average balance of monetary policy portfolios and acquisitions of the asset purchase program on Banco de Portugal's balance sheet increased  albeit less significantly than in 2017  to 49.319 million euros. The public sector debt purchase program (PSPP) is the most representative, with an average weight of 88% in the total volume of portfolios. As the monetary authority of the Eurosystem, Banco de Portugal also promoted the timely adoption by payment service providers of the requirements arising from the new Legal Regime of Payment Services and Electronic Money. In September, the Interbank Clearing System (SICOI)  managed by Banco de Portugal and which processes the majority of payment transactions ordered by individuals and companies in Portugal  began to allow immediate transfers. Banco de Portugal also joined the Eurosystem's immediate settlement service (TIPS), which went live on 30 November. Banco de Portugal also participated in the preparatory work for the launch of the 100 and 200 euro banknotes of the Europa series, which entered into circulation on May 28. It also concluded an agreement to regularise surplus e-money with the Central Bank of Slovakia, translated into sending 10 million euro coins (in surplus in Portugal) to that country for exchange for 20 million euro coins (in surplus in Slovakia). Financial stability As part of its mission to safeguard financial stability, Banco de Portugal acts daily to promote the robustness of credit institutions and the confidence of economic agents. The national banking sector has made a significant adjustment in recent years in response to a more demanding regulatory and supervisory framework, which has enabled: Improve solvency; Reinforce the liquidity position; Reduce substantially non-performing assets; Improve profitability. In 2018, Banco de Portugal continued to participate in the development of new EU legislation and regulations to strengthen the legal framework for credit institutions and investment firms in the prudential, behavioural, resolution and prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing. It also collaborated in the work to complete the Banking Union and to review the functioning of the European System of Financial Supervision. As I have already mentioned, Banco de Portugal has adopted a macroprudential measure, in the form of a recommendation, which has set limits on some criteria used by institutions in granting new credits to consumers. On May 29, the first report evaluating compliance with this measure was released. The analysis indicates that the defined limits are being adequate and effective in meeting the established objectives. The measure will be reassessed in the first quarter of 2020. Banco de Portugal acted on the sustainability challenges of the national banking system, promoting a strong scrutiny of the institutions' government and internal control mechanisms, the strengthening of capital and liquidity positions, the strengthening of business models and the reduction of non-productive loans and other assets considered problematic, based on a bank-to-bank intervention. At the end of 2018, the stock of non-performing loans totalled EUR 25.9 billion, about half of the maximum of EUR 50.5 billion recorded in June 2016. In 2018, the perimeter of Banco de Portugal's behavioral supervision was also extended. With the entry into force of the legal regime of credit intermediaries and the new mortgage credit regime, the Bank began to perform functions in the authorization, registration and supervision of the activity of credit intermediaries, as well as in the certification and monitoring of the training entities of credit intermediaries and employees of the institutions involved in the commercialization of housing credit. It was also responsible for supervising the activity of payment initiation service providers and the account information service, under the entry into force of the new payment services and electronic money scheme. Also in 2018: In order to prevent and suppress illicit financial activity, Banco de Portugal carried out investigation scans in the context of 218 cases. In the context of the prevention of money laundering and the financing of terrorism, conducted 20 inspection actions, issued 198 supervisory measures and appreciated implementation of 354 measures adopted following inspection actions carried out in previous years. Following its supervisory action, the Bank initiated 113 supervisory proceedings and concluded 195 cases. Banco de Portugal defended the legality of resolution and sanctioning measures in a large number of cases, mainly arising from the resolution measures applied to BES and BANIF. I would like to highlight, already in 2019, the judgment delivered on 12 March unanimously of the twenty Judges of the Administrative Court of Circulo de Lisboa, who considered the legal regime of the resolution to be unconstitutional and confirmed the full legality of the bes resolution measure. The Judgment criticizes bes' performance as a supervised entity and attests to the appropriate way Banco de Portugal acted as supervisor. Banco de Portugal also remains particularly attentive to the impact of technological developments in the financial sector. As we can all see, in recent years there have been very significant changes in the provision of financial services, and a rapid process of digital transformation in the financial system is underway. In 2018, the Bank monitored developments in innovation in financial products and services in the national and international forums in which it participates, held meetings with Fintech, created a dedicated contact channel (Fintech) and launched, in partnership with the Insurance and Pension Fund Supervisory Authority, the Securities Market Commission and Portugal Fintech, Portugal FinLab, a communication platform between financial sector innovators and Portuguese regulators. Production and dissemination of knowledge Banco de Portugal continued to produce analysis and research on the Portuguese economy, the euro area economy and the financial system. In 2018, research focused on the priority themes set out in the 2017-2020 study agenda: The new challenges to monetary policy and financial stability; Or economic growth Portuguese in the context of the euro area; and Or institutions and public policies in Portugal and the European Union. Forty-seven studies were completed and, at the end of the year, 113 others were in progress or in the final review phase. At the end of the year, the Research Laboratory with Microdata of Banco de Portugal, installed in Porto, took in 34 scientific projects. Banco de Portugal, as a national statistical authority, launched in 2018 a new Credit Responsibility Centre that has enabled it to strengthen the quality of the information it works with and provides to the financial system, citizens and businesses. Studies and statistics play a crucial role in advising monetary, economic and prudential policy and their dissemination contributes to disseminating knowledge and stimulating public debate. In this sense, the Bank diversified the channels of contact with the public and intensified its communication actions, including on social networks. Internal management In 2018, the Bank continued to improve its governance model, organisation and processes, with reference to the best practices of the Eurosystem and the efficient management of the resources made available to it. I would like to stress the strengthening of the internal regulatory regime on ethics and conduct, with the systematisation of procedures for the prevention of conflict of interest and the control of limits on private financial transactions. At the same time, following the ECB's adoption of the Single Code of Conduct, the members of the Management Board have become subject to a set of conduct requirements and harmonised control mechanisms at European level. In the field of data protection, the Data Protection Office conducted a thorough diagnosis on the processing of personal data and adopted an action plan to ensure compliance with the new General Data Protection Regulation. Banco de Portugal continued to manage, in an integrated manner, the financial risks and operational risks to which it is exposed in the performance of its activity. The internal audit function was subject to a quality assessment carried out by an accredited entity, which concluded compliance in all areas. Banco de Portugal also continued to invest heavily in the development of technical, behavioral and management skills of its employees. The training of its human resources is essential for the Bank to intervene with quality, both nationally and internationally. III. Balance Sheet and Accounts I will conclude my speech with some notes on banco de Portugal's 2018 accounts. At the end of 2018, the Bank's balance sheet amounted to EUR 157 953 million, representing an increase of EUR 4 988 million compared to 2017. I would like to highlight four aspects underlying developments in this period: i. Increased participation in the public sector asset purchase programme in secondary market (PSPP), in the debt securities component portuguese public service, which reached EUR 31 billion at the end of the year (increase in eur 4 900 million); ii. The decrease of EUR 1 407 million in net management assets resulting from the decision to reduce the foreign currency trading book - with reflecting the reduction of exposure to foreign exchange risk  which had as its counterpart a intra-Eurosystem (TARGET) responsibilities. This reduction translates into the Bank's investment options, within the flexibility allowed by the eurosystem framework; iii. The increase of EUR 481 million in the value of gold in the balance sheet (valued at 13 EUR 786 million at the end of 2018), due to the rise in the price of in euros. The amount of gold remained unchanged at 382.5 tons; iv. The increase of EUR 1 377 million of banknotes in circulation (totalling 28 EUR 051 million), reflecting the growth in the total number of banknotes in circulation in the Eurosystem. Banco de Portugal's net profit in 2018 was 806 million (656 million in 2017). Of the components of the net result, let me point out three aspects: i. The positive contribution of the interest margin, which totalled EUR 1 065 million. Or increase compared to 2017 ( EUR 55 million) resulted mainly from the increase in the volume of the PSPP in the government securities component; ii. The positive results in financial operations amounting to EUR 68 million euros; iii. The net income from the distribution of monetary income in the amount of EUR 73 million representing a reduction of EUR 54 million compared to 2017. The movement of the provision for general risks in 2018 resulted mainly from the structural reduction of exposure to foreign exchange risk, following the decision to change investment policies from a long-term perspective, leading to a decrease in the amount of foreign currency-denominated assets in asset management portfolios. Administrative expenditures totalled EUR 206 million, reducing 2 million euros compared to 2017 (-0.8%). This decrease resulted from a decrease of EUR 4 million in third-party supplies and services (-7.7%) due to a large reduction in legal advice expenditure stemming from resolution measures (-6 million euros), partially offset by an increase of EUR 2 million in personnel expenditure (1.8%). This increase was due, inter alia, to the impact of the wage update of 0.75%, in line with that defined by the Portuguese Association of Banks for 2018. It should be noted that the average number of bank staff has not changed compared to 2017, in line with what is expected. The result obtained in 2018 enabled a distribution of dividends to the State of 645 million euros (525 million euros in 2017). The total value of dividends and current income tax for 2018 amounted to EUR 1003 million (EUR 796 million in 2017). Thank you very much. 1 Prepared for presentation. Activity and Accounts Report 2018
text_original: Interveno inicial do Governador, Carlos da Silva Costa, na audio anual pela Comisso de Oramento, Finanas e Modernizao Administrativa (COFMA) da Assembleia da Repblica ao abrigo do artigo 54. da Lei Orgnica do Banco de Portugal 11 jun. 2019 Interveno inicial[1] Senhora Presidente, Senhoras e Senhores Deputados, Bom dia, O Banco de Portugal divulgou, em 10 de maio, o Relatrio do Conselho de Administrao  Atividade e Contas relativo a 2018. Em 8 de maio, tinha j divulgado o Boletim Econmico com a anlise da economia portuguesa em 2018. Ainda em maio divulgou os Relatrios de Implementao da Poltica Monetria, de Emisso Monetria, de Acompanhamento da Medida Macroprudencial sobre Crditos a Consumidores e, mais recentemente (5 de junho), publicou o Relatrio de Estabilidade Financeira. Em abril tinham j sido disponibilizados os Relatrios de Superviso Comportamental, dos Sistemas de Pagamentos, da Atividade Estatstica e da Atividade de Cooperao relativos a 2018. Todos estes relatrios esto disponveis no stio institucional do Banco de Portugal na Internet, dando expresso  sua poltica de transparncia e de prestao pblica de contas. A respetiva leitura permite no s enquadrar a atividade do Banco de Portugal em 2018 no contexto nacional e internacional, como possibilita a obteno de informao mais detalhada sobre reas especficas da sua atuao. Na minha interveno inicial  que, como habitualmente, tambm ser disponibilizada na Internet  comearei por caraterizar muito sumariamente o contexto interno e externo em que decorreu a atividade do Banco de Portugal em 2018. Em seguida farei um balano, necessariamente no exaustivo, dessa atividade e terminarei com algumas notas sobre o Balano e Contas. Como sempre, terei todo o prazer em desenvolver alguns dos pontos mencionados, em resposta s questes que os Senhores Deputados entendam colocar. I. Enquadramento Em 2018, a poltica econmica na rea do euro, manteve-se orientada para a promoo da estabilidade de preos e de um crescimento sustentado, num contexto internacional caraterizado por menor dinamismo da atividade econmica mundial, recrudescimento de tenses comerciais e geopolticas, maior incerteza e condies financeiras mais restritivas. Em Portugal, a atividade econmica expandiu-se pelo quinto ano consecutivo, embora a um ritmo mais moderado. O produto real superou, pela primeira vez, o nvel alcanado antes da crise financeira internacional e prosseguiu a reduo do endividamento dos vrios setores da economia e, por esta via, a correo dos desequilbrios acumulados no passado. Uma dcada aps o eclodir da crise financeira internacional, o sistema financeiro da Unio Europeia  incluindo o sistema bancrio portugus  est mais capitalizado e mais escrutinado, na sequncia (i) das profundas reformas de natureza regulamentar e institucional introduzidas no ps-crise (algumas ainda incompletas, como  o caso da Unio Bancria) e (ii) de novos modelos e prticas de superviso. Todavia, persistem inmeros desafios e incertezas para os quais todos os intervenientes no processo de tomada de deciso, incluindo os bancos centrais do Eurosistema, tm de estar vigilantes e preparados. O Banco de Portugal est e continuar atento e empenhado na resposta aos desafios que se colocam ao sistema financeiro nacional. A sua influncia nas decises com impacto nas economias portuguesa e da rea do euro vai depender do mandato que lhe estiver atribudo e da sua capacidade para perspetivar e responder aos desafios que se colocam, nos planos nacional e europeu. II. Atividade em 2018 Em 2018, o Banco de Portugal manteve-se fiel aos compromissos de exigncia, de aperfeioamento e de autossuperao, transversais s vrias prioridades definidas no seu Plano Estratgico para 2017-2020 . A atividade do Banco de Portugal decorreu num contexto marcado por mltiplos desafios. Permitam-me que destaque cinco: i. A evoluo da poltica monetria do Eurosistema  em especial das medidas no convencionais , preservando condies favorveis de financiamento  economia; ii. Os desafios de sustentabilidade do sistema bancrio nacional, que exigiram um direcionamento particular da ao de superviso para os mecanismos de governo e de controlo interno, risco de crdito, posies de capital e de liquidez e modelos de negcio; iii. A salvaguarda da estabilidade do sistema financeiro nacional, incluindo a anlise contnua de vulnerabilidades e riscos sistmicos e a adoo de uma medida macroprudencial para mitigar os riscos associados  concesso de novo crdito  habitao, crdito com garantia hipotecria ou equivalente e crdito ao consumo; iv. O alargamento das responsabilidades de superviso comportamental, decorrente da entrada em vigor de nova legislao; v. O impacto das alteraes tecnolgicas e da transformao digital na atividade de intermediao financeira e nos sistemas de pagamentos e o necessrio ajustamento das competncias e da estrutura organizativa do Banco de Portugal. Feito este enquadramento inicial, passarei brevemente em revista a atividade desenvolvida em 2018, estruturando-a em torno das quatro linhas gerais de orientao estratgica definidas pelo Conselho de Administrao para o quadrinio 2017-2020. Autoridade monetria No que respeita s funes de autoridade monetria, o Banco de Portugal participou nas decises de poltica monetria no quadro do Conselho do Banco Central Europeu (BCE). Em 2018, a poltica monetria do Eurosistema prosseguiu a orientao acomodatcia e continuou a proporcionar condies de financiamento favorveis s economias da rea do euro. Em dezembro, o Conselho do BCE decidiu cessar as aquisies lquidas mensais do programa de compra de ativos, mas anunciou que continuaria a reinvestir a totalidade dos pagamentos de capital dos ttulos vincendos num perodo prolongado aps a primeira subida das taxas de juro oficiais. O Banco de Portugal assegurou a execuo da poltica monetria nica junto das instituies de crdito residentes e participou na aquisio de ativos financeiros no mbito dos programas de compra de ativos. Em 2018, o saldo mdio das carteiras de poltica monetria e das aquisies do programa de compra de ativos no balano do Banco de Portugal aumentou  ainda que de forma menos significativa do que em 2017  para 49 319 milhes de euros. O programa de compra de dvida do setor pblico (PSPP)  o mais representativo, com um peso mdio de 88% no volume total das carteiras. Enquanto autoridade monetria do Eurosistema, o Banco de Portugal promoveu ainda a adoo atempada pelos prestadores de servios de pagamento, dos requisitos decorrentes do novo Regime Jurdico dos Servios de Pagamento e da Moeda Eletrnica. Em setembro, o Sistema de Compensao Interbancria (SICOI)  gerido pelo Banco de Portugal e que processa a generalidade das operaes de pagamento ordenadas pelos particulares e pelas empresas em Portugal  passou a permitir a realizao de transferncias imediatas. O Banco de Portugal ligou-se tambm ao servio de liquidao de pagamentos imediatos do Eurosistema (TIPS), que entrou em funcionamento em 30 de novembro. O Banco de Portugal participou ainda nos trabalhos preparatrios do lanamento das notas de 100 e 200 euros da srie Europa, que entraram em circulao no passado dia 28 de maio. Tambm celebrou um acordo de regularizao de excedentes de moeda metlica com o Banco Central da Eslovquia, traduzido no envio, para aquele pas, de 10 milhes de moedas de 2 euros (excedentrias em Portugal), por troca de 20 milhes de moedas de 1 euro (excedentrias na Eslovquia). Estabilidade financeira No quadro da sua misso de salvaguarda da estabilidade financeira, o Banco de Portugal atua diariamente para promover a robustez das instituies de crdito e a confiana dos agentes econmicos. O setor bancrio nacional realizou nos ltimos anos um ajustamento significativo, em resposta a um quadro regulatrio e de superviso mais exigente, que permitiu: Melhorar a solvabilidade; Reforar a posio de liquidez; Reduzir substancialmente os ativos no produtivos; Melhorar a rendibilidade. Em 2018, o Banco de Portugal continuou a participar no desenvolvimento de nova legislao e regulamentao da Unio Europeia destinada a reforar o quadro legal aplicvel s instituies de crdito e empresas de investimento, nas vertentes prudencial, comportamental, de resoluo e de preveno do branqueamento de capitais e do financiamento do terrorismo. Tambm colaborou nos trabalhos destinados a completar a Unio Bancria e a rever o funcionamento do Sistema Europeu de Superviso Financeira. Como j referi, o Banco de Portugal adotou uma medida macroprudencial, sob a forma de recomendao, que estabeleceu limites a alguns critrios utilizados pelas instituies na concesso de novos crditos aos consumidores. No passado dia 29 de maio foi divulgado o primeiro relatrio de avaliao do cumprimento desta medida . A anlise efetuada aponta para que os limites definidos estejam a ser adequados e eficazes no cumprimento dos objetivos estabelecidos. A medida ser novamente avaliada no primeiro trimestre de 2020. O Banco de Portugal atuou sobre os desafios de sustentabilidade do sistema bancrio nacional, promovendo um forte escrutnio dos mecanismos de governo e de controlo interno das instituies, o reforo das posies de capital e de liquidez, o robustecimento dos modelos de negcio e a reduo dos emprstimos no produtivos e de outros ativos considerados problemticos, com base numa interveno banco a banco. No final de 2018, o stock de emprstimos no produtivos totalizava 25,9 mil milhes de euros, cerca de metade do mximo de 50,5 mil milhes de euros, registado em junho de 2016. Em 2018 foi tambm alargado o permetro da superviso comportamental do Banco de Portugal. Com a entrada em vigor do regime jurdico dos intermedirios de crdito e do novo regime do crdito hipotecrio, o Banco passou a desempenhar funes na autorizao, no registo e na superviso da atividade dos intermedirios de crdito, bem como na certificao e na monitorizao das entidades formadoras dos intermedirios de crdito e dos funcionrios das instituies envolvidos na comercializao do crdito  habitao. Passou ainda a ser responsvel por fiscalizar a atividade dos prestadores do servio de iniciao do pagamento e do servio de informao sobre contas, por fora da entrada em vigor do novo regime dos servios de pagamento e da moeda eletrnica. Ainda em 2018: Para prevenir e reprimir a atividade financeira ilcita, o Banco de Portugal efetuou diligncias de averiguao no contexto de 218 processos. No mbito da preveno do branqueamento de capitais e do financiamento do terrorismo, conduziu 20 aes de inspeo, emitiu 198 medidas supervisivas e apreciou a implementao de 354 medidas adotadas na sequncia de aes de inspeo realizadas em anos anteriores. Na sequncia da sua ao de superviso, o Banco instaurou 113 processos de contraordenao e concluiu 195 processos. O Banco de Portugal defendeu a legalidade das medidas de resoluo e sancionatrias no mbito de um elevado nmero de processos, decorrentes, sobretudo, das medidas de resoluo aplicadas ao BES e ao BANIF. Gostaria de destacar, j em 2019, o Acrdo proferido, no passado dia 12 de maro, por unanimidade dos vinte Juzes do Tribunal Administrativo de Crculo de Lisboa, que considerou no inconstitucional o regime jurdico da resoluo e confirmou a plena legalidade da medida de resoluo do BES. O Acrdo critica a atuao do BES enquanto entidade supervisionada e atesta a forma adequada como o Banco de Portugal atuou enquanto supervisor. O Banco de Portugal continua, tambm, particularmente atento ao impacto da evoluo tecnolgica no setor financeiro. Como todos podemos constatar, nos ltimos anos ocorreram mudanas muito significativas na oferta de servios financeiros, estando em curso um processo veloz de transformao digital no sistema financeiro. Em 2018, o Banco acompanhou os desenvolvimentos em matria de inovao nos produtos e nos servios financeiros nos fruns nacionais e internacionais em que participa, promoveu reunies com Fintech, criou um canal de contacto dedicado (Fintech+) e lanou, em parceria com a Autoridade de Superviso de Seguros e Fundos de Penses, a Comisso do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios e a Portugal Fintech, o Portugal FinLab, uma plataforma de comunicao entre inovadores do setor financeiro e os reguladores portugueses. Produo e divulgao de conhecimento O Banco de Portugal continuou a produzir anlise e investigao sobre a economia portuguesa, a economia da rea do euro e o sistema financeiro. Em 2018, a investigao centrou-se nos temas prioritrios definidos na agenda de estudos para 2017-2020: Os novos desafios  poltica monetria e  estabilidade financeira; O crescimento econmico portugus no contexto da rea do euro; e O futuro das instituies e polticas pblicas em Portugal e na Unio Europeia. Foram concludos 47 estudos e, no final do ano, 113 outros estavam em curso ou em fase final de reviso. No final do ano, o Laboratrio de Investigao com Microdados do Banco de Portugal, instalado no Porto, acolhia 34 projetos cientficos. O Banco de Portugal, na qualidade de autoridade estatstica nacional, lanou, em 2018, uma nova Central de Responsabilidades de Crdito que lhe permitiu reforar a qualidade da informao com que trabalha e que presta ao sistema financeiro, aos cidados e s empresas. Os estudos e as estatsticas assumem um papel crucial no aconselhamento de poltica monetria, econmica e prudencial e a sua divulgao contribui para disseminar o conhecimento e estimular o debate pblico. Neste sentido, o Banco diversificou os canais de contacto com o pblico e intensificou as suas aes de comunicao, incluindo nas redes sociais. Gesto interna Em 2018, o Banco prosseguiu o aperfeioamento do seu modelo de governo, organizao e processos, tendo como referncia as melhores prticas do Eurosistema e a gesto eficiente dos recursos colocados  sua disposio. Saliento o reforo do regime normativo interno em matria de tica e conduta, com a sistematizao dos procedimentos de preveno de conflito de interesses e de controlo dos limites s transaes financeiras privadas. Paralelamente, na sequncia da aprovao, pelo BCE, do Cdigo de Conduta nico , os membros do Conselho de Administrao passaram a estar sujeitos a um conjunto de requisitos de conduta e mecanismos de controlo harmonizados a nvel europeu. No domnio da proteo de dados, o Gabinete de Proteo de Dados conduziu um diagnstico exaustivo sobre o tratamento de dados pessoais e adotou um plano de ao para assegurar a conformidade com o novo Regulamento Geral da Proteo de Dados. O Banco de Portugal continuou a gerir, de forma integrada os riscos financeiros e os riscos operacionais a que est exposto no desempenho da sua atividade. A funo de auditoria interna foi sujeita a uma avaliao de qualidade realizada por uma entidade credenciada, que concluiu pela conformidade em todos os domnios. O Banco de Portugal continuou tambm a investir fortemente no desenvolvimento de competncias tcnicas, comportamentais e de gesto dos seus colaboradores .A capacitao dos seus recursos humanos  fundamental para que o Banco intervenha com qualidade, quer a nvel nacional quer internacional. III. Balano e Contas Concluirei a minha interveno com algumas notas sobre as contas do Banco de Portugal de 2018. No final de 2018, o balano do Banco ascendia a 157 953 milhes de euros, representando um aumento de 4 988 milhes de euros em relao a 2017. Gostaria de destacar quatro aspetos subjacentes  evoluo neste perodo: i. O aumento da participao no programa de compra de ativos do setor pblico em mercado secundrio (PSPP, na sigla inglesa), na componente de ttulos de dvida pblica portuguesa, que atingiu no final do ano 31 mil milhes de euros (acrscimo de 4 900 milhes de euros); ii. A diminuio de 1 407 milhes de euros nos ativos de gesto lquidos , decorrente da deciso de reduo da carteira de negociao em moeda estrangeira  com reflexo na reduo da exposio ao risco cambial , que teve como contrapartida um decrscimo das responsabilidades intra-Eurosistema (TARGET). Esta reduo traduz as opes de investimento do Banco, dentro da flexibilidade permitida pelo enquadramento do Eurosistema; iii. O aumento de 481 milhes de euros no valor do ouro no balano (avaliado em 13 786 milhes de euros no final de 2018), decorrente da subida da respetiva cotao em euros. A quantidade de ouro manteve-se inalterada em 382,5 toneladas; iv. O acrscimo de 1 377 milhes de euros das notas em circulao (totalizando 28 051 milhes de euros), reflexo do crescimento do total de notas em circulao no Eurosistema. O resultado lquido do Banco de Portugal em 2018 foi de 806 milhes de euros (656 milhes de euros em 2017). Das componentes do resultado lquido, permitam-me que saliente trs aspetos: i. O contributo positivo da margem de juros, que totalizou 1 065 milhes de euros. O acrscimo face a 2017 (+ 55 milhes de euros) resultou, maioritariamente, do aumento do volume do PSPP na componente de ttulos governamentais; ii. Os resultados positivos em operaes financeiras no montante de 68 milhes de euros; iii. O resultado lquido da repartio do rendimento monetrio no valor de 73 milhes de euros, representando uma reduo de 54 milhes de euros em relao a 2017. A movimentao da proviso para riscos gerais em 2018 resultou, essencialmente, da reduo estrutural de exposio ao risco cambial, na sequncia da referida deciso de alterao, numa perspetiva de longo prazo, das polticas de investimento, conduzindo  diminuio do montante de ativos denominados em moeda estrangeira nas carteiras de gesto de ativos. Os gastos de natureza administrativa totalizaram 206 milhes de euros, reduzindo-se 2 milhes de euros face a 2017 (-0,8%). Esta diminuio resultou do decrscimo de 4 milhes de euros em fornecimentos e servios de terceiros (-7,7%) devido, em grande medida  reduo de gastos com assessoria jurdica no mbito das medidas de resoluo (-6 milhes de euros), parcialmente compensada por um aumento de 2 milhes de euros dos gastos com pessoal (+1,8%). Este aumento decorreu, designadamente, do impacto da atualizao salarial de 0,75%, em linha com o definido pela Associao Portuguesa de Bancos para 2018.  de sublinhar que o nmero mdio de efetivos do Banco no se alterou relativamente a 2017, em linha com o previsto. O resultado apurado em 2018 possibilitou uma distribuio de dividendos ao Estado de 645 milhes de euros (525 milhes de euros em 2017). O valor total de dividendos e imposto sobre o rendimento corrente relativos a 2018 ascendeu a 1003 milhes de euros (796 milhes de euros em 2017). Muito obrigado. 1 Preparado para apresentao. Title: Opening speech of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, in the presentation organized by ASFAC of the study conducted by a Team of Nova SBE on the impact of consumer credit on the Portuguese economy
text: Opening speech of the Vice-Gov... Opening speech of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, in the presentation organized by ASFAC of the study conducted by a Team of Nova SBE on the impact of consumer credit on the Portuguese economy 25 Jun 2019 1. I begin by greeting, in the person of the President of the Board, Dr. Antonio Menezes Rodrigues, all the members of the governing bodies of ASFAC -Association of Specialized Credit Institutions, as well as all the speakers and participants in this important and timely initiative. On behalf of Banco de Portugal I thank you for the invitation and I assure you that I am happy to meet here. As we know, the purpose of this initiative is to publicly present a study on the impact of consumer credit on the Portuguese economy carried out by a team of researchers and professors from the School of Business and Economics of the Universidade Nova de Lisboa, led by Prof. Pedro Brinca. It is very important for the development of the financial system Portuguese that the associations of companies in the sector have an active and dynamic attitude, promoter of the study and debate on the most important topics, which generates critical mass and goes beyond the mere corporate motivations of occasion. In order to improve the financial system, the debate must be informed, rigorous and participated, involving political bodies, regulatory and supervisory authorities, the academic world and, of course, companies. In this sense, the realization of this study is, in itself, important. Regardless of your assessment  which obviously is not fit to do here  the initiative of promoting it is in itself a source of rejoicing. As I mentioned in the speech I gave at the ASFAC Annual Conference held last year, "consumer credit is inextricably linked to a model of society that places consumption as a central value", and therefore has a genesis in contemporary societies. For this very part, consumer credit is now a phenomenon with broad economic and social implications, and is rooted, even in different ways, in all developed economies. It's useless, so demonize him. It must be relocated and monitored in order to adequately protect bank customers and also to prevent systemic risk. And, from a broader perspective, we also avoid harmful consequences of various order for the social fabric. We therefore need to study the issue of consumer credit in depth in all aspects that contribute to its proper knowledge, particularly in the economic, legal and regulatory aspects but also, for example, in the sociological aspect. Only in this way can public action about you be clarified. 2. Very soon, Banco de Portugal will publish the Retail Banking Markets Monitoring Report for 2018. In this Report, as usual, abundant information will be made available on the evolution of consumer credit in general and in each of its three modalities, the following being: personal credit, car credit and revolving credit. Anticipating some figures, we can already mention that in 2018 the contracting of consumer credit maintained the growth trend that has been seen since 2013, but the increase was lower than in previous years. Indeed, in 2018 the amount of consumer credit granted increased by 10.1% compared to 2017, thus below the 12% growth in 2017 and the growth of 17.5% recorded in 2016. This downward trend is also mentioned in the Macroprudential Recommendation Follow-up Report on new consumer credits, published by Banco de Portugal last month. It says that for new consumer credit operations there was "a slowdown in the second half of 2018 and the first months of 2019". It is therefore verified that this slowdown coincided with the entry into force in July 2018 of the much-referred macroprudential measure. The most recent figures are therefore clear about the slowdown in consumer credit either as an effect of the macroprudential measure or by endogenous factors to the evolution of the economy or, more likely, by the combination of both. It is not at all bad news, as previous growth rates were manifestly very high, even considering the recession-hit downturn. Moreover, it should be noted that in 2018 there was an increase in non-compliance in the field of consumer credit. In another plan, it is verified that in 2018 the trend of growth of the weight of institutions with specialized activity in the granting of consumer credit was maintained. These entities accounted for 57.2% of the credit granted. As for the marketing channel, 54.1% of the amount of consumer credit was granted directly to the credit institution and the remaining 45.9% through the commercial establishment where the goods are bought, values that are in line with those verified in 2017. It is also important to note that the maximum rates applicable to consumer credit  a very important regulatory instrument  decreased in most segments and subsegments, although less markedly than in 2017. 3. The entry into force of the legal regime of credit intermediaries, on 1 January 2018, extended the perimeter of behavioral supervision, thus bringing a new regulatory framework for the supervisor and the supervised, with great impact in the field of consumer credit. We are fully convinced that, despite the natural difficulties of the transition, this regulatory evolution will translate into a clear gain towards a more disciplined and efficient credit market. Under a legislative change made at the end of 2018 and which we consider entirely appropriate, it was allowed that entities that already carried out the activity of credit intermediary before 1 January 2018 and to submit the application for authorisation until the end of that year continue to operate without authorization from Banco de Portugal until 31 July 2019. Between January 1, 2018 and June 22, 2019, Banco de Portugal received the impressive number of 5988 applications for authorization to exercise the activity of credit intermediary with a strong concentration in the last months of 2018. Of these cases, 4822 are closed: 3827 with the granting of the authorization and 995 with the rejection. There is therefore a stock of 1166. It's been a great effort for everyone. As was its duty, Banco de Portugal dedicated itself to this task with a true spirit of mission. As I had the opportunity to mention in the opening note of the 2018 Behavioral Supervision Report, for some the legal regime may be seen as too demanding. However, the Bank's duty is to comply with the legislation on credit intermediaries strictly, but also  undoubtedly  with adequacy, proportionality and common sense. That's what we've been trying to do. 4. By the action of the European and national authorities, the granting of consumer credit is now a heavily regulated activity. And it is also an intensely supervised activity. In fact, Banco de Portugal is fully committed to fulfilling its mandate in the area of behavioral supervision as its Report, published in April, unequivocally demonstrates. But the times are complex and of dizzying evolution. The digitisation of markets, for example, brings enormous challenges and will test hard the adaptability and implementation of regulators and supervisors, as well as the effectiveness of their action. This will be the case in all areas of its scope and particularly in the field of consumer credit. So we need to walk together. Banco de Portugal is not self-centered. It is open to the outside world, whether in the framework of the supervisory dialogue or in active participation in the European institutions and in the wider international institutions. 5. We are experiencing a period of great uncertainty at European and global level. Both at political and economic level. To say this is to assert a common place, but it does not diminish the importance of recognizing it. In greater or lesser gau, in all periods there are factors of uncertainty. This time, however, uncertainty focuses on structural factors of our collective life. The evolution of the European Union, the outcome of the serious geopolitical and geoeconomic tensions in progress, the intensity and speed of the digital revolution, the consequences of demographic change and climate change make up a particularly demanding picture. The process of appointing the new leaders of the European Union for the next five years is underway. European politics has long become Portugal's internal policy. For multiple reasons, the difficulty and specificity of the times do not allow us to be unrelated. It is also for this reason that Portugal has robust, motivated institutions, aware of their responsibilities and without "fear of existing", to use the expression of the philosopher Jose Gil. At Banco de Portugal we work daily for this. But today the reason for our presence here is the presentation of the study on the impact of consumer credit on the Portuguese economy. Therefore, the momentum is of its authors, whom I congratulate. Thank you so much for your attention.

Interveno de abertura do Vice-Governador, Lus Mximo dos Santos, na Apresentao organizada pela ASFAC do estudo realizado por equipa da Nova SBE sobre o impacto do crdito ao consumo na economia portuguesa 25 jun. 2019 1. Nesse sentido, a realizao deste estudo , s por si, importante. Independentemente da sua avaliao  que obviamente no cabe aqui fazer  a iniciativa de o ter promovido  em si mesma motivo de regozijo. Por isso mesmo, o crdito ao consumo  hoje um fenmeno com largas implicaes econmicas e sociais, encontrando-se enraizado, ainda que de diferentes modos, em todas as economias desenvolvidas.  intil, portanto, diaboliz-lo.  preciso sim regul-lo e fiscaliz-lo de modo a proteger adequadamente os clientes bancrios e tambm prevenir o risco sistmico. E, numa perspetiva mais ampla, evitar igualmente consequncias nefastas de ordem vria para o tecido social. Precisamos, portanto, de estudar o tema do crdito ao consumo com profundidade em todas as vertentes que contribuem para o seu adequado conhecimento, designadamente nas vertentes econmica, jurdica e regulatria mas tambm, por exemplo, na vertente sociolgica. S desse modo a atuao pblica a seu respeito pode ser esclarecida. 2. Muito em breve, o Banco de Portugal publicar o Relatrio de Acompanhamento dos Mercados Bancrios de Retalho referente a 2018. Em tal Relatrio ser disponibilizada, como habitualmente, abundante informao sobre a evoluo do crdito ao consumo em geral e em cada uma das suas trs modalidades, a saber: crdito pessoal, crdito automvel e crdito revolving. Antecipando alguns nmeros, podemos desde j referir que em 2018 a contratao de crdito ao consumo manteve a tendncia de crescimento que se verifica desde 2013, mas o aumento foi inferior ao verificado nos anos anteriores. Com efeito, em 2018 o montante de crdito ao consumo concedido aumentou 10,1% face a 2017, abaixo, portanto, do crescimento de 12% verificado em 2017 e do crescimento de 17,5% registado em 2016. Essa tendncia de desacelerao  tambm referida no Relatrio de Acompanhamento da Recomendao macroprudencial sobre novos crditos a consumidores, publicado pelo Banco de Portugal no ms passado. A se diz que relativamente s novas operaes de crdito ao consumo se observou um abrandamento na segunda metade de 2018 e nos primeiros meses de 2019. Verifica-se, portanto, que esse abrandamento coincidiu com a entrada em vigor, em julho de 2018, da aludida medida macroprudencial. Os nmeros mais recentes so, pois, claros, quanto  desacelerao do crdito ao consumo seja por efeito da medida macroprudencial seja por fatores endgenos  evoluo da economia ou, mais provavelmente, pela conjugao de ambos. No  de todo uma m notcia, pois as anteriores taxas de crescimento eram manifestamente muito elevadas, mesmo considerando a retrao ocorrida no perodo da recesso. Alis, importa ter presente que em 2018 se verificou um aumento do incumprimento no mbito do crdito ao consumo. Noutro plano, verifica-se que em 2018 se manteve a tendncia de crescimento do peso das instituies com atividade especializada na concesso de crdito ao consumo. Estas entidades foram responsveis por 57,2% do crdito concedido. Quanto ao canal de comercializao, 54,1% do montante de crdito ao consumo foi concedido diretamente na instituio de crdito e os restantes 45,9% atravs do estabelecimento comercial onde  efetuada a compra do bem, valores que esto em linha com os verificados em 2017.  tambm importante assinalar que as taxas mximas aplicveis no crdito ao consumo  um instrumento regulatrio muito importante  diminuram na generalidade dos segmentos e subsegmentos, embora de forma menos acentuada do que em 2017. 3. A entrada em vigor do regime jurdico dos intermedirios de crdito, em 1 de janeiro de 2018, alargou o permetro da superviso comportamental, trazendo, assim, um novo quadro regulatrio para o supervisor e os supervisionados, com grande impacto no domnio do crdito ao consumo. Estamos plenamente convictos de que, apesar das naturais dificuldades da transio, esta evoluo regulatria se ir traduzir num claro ganho no sentido de um mercado de crdito mais disciplinado e eficiente. Nos termos de uma alterao legislativa efetuada no final de 2018 e que consideramos inteiramente adequada, foi permitido que as entidades que j exerciam a atividade de intermedirio de crdito antes de 1 de janeiro de 2018 e que apresentassem o pedido de autorizao at ao final desse ano continuassem a atuar sem autorizao do Banco de Portugal at 31 de julho de 2019. Entre 1 de janeiro de 2018 e 22 de junho de 2019, o Banco de Portugal recebeu o impressionante nmero de 5988 pedidos de autorizao para o exerccio da atividade de intermedirio de crdito com uma forte concentrao nos ltimos meses de 2018. Desses processos, 4822 esto encerrados: 3827 com a concesso da autorizao e 995 com o indeferimento. Existe, portanto, um stock de 1166. Tem sido um grande esforo para todos. Como era seu dever, o Banco de Portugal dedicou-se a esta tarefa com verdadeiro esprito de misso. Como tive oportunidade de referir na nota de abertura do Relatrio de Superviso Comportamental referente a 2018, para alguns o regime legal poder ser visto como demasiado exigente. Porm, o dever do Banco  cumprir a legislao sobre os intermedirios de crdito com rigor, mas tambm  sem dvida -com adequao, proporcionalidade e bom senso.  isso que temos procurado fazer. 4. Por fora da ao das autoridades europeias e nacionais, a concesso de crdito ao consumo  hoje uma atividade fortemente regulada. E  tambm uma atividade intensamente fiscalizada. Na verdade, o Banco de Portugal est totalmente comprometido com o cumprimento do seu mandato na rea da superviso comportamental como o respetivo Relatrio, publicado em abril, inequivocamente demonstra. Mas os tempos so complexos e de evoluo vertiginosa. A digitalizao dos mercados, por exemplo, traz desafios enormes e vai testar duramente a capacidade de adaptao e concretizao das entidades reguladoras e supervisoras, bem como a eficcia da sua ao. Assim ser em todas as reas do seu mbito de atuao e particularmente no domnio do crdito ao consumo. Precisamos, por isso, de caminhar em conjunto. O Banco de Portugal no est autocentrado. Est aberto ao exterior, seja no plano do dilogo de superviso, seja na ativa participao nas instituies europeias e nos fora internacionais de mbito mais vasto. 5. Vivemos um perodo de grande incerteza no plano europeu e mundial. Tanto a nvel poltico como econmico. Diz-lo  afirmar um lugar-comum mas nem isso diminui a importncia de o reconhecermos. Em maior ou menor gau, em todos os perodos se verificam fatores de incerteza. Desta vez, porm, a incerteza incide sobre fatores estruturantes da nossa vida coletiva. A evoluo da Unio Europeia, o desfecho das graves tenses geopolticas e geoeconmicas em curso, a intensidade e a rapidez da revoluo digital, as consequncias da evoluo demogrfica e das alteraes climticas compem um quadro especialmente exigente. Est em curso o processo de designao dos novos dirigentes da Unio Europeia para os prximos cinco anos. H muito que a poltica europeia passou a ser poltica interna de Portugal. Por mltiplas razes, a dificuldade e a especificidade dos tempos no nos autorizam desatenes. Tambm por isso  fundamental Portugal contar com instituies robustas, motivadas, conscientes das suas responsabilidades e sem medo de existir, para usar a expresso do filsofo Jos Gil. No Banco de Portugal trabalhamos diariamente para isso. Mas hoje o motivo da nossa presena aqui  a apresentao do estudo sobre o impacto do crdito ao consumo na economia portuguesa. Por isso, o momentum  dos seus autores, a quem desde j felicito. Muito obrigado pela vossa ateno.

Title: Intervention of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, at the "CIRSF Annual International Conference 2019": "Banking Behavioral Supervision: importance and main challenges"
text: Compatible... Intervention of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, at the "CIRSF Annual International Conference 2019": "Banking Behavioral Supervision: importance and main challenges" 04 jul. 2019 1. Let me begin by thanking you for inviting me to participate in the Annual Conference of the Centre for Research, Regulation and Financial Supervision (CIRSF), which, due to the excellence of successive editions, has become a reference event with regard to reflection on the most important topics of the financial sector. I greet all the speakers and participants and i greet, in particular, Prof. Luis Morais, whom I warmly congratulate on this cirsf initiative. It is important that the themes of behavioural supervision in the financial sector are further analysed and discussed. My intervention will focus on the subject of banking behavioural supervision. I will focus on the reasons for its importance for the pursuit of financial stability, the emergence of what has been called a "new paradigm" of behavioural supervision, and some of the main challenges that are currently facing it, in particular in the light of the digital transformation of financial services. 2. In Portugal, a specialised (or tripartite) supervisory system shall be in place, so that each of the three regulatory and supervisory authorities of the financial system shall exercise behavioural supervision functions within its sphere of action. As I have had occasion to stress on several occasions and it is, moreover, relatively consensual, there are no ideal supervisory models. In the financial crisis, no model was immune to serious problems. The causes of the crisis were different in nature and cross-sectional to the different models. This does not mean that it is not possible to identify more correct institutional solutions than others, not so much through an absolute superiority of a model in relation to too much, but above all by considering its suitability for the financial system of the country in which it is in force and, in the case of the Member States of the European Union, its coherence with the European architecture. For my part, I clearly favour the maintenance of the tripartite institutional model. Without prejudice to recognizing, without a doubt, that various legislative improvements are needed, in order to make it possible to extract all the potential from the current system. 3. Banco de Portugal is the national authority for banking regulation and behavioural supervision. In this capacity, it exercises regulatory, supervisory and sanctioning powers of the conduct of entities subject to its supervision with regard to the marketing of retail banking products and services, i.e.: bank deposits and their accounts; housing credit; consumer credit; and payment instruments (including cards, transfers, cheques and direct debits). The marketing of other financial products, even by credit institutions, is not subject to the behavioral supervision of Banco de Portugal. Banking behavioural supervision aims to ensure the transparency of the information provided by supervised entities to their customers in the marketing of banking products and services and ensure compliance with the regulatory framework of these products and services. But the objectives of behavioural supervision cannot be pursued effectively if one acts only on the supply side: demand must also be acted on the demand side. How people deal with money, how they make their consumer decisions, what motivates them to save or use credit depends on their financial knowledge, attitudes and behaviours; and these are decisive, not now, international studies, in particular surveys on the subject, show deficits in financial literacy in all the countries in which they are carried out. Increasing the financial knowledge of the population is, however, a difficult task. Initiatives in this area do not produce immediate results and it is therefore important to develop structured, lasting and diversified projects according to objectives and target audiences. This is what Banco de Portugal has done, in collaboration with the other supervisory entities, within the framework of the National Council of Financial Supervisors, implementing the National Financial Training Plan, and through its own initiatives. The role of schools is crucial and irreplaceable. But financial education policies are now also clearly assumed as a mission of central banks, especially when they are also responsible for supervision. In fact, a current strategy for behavioral supervision must necessarily be based on three pillars: the definition of an appropriate regulatory framework, the monitoring of compliance through intrusive action, based on innovative methodologies and instruments, and a policy of promoting financial literacy, which some  especially in Brazil  call the eloquent expression of "financial citizenship". And it is precisely from this triangle that Banco de Portugal has interpreted and executed the mandate that the legislator conferred on it in the field of banking behavioral supervision. 4. The consequences of the financial crisis have led to an intensification and refinement of prudential and behavioural regulation. Housing and consumer credit, for example, is now much more regulated as a result of the action of the European and national legislators. But the changes are not only quantitative: they refer to the nature of the regulation itself. We don't just have more regulation. We have a different regulation. In fact, banking behavioural supervision now has the skills to intervene in new areas, with an impact on the business model of institutions. For example, it is empowered to intervene upstream of the procurement process by assessing the conformity of the internal procedures adopted by the institutions in the context of the creation and distribution of banking products and services, and should ensure the adequacy of those products and services and the channels chosen for the distribution, the characteristics, needs and objectives of their target audiences1. It can therefore be said with property that a new paradigm of regulation and behavioral supervision has emerged. Greater powers and more complex exercise, which are a source of greater responsibility at various levels. The Guidelines of the European Banking Authority on governance and monitoring procedures for retail banking products  already adopted in Portugal  have transported us to a world of enormous demand. The policy of remuneration of the workers of the institutions has become subject to a set of new duties with relevance to behavioral supervision. Institutions are obliged to implement mechanisms for approving and monitoring the remuneration policies of their workers involved in the development, marketing and granting of mortgage credit. There are rules on the requirements regarding the level of training and knowledge of workers dealing with customers. This new paradigm of behavioural supervision resulting from much of European legislation has led to levels of hard-to-absorb demands for both institutions and supervisors. And to a degree of intrusion not always easy to manage, particularly as to the boundary between regulation and management. But in the face of the financial crisis, strengthening behavioural supervision was inevitable in defence of the banking sector itself. 5. We often hear conflicts of interest invoke dwell erred between prudential supervision In fact, the failure to comply with the duties of conduct, especially when it is intense and enduring, directly against the pursuit of financial stability in so far as it calls into question the essential value on which the financial sector is based: trust. If institutions do not internalise a culture of compliance with standards of conduct before their clients, is it reasonable to expect them to do so in other areas? The fulfillment-oriented culture does not exist segmented: it either exists globally or is a facade that yields to the first difficulty. Moreover, in good rigour, even from other instruments, the main issues related to prudential supervision are also focused on behavioral issues: what is health and safety management after all but the sum of many attitudes and decisions? What is the basis of corporate governance rules other than the prevention of undue behavior? What is the basis for monitoring the adequacy of the members of the administrative and supervisory bodies but the prevention of misconduct whether they are deliberate or not? As Bank of England Governor Mark Carney 2 rightly said, the banking crisis of the last decade was "a twin crisis of solvency and legitimacy." Unfortunately, the undue behaviour in the financial sector continued even after the crisis, of which the case of libor manipulation is only a very serious example. Also in the words of Mark Carney, "an industry with the importance of the financial industry needs both capital in the economic sense and capital towards society" and presented the following bumblebees: in the UK, in 2017, only 20% of citizens considered that banks were well managed, against 90% at the end of the 19803s. And we all know from experience in their respective countries that the UK is not isolated on this path. Are the citizens wrong? Is it just an unjustified perception? Much has been learned from the crisis. But it is undeniable that there is still a long way to go before confidence reaches the levels that the sector needs and deserves because of its key role for economic development. The best managers, however, have long realized that, in the medium and long term, fulfillment-oriented culture is a source of lasting income and a basis for sustainability. And this perspective could even be increased, for example, if among the criteria of variable remuneration of managers there were indicators related to regulatory compliance and the sanctions applied to the institution. Aligning incentives in favour of good practice is a path that should be further explored. A climate of trust in the institutions facilitates the work of managers and is, moreover, a very important advantage in scenarios of change and uncertainty, such as those we go through. For too long, Adam Smith's belief in the "invisible hand" was invoked in a hasty and superficial way, forgetting that to correctly interpret his economic thought we had to summon the integrality of his philosophical thought, namely what he expressed in the work "Theory of Moral Feelings". Any system of ideas that is brought into practice neglecting the ethical aspects of behavior is doomed to become a caricature of itself and, unfortunately, historical examples abound in this regard. Economics is a social science and not an experimental science. The proper consideration of its comportamental dimension is therefore fundamental. In this sense, the Nobel Prize awarded in 2017 to Richard Thaler was an important sign at an opportune time. As the financial crisis has shown, many decisions have been motivated not by economic rationality but by objectives of another nature. 6. The sale of non-performing loans by banking institutions (NPL) is a major priority of the European strategy for the pursuit of financial stability. But it is important to ensure that this objective is achieved without compromising the legitimate protection of borrowers' rights, on the fact that the claims The solution to this problem must be found at European level. Work on the proposal for a Directive known as the "Credit Servicers Directive" has made some positive progress from the point of view of this objective. But we will see how the situation will evolve in the European political cycle that has now begun, since it has not been possible to adopt the Directive in the previous European legislature. This is a problem with profound social repercussions and all attention must be paid. In a different plan  which already draws from the field of banking behavioural supervision, aware of the nature of the products concerned  it is also essential to ensure adequate levels of transparency when it comes to placing retail customers of mrel-eligible debt securities. 7. The most important challenge currently for banking behavioural supervision is digital transformation. The recent technological innovation has redefined the way financial products and services are marketed. This innovation brings opportunities and benefits for consumers, while increasing existing risks and creating new problems. Some of the risks and disadvantages are already known, but others may emerge as financial institutions embrace new technologies. The impact of the technological revolution on financial markets not only affects the very functioning of markets, but also alters the behaviour of consumers who participate in them (who are increasingly digital and require greater convenience and speed). With this desideratum, the conduct supervisor is in a complex position: ensuring the balance between innovation, consumer protection, security and financial stability. To this end, behavioural supervision must act dynamically, in particular by promoting the necessary regulatory changes. The massive use of consumer data by financial institutions may require the creation of specific and targeted rules for the use of non-traditional data sources, to promote greater transparency in the use of algorithms or, further, to the need to adopt robust algorithms that are tailored to the interests of consumers, promoting their periodic review. The European supervisory authorities reinforced in the Joint Committee Final Report on Big Data the need for monitoring the Big Data phenomenon by regulators and supervisors and passed on a set of best practices to financial institutions on its use. Conduct supervisors themselves are faced with the imperative need to adopt new supervisory methods and tools, in line with technological developments. In Portugal, the strategy of behavioral supervision in the face of technological developments is based on the following vectors: Monitor technological developments; Monitor marketing of financial products and services; Eliminate regulatory barriers; Ensure a technological neutrality; Promote digital financial training. In developing economies, the digital context has the advantage of increasing levels of financial inclusion. On the other hand, more developed economies should take into account the risk of exclusion of segments of the population with low digital literacy, which is particularly relevant in societies with ageing populations. The supervisor must first guarantee the same rights to consumers, regardless of the channel they use in the acquisition of banking products and services, ensuring the principle of technological neutrality  "same business, same risks, same rules, same supervision". The European Commission is reviewing the Consumer Credit Directive and the Directive on distance marketing of financial services provided to the European Union, cross-border marketing of financial services is further enhanced by the possibility of providing services under the freedom of services scheme ("LPS"). This reality calls into question the scope of action of the conduct supervisor, a problem to which it is urgent to respond. The European supervisory authorities have paid particular attention to this topic, and the report on "cross-border supervision of retail financial services", which is awaiting publication, has recently been adopted. 8. On the economic and social impact of new digital technologies there are very different views. But everyone agrees that it's structural and profound. As in all times, problems do not lie in the technologies themselves, but in the use we make of them. A new world has arrived and is developing under our eyes. Whether or not it will be a "brave new world", in the sense that Aldous Huxley gave him in his famous novel, it is up to each of us to contribute to the answer. Thank you so much for your attention. 1 Cf. Behavioral Supervision Report 2017, pp. 31-32. 2 . 3 Ibid.
