Interveno do Vice-Governador, Lus Mximo dos Santos, na "CIRSF Annual International Conference 2019": "Superviso Comportamental Bancria: importncia e principais desafios" 04 jul. 2019 1. Permitam-me que comece por agradecer o convite para participar na Conferncia Anual do Centro de Investigao, Regulao e Superviso Financeira (CIRSF), a qual, pela excelncia das sucessivas edies, se tornou num evento de referncia no que diz respeito  reflexo sobre os temas mais importantes do setor financeiro. Cumprimento todos os oradores e participantes e sado, muito em particular, o Prof. Lus Morais, a quem felicito vivamente por mais esta iniciativa do CIRSF.  importante que os temas da superviso comportamental no setor financeiro sejam ainda mais analisados e debatidos. A minha interveno ir incidir sobre o tema da superviso comportamental bancria. Centrar-me-ei nas razes da sua importncia para a prossecuo da estabilidade financeira, na emergncia do que se tem vindo a designar como um novo paradigma de superviso comportamental, e nalguns dos principais desafios que atualmente se lhe colocam, designadamente em funo da transformao digital dos servios financeiros. 2. Em Portugal vigora um sistema de superviso especializada (ou tripartida), pelo que cada uma das trs autoridades de regulao e superviso do sistema financeiro exerce funes de superviso comportamental no mbito da sua esfera de ao. Como j tive ocasio de sublinhar em diversas ocasies e , de resto, relativamente consensual, no h modelos de superviso ideais. Na crise financeira, nenhum modelo ficou imune a problemas graves. As causas da crise foram de outra ndole e transversais aos diferentes modelos. O que no significa que no seja possvel identificar solues institucionais mais corretas do que outras, no tanto por via de uma superioridade absoluta de um modelo em relao aos demais, mas, sobretudo, pela ponderao da respetiva adequao ao sistema financeiro do pas em que vigora e, no caso dos Estados-membros da Unio Europeia, da sua coerncia com a arquitetura europeia. Pela minha parte, favoreo claramente a manuteno do modelo institucional tripartido. Sem prejuzo de reconhecer, sem a menor dvida, que so necessrias melhorias legislativas vrias, de modo a permitir extrair do sistema vigente todas as potencialidades. 3. O Banco de Portugal  a autoridade nacional de regulao e de superviso comportamental bancria. Nessa qualidade, exerce poderes regulatrios, fiscalizadores e sancionatrios da conduta das entidades sujeitas  sua superviso no que respeita  comercializao de produtos e servios bancrios de retalho, a saber: depsitos bancrios e suas contas; crdito  habitao; crdito aos consumidores; e instrumentos de pagamento (incluindo cartes, transferncias, cheques e dbitos diretos). A comercializao de outros produtos financeiros, mesmo que por instituies de crdito , no est sujeita  superviso comportamental do Banco de Portugal. A superviso comportamental bancria tem como objetivo garantir a transparncia da informao prestada pelas entidades supervisionadas aos seus clientes na comercializao de produtos e servios bancrios e assegurar o cumprimento do quadro normativo destes produtos e servios. Mas os objetivos da superviso comportamental no podem ser prosseguidos eficazmente se se atuar apenas do lado da oferta: h que atuar tambm do lado da procura. A forma como as pessoas lidam com o dinheiro, como tomam as suas decises de consumo, o que as motiva a poupar ou a recorrer ao crdito depende dos seus conhecimentos, atitudes e comportamentos financeiros; e estes so determinantes, no Ora, os estudos internacionais, nomeadamente os inquritos sobre o tema, evidenciam dfices de literacia financeira em todos os pases em que so realizados. Aumentar os conhecimentos financeiros da populao , contudo, uma tarefa difcil. As iniciativas neste domnio no produzem resultados imediatos e, por isso,  importante desenvolver projetos estruturados, duradouros e diversificados em funo dos objetivos e dos pblicos-alvo.  isso que o Banco de Portugal tem feito, em colaborao com as demais entidades supervisoras, no mbito do Conselho Nacional de Supervisores Financeiros, dando execuo ao Plano Nacional de Formao Financeira, e atravs de iniciativas prprias. O papel das escolas  crucial e insubstituvel. Mas as polticas de educao financeira so hoje tambm claramente assumidas como uma misso dos bancos centrais, sobretudo quando so tambm responsveis pela superviso. De facto, uma estratgia atual para a superviso comportamental tem necessariamente de assentar em trs pilares: a definio de um quadro regulatrio adequado, a fiscalizao do seu cumprimento atravs de uma ao intrusiva, assente em metodologias e instrumentos inovadores, e uma poltica de promoo da literacia financeira, que alguns  sobretudo no Brasil  designam pela eloquente expresso de cidadania financeira. E  justamente a partir desse tringulo que o Banco de Portugal tem interpretado e executado o mandato que o legislador lhe conferiu no domnio da superviso comportamental bancria. 4. As consequncias da crise financeira levaram a uma intensificao e refinamento da regulao prudencial e comportamental. A concesso de crdito  habitao e ao consumo, por exemplo, so hoje muito mais reguladas em resultado da ao do legislador europeu e nacional. Mas as alteraes no so apenas quantitativas: referem-se  natureza da prpria regulao. No temos apenas mais regulao. Temos uma regulao diferente. Com efeito, a superviso comportamental bancria dispe hoje de competncias para intervir em novas reas, com impacto no modelo de negcio das instituies. Por exemplo, est munida de poderes para intervir a montante do processo de contratao, atravs da avaliao da conformidade dos procedimentos internos adotados pelas instituies no mbito da criao e distribuio de produtos e servios bancrios, devendo garantir a adequao desses produtos e servios e dos canais escolhidos para a sua distribuio, s caratersticas, necessidades e objetivos dos respetivos pblicos-alvo1. Pode, pois, dizer-se com propriedade que emergiu um novo paradigma da regulao e da superviso comportamental. Maiores poderes e de exerccio mais complexo, que so fonte de maior responsabilidade a diversos nveis. As Orientaes da Autoridade Bancria Europeia relativas aos procedimentos de governao e monitorizao de produtos bancrios de retalho  j adotadas em Portugal  transportaram-nos para um mundo de enorme exigncia. A poltica de remunerao dos trabalhadores das instituies passou a estar sujeita a um conjunto de novos deveres com relevncia para a superviso comportamental. As instituies esto obrigadas a implementar mecanismos de aprovao e monitorizao das polticas de remunerao dos seus trabalhadores envolvidos na elaborao, comercializao e concesso de crdito hipotecrio. Existem regras sobre as exigncias quanto ao nvel de formao e conhecimentos dos trabalhadores que lidam com os clientes. Este novo paradigma da superviso comportamental resultante de muita da legislao europeia levou a patamares de exigncia difceis de absorver, tanto para as instituies como para os supervisores. E a um grau de intruso nem sempre fcil de gerir, designadamente quanto  fronteira entre regulao e gesto. Mas face ao sucedido no decurso da crise financeira, o reforo da superviso comportamental foi inevitvel em defesa do prprio setor bancrio. 5. Frequentemente, ouvimos invocar conflitos de interesse entre a superviso prudencial Na verdade, o desrespeito dos deveres de conduta, sobretudo quando se revele intenso e duradouro, atenta diretamente contra a prossecuo da estabilidade financeira na medida em que pe em causa o valor essencial em que est assente o setor financeiro: a confiana. Se as instituies no interiorizarem uma cultura de cumprimento das normas de conduta perante os seus clientes ser razovel esperar que o faam noutros domnios? A cultura orientada para o cumprimento no existe segmentada: ou existe globalmente ou  uma fachada que cede  primeira dificuldade. Alis, em bom rigor, ainda que a partir de outros instrumentos, as principais questes ligadas  superviso prudencial esto tambm focadas em questes comportamentais: o que  afinal a gesto s e prudente seno a soma de muitas atitudes e de muitas decises? Qual  o fundamento das regras de corporate governance seno a preveno de comportamentos indevidos? Qual  o fundamento do controlo da adequao dos membros dos rgos de administrao e de fiscalizao seno a preveno de comportamentos incorretos sejam eles deliberados ou no? Como bem afirmou o Governador do Banco de Inglaterra, Mark Carney 2, a crise bancria da ltima dcada foi uma crise gmea de solvncia e legitimidade. Infelizmente, os comportamentos indevidos no setor financeiro continuaram mesmo depois da crise, de que o caso da manipulao da Libor  apenas um exemplo muito grave. Ainda nas palavras de Mark Carney, uma indstria com a importncia da indstria financeira precisa tanto de capital em sentido econmico como de capital perante a sociedade e apresentava os seguintes desoladores nmeros: no Reino Unido, em 2017, s 20% dos cidados considerava que os bancos eram bem administrados, contra 90% no final da dcada de 19803. E todos sabemos, por experincia prpria nos respetivos pases, que o Reino Unido no est isolado nesse percurso. Estaro os cidados enganados? Ser apenas uma perceo injustificada? Muito foi aprendido com a crise. Mas  inegvel que  preciso percorrer ainda um caminho longo para que a confiana volte a atingir os nveis que o setor precisa e merece dado o seu papel fundamental para o desenvolvimento econmico. Os melhores gestores, porm, h muito que perceberam que, a mdio e longo prazo, a cultura orientada para o cumprimento  uma fonte de proveitos duradouros e base de sustentabilidade. E essa perspetiva poderia at ser incrementada, por exemplo, se entre os critrios da remunerao varivel dos gestores houvesse indicadores relativos ao cumprimento regulatrio e s sanes aplicadas  instituio. Alinhar os incentivos em favor das boas prticas  um caminho que deve ser mais explorado. Um clima de confiana nas instituies facilita o trabalho dos gestores e constitui, alis, uma vantagem muito importante em cenrios de mudana e incerteza, como so aqueles que atravessamos. Durante demasiado tempo, a crena na mo invisvel de Adam Smith foi invocada de forma apressada e superficial, esquecendo que para interpretar corretamente o seu pensamento econmico tnhamos de convocar a integralidade do seu pensamento filosfico, designadamente o que expressou na obra Teoria dos Sentimentos Morais. Qualquer sistema de ideias que seja levado  prtica negligenciando os aspetos ticos do comportamento est condenado a tornar-se uma caricatura de si prprio e, infelizmente, abundam os exemplos histricos nesse sentido. A economia  uma cincia social e no uma cincia experimental. A adequada considerao da sua dimenso comportamental , pois, fundamental. Nesse sentido, o Prmio Nobel atribudo, em 2017, a Richard Thaler foi um sinal importante e num momento oportuno. Como a crise financeira demonstrou, muitas decises foram motivadas no pela racionalidade econmica mas por objetivos de outra natureza. 6. A venda de crditos no produtivos por parte das instituies bancrias (NPL, no acrnimo em ingls)  uma prioridade maior da estratgia europeia para a prossecuo da estabilidade financeira. Mas importa assegurar que esse objetivo  alcanado sem comprometer a legtima tutela dos direitos dos muturios, pelo facto de os crditos A soluo para esse problema deve ser encontrada  escala europeia. Os trabalhos relativos  proposta de Diretiva conhecida por diretiva dos credit servicers tiveram alguns avanos positivos do ponto de vista desse objetivo. Mas veremos como evoluir a situao no ciclo poltico europeu que agora se iniciou, visto que no foi possvel aprovar a Diretiva na legislatura europeia anterior. Trata-se de um problema com profundas repercusses sociais e a que deve ser prestada toda a ateno. Num plano diferente  que j extravasa o domnio da superviso comportamental bancria, atenta a natureza dos produtos em causa   tambm indispensvel garantir adequados nveis de transparncia quando esteja em causa a colocao junto de clientes de retalho de ttulos de dvida elegveis para efeito de MREL. 7. O desafio mais importante que atualmente se coloca  superviso comportamental bancria  o da transformao digital. A recente inovao tecnolgica veio redefinir a forma de comercializao dos produtos e servios financeiros. Esta inovao acarreta oportunidades e benefcios para os consumidores, ao mesmo tempo que amplia riscos existentes e cria novos problemas. Alguns dos riscos e desvantagens so j conhecidos, mas outros podero emergir  medida que as instituies financeiras vo adotando as novas tecnologias. O impacto da revoluo tecnolgica nos mercados financeiros afeta no s o prprio funcionamento dos mercados, mas tambm altera o comportamento dos consumidores que neles participam (que so cada vez mais digitais e exigem maior convenincia e rapidez). Com este desiderato, o supervisor de conduta depara-se com uma posio complexa: assegurar o equilbrio entre a inovao, a proteo do consumidor, a segurana e a estabilidade financeira. Para este efeito, a superviso comportamental deve atuar de forma dinmica, designadamente promovendo as necessrias alteraes regulatrias. A massiva utilizao dos dados dos consumidores pelas instituies financeiras pode requerer a criao de regras especficas e direcionadas para a utilizao de fontes no tradicionais de dados, para a promoo de uma maior transparncia na utilizao de algoritmos ou, ainda, para a necessidade de adotar algoritmos robustos e ajustados aos interesses dos consumidores, promovendo para esse efeito a sua reviso peridica. As autoridades europeias de superviso reforaram, no Joint Committee Final Report on Big Data, a necessidade de monitorizao do fenmeno Big Data por parte dos reguladores e dos supervisores e transmitiram um conjunto de boas prticas s instituies financeiras sobre a sua utilizao. Os supervisores de conduta esto eles prprios confrontados com a imperiosa necessidade de adotarem novos mtodos e ferramentas de superviso, em linha com os desenvolvimentos tecnolgicos. Em Portugal, a estratgia da superviso comportamental face  evoluo tecnolgica assenta nos seguintes vetores: Acompanhar a evoluo tecnolgica; Monitorizar a comercializao de produtos e servios financeiros; Eliminar barreiras regulatrias; Assegurar a neutralidade tecnolgica; Promover a formao financeira digital. Nas economias em desenvolvimento, o contexto digital tem como vantagem a possibilidade de incrementar os nveis de incluso financeira. Em contraponto, as economias mais desenvolvidas devero ter em ateno o risco de excluso de segmentos da populao com baixa literacia digital, o que  particularmente relevante em sociedades com populaes envelhecidas. O supervisor deve garantir, em primeiro lugar, os mesmos direitos aos consumidores, independentemente do canal por eles utilizado na aquisio de produtos e servios bancrios, assegurando o princpio da neutralidade tecnolgica  same business, same risks, same rules, same supervision. A Comisso Europeia encontra-se a rever a Diretiva do crdito aos consumidores e a Diretiva respeitante  comercializao  distncia de servios financeiros prestados a Na Unio Europeia, a comercializao transfronteiria de servios financeiros  ainda potenciada pela possibilidade de disponibilizao de servios ao abrigo do regime da liberdade da prestao de servios (LPS). Esta realidade pe em causa o mbito de atuao do supervisor de conduta, problema a que urge dar resposta. As autoridades de superviso europeia tm dedicado especial ateno a este tpico, tendo sido aprovado recentemente o relatrio sobre cross-border supervision of retail financial services, que aguarda publicao. 8. Sobre o impacto econmico e social das novas tecnologias digitais h vises muito distintas. Mas todos concordam que  estrutural e profundo. Como em todas as pocas, os problemas no residem nas tecnologias em si, mas no uso que fazemos delas. Um mundo novo j chegou e est a desenvolver-se sob os nossos olhos. Title: Intervention of the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the Diploma Award Ceremony of the XVII Executive MBA of AESE Business School
text: Intervention of the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the Diploma Award Ceremony of the XVII Executive MBA of AESE Business School 27 jul. 2019 Intervention [1] Exma. Dean da AESE Business School, Exmos. Executive MBA finalists, Ladies and gentlemen, Good morning, everyone. It is with great pleasure that I join the award ceremony of the seventeenth Executive MBA of The AESE. The occasion and the place invite me to share with you brief reflections on the decisive and indispensable contribution that institutions like this can make to the development of our country. The essential points of these reflections, which I will develop during my speech, are as follows: First, it is clear to everyone that the aspirations of individual well-being and collective equity of Portuguese society exceed the production capacity of the economy; Second, the qualification of human resources and the quality of management models are important 'levers' of this productive capacity of the economy; Finally, the quality of management models benefits when companies are able to reorganize themselves, gain dimension and ensure adequate separation between ownership and management. Insufficient production capacity Let's start with the diagnosis. Over the past two decades, nominal GDP per capita Portuguese has remained 30 to 40 percent below the European Union average, a gap that has not been surpassed by the path of convergence that has occurred in the past latest. Correcting this indicator of differences in purchasing power between countries, we have even found a trajectory of divergence in the last two decades. This evidence attests to the margin of progression that we have and that can only be bridged with more and better economic growth. We also know that what is between the Portuguese economy and the front-line economy of advanced economies is the productivity of every hour worked and not the number of hours each person works. There are two 'levers', of this hourly productivity, which I would like to highlight: First, the qualification of human resources, including the qualification of managers; And second, the adequacy, robustness and quality of management models. Widely known academic studies, notably by Professor John Van Reenen, estimate that 27% of the productivity gap between Portugal and the most productive economy analyzed  that of the USA  is related to the difference in quality of management. The qualification of human resources As regards the qualification of human resources, Portugal has made considerable improvements in recent years. However, there remain significant distances from European averages, so we need to continue to improve the formal education of our workers. In particular, older workers, who typically have fewer qualifications, can benefit greatly from lifelong vocational training strategies, which give them the tools they need to make the best use of jobs of the present and the future. This prescription is valid not only so that managers continually renew their own skills, but also to ensure that the workers they lead also benefit from this continuous renewal of knowledge and knowledge. Naturally, the promotion of the qualification of human resources cannot be limited to the increase in the number of years of schooling of the population. Inclusive growth requires two conditions to be met: First, it is necessary to ensure that the education system anticipates and adjusts to the that the productive sector needs. The educational offer must promote the development of transversal competencies such as leadership, interpersonal relationships or problem-solving capacity, and must also respond to the requirements of technological development of the country; Secondly, we must ensure that the legislative framework, the administrative context and the own management of enterprises generate the ability to absorb the skills Developed. If this is not the case, we will be faced with unemployment and brain drain, via emigration of specialized staff. AESE Business School thus produces human capital and knowledge decisive in promoting the productivity of our economy, and, in this way, indispensable for the development of our country. The adequacy, robustness and quality of management models For the combination of capital and work to result in the production desired by the market, we need an entrepreneur, an organization and a management model. The management model reflects the articulation that the manager prints to the triangle that unites environment, organization and strategy. That is, the management model defines an organization, which designs a strategy, in order to make the best advantage, and even influence, the environment that surrounds it. This articulation generates a differentiation of the company's performance from the performance it would naturally have if it only passively adjusted to the environment in which it is included. An illustrative example of this differentiation is visible in the comparison between the trajectory of large companies in the textile sector of Vale do Ave and Galicia in recent decades. The differences in performance do not reside in the sector category, which is identical, do not reside in the workers, who come from the same sociocultural stratum, nor reside in the geographies where they are included, which are very close. The differences stem precisely from the management models that have been put in place. With regard to the quality of management models, our country still has good scope for progression to explore, as is evident in the latest edition of the Global Competitiveness Index, published by the World Economic Forum. portugal is behind 15 economies of the European Union and, in the list of indicators our country gets worse ranking, some are related to the quality of management models, namely a attitude towards risk, in which we occupy position 80 out of 140 economies, a predisposition to delegate authority - position 70 out of 140 - and the integration of disruptive ideas - position 46 out of 140. National data also show an important potential for increased productivity by improving management. In 2017, the National Institute of Statistics launched the first edition of its Survey on Management Practices. This survey was aimed at top managers of companies based in Portugal and aimed to collect qualitative information about the management practices of these companies, in various areas, from strategy to organization, through monitoring of objectives and decision-making. The analysis of the survey results shows that companies with best management practices have higher gross added value per worker, i.e. have higher levels of productivity per worker. How can they improve management models? I would like to highlight two vectors through which business fabric management models Portuguese can progress. The first is the quality and size of the organization. An organization well designed and adapted to the challenges of the company allows to mobilize the functions and competencies most relevant to its success. Today, any company with ambition faces globalized, complex, extensive and constantly changing markets. Such challenges therefore require organizations of high size, capable of monetizing and mobilizing resources with quality and diversified valences. Empirical research has already found evidence that corroborates the importance of the size and quality of the organization: on the one hand, there is a positive relationship between the size of the company and the quality of management; on the other hand, data for Portugal also show a notoriouspositive relationship between between the size of companies and their productivity; in particular, when Portuguese companies are reorganized in response to a external shock, adding a new hierarchical line of managers, their productivity accelerates, in addition to all this evidence that, over the last few decades, the size of Portuguese companies has been decreasing, which represents an important challenge. In a productive fabric like ours, largely populated by family businesses in transition to the 3rd generation, the increase in the size of organizations is closely linked to the business vision of the families who hold their capital. Which brings me to the third vector I would like to highlight: the relationship between ownership and management. Empirical research has also found evidence that: the presence of external share capital to a given founding family is associated with best management practices and as a general rule, the quality of management is higher in cases where it is delivered to persons outside the family that owns the company. This means that, in a context such as Portuguese, where family businesses predominate, the concern with improving the quality of management implies that a serious impact is on the separation of entrepreneurial, capital and management functions. Public policies can play an important role here in encouraging professionalization of management in family businesses, by various means: First, revisiting the tax treatment of the distribution of results, to foster an appropriate balance between profit distribution and profit reinvestment; Second, generalizing the obligation to submit audited accounts by companies in order to ensure that the manager has the necessary room for manoeuvre to be to counterbalance the various legitimate interests  stakeholders  in the most beneficial to the company; Third, developing and making available a new "legal institute" of "holding that concentrates the holdings of a given family and that, in this way, legally typifies a model of centralised management of the shareholdings of members of a family; this model must be optional, supplementary and adjusted to the specificities of family businesses, with statutory and tax treatment What commitment to its companies and the territory of the holding company. where they are located; to ensure indispensable legal certainty; And that is simple and easily accessible by smaller companies. Finally, economic policy actors can also provide an important contribution to promoting widespread knowledge about the impact of the quality of management in the productivity of companies. This same contribution is also assumed by Banco de Portugal, Through including the theme of quality of management in its research agenda; Through production, availability and analysis of statistical information of quality that can support the study of the subject; And further raising awareness of the banking system of the importance of taking management models in the risk assessment of companies and their projects and not just the real guarantees. In a way, there is no doubt that the quality of management is central to the challenge of promoting productivity. The good news is that Portugal still has a lot to gain from triggering this lever. In times like today, marked by such strong heterogeneity and so low global dynamism in productivity, it is imperative that we do not waste this strategic opportunity. Allow me to end by thanking you for inviting me to participate in this ceremony. I hope that all those who today successfully complete their formative career can provide the Portuguese economy with more open, dynamic and proactive management models, capable of catapulting Portugal to higher levels of productivity, development and well-being. text_original: Interveno do Governador, Carlos da Silva Costa, na Cerimnia de Entrega de Diplomas do XVII Executive MBA da AESE Business School 27 jul. 2019 Interveno [1] Exma. Dean da AESE Business School, Exmos. Finalistas do Executive MBA, Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, Muito bom dia a todos.  com enorme gosto que me associo  cerimnia de entrega de diplomas do dcimo stimo Executive MBA da AESE. A ocasio e o local convidam-me a partilhar convosco breves reflexes sobre o contributo decisivo e imprescindvel que instituies como esta podem dar para o desenvolvimento do nosso Pas. Os pontos essenciais dessas reflexes, que desenvolverei durante a minha interveno, so os seguintes: Em primeiro lugar,  claro para todos que as aspiraes de bem-estar individual e de equidade coletiva da sociedade portuguesa excedem a capacidade de produo da economia; Segundo, a qualificao dos recursos humanos e a qualidade dos modelos de gesto so importantes alavancas dessa capacidade produtiva da economia; Finalmente, a qualidade dos modelos de gesto sai beneficiada, quando as empresas so capazes de se reorganizar, ganhar dimenso e garantir uma adequada separao entre propriedade e gesto. Insuficiente capacidade produtiva Comecemos pelo diagnstico. Ao longo das ltimas duas dcadas, o PIB nominal per capita portugus manteve-se 30 a 40 por cento abaixo da mdia da Unio Europeia, hiato que no foi superado pela trajetria de convergncia que se tem verificado no passado mais recente. Corrigindo este indicador das diferenas de poder de compra entre pases, encontramos mesmo uma trajetria de divergncia nessas ltimas duas dcadas. Esta evidncia atesta a margem de progresso que temos e que s pode ser colmatada com mais e melhor crescimento econmico. Sabemos tambm que o que separa a economia portuguesa do peloto da frente das economias avanadas  a produtividade de cada hora trabalhada e no o nmero de horas que cada pessoa trabalha. H duas alavancas, dessa produtividade horria, que gostaria de destacar: Primeiro, a qualificao dos recursos humanos, incluindo a qualificao dos gestores; E, segundo, a adequao, robustez e qualidade dos modelos de gesto. Estudos acadmicos largamente conhecidos, nomeadamente da autoria do Professor John Van Reenen, estimam que 27% da diferena de produtividade entre Portugal e a economia mais produtiva analisada  a dos EUA  se relaciona com a diferena de qualidade de gesto. A qualificao dos recursos humanos Em matria de qualificao dos recursos humanos, Portugal tem registado, nos ltimos anos, melhorias considerveis. Permanecem, contudo, hiatos significativos em relao s mdias europeias, pelo que  necessrio continuar a melhorar a educao formal dos nossos trabalhadores. Em particular, os trabalhadores mais velhos, que tm tipicamente menos qualificaes, podem beneficiar muito de estratgias de formao profissional ao longo da vida, que lhes deem as ferramentas necessrias para aproveitarem da melhor forma os empregos do presente e do futuro. Esta prescrio  vlida, no s para que os gestores renovem continuamente as suas prprias competncias, mas tambm para que cuidem de assegurar que os trabalhadores que lideram beneficiam tambm dessa renovao contnua de conhecimento e saber. Naturalmente, a promoo da qualificao dos recursos humanos no pode resumir-se ao aumento do nmero de anos de escolaridade da populao. Um crescimento inclusivo exige que sejam satisfeitas duas condies: Primeiro, h que garantir que o sistema educativo antecipa e se ajusta aos perfis de que o setor produtivo necessita. A oferta educativa tem de promover o desenvolvimento de competncias transversais como a liderana, as relaes interpessoais ou a capacidade de resoluo de problemas, e tem tambm de responder s exigncias de desenvolvimento tecnolgico do pas; Segundo, temos de assegurar que o quadro legislativo, o contexto administrativo e a prpria gesto das empresas geram a capacidade para absorver as competncias desenvolvidas. Se assim no for, estaremos confrontados com fenmenos de desemprego e de brain drain, via emigrao de quadros especializados. A AESE Business School produz, assim capital humano e de conhecimento decisivos na promoo da produtividade da nossa economia, e, por essa via, imprescindveis para o desenvolvimento do nosso pas. A adequao, robustez e qualidade dos modelos de gesto Para que a combinao de capital e trabalho resulte na produo desejada pelo mercado, necessitamos de um empreendedor, de uma organizao e de um modelo de gesto. O modelo de gesto reflete a articulao que o gestor imprime ao tringulo que une ambiente, organizao e estratgia. Isto , o modelo de gesto define uma organizao, que desenha uma estratgia, de forma a tirar o melhor partido, e mesmo influenciar, o ambiente que a rodeia. Esta articulao gera uma diferenciao do desempenho da empresa face ao desempenho que ela naturalmente teria se apenas se ajustasse passivamente ao ambiente em que se insere. Um exemplo ilustrativo desta diferenciao  visvel na comparao entre a trajetria das grandes empresas do setor txtil do Vale do Ave e da Galiza, nas ltimas dcadas. As diferenas de desempenho no residem na categoria setorial, que  idntica, no residem nos trabalhadores, que provm do mesmo estrato sociocultural, nem residem nas geografias onde se inserem, que so muito prximas. As diferenas decorrem precisamente dos modelos de gesto que foram postos em prtica. No que diz respeito  qualidade dos modelos de gesto, o nosso pas tem ainda boa margem de progresso para explorar, como fica patente na mais recente edio do Global Competitiveness Index, publicado pelo World Economic Forum. Portugal fica atrs de 15 economias da Unio Europeia e, na lista de indicadores em que o nosso pas obtm pior classificao, contam-se alguns relacionados com a qualidade dos modelos de gesto, nomeadamente a atitude perante o risco, em que ocupamos a posio 80 em 140 economias, a predisposio para delegar autoridade  posio 70 em 140  e a integrao de ideias disruptivas  posio 46 em 140. Tambm os dados nacionais revelam um importante potencial de aumento da produtividade atravs da melhoria da gesto. O Instituto Nacional de Estatstica lanou, em 2017, a primeira edio do seu Inqurito s Prticas de Gesto. Este inqurito foi dirigido a gestores de topo de empresas sediadas em Portugal e visou recolher informao qualitativa sobre as prticas de gesto destas empresas, em domnios variados, desde a estratgia  organizao, passando pela monitorizao de objetivos e pela tomada de deciso. A anlise dos resultados do inqurito revela que as empresas com melhores prticas de gesto apresentam maior valor acrescentado bruto por trabalhador, isto , apresentam nveis superiores de produtividade por trabalhador. Como podem melhorar os modelos de gesto? Gostaria de destacar dois vetores atravs dos quais os modelos de gesto do tecido empresarial portugus podem progredir. O primeiro  a qualidade e dimenso da organizao. Uma organizao bem desenhada e adaptada aos desafios da empresa permite mobilizar as funes e competncias mais relevantes para o seu sucesso. Nos nossos dias, qualquer empresa com ambio enfrenta mercados globalizados, complexos, extensos e em constante mutao. Tais desafios requerem, portanto, organizaes de dimenso elevada, capazes de rentabilizar e mobilizar recursos com qualidade e valncias diversificadas. A investigao emprica j encontrou evidncia que corrobora a importncia da dimenso e da qualidade da organizao: por um lado, h uma relao positiva entre a dimenso da empresa e a qualidade da sua gesto; por outro lado, dados para Portugal revelam tambm uma notria relao positiva entre a dimenso das empresas e a sua produtividade; em particular, quando as empresas portuguesas se reorganizam em resposta a um choque externo, acrescentando uma nova linha hierrquica de gestores, a sua produtividade acelera, acresce a toda esta evidncia que, ao longo das ltimas dcadas, a dimenso das empresas portuguesas tem vindo a diminuir, o que representa um desafio importante. Num tecido produtivo como o nosso, muito povoado por empresas familiares em transio para a 3. gerao, o aumento da dimenso das organizaes est intimamente ligado  viso empresarial das famlias que detm o respetivo capital. O que me leva ao terceiro vetor que gostaria de destacar: a relao entre a propriedade e a gesto. A investigao emprica tambm j encontrou evidncia de que: a presena de capital social externo a uma dada famlia fundadora est associada a melhores prticas de gesto e regra geral, a qualidade da gesto  superior nos casos em que ela  entregue a pessoas externas  famlia que detm a propriedade da empresa. O que significa que, num contexto como o portugus, em que predominam empresas familiares, a preocupao com a melhoria da qualidade de gesto implica que se reflita seriamente sobre a separao das funes empreendedora, detentora de capital e de gesto. As polticas pblicas podem desempenhar aqui um importante papel de incentivo  profissionalizao da gesto nas empresas familiares, por diversas vias: Primeiro, revisitando o tratamento fiscal da distribuio de resultados, para fomentar um equilbrio adequado entre distribuio de resultados e reinvestimento de lucros; Segundo, generalizando a obrigatoriedade de apresentao de contas auditadas por parte das empresas, por forma a garantir ao gestor a margem de manobra necessria para contrabalanar os vrios interesses legtimos  os stakeholders  da forma mais benfica para a empresa; Terceiro, desenvolvendo e disponibilizando um novo instituto jurdico de holding familiar, que concentre as participaes de uma dada famlia e que, desse modo, tipifique juridicamente um modelo de gesto centralizada das participaes sociais dos membros de uma famlia; este modelo deve ser opcional, supletivo e ajustado s especificidades das empresas familiares, com um tratamento estatutrio e fiscal Que induza o compromisso da holding com as suas empresas e com o territrio onde esto situadas; Que garanta a indispensvel segurana jurdica; E que seja simples e de fcil acesso por empresas de menor dimenso. Finalmente, os agentes de poltica econmica podem ainda prestar um importante contributo ao promover o conhecimento generalizado sobre o impacto da qualidade da gesto na produtividade das empresas. Esse mesmo contributo  tambm assumido pelo Banco de Portugal, Atravs da incluso do tema da qualidade da gesto na sua agenda de investigao; Atravs da produo, disponibilizao e anlise de informao estatstica de qualidade que possa apoiar o estudo do tema; E ainda sensibilizando o sistema bancrio para a importncia de tomar em linha de conta os modelos de gesto na avaliao de risco das empresas e dos seus projetos e no apenas as garantias reais. Em suma, no restam dvidas de que a qualidade da gesto  central ao desafio de promoo da produtividade. A boa notcia  que Portugal tem ainda muito a ganhar em acionar esta alavanca. Em tempos como os de hoje, marcados por to forte heterogeneidade e to baixo dinamismo global na produtividade, torna-se imperativo que no desperdicemos esta oportunidade estratgica. Permitam-me que termine agradecendo o convite para participar nesta cerimnia. Title: Opening remarks by Director Ana Paula Serra at the European System of Central Banks' Day-Ahead Conference
text: Opening remarks by Director Ana Paula Serra at the European System of Central Banks' Day-Ahead Conference 21 Aug. 2019 On behalf of the Board of Directors of the Banco de Portugal and myself I would like to welcome to you. We are glad that this event is being held in Lisbon, at our central banks premises, for the second time. It is a pleasure for me to have the opportunity to address you on this occasion and let me thank you all for being here. I will be brief since it is going to be a long day and we need to spare our precious time for the discussions of the topics that will be addressed today. The main objective of the Day-Ahead conferences is to create an opportunity for interaction among research economists within the ESCB, other central banks and academia. The Day-Ahead conferences are hosted before one of the two best European annual conferences: the EEA (European Economic Association) or the EFA (European Finance Association). These two large conferences bring together economists working on the forefront of economic and financial research and therefore holding the Day-Ahead conference is a great opportunity and a very efficient way to promote a close interaction between these researchers and central banks. Probably most of you know but let me remind you that these conferences started in Stockholm at the Riksbank in 2011. Since then, thanks to Kasper Roszbach, from Norges Bank, and Wilko Bolt, from De Nederlandsche Bank, year after year, the Day-Ahead venture has been a successful event of the Eurosystem, gathering high-quality and policyrelevant research oriented towards banking, finance, and monetary economics. We have had Day Ahead Conferences at Bank of Spain, Bank of England, Banque de France, Austrian National Bank, Norges Bank and Banco de Portugal. The 2020 conference will be held in De Nederlandsche Bank in Amsterdam. Banco de Portugal already had the honor of hosting the Day-Ahead conference first in 2017, when the EEA was held in Lisbon. Eight top quality papers were presented then, focusing on four topics: Financial Distress, Financial Regulation, and Heterogeneity Inequality, Financial Crises and Real Effects Financial Imbalances and Monetary Policy Bank Capital and Bank Credit This year, Nova SBE hosts the 46th Annual Meeting of the European Finance Association on its new campus in Carcavelos. Banco de Portugal is supporting the EFA and is again honored to host the Day-Ahead conference. This conference has greatly benefited from the immense and careful work of the Organizing Committee. Many thanks to Kasper Roszbach (Norges Bank), Wilko Bolt (De Nederlandsche Bank), and to the local organizers Diana Bonfim (Banco de Portugal) and Ettore Panetti (Banco de Portugal). We were privileged to rely on a great scientific committee, from academia, from ESCB and other central banks. They helped us define the great program that we have ahead of us today. Many thanks to all, to those that could not attend and to those that are here with us today. The conference today will for sure greatly benefit also from the work of the seven discussants that agreed to offer their views and suggestions on the papers presented. The session chairs will also ensure that there is a lively and constructive debate. Thank you. Last but certainly not the least, we would like to thank Victoria Ivashina from Harvard Business School. She is the Lovett-Learned Chaired Professor of Finance at Harvard Business School, where she is also the faculty chair of the Global Initiative for the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). She is a research associate at NBER, a research fellow at CEPR, and a visiting scholar at Boston Fed and the ECB. Her research has been published in the top journals in finance and economics and is regularly cited in media outlets including The Economist, The Financial Times, and The Wall Street Journal Professor Ivashina will give a keynote speech about pension investments around the world in the last decade. The rise of the so-called shadow banking sector in the financial system makes this discussion very timely and relevant for researchers and policymakers at central banks. Today, seven papers will be presented. These were selected out of a recorded number of 199 submissions. The submissions came from 70 different institutions, 25 of which are central banks. The call for papers was anchored on some of the priorities defined in Banco de Portugals research agenda: Financial intermediation Prudential regulation Monetary policy after the crisis The interaction between monetary, prudential and fiscal policies. The papers that were selected and that will be presented today offer important and high quality contributions to the current academic and policy debates. We have a mixture of empirical and theoretical papers that were grouped into four sessions. These are: Stress-testing the banking system Bank capital and crises Savings and real-estate wealth Bank funding and lending These papers are built upon many of the lessons learned in the 10 years since the collapse of Lehman Brothers and also on what policymakers have changed since then, with stricter requirements on capital and reinforcement of risk prevention and reduction, aimed at improving banks resilience. Sound conceptual frameworks and lots of supporting evidence are needed to build a stock of knowledge that stands the test of time. Central bankers rely on these valuable inputs to develop or refine existing micro and macro prudential rules and sustain regulatory policy recommendations. For central bankers the challenge is to make sure that not only that the existing framework provides indeed stronger safety nets for the financial system when facing similar risks but also that the banking system has the capacity to finance investment and growth. To conclude I would like you to know that I believe that your papers will surely help us be better prepared for the challenges ahead. I wish you all a pleasant stay in Lisbon.

Title: Opinion article by Administrator Hlder Rosalino in the Expresso Journal: "Safer payments with the same simplicity"
text: Administrator opinion article... Opinion article by Administrator Helder Rosalino in the Expresso Journal: "Safer payments with the same simplicity" 14 set. 2019 September 14 marks the beginning of the open banking era, which translates into the possibility for bank customers to share their own financial information, so far only in the possession of banks, with new entrants (e.g. fintech). For this to be possible, banks are obliged to offer open interfaces (API - Application Programming Interface) so that these new entrants, as long as properly accredited, can access bank accounts, based on the prior consent of their holder. From this access, fintech and the banks themselves will be able to develop innovative services, integrating multiple channels and offers. You'll be able to incorporate basic banking services (such as payment initiation or account information) into another product or app, just as Google Maps provides maps that support multiple transport and location apps. The value chain of the financial system, especially in the area of payments, will tend to change substantially, promoting new business models and multiplying the offer to customers. In this new paradigm, banks will progressively tend to lose space in the relationship with bank customers, to the extent that they are no longer the sole owners of their financial transactionality. This movement is reinforced by large digital trends and changing consumer behavior, increasingly based on the search for personalized experiences, the integration of services and channels (mobile first) and cost reduction. This is a far-reaching development in the configuration of financial intermediation models, allowed by the entry into force of the Revised Payment Services Directive (DSP2). This regulatory change is an opportunity and a competitive advantage for the development of financial innovation in Europe, of which may benefit new financial operators, established banks and also economic actors, whether business et ase., or individuals. In the age of Open Banking, security takes on a central and enhanced dimension. Therefore, on 14 September, new security rules based on the concept of strong authentication also enter into force in Portugal and other Countries of the European Union. The goal is to increase the security, not only of electronic payments but also of the interaction of citizens with their own bank in homebanking and app environment. Strong authentication is the procedure by which banks will now validate the identity of the customer and the legitimacy of electronic payment transactions, in particular those that may involve risk of online financial fraud. In practice, this enhanced security in the authentication process obliges banks to ask their customers for at least two elements to prove their identity, whenever they access their payment account online, initiate an electronic payment transaction or carry out, through a remote channel, an action that may involve a risk of payment fraud or other abuse. The requested elements must belong to two of the three categories of strong authentication: Knowledge, something that only the user knows, for example a password or a code; Possession, something that only the user has, for example, a mobile phone; and Inerence, something that constitutes a biometric characteristic of the client, for example, fingerprint or facial recognition. The national financial system has been working hard in recent months to respond to new challenges, both in the availability of API and in the implementation of strong authentication mechanisms. Portugal is currently one of the EU countries with the highest degree of API availability, with 99.9% of bank accounts already accessible through these interfaces. In addition to new entrants, banks are also submitting proposals for account information aggregation services, taking advantage of the new regulatory framework to innovate in the services offered to their customers. Open Banking is increasingly seen as an opportunity for banks and new financial operators to respond effectively to the needs of their customers. Strong authentication has also been progressively adopted by banks, with the aim of increasing security and, at the same time, maintaining the simplicity and convenience of making payments. Banco de Portugal has promoted the timely implementation of the new rules for Open Banking and strong authentication, interacting with market agents, namely through the Interbank Commission for Payment Systems and the Forum for Payment Systems. And it will continue, as so far, committed to promoting an increasingly innovative and secure payment market. Video - Do you use your bank's homebanking or app? Learn what's changed

Title: Concluding remarks by Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the conference cycle The Economy and the Future - "Management quality, governance and economic productivity"
text: Conference cycle "A Economia e o Futuro (The Economy and the Future) Faculdade de Economia da Universidade do Porto 23 September 2019 Carlos da Silva Costa, Governor of Banco de Portugal 2 Good afternoon. It gives me great pleasure to be here at this session, which places the themes of management quality and governance models and practices on the agenda of this opening of the academic year. These themes dominated the conference cycle of the last academic year and have strategic importance for our countrys economic development, with schools such as this one playing a key role in this field. We realise that we need more and better economic growth to move our productive capacity closer to Portuguese society's legitimate aspirations of individual well-being and collective equity. In the case of Portugal, more economic growth does not mean working longer hours; it means considerably increasing the productivity of each hour worked. This necessarily involves investment in improving management quality, in a broad sense, which includes not only the managers skills, but also the suitability of management models and governance practices. Indeed, the relationship between firms management and their productivity is well documented. Well-known academic studies by Professor John Van Reenen estimate that approximately 30% of the productivity differences between countries are explained by differences in management quality[3]. Other research specifically shows the impact of the quality of entrepreneurs and managers on their firms performance. Leaders with higher levels of formal qualifications build more productive organisations that can grow faster [4]. An important part of this impact naturally operates through the management models adopted, in terms of the interaction between environment, organisation and strategy, as chosen by the manager. The 2018 Global Competitiveness Index published by the World Economic Forum [5] shows that Portugal has room for improvement in the quality of its management models. The list of indicators for which we rank less favourably includes: Attitude to risk, for which we come 80th out of 140 economies; Willingness to delegate authority, 70th out of 140; And integration of disruptive ideas, 46th out of 140. So, we need managers and governance and management models that open themselves up to risk and disruption, promoting decentralised decision-making. The innovations of the last few decades, in the field of information and communication technologies, have made the production and distribution environments extremely volatile. Firms need to respond continuously to new markets, products and processes and for this purpose have to sustain fast and permanent mutation. This state of constant mutation requires intelligent and agile management. In this regard it is also important that management opens itself to the world. Research shows that the presence of a manager with experience of exporting increases the likelihood that the firm will start, maintain or intensify its export activities [6]. The exposure to international markets offers managers valuable opportunities to learn, positively differentiating the quality of the management models. This is particularly relevant for Portugal, where we will have to continue to redirect resources to the tradable sector, if we want more balanced and sustainable economic growth. On a recent visit to a number of small and medium-sized enterprises in the north of the country, from sectors as diverse as industrial-use textiles, footwear, metalworking and renewable energies, Banco de Portugal has had the chance to see the excellent examples of managers and management models existing in our country. This tour of the business community arose as part of the strategic relationship that Banco de Portugal aims to maintain with the broad range of stakeholders interested in the Banks products. Visiting the firms where they operate provided deeper insights into their environment, strategies and management practices. The main success factors identified by the firms we visited included investment in internationalisation, customer orientation, openness to innovation, product differentiation and a very clear focus on long-term sustainability. The subject of firms sustainability is particularly relevant for the Portuguese economy, as our manufacturing base has a strong component of family firms being handed down to the third generation. Here, it is vital to think how we can reconcile the family ownership of firms and the professionalism of management. A firm whose limits are the horizons of its founder or the founders family runs the risk of being constrained by the management capabilities and control of that founder or family, or becoming attached to its first product, process or technology. In turn, these constraints limit the size and longevity of firms, resulting in a community of relatively small or ephemeral firms, which inevitably influences the economys aggregate productivity [7]. To free firms from these limitations and ensure their sustainability, they must gain scale, professionalise their management and build a complex organisation that responds effectively to the market and embraces innovation. The openness and growth of the firms capital have strategic importance for responding robustly to all these challenges. In this regard I have argued for the development of a standardised model for family holding companies with statutory recognition and a tax regime that not only reconcile family ownership and professional management, but also incorporate and protect the aspirations of all the stakeholders, thereby opening the way to more solid governance models. These family holding companies have been introduced in various countries, including Spain, to facilitate family firms governance and transmission from generation to generation. These holding companies allow the equity, which is easily shared among heirs, to be separate from the management, which should not be shared and need not be bequeathed. The experience of those working in support of Spanish family firms suggests that a family firm paradigm should evolve into a corporate family paradigm. In this, the firms interests take centre stage in the familys decisions over the succession formulas and the governance models. We should remember that governance models, even in firms based around families, have consequences for society: governance is not a private subject, it is a matter of public interest. There is a common interest that overrides private interests, which is that of the continuity of institutions. When a firm collapses, it takes with it a set of expectations. Institutions have a social capital, the loss of which has a negative impact on the economy and a cost for economic and social development. This means that governance does not only involve the establishment of a balance between equity owners, or between the latter and the managers, but involves all the stakeholders. The markets themselves are now requiring firms to broaden their set of stakeholders and the value system that guides their decisions. A growing number of consumers use their value set to guide their choices. More and more investors use sustainability requirements when choosing projects. The new generations of workers entering the job market for the first time will quickly abandon firms that they do not regard as responsible. There were clear signs of good governance also contributing to the success of the firms that Banco de Portugal visited in the north of the country. In several of the firms, the patience of the owners and their long-term stance are key drivers of their day-to-day success, relieving the pressure to make immediate profit; in one of the examples, the founding family even created a fund and transferred ownership of the firm to it, giving up executive power. We also came across great involvement from knowledge centres, customers, the local community and even competitors, in many of the firms strategic, productive or marketing processes. In regard to labour, the leaders widely recognised the importance of always keeping their workers satisfied and fulfilled. This recognition is exemplified in the effort they make to offer an attractive work environment and opportunities to develop skills. The success of the firms that received us is not limited to the people working within them. It mobilises the whole local community and in some cases develops a whole region, especially when it leads to the creation of industrial clusters or virtuous circles of intrasectoral cooperation. In sum, management quality results not only from the managers human capital, but also the management model adopted by them and the governance model that lets them balance all the interests hinging on the firms performance. It would have been hard to choose a better topic for this session, given that the quality of governance and management are core elements of aggregate productivity and as a result are indispensable for the Portuguese economy's sustainable economic development. I would like to finish by thanking you for the invitation to be here, wishing the Faculdade de Economia da Universidade do Porto a prosperous academic year ahead, and leaving you with a very clear challenge. Education and research can perform a key role in understanding and overcoming obstacles to the improvement of management models, while identifying and measuring the relationships between management quality, productivity and financing. With this in mind and by way of example, I leave you with some questions that are particularly relevant from Banco de Portugals viewpoint and that belong on a research agenda that advances reflection on governance and management quality: how can the capitalisation of firms lead to better management? how can management quality prevent default on financial commitments? or, how can financial stability be helped if commercial banks attribute greater relevance to the management models, in the assessment they make of corporate clients risk? I believe that this school and the generations of economists and managers that it teaches year upon year are best placed to produce important knowledge in these areas, while helping firms on the ground renovate and modernise their governance and management models. Thank you very much. Title: Intervention of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, at the end of the Conference "20 years Srvulo" in the session on the future of the financial system
text: Compatible... Intervention of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, at the end of the Conference "20 years Servulo" in the session on the future of the financial system 27 set. 2019 1. Let me begin by thanking the organizers of this Conference for the invitation addressed to me. I would like to leave a special word for Professor Servulo Correia, of whom I had the privilege of being a student in the distant school year of 1981-82, and whom I have always continued to admire for the excellence of his teaching and work but also for his action as a committed citizen in collective life. 2. The programme of this Conference was designed to discuss the future in different relevant areas of our economic and legal life. In my opinion, the best appreciations of the future of societies are more often found in artists, namely writers and filmmakers, than in social science worshipers, with the exception of some famous essayists. Also entrepreneurs and managers are well placed to tell us about the future. Anticipating behaviour is at the origin of their action, because by nature they have to take risks. To do this clearly, they need to identify trends in consumer and consumer behaviour, the evolution of technology, i.e. they have to anticipate market developments. I will focus my intervention on aspects of the behavioural dimension in the context of the digital transformation process. 3. To predict the future, to obtain for ourselves and for our projects the advantage of early knowledge, is a desire that has always accompanied us and that even the recognized difficulty of its realization is not able to make it fade. From the oracles of antiquity to the most complex algorithms served by today's artificial intelligence, the ability to extract an early view, a prediction about a trend, a possibility, a probability about the future of a human, economic or social phenomenon is something fascinating. In the business world, and in particularly in the financial industry, it can be the difference between media and overdoor even between disappearance and success. In this way, this impulse, which in every present impels us to the knowledge of the future, is very old. Many argue that innovation is happening faster today than our ability to adapt to it. That is - or could be - the truly new fact. We try to look to the future by analyzing the present and the past. Some of those who sensed the global financial crisis ten years ago - and took economic advantage of it - did so on the basis of the study of statistics on the behavior of the mortgage market in the United States on the eve of the crisis of 1929. Even in the context of new technologies, looking to the future is, in any case, a very difficult and highly fallible exercise. It is a fact, for example, that algorithms they also fail[1]. The projections based on the best available information and knowledge may be based on events of a disruptive, traumatic nature, unexpected combinations resulting from simultaneous scientific acquisitions, the emergence of "black swans", in the consecrated expression of Nassim Taleb. In fact, we must keep in mind that, as some claim, the "impossible facts" are just beginning[2]. 4. In recent years, there have been countless works, reports from national and international organisations, public and private, political decision-making bodies at various levels, as well as events of all kinds on the future of banking activity. It is natural that this is the scale of the transformations that are underway. In the fourth industrial revolution, technological advances are simultaneously exponential and combinatorial, that is, technological advances are taking place in an integrated and transversal way, not only to be applied in specific domains. These characteristics lead many authors  in my view - to argue that the ongoing process of transformation of society is unparalleled, and there are even those who claim that humanity will change more in the next twenty years than in the last three hundred[3]. But no different from technological transformations, they do not make basic economic constraints disappear. We cannot, in fact, lose sight of this essential point: technology is a means of increasing profitability through greater efficiency of business models and promoting economic and social development. But in order to fulfil its ultimate mission, it must be part of a dynamic economy, which distributes wealth satisfactorily, and be protected by the framework of a rule of law that, among other things, ensures fundamental rights and the fluidity of contractual relations. Marshall McLhuan, in his pioneering studies on communication in the 20th century, stressed that "we shape our tools and therefore our tools shape us." In fact, technological evolution conditions us  and much  especially in the current context in which technologies have become more efficient and intrusive than ever before. But technology does not necessarily have to determine our choices: there is a biunivocal relationship  technology and society influence each other. Not everything that is technologically feasible is desirable or ethically acceptable. And sometimes it might not be legal. It is up to each of us, in their respective professions, and also as citizens, to ensure that this does not happen. The future is us who built it. 5. The cross-cutting dimension of the digital transformation process allows us to say that we are facing a profound change in the way societies are organisationand function, and not only in the face of a mere change in the financial economic paradigm. That is also why the discussion about the future of the banking sector is very important. It's just that the financial sector - and the banking sector in particular - have long played a crucial role in modern societies. The banking sector took its first steps in the Renaissance era, strengthened itself in the context of successive industrial revolutions, to the point that one of the characteristics of the contemporary economic model is "financialization", which means that the banking sector  for good and for evil  has taken a central role in social life. This centrality also contributes to the banking sector and the financial sector in general being changing rapidly. An example of this mutation is the emergence of Fintechs. This is a phenomenon of the greatest importance. It enriches the economic fabric, diversifies the supply of financial products and services, increases competition and therefore benefits consumers. Many will stand by the way, which in no way pinches the importance of the phenomenon itself, because it is something natural in a process that is still affirming. Some understand that Fintechs are a deadly threat to the banking industry. The banking sector will definitely not remain the same as it is; but the vaticinium of its disappearance in the long term seems to me not only to be vastly exaggerated, paraphrasing Mark Twain, but, more than that, unfounded and simplistic in that it underestimates the adaptability of the sector, its accumulated experience, the unfungible character of part of its functions and the critical mass it is able to mobilize. We have also found another plan that neither television killed the radio or the cinema nor the Internet killed the television. But they've all changed profoundly. And that's what I think is going to happen in the banking sector. In order to successfully cope with the ongoing change, financial institutions will have to fully take on and assimilate technological developments and the centrality of the relationship with customers, as well as the importance of strategic partnerships with new actors in the financial sector None of these ideas is, in itself, a novelty. On the contrary, they have long been in the DNA of good bank management. But the terms on which their implementation is placed today are very different from what they were in the past. The worst mistake would be to be in a state of denial as to the depth of the change process. Devaluing the current technological evolution, emphasizing the perspective that it is just another of the successive waves of innovation with which the sector has always done well, does not help to create an environment conducive to change. The importance of sound management decisions is even more critical today. Indeed, in a sector still recovering from the crisis and where capital does not abound, it is essential that the high investments needed for digital transformation fully achieve the objectives pursued and are efficient. In the face of the avalanche of change, we must have the audacity of humility: the hypercomplexity of matters advises against attitudes of self-reliance. As one author points out, "the greatest danger of artificial intelligence is by far people to conclude too early that they understand it"[4]. 6. The creation of a value-driven, value-driven culture is essential to the future of banking in the context of its digital transformation. At the base of banking activity has always been trust. The most lasting damage to the industry has always occurred when there have been bouts of trust. In the digital age this is even more true, because reality is much more immaterial and customers are, on the one hand, in a position of greater potential vulnerability, but on the other, they have a much greater breadth of choice and responsiveness. For this reason, the effects of any breach of trust are amplified by the very nature of digital relationships. We have seen as it is, in multiple sectors of economic activity, including large technology companies. However, in a world where technology is accessible, disseminated and developed as never before, and where its use is permanent and widespread, the importance of the values and culture of the organization as a factor in its affirmation and differentiation in the market is reinforced. Therefore, a culture of compliance with law in general and regulatory standards, in particular, is an essential factor to generate the confidence indispensable to the development of the business. But it's not enough. It is necessary that the promotion of good practices is a reality internalized by all levels of management and employees and that the incentive system is consistent with this objective. It is not just a question of regulatory compliance: it is about building an institutional culture, which is something much wider and deeper, because it is immaterial. 7. I share the concern of those who, especially in certain areas, point to regulatory excesses. We are all aware that the costs of regulation are high today. But the costs of its insufficiency or absence, as the global financial crisis has shown well, are much higher and longer lasting. For its part, the speed of technological and market developments advises a permanent control of the quality of legislation and the regulatory framework in general, so as to avoid becoming an obstacle to innovation. And it is essential, in defense of the financial system itself, that it is fully guaranteed, through supervisory entities and, ultimately, the courts, the full effectiveness of the applicable regulatory framework. 8. The use of big data for the most diverse purposes is an essential pillar of the fourth industrial revolution. Transforming this data into information and the information thus obtained into knowledge is something that brings fantastic advantages but also enormous risks. Thus, ensuring the protection of personal data is now an indispensable condition for building trust in any organisation, including naturally in banking institutions, which I stress, even though it is a matter outside the scope of action of Banco de Portugal, because, as we know, it is a matter that is committed primarily to the institutions themselves and, supervisory authorities, to the National Data Protection Commission. In a sense, it is my belief that the devaluation of law and ethical behavior were core factors of the financial crisis. That path, however, is being reversed. But it is necessary to extract from the banking management plan all the lessons in this regard. Only in this way will an institutional culture be created anchored in solid values, which will be decisive to successfully overcome digital transformation and ensure the future of the sector. 9. It is now a common place for management to point out the recognition of the "importance of people", even if there is not always coherence with this purpose. However, in a world of homogenized use of technology, human capital will tend to be the "making a difference" factor. Human creativity is not disposable. It can even be said that in the age of algorithms it is even more decisive[5]. The use of digital technology must be ethically framed, as people and societies need ethics under penalty of collapse in the longer term. Digital ethics are thus becoming an important field of study and will tend to be increasingly. There are even those who suggest the creation of a Global Digital Ethics Council, tasked with defining the fundamental rules and the most basic and universal values of an increasingly digital society[6]. A new field opens up for regulation and/or self-regulation, with a view to ensuring that digital transformation provides us with the individual and social net gain that is at your fingertips. In conclusion, in the area of technological evolution and behavioral demands, the challenges that this new world, which is unveiled before us, poses to the banking sector are enticing and difficult. Discussing them publicly is also an exercise in citizenship and to that extent this event could not have been more timely. Thank you so much for your attention. [1] Cf. Hannah Fry, Hello Future  As a Human Being in the Age of Algorithms , Planet, 2019, pp. 32-38 and 241-245. [2] Cf. Tom Chatfield, How to make the most of the digital age, Paper Moon, 2019, p. 13. [3] Cf. Gerd Leonard, Technology vs. Humanity, Gradiva, 3rd ed., 2019, p. 19. [4] Cf. Eliezer Yudkowsky, quoted by Gerd Leonard, ob. cit., p. 29. [5] Cf. Hannah Fry, ob. cit., p. 245. [6] Cf. Gerd Leonhard, ob. cit., p. 206.
text_original: Lu... Interveno do Vice-Governador, Lus Mximo dos Santos, no encerramento da Conferncia 20 anos Srvulo na sesso sobre o futuro do sistema financeiro 27 set. 2019 1. Permitam-me que comece por agradecer aos organizadores desta Conferncia o convite que me foi dirigido.
