O programa desta Conferncia foi pensado para debater o futuro em diferentes reas relevantes da nossa vida econmica e jurdica. Na minha opinio, as melhores apreciaes sobre o devir das sociedades encontram-se mais frequentemente em artistas, designadamente escritores e cineastas, do que em cultores das cincias sociais, com a exceo de alguns ensastas clebres. Tambm os empresrios e os gestores esto bem colocados para nos falar sobre o futuro. Antecipar comportamentos est na gnese da sua ao, pois, por natureza, tm de assumir riscos. Para o fazerem com lucidez, tm de identificar as tendncias do comportamento dos consumidores e das organizaes, da evoluo da tecnologia, ou seja, tm de antecipar a evoluo dos mercados. Irei centrar a minha interveno em aspetos que se prendem com a dimenso comportamental no contexto do processo de transformao digital. 3. Prever o futuro, obtermos para ns e para os nossos projetos a vantagem do conhecimento antecipado,  um desejo que nos acompanha desde sempre e que nem a reconhecida dificuldade da sua concretizao  capaz de fazer esmorecer. Dos orculos da antiguidade aos mais complexos algoritmos servidos pela inteligncia artificial de hoje, a capacidade de extrair uma viso antecipada, uma previso sobre uma tendncia, uma possibilidade, uma probabilidade sobre o devir de um fenmeno humano, econmico ou social  algo de fascinante. No mundo empresarial, e em particular na indstria financeira, pode ser a diferena entre a mediania e a superao ou mesmo entre o desaparecimento e o sucesso. Visto assim, este impulso, que em cada presente nos impele para o conhecimento do futuro,  muito antigo. Muitos sustentam que atualmente a inovao est a acontecer mais rapidamente do que a nossa capacidade de nos adaptarmos a ela. Esse   ou poder ser -o facto verdadeiramente novo. Tenta-se perspetivar o futuro atravs da anlise do presente e do passado. Alguns dos que pressentiram a crise financeira global de h dez anos -e disso tiraram proveito econmico  fizeram-no baseando-se no estudo das estatsticas sobre o comportamento do mercado hipotecrio nos Estados Unidos nas vsperas da crise de 1929. Mesmo no contexto das novas tecnologias, perspetivar o futuro , em qualquer caso, um exerccio muito difcil e altamente falvel.  um facto, por exemplo, que os algoritmos tambm falham[1]. As projees fundadas na melhor informao e conhecimento disponveis podem gorar-se em virtude de acontecimentos de natureza disruptiva, traumticos, combinaes inesperadas decorrentes de aquisies cientficas simultneas, a emergncia de cisnes negros, na consagrada expresso de Nassim Taleb. Na verdade, temos de ter presente que, como alguns afirmam, os factos impossveis esto apenas a comear[2]. 4. Nos ltimos anos, so incontveis as obras, os relatrios de organizaes nacionais e internacionais, pblicas e privadas, de instncias de deciso poltica a diversos nveis, bem como eventos de todo o gnero sobre o futuro da atividade bancria.  natural que assim seja face  dimenso das transformaes que esto em curso. Na quarta revoluo industrial o avano tecnolgico  simultaneamente exponencial e combinatrio, isto , os avanos tecnolgicos esto a dar-se de forma integrada e transversal, no se limitando a ser aplicados em domnios especficos. Essas caractersticas levam muitos autores  a meu ver bem -a sustentar que o processo em curso de transformao da sociedade no tem paralelo, havendo mesmo quem afirme que a Humanidade vai mudar mais nos prximos vinte anos do que nos ltimos trezentos[3]. Mas por mais impactantes que sejam as transformaes tecnolgicas elas no fazem desaparecer os constrangimentos econmicos bsicos. No podemos, de facto, perder de vista esse ponto essencial: a tecnologia  um meio para aumentar a rentabilidade atravs de uma maior eficincia dos modelos de negcio e promover o desenvolvimento econmico e social. Mas para cumprir a sua misso ltima tem de fazer parte duma economia dinmica, que distribua a riqueza de modo satisfatrio, e estar protegida pelo enquadramento de um Estado de Direito que, entre outras coisas, assegure os direitos fundamentais e a fluidez das relaes contratuais. Marshall McLhuan, nos seus estudos pioneiros sobre comunicao no sculo XX, sublinhou que ns moldamos as nossas ferramentas e, por conseguinte, as nossas ferramentas moldam-nos a ns. Na verdade, a evoluo tecnolgica condiciona-nos  e muito -, sobretudo no atual contexto em que as tecnologias se tornaram mais eficientes e intrusivas do que nunca. Mas a tecnologia no tem necessariamente que determinar as nossas escolhas: h uma relao biunvoca  tecnologia e sociedade influenciam-se mutuamente. Nem tudo o que  tecnologicamente vivel  desejvel ou eticamente aceitvel. E, por vezes, pode no ser legal. Cabe a cada um de ns, nas respetivas profisses, e tambm enquanto cidados, garantir que isso no acontece. O futuro somos ns que o construmos. 5. A dimenso transversal do processo de transformao digital permite-nos dizer que estamos perante uma mudana profunda do modo de organizao e funcionamento das sociedades e no apenas perante uma mera alterao do paradigma econmicofinanceiro. Tambm por isso a discusso sobre o futuro do setor bancrio  muito importante.  que o setor financeiro -e o setor bancrio em especial -desempenham h muito um papel crucial nas sociedades modernas. O setor bancrio deu os primeiros passos na poca do Renascimento, reforou-se no contexto das sucessivas revolues industriais, a ponto de uma das caractersticas do modelo econmico contemporneo ser a financeirizao, que significa que o setor bancrio  para o bem e para o mal  assumiu um papel central na vida social. Essa centralidade contribui tambm para que o setor bancrio e o setor financeiro em geral estejam em mutao acelerada. Exemplo dessa mutao  a emergncia das Fintechs. Trata-se de um fenmeno do maior relevo. Vem enriquecer o tecido econmico, diversificar a oferta de produtos e servios financeiros, aumentar a concorrncia e, portanto, beneficiar os consumidores. Muitas ficaro pelo caminho, o que em nada belisca a importncia do fenmeno em si, pois  algo natural num processo que  ainda de afirmao. H quem entenda que as Fintechs so uma ameaa mortal para o setor bancrio. Decididamente, o setor bancrio no continuar igual ao que ; mas o vaticnio do seu desaparecimento a prazo parece-me no s largamente exagerado, parafraseando Mark Twain, mas, mais do que isso, infundado e simplista na medida em que subestima a capacidade de adaptao do setor, a sua experincia acumulada, o carter infungvel de uma parte das suas funes e a massa crtica que  capaz de mobilizar. Verificamos, alis, noutro plano, que nem a televiso matou a rdio ou o cinema, nem a Internet matou a televiso. Porm, todos mudaram profundamente. E  isso que penso que ir acontecer no setor bancrio. Para fazerem face de forma bem-sucedida  mutao em curso, as instituies financeiras tero de assumir e assimilar plenamente a evoluo tecnolgica e a centralidade da relao com os clientes, bem como a importncia das parcerias estratgicas com os novos atores do setor financeiro Nenhuma destas ideias , em si mesma, uma novidade. Pelo contrrio, esto h muito no ADN da boa gesto bancria. Mas os termos em que a respetiva execuo se coloca hoje so muito diferentes do que eram no passado. O pior erro seria ficar em estado de negao quanto  profundidade do processo de mudana. Desvalorizar a evoluo tecnolgica em curso, enfatizando a perspetiva de que se trata apenas de mais uma das sucessivas vagas de inovao com as quais o setor sempre se deu bem, no ajuda a criar um ambiente propcio  mudana. A importncia da solidez das decises de gesto  hoje ainda mais crtica. Com efeito, num setor ainda a recuperar da crise e onde o capital no abunda,  fundamental que os elevados investimentos necessrios  transformao digital atinjam plenamente os objetivos visados e sejam eficientes. Perante a avalanche da mudana, devemos ter a audcia da humildade: a hipercomplexidade dos assuntos desaconselha atitudes de autossuficincia. Como refere um autor, o maior perigo da inteligncia artificial , de longe, as pessoas conclurem demasiado cedo que a compreendem[4]. 6. A criao de uma cultura orientada para o cumprimento e pautada por valores afigurase-me essencial para o futuro da banca no contexto da sua transformao digital. Na base da atividade bancria sempre esteve a confiana. O dano mais duradouro para o setor sempre se deu quando se verificaram quebras de confiana. Na era digital isso  ainda mais verdadeiro, pois a realidade  muito mais imaterial e os clientes esto, por um lado, numa posio de maior vulnerabilidade potencial, mas, por outro, tm uma muito maior amplitude de escolha e capacidade de reao. Por isso mesmo, os efeitos de qualquer quebra de confiana so amplificados pela prpria natureza das relaes digitais. Temos visto como assim , em mltiplos setores da atividade econmica, incluindo as grandes empresas tecnolgicas. Ora, num mundo em que a tecnologia est acessvel, disseminada e desenvolvida como nunca, e em que a sua utilizao  permanente e generalizada, resulta reforada a importncia dos valores e da cultura da organizao como fator da sua afirmao e diferenciao no mercado. Por isso, uma cultura de cumprimento do direito, em geral, e das normas regulatrias, em especial,  um fator essencial para gerar a confiana indispensvel ao desenvolvimento do negcio. Mas no chega.  preciso que a promoo das boas prticas seja uma realidade interiorizada por todos os nveis de gesto e pelos colaboradores e que o sistema de incentivos seja coerente com esse objetivo. No se trata apenas de uma questo de conformidade regulatria: trata-se da edificao de uma cultura institucional, que  algo muito mais vasto e profundo, porque imaterial. 7. Partilho a preocupao daqueles que, sobretudo em determinadas reas, assinalam excessos regulatrios. Todos temos conscincia de que os custos da regulao so hoje elevados. Mas os custos da sua insuficincia ou ausncia, como a crise financeira global bem demonstrou, so muito maiores e mais duradouros. Por seu turno, a velocidade da evoluo tecnolgica e dos mercados aconselha a um permanente controlo da qualidade da legislao e do quadro regulatrio em geral, de modo a evitar que se torne um obstculo  inovao. E  fundamental, em defesa do prprio sistema financeiro, que seja plenamente garantida, atravs das entidades de superviso e, em ltima anlise, dos tribunais, a plena efetividade do quadro normativo aplicvel. 8. A utilizao de megadados (big data) para os mais diversos fins constitui um pilar essencial da quarta revoluo industrial. Transformar esses dados em informao e a informao assim obtida em conhecimento  algo que traz vantagens fantsticas mas tambm riscos enormes. Assim, a garantia da proteo dos dados pessoais  hoje uma condio indispensvel para a criao de confiana em qualquer organizao, incluindo naturalmente nas instituies bancrias, aspeto que sublinho, muito embora se trate de matria fora do mbito de ao do Banco de Portugal, pois, como sabemos,  matria que est cometida, em primeira linha, s prprias instituies e, no plano das autoridades de superviso,  Comisso Nacional de Proteo de Dados. Em suma,  minha convico que a desvalorizao do Direito e do comportamento tico foram fatores nucleares da crise financeira. Esse caminho, porm, est a ser invertido. Mas  preciso extrair no plano da gesto bancria todas as ilaes a esse respeito. S assim se criar uma cultura institucional ancorada em valores slidos, que ser decisiva para ultrapassar com sucesso a transformao digital e garantir o futuro do setor. 9.  hoje um lugar-comum da gesto assinalar o reconhecimento da importncia das pessoas, ainda que nem sempre haja coerncia com esse propsito. Contudo, num mundo de utilizao homogeneizada da tecnologia, o capital humano tender a ser o fator que faz a diferena. A criatividade humana no  descartvel. Pode at dizer-se que na era dos algoritmos ela  ainda mais decisiva[5]. A utilizao da tecnologia digital deve ser eticamente enquadrada, pois as pessoas e as sociedades precisam de tica sob pena de colapso a prazo mais ou menos longo. A tica digital est assim a tornar-se um importante campo de estudo e tender a s-lo cada vez mais. H mesmo quem sugira a criao de um Conselho de tica Digital Global, incumbido de definir as regras fundamentais e os valores mais bsicos e universais de uma sociedade cada vez mais digital[6]. Um novo campo se abre para a regulao e / ou para a auto regulao, tendo em vista garantir que a transformao digital nos proporciona o ganho lquido individual e social que est ao seu alcance. Em concluso, no plano da evoluo tecnolgica e das exigncias comportamentais os desafios que este mundo novo, que se desvenda diante de ns, coloca ao setor bancrio so aliciantes e difceis. Debat-los publicamente  tambm um exerccio de cidadania e nessa medida este evento no podia ter sido mais oportuno. Muito obrigado pela vossa ateno. [1] Cf. Gerd Leonhard, ob. cit., p. 206.

Title: Concluding remarks by Director Luis Laginha de Sousa at the Banco de Portugal's 2019 Conference on Financial Stability
text: Concluding remarks by Director Luis... Concluding remarks by Director Luis Laginha de Sousa at the Banco de Portugal's 2019 Conference on Financial Stability 08 Oct. 2019 As we reach the end of this Conference, I would like to spend the next few minutes highlighting some takeaways that can be drawn from the fantastic group of speakers weve had today. I will also try to share a personal perspective in relation to each of the main takeaways not just about macroprudential and financial stability but also about other topics that either are related or have an impact on them. Let me start by thanking the speakers for sharing their ideas with us and the effective contributions of their work. The presentations we witnessed allowed us to promote very interesting and stimulating discussions. This thank-you note, is also extended to all the other participants in this conference. They contributed to make it a success, by bringing out very important issues for financial stability and macroprudential policy. The four takeaways Ive selected are far from comprehensive, and they should be seen as an appetiser, since the main course is the reflection that should be made based on what weve learned and on what we would like to prioritise going forward. The first takeaway is related to macroprudential policy impacts and the economys cyclical position. If we were to rebrand macroprudencial policy with a different name, one of the alternatives to consider would probably be on the job training. The reason to perform such a rebrand, is not because we are tired of listening to an expression that has been used too many times already. It is rather because, over recent years, macroprudential policy has been gradually implemented and consolidated across different jurisdictions and in spite of the still short period that has passed since the global financial crisis, the economic environment and the financial system have changed substantially in many European countries, albeit at differing paces. Ive used the expression short period but Im aware that it probably seemed like an eternity for those who were most severely hit by the crisis. During this short period, substantial regulation and supervision reforms have been introduced across the financial sector, most notably the establishment of the Banking Union, the implementation of recovery and resolution schemes for credit institutions and the review of the regulatory framework governing the banking system, including the quantitative and qualitative strengthening of capital requirements under the Basel III Accord. I should have probably said the establishment of two-thirds of the Banking Union since one-third, which is a very important third is still and very painfully missing and this is also part of the on the job training, which consists of assuming we have three pillars, while in reality there are only two, but economists are masters in the art of assumptions, as we were told in the famous story of the can opener. Macroprudential policy has been implemented within this unique context, establishing itself as an autonomous economic policy area interacting with other policy domains. Along the way, macroprudential authorities in the EU have been increasingly active in safeguarding financial stability but also facing many challenges, against the background of recovering economic activity and also significant restructuring in the banking sector. In parallel, signs of a reversal in the financial cycle have erupted, together with the momentum in the real estate market. The question that still remains though, taking into consideration that macroprudential policy interacts with other policy areas, is how to quantify the ultimate effects of macroprudential policy; not only the impacts on financial and credit markets, but also on economic activity. Better understanding the transmission channels of macroprudential instruments is also of utmost importance, both to assess their impact on the financial cycle and on the real economy, as well as to evaluate the benefits and costs of adopting macroprudential measures. Conceptually, a desired macroprudential policy is one which maximises the benefits, while minimising the costs to society, hopefully with a net positive result in the end. The evidence shows that in the long-run, countries which make use of macroprudential tools, other things being equal, do experience stronger GDP growth and have a more reduced probability of a crisis, which leads to less volatile output growth. But in the short term, macroprudential policies might negatively impact output growth, namely by affecting credit supply, investment and even private consumption. All these different and sometimes contradictory effects are influenced both by the openness of each economy and by its financial development, which in turn shape the capacity of targeted agents to evade and circumvent macroprudential policies, and can also lead to leakages to occurring, through the activity of non-targeted agents, either in the domestic domain or at cross-border level. The second takeaway is about the association of macroprudential policy to the residential real estate market. Im not bringing this takeaway because of the number of times we are asked, and not just by the media, whether or not we have a bubble in the Portuguese RRE market? Im bringing it because one of the main risks to financial stability that has led to the adoption of macroprudential measures by many countries is related to developments in the RRE sector. Macroprudential authorities have been paying particular attention to the dynamics of the RRE sector: the acceleration in house prices, especially over the past few years, often combined with rapid growth in loans to households and also with an increase in households indebtedness, are very important risk factors. To address these risks, many authorities have chosen to combine a number of different instruments, such as limits on the LTV ratio with limits on DSTI/DTI ratios, at times also coupled with limits on maturity or even amortisation requirements. When we look at the international landscape to assess how different authorities have handled the practical implementation of measures, we can observe a very heterogeneous approach, be it in terms of the legal form adopted, or the policy design, or the type of exemptions considered, or even the type of phasing-in arrangements. But apart from the mentioned heterogeneity, there is one totally common understanding that is shared by those same authorities. The common understanding is that the combination of different types of borrower-based measures reinforces their effectiveness and also their respective ability to achieve policy goals while doing so, at a minimum cost. I cannot avoid this opportunity to highlight once more the borrower-based macroprudential recommendation adopted by Banco de Portugal on new mortgage and consumer loans, which also combines different instruments (LTV, DSTI and maturity limits) and we were particularly satisfied to see that due to this recommendation, the ESRB in its 23 September report, included Portugal in a minority Group, which, in this case, is also a Very Good Minority Group. The ESRB concluded that in spite of the level of risk associated to the RRE market in Portugal, the macroprudential measure implemented was considered to be fully adequate and sufficient, to mitigate that risk. An additional side note on this to stress that this assessment is not just something that Banco de Portugal, as the macroprudential authority feels proud of; this is also a relevant benefit for citizens, for companies, and for the Government, if we take into consideration potential impacts on financing costs resulting from a higher risk profile. The third takeaway has to do with issues in policies meant to address risks stemming from non-financial corporations. Some EU Member States faced a significant increase of non-performing loans associated to non-financial corporations, either as a direct result of the crisis, or as a combination of the crisis with high levels of debt that were built up before the crisis. The academic literature has devoted substantial attention to the assessment of debt sustainability of non-financial corporations and its macroeconomic and financial implications. One of the most relevant research topics in this field is the assessment of debt sustainability of non-financial corporations against the background of different economic and financial scenarios. In order to perform the research which is necessary for this assessment, having data at the loan level, also known as microdata, is of paramount importance. But in spite of the importance Ive just mentioned, the use of macroprudential instruments targeted at the non-financial corporations sector is not as widespread as in the case of households. Academic contributions are still scarce and the challenges are more significant than in the households sector given the intrinsic characteristics of firms. As a consequence, this is clearly one area where further research is needed, in order to develop analytical frameworks, both for ex-ante calibration of instruments as well as for ex-post assessment of policies impacts. But here, and even if microdata is critical to ensure macroprudential measures as robust as possible, I believe the situation seems so obvious that we cannot become trapped by the so-called analysis paralysis! I would dare to say that it is crucial to move from a fundamentally debt-based economy to a more capital-or more equity-based economy, particularly when we refer to the corporate world. This is clearly a topic where the problem is known, is understood, is recognised, but then, when it comes to removing disincentives and if possible introducing incentives, things either move very slowly or do not move at all, not to mention that moving backwards is sometimes how it looks. Nevertheless, I dont believe that it would be adequate to put all the pressure on policies as they are not a perfect substitute for one key element, which is the willingness of economic agents, but again, as we all know, economic agents react and adapt to the incentives, and therefore policies should be able to provide the right incentives. And to finalise my comments on this third takeaway, a quick remark on the CMU is also justified. Without discarding the need for a Capital Markets Union, the way it will be achieved is not irrelevant to determining whether it will be capable of fulfilling its promises. I believe it is important to stress that the very simple rule of first things first should apply and that rule is the equivalent of saying that before having a Capital Markets Union we need to have capital markets, in ways that allow their benefits to spread across and within different geographies instead of just promoting concentration at the centre. History has shown us that in the past, even without a union of capital markets weve had periods in which capital markets, with the right incentives, played a more relevant role in financing the economy in a more balanced way, and as such, theres no need to reinvent the wheel here. The fourth and last takeaway I would like to mention has to do with the challenges ahead for macro-prudential policymakers. I will briefly highlight four main challenges that are ahead of us. One challenge results from on one hand, the multiplicity of macroprudential policy goals and on the other hand, the relative similarity of policy instruments. This situation creates the risk of an overload of policy measures if different sources of risk are to become targeted separately. In order to address this risk, we need a comprehensive approach to policymaking. The development of a concept of a stance of macroprudential policy to guide policy decisions would also be very helpful. The work that the ESRB has been undertaking in this field, part of which has been recently published, is very welcome. Another challenge results from the heterogeneity of macroprudential policy at international level. This may be a consequence of the specific characteristics of each Member State, or of its position in the financial cycle or even of different preferences of national macroprudential authorities. A third challenge is the result of our still very modest experience in the use of macroprudential instruments and consequently, the high uncertainty that surrounds their expected effects. So far, the considerations on the interaction between different macroprudential instruments are mostly based on a conceptual framework of how macroprudential policy is expected to operate. The fourth and final challenge I would like to mention addresses the optimal choice of macroprudential instruments and the fact that such a choice seems to be related to the phase of the financial cycle and to its relationship with real estate market developments, which often have been at the core of past financial crises. In an ideal world, the comparison with the appropriate counterfactual would be the best methodological approach to take, but unfortunately, that is not always available. We also know that further assessing the macroprudential policys ability to mitigate systemic risk will only be possible when a full financial cycle has been completed. But even if we do not live in the ideal world and we do not have a full completion of an entire financial cycle, there are important takeaways when it comes to the optimal choice of macroprudential instruments: Be it the answers we do know already with a reasonable degree of certainty, be it the questions we know we need to raise before taking action. Starting with the things we do already know with a reasonable degree of certainty, an important one is that in periods where the financial cycle enters an expansionary phase, it seems more appropriate to adopt measures that impact on credit flows, such as borrower-based measures, and at subsequent stages when there are signs that the financial cycle is in a more mature expansionary phase, activating cyclical capital-based measures may be the most appropriate policy response. For the questions we know we need to raise before taking action, the list is already quite comprehensive. A few examples of such questions could be: Should the instrument be designed as a rule or should the macroprudential authority act in a discretionary manner? Should the macroprudential authority start by adopting a binding measure or opt instead for a non-binding one and monitor the degree of compliance and effectiveness? What is the best alternative to mitigate the risk of inaction bias? All this of course allows us to say that the current environment clearly tests the capacity of macroprudential policymakers to mitigate systemic risks and also tests the capacity of research to correctly identify them and assess the impact of policy measures. We are still far from the point where the known knowns are predominant in comparison to the known unknowns not to mention the unknown unknowns which stubbornly tend to reveal themselves in a totally impolite and unexpected way. As such, it is of utmost importance to continue this discussion with all macroprudential stakeholders and promote further research on policy issues in this field. After everything Ive just said, there is however a missing component, which If I didnt mention it could be perceived as missing the elephant in the room, but Ive deliberately skipped it, because it is such a relevant topic that trying to address it at this point would be merely superficial and detrimental to the centre stage it deserves. Im talking of course about the financial stability threat deriving from climate change and energy transition, and also the challenge that it poses to macroprudential authorities. I just would like to add that we are dedicating serious attention to this topic and when we feel the time is right, more news on the topic will be made available. Let me finish as I started, by thanking all our speakers and participants again. A big thank you also to the entire team involved in the organisation of this Conference. Organising a Conference such as this one is a truly joint effort involving many Departments and since it is impossible to name all those who gave their support, I would like to convey a strong word of appreciation to Anabela Marques, from the Financial Stability Department and through her, to all those that made this Conference possible. For all those who have attended this Conference, I look forward to seeing you all next time. And for those who are travelling back home, I wish you all a safe journey. Good bye and thank you. Title: Opening speech by the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the 29th Lisbon Meeting between the Central Banks of portuguese-speaking countries
text: Intervention of opening of the Government... Opening speech by the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the 29th Lisbon Meeting between the Central Banks of portuguese-speaking countries 11 out. 2019 Mr Secretary of State for the Budget, Ambassadors, Governors, dear guests I thank you all for coming. It is with great pleasure that I begin the work of the 29th Lisbon Meeting, an event that brings together the Central Banks of portuguese-speaking countries annually. The longevity of the Lisbon Meeting is a reflection of the significant expression and importance that cooperation assumes in the life of Banco de Portugal, following the evolution of the Community of Portuguese-speaking central banks, as well as developments in the agendas of central banks worldwide. Benefiting from a historical legacy that drives cooperation, Banco de Portugal has a broad vision that in each concrete period has allowed to interpret and respond to the demands of cooperation, by incorporating and deepening new actors and institutions, sometimes of new themes and methodologies. The cooperation was cementing the institutional ties between the central banks of portuguese-speaking countries: with the younger ones, it evolved as they were created and consolidated and now responds to demanding and dynamic bodies, facing specific and complex global and regional circumstances. It was able to put into dialogue actors in the G20 and responsible for institutions integrated into microstates. It has remained perennial in sometimes volatile circumstances and has been able to adapt to the political, social, economic and financial constraints of recent decades. It found renewed opportunities with the participation of Banco de Portugal in the European System of Central Banks and the Eurosystem, as well as in the important dialogue with partners in the European geographical neighbourhood, in the context of the candidate countries and potential candidates. It also found reinforced aspects in the special relationship with Brazil and Latin America, as well as in the ancestral relationship with Asia. Europe has not corseted cooperation, but has paved the way for more. The presence of Banco de Portugal in the context of European and international bodies, both in decision-making bodies and in technical structures, refers to standards of demand on the border of contemporary central banking, which, of course, has an enriching and catalytic effect on cooperation. The themes at the heart of the global debate have expression in the central banks and, of course, repercussions on the cooperation developed by banco de Portugal. I refer to the focus on the issues raised by the financial crisis, the sovereign debt crisis, the digital revolution, financial inclusion or sustainable financing, in addition to traditional areas. In all these, but also in the support, management and infrastructure functions of central banks, cooperation has grown quantitatively and qualitatively. The financial crisis has made cooperation between central banks an even more fundamental and pressing issue by demonstrating, among other things, the relevance and urgency of a reflection on the factors on which global monetary and financial stability is based. Cooperation has gained scale and the crisis has strengthened the catalyst role and stressed the good virtue of joint solutions. I am pleased that Banco de Portugal has always recognised the strategic importance of cooperation, consistently reinforcing it over almost three decades in terms of intensity, variety and scope. Responding to the challenge launched at the Governors Meeting that Macau hosted last May, the central theme chosen for today's Meeting was on the Implications of Technological Innovation in Financial Activity. Central banks' concern about technological innovation is real. In the first place, the various challenges and associated opportunities, in particular in terms of payment systems, financial stability and supervision, also due to the intervention of unsupervised operators, without forgetting the scale of the fight against money laundering and the protection of the financial services customer. It was also suggested at the time the organisation of a network for monitoring and joint discussion of topics in the sphere of financial innovation. At this Lisbon Meeting, we will hear the conclusions of the groups formed in this area - in which representatives of all the Central Banks of the Portuguese-speaking Countries worked - and to which I express my thanks. The round table, which will follow, will be an opportunity for us to discuss these ideas. The Lisbon Meeting - which thus returns to the city that gave its name after the extraordinary experience that was its realization in Dili in 2018 - is, as always, an opportunity to discuss the topics of the annual meetings of the IMF and the World Bank. In a framework marked by economic cooling, trade and geopolitical tensions, uncertainty and loss of confidence, we are transported to another crucial dimension of cooperation. Cooperation to find coherent economic policy solutions (monetary and financial, fiscal and structural) and an appropriate institutional framework, focused on supporting the world economy and national economies, also protecting them from key risks. It is therefore not a simple option, it is the responsibility of decision-makers, particularly central banks. It is also essential to contribute within the organizations to this plan and Banco de Portugal is on the side of the search for multilateral responses: it does so in the context of its action with the Fund; within the framework of its European and international representations; interaction with cooperation partners; relationship with other national authorities. It also makes you aware that the quality and credibility of the policies themselves are the first and irreplaceable line of defence and that this is a crucial purpose of cooperation. In the afternoon, in a restricted working session, we will therefore discuss in particular the main themes of the annual meetings of the IMF and the World Bank, which will be dominated by the global economic and financial perspectives, and the state of affairs regarding the policy agenda, facilities and resources of the Fund. Banco de Portugal monitors, within its tasks, discussions, in particular at the European level, in order to find a solution that preserves the Fund at the heart of the global financial network and with adequate resources. At the same time, it monitors the work and initiatives aimed at enhancing the quality of policies and surveillance, benefiting in much of the experience of its recent relationship and the knowledge capital provided by its action, both in the regular and in the program context. Experience and knowledge that has been invited to share in multiple initiatives. In this afternoon session, we will also discuss the cooperation activity between our central banks, discussing their main developments and future challenges. On this last point, I would like to publicly note the satisfaction of seeing the consolidation of Banco de Portugal's cooperation, for which decisive steps have also contributed in the last 10 years. Banco de Portugal participates annually in more than 130 cooperation actions  2019 will be a particularly intense year, with close to 160 actions involving about 300 of its employees and more than 400 employees of other central banks, of which about half are our guests in Portugal. Although cooperation with Portuguese-speaking countries is the most significant part, contacts with partners from the rest of the world have been expanding and strengthening, reaching about 40, spread across the various continents. This evolution does not diminish the strategic importance of the Lusophone framework, but rather adds perspective and depth to it. In addition to the mere reality of these figures, there are still, in the last 10 years, some aspects that I would like to highlight: a cooperation that consolidates the universe of partners; whereas it is modern in the way it covers institutions and individuals; which is shared with other actors; which communicates and calls on society more generally. To illustrate, I will refer to some of the results. First, the consolidation of the universe of partners, right from the lusophony level. I would like to point out, in particular, the presence of the Central Bank of Brazil in the cooperation between the Central Banks of portuguese-speaking countries, which, undeniably, has been translated into enormous added value. We have won a lot, both in terms of bilateral initiatives and in terms of synergies and the dynamics of multilateral events. But, as I have already said, consolidation has also taken place at the level of other geographies, right from the outset in the enlargement of the European Union, but also in Latin America and Asia. Banco de Portugal has signed 12 technical cooperation agreements. I myself signed six  with the central banks of the West African States in 2010, Timor-Leste in 2013, Brazil in 2014, Morocco in 2017 and Chile, still a few days in Santiago, and with the Monetary and Foreign Exchange Authority of Macau in 2018. These agreements prove the dynamics and interest in cooperation with Banco de Portugal. The second aspect I would like to highlight is the increasing appreciation of communication and public dissemination of information and cooperation initiatives. Framed in the more general purpose of communication to the public, contribution to a more informed society and accountability, Banco de Portugal has long developed regular publications in relevant areas of cooperation. The cooperation publications cover information and analysis on emerging and developing economies and on banco de Portugal's cooperation activity. The strategic effort to improve the quality of content and effectiveness in interacting with different audiences has also been extended to cooperation publications, which have been reshuffled this year: last April a renewed edition of the Annual Report on Cooperation Activity was published; today we published on our website and on the Portal of the Central Banks of Portuguese-speaking Countries, in fact one of our shared products, the most recent edition of the Evolution of the Economies of PALOP and Timor-Leste. A third example worthy of prominence in this journey of a decade  still taking the first steps, but undoubtedly promising  is the opening to the Central Banks of the Portuguese-speaking Countries of the Banco de Portugal Academy. The possibility of accessing the technological platform for the Bank's employees and training in areas of leadership, communication and softskills in general is a contribution to strengthening the management skills of organizations. I am sure that the deepening of this project  started this year  will bring relevant results in the future. The opening to the Banco de Portugal Academy is an illustration of the sense of modernity of our cooperation, in this case by valuing the dimensions of the individual's training, in addition to institutional training, and by the topics addressed. With this focus on training, the Bank has developed intense work with other bodies, which would highlight the Institute for Capacity Development of the International Monetary Fund, collaborating in the realization of courses in Portuguese language aimed at employees of the ministries of finance and economy, statistical institutes and central banks of Lusophony, the true technical backbone of these countries in the economic and financial sphere. This is a sign of confidence in the Bank's cooperation. Collaboration with other entities is, moreover, one of the features of the Bank's cooperation and which finds very diverse materializations. On a different level, of course, I cannot fail to mention here the participation in the structures of the Exchange Agreement between Portugal and Cape Verde and in the Economic Agreement between Portugal and Sao Tome and Principe, which have just served twenty years and ten years, respectively. Examples of Banco de Portugal's willingness to involve its resources in the context of cooperation, in this case, framed by other national authorities and the two partner countries. In the more general perspective, the Bank also has a cooperation involvement within civil society, ranging from the willingness to participate in numerous initiatives to the financing of scholarships for Lusophone students committed to returning to their countries. On several occasions I have already referred to the echo obtained outside the Lusophone context by the adoption of the guiding principles and recommendations of cooperation between the Central Banks of portuguese-speaking countries. Our organisational model is a reference for best practices in the European System of Central Banks. We are also still motivated to work within the European framework to bring the words that Africa now raises into deeds. Cooperation strengthens and prestigious our central banks. For our part, the effort to remain in the state of the art of cooperation is permanent and developed in coherence and in a transversal way, not forgetting it in the bodies we integrate and in the dialogues we lead. Banco de Portugal can offer this global perspective because it has the most comprehensive and complex mandate in the universe of central banks, including monetary policy, financial stability, resolution, prudential and behavioral supervision. Monetary and financial stability is a public good. The benefits and contributions of cooperation to this global cause should not be underestimated. Therefore, I would strengthen the strategic direction that was established at last year's Meeting in Dili to anchor cooperation on international agendas, with particular focus on the points of the IMF's Global Policy Agenda, on extending cooperation on a global scale and increasing resilience and sustainable and inclusive growth. We are committed, as you know, to the inclusion of these issues in joint initiatives at the highest level, giving them greater visibility and involving, whenever possible, our European and international partners. In conclusion, I could not fail to emphasize that one of the most vivid traits I keep from the years I take as governor is the professionalism and enthusiasm that cooperation between Portuguese-speaking Central Banks encourages at all levels of Banco de Portugal, from the Board of Directors to the Employees of the different departments that are committed to participate in the corresponding actions and events. It has long been known here that there are no longer strictly domestic problems and that cooperation is essential to overcome the difficulties of our common home. Thank you very much. Interveno de abertura do Governador, Carlos da Silva Costa, no XXIX Encontro de Lisboa entre os Bancos Centrais dos Pases de Lngua Portuguesa 11 out. 2019 Senhor Secretrio de Estado do Oramento, Senhores Embaixadores, Senhores Governadores, caros convidados Agradeo a todos a presena.  com grande prazer que dou incio aos trabalhos do 29. Encontro de Lisboa, evento que rene anualmente os Bancos Centrais dos Pases de Lngua Portuguesa. A longevidade do Encontro de Lisboa  reflexo da significativa expresso e importncia que a cooperao assume na vida do Banco de Portugal, acompanhando a evoluo da comunidade dos bancos centrais de lngua portuguesa, bem como os desenvolvimentos nas agendas dos bancos centrais, a nvel mundial. Beneficiando de um legado histrico que impele  cooperao, o Banco de Portugal tem uma viso larga que em cada perodo concreto tem permitido interpretar e dar resposta s exigncias da cooperao, por incorporao e aprofundamento ora de novos atores e instituies, ora de novos temas e metodologias. A cooperao foi cimentando os laos institucionais entre os bancos centrais dos pases de lngua portuguesa: com os mais jovens, evoluiu  medida que se foram criando e consolidando e, agora, responde a organismos exigentes e dinmicos, enfrentando circunstncias globais e regionais especficas e complexas. Foi capaz de pr em dilogo intervenientes no G20 e responsveis de instituies integradas em microestados. Manteve-se perene em circunstncias por vezes volteis e soube adaptar-se s condicionantes polticas, sociais, econmicas e financeiras das ltimas dcadas. Encontrou renovadas oportunidades com a participao do Banco de Portugal no Sistema Europeu de Bancos Centrais e no Eurosistema, bem como no importante dilogo com os parceiros na vizinhana geogrfica europeia, no contexto dos pases candidatos e potenciais candidatos. Encontrou ainda vertentes reforadas na relao especial com o Brasil e a Amrica Latina, assim como na relao ancestral com a sia. A Europa no espartilhou a cooperao, antes abriu mais caminho. A presena do Banco de Portugal no contexto dos organismos europeus e internacionais, quer nos rgos de deciso quer nas estruturas tcnicas, remete para padres de exigncia na fronteira da banca central contempornea, o que, naturalmente, tem um efeito enriquecedor e catalisador sobre a cooperao. Os temas no centro do debate mundial tm expresso nos bancos centrais e, naturalmente, repercusso na cooperao desenvolvida pelo Banco de Portugal. Refirome ao enfoque nas questes suscitadas pela crise financeira, a crise das dvidas soberanas, a revoluo digital, a incluso financeira ou o financiamento sustentvel, para alm das reas tradicionais. Em todas estas, mas tambm nas funes de suporte, de gesto e infraestruturais dos bancos centrais, a cooperao registou um crescendo quantitativo e qualitativo. A crise financeira tornou a cooperao entre os bancos centrais um tema ainda mais fundamental e premente ao demonstrar, entre outros aspetos, a relevncia e a urgncia de uma reflexo sobre os fatores em que assenta a estabilidade monetria e financeira global. A cooperao ganhou escala e a crise permitiu o reforo do papel catalisador e salientou a boa virtude das solues conjuntas. Congratulo-me por o Banco de Portugal sempre ter reconhecido a importncia estratgica da cooperao, reforando-a consistentemente ao longo de quase trs dcadas em termos de intensidade, variedade e abrangncia. Respondendo ao desafio lanado no Encontro de Governadores que Macau acolheu em maio passado, o tema central escolhido para o Encontro de hoje recaiu sobre as Implicaes da Inovao Tecnolgica na Atividade Financeira .  real a preocupao dos bancos centrais em matria de inovao tecnolgica. Desde logo, pelos vrios desafios e oportunidades associados, nomeadamente a nvel dos sistemas de pagamentos, da estabilidade financeira e da superviso, tambm devido  interveno de operadores no supervisionados, sem esquecer a dimenso do combate ao branqueamento de capitais e da proteo do cliente de servios financeiros. Foi igualmente sugerida, na altura, a organizao de uma rede para acompanhamento e debate conjunto de temas na esfera da inovao financeira. Neste Encontro de Lisboa, ouviremos as concluses dos grupos formados nesse mbito  em que trabalharam representantes de todos os Bancos Centrais dos Pases de Lngua Portuguesa -e aos quais transmito o meu agradecimento. A mesa redonda, que se vai seguir, constituir uma oportunidade para debatermos essas ideias. O Encontro de Lisboa -que assim regressa  cidade que lhe deu nome depois da extraordinria experincia que foi a sua realizao em Dli em 2018  constitui, como sempre, uma oportunidade para discutir os temas das reunies anuais do FMI e do Banco Mundial. Num quadro marcado por arrefecimento econmico, tenses comerciais e geopolticas, incerteza e perda de confiana, somos transportados para outra dimenso crucial da cooperao. A cooperao para encontrar solues coerentes de poltica econmica (monetria e financeira, oramental e estrutural) e um adequado enquadramento institucional, focada no apoio  economia mundial e s economias nacionais, protegendo-as tambm dos principais riscos. No se trata, pois, de uma simples opo,  uma responsabilidade dos decisores, nomeadamente dos bancos centrais.  fundamental contribuir tambm no seio das organizaes para este desgnio e o Banco de Portugal coloca-se do lado da procura de respostas multilaterais: f-lo no contexto da sua ao com o Fundo; no quadro das suas representaes europeias e internacionais; na interao com os parceiros da cooperao; no relacionamento com as demais autoridades nacionais. F-lo ciente igualmente de que a qualidade e a credibilidade das polticas prprias so a primeira e insubstituvel linha de defesa e que este  um propsito crucial da cooperao. Na parte da tarde, em sesso de trabalho restrita, discutiremos pois em concreto os principais temas das reunies anuais do FMI e do Banco Mundial, que sero dominadas pelas perspetivas econmicas e financeiras globais, e o ponto de situao quanto  agenda de poltica, s facilidades e aos recursos do Fundo. O Banco de Portugal acompanha, no quadro das suas atribuies, as discusses, nomeadamente na esfera europeia, no sentido de ser encontrada uma soluo que preserve o Fundo no centro da rede financeira global e dotado de adequados recursos. Ao mesmo tempo, acompanha os trabalhos e iniciativas destinadas a reforar a qualidade das polticas e da surveillance, beneficiando em muito da experincia do seu relacionamento recente e do capital de conhecimento proporcionado pela sua ao, quer no contexto regular quer em programa. Experincia e conhecimentos que tem sido convidado a partilhar em mltiplas iniciativas. Nessa sesso da tarde, abordaremos, tambm, a atividade de cooperao entre os nossos bancos centrais, debatendo os seus principais desenvolvimentos e desafios futuros. Sobre este ltimo ponto, gostaria de, publicamente, dar nota da satisfao em ver a consolidao da cooperao do Banco de Portugal, para o que contriburam passos decisivos tambm nestes ltimos 10 anos. O Banco de Portugal participa anualmente em mais de 130 aes de cooperao  2019 ser um ano particularmente intenso, com perto de 160 aes -envolvendo cerca de 300 dos seus colaboradores e mais de 400 colaboradores de outros bancos centrais, dos quais cerca de metade so nossos convidados em Portugal. Ainda que a cooperao com os pases de lngua portuguesa constitua a parte mais significativa, os contactos com parceiros do resto do mundo tm vindo a alargar-se e a reforar-se, chegando a cerca de 40, distribudos pelos vrios continentes. Esta evoluo em nada diminui a importncia estratgia do quadro lusfono, antes lhe acrescenta perspetiva e profundidade. Para alm da simples realidade destes nmeros, h ainda, nos ltimos 10 anos, alguns aspetos que gostaria de salientar: uma cooperao que consolida o universo dos parceiros; que  moderna na forma como abrange as instituies e os indivduos; que  partilhada com outros atores; que comunica e interpela a sociedade de forma mais geral. Para ilustrar, referir-me-ei a alguns resultados. Em primeiro lugar, a consolidao do universo de parceiros, desde logo ao nvel da Lusofonia. Destaco, em particular, a presena do Banco Central do Brasil na cooperao entre os Bancos Centrais dos Pases de Lngua Portuguesa, a qual, de forma inegvel, se tem traduzido numa enorme mais-valia. Ganhmos muito, quer a nvel das iniciativas bilaterais, quer a nvel das sinergias e dinmica dos eventos multilaterais. Mas, como j referi, a consolidao deu-se igualmente a nvel de outras geografias, desde logo no mbito do alargamento da Unio Europeia, mas tambm na Amrica Latina e na sia. O Banco de Portugal tem firmados 12 acordos de cooperao tcnica. Eu prprio assinei seis  com os bancos centrais dos Estados da frica Ocidental, em 2010, de Timor-Leste em 2013, do Brasil, em 2014, Marrocos, em 2017, e Chile, ainda h escassos dias em Santiago, e com a Autoridade Monetria e Cambial de Macau, em 2018. Estes acordos comprovam a dinmica e o interesse na cooperao com o Banco de Portugal. O segundo aspeto que gostaria de destacar  a valorizao crescente da comunicao e divulgao pblica da informao e das iniciativas da cooperao. Enquadrado no propsito mais geral de comunicao ao pblico, de contribuio para uma sociedade mais informada e de prestao de contas, o Banco de Portugal h muito que desenvolve publicaes regulares em domnios relevantes da cooperao. As publicaes da cooperao abrangem informao e anlise sobre as economias emergentes e em desenvolvimento e sobre a atividade de cooperao do Banco de Portugal. O esforo estratgico no sentido da melhoria da qualidade de contedos e da eficcia na interao com os diferentes pblicos foi alargado tambm s publicaes de cooperao, as quais foram alvo de remodelao no corrente ano: em abril passado foi publicada uma edio renovada do Relatrio Anual da Atividade de Cooperao; hoje mesmo divulgmos no nosso site e no Portal dos Bancos Centrais de Pases de Lngua Portuguesa, alis um dos nossos produtos partilhados, a edio mais recente da Evoluo das Economias dos PALOP e de Timor-Leste. Um terceiro exemplo merecedor de destaque neste percurso de uma dcada  ainda a dar os primeiros passos, mas sem dvida promissor   a abertura aos Bancos Centrais dos Pases de Lngua Portuguesa da Academia do Banco de Portugal. A possibilidade de aceder  plataforma tecnolgica destinada aos colaboradores do Banco e  formao em reas de liderana, comunicao e de softskills em geral  um contributo para o reforo das competncias de gesto das organizaes. Estou certo de que o aprofundamento deste projeto  iniciado no corrente ano  trar resultados relevantes no futuro. A abertura  Academia do Banco de Portugal  uma ilustrao do sentido de modernidade da nossa cooperao, neste caso pela valorizao das dimenses da capacitao do indivduo, em complemento  capacitao institucional, e pelos temas abordados. Com este enfoque na formao, o Banco tem desenvolvido intenso trabalho com outros organismos, de que destacaria o Instituto de Desenvolvimento de Capacidades do Fundo Monetrio Internacional, colaborando na realizao de cursos em lngua portuguesa destinados a colaboradores dos ministrios das finanas e economia, dos institutos de estatstica e dos bancos centrais da lusofonia, a verdadeira espinha dorsal tcnica destes pases na esfera econmica e financeira. Trata-se de um sinal de confiana da cooperao do Banco. A colaborao com outras entidades , alis, um dos traos da cooperao do Banco e que encontra materializaes muito diversas. Num plano distinto,  certo, no posso deixar de citar aqui a participao nas estruturas do Acordo Cambial entre Portugal e Cabo Verde e no Acordo Econmico entre Portugal e So Tom e Prncipe, que acabam de cumprir vinte anos e dez anos, respetivamente. So exemplos da disponibilidade do Banco de Portugal para envolver os seus recursos no contexto da cooperao, neste caso, enquadrada por outras autoridades tanto nacionais como dos dois pases parceiros. Na perspetiva mais geral, o Banco tem tambm envolvimento de cooperao no quadro da sociedade civil, indo desde a disponibilidade para participar em inmeras iniciativas, at ao financiamento de bolsas de estudo destinadas a estudantes lusfonos comprometidos em regressar aos seus pases. Em diversas ocasies j me referi ao eco obtido fora do contexto Lusfono pela adoo dos princpios e recomendaes orientadores da cooperao entre os Bancos Centrais dos Pases de Lngua Portuguesa. O nosso modelo organizativo  uma referncia para as melhores prticas a nvel do Sistema Europeu de Bancos Centrais. Continuamos tambm motivados a trabalhar no quadro europeu para vir a materializar em atos as palavras que frica agora suscita. A cooperao fortalece e prestigia os nossos bancos centrais. Pelo nosso lado, o esforo de nos mantermos no estado da arte da cooperao  permanente e desenvolvido em coerncia e de forma transversal, no a esquecendo nos organismos que integramos e nos dilogos que protagonizamos. O Banco de Portugal pode oferecer esta perspetiva global pois tem um mandato dos mais abrangentes e complexos no universo dos bancos centrais, ao incluir a poltica monetria, a estabilidade financeira, a resoluo, a superviso prudencial e comportamental. A estabilidade monetria e financeira  um bem pblico. Os benefcios e contributos da cooperao para essa causa global no devem ser subestimados. Por isso, reforo a orientao estratgica que foi estabelecida no Encontro do ano passado, que teve lugar em Dli, de ancorar a cooperao nas agendas internacionais, com particular enfoque nos pontos da Global Policy Agenda do FMI, respeitantes ao alargamento da cooperao  escala global e ao aumento da resilincia e do crescimento sustentvel e inclusivo. Comprometemo-nos ento, como sabem, com a incluso destes temas nas iniciativas conjuntas, ao mais alto nvel, dando-lhes maior visibilidade e envolvendo, sempre que possvel, os nossos parceiros europeus e internacionais. Ao concluir, no poderia deixar de sublinhar que um dos traos mais vivos que guardo dos anos que levo de governador  o profissionalismo e o entusiasmo que a cooperao entre Bancos Centrais de Lngua Portuguesa concita a todos os nveis do Banco de Portugal, desde o Conselho de Administrao aos Colaboradores dos diferentes departamentos que empenhadamente participam nas correspondentes aes e eventos. H muito que por aqui se sabe que j no h problemas estritamente domsticos e que a cooperao  essencial para ultrapassar as dificuldades da nossa casa comum. Muito obrigado. Title: Interview of the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, to the Business Journal
text: Interview of the Governor, Carlos da... Interview of the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, to the Business Journal 15 out. 2019 What are the growth expectations for the Portuguese economy? A growth of 2% for this year and a slight slowdown next year, with risks resulting from the external environment. The prospect of growth is very much dependent on the European Union, the trade war between the US and China and the customs measures already announced by the US, the impact of any brexit exit. It is also dependent on geopolitical factors and, finally, economic policy, in particular the budgetary policy of European countries that have room for manoeuvre. What is the impact for Portugal of Germany's possible technical recession? Germany is of great importance because it is the most important economy in the European Union. And, in our case, he is a great customer of Portuguese companies. It is also important because it is a country that has budgetary room for manoeuvre to trigger measures to offset the impact of reducing international demand by launching public spending programmes, including investment. The President of the ECB called for the use of budgetary policy. Is monetary policy exhausted? No. Monetary policy did what it had to do. First, it provided the stability conditions that were necessary for the European financial system and the liquidity of which the banking system needed. Second, it provided liquidity to the economy and thereby avoided deflation. And thirdly, it has given liquidity and low cost to the economies of the Eurozone. When we, the Board of Governors and Mario Draghi, call for fiscal policy to complement monetary policy, we are saying that accommodative monetary policy is necessary, but it is no longer enough. What kind of budgetary policy can Portugal have? Our fiscal policy is heavily dependent on levels of public indebtedness. We must not only comply with the budgetary rules of the European Union, but above all remain credible from the market point of view, which means that there may be some capacity to accommodate the impacts of an economic crisis through the functioning of [automatic] stabilisers, but we have no room for such an active fiscal policy as, for example, Germany. In a crisis, can Portugal let the automatic stabilisers operate and record a budget deficit? It has scope to do so, but it must be credible as to the future path of debt in terms of GDP ratio. If this margin is used in a way that undermines sustainability  i.e. not a temporary but permanent use  if there is no equivalent GDP growth, an understandable concern of the markets is generated. What image would you attribute to the economy right now? It is an economy that has been able to stabilize the four engines that determine its trajectory. I once used the image of an airplane with four engines. One engine is consumption, another is private investment, another is public expenditure and another is exports. There was a time when the balance of these four engines was not ensured and, therefore, we had an external imbalance, budgetary and an increase in indebtedness. Today what is pulling the economy, or pulled the economy, are exports. However, we must be very attentive to the evolution of these four engines. For this balance, has there been an excessive commitment to investment? We did what we had to do to restore a trajectory that inspires confidence in the markets and ensures sustainability. From now on we have to demonstrate that the trajectory is sustainable. Fiscal policy must continue to respond to two types of pressures: one resulting from growth needs and the supply of public goods and investment; and another of the need to ensure that the response does not trigger a growth in spending that generates new deficits and debt perceived as unsustainable. Hasn't it been demonstrated yet? The markets have a very positive perception and the proof of this is the evolution that has occurred in the "yields" of public debt. The prices we finance are a demonstration of credibility. Simply the credibility and perception of markets must be systematically confirmed by the continuation of the policy. When you are at a high level of indebtedness, you always have to be very careful not to frustrate the expectations of the markets. What is the weight it attaches to monetary policy in Portugal's recovery? Why did we get it back? Because there was, first, a [positive] external environment, according to a favourable monetary policy, and a third an adequate internal economic policy. The first two factors did not guarantee the result. They were favorable conditions, but they would only produce results if internal policies were adequate to take advantage of these circumstances. There is a fourth extremely important factor that was the response of exporting companies. The quality of policies means the credibility and sustainability of fiscal policy first, but also of economic policies and the responses of actors. How do you look at the contribution of tourism to the Portuguese economy? There's a structural transformation. We had a seasonal and bathing tourism (with the exception of Madeira, where there was throughout the year). We maintain this tourism and we also have urban tourism, which comes for shorter periods and seeks essentially to benefit from Portuguese urban life. This tourism is of a completely different nature and also of a market segment that generates greater value. But there is still a large imbalance between coastline and inland. This poses challenges, namely the exhaustion of services. That's the question you're going to ask. We have to think that our response to the tourist should not be just provide you with sleep and a restaurant, we have to fill in the time and offer you an experience that ensnares you. Are we aware of it? Flows are consistently growing, the novelty factor and the attraction factor are working. It is necessary to consolidate these flows and create the idea that going to Porto, Covilha or Lisbon is an experience that must be repeated, as in other European cities. We have to be the ones on the supply side who justify why they have to come. A reinvented tourist product generates added value and the ability to pay salaries and generate jobs. Is it possible to have an economy that pays good sustained wages in tourism? If the rest of the economy is good. On the day when you have an economy in the tradables that generates good added value and pays good wages, the tourism sector will have to keep up. When he goes to Rome, he pays the wages of the Romans who are aligned with the average local wages. When you go to Paris, you pay the average Parisian salary. It is clear that for this it also has to have a value proposition that justifies the payment. Banco de Portugal has stressed the importance of immigration in Portugal and the economic benefits to counteract trends such as ageing. We have an unfavorable situation because we have a low birth rate and a population that is progressively older. This means that in terms of the active population  of Portuguese origin  the trend is towards reduction. If we want to increase the product we must appeal to workers who will come from abroad and who have to have the necessary skills to integrate into the productive fabric, and a cultural substrate that facilitates integration. When you say "make appeal" do you talk, for example, about creating tax incentives? The question is basically one: create an environment that will lead to workers with the qualifications sought to consider that the destination Portugal is interesting. Entrepreneurs in the export sector complain of a shortage of skilled workers, and they even complain of a shortage of workers. For these companies it is essential that there is an influx of skilled workers. From a social point of view, these workers allow an increase in the product and a support of our social model. We all win: they who come looking for work and the Portuguese economy that sees its growth potential increased How can such a favourable environment be created without generating, from a fiscal point of view, an injustice for nationals? The tax issue is not necessarily more decisive. There are many more issues related to the cultural context, cosmopolitanism, the nature of the company. What is essential is the level of remuneration that we are able to pay, the level of satisfaction they withdraw. We are not talking about low-skilled foreign nationals, they are very skilled. At the European level we have a process of cross-migration: engineers, nurses or doctors emigrating and at the same time skilled workers coming in from other sources. We must be able to manage this balance very well because the balance has to be positive, even if we have a loss of investment in education, by transferring more skilled workers abroad and receiving less skilled workers in return. When we receive a worker with a higher level of education, we benefit from an investment by a society in that worker. But should there be campaigns directed at these workers? This is an issue that should be managed at sectoral and business level. There has to be an understanding between public policy and employers. The exercise is only interesting if it generates jobs, product growth and benefit for the national economy. The contribution of foreign workers to the national economy is positive and wrong perceptions cannot affect in any way the way we welcome them or how they contribute to the Portuguese economy. How do you read the election results? One of the major institutional innovations in Portugal is that for the first time the sustainability of public finances has become a value shared across the political spectrum. And this is an extremely important element that is proper to societies such as the Dutch, the Swedish or the German. Having a society that is attentive to imbalances that can be factors of unsustainability, of a paraarranca logic, is extremely positive. If we agree on the size of this room, and that we should not tear down the walls, whether we organize the furniture further left or more to the right, this is not the important part for an economist and for the Governor of Banco de Portugal. Portuguese society has realized that there is no possibility of ignoring the restrictions resulting from the economy, financial markets and that these restrictions must be addressed with credible behaviour and an allocation of resources that ensures the growth of the potential product. The solution to all Portuguese problems is called economic growth. The key to our problems lies in the growth of the potential product having slowed down. More than that, we have lost the capacity for convergence to the European average. The average gives us a reference of what the movement of the platoon was and how we positioned ourselves. We've lost progressive contact with the front platoon. There's been a recovery in the last few years, right? Sure. But also because there are temporary factors. Neither the loss that occurred at some point was long-term, nor is recovery independent of the loss that occurred. There is a phenomenon of rebalancing here. That is why in these matters it does not matter to look at the value of the year, but rather at the average over a period because that is what gives us the trend. Fluctuation around the trend does not eliminate the trend. And the tendency is a kind of force of gravity that grabs us, either in the upward or downward direction. Don't you admit that this recovery could be the trend reversal? I hope so. But for this we need to confirm three things: more investment, what is happening, more capital per worker, better level of education; and greater management intensity, which is dependent on the organization and size of the production units.
