Num clebre discurso em 1962, o Presidente dos Estados Unidos, John F. Kennedy, afirmou que escolhemos ir  Lua no porque seja fcil mas porque  difcil. Aprofundar, com sucesso, a UEM no  seguramente to difcil quanto ir  Lua; mas requer, sem dvida, coragem e lucidez para tomar decises to difceis quanto necessrias. 3. O ano de 2019  um ano rico em efemrides: nele se assinalam, por exemplo, os cem anos da criao da Organizao Internacional do Trabalho, os setenta e cinco anos da realizao da Conferncia de Bretton-Woods, os vinte e cinco anos da concluso do Uruguay Round, que deu origem  Organizao Mundial do Comrcio e, claro, os vinte anos do euro, que hoje aqui evocamos. Tudo acontecimentos muito distintos entre si, mas com um trao a uni-los: a ideia de que a cooperao e a integrao econmica internacional so instrumentos positivos para prosseguir o bem-estar dos povos, a convico de que a existncia de uma ordem internacional, que faa imperar o direito sobre a pura lgica da fora,  algo precioso para a convivncia pacfica. Ao assinalar com esta Conferncia os vinte anos do euro, o Banco de Portugal  que  um participante ativo no processo de criao da UEM desde o seu incio  pretendeu assinalar uma data to relevante na nossa vida coletiva para fomentar o debate, sem tabus, avaliar o caminho percorrido e os desafios que continuamos a ter de superar. No primeiro painel, focmo-nos na difcil e crucial questo da articulao de uma poltica monetria centralizada com polticas oramentais apenas harmonizadas. No segundo, revisitmos os princpios fundamentais fixados nos Tratados e o modo como foram sendo aplicados em concreto. No terceiro, pusemos em destaque as consequncias geopolticas do euro, ou no fosse um dos objetivos centrais da sua criao afirmar uma identidade monetria europeia, designadamente diminuindo a dependncia face ao dlar dos Estados Unidos. As consequncias da criao do euro ultrapassam, em muito, as fronteiras da Unio Europeia. Qualquer que seja o ngulo considerado, trata-se de um acontecimento maior da histria mundial, desde logo pelas suas repercusses nas relaes monetrias e econmicas internacionais e em termos geopolticos, e, por isso mesmo, decidimos avaliar estes vinte anos tambm nessa dimenso. Ao chegarmos ao fim dos trabalhos, creio que  legtimo dizer que alcanmos plenamente os objetivos desta Conferncia. Agradecemos s insignes personalidades que, com ocupaes e agendas to preenchidas, nos honraram ao aceitar o convite para serem oradores. Agradecemos tambm a presena de todos quantos participaram no evento. E, claro, agradeo s equipas do Banco de Portugal que o tornaram uma realidade. Esto, assim, encerrados os trabalhos da Conferncia. Muito obrigado a todos. [1] Cf. Lus Mximo dos Santos, A estreia do euro, in A Unio Europeia e Portugal: a atualidade e o futuro, Almedina, 2005, p. 96.

Title: Intervention of Administrator Hlder Rosalino at the opening of the Interbank Meeting on Payment Systems
text: Intervention of the Administrator Helder... Intervention of Administrator Helder Rosalino at the opening of the Interbank Meeting on Payment Systems 19 nov. 2019 I would like to begin by welcoming everyone present at this second Interbank Meeting on Payment Systems that Banco de Portugal promotes in 2019. About 6 months ago, last May, Banco de Portugal held an interbank meeting focused on the entry into force of the technical requirements arising from the revised Payment Services Directive (DSP2), in particular with regard to strong customer authentication and common and secure communication. These requirements entered into force on 14 September, so it is important now, after about two months, to carry out a brief balance of this change, as well as to identify the situations that still need action by payment and monitoring service providers by Banco de Portugal. In this context, the supervisory flexibility determined by the European Banking Authority (EBA), which has allowed national competent authorities (in this case Banco de Portugal) to monitor full compliance with strong authentication requirements in online card payment transactions by 31 December 2020. This full compliance implies efforts on the supply side (banks) and the use of cards (merchants), efforts that Banco de Portugal will monitor very closely, interacting bilaterally with the different actors and, in particular, through the Forum for Payment Systems. At the same time, a central theme of today's meeting refers to recent developments in eurosystem projects, in particular on: . TIPS - TARGET Instant Payments Settlement and the support of the Portuguese community in September next year; . the new real-time gross settlement services, which will result from the consolidation of TARGET2 with TARGET2-Securities, and which will go into production in November 2021; . the Eurosystem Collateral Management System ( ECMS ), the harmonised collateral management system of the Eurosystem's national central banks, which is scheduled to start in 2022. Euro area central banks have sought to evolve their market infrastructure (TARGET2, TARGET2 Securities and TIPS) to enable banks to develop more efficient, robust and secure market solutions that respond to users' needs. More than 20 years after the launch of the first TARGET, with the stabilisation of coexistence with TARGET2-Securities, the recent creation of the TIPS service, and in times of great technological innovation, an investment in the modernization, rationalisation and flexibility of the Eurosystem's market infrastructures is justified. This investment will enable a technological upgrade of the system, a deeper deepening of pan-European integration in the level of market infrastructures, the optimization of synergies between the different business aspects (cash and securities) and greater flexibility of participants in their treasury management. This is a very ambitious project that has foreseen a big bang production, so it is absolutely crucial that everyone is aware of the project planning, the requirements to be implemented, the impacts for your organisations and also for the system as a whole. Without prejudice to all the information that we will share and discuss with you today, Banco de Portugal once again expresses its willingness to support and clarify you throughout the development of the project. Finally, and on a slightly different level, we will also take this opportunity to clarify the impacts of the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2019/518, which amends Regulation (EC) No 924/2009 on cross-border payments in the Community. The amendment now brought by the new Regulation focuses mainly on exchange conversion charges, card payments and credit transfers, by introducing additional reporting obligations for payment service providers and entities providing exchange rate conversion services in ATM and POS. These new obligations shall apply on 19 April 2020 or 19 April 2021, depending on the rules in question. Payment service providers will have to adapt to the new standards, assessing technical impacts, for example at the level of the terminal park (ATM and POS) and the contracts currently in force. This set of issues reflects a moment of transformation in the provision of payment services in Europe in the short and medium term. The European retail payments market has evolved towards increasing integration and harmonisation, with the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) being the most visible example of this process. This harmonisation has been achieved by promoting payment instruments with pan-European scope and by defining uniform legal and technical requirements (such as credit transfers, direct debits and, more recently, immediate transfers). However, SEPA is still an unfinished job at physical points of sale or in an e-commerce environment, as there is no real pan-European solution for point-of-interaction (POI) payments at point-of-interaction (POI). There is still a wide range of solutions and payment instruments of an exclusively national nature, which do not allow widespread and uniform use at European level. This is a point that deserves special attention, efforts and action by the Eurosystem in its catalyst role in promoting that immediate transfers are effectively such a pan-European payment instrument in the short term. Without further ado, we will then follow the agenda. We thank you once again for your presence and the interest shown in the topics proposed for this session. Thank you very much. Banco de Portugal analyzed with the financial system the main challenges associated with payment systems
text_original: Interveno do Administrador Hlder... Interveno do Administrador Hlder Rosalino na abertura da Reunio Interbancria sobre Sistemas de Pagamentos 19 nov. 2019 Gostaria de comear por dar as boas-vindas a todos os presentes nesta segunda Reunio Interbancria sobre Sistemas de Pagamentos que o Banco de Portugal promove em 2019. H cerca de 6 meses, em maio passado, o Banco de Portugal realizou uma reunio interbancria centrada na entrada em vigor dos requisitos tcnicos decorrentes da Diretiva de Servios de Pagamento revista (DSP2), em particular no que se refere  autenticao forte do cliente e  comunicao comum e segura. Estes requisitos entraram em vigor no passado dia 14 de setembro, pelo que importa agora, passados cerca de dois meses, realizar um breve balano desta alterao, bem como identificar as situaes que ainda carecem de ao dos prestadores de servios de pagamento e de monitorizao por parte do Banco de Portugal. Assume particular destaque, neste contexto, a flexibilidade supervisiva determinada pela Autoridade Bancria Europeia (EBA), que veio permitir s autoridades competentes nacionais (no caso, ao Banco de Portugal) monitorizar o pleno cumprimento dos requisitos de autenticao forte nas operaes de pagamento online com carto at 31 de dezembro de 2020. Este pleno cumprimento implica esforos do lado da oferta (bancos) e da utilizao dos cartes (comerciantes), esforos esses que o Banco de Portugal ir acompanhar muito de perto, interagindo bilateralmente com os diferentes intervenientes e, nomeadamente, atravs do Frum para os Sistemas de Pagamentos. Paralelamente, um tema central da reunio de hoje refere-se aos desenvolvimentos recentes no mbito dos projetos do Eurosistema, em particular sobre: . o TIPS  TARGET Instant Payments Settlement e a adeso da comunidade portuguesa em setembro do prximo ano; . os novos servios de liquidao por bruto em tempo real, que resultaro da consolidao do TARGET2 com o TARGET2-Securities, e que entraro em produo em novembro de 2021; . o ECMS  Eurosystem Collateral Management System , o sistema harmonizado de gesto de colateral dos bancos centrais nacionais do Eurosistema, cujo arranque est previsto para 2022. Os bancos centrais da rea do euro tm procurado evoluir as suas infraestruturas de mercado (o TARGET2, o TARGET2 Securities e o TIPS) de forma a permitir aos bancos o desenvolvimento de solues de mercado mais eficientes, robustas e seguras, e que respondam s necessidades dos utilizadores. Passados mais de 20 anos do lanamento do primeiro TARGET, com a estabilizao da coexistncia com o TARGET2-Securities, a recente criao do servio TIPS, e em tempos de grande inovao tecnolgica, justifica-se um investimento na modernizao, racionalizao e flexibilizao das infraestruturas de mercado do Eurosistema. Esse investimento ir possibilitar um upgrade tecnolgico do sistema, um maior aprofundamento da integrao pan-europeia ao nvel das infraestruturas de mercado, a otimizao de sinergias entre as diferentes vertentes de negcio (cash e ttulos) e uma maior flexibilidade dos participantes na sua gesto de tesouraria. Este  um projeto muito ambicioso e que tem prevista uma entrada em produo em big bang, pelo que  absolutamente crucial que todos estejam cientes do planeamento do projeto, dos requisitos a implementar, dos impactos para as vossas organizaes e tambm para o sistema como um todo. Sem prejuzo de todas as informaes que hoje iremos partilhar e discutir convosco, o Banco de Portugal expressa, uma vez mais, a sua disponibilidade para vos apoiar e esclarecer ao longo do desenvolvimento do projeto. Por ltimo, e num plano ligeiramente diferente, aproveitaremos igualmente esta ocasio para clarificar os impactos decorrentes da implementao do Regulamento (UE) 2019/518, que vem alterar o Regulamento (CE) n. 924/2009, relativo aos pagamentos transfronteirios na Comunidade. A alterao agora trazida pelo novo Regulamento incide principalmente sobre os encargos de converso cambial, nos pagamentos com carto e nas transferncias a crdito, ao introduzir obrigaes de informao adicionais para os prestadores de servios de pagamento e para as entidades que prestem servios de converso cambial em ATM e POS. Estas novas obrigaes sero aplicveis a 19 de abril de 2020, ou 19 de abril de 2021, consoante as normas em causa. Os prestadores de servios de pagamentos tero que se adaptar s novas normas, avaliando os impactos tcnicos, por exemplo ao nvel do parque de terminais (ATM e POS) e dos contratos atualmente em vigor. Este conjunto de assuntos reflete um momento de transformao na prestao de servios de pagamento na Europa, no curto e mdio prazo. O mercado de pagamentos de retalho europeu tem evoludo no sentido de uma crescente integrao e harmonizao, sendo a rea nica de Pagamentos em Euros (SEPA) o exemplo mais visvel deste processo. Esta harmonizao tem sido efetuada atravs da promoo de instrumentos de pagamento com alcance pan-europeu e da definio de requisitos legais e tcnicos uniformes (como nas transferncias a crdito, nos dbitos diretos e, mais recentemente, nas transferncias imediatas). No entanto, a SEPA  ainda um trabalho inacabado nos pontos de venda fsicos ou em ambiente de comrcio eletrnico, uma vez que no existe uma verdadeira soluo paneuropeia para pagamentos nos pontos de venda fsicos e online (point-of-interaction  POI). Continuam a existir um conjunto vasto de solues e de instrumentos de pagamento de cariz exclusivamente nacional, que no permitem uma utilizao generalizada e uniforme a nvel europeu. Este  um ponto que merece especial ateno, esforos e ao do Eurosistema no seu papel catalisador, no sentido de promover que, no curto prazo, as transferncias imediatas se constituam efetivamente como esse instrumento de pagamento paneuropeu. Sem mais demoras, seguiremos ento a ordem dos trabalhos. Agradecemos mais uma vez a vossa presena e o interesse demonstrado nos temas propostos para esta sesso. Muito obrigado. Banco de Portugal analisou com o sistema financeiro os principais desafios associadosaos sistemas de pagamentos

Title: Opening speech of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, at the WTO Conference: 25 years
text: Opening speech of the Vice-Gov... Opening speech of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, at the WTO Conference: 25 years 28 nov. 2019 1. Very good morning to all. I greet Ms. Paula Vaz Freire, Professors Miguel Moura e Silva and Pedro Infante da Mota, as well as the different speakers and all participants in this Conference. First of all, I thank you for your invitation to be with you. According to a well-known statement, one should never go back to a place where one was happy. And I was happy at the Faculty of Law of the University of Lisbon (FDUL), in many moments of my career as a student and then as a teacher for another 20 years. It turns out, however, that I do not feel like i'm coming back, because I don't really think I've ever left. Well, you can't go back to a place you've never been from. And I don't think it's a one-time case. The knowledge, the academic background, the life experience, the friendships we acquire in this house never leave us. They are with us on a permanent basis when it comes to large university institutions, such as FDUL. From FDUL it can be said the same thing that Fernando Pessoa wrote for a Coca-Cola advertising campaign that never came to fruition: first it is strange, then it is entrenched. I would also like to congratulate the organizers of the Conference, as it is an initiative of the greatest interest and opportunity and that is only possible because FDUL has been able to develop, over the years, the studies on international trade, which had in Prof. Paulo Pitta and Cunha a pioneer, today coexisting several generations of teachers and researchers of the highest level. 2. I had the opportunity to say a few days ago, at a conference organized by Banco de Portugal on the 20th anniversary of the euro, that 2019 is a year rich in ephemeris and I gave, in addition to what we were recalling, the 100th anniversary of the creation of International Labour Organization, the seventy-five years of the Bretton-Woods Conference and the twenty-five years of the conclusion of the Uruguay Round, which created the World Trade Organization (WTO), beginning on 1 January 1995, the anniversary that is precisely the motto of this conference. All these events - I mentioned then - are very different from each other but have a common trait to unite them: the idea that international economic cooperation and integration are positive instruments for pursuing the well-being of peoples, the conviction that the existence of an international order, which enforced the law over the pure logic of force, is something precious to international peace. Now, in the face of the crisis of the multilateral trading system  which has lasted for a long time and has been getting worse  it is essential to debate all its problems without taboos or pre-judgments, stimulate academic and civic debate, question old and new truths, reflect on where we have arrived, to look where we want or can go, in a context as complex and challenging as the present one. This two-day conference and such illustrious speakers is certainly an excellent opportunity to have this debate. 3. The entry into operation of the WTO was undoubtedly an event of great scope at international political and economic level. The end of the Cold War and the advent of globalization created the conditions so that, from the precious legacy of GATT (which was the most enduring and successful organization qualified as "provisional" that I know), the WTO could be born, materializing, many years later and in new forms, the frustrated project of the creation of the International Trade Organization, in 1948. The expectations it generated were enormous, as, after all, the l'air du temps of that period. There were, of course, good reasons for this, such was the scale of the step taken with the conclusion of the Uruguay Round negotiations, the overall results of which brought the multilateral trading system to another level compared to the GATT system. But part of this optimism was not strange the concept, at the time very in vogue, of "end of history", supported by Francis Fukuyama. Twenty-five years later, we have seen - in some cases with astonishment, in others with great satisfaction and in too many with deep disorientation - that, after all, history is not really over. 4. While the lack of concrete results is one of the elements of the WTO crisis, its causes go far beyond that. The Trade Facilitation Agreement, which entered into force in December 2017, while important, is of course not sufficient to conceal the wto's profound lack of results, in particular in the face of the total inability to conclude the Doha Round. The failure to close a deal under the Doha Round is negatively impressive, but the current WTO crisis is much more than a crisis stemming from the lack of concrete results. The WTO crisis and, consequently, of the multilateral trading system, is rooted in profound factors and is not denied by anyone today, which is, moreover, a good sign. Much worse would actually be to think that we are faced with mere passing clouds, which can easily be inversioned, for example, with the change of political leadership in this or that country, however important it may be. Also very positive is the fact that there have already been several reform proposals, namely, but not only, at European Union level. In fact, the root of the problems is that since 1995 the world has changed the WTO remained the same. In the last twenty-five years, China has become a member of the WTO (in 2001), a new geoeconomy and a new geopolitics have emerged progressively but unstoppable, and power relations at the international level have changed profoundly, there is a permanent technological revolution, the process of digital transformation is having repercussions in all areas of economic and social life at enormous speed and, therefore, all this means that the nature and characteristics of international trade and the world economy are now very different from what they were in 1995. With an aggravating factor with regard to this misadjustment: it is that the WTO began to operate in 1995 but many of the substantive rules of international trade resulting from the Uruguay Round have an even more distant origin in time, since they were negotiated in the second half of the 1980s, as the negotiating round began in 1986. While it is a fact that, depending on the evolution of the characteristics of the world economy and international trade, the application of wto material rules has become more complex, it is still interesting to see that the most serious crisis has taken place at institutional level, more specifically in the context of the dispute settlement system, in particular with regard to the so-called Adback Body. This is, as we all know, the blockade adopted by the United States Government, from 2017 onwards, with regard to the designation of members for the Appellate Body, which will lead to the time being that within a few days  more specifically from 11 December  that body will cease to meet the statutory conditions to continue operating, thus being paralyzed and totally ineffective, the WTO dispute settlement system. Since July 2017, no appointment has been made and is therefore the Ad's Body with an increasingly reduced composition as the mandates of the members in office cease. However, this crisis, in addition to being serious in itself, is very symbolic and revealing, in that it focuses on the essential issue of rule of law at the international level. The WTO dispute settlement system has been rightly hailed  as one of the most relevant outcomes of the Uruguay Round. In 1997, I had, moreover, the opportunity to writing on the subject[2], making its praise conditional on the cautions that would have to exist against its excessive or inappropriate use, warning of the risks of a possible "litigant frenzy" or the unrealism, in the context of the WTO, of an overly jurisprudential view or of "judicial activism". He also said that the complexity of it made it a paradise for jurists. Unfortunately, it eventually became a central instrument in the political battle over the WTO. The dispute settlement system, in a sense, did not disappoint. Its operation, in global terms, has been quite impressive and, in general, valued positively. Between 1996 and 2017, Appellate Body delivered 176 decisions, which have been complied with. It should be in mind that the United States has always been reluctant to accept the dispute settlement mechanism. And the criticism of it is cross-cutting to several American administrations. The reasons for the discontent of the US Government  and several other States, are based on an alleged delivery of over-mandated decisions, invoking that the members of the Aisnation body would thus legislate, unduly creating new rights and obligations, something that can only happen by amending the treaties. It is also claimed that if there is a longer-term overtaking of the mandate, there is no instrument to correct this situation. It also invokes excessive decision-making, demonstrated by cases in which the maximum period set for delivering the decision has been exceeded. Whether and to what extent these reasons are well founded is a good subject for consideration at this conference. In any event, this position of strength of the United States has led to proposals for a possible change in WTO rules, including on the dispute settlement system, and it is not impossible for that to be the ultimate objective of the United States' positions, no one ignoring, however, that any agreement to that effect will be very difficult to achieve. 5. Behind all these differences, of course, is the fact that the multilateral trading system is in tension because of the United States' trade conflicts with the European Union and, especially with China, in the context of global competition between these two countries. Can multilateralism survive this gigantic conflict? In my view, yes, from the outthen because there is a strong economic interdependence between the United States and China. No war, even commercial, is endless, and the pressure for negotiation is all the stronger as none of the contenders can come out as a clear winner. On the contrary, this is clearly a situation in which all economies will have much to lose. It does not seem realistic to think that it is possible for any country to dispense with the multilateral trading system. All conflicts lead to new balances, and may be more or less difficult to achieve and generate more or less costs along the way. The goal of a reformist is to create space for reforms to emerge, thereby facilitating the emergence of new levels of balance. International trade is fundamental to promoting economic well-being. The upheave of flows of international trade, whatever their nature, is deeply disturbing to economic and political stability. Banco de Portugal, for example, has pointed out in several reports the risks resulting from trade tensions between the United States, China and the European Union. Risks to national and global economic growth and, consequently, to financial stability at national and global level. Despite the crisis, it is not possible to dispense with the WTO. It may be more or less liberal[3], but there must be a world trade order, a global legal framework for international trade relations. Another scenario is not credible, much less in the world of our day. No State, at least for a long period, is prepared or wishes to live without a minimum degree of predictability and legal certainty in international trade. The WTO is therefore doomed to retire in the interests of all its members. In holding this conference, its organizers make a contribution to this. Thank you so much for your attention. [1] Nesse sentido, cf. Simon J. Evenett, Triage? Assessing the EUs Modernization Proposals for the WTO, in Intereconomics 2018, Leibniz Informtion Centre for Eeconomics, p.255. [2] Cf. Luis Maximo dos Santos, "The WTO Dispute Settlement Mechanism: A Deserved Compliment?", in The World Trade Organization and Dispute Resolution, FLAD, 1998, pp. 53-64. [3] A esse respeito, saliente-se o desafiador ponto de vista de Rorden Wilkinson, que, muito embora nao subscreva, nao deixa de ter alguma pertinencia: Despite a prevailing perception and attendant rhetoric to the contrary, the WTO is not about free trade; nor has it, or the GATT, ever been. It has always been, and remains, a political institution constructed and deployed to serve a particular purpose. It is about facilitating and entrenching in international law political bargains that enable the economic agents of participating governments to pursue opportunities in some markets while protecting others.. Cf. Rorden Wilkinson, The WTO  Crisis and the governance of global trade, Routledge, 2006, p. 17.
text_original: Interveno de abertura do Vice-Gov... Interveno de abertura do Vice-Governador, Lus Mximo dos Santos, na Conferncia OMC: 25 anos 28 nov. 2019 1. Muito bom dia a todos. Cumprimento a Senhora Professora Paula Vaz Freire, os Senhores Professores Miguel Moura e Silva e Pedro Infante da Mota, bem como os distintos oradores e todos os participantes nesta Conferncia. Antes de mais, agradeo o convite que me foi dirigido para estar convosco. Segundo uma afirmao muito conhecida, nunca se deve voltar a um local onde se foi feliz. E eu fui feliz na Faculdade de Direito da Universidade de Lisboa (FDUL), em muitos momentos do meu percurso como estudante e, depois, como docente durante mais 20 anos. Sucede, porm, que eu no me sinto a voltar, pois considero que, verdadeiramente, no cheguei a sair. Ora, no se pode voltar a um local de onde nunca se saiu. E julgo no ser caso nico. O conhecimento, a formao acadmica, a experincia de vida, as amizades que adquirirmos nesta casa nunca saem de ns. Esto connosco em permanncia quando se trata de grandes instituies universitrias, como  o caso da FDUL. Da FDUL pode dizer-se o mesmo que Fernando Pessoa escreveu para uma campanha publicitria da Coca-Cola que nunca chegou a realizar-se: primeiro estranha-se, depois entranha-se. Gostaria tambm de felicitar os organizadores da Conferncia, visto tratar-se de uma iniciativa do maior interesse e oportunidade e que s  possvel porque a FDUL soube desenvolver, ao longo dos anos, os estudos sobre comrcio internacional, que tiveram no Prof. Paulo Pitta e Cunha um pioneiro, coexistindo hoje vrias geraes de professores e investigadores da mais elevada craveira. 2. Tive ocasio de dizer h alguns dias, numa conferncia organizada pelo Banco de Portugal sobre os 20 anos do euro, que o ano de 2019  um ano rico em efemrides e dei, como exemplos, alm da que estvamos a evocar, os cem anos da criao da Organizao Internacional do Trabalho, os setenta e cinco anos da realizao da Conferncia de Bretton-Woods e os vinte e cinco anos da concluso do Ronda do Uruguai, que criou a Organizao Mundial do Comrcio (OMC), com incio de funes em 1 de janeiro de 1995, aniversrio que, precisamente, constitui o mote desta conferncia. Todos esses acontecimentos -referi ento -so muito distintos entre si mas tm um trao comum a uni-los: a ideia de que a cooperao e a integrao econmica internacional so instrumentos positivos para prosseguir o bem-estar dos povos, a convico de que a existncia de uma ordem internacional, que faa imperar o direito sobre a pura lgica da fora,  algo precioso para a paz internacional. Ora, perante a crise do sistema comercial multilateral  que dura h muito e tem vindo a agravar-se - fundamental debater todos os seus problemas sem tabus nem pr-juzos, estimular o debate acadmico e cvico, questionar velhas e novas verdades, refletir sobre onde chegmos, perspetivar para onde queremos ou podemos ir, num contexto to complexo e desafiante como  o atual. Esta conferncia com dois dias de durao e to ilustres oradores , seguramente, uma excelente oportunidade para fazer esse debate. 3. A entrada em funcionamento da OMC foi, indubitavelmente, um acontecimento de enorme alcance no plano poltico e econmico internacional. O fim da Guerra Fria e o advento da globalizao criaram as condies para que, a partir do precioso legado do GATT (que constituiu a mais duradoura e bem-sucedida organizao qualificada como provisria que conheo), a OMC pudesse nascer, materializando, muitos anos depois e em novos moldes, o frustrado projeto da criao da Organizao Internacional de Comrcio, em 1948. As expetativas que gerou foram enormes,  medida, afinal, do lair du temps desse perodo. Havia,  verdade, boas razes para isso, tal foi a dimenso do passo dado com a concluso das negociaes da Ronda do Uruguai, cujos resultados globais elevaram o sistema comercial multilateral para outro patamar comparativamente ao sistema do GATT. Mas a uma parte desse otimismo no foi estranho o conceito,  poca muito em voga, de fim da Histria, sustentado por Francis Fukuyama. Ora, vinte e cinco anos depois, verificamos  nuns casos com espanto, noutros com grande satisfao e em demasiados com profunda desorientao -, que afinal, a Histria no acabou mesmo. 4. Embora a falta de resultados concretos seja um dos elementos da crise da OMC, as suas causas vo muito para alm disso. O Acordo sobre a Facilitao do Comrcio, que entrou em vigor em dezembro de 2017, conquanto importante, no , evidentemente, suficiente para escamotear a profunda falta de resultados da OMC, em especial, perante a total incapacidade de concluir a Ronda de Doha. A incapacidade de fechar um acordo no mbito da Ronda de Doha impressiona negativamente, mas a crise atual da OMC  muito mais do que uma crise decorrente da falta de resultados concretos. A crise da OMC e, consequentemente, do sistema comercial multilateral, radica em fatores profundos e no  hoje negada por ningum, o que , alis, um bom sinal. Muito pior seria, na verdade, pensar que estamos perante meras nuvens passageiras, passveis de fcil inverso, por exemplo, com a mudana de uma liderana poltica neste ou naquele pas, por mais importante que seja. Muito positivo  tambm o facto de existiram j varias propostas de reforma, designadamente, mas no s, ao nvel da Unio Europeia. De facto, a raiz dos problemas reside no facto de desde 1995 o mundo ter mudado profundamente enquanto a OMC se manteve igual[1]. Nos ltimos vinte e cinco anos, a China tornou-se membro da OMC (em 2001), surgiu, de modo progressivo mas imparvel, uma nova geoeconomia e uma nova geopoltica, as relaes de poder no plano internacional alteraram-se profundamente, vive-se numa revoluo tecnolgica permanente, o processo de transformao digital est a repercutirse em todos os domnios da vida econmica e social a uma enorme velocidade e, portanto, tudo isso significa que a natureza e as caractersticas do comrcio internacional e da economia mundial so hoje muito distintas do que eram em 1995. Com uma agravante no que diz respeito a esse desajustamento:  que a OMC comeou a funcionar em 1995 mas muitas das regras substantivas do comrcio internacional resultantes da Ronda do Uruguai tm uma origem ainda mais distante no tempo, visto que foram negociadas na segunda metade da dcada de 1980, pois a ronda negocial iniciou-se em 1986. Se  um facto que em funo da evoluo das caractersticas da economia mundial e do comrcio internacional a aplicao das regras materiais da OMC se tornou mais complexa, no deixa de ser interessante verificar que a crise mais grave veio a dar-se no plano institucional, mais concretamente no mbito do sistema de resoluo de litgios, em particular no que diz respeito ao chamado rgo de Recurso. Trata-se, como todos sabemos, do bloqueio que o Governo dos Estados Unidos adotou, a partir de 2017, relativamente  designao de membros para o Appellate Body, que levar a que dentro de poucos dias  mais concretamente a partir de 11 de dezembro -, o referido rgo deixe de reunir as condies estatutrias para continuar a funcionar, ficando assim paralisado e totalmente ineficaz, por inoperativo, o sistema de resoluo de litgios da OMC. Desde julho de 2017 que nenhuma nomeao  feita, estando, portanto, o rgo de Recurso com uma composio cada vez mais reduzida  medida que cessam os mandatos dos membros em funes. Ora, esta crise, para alm de grave em si mesma,  muito simblica e reveladora, na medida em que se centra na questo essencial da rule of law no plano internacional. O sistema de resoluo de litgios da OMC foi saudado  a meu ver justamente  como um dos resultados mais relevantes da Ronda do Uruguai. Em 1997, tive, alis, ocasio de escrever sobre o tema[2], fazendo o seu elogio condicionado s cautelas que teriam de existir contra o seu uso excessivo ou inapropriado, alertando para os riscos de um eventual frenesim litigante ou para o irrealismo, no contexto da OMC, de uma viso demasiado jurisidicionalizante ou de ativismo judicial. E disse tambm que a complexidade do mesmo o tornava um paraso para os juristas. Infelizmente, acabou por se tornar num instrumento central na batalha poltica em torno da OMC. O sistema de resoluo de litgios, num certo sentido, no desiludiu. O seu funcionamento, em termos globais, tem sido bastante impressivo e, em geral, valorizado positivamente. Entre 1996 e 2017 o Appellate Body proferiu 176 decises, que tm vindo a ser cumpridas. Importa ter presente que os Estados Unidos sempre foram relutantes na aceitao do mecanismo de resoluo de litgios. E as crticas ao mesmo so transversais a diversas administraes americanas. As razes do descontentamento do Governo dos EUA  e de vrios outros Estados, digase -radicam numa alegada prolao de decises em excesso de mandato, na invocao de que os membros do rgo de Recurso estariam desse modo a legislar, criando indevidamente direitos e obrigaes novos, algo que s pode acontecer por via de alterao aos tratados. Alega-se, tambm, que havendo ultrapassagem do mandato, no h um instrumento para corrigir essa situao. E invoca-se, igualmente, uma excessiva morosidade decisria, demonstrada pelos casos em que tem sido ultrapassado o prazo mximo estabelecido para proferir a deciso. Se -e em que medida -tais razes so ou no procedentes,  um bom tema para anlise nesta conferncia. Em qualquer caso, esta posio de fora dos Estados Unidos tem levado a que surjam propostas para uma eventual alterao das regras da OMC, incluindo quanto ao sistema de resoluo de litgios, e no  impossvel que seja esse mesmo o objetivo ltimo das posies dos Estados Unidos, ningum ignorando, contudo, que qualquer acordo nesse sentido ser muito difcil de obter. 5. Por trs de todas estas divergncias, est, evidentemente, o facto de o sistema comercial multilateral se encontrar em tenso, por fora dos conflitos comerciais dos Estado Unidos com a Unio Europeia e, muito especialmente com a China, no quadro da competio global entre esses dois pases. Conseguir o multilateralismo sobreviver a esse gigantesco conflito? No meu entender, sim, desde logo porque h uma forte interdependncia econmica entre os Estados Unidos e a China. Nenhuma guerra, mesmo comercial,  infinita, e a presso para a negociao  tanto mais forte quanto nenhum dos contendores pode sair como um claro vencedor. Pelo contrrio, trata-se, claramente, de uma situao em que todas as economias tero muito a perder. No se me afigura realista pensar que seja possvel a algum pas prescindir do sistema comercial multilateral. Todos os conflitos conduzem a novos equilbrios, podendo ser mais ou menos difceis de alcanar e gerar mais ou menos custos pelo caminho. O objetivo de um reformista  criar espao para que as reformas surjam, facilitando, assim, o surgimento de novos patamares de equilbrio. O comrcio internacional  fundamental para a promoo do bem-estar econmico. A disrupo nos fluxos do comrcio internacional, qualquer que seja a sua natureza,  profundamente perturbadora da estabilidade econmica e poltica. O Banco de Portugal, por exemplo, tem assinalado, em vrios relatrios, os riscos que resultam das tenses comerciais entre os Estados Unidos, a China e a Unio Europeia. Riscos para o crescimento econmico nacional e mundial e, consequentemente, para a estabilidade financeira no plano nacional e no plano global. Apesar da sua crise, no  possvel prescindir da OMC. Pode ser mais ou menos liberal[3], mas tem de haver uma ordem comercial mundial, um enquadramento jurdico global para as relaes comerciais internacionais. Outro cenrio no  credvel, muito menos no mundo dos nossos dias. Nenhum Estado, pelo menos por um perodo longo, est preparado ou deseja viver sem um grau mnimo de previsibilidade e segurana jurdica no plano do comrcio internacional. A OMC est, pois, condenada a reformar-se no interesse de todos os seus membros. Ao realizarem esta conferncia, os seus organizadores assumem, no plano das ideias, um contributo para que assim seja. Muito obrigado pela vossa ateno. [1] Nesse sentido, cf. Simon J. Evenett, Triage? Assessing the EUs Modernization Proposals for the WTO, in Intereconomics 2018, Leibniz Informtion Centre for Eeconomics, p.255. [2] Cf. Lus Mximo dos Santos, O Mecanismo de Resoluo de Litgios da OMC: Um Elogio Merecido?, in A Organizao Mundial de Comrcio e a Resoluo de Litgios, FLAD, 1998, pp. 53-64. [3] A esse respeito, saliente-se o desafiador ponto de vista de Rorden Wilkinson, que, muito embora no subscreva, no deixa de ter alguma pertinncia: Despite a prevailing perception and attendant rhetoric to the contrary, the WTO is not about free trade; nor has it, or the GATT, ever been. It has always been, and remains, a political institution constructed and deployed to serve a particular purpose. It is about facilitating and entrenching in international law political bargains that enable the economic agents of participating governments to pursue opportunities in some markets while protecting others.. Cf. Rorden Wilkinson, The WTO  Crisis and the governance of global trade, Routledge, 2006, p. 17.

Title: Intervention of Administrator Ana Paula Serra in the Workshop of Banco de Portugal for non-executive directors and members of the supervisory bodies of financial institutions
text: Intervention of The Administrator Ana P... Intervention of Administrator Ana Paula Serra in the Workshop of Banco de Portugal for non-executive directors and members of the supervisory bodies of financial institutions 13 Dec. 2019 Good morning. 1. Welcome to this working session, which is part of the initiatives that Banco de Portugal has been promoting for the good government of Portuguese banks. 2. Within our competences, both as prudential supervisors integrated in the Single Supervisory Mechanism, and as promoters, with the Government and the Assembly of the Republic, of legislative initiatives for the transposition of European Union directives that bring greater demands to the sector, or within our own regulatory powers, aligned with the guidelines of the European Banking Authority and Basel, we have been organizing various initiatives to encourage reflection and promote best practices in the banking sector. 3. Let me highlight the initiatives we have developed in the last two years on the assessment of the adequacy of the members of the administrative and supervisory bodies, which preceded the review of the instruction regulating this matter. I would also like to like to see a thorough review that we will promote to the framework for internal control of the institutions and which will be presented for public consultation early next year. 4. We want these processes to be open, transparent and participated, and to promote the alignment of the efforts of market players in promoting greater transparency and quality of conduct, thus contributing to increase confidence in the sector. 5. We consider that the challenges of the institutions we supervise are the challenges of Banco de Portugal. We consider that there is no opposition, and there can and should even be alignment between what, supervisors, Banco de Portugal and the European Central Bank aim to achieve and what institutions need to become more resilient. This resilience is a necessary condition for financial stability, which is the purpose of the actions of Banco de Portugal and the European Central Bank. 6. It is not too much to remember that, since the 2008 crisis, as in crises that preceded it, the challenge of trust is for everyone. We must therefore prevent weaknesses in the government of banks from resulting in the transmission of problems in the banking sector and in the economy as a whole. 7. Much has been done to improve institutions' capital ratios and decrease non-stop credit by seeking solutions that make banks more resilient. The work on the various fronts  whether in technical and economic measures or in measures of an organizational, management and behavioral nature  aims to strengthen market confidence and ensure that the Bank assumes its role in full leverage and support for the improvement of the economic conditions of the country's business fabric and families. 8. We believe that this is a path that we must follow together, sharing reflections, concerns, initiatives, doubts and, at every step, disseminating best practices, so that they become widespread practices. This session today is an example of this. 9. It is certain that the reputation of banking is also related to the state of the economy: in times of crisis, there is greater suspicion about the banking sector. However, the scrutiny on the sector has come to stay, even outside of crisis scenarios. 10. We are fully aware that this scrutiny falls, at first instance, on the banks, but it also falls on the supervisor. In this sense, it is important to ensure that we define principles and implement strategies, proactively, mitigating risks related to unwanted devies. 11. The new Capital Requirements Directive (CRD 5) and its Regulation require changes to address many of these concerns. 12. In the national market, we have the challenges, already known, of adapting to language and regulatory frameworks perhaps removed from our classical corporate traditions, so we will have to focus on the ultimate objectives desired with the challenge of transparency, reinforcement in the decision-making process and care and vigilance on ethical behaviors in the sector. And the latest objectives, in the case of banks, go far beyond the interest of shareholders. It is about preserving the interests of many other stakeholders and the public interest. 13. I believe that we all want to do better, to increase the quality of decisions in the institutions. We should not fear transparency but instead take it as an ally. There are challenges on how to implement new decision models in a sector where secrecy has always played an important role, in many senses with legitimacy, namely by protecting the interest of depositors and customers. However, a transparent institution is more robust than an opaque institution. 14. In this context, the ladies and gentlemen gathered here, as non-executive directors or as members of the supervisory body, play a key role. 15. What you have been required requires an up-to-date reading of the traditional corporate organisation framework, in this change that is already underway. 16. Expect:: i. are agents of increased scrutiny of management decisions; ii. require access to the information necessary to play your role, bearing on the work of those who often answer you, those responsible for control, risk management and risk management functions. compliance in the institution, but also to others with more executive functions; iii. continually challenge executive management and promote the best decisions, ensuring that decision-making processes are properly supported and documented and that, thus, can be scrutinized not only by you, but by the stakeholders, shareholders, customers, supervisors and others. 17. For this supervisory role to be carried out successfully, it is necessary, first of all, that each one positions himself as someone who is called to collaborate with the executive administration and who offers support in identifying risks and improving the overall quality of decisions. Another essential aspect is to ensure regular interaction with executive bodies. 18. The demands that Banco de Portugal has made, especially in the last four years, at the level of individual adequacy requirements, such as professional qualification and experience, independence or availability, non-executive directors and members of supervisory bodies, are prerequisites for being in fact able to perform these functions fully. 19. It is expected, I would say "demanded", that they be critical, that is, that they challenge and improve decisions, precisely because those involved in day-to-day management may not take into account all the angles and risks of a decision. 20. As the European Central Bank (ECB) said in a seminar dedicated to independent directors, your role requires "Noses in, fingers out". Ainda citando o BCE, numa outra metafora que me parece feliz:  What do non-executive directors on banks boards and lighthouses have in common? They both oversee, guide and support operations while keeping a healthy distance. For lighthouses this means guiding ships effectively without being at sea. 21. We know that this is not an easy role, it is not a convenient role, and that this is not the tradition in Portugal for this type of acting and posture. It is therefore expected that in your institutions you will come across some resistance. But you are on your side the legitimacy to ask and to demand more. 22. We believe that space should be left to the institution's own organization and to each of you to define the best strategy of action to achieve the objectives that are intended. Still, it is foreseeable and natural that doubts remain on your side about what is expected of you. 23. It is therefore up to us as supervisors to clearly share these expectations regarding your lines of action in the institutions. 24. The regulation and supervision of compliance with the rules does not in themselves guarantee good governance and are not at all a substitute for good government practices. We know that, as important as it is to set rules and provide guidance, good government have to do with the prevailing culture in the organization. We believe that, also in this field, your role is very relevant and that they can bring about the necessary change. Thus, in addition to ensuring that, proactively, institutions operate prudently, in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, it is also important that they promote and verify a conduct of integrity. 25. Seeking to chart a course among the many guidelines, guidelines, good practices and traditions that involve the performance of non-executive directors and even members of the supervisory body, let me mention, in a non-exhaustive way, four essential topics: 1. It is essential to establish a clear and transparent framework of competences: who does what and at what time; 2. It is necessary for each actor to take on his or her individual role, to recognise the their own responsibilities and are accountable for their exercise; 3. It is necessary to define what information is indispensable for each intervention, with which advance must be waived and to whom is the responsibility of this decision of access in concrete; 4. It is essential that each, together with the institution, ensures that it has conditions for the effective exercise of their work, whether personal conditions - knowledge, independence and exemption from conflicts of interest, availability of institutional conditions - free and timely access to information and information employees of the institution, empowerment and (certainly) adequate remuneration. 26. To help us reflect on these topics, we invited Professor Dr. Jose Ferreira Gomes, who has studied and worked on the theme of corporate administration and supervision, having produced, in 2017, a very complete thesis on this subject and that includes many examples on the banking and financial sector. Professor Dr. Jose Ferreira Gomes continues to work with the sector these themes, presenting a new look that seems to us that require. We can certainly reflect with greater quality, enjoying the extensive studies he has done on this issue, particularly at the level of comparative law, and I am grateful for his willingness to be here today. 27. Without wanting to go any further, it should be stressed that at this stage we only want to launch the challenge of reflection and, therefore, I would like to ask you to share your doubts and experiences with the greatest possible openness, so that we can all be enriched from this session. 28. I believe that this is the first time that Banco de Portugal has only called on people who have exclusively supervisory functions of the banks, which in itself is also a sign of the recognition of the specific role of your work and what you can bring to the benefit of the institutions' cultures of government. 29. I end with a word of thanks for your presence and wishes for a productive and enriching session.

Title: Intervention of the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, in the 2nd edition of the Banking Summit promoted by the Portuguese Association of Banks: "National banking system: where it came from, where it is and future challenges"
text: Intervention of the Governor, Carlos d... Intervention of the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, in the 2nd edition of the Banking Summit promoted by the Portuguese Association of Banks: "National banking system: where it came from, where it is and future challenges" 30 jan. 2020 Intervention [i] Good afternoon It is with great pleasure that I participate in the 2nd edition of the Banking Summit promoted by the Portuguese Association of Banks, which brings us together today to discuss "What banking do we want for Portugal?". Seeking to contribute to an informed debate, and making use of my experience over the last decade as Governor of Banco de Portugal, I propose to make a comprehensive reading on the evolution of the national banking system and the challenges with which it is faced. Thus, I organized my intervention according to three periods: i. The period before the crisis marked: credit exuberance (a reflection of a large risk appetite and a high risk appetite and a availability of funding) and inadequate assessment and management of the risk; financing the taking of stakes in the capital of companies and financial institutions, and by financing a construction and public works boom that was dependent on a leverage process that was, in the long run, unsustainable; ii. The period of the crisis marked: By interruption of access to finance for international markets; by the decline in domestic demand for goods and services (with particular impact on the construction and public works sector); the effect of the breakdown of economic activity on the generality of companies and individuals; and, as a result of this dynamic, the emergence of credits at risk and devaluation of shareholdings (both those of the own portfolio and the credit guarantee given to highly competitive investors leveraged); iii. The after the crisis marked: new regulatory challenges, including the requirement of higher levels of capital and new prudential requirements; new non-bank competitors vying for market shares; new technologies that change the business model - in particular, by the from a face-to-face relationship to a digital relationship  and which require large investments and scale to be profitable. The pre-crisis context I start with a description of the period before the crisis to frame the evolution observed in the banking system Portuguese. In the mid-1990s, at a time when the process of recovering the level of development was underway in relation to the other European countries, the Portuguese economy did not have significant macroeconomic imbalances. With financial liberalisation resulting from the creation of the single market and the prospect of euro support, financing has become cheaper and more affordable, resulting in a strong expansion of credit, in parallel with a reduction in the savings rate of households. Between 1995 and 2010, the weight of private sector credit stock in Gross Domestic Product (GDP) tripled, increasing from 61% to 189% of GDP. The transformation ratio, i.e. the ratio of loans to deposits, rose from 63% to 149%. An important share of this credit was channelled to the financing of the acquisition of equity interests in companies and financial institutions and to the financing of investments in economic sectors heavily dependent on domestic demand, including construction and public works and other sectors producing non-tradable goods. The consequences of this credit allocation would manifest itself in the context of the subsequent economic crisis: a very significant portion of loans that defaulted during the crisis originated in credit operations before the crisis[ii]. On the other hand, this credit exuberance was not accompanied by the growth of the potential product. Studies by Banco de Portugal indicated that in 2008, about 30% of total credit to companies had been channeled to companies with less productivity[iii]. This means that the abundance of funding from abroad has enabled for more than a decade to meet financing needs not covered by domestic savings, but has not been reflected either in increased productivity or increased potential product. As a result, between the mid-1990s and 2008, the current and capital account increased from an almost zero balance to a deficit of 10.6% of GDP, and the external indebtedness of the economy was largely mediated by the Portuguese banking system. In hindsight, it is clear that a less demanding regulatory context, a pro-cyclical fiscal policy, combined with the complacency of international financial markets, and the absence of measures that we now call macroprudential policy have enhanced the stimulus to public and private indebtedness that resulted from the process of financial integration and the reduction of interest rates that accompanied the transition to the single currency. The result was the accumulation of important macro-financial imbalances that, in 2008, made the Portuguese economy particularly vulnerable to the international financial crisis. The response to the crisis From 2007 on, as we are still well present, the international financial system began to suffer successive shocks that led to the so-called Great Financial Crisis, comparable to the crisis that led to the Great Depression in 1929. The collapse of Lehman Brothers bank in September 2008 is the climax of this series of shocks, causing a shock wave that has affected the world economy. It was the end point of a period based on increasing deregulation and reduced supervision in the name of self-regulation. This succession of concussions was reflected in Europe in the form of successive vacancies. The first financial institutions to face difficulties were those with high exposure to the securitisation of US real estate credit, located in economies with surplus savings and, consequently, large institutional investors, notably in the UK, The Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and France. A new wave followed that affected financial institutions that had actively participated in the financing of credit bubbles in their housing markets, notably in Ireland and Spain. A third wave hit the institutions that had financed the expansion of their credit portfolio using the international financial market and, therefore, had high transformation ratios and a great dependence on fundraising in the financial markets, which had been compromised in the meantime. The last wave hit both sovereigns with low potential growth and high levels of indebtedness and great dependence on external financing, as well as financial institutions with high dependence on external financing. Although, in the latter case, with an intensity that was a function of the sovereign's ability to ensure its solvency. In the latter wave, growing nervousness and risk aversion on the part of international investors have launched the specter of debt default/restructuring and the risk of renaming, giving rise to the so-called sovereign debt crisis. In this, countries perceived as having weaker budgetary situations or problems in their banking systems, notably Greece, Ireland, Portugal, Spain and Cyprus, were faced with the interruption of market financing at sustainable prices and had to resort to official funding in the form of conditional assistance programmes[iv]. It was with this scenario that I was confronted when I took office as Governor of Banco de Portugal in June 2010. As I mentioned at the time: "[it was] imperative and urgent to demonstrate to external funding agents that indebtedness trajectories [were] sustainable. To do so, [there was] to adjust gradually but with determination the external financing needs of the intensity of the restriction that we faced[we] and that would manifest [would] with all the more the lower the confidence that the funding agents deem to be able to deposit not Country."; the "international financial crisis has recalled that the stability of the conditions the activity of other sectors." In this sense, at the time of my inauguration, I identified the need for "microprudential supervision to apply a principle of systematic doubt (...) to be able to assume a countercyclical role.", which implied an "inquiry into (...) the soundness of the (...) fundamentals, future risks and their representation in the balance sheet of the supervised institution", "ensuring[if] that the perimeter of abrang supervision[ia] institutions and all products of a banking nature"[v]. Giving expression to this challenge, and in line with international requirements and standards, Banco de Portugal's banking supervision has become more intrusive, skeptical, challenging, proactive, comprehensive, adaptable and conclusive. To this end, Banco de Portugal has introduced a wide range of amendments, both in its internal organisation and in supervisory methods, and its legal powers have also been strengthened supervisory authority[vi]. At the beginning of 2011, Banco de Portugal recommended that credit institutions retain the results of the 2010 financial year, in an amount that would ensure the effective strengthening of own funds, with a view to adequate preparation for the compliance with the capital requirements of Basel III[vii]. In the first half of 2011, Portugal had been caught in the whirlwind of the sovereign debt crisis, after a one-year period in which 10-year government debt interest rates on the secondary market doubled. Investor doubts eventually resulted in the country's discontinuation of the country's ability to obtain financing on international markets at sustainable prices. The use of external financial assistance has become inevitable under a programme of negotiated with the European Union and the International Monetary Fund, based, as is known, on three pillars: fiscal consolidation, the stability of the financial system and the structural transformation of the Portuguese economy. In discussions on the pillar of the financial system, Banco de Portugal was confronted with the requirement of the three institutions to promote an adjustment of the balance sheet of the banking system similar to that carried out in other European countries. This adjustment would imply an immediate and very significant devaluation of the banks' assets, reflecting the application of extremely penalizing credit recovery assumptions in a logic of immediate selling (gone concern). This requirement would entail a massive public recapitalisation of the majority of banking groups and would have three consequences: i. would compete with public sector funding in the total envelope of the programme; ii. would determine a state-controlled takeover of recapitalised banks; and iii. would require the negotiation of particularly severe restructuring measures with the Directorate-General for Competition, in particular in terms of reducing activity which would materially and structurally affect the national economy. Such an option, although apparently the easiest from a strict supervisory perspective, as it would immediately leave credit institutions with a clean and well-provisioned balance sheet, would have a strong burden on taxpayers and would have had an overwhelming and lasting effect on the country's economic recovery capacity. This is because, either it was accommodated by an increase in the total envelope of the programme (which seemed unfeasible), and would entail a significant increase in public debt to levels that would jeopardise its sustainability and trigger restructuring risks; or it was accommodated within the agreed envelope, which would imply a much stronger adjustment of public finances with an impact on economic activity and, consequently, on the quality of the banks' assets. Bearing in mind its mission to protect financial stability, Banco de Portugal advocated for an alternative solution, which resulted in the progressive coverage of impairment losses as they materialized. This solution allowed the losses to be offset by the results generated and by capital increases, partly with temporary recourse to public funds[viii]. In order to ensure that the levels of unevenness recognised for the credit portfolios were adequate and that the methodologies and procedures, including the valuation of collaterals associated with exposures, were sufficiently conservative and aligned with best practices, Banco de Portugal carried out, from 2011, a set of inspections across the eight largest banking groups in Portugal on a consolidated basis. [ix] [x] , As expected, the adjustment process itself generated additional unevenness. Thus, between 2012 and 2015, the activity of national banks was affected by adverse developments in the macroeconomic scenario, with an impact on growth and unemployment. The increase in NPL was particularly pronounced in the non-tradable goods sector  the most affected by the reduction in domestic demand in the context of the inevitable correction of accumulated imbalances  reflecting the decline in demand based on a path of unsustainable indebtedness of private and public actors. This npl increase was also compounded by losses resulting from financing granted to investors heistly leveraged to acquire equity interests in companies and financial institutions. It should be recalled that between the end of 2008 and mid-2016, the NPL of the Portuguese more than tripled as a percentage of bank credit. At their peak in mid-2016, NPL accounted for almost 18% of total bank loans; significantly higher than the 7.7% recorded in September 2019. Between 2010 and 2018, banks operating in Portugal recorded more than 46.5 billion in disability, of which 34.9 billion for credit (including credit for the acquisition of shareholdings, for construction and public works projects, real estate and tourism, for shareholders and on a smaller scale for housing) and 11.7 billion for other assets (including holding shares and financial operations). This significant increase in NPL has greatly affected the profitability of institutions and their market valuation. An assessment that was further penalised by uncertainty as to the extent of any future losses. However, it should be noted that Banco de Portugal's analyses show that there is no evidence that the NPL ratio alone had an impact on bank credit supply to companies between 2009 and 2018 and that it was an active restriction on demand satisfaction. Higher levels of NPL were not felt so much in meeting demand, but above all in the propensity of banks to start new credit relationships in the post-crisis period (2016-2018), which refers to scrutiny more conservative in accepting new credit customers[xi]. In the absence of a solution that would allow for a sharp reduction in the level of NPL, without jeopardising financial stability, such as NAMA in Ireland and SAREB in Spain,[xii] national credit institutions have been implementing the solutions best suited to their own situation, in line with reduction plans submitted to supervisory authorities[xiii]. Over the past few years, the coverage of impairment losses has been accompanied by the necessary deleveraging of the system and capital increases that totalled more than 30 billion between 2010 and 2018,[xiv] and the Tier 1 capital ratio was strengthened from 8.2% to 13.9%. Future challenges These developments reflect the necessary correction of the imbalances accumulated in recent decades, as well as the need to observe a more stringent regulatory framework both in prudential terms and in terms of safeguarding financial stability, in particular by strengthening the capacity to absorb losses[xv][xvi]. , Today, national banks are more capitalized, have improved the quality of their balance sheets, have greater stability in the intermediation of resources and have abundant liquidity. They also have better productivity rates and, recently, recovered their profitability[xvii]. However, as I have recently stated,[xviii] and as has been reiterated in the Financial Stability Reports of Banco de Portugal, there remain enormous challenges for the sector, in a context of moderate economic growth in the coming years, low interest rates and still high indebtedness of public and private agents. Thus, it is necessary that: Banks internalize and anticipate regulatory dynamics and respect the supervisory rules not only an obligation but also an advantage competitive market confidence-generating, i.e. they have to: meet capital and liquidity ratios, stress requirements, and be diligent and effective in preventing money laundering and financing terrorism, among others; o eliminate elements of uncertainty as to (i) the nature and origin of its liabilities, (ii) the valuation of its assets, (iii) as well as business models and strategies, from a limited transparency approach to a comprehensive approach to transparency adjusted to information needs, in terms of content and each interested party. Banks must ensure that the lines of defence (i.e. the supervisory body) management, the supervisory body and the external auditor) are fully operational and focused on the sustainability of the institutions and the safeguarding of public confidence in its activity. Only in this way will they be able to avoid the materialization events that call into question their financial soundness and public confidence. Banks must continue to reduce non-performing assets, in line with the guidelines and reduction plans submitted to supervisory authorities, at the same time as continue to strengthen their loss-absorbing capacity. It is, therefore, (i) that the rates of active operations reflect the nature and risk of applications and (ii) that actively monitor the credit worthiness of borrowers the time horizon of operations, and which do not fall into the temptation of search for [xix] yield and in the evergreening trap. Banks have to diversify their sovereign portfolios in terms of issuers, as well as reduce the correlation of their risk profiles, taking into account that reassessment of risk premiums and greater discrimination against risk premiums and greater discrimination of risk premiums and greater discrimination in risk premiums are not excluded. markets, or any regulatory developments that impose concentration limits. [xx] Banks need to be prepared for a situation where the capital market contribute more to the financing of the real economy, in a context where the promoting sustainable financing is gaining precedence and where climate risks and the transition to a greener economy are now unavoidable. [xxi] Finally, incumbent institutions must be prepared to face the competition from new entities with a competitive advantage based on digital-based transactional platforms and models. As I pointed out a few months ago,[xxii] to this end, it is necessary for the banking system to take a proactive stance, assessing competitiveness in a timely manner and viability of your business model(s) and continuing to review its processes and technologies in order to ensure a reduction in its production costs and improve the responsiveness to revealed market preferences. Only in this way will it be able to respond to the competitive pressures of these new competitors, which will tend to aggravate the costs of excess installed capacity, increasing the urgency of larger-scale movements and more efficiency and triggering consolidation movements. I am sure that the Portuguese financial system has already understood the diversity and scope of the challenges it is facing, and that it will therefore give priority to eliminating the legacy of the crisis in order to ensure the confidence and interest of investors. This priority is a condition for a successful response to the challenges resulting from the new regulatory framework, new business models, new competitors and the trend towards a higher volume of financing of medium and large enterprises through large international institutions or the capital market.
