Title: Article by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in the "Jornal Econmico": A joint response to a common challenge is needed
text: Article by Governor Carlos da Silva... Article by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in the "Jornal Economico": A joint response to a common challenge is needed 20 Mar. 2020 The pandemic crisis we are now facing will have a profound impact on the world economy. Its duration and size are still surrounded by great uncertainty. The effects on economic activity and employment depend on the extent and duration of the containment measures that are eventually considered necessary to avoid the collapse of health systems and minimise the loss of human lives associated with the pandemic outbreak. They also depend critically on the measures adopted by the authorities to safeguard the economic system over the course of the containment period, and the rationality of economic agents behaviour, based on the degree of confidence in a fast recovery over the subsequent period. In the absence of appropriate measures, the impact of this pandemic on GDP could be larger than that of the Great Financial Crisis. Contrary to the circumstances leading up to the 2008 crisis, which started in the financial system, the situation we are now facing reflects the propagation of a health crisis into the real economy, with its effects amplified by the international financial system. The cause is not idiosyncratic, it is common to all economies, and it does not lie in economic policy imbalances. This being an exogenous shock, and surely temporary, affecting all European economies, a joint response to this common challenge is called for. It is essential and urgent that the different players  central banks, regulators and supervisors, and especially European institutions and national governments  take decisive and joint action at national, European and global levels. Firstly, the pandemic must be fought resolutely with an appropriate healthcare response. Secondly, and at the same time, action is required on demand and supply, so as to safeguard income and the productive potential for as long as the pandemic lasts, ensuring that jobs are still available when workers return from preventive isolation and recovery from this shock begins. Given that it is a common challenge, at budgetary level, funding the necessary effort for the healthcare response and policies to support the economy in every Member State should therefore benefit from innovative and exceptional measures, such as the issuance of so-called Eurobonds. This situation is clearly cut out for EU funding, insofar as there is a common interest and no moral risk. As is evident, monetary policy is already proactively in the field, and a set of unprecedented measures has been adopted to ensure financial sector liquidity. An example is the decision of the Governing Council of the ECB to create a bold Pandemic Emergency Purchase Programme in terms of size, flexibility, duration and commitment to supporting families, firms, banks and governments in the euro area. However, despite being a necessary condition, it is not sufficient. The financial system now plays a critical role, preventing temporary cash flow difficulties for firms and families from becoming insolvencies. Making use of available liquidity, the financial system is responsible for ensuring that funding to the real economy continues, at a time when  as a result of an abrupt and very sharp drop in revenue  firms across the board will face serious cash flow constraints. Firms will struggle to pay wages, taxes, contributions and suppliers, and service their debt. These cash flow difficulties can seriously compromise recovery unless addressed by medium-term funding that guarantees repayments can be extended over time and safeguards the working capital needed for business continuity. Under these circumstances, it is absolutely essential that the financial system, in particular banks, maintain active credit lines, continue to approve new loans and are willing to accept interest payment and principal repayment moratoria and extend the maturities of credit granted. For this to be possible, it is important to minimise capital consumption and mitigate credit risk. This requires public credit guarantee mechanisms, namely through recourse to national promotional banks or public budget guarantees, by using the flexibility that the European Commission promptly introduced into State aid rules and fiscal rules. In fact, to continue to grant credit in a context of an exponential increase in risk and uncertainty, banks need not only to be assured (by central banks) that they will not be short on liquidity, but also that they will not be penalised in their capital and that the risk taken is within their capabilities. In other words, in the absence of public guarantees, ongoing funding of the economy can be jeopardised both by the increase in risk and the increase in capital consumption resulting from default. We are now facing a transition period, where we must be strong enough to cross this torrential river and resume our normal course, that is recover our pre-crisis production potential. Banco de Portugal is monitoring developments in cooperation with the competent authorities. This public health situation, which may turn into an economic and financial crisis, requires unity and joint action from all those responsible at national and international level. It is thus essential that each player assumes their role in a decisive and coordinated manner, with the common goal of reducing uncertainty, conveying confidence and moderating the impacts of the pandemic on firms and the workforce.

Title: Article by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in Reuters: European solidarity as the solution to the coronavirus emergency
text: Article by Governor Carlos da Silva... Article by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in Reuters: European solidarity as the solution to the coronavirus emergency 23 Mar. 2020 Contrary to the circumstances that led to the 2008 crisis, the situation we are now facing reflects the propagation of a health crisis into the real economy, with its effects being amplified by the international financial system and global value chains. The cause is not idiosyncratic, it is common to all economies, and it does not lie in economic policy imbalances. To an exogenous and certainly transitory shock common to all European economies a joint response is needed. Notwithstanding the much welcomed flexibility by the European Commission regarding State Aid and the Stability and Growth Pact, such flexibility is not sufficient. National solutions continue constrained by the implications they may have on the sustainability of Member States debt. In order to successfully address this emergency, all Member States regardless of the budgetary situation, must stand financially together, otherwise they risk financial markets exploiting the weakest link. Failure to cooperate in this crisis would permanently scar the European project. As Member States have different scope for action in their budgets, solutions must be found in order to avoid that the coronavirus emergency becomes a second sovereign debt crisis. Initiatives are needed to allow members to finance their efforts to contain the impact of the pandemic by making their borrowing costs less dependent on individual fiscal situations. Different proposals have been put forward on the possibility of using the European Stability Mechanism (ESM) existing credit lines, or the creation of newly dedicated lines to address the coronavirus emergency. Nevertheless these solutions are flawed because their usage would still impact Member States total debt. Although Eurobonds would be the appropriate solution, currently there is no ready-touse vehicle for joint debt issuance by Member States. Innovative solutions are thus needed. One option that deserves further analysis is the possibility of having the ESM issuing Corona bonds, with the proceeds being channelled to all Member States in need, repayable through the European Unions long-term budget (the multiannual financial framework) without upfront impacting Member States individual fiscal positions. These Corona bonds should be of very long maturity, say 30 years, in order to dilute the impact on Member States yearly contributions. The proceeds should be allocated to the financing of Covid-19 relief effort in proportion to the severity of the public health and economic challenges encountered. Different from standard ESM facilities, and commensurate with the emergency at hand, conditionality should consist in Member States committing to use the funds in Covid-19 related spending and removing these efforts once the crisis is over. Such Corona bonds would complement and reinforce the recently announced Pandemic Emergency Purchase Programme by the European Central Bank. European solidarity and risk sharing should now make a decisive contribution in order to counter the public health crisis and mitigate the economic impact the coronavirus emergency is having throughout all Member States.

Title: Interview of the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, to expresso
text: Interview of the Governor, Carlos da... Interview of the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, to expresso 30 mar. 2020 Is the Portuguese economy prepared for the crisis? No economy is prepared for such a crisis. The countries are all on the same plane. The pandemic comes at a lower stage of the economic cycle, in which weaknesses remain linked to high levels of public and private indebtedness in several economies, including the Portuguese one. As a result of this pandemic, the outlook for the Portuguese economy has deteriorated sharply and significantly. We admit that the shock caused by the pandemic should peak in the second quarter of this year and that there will be a gradual normalisation from the second half of the year. The moment we are going through will have profound impacts on the national and world economy, the duration and size of which are still surrounded by enormous uncertainty. The cause is not specific to an economy, is transversal to all economies, and does not originate from imbalances in economic policy. But we cannot ignore the concerns about the sustainability of some countries' public debt, the risk of fragmentation in the euro area bond markets, a risk that will be a function of the nature of the response at European level. This crisis is very different and worse than that of 2008-2009... Contrary to the circumstances that led to the 2008 crisis, the situation we are facing now has as a starting point a health crisis that is transmitted to the real economy, which then is transmitted to the national banking system, with its effects being amplified by the international financial system and global production chains. What's the answer? The first priority is to tackle the pandemic at any cost, with an adequate and effective health response. The value of human life overlaps with everything else and cannot be arbitnaised between costs and human lives. An insufficient response will have lasting economic consequences and will call into question social cohesion and the collective spirit to face the future. In Portugal, the shock will be deeper in certain sectors... The national economy has specific characteristics that make it vulnerable to the nature of the shock at stake, namely the weight of the tourism sector in economic activity, integration into global value chains, such as the automotive sector, and dependence on external access to raw materials. The impact of this shock is accentuated by the nature and situation of the business fabric, dominated by small companies and with a relatively fragile financial situation. Finally, this shock will have a major impact on the domestic demand side, given the high percentage of families who are close to or below the poverty line in Portugal. Without assets, they have a small margin of absorption from the impact of the crisis. Should the ECB and monetary policy be concerned about public debt spreads? What instruments should they use? As President Lagarde explained in the week following the adoption of the measures on 12 March, conditions in the euro area have deteriorated considerably. The assessment of the economic situation has become darker as deep uncertainty about the economic consequences has become visible in all asset classes, both in the euro area and globally. This led the ECB to launch a special programme of EUR 750 billion when, days earlier, on 12 March, had it unanimously approved a 120 billion boost of the current 'normal' programme? Following deteriorating conditions in the euro area, the Governing Council of the ECB announced a new temporary asset purchase programme due to the phemic emergency, with an envelope of 750 billion by the end of the year. It will be available to all jurisdictions and will remain in force until it is assessed that this crisis phase has come to an end, with purchases made flexibly. Is there a risk that we will have a debt crisis in the euro zone if there is no any form of debt mutualisation? We are facing a situation of total uncertainty. That said, in order to respond successfully to this emergency, all Member States, regardless of their budgetary position and their level of indebtedness, must remain financially supportive and responsive. Otherwise, we run the risk of the euro zone breaking down by the weakest link, due to the very significant costs that the response to this crisis will entail or the inability to mobilise resources. How do these coronabonds that you advocate from traditional eurobonds differ? Although eurobonds were the right solution, there is currently no 'vehicle' available for joint debt issuance by Member States nor has the European Union achieved a fiscal union that allows it. Innovative solutions are needed. One option that deserves further analysis is the possibility of the European Stability Mechanism [ESM] issues coronabonds, with the resources to be channelled to the Member States and reimbursable in the long term through the Community budget and, to that end, contemplated in the multiannual financial framework (for example, if a joint effort of 10% of GDP, similar to that of the US, reimbursed for 50 years, was made, annual transfers to the Community budget would be 0.2%). This approach would have no immediate impact on the individual budgetary positions of the Member States and would cement the idea of European solidarity in the face of a systemic threat. These coronabonds must be very mature, to dilute the impact on member states' annual contributions. Resources should be allocated on the basis of the cost of the response to covid-19 and taking into account the seriousness of public health challenges and the economic impact of the health shock. The required conditionality should be limited to Member States committing to use the funds in expenditure related to the impact of covid-19 and to remove these efforts as soon as the crisis is over. Is the moratorium on capital payments on bank loans a good solution to reduce the impact of the pandemic on the economy? No doubt, but it's not enough. Moratoriums are fundamental, but they will only be effective if they are accompanied by public guarantees corresponding to what needs to be done to reconcile three concerns: the continuity of business activity after the health crisis (preventing cash problems from falling into insolvency), safeguarding the financing capacity of the banking system (minimising capital consumption) and minimising the impact on public finances (favouring public guarantees in financial aid). The financial system has a critical role to play, preventing temporary cash flow difficulties for businesses and households from becoming insolvency. Making use of available liquidity (which is guaranteed to them by central banks), it is up to the financial system that it is up to ensure the continuity of financing to the real economy, at a time when, as a result of a sharp and very sharp drop in revenue, companies will, in a general way, face serious cash constraints. That is, it is preferable to take the risk of supporting some zombie companies than to let viable companies go bankrupt. Are household incomes and employment the other side of this crisis? Naturally. Household income must be guaranteed in order to avoid a negative spiral between demand and supply. The need to safeguard production capacity requires maintaining contractual links between the company and its workers, which means that support for families should focus on paying the wages that fuel demand and preserve the productive capacity of companies. Thus, the financing of companies should include not only the moratorium on overdue obligations but also the additional financing to pay workers and suppliers, without prejudice to the proper sharing of costs of maintaining employment with Social Security. What about the moratoriums on family credit? Families most affected by the pandemic shock should be able to access moratoriums on interest payments and capital repayment of home loans, as well as extend the terms of these financings so that they can absorb the shock of reducing their income. In this context, Banco de Portugal has already decided that new personal loans with maturities of up to two years intended to mitigate situations of temporary liquidity insufficiency by households no longer have to comply with some of the limits provided for in the macroprudential recommendation for credit, thus facilitating access to this type of credit. The ECB has not yet made it clear that renegotiations of loans through moratoriums will not weigh on banks' balance sheets. What are you waiting for? Will there be flexibility, but it is not yet defined in the legislation? What can you tell us about this? In order for the financial system to ensure its role, it is important to minimise capital consumption and mitigate credit risk. The relevant European authorities have already announced greater regulatory flexibility, both in terms of capital and in terms of prudential treatment of claims covered by moratoriums and public guarantees. But, as I said, complementary measures in the form of public credit guarantees are also indispensable, which limit the increase in risk assumed by banks. These guarantees can be realised by using promotional financial institutions, the so-called promotional banks, or taking the form of guarantees from the public budget, making use of the flexibility that the European Commission promptly introduced in state aid rules and budgetary rules. In the absence of public guarantees, the volume and cost of financing to the economy will be penalised, both by the increased risk and by the increase in capital consumption resulting from defaults. text_original: Entrevista do Governador, Carlos da... Entrevista do Governador, Carlos da Silva Costa, ao Expresso 30 mar. 2020 A economia portuguesa est preparada para o embate desta crise? Nenhuma economia est preparada para uma crise desta natureza. Os pases esto todos no mesmo plano. A pandemia surge numa fase descendente do ciclo econmico, em que subsistem fragilidades ligadas aos elevados nveis de endividamento pblico e privado em vrias economias, incluindo a portuguesa. Em consequncia desta pandemia, as perspetivas para a economia portuguesa deterioraram-se abrupta e significativamente. Admitimos que o choque provocado pela pandemia deva atingir o seu pico no segundo trimestre deste ano e que haja uma normalizao gradual a partir do segundo semestre. O momento que estamos a atravessar ter impactos profundos na economia nacional e mundial, cuja durao e dimenso esto ainda rodeadas de enorme incerteza. A causa no  especfica de uma economia,  transversal a todas as economias, e no tem origem em desequilbrios da poltica econmica. Mas no podemos ignorar que podero surgir preocupaes com a sustentabilidade da dvida pblica de alguns pases, com risco de fragmentao nos mercados de ttulos da rea do euro, risco que ser funo da natureza da resposta ao nvel europeu. Esta crise  muito diferente e pior do que a de 2008-2009... Contrariamente s circunstncias que conduziram  crise de 2008, a situao com que nos defrontamos agora tem como ponto de partida uma crise sanitria que se transmite para a economia real, que depois se transmite ao sistema bancrio nacional, com os seus efeitos a serem amplificados pelo sistema financeiro internacional e pelas cadeias de produo globais. Qual  a resposta a dar? A primeira prioridade consiste em atacar a pandemia a qualquer custo, com uma resposta sanitria adequada e eficaz. O valor da vida humana sobrepe-se a tudo o resto, no se podendo arbitrar entre custos e vidas humanas. Uma resposta insuficiente ter consequncias econmicas duradouras e por em causa a coeso social e o nimo coletivo para enfrentar o futuro. Em Portugal, o choque ser mais profundo em determinados sectores... A economia nacional apresenta caractersticas especficas que a tornam vulnervel  natureza do choque que est em causa, nomeadamente o peso do sector do turismo na atividade econmica, a integrao nas cadeias de valor globais, como o caso do sector automvel, e a dependncia do acesso externo a matrias-primas. O impacto deste choque  acentuado pela natureza e pela situao do tecido empresarial, dominado por empresas de pequena dimenso e com situao financeira relativamente frgil. Por ltimo, este choque ter um impacto grande do lado da procura interna, dada a elevada percentagem de famlias que esto perto ou abaixo do limiar de pobreza em Portugal. Sem patrimnios, tm uma reduzida margem de absoro do impacto da crise. O BCE e a poltica monetria devem preocupar-se com os spreads da dvida pblica? Que instrumentos devem usar? Como explicou a presidente Lagarde, na semana a seguir  adoo das medidas de 12 de maro, as condies na rea do euro deterioraram-se de forma considervel. A avaliao da situao econmica tornou-se mais sombria, uma vez que a profunda incerteza em relao s consequncias econmicas se tornou visvel em todas as classes de ativos, tanto na rea do euro como a nvel mundial. O que levou o BCE a lanar um programa especial de 750 mil milhes de euros quando, dias antes, a 12 de maro, tinha j aprovado por unanimidade um reforo de 120 mil milhes de euros do programa normal em curso? Na sequncia da deteriorao das condies na rea do euro, o Conselho de Governadores do BCE anunciou um novo programa temporrio de compra de ativos devido  emergncia pandmica, com um envelope de 750 mil milhes de euros at ao final do ano. Estar disponvel para todas as jurisdies e permanecer em vigor at se avaliar que esta fase de crise chegou ao fim, sendo as compras efetuadas de forma flexvel. Existe o risco de termos uma crise das dvidas na zona euro se no houver uma forma qualquer de mutualizao de dvida? Estamos perante uma situao de incerteza total. Dito isto, para responder com xito a esta emergncia, todos os Estados-membros, independentemente da sua situao oramental e do seu nvel de endividamento, devem manter-se financeiramente solidrios e com idntica capacidade de resposta. Caso contrrio, corremos o risco de a zona euro quebrar pelo elo mais fraco, devido aos custos muito significativos que a resposta a esta crise vai comportar ou  incapacidade de mobilizao de recursos. Em que se distinguem estas coronabonds que advoga das eurobonds tradicionais? Embora as eurobonds fossem a soluo adequada, atualmente no existe um veculo disponvel para emisso conjunta de dvida pelos Estados-membros nem a Unio Europeia alcanou uma unio oramental que o permita. So necessrias solues inovadoras. Uma opo que merece uma anlise mais aprofundada  a possibilidade de o Mecanismo Europeu de Estabilidade [MEE] emitir coronabonds, com os recursos a serem canalizados para os Estados-membros e reembolsveis a longo prazo atravs do oramento comunitrio e, para o efeito, contempladas no quadro financeiro plurianual (a ttulo de exemplo, se fosse feito esforo conjunto de 10% do PIB, semelhante ao dos EUA, reembolsado a 50 anos, as transferncias anuais para o oramento comunitrio seriam de 0,2%). Esta abordagem no teria impacto imediato nas posies oramentais individuais dos Estados-membros e cimentaria a ideia de solidariedade europeia perante uma ameaa sistmica. Estas coronabonds devem ter uma maturidade muito longa, para diluir o impacto nas contribuies anuais dos Estados-membros. Os recursos devem ser alocados em funo do custo da resposta  covid-19 e tendo em conta a gravidade dos desafios de sade pblica e do impacto econmico do choque sanitrio. A condicionalidade requerida dever cingir-se a que Estados-membros se comprometam a usar os fundos em gastos relacionados com o impacto da covid-19 e a remover esses esforos assim que a crise terminar. A moratria no pagamento de capital nos emprstimos dos bancos  uma boa soluo para reduzir o impacto da pandemia na economia? Sem dvida, mas no basta. As moratrias so fundamentais, mas s sero eficazes se forem acompanhadas por garantias pblicas correspondentes ao que  necessrio fazer para conciliar trs preocupaes: a continuidade da atividade das empresas depois da crise sanitria (evitando que problemas de tesouraria desemboquem em insolvncias), a salvaguarda da capacidade de financiamento do sistema bancrio (minimizando o consumo de capital) e a minimizao do impacto nas finanas pblicas (privilegiando as garantias pblicas em detrimento das ajudas financeiras). O sistema financeiro tem um papel crtico a desempenhar, evitando que dificuldades temporrias de tesouraria das empresas e das famlias se transformem em situaes de insolvncia. Fazendo uso da liquidez disponvel (o que lhes  garantido pelos bancos centrais),  ao sistema financeiro que cabe assegurar a continuidade do financiamento  economia real, numa altura em que, fruto de uma quebra brusca e muito acentuada de receita, as empresas iro, de forma generalizada, enfrentar srios constrangimentos de tesouraria. Ou seja,  prefervel correr o risco de apoiar algumas empresas zombie do que deixar ir  falncia empresas viveis. O rendimento das famlias e o emprego so a outra face desta crise? Naturalmente.  preciso garantir o rendimento das famlias, para evitar uma espiral negativa entre a procura e a oferta. A necessidade de salvaguardar a capacidade de produo requer a manuteno dos laos contratuais entre a empresa e os seus trabalhadores, o que significa que o apoio s famlias deve privilegiar o pagamento dos salrios que alimentam a procura e preservam a capacidade produtiva das empresas. Assim, o financiamento das empresas deve contemplar no s a moratria de obrigaes vincendas como o financiamento adicional para pagar aos trabalhadores e aos fornecedores, sem prejuzo de partilha adequada de custos da manuteno do emprego com a Segurana Social. E sobre as moratrias no crdito s famlias? As famlias mais afetadas pelo choque da pandemia devero ter a possibilidade de aceder a moratrias no pagamento de juros e na amortizao de capital de crditos  habitao, bem como de estender os prazos destes financiamentos, para que possam absorver o choque da reduo do seu rendimento. Neste contexto, o Banco de Portugal j decidiu que os novos crditos pessoais com maturidades at dois anos destinados a mitigar situaes de insuficincia temporria de liquidez por parte das famlias deixam de ter de cumprir alguns dos limites previstos na recomendao macroprudencial para o crdito, facilitando por isso o acesso a este tipo de crdito. O BCE ainda no deixou claro que as renegociaes de emprstimos atravs de moratrias no vo pesar no balano dos bancos. Do que  que esto  espera? Haver flexibilidade, mas ainda no est definida na legislao? O que nos pode dizer sobre isto? Para que o sistema financeiro assegure o seu papel, importa minimizar o consumo de capital e mitigar o risco de crdito. As entidades europeias competentes anunciaram j uma maior flexibilidade regulatria, quer em termos de capital quer em termos de tratamento prudencial dos crditos abrangidos por moratrias e garantias pblicas. Mas, como referi, so tambm indispensveis medidas complementares, sob a forma de garantias pblicas ao crdito, que limitem o aumento do risco assumido pelos bancos. Estas garantias podem ser concretizadas atravs do recurso a instituies financeiras de carcter promocional, os designados bancos de fomento, ou assumir a forma de garantias do oramento pblico, fazendo uso da flexibilidade que a Comisso Europeia prontamente introduziu nas regras de auxlios de Estado e nas regras oramentais. Na falta de garantias pblicas, o volume e o custo do financiamento  economia sero penalizados, tanto pelo aumento de risco como pelo aumento de consumo de capital resultante de incumprimentos. Title: Interview of Administrator Luis Laginha de Sousa to the Business Journal
text: Interview with Administrator Luis La... Interview of Administrator Luis Laginha de Sousa to the Business Journal 30 mar. 2020 Portugal, like other European countries, is being affected by a pandemic. What will be the impact? At the moment it is certain that we are facing a very acute, very severe impact. But Banco de Portugal's belief is that it will be temporary. We will have serious effects, but of course they will tend to be destitubly in the future and there will certainly be  it is our conviction  a return to normality. We must have measures that can address what are the short-term challenges, but we must also be very clear about what are operating rules that must exist in the future. Banking has complied with the rules set for credit, reducing risk. Will the pandemic lead to a deterioration in the credit risk profile granted? There will certainly be more difficulties and it is to be hoped that there will be a de facto deterioration of the risk profile of the various economic agents. In the face of a shock of this magnitude no one of common sense can say that this degradation will not exist. In the light of this crisis, Banco de Portugal has decided to relax the macroprudential recommendation, in particular as regards the criteria in personal credit agreements. Why this measure? Because the understanding is that we are facing a situation where access to liquidity can be an essential element for some borrowers. So it's a contribution within what the assessment we made and what we thought was reasonable. It is a contribution of flexibility to allow financial institutions, while still making the analysis they have to do, if they believe that there is scope to make such a grant of credit, other than because of the macroprudential recommendation that they stop providing credit to citizens so that they can deal with what is the intended use for that credit. Can't this measure later be a burden on families? We must keep in mind that the granting of credit must always have behind the assumption that those to whom the financial institution is granting the credit will proceed with the payment. [If there is no such perspective, then] credit is not the appropriate instrument to meet these needs. That is where social policies have to come in and another kind of support has to come in. We must make as much more flexible as possible within the instruments that exist, but we must not unanchor the criteria for granting credit from what are prudent criteria because there will be a postcovid-19. The banks praised the measure. However, they say more needs to be done. What other measures can be taken? Our understanding is that it is at the level of capital instruments  what are commonly called buffers, that is, the reserves to which financial institutions are obliged  that much of the responsiveness that the financial system will be able to deal with is a part of the problems posed by covid-19. There are different levels of use of capital instruments, of capital ratios. We will look at the capital instruments that exist. There is another buffer that exists and we will analyze and see if, through the channels themselves and at the moment, some adjustment makes sense. Are you looking at the possibility of banks releasing these cushions from capital? You need to see what limits of flexibility can be given to institutions to use their capital buffers. There is a set of rules for using these buffers that depend on the Single Supervisory Mechanism and there are certain types of rules that have to be centrally defined. Then there are "buffers" that are on the side of the macroprudential authority, Banco de Portugal. [Each authority] has to analyze and then follow its own circuits. We are naturally looking at any flexibility assumptions that make sense in this context. Is there any prospect of when a decision might be made? I can't go beyond what I said. We're looking into it. How does the BdP see the credit moratoriums? We have actively contributed [to the design of the moratoriums]. Of course, one thing is our contributions, it is another thing the incorporation of those contributions by those who will have to implement and translate it into law. We are in favour of [these moratoriums] and we have tried to channel into the discussion everything that in our perspective, and looking at the financial system, it was important, on the one hand, to allow the financial system to do what it can and should do and, on the other hand, to prevent this from being done in a way that then enhances the situation of the sector. It refers to the impact of the measure on the ratios of malparado... Exactly. We have to be very careful in the way we do it. Of course there is a very great desire here to avoid the immediate problem of companies as much as possible, but we have to have the notion that they will come after shockwaves of this negative situation and the financial system will have to deal with it. The measures they are taking today cannot themselves further aggravate these shock waves that will necessarily exist in the future. I would like to pass on the message that Banco de Portugal's position is clearly favourable, and that it has had a strong participation in the discussion and in contributing to the implementation of the moratorium, seeking to safeguard what seems relevant from the point of observation in which the BdP is. How long will the ECB "turn a blind eye" to the potential increase in the malparado? As you will understand, I cannot answer that question. The ECB has spoken very clearly - clear within what can be said. It has given very clear signs of being on the side of those who are looking to contribute to a solution to a very serious problem. So at the moment, the focus is on being clearly part of the solution and giving all the necessary support to the economies. Title: Article by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in the Eurofi | Magazine, Zagreb 2020: "Safeguarding financial stability at local level within the Banking Union"
text: Article by Governor Carlos da Silva... Article by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in the Eurofi Magazine, Zagreb 2020: "Safeguarding financial stability at local level within the Banking Union" 23 Apr. 2020 Whilst we must not underestimate the remarkable progress achieved in recent years, we should acknowledge that Europes financial architecture still needs to be completed and strengthened. Without a pan-European banking system, EDIS, and adequate resolution and liquidation mechanisms, financial crises tend to be local. The responsibility of ensuring financial stability and depositors confidence lies with individual sovereigns, which have limited instruments and room for intervention. As we stand, effective risk-sharing mechanisms have not been put in place. The sovereign-bank doom loop  the trigger for creating the Banking Union  persists. Indeed, supervisory and resolution decisions are mostly European, whereas the ultimate guarantor of financial stability remains national: banks are European in life but remain national in death, creating a mismatch between control and liability. As it is clear now, not all countries were ready to implement the Bank Recovery and Resolution Directive (BRRD) as scheduled. This implied that over recent years, some countries have had to resort to alternative instruments to safeguard financial stability  these decisions were met with outcry and criticism as they were perceived as attempts to circumvent the existing rules. It could be argued that the current setup made bank liquidations an easy way out for European authorities as the ensuing financial and political costs lie with national authorities. It should not be forgotten that few things can be more destructive to public trust in European institutions than threats to financial stability. In this regard, the conclusions reached by Denmark and Sweden on the (public) analysis of their possible participation in the Banking Union deserve careful consideration by having clearly identified the risk of conflict arising between the local objectives of financial stability and in the Banking Union as a whole. Against this background, the harmonisation of EU banks liquidation regimes has been heralded as one way forward. However, in the absence of an appropriate legal framework, liquidation might imply the immediate interruption of lending support, as well as the suspension of payments; it may have disruptive effects for creditors, depositors and other stakeholders, ultimately reinforcing the sovereign-bank doom loop. Instead of moving immediately towards such harmonisation, efforts must be made to establish an enabling framework for the orderly management of failing banks of locally systemic importance, combining elements of the resolution and liquidation frameworks, with a view to minimising losses and protecting depositors and non-financial borrowers. Such an enabling framework should include the definition of high-level principles to be agreed by all Member States for application at national level. For those banks assessed as not having (European) public interest, room for manoeuvre should be available in view of national preferences. Recourse to alternative measures as foreseen in the Directive on Deposit Guarantee Schemes or to public funds, as an ultimate backstop, should be considered in this regard. It also goes without saying that further stabilisation mechanisms  a fully-fledged EDIS, the provision of liquidity in resolution, a common euro area safe asset  and addressing home-host tensions are also needed and urgent. This is even more so, as pressure for consolidation to increase profitability and efficiency of the European banking sector is increasing, and raises the question of how to reconcile further integration with safeguarding financial stability at local level in the current incomplete and imperfect set up. On the one hand, supervisors and regulators should provide a stable view of the supervisory and regulatory frameworks allowing market participants to make informed decisions. On the other hand, without risk sharing and pan-European banks, sovereigns need to find the means to protect competition in their local markets and to safeguard the flow of funding to the economy when branches and subsidiaries of foreign banks exit during a downturn (as observed during the previous crisis). Summing up, decisive political will to move forward with the completion of the Banking Union is required. As the impacts of the coronavirus reverberate, this must now also be a priority for policy-makers and relevant institutions. Failure to do so can call the future of the European project into question.

Title: Interview of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, to expresso
text: Interview of the Deputy Governor, Luis... Interview of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, to expresso 04 May. 2020 Is the help Portugal is giving to businesses and families enough? The degree of anomalous and atypical uncertainty of this crisis will imply making a kind of navigation in sight. In this first phase, the essential was done. I don't want to make a final judgment, because there are measures that are fine, others will need to be reviewed later. This is one of those crises that will only be resolved with a very deep sense of community, both at national and European level. One cannot just wait for the Government's measures to avoid a second lockdown, which will have even more aggressive consequences for economic activity. The citizens themselves have to do their job. Bankers went to parliament to say that credit moratoriums should be extended beyond September. Do you have the same opinion? This will surely be one of the points that until June 30 can be extended. But that doesn't mean that when the legislation came out the measure was wrong. That was the period that the European Banking Authority set. In the moratoriums, there is capitalization of interest and the benefits will increase. How do you see that? The consumer can only request the suspension of capital and then the amount of the debt will not be increased. We are in a low interest rate context and there is a margin to avoid this effect, especially in home loans. Is portugal's high debt conditioning the aid granted, as other countries are channeling more robust funds? This is not only for Portugal. The countries are not all in the same situation and that is precisely why there must be several levels to address this crisis, and the European level is decisive. Because otherwise, in the long term, we will exacerbate problems that already existed and came from behind at the level of inequality between states. It is essential that the European response gives confidence in cost-sharing. Countries such as Portugal and Italy certainly have less scope, in terms of their public finances, to provide support than other less indebted states. Should banks not give profits, as the leader of the PSD has already stated? Of course, the banking sector will suffer from the fall in economic growth and the fall in household income, which will inevitably exist. What's the question about that? What is needed is for the sector to be competent and expeditious within the framework of the legislation defined to ensure the necessary liquidity flows. Don't think that the banking sector is enriched and the economy depletors. There are no strong economies with weak financial systems, nor strong financial systems with weak economies. We're going to have much weaker banks. It remains to be seen how much more, and it depends on the uncertainty factor and the duration of the crisis, which we do not know what it will be. There are several dependencies, from the outcenter the evolution of the health issue and the reaction of people post-covid-19. How is it to ensure that the bank will not be penalised for being more flexible? Banks have to do their job, they cannot do without an appropriate risk analysis. But we live in a time when we are all summoned, so are the bank, but you have to be convinced that the client will reimburse you. In this crisis, which is global, we must be aware that there is no geography to be pulled by the others, they are all deeply affected by the same evil. That is also why the IMF predicts that the decline in the world economy will be the largest since the 1929 crisis. With the pandemic, will bad credit go back to highs? The degree of uncertainty makes this estimate very difficult. It is clear that if we think that part of the growth we have had in recent years, for example, is very much linked to the tourism sector, it is natural that this sector will reinse and, having been investment granted even very judiciously, on the basis of certain assumptions, these assumptions have changed in a radical way, and therefore no one can guarantee anything. What needs to be guaranteed is quality management both on the business side, guiding what was being done to the foreign market to the internal market, to explore new opportunities, as well as on the banks side, with regard to their valuation capacity. I believe that's being done. It is not worth thinking that the banking sector will not be reached in the long term if we have a very profound economic crisis as indicated. Of course you will. The crisis is global, it takes many economies dependent on other... In crises there are always better economic zones than others, and it has suddenly revealed that there were essential products that were very dependent on other areas also affected, such as products imported from China. Europe will probably have to think of a new industrial policy, which does not imply a protectionist policy, but which makes the European economy less vulnerable. Can the challenges at the moment anticipate new aid to the bank in a year's time? I would say that, from the outset, the path of the banking sector was exceptional. This is not to say that all the wounds of the 2008 crisis have already been overcome, but the system is incomparably better, more capitalised, better organised and better managed. When it was from the previous financial crisis, banks helped themselves to help the economy, because otherwise the disruptive degree would be even higher. What I am asked is more in the field of futurology, it depends on how economic activity recomp. There is a problem in principle, an environment of deep economic downturn, which is never good for the banking sector. Because customers are companies and individuals, and if they are not financially well, the sector cannot be either. It is not, at the moment, serious or rational to foresee this or that, the resilience of our banks is greatly enhanced. Can the ECB do more? The European Union (EU) can do more. The ECB has done enough. You can't expect the ECB to do everything, that's not going to work. It would even be a sign of weakness, and markets are aware, because that would reflect that, on a political level, there is no broad will to find other solutions. The latter European Council opens up interesting and positive expectations, although it is still very dependent on how support for recovery will be shared, i.e. what will be funding and grants. The assembly of all this forces us to be started. It is in the concrete content of the measures that the near future will be played out. What response should the EU have given? Europe needs a solution where different countries feel comfortable. This is always how the European project progressed. No one can be in a union if you lose all the time. This innovative nature of the crisis also demands some ability to innovate. In fact, history tells us that the different types of crises have led to different solutions. Each State has national interests that have not disappeared, but there is a common interest and this involves accommodating the different national interests in a sufficiently satisfactory way (not 100%) so that no one feels depresed in that union. This is what's going to be at stake. What creativity does the EU need? I do not want to be padded for any of the various possible instruments, there is a path started, but I think that the larger the size of the subsidies to the detriment of loans, the better for the more indebted states. The budgetary instrument discusses which part will work through loans or grants; the President of the European Commission spoke in a mix. There are many technical solutions, but deep down, what has to be shared are the costs. One of the things that has always been in evidence is that the EU was not prepared for asymmetric shocks, but this is a symmetrical shock, the pandemic has not only hit the southern or northern states, it has affected both, and so more sense makes it more sense that the common response does not perpetuate unbalanced situations. Can the EU's bankruptcy be at stake? I wouldn't go that way. There are differences in the paths, but that does not mean that it is impossible to find a satisfactory path. I believe this will eventually prevail. Even in the most powerful countries in Europe there are weaknesses - Germany's relationship with China, for example, we do not know how it will evolve - and so the countries of the North do not think they can be, if they are lucid in their assessment, interested in solutions that do not promote the economic situation of their neighbours further south. What would be better for Portugal? That's a political matter. The most important thing is to focus on the final result, which will advance the well-being and economic development of the Member States. We're all in the same boat. Was there an opportunity to anticipate the Novo Banco mechanism? What savings did you expect? What was considered was to reduce uncertainty, increase predictability, prevent the limit from being reached, which was not certain and that we would have to work on. Today, the degree of uncertainty has increased in this regard. It cannot be said that it was good or that it was bad in abstract, it would depend on the concrete agreement, but there was press that caricaturou the solution by saying that we would anticipate the closure of the mechanism paying the 3.89 billion. Well, that was ridiculous. If there was a global agreement, it would always be with a significant discount to the amount. Around 500 million? That's irrelevant now. If it were necessary to intervene in a bank because of the pandemic, would it be the national or the European Resolution Fund? It would hardly configure any situation on account of the Portuguese. The architecture constituted, although imperfect because it does not have the third pillar (the deposit guarantee fund), is the existence of the European resolution fund. If there's any stress on a small and medium-sized bank, how would you do it? I don't feel like there's any situation that's going to come up. But each bank's resolution plans predict how to deal with it, that's what they exist for. Traditional resolution tools, selling activity, and creating a transition bank in the current deteriorated context may not be easy to trigger. It is easier to apply a resolution measure in certain contexts than in others. In this would be difficult because the bank purchases have not been many. In Portuguese banking will there not be situations of stress? All the work, and it was a lot, on the part of the banks, reinforced them, but no one can say that this or that will not happen. Today, what I can say is that there is a stronger resilience of the sector, even with an adverse shock. It's not regulatory optimism. They're facts. The Resolution Fund is responsible for the legal proceedings that are against the Fund and the Novo Banco. Have there ever been convictions? The Fund was not convicted at all. All resolution litigation has been the subject of favorable court decisions. How do you justify that Banif's creditors are still unsure whether they have to receive anything five years after the resolution? The evaluation that has to be made for this purpose is not completed. There were operational aspects that made it difficult to complete. I recognise that the delay is excessive, but we will soon have this assessment.

H vrias dependncias, desde logo a evoluo da questo sanitria e a reao das pessoas ps-covid-19. Como se garante que a banca no ir ser penalizada por estar a ser mais flexvel? Os bancos tm de fazer o seu trabalho, no podem prescindir de uma anlise de risco adequada. Mas vivemos um momento em que todos somos convocados, a banca tambm, mas tem de estar convicta de que o cliente a vai reembolsar. Nesta crise, que  global, temos de ter conscincia de que no existe uma geografia a puxar pelas outras, esto todas profundamente afetadas pelo mesmo mal.  tambm por isso que o FMI prev que o decrscimo da economia mundial seja o maior desde a crise de 1929. Com a pandemia, o crdito mal parado vai voltar a mximos? O grau de incerteza torna essa estimativa muito difcil.  evidente que se pensarmos que uma parte do crescimento que tivemos nos ltimos anos, por exemplo, est muito ligado ao sector do turismo,  natural que esse sector se ressinta e, tendo havido investimentos concedidos at muito criteriosamente, com base em determinados pressupostos, esses pressupostos alteraram-se de uma forma radical, e, por isso, ningum pode garantir nada. O que  preciso garantir  qualidade de gesto tanto do lado das empresas, orientando o que estava a ser feito para o mercado externo para o mercado interno, para explorar novas oportunidades, como do lado dos bancos, no que diz respeito  sua capacidade de avaliao. Acredito que isso est a ser feito. No vale a pena pensar que o sector bancrio no ser, a prazo, atingido se tivermos uma crise econmica muitssimo profunda como se indicia. Claro que vai. A crise  global, apanha muitas economias dependentes de outras... Nas crises h sempre zonas econmicas melhores do que outras, e esta revelou, de repente, que havia produtos essenciais que estavam muito dependentes de outras zonas igualmente afetadas, como, por exemplo, de produtos importados da China. Provavelmente, a Europa vai ter de pensar numa nova poltica industrial, o que no implica uma poltica protecionista, mas que deixe a economia europeia menos vulnervel. Os desafios que se colocam neste momento podem antecipar novas ajudas  banca daqui a um ano? Diria que,  partida, o trajeto do sector bancrio foi excecional. No quer dizer que j tivessem sido superadas todas as feridas da crise de 2008, mas o sistema est incomparavelmente melhor, mais capitalizado, melhor organizado e melhor gerido. Quando foi da crise financeira anterior, ajudaram-se os bancos para ajudarem a economia, porque, caso contrrio, o grau disruptivo seria ainda maior. O que me perguntam  mais do domnio da futurologia, depende de como a atividade econmica se recompuser. H um problema de princpio, um ambiente de retrao econmica profunda, o que nunca  bom para o sector bancrio. Porque os clientes so as empresas e os particulares, e se estes no estiverem financeiramente bem, o sector tambm no pode estar. No , neste momento, srio nem racional antever isto ou aquilo, a capacidade de resistncia dos nossos bancos est bastante reforada. O BCE pode fazer mais?  possvel a Unio Europeia (UE) fazer mais. O BCE j fez bastante. No se pode esperar que seja o BCE a fazer tudo, isso no vai dar. Seria at um sinal de fraqueza, e os mercados esto atentos, porque isso refletiria que, no plano poltico, no h uma vontade alargada de encontrar outras solues. Este ltimo Conselho Europeu abre expectativas interessantes e positivas, embora esteja ainda muito dependente de como se vo repartir os apoios para a recuperao, ou seja, o que ser financiamento e subvenes. A montagem de tudo isto obriga-nos a ser comedidos.  no contedo concreto das medidas que se vai jogar o futuro prximo. Que resposta a UE devia ter dado? A Europa precisa de uma soluo em que os diferentes pases se sintam confortveis. Foi sempre assim que o projeto europeu progrediu. Ningum pode estar numa unio se estiver sempre a perder. Este carter inovador da crise tambm reclama alguma capacidade de inovar. Alis, a Histria diz-nos que as diferentes tipologias das crises levaram a solues diferentes. Cada Estado tem interesses nacionais que no desapareceram, mas h um interesse comum e isso passa por acomodar os diferentes interesses nacionais de forma suficientemente satisfatria (no a 100%) para que ningum se sinta preterido nessa unio.  isto que vai estar em jogo. De que criatividade precisa a UE? No quero estar a manifestar preferncia por nenhum dos diversos instrumentos possveis, h um caminho encetado, mas penso que quanto maior for a dimenso das subvenes em detrimento dos emprstimos, melhor para os Estados mais endividados. No instrumento oramental discute-se qual a parte que vai funcionar atravs de emprstimos ou subvenes; a presidente da Comisso Europeia falou num mix. H muitas solues tcnicas, mas, no fundo, o que tem de se partilhar so os custos. Um dos aspetos que sempre esteve em evidncia  o de que a UE no estava preparada para choques assimtricos, mas este  um choque simtrico, a pandemia no atingiu s os Estados do Sul ou do Norte, afetou ambos, e por isso mais sentido faz que a resposta comum no perpetue situaes de desequilbrio. A falncia da UE pode estar em causa? No iria por a. H divergncias quanto aos caminhos, mas isso no quer dizer que seja impossvel encontrar um caminho satisfatrio. Acredito que isso acabar por prevalecer. Mesmo nos pases mais poderosos da Europa existem fragilidades -a relao da Alemanha com a China, por exemplo, no sabemos como ir evoluir -, e portanto os pases do Norte no creio que possam estar, se forem lcidos na sua avaliao, interessados em solues que no promovam a situao econmica dos seus vizinhos mais a sul. O que seria melhor para Portugal? Essa  uma matria poltica. O mais importante  fixarmo-nos no resultado final, que faa progredir o bem-estar e o desenvolvimento econmico dos Estados-membros. Estamos todos no mesmo barco. Perdeu-se uma oportunidade em antecipar o mecanismo do Novo Banco? Que poupana esperava? O que se equacionou foi reduzir a incerteza, aumentar a previsibilidade, evitar que fosse alcanado o limite, coisa que no era certa e em que teramos de trabalhar. Hoje, o grau de incerteza aumentou a esse respeito. No se pode dizer que era bom ou que era mau em abstrato, dependeria do concreto acordo, mas houve imprensa que caricaturou a soluo ao dizer que amos antecipar o fecho do mecanismo pagando os  3,89 mil milhes. Ora, isso era ridculo. Se houvesse acordo global, seria sempre com um desconto significativo face ao montante.  volta dos  500 milhes? Isso agora  irrelevante. Se fosse necessrio intervir num banco por causa da pandemia, seria o Fundo de Resoluo nacional ou o europeu? Dificilmente configuraria qualquer situao por conta do fundo portugus. A arquitetura constituda, embora imperfeita porque no tem o terceiro pilar (o fundo de garantia de depsitos),  a existncia do fundo de resoluo europeu. Havendo algum stresse num banco de pequena e mdia dimenso, como se faria? No sinto que haja alguma situao que venha a colocar-se. Mas, os planos de resoluo de cada banco preveem como lidar com ela,  para isso que existem. As ferramentas tradicionais de resoluo, a venda da atividade e a criao de um banco de transio, no atual contexto deteriorado podem no ser fceis de acionar.  mais fcil aplicar uma medida de resoluo em determinados contextos do que noutros. Neste seria difcil porque as aquisies bancrias no tm sido muitas. Na banca portuguesa no vai haver situaes de stresse? Todo o trabalho, e foi muito, da parte dos bancos, reforou-os, mas ningum pode dizer que no acontecer isto ou aquilo. Hoje, o que posso dizer  que h uma capacidade de resistncia do sector mais forte, mesmo com um choque adverso. No  otimismo de regulador. So factos. O Fundo de Resoluo  responsvel pelos processos judiciais que so contra o Fundo e o Novo Banco. J houve condenaes? O Fundo no foi condenado em nada. Todo o contencioso referente  resoluo tem sido alvo de decises favorveis dos tribunais. Como justifica que os credores do Banif ainda no tenham a certeza sobre se tm de receber alguma coisa, cinco anos aps a resoluo? No est concluda a avaliao que tem de ser feita para esse efeito. Houve aspetos operacionais que dificultaram a sua concluso. Reconheo que o atraso  excessivo, mas em breve teremos essa avaliao.

Title: Opinion article by Administrator Hlder Rosalino in ECO: "The response of payment systems in times of crisis"
text: Administrator opinion article... Opinion article by Administrator Helder Rosalino in ECO: "The response of payment systems in times of crisis" 19 May. 2020 Banco de Portugal has two main tasks: maintaining price stability and promoting the stability of the financial system. In addition to these functions, it is up to it to regulate, monitor and promote the proper functioning of payment systems. Promoting the proper functioning of payment systems is a nuclear responsibility of Banco de Portugal, as these systems are crucial for economic agents to develop their activities, with the utmost confidence in the payment services and instruments at their disposal. It is imperative that payment systems are always available and operate continuously and efficiently, not only in periods of social stability and economic expansion, as has happened in recent years, but especially in public health emergencies, such as that created during the first months of 2020 with the COVID-19 pandemic. Ensuring this availability and efficiency in a pandemic situation and encouraging the adoption of social containment and containment measures required an unprecedented adaptability and response of national payment systems, involving several entities under the coordination of Banco de Portugal. In 2019, on average 8.7 million transactions per day were processed in retail payment systems alone, amounting to EUR 1.9 billion. These figures reveal the importance that payment systems have on our lives and the impact we would all feel if, for some reason, they stopped working. What would it be if, for an hour, we couldn't use payment cards, make transfers or pay with direct debits? What if it was for a day or a week? This has never happened because the payment infrastructures that support the functioning of the financial system and the Portuguese economy have always responded fully. In recent years we have seen a progressive strengthening of the use of electronic payment instruments (direct debits, credit transfers, immediate transfers and payment card) to the detriment of paper instruments. We have also seen a greater preponderance of technology in payment services and a greater focus on the speed, convenience and experience of users. In 2019, some trends were also accentuated, which until then were little marked. This is the case with the use of contacless payments and online purchases, which have begun to be used more significantly, with consumers increasingly valuing their speed and convenience. The first months of 2020, with the evolution of the pandemic, have accentuated this trend, with significant growth in card purchases made using contactless technology and online shopping, despite an unprecedented reduction in card payments. Purchases with contactless technology increased by 60% in number, while online purchases increased by 11% compared to the same period. At a time when it became important to take measures to contribute to the containment of COVID-19 and that could ensure the functioning of the economy and make payments in an environment of greater social distancing, many consumers chose to make their purchases online and make payments via contactless cards (with the limit per operation going from 20 to 50) or through the merchant's website, your bank's homebanking or app. In this way, the fact that Portuguese consumers have at their disposal digital, resilient, convenient and secure payment solutions has contributed unequivocally to minimise the impacts of COVID-19 on their daily lives. The reality observed over the first months of 2020 may signal that the way we will pay in the future will be different from the one we pay until 2019. These new ways of buying and paying have become part of our daily life and it is expected that, from this moment on, they will become rooted in the habits of consumers. As always, Banco de Portugal, in fulfilling its mandate in the context of payment systems, is available and proactive not only to support the activity of economic agents in exceptional situations such as that we live in, but also to respond to the challenges of digital transformation and promote the development of more innovative payment services, safe and efficient.
