Artigo de opinio do Administrador Hlder Rosalino no ECO: "A resposta dos sistemas de pagamento em tempo de crise" 19 mai. 2020 O Banco de Portugal tem duas misses principais: a manuteno da estabilidade dos preos e a promoo da estabilidade do sistema financeiro. A par destas funes, compete-lhe regular, fiscalizar e promover o bom funcionamento dos sistemas de pagamentos. A promoo do bom funcionamento dos sistemas de pagamentos  uma responsabilidade nuclear do Banco de Portugal, na medida em que estes sistemas so cruciais para que os agentes econmicos possam desenvolver as suas atividades, com a mxima confiana nos servios e instrumentos de pagamento que tm  sua disposio.  imperativo que sistemas de pagamentos estejam sempre disponveis e funcionem de forma contnua e eficiente, no s em perodos de estabilidade social e de expanso econmica, como aconteceu nos ltimos anos, mas sobretudo em situaes de emergncia de sade pblica, como a criada ao longo dos primeiros meses de 2020 com a pandemia do COVID-19. Garantir essa disponibilidade e eficincia numa situao de pandemia e em que se incentiva a adoo de medidas de conteno social e confinamento exigiu uma capacidade de adaptao e de resposta dos sistemas de pagamentos nacionais sem precedentes, envolvendo vrias entidades sob a coordenao do Banco de Portugal. Em 2019, s nos sistemas de pagamento de retalho foram processadas, em mdia, 8,7 milhes de operaes por dia, no valor de 1,9 mil milhes de euros. Estes nmeros so reveladores da importncia que os sistemas de pagamento tm na nossa vida e do impacto que todos sentiramos se, por alguma razo, deixassem de funcionar. O que seria se, durante uma hora, no consegussemos usar cartes de pagamento, fazer transferncias ou pagar com dbitos diretos? E se fosse durante um dia ou uma semana? Tal nunca aconteceu porque as infraestruturas de pagamentos que suportam o funcionamento do sistema financeiro e da economia portuguesa responderam sempre de forma plena. Nos ltimos anos temos assistido a um progressivo reforo da utilizao dos instrumentos de pagamento eletrnicos (dbitos diretos, transferncias a crdito, transferncias imediatas e carto de pagamento) em detrimento dos instrumentos em papel. Temos tambm presenciado uma maior preponderncia da tecnologia nos servios de pagamento e um maior foco na rapidez, convenincia e experincia dos utilizadores. Em 2019, acentuaram-se tambm algumas tendncias que at ento eram pouco marcadas.  o caso da utilizao dos pagamentos contacless e das compras online, que comearam a ser utilizados de forma mais significativa, com os consumidores a valorizarem cada vez mais a sua rapidez e convenincia. Os primeiros meses de 2020, com a evoluo da pandemia, vieram acentuar esta tendncia, com crescimentos assinalveis nas compras com carto efetuadas com recurso  tecnologia contactless e nas compras online, isto apesar de se ter verificado uma reduo sem precedentes nos pagamentos com carto. As compras com a tecnologia contactless aumentaram 60% em nmero, enquanto as compras online efetuadas aumentaram 11%, face ao perodo homlogo. Numa altura em que se tornou importante adotar medidas que contribussem para a conteno da COVID-19 e que pudessem assegurar o funcionamento da economia e a realizao de pagamentos num ambiente de maior distanciamento social, muitos consumidores optaram por efetuar as suas compras online e realizar os pagamentos atravs de cartes contactless (com o limite por operao a passar de 20 para 50) ou atravs do site do comerciante, do homebanking ou da app do seu banco. Desta forma, o facto dos consumidores portugueses terem  sua disposio solues de pagamentos digitais, resilientes, convenientes e seguras contribuiu inequivocamente para minimizar os impactos da COVID-19 no seu quotidiano. A realidade observada ao longo dos primeiros meses de 2020 pode sinalizar que a forma como pagaremos no futuro ser diferente daquela com que pagmos at 2019. Estas novas formas de comprar e pagar passaram a fazer parte do nosso dia-a-dia e  expectvel que, a partir deste momento, fiquem enraizadas nos hbitos dos consumidores. Como sempre, o Banco de Portugal, no cumprimento do seu mandato no mbito dos sistemas de pagamentos, est disponvel e proactivo no s para apoiar a atividade dos agentes econmicos em situaes excecionais como aquela que vivemos, mas tambm para responder aos desafios da transformao digital e promover o desenvolvimento de servios de pagamento mais inovadores, seguros e eficientes.

Title: Interview of the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, to expresso
text: Interview of the Governor, Carlos da... Interview of the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, to expresso 25 May. 2020 Do you get the feeling that your image will always be glued to these more negative aspects? My image will be associated with responding to the challenges, which were enormous. The response to the great financial crisis, the sovereign debt crisis, the republic's loss of market access. Then it was the facts related to the resolution of two banks  BES and Banif  and then the sale of Novo Banco, which resulted from that resolution. And now, at the end of his term, the crisis resulting from the covid-19 pandemic and that has major implications for the economy. And as the banking system is a reflection of the economy, it will also have major implications for banks if we do not know how to take the necessary measures. All negative aspects... What is negative or positive? The negative was if we had not safeguarded depositors' deposits  there was not a euro lost in depositors. The negative was if we had an interruption in the financing of the economy and the banks never had a situation where they could not respond to the credit request. Then we had no need to apply controls to capital movements, we had no depositors to put the money out of the country. If you look at financing the economy and the evolution of deposits and compare with the case of other euro area countries that have had problems of the same nature, they find that the confidence of depositors has remained intact, that business confidence in the ability of banks to provide credit has remained and, above all, that there has not been, in no way, capital flight. This is the great balance sheet of this period. In his words, it is a positive balance, but the image to which they often associate it is not that. Do you feel wronged? The criticism scares me only if they are made in the name of the general interest. If criticism is made in the name of private interests, I understand them, but I cannot accept them. If they were criticising me demonstrating that there was an alternative route with lower costs, I would have to recognise, in the name of the general interest, that it would have been better to be done. And there was no alternative? When you look back, don't you feel like you could have come another way? We've done better than the others we're compared to. We recapitalized through public loans that were repaid to the advantage of the State. We recapitalized with the obligation to reconstitute capital, as was the case with Banif  which failed for reasons that have nothing to do with Banco de Portugal. And we had to intervene in a situation where there was no capacity to recapitalise, which was the case with BES, whose alternatives were its liquidation or resolution. A much-criticized resolution... It was the only one that minimized costs for the economy, was the only one that safeguarded depositors and was the only one that insisted on a point that is the so-called cost-sharing by shareholders and senior creditors, according to the resolution rules. A solution whose recapitalisation is made by the banking system as a whole, through the Resolution Fund. As this is not capitalized, had to benefit from a state loan, but it is a loan that will be repaid over time, like any other loan. Do you think the criticisms they make to you are personal attacks? No. I think it is legitimate for particular interests to consider themselves affected and express that dissatisfaction. What particular interests? Imagine a shareholder. The shareholder of a Portuguese bank, a Spanish bank or a Greek bank naturally has a distinction on the day he is called upon to participate in the bank's bail in, i.e. in absorbing losses. Imagine great debtors who lived in a quiet peace with the banking system... it is natural that the process which led to clarification of the situation is not to your liking. But the criticism stemming from him was at the level of political agents... And they're perfectly acceptable. I live with them as long as the general interest that animates them is explained. I was the first to review if there was anything we could have done differently. Can you identify anything you would have done differently? When we passed the law on resolution, Banco de Portugal took on a burden it was not expecting to have. I think you should have done a rebalancing, but when you're in front, in the face of an emergency, you're not going to rethink what you have to do. Another example was the articulation between supervisors. I have always argued that it was possible to have a better articulation, but it depends on the ability of people and institutions to respond to this call. Today, the National Council of Financial Supervisors works in an exemplary way, and there has been no change, other than at the level of the people and the will of the institutions. On the other, the National Council for Financial Stability remains a sleeper entity. Depended on Banco de Portugal? No. Banco de Portugal does not convene this Council. Who summons you? The Ministry of Finance. It's not a criticism, it's just an aspiration. I always thought that the supervisory architecture needed (and needs) some reinforcements. This is contained in the document that Banco de Portugal delivered in due course and the organic bill that we delivered in 2012 to the Ministry of Finance. It is necessary that those who have the right powers have the right powers, under penalty of being held accountable for what they cannot guarantee. It says coordination between the various supervisors has improved. Interestingly, there were changes in the mandate in the other supervisors, but not at Banco de Portugal. Is this also the fruit of the people who were ahead of the other supervisors? It is the result of circumstances, of the fact that we are all too absorbed by current problems that did not give us the ability to reflect on what was important but that was not so urgent. And the fact that mistrust between institutions has been alleviated, which facilitates dialogue. There was some mistrust with the other supervisors when they were run by others... That's a good question. And it's coming from behind. This architecture was created before I got here. What happened was a kind of progressive desanuviamento, until we got to where we are. Today we have a permanent secretariat of the National Council of Financial Supervisors, we have a very active attitude of monitoring dialogue between the three supervisors and, to get an idea, we are holding weekly or fortnightly meetings to monitor the current crisis situation, which shows a close proximity. There were disagreements and animosity between Banco de Portugal and CMVM in the theme of ges' victims. Opinions on the solutions adopted differed greatly. Have was a greater articulation been important at that time? Banco de Portugal's position was the position that was confirmed in matters of judicial rights. We have always said that commercial paper was an issue that does not come from bank obligations. They were not the issuers of the securities, but rather the emitters of it. They were therefore not responsible, unless there was a so-called miss selling, an abusive sale. This was eventually generally accepted, and what happened afterwards was a solution, which I value, to find an answer to the dissatisfaction of the bearers of this commercial role that has nothing to do with the decisions of Banco de Portugal. The marketing of commercial paper is subject to market rules and is therefore subject to market surveillance in accordance with the law. Returning to the general balance sheet, what was the most difficult moment of your term? There were so many difficult moments... Can't you list it? Can. The first was when we began to feel that the adjustment programme was necessary, that we were approaching a risk of default of the Republic from January 2011. At that time I had a friend as finance minister [Teixeira dos Santos]. Was it easier? At that moment I was convinced that the Minister of Finance was as aware of the problem as I was, he obviously had limitations, which resulted from a different role that was his own, and was also looking for a solution. For example, when the presidents of the banks visited him, he invited me to be present, and this demonstrates a great convergence of concerns. The fact that throughout this process we have had the opportunity, on several occasions, to carry out reciprocal verification of information, means that we were aware. But everyone was playing their part. It will hardly go, the Bank of Portugal or the Ministry of Finance, if one of the actors replaces the other. It is necessary a dialectic and convergent views, but formed from different angles. Returning to the most difficult moments... The second moment is, of course, the negotiation of the economic and financial assistance programme. There were times when it was necessary to state before the troika that the proposal was not appropriate, there was some friction, not to say much friction. Fortunately, we were convincing. The third was when we had to check the situation of the banking system. Banks' balance sheets were reviewed through external audits, and it was in this context that capitalization needs were identified. The room is the moment when I see that the Espirito Santo Group, a non-financial area, was in enormous difficulties, and I have to decide the isolation to prevent the non-financial area from contagious and drag the bank. The fifth moment is when I notice, at the end of July 2014, that bes' problems were hidden and that they were of a totally unknown dimension to Banco de Portugal  and also by the Board of Directors and the external auditor. Another important moment, and it is on this same occasion, is when we discovered, through the National Bank of Angola, that the situation of BES Angola was very different from that reported to us. And then the resolution... The resolution, having been made with the creation of the transitional bank, will be seen as perhaps the one that has least impacted in terms of financial stability and the one that has most preserved both the financing of the economy and the confidence of depositors. Having a mark on the market on Monday and retaining the trust of depositors is a remarkable fact. It is true that it is a great challenge, because it is not easy to make a resolution with the creation of a transition bank. I very much doubt that the European resolution authority will ever want to go down this route, because it is very laborious, contrary to the solution found in other cases, such as the sale of the assets to another bank or simply the liquidation. At the bank, who else let you down? Those who took risks for which they had no capital or for which they had no mandate from shareholders. Were there too many? Some. Shareholders who were not consequential and who had a risk appetite for which they did not provide the capital. The fact that we had a system in which banks served as levers of inconsistent business projects raised major questions from the point of view of their solidity in a crisis situation. He had, therefore, many disappointments. I'd say I've had a lot of worries. Interestingly, these disappointments did not include politicians. As governor of Banco de Portugal he had three prime ministers. Which one gave you more leeway? The independence of Banco de Portugal does not depend on the design of room for manoeuvre. Have you ever felt that Banco de Portugal's independence was at stake during its mandates? Banco de Portugal's independence would only be at issue if I made Banco de Portugal's decision-making process subject to third parties. Haven't you ever felt your place at stake? The governor only leaves his seat either willingly or if he has made the mistakes that are foreseen and which have to be sanctioned in court. So you never thought about leaving? Of course i'm not. I have no reason to fear any kind of court decision about my performance, I am completely reassured. Did anyone advise you to slam the door, even in personal terms? No. It's only natural for my friends to say that it takes a lot of patience to bear some... It is natural for everyone to want to see if the reorientation of the bank goes in a different direction from that being pursued by the governor. But it is also natural that others have quietly said, "I hope he will keep." I had a mandate to exercise. On the day he decided to throw the towel on the floor he was proving that the independence of Banco de Portugal could be called into question by jeopardising the governor. The current prime minister, Antonio Costa, has always made a lot of point of saying publicly that he would not have reappointed him if he were prime minister at the time. Has this been reflected in your work in recent years? No, not at all. It is natural for a new prime minister to want a new governor, with a profile he thinks is appropriate. Nor do I consider this to be a demonstration of a willingness to subordination... that's what it is. I have a profile that is not, for some, so nice. That's life. We don't do any beauty or popularity contests here. Regarding the articulation that you say is necessary with the Ministry of Finance, did you feel that this second term was more complicated? I felt that in the moments when it was necessary to work together it was possible. Banif's resolution was made with this government. The sale of Novo Banco was made with this Government. In matters where it was necessary to amend legislation, the contributions of Banco de Portugal were made. The relationship between Banco de Portugal and the Government is not an echo chamber relationship. It is a dialogue structured according to problems and takes place whenever these problems require it. This Government has tried, and has already announced that it will try again, to change the legal framework of financial supervision and in some way also of Banco de Portugal. Do you feel that this Government has called into question the independence of Banco de Portugal? On the day the ECB delivered an opinion on the revision of the model of supervision of the financial system, the Government and its finance minister said they would take due account of that opinion. People do not know the framework that results from our participation in the European System of Central Banks and naturally tend to reflect more in a public administration framework than in a framework of relationship between independent entities. It's only natural. Was your relationship with Mario Centeno the same as your relationship with Teixeira dos Santos or Maria Luis Albuquerque? The institutional and personal relationship was the one that was imposed on each topic. Os bancos tm todo o interesse em conceder crdito, desde que esse crdito seja recupervel, e se no for recupervel ns no temos interesse que os concedam. O que temos de perguntar , porque  que o crdito, por vezes, no  concedido?

Title: Interview of the Administrator, Hlder Rosalino, to Antena 1 and the Business Journal
text: Interview of the Administrator, Elder... Interview of the Administrator, Helder Rosalino, to Antena 1 and the Business Journal 08 Jun 2020 Should the suspension of commissions for payment transactions through digital channels be prolonged? It is a measure of exceptional character, it was approved by decree-law of the Government, it is up to the Government to decide on the matter. But isn't it justified? Let's take a look. What is important is that the commissions are proportionate, transparent and appropriate to the service provided. Maintaining "ad eternum" the impossibility of charging commissions for online payments was to derail a business model of many entities that innovate, that bring solutions to consumers and that offer digital solutions and experiences to consumers. Could there be a middle ground? This is a matter of the market. We are in a market economy and the commissions that are charged by those who provide service must be proportionate to the service they provide and to the quality of the service they provide, they must be transparent and must comply with the regulations in force. And they were? They were, in general. We can discuss specific issues, but commissioning for these services is perfectly natural and it would be unthinkable that this commissioning did not exist because these entities, which are on the market, live from these commissioning. Is that the answer to what is now being discussed in the specialty about the limits to commissions on MBWay? It is a very sensitive topic and I would like not to do demagoguery in relation to the subject. MBWay is an extremely successful solution in Portugal. It grew 250% between 2018 and 2019 in terms of users. There are a very large number of MBWay users and it has been extremely innovative in Portugal. Initially it wasn't paid for. MBWay is a commercial solution developed by SIBS that did not charge for the application. What happened was a change in trade policy. Banks wanted to call MBWay traffic to their platforms and started charging for transactions that were made in the SIBS application, but most MBWay operations remain unpaid if it is done in bank applications. Now SIBS has done a very significant innovation work in this area. And get into that logic, a little demagogic, that you shouldn't charge for using MBWay, what are you going to do? First, it may hinder investment in innovation and the offer of new innovative solutions that generate value for consumers and citizens. On the other hand, there should not be a cross-subsidization, eventually paying itself otherwise. It is preferable for commissions to be known, for consumers to be able to negotiate and to be able to understand what is being charged. What's going on, okay? I do not discuss the value of commissions, perhaps there are banks that are charging commissions that should be lower. The BdP has also taken a stand on this matter, saying that commissions should be proportionate to the service, and there should be a scale effect, the more operations captured the lower the commission should be. Now, it is unreasonable to understand that innovative, value-added, value-added services that improve our experience and support business models cannot be charged. I do not enter into the demagoguery of thinking that commissions should be lower or higher, there should be transparency, proportionality and adequacy. SIBS is criticized, notably by fintech, for the "open banking" platform that they say is not open. Should the BdP work in this area? The BdP must not only act but it does. And we've been acting. SIBS is a key partner. SIBS's open banking solution was the majority of banks. There has indeed been criticism from some fintech stooes that they have not been called upon to define the requirements of this platform. We questioned SIBS who says it created this opportunity, fintech say that this opportunity was not given at the same level as the other credit institutions. Our opinion is that there was dialogue, we ourselves promoted dialogue between fintech and SIBS. Have you concluded that there is no unfair competition from SIBS because the banks are shareholders and customers? This is a theme that goes beyond the "open banking" solution. SIBS, what it has been telling us, is that it has opened its initiatives to fintech and that makes us comfortable because we know that happens. Of course, SIBS responds, above all and for the most part, to the demand of credit institutions. In the state of emergency it was advised to use the cards, namely "contactless", which even led to the increase of the plafond to 50 euros. What swing do you take? This period of confinement posed a great challenge to payment systems in Portugal. And, in fact, the investment made in Portugal in recent years, of modernization of the payment system, has now brought that return. It was possible to quickly increase payments through contactless, which went from the limit of 20 to 50 euros. And while card usage was declining, withdrawals were declining and purchases were declining, contactless usage increased by 123% in April. Likewise, online payments increased by 53%. This means that not only were the systems prepared to provide this response, but the authorities were able to adapt the systems, keep them running and create the features to meet this challenge, but users also had the ability to adapt. Is it a tendency to stay? We are convinced that this amendment will leave a mark and perhaps we will pay, from now on, in a different way. And, I would like to reinforce this idea, the payment systems in Portugal gave an excellent answer. Is the limit of 50 euros to maintain or was it only during the state of emergency? It was defined in legal diploma to take effect until the end of the first semester. But we're going to have to reevaluate. The change to the 20 euro limit was already being studied with the banking system and the entities representing traders because it was small, and in other countries it is already higher. We were already looking at increasing that limit and perhaps that has to go to the table in order to review that limit going forward. The average payment for "contactless" was around seven euros before this crisis, and has now passed to 21 euros, above the limit of 20 euros. Whose decision is up to? The decision rests with the financial system and the operators. There was legislative action by the Government in this context, but the limit of use is defined by the regulator, Banco de Portugal, and by the market. It's a matter that's going to have to be discussed between us. There are many cards that are not "contactless". Most cards already have the "contactless" technology, the payment terminals are the ones they didn't have. There is now a major reconversion of the terminals and therefore this is a theme that will be overcome. Are there any of these agents who are reticent? No, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, There is a great deal of consensus on this. Could the value be higher? More than 50 euros I think it will hardly be, because 50 euros is already quite reasonable. Will the cards necessarily be "contactless"? Very quickly all the cards will have. At this time between 70% and 80% of terminals already allow technology and cards at a higher percentage. So we're moving in that direction. Then the user's option is. The ECB has strengthened its emergency programme to respond to the economic impact caused by the pandemic. Is it right for the ECB to be acting in this way? The board of governors' decision was to add an additional 600 billion to the 750 billion that had been approved in this programme to support the crisis, the so-called PEPP. This program is of great importance, and it has been a very positive response. And once again, monetary policy has not defrauded expectations, it has lived up to expectations. Has the ECB lived up to expectations? Has. Once again it lived up to expectations now when many people thought that the ECB's toolbox and monetary policy was exhausted. The governing council of the ECB of the entire Eurosystem, and it must be remembered that in the council each governor has one vote, and they are all the same, answered once again. And this has allowed 10-year Portuguese government debt rates to recover to pre-crisis levels; and that there are negative rates until the maturity of the four years, and in the pre-crisis period we already had the lowest interest rates ever. Which means that this is actually enabling the economy to be financed. This public debt purchase program is accompanied by a liquidity-contracting program to the financial system. Of course banks are not giving money without control, they continue to assess customer risks. In other words, is the bank able to do so? You have conditions. This monetary policy has the mechanism of liquidity-decommitment at negative rates. Banks, delivering collateral, access central bank credit at negative rates. A liquidity-free-up programme is approaching that can have negative rates of 1%, i.e. banks finance themselves and still get paid for what they get from credit. This rate of 1% is only paid if there is a demonstration that this credit went to the economy, so negative remuneration is conditioned to ensure that there is monetary transmission to the economy. Mario Draghi argued that it should be lost. I don't know if he stands up for it. I don't think he ever defended that. Today rates are historically low, there have never been such low rates on access to credit by households and especially businesses, and therefore credit is very low and transmission is happening. Isn't banking taking advantage of these negative rates to have more margin in the credit it allocates? Banking only accesses these negative rates if it credits the economy. Of course, banking, by having interest rates on its financing much lower, the incentives it has is to grant credit at lower rates. Which isn't happening. So you're not? If I just said that rates are the lowest historically. "Spreads" that go in the house of 1% or 2% for companies are very low. Spreads are charged depending on the risk, and there must be a risk assessment in the middle. Not all businesses and households finance themselves at the same rate, it naturally depends on the risk they pose. Is the bank still doing business? I do not have the responsibility for supervision or prudential monitoring of the financial system, but in recent years the bank had returned to profits, today has several indicators that are better than in the past, liquidity ratios, capital ratios, profitability, return on assets. The system plays a key role. It has the advantage of having these lines of financing at much lower rates, but it also has the risks of the economic crisis that will affect the national economic fabric, which will certainly bring risks to the banking system. Has too much pressure been put on banking in this crisis? How did the bank respond? The bank responded very well. The bank was on the front line. There were a number of initiatives taken at legislative level but there was also a number of initiatives adopted by the bank itself. We are talking about the moratoriums, the public moratorium on housing credit to which more than 500,000 households have already joined, and private moratoriums, for consumer credit and for other areas of credit. And then the bank responded very positively, has fulfilled what was expected of the bank. Was the criticism unfair? There's always criticism. Some people always wait longer, some people don't have all the information. I think the banking did its part, the public authorities played their part on this matter the country gave a good response in various dimensions. Was the bank prepared for this shock? I was much more prepared now than in the previous crisis. The level of NPL (low) has dropped a lot, capital and liquidity ratios were much better and the country's economic situation, with successive economic growth in recent years and much easier financing, has had direct and beneficial effects on banking that was much better and is therefore also responding quite well in this context. Will there be private and public Portuguese debt to fulfill the capital key of Portugal? Yes, there will be. Portugal has 260 billion in debt. Banco de Portugal has more than 40 billion public debt on its balance sheet, and is already the largest individual lender in the state Portuguese. This represents 16% of total public debt. But the bank can only buy market-tradable debt, there is debt that is not tradable, notably from the institutional creditors who financed the adjustment plan and the aphorus certificates. Therefore, if we consider only tradable, the BdP has 25% of the public debt in its balance sheet, still far from 100%. So we have public debt to buy, and we are buying and fulfilling our role very well. We have been able to contribute to having historically low government interest rates. And that's very important. The State is financing itself at very low costs and this debt that is on our balance sheet allows the BdP, in which it has positive interest, to remunerate the shareholder. In the last four years, between dividends and taxes, it has delivered 3.5 billion euros to the shareholder, and much of that income comes from the government bonds it has. Are you going to keep going? We have a stock of government debt with positive, low but positive interest rates, so we will continue to have yields because the maturity of the debt in our balance sheet is 5, 6, 7 years and we will continue to have positive results from that debt. Now, what we are going to buy, if it is issued at negative interest, of course we will not have results, but this is very good for the state. We don't give you dividends, but the state, on the other hand, pays no interest. What if the Bundesbank leaves the asset purchase program because of the decision of the German Constitutional Court (TC) ? This is a topic that is still under legal debate. The CT decision did not affect compliance with the program. The decision was about the previous program and not on the path. But it can be extensible. Of course, it can be extended, although they are two different programs. This is a program to support a crisis, theoretically short-term, if it extends for many more years one can put the problem, but for now it does not arise. Isn't the ECB spilling its mandate? Who am I to say that. The Court of Justice of the European Union, which is to whom the ECB reports from the point of view of applicable jurisdiction, has already said that the ECB is acting within the mandate. The ECB has made several criticisms of the Government's proposed law on financial supervision, citing incompatibility with the European system of central banks, little clarity in the proposal and increased political pressure. Is there any more clarity in this proposal? The Government has made a proposal to change the supervisory architecture with changes to what is the mandate and organic law of the BdP and other regulators. The BdP issued an opinion, there were aspects that it thought should evolve in the sense that it was proposed, in others it thought they should have different developments. The ECB has delivered an opinion on this matter, the Government has taken good note of these opinions, there have been public interventions by the Ministry of Finance that it would take into account what the opinions of the ECB and the regulators who have been consulted on this matter are, and therefore this is in the sphere of the Ministry of Finance. I think there was a natural institutional dialogue between regulators and the government, of course the ECB also made the intervention it thought it should make, in defence of the independence of central banks, in defence of the mandate of central banks and the Eurosystem which is a mandate that requires strong independence. However the reform stopped. Is she buried for good? I have no idea. I assume that the Government and the authorities want to make an evolution of the institutional framework and some need for evolution is justified and the BdP has made contributions to this development. The fact that it is said that the Minister of Finance, Mario Centeno, could go to the BdP may have stopped the reform? I'm not going to talk about going from A, B or C to the BdP. I know exactly what my role is and my place. I don't do evaluations on that subject. But does it make sense for a minister to leave the government to take up a position in the BdP, namely governor or administrator? I'm not going into that debate. I've been well prepared not to answer those questions. His term ended in September. Is it a board of Banco de Portugal, is there a prospect of continuing in administration? I am a staff of the BdP and I am already doing 26 years of Banco de Portugal. I came as a technician, by public tender, I was core coordinator, area coordinator, deputy director, director, i went through several departments and several areas of central banking, I think I am a person who knows well the central bank in various dimensions. In the meantime I've been on the board of directors, and I didn't consider it to get me off my career in the BdP. Why hasn't it been replaced or renewed? There are contexts of prolongation to find the right moments to make recompositions on the board of directors. When can it happen? I have no idea, but of course it's going to have to work itself out. When he left the government , he returned to the BdP... For director. Shortly thereafter he was appointed administrator. Didn't you feel any kind of embarrassment because you had government functions? I didn't feel any embarrassment. I considered it to be an evolution within what was my central banking and public service skills. And above all I think I have a knowledge of various areas of central banking that make me useful in any circumstance and in any context to the BdP. Does the way the governor is appointed guarantee exemption? The BdP today has a very robust and very mature institutional framework. The dialogue is very intense with the public institutions, with the Government, so I think that appointments are made with great discretion, with a lot of demand, rigor and this dialogue requires. Don't you see any reason to change? There may be adjustments. But frankly, I don't have a structured idea about that. The requirements to be on the board of directors of the BdP are very great, it is necessary that they have a set of competences of various orders.

Entrevista do Administrador, Hlder Rosalino,  Antena 1 e ao Jornal de Negcios 08 jun. 2020 A suspenso de comisses de operaes de pagamento atravs dos canais digitais deve ser prolongada?  uma medida de carter excecional, foi aprovada por decreto-lei do Governo, compete ao Governo decidir sobre a matria. Mas j no se justifica? Vamos l ver. O que  importante  que as comisses sejam proporcionais, transparentes e adequadas ao servio prestado. Manter ad eternum a impossibilidade de cobrar comisses dos pagamentos online era inviabilizar um modelo de negcio de muitas entidades que inovam, que trazem solues para os consumidores e que oferecem solues e experincias digitais aos consumidores. Poderia haver um meio-termo? Isso  uma questo de mercado. Estamos numa economia de mercado e as comisses que so cobradas por quem presta servio tm de ser proporcionais ao servio que presta e  qualidade do servio que presta, tm de ser transparentes e tm de cumprir a regulamentao em vigor. E eram? Eram, em geral. Podemos discutir questes pontuais, mas o comissionamento por estes servios  perfeitamente natural e seria impensvel que esse comissionamento no existisse porque estas entidades, que esto no mercado, vivem desses comissionamentos.  essa a resposta para o que est agora a ser discutido na especialidade sobre os limites s comisses no MBWay?  um tema muito sensvel e eu gostaria de no fazer demagogia em relao ao tema. O MBWay  uma soluo extremamente bem-sucedida em Portugal. Cresceu 250% entre 2018 e 2019 em termos de utilizadores. H um nmero muito grande de utilizadores de MBWay e tem sido extremamente inovador em Portugal. Inicialmente no se pagava. O MBWay  uma soluo comercial desenvolvida pela SIBS que no cobrava pela aplicao. O que se verificou foi uma alterao de poltica comercial. Os bancos quiseram chamar o trfego do MBWay para as suas plataformas e passaram a cobrar as operaes que eram feitas na aplicao da SIBS, mas a maior parte das operaes do MBWay continua a no ser paga se for feita nas aplicaes dos bancos. Agora, a SIBS tem feito um trabalho de inovao neste domnio muito significativo. E entrar naquela lgica, um bocadinho demaggica, que no se deve cobrar pela utilizao do MBWay, o que vai fazer? Primeiro, pode inviabilizar o investimento na inovao e na oferta de novas solues inovadoras e geradoras de valor para o consumidor e cidado. Por outro lado, no deve  haver uma subsidiao cruzada, acabando por se pagar de outra maneira.  prefervel que as comisses sejam conhecidas, que o consumidor possa negociar e ter capacidade de perceber o que est a ser cobrado. O que est, est bem? Eu no discuto o valor das comisses, porventura h bancos que esto a cobrar comisses que deviam ser mais baixas. O BdP tambm j tomou posio sobre essa matria, dizendo que as comisses devem ser proporcionais ao servio, e haver efeito de escala, quanto mais operaes captadas mais baixa deve ser a comisso. Agora, no  razovel entender que servios inovadores, que tm valor acrescentado, que melhoram a nossa experincia e que suportam modelos de negcio no possam ser cobrados. No entro na demagogia de achar que as comisses devem ser mais baixas ou altas, deve  haver transparncia, proporcionalidade e adequao. A SIBS  criticada, nomeadamente pelas fintech, pela plataforma de open banking que dizem no estar aberta. O BdP devia atuar nessa rea? O BdP no s deve atuar como atua. E temos atuado. A SIBS  um parceiro fundamental. A soluo de open banking da SIBS teve a adeso da generalidade dos bancos. Efetivamente houve crticas por parte de algumas fintech no sentido de dizerem que no foram chamados para a definio dos requisitos dessa plataforma. Ns questionmos a SIBS que diz que criou essa oportunidade, as fintech dizem que essa oportunidade no foi dada ao mesmo nvel que s restantes instituies de crdito. A nossa opinio  de que houve dilogo, ns prprios promovemos dilogo entre as fintech e a SIBS. Concluram que no h concorrncia desleal da SIBS pelo facto de os bancos serem acionistas e clientes? Esse  um tema que vai alm da soluo de open banking. A SIBS, o que nos tem dito,  que tem aberto as suas iniciativas s fintech e isso deixa-nos confortveis porque sabemos que isso acontece. Evidentemente, a SIBS responde, sobretudo e maioritariamente,  procura das instituies de crdito. No estado de emergncia foi aconselhada a utilizao dos cartes, nomeadamente contactless, que at levou ao aumento do plafond para os 50 euros. Que balano faz? Este perodo de confinamento colocou um desafio muito grande aos sistemas de pagamento em Portugal. E, de facto, o investimento feito em Portugal nos ltimos anos, de modernizao do sistema de pagamentos, trouxe agora esse retorno. Foi possvel rapidamente incrementar os pagamentos atravs de contactless, que passou do limite de 20 para 50 euros. E enquanto a utilizao do carto estava a diminuir, os levantamentos estavam a diminuir e as compras estavam a diminuir, a utilizao do contactless aumentou 123% no ms de abril. Do mesmo modo, os pagamentos online aumentaram 53%. O que significa que no s os sistemas estavam preparados para dar esta resposta, como as autoridades tiveram capacidade de adaptar os sistemas, mantlos a funcionar e criar as funcionalidades para darem resposta a este desafio, como tambm os utilizadores tiveram a capacidade de se adaptar.  uma tendncia para ficar? Estamos convencidos de que esta alterao vai deixar marca e porventura vamos pagar, a partir de agora, de uma forma diferente. E, eu gostava de reforar esta ideia, os sistemas de pagamento em Portugal deram uma excelente resposta. O limite de 50 euros  para manter ou foi s durante o estado de emergncia? Foi definido em diploma legal para vigorar at ao final do primeiro semestre. Mas teremos de reavaliar. J estava a ser estudada, com o sistema bancrio e as entidades que representam os comerciantes, a alterao do limite dos 20 euros, porque era pequeno, e noutros pases j  superior. Estvamos j a estudar o aumento desse limite e, porventura, isso tem de ir para cima da mesa, no sentido de rever esse limite daqui para a frente. O pagamento mdio por contactless estava na casa dos sete euros antes desta crise, e agora passou para os 21 euros, acima do limite dos 20 euros. A deciso cabe a quem? A deciso cabe ao sistema financeiro e aos operadores. Houve uma atuao legislativa do Governo neste contexto, mas o limite da utilizao  definido pelo regulador, o Banco de Portugal, e pelo mercado.  uma matria que vai ter de ser discutida entre ns. H muitos cartes que no so contactless. A maioria dos cartes j tem a tecnologia contactless, os terminais de pagamento  que no tinham. Est a haver agora uma grande reconverso dos terminais e, portanto, este  um tema que vai ser ultrapassado. H alguns desses agentes que esteja reticente? No, no, no. H um grande consenso relativamente a esta matria. Poder ser superior o valor? Superior a 50 euros acho que dificilmente ser, porque 50 euros j  bastante razovel. Os cartes vo ser obrigatoriamente contactless? Muito rapidamente todos os cartes vo ter. Neste momento entre 70% e 80% dos terminais j permitem a tecnologia e os cartes numa percentagem maior. Portanto, estamos a caminhar nesse sentido. Depois, a opo  do utilizador. O BCE reforou o programa de emergncia para responder ao impacto econmico causado pela pandemia. Faz bem o BCE estar a atuar desta forma? Houve a deciso do conselho de governadores de acrescentar mais 600 mil milhes de euros aos 750 mil milhes de euros que tinham sido aprovados neste programa de apoio  crise pandmica, o chamado PEPP. Este programa  de grande importncia, e tem sido uma resposta muito positiva. E, mais uma vez, a poltica monetria no defraudou as expectativas, correspondeu s expectativas. O BCE tem correspondido s expectativas? Tem. Mais uma vez correspondeu s expectativas agora quando muita gente achava que a caixa de ferramentas do BCE e da poltica monetria estava esgotada. O conselho de governadores do BCE de todo o Eurosistema, e  preciso lembrar que no conselho cada governador tem um voto, e so todos iguais, respondeu mais uma vez. E isso permitiu que as taxas de dvida pblica portuguesa a 10 anos j tenham recuperado para nveis pr-crise; e que haja taxas negativas at  maturidade dos quatro anos, sendo que no perodo pr-crise j tnhamos as taxas de juro mais baixas de sempre. O que significa que isto est de facto a permitir financiar a economia. Este programa de compra de dvida pblica  acompanhado por um programa de cedncia de liquidez ao sistema financeiro. Naturalmente os bancos no esto a dar dinheiro sem controlo, continuam a avaliar os riscos dos clientes. Ou seja, a banca tem condies para o fazer? Tem condies. Esta poltica monetria tem o mecanismo de cedncia de liquidez a taxas negativas. Os bancos, entregando colaterais, acedem a crdito nos bancos centrais a taxas negativas. Aproxima-se um programa de cedncia de liquidez que pode ter taxas negativas de 1%, ou seja, os bancos financiam-se e ainda recebem por aquilo que obtm de crdito. Essa taxa de 1% s  paga se houver a demonstrao de que esse crdito foi para a economia, portanto, a remunerao negativa tem como condio garantir que h transmisso monetria  economia. Mario Draghi defendeu que devia ser a fundo perdido. No sei se ele defende isso. Eu acho que ele nunca defendeu isso. Hoje as taxas esto historicamente baixas, nunca houve taxas to baixas no acesso ao crdito por parte das famlias e sobretudo das empresas e, portanto, o crdito est muito baixo e a transmisso est a acontecer. A banca no se est a aproveitar dessas taxas negativas para ter mais margem no crdito que atribui? A banca s acede a essas taxas negativas se der crdito  economia. Evidentemente, a banca, ao ter taxas de juro no seu financiamento muito mais baixas, os incentivos que tem  para conceder crdito a taxas mais baixas. O que no est a acontecer. Ento no est? Se eu acabei de dizer que as taxas so as mais baixas historicamente. Spreads que andam na casa de 1% ou 2% para as empresas so muito baixos. Os spreads so cobrados em funo do risco, e tem de haver pelo meio uma avaliao de risco. Nem todas as empresas e famlias se financiam  mesma taxa, depende naturalmente do risco que representam. Ainda assim a banca est a fazer negcio? Eu no tenho a responsabilidade pela superviso nem pelo acompanhamento prudencial do sistema financeiro, mas a banca tinha, nos ltimos anos, voltado aos lucros, tem hoje vrios indicadores que esto melhores do que no passado, rcios de liquidez, rcios de capital, rentabilidade, retorno dos ativos. O sistema tem um papel fundamental. Tem a vantagem de ter estas linhas de financiamento a taxas muito mais baixas, mas tambm tem os riscos da crise econmica que vai afetar o tecido econmico nacional, que trar seguramente riscos para o sistema bancrio. Foi colocada demasiada presso sobre a banca nesta crise pandmica? Como  que a banca respondeu? A banca respondeu muito bem. A banca esteve na linha da frente. Houve um conjunto de iniciativas adotadas a nvel legislativo mas tambm houve um conjunto de iniciativas adotadas pela prpria banca. Estamos a falar das moratrias, na moratria pblica para o crdito  habitao a que j aderiram mais de 500 mil famlias, e as moratrias privadas, para o crdito ao consumo e para outros domnios do crdito. E a a banca respondeu de forma muito positiva, tem cumprido com aquilo que era esperado da banca. As crticas foram injustas? Crticas h sempre. H quem espere sempre mais, h quem no tenha toda a informao. Acho que a banca fez o seu papel, as autoridades pblicas fizeram o seu papel Sobre esta matria o pas deu uma boa resposta em vrias dimenses. A banca estava preparada para este choque? Estava muito mais preparada agora do que na crise anterior. O nvel de NPL (malparado) caiu bastante, os rcios de capital e de liquidez estavam bastante melhores e a situao econmica do pas, com crescimentos econmicos sucessivos nos ltimos anos e com muito mais facilidade de financiamento, tiveram efeitos diretos e benficos sobre a banca que estava bastante melhor e, por isso, est a responder tambm bastante bem neste contexto. Vai haver dvida portuguesa privada e pblica para cumprir a chave de capital de Portugal? Sim haver. Portugal tem 260 mil milhes de euros de dvida. O Banco de Portugal tem mais de 40 mil milhes de dvida pblica no balano,  j o maior credor individual do Estado portugus. Isto representa 16% do total da dvida pblica. Mas o banco s pode comprar dvida transacionvel em mercado, h dvida que no est transacionvel nomeadamente dos credores institucionais que financiaram o plano de ajustamento e os certificados de aforro. Portanto, se considerarmos s a transacionvel, o BdP tem 25% da dvida pblica no seu balano, ainda longe de 100%. Portanto, temos dvida pblica para comprar, e estamos a comprar e a cumprir muito bem o nosso papel. Temos conseguido contribuir para que tenhamos taxas de juro da dvida pblica historicamente baixas. E isso  muito importante. O Estado est a financiar-se a custos muito baixos e essa dvida que est no nosso balano permite ao BdP, naquela que tem juros positivos, remunerar o acionista. Nos ltimos quatro anos, entre dividendos e impostos, entregou 3,5 mil milhes de euros ao acionista, e grande parte desse rendimento vem dos ttulos de dvida pblica que tem. Vai continuar? Temos um stock de dvida pblica com taxas de juro positivas, baixas mas positivas, portanto, vamos continuar a ter rendimentos porque a maturidade da dvida no nosso balano anda nos 5, 6, 7 anos e vamos continuar a ter resultados positivos provenientes dessa dvida. Agora, a que vamos comprar, se for emitida a juros negativos, evidentemente no vamos ter resultados, mas isso  muito bom para o Estado. No lhe entregamos em dividendos mas o Estado, por outro lado, no paga juros. E se o Bundesbank sair do programa de compra de ativos por causa da deciso do Tribunal Constitucional (TC) alemo? Esse  um tema que ainda est em debate jurdico. A deciso do TC no afetou o cumprimento do programa. A deciso foi sobre o programa anterior e no sobre o pandmico. Mas pode ser extensvel. Claro, pode-se estender, embora sejam dois programas diferentes. Este  um programa para apoiar uma crise, teoricamente de curto prazo, se se estender por muitos mais anos pode-se colocar o problema, mas para j no se coloca. O BCE no est a extravasar o seu mandato? Quem sou eu para dizer isso. O Tribunal de Justia da Unio Europeia, que  a quem o BCE reporta do ponto de vista de jurisdio aplicvel, j disse que o BCE est a atuar dentro do mandato. O BCE fez vrias crticas  proposta de lei do Governo sobre a superviso financeira, referindo incompatibilidade com o sistema europeu de bancos centrais, pouca clareza na proposta e aumento de presso poltica. Faz falta mais clareza nesta proposta? O Governo fez uma proposta de alterao da arquitetura de superviso com alteraes naquilo que  o mandato e a lei orgnica do BdP e de outros reguladores. O BdP emitiu um parecer, houve aspetos que achou que deviam evoluir no sentido em que era proposto, noutros achou que deviam ter evoluo diferente. O BCE emitiu parecer sobre esta matria, o Governo tomou boa nota desses pareceres, houve intervenes pblicas do Ministrio das Finanas de que iria levar em considerao aquilo que eram os pareceres do BCE e dos reguladores que foram consultados sobre esta matria, e portanto isso est na esfera do Ministrio das Finanas. Acho que houve um dilogo institucional natural entre reguladores e o Governo, naturalmente o BCE tambm fez a interveno que achou que devia fazer, na defesa da independncia dos bancos centrais, na defesa do mandato dos bancos centrais e do Eurosistema que  um mandato que exige uma forte independncia. Entretanto a reforma parou. Est enterrada de vez? No fao ideia. Presumo que o Governo e as autoridades queiram fazer uma evoluo do quadro institucional e alguma necessidade de evoluo justifica-se e o BdP deu contributos para essa evoluo. O facto de se falar que o ministro das Finanas, Mrio Centeno, poder ir para o BdP pode ter travado a reforma? Eu no vou falar sobre a ida de A, B ou C para o BdP.  uma matria em que no me compete entrar nessas avaliaes. Eu sei bem qual  o meu papel e o meu lugar. Eu no fao avaliaes sobre essa matria. Mas faz sentido que um ministro saia do Governo para assumir um cargo no BdP, nomeadamente de governador ou administrador? No vou entrar nesse debate. Venho bem preparado para no responder a essas perguntas. O seu mandato terminou em setembro.  quadro do Banco de Portugal, h perspetiva de continuar na administrao? Sou quadro do BdP e j estou a fazer 26 anos de Banco de Portugal. Entrei como tcnico, por concurso pblico, fui coordenador de ncleo, coordenador de rea, diretor adjunto, diretor, percorri vrios departamentos e vrias reas da banca central, acho que sou uma pessoa que conhece bem a banca central nas vrias dimenses. Entretanto passei a desempenhar funes no conselho de administrao e no considerei que isso me desviasse do meu percurso do BdP. Encarei toda a minha carreira no BdP, incluindo este meu mandato, como uma linha de continuidade. No foi entretanto substitudo ou renovado porqu? H contextos de prolongamento para encontrar os momentos certos para fazer recomposies no conselho de administrao. Quando poder acontecer? No fao ideia, mas evidentemente ter de se resolver. Quando saiu do Governo regressou ao BdP... Para diretor. Pouco tempo depois foi nomeado administrador. No sentiu qualquer tipo de constrangimentos por ter tido funes governativas? No senti qualquer constrangimento. Considerei que era uma evoluo dentro daquilo que eram as minhas competncias de banca central e de prestao de servio pblico. E sobretudo acho que tenho um conhecimento de vrias reas de banca central que me tornam til em qualquer circunstncia e em qualquer contexto ao BdP. A forma como o governador  nomeado garante iseno? O BdP hoje tem um quadro institucional muito robusto e muito maduro. O dilogo  muito intenso com as instituies pblicas, com o Governo, portanto acho que as nomeaes so feitas com muito critrio, com muita exigncia, rigor e esse dilogo exige. No v razo para mudar? Pode haver ajustamentos. Mas francamente no tenho uma ideia estruturada sobre essa matria. As exigncias para se estar no conselho administrao do BdP so muito grandes,  necessrio que tenham um conjunto de competncias de diversas ordens.

Title: Intervention of Administrator Hlder Rosalino at the opening of the Interbank Meeting on Payment Systems
text: Intervention of the Administrator Helder... Intervention of Administrator Helder Rosalino at the opening of the Interbank Meeting on Payment Systems 19 Jun 2020 Interbank meeting. Banco de Portugal highlighted a very positive response from payment service providers in the context of the pandemic See statement I would like to begin by welcoming everyone present at this first Interbank Meeting on Payment Systems that Banco de Portugal promotes in 2020. In view of the circumstances we are experiencing in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, this is also the first time that Banco de Portugal has held such a meeting remotely. In fact, the period we are going through, and in particular the stage in which the State of Emergency, has put to the test the different sectors of economic activity in general and infrastructure and the provision of payment services in particular. The continued availability and efficient functioning of payment systems and services is essential so that different economic operators can continue to develop their activities with maximum confidence, not only in periods of stability but, above all, in public health emergencies such as the current one. In this very adverse environment, payment services have responded to users' concerns with resilience, convenience and security. There have been significant developments in the behaviour of the various payment market players, both in terms of supply and demand for payment services, during this period. New habits have been created that, predictably, could be consolidated in the future. For example, trends have been accentuated so far with little marked with regard to the use of immediate transfers, contactless technology (whether through cards or apps) and online operations, the result of their convenience in a context of social distancing. To increase the use of technology contributed to a large extent to the increase in the ceiling per operation from EUR 20 to EUR 50. Portugal pioneered this amendment, which was later widely adopted by other European countries and even recommended by the European Banking Authority (EBA). This was a very positive initiative of the national community, which easily took root in the day-to-day life of consumers and traders. However, the main focus of this meeting is to update initiatives and projects in the area of payments, which despite the pandemic context, have evolved: on the one hand, RTGS services and, on the other hand, the implementation of strong customer authentication requirements and common and secure communication under the revised Payment Services Directive (DSP2). The last Interbank Meeting was held by Banco de Portugal last November, when these topics were already addressed, and it is important to note the developments that have occurred in the meantime. Firstly, in the context of the Eurosystem projects, it is worth noting the development of the work of the Portuguese community with a view to linking the national system to the European SERVICE TIPS (TARGET Instant Payment Settlement), as well as the evolution of TARGET services, a structuring project for the banking community in Europe, which introduces significant changes in the "backbone" of the financial system. Given its nature, the project presents significant risks - institutions that are not properly prepared will have their activity conditioned by the fact that they lose access to central bank currency  but it is also a unique opportunity to modernise internal applications and optimize processes. Given the criticality of the project and the need for all participants to be on board, combined with the impacts of COVID-19, which forced institutions to give priority to "run the institution" over "change the institution", the market has called for a postponement of the implementation date. As of today, the Eurosystem has not yet taken a decision, which is why it is important to remember that, even if there is a postponement, the pace of work should be maintained in order to minimise risks and take advantage of any time buffers to make the most of the opportunities offered by the project. Secondly, almost nine months after the entry into force of the technical requirements resulting from the Revised Payment Services Directive (DSP2), it is now important to take a brief assessment of the implementation of strong customer authentication and common and secure communication. In particular, it is important to systematize situations that still need action by payment and monitoring service providers by Banco de Portugal. In this context, the supervisory flexibility provided for by the EBA is particularly notet, which has allowed national competent authorities to monitor full compliance with strong authentication requirements in online card payment transactions by 31 December 2020. This process involves efforts by payment service providers and users (notably merchants), efforts that Banco de Portugal has been closely monitoring, interacting bilaterally with the different actors and, multilaterally, through the Payment Systems Forum. Without further ado, we will then follow the agenda. We thank you once again for your presence and the interest shown in the topics proposed for this session. Interbank meeting. BdP highlighted very positive response from payment service providers in the context of the pandemic
text_original: Interveno do Administrador Hlder... Interveno do Administrador Hlder Rosalino na abertura da Reunio Interbancria sobre Sistemas de Pagamentos 19 jun. 2020 Reunio interbancria. De facto, o perodo que atravessamos, e em particular a fase em que vigorou o Estado de Emergncia, colocou  prova os diferentes setores da atividade econmica, em geral, e as infraestruturas e a prestao de servios de pagamento, em particular. Em segundo lugar, decorridos praticamente nove meses desde a entrada em vigor dos requisitos tcnicos resultantes da Diretiva de Servios de Pagamento revista (DSP2), importa agora realizar um breve balano no que se refere  implementao da autenticao forte do cliente e da comunicao comum e segura. Em particular, importa sistematizar as situaes que ainda carecem de ao por parte dos prestadores de servios de pagamento e de monitorizao por parte do Banco de Portugal. Neste contexto, assume particular destaque a flexibilidade supervisiva prevista pela EBA, que veio permitir s autoridades competentes nacionais monitorizar o pleno cumprimento dos requisitos de autenticao forte nas operaes de pagamento online com carto at 31 de dezembro de 2020. Este processo implica esforos pelos prestadores de servios de pagamento e pelos utilizadores (designadamente comerciantes), esforos esses que o Banco de Portugal tem vindo a acompanhar muito de perto, interagindo bilateralmente com os diferentes intervenientes e, de forma multilateral, atravs do Frum para os Sistemas de Pagamentos. Sem mais demoras, seguiremos ento a ordem dos trabalhos. Agradecemos mais uma vez a vossa presena e o interesse demonstrado nos temas propostos para esta sesso. Reunio interbancria.
