Title: Article by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in Reuters: Time to collectively repair the pipelines while we have an umbrella
text: Article by Governor Carlos da Silva... Article by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in Reuters: Time to collectively repair the pipelines while we have an umbrella 08 Jul. 2020 The pandemic crisis will have a profound impact on the world economy. Its duration and size are still surrounded by great uncertainty. Although temporary, this shock risks leaving long-lasting scars if policymakers and authorities do not coordinate their responses. To an exogenous shock common to all economies, authorities initially responded uncoordinatedly. As the virus spread and the economic consequences of the pandemic became clear, efforts were deployed to coordinate policy response, but so far the burden has lain mostly on individual nations. Monetary policy eased significantly, cushioning the impact of the shock by providing ample liquidity. Labour market policies, payment moratoria and government guarantees on loans to corporates, among others, have been deployed across countries. Regulators and supervisors have adopted complementary measures exploring the flexibility of the existing regulatory framework to mitigate the immediate impact on banks balance sheets. The impact of the adopted policies will be a function of the structural features of the economies productive sectors, the liquidity and solvency positions of economic agents, the available fiscal space, as well as timing and policymakers clairvoyance (linked to the timely identification of problems, quality of policies and sufficiency of response). A clear distinction needs to be made across four stages of policies: (i) relief (payment moratoria), (ii) repair (recapitalisation of viable firms), (iii) recover (launch of domestic demand and productive investment), and (iv) reorient (towards sustainable and digital development). As economies emerge from the pandemic, pre-existing financial vulnerabilities will be compounded by additional public and private sector debt ensuing from policy action. Corporate and household debt burdens risk becoming unmanageable in case of severe economic contraction, putting at stake their solvency. Authorities and policymakers should make use of the oxygen balloon created by payment moratoria and regulators flexibility to implement solutions to reduce insolvency risks. In the European context, the Next Generation EU proposal is timely and goes in the right direction. However, it raises important challenges to companies and banks asset quality as it aims to reorient the economy but fails to timely support the repair and recovery stages: we will not be able to reorient business models if in the meantime companies go bankrupt. As the IMF recently noted, policy support will need to gradually shift toward encouraging people to return to work, and to facilitating a reallocation of workers to sectors with growing demand and away from shrinking sectors. Policy options need to be exploited to prevent the current corporate liquidity crisis from evolving into an insolvency crisis: avoiding the zombification of companies and of the labour market is now of the essence. Before policymakers unwind measures adopted at the peak of the crisis, solutions need to be implemented to enable the capitalisation of companies and avoid cliff effects. Proposals have been put forward comprising the possibility to convert government guaranteed credit into equity or quasi-equity in the form of preferred shares or, for privately held firms, higher profit taxes in the future. Options to identify and triage unviable firms deserve careful consideration while mitigating risks to labour markets and social cohesion. For unviable firms, expedited insolvency procedures should be implemented to preserve value. At European level, these solutions need to be coordinated under the auspices of the Capital Markets Union development so as to avoid national solutions protecting local firms and economic sectors that would risk the singleness of the EU market. On the banking sector the impact will reverberate through asset quality dynamics with increased non-performing loan ratios. Systemic TARP-style solutions will be required at European level, even if implemented at national level. These will require additional flexibility concerning the interplay between state aid and the Bank Recovery and Resolution Directive compatible with the challenge at hand. Moral hazard issues related to pre-pandemic risk-taking behaviour will arise and need to be addressed politically as a means to gain trust to reinvigorate the Banking Union project. Unless Member States address this as a matter of urgency, we risk a repeat of the discussions post-sovereign debt crisis, with the ensuing consequences to the economic recovery and trust in European institutions, already stressed by the health crisis response. Notwithstanding the improvements observed in the European banking system postglobal financial crisis, the situation is uneven across countries. As asset quality and profitability deteriorate, over-capacity will reveal itself amid a renewed push for digital solutions fast forwarded by the lockdown period. In this context, to preserve (local) financial stability efforts must be made to establish an enabling European framework for the orderly management of failing banks of locally systemic importance, combining elements of the resolution and liquidation frameworks, with a view to minimising losses and protecting depositors and non-financial borrowers. Such a framework should include the definition of high-level principles to be agreed by all Member States for application at national level. For those banks assessed as not having (European) public interest, there should be room for manoeuvre in view of national preferences. Recourse to alternative measures as foreseen in the Directive on Deposit Guarantee Schemes or to public funds, as an ultimate backstop, should be thus considered. Without risk-sharing and pan-European banks, sovereigns need to find the means to protect competition in their local markets and to safeguard the flow of funding to the economy in the event branches and subsidiaries of foreign banks exit during a downturn. Such options should be clearly decoupled from (past) bailout discussions and the ensuing political and social consequences. Few things can be more destructive to public trust in European institutions than threats to financial stability, and Member States can only avoid jeopardising European social and political cohesion by acting pre-emptively. Confronted with a storm, we were able to take shelter (relief) but we now need to repair the damage and ensure that we are able to recover and reorient the economies to weather new storms. As we did not finish repairing the roof when the sun was shining, let us now collectively repair the pipelines while we have an umbrella, so as not to stifle the recovery.

Title: Interview of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, to the Business Journal
text: Interview of the Deputy Governor, Luis... Interview of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, to the Business Journal 13 jul. 2020 Maximo dos Santos, deputy governor of Banco de Portugal (BdP), says that the new financial crisis, caused by the pandemic, could lead the Portuguese to increase savings levels, as has happened in other situations of financial stress. However, he warns, this "crisis is special", not excluding the possibility of witnessing the so-called "savings paradox", in what could be detrimental to the economy. "Consumption will tend to be curbed and the precautionary reason is already being felt, for example, in the increase in bank deposits. It's nothing new: already in the financial crisis the Portuguese adopted prudent financial behavior stemming from uncertainty about the future, reducing expenses and increasing savings levels," says Maximo dos Santos, in a written interview with Negocios, when asked about whether the pandemic will bring an increase in the savings levels of the Portuguese. A growth that the head of the BdP considers to be positive. "The low savings rate has long been one of the problems identified in our economy, as it hinders investment and fosters indebtedness. Therefore, the increase in savings is a positive thing," he says. But he warns: "This crisis is very special. In the face of the climate of widespread fear about the economic future, it cannot be excluded that the situation known as the saving paradox occurs. For this also, public economic stimulus is central to this crisis." The term of economist John Maynard Keynes means that if everyone decides to save at the same time, because there is uncertainty about the future, the fall in demand and the effects on consumption will paradoxically reduce savings. This behavior ends up being detrimental to the economy, since with more savings, there is less consumption of business goods. The latest oecd/INFE 2020 international survey on adult financial literacy shows that national performance shows greater stress and financial concern (with the payment of bills or that money is not enough, for example) and less proactivity in the application of savings than the average of participating countries. Among the interviewees, 63.5% show proactivity in the application of savings, according to the survey results released at the end of June by the BdP. "Despite having greater concern about the payment of bills or that money is not sufficient and less proactivity in the application of savings, Portugal has achieved above-average results with regard to systematic control of personal finances, weighting of expenses, timely payment of accounts, setting long-term financial objectives and not using credit to make ends meet expenses", says Maximus of Saints. Portugal ranked 7th in the global financial literacy indicator in the 2020 international survey on adult financial literacy promoted by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development's International Network on Financial Education in 26 countries. For the deputy governor, "the results achieved by Portugal in this survey are undoubtedly very positive for the country and constitute an additional stimulus to continue a work that is fundamental, that has to be permanent and in which there is much to do". Portugal comes in 5th place in the indicator of financial attitudes, occupying the same position in the indicator of financial behaviors. In the area of financial knowledge it ranks 16th. "The promotion of information and financial training has been assumed for several years now as a key pillar of behavioral supervision of retail banking markets," he says. A bet that guarantees that will remain despite the departure of Carlos Costa from the office of governor after a term of a decade. "It is a strategic institutional option shared internationally and, therefore, it is beyond personal contingencies," says Maximo dos Santos, refusing to comment on the possibility of Mario Centeno playing this role. Banking is facing a "very difficult and demanding job" in the face of the new financial crisis caused by the pandemic. The opinion is of Maximo dos Santos, deputy governor of Banco de Portugal, in a written interview with Negocios. The person in charge notes, however, that the sector is now better prepared to overcome this obstacle and adjust to a new reality than before, in a period when it eventually accelerated the scanning process. "Prepared for a crisis with these characteristics no one was. Adjusting to the crisis is an inevitability and a condition to overcome it", begins by saying Maximo dos Santos, when asked by Negocios about whether the bank is prepared to adjust and overcome the new crisis. "But, as I myself have signed on another occasion, it will be a very difficult and demanding job, although the starting point is undeniably better and some lessons from past crises have certainly been learned," says the official. The authorities have taken a number of measures to support banks and allow them to be able to lend to the economy, either by easing the rules around capital ratios or recommendations so that dividends are not distributed for now. On the other hand, the Government also advanced with credit moratoriums with the aim of supporting families and companies most penalized by the pandemic, allowing to postpone, until March 31, 2021, the payment of debts to financial institutions. This was also an oxygen balloon for the banking sector. The banks themselves are already preparing for possible future losses by setting aside more than 200 million in provisions in the first quarter. This is at a time when financial institutions have also had to focus even more on digitisation, promoting the use of digital channels with customers who have been confined due to the pandemic. This is an evolution that requires a greater focus on the digital financial education of bank customers in the face of the risk of cyber-attacks. "Digital channels (online and mobile/apps) facilitate access to financial products and services and have proved essential in the current context of pandemic and the need for social distancing, even though credit institutions have always maintained public service. From this point of view, the pandemic accentuated a trend that was already unstoppable," says Maximo dos Santos to Business. "We all know, however, that the use of digital channels has also associated a number of risks," including cyber-attacks, he adds. "Financial training in the digital domain is therefore fundamental and Banco de Portugal is well aware of this," he says, recalling that some steps have already been taken to promote digital financial education through campaigns and the Banking Customer Portal. "Of course, there are still small steps on a very long way to obtain acceptable parameters of digital financial education," he says. Asked whether the portuguese's digital financial education is sufficient at a time when the number of cyberattacks increases, Maximo dos Santos says that "affirmatively answering this question would be a total mystification", since "cyberattacks are one of the great problems of our time". These "pose issues that go far beyond financial education, although this is also fundamental in the context of its prevention", he concludes.
text_original: Entrevista do Vice-Governador, Lus... Entrevista do Vice-Governador, Lus Mximo dos Santos, ao Jornal de Negcios 13 jul. 2020 Mximo dos Santos, vice-governador do Banco de Portugal (BdP), afirma que a nova crise financeira, provocada pela pandemia, poder levar os portugueses a aumentarem os nveis de poupana, tal como tem acontecido noutras situaes de stress financeiro. No entanto, alerta, esta crise  especial, no excluindo a possibilidade de se vir a assistir ao chamado paradoxo da poupana, naquele que poder ser um comportamento prejudicial para a economia. O consumo tender a ser refreado e o motivo precauo j est a sentir-se, por exemplo, no aumento dos depsitos bancrios. No  nenhuma novidade: j na crise financeira os portugueses adotaram comportamentos financeiros prudentes perante a incerteza quanto ao futuro, reduzindo as despesas e aumentando os nveis de poupana, afirma Mximo dos Santos, numa entrevista por escrito ao Negcios, quando questionado sobre se a pandemia trar um aumento dos nveis de poupana dos portugueses. Um crescimento que o responsvel do BdP considera ser positivo. A baixa taxa de poupana  h muito um dos problemas identificados na nossa economia, pois dificulta o investimento e fomenta o endividamento. Logo, a subida da poupana  algo positivo, refere. Mas deixa um alerta: Esta crise  muito especial. Face ao clima de medo generalizado sobre o futuro econmico, no  de excluir que ocorra a situao conhecida por paradoxo da poupana. Tambm por isso, os estmulos econmicos de carter pblico so centrais nesta crise. O termo do economista John Maynard Keynes significa que se todos decidirem poupar ao mesmo tempo, porque h incerteza em relao ao futuro, a queda da procura e os efeitos no consumo acabaro, paradoxalmente, por reduzir as poupanas. Este comportamento acaba por ser prejudicial para a economia, j que com mais poupana, h menos consumo dos bens das empresas. O mais recente inqurito internacional  literacia financeira dos adultos 2020 da OCDE/INFE mostra que o desempenho nacional revela maior stress e preocupao financeira (com o pagamento das contas ou que o dinheiro no seja suficiente, por exemplo) e menor proatividade na aplicao de poupana do que a mdia dos pases participantes. Entre os entrevistados, 63,5% mostram proatividade na aplicao da poupana, de acordo com os resultados do inqurito divulgados no final de junho pelo BdP. Apesar de ter maior preocupao com o pagamento das contas ou que o dinheiro no seja suficiente e menor proatividade na aplicao da poupana, Portugal obteve resultados acima da mdia no que se refere ao controlo sistemtico das finanas pessoais,  ponderao das despesas, ao pagamento atempado das contas,  definio de objetivos financeiros de longo prazo e  no utilizao de crdito para fazer face a despesas quotidianas, diz Mximo dos Santos. Portugal ficou em 7. lugar no indicador global de literacia financeira no inqurito internacional  literacia financeira dos adultos 2020 promovido pela International Network on Financial Education da Organizao para a Cooperao e Desenvolvimento Econmico junto de 26 pases. Para o vice-governador, os resultados alcanados por Portugal nesse inqurito so indiscutivelmente muito positivos para o pas e constituem um estmulo adicional para continuar um trabalho que  fundamental, que tem de ser permanente e em que h muito para fazer. Portugal surge em 5. lugar no indicador de atitudes financeiras, ocupando a mesma posio no indicador de comportamentos financeiros. Na vertente de conhecimentos financeiros ocupa a 16. posio. A promoo da informao e da formao financeira foi assumida h j vrios anos como um pilar fundamental da superviso comportamental dos mercados bancrios de retalho, refere. Uma aposta que garante que se vai manter apesar da sada de Carlos Costa do cargo de governador depois de um mandato de uma dcada.  uma opo institucional estratgica partilhada internacionalmente e, portanto, est para l das contingncias pessoais, diz Mximo dos Santos, recusando-se a comentar a possibilidade de Mrio Centeno vir a desempenhar este papel. A banca tem pela frente um trabalho muito difcil e exigente perante a nova crise financeira provocada pela pandemia. A opinio  de Mximo dos Santos, vice-governador do Banco de Portugal, numa entrevista por escrito ao Negcios. O responsvel nota, ainda assim, que o setor est hoje mais bem preparado para superar este obstculo e ajustar-se a uma nova realidade do que antes, num perodo em que acabou por acelerar o processo de digitalizao. Preparado para uma crise com estas caractersticas ningum estava. Ajustar-se  crise  uma inevitabilidade e uma condio para a superar, comea por dizer Mximo dos Santos, quando questionado pelo Negcios sobre se a banca est preparada para se ajustar e superar a nova crise. Mas, como eu prprio j assinalei noutra ocasio, vai ser um trabalho muito difcil e exigente, embora o ponto de partida seja inegavelmente melhor e algumas lies de crises passadas tenham certamente sido aprendidas, afirma ainda o responsvel. As autoridades tm adotado vrias medidas para apoiar os bancos e permitir que estes tenham capacidade para emprestar  economia, seja atravs da flexibilizao das regras em torno dos rcios de capital ou das recomendaes para que no sejam, por agora, distribudos dividendos. Por outro lado, o Governo tambm avanou com moratrias no crdito com o objetivo de apoiar as famlias e empresas mais penalizadas pela pandemia, permitindo adiar, at 31 de maro de 2021, o pagamento das dvidas junto das instituies financeiras. Este foi tambm um balo de oxignio para o setor bancrio. Os prprios bancos j se esto a preparar para eventuais perdas futuras, ao terem colocado de parte mais de 200 milhes de euros em provises no primeiro trimestre. Isto num perodo em que as instituies financeiras tiveram tambm de apostar ainda mais na digitalizao, promovendo a utilizao dos canais digitais junto dos clientes que estiveram confinados devido  pandemia. Uma evoluo que obriga a uma maior aposta na educao financeira digital dos clientes bancrios, perante o risco de ciberataques. Os canais digitais (online e mobile/apps) facilitam o acesso aos produtos e servios financeiros e revelaram-se essenciais no atual contexto de pandemia e de necessidade de distanciamento social, ainda que as instituies de crdito tenham mantido sempre o atendimento ao pblico. Desse ponto de vista, a pandemia acentuou uma tendncia que era j imparvel, diz Mximo dos Santos ao Negcios. Todos sabemos, no entanto, que a utilizao de canais digitais tem tambm associado um conjunto de riscos, nomeadamente os ciberataques, acrescenta. A formao financeira no domnio digital , pois, fundamental e o Banco de Portugal est bem consciente disso, refere, relembrando que j foram dados alguns passos para promover a educao financeira digital, atravs de campanhas e do Portal do Cliente Bancrio. Como  bvio, so ainda pequenos passos de um caminho muito longo para obtermos parmetros aceitveis de educao financeira digital, diz. Questionado sobre se a educao financeira digital dos portugueses  suficiente num momento em que aumenta o nmero de ciberataques, Mximo dos Santos diz que responder afirmativamente a essa pergunta seria uma total mistificao, j que os ciberataques so um dos grandes problemas do nosso tempo. Estes colocam questes que vo muito para alm da educao financeira, embora esta tambm seja fundamental no contexto da sua preveno, conclui.

Title: Interview with Governor Carlos da Silva Costa by David Marsh, Chairman, OMFIF
text: Interview with Governor Carlos da Silva Costa by David Marsh, Chairman, OMFIF 17 Jul. 2020 David Marsh: Thank you for agreeing to this conversation, Mr Governor. You are within a few weeks of stepping down from your post as governor of the central bank and a member of the Governing Council of the European Central Bank. You have seen a lot in this time. How would you say that this crisis is different from the one in Europe in 2010- 15? What lessons have we learned? speed for different countries. It first hit the northern countries, with a savings surplus, because they invested a lot in American paper and junk bonds. The first banks hit were from the UK, Belgium, the Netherlands, France and Germany. Only after we had the second wave did it hit the southern banks, because they were unable to access the capital markets. The third wave was the sovereign crisis affecting countries with high debts and deficits. DM: And now we have a crisis that impacts all countries at the same time CC: An external shock, not an economic or financial shock, impacting first the sanitary conditions, then the supply side through policies to contain contagion, then cash flows and income, and then demand. In parallel, we have seen an impact on the financial sector because as people were unable to reimburse capital or to pay interest, which led to wise decisions to accept moratoria on interest payments and reimbursements. The impact depended on the measures taken by policy-makers: on moratoria, on incomes, through short-time working (layoffs to preserve production capacity), and on state budgets. DM: A symmetrical shock, but with asymmetric effects. Are you worried that different countries in Europe will recover at different rates? Some countries have much more financial firepower, and they can expand their budget deficits much more quickly than other countries? CC: I'm very concerned. First, on the sanitary level. If the answer is not the right one, as it is a common threat, the problem will stay at the level of the weakest link in the chain. We cannot save ourselves if others are not safe. Second, if we don't take into account that public money is needed to preserve social cohesion and the social fabric, we will create a lasting problem. If countries exit from the crisis at a different pace and with different levels of social cohesion and economic force, it will have a great impact in political terms, because it will feed populism  a big risk to the acceptance of the European Union. If you compare the costs, solidarity will be cheaper than the opportunity cost of breaking supply chains, breaking the internal market and breaking social solidarity. DM: How important is it to make sure that the European Central Bank acts in a complementary way with fiscal policies? CC: Central bank action, during the last 10 years, has been essential. In the first crisis, the central bank was essential for ensuring the role of lender of last resort when banks couldnt refinance themselves in capital markets. The central bank was critical to preserve monetary union, because it was necessary to ensure that the transmission of monetary policy was not impaired by redenomination risk and fragmentation. The European Central Bank and national central banks have also acted in the secondary market to ensure there was no fragmentation in sovereign debt markets. This is continuing. It is necessary to ensure the transmission of monetary policy. And it is very important to ensure that the funding enters the economy: to ensure that sovereign debt is not disturbed, and that the banks continue to lend with the right incentives  to stop any disturbance from the risk of fragmentation. DM: What about the fiscal side? We now have a European programme of more than 2tn. How important is it to get to the EU recovery fund going, so the ECB is not the only game in town? CC: Its very important. In the global financial crisis, the central bank and monetary policy represented the only game in town, because the problem flowed from the financial sector to the real economy. Now, we are facing a different problem. The problem flows from the health side to the real economy and after that to the financial sector. We need to ensure that the real economy stays alive after the sanitary crisis. We started with relief, through moratoria, layoffs and provision of liquidity including with the ECBs pandemic emergency purchase programme. Then comes the repair phase, avoiding insolvencies of companies that are viable but are under big pressure in terms of treasury and liquidity: there is the need to reprofile debt to ensure that liquidity problems will not impair the company. DM: And the banks? CC: Prudential rules for banks need to be implemented flexibly to avoid that such reprofiling of debt becomes a big source of impairments, impacting banks capital, their capacity to lend, and, in the worst outcome, risking failure and requiring recapitalisation. We need a fiscal policy that pays attention to the health of the corporate sector to preserve the health of the financial sector. DM: Where does the EU recovery fund fit in? CC: This repair phase is more a question for national authorities. Afterwards, we have a third phase. That is the recovery phase. The fourth one will be the reorientation phase; that is digital and greening. The recovery fund kicks in in these last two phases. DM: Is there a danger that Europe will not do enough and, again, the ECB will be the only player in town? CC: We need to create confidence that the economic actors will not be abandoned, that the national public authorities commit to the funds that are needed. Exceptional spending for exceptional circumstances. European decisions are needed to support the national authorities on the debt side, through grants to alleviate the impact on the public national debt and to support investment in the recovery phase. DM: How important is the European Stability Mechanism? Could Portugal go to the ESM? That would help Italy. As you know, Italy is worried about the ESM. They see a stigma attached to this. Could you be a pioneer? CC: It's not a question for a central banker, its a question for the finance minister. DM: But what do you think as a Portuguese citizen? CC: We need to be realistic. The European Stability Mechanism is a real advance in the right direction. But is in some ways suffering from some sins coming from the way it was born. DM: Lets turn to the PEPP. Why did you raise the amount, from 750bn to 1.35tn, on 4 June? There isn't so much pressure in the market at the moment. Was it necessary? Some people think you did too much on 4 June. CC: It's good they say that because this means that they are confident that there will always be action in the market. Its important that people are confident that there will be no lack of intervention, if needed. DM: Do you think it's possible that you may not use it all up? You've got another 1tn between now and the end of June 2021. Is it possible that that may be more than enough and you could end the programme not having used it all? CC: It is a nice idea, because it means that we were credible in what we are doing. Our objective is to do what is necessary to avoid fragmentation of the monetary union. If we look at the yield curves, we see them behaving in a way that shows that markets are confident that we can transmit our monetary policy without any difficulties. DM: Can you define what is an acceptable and non-acceptable spread? Christine Lagarde said on 12 March the ECB is not there to close the spreads, but it looks as though that is what you are trying to do. CC: We are trying to determine whether the yield curve is the result of normal market functioning or is it the result of mistrust. If it is a result of mistrust, we need to act. If it is the result of a normal market working, then we need to let the market to do the job. People will look to sovereigns if they trust sovereigns. This means that the Portuguese bonds are falling in yield because people are looking for investments that are safe. Its necessary that they are confident of our participation in the monetary union and above all that we will remain able to intervene if there is a problem. DM: There are going to be more demands on accountability, transparency, and so on, because central banks are now so important and so influential. Are you happy with the results of the German constitutional court action? CC: The German constitutional court ruling is a domestic issue. The issue was whether the proportionality of the ECBs public sector purchase programme, started in 2015, was examined before the decision to start it. Its now clear that proportionality was checked. Until now, it was not necessary to show that the checking was done. It is necessary in future to give to my German colleagues the possibility to show that it was done. The evidence that we provided to the Bundesbank showed that the ECB was diligent. We did our job, even if it was not made public. DM: Will it have an effect on Portugal? Will your successor Mr. Centeno have to go to parliament from time to time to explain the actions? Will the German episode have repercussions on Portugal? CC: For the moment, I'm not able to say that. We would need to have a parliamentary monetary commission that is well informed and able to discuss European monetary policy for that purpose. DM: You've been on the council for 10 years. You've seen three different presidents. How would you define the differences and the similarities between Jean-Claude Trichet, Mario Draghi and Christine Lagarde? CC: We were fortunate to have the right chair at the right moment. With Jean-Claude Trichet, it was very important to build up the ECB. We needed to be patient, to negotiate a lot. It was necessary to build from scratch. The qualities of Jean-Claude Trichet fit very well with these needs. When Mario Draghi arrived, we needed someone who was clairvoyant. And at the same time understood very well the rapport de force, when it was possible to move forward or not. And to understand when there was a majority behind him. Mario Draghi understands what is essential and he did it very well. In the phase we are in now, its necessary to mix the Trichet and Draghi approaches. Christine Lagarde has the qualities to ensure this mix: giving enough attention to take steps forwards, but at the same time ensuring that the links stay close and strong. She is the right person for the right moment. DM: One of your colleagues on the governing council said to me that he's never seen somebody so socially competent as Christine Lagarde. She likes to get people on side, she talks to people. She spoke to the hawks to try to make sure they weren't too irritated. CC: Its a question of priorities. Sometimes you need to move faster. Sometimes you need to move more cohesively. When it's necessary to move faster, you need to use your time differently. When its possible to move in more orderly fashion, you need to spend time doing it. I think that in the present conditions, it's easier, in terms of consensus building, because we're facing an external shock. This is a shock common to all, where there is no risk of different evaluations about the national actions of different countries. It's easier to create a bloc for team building. DM: There are a lot of smaller countries now in monetary union. It started off with 11. Portugal was one of them. There's now another eight. How does that change the governance? Linked to this, do you foresee new countries joining monetary union in the next five years? CC: Some countries are asking to join the exchange rate mechanism [Bulgaria and Croatia  announced on 12 July]  the beginning of a move towards accession. Concerning the working of the Governing Council, I have seen in the past, from my times in Brussels, how it works when people are representing national interests and national economies. I dont see that now. Our mandate concerns the euro area economy. What divides us is not the national approach. It is the way we look to the same indicators. Some Council members are more optimistic. Others are more pessimistic about the evolution of prices, and about the possibility to provide nominal stability. If you introduce more people on the Council, it changes the density of the views, not the underlying issues about of forming a consensus. DM: Are you in the optimistic camp? CC: I am in the realistic camp. I was one of the first, at the beginning of March, to issue a serious alert on the implications of the pandemic. I saw subsequently that my colleagues understood what I was saying. DM: Regarding the mandate, lets go back to the PEPP briefly. Some people say the PEPP is there to improve the transmission. Others say is it there to get inflation up to 2%. Which is it? CC: If you want to comply with our mandate, you need to ensure that monetary policy will raise inflation to the target, that is, close to, but below, 2%. To do this, you need to ensure that the monetary policy is transmitted appropriately. There are two risks to the transmission: overall fragmentation, and monetary and banking transmission. We need to act on the two, to meet the final goal that is ensuring inflation will go up. This requires a repaired economy with employment and economic growth. There is no nominal stability if there is no transmission of monetary policy. And if there is no transmission of monetary policy, there will be no recovery. And if there is no recovery, there will be no revival. DM: You said before that everybody on the Council is there not to represent their country but because they care about the euro area-wide mandate. One former member of the Governing Council says that was true up to the financial crisis. After that, he says, they became much more representative of their national countries. Is it a good or a bad thing that more members are joining these days directly from their posts as finance ministers? CC: You should not accept this as a presumption of how the Governing Council behaves. If you know how the financial markets in your country are working, how the transmission of monetary policies is functioning, you are able to speak to your colleagues about the risks we all are facing. And if we are doing that, bringing our stone to a common building, it's very useful. This is not based on positions favouring different nations. It is based on knowledge of reality. For instance, when my German colleague informs us about how prices are developing in Germany, it's very useful for understanding our overall situation and stance. Taking into account the mandate, the dynamics and the culture of the Governing Council, it's very difficult to think that someone coming from the political side will influence the way the body works. On the contrary, what do you see is acclimatisation of new members by those already there. DM: Maybe the ECB has become mature enough that it can cope with this. If you remember, at the very beginning, the German government wanted to nominate Jurgen Stark in 1998 to become the first chief economist. But in the end, they said, No, we'll choose Otmar Issing because Stark is too close to the government. But now, 22 years later, perhaps it's possible. The ECB has got bigger, its become more established. Maybe now it's more possible to bring in somebody from politics without interfering with the basic ethos of the central bank. CC: You are right. The culture of the institution is already very established. Also, we have several lawyers coming from the Committees to the Governing Council. So, you have the servants of ECB themselves, very proud and very independent. And you have the independence among the governors. No one wants to be seen as a political puppet. DM: We call it the Thomas a Becket effect. Sometimes a government will bring people in, thinking that they're going to be very close to the government, and they turn out to be actually very independent. Maybe we'll see that also with your successor. Thank you for this interview. You put together these ideas into a very coherent and compelling narrative. I look forward to staying in touch after you cease to be governor. CC: A final word: if there is a moment when we need to create some virtual or real meeting point among central banks, to speak about monetary policy and financial stability problems, it is now. It is a very important role you can play in this situation. When times are good, nobody cares too much. When times are bad, we need to speak about independence, about the efficiency and effectiveness of instruments, in the right setting  in parallel institutions such as OMFIF. DM: OMFIF was set up to do that. To be a neutral forum and an independent forum. We do not take sides. Thank you very much.

Title: Inauguration speech of the Governor of Banco de Portugal
text: Gove's swearing-in speech... Inauguration speech of the Governor of Banco de Portugal 20 jul. 2020 Ex.mo President of the Court of Auditors, Ex.mo Minister of State and Finance, Ex.ma Chairman of the Parliamentary Committee on Budget and Finance Ladies and gentlemen, Secretaries of State, E.g. Members of the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal and other guests, Ladies and gentlemen, Today, as Governor of Banco de Portugal, I take upon you, with honor and enthusiasm, a commitment to public service. It is even with a great honor that I do so in the Noble Hall of the Ministry of Finance, a living witness to the importance that for the Portuguese Republic has the cooperation and independence of its institutions. Through the history of this Hall pass the Ministry of Finance, the Court of Auditors, Banco de Portugal, other financial supervisors and so many institutions that have the duty and responsibility to ensure the institutional prestige of the Portuguese Republic. The role of each of them does not develop in the strict competences that are committed to them, in an airtight way, but in a healthy institutional cooperation that, preserving the identity of each one, makes the whole more than the sum of the parties. My relationship with Banco de Portugal has been going on since 1993. By the hand of who is a reference for all who study Economics and Finance, Professor Antonio Sampaio e Melo. With your encouragement, I got a phD from Harvard University, making a commitment to come back. And I returned to Banco de Portugal in 2000. In this way it was very much what I learned to acerca of its dimension. Your unique ability to form. To give Portugal many of its highest paintings. Its importance in supervision, in the indispensable support for the regulation of the banking system, but also in the economic analysis and development of the economic sciences in our country. Banco de Portugal is central. Whether when it is able to successfully meet its objectives, which is so often not perceived by society, or when it fails in this fulfillment, which always has enormous impact and visibility. Over the course of 25 years I have learned that independence is exercised by action, by the materialization of a vocation for public service. Independence is not a mere attribution, something that is bestowed upon us. I believe, as my path shows, that accountability, transparency and independence are essential factors for democratic balance and the development of institutions. But more importantly, I bring resilience into action into this new cycle, accompanied by dialogue and time. We should never live outside of our time. We must give our decisions time to produce their effects. It is, therefore, with pride, responsibility and sense of commitment towards the institutions of the Republic and the Portuguese, that today I am here (in the magnificent Noble Hall of the Ministry of Finance) intact and in an assumed way, to start a new cycle in a centenary institution that we all respect. In recent years, I have added to my academic and senior staff of Banco de Portugal, i have added to the exercise of government functions as Minister of Finance and as President of the Eurogroup. This path allowed me to acquire and mature knowledge and knowledge, which were the essential bases for successfully and pondering public positions. I trust that this capital, which I carry with me, will also ensure full compliance with my responsibilities in this challenge. The last few years have been marked by the assumption of unique responsibilities in critical areas for the economic and financial development of Portugal and Europe. The capital that I accumulated, from the banks of Quelhas to harvard, through the Bank of Portugal, Terreiro do Paco or Brussels constitute an added value that I will always use in the exercise of the functions of Governor. In the last decade, Portugal has undergone a profound economic transformation of which I have been not only a privileged witness, but also an influential actor. I do not hide the immense pride I bring with me from this unique experience and to have shared it like many of you. From the definition of a roadmap to complete the Banking Union, to the deepening of the Capital Markets Union, through the creation of a euro area budgetary capacity, everything has contributed to a very rich experience. This is now added to the monetary dimension, which plays a decisive role in the moment we are living in, but which is only effective if coordinated with the other dimensions of economic policy. I believe in the international role that the Euro can play as an instrument of European policy. I will therefore continue to be your greatest defender. The country needs, as never before, strong and renewed institutions and leaders capable of facing the challenges that are facing us with determination, in a competitive European and global context. It is with great enthusiasm, but above all with responsibility and full awareness of future challenges, that I face the leadership of Banco de Portugal, a central institution for the Republic. Banco de Portugal has to be a reference institution. It brings together many of the best technicians formed in the best Portuguese Universities. It must become synonymous with collective action with the other national and European institutions in order to meet the many challenges of the near future. Banco de Portugal faces four strategic challenges: Ensure efficient and demanding, proactive supervision that, by building trust, creates value, in a world where the digital transition has profoundly altered the provision of financial services; To participate and influence European monetary policy in favour of the growth of the the euro, inclusive and stable, in a context of low interest rates and where measures monetary policy have a strengthened role; Define a macroprudential policy that ensures system stability and does not allow the accumulation of systemic risks, which jeopardise the stability of the system and efficient financing of the economy; Credibility of banking strategies, mechanisms and resolution process, ensuring financial stability and protecting the public office. Banco de Portugal watches over the stability of the national financial system and has the duty and competence to advise the Government in these areas. This role must be played with a single objective: to contribute to the design of a national strategy, based on active participation in the Eurosystem and in increasing proximity to national institutional actors. The independence of the Central Bank is neither questioned nor imposed. To Banco de Portugal, it is not up to have states of soul, about the nature of its independence, much less its Governor. But it is also not up to Banco de Portugal to live for itself and closed on itself. This does not ensure independence, it creates irrelevance. The technical, public and political intervention capacity and reputational capital of the entire institution, starting with the Governor, are the best guarantee of a solid, cohesive and living institution for society. I have learned, at every stage of my life, that a good preparation is the "mother" of all achievements. That we owe it to our work and adaptability and to our employees (always to our employees), to do better and adopt new approaches that deepen the performance of institutions. I don't believe in split strategies to rein. I never ask an unanswered question until I hear the other side. I've always run the institutions I've been through open doors, because that's what I learned at Harvard, where so many know what it's like to run a country or a central bank. Banco de Portugal can and must contribute decisively to the definition of coherent, open-door national policies and to a national strategy that will enable Portugal to overcome the important challenges facing it in Europe and in the world. That's how it's going to be with me. This is how I am, since today, with great honor the Governor of a Bank of Portugal at the service of Portugal. Thank you very much, thank you very much.
text_original: Discurso de tomada de posse do Gove... Discurso de tomada de posse do Governador do Banco de Portugal 20 jul. 2020 Ex.mo Senhor Presidente do Tribunal de Contas, Ex.mo Senhor Ministro de Estado e das Finanas, Ex.ma Senhor Presidente da Comisso Parlamentar de Oramento e Finanas Ex.mos Senhores Secretrios de Estado, Ex.mos Senhores Membros do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Portugal e restantes convidados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Hoje, ao iniciar funes como Governador do Banco de Portugal, assumo perante vs, com honra e entusiasmo, um compromisso de servio pblico.  mesmo com uma enorme honra que o fao no Salo Nobre do Ministrio das Finanas, testemunho vivo da importncia que para a Repblica Portuguesa tem a cooperao e a independncia das suas instituies. Pela histria deste Salo passam o Ministrio das Finanas, o Tribunal de Contas, o Banco de Portugal, restantes supervisores financeiros e tantas instituies que tm o dever e a responsabilidade de assegurar o prestigio institucional da Repblica Portuguesa. O papel de cada uma delas no se desenvolve nas estritas competncias que lhe esto cometidas, de uma forma hermtica, mas numa cooperao institucional s que, preservando a identidade de cada uma, faa do todo mais do que a soma das partes. A minha relao com o Banco de Portugal vem desde o j longnquo ano de 1993. Pela mo de quem  uma referncia para todos os que estudam Economia e Finanas, o Professor Antnio Sampaio e Melo. Com o seu incentivo doutorei-me pela Universidade de Harvard, assumindo desde logo o compromisso de voltar. E voltei ao Banco de Portugal em 2000. Neste trajecto foi muito o que aprendi acerca da sua dimenso. Da sua capacidade mpar de formar. De dar a Portugal muitos dos seus mais altos quadros. A sua importncia na superviso, no apoio indispensvel  regulao do sistema bancrio, mas tambm na anlise econmica e no desenvolvimento das cincias econmicas no nosso pas. O Banco de Portugal  fulcral. Seja quando consegue cumprir com sucesso os seus objectivos, o que tantas vezes no  apercebido pela sociedade, seja quando falha nesse cumprimento, o que tem sempre enorme impacto e visibilidade. Ao longo de 25 anos aprendi que a independncia se exerce pela ao, pela materializao de uma vocao para o servio pblico. A independncia no  uma mera atribuio, algo que nos  outorgado. Acredito, como o meu percurso demonstra, que a prestao de contas, a transparncia e a independncia so fatores essenciais ao equilbrio democrtico e ao desenvolvimento das instituies. Mas, mais importante, levo para este novo ciclo a resilincia na ao, acompanhada pelo dilogo e pelo tempo. Nunca devemos viver fora do nosso tempo. Devemos dar tempo s nossas decises para que elas produzam os seus efeitos. , por isso, com orgulho, responsabilidade e sentido de compromisso perante as instituies da Repblica e os portugueses, que hoje estou aqui (no magnfico Salo Nobre do Ministrio das Finanas) ntegro e de forma assumida, a iniciar um novo ciclo numa instituio centenria que todos respeitamos. Ao meu curriculum acadmico e de quadro superior do Banco de Portugal acrescentei, nos ltimos anos, o exerccio de funes governativas como Ministro das Finanas e como Presidente do Eurogrupo. Este trajeto permitiu-me adquirir e amadurecer o conhecimento e o saber, que foram as bases essenciais para exercer, com sucesso e ponderao, cargos pblicos. Confio que esse capital, que transporto comigo, permitir de igual modo assegurar o cabal cumprimento das minhas responsibilidades neste desafio. Os ltimos anos foram marcados pela assuno de responsabilidades nicas em reas crticas para o desenvolvimento econmico e financeiro de Portugal e da Europa. O capital que acumulei, desde os bancos do Quelhas aos de Harvard, passando pelos do Banco de Portugal, do Terreiro do Pao ou de Bruxelas constituem uma mais-valia que utilizarei sempre no exerccio das funes de Governador. Na ltima dcada, Portugal passou por uma profunda transformao econmica da qual fui, no s uma testemunha privilegiada, mas tambm ator influente. No escondo o imenso orgulho que trago comigo desta experincia nica e de a ter partilhado como muitos de vs. Desde a definio de um roteiro para completar a Unio Bancria, ao aprofundamento da Unio de Mercado de Capitais, passando pela criao de uma capacidade oramental da rea do Euro, tudo contribuiu para uma experincia muito rica. A esta junta-se agora a dimenso monetria, que tem um papel determinante no momento que vivemos, mas que, s  eficaz se coordenada com as outras dimenses da poltica econmica. Acredito no papel internacional que o Euro pode desempenhar enquanto instrumento da poltica europeia. Continuarei, por isso, a ser o seu maior defensor. O Pas precisa, como nunca, de instituies fortes e renovadas e de lideranas capazes de enfrentar os desafios que se nos pem com determinao, num contexto europeu e mundial competitivo.  com enorme entusiasmo, mas sobretudo com responsabilidade e plena conscincia dos desafios futuros, que encaro a liderana do Banco de Portugal, uma instituio central para a Repblica. O Banco de Portugal tem que ser uma instituio de referncia. Congrega muitos dos melhores tcnicos formados nas melhores Universidades portuguesas. Tem de se tornar sinnimo de ao coletiva com as restantes instituies nacionais e europeias, para enfrentar os inmeros desafios do futuro prximo. O Banco de Portugal enfrenta quatro desafios estratgicos: Assegurar uma superviso eficiente e exigente, proactiva, que, criando confiana, crie valor, num mundo em que a transio digital tem alterado profundamente a prestao de servios financeiros; Participar e influenciar a poltica monetria europeia, em prol do crescimento da rea do euro, inclusivo e estvel, num contexto de taxas de juros baixas e em que as medidas de poltica monetria no convencionais tm um papel reforado; Definir uma poltica macroprudencial que assegure a estabilidade do sistema financeiro e no permita a acumulao de riscos sistmicos, que ponham em causa a estabilidade do sistema e o financiamento eficiente da economia; Credibilizar as estratgias, os mecanismos e o processo de resoluo bancria, assegurando a estabilidade financeira e protegendo o errio pblico. O Banco de Portugal vela pela estabilidade do sistema financeiro nacional e tem o dever e a competncia para aconselhar o Governo nestes domnios. Este papel deve ser desempenhado com um objetivo nico: o de contribuir para o desenho de uma estratgia nacional, fundada numa participao ativa no Eurosistema e numa proximidade crescente com os atores institucionais nacionais. A independncia do Banco Central no se questiona, nem se impe. Ao Banco de Portugal, no cabe ter estados de alma, acerca da natureza da sua independncia, muito menos ao seu Governador. Mas tambm no cabe ao Banco de Portugal viver para si prprio e fechado sobre si prprio. Isso no assegura a independncia, cria a irrelevncia. A capacidade tcnica, de interveno pblica e poltica e o capital reputacional de toda a instituio, comeando pelo Governador, so a melhor garantia de uma instituio slida, coesa e que viva para a sociedade. Aprendi, em todas as fases da minha vida, que uma boa preparao  a me de todas as conquistas. Que devemos ao nosso trabalho e capacidade de adaptao e aos nossos colaboradores (sempre aos nossos colaboradores), o fazermos melhor e o adoptarmos novas abordagens que aprofundem o desempenho das instituies. No acredito em estratgias de dividir para reinar. Nunca dou uma pergunta por respondida enquanto no ouvir o outro lado. Sempre geri as instituies por onde passei de portas abertas, porque foi isso que aprendi em Harvard, onde tantos sabem o que  governar um pas ou um banco central. O Banco de Portugal pode e deve contribuir decisivamente para a definio de polticas nacionais coerentes, de portas abertas, e para uma estratgia nacional que permita a Portugal vencer os importantes desafios que se lhe colocam na Europa e no mundo. Assim ser comigo.  assim que sou, desde hoje, com muita honra o Governador de um Banco de Portugal ao servio de Portugal. Muito obrigado!

Title: Opinion article of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, in the Economic Journal: "Somos Comunidade"
text: Vice-Government opinion article... Opinion article of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, in the Economic Journal: "Somos Comunidade" 11 set. 2020 Further apart in time, all the countries have led to profound social changes, even if history has often not valued them sufficiently as a factor in the advent of new times. The Covid 19 pandemic will be no exception. The debate on whether the pandemic is, above all, accelerating trends already underway or whether, more than that, it will generate "a real new world", for example in the global geopolitical and geoeconomic order, in the structuring of political regimes, in the digital transformation of our way of life, in the way we work and, ultimately, how we relate and live. Probably the two perspectives are right, because they are not excluded, but they converge, since, in fact, the tremendous acceleration of the trends that were already manifested is, in itself, something powerful enough to generate the so-called "new world". Social distancing contradicts the essence of the human being. We do not exist without others; we need their closeness to be made and happy. Even the "digital man" needs great collective celebrations. From the communion that comes from participating in a religious celebration, in a political celebration, of sharing the pleasure of the arts, or even, more prosaically, the passion for a sport or a club. Therefore, with the need for social distancing now a fact, which is expected to be transitory, all public policies  especially the economic one  must put their instruments at the service of preserving the essential: ensuring that we remain a community and not an archipelago of impotence. If we lose this, we lose everything. Not by chance, fraternity  a word/concept that, for too long, almost it cannot be written without generating in readers a cynical smile - it is at the center of Christianity, but it was also one of the mottos of the French Revolution. A pandemic is so attentive to the human condition that looking at it as "an opportunity" sums up the rhetoric of uninspired politicians and managers. A different thing is to say that our future will be dictated by how we are able to deal with it. The pandemic has united the world in the same concerns. It did not reach the countries and the inhabitants equally, but in all awakened the feeling of the eternal fragility of the human being, the fear of socobrar. It broke man's sense of omnipotence that technology had been feeding, reminded us that, despite its extraordinary successes, science has limitations. Started under the sign of apocalyptic terrorism, on September 11, 2001, the 21st century saw two tremendous crises emerge within ten years: the global financial crisis and the crisis caused by the pandemic. It's too hard for only ten years. If, in the case of the "Spanish flu", the war (World First) spread the pandemic, I do not believe that the risk of the pandemic spreading the war is high this time. But violence is lurking in many other forms. The best antidote to prevent it is to promote economic and social policies focused on strengthening Community ties, which combat the pandemic of inequality - long expanding, even recognizing the positive results that, from a global point of view, globalisation has brought in the fight against poverty - which enhance the feeling that we all count, that prevent "social distancing" from being the definitive triumph of indifference to the fate of our fellow citizens. The economy should never have lost sight of what is a social science. We know that our current levels of consumption are not sustainable. But its indispensable moderation must be done without generating other forms of unsustainability, especially that of growing poverty. Artigo de opinio do Vice-Governador, Lus Mximo dos Santos, no Jornal Econmico: "Somos Comunidade" 11 set. 2020 Por mais distantes no tempo, todas as pandemias conduziram a profundas alteraes sociais, mesmo que, muitas vezes, a Histria no as tenha valorizado suficientemente enquanto fator de advento de novos tempos. A pandemia da Covid 19 no vai ser exceo. Tem sido interessante o debate sobre se a pandemia est, sobretudo, a acelerar tendncias j em curso ou se, mais do que isso, ir gerar um verdadeiro novo mundo, seja, por exemplo, na ordem geopoltica e geoeconmica mundial, na estruturao dos regimes polticos, na transformao digital do nosso modo de vida, na maneira como trabalhamos e, em ltima anlise, como nos relacionamos e vivemos. Provavelmente as duas perspetivas esto certas, pois no se excluem, antes convergem, uma vez que, na verdade, a tremenda acelerao das tendncias que j se manifestavam , s por si, algo suficientemente poderoso para gerar o dito novo mundo. O distanciamento social contraria a essncia do ser humano. Ns no existimos sem os outros; precisamos da sua proximidade para nos realizarmos e sermos felizes. Mesmo o homem digital precisa de grandes celebraes coletivas. Da comunho que advm de participarmos numa celebrao religiosa, numa celebrao poltica, de partilharmos o prazer das artes, ou mesmo, mais prosaicamente, a paixo por um desporto ou um clube. Por isso, sendo neste momento a necessidade do distanciamento social um facto, que se espera transitrio, todas as polticas pblicas  em especial a econmica -, tm de colocar os seus instrumentos ao servio da preservao do essencial: garantir que continuamos a ser uma comunidade e no um arquiplago de impotncias. Se perdermos isso, perdemos tudo. No por acaso, a fraternidade  uma palavra / conceito que, h demasiado tempo, quase no pode ser escrita sem gerar nos leitores um sorriso cnico -, est no centro do cristianismo, mas foi tambm um dos lemas da Revoluo Francesa. Uma pandemia  algo to atentatrio da condio humana que olh-la como uma oportunidade soa a retrica de polticos e gestores pouco inspirados. Coisa diferente  dizer que o nosso futuro ser ditado pelo modo como formos capazes de lidar com ela. A pandemia uniu o mundo nas mesmas preocupaes. No atingiu os pases e os habitantes por igual, mas em todos despertou o sentimento da eterna fragilidade do ser humano, o medo de soobrar. Quebrou o sentimento de omnipotncia do Homem que a tecnologia vinha alimentando, fez-nos relembrar que, apesar dos seus extraordinrios xitos, a cincia tem limitaes. Iniciado sob o signo do terrorismo apocalptico, com o 11 de setembro de 2001, o sculo XXI viu surgirem duas tremendas crises no espao de dez anos: a crise financeira global e a crise provocada pela pandemia.  muito duro para apenas dez anos. Se, no caso da gripe espanhola, a guerra (Primeira Mundial) espalhou a pandemia, no creio que seja elevado o risco de, desta vez, ser a pandemia a espalhar a guerra. Mas a violncia est  espreita sob muitas outras formas. O melhor antdoto para a prevenir  promover polticas econmicas e sociais centradas no reforo dos laos comunitrios, que combatam a pandemia da desigualdade -h muito em expanso, mesmo reconhecendo os resultados positivos que, de um ponto de vista mundial, a globalizao trouxe no combate  pobreza -, que enrazem o sentimento de que todos contamos, que impeam que o distanciamento social seja o definitivo triunfo da indiferena perante o destino dos nossos concidados. A economia nunca deveria ter perdido de vista que  uma cincia social. Sabemos que os nossos atuais nveis de consumo no so sustentveis. Mas a sua indispensvel moderao tem de ser feita sem gerar outras formas de insustentabilidade, em especial a da pobreza crescente.
