Title: Opening remarks by Director Luis Laginha de Sousa at Sustainable Finance  Sharing experiences on green financial services
text: Opening remarks by Director Luis La... Opening remarks by Director Luis Laginha de Sousa at Sustainable Finance  Sharing experiences on green financial services 15 Sep. 2020 The primary responsibility for managing the transition to a low carbon economy rests with the elected governments. However, if it is true that climate change is indeed the greatest and widest ranging market failure ever seen, a smooth low-carbon transition will require the implementation of a comprehensive set of policies, some of which might involve the collaboration of central banks and financial regulators. (Campiglio, E. et al (2018), Climate change challenges for central banks and financial regulators, in Perspective, Nature Climate Change, Vol 8, June 2018, pp. 462-468) 1.Introduction I would like to thank Mr Paulo Soares de Oliveira for the kind invitation to join you today. Also, allow me to salute this mornings speakers as well as all participants that have joined us today, either present here or watching via live streaming. It is a great pleasure to open this PSO-sponsored event, on the topic of sustainable finance and the risks and opportunities it poses to the Portuguese financial system. This topic is one of the few which can compete, in terms of attention and importance, with that other topic which has caught us by surprise and taken root since the beginning of the year, only to obstinately remain the centre of attention. Before I move on, I have an important clarification related to the concept of sustainability. This concept covers several components, which have been aggregated into three factors, mirrored by the ESG acronym (Environmental, Social and Governance). In the scope of this conference and my address, I will focus on one component only (the environmental component) and, within it, climate change, as the main determinant of sustainability. I have structured this address in such a way as to fit in my 20-minute window, which implied prioritising breadth (however brief) over depth. I will start by making it clear where we are starting from, that is, what can be deemed the root cause of the problem we face when we discuss sustainability or climate change. It is key to show clarity in this prime aspect of the problem, as this is a prerequisite to help establish who must act to deal with it and how they must act. This is not passing the buck: the point is simply to help ensure that everyone does their part, bypass incorrect assumptions and, therefore, minimise the possibility of overlapping action in some areas, while others have considerable gaps. Next, in my address, I will try to synthetically elaborate on the financial system, ie: Why is this a pressing topic for the financial system? What are the main aspects that must be considered when addressing this topic, including that of central banks as supervisors and, albeit to a lesser extent, also regulators, of the financial system and, particularly, the banking system? I will also try to share some information focused on the Banco de Portugals approach to these matters. And I will conclude with a few ideas or key messages worth bearing in mind. 2.Getting to the root of the problem Surely, the overwhelming majority of those present have come across the expression everything is economy. And although it may sound like an overstatement, a closer look removes any concerns regarding a possible hyperbole. Indeed, the topic discussed here today is yet more proof that this is not an overstatement. This expression mirrors the fact that behind every decision made by both individuals and organisations there is an economic rationale. Decisions made by individuals may be simple, with little or no impact on those around us, such as, for instance, the option of sleeping in for an extra 15 or 20 minutes in the morning or of getting up without that extra time of slumber. While this may sound odd, there is an economic rationale behind this decision. It concerns each persons assessment of the benefit they reap from those extra 20 minutes of sleep vs. the benefit that they draw from those same 20 minutes, if they are up and about, that is, the opportunity cost. One such decision will impact only the decision-maker and, as such, has no consequence on others around them, which means that it does not bring about what economists refer to as externalities and, if it does, they will most likely be negligible. At the other end of the economic relevance spectrum, and due to the externalities it entails (as well as its opportunity cost), is the topic we will be discussing today. At the root of the sustainability issue and the pressing need to address it is, in all likelihood, the largest worldwide mis-pricing phenomenon in living memory, to the extent that its negative externalities (stemming from the environmental impacts of several activities) have not yet been correctly incorporated into the prices of products and services charged by the various economic agents. This means all those who carry out such activities, those who incorporate them as intermediate products or services, those who act as final consumers, but also those who fund such activities. If we believe that this is the main problem, then its solution must entail the adjustment of relative prices separating products and services with a negative externality from those with no such externality. And when we talk of changes to relative prices, this means, making some prices more expensive against others, which is clearly a matter that mostly falls within the jurisdiction of whoever makes economic and tax-related choices. However, this does not mean that in this path of adjustments to the prices of products and services, there is not also a major role to be played both by the financial sector and the supervisors and regulators of the financial sector, in general, and the banking sector, in particular. This bring us to the following item in my address. 3.Going into why this topic is relevant to the financial system and central banks I will endeavour to flag three aspects that make this topic particularly relevant to the financial system and central banks in particular: The first is financial stability, which is strongly connected to the mandate of central banks and has implications for the entire financial system as well as the non-financial sector. Further on, I will elaborate on this. The second aspect regards monetary policy. While monetary policy is the responsibility of central banks, with very profound implications for economic agents, anything that may impact on its proper functioning is always a matter of major concern for central banks. The third is the strategic dimension that sustainability concerns have been gaining in a growing number of members of the central banking community, mirroring developments in the corporate sector. 4.Aspect 1  Financial stability We have been witnessing growing developments in both the visibility and predictability (in the sense that they are more and more expected) of the effects and risks associated with climate change, at least in qualitative terms. These risks are typically classified under two major categories: Physical risks, related to the greater frequency and intensity of natural disasters (droughts, floods, fires, hurricanes, etc.) and to the consequences of environmental degradation (pollution, ocean acidification, increase in temperature, loss of biodiversity, etc.); And transition risks, associated with the (unavoidable) adjustment to a greener economic system and society, and due to regulatory or tax changes, technological developments, changes in consumer preferences, or even the increase in litigation. Great uncertainty still surrounds the quantification of these impacts, the determination of the time horizon in which the associated costs will take place and will be calculated. However, despite this uncertainty, there are few people who doubt whether climate change produces non-linear effects, often irreversible, which go beyond national borders and entail huge costs. It is also acknowledged that costs are asymmetrical across countries, regions and even sectors of activity, given that the magnitude and distribution of the impacts are conditional on several factors, such as: The degree of exposure to environmental risk and the degree of resilience of the country, region, or sector of activity or even of a specific company; The mitigation and adaptation measures eventually adopted by the competent authorities (and their timing); And the response of economic agents. Due to the aforementioned factors, it can be concluded that the climate change phenomenon is a relevant issue to the financial system, at two key levels. On the one hand, environmental risks are a source of financial risk, to the extent that both physical and transition risks tend to spill over into the availability and valuation of assets which are funded or used as collateral by the financial system. These risks must, therefore, be reflected in the types and prices of funding transactions. We have often heard defend that subsidies be granted to all things green, but the line taken by Banco de Portugal is that the price of funding should accurately reflect the associated risk. On the other hand, the transition to a greener economy implies a very sizeable volume of investment in the course of several decades, and as this investment does not arise spontaneously, it must be funded. To meet the purpose set by the European Union of reaching carbon neutrality by 2050, in net terms, this would mean additional investments in the range of 175 to 290 billion euro per year (equivalent to between 1.1% and 1.8% of the EUs GDP). If we consider the constraints in terms of savings, indebtedness, risk appetite, it does not require much effort to imagine how much this topic is of particular importance to a country like Portugal and its financial system. Given the amounts of financial resources needed and the different ways in which they must be applied, the levels of investment needed to reach carbon neutrality will only be achievable if three conditions are met: A combination of public and private investment; A combination of traditional financing and other modalities (equity, quasi-capital, venture capital, ...); That the financial system, as a whole, plays its proper role in channelling financial flows to the so-called green investment. And it is not enough to be dyed green, it must be inherently green! It is not difficult to understand how much of a business opportunity this increased demand for funding is for the financial system. But this opportunity also poses hefty challenges: On the one hand, this means financing investments with a very substantial potential for accelerating technological progress and creating value; On the other hand, the difficulties concerning the calculation of risk premia on this type of investment and the adequacy of financing instruments pose challenges which financial operators cannot overlook. Financial institutions which retain, in their balance sheet, the risk of investing the resources at their disposal must ensure that the price that they charge for the financing operations properly reflects the degree of sustainability of the asset underlying that investment. The cost of financing cannot merely cover the traditional market risks associated with competition and technological developments and must also take into account environmental risks. Environmental risks, in turn, are conditional on the timeliness and efficiency of the regulatory and tax measures that may be taken as a response to the climate challenge, as well as possible structural changes in supply and demand, which, on the other hand, stem from the increased sensitivity of consumers to environmental matters and the growing scarcity of those natural resources. A calculation of profitability that disregards environmental risk over the time horizon relevant to the investment of resources will almost inevitably tend to overestimate the feasibility of the investment. Guaranteeing that risks are properly assessed, either to prevent an excess build-up or to ensure that capital buffers are adequate, to be able to ensure resilience should risks materialise, is a concern directly connected to a key mandate of central banks and supervisory authorities, that is, the maintenance of financial stability. Safeguarding financial stability does not mean preventing bankruptcies or losses, but rather ensuring that, should they occur, they can be absorbed without jeopardising the functioning of the system as a whole. However, as in many other situations, in this case it is also easier said than done, and many obstacles must be overcome to enable and encourage, in practice, this internalisation of environmental sustainability costs in the pricing of transactions. These obstacles may be grouped into two major categories. One is due to the lack of granular information, at corporate level, that is reliable, comparable and makes it possible to build benchmarks and classify the nature and risk of investments. The small quantity and low quality of data limit information made available to investors and the financial markets, which results in lack of transparency and information asymmetries, thus hampering the development of sustainable finance. However, we must acknowledge the progress that has been made in this domain, such as the release in mid-2017 of the Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures and, more recently, the adoption of the European regulation to facilitate sustainable investment, also known as the Taxonomy Regulation. This regulation, which was approved in June and should be fully operational by 2022, lays down criteria to determine whether an economic activity is environmentally sustainable, thus making it possible to gauge the degree of sustainability of a given investment. A second challenge stems from the very nature of the sustainable investment projects. Such projects often involve innovative technologies and governance models, entail substantial I&D costs, are highly capital-intensive, pose high risks and have very long materialisation horizons (10, 20 or even 30 or more years). The development of bond and credit markets geared towards green finance will not therefore suffice to meet demand, also because many of the projects in question are not the best suited to debt financing. Rather, and as stated above, many projects require additional financing instruments, such as equity, quasi-equity or venture capital instruments. 5.Aspect 2  Monetary policy I shall be very telegraphic here. As I have said, the risks related to climate change translate into financial risk and are therefore the object of attention by the authorities responsible for preserving financial stability. In addition to preserving financial stability, another key component of central banks' mandates, which can be particularly impacted by both climate change and the corresponding mitigation measures is monetary policy. Here, I would just like to stress that the point of contact for sustainability with monetary policy, is directly related to the fact that climate change and the corresponding mitigation and adaptation policies, will have a relevant impact on supply and demand. That impact is likely to influence the neutral interest rate and the monetary transmission mechanism, thereby affecting the conduct of monetary policy. Given the importance of monetary policy, which I believe has been very visible to all, no central bank can neglect any aspect that might impact the functioning of that monetary policy. 6.Aspect 3  Central banks strategy The third and final aspect I would like to refer, also in a telegraphic way, is that central banks and financial supervisors, besides having to pay increasing attention to sustainability, due to its impact on the two core areas of their mandates -preserving financial stability and the conduct of monetary policy -are also following the path of other entities, from the financial sector and beyond, to incorporate in their strategic plans and their day-to-day management the ESG -Environmental, Social and Governance parameters. Indeed, as organisations having an impact on the environment themselves, they want to do their part and make their contribution and, in this way, also set an example. The cross-cutting and supranational aspect of these concerns led to the creation, in December 2017, of the so-called NGFS -Central Banks and Supervisors Network for Greening the Financial System, which aims to define and promote good practices in the management of environmental risks in the financial sector and support the transition to a more sustainable economy. The Network currently has 69 members and 13 observers from around the world, including the Banco de Portugal, which joined in December 2018. I would like to take this opportunity to stress that having been connected to the business world where competition is the name of the game, it is indeed a privilege to note that the Central Banks and Financial Supervisors community has a remarkable ability to share information and to cooperate in a very open and committed manner. And this brings me to the last point that I wanted to share with you before concluding. 7.Going more specifically into what the BdP has been up to The Banco de Portugal could not be oblivious to concerns about sustainability and sustainable financing. "Banco de Portugal's Commitment to Sustainability and Sustainable Financing", released last March, frames the Bank's response to sustainability challenges (in particular, those arising from climate change) and sets out four action plans: The identification and assessment of climate-related risks; The adoption of internal sustainability practices; Participation in national and international fora; and, finally, Communication and collaboration with other entities. Going into more detail on each of the action plans I mentioned before. First, we have integrated the identification and assessment of climate-related risks into our research agenda, and several research projects are in progress. In this context, I would like to highlight two studies, which are in the process of being completed and which we hope to release soon: The first study seeks to assess the Portuguese banking system's exposures to non financial corporations in relevant sectors from the standpoint of climate change, with the objective of identifying the banking sector's vulnerabilities to the transition to a low carbon economy. We believe that it is critical to be well aware of the risks that are already present in the balance sheets of financial institutions, due to their exposure to the sectors most severely impacted by the energy transition (increase in carbon price). The second study addresses the geophysical, technological, and economic aspects of climate change and economic policies to mitigate its effects. We hope and wish that these studies will make a positive contribution to "fact based decisions" and hopefully "good fact based decisions". Our second action plan is the implementation of internal sustainability practices, namely in the management of the Bank's asset portfolio and the reduction of the Bank's ecological footprint as an organisation. About a year ago, the Bank incorporated the ESG principles into its own investment asset management guidelines, and work is currently underway to implement the new rules. Given the size of the BdP Balance Sheet, it is clear how important these guidelines can be in resource allocation in the investment portfolio. Already this year, by the end of January, the Bank joined the Lisbon Green Capital 2020 Commitment, an initiative of the Lisbon City Council, under which the Bank has committed to take, by 2030, 10 actions in four key areas to combat climate change, i.e., energy, water, circular economy, and citizenship. In early September, we have signed a partnership contract with the Portuguese Environment Agency, the Directorate-General for Territory, the Faculty of Sciences of the University of Lisbon and the Portuguese Institute for the Sea and Atmosphere for a roadmap on adapting to climate change in the 21st century in Portugal. The third priority action plan we have set concerns the bank's intervention in national and international fora where measures with potential impact on the financial system are discussed. This is a field where much has happened, and on different "stages". At the international level, the Banco de Portugal currently comprises 12 working groups, committees and other sub-structures specifically focused on this issue, within the European Central Bank, the European Systemic Risk Board, the European Banking Authority, the Bank for International Settlements and the aforementioned Central Banks and Supervisors Network for Greening the Financial System. And our "integrating working groups" concept is not just about being there to listen to what other people say, although this is also important. A key element of this participation is the highly active contribution in order to include in the discussion aspects that are relevant to our economy and our financial system. We must bear in mind that it is in many of these working groups that guidelines are prepared to be incorporated into the rules established at European level and applied to each of the EU member states. In a context where the rules under which we operate are increasingly set at European rather than national level, we need to be able to follow-up and monitor everything that can impact us through a supranational regulatory approach, aiming to avoid negative impacts and, if possible, influence decisions so that they can be positive for the economy and for the country as a whole. At domestic level, the Bank takes part in a think tank on Sustainable Finance ( Grupo de Reflexao para o Financiamento Sustentavel-GRFS), a group coordinated by the Ministry of Environment and Climate Action, and which comprises the three financial supervisors, financial sector business associations and various financial institutions. Finally, the Banco de Portugals fourth and last action to address sustainability challenges is communication and cooperation with external entities , and covers the establishment of contacts, networking, and the implementation of disclosure initiatives. In this field, the Bank has participated in various conferences and seminars, published articles in specialised magazines and cooperated with the media. 8.Conclusion To conclude, I would like to highlight three key ideas: The concern for sustainability, particularly in its environmental aspect, poses huge, complex challenges, but also tremendous opportunities not to be ignored by the financial system; Environmental risk and the transition to a higher level of sustainability are a source of financial risk and have structural implications on both supply and demand, which puts this issue at the centre of central banks' and financial supervisors' attention because of their implications on two crucial areas of their mandates, financial stability and monetary policy implementation. To this extent, central banks, financial supervisors, and the financial community in general cannot ignore sustainability issues. Sustainable financing is a prerequisite for a successful transition to a "greener" economy and society, but it does not replace the need for a comprehensive and coherent environmental policy on the part of the executive branch of government, as responsible for economic and fiscal policy options. Economic agents are rational. They need, above all, the right incentives, and disincentives, to align their behaviours with maximisation of usefulness for the society, and the achievement of this alignment falls within the scope of economic and fiscal policy initiatives. I conclude by thanking PSO once again for inviting me to be here today, wishing you an excellent and fruitful morning's work and suggesting an image to inspire you in many important decisions lying ahead. The good news is that we do not need to cross borders to see this image and get inspired, just go to the INE (Statistics Portugal) website, and read what is written on the stainedglass window by Abel Manta, a Portuguese artist. The sentence is written in Latin (Ad divitias per scientiam nvmerorvm) which in English means ... prospering by getting acquainted with numbers .... What the Anglo-Saxons call fact based decisions Good morning and thank you very much!

Title: Opening speech by the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Mario Centeno, at the 30th Lisbon Meeting
text: Intervention of opening of the Government... Opening speech by the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Mario Centeno, at the 30th Lisbon Meeting 09 out. 2020 E.g. Governors, Mr Ambassadors, Invited Faces and Dear Guests, It is with great honor that I begin the work of the 30th Lisbon Meeting, thanking everyone for your willingness to be present. The Lisbon Meetings are a privileged moment for cooperation between our countries, whose history is long and multivariate, and in which the Central Banks of portuguese-speaking countries are also part. I intend to continue to promote them by preserving and strengthening an important forum for discussion of topics of common interest that allows us to exchange, always fruitful, ideas about the challenges of the present and the future while sharing the lessons of our recent successes. In this year as difficult as unimaginable, we did not question the realization and continuity of the Meeting, but we have redoubleoured our commitment to adapting to the framework we face. We thus preserve this unique opportunity to discuss the main themes of the annual meetings of the IMF and the World Bank, which will also take place in virtual format, helping us to look at the role of our central banks, to understand the limits and ambition of their action. The crisis has created enormous disruptions: a drop in activity and unprecedented uncertainty have forced massive interventions by the authorities. Global economic activity fell 5.2% compared to the first half of 2019; international trade, an integral part of the interconnection and cooperation between economies, fell by 12.5% in the same period. The services, which involve closer personal contacts, had falls that far exceeded, about double, those seen in the last financial crisis. Although also falling, the industry had a more moderate reduction than in the previous crisis. In view of this exogenous shock and seismic proportions, the margin of policy flexibility and exceptional measures were adopted with a view to reducing the impacts and creating the conditions for recovery to be as rapid as possible and taking advantage of the conditions that pre-existed and which were not at the origin of this strong shock. Just as the pandemic has affected our economies differently, so too did the response varied between different regions. The reasons are varied, from the outthen because the perspectives on the pandemic vary; then because economies differ in their sectoral composition  more or less services, more or less openness to the outside  and, as such, to the same shock they are affected differently; but also because the institutional framework differs, for example, in the European Union we had to explore margins present in our Treaties which did not seem to be available to build a firm and cooperative response; finally, but not least, because the available resources are different. I am sure that during this Meeting we will be able to learn from the idiosyncratic experiences of each of the Portuguese-speaking countries and also from the intervention of our guest speaker, Prof. Susana Peralta, who I take this opportunity to greet and thank for their availability. In the face of the uncertainty that strikes us, we know how primary international cooperation is. Primary in combating the pandemic, which is essential in mitigating adverse effects on economies and populations. Primordial in preparing for the future. Central banks are at the forefront of policy responses, know the challenges ahead, and have not been hiding in reductive mandates. That is what we have done, not only in Europe, but also in the different geographies. Within our jurisdictions, because the severity of the crisis created immediate liquidity difficulties, which would also have immediate impacts on the stability of our financial systems, central banks have strengthened or created new mechanisms to support the liquidity of the banking system. But also between jurisdictions were created mechanisms to access liquidity in dollars and euros, which allowed to maintain international financial flows and avoid inrtions that would spread even more severe crisis. The continued urgency of the policy response, adjusted to the different stages of recovery, as well as the opportunity to invest in a future with growth and to respond to medium and long-term challenges, such as environmental sustainability and digitisation, frame national action but also the reaction of international institutions. In addition, the need to preserve the development progress already achieved and support for the most vulnerable countries, present in the various international initiatives promoted in the wake of the crisis. These topics, along side the cooperation activity and their main developments and future challenges, will be the subject of in-depth debate throughout today. Let me now have a few words about banco de Portugal's cooperation activity. Cooperation reacted quickly to particularly difficult circumstances. We have benefited from continued preparation of many years and great trust between partners. Flexibility, the exploitation of remote resources, the valorization of multilateral actions, basic principles of cooperation, have proved decisive. Many face-to-face actions have been converted into videoconferences, many adjusted programs, many interlocutors and readily mobilized partners. New needs have arisen, such as the exchange of experience in the management of the health crisis caused by COVID-19 and in the implementation of emergency measures for financial institutions. These themes and actions dictated by the emergency have added to a solid cooperation in the core areas of central banking, such as supervision and financial stability, statistics, and, in payment systems, the most expressive in terms of the number of actions. However, it is not limited to these areas, including the areas of support, which are crucial to the full delivery of the mandate of our banks. In 2020, despite all the constraints, Banco de Portugal expects to participate in about 100 cooperation actions, 80 of which were remotely involved, involving almost 300 of its employees. Cooperation with Portuguese-speaking countries represents three quarters of the total actions. Contacts with partners from other geographies continue to expand and strengthen, reaching around 40, spread across the various continents. This is an evolution that in no way diminishes the strategic importance of the lusophony framework. On the contrary, I understand it as an enriching and differentiating factor that benefits it. The Bank articulates its action in multilateral terms, at European and international level. But it also cooperates in liaison with other national and external authorities and entities. In this regard, I see that Banco de Portugal has ensured participation in the structures of the Exchange Agreement between Portugal and Cape Verde and in the Economic Agreement between Portugal and Sao Tome and Principe. These Agreements have recently served twenty years and ten years, respectively, highlighting the depth and importance of the Bank's cooperation in a national strategic logic. It was invested in the creation of a knowledge capital transversal to the employees of our institutions. In several relevant areas, we have taken training courses at different levels. We have also increasingly valued individual empowerment in so-called soft skills. After a first year of enlargement to the Central Banks of portuguese-speaking countries of the possibility of access to the Banco de Portugal Academy, there is now a huge support for this online formative platform. This will not only be the result of the diversion of face-to-face actions, but a sign of a deep understanding of the impact on the efficiency and productivity of human resource training, in aspects essential to modern organizations. The Bank also has involvement in the civil society framework, participating in numerous initiatives, and valued research. Highlight the project of dissemination and research on the documentation of archive relevant to the history of economic relations between the former territories belonging to the Monetary Zone of the Shield, from 1960 to the current monetary regimes. I would like to thank you for the cooperation and contributions of all, in particular the Banks of Cape Verde and Mozambique. Finally, I highlight the communication and publications in the area of cooperation, where we continue to work - today we have announced the Evolution of the Economies of PALOP and Timor-Leste 2019-20 - thus contributing to the knowledge of these economies and to the importance of their economic and financial relations with Portugal. The pandamic outbreak and the current international situation highlight the relevance of cooperation between central banks by demonstrating, among other things, the need for a joint reflection on the challenges and opportunities of this crisis. I am pleased that Banco de Portugal has always recognised the strategic importance of the cooperation that has consistently increased, intensified and modernised for three decades. I invite you now to listen to Professor Susana Peralta, professor at the New School of Business & Economics. Professor Susana Peralta holds a PhD from the Belgian University, Universite Catholique de Louvain, and has developed her research in the areas of political economy and public economy. He will tell us about the "Challenges and opportunities in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic". In the end, I challenge the representatives of the Portuguese-speaking Central Banks and also distinguished guests to, if they wish, share some reflections. Follow live the XXX Lisbon Meeting between the Central Banks of the Countries of Portuguese language
text_original: Interveno de abertura do Governad... Interveno de abertura do Governador do Banco de Portugal, Mrio Centeno, no XXX Encontro de Lisboa 09 out. 2020 Ex.mos Senhores Governadores, Ex.mos Senhores Embaixadores, Caras Convidadas e Caros Convidados,  com muita honra que dou incio aos trabalhos do 30. Encontro de Lisboa, agradecendo a todos a vossa disponibilidade para estarem presentes. Os Encontros de Lisboa so um momento privilegiado para a cooperao entre os nossos pases, cuja histria  longa e multivariada, e na qual os Bancos Centrais dos Pases de Lngua Portuguesa tambm se inserem. Pretendo continuar a promov-los preservando e reforando um importante frum de discusso dos temas de interesse comum e que nos permite uma troca, sempre frutuosa, de ideias sobre os desafios do presente e do futuro ao mesmo tempo que partilhamos as lies dos nossos sucessos recentes. Assim preservamos esta oportunidade nica para discutir os principais temas das reunies anuais do FMI e do Banco Mundial, que tambm decorrero em formato virtual, ajudando-nos a perspetivar o papel dos nossos bancos centrais, a perceber os limites e a ambio da sua ao. A crise pandmica criou enormes disrupes: uma quebra da atividade e uma incerteza sem precedentes obrigaram a intervenes massivas das autoridades. A atividade econmica global caiu 5,2% face ao primeiro semestre de 2019; o comrcio internacional, parte integrante da interligao e cooperao entre as economias, caiu 12,5% no mesmo perodo. Os servios, que implicam contactos pessoais mais prximos, tiveram quedas que excederam largamente, cerca do dobro, as verificadas na ltima crise financeira. Apesar de tambm cair, a indstria teve uma reduo mais moderada do que na anterior crise. Em face deste choque exgeno e de propores ssmicas, foi explorada a margem de flexibilidade de poltica e adotadas medidas excecionais, tendo em vista minorar os impactos e permitir criar as condies para que a recuperao seja o mais rpida possvel e aproveite das condies que pr-existiam e que no estiveram na origem deste forte abalo. Assim como a pandemia afetou de forma diversa as nossas economias, tambm a resposta variou entre as diferentes regies. As razes so variadas, desde logo porque as perspetivas sobre a pandemia variam; depois porque as economias diferem na sua composio setorial  mais ou menos servios, mais ou menos abertura ao exterior  e, como tal, para o mesmo choque so afetadas de forma diversa; mas, tambm, porque o enquadramento institucional difere, por exemplo, na Unio Europeia tivemos que explorar margens presentes nos nossos Tratados que pareciam no estar disponveis para construir uma resposta firme e cooperante; finalmente, mas no menos importante, porque os recursos disponveis so diferentes. Tenho a certeza que durante este Encontro poderemos aprender com as experincias idiossincrticas de cada um dos pases de lngua portuguesa e tambm com a interveno da nossa oradora convidada, a Prof. Susana Peralta, que aproveito desde j para saudar e agradecer a disponibilidade. Perante a incerteza que nos atinge, sabemos como a cooperao internacional  primordial. Primordial no combate  pandemia, primordial na mitigao dos efeitos adversos sobre as economias e as populaes. Primordial na preparao do futuro. Os bancos centrais esto na primeira linha das respostas de poltica, sabem os desafios que tm pela frente, e no se esconderam em mandatos redutores. Foi isso que fizemos, no s na Europa, mas tambm nas diferentes geografias. Dentro das nossas jurisdies, porque a severidade da crise criou dificuldades imediatas de liquidez, que teriam impactos tambm eles imediatos na estabilidade dos nossos sistemas financeiros, os bancos centrais reforaram ou criaram novos mecanismos de apoio  liquidez do sistema bancrio. Mas tambm entre jurisdies foram criados mecanismos de acesso a liquidez em dlares e euros, que permitiram manter os fluxos financeiros internacionais e evitar disrupes que propagariam ainda mais to severa crise. A continuada urgncia da resposta de poltica, ajustada s diferentes fases da recuperao, bem como a oportunidade de investir num futuro com crescimento e que permita responder aos desafios de mdio e longo prazo, como os da sustentabilidade ambiental e da digitalizao, enquadram a ao nacional mas tambm a reao das instituies internacionais. Acresce o imperativo da preservao dos progressos de desenvolvimento j alcanados e do apoio aos pases mais vulnerveis, presente nas diversas iniciativas internacionais promovidas na sequncia da crise. Estes temas, a par da atividade de cooperao e os seus principais desenvolvimentos e desafios futuros, sero objeto de debate aprofundado ao longo do dia de hoje. Permitam-me agora umas palavras sobre a atividade de cooperao do Banco de Portugal. A cooperao reagiu rapidamente s circunstncias particularmente difceis. Beneficimos de uma preparao continuada de muitos anos e de uma grande confiana entre os parceiros. A flexibilidade, a explorao de meios remotos, a valorizao das aes multilaterais, princpios basilares da cooperao, revelaram-se decisivos. Muitas aes presenciais foram reconvertidas em videoconferncias, muitos programas ajustados, muito interlocutores e parceiros prontamente mobilizados. Surgiram novas necessidades, como a troca de experincias na gesto da crise sanitria provocada pela COVID-19 e na implementao de medidas de emergncia para as instituies financeiras. Estes temas e aes ditados pela emergncia acresceram a uma slida cooperao nas reas core da banca central, como seja, na superviso e estabilidade financeira, na estatstica, e, nos sistemas de pagamentos, os mais expressivos em termos do nmero de aes. Porm, no se esgota nessas reas, incluindo ainda as reas de apoio, cruciais  prestao plena do mandato dos nossos bancos. Trata-se de uma evoluo que em nada diminui a importncia estratgica do quadro da lusofonia. Antes pelo contrrio, entendo-a como um fator enriquecedor e diferenciador que a beneficia. O Banco articula a sua ao em termos multilaterais, no plano europeu e internacional. Mas, coopera tambm em articulao com outras autoridades e entidades nacionais e externas. A este respeito, noto que o Banco de Portugal assegurou a participao nas estruturas do Acordo Cambial entre Portugal e Cabo Verde e no Acordo Econmico entre Portugal e So Tom e Prncipe. Estes Acordos cumpriram recentemente vinte anos e dez anos, respetivamente, evidenciando a profundidade e importncia da cooperao do Banco numa lgica estratgica nacional. Investiu-se na criao de um capital de conhecimento transversal aos colaboradores das nossas instituies. Em vrios domnios relevantes, realizmos cursos de formao a diferentes nveis. Temos tambm vindo crescentemente a valorizar a capacitao individual nas chamadas soft skills. Depois de um primeiro ano de alargamento aos Bancos Centrais dos Pases de Lngua Portuguesa da possibilidade de acesso  Academia do Banco de Portugal, observa-se agora uma enorme adeso a esta plataforma formativa on-line. Tal no ser apenas fruto do desvio de aes presenciais, mas um sinal de uma compreenso profunda do impacto na eficincia e produtividade da formao dos recursos humanos, em aspetos essenciais s organizaes modernas. O Banco tem tambm envolvimento no quadro da sociedade civil, participando em inmeras iniciativas, e valorizado a investigao. Destaque para o projeto de divulgao e investigao sobre a documentao de arquivo relevante para a histria das relaes econmicas entre os antigos territrios pertencentes  Zona Monetria do Escudo, desde 1960 at aos regimes monetrios atuais. Aproveito para agradecer a cooperao e os contributos de todos, em particular dos Bancos de Cabo Verde e de Moambique. Destaco, por ltimo, a comunicao e publicaes na rea da cooperao, onde continuamos a trabalhar -hoje mesmo divulgmos a Evoluo das Economias dos PALOP e de Timor-Leste 2019-20  prestando deste modo um contributo para o conhecimento destas economias e para a importncia das suas relaes econmicas e financeiras com Portugal. O surto pandmico e a atual conjuntura internacional colocam em evidncia a relevncia da cooperao entre os bancos centrais ao demonstrar, entre outros aspetos, a premncia de uma reflexo conjunta sobre os desafios e oportunidades da presente crise. Congratulo-me pelo Banco de Portugal sempre ter reconhecido a importncia estratgica da cooperao que consistentemente alarga, intensifica e moderniza h trs dcadas. Convido-vos agora a ouvir a Professora Susana Peralta, docente na Nova School of Business & Economics. A Professora Susana Peralta  doutorada pela universidade belga, Universit Catholique de Louvain, e tem desenvolvido a sua investigao nas reas da economia poltica e economia pblica. Ir falar-nos sobre os Desafios e oportunidades no contexto da pandemia COVID-19. No final, desafio os representantes dos Bancos Centrais de Lngua Portuguesa e tambm distintos convidados a, se o desejarem, partilharem algumas reflexes. Title: Initial intervention by the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Mario Centeno, at the Grand Meeting: Banca do Futuro
text: Initial intervention of the Governor of... Initial intervention by the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Mario Centeno, at the Grand Meeting: Banca do Futuro 27 out. 2020 Good morning, everyone. I want to begin by thanking the invitation of the Business Journal to be here today, congratulating the initiative and the theme that was chosen. The existence of a healthy, robust and dynamic financial system is essential to support the economy, to support businesses and families. The Constitution of the Portuguese Republic clearly establishes the functions of the financial system: to ensure the formation, capture and security of savings and to ensure the application of the financial resources necessary for economic and social development. Many of the identified risks and weaknesses are known, and the difficulties that banks have encountered in adverse economic contexts and high uncertainty are known. But it was and is essential that each institution is determined to design and implement sustainable, realistic business models with an increasingly transparent accountability. On the supervisors' side, prudential supervision has undergone significant changes, which have strengthened it. Prudential supervision is now more proactive, more comprehensive, more conclusive, more foresight. All this increases its effectiveness and the resilience of the system. The European integration process has made an important contribution, notably with the entry into force of the Single Supervisory Mechanism. The networking of European supervisors facilitates the sharing of experience and the adoption of best practices. This new framework was visible in how we reacted to the chemical outbreak and we downplayed its implications for financial stability. Initially, the reaction to uncertainty and risks surrounding the chemical surge led to liquidity tensions in global financial markets, calling into question their stability. The traditional "runaway for quality" behavior of investors in episodes of uncertainty was followed by an unprecedented "money rush" in which even U.S. Treasury bonds became unliquid. The containment measures adopted disrupted economic activity in vast sectors, triggering massive increases in underemployment. In the absence of concerted public intervention, we would have seen a credit and liquidity crisis, which would lead to a wave of insolvencies with consequences for economic and financial stability. Governments, central banks, financial regulators and, in Europe, the Community institutions have been more coordinated than ever. The response of the different public policies was effective, achieving their short-term objectives. In a very brief way, we can say that governments acted in the labor market and ensured liquidity with moratoriums and guaranteed credits. Central banks have provided emergency liquidity lines and relaxed prudential rules. Markets stabilized and credit flowed to businesses and households. Companies have preserved productive conditions and households have increased their savings. In the second phase of the crisis, the gradual lifting of restrictions on economic activity led to an immediate and faster and more intense recovery than expected economic indicators. PMIs (to give just one example) for the euro area, The United States or the United Kingdom have experienced a "V-in" development. Growth forecasts for 2020 were revised higher at the end of the third quarter, although still in a context of uncertainty, now driven by the evolution of the second vacancy Covid.Despite this positive development, the crisis is not yet over, and it is already safe to say that it has created some legacies for financial stability in the medium term and consequent challenges. In the short term, the authorities will take difficult decisions on the adaptation, extension or phasing-out of existing support measures. Or new measures should be adopted. The commitment of european budgetary and monetary authorities is to keep an eye on developments in the economy and its vulnerabilities. I'm sure they will remain. We must keep in mind that the authorities' decision entails two opposing trends. On the one hand, an early withdrawal of employment and credit support will have a destabilising effect on supply conditions and the pace of economic recovery. Companies with high leverage, even if viable, would face credit rationing problems. On the other hand, the extension of support measures would lead to an undesirable maintenance of employment and credit allocation to unviable companies, which will weigh on future growth prospects, always dependent on the reallocation of scarce resources. With uncertainty high and recovery still weak, the risks of an early withdrawal of support seem serious, requiring cautious assessments. The proper modulation of exit strategies should take into account developments in health, economic and financial developments. One of the legacies of the crisis is the increase in state and non-financial corporate indebtedness. In the medium term, over-indebtedness can lead to reduced investment, weakening competitiveness and economic growth. To address this difficulty, measures to strengthen corporate capital are needed to reduce leverage and increase their debt service capacity. Several options have been proposed and, in some countries, already implemented, such as direct support (read transfers), participation in share capital or subordinated debt instruments with public capital or tax incentives in order to favor injections of private capital in companies. In all these cases, market instruments should be preferred. Efficient use of public funds requires the establishment of procedures enabling the effective identification of undertakings that are not viable and should not be receiving such support. In parallel it is necessary to ensure the resilience of the banking system in the face of a likely increase in credit losses. Banks face the crisis with stronger capital and liquidity positions than in the global financial crisis, notably because of the regulatory reforms that followed. This new reality allowed banks to be part of the solution, unlike the financial crisis where they were "part of the problem". Supervisors used the available space to free up macroprudential buffers and to flexibly interpret microprudential requirements, allowing banks to absorb losses and maintain credit flow. None of these measures are risk-free, but the factual counter of doing nothing was not an option: the risks were unaffordable. Everything must be done to prevent this exogenous and unprecedented shock from being able to rely on banks among its victims. That's why discussing the banking of the future is so important. I believe that the response to these challenges is not only focused on national solutions. Unresolved issues with the crisis management structure in Europe should be of urgent attention. I am talking not only about completing the Banking Union, but beyond deepening the Capital Market Union and all the matters that prevent the establishment of strong financial integration between the euro area countries. Among other measures, harmonising insolvency proceedings and finalising the creation of support for the Single Resolution Fund as part of the crisis management framework should be taken immediately. The conclusion of the treaty review of the Single European Mechanism and a European Deposit Guarantee Scheme are steps that would increase confidence in the system and favour all jurisdictions. No exceptions. This debate was left to conclude due to the pandemic. But the EuroGroup must resume it and the European Council should take measures to strengthen the financial, economic and budgetary dimension of monetary union. Financial stability will thus be taxed by these measures. The euro is at the height of its popularity among euro area citizens. It is for them that central banks, governments and agents of the financial system work. We can't let them down at this stage. These debates have always been held in Europe under the mantle of lack of confidence, undoubtedly the heaviest legacy of the previous financial crisis. A brake on the adoption of risk-sharing measures for more than six years. The first exceptions to this rule were the adoption of the Single Resolution Fund backstop and the approval of the embryo of the first and true budget for the euro area, in English BICC. The completion of the Third Aid Programme for Greece, the continued reduction in non-performing credit in euro area countries and the fact that 14 of the 19 euro area countries achieved the medium-term budgetary objectives earlier this year were the most important ingredients for political will to change. And it was this environment that allowed the speed and intensity of the measures adopted since April 2020. This time it was really different. Europe has made numerous progress in effective fiscal and financial integration in recent months. A very visible face of this integration was last week the implementation of the first of several European debt issues. The result was exceptional: 17 billion with a record demand of 233 billion. Europe and its decision-makers are to be congratulated. Until recently many thought it was impossible and even undesirable. We must not shrink in the face of these enormous successes. What better contribution could we ask for financial stability in Portugal and Europe? I have already said that central bank interventions have been effective, but the expectation of unlimited public intervention in the event of systemic market disruption can create moral hazard and, consequently, make a further disruption more likely. We can't allow that to happen. The market cannot but be present to complement public support. The crisis has accelerated trends that will transform the banking sector in the future. The coming months will be challenging and the coming years will see substantial structural transformations. Complex decisions with far-reaching consequences will have to be made by authorities and private actors around the world. Digitisation, technological innovation and the reduction of the ecological footprint will all be accelerated as we come out of this crisis. But first it is necessary to look at the present. In many countries the response to the health crisis was effective without full containment. Social distancing is not synonymous with confinement. The use of masks, testing and the identification of outbreaks are very effective substitutes. We should use them. The "almost perfect" V-response that the economy has given to the partial reduction of confinement should be read as a breath to adapt the measures at this stage, letting the economy function, without losing sight of our security. New risks are added to the experience accumulated with the policies adopted. Just a year ago we were concerned about a half-percentage point slowdown in the world economy. Learning and risk identification are part of the reason for the social and economic advances we have witnessed in recent decades. After six years of consecutive growth and more than 13 million jobs created in the euro area, we don't need to start all from scratch. These must be days of hope. And banking in Portugal must be one of the engines of that hope. Responding to challenges with the same determination that we have faced in the past. I believe that today we can say that there is a rejuvenation in the governance of the main national banking institutions. About 58% of the executive directors currently in office in the seven largest national banking institutions have been in management positions in the national banking sector for 12 or less years, which demonstrates a trend of renewal of the composition of the management bodies since the period of the financial crisis of 2008. It is with this determination of change that we must continue. Thank you very much.
text_original: Interveno inicial do Governador d... Interveno inicial do Governador do Banco de Portugal, Mrio Centeno, no Grande Encontro: Banca do Futuro 27 out. 2020 Bom dia a todos. Quero comear por agradecer o convite do Jornal de Negcios para estar aqui hoje, felicitando a iniciativa e o tema que foi escolhido. A existncia de um sistema financeiro saudvel, robusto e dinmico  fundamental para apoiar a economia, para apoiar as empresas e as famlias. A Constituio da Repblica Portuguesa estabelece de forma clara as funes do sistema financeiro: garantir a formao, a captao e a segurana das poupanas e garantir a aplicao dos meios financeiros necessrios ao desenvolvimento econmico e social. Muitos foram os riscos e debilidades identificados, so conhecidas as dificuldades que os bancos atravessaram, em contextos econmicos adversos e de elevada incerteza. Mas foi e  essencial que cada instituio esteja determinada em desenhar e implementar modelos de negcio sustentveis, realistas, com uma prestao de contas cada vez mais transparente. Do lado dos supervisores, a superviso prudencial passou por alteraes significativas, que a vieram robustecer. A superviso prudencial  hoje mais proactiva, mais abrangente, mais conclusiva, mais prospetiva. Tudo isto aumenta a sua eficcia e a resilincia do sistema. O processo de integrao europeia deu um importante contributo, designadamente com a entrada em vigor do Mecanismo nico de Superviso. O funcionamento em rede das autoridades de superviso europeias facilita a partilha de experincias e a adoo das melhores prticas. Este novo enquadramento foi visvel na forma como reagimos ao surto pandmico e minimizmos as suas implicaes para a estabilidade financeira. Inicialmente, a reao  incerteza e aos riscos em torno do surto pandmico levaram a tenses de liquidez nos mercados financeiros globais, colocando em causa a sua estabilidade. O comportamento tradicional de fuga para qualidade dos investidores em episdios de incerteza foi seguido por uma "corrida por dinheiro" sem precedentes em que at os ttulos do Tesouro dos EUA se tornaram ilquidos. As medidas de confinamento adotadas interromperam a atividade econmica em vastos setores, desencadeando aumentos macios no subemprego. Na ausncia de uma interveno pblica concertada, teramos assistido a uma crise de crdito e de liquidez, que levaria a uma vaga de insolvncias com consequncias na estabilidade econmica e financeira. Governos, bancos centrais, reguladores financeiros e, na Europa, as instituies comunitrias estiveram mais coordenadas do que nunca. A resposta das diferentes polticas pblicas foi eficaz, alcanando os seus objetivos de curto prazo. De forma muito resumida, podemos dizer que os governos atuaram no mercado de trabalho e garantiram a liquidez com moratrias e crditos garantidos. Os bancos centrais disponibilizaram linhas de liquidez de emergncia e flexibilizaram as regras prudenciais. Os mercados estabilizaram e o crdito fluiu para empresas e famlias. As empresas preservaram as condies produtivas e as famlias aumentaram a poupana. Na segunda fase da crise, o levantamento gradual das restries  atividade econmica levou a uma recuperao imediata e mais rpida e intensa do que o previsto dos indicadores econmicos. Os PMIs (para dar apenas um exemplo) para a rea do euro, Estados Unidos ou Reino Unido, registaram uma evoluo em V. As previses de crescimento para 2020 foram revistas em alta no final do terceiro trimestre, embora ainda num contexto de incerteza, agora impulsionada pela evoluo da segunda vaga Covid.Apesar desta evoluo positiva, a crise ainda no acabou, e j  seguro dizer que criou alguns legados para a estabilidade financeira a mdio prazo e consequentes desafios. No curto-prazo, as autoridades tomaro decises difceis sobre a adaptao, extenso ou eliminao progressiva das medidas de apoio em vigor. Ou novas medidas devero ser adotadas. O compromisso das autoridades oramentais e monetrias europeias  o de se manterem atentas  evoluo da economia e das suas vulnerabilidades. Estou certo que assim permanecero. Devemos ter presente que a deciso das autoridades comporta duas tendncias opostas. Por um lado, uma retirada precoce dos apoios ao emprego e ao crdito ter um efeito desestabilizador nas condies de oferta e no ritmo de recuperao econmica. Empresas com alta alavancagem, mesmo se viveis, enfrentariam problemas de racionamento de crdito. Por outro lado, a extenso das medidas de apoio daria origem a uma indesejvel manuteno do emprego e de afetao de crdito a empresas inviveis, o que pesar nas perspetivas de crescimento futuras, sempre dependentes da realocao de recursos escassos. Com a incerteza elevada e a recuperao ainda fraca, os riscos de uma retirada precoce dos apoios parecem srios, exigindo avaliaes cautelosas. A modulao adequada das estratgias de sada deve levar em considerao a evoluo dos desenvolvimentos sanitrios, econmicos e financeiros. Um dos legados da crise  o aumento do endividamento do Estado e das empresas no financeiras. A mdio prazo, o sobre-endividamento pode levar  reduo do investimento, enfraquecendo a competitividade e o crescimento econmico. Para fazer face a esta dificuldade, so necessrias medidas de fortalecimento do capital das empresas, para reduzir a alavancagem e aumentar sua capacidade de servio da dvida. Vrias opes foram propostas e, em alguns pases, j implementadas, tais como apoios (leia-se transferncias) diretos, participao no capital social ou instrumentos de dvida subordinada com capital pblico ou incentivos fiscais de modo a favorecer injees de capital privado nas empresas. Devem, em todos estes casos, ser privilegiados instrumentos de mercado. Uma utilizao eficiente dos fundos pblicos exige o estabelecimento de procedimentos que permitam uma identificao efetiva das empresas que no sendo viveis, no devem ser recetoras destes apoios. Em paralelo  necessrio garantir a resilincia do sistema bancrio em face de um provvel aumento nas perdas de crdito. Os bancos enfrentam a crise pandmica com posies de capital e liquidez mais slidas do que na crise financeira global, nomeadamente por causa das reformas regulatrias que se seguiram. Esta nova realidade permitiu fazer dos bancos parte da soluo, ao contrrio da crise financeira onde eles foram parte do problema. As autoridades de superviso utilizaram o espao disponvel para libertar os buffers macroprudenciais e para uma interpretao flexvel dos requisitos microprudenciais, permitindo que os bancos absorvam perdas e mantenham o fluxo de crdito. Nenhuma destas medidas  isenta de riscos, mas o contra factual de no fazer nada no era opo: os riscos eram incomportveis. Tudo deve ser feito para evitar que este choque exgeno e sem precedentes possa contar com os bancos entre as suas vtimas. Por isso discutir a banca do futuro  to importante. Penso que a resposta a estes desafios no est apenas centrada nas solues nacionais. Questes no resolvidas com a estrutura de gesto de crises na Europa devem merecer uma ateno urgente. Estou a falar no s de concluir a Unio Bancria, mas, mais alm, de aprofundar a Unio de Mercado de Capitais e todas as matrias que impedem o estabelecimento de uma forte integrao financeira entre os pases da rea do Euro. Entre outras medidas, harmonizar os procedimentos de insolvncia e finalizar a criao de um apoio para o Fundo nico de Resoluo como parte do quadro de gesto de crises devem ser tomadas de imediato. A concluso da reviso do Tratado do Mecanismo nico Europeu e de um Sistema de Garantia de Depsitos Europeu so passos que aumentariam a confiana no sistema e favoreceriam todas as jurisdies. Sem excees. Este debate ficou por concluir devido  pandemia. Mas o EuroGrupo deve retom-lo e o Conselho Europeu deve adotar as medidas para reforar a dimenso financeira, econmica e oramental da Unio Monetria. A estabilidade financeira ser assim tributria destas medidas. O euro est no auge da sua popularidade entre os cidados da rea do euro.  para eles que bancos centrais, governos e agentes do sistema financeiro trabalham. No os podemos desiludir nesta fase. Estes debates sempre foram mantidos na Europa sob o manto da falta de confiana, sem dvida o mais pesado legado da anterior crise financeira. Um travo  adoo de medidas de partilha de risco durante mais de seis anos. As primeiras excees a esta regra foram a adoo do backstop do Fundo nico de Resoluo e a aprovao do embrio do primeiro e verdadeiro oramento para a rea do euro, em ingls BICC. A concluso do Terceiro Programa de ajuda  Grcia, a continuada reduo do crdito no performante nos pases da rea do euro e o facto de, no incio deste ano, 14 dos 19 pases da rea do euro terem atingido os objetivos oramentais de mdio prazo foram os mais importantes ingredientes para que a vontade poltica mudasse. E foi este ambiente que permitiu a rapidez e intensidade das medidas aprovadas desde abril de 2020. Desta vez foi mesmo diferente. A Europa conseguiu inmeros progressos na efetiva integrao oramental e financeira nos ltimos meses. Uma face bem visvel desta integrao foi, na semana passada, a concretizao da primeira de vrias emisses de dvida europeia. O resultado foi excecional: 17 mil milhes de euros com uma procura recorde de 233 mil milhes. A Europa e os seus decisores esto de parabns. At h pouco tempo muitos pensavam que era impossvel e, at, indesejvel. No nos devemos encolher perante estes sucessos enormes. Que melhor contribuio poderamos pedir para estabilidade financeira em Portugal e na Europa? J o disse, as intervenes dos bancos centrais tm sido eficazes, mas a expectativa de uma interveno pblica ilimitada no caso de perturbao sistmica do mercado pode criar risco moral e, consequentemente, tornar mais provvel uma nova perturbao. No podemos permitir que isso acontea. O mercado no pode deixar de estar presente, para complementar os apoios pblicos. A crise acelerou as tendncias que transformaro o setor bancrio no futuro. Os prximos meses sero desafiadores e os prximos anos assistiro a transformaes estruturais substanciais. Decises complexas com consequncias de longo alcance tero que ser tomadas pelas autoridades e pelos agentes privados em todo o mundo. A digitalizao, a inovao tecnolgica e a diminuio da pegada ecolgica sero todos acelerados  medida que samos desta crise. Mas primeiro  necessrio olhar para o presente. Em muitos pases a resposta  crise sanitria foi eficaz sem um confinamento total. Distanciamento social no  sinnimo de confinamento. A utilizao de mscaras, a realizao de testes e a identificao de surtos so substitutos muito eficazes. Devemos us-los. A resposta em V quase perfeito que a economia deu  reduo parcial do confinamento deve ser lida como um alento para adaptarmos as medidas nesta fase, deixando a economia funcionar, sem perder de vista a nossa segurana.  experincia acumulada com as polticas adotadas juntam-se novos riscos. H precisamente um ano estvamos preocupados com uma desacelerao de meio ponto percentual da economia mundial. Aprendizagem e identificao de riscos, fazem parte da razo de ser dos avanos sociais e econmicos que testemunhmos nas ltimas dcadas. Aps seis anos de crescimento consecutivo e mais de 13 milhes de empregos criados na rea do euro, no precisamos de comear tudo do zero. Estes devem ser dias de esperana. E a banca em Portugal deve ser um dos motores dessa esperana. Respondendo aos desafios com a mesma determinao que os enfrentmos no passado. Julgo que podemos hoje afirmar que existe um rejuvenescimento na governao das principais instituies bancrias nacionais. Cerca de 58% dos administradores executivos atualmente em funes nas sete maiores instituies bancrias nacionais encontram-se a exercer cargos de administrao no setor bancrio nacional h 12 ou menos anos, o que demonstra uma tendncia de renovao da composio dos rgos de administrao desde o perodo da crise financeira de 2008.  com essa determinao de mudana que devemos continuar. Muito obrigado.

Title: Intervention of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, at the close of the CNSF Colloquium - Three years of General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
text: Compatible... Intervention of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, at the close of the CNSF Colloquium -Three years of General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) 05 nov. 2020 I would like to begin these brief words by pointing out the relevance and opportunity of this Colloquium, also stressing that it was an honour for Banco de Portugal to welcome and participate in this initiative carried out within the framework of the National Council of Financial Supervisors. It is just another proof of how cooperation between financial supervisors is actually working and a small example of how it is so important for the financial sector and therefore for the country. It goes without stressing how the protection of personal data is now more fundamental than ever, but also more difficult to achieve. The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) became mandatory as of May 25, 2018. There has long been legislation and data protection policies at national and European level, but the GDPR has been introduced by legal form  a European regulation  by methodology and, as well as various aspects relating to the rights it has enshrined for data subjects. At Banco de Portugal we have an increased responsibility in this matter: as a public entity we have a duty to be exemplary in compliance with the law; as a regulatory and supervisory body we should seek to set an example for the supervised, despite the diversity of their situations. Recognizing that the task of applying the GDPR would be arduous, we began to prepare it with adequate advance in advance at the institutional and operational level, knowing that the key to being successful in this area lies in the dissemination of an organizational culture based on the awareness that data protection is a task of each and every employee of the Bank. The topics chosen for this Colloquium have not escaped  and are well -- controversial topics: the relations between the GDPR and Law No. 58/2019 of 8 August, the powers of the National Data Protection Commission, the status and role of the Data Protection Officer (not always well understood), the consequences of Brexit, and the crucial problem of data transfers outside the European Union, in particular in the challenging context arising from the Judgment of the Court of Justice of the European Union of 16 July 2020, which declared invalid commission decision 2016/1250 on the level of protection provided by the EU-US Privacy Shield, and made us think  paraphrasing an expression that became famous in the case of a case that occurred in the 18th century in Germany  that there are still judges in Luxembourg. All these topics are, for different reasons, very important and that is why the Colloquium was so interesting. Personal data and what can be done with them are central in contemporary society, they are one of the crucial raw materials of our time. This is a true across all economic activity, but in the financial sector it gains even more prominence. With regard to the use of personal data by the financial sector, traditional or not, as the President of the International Payment Bank (BIS), Agustin Carstens, the different regulatory authorities are faced with complex trade-offs between stability, efficiency and privacy defense [1]. On 24 September this year, the European Commission presented the so-called Digital Finance Package, which aims to be a new and ambitious approach to encourage responsible innovation for consumers and businesses. This important document defines a strategy to prevent the fragmentation of the digital single market, reaffirming the principle that the same activity and the same risks should apply to the same rules, which includes the need to ensure a level playing field between financial service providers, be they banks or technology companies (fintechs or bigtechs), ensuring the existence of a level playing field, and stresses the need to ensure digital operational resilience by halting the path to cyber-attacks and improving control of services externalizados[2]. There is a lot of way to go with regard to the protection of personal data in the country in general and in the financial sector in particular, but also a lot of space for financial institutions to take advantage of the legitimate use of personal data, making banking and financial activity more efficient and therefore more profitable. The massive use of teleworking as a result of the Covid19 pandemic has brought about new problems with regard to the protection of personal data. At a time of enormous fragility in our companies, where resources are scarce to survive as much as to invest, some way of taking advantage of European funds for economic recovery should be foreseen to assist in financing the investments necessary to ensure the robustness of our companies' activity with the GDPR, especially small and medium-sized ones, and to make a strategy in this direction. It is important not to lose sight of the fact that such conformity is an important competitive advantage, especially in the context of the single market and the global market. The debate on the problems related to the use of personal data calls for various sciences, raises philosophical, ethical and political questions. In the field of financial activity, we are only at the beginning of a path that will have to deepen the dialogue between regulatory and supervisory authorities in the financial sector and data protection control authorities. Much study is required, a lot of reflection induced by experience will arise. How should we, for example, delimit the boundaries between banking behavioural supervision and respect for the protection of personal data, which are protected within its own regulatory and institutional framework? Or how should we articulate the protection of bank secrecy, when individuals are concerned, and the rules of data protection? Personal data has always been at the heart of financial activity. But digital transformation has taken the theme to other levels, due to the impact of new technologies, the generalization of their use, the risks it entails, the complexity of situations and the requirement that it is indispensable to observe the benefit of a "decent society", to use an expression very dear to Prof. Eduardo Paz Ferreira. There is therefore no shortage of reasons for the members of the National Council of Supervisors and the National Data Protection Commission to meet again in other initiatives of this kind, which will surely happen sooner sooner sooner than later. Thank you so much for your attention. [1]Cf. in Digital identities could protect customer data  Carstens, Central Banking Newsdesk, 14 Nov 2019. [2] On the subject of the control of outsourced services, cf. the EBA Guidelines on the provision of services in banking, revised in 2019, and which address, among others, the theme of the cloud  EBA/GL/2019/02, and the Circular Letter of Banco de Portugal No CC/201900000065, of 15 October
