Artigo de opinio do Vice-Governador, Lus Mximo dos Santos, no Jornal de Negcios: "O Cdigo da Atividade Bancria: uma reforma indispensvel" 09 nov. 2020 O quadro jurdico fundamental que rege a atividade bancria encontra-se, ainda hoje, previsto no Regime Geral das Instituies de Crdito e das Sociedades Financeiras (RGICSF), aprovado em 1992.  poca, foi um importante contributo para a modernizao do nosso sistema financeiro, fazendo-o acertar o passo com o processo de integrao europeia, ento na fase inicial da construo do mercado nico bancrio. Quando foi criado, o RGICSF era um diploma bem estruturado, mas hoje  uma demonstrao cabal de como a legislao pode envelhecer mal. Desde a sua entrada em vigor, em 1 de janeiro de 1993, o RGICSF foi j objeto de cinquenta e trs (!) alteraes (quase duas por ano de vigncia, portanto), sendo hoje uma manta de retalhos, sem estrutura que lhe d coerncia, de uma complexidade que compromete a sua funo, de leitura difcil, mesmo para os peritos, muitas vezes a roar a ininteligibilidade. Paradoxalmente, e apesar de tantas alteraes, o RGICSF  hoje um diploma to desatualizado que nem sequer est adaptado, por exemplo, s modificaes decorrentes da entrada em vigor do mecanismo nico de superviso, em novembro de 2014, no contexto da unio bancria europeia. Em boa verdade, no era sequer razovel esperar que pudesse ter acomodado com xito as sucessivas revolues da atividade bancria e da sua regulao, bem como do respetivo enquadramento institucional, ocorridas desde 1992, to intensas e profundas que foram. , pois, indispensvel substituir o RGICSF por uma legislao  altura das necessidades atuais,  beira de entrarmos na terceira dcada do sculo XXI. Consciente do seu papel insubstituvel nesta matria e dos seus deveres perante a comunidade, o Banco de Portugal mobilizou-se para colocar  disposio do Pas e, em particular, dos responsveis pela funo legislativa, um Anteprojeto de Cdigo da Atividade Bancria que, se aprovado, substituir o RGICSF e, alm disso, assegura a transposio e a implementao de vrios instrumentos legislativos de direito europeu, que compem o chamado banking package. Foi uma tarefa rdua, que levou vrios anos, e que convocou o melhor de muitos colaboradores do Banco de Portugal. Naturalmente, houve articulao com o Governo, nesta e na anterior legislatura, e com os outros reguladores e supervisores do setor financeiro: a Comisso do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios e Autoridade de Superviso dos Seguros e Fundos de Penses. De 29 de outubro a 4 de dezembro, o Anteprojeto de Cdigo da Atividade Bancria est em consulta pblica, no stio do Banco de Portugal, de modo a recolher contributos que possam enriquec-lo e contribuir para o seu avano, no sendo, como  bvio, um projeto finalizado. No espao adequado a um artigo de jornal, no  possvel expor as alteraes que o Anteprojeto contm relativamente ao RGICSF. Sublinharia, contudo, trs aspetos estruturantes: (i) uma nova sistemtica, que toma por modelo o ciclo de vida das instituies a que se aplica e que est construda de modo a salvaguardar, na maior medida possvel, a estabilidade normativa do Cdigo, designadamente remetendo aspetos de ndole mais tcnica para o poder regulamentar do Banco de Portugal; (ii) a previso de uma norma de articulao de competncias, que explicita o quadro europeu em que o Banco de Portugal exerce os seus poderes; e (iii) a reformulao do regime aplicvel  cultura organizacional, governo societrio e gesto de conflitos de interesses no seio da atividade bancria, reforando o necessrio alinhamento do mercado nacional pelo benchmarking internacional e acolhendo mltiplas recomendaes oriundas, nos ltimos anos, de comisses parlamentares de inqurito sobre o setor financeiro portugus. Diz-se muitas vezes que as reformas no se fazem por decreto. Mas julgo que ningum negar que uma legislao de qualidade  um fator crtico para o bom desempenho deste setor fundamental da economia portuguesa, pelo que, nesta oportunidade, s posso formular votos de que a consulta pblica do Anteprojeto de Cdigo da Atividade Bancria contribua para a concretizao desta importantssima reforma regulatria h muito aguardada.

Title: Keynote Speech by Director Ana Paula Serra in the "CIRSF Annual International Conference 2020": "Economic Recovery and Financial Stability"
text: Keynote Speech by Director Ana Paul... Keynote Speech by Director Ana Paula Serra in the "CIRSF Annual International Conference 2020": "Economic Recovery and Financial Stability" 12 Nov. 2020 Good afternoon. Let me start by thanking Luis Morais for the invitation to participate in this conference. It is a great pleasure to participate in this panel together with Mario Nava. As we face what some call a second wave of COVID-19, the full impact and consequences of this unfortunate lasting pandemic on the real economy and on the banking sector are still uncertain. I think that we all acknowledge that this time is different from the previous crisis of 20072008 or, in the particular case of Portugal, from the crisis of 2011-2013. Now, the origin of the crisis is external from the financial system and it affects the entire world simultaneously. In the particular case of the euro area, banks starting point, in terms of capital and liquidity ratios, is much better. By the end of 2019, the CET1 ratio stood at 14.7%, the leverage ratio was 5.6% and LCR (liquidity coverage ratio) and NSFR (net stable funding ratio) stood, respectively, at 146% and 114%. Banks were indeed better equipped and prepared to deal with this new crisis. The banking sector buffers were such that the sector was able to withstand the immediate shock and may face the downturn that will come more easily. This way, the banking sector, has so far and hopefully will continue to act as a stabilizer, enabling economic recovery. Governments, central banks, supervisors and regulators were key to the management of the Covid-19 crisis. Several important measures implemented by national and European authorities and governments had a direct and significant impact in the banking sector and the timing of adoption of these measures was also key to sustain markets and banks. First, payment moratoria to households, mortgage and personal loans, and to NFCs. The maturity of the postponements, principal or principal and interest, varies between 6 to 18 months, giving time to the companies and individuals to recover their cash-flows affected by the crisis. Associated to that, EBA guidelines granted flexibility to banks on the application in the prudential framework regarding default, forbearance on these payment holidays. Banks also benefited from the flexibility in IFRS9 application, adopting a forward looking judgment of distress in order to avoid excessive procyclicality. Second, ECB and euro area NCA allowed banks flexibility in the use of P2G and capital buffers and issued recommendations to suspend the distribution of dividends for the financial years of 2019 and 2020. CRR quick fix provided banks with relevant RWA reduction and further capital releases and extra flexibility. All the measures have strengthened banks capital positions to provide support to the real economy and absorb losses. This was also possible thanks to the Public Guarantee Schemes given to micro, small and medium companies and the very accommodative monetary policy measures. Let me stress in particular the role of TLTRO III and collateral framework easing measures. These were critical to assure banks building up of liquidity buffers used, at least partially, to grant loans and deal with moratoria. Thus, unlike in previous crises, there was no tightening of credit. National and European policy measures have played and are still playing a very important role in containing the impact of the crisis. The short-term outlook for the European economies remains uncertain and the impact of lockdown measures were only anticipated in adverse scenarios. Yet, if the pace of recovery is similar to what we witnessed over the summer, if we are able to fight the pandemic in an effective was by early 2021, the negative effects of the crisis may somehow be contained. While the careful unwinding of moratoria and other flexibility measures should be and is underway, supervisors have to be careful not to unwind the relevant measures too early or too fast, precipitating cliff effects, and avoiding lack of coordination that would risk diminishing the effect of measures implemented by other authorities. ECB and Banco de Portugal have already communicated the build-up of capital buffers needs to start by the end of 2022. Supervisors recognize the need to act prudently and therefore contribute on their part to a soft landing but they need to make sure that banks are properly preparing to deal with the expected deterioration in the quality of their assets. So, the first balance, is that the extensive regulatory and institutional reforms carried out in the EU in recent years, and more importantly in the Euro area, together with a timely adoption of micro and macro prudential measures and monetary policy measures to address the crisis caused by the pandemic, were key to ensure that the banking system was part of the solution and was able to address the paramount current challenges. Yet while the banking sector proved to be resilient so far, there are huge challenges ahead and there are important elements in the regulatory framework that are missing and that become more evident when we turn to crisis management mode. A more detailed answer to this question inevitably leads me to address the status in the construction of the Banking Union. An integrated framework to ensure financial stability in the euro area, and to minimize the cost of bank failures to EA citizens, implies the implementation of 3 interlinked pillars: (1) common supervision, (2) common mechanisms to resolve banks and (3) a single deposit guarantee scheme. This vision was endorsed back in 2012, by the Presidents of the Council, of the European Commission, of the European Parliament, of the Eurogroup and of the ECB. Since then, there were notable developments. The first pillar, the SSM, is completed, and after 6 years since its beginning in November 2014 it is entering now a more mature phase. This high maturity was clearly visible in the smooth and closed coordination between ECB and NCAs through the crisis enabling to ensure full consistency of the measures that were applied both to SIs and LSIs. The second pillar is also ongoing and advancing at a fast pace. While theoretically it applies to all banks, in practice it has shown some difficulties namely with regard to the resolution framework for smaller banks. Not all institutions meet the requirements to benefit from the regime and access the mutualized funds of the Single Resolution Fund. Therefore, they are now left with one option, liquidation, even when they are systemic relevant at a regional or national level with the resulting consequences for financial stability. The third pillar of the Banking Union, a common deposit insurance scheme, has not yet been implemented. There has been no agreement on a fully fledged EDIS and the debate has turned to alternatives that could solve the inconsistencies and difficulties of an incomplete banking union, such as provision of liquidity to national Deposit Guarantee Schemes. In the current context of the Covid19 pandemic crisis, the difficulties are amplified and call for a careful but urgent policy reflection on whether the existing crisis framework is sufficient to properly deal with bank failures in a systemic scenario. It is important to revisit the resolution regime and reconsider precautionary recapitalization rules. The resolution framework could probably be well complemented by alternative financing mechanisms, increasing banking sector resilience and cost efficiency. Another important related topic that has to do with the role of preventive measures in the crisis management framework. In particular, recent experiences suggest that DGSs could also be used prevent the failure of banks, as this setting could translate into lower the costs of intervention as compared to a pay-out. Another related and very important topic is the balance between home and host countries. While banking market integration should be pursued, with the dismantling of barriers to cross-border flows, this cannot be done at the expenses of financial stability and host DGS. In the case of significant subsidiaries, waivers of capital and liquidity requirements cannot be granted since there are no sound effective safeguards of intragroup support. While these conditions are not met, host countries competent authorities rightfully demand the application of prudential requirements. These are a few issues, among others, that need to be addressed in a future updated framework. Step by step, we are progressing and I trust that, in time, we will bring the Banking Union to a closure. The sooner the better. Let me stop here. Thank you for your attention.

Title: Intervention of Administrator Hlder Rosalino at the opening of the Interbank Meeting on Payment Systems
text: Intervention of the Administrator Helder... Intervention of Administrator Helder Rosalino at the opening of the Interbank Meeting on Payment Systems 12 nov. 2020 [Performed remotely] I would like to begin by welcoming everyone present at this Interbank Meeting on Payment Systems, the second one that Banco de Portugal promotes in 2020. Again, in view of the circumstances we are experiencing in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, it is again necessary to hold such a meeting remotely. Since the previous Interbank Meeting, held on June 18, there have been several advances in a number of relevant topics, proof that the current circumstances have not prevented the banking community, together with Banco de Portugal, from progressing and achieving goals, maintaining the availability and efficient functioning of payment systems and services as an essential element of economic activity and giving maximum confidence to the various agents. As on that date, the current framework remains adverse. However, payment services have responded to users' concerns with resilience, convenience and security. In recent months, I have essentially detached five elements: (i) The transitional measure taken at the beginning of the containment phase, to increase the ceiling for contactless transactions from EUR 20 per transaction to EUR 50, was well accepted by traders and consumers and, to this end, made definitive in July. This increase has led to increased use of this form of payment in recent months and we expect it to consolidate in the future; (ii) Also in July, the National Migration Plan for Strong Customer Authentication was published in card e-commerce transactions, which establishes a set of actions and deadlines for this migration to run smoothly until 31 december, the date on which the supervisory flexibility phase provided for by the European Banking Authority (EBA) ends. This is one of the topics that we will discuss at this interbank meeting. (iii) Later, in mid-October, the link ing of the national immediate transfer solution to TIPS (TARGET Instant Payment Settlement) was established, thus ensuring European interoperability in immediate transfers, a step that will allow the increasing use of this instrument in a true "SEPA spirit"; (iv) On October 23, TARGET2 recorded the largest incident since its implementation in 2007, with central bank currency settlement services unavailable for about 10 hours. The positive note is that, despite the adversities, after the recovery of the system, the combined action of Banco de Portugal, SIBS FPS and the participating institutions made it possible to ensure the settlement of the necessary payments, in an amount exceeding EUR 1 billion. We take the opportunity to ensure that this incident, caused by technical issues at the level of the single centralised platform, is being properly analysed by the Eurosystem in all its perspectives and the necessary measures will be taken to prevent it from occurring again. (v) Finally, we must highlight the recent adoption, and publication, of the "National Strategy for Retail Payments Horizon 2022", resulting from the work carried out within the Framework of the Payment Systems Forum and which benefited from broad consensus and contributions obtained through public consultation. The Strategy is a structuring document for the evolution of the retail payments market in Portugal in the next two years and intends to act on 4 pillars: promoting a more informed society; enhance the benefits of digital transformation; contribute to a regulatory environment that promotes innovation and efficiency; and promote the adoption of safer payment solutions. We are therefore looking at a more digital services and providing modern, efficient, secure and, to a large extent, increasingly european integration. I would like to point out that, in the face of rapid technological changes in the retail payments ecosystem and the very significant changes in consumer preferences, the Eurosystem has decided to exploit the pros and cons of issuing a digital central bank currency, the digital euro. Through its "Report on a digital euro" released in early October, the Eurosystem laid the groundwork for a wide-ranging debate that will gain greater visibility in the coming months. At today's session, because of the importance we believe this issue may have for payment service providers, we will present the main messages of the report and invite you to participate in the public consultation of the document, which will run until 12 January. However, today's session aims, above all, to update ongoing issues in the field of payments, and which are approaching new stages of development: (i) The new planning of the project for the evolution of TARGET services, in particular following the decision to postpone the go-live of the project by one year to November 2022, and because it is essential for its success that all actors are properly prepared at the time of production. In this context, the new planning of the project for the evolution of TARGET services will be presented. (ii) The introduction of measures to ensure pan-European reachability of immediate transfers by the end of next year, based on TIPS, allowing individuals and businesses to make real-time electronic payments to and from any European country. We will briefly describe the measures to be implemented to ensure this true interoperability. (iii) The reference date of December 31, 2020, critical for the implementation of strong customer authentication requirements and common and secure communication in the context of the revised Payment Services Directive, approaches. In the context of card e-commerce, and given that we are approaching Christmas, a crucial time of year for e-commerce, and even more so this year given the situation of the pandemic we are going through, it is urgent to systematise situations that still need action by payment service providers, so that migration occurs without any problems until 31 December. It should be noted that, in addition to closely monitoring the plans of payment service providers, Banco de Portugal has carried out actions with the other actors that will have to be equally prepared: merchants and users. In the first case, a clarification session was held with these entities; in the second case, this week a communication campaign on social networks and institutional website of Banco de Portugal, which will extend next week to television channels, and which aims precisely to alert users to the new rules and the need to contact their payment service provider. We challenge all payment service providers to take advantage of the materials of this campaign to strengthen communication actions with your customers. Finally, a status on the implementation of the common and secure communication requirements will also be made following the publication by Banco de Portugal in July of this year. Without further ado, we will then follow the agenda. We thank you once again for your presence and the interest shown in the topics proposed for this session. Thank you very much.
text_original: Interveno do Administrador Hlder... Interveno do Administrador Hlder Rosalino na abertura da Reunio Interbancria sobre Sistemas de Pagamentos 12 nov. 2020 [Realizada por via remota] Gostaria de comear por dar as boas-vindas a todos os presentes em mais esta Reunio Interbancria sobre Sistemas de Pagamentos, a segunda que o Banco de Portugal promove em 2020. Uma vez mais, atendendo s circunstncias que vivemos, no contexto da pandemia COVID-19, volta a ser necessrio realizar uma reunio desta natureza por via remota. Desde a realizao da Reunio Interbancria anterior, ocorrida em 18 de junho, verificaram-se diversos avanos num conjunto de temas relevantes, prova de que as circunstncias atuais no impediram a comunidade bancria, em conjunto com o Banco de Portugal, de progredir e alcanar metas, mantendo a disponibilidade e o funcionamento eficiente dos sistemas e servios de pagamento como elemento essencial  atividade econmica e conferindo a mxima confiana aos diversos agentes. Tal como naquela data, o enquadramento atual continua adverso. Porm, os servios de pagamento tm respondido s preocupaes dos utilizadores com resilincia, comodidade e segurana. Nos ltimos meses, destaco essencialmente cinco elementos: (i) A medida transitria tomada no incio da fase de confinamento, de incrementar o limite mximo das operaes contactless, de 20 euros por operao para 50 euros, foi bem aceite por comerciantes e consumidores e, neste sentido, tornada definitiva em julho. Este aumento conduziu a uma maior utilizao desta forma de pagamento nos ltimos meses e temos a expectativa de que dever consolidar-se no futuro; (ii) Ainda em julho, foi publicado o Plano Nacional de Migrao para a Autenticao Forte do Cliente nas transaes de comrcio eletrnico com carto, que estabelece um conjunto de aes e prazos para que esta migrao decorra sem sobressaltos at 31 de dezembro prximo, data em que termina a fase de flexibilidade supervisiva prevista pela Autoridade Bancria Europeia (EBA). Este  um dos temas que iremos discutir nesta reunio interbancria. (iii) Mais tarde, em meados de outubro, concretizou-se a ligao da soluo nacional de transferncias imediatas ao TIPS (TARGET Instant Payment Settlement), assegurando, assim, a interoperabilidade europeia nas transferncias imediatas, um passo que permitir uma crescente utilizao deste instrumento num verdadeiro esprito SEPA; (iv) A 23 de outubro, o TARGET2 registou o maior incidente desde a sua implementao em 2007, tendo os servios de liquidao de pagamentos em moeda de banco central ficado indisponveis por cerca de 10 horas. A nota positiva  que, apesar das adversidades, aps a recuperao do sistema, a ao conjugada do Banco de Portugal, SIBS FPS e das instituies participantes permitiu assegurar a liquidao dos pagamentos necessrios, num montante superior a mil milhes de euros. Aproveitamos para assegurar que este incidente, causado por questes tcnicas ao nvel da plataforma nica centralizada, est a ser devidamente analisado pelo Eurosistema, em todas as suas perspetivas, e sero tomadas as medidas necessrias para evitar que volte a ocorrer. (v) Por ltimo, temos de salientar a recente aprovao, e publicao, da Estratgia Nacional para os Pagamentos de Retalho | Horizonte 2022, resultante do trabalho desenvolvido no mbito do Frum para os Sistemas de Pagamentos e que beneficiou de amplo consenso e contributos obtidos atravs de consulta pblica. A Estratgia  um documento estruturante para a evoluo do mercado de pagamentos de retalho em Portugal nos prximos dois anos e pretende atuar em 4 pilares: promover uma sociedade mais informada; potenciar os benefcios da transformao digital; contribuir para um enquadramento regulamentar que promova a inovao e a eficincia; e promover a adoo de solues de pagamento mais seguras. Vivemos, pois, uma evoluo para servios mais digitais e para disponibilizao de solues modernas, eficientes, seguras e, em grande medida, cada vez com maior integrao europeia. Aproveito para destacar que, em face das rpidas alteraes tecnolgicas que se tm verificado no ecossistema dos pagamentos de retalho e das mudanas muito significativas das preferncias dos consumidores, o Eurosistema decidiu explorar os prs e contras de emitir uma moeda digital de banco central, o euro digital. Atravs do seu Report on a digital euro divulgado no incio de outubro, o Eurosistema lanou as bases para um amplo debate que ganhar maior visibilidade nos prximos meses. Na sesso de hoje, pela importncia que entendemos que este tema poder ter para os prestadores de servios de pagamento, iremos apresentar as principais mensagens do relatrio e convidar-vos a participarem na consulta pblica ao documento, que decorrer at 12 de janeiro. No entanto, a sesso de hoje visa, sobretudo, proceder  atualizao de temas em curso no domnio dos pagamentos, e que se aproximam de novas fases de desenvolvimento: (i) O novo planeamento do projeto de evoluo dos servios TARGET , em especial no seguimento da deciso de adiar o go-live do projeto por um ano, para novembro de 2022, e porque  essencial para o seu sucesso que todos os intervenientes se encontrem devidamente preparados aquando da entrada em produo. Neste contexto, ser apresentado o novo planeamento do projeto de evoluo dos servios TARGET. (ii) A introduo de medidas para assegurar a reachability pan-europeia das transferncias imediatas at ao final do prximo ano, com base no TIPS, permitindo aos particulares e empresas efetuarem pagamentos eletrnicos em tempo real de e para qualquer pas europeu. Iremos descrever, de forma breve, as medidas a implementar de modo a assegurar esta verdadeira interoperabilidade. (iii) Aproxima-se a data de referncia de 31 de dezembro de 2020, crtica para a implementao dos requisitos de autenticao forte do cliente e comunicao comum e segura no contexto da Diretiva de Servios de Pagamento revista. No contexto do comrcio eletrnico com carto, e atendendo a que nos estamos a aproximar do Natal, uma altura do ano crucial para o comrcio eletrnico, e ainda mais este ano dada a situao da pandemia que atravessamos, urge sistematizar as situaes que ainda carecem de ao por parte dos prestadores de servios de pagamento, para que a migrao ocorra sem sobressaltos at 31 de dezembro. De notar que, para alm de acompanhar muito de perto os planos dos prestadores dos servios de pagamento, o Banco de Portugal tem realizado aes junto dos restantes intervenientes que tero de estar igualmente preparados: comerciantes e utilizadores. No primeiro caso, foi realizada uma sesso de esclarecimento com estas entidades; no segundo caso, iniciou-se esta semana uma campanha de comunicao nas redes sociais e website institucional do Banco de Portugal, que se alargar na prxima semana aos canais de televiso, e que visa, precisamente, alertar os utilizadores para as novas regras e para a necessidade de entrarem em contacto com o seu prestador de servios de pagamento. Desafiamos todos os prestadores de servios de pagamento a aproveitaram os materiais desta campanha, para reforarem as aes de comunicao com os vossos clientes. Por fim, ser ainda efetuado, no seguimento da publicao pelo Banco de Portugal, em julho deste ano, de uma carta-circular que sistematizava as desconformidades das interfaces dedicadas identificadas, um ponto de situao sobre a implementao dos requisitos de comunicao comum e segura. Sem mais demoras, seguiremos ento a ordem dos trabalhos. Agradecemos mais uma vez a vossa presena e o interesse demonstrado nos temas propostos para esta sesso. Muito obrigado.

Title: Intervention of Deputy Governor Luis Maximo dos Santos at the CIRSF Annual Conference: "Banking behavioral supervision: new challenges and perspectives"
text: Intervention of The Deputy Governor Luis... Intervention of Deputy Governor Luis Maximo dos Santos at the CIRSF Annual Conference: "Banking behavioral supervision: new challenges and perspectives" 12 nov. 2020 I would like to begin by thanking you for inviting me to participate in the Annual Conference of the Centre for Research, Regulation and Financial Supervision. I greet and congratulate Professor Luis Morais, as well as all those who contributed to the possible realization of this Conference, for the determination revealed to prevent this dramatic year of the Covid-19 pandemic from also being deprived of this event. I also greet all the other speakers and participants. The Covid-19 pandemic and the measures taken to combat it have greatly impacted all economic and social activity and, therefore, banking and financial activity in general. A new context has been created that conditions  even when we do not yet know  the actions of all economic agents: families, companies and the State. It should be stressed that, this time, overcoming some initial hesitations, coming mainly from political actors, the response of public authorities has been strongly converged and coordinated at European and national level, using all possible instruments: monetary policy, and it should be stressed once again the expeditious and correct action of the ECB; budgetary policy, with the suspension of existing European budgetary rules and the adoption of an unprecedented stimulus package; to regulatory and supervisory policy in its various plans: macro and micro prudential and behavioral, with various measures to alleviated regulatory requirements. The scale of the crisis, its abrupt and global character, combining a shock of supply and demand, did not leave much room for the attitude of the various public authorities to be different. This crisis generates - it is true - asymmetric effects, but it is still more symmetrical and profound than the global financial crisis, which facilitated greater consensus and speed in responses to be adopted. Therefore, what happened during the financial crisis was not repeated. At the moment, it is far from clear what the profile of the economic recovery will be. The answer to this question will decisively affect our future and what will happen to the banking system and will illuminate the real scale of the problems we will have to face, which, even in the most optimistic cases, in my view, will always be of high magnitude. I will focus on the additional challenges that the pandemic has brought to banking behavioural supervision and the importance of banking to ensure confidence in the banking system and thereby contribute to financial stability. In fact, this crisis has proved to be an occasion  which was obviously dispensed with  to demonstrate that the purposes of prudential supervision and behavioural supervision, rather than conflicting, converge on the ultimate purpose of strengthening the banking system. In fact, the stability of the institutions will not be achieved without providing their clients, while respecting the general regulatory framework, adequate and reasonable solutions to their problems. The pandemic has accelerated consumers' use of banking products in all areas. It was a trend that had been going on for a long time, but with the pandemic, by force of circumstances, the increase was evident. This acceleration is an additional challenge for behavioral supervisors. In this context, it should be noted that, in June of this year, Banco de Portugal established, as a result of Guidelines from the European Banking Authority and its own experience in supervising the marketing of financial products and services through digital channels, a set of good practices to be observed by banks in the marketing of banking products and services through digital channels. On the other hand, at the very beginning of the pandemic, Banco de Portugal adopted several regulatory measures in the area of behavioural supervision, depending on the circumstances created by the pandemic, namely: (i) Flexibilization of certain regulatory provisions; (ii) Recommendation to institutions for the need to comply with the European Banking Authority Guidelines on public and private moratoriums applied to credit operations; (iii) Regulation of the duties of providing information to bank customers to be observed by the institutions in relation to moratoriums; (iv) Definition of the content of the information that institutions should report to Banco de Portugal with regard to the application of moratoriums. The current picture is very demanding for all supervisors of conduct in the banking sector. The pandamic context threatens the solvency of many customers by the effect of loss of income and increased unemployment; litigation with institutions will tend to increase and, therefore, complaints directed at the supervisor as well; financial training  one of the structuring pillars of Banco de Portugal's action in the behavioral field  will have to be revised and adjusted to conditions compatible with the pandemic, which, moreover, has been happening since the beginning of the second half of this year. On the other hand, the technological revolution also involves a revolution in the way of supervising and is thus a complex challenge for us to have good and effective regulation. The so-called RegTech is a path of no return, but it is still at its beginning. But the use of digital technologies has no magical or saving virtues, nor does it solve problems by itself. The speed of innovation has as a counterpart that obsolescence is also faster, being, therefore, shorter the cycles of innovation and the gains they generate. The ongoing process of digital transformation has enchanting, almost magical effects when we hear certain speakers. But knowing, in the deepest sense of the word, is much more than using technology. Knowledge does not come solely from the technological process. It is, moreover, curious to see how the extraordinary technological development coincides at a time when, paradoxically, concepts and visions that would be said to be pre-Enlightenment gain ing in society. The permanent revolution of our way of life therefore obliges us not to lose sight of the dimension of human behaviour at its base. In an era of massive diffusion of technology, it is the human factor that will tend to make a difference and be the basis of lasting economic success. The solidity of institutions must be based on the ethics practiced and not on the proclaimed ethics. For reasons we all know, this is even more true as far as the banking sector is concerned. The year 2020 has already marked our lives. Suddenly, the whole world found itself confronted with a pandemic that undermines the foundations of our life in society. From unbelief, we quickly moved on to deepest fear. The fragility of our condition emerged with surprising and overwhelming evidence in the hypertechnological society of our time. Homo Deus, to use the concept of the Israeli essayist Yuval Harari, saw himself faced with an unexpected return to a very distant past, which we knew possible, but actually only imagined as abstraction. Guided by the instinct of survival, societies and countries reacted, although not exactly the same, nor at synchronized rhythms, adopting measures that at the moment immediately before would be deemed unthinkable. At Banco de Portugal we are united in the face of this hard test and we will do everything to meet the demands we are faced with in our mission and thus generate confidence in the banking sector Portuguese and its customers. Thank you so much for your attention.
text_original: Interveno do Vice-Governador Lus... Interveno do Vice-Governador Lus Mximo dos Santos na Conferncia Anual do CIRSF: "Superviso comportamental bancria: novos desafios e perspetivas" 12 nov. 2020 Gostaria de comear por agradecer o convite para participar na Conferncia Anual do Centro de Investigao, Regulao e Superviso Financeira. Cumprimento e felicito o Professor Lus Morais, bem como todos os que contriburam para que a realizao desta Conferncia fosse possvel, pela determinao revelada em evitar que neste dramtico ano da pandemia da Covid-19 ficssemos privados tambm deste evento. Sado igualmente todos os demais oradores e participantes. A pandemia da Covid-19 e as medidas adotadas para a combater impactaram enormemente em toda a atividade econmica e social e, portanto, na atividade bancria e financeira em geral. Foi criado um novo contexto que condiciona  at quando ainda no sabemos  a atuao de todos os agentes econmicos: famlias, empresas e Estado. Importa sublinhar que, desta vez, superadas algumas hesitaes iniciais, provenientes, sobretudo, dos agentes polticos, a resposta das autoridades pblicas foi fortemente convergente e coordenada a nvel europeu e nacional, recorrendo a todos os instrumentos possveis:  poltica monetria, sendo de sublinhar, mais uma vez, a atuao expedita e acertada do BCE;  poltica oramental, com a suspenso das regras oramentais europeias em vigor e a adoo de um pacote de estmulos sem precedentes;  poltica regulatria e de superviso nos seus diversos planos: macro e micro prudencial e comportamental, com vrias medidas de alvio dos requisitos regulatrios. A dimenso da crise, o seu carter abrupto e global, conjugando um choque da oferta e da procura, no deixou muito espao para que a atitude dos diversos poderes pblicos pudesse ser outra. Esta crise gera - verdade -efeitos assimtricos, mas, ainda assim,  mais simtrica e profunda do que a crise financeira global, o que facilitou maior consenso e rapidez nas respostas a adotar. No se repetiu, portanto, o que se passou aquando da crise financeira. Neste momento, est longe de ser claro qual vai ser o perfil da recuperao econmica. A resposta a essa pergunta condicionar decisivamente o nosso futuro e o que se passar com o sistema bancrio e ir iluminar qual a real dimenso dos problemas que teremos de defrontar, os quais, mesmo nas hipteses mais otimistas, a meu ver, sero sempre de elevada magnitude. Irei focar-me nos desafios adicionais que a pandemia trouxe  superviso comportamental bancria e  importncia da mesma para garantir a confiana no sistema bancrio e, desse modo, contribuir para a estabilidade financeira. Na verdade, esta crise tem-se revelado uma ocasio  que obviamente se dispensava  para demonstrar que as finalidades da superviso prudencial e da superviso comportamental, ao invs de conflituarem, convergem no propsito ltimo de robustecer o sistema bancrio. De facto, no se conseguir a estabilidade das instituies sem propiciar aos seus clientes, no respeito do quadro regulatrio geral, solues adequadas e razoveis para os respetivos problemas. A pandemia veio acelerar, em todos os domnios, o recurso aos canais digitais por parte dos consumidores de produtos bancrios. Era uma tendncia h muito em curso, mas com a pandemia, por fora das circunstncias, o incremento foi evidente. Essa acelerao constitui um desafio adicional para os supervisores comportamentais. Neste contexto, importa realar que, em junho deste ano, o Banco de Portugal fixou, em decorrncia de Orientaes da Autoridade Bancria Europeia e da sua prpria experincia na superviso da comercializao dos produtos e servios financeiros atravs de canais digitais, um conjunto de boas prticas a observar pelos bancos na comercializao de produtos e servios bancrios atravs de canais digitais. Por outro lado, logo na fase inicial da pandemia, o Banco de Portugal adotou vrias providncias regulamentares, no plano da superviso comportamental, em funo das circunstncias criadas pela pandemia, designadamente: (i)Flexibilizao de determinadas disposies regulatrias; (ii)Recomendao s instituies para a necessidade de darem adequado cumprimento s Orientaes da Autoridade Bancria Europeia relativas a moratrias pblicas e privadas aplicadas a operaes de crdito; (iii)Regulamentao dos deveres de prestao de informao aos clientes bancrios a observar pelas instituies relativamente s moratrias; (iv)Definio do contedo da informao que as instituies devem reportar ao Banco de Portugal no que diz respeito  aplicao de moratrias. O quadro atual mostra-se muito exigente para todos os supervisores de conduta no domnio do setor bancrio. O contexto pandmico ameaa a solvncia de muitos clientes, pelo efeito de perda de rendimento e do aumento do desemprego; a litigiosidade com as instituies tender a aumentar e, portanto, as reclamaes dirigidas ao supervisor tambm; a formao financeira  um dos pilares estruturantes da atuao do Banco de Portugal no domnio comportamental -ter de ser revista e ajustada a condies compatveis com a pandemia, o que, alis, j est a acontecer desde o incio do segundo semestre deste ano. Por outro lado, a revoluo tecnolgica implica tambm uma revoluo no modo de fazer superviso e constitui, assim, um desafio complexo para que tenhamos uma boa e eficaz regulao. O chamado RegTech  um caminho sem retorno, mas est ainda no seu incio. Mas o recurso s tecnologias digitais no tem virtudes mgicas ou salvficas, nem resolve os problemas s por si. A rapidez da inovao tem como contrapartida que a obsolescncia seja tambm mais rpida, sendo, portanto, mais curtos os ciclos de inovao e os ganhos que geram. O processo de transformao digital em curso tem efeitos encantatrios, quase mgicos, quando ouvimos certos oradores. Mas conhecer, no mais profundo sentido da palavra,  bem mais do que usar tecnologia. O conhecimento no advm unicamente do processo tecnolgico. , alis, curioso verificar, como o extraordinrio desenvolvimento tecnolgico coincide num tempo em que, paradoxalmente, ganham terreno na sociedade conceitos e vises que se diriam pr-iluministas. Por isso, a revoluo permanente do nosso modo de vida obriga-nos a no perder de vista que na sua base est, sem dvida, a dimenso do comportamento humano. Numa era de difuso massiva da tecnologia,  o fator humano que tender a fazer a diferena e a ser a base do xito econmico duradouro. A solidez das instituies tem de assentar na tica praticada e no na tica proclamada. Por razes que todos sabemos, isso  ainda mais verdadeiro no que ao setor bancrio diz respeito. O ano de 2020 j marcou as nossas vidas. De sbito, o mundo inteiro viu-se confrontado com uma pandemia que mina as bases da nossa vida em sociedade. Da incredulidade, rapidamente passmos ao medo mais profundo. A fragilidade da nossa condio emergiu com uma evidncia surpreendente e esmagadora na hipertecnolgica sociedade do nosso tempo. O Homo Deus, para usar o conceito do ensasta israelita Yuval Harari, viuse confrontado com um inesperado regresso a um passado muito distante, que sabamos possvel, mas na verdade s imaginvamos como abstrao. Guiados pelo instinto de sobrevivncia, as sociedades e os pases reagiram, ainda que no de modo exatamente igual, nem a ritmos sincronizados, adotando medidas que no momento imediatamente anterior se julgariam impensveis. No Banco de Portugal estamos unidos perante mais esta prova dura e tudo faremos para corresponder s exigncias com que estamos confrontados na nossa misso e, assim, gerar confiana no setor bancrio portugus e nos seus clientes. Muito obrigado pela vossa ateno.

Title: Speech by the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Mario Centeno, at the 10th Banco de Portugal Conference "Economic development Portuguese in the European area": The challenge for the design of public policies
text: Intervention of the Governor of the Bank... Speech by the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Mario Centeno, at the 10th Banco de Portugal Conference "Economic development Portuguese in the European area": The challenge for the design of public policies 16 nov. 2020 We are facing a crisis that has all the characteristics of a temporary crisis. The extraordinary reaction of economic activity to the reduction of containment measures at the end of spring was a clear demonstration of this temporary nature. However, its intensity and some of the longer-lasting consequences oblige us to be more demanding in defining public policies for each phase of the crisis, but mainly for the period after the crisis. And this is the most suitable forum to put this challenge Let me tell you briefly what you're going to be staying with us: what's not temporary. It is not temporary, from the outthen, the increase in debt: public debt and private debt. Even if the increase in private savings can respond in part to this challenge, particularly in the size of private debt, a level of public debt remains, which was shrinking in the period before the crisis, but which now has a leap that economists like to describe as discreet. And there will also be greater inequality with us, precisely what we discussed this morning. This new inequality adds to a new generation suffering two massive crises in less than 10 years. The labour economy has known for many years the importance that the initial moments of insertion in the labour market have in defining the entire trajectory in the market and here we have a generation composed of many tens of thousands of workers who entered the labour market and were faced with two crises in succession. These are some of the factors that will stay with us and that we have to think about when we approach the issue of public policy making. What requirements would you like to put on the table in the challenge I propose to you? What does the temporary nature of the crisis impose on public policies? I'm going to focus on four factors. The first is that, more than ever, new policies must act on the sidelines. Debt levels make massive interventions in social support and the economy prohibitive. We have to be even more demanding than before and therefore we must be more focused. Support should be focused, we must avoid at all costs supporting unviable business projects and we should focus support on workers with greater difficulty in including inclusion in the post-pandamic labour market. If this is a common concern in the definition of public policies today, in the situation we are in, this priority becomes even more evident. The second dimension is that public support should be temporary. In the face of a non-structural crisis, we must not change the fundamental characteristics of our social and economic support system. We should be even more focused, but with temporary support. In fact, permanent changes at this time will distort the mechanisms to support the resumption of activity and become more difficult to adapt in the future. And they run the risk of not responding to the demands of the nature of the crisis at hand. The third dimension in the definition of public policies is a little more clear from this logic of supporting inequality and the labour market, but it is absolutely crucial for the recovery. Public funds that are devoted to investment should give priority to projects that are already underway and that show sustainability, not only financially, but also environmentally. That is the transition we are called. Public investment, which is, moreover, essential for the development of the country, must be thought of in order to catalyze private investment, which, in fact, constitutes the vast majority of total investment in any economy and also in Portugal. For an effective recovery, in so that the measures we are defining in social and economic support are felt and impacted, public resources must be focused on projects that are underway and which are already a huge public effort. The fourth dimension of the challenge is to seek employment support that promotes employment not in the same companies and sectors, but in new hires and net job creation. This is a theme that is always present in crises of the dimension of the one we are living. The final phase of the recovery is characterised by an active redeployment of employment between companies and between sectors. This is natural evolution. There is an increase in relocation and redeployment that is closely linked to improved productivity and, therefore, also to the reduction of levels of inequality by promoting the labour market. We must move this support to this relocation activity. It must be supported, we must not have policies that constitute barriers to this mobility. Defining these policies is not trivial, but the focus of the drawing should move in this direction. I note that this change should not promote  and does not tend to promote  the disprotection of workers' incomes. But, on the contrary, it promotes the progression of income of these same workers between jobs. These challenges in defining public policies can be framed very easily in what was also the challenge that Professor Richard Blundell left us here. When having to act on the sidelines, by having to be focused, by having to be inclusive and encompassing the different dimensions of economic activity, the policy mix must be directed to policies ranging from human capital policies, education and training; labour market policies, which also include the minimum wage; and, of course, to companies, to competition and regulatory policies, which are those which, at the end of any transformation process, will be the mechanisms for bringing public policies closer to people, businesses and society as a whole. These policies should be designed with businesses and workers in mind at the same time. I will leave you with two or three figures of what has been the Portuguese experience since the end of the great economic recession we suffered in the context of the adjustment programme. Between 2019 and 2013, salaries declared to Social Security in Portugal increased by 32% in nominal terms. This 32% represented an increase of EUR 12 billion in the amount of salary paid in Portugal. That's 6% of GDP rising in the wage bill. This in a context of low inflation. What is most surprising is that, from this increase, 10% corresponded to the average salary  there was an increase in the average salary representing something like EUR 3.9 billion if we kept the employment level constant  but 8.5 billion euros, the remaining 22%, went to the growth of wage employment in Portugal. In other words, since the end of the crisis, the labour market in Portugal has absorbed 22% more workers with salaried social security records. This dynamic has to be taken up again, with more efficient markets and more targeted policies. The challenge I leave to researchers is: how we have been able to complement public policies so that we can join forces with all the resources generated in the labor market, in order to reduce income inequality in Portugal. I see no way this will happen if it is not through income generated in the markets  and the labour market in Portugal gave an extraordinary response in the period after the 2011-2013 crisis  and thus allow the country to be more competitive to give jobs to the many talents it forms every year in its education system, at different levels. Now I leave you with some of these brilliant talents that will so deservedly be distinguished by their work at the Portuguese University. I am sure that this talent will be transluded to the labour market and will see its value in terms of insertion and progression in the labour market. This is the need and challenge of public policies in Portugal. Inequality must be tackled in this very wide range of actions and it cannot leave anyone out: neither in the strict sense of inequality nor of those who have to respond to it. Thank you very much and congratulations to the winners. 10th Banco de Portugal Conference "Economic development Portuguese the European area"

Conferncia do Banco de Portugal "Desenvolvimento econmico portugus no espao europeu": O desafio para o desenho de polticas pblicas 16 nov. 2020 Estamos perante uma crise que tem todas as caractersticas de uma crise temporria. A extraordinria reao da atividade econmica  reduo das medidas de confinamento, no fim da primavera, foi uma clara demonstrao deste carter temporrio. No entanto, a sua intensidade e algumas das consequncias mais duradouras, obrigamnos a ser mais exigentes na definio das polticas pblicas para cada uma das fases da crise, mas, principalmente, para o perodo a seguir  crise. E este  o frum mais adequado para colocar este desafio Deixem-me falar brevemente do que  que vai ficar connosco: o que  que no  temporrio. No  temporrio, desde logo, o aumento da dvida: da dvida pblica e da dvida privada. Mesmo que o aumento da poupana privada possa responder em parte a este desafio, em particular na dimenso da dvida privada, mantm-se um nvel de dvida pblica, que vinha a reduzir-se no perodo anterior  crise, mas que agora tem aqui um salto que os economistas gostam de descrever como discreto. E vai manter-se tambm connosco uma maior desigualdade, precisamente aquilo que discutimos esta manh. Esta nova desigualdade acresce a uma nova gerao que sofre duas crises massivas em menos de 10 anos. A economia do trabalho sabe, h muitos anos, a importncia que os momentos iniciais de insero no mercado de trabalho tm na definio de toda a trajetria no mercado e temos aqui uma gerao composta por muitas dezenas de milhares de trabalhadores que entraram no mercado de trabalho e foram confrontados com duas crises em sucesso. Estes so alguns dos fatores que vo ficar connosco e que ns temos que pensar neles quando abordamos a questo da definio de polticas pblicas. Quais so os requisitos que gostaria de pr em cima da mesa no desafio que vos proponho? O que  que o carter temporrio da crise impe s polticas pblicas? Vou focar-me em quatro fatores. O primeiro  o de que, mais do que nunca, as novas polticas devem atuar na margem. Os nveis de dvida tornam proibitivas intervenes massivas nos apoios sociais e  economia. Temos que ser ainda mais exigentes do que antes e, portanto, devemos ser mais focados. Os apoios devem ser focados, devemos evitar a todo o custo apoiar projetos empresariais inviveis e devemos concentrar os apoios nos trabalhadores com maior dificuldade de incluso no mercado de trabalho ps-pandmico. Se esta  uma preocupao habitual na definio de polticas pblicas, hoje, na situao em que nos encontramos, esta prioridade torna-se ainda mais evidente. A segunda dimenso  a de que os apoios pblicos devem ser temporrios. Perante uma crise que no  estrutural, no devemos alterar as caractersticas fundamentais do nosso sistema de apoio social e econmico. Devemos ser ainda mais focados, mas com apoios temporrios. Na verdade, alteraes permanentes neste momento iro distorcer os mecanismos de apoio  retoma da atividade e tornam-se mais difceis de adaptar no futuro. E correm o risco de no responder s exigncias da natureza da crise que temos em mos. A terceira dimenso na definio das polticas pblicas foge um pouco mais a esta lgica de apoio  desigualdade e ao mercado de trabalho, mas  absolutamente crucial para a retoma. Os fundos pblicos que forem devotados ao investimento devem dar prioridade aos projetos que j esto em curso e que mostram sustentabilidade, no apenas financeira, mas tambm ambiental.  essa a transio a que estamos chamados. O investimento pblico, que , alis, essencial para o desenvolvimento do pas, deve ser pensado de forma a catalisar o investimento privado, que, na verdade, constitui a vastssima maioria do investimento total em qualquer economia e tambm em Portugal. Para uma retoma eficaz, para que as medidas que estamos a definir nos apoios sociais e econmicos se faam sentir e tenham impacto, os recursos pblicos devem estar focados em projetos que esto em curso e que constituem j um enorme esforo pblico. A quarta dimenso do desafio  a de procurarmos apoios ao emprego que promovam o emprego no nas mesmas empresas e setores, mas em novas contrataes e na criao lquida de emprego. Este  um tema que est sempre presente em crises da dimenso daquela que estamos a viver. A fase final da retoma  caracterizada por uma ativa reafectao de emprego entre empresas e entre setores. Esta  a evoluo natural. H um aumento da realocao e da reafetao que est intimamente ligado  melhoria da produtividade e, portanto, tambm  reduo dos nveis de desigualdade pela promoo que faz do mercado de trabalho. Devemos mover esses apoios para esta atividade de realocao. Ela deve ser apoiada, no devemos ter polticas que se constituam como barreiras a esta mobilidade. Definir estas polticas no  trivial, mas o foco do desenho deve mover-se nesse sentido. Fao notar que esta mudana no deve promover  e no tende a promover  a desproteo de rendimento dos trabalhadores. Mas, pelo contrrio, promove a progresso de rendimento desses mesmos trabalhadores entre empregos. Estes desafios  definio de polticas pblicas podem ser enquadrados muito facilmente naquilo que foi tambm o desafio que o Professor Richard Blundell aqui nos deixou. Ao ter que atuar na margem, ao ter que ser focado, ao ter que ser inclusivo e englobador das diferentes dimenses da atividade econmica, o mix de polticas deve dirigir-se a polticas que vo desde as polticas de capital humano, da educao e da formao; as polticas de mercado de trabalho, que incluem tambm o salrio mnimo; e, obviamente, s empresas, s polticas de concorrncia e regulao, que so aquelas que, no fim de qualquer processo de transformao, vo constituir os mecanismos de aproximao das polticas pblicas s pessoas, s empresas e  sociedade como um todo. Estas polticas devem ser desenhadas a pensar nas empresas e nos trabalhadores em simultneo. Vou deixar-vos com dois ou trs nmeros do que foi a experincia portuguesa desde o fim da grande recesso econmica que sofremos no contexto do programa de ajustamento. Entre 2019 e 2013, os salrios declarados  Segurana Social em Portugal aumentaram 32% em termos nominais. Esses 32% representaram mais 12 mil milhes de euros de massa salarial paga em Portugal. So 6% do PIB de aumento da massa salarial. Isto num contexto de baixa inflao. O mais surpreendente  que, deste aumento, 10% correspondeu ao salrio mdio  houve um aumento do salrio mdio que representa qualquer coisa como 3,9 mil milhes de euros, se mantivssemos o nvel emprego constante , mas 8,5 mil milhes de euros, os restantes 22%, foram para o crescimento do emprego assalariado em Portugal. Ou seja, desde o fim da crise, o mercado de trabalho em Portugal absorveu mais 22% de trabalhadores com registos assalariados na Segurana Social. Esta dinmica tem que ser retomada, com mercados mais eficientes e com polticas mais direcionadas. O desafio que deixo aos investigadores : como conseguimos complementar as polticas pblicas para que una esforos com todos os recursos gerados no mercado de trabalho, de modo a reduzir a desigualdade de rendimentos em Portugal. No vejo maneira disso acontecer se no for atravs de rendimentos gerados nos mercados  e o mercado de trabalho em Portugal deu uma resposta extraordinria no perodo posterior  crise de 2011-2013  e permitir, assim, que o pas seja mais competitivo para dar emprego aos inmeros talentos que forma todos os anos no seu sistema de ensino, nos diferentes nveis. Agora deixo-vos com alguns desses brilhantes talentos que to merecidamente vo ser distinguidos pelos seus trabalhos na Universidade portuguesa. Estou certo que esse talento se transpor para o mercado de trabalho e ver valorizar a sua valia em termos de insero e progresso no mercado de trabalho.  essa a necessidade e o desafio das polticas pblicas em Portugal. A desigualdade tem que ser combatida neste conjunto muito vasto de aes e no pode deixar ningum de fora: nem no sentido estrito da desigualdade nem daqueles que tm que lhe dar resposta. Muito obrigado e felicidades aos premiados. 10. Conferncia do Banco de Portugal "Desenvolvimento econmico portugus no espao europeu"

Title: Opening speech by Banco de Portugal Governor Mario Centeno at the Money Conference
text: Intervention of opening of the Government... Opening speech by Banco de Portugal Governor Mario Centeno at the Money Conference 20 nov. 2020 Good morning, everyone. In these times we live in, it is important to reflect on the challenges brought by the COVID-19 pandemic, not only to the financial system, but also to the economy and society. I therefore welcome the initiative of TSF and Cash. The risks of the financial system stem from the impact of the pandemic at this point and our attention is focused on these developments. The existence of a healthy, robust and dynamic financial system is essential to support the economy, businesses and families and ensure the economic and social development of the country. Portugal took too long to act on that front. It did so after most European countries, in the context of the financial and sovereign crises, and this had consequences in supporting the economy, businesses and families in the exit crisis. During the last decade, the risks and weaknesses of financial institutions have been highlighted, which have encountered difficulties in adverse economic circumstances and high uncertainty. And the country realized the cost, in terms of equity and efficiency, of not having a financial system prepared. At the end of 2015, the Portuguese financial system was undercapitalized, with unastable shareholder structures, in breach of business plans and obligations assumed before the authorities. Today, no one recognizes these problems in the banking system Portuguese. In the last decade, measures have been adopted by banks  managers and shareholders  by legislators and regulators and supervisors that have increased the resilience of the financial system. These measures have transcended national spaces and have rightly taken on a European dimension. The process of European integration, of which, in the Banking Union, the creation of the Single Supervisory Mechanism is an example, played a very important role. In the run-up to the crisis, we have accumulated reliable capital, risk reduction and even risk sharing that we cannot undo. The importance of this framework was evident in the reaction to the inesterical outbreak, not only in the size of the support, but also in its speed and scope. This response has so far made it possible to minimise the implications and transmission to financial stability. The response to the pandemic has imposed the action of governments, central banks, financial regulators and, at European level, the Community institutions. Having a resilient financial system was crucial to the speed and intensity of the measures adopted. By having stronger capital and liquidity positions than in the previous financial crisis, the banking system contributed to the accommodation of the initial pandemic shock, ensuring that economic agents had the necessary credit at their disposal and reducing deleveraging pressures. The banks were part of the solution, they were not part of the problem. But the financial system still faces enormous challenges. Containment measures taken to respond to the first wave of the pandemic disrupted economic activity in vast sectors, triggering massive increases in underemployment. And without concerted public intervention, we would have seen a credit and liquidity crisis, which would lead to a wave of insolvencies with consequences for economic and financial stability. The response of the different public policies was effective, achieving their objectives. Governments acted in preserving employment and ensured liquidity with moratoriums and secured credits. Central banks have provided massive emergency liquidity lines and supervisors have relaxed prudential rules. Markets stabilized and credit flowed to businesses and households. Companies have preserved productive conditions and households have increased their savings. When we were reacting to the crisis in a context where we had no "instruction book", given the global, unprecedented and unexpected character of the crisis, the result was positive. In a second phase, the gradual lifting of restrictions on economic activity led to an immediate and faster and more intense recovery than anticipated. Despite this positive development, and even if we did not have a second wave, we could say that the crisis was not over yet. In any case, it is already safe to say that it has created legacies for financial stability in the medium term. The commitment of european budgetary and monetary authorities is to keep an eye on developments in the economy and its vulnerabilities. I'm sure they will remain. The action of central banks should continue to show all the availability, flexibility and speed of action we have seen so far. An approach that will not fail to be demonstrated at the next Governing Council meeting in December, which in December is expected to recalibrate its instruments to ensure that financing conditions remain favourable to support the economic recovery and neutralise the negative impact of the pandemic on the path of inflation. Eurosystem policies, together with measures taken by national governments and European institutions, remain essential to support access to finance, including for those most affected by the ramifications of the pandemic. These measures include the possible expansion of the asset purchase programme (PEPP), with the flexibility that was introduced in the spring. Budgetary authorities are also committed to the adequacy of their response to the evolution of the crisis. The budget plans presented in the autumn for 2021 show that the budgetary position will remain the same as the consequences of the crisis. The budgetary space created in the previous period made room for all countries to react with fiscal stimulus. That's good news. With uncertainty high and recovery still partial, the risks of an early withdrawal of support seem serious, requiring careful assessments. The proper modulation of exit strategies should take into account developments in health, economic and financial developments. The different authorities should also coordinate this moment of policy change. We know that the crisis, like all crises, has generated losses. These losses are, as always with crises, asymmetrically distributed among the members of society. Inequality increases. And the dispersion of losses over time is the only way to prevent the impossibilities and inevitability of having no alternative in the future. The conclusion I draw is that we know from now that the crisis has brought with it an increase in public debt and private debt, as well as an increase in inequality. This reality must be taken into account when defining public policies. But at a conference on the financial system, it is also an opportunity to focus on the challenges facing bank customers, particularly non-financial companies, and the risks that can lead to increased indebtedness. The economic scenarios we have outlined always depend on the starting point. Let us see then what the reality of Portuguese non-financial corporations, whose portrait the INE updated at the end of October and which unfortunately went almost unnoticed. Non-financial companies represent a universe of more than one million and three hundred thousand companies. From the lowest point of the sovereign debt crisis (2013 to the generality of indicators), this enormous productive universe has had a unique transformation and in itself unprecedented. Unprecedented because it added sustainability to productive sectors that many said would not be able to promote the convergence of the Portuguese economy with European averages. Happened. Vab grew 43%, gross operating surplus more than 50%. This increase in activity and results was achieved with the simultaneous combination of two unusual factors: a massive increase in investment, with an additional 113% of FBCF (private investment more than doubled) and a reduction in the debt-to-asset ratio, which fell by more than 53 percentage points. And companies have become more efficient, with Labour Productivity growing by 15%. This growth was inclusive, i.e. it had employment and pay. In fact, the number of people in service in these companies increased by 25% and total remuneration by 41% in just six years. The weight of remuneration in vab grew by 3.3 pp, reaching a value close to 60%. Financial deleveraging, investment, more employment and more efficient. This was the picture of the country we built after the sovereign crisis and until the end of 2019. We owe it to the efforts of Portuguese companies. We didn't get to the crisis without homework done. We can continue to deny the country we have, but it only helps the country, not the Portuguese. It was, moreover, with these figures, which go out of the indicators before the financial crisis in a very broad way, that we reached the end of 2019. That is, we arrived at the beginning of 2020 with a unique business dynamics in Portugal. This dynamic is explained by what has happened in SMEs. SME investment increased by 131% and productivity by 23%. The reduction in the debt burden on the asset reached 65 pp and the solvency index progressed by 18 pp. All of these, indicators above the national average. The sectoral reality is even more impressive of the transformation that has occurred in Portugal, especially in the last five years. The increase in productivity was higher in the sectors most affected by the crisis: 50% in Housing and Catering; 52% in Real Estate; 32% in manufacturing and 26% in commerce. Deleveraging was particularly strong in Commerce and Real Estate, minus 100 pp, debt goes from 280% of assets to 180%. Of course, the pandemic put a brake on some of these developments and put challenges to all of them. This brake was severe, but it will be temporary if we can maintain production capacity and are prepared, and we have already demonstrated from June that we were, to resume the activity completely. We must be aware that in the medium term, over-indebtedness can lead to reduced investment, weakening competitiveness and economic growth. To address this difficulty, measures to strengthen corporate capital are needed to reduce leverage and increase their debt service capacity. Efficient use of public funds requires the establishment of procedures enabling the effective identification of viable undertakings, which should be the privileged receivers of this support. In parallel, it is necessary to ensure the resilience of the banking system in the face of a likely increase in credit losses. On the one hand, banks have begun to provision credit risks from the outset, thus taking an appropriate prudential step. But on the other hand, the banking system continues to face profitability problems and must respond to the challenges posed by digitisation. The solutions to these challenges should not only originate in each country, but should have a European focus. Financial institutions also have to play their part by responding to challenges with determination and making decisions that do not forget the importance of their responsible contribution to supporting the economy, businesses and families. Always keeping in mind the concern to defend your resilience. The banking sector has endured the crisis quite well so far, despite a number of risks and vulnerabilities. It helped absorb the shock and avoided a credit crisis that would have been detrimental to the economy. But we must not lose sight of the main structural weaknesses of the European banking sector, which were evident before this crisis. We need to continue to reduce overcapacity and improve cost-effectiveness to cope with low profitability by looking for business models that respond to an increasingly digital economy. I hope that this morning's debate will make a very useful contribution to the banking system continuing to be a responsible agent in responding to the crisis and know and face the challenges that will follow. Thank you very much.
text_original: Interveno de abertura do Governad... Interveno de abertura do Governador do Banco de Portugal, Mrio Centeno, na Money Conference 20 nov. 2020 Bom dia a todos. Nestes tempos que vivemos,  importante refletir sobre os desafios trazidos pela pandemia da COVID-19, no s ao sistema financeiro, mas tambm  economia e  sociedade. Sado, por isso, a iniciativa da TSF e do Dinheiro Vivo. Os riscos do sistema financeiro derivam neste momento do impacto da pandemia e a nossa ateno est centrada nesses desenvolvimentos. A existncia de um sistema financeiro saudvel, robusto e dinmico  fundamental para apoiar a economia, as empresas e as famlias e garantir o desenvolvimento econmico e social do pas. Portugal tardou demasiado tempo em atuar nessa frente. F-lo depois da generalidade dos pases europeus, no contexto das crises financeira e soberana, e isso teve consequncias no apoio  economia, s empresas e s famlias na sada crise. Durante a ltima dcada, foram colocados em evidncia os riscos e debilidades das instituies financeiras, que atravessaram dificuldades em circunstncias econmicas adversas e de elevada incerteza. E o pas percebeu o custo, em termos de equidade e eficincia, de no ter um sistema financeiro preparado. No final de 2015, o sistema financeiro portugus estava subcapitalizado, com estruturas acionista instveis, em incumprimento de planos de negcios e obrigaes assumidas perante as autoridades. Hoje, ningum reconhece estes problemas no sistema bancrio portugus. Na ltima dcada foram adotadas medidas pelos bancos  gestores e acionistas , pelos legisladores e reguladores e pelos supervisores que permitiram aumentar a resilincia do sistema financeiro. Estas medidas transcenderam os espaos nacionais e tomaram, e bem, uma dimenso europeia. O processo de integrao europeia, de que, na Unio Bancria,  exemplo a criao do Mecanismo nico de Superviso, teve um papel muito importante. No perodo anterior  crise pandmica, acumulmos um capital de confiana, de reduo do risco e at de partilha de risco que no podemos desbaratar. A importncia deste enquadramento foi evidente na reao ao surto pandmico, no apenas na dimenso do apoio, mas tambm na sua rapidez e abrangncia. Esta resposta permitiu, at este momento, minimizar as implicaes e a transmisso  estabilidade financeira. A resposta  pandemia imps a ao de Governos, bancos centrais, reguladores financeiros e, no plano europeu, das instituies comunitrias. Termos um sistema financeiro resiliente foi determinante para a rapidez e intensidade das medidas aprovadas. Por ter posies de capital e liquidez mais slidas do que na anterior crise financeira, o sistema bancrio contribuiu para a acomodao do choque inicial da pandemia, garantindo que os agentes econmicos tivessem  sua disposio o crdito necessrio e reduzindo as presses de desalavancagem. Os bancos fizeram parte da soluo, no foram parte do problema. Mas o sistema financeiro enfrenta ainda enormes desafios. As medidas de confinamento adotadas para responder  primeira vaga da pandemia interromperam a atividade econmica em vastos setores, desencadeando aumentos macios no subemprego. E sem uma interveno pblica concertada, teramos assistido a uma crise de crdito e de liquidez, que levaria a uma vaga de insolvncias com consequncias na estabilidade econmica e financeira. A resposta das diferentes polticas pblicas foi eficaz, alcanando os seus objetivos. Os governos atuaram na preservao do emprego e asseguraram a liquidez com moratrias e crditos garantidos. Os bancos centrais disponibilizaram linhas de liquidez de emergncia massivas e os supervisores flexibilizaram as regras prudenciais. Os mercados estabilizaram e o crdito fluiu para empresas e famlias. As empresas preservaram as condies produtivas e as famlias aumentaram a poupana. Quando estvamos a reagir  crise num contexto em que no tnhamos livro de instrues, dado o caracter global, indito e inesperado da crise, o resultado foi positivo. Numa segunda fase, o levantamento gradual das restries  atividade econmica levou a uma recuperao imediata e mais rpida e intensa do que o previsto. Apesar desta evoluo positiva, e mesmo que no tivssemos uma segunda vaga, podamos dizer que a crise ainda no tinha acabado. Em qualquer caso, j  seguro dizer que criou legados para a estabilidade financeira a mdio prazo. O compromisso das autoridades oramentais e monetrias europeias  o de se manterem atentas  evoluo da economia e das suas vulnerabilidades. Estou certo que assim permanecero. A ao dos bancos centrais dever continuar a mostrar toda a disponibilidade, flexibilidade e rapidez de atuao a que assistimos at aqui. Uma abordagem que no deixar de ser demonstrada na prxima reunio do Conselho do BCE, que em dezembro dever recalibrar os seus instrumentos para assegurar que as condies de financiamento permanecem favorveis para apoiar a recuperao econmica e neutralizar o impacto negativo da pandemia na trajetria de inflao. As polticas do Eurosistema, juntamente com as medidas adotadas pelos governos nacionais e instituies europeias, continuam a ser essenciais para apoiar o acesso ao financiamento, incluindo para os mais afetados pelas ramificaes da pandemia. Estas medidas incluem a possvel expanso do programa de compras de ativos (PEPP), com a flexibilidade que foi introduzida na primavera. As autoridades oramentais tambm esto comprometidas com a adequao da sua resposta  evoluo da crise. Os planos oramentais apresentados no outono para 2021 mostram que a posio oramental vai manter-se de acomodao das consequncias da crise. O espao oramental criado no perodo anterior abriu espao para que todos os pases pudessem reagir com estmulos oramentais. So boas notcias. Com a incerteza elevada e a recuperao ainda parcial, os riscos de uma retirada precoce dos apoios parecem srios, exigindo avaliaes cautelosas. A modulao adequada das estratgias de sada deve levar em considerao a evoluo dos desenvolvimentos sanitrios, econmicos e financeiros. As diferentes autoridades devero tambm coordenar entre si esse momento de alterao das polticas. Sabemos que a crise, como todas as crises, gerou perdas. Estas perdas so, como sempre acontece com as crises, assimetricamente distribudas entre os membros da sociedade. A desigualdade aumenta. E a disperso das perdas ao longo do tempo  a nica forma de evitar que, no futuro mais ou menos distante, surjam de novo as impossibilidades e inevitabilidades de no haver alternativa. A concluso que retiro  a de que sabemos desde j que a crise trouxe consigo um aumento da dvida pblica e da dvida privada, tal como um acentuar da desigualdade. Esta realidade tem de ser tida em conta na definio de polticas pblicas. Mas numa conferncia sobre o sistema financeiro,  tambm uma oportunidade para nos focarmos nos desafios que se colocam aos clientes bancrios, nomeadamente, s empresas no financeiras, e nos riscos que pode trazer o aumento do endividamento. Os cenrios econmicos que traamos dependem sempre do ponto de partida. Vejamos ento qual a realidade das sociedades no financeiras portuguesas, cujo retrato o INE atualizou no final do ms de outubro e que infelizmente passou quase desapercebido. As empresas no financeiras representam um universo de mais de um milho e trezentas mil empresas. Desde o ponto mais baixo da crise de dvida soberana (2013 para a generalidade dos indicadores), este enorme universo produtivo teve uma transformao nica e em si mesmo indita. Indita porque acrescentou sustentabilidade a setores produtivos que muitos diziam que no conseguiriam promover a convergncia da economia portuguesa com as mdias europeias. Aconteceu. O VAB cresceu 43%, o Excedente Bruto de Explorao mais de 50%. Este aumento da atividade e dos resultados foi conseguido com a conjugao simultnea de dois fatores inusuais: um aumento massivo do investimento, com mais 113% de FBCF (o investimento privado mais do que duplicou) e uma reduo do rcio da Dvida sobre o Ativo, que caiu mais de 53 pontos percentuais. E as empresas tornaram-se mais eficientes, com a Produtividade do Trabalho a crescer 15%. Este crescimento foi inclusivo, ou seja, contou com o emprego e as remuneraes.
