Na verdade, o nmero de pessoas ao servio nestas empresas aumentou 25% e as remuneraes totais 41%, em apenas seis anos. O peso das remuneraes no VAB cresceu 3,3 pp, atingindo um valor prximo dos 60%. Desalavancagem financeira, investimento, mais emprego e mais eficientes. Foi este o retrato do pas que construmos aps a crise soberana e at ao final de 2019. Devemos isso ao esforo das empresas portuguesas. No chegmos  crise pandmica sem o trabalho de casa feito. Podemos continuar a negar o pas que temos, mas isso s ajuda os demais, no os portugueses. Foi, alis, com estes nmeros, que superam os indicadores anteriores  crise financeira de forma muito alargada, que chegmos ao final de 2019. Ou seja, chegmos ao incio de 2020 com uma dinmica empresarial nica em Portugal. Esta dinmica  explicada pelo que aconteceu nas PME. O investimento das PME aumentou 131% e a produtividade 23%. A reduo do peso da dvida no ativo atingiu 65 pp e o ndice de solvabilidade progrediu 18 pp. Todos estes, indicadores acima da mdia nacional. A realidade setorial  ainda mais impressiva da transformao que ocorreu em Portugal, em especial nos ltimos cinco anos. O aumento da produtividade foi maior nos setores mais atingidos pela crise pandmica: 50% no Alojamento e Restaurao; 52% no Imobilirio; 32% na Indstria Transformadora e 26% no Comrcio. A desalavancagem foi particularmente forte no Comrcio e no Imobilirio, menos 100 pp, a dvida passa de 280% do ativo para 180%. Claro que a pandemia colocou um travo a alguns destes desenvolvimentos e colocou desafios a todos eles. Este travo foi severo, mas ser temporrio se conseguirmos manter a capacidade produtiva e estivermos preparados, e j demonstrmos a partir de junho que estvamos, para retomar a atividade por completo. Temos que estar conscientes de que a mdio prazo, o sobre-endividamento pode levar  reduo do investimento, enfraquecendo a competitividade e o crescimento econmico. Para fazer face a esta dificuldade, so necessrias medidas de fortalecimento do capital das empresas, para reduzir a alavancagem e aumentar sua capacidade de servio da dvida. Uma utilizao eficiente dos fundos pblicos exige o estabelecimento de procedimentos que permitam uma identificao efetiva das empresas viveis, que devem ser as recetoras privilegiadas destes apoios. Em paralelo,  necessrio garantir a resilincia do sistema bancrio em face de um provvel aumento nas perdas de crdito. Por um lado, as entidades bancrias comearam desde logo a provisionar os riscos de crdito, dando assim um passo prudencial adequado. Mas, por outro lado, o sistema bancrio continua a enfrentar problemas de rentabilidade e tem de responder aos desafios provocados pela digitalizao. As solues para estes desafios no devem ter apenas origem em cada um dos pases, mas devero ter um enfoque europeu. As instituies financeiras tambm tm de desempenhar o seu papel, respondendo aos desafios com determinao e tomando decises que no esqueam a importncia do seu contributo responsvel para o apoio  economia, s empresas e s famlias. Tendo sempre presente a preocupao de defender a sua resilincia. O setor bancrio resistiu bastante bem  crise at ao momento, apesar de uma srie de riscos e vulnerabilidades. Ajudou a absorver o choque e evitou uma crise de crdito que teria sido prejudicial para a economia. Mas no devemos perder de vista as principais fraquezas estruturais do setor bancrio europeu, que eram evidentes antes desta crise.  preciso continuar a reduzir o excesso de capacidade e a melhorar a relao custo-eficcia para fazer face  baixa rentabilidade, procurando modelos de negcio que respondam a uma economia cada vez mais digital. Espero que o debate desta manh d um contributo muito til para que o sistema bancrio continue a ser um agente responsvel na resposta  crise pandmica e saiba e consiga enfrentar os desafios que se seguiro. Muito obrigado.

Title: Opening remarks by Vice-Governor Luis Maximo dos Santos at the AFI-BdP Virtual Member Training on Designing National Strategy for Financial Education and its Implementation and Monitoring
text: Virtual Member Training on Designing National Strategy for Financial Education and its Implementation and Monitoring 23 Nov. 2020 Dear Dr. Alfred Hannig, Executive Director of the Alliance for Financial Inclusion Ladies and gentlemen, Good morning, good afternoon or good evening (depending on where you are) and welcome to this Virtual Training on Designing, Implementing and Monitoring a National Strategy for Financial Education. I am very pleased to see so many delegates of central banks and other financial authorities coming from different countries across the world. Banco de Portugal is honoured to co-host this event with AFI and we would be delighted to welcome you in Lisbon. Unfortunately, this is not possible due to the Covid-19 pandemic. These are, indeed, especially challenging times. Our countries have been severely impacted by the outbreak of coronavirus, which started as a health crises but rapidly evolved into a dramatic economic downturn. National authorities have been trying to weather the storm with support measures to mitigate the sharp reduction in income of households and small businesses. These measures, however, will hardly be enough if households and small businesses lack financial resilience from the outset. And figures are not optimistic. The results from a recent OECD survey on the financial literacy of adults show that, prior to the Covid-19 pandemic, more than 50 percent of adults in the 25 participating countries could not cover their living expenses for more than one month, should they lose their main source of income. The importance of financial literacy has never been clearer. Many (like us) have long considered financial literacy has an essential tool for individuals to manage their financial affairs wisely and to be prepared for the unexpected. But following the outbreak of Covid19, financial literacy became a survival skill which everyone needs to build greater resilience and to navigate a sea of uncertainty. If there is one thing that we have learned from this year is that the world is fundamentally unpredictable. So this training could not have come at a better time. Over the next three days, we will be discussing the importance of having financial literacy at the top of the policy agenda and how to design, implement and evaluate a national strategy for financial education. Having a national strategy is essential to create a coordinated, sustainable and effective nation-wide approach to financial education. Promoting financial literacy of a countrys population is always a long-term endeavour which typically entails aligning the expectations, the agenda and the modus operandi of different actors. Having a national strategy in place helps to achieve greater coordination and a lasting commitment from relevant stakeholders. Last but not least, as we move into the Digital Age a special focus should be given in the national strategy to digital financial literacy. In the last few years, digitalization has been reshaping the financial services industry, with bank customers increasingly using digital channels, such as mobile apps and online platforms, for making payments or taking out credit in a fast and convenient way. When using these digital channels, however, they are exposed to cybersecurity risks, such as online fraud and scams, which may lead to money or identity theft. The outbreak of the Covid-19 pandemic has accelerated the digitalization trend and exacerbated the risks arising from the use of digital channels. Bank customers who were already using digital channels typically increased their use, while those less familiar with new technologies were compelled to enter the digital age, often ill-prepared to do so. Not surprisingly, cybercrime rose to record highs in 2020, hand-in-hand with the sharp increase in the number of bank customers going online. So while it is still unclear what the world will look like in post-Covid times, digital financial literacy is very likely to become an increasingly important skill to participate in this new digital economy. Banco de Portugal has been following all these trends very closely for more than a decade. We see financial education as an essential complement to consumer protection under our banking conduct supervision mandate. Banco de Portugal is a founding member of the OECD International Network on Financial Education and we launched our bank customer website in 2008. Ten years ago, in 2010, we conducted our first national survey on financial literacy and one year later launched our national strategy for financial education, together with the other two Portuguese financial supervisors: The Securities Market Commission and the Insurance and Pension Funds Supervisory Authority. In 2016, we designed our Digital Financial Literacy Strategy as part of the central banks strategic plan and we incorporated digital financial literacy in the national strategy for financial education. Our collaboration with AFI started in 2017 when a group of seven central banks of the Portuguese speaking countries, including Banco de Portugal, signed a memorandum of technical cooperation in the field of financial inclusion and education with AFI. Since then, Banco de Portugal has had the opportunity and privilege to work with AFI in many joint-projects, including several training courses targeted at central bank experts, but also participation in conferences, workshops and seminars and, more recently, webinars and online events. Dr. Alfred Hannig, ladies and gentlemen, Let me conclude by saying that, as a monetary authority and financial supervisor, Banco de Portugal has a clear mandate to promote financial stability, which is key for sustainable economic growth. But to ensure financial stability is also need that bank customers are able to take wise financial decisions. As such, for many years we have been advocating that financial literacy should be on the top of the policy agenda. Still, we could not imagine how critical it would turned out to be, until we were hit by a global pandemic in 2020. I wish you all an inspiring and fruitful training. Thank you very much for your attention.

Title: Opening address by Director Ana Paula Serra at the Workshop on Data Visualization
text: Opening address by Director Ana Pau... Opening address by Director Ana Paula Serra at the Workshop on Data Visualization 18 Dec. 2020 Good afternoon and welcome. I would like to thank all of you for participating in this conference. I also thank the organizers and all the speakers. It is my pleasure to be here today at the Opening of this workshop. This allows me to say a few words on the importance of this initiative and how it fits well with the overall strategy of the Banco de Portugal. As you all know, like any other central bank, the Banco de Portugal is a data-driven organization. As such, data management and data skills training have been among the strategic objectives of the Bank for a few years now. This is the case with regard to the strategic plan 2017-2020, now coming to an end, and it will also be the case for the next strategic plan. Let me mention two very relevant strategic initiatives in this regard: the integrated data management project and the School of Data Science. These two projects are very closely related. Indeed, as we progressed with the new data architecture of the Bank, of which the data warehouse is a key pillar, we concluded that this could not work on the basis of traditional IT support and would only be effective if we assured that our people had the proper skills to support it. To achieve this transformation from request-based to autonomous data exploration and management, we needed to empower our people with new knowledge and skills. The challenge, of course, was how to develop a data science school in a short period of time and with contained resources. We put together a multidisciplinary team to think it over. We gathered people from the HR, IT, Statistics and Economics departments to think it over. We finally came up with an innovative, flexible framework that we think is capable of addressing our needs, of building the skills to master the data tools, the techniques and the methods required to leverage our work. We started in July with a group of 112 participants and later in October we expanded the cohort to 83 more. Since we started, we totaled 4,600 training hours and 272 courses. Courses cover topic areas such as data literacy, data science, computer science, IT. The most popular courses are SQL for data science, Python and R programming and data visualization. So far, not only the participation but also the feedback is extremely positive. I was happy to learn that the workshop today was jointly organized by BPLIM and the Banco do Portugals Academia, which is our training and learning academy that hosts among the School of Data Science other things. As mentioned, Data Visualization courses are among the most sought after. They have been supported by Power BI in a live training format provided by the IT department. Over the next two days we will learn more about the fundamentals and challenges of data visualization. This is very important for us given that we all know the relevance of effective communication. Running in parallel with the workshop, we will also have a training course on data visualization for the participants of the School of Data Science. I thank in advance Edith Maulandi for this. Let me also thank again all the speakers: Alberto Cairo, Yan Holtz, Chiari Sofis, Christophe Hurter and Christophe Bontemps. Special thanks go to Christophe Bontemps, who has shared his precious advice on how to best structure this workshop and identify high-quality speakers. Let me finish by wishing you a fruitful workshop.

Title: Speech by the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Mario Centeno, in the Budget and Finance Committee
text: Intervention of the Governor of the Bank... Speech by the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Mario Centeno, in the Budget and Finance Committee 22 Dec. 2020 Mr President, Ladies and gentlemen, Financial stability is a global, collective objective that requires concerted action by all institutions and stakeholders. I therefore welcome you and your honours for giving me the opportunity to publicly express, as Governor of Banco de Portugal, the importance I attach to financial stability for the economic and social success of Portugal. Allow, therefore, without following any order of importance that speaks to you about the role of each institutional sector for the financial stability of the Portuguese economy. Families require an attitude of responsibility in their consumption and savings decisions, which are often linked with credit. In particular, it makes it possible to smooth consumption throughout economic and life cycles. In the difficult moment we live in the Portuguese and world economy, credit assumes greater importance. But by the nature of credit activity also carries greater risk. Families have demonstrated an alignment with the rest of the country in building a stable financial environment. After the storm of the 2008 financial crisis, compounded by the ensuing sovereign crisis, private debt to disposable income has fallen by 35 percentage points since 2009. In December 2019, private debt accounted for 94% of disposable income, while in the euro area the average was 95%. The path taken is remarkable, especially if we notice that in December 2013, relative positions were contrary and the debt differences significant: 24 percentage points plus household indebtedness in Portugal. The effort must be of collective admiration from decision-makers  national and European  and should not be called into question. Companies require a robust position in their exposure to debt. But as in households, a certain degree of leverage is natural in companies too. Companies are responsible for making the best investment decisions, which are often financed with the savings of other economic agents through direct financing  bond issuance or capital reinforcement  or indirect  bank financing. Once again, in a process common to all institutional sectors, the savings, capitalization and debt indicators of our companies have improved since the previous crisis. I recall one of the most significant developments, the reduction of financial debt, which has fallen by 34 percentage points since 2012. In 2013, gross debt of non-financial corporations represented 122% of GDP; in 2019, had fallen by 24 percentage points to 92% of GDP. In the euro area, this ratio has remained constant around 88% of the area's GDP. In this case, the Portuguese companies were unable to reverse the positions on their European counterparts, but it was very little. However, they have taken an assinable path, which has allowed them to face the current crisis with a responsiveness that we have lacked in previous crises. The capitalization of companies, measured by the ratio between equity and total assets, was at the end of the first half of 2020, despite difficult times, at about 39%; 4 percentage points more than 5 years ago. Public administrations also require a strong position. The State is responsible for being the economic agent with the most temporal and liquidity patience, which in economics are almost synonymous. Losing this status has well-known consequences for all of us. But it is only possible to play this role if it has the financial capacity to temporarily replace the remaining economic operators until they re-meet better financial conditions. The role of straightening and countercyclical policies is the same. And it must be preserved. Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, The period we live in is illustrative of the diverse roles that each economic agent plays. The impatience that often characterizes the decision-making process, so often confused with the absence of alternatives, is not compatible with this important function for the State. But fortunately, the Portuguese has created, like businesses and households, budgetary space in the recent past, with primary surpluses of more than 3% and even a budget surplus in 2019. This capacity is now being made available to families and businesses, building a bridge to cross this pisemic storm. Banco de Portugal and its Governor are committed to this success of the Portuguese economy. The defense made, in Portugal and Europe, of monetary policies and regulation and supervision, which allow a more robust banking and financial sector and the creation of conditions for an effective transmission of monetary policy are our way of contributing to the success of the euro area and Portugal. Financial stability involves the irreplaceable effort of the banking system, which in recent years has accompanied the widespread deleveraging of the Portuguese economy. A reduction in the credit-to-deposit ratio, which has fallen by 66 pp since 2008 and the total capital ratio, rose from 9.4% in 2008 to 16.9% in 2019. Non-default loans on banks' balance sheets have been reduced by 35 billion since 2016, while credit has been able to recover by more than 20 billion. Along the way, the banking system was able to strengthen the financing of the Portuguese economy with the outbreak of the health crisis. Between March and September 2020, new business lending operations increased by 15% year-on-year. Of these new loans, around 38% had a public guarantee and were mainly for small and medium-sized enterprises and companies with lower pre-pandemic risk. In addition to the role played by public guarantees, the monetary and regulatory policy decisions of the European authorities have also played a key role in avoiding the financial segmentation of Europe. In Portugal, the financing obtained by the banking system from the Eurosystem reached 7.7% of the asset in June, increasing by 3.2 pp compared to December 2019. I would like to uncover the relevance of targeted long-term refinancing operations III (TLTRO III), which banks have substantially appealed to in June 2020. Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, I am here today in this Commission at Parliament's disposal to assess possible alternatives to strengthening the banking system and its role in the recovery of the Portuguese economy. Where the role of moratoriums is essential and should continue to be, but where the effort to preserve capital should be accompanied by measures to enable banks to overcome the crisis while maintaining the same contribution of support to the economy that they have so far made. We point to vulnerabilities and risks, but also mitigating. On the negative side, the high indebtedness of the various institutional sectors despite the path of reduction; the loss of value of the collaterals that support the loans granted; the decrease in the profitability of companies, which puts pressure on credit compliance; the labour market, where the reduction in the number of hours worked puts pressure on the level of employment, despite public policies of preservation of employment (simplified layoff) and income support (moratoriums; layoff). On the positive side, they have contributed to mitigating these vulnerabilities and risks, and economic and monetary policies appropriate to the different moments of the crisis should continue to do so. Last week, the European Central Bank already signaled the importance of adapting its policy to the new pheamic reality arising from the second wave. Together with the other European and national institutions it will be necessary to design policies that avoid an abrupt halt in the support that has been so fundamental in these months. But I would like to reinforce the message that is always behind any analysis of financial stability: everyone's contribution is essential. The value of this contribution translates into the financing costs of all and is the result of the credibility achieved. All attempts to raise doubt on this path enhance the risks and vulnerabilities that we have so hard been able to avoid. Within the biggest economic crisis, which could thus become social and financial, the country must remain focused on responding to the crisis, which requires the maintenance and adaptation of economic policies until its end. Thank you very much.
text_original: Interveno do Governador do Banco... Interveno do Governador do Banco de Portugal, Mrio Centeno, na Comisso de Oramento e Finanas 22 dez. 2020 Senhor Presidente, Senhoras e senhores deputados, A estabilidade financeira  um objetivo global, coletivo e que requer uma atuao concertada de todas as instituies e partes envolvidas. Sado, por isso, as Senhoras e os Senhores Deputados por me darem a oportunidade de expor publicamente, enquanto Governador do Banco de Portugal, a importncia que atribuo  estabilidade financeira para o sucesso econmico e social de Portugal. Permitam, por isso, sem seguir nenhuma ordem de importncia que vos fale sobre o papel de cada setor institucional para a estabilidade financeira da economia portuguesa. Das famlias requer-se uma atitude de responsabilidade nas suas decises de consumo e poupana, que so muitas vezes interligadas com recurso ao crdito. Em particular, permite alisar o consumo ao longo dos ciclos econmico e de vida. No momento difcil que vivemos na economia portuguesa e mundial, o crdito assume maior importncia. Mas pela natureza da atividade creditcia tambm traz maior risco. As famlias tm demonstrado um alinhamento com o restante pas na construo de uma envolvente financeira estvel. Depois da tormenta da crise financeira de 2008, agravada pela crise soberana que se lhe seguiu, o endividamento dos particulares relativamente ao rendimento disponvel caiu 35 pontos percentuais desde 2009. Em dezembro de 2019, o endividamento dos particulares representava 94% do rendimento disponvel, enquanto na rea do euro a mdia era de 95%. O caminho percorrido  notvel, sobretudo se notarmos que, em dezembro de 2013, as posies relativas eram contrrias e as diferenas de endividamento significativas: mais 24 pontos percentuais de endividamento das famlias em Portugal. O esforo deve merecer a admirao coletiva dos decisores  nacionais e europeus  e no deve ser posto em causa. Das empresas, requer-se uma posio robusta na sua exposio  dvida. Mas tal como nas famlias, tambm nas empresas um determinado grau de alavancagem  natural. s empresas compete tomar as melhores decises de investimento, que muitas vezes so financiadas com as poupanas de outros agentes econmicos atravs de financiamento direto  emisso de obrigaes ou reforo do capital  ou indireto  financiamento bancrio. Mais uma vez, num processo comum a todos os setores institucionais, os indicadores de poupana, capitalizao e endividamento das nossas empresas melhoram desde a anterior crise. Relembro um dos mais expressivos desenvolvimentos, a reduo da dvida financeira, que caiu 34 pontos percentuais desde 2012. Em 2013, a dvida bruta das sociedades no financeiras representava 122% do PIB; em 2019, tinha cado 24 pontos percentuais para 92% do PIB. Na rea do euro, este rcio tem-se mantido constante em torno dos 88% do PIB da rea. Neste caso, as empresas portuguesas no conseguiram inverter as posies relativas face s congneres europeias, mas foi por muito pouco. No entanto, percorreram um caminho assinvel, o que permitiu que enfrentassem a atual crise com uma capacidade de resposta que nos faltou em crises anteriores. A capitalizao das empresas, medida pelo rcio entre o capital prprio e o total do ativo, estava no final do primeiro semestre de 2020, apesar dos momentos difceis, em cerca de 39%; mais 4 pontos percentuais do que h 5 anos atrs. Das administraes pblicas, requer-se tambm uma posio slida. Ao Estado compete ser o agente econmico com mais pacincia temporal e de liquidez, que em economia so quase sinnimos. Perder este estatuto tem consequncias bem conhecidas pata todos ns. Mas s  possvel desempenhar esse papel se tiver capacidade financeira para se substituir temporariamente aos restantes agentes econmicos at que estes voltem a reunir melhores condies financeiras. O papel de alisamento e das polticas contra cclicas  esse mesmo. E deve ser preservado. Senhor Presidente, senhoras e senhores deputados, O perodo que vivemos  ilustrativo dos papis diversos que cada agente econmico desempenha. A impacincia que muitas vezes carateriza o processo de deciso, tantas vezes confundido com a ausncia de alternativas, no  compatvel com esta importante funo para o Estado. Mas, felizmente, o Estado portugus criou,  semelhana de empresas e famlias, espao oramental no passado recente, com excedentes primrios superiores a 3% e mesmo um excedente oramental em 2019. Esta capacidade est agora a ser posta  disposio das famlias e empresas, construindo uma ponte para atravessarmos esta tormenta pandmica. O Banco de Portugal e o seu Governador esto comprometidos com este sucesso da economia portuguesa. A defesa feita, em Portugal e na Europa, de polticas monetria e de regulao e superviso, que permitem um setor bancrio e financeiro mais robusto e a criao de condies para uma eficaz transmisso da poltica monetria so a nossa forma de contribuir para o sucesso da rea do euro e de Portugal. A estabilidade financeira envolve o esforo insubstituvel do sistema bancrio, que nos ltimos anos acompanhou a desalavancagem generalizada da economia portuguesa. Uma reduo do rcio entre crdito e depsitos, que caiu 66 pp desde 2008 e o rcio de fundos prprios totais que subiu de 9,4% em 2008 para 16,9% em 2019. Os emprstimos em incumprimento nos balanos dos bancos reduziram-se, desde 2016, 35 mil milhes de euros, ao mesmo tempo que o crdito conseguiu recuperar mais de 20 mil milhes de euros. Pelo caminho feito, o sistema bancrio teve condies para reforar o financiamento da economia portuguesa com o eclodir da crise sanitria. Entre maro e setembro de 2020, as novas operaes de emprstimo a empresas aumentaram 15% em termos homlogos. Destes novos emprstimos, cerca de 38% tinham uma garantia pblica e destinaram-se sobretudo a pequenas e mdias empresas e a empresas com menor risco pr-pandemia. Para alm do papel desempenhado pelas garantias pblicas, as decises de poltica monetria e regulatria das autoridades europeias desempenharam, tambm, um papel fundamental, evitando a segmentao financeira da Europa. Em Portugal, o financiamento obtido pelo sistema bancrio junto do Eurosistema atingiu em junho 7,7% do ativo, aumentando 3,2 pp face a dezembro de 2019. Destaco a relevncia das operaes de refinanciamento a prazo alargado direcionada III (TLTRO III), a que os bancos recorreram de forma substancial em junho de 2020. Senhor Presidente, senhoras e senhores deputados, Estou hoje aqui nesta Comisso  disposio do Parlamento para avaliarmos as possveis alternativas ao reforo do sistema bancrio e do seu papel para a recuperao da economia portuguesa. Onde o papel das moratrias  essencial e dever continuar a ser, mas onde o esforo de preservao de capital dever ser acompanhado de medidas que permitam aos bancos ultrapassar a crise mantendo o mesmo contributo de apoio  economia que at aqui tm dado. Apontamos vulnerabilidades e riscos, mas tambm mitigantes. Do lado negativo, o elevado endividamento dos vrios setores institucionais apesar da trajetria de reduo; a perda de valor dos colaterais que suportam os emprstimos concedidos; a diminuio da rendibilidade das empresas, que coloca presses sobre o cumprimento creditcio; o mercado de trabalho, onde a reduo do nmero de horas trabalhadas coloca presso sobre o nvel de emprego, apesar das polticas pblicas de preservao do emprego (layoff simplificado) e de apoio ao rendimento ( moratrias; layoff). Do lado positivo, contriburam para mitigar estas vulnerabilidades e riscos, e devem continuar a faz-lo, as polticas econmicas e monetrias adequadas aos diferentes momentos da crise. Na passada semana, o Banco Central Europeu j deu sinais da importncia de adequar a sua poltica  nova realidade pandmica decorrente da segunda vaga. Em conjunto com as outras instituies europeias e nacionais ser necessrio desenhar polticas que evitem uma paragem abrupta dos apoios que to fundamentais tm sido nestes meses. Mas queria reforar a mensagem que est sempre subjacente a qualquer anlise de estabilidade financeira: o contributo de todos  essencial. O valor deste contributo traduz-se nos custos de financiamento de todos e  o resultado da credibilidade conquistada. Todas as tentativas de gerar dvidas sobre este caminho potenciam os riscos e as vulnerabilidades que to arduamente soubemos evitar. No seio da maior crise econmica, que se poderia assim tornar social e financeira, o pas deve permanecer focado na resposta  crise, que requer a manuteno e adaptao das polticas econmicas at ao seu final. Muito obrigado.

Title: Opinion article of the Governor, Mario Centeno, in the Express: The requirement that falls on 2021
text: Governor's opinion piece, Bad... Opinion article of the Governor, Mario Centeno, in the Express: The requirement that falls on 2021 28 Dec. 2020 The year 2020 ends in the opposite way to the one as it began. Science has pointed to the way out of the pandemic. The biggest challenge ahead will not be dealing with an invisible virus that imposes distance on us, but resisting the complacency and opportunism that always lurks when political emergency passes. The reaction to the pandemic was rapid and effective, although not always with the weighting that everyone could understand or desire. Under threat that wasn't ours, we broke taboos. We understand the limits of our individual freedom and respond, in democracy, to the challenges we had not identified. Portugal has proved the role that, in times of crisis, it is up to public policies in supporting citizens, workers and companies, without deluding themselves about their limitations. This demonstrated the reason for the work spent to create space and responsiveness, without undersupcising the functions of the State or financial stability. Alongside the European institutions, it is the State that has an obligation to be always ready and able to act. In Europe, the political reaction was made by new common policies. In just three months, the ECB, the Eurogroup, the Commission and the European Council have understood the need to act. Monetary policy and fiscal policy, which is unfortunately not yet common enough, have been coordinated as never before in the history of the euro. It would be a mistake not to continue in 2021. The key element of this response was built on the draft budget for the euro  an instrument for coordinating public investments and reforms for all Member States, but flexible to support those most affected. The agreement for the issue of European debt gave it the financial power that was lacking. And that's how funds to support the economy, businesses and households resulted in a number of twelve zeros. We have not yet got rid of the idea that we take the most important steps in the storm. If, as it seems, the sun shines again in 2021, with the control of the pandemic by the vaccine, nothing would be more wrong than to reverse and stop the process of European integration and return to the old rhetoric of doubt and the false opposition between reducing risk or sharing. This is the requirement that falls on 2021. In this sense, the coming year is much more difficult and decisive for our collective future than 2020. History will be able to put the answer we built last spring in the highlight pages of European construction, but 2021 is expected to grow to the responsibility of succeeding it. Portugal has, as it has had in recent years, a crucial role. Not only because it holds the Presidency of the European Union in the first half of the year, but it is an example of how confidence in Europe is made of commitments and their fulfilment. We can't scude that capital. * In recent years, the Portuguese economy has exceeded all the predictions of those who did not believe in their capacity for renewal, nor of their policies to meet the objectives with which they were committed. In 2021, to understand how Portugal can fulfil our desire to overcome the crisis and resume convergence with the EU, we must understand how it got here. And few, very few could predict it. In the financial and banking system, we must face the last phase of a long stabilisation process, which has responded to the consequences of the global financial crisis of 2008 and deepened with the sovereign debt crisis. In 2021, Portugal has to conclude what most European countries concluded before 2012. Doubts about compliance by each of the parties involved - banks, state, regulators and supervisors - cannot but be that doubt, and become certainties of stabilisation as soon as possible. Portugal cannot lose in weeks what took more than five years to build. Your external credibility cannot be questioned. The State must fulfil its role as an economic and social stabiliser by credibility with fiscal policy and promoting social measures that support families. The surplus of public accounts and the path of debt reduction are not mirages, but what allowed the public bet in this difficult phase. We can concentrate on the essential functions of the state without fear that we will not be able to do so financially. Any hesitation in this area will cause 2021 to mark a setback of negative consequences, especially when the other countries focus on the recovery phase of their economies. In a modern economy, the financial sector and the State are instrumental in the productive capacity of businesses and families. The first signs of 2020, in the run-up to 2021, show that the lesson is not fully learned. In Portugal we cannot repeat the mistake; to maintain a vision of the financial sector incompatible with the construction of a modern country. The non-financial sector is represented by a universe of more than one million and three hundred thousand companies. From the lowest point of the sovereign debt crisis, this enormous productive universe has had a unique and unprecedented transformation in itself. Unprecedented, because it added sustainability to productive sectors that many said would not be able to promote the convergence of the Portuguese economy with European averages. But this convergence happened, and the production of these companies in six years grew by 50%. This increase in activity was due to the combination of two unusual factors: investment more than doubled and corporate indebtedness measured by comparison with their assets (assets) fell in half. And companies have become more efficient, with labour productivity growing by 15%. This growth was inclusive, with jobs and salaries. The number of workers in these companies increased by 25% and total salaries by 41% in just six years. The weight of value added remuneration grew by 3.3 percentage points, reaching a value close to 60%. Financial deleveraging, investment, more employment and more productive workers. This was the picture of the country we built after the sovereign crisis and until the end of 2019. We owe it to the efforts of Portuguese companies and families. We didn't get to the crisis without the homework done. If we leave him in the middle now, little or nothing will have served. We can continue to deny the country we have, but it only helps the country, not the Portuguese. And 2021 has with it that requirement, and it's no small thing. The dynamic I have described is explained by what has happened in Small and Medium Enterprises. Its investment increased by 131% and productivity by 23%. The reduction in the debt burden on the asset reached 65 percentage points and the solvency index progressed by 18 percentage points. All these indicators are above the national average. The sectoral reality is even more impressive of the transformation that has occurred in Portugal, especially in the last five years. The increase in productivity was higher in the sectors most affected by the crisis: 50% in Housing and Catering; 52% in Real Estate; 32% in manufacturing and 26% in commerce. Deleveraging was particularly strong in Commerce and Real Estate, minus 100 percentage points, debt went from 280% of assets to 180%. The pandemic has put a brake on some of these developments and challenges for all of them. This brake was severe, but it will be temporary if we can maintain production capacity and are prepared. We have already demonstrated, from June, that we are ready to resume the activity altogether. In this crisis, investment has shown a resilience that we have never seen in past crises. This is the sign that the country is prepared to not only resume activity, but to go further. * We must be aware that, in the medium term, over-indebtedness can be a brake on investment, weakening competitiveness and economic growth. To address this difficulty, measures to strengthen corporate capital are needed to reduce leverage and increase their debt service capacity. Europe must be part of this effort, as is the case in all major economic areas of the world. We cannot be Europe only when there are crises. The efficient use of public funds requires the establishment of procedures enabling the identification of viable undertakings and projects, which should be the privileged receivers of this support. It's not the time to discover dreams, it's time to love reality. Project by project, measure to measure, evaluated and without leaving accounts for the future. In the past, the mistake was forgetting the future. At present, there is no room for error. The ability to invest defines the near future. The pandemic was not the product of excesses and imbalances and does not justify an economic adjustment. But the crisis can influence how we produce, work and consume and should accelerate climate and digital transitions. We will have to be prepared to invest in people, in education and training, in a qualitative leap. In parallel, it is necessary to ensure the resilience of the banking system to cope with a likely increase in credit losses. Despite the relief of moratoriums and publicly guaranteed credit, banks began to provision credit risks. But the banking system continues to face profitability problems and must respond to the challenges posed by digitisation. In other jurisdictions financial systems are strengthened and consolidated, Portugal decided to play a different role in the last weeks of 2020. Continuing, 2021 and the following years will pay a high price. So I go back to the initial proposition: the biggest challenge we face is 2021. Greater than 2020, the year in which we were able to be united, in Portugal and Europe. If 2021 goes the other way it will not be a tax worthy of all that we achieved in 2020. Because it is easier to respond to a shock, even when it has seismic dimensions, than to our own difficulties. These always make us more sozinhos.
text_original: Artigo de opinio do Governador, M... Artigo de opinio do Governador, Mrio Centeno, no Expresso: A exigncia que recai sobre 2021 28 dez. 2020 O ano de 2020 termina da forma oposta quela como comeou. A cincia apontou o caminho de sada da pandemia. O maior desafio que temos pela frente no ser lidar com um vrus invisvel, que nos impe distncia, mas resistir  complacncia e ao oportunismo que sempre espreitam quando a emergncia poltica passa. A reao  pandemia foi rpida e eficaz, ainda que nem sempre com a ponderao que todos podiam entender ou desejar. Sob ameaa que no era nossa, rompemos tabus. Entendemos os limites da nossa liberdade individual e demos resposta, em democracia, aos desafios que no tnhamos identificado. Portugal provou o papel que, em tempos de crise, cabe s polticas pblicas no apoio aos cidados, trabalhadores e empresas, sem se iludir sobre as suas limitaes. Nisso ficou demonstrada a razo do trabalho passado para criar espao e capacidade de resposta, sem colocar em causa as funes do Estado, nem a estabilidade financeira. A par das instituies europeias,  o Estado que tem a obrigao de estar sempre pronto e capaz de agir. Na Europa, a reao poltica fez-se de novas polticas comuns. Em apenas trs meses, o BCE, o Eurogrupo, a Comisso e o Conselho Europeu compreenderam a necessidade de agir. A poltica monetria e a poltica oramental, esta infelizmente ainda no suficientemente comum, coordenaram-se como nunca antes na histria do euro. Seria um erro no lhe dar continuidade em 2021. O elemento fundamental dessa resposta foi construdo sobre o projeto do oramento para o euro  um instrumento de coordenao de investimentos pblicos e reformas para todos os Estados Membros, mas flexvel para apoiar os mais afetados. O acordo para a emisso de dvida europeia conferiu-lhe o poder financeiro que faltava. E foi assim que os fundos no apoio  economia, s empresas e s famlias resultaram num nmero com doze zeros. No nos livrmos ainda da ideia de que damos os passos mais importantes na tormenta. Se, como tudo indica, o sol voltar a brilhar em 2021, com o controle da pandemia pela vacina, nada seria mais errado do que reverter e parar o processo de integrao europeia e voltar  velha retrica das dvidas e da falsa oposio entre a reduo do risco ou da sua partilha. Essa  a exigncia que recai sobre 2021. Neste sentido, o prximo ano  muito mais difcil e determinante para o nosso futuro coletivo do que 2020. A histria saber colocar a resposta que construmos na ltima Primavera nas pginas de destaque da construo europeia, mas 2021 dever crescer para a responsabilidade de lhe suceder. Portugal tem, como teve nos ltimos anos, um papel crucial. No apenas porque ocupa a Presidncia da Unio Europeia no primeiro semestre, mas  o exemplo de como a confiana na Europa se faz de compromissos e do seu cumprimento. No podemos desbaratar esse capital. * Nos ltimos anos, a economia portuguesa superou todas as previses de quem no acreditava na sua capacidade de renovao, nem das suas polticas cumprirem os objetivos com que se comprometiam. Em 2021, para entender como Portugal pode cumprir o nosso desejo de ultrapassar a crise e retomar a convergncia com a UE, devemos compreender como aqui chegou. E poucos, muito poucos o souberam prever. No sistema financeiro e bancrio, temos de enfrentar a ltima fase de um longo processo de estabilizao, que respondeu s consequncias da crise financeira global de 2008 e se adensaram com a crise da dvida soberana. Em 2021, Portugal tem que concluir aquilo que a generalidade dos pases europeus concluiu antes de 2012. As dvidas sobre o cumprimento por cada uma das partes envolvidas -bancos, Estado, reguladores e supervisores -no podem deixar de ser isso mesmo, dvidas, e tornarem-se certezas de estabilizao o mais depressa possvel. Portugal no pode perder em semanas o que levou mais de cinco anos a construir. A sua credibilidade externa no pode ser questionada. O Estado deve cumprir o seu papel de estabilizador econmico e social, credibilizando a poltica oramental e promovendo as medidas sociais que apoiem as famlias. O excedente das contas pblicas e a trajetria de reduo da dvida no so miragens, mas sim o que permitiu a aposta pblica nesta fase difcil. Podemo-nos concentrar nas funes essenciais do Estado sem receio de que financeiramente no o consigamos fazer. Qualquer hesitao neste domnio far com que 2021 marque um retrocesso de consequncias negativas, em especial quando os demais pases se concentram na fase de recuperao das suas economias. Numa economia moderna, o setor financeiro e o Estado so instrumentais para a capacidade produtiva das empresas e das famlias. Os primeiros sinais de 2020, na preparao de 2021, demonstram que a lio no est totalmente aprendida. Em Portugal no podemos repetir o erro; manter uma viso do setor financeiro incompatvel com a construo de um pas moderno. O sector no financeiro  representado por um universo de mais de um milho e trezentas mil empresas. Desde o ponto mais baixo da crise de dvida soberana, este enorme universo produtivo teve uma transformao nica e em si mesmo indita. Indita, porque acrescentou sustentabilidade a setores produtivos que muitos diziam que no conseguiriam promover a convergncia da economia portuguesa com as mdias europeias. Mas essa convergncia aconteceu, e a produo destas empresas em seis anos cresceu 50%. Este aumento da atividade deveu-se  conjugao de dois fatores inusuais: o investimento mais do que duplicou e o endividamento das empresas medido por comparao com os seus bens (ativos) caiu para metade. E as empresas tornaram-se mais eficientes, com a produtividade do trabalho a crescer 15%. Este crescimento foi inclusivo, contou com o emprego e as remuneraes. O nmero de trabalhadores nestas empresas aumentou 25% e as remuneraes totais 41%, em apenas seis anos. O peso das remuneraes no valor acrescentado cresceu 3,3 pontos percentuais, atingindo um valor prximo dos 60%. Desalavancagem financeira, investimento, mais emprego e trabalhadores mais produtivos. Foi este o retrato do pas que construmos aps a crise soberana e at ao final de 2019. Devemos isso ao esforo das empresas e das famlias portuguesas. No chegamos  crise pandmica sem o trabalho de casa feito. Se o deixamos agora a meio, de pouco ou nada ter servido. Podemos continuar a negar o pas que temos, mas isso s ajuda os demais, no os portugueses. E 2021 tem consigo essa exigncia, e no  coisa pouca. A dinmica que descrevi  explicada pelo que aconteceu nas Pequenas e Mdias Empresas. O seu investimento aumentou 131% e a produtividade 23%. A reduo do peso da dvida no ativo atingiu 65 pontos percentuais e o ndice de solvabilidade progrediu 18 pontos percentuais. Todos estes indicadores esto acima da mdia nacional. A realidade setorial  ainda mais impressiva da transformao que ocorreu em Portugal, em especial nos ltimos cinco anos. O aumento da produtividade foi maior nos setores mais atingidos pela crise pandmica: 50% no Alojamento e Restaurao; 52% no Imobilirio; 32% na Indstria Transformadora e 26% no Comrcio. A desalavancagem foi particularmente forte no Comrcio e no Imobilirio, menos 100 pontos percentuais, a dvida passou de 280% do ativo para 180%. A pandemia colocou um travo a alguns destes desenvolvimentos e desafios a todos eles. Este travo foi severo, mas ser temporrio se conseguirmos manter a capacidade produtiva e estivermos preparados. J demonstrmos, a partir de Junho, estarmos prontos para retomar a atividade por completo. Nesta crise, o investimento mostrou uma resilincia que nunca observmos em crises passadas. Este  o sinal de que o pas est preparado para no s retomar a atividade, mas para ir mais alm. * Temos de estar conscientes de que, a mdio prazo, o sobre-endividamento pode ser um travo ao investimento, enfraquecendo a competitividade e o crescimento econmico. Para fazer face a esta dificuldade, so necessrias medidas de fortalecimento do capital das empresas, para reduzir a alavancagem e aumentar a sua capacidade de servio da dvida. A Europa deve fazer parte deste esforo, como acontece em todas as grandes reas econmicas do mundo. No podemos ser Europa s quando h crises. A utilizao eficiente dos fundos pblicos exige o estabelecimento de procedimentos que permitam uma identificao das empresas e dos projetos viveis, que devem ser as recetoras privilegiadas destes apoios. No  o momento de descobrir os sonhos,  o momento de acudir  realidade. Projeto a projeto, medida a medida, avaliadas e sem deixar contas para o futuro. No passado, o erro foi esquecer o futuro. No presente, no h espao para o erro. A capacidade de investir define o futuro mais prximo. A pandemia no foi o produto de excessos e desequilbrios e no justifica um ajustamento em sentido econmico. Mas a crise pode influenciar a forma como produzimos, trabalhamos e consumimos e dever acelerar as transies climtica e digital. Teremos de estar preparados para investir nas pessoas, em educao e formao, num salto qualitativo. Em paralelo,  necessrio garantir a resilincia do sistema bancrio para enfrentar um provvel aumento nas perdas de crdito. Apesar do alvio das moratrias e do crdito com garantia pblica, as entidades bancrias comearam desde logo a provisionar os riscos de crdito. Mas o sistema bancrio continua a enfrentar problemas de rentabilidade e tem de responder aos desafios provocados pela digitalizao. Noutras jurisdies reforam-se e consolidam-se os sistemas financeiros, Portugal decidiu jogar um papel diferente nas ltimas semanas de 2020. A continuar, 2021 e os anos seguintes pagaro um preo elevado. Por isso volto  proposio inicial: o maior desafio que enfrentamos  2021. Maior do que o de 2020, o ano em que conseguimos estar unidos, em Portugal e na Europa. Se 2021 seguir outro caminho no ser um digno tributrio de tudo o que conseguimos em 2020. Porque  mais fcil responder a um choque, mesmo quando tem dimenses ssmicas, do que s nossas prprias dificuldades. Essas deixam-nos sempre mais sozinhos.

Title: Opinion article of the Governor, Mario Centeno, in the Daily News: The evolution of policies in 2021
text: Governor's opinion piece, Bad... Opinion article of the Governor, Mario Centeno, in the Daily News: The evolution of policies in 2021 30 Dec. 2020 In response to the pandemic, all decision-makers in all areas and jurisdictions were swift, innovative and coordinated. The crisis arose with a temporary and symmetrical nature, affected all sectors dramatically, but evolved according to the rules of confinement and became very asymmetric. Thus, the measures adopted should, in 2021, be adapted to the evolution of the crisis and should serve to prepare for recovery. This was the strategy adopted in December in the recalibration of the most effective monetary policy instruments. Although vaccination prospects are encouraging, the depth of the second wave, its duration and the associated containment measures were not foreseen and required a response. The preservation of favourable financing conditions recommended recalibrating the two main instruments, the Sovereign Asset acquisition programme (PEPP) and extending the granting of liquidity to the banking sector (TLTRO). The objective is to ensure favorable conditions in all sectors of the economy, in a context of strong asymmetry of the impact of the crisis. Maintaining favourable financing conditions can be achieved with flows of asset purchases that do not exhaust the new financial envelope over the PEPP net purchasing horizon. Similarly, this envelope can be recalibrated if necessary. PEPP has sufficient flexibility to avoid the risk of fragmentation. The results speak for themselves: Portugal managed to put debt to a year with the lowest rate of return among euro area countries and the interest differentials between Portugal and Germany are at lows since 2010. The crisis today is uneven. A challenge for politics. The conditions for access to credit should be favourable, although loans without economic sustainability should not be encouraged. Unlike previous crises, monetary and fiscal policy adopted by Member States and Europe are working together and have avoided a prolonged catastrophic fall. In the coming months, monetary policy will continue to support all sectors of the economy and ensure that credit flows through the economy. For their part, budgetary authorities should avoid the negative impacts associated with the abrupt termination of some measures. The degree of implementation of the measures in Portugal was very high. Income support, such as simplified layoff, and liquidity support, such as moratoriums, for their impact and effectiveness, should be maintained throughout the year, but should be adapted to the evolution of the economic crisis. Moratoriums are not a credit pardon. Families and businesses must resume the repayment of credits, but gradually and effectively, allowing a return to normality without any overlaps. By September 2021, it is estimated that up to 11 billion of repayments provided for in the credit plans will be postponed due to the moratoriums. It is not a debt accumulation, but a postponement of the payment, accommodating this moment to the return of activity to levels closer to the period before the crisis. In fact, the same is expected to happen with the Budgetary Rules in Europe and the monetary policy of the Eurosystem. It is up to the banking system, businesses, families and the State to prepare this moment, according to the needs of each one, but ensuring that vaccination and obtaining group immunity is concomitant with the resumption of previous responsibilities. A light has been lit, marking the first day of the rest of the pandemic, this light is certainly one of hope but it also illuminates our collective responsibility.
text_original: Artigo de opinio do Governador, M... Artigo de opinio do Governador, Mrio Centeno, no Dirio de Notcias: A evoluo das polticas em 2021 30 dez. 2020 Em resposta  pandemia, todos os decisores, em todas as reas e jurisdies, foram cleres, inovadores e coordenados. A crise surgiu com uma natureza temporria e simtrica, afetou todos os setores de forma dramtica, mas evoluiu de acordo com as regras do confinamento e tornou-se muito assimtrica. Assim, as medidas adotadas devem, em 2021, ser adaptadas  evoluo da crise e devem servir para preparar a recuperao. Esta foi a estratgia adotada em dezembro na recalibrao dos mais eficazes instrumentos de poltica monetria. Embora as perspetivas de vacinao sejam animadoras, a profundidade da segunda vaga, a sua durao e as medidas de conteno associadas no foram previstas e requeriam uma resposta. A preservao de condies de financiamento favorveis recomendava recalibrar os dois instrumentos principais, o programa de aquisio de ativos soberanos (PEPP) e alargar a concesso de liquidez ao setor bancrio (TLTRO). O objetivo  garantir condies favorveis em todos os setores da economia, num contexto de forte assimetria do impacto da crise. A manuteno de condies de financiamento favorveis pode ser conseguida com fluxos de compra de ativos que no esgotem o novo envelope financeiro ao longo do horizonte de compras lquidas do PEPP. Da mesma forma, este envelope pode ser recalibrado, se necessrio. O PEPP tem a flexibilidade suficiente para evitar o risco de fragmentao. Os resultados falam por si: Portugal conseguiu colocar dvida a um ano com a taxa de retorno mais baixa entre os pases da rea do euro e os diferenciais de juro entre Portugal e a Alemanha esto em mnimos desde 2010. A crise hoje  desigual. Um desafio para as polticas. As condies de acesso ao crdito devem ser favorveis, embora no se devam incentivar emprstimos sem sustentabilidade econmica. Ao contrrio das crises anteriores, a poltica monetria e oramental adotadas pelos Estados-Membros e na Europa esto a funcionar em conjunto e evitaram uma queda catastrfica prolongada. Nos prximos meses, a poltica monetria continuar a apoiar todos os setores da economia e garantir que o crdito flui pela economia. Pelo seu lado, as autoridades oramentais devem evitar os impactos negativos associados ao trmino abrupto de algumas medidas. O grau de implementao das medidas em Portugal foi muito elevado. Os apoios ao rendimento, como o layoff simplificado, e os apoios  liquidez, como as moratrias, pelo seu impacto e eficcia, devem ser mantidos ao longo do ano, mas devem ser adaptados  evoluo da crise econmica. As moratrias no so um perdo de crdito. As famlias e as empresas devem retomar o reembolso dos crditos, mas de forma gradual e efetiva, permitindo um retorno  normalidade sem sobressaltos. At Setembro de 2021, estima-se que at 11 mil milhes de euros de reembolsos previstos nos planos de crditos venham a ser adiados devida s moratrias. No se trata de um acumular de dvida, mas sim de um adiamento do pagamento, acomodando esse momento ao retorno da atividade a nveis mais prximos do perodo anterior  crise. Na verdade, o mesmo espera-se que venha a acontecer com as Regras Oramentais na Europa e com a poltica monetria do Eurosistema. Cabe ao sistema bancrio, s empresas, s famlias e ao Estado preparar esse momento,  medida das necessidades de cada um, mas garantindo que a vacinao e a obteno de imunidade de grupo seja concomitante com o retomar das responsabilidades anteriores. Acendeu-se uma luz, que marca o primeiro dia do resto da pandemia, essa luz  certamente de esperana mas tambm ilumina a nossa responsabilidade coletiva.

Title: Opinion article by Administrator Hlder Rosalino in Exame Magazine: The Digital Euro
text: Administrator opinion article... Opinion article by Administrator Helder Rosalino in Exame Magazine: The Digital Euro 29 jan. 2021 Payment systems are undergoing an unprecedented digital transformation, greatly accelerated by the pandemic situation we are experiencing. While banknotes and coins remain an important means of payment, electronic payment instruments (such as cards and immediate transfers) are increasingly used. Promoting the smooth functioning of payment systems is one of the key functions of central banks, which is why Banco de Portugal has been participating, from the first hour, in the work of the European Central Bank (ECB) for the possible issuance of a digital central bank currency - the digital euro. These works recognise, as a starting point, that the issuance of a central bank digital currency in the euro area has not been necessary to date. But they also recognise that it could be an important option if some scenarios such as the very significant reduction in the use of cash, the emergence of private forms of currency (such as so-called stablecoins) materialise in the future, or the lack of efficient private pan-European payment solutions. In these scenarios, the digital euro will contribute to ensuring the independence of the European economy and maintaining financial stability, in addition to promoting the strengthening of the international role of the euro. But what is the digital Euro? It is a central bank digital currency made available to the general public (including individuals and businesses) to be used in retail payments. It will be issued by the ECB and made available to European citizens and agents as a reliable, risk-free and cost-free digital payment means for its basic functionalities. In practice, the digital euro will be a way for European citizens to have access to (therefore, risk-free) dematerialised and in the context of an increasingly digital payment system. The digital Euro should have functionalities similar to any other modern solution for payments at physical and online points of sale, be made available throughout the euro area and respond in a non-discriminatory way to the needs of all segments of the population, promoting inclusion. For the concepts to be clear, it is advisable to distinguish the digital euro from other forms of currency or "assets". Because it is issued by the central bank and therefore has no risk, it differs from bank deposits and electronic money, which are the liabilities of supervised entities, and from so-called stablecoins, which are usually liabilities of unregulated institutions. In these cases, even when it comes to supervised institutions, the risk of liquidity and solvency is never nil. It is also distinguished from so-called crypto-assets, which are generally not liabilities of any entity. One of the best-known examples of crypto-assets are so-called bitcoins, which can be used to make payments, but which are in fact mainly used as investment assets and at high risk. But what concrete benefits can the digital Euro bring to citizens? From the outset, it will be able to combine the security and universality of cash, because it will also be issued by a central bank, it will be of widespread access, and will have the benefits of technological innovation associated with electronic payments. It can make international payments more efficient, less costly, faster and less time-time consumers. It will increase the range of payment solutions available and can contribute to more efficient and resilient payment services. Finally, being a modern and risk-free payment instrument can reduce the appetite for riskier private solutions, especially if issued by non-supervised entities at national or European level. The introduction of the digital euro could put the euro area at the forefront of innovation, but not without first meeting a number of important challenges. Depending on its design, the digital euro could have implications, for example, in the functioning of payment systems, the granting of credit to the economy, financial stability and the conduct of monetary policy. The decision on the possible development and launch of the digital euro will be preceded by widespread public auscultation, an intense debate between the central banks of the euro area and a contained trial phase. Almost 20 years ago, the euro came into the hands of European consumers in the form of banknotes and coins. Since then, it has effectively fulfilled its role as a means of payment, unit of account and reserve value. The mission of central banks is to ensure confidence in the currency and this means working to ensure that the euro continues to fulfil its role in a more digital reality. Confidence in the euro, particularly as a means of payment, will always be a priority.
