Interveno de encerramento do Vice-Governador Lus Mximo dos Santos na "Fintech Meeting: Onboarding Digital -uma abordagem baseada no risco": Estabelecimento da relao de negcio por meios digitais 29 abr. 2021 As inovaes tecnolgicas e o processo de transformao digital a que temos assistido nos ltimos anos tm contribudo decisivamente para uma progressiva desmaterializao dos servios financeiros prestados aos clientes, tanto no momento do estabelecimento da relao de negcio como no seu desenvolvimento posterior. Por razes bvias, a pandemia da COVID-19 intensificou ainda mais essa tendncia, que j se vinha afirmando com enorme fora. Um dos temas associados  digitalizao do sistema financeiro que mais tem gerado interesse por parte de diversos stakeholders -governos, supervisores financeiros, prestadores de servios financeiros, fintechs, e consultores   precisamente o onboarding digital, ou seja, o momento em que os clientes entram e mergulham nesse admirvel mundo novo. Felicito, pois, o DAS por esta iniciativa, focada na anlise desse momento do ponto de vista da superviso preventiva do branqueamento de capitais e do financiamento do terrorismo (BC/FT), sendo certo, no entanto, que o processo de transformao digital em curso impacta na generalidade da atividade do Banco de Portugal e, em particular, em todas as formas de superviso que fazem parte do nosso mandato. Ao longo da Histria, o avano tecnolgico tem sido, em geral, um motor poderoso e contnuo da melhoria de vida das pessoas; mas a tecnologia no  intrinsecamente boa ou m: isso depende sempre do uso que o Homem faz dela. Na verdade, mesmo nas formas mais sofisticadas atualmente conhecidas da denominada inteligncia artificial no se vislumbra outro ser moral que no seja o ser humano. O progresso tecnolgico sempre deu novos e poderosos instrumentos  comunidade e s suas autoridades para combater as condutas delinquentes, mas tambm  verdade que sempre forneceu novas oportunidades e meios em quem quer incorrer nelas. No espanta, portanto, que o processo de transformao digital faa surgir novos riscos relativos ao BC/FT a que as instituies ficam expostas, conforme, alis, tem vindo a ser amplamente reconhecido e divulgado por diferentes autoridades, incluindo o Banco de Portugal. O Banco de Portugal tem acompanhado ativamente esta temtica desde a sua gnese, designadamente produzindo novos instrumentos regulatrios, tais como a Instruo n. 9/2017, de 3 de julho, que estabeleceu pela primeira vez a possibilidade de recurso  videoconferncia, ou o Aviso n. 2/2018, de 26 de setembro, que estabeleceu a possibilidade de comprovao de elementos identificativos por recurso a prestadores qualificados de servios de confiana, opo que veio mais tarde a ser consagrada pela prpria Lei n. 83/2017, de 18 de agosto. Pela sua prpria natureza, a preveno adequada dos riscos relativos ao BC/FT decorrentes do processo de transformao digital, no se resolve, de todo, apenas com medidas adotadas pelas autoridades nacionais ou mesmo pelo Estado portugus. De facto, os contornos do quadro normativo aplicvel em matria de onboarding digital dependem, em larga medida, de opes e decises internacionais.  por isso mesmo que aguardamos com expectativa a evoluo regulatria europeia, em particular as consequncias que resultaro da Estratgia Financeira Digital (Digital Finance Strategy) da Comisso Europeia, adotada em setembro de 2020. Especial expetativa neste contexto merecem os trabalhos preparatrios  em que o Banco de Portugal participa  da emisso, pela Autoridade Bancria Europeia, de uma proposta de orientaes que verse, nomeadamente, sobre: i. Os tipos de documentao digital e de tecnologias inovadoras que podem ser aceites no mbito do cumprimento de deveres de identificao e diligncia, e as condies que devem ser cumpridas quanto  respetiva implementao; ii. As condies em que a entidade financeira pode recorrer a informao recolhida por entidades terceiras. Por outro lado, as futuras propostas legislativas relativas a um novo quadro em matria de preveno do BC/FT  em que se inclui uma proposta de regulamento  atravs das quais a Comisso Europeia pretende continuar a definir e a harmonizar os requisitos em matria de cumprimento dos deveres de identificao e de diligncia, com vista a facilitar o recurso a tecnologias inovadoras e a prestao de servios financeiros transfronteirios. Est prevista a disponibilizao de um primeiro draft deste pacote legislativo para maio de 2021. Perante este cenrio, o dilogo e o estabelecimento de sinergias entre diferentes players do mercado ser, necessariamente, um ponto-chave para aproveitar as vantagens das novas tecnologias e da criao de uma economia digital, minimizando os riscos da sua utilizao indevida. A atuao do Banco de Portugal orienta-se por uma metodologia que no comporta o preconceito. Pelo contrrio, temos promovido vrias iniciativas  de que a Fintech Meeting de hoje  apenas mais um exemplo -precisamente com o objetivo de criar fruns onde melhor possamos apresentar ao setor as nossas expectativas e, em paralelo, obter feedback sobre estes temas, na busca permanente por solues eficazes, seguras e plenamente compliant. A complexidade das matrias e dos desafios com que todos estamos confortados faz-nos reconhecer, sem dificuldade, que todos temos a aprender uns com os outros. Ficou muito claro da nossa reunio de hoje como uma abordagem em funo do risco  a melhor metodologia para alcanar os nossos objetivos, que, evidentemente, no se cingem ao momento onboarding, mas antes tm de acompanhar, de forma dinmica, toda a relao de negcio. Por outro lado, reafirmamos que o Banco de Portugal privilegia uma abordagem tecnologicamente neutra; ou seja, pretende-se uma regulao que nem entrave a inovao nem promova determinadas solues em detrimento de outras. Com isso, queremos garantir que a evoluo segue o seu curso sem dirigismos que se nos afiguram deslocados. Num recente artigo[1], Fernando Restoy escreveu que a regulao adequada das fintech deve obedecer a dois princpios fundamentais: a prudncia, para evitar o desencorajamento da inovao e salvaguardar bens pblicos fundamentais como a estabilidade financeira e a integridade do mercado, e a determinao, para prevenir os riscos assim que so identificados e construir uma slida cooperao entre autoridades de diferentes reas e jurisdies. Trata-se de uma boa sntese, sem dvida mais fcil de enunciar do que concretizar, mas que pode e deve servir de inspirao a todos os que tm que lidar com estes temas. Muito obrigado pela vossa ateno. [1] Cf. Fernando Restoy, Regulating fintech: what is going on, and where are the challenges, in SUERF  The European Money and Finance Forum, SUERF Policy Note, n. 34, February 2020, p. 8.

Title: Interview of Administrator Hlder Rosalino to the Business Journal
text: Media Public Interventions All Of The Administrator Helder... Interview of Administrator Helder Rosalino to the Business Journal 03 May. 2021 Has the increase in commissions on immediate transfers, in particular those made through MB Way, have had any impact on their use? You have to separate two instruments. In our statistics, MB Way operations are counted as card operations. Then there are those that we consider the real immediate transfers and that the European Commission (EC) and the European Central Bank (ECB) argue that they will be the new standard in payment systems. Instant transfers are account account, I don't need to associate my card with anything, and there are no restrictions; unlike MB Way, where there needs to be a user community. In relation to the impact of commissions, MB Way is massively used and continues to grow. I believe it will continue to play a leading role in the payment system. Commissions have not departed consumers from this service. Exactly. On the other hand, immediate transfers, which we defend as the normal future, grew 80% in volume and 50% in value in 2020. But the starting point is very low because they were launched in 2019. This is an issue that concerns us. There is a commissioning policy that considers this to be a "premium" segment. Immediate transfers are the ones we most want to develop... Can committees delay this development? Exactly. Normal credit transfers are a mass product, we pay nothing for making a transfer in most cases. But if we want to make an immediate transfer, we pay and the commissions are relatively high. A few days ago, the EC launched a public consultation on immediate transfers to survey the use of this service. The European strategy focuses on immediate transfers as the paradigm of European payment systems, with European platforms based on immediate transfers account account. In a statement we sent to the banks, we noted that the EC is making this withdrawal and that it does not set aside the possibility of setting a commissioning policy for immediate transfers. That is, impose limits? Impose limits. In essence, to correct what is not the market trend that the EC wants, which is to have a strong European payment system, with common standards, based on immediate transfers on European platforms and infrastructures. What should happen, in my opinion, was a policy of greater equalisation of immediate transfers to credit transfers. That is where we want to make the way at European level. Hence this public consultation to see how the use of immediate transfers is, so that the European Commission can then regulate, as it regulates prices in relation to other payment systems. And what is the banks' position on that? They say that it is their trade policy, that they have the legitimacy to define that policy and that they make their assessment of what the commissions should be in each of the payment systems, within the margins of manoeuvre they have. And they also say that they have made large investments in the implementation of the system of immediate transfers in Portugal and that they are still in the recovery phase of this investment, and that these commissioning slates aim to recover this investment. They are therefore not open to lowering costs. The banks also have another important issue, is that are the shareholders of SIBS, which makes mb way available. All this weighs. They have no need to attract consumers to immediate transfers. The market in Portugal is served as an immediate transfer solution, which works well because it has 3 million users or more. This is somehow limiting the growth of immediate transfers. But the issue will evolve, I am convinced that the EC will make developments in this direction. Soon? I think so, yes. Contactless growth has not only been accelerated, but consistent. It already accounts for more than a third of card payments. How far can you grow up? We will tend to converge on the European average. There are countries where contactless represents 80% of card payments. We have a margin of almost 40% today to 80%. We will certainly exceed 50% in a short time. Today, 60% of cards have "contactless" and of these, 99% have this technology active. On the other hand, not all payment terminals accept this technology. This applies a lot to public transport. We haven't used contactless in transport yet because operators don't have the technology available yet. But there are projects going on in this direction. Is it possible to reach a massification of contactless public transport and other services? It's almost inevitable. We're breaking down barriers. The first is the habit of payment. People who could have the most resistance already use it. The barrier of "contactless" technology on the cards is also in the process of being broken. Another barrier remains to be overcome, which is that all payment terminals accept the technology, but that will also be done. There will always be a fringe that may be more resilient, but the overwhelming majority of payments that can be made on the physical site will be with "contactless". To sustain this growth, is it necessary to raise the ceiling to which it is possible to make contactless payments without code? The limit in Portugal was 20 euros before the pandemic. Banco de Portugal and the Government quickly converged to increase the limit to 50 euros, which is the maximum allowed by European directives. Today, the average value of the payment with "contactless" is 24 euros, higher than the limit that existed before the pandemic. At our interbank meetings for payments and the Payment Systems Forum, there is a question that we should think about increasing the 50 limit. But we cannot, because the limit of EUR 50 is set by european directive. The good news is that in the EBA [European Banking Authority], the need to review this limit is already being put on the table. Do you admit to increase it? This is already discussed in EBA groups and in European groups where payment systems are discussed. This theme is being discussed because, in fact, we all see the advantage. That resistance that existed in relation to "contactless" is not placed, the possibility of loss is limited and, on the other hand, one cannot do more than a certain number of operations per day. The risk that is associated with the loss of a card and its use is controlled. Can the number of uses per day also increase? The two things can probably be increased. If we increase the value, for example, to 100 euros, instead of doing four operations, maybe we can do six, seven or eight. It's a topic that's under discussion, there's still not much traction in this discussion, but it's being put on the table. The ECB is still defining whether it decides to move forward with the digital euro. What obstacles are there? This project has several steps. The first culminated in the production of an evaluation report, which examined the advantages of the digital euro, the risks to financial stability and the implementation of monetary policy and under what circumstances the digital euro may be necessary. The second was a public consultation, which had more than 8,000 responses. The current stage is trying to explain the technological support possibilities of the digital euro. We hope to have answers soon. After completing this experimentation work, we will move on to the research phase, which will tell you how the digital euro would have to be designed. The investigation will take two years, with a three-month break. It's not until two or three years from now that the decision can be made. Doesn't all this time make Europe left behind in this matter? It is very difficult to be faster, these things are very complex and we are in a monetary area with many countries, it has to be done with the consensus of all. The President of the ECB has said for some time that in four or five years we may be in a position to decide to issue a digital euro. There may be countries that come first to this result, but I also do not see an absolute need to do so before. One of the main consequences for commercial banking is the possibility for individuals to have money in a central bank account. Where is the bank positioned? It is important to say that we can have digital euro, but we do not have to have an account at the central bank. We can have an account in a commercial bank that provides a digital euro and, of course, banks will be remunerated for this function of making the digital account available, not withdrawing revenue from the banking system, nor withdrawing funds, because deposits are a source of financing for the bank. The ECB has said that it does not want to replace the financial system, nor in raising funds, nor in the development of the direct activity of bank customers. Is there a possibility that the digital euro is allocated in retail banking and used as a resource for lending? The goal is to maintain the current financial system fundraising model, without prejudice to the digital euro. The radical scenario would be for everyone to have central bank accounts and no one to have an account with commercial banks, so commercial banks will not capture deposits and lose their main source of financing, they have to go looking for alternative, more expensive resources, impairing their financial intermediation capacity. That's not what you want. The aim is for the digital euro to be mediated by commercial banking. He said that the amount of digital euros that it is being held could be limited. Doesn't that also limit digital euro support? In fact, the digital euro may have ceilings to be held. But these questions are still open: whether it will be restricted or unrestricted access, in the sense of being able or not to have the amount you want, whether you will be paid or not, i.e. I can receive remuneration for that deposit or pay remuneration for that deposit, because it has no risk. If there's no risk, Maybe I have to pay to have digital currency at the central bank; or, else, I should receive it, because it's a deposit and I'm handing over my resources to someone who can use them. When the digital euro is issued, if it is issued, all these issues must be fully resolved. Can it be accepted that retail banking has to review business models because of the digital euro? Some impact will exist. But it is not intended to remove the role that the financial system has in the market. And on the consumer side, what does the existence of a digital euro change? The goal of the digital euro is to provide a global means of payment of a risk-free digital nature. Today, this role is played by the notes. The banknotes have no risk, we can use them with the guarantee that it is a payment method issued by the central bank. When we use MB Way or a credit transfer medium, we are using an electronic payment method. It's a payment with euros, but it's got a deposit account behind it, it's in a bank. The bank develops an activity of deposit collection and lending, which has risk. We have confidence and we have there the money, but we're erasing it with electronic money, from commercial banking. There's risk. There's risk. We're paying with commercial bank currency. The monetary base is nine or ten times smaller than the monetary mass, there is much more money circulating than that which exists. Banks multiply the money. That's why the Deposit Guarantee Fund exists up to 100,000. On the day i can make payments with the digital euro, I know that behind the account is not a commercial bank, but a central bank. The risk disappears. What is the state of the National Strategy for Retail Payments? We already have several initiatives underway. We are mainly working on contactless and immediate transfers to allow immediate batch transfers and to increase the current limit of EUR 15,000. We are assessing the necessary requirements for the non-face-to-face collection of direct debits authorisations and making legislative withdrawals to identify payments, in particular to the Public Administration, that require payment by cheque. And we are working with the system to make it mandatory to accept at least one electronic means of payment at points of sale. The results at the moment are promising. We're completely within the goal. On the requirement to accept at least one electronic means of payment, do you already have feedback from the merchants on this measure? This is one of the most ambitious measures and is not only dependent on the Payment Systems Forum, it also depends on legislative changes and the will of the Government or even Parliament. There is great interest from all parties in moving into a situation where all points where payments are made have the possibility, and the obligation, to accept at least one electronic means of payment. Cash is the only way no one can refuse. But with the increasing digitisation and preponderance of electronic payments, it is beginning to make little sense for a trader to refuse to receive electronic payments. The question that arises has to do with the business model behind it. If I am obliged to accept an electronic means of payment, I will have to have an infrastructure to accept that payment, a contract with an institution to make that transaction for me. And so I'm going to have to pay commissions. If traders are forced to bear a cost, then will there have to be limits on that cost? That's the whole point. It is necessary to find a balanced business model, which does not unbalance the relations between all operators, in order to entail costs for few benefits. A business model must be created that respects the specificity and idiosyncrasy of each pay market participant. So it is perhaps the most ambitious and most difficult measure, but it is already being studied. And on the political side, is there openness to making these legislative changes? We didn't get to that point. In the Forum for Payment Systems we have many representatives of public bodies, but not representatives of political power. If banks and traders understand that they can simplify any process to use direct debits or transfers, for example, we understand ourselves there, Banco de Portugal makes a pivot, creates the conditions and the measure is implemented. There are measures in which the only result that the Forum can produce is to make a proposal and deliver the proposal to political power.

Title: Statement by the Deputy Governor of Banco de Portugal and Chairman of the Resolution Fund's Management Committee, Luis Maximo dos Santos, in the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry to the losses recorded by Novo Banco and attributed to the Resolution Fund
text: Media Public Interventions all Statement of the Deputy Governor of Ba... Statement by the Deputy Governor of Banco de Portugal and Chairman of the Resolution Fund's Management Committee, Luis Maximo dos Santos, in the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry to the losses recorded by Novo Banco and attributed to the Resolution Fund 18 May. 2021 Mr President, Ladies and gentlemen, 1. I will take this opportunity to share some reflections on the subject-matter of this Committee of Inquiry. After almost seven years on the measure of resolution applied by Banco de Portugal to Banco Espirito Santo, it has to be stated unequivocally that we are here today for a single and exclusive reason: the acts of several directors of Banco Espirito Santo that materialized serious violations of elementary principles of sound and prudent management, which have translated, including, in a criminal indictment against 25 defendants, 18 individuals and 7 legal persons of the BES/GES universe, for various crimes as serious as: active and passive corruption in the private sector, qualified fraud, money laundering, market manipulation, infidelity, falsification of documents and  i don't know any other case in the financial sector) criminal association, in this case for 12 natural persons and 5 legal persons. Every citizen aware of what a rule of law is knows that the presumption of innocence is a structuring principle of a civilized society. But, let's face it, such an accusation is of unprecedented gravity with regard to the financial sector. It should also be noted that two of the misdemeanor proceedings brought by Banco de Portugal on the events of the BES have already become final. One of them condemned, among other defendants, the Chairman of the Bes Executive Committee, to date of the facts, by the commission of deceptive acts of ruinous management to the detriment of depositors, investors and other creditors, in a fine of 3,700,000 and in the ancillary penalty for disqualification from office for a period of 8 years. And there are three more misdemeanor proceedings with a sentencing decision handed down by Banco de Portugal, one with judicial confirmation at first instance and the other two awaiting trial. It is in these acts that undoubtedly lies the first and decisive cause of everything that has happened in this important institution of the banking sector Portuguese. Therefore, under no circumstances can we devalue or relativize them. Without them, there would have been no need to apply the resolution measure to bes  by the way, it should be stressed, several times validated in court as to the legality of its grounds  the Novo Banco would not even exist and therefore its sale would not have happened. In other words, wanting to understand what happened after the 2014 resolution without having this framework permanently present, without being aware that it is this the inescapable starting point of all reflection on this matter would be a purely and simply meaningless exercise. In an age prone to historical revisionism of all hues, with the delay of justice, and a society that does not cultivate memory, a culture broth favorable to the bleaching of serious actions and the lack of understanding of the dilematic situations in which public authorities who have had to deal with this terrible legacy have been placed. To a young man who is now 18 years old and who reads newspapers or sees television will seem to him, listening to some reports and statements, that the problems of the Novo Banco originate directly in it and are all his responsibility or, even worse, the public authorities who have the ungrateful task of leading to an acceptable end so difficult mission. Sometimes it permeates the idea that it does not seem to matter that successive audits, in particular those that Deloitte carried out under Law No 15/2019 of 12 February, which this Parliament has adopted in good time, demonstrate abundantly the opposite; it does not seem to appreciate what successive statements of the so-called great debtors make very clear as to why we arrived here. Or even if the audit of the Public Financing of the Novo Banco carried out by the Court of Auditors expressly states that "the public financing of Novo Banco contributed to financial stability, especially because it avoided the liquidation of the bank and reduced systemic risk", not to mention an Opinion of the Attorney General's Office issued last year. I believe in the virtualities of this CPI and I believe it can add more light to the so intricate process with which unfortunately the country is still confronted. But in a society where perennial values seem to have been replaced by the impact of headlines and the effectiveness of communication agendas, I believe it is necessary to highlight the real context in which, in my view, this IPC must be understood. 2. I would also like to leave a few words about my participation in this whole process. I joined the administration of Banco de Portugal on June 20, 2016 and in September 2017 I became Deputy Governor. On the governor's proposal, the Board of Directors assigned me, in 2016, the portfolios relating to the Department of Behavioral Supervision, the Department of Legal Services and the Department of Investigation and Sanctioning Action, as well as the chairmanship of the Deposit Guarantee Fund's Management Committee, to which later the responsibility of the Data Protection Office and the representation of banco de Portugal in the Banco de Portugal Directive Committee on Compensation To Investors. In June 2016, the second process of sale of Novo Banco was already underway, led by a team led by Dr. Sergio Monteiro, who reported directly to my then colleague, Deputy Governor Dr. Jose Ramalho, who has already had the opportunity to testify at this Commission. On March 1, 2017, following the resignation of my colleague, I was appointed, by unanimous resolution of the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal, Chairman of the Resolution Fund's Directive Committee, and was also responsible for the field of the Resolution Department, whose formal creation i have promoted, and the representation of Portugal in the Single Resolution Board. As is apparent from the documents which were provided to you, the negotiations on the sale of Novo Banco were already well advanced at that time. On 31 March 2017, that is, one month after assuming the chairmanship of its Management Committee, the Resolution Fund  complying with Banco de Portugal's determination as a national resolution authority  signed the agreements relating to the sale of 75% of Novo Banco's capital to Nani Holdings (Lone Star), already made available to this Commission. On October 18, 2017, all previous authorizations and conditions were met and the sale was completed. Although, as is apparent from the foregoing, Having entered this process with the train in progress, I never had the slightest doubt that the sale of Novo Banco was a necessary and right decision, in the light of the existing context, taking into account the constraints faced by Banco de Portugal and the Government and, in particular, taking into account the weighting of the alternative which was placed, that is to say, the liquidation of the institution. We must keep in mind that on 18 October 2017 the three-year period with which Portugal had committed to the European Commission to sell Novo Banco was already exceeded by more than three months. The sale of Novo Banco in 2017 was therefore indispensable to safeguard financial stability with the inherent macroeconomic benefits in various plans. Did the solution found have costs? Of course i do. But as in the famous phrase "if you think education is expensive, do not want to know the cost of ignorance", here too one can say that the cost of not pursuing the goal of financial stability would be incomparably higher. Without further regard to this point, I would like to stress that the Decision of the European Commission authorising state aid to Novo Banco expressly states that only the direct losses of a possible liquidation of Novo Banco in 2017 would be in the order of EUR 14 billion. 3. With the sale of Novo Banco, a new, demanding and unprecedented stage was opened for the Resolution Fund: to adequately exercise the powers conferred on it by the contract, especially in the area of the Contingent Capitalization Agreement. One of the first decisions made was to create a special team in the Resolution Department for this purpose. I was fully aware of the risks that this mission entailed, but I always believed in the capacity of the Banco de Portugal staff who executed it. The Resolution Fund considers that it has carried out in a rigorous, appropriate and judicious manner the functions that are in its framework of the agreements concerning the sale of 75% of novo banco's capital, very in particular with regard to the Contingent Capitalization Agreement. The examples and results of this are multiple and correspond to a daily work of several Banco de Portugal teams that support the Fund, as provided for by law. The documents are in the possession of the Honourable Members and I am sure that their technical soundness leaves no room for doubt. I would also stress that they will find no dissonance between the technical notes of the Bank's services and the decisions taken by the Fund Directive Commission, naturally after their scrutiny and debate, let alone forgotten or unfollowed technical notes. Of the 240 transactions submitted to it by Novo Banco for pronunciation, only 35% were approved in the exact terms proposed. Eighty-five operations were approved on condition that certain requirements of the Fund were met, thirty-eight were approved with recommendations and twenty-eight did not even merit authorization. On the other hand, the value of the resolution fund's disputes with Novo Banco pending before or in the process of reaching an approximate amount of EUR 331 million. Apart from the resolution fund's intervention and the 3.89 billion limit would probably be reached this year. In the Audit of the Court of Auditors to which I have already referred, the Resolution Fund set out in detail its views and grounds, which are publicly disclosed by both the Court and the Resolution Fund. And, I stress, they converge with those of Banco de Portugal. On the question of the demonstration, validation and verification of amounts payable and in particular the calculation of capital, I draw the attention of members to the documentation we refer to this Commission on 11 May, and in particular to the letter sent to the Resolution Fund on 23 April 2021 by the European Central Bank, in the person of the Chairman of the Single Supervisory Board, Mr Andrea Enria, who clearly confirms the correction of the positions supported by the Fund in this matter. In any case, we have already formalized with Novo Banco - long before, therefore, the 6-month period set to demonstrate compliance with its recommendations or provide justification for not having complied with them  the agreement on the Reference Map for the Contingent Capitalization Agreement, which is alluded to in the recommendation set out in paragraph 276 of the Audit. On 7 April 2021, Novo Banco made, under the Contingent Capitalization Agreement, the request for payment of 598,311,568.00, with reference to the 2020 accounts, necessary to raise the CET 1 ratio to 12.00% at the end of 2020. Once the analysis of all relevant elements is finished, which we say may happen in the coming days, we will inform the Minister of State and Finance of the amount of payment that the Resolution Fund considers due to the Novo Banco, pursuant to the Contingent Capitalization Agreement, by reference to the 2020 accounts. Ladies and gentlemen The complexity and relevance of this theme justify all public scrutiny. But understanding of what is at stake is averse to simplistic and passionate judgments. Rather, it calls for balanced and contextualized considerations, because only then can we illuminate the path we still have left to take. Despite its short and troubled life, Novo Banco remains one of the main banks of the national banking system, maintaining the definition of systemic institution. According to data as of December 31, 2020, its assets reach EUR 44.4 billion. It employs about 4,500 employees and has almost 1.5 million customers and depositors. It raises more than 26 billion in deposits. It has a market share of 14% in the segment of deposits to companies and about 16% in the business credit segment, an indicator that is well demonstrated by its important role in financing the national economy, which becomes more relevant in the context experienced by the crisis generated by the pandemic. However, 25% of this bank's capital is public, through the participation of the Resolution Fund. We can therefore say that if we exclude CGD, it is the largest public participation in the capital of a bank. This is a given of the greatest importance to assess the final balance of this whole operation and I do not think it has been sufficiently emphasized. I thank you for your attention and I am now at your disposal to answer the questions you wish to address to me.
