Declarao do Vice-Governador do Banco de Portugal e Presidente da Comisso Diretiva do Fundo de Resoluo, Lus Mximo dos Santos, na Comisso de Inqurito Parlamentar s perdas registadas pelo Novo Banco e imputadas ao Fundo de Resoluo 18 mai. 2021 Senhor Presidente, Senhoras e Senhores Deputados, 1. Vou aproveitar a oportunidade que esta interveno me propicia para partilhar algumas reflexes sobre o objeto desta Comisso de Inqurito. Volvidos quase sete anos sobre a medida de resoluo aplicada pelo Banco de Portugal ao Banco Esprito Santo, tem de ser afirmado inequivocamente que estamos hoje aqui por uma nica e exclusiva razo: os atos de diversos administradores do Banco Esprito Santo que materializaram graves violaes de princpios elementares de gesto s e prudente, que se traduziram, inclusivamente, numa acusao criminal contra 25 arguidos, 18 pessoas singulares e 7 pessoas coletivas do universo BES/GES, por vrios crimes to graves quanto: corrupo ativa e passiva no setor privado, burla qualificada, branqueamento de capitais, manipulao de mercado, infidelidade, falsificao de documentos e  pasme-se (no conheo nenhum outro caso no setor financeiro) associao criminosa, neste caso relativamente a 12 pessoas singulares e 5 pessoas coletivas. Qualquer cidado consciente do que  um Estado de Direito sabe que a presuno de inocncia  um princpio estruturante de uma sociedade civilizada. Mas, convenhamos, uma tal acusao  de indita gravidade no que ao setor financeiro diz respeito. Importa referir tambm que dois processos de contraordenao instaurados pelo Banco de Portugal sobre os acontecimentos do BES j transitaram em julgado. Um deles condenou, entre outros arguidos, o Presidente da Comisso Executiva do BES,  data dos factos, pela prtica de atos dolosos de gesto ruinosa em detrimento de depositantes, investidores e demais credores, em coima de 3.700.000 e na sano acessria de inibio do exerccio de funes por um perodo de 8 anos. E h mais trs processos de contraordenao com deciso condenatria proferida pelo Banco de Portugal, um com confirmao judicial em primeira instncia e os outros dois aguardando julgamento.  nesses atos que indubitavelmente reside a causa primeira e determinante de tudo o que aconteceu nessa importante instituio do setor bancrio portugus. Por isso mesmo, em nenhuma circunstncia podemos desvaloriz-los ou relativiza-los. Sem eles, no teria havido necessidade de aplicar a medida de resoluo ao BES  j agora, sublinhe-se, vrias vezes validada em tribunal quanto  legalidade dos seus fundamentos -, o Novo Banco nem sequer existiria e, portanto, a sua venda no teria acontecido. Por outras palavras, querer perceber o que se passou depois da resoluo de 2014 sem ter esse enquadramento permanentemente presente, sem ter conscincia de que  esse o ponto de partida inescapvel de toda a reflexo sobre esta matria, seria um exerccio pura e simplesmente sem sentido. Numa poca propensa a revisionismos histricos de todos os matizes, com a demora da justia, e uma sociedade que no cultiva a memria, gera-se um caldo de cultura favorvel ao branqueamento de aes graves e  no compreenso das dilemticas situaes em que foram colocadas as autoridades pblicas que tiveram de lidar com este terrvel legado. A um jovem que hoje tenha 18 anos e que leia jornais ou veja televiso parecer-lhe-, ouvindo alguns relatos e declaraes, que os problemas do Novo Banco tm origem direta nele e so todos da sua responsabilidade ou, pior ainda, das autoridades pblicas que tm a ingrata tarefa de conduzir a um final aceitvel to difcil misso. s vezes, perpassa a ideia que parece no importar que sucessivas auditorias, designadamente as que a Deloitte realizou ao abrigo da Lei n. 15/2019, de 12 de fevereiro, que em boa hora este Parlamento aprovou, demonstrem abundantemente o contrrio; parece no se valorizar o que sucessivos depoimentos dos ditos grandes devedores deixam muito claro quanto s razes por que aqui chegmos. Ou mesmo que a auditoria ao Financiamento Pblico do Novo Banco levada a cabo pelo Tribunal de Contas refira expressamente que o financiamento pblico do Novo Banco concorreu para a estabilidade financeira, sobretudo por ter evitado a liquidao do banco e reduzido o risco sistmico, para no falar de um Parecer da Procuradoria-Geral da Repblica emitido no ano passado. Acredito nas virtualidades desta CPI e considero que pode acrescentar mais luz a to intricado processo com que infelizmente o Pas ainda se confronta. Mas numa sociedade em que os valores perenes parecem ter sido substitudos pelo impacto das headlines e da eficcia das agendas comunicacionais, entendo ser necessrio pr em evidncia o verdadeiro contexto em que, a meu ver, esta CPI deve ser entendida. 2. Gostaria tambm de deixar algumas palavras sobre a minha participao em todo este processo. Ingressei na administrao do Banco de Portugal em 20 de junho de 2016 e em setembro de 2017 passei a Vice-Governador. Por proposta do Governador, o Conselho de Administrao atribuiu-me, em 2016, os pelouros relativos ao Departamento de Superviso Comportamental, ao Departamento de Servios Jurdicos e ao Departamento de Averiguao e Ao Sancionatria, bem como a presidncia da Comisso Diretiva do Fundo de Garantia de Depsitos, a que se adicionaram, mais tarde, a responsabilidade pelo Gabinete de Proteo de Dados e a representao do Banco de Portugal na Comisso Diretiva do Sistema de Indemnizao aos Investidores. Em junho de 2016, estava j em curso o segundo processo de venda do Novo Banco, conduzido por uma equipa liderada pelo Dr. Srgio Monteiro, que reportava diretamente ao meu ento colega, o Vice-Governador Dr. Jos Ramalho, que j teve ocasio de prestar depoimento nessa Comisso. Em 1 de maro de 2017, na sequncia da renncia ao mandato desse meu colega, fui designado, por deliberao unnime do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Portugal, Presidente da Comisso Diretiva do Fundo de Resoluo, ficando tambm responsvel pelo pelouro do Departamento de Resoluo, cuja criao formal entretanto promovi, e pela representao de Portugal no Conselho nico de Resoluo. Como resulta dos documentos que foram facultados aos Senhores Deputados, as negociaes relativas  venda do Novo Banco estavam j nessa altura bastante avanadas. Em 31 de maro de 2017, ou seja, um ms depois de ter assumido a presidncia da respetiva Comisso Diretiva, o Fundo de Resoluo  cumprindo determinao do Banco de Portugal enquanto autoridade nacional de resoluo -, assinou os acordos relativos  venda de 75% do capital do Novo Banco  Nani Holdings (Lone Star), j disponibilizados a esta Comisso. Em 18 de outubro de 2017, todas as autorizaes e condies precedentes ficaram reunidas e a venda ficou concluda. Apesar de, como resulta do exposto, ter entrado nesse processo com o comboio em andamento, nunca tive a menor dvida de que a venda do Novo Banco foi uma deciso necessria e acertada,  luz do contexto existente, tendo em conta os constrangimentos com que o Banco de Portugal e o Governo estavam confrontados e, muito particularmente, tendo em conta a ponderao da alternativa que se colocava, a saber, a liquidao da instituio. No podemos deixar de ter presente que em 18 de outubro de 2017 estava j ultrapassado em mais de trs meses o prazo de trs anos com que Portugal se tinha comprometido perante a Comisso Europeia para proceder  venda do Novo Banco. A venda do Novo Banco em 2017 foi, pois, indispensvel para salvaguardar a estabilidade financeira com os inerentes benefcios macroeconmicos em vrios planos. A soluo encontrada teve custos? Claro que sim. Mas tal como na clebre frase se acha que a educao  cara, no queira saber o custo da ignorncia, tambm aqui se pode dizer que o custo de no prosseguir o objetivo da estabilidade financeira seria incomparavelmente maior. Sem me alongar em mais consideraes no que a esse ponto diz respeito, gostaria de sublinhar que a Deciso da Comisso Europeia que autorizou o auxlio de estado ao Novo Banco refere expressamente que s as perdas diretas de uma eventual liquidao do Novo Banco em 2017 seriam na ordem dos 14 mil milhes de euros. 3. Com a venda do Novo Banco, nova, exigente e indita etapa se abriu para o Fundo de Resoluo: exercer adequadamente os poderes que o contrato lhe conferia, em especial no domnio do Acordo de Capitalizao Contingente. Uma das primeiras decises tomadas foi a de criar no Departamento de Resoluo uma equipa especial para o efeito. Tive plena conscincia dos riscos que esta misso implicava mas acreditei sempre na capacidade dos quadros do Banco de Portugal que a executaram. O Fundo de Resoluo considera que tem desempenhado de forma rigorosa, adequada e criteriosa as funes que lhe cabem no quadro dos acordos que respeitam  venda de 75% do capital do Novo Banco, muito em particular, no que ao Acordo de Capitalizao Contingente diz respeito. Os exemplos e os resultados disso so mltiplos e correspondem a um trabalho dirio de vrias equipas do Banco de Portugal que do apoio ao Fundo, conforme previsto na lei. Os documentos esto em poder dos Senhores Deputados e estou certo que a sua solidez tcnica no deixa margem para dvidas. Sublinho tambm que no encontraro qualquer dissonncia entre as notas tcnicas dos servios do Banco e as decises tomadas pela Comisso Diretiva do Fundo, naturalmente aps o seu escrutnio e debate, nem muito menos notas tcnicas esquecidas ou sem seguimento. Das 240 operaes que lhe foram submetidas pelo Novo Banco para pronncia, apenas 35% foram aprovadas nos exatos termos propostos. Oitenta e cinco operaes foram aprovadas na condio de serem cumpridas determinadas exigncias do Fundo, trinta e oito foram aprovadas com recomendaes e vinte e oito no mereceram sequer autorizao. Por outro lado, o valor dos litgios do Fundo de Resoluo com o Novo Banco pendentes em Tribunal arbitral ou em vias disso atinge j o valor aproximado de 331 milhes de euros. No fora a interveno do Fundo de Resoluo e o limite de 3,89 mil milhes de euros provavelmente seria atingido este ano. Na auditoria do Tribunal de Contas a que j me referi, o Fundo de Resoluo exps detalhadamente os seus pontos de vista e os respetivos fundamentos, que esto publicamente divulgados tanto pelo Tribunal como pelo Fundo de Resoluo. E, sublinho, convergem com os do Banco de Portugal. Sobre a questo da demonstrao, validao e verificao dos valores a pagar e em particular do clculo de capital, chamo a ateno dos Senhores Deputados para a documentao que remetemos a esta Comisso no dia 11 de maio, e em particular para a carta enviada ao Fundo de Resoluo, em 23 de abril de 2021, pelo Banco Central Europeu, na pessoa do Presidente do Conselho nico de Superviso, Senhor Andrea Enria, que confirma, com toda a clareza, a correo das posies sustentadas pelo Fundo nesta matria. Em qualquer caso, formalizmos j com o Novo Banco -muito antes, portanto, do prazo de 6 meses fixado para demonstrar o cumprimento das suas recomendaes ou apresentar justificao para as no ter cumprido  o acordo sobre o Mapa de Referncia referente ao Acordo de Capitalizao Contingente, a que se alude na recomendao constante do pargrafo 276 da Auditoria. Em 7 de abril de 2021, o Novo Banco efetuou, ao abrigo do Acordo de Capitalizao Contingente, o pedido de pagamento de 598.311.568,00, com referncia s contas de 2020, necessrio para elevar o rcio CET 1 para 12,00% no final de 2020. Assim que estiver finda a anlise de todos os elementos pertinentes, o que contamos que possa acontecer nos prximos dias, informaremos o Senhor Ministro de Estado e das Finanas do montante do pagamento que o Fundo de Resoluo considera devido ao Novo Banco, nos termos do Acordo de Capitalizao Contingente, por referncia s contas de 2020. Senhoras e Senhores Deputados A complexidade e a relevncia deste tema justificam todo o escrutnio pblico. Mas a compreenso do que est em causa  avessa a juzos simplistas e apaixonados. Antes reclama ponderaes equilibradas e contextualizadas, pois s assim poderemos iluminar o caminho que ainda nos resta fazer. Apesar da sua vida curta e atribulada, o Novo Banco continua a ser um dos principais bancos do sistema bancrio nacional, mantendo a definio de instituio sistmica. Segundo dados a 31 de dezembro de 2020, o seu ativo atinge os 44,4 mil milhes de euros. Emprega cerca de 4500 colaboradores e tem quase 1,5 milhes de clientes e depositantes. Capta mais de 26 mil milhes de euros em depsitos. Tem uma quota de mercado de 14% no segmento dos depsitos s empresas e de cerca 16% no segmento do crdito s empresas, indicador que  bem demonstrativo do seu importante papel no financiamento da economia nacional, que mais relevante se torna no contexto vivido pela crise gerada pela pandemia. Ora, 25% do capital deste banco  pblico, por via da participao do Fundo de Resoluo. Podemos por isso dizer que, se excluirmos a CGD, se trata da maior participao pblica no capital de um banco. Trata-se de um dado da maior relevncia para avaliar o balano final de toda esta operao e julgo que no tem sido suficientemente enfatizado. Agradeo a vossa ateno e fico agora  disposio das Senhoras e dos Senhores Deputados para responder s perguntas que me queiram dirigir.

Title: Intervention of the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Mario Centeno, in the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry to losses recorded by Novo Banco and attributed to the Resolution Fund
text: Media Public Interventions All Of The Governor of the Bank... Intervention of the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Mario Centeno, in the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry to losses recorded by Novo Banco and attributed to the Resolution Fund 18 May. 2021 Mr President, Ladies and gentlemen, "Once and for all." So begin many of the stories that enchant us. But the history of the banking system globally during the financial crisis and sovereign debt, does not have that charm. For a long time, packed by the illusion and arrogance of self-regulation that was deemed self-sufficient, banking and financial institutions accumulated extreme risks, in the form of unviable financial assets, whose performance did not allow ab initio to satisfy the promised remuneration or even the reimbursement of invested capital. But it didn't stop there. When it became clear the unsustainable weight of unviable financial assets, pleonasically called complex structured financial products, financial intermediaries and issuers went into denial of reality. Under the opaque veil of governance models, in which boards of directors and supervisory bodies did not take care of their most basic responsibilities and merely grew the problem, depending on the inevitable. In a context where gaps in the legal and institutional framework of the euro area banking, financial and monetary system have become clear, the accumulation of risks by many public and private banking institutions has been fatal. Many banks have not borne the impact of the financial crises and the sovereign debt crisis that followed it, and, as is well known, the European economy has been plunged into the biggest post-war economic and financial crisis. In this context, it was necessary to reform and complete the institutional legal framework. I'd say it was necessary to reinvent it. Regardless of its latitude and development, there has not been a single banking system in Europe that has escaped this crisis. One way or another. Earlier (better) or later (worse). All governments have been called upon to intervene in their banking systems. In the name of financial stability and the public interest. They did it by protecting the bank depositors. Capitalizing on the banks. Protecting taxpayers when called upon to intervene through the state. Creating risk mitigation mechanisms inherent to banking and financial activity. Adopting uniform European rules for all systemic banks. Creating a genuine Banking Union to preserve the European Union. At one point, even the idea of a private bank, in a market regulated by the state, was at risk. But regulators, supervisors and central banks found a regulatory framework that put an end to self-regulation and reorganized the market. In the European framework, two nerve pillars stand out: the Banking Union in its various aspects and the Banking Restructuring and Resolution Scheme. Banking activity in Europe has not been the same again after the creation and subsequent deepening of these pillars. But Portugal arrived late to the process of reform and sanitation of the banking system. In the financial economy there is no bad luck. There are timely decisions, determination in action, give full and complete response. Bad luck is doing the opposite of this. What cost the country procrastination? How much did the country cost shudder and partial responses? How much did it cost Portugal to fail to sell Novo Banco in 2015? In November 2015 Portugal had 80% of the assets of its banking system in institutions suffering from one of four evils. Some suffered from everyone at the same time. (1) many institutions were decapitalised, but the paef capital intended to capitalise on them had not been used; (2) some were on the verge of resolution, because the situation was such that they had already lost the minimum conditions to operate; (3) many of those who depended in some way on the Government, having received public money, had no business and restructuring plans and were adrift; (4) others had unastable shareholder structures and were having serious governance and even compliance problems, calling into question the credibility of European supervisors. There is no modern economy compatible with a banking system in these conditions, unable to finance investment, innovation and job creation. Since 2008, they have disappeared from the banking system Portuguese the LBW; the BPP; BANIF; and BES. Nationalized, liquidated or resolved. What happened in Portugal was apparently not very different from what happened in other European countries. Except for the late and systemic size of BES, a rare and even unique case in Europe, given the weight it had in the banking system. Ladies and gentlemen, This CPI focuses on a banking institution that has its doors open to the public. That you are financing yourself in the market to strengthen your own funds, which protect your depositors. That came out of a particularly complex process, and that it is the third largest bank to operate in Portugal. Such a situation therefore requires special care. It requires special qualifications from those who administer the institution. It requires recognition for the collective effort with which we are still confronted today. And it demands respect from everyone for those who work in it, trust their savings, or invest. The overwhelming majority of the issues raised in this CPI concern BES. They had their origin in BES and not nb. We should always keep this in mind. In 2014, the third largest national bank was settled. As I said, this resolution resulted only from the actions and omissions of the successive bes boards of directors. There was no bad luck here either. If luck is what happens when preparation meets opportunity, bad luck happens when incompetence meets the deed and the practice of ruinous management acts. And it must therefore be responsible, as is already proven in court. Let me remind you that there are hundreds of legal proceedings in portuguese courts at the moment. The judicial proceedings regarding the national conviction by Banco de Portugal of the bes managers have become final. A process of greater relevance by imputation of guilt and responsibility. BES was the only large national bank that did not use the aid mechanisms designed during the Assistance Programme from 2011 to 2014. BES was the only bank in Portugal, in the midst of the sovereign debt crisis, which did not need public support for its solvency. BES was the only one that ended. 34 days after you have completed the Assistance Program. BES spreads a mantle of loss and uncertainty on the Portuguese banking system and society. After all the problems of the biggest financial crisis were not yet clean. The BES resolution dictated all subsequent events, made in the light of the European banking resolution framework, BRRD, transposed, however, into national legislation. The creation of the Novo Banco on 4 August 2014 was accompanied by the rules, agreed with the European Commission, on how the short life of the transitional bank would take place. I had two years to live, tops. And the proceeds of the sale should pay the loan of the State and banks to the FdR. A bank that would have to live a troubled period, without more capital, manifestly insufficient, with which it had been born (the FdR was prevented from capitalizing). The sale of Novo Banco failed a year later because none of the offers allowed the bank was sold with the result it had been promised. What a real surprise! What a surprise anyone would want to buy a sub-capitalized bank full of problematic assets, for a higher value than what was injected at the time of resolution. In 2015 it was less than a year before the bank was liquidated, the murky alternative to the sale assumed by the Republic in 2014. How much would the settlement cost? A difficult estimate in a bank of this size. EUR 14 billion would be the immediate and direct cost, which would increase direct costs to the deposit guarantee system and indirect costs for the rest of the banking system. Without the sale of the asset underlying the loan made to the FdR, this was another NPL in the Portuguese economy. But not "just another" NPL, it would be the generator of all defaults, which would drag the entire bankroll with it. The extension of the sale period was, of course, negotiated with the European competition authority, resulting in a strengthening of commitments in the face of the signs of difficulty that the financial system presented and the lack of credibility that existed. This is how, between the end of 2015 and October 2017, the BANIF resolution was made. CGD was capitalized by its sole shareholder, the State Portuguese. FdR became solvent. And two of the largest Portuguese private banks found capital to stabilize their shareholder structure. And that's also how the sale of NB was promoted in 2017 and non-credit and risk of default began to fall in 2016, reaching today a value of less than 5%, almost 4 times lower than the values of that time. Only these concerted and coordinated actions between the European and national authorities have given national banking a future. Only in this way was it possible to improve the classification of Portuguese sovereign debt. This is the only way to get Portugal out of the Excessive Deficit Procedure in which it had been in place for almost 10 years. The sale of a transitional bank, such as the NB, was not a sale of any "any property", which if not sold today is sold tomorrow. This appeal to procrastination is called bad luck in finance. It was the ability to meet the commitments that allows our companies today to have access to the world's largest market for goods and services and to finance themselves at interest rates equal to those of other European companies. The nationalization of a financial institution is not the same as the nationalization of an industrial enterprise. Have we forgotten the nationalization of LBW? Have we forgotten how much it cost and still cost today? Bank resolution is the mechanism for ensuring that costs of intervention in the banking system follow the principle of fiscal neutrality and protect taxpayers. This year, the 27 countries of the European Union ratified an amendment to the Treaty on the European Stability Mechanism guaranteeing fiscal neutrality (in the medium/long term) whenever the ESM has to finance the resolution of banks in the European Union. And it guarantees it in the same way that the FdR secured the financing of the BES resolution, with loans from banks and the Treasury. The sale of NB is the result of a legal imperative, was the form found, difficult, with risks to the FdR, in the framework of the operation of a contingent capital mechanism. This mechanism prevented its operating limit, EUR 3 890 million, from being recorded immediately in public accounts in 2017. Because it's not a guarantee. This mechanism has enabled close and effective monitoring of the asset management processes included in it. It allows these risks to be diluted over time and since 2018 we have faced its value and a reality: the Novo Banco was new, but heir to old problems and with many complex challenges ahead of us. It wasn't a good bank. It was necessary to makehim a good bank. And its restructuring ends this year. Attested by the European Commission. So the Portuguese institutions allow it. I end by recalling what is most important at this stage. Understand that Novo Banco is a reference institution in the national banking space. Which is the preferred bank by millions of families and businesses to deposit their savings and to obtain financing, to invest, innovate and create quality jobs. Let us remember that often, when we say NB, we mean "bes legacy". And of course, let us never lose sight of the demand that today, and in such an increased and challenging way, has to fall on the national banking. To support the national economy, to meet its obligations to the FdR, not to allow periods such as those we have lived for a decade to be repeated and which have determined the resolution of the BES. Thank you very much.
text_original: Media > Intervenes Pblicas > Ver todas > Interveno do Governador do Banco... Interveno do Governador do Banco de Portugal, Mrio Centeno, na Comisso de Inqurito Parlamentar s perdas registadas pelo Novo Banco e imputadas ao Fundo de Resoluo 18 mai. 2021 Senhor Presidente, Senhoras e senhores deputados, Era uma vez. Assim comeam muitas das estrias que nos encantam. Mas a histria do sistema bancrio a nvel global durante a crise financeira e das dvidas soberanas, no tem esse encanto. Durante muito tempo, embaladas pela iluso e arrogncia de uma auto-regulao que se julgava autossuficiente, as instituies bancrias e financeiras acumularam riscos extremos, sob a forma de ativos financeiros inviveis, cuja performance no permitia ab initio satisfazer a remunerao prometida ou mesmo o reembolso do capital investido. Mas no ficou por a. Quando se tornou manifesto o insustentvel peso dos ativos financeiros inviveis, pleonasticamente denominados de produtos financeiros estruturados complexos, os intermedirios financeiros e emitentes enveredaram pela negao da realidade. Sob o vu opaco de modelos de governao, em que conselhos de administrao e rgos de fiscalizao, no cuidavam das suas responsabilidades mais elementares e se limitavam a fazer crescer o problema, adiando o inevitvel. Num contexto em que as lacunas do enquadramento jurdico-institucional do sistema bancrio, financeiro e monetrio da rea do euro se tornaram manifestas, a acumulao de riscos por muitas instituies bancrias, pblicas e privadas, foi fatal. Muitos bancos no suportaram o impacto das crises financeiras e da crise das dvidas soberanas que lhe sucedeu, e, como  bem sabido, a economia europeia viu-se mergulhada na maior crise econmica e financeira do ps-guerra. Nesse contexto, foi necessrio reformar e completar o enquadramento jurdicoinstitucional. Diria mesmo que foi necessrio reinvent-lo. Independentemente da sua latitude e do seu desenvolvimento, no houve um nico sistema bancrio na Europa que tenha escapado a esta crise. De uma forma ou de outra. Mais cedo (melhor) ou mais tarde (pior). Todos os Governos foram chamados a intervir nos seus sistemas bancrios. Em nome da estabilidade financeira e do interesse pblico. Fizeram-no protegendo os depositantes bancrios. Capitalizando os bancos. Protegendo os contribuintes, quando chamados a intervir atravs do Estado. Criando mecanismos de mitigao do risco inerente  atividade bancria e financeira. Adotando regras europeias uniformes para todos os bancos sistmicos. Criando uma verdadeira Unio Bancria para preservar a Unio Europeia. Num certo momento, mesmo a ideia de uma banca privada, num mercado regulado pelo Estado, esteve em risco. Mas os reguladores, supervisores e bancos centrais encontraram um quadro regulatrio que ps fim  autorregulao e reorganizou o mercado. No quadro europeu, destacam-se dois pilares nevrlgicos: a Unio Bancria nas suas diversas vertentes e o Regime de Reestruturao e Resoluo Bancria. A atividade bancria na Europa no voltou, com efeito, a ser a mesma aps a criao e o subsequente aprofundamento destes pilares. Mas Portugal chegou tarde ao processo de reforma e de saneamento do sistema bancrio. Na economia financeira no h azar. H tomar decises atempadas, determinao na ao, dar resposta cabal e completa. Azar  fazer o contrrio disto. O que custou ao pas a procrastinao? Quanto custaram ao pas respostas titubeantes e parciais? Quanto custou a Portugal falhar a venda do Novo Banco em 2015? Em novembro de 2015 Portugal tinha 80% dos ativos do seu sistema bancrio em instituies que padeciam de um de quatro males. Algumas padeciam de todos ao mesmo tempo. (1) muitas instituies estavam descapitalizadas, mas o capital do PAEF destinado a capitaliz-las no tinha sido usado; (2) algumas estavam  beira da resoluo, porque a situao era tal que tinham j perdido as condies mnimas para operar; (3) muitas das que dependiam de alguma forma do Governo, por ter recebido dinheiro pblico, no tinham planos de negcio e de reestruturao e estavam  deriva; (4) outras tinham estruturas acionistas instveis e estavam com graves problemas de governao e at de compliance, pondo em causa a credibilidade junto de supervisores europeus. No h nenhuma economia moderna compatvel com um sistema bancrio nestas condies, incapaz de financiar o investimento, a inovao e a criao de emprego. Desde 2008, desapareceram do sistema bancrio portugus o BPN; o BPP; o BANIF; e o BES. Nacionalizados, liquidados ou resolvidos. O que aconteceu em Portugal no foi aparentemente muito diferente do que aconteceu em outros pases europeus. Exceto por tardio e pela dimenso sistmica do BES, um caso raro e at nico na Europa, face ao peso que tinha no sistema bancrio. Senhoras e Senhores Deputados, Esta CPI incide sobre uma instituio bancria que tem as portas abertas ao pblico. Que se est a financiar no mercado para robustecer os seus fundos prprios, que protegem os seus depositantes. Que saiu de um processo particularmente complexo, e que  o terceiro maior banco a operar em Portugal. Tal situao impe, por isso, um cuidado especial. Exige de quem administra a instituio qualificaes especiais. Exige o reconhecimento pelo esforo coletivo com que ainda hoje somos confrontados. E exige de todos respeito por quem nela trabalha, confia as suas poupanas, ou investe. A esmagadora maioria das questes levantadas nesta CPI dizem respeito ao BES. Tiveram a sua origem no BES e no no NB. Devemos ter isso sempre presente. Em 2014, foi resolvido o terceiro maior banco nacional. Como disse, esta resoluo resultou apenas e s das aes e omisses dos sucessivos conselhos de administrao do BES. Tambm aqui no houve azar. Se a sorte  o que acontece quando a preparao encontra a oportunidade, o azar acontece quando a incompetncia encontra o dolo e a prtica de atos de gesto ruinosa. E deve, por isso, ter responsveis, como alis j est judicialmente comprovado. Deixem-me recordar-vos que neste momento h centenas de processos judiciais tramitando, em diferentes fases, nos tribunais portugueses. Transitou em julgado o processo judicial a propsito da condenao contraordenacional pelo Banco de Portugal dos gestores do BES. Um processo da maior relevncia pela imputao de culpa e de responsabilidade. O BES foi o nico banco de grande dimenso nacional que no recorreu aos mecanismos de auxlio desenhados aquando do Programa de Assistncia de 2011 a 2014. O BES era o nico banco em Portugal, em plena crise das dvidas soberanas, que no tinha necessidade de apoio pblico  sua solvabilidade. O BES foi o nico que acabou. 34 dias depois de ter terminado o Programa de Assistncia. O BES espalha sobre o sistema bancrio e sobre a economia e a sociedade portuguesas um manto de perdas e incerteza. Afinal os problemas da maior crise financeira ainda no estavam limpos. A resoluo do BES ditou todos os acontecimentos posteriores, feitos  luz do quadro de resoluo bancria europeia, a BRRD, transposta, entretanto, para a legislao nacional. A criao do Novo Banco no dia 4 de agosto de 2014 foi acompanhada das regras, acordadas com a Comisso Europeia, de como a vida, curta, do banco de transio se iria processar. Tinha dois anos de vida, no mximo. E o produto da venda deveria pagar o emprstimo do Estado e dos bancos ao FdR. Um banco que teria que viver um perodo conturbado, sem mais capital, manifestamente insuficiente, com que tinha nascido (o FdR estava impedido de o capitalizar). A venda do Novo Banco falhou um ano depois porque nenhuma das ofertas permitia que o banco fosse vendido com o resultado que tinha sido prometido. Que grande surpresa de facto! Que surpresa ningum querer comprar um banco sub capitalizado e cheio de ativos problemticos, por um valor superior ao que foi injetado no momento da resoluo. Em 2015 faltava menos de um ano para evitar a liquidao do banco, a tenebrosa alternativa  venda assumida pela Repblica em 2014. Quanto custaria a liquidao? Uma estimativa difcil, num banco desta dimenso. 14 mil milhes de euros seria o custo imediato e direto, a que acresceriam os custos diretos para o sistema de garantia de depsitos e os custos indiretos para o resto do sistema bancrio. Sem a venda do ativo subjacente ao emprstimo feito ao FdR, este era mais um NPL na economia portuguesa. Mas no apenas mais um NPL, seria o gerador de todos os incumprimentos, que arrastaria toda a banca com ele. O prolongamento do perodo de venda foi, naturalmente, negociado com a autoridade de concorrncia europeia, implicando um reforo dos compromissos, perante os sinais de dificuldade que o sistema financeiro apresentava e a falta de credibilidade existente. Foi assim que, entre finais de 2015 e outubro de 2017, foi feita a resoluo do BANIF. A CGD foi capitalizada, pelo seu nico acionista, o Estado Portugus. O FdR se tornou solvente. E dois dos maiores bancos privados portugueses encontraram capital para estabilizar a respetiva estrutura acionista. E foi tambm assim que se promoveu a venda do NB em 2017 e o crdito malparado e em risco de incumprimento comeou a descer em 2016, atingindo hoje um valor inferior a 5%, quase 4 vezes inferior aos valores de ento. Apenas estas aes concertadas e coordenadas entre as autoridades europeias e nacionais permitiu dar um futuro  banca nacional. S assim foi possvel melhorar a classificao da dvida soberana portuguesa. S assim foi possvel que Portugal sasse do Procedimento por Dfices Excessivos em que se encontrava h quase 10 anos. A venda de um banco de transio, como o NB, no foi uma venda de uma qualquer propriedade, que se no se vende hoje vende-se amanh. Este apelo  procrastinao chama-se azar em finanas. Foi a capacidade de cumprir os compromissos que permite s nossas empresas terem hoje acesso ao maior mercado de bens e servios do mundo e financiar-se a taxas de juro iguais s das demais empresas europeias. A nacionalizao de uma instituio financeira no  o mesmo que a nacionalizao de uma empresa industrial. J nos esquecemos da nacionalizao do BPN? J nos esquecemos de quanto ela custou e ainda hoje custa? A resoluo bancria  o mecanismo que permite garantir que os custos com a interveno no sistema bancrio seguem o principio da neutralidade oramental e protegem os contribuintes. Este ano, os 27 pases da Unio Europeia ratificaram uma alterao ao Tratado do Mecanismo Europeu de Estabilidade que garante a neutralidade oramental (a mdio/longo prazo) sempre que o MEE tenha que financiar a resoluo de bancos na Unio Europeia. E garante-o da mesma forma como o FdR assegurou o financiamento da resoluo do BES, com emprstimos dos bancos e do Tesouro. A venda do NB resulta de um imperativo legal, foi a forma encontrada, difcil, com riscos para o FdR, no quadro do funcionamento de um mecanismo contingente de capital. Este mecanismo evitou que o seu limite de atuao, 3890 milhes de euros, fossem registados imediatamente nas contas pblicas em 2017. Porque no se trata de uma garantia. Este mecanismo permitiu uma monitorizao apertada e eficaz dos processos de gesto dos ativos que nele esto includos. Permite que estes riscos se diluam ao longo do tempo e desde 2018 nos tenhamos confrontado com o seu valor e com uma realidade: o Novo Banco era novo, mas herdeiro de velhos problemas e com muitos e complexos desafios pela sua frente. No era um banco bom. Foi preciso fazer dele um bom banco. E a sua reestruturao termina este ano. Atestada pela Comisso Europeia. Assim as instituies portuguesas o permitam. Termino, relembrando o que  mais importante nesta fase. Entender que o Novo Banco  uma instituio de referncia no espao bancrio nacional. Que  o banco preferido por milhes de famlias e empresas para depositar as suas poupanas e para obter financiamento, para investir, inovar e criar emprego de qualidade. Lembremo-nos de que amide, quando dizemos NB, queremos dizer legado do BES. E claro, nunca percamos de vista a exigncia que hoje, e de modo to acrescido e desafiante, tem mesmo que recair sobre a banca nacional. A de apoiar a economia nacional, de fazer face s suas obrigaes para com o FdR, de no permitir que se repitam perodos como os que vivemos h uma dcada e que determinaram a resoluo do BES. Muito obrigado.

Title: Speech by Administrator Luis Laginha de Sousa at the Conference "Sustainable financing: new developments" organised under the Portuguese Presidency of the Council of the EU (English only)
text: Intervencao do Administrador Luis Laginha de Sousa na Conferencia "Financiamento sustentavel: novos desenvolvimentos" organizada no ambito da Presidencia Portuguesa do Conselho da UE (apenas em ingles) 25 mai. 2021 Roundtable: Green Bank in Portugal  challenges and the real impact on the national economy I would like to start by thanking the organisation for the kind invitation to participate in this Conference. Addressing a topic that is probably one of the few capable of challenging the position of the pandemic in terms of relevance is an invitation which cannot be refused. I would also like to salute my fellow participants in this roundtable. It is truly a great pleasure to be here. Not just because being and talking among people, instead of being behind the screen, brings back a sense of normality. But also because I very much welcome this opportunity to address the critical issues of sustainable finance and climate change --as seen from the lenses of the Central Bank. I trust we will be able to provide some interesting insights into the risks and opportunities we all face in this common goal of moving forward towards a more sustainable future. In order to stay in sync with the rules of effective and efficient communication, I will try to emphasise four key messages, in a very synthetic way, in this initial address. These four key messages cover: Acknowledgement; Green recovery; Roles; and Mechanisms. Depending on how our debate evolves, I hope to be able either to cover additional topics or to go a little deeper on those already covered. Particularly in what relates to how the financial system and Banco de Portugal can provide a contribution on this common challenge of sustainability. To start with, my first point is to clearly state that Banco de Portugal, in its role as Central Bank of the Portuguese Republic, acknowledges the national and global relevance of sustainability issues. This means that Environmental, Social and Governance issues must be regarded as relevant for both the world economy and the Portuguese economy. We also recognise that climate change is a global risk that calls for global cooperation and solutions. And we believe that urgent, coordinated and determined action, on a global scale, is key to cope with the economic and social impacts which are laying ahead of us. We also know that these impacts  apart from potentially taking the form of cliff effects rather than materialising in a linear way  are deemed to be broad, deep and largely irreversible. My second point is related to the so called green recovery. Before saying anything else, and for the sake of clarity, let me just add that, as a Central Bank, we do not dispute the scientific claim that we need to move towards a carbon neutral, or even negative, economic model. Having this in mind, what I would like to emphasise in this second point is that if Science is right about the importance of moving towards a carbon neutral or even carbon negative economic model, then the critical importance of climate change and other longterm sustainability issues cannot be pushed aside by the urgency of the pandemic crisis. There is a growing consensus being formed around the notion that Covid-19 has had a huge short term symmetric impact, but it will ultimately lead to asymmetric outcomes, as the crisis follows its course. And the consensus is also growing around the group of those that underscore the synergies between the need to crawl back from the current crisis and the need to advance towards carbon neutrality. The notion of a green recovery has been, by now, repeatedly stressed --and that notion has a lot of fertile ground to be encouraged and deepened. This takes me to my third point, which has to do with the Roles that each agent needs to perform on the path towards a greener and more sustainable future. And I start by stating something that has become increasingly obvious: if we are to succeed in the collective endeavour to mitigate and adapt to climate change, then the entire society must contribute. Corporations, consumers, NGOs, the scientific community  they all have a role to play. And since all  means all  that is also certainly the case of the financial sector and central banks. But we cannot forget that the root cause of climate change is what can probably be considered as the largest mispricing phenomenon that mankind has ever witnessed. And if we believe that were dealing with an economic problem known as a negative externality, then we have to conclude that climate change must be tackled, first and foremost, by political authorities. They are the ones with the legitimacy and control over the most effective instruments to deal with the root of the problem. Coming to my fourth and last point, it addresses the mechanisms which are more likely to produce the desired outcome, in terms of economic agents behaviour. And the view we have is that climate policy is more efficient if it builds on market mechanisms. Naturally, this statement comes with a caveat: such mechanisms must be allowed to operate in an open and competitive way. Which in turn requires preserving a level playing field. If we look at recent developments regarding the European Unions emissions trading system, they can be seen as a good example. The price of carbon allowances in the ETS market has been hitting consecutive records since late 2020. It rose above 56 euro per tonne last week, which compares with 23 euro per tonne at the beginning of the rally, and less than 8 euro per tonne in early 2018. This trend follows the announcement, by European Union leaders, that they will now aim for a 55% reduction in GHG emissions by 2030, compared to 1990. The previous target was 40%, and this increased ambition seems to have been perceived has an indication that carbon permits will become scarcer  and therefore more valuable. Price effectively paid is one of the most powerful, if not the most powerful, influencers of economic agents behaviour. Choosing mechanisms that allow the true cost of products and activities to be reflected in their price, which includes their respective negative externalities, is clearly, whenever possible, the best option to consider. There is, of course, much more to be said about this, but I will stop here, in order not to exceed the time that was allocated to these initial remarks.

Title: Intervention of Administrator Luis Laginha de Sousa at the ISCTE Conference - "Research for Sustainability": "Research for Sustainability - The perspective of a Central Bank"
text: Media Public Interventions See all Intervention of Administrator Luis L... Intervention of Administrator Luis Laginha de Sousa at the ISCTE Conference -"Research for Sustainability": "Research for Sustainability - The perspective of a Central Bank" 25 May. 2021 Framing Good morning, everyone. I thank ISCTE for the invitation to be here today and I greet my panelists. It is a huge pleasure to participate in this debate dedicated to research for sustainability. Even when the theme of sustainability is mediatically drowned out by the pandemic, as has been the case for about a year and a half, it remains absolutely unavoidable and without the minimally pinched relevance. And there are several characteristics that make sustainability unavoidable: its profound timeliness; their criticality to our collective future; its scope; and also its complexity. Something that combines all these characteristics, could not fail to question an entity like Banco de Portugal that, as central bank of the Portuguese Republic, has devoted increasing attention to this theme, because it intersects with several areas of its activity. The title of this panel also includes a word which is often, I would say too often, too much, to owe of discussions on sustainability: it is the word "research". It is a word that means a lot to an entity like Banco de Portugal, and so it is also with special satisfaction that I am here to try to share, even synthetically, the perspective with which Banco de Portugal approaches this theme On a subject which, as I have said, is so vast and complex, I will narrow the angle of approach. For this, I will help myself from three dimensions, signaling in each one the focus of my intervention. The first dimension is the concept of sustainability. The acronym ESG places the emphasis on the environmental, social and government components of organizations and has established itself as the dominant concept of sustainability in the universe of public policies, companies and investors. From the perspective of a central bank and financial supervisor, the environmental aspect of sustainability is particularly relevant, and that is why I bring to share with you. This is because environmental risks associated with phenomena such as climate change or biodiversity loss are an important source of financial risk. The second dimension of which should be limited relates to the nature of research. I will only refer to applied research, because it is the one that predominates in a central bank. This does not mean a lesser regard for fundamental research, which is closer to academia, nor in relation to research and development, which is closer to public policies and the business world. These are also of the utmost importance, but my panelists are certainly more empowered to talk about them. In relation to the third dimension, I will not invoke areas of knowledge other than those in the field of economy and finance, because this is where Banco de Portugal operates. It is not difficult to recognize that on ecology, meteorology and many other scientific fields relevant to the environment, little or nothing would have to add. In a statement, I will focus my intervention on research, of an applied nature, related to the economic and financial implications of environmental risks. And within this framework, I will address two aspects: First, I will try to explain the contact points between the sustainability and the mandate of Banco de Portugal; And secondly, I'm going to share some notes on the role that research can play. For this, I will use some examples of projects that we have development at Banco de Portugal. 1. Environmental sustainability and the mandate of Banco de Portugal Entering the first aspect, on the points of contact between environmental sustainability and the mandate of Banco de Portugal, it can be said that climate change enters our concerns "through the main door". This is because it has become clear for some years now that climate change has a direct impact on our mandate, specifically in the task of safeguarding the stability of the financial system. This direct link with the central bank's mandate results from climate change being an important source of risk for financial institutions, be they banks, insurers or asset and pension fund managers. This source of risk is associated with two major types of risk: On the one hand, we have so-called physical risks related to disasters such as droughts, floods, fires and hurricanes, which are increasingly recurrent and intense, and also with long-term processes, such as rising ocean levels, or the change in precipitation patterns. These phenomena destroy or wear down assets that have been financed, or that are used as collateral, by the banking system, or assets that are part of the portfolios of investment funds, or which are covered by the insurance companies. On the other hand, we have so-called transition risks related to the adjustment of the economy to decarbonisation. This adjustment stems, for example, from change in taxation or environmental protection regulations and the fact that these changes could impact less environmentally friendly companies. Can also result from the increase in legal litigation associated with the change in the framework, or result simply from changing the preferences of consumers, who are now much more attentive to the harms of over-emission carbon dioxide. And all this can happen in a nonlinear way, i.e., with the so-called cliff effects. If we do not identify, assess and adequately mitigate both physical and transition risks, climate change becomes a threat to financial stability. Banco de Portugal has in its mandate the responsibility both for safeguarding the stability of the financial system and for banking supervision. It is therefore responsible for promoting the resilience of the financial sector throughout the transition process that is being triggered by policies to combat climate change. Moreover, when we talk about impacts generated by climate change, or generated by biodiversity loss and the policies of adaptation and mitigation of these phenomena, it is not only at the level of the mission to safeguard the stability of the financial system that these impacts are felt in Banco de Portugal. All this is likely to impact, in a materially relevant way, variables such as credit or supply and aggregate demand for goods and services and, in this way, influence factors such as the natural interest rate, the transmission of monetary policy and the price formation mechanism itself. This results in a direct link to another component of Banco de Portugal's mandate: it is the responsibility for defining and conducting monetary policy in the euro area. Although it is a shared responsibility with the other central banks in the euro area and the ECB, it cannot be ruled out. Intervening properly in the fulfilment of our mandate means fully understanding how climate change could affect the Eurosystem's ability to achieve its primary objective of maintaining price stability. 2. What role for (central bank) research? After the link between the theme of climate change and the mandates of central banks, in this case Banco de Portugal, the question that follows, taking into account the theme of the Panel is: what this has to do with research and, in particular, with research, of an applied nature and focused on the areas of economy and finance, typically carried out by a central bank? The answer is simple, and without doubt: it is all about, in that it is research that sustains the development of theoretical models and empirical applications that support the definition of policies. Just as a good diagnosis is essential to define appropriate therapy when we are affected by a health problem, also in relation to the financial system and the economy we need, first of all, to understand the implications of environmental risks and transition policies for: cyclical and structural evolution of the economy; the financial system; and the conduct of monetary policy. We then need to incorporate climate and environmental factors into our forecasting and economic analysis models. Finally, we need to improve the macro and micro prudential supervision model, with a dual objective: On the one hand, promoting the resilience of the financial system  if it is true that the ideal is avoid shocks, this is not always possible and therefore the second best option, which is often the first and only, is to ensure that the financial system as a whole, it can absorb and digest shock while still performing its functions; On the other hand, it is important to encourage financial institutions to make progress in identification, measurement and mitigation of the climatic and environmental risks to which they are, subject, in the medium and long term horizon. For all these purposes, research is an absolutely critical component, and this criticism has been recognized in Banco de Portugal's approach to environmental sustainability and sustainable financing: the theme has been part of the Bank's scientific activity for some years, and has gained relevance and scope. Therefore, with regard to 'Research', I would like to address in particular three components. The first component - in the field of economic modelling, to mention, without going into detail, two ongoing projects involving researchers from Banco de Portugal: A project that models the transition to a global economy based on renewable energy [1]; And another that develops an economic model to estimate the effects, in different sectors of activity and between countries, climate change mitigation policies [2]. The path will, of course, be to make "mainstream" the inclusion of climate variables in the climate and forecast models, so that their macroeconomic impacts can be properly considered in the analyses we make. The second component of research is more empirical and support for policy formulation. We first assessed the exposure of the Portuguese to the sectors of activity most sensitive to the transition to a low-carbon economy. The preliminary results of this study, which we will release in the coming months, suggest that more than 60% of bank exposures to non-financial corporations are in sectors relevant to climate policy. We also plan to start later this year a work of modeling credit risk parameters that integrates variables related to climate change for the purpose of scenario analysis. Another work, which is being completed and disseminating in the second half of the year, systematises existing knowledge on the geophysical, technological and economic aspects of climate change and on economic policies aimed at mitigating its effects, with a focus on the Portuguese. At international level, we have participated in the ongoing work at the European Central Bank on the implications of climate change for the conduct of monetary policy. This work is part of the review of the monetary policy strategy, which is expected to be completed in the second half of this year. We also contribute to the work of NGFS -Network of Central Banks and Supervisors for Greening the Financial System, which has been taking on itself as an international benchmark. NGFS, since it was launched and as far as research is concerned, has placed particular emphasis on aspects such as the development of climate scenarios and the possible identification of a climate-based risk differential. More recently, the study of biodiversity loss and the resulting economic and financial implications has gained prominence. A final note to highlight the work on a project coordinated by the Portuguese Environment Agency to assess the vulnerability of the national territory to climate change in the 21st century. The results should be presented by the end of 2023. It is a project that aims to support the formulation of public policies to adapt to climate change and the energy transition, for different sectors of activity and levels of territorial intervention. Banco de Portugal has the responsibility to assess the effects of climate change and its mitigation measures on variables such as gross domestic product, consumption, investment and employment. The third and final research component I would like to highlight is the critical importance of the data. If research is instrumental to our mission, the data is instrumental in research. I cannot therefore conclude without a brief reference to the critical importance of the data, which has also already been referred to as 21st century oil (we'll probably have to change this characteristic to something greener!). To understand the interaction between climate change and the economy and thus sustain policy making, it is crucial that public and private entities dissemine climate data. This is especially important for climate scientists in understanding and simulating trajectories, which often serve as input to the models that economists use in the elaboration of scenarios. This is where the mission of BPLIM, the Microdata Research Laboratory of Banco de Portugal, is part of the mission of The Bank of Portugal, which provides advanced support to internal and external researchers in the use of Portuguese microdata. BPLIM is studying the possibility of including temperature and precipitation data with a fine geographical location. By crossing this type of data with companies and their location, it will be possible to carry out studies with local emphasis on the interactions between climate and business activity. Having information available, of quality and comparable is also a necessary condition for each financial institution to make an appropriate assessment, management and recovery of climate and environmental risks. To that extent, it is also a critical factor in driving the transition to a greener economy. For this reason, Banco de Portugal is also committed to contributing, within its mandate, to the international efforts to develop climate information reports that are complete, useful, consistent and comparable. Final Notes In conclusion, and because the intervention is already longer than desirable, although shorter than the subject requires, I would like to emphasize that the construction of scientific knowledge on a subject as vast as climate change, and including its consequences for all economic agents, is a process that will accompany us throughout the future that we have managed to include. I tried to show that an research agenda that integrates the concerns that result from the interaction between environmental sustainability and the financial system or monetary policy is instrumental in fulfilling the central bank's mission. We will therefore continue to allocate resources to the rigorous study of the impacts of climate change, with the aim of advising the Portuguese authorities and serving the public interested in this issue that can only be seen as crucial for the future of the country. We hope, and hope, that these studies will be positive contributions to 'fact-based decisions' and desirably 'good fact-based decisions'. Very obrigado.
