A maior parte das contraordenaes foi sendo validada pelos tribunais de primeira instncia, da Relao, do Constitucional, disse. Estou muito  vontade, porque do ponto de vista dos processos conduzidos pelo BdP, os resultados tm sido extremamente positivos, declarou o nmero dois do supervisor. Para Mximo dos Santos, pode haver problemas legislativos que tm de ser vistos para evitar estes casos. No embarco no discurso de que h garantias a mais para os arguidos. Agora, h uso abusivo delas, no h dvida nenhuma, afirma, sem contudo querer dizer o que poderia mudar. Temos o dever, todos, reguladores, tribunais, Procuradoria, poder poltico, de nos organizar de modo a que os objetivos da comunidade sejam atingidos.  evidente que nem sempre  fcil. J passei pelo BPP, pelo BES mau, nunca alardeei espritos justicialistas, porque no  justia. Ns queremos fazer a justia do Estado de direito democrtico. O que se verifica  que, infelizmente, por vezes, esse objetivo acaba por se perder e isso  que no pode acontecer, conclui. Havendo a dissoluo do Parlamento, e sendo este um diploma que tinha de ser sob a forma de proposta de lei, teremos de aguardar pelo novo Parlamento. O que queria deixar claro  o seguinte: seja qual for o Governo, a composio do Parlamento, eu tenho a certeza que o Cdigo da Atividade Bancria (CAB) no vai ser deixado para trs. No  pelo facto de ser atravs dele que se procede  transposio de diretivas;  porque o CAB  mesmo necessrio. No temos uma reforma profunda na legislao do sistema financeiro desde 1992. A convico  de Lus Mximo dos Santos, o vice-governador do Banco de Portugal, que est por trs da proposta de uma nova legislao para o sector da banca. O dossi passou por uma consulta pblica, foi apresentado ao Ministrio das Finanas em abril, mas, com a queda da Assembleia da Repblica (AR) e consequente fim do Governo, no vai seguir em frente. O Banco de Portugal (BdP) props este novo Cdigo porque a legislao atual  uma manta de retalhos absolutamente contrria a todas as boas regras da legstica, e inclusivamente no foi atualizado face ao surgimento do Mecanismo nico de Superviso, em 2014. Para Mximo dos Santos, no  s a sigla  RGICSF, de Regime Geral das Instituies de Crdito e Sociedades Financeiras  que precisa de mudar. Isso no vai estar, creio eu, minimamente em questo, porque  uma necessidade. Seja quem for que v constituir o prximo Governo vai olhar com todo o interesse para o trabalho que o BdP fez, acredita. As reformas das coisas no se fazem atravs da legislao, mas muitas vezes fazem-se com ela.  daqueles casos em que uma nova legislao  absolutamente indispensvel, considera Mximo dos Santos. E se um prximo Governo no a considerar essencial? Teremos uma legislao num sector crucial com uma qualidade muito deficiente, e com problemas diversssimos. Houve desinteresse do Ministrio das Finanas? Temos de reconhecer que  uma alterao complexa e ambiciosa, e h prioridades, e muita coisa a fazer. Na estrutura da superviso tambm  necessrio fazer mudanas, nomeadamente no que diz respeito ao Conselho Nacional de Supervisores Financeiros (CNSF), que agrega os trs supervisores financeiros: Banco de Portugal, CMVM e ASF. Foi criado em 2000, teve umas alteraes em 2008, 2013, 2015, mas que so de pormenor, com tudo o que entretanto aconteceu,  um rgo que pode ser potenciado. Tem de ser ajustado ao novo formato, aos novos tempos que estamos a viver, acredita. Por exemplo, problematiza Mximo dos Santos, o BdP tem direito a dois participantes, o governador e o membro da administrao com o pelouro da superviso, mas no especifica que tipo de superviso, se prudencial, se comportamental, se do branqueamento de capitais, reas que no existiam, com esta diviso, aquando da sua constituio.  um rgo muitssimo importante, mas precisa de ser revisto em vrios nveis, em funo da evoluo que o sistema financeiro teve, continua, referindo, por exemplo, o trabalho que tem sido feito na promoo da literacia financeira. Mximo dos Santos foi nomeado administrador em 2016, subiu a vice-governador um ano depois e tem mandato at setembro de 2022. Sobre uma reconduo no cargo, no respondeu, j que a competncia ser do Governo. O vice-governador  favorvel a um s mandato, mais extenso, mas sem renovao, para que a reconduo no dependa de uma escolha poltica.

Title: Article by Administrator Hlder Rosalino on the Express: "Digital Coins  the space race (monetary) of the 21st century"
text: Article by Administrator Helder Rosalino on the Express: "Digital Coins  the space race (monetary) of the 21st century" 13 Dec. 2021 The way we make payments has undergone profound changes in recent years, as a result of the emergence and dissemination of new technologies and consumer preference for more convenient, fast and cheaper payments. Concepts suchas d istributed ledger technology/DLT, blockchain, cryptoactives, bitcoins, stablecoins and Central Bank Digital Currency accentuate the idea that the global payment ecosystem and traditional forms of money issuance are changing rapidly. A new reality is emerging and could confront the digital currencies issued by central banks and so-called virtual private currencies (decentralized crypto currencies). When Bitcoin, the best known of the cri ptoativos, appeared in 2008, central banks in several countries issued warnings to consumers, underlining the risks associated with their detention and use. These risks, which persist, may involve the partial or total loss of funds (for lack of legal protection conferring repayment rights); result of fraudulent action on trading platforms; or simply stem from its high volatility and the impossibility of converting to fiat currency with legal course. For central banks, criptoativos are not real currencies, because they do not simultaneously fulfill the three functions of a currency: value reserve, unit of account and means of payment. As they do not have behind a legal obligation or an entity that guarantees them are, as a rule, very volatile. As a way to reduce this volatility, stablecoins emerged, based on solutions offered by major technology companies that advertise them as a way to overcome some of the constraints of traditional payment solutions, especially in internationalt ransacoes. This type of cryptoassets seeks to ensure the stability of their value association with a reference basket composed of stable assets or currencies. The increasing use of cryptoassets may conditionsome of the central bank's main tasks: preserving financial stability, maintaining price stability and promoting the proper functioning of payment systems. Therefore, since 2016, the discussion around Central Bank Digital Currencies has intensified, as a response of monetary authorities to the growing use of cryptoassets. In October 2020, the European Central Bank (ECB) published a report on the possible issuance of a digital euro area central bank currency, in which it assumes that the issue of the digital euro may be necessary, among other scenarios, by the threat of the emergence of another form of currency that becomes a credible alternative to the euro (as a means of exchange and reserve of value). The threat could come both from a Digital Currency of the Central Bank from another authority that wants to impose itself on the monetary space (China has already begun large-scale testing with the digital Yuan) and from a private initiative, the stablecoin type, that is a global dimension. If it is issued , the digital Euro will be the digital currency of the Eurosystem, made available to individuals and businesses for use in retail payments. The big difference from cryptoassets is that it will have legal status, i.e. it will be accepted as a means of payment throughout the euro area. It will be a way for citizens to continue to have access to central bank currency in an environment where there is a growing preference for more digital means of payment. Paradoxically, central banks hope that theirdigital currencies will succeed, but at the same time admit to preventing their overuse, as such behaviour could lead to financial deintermediation (of commercial banks) and the replacement of private payment solutions. Several mechanismsare in place to mitigate the risk of financial deintermediation, such as imposing a value limit for retail payments with central bank digital currency or simply for their detention, or the definition of a system of remuning actionin tiers. The following questions can then be asked. If central banks limit the use of their digital currencies, how can these currencies be considered by consumers to be genuine currencies? Willcentral b anco digital currencies, with more restricted features, be attractive enough to consumers and respond to the needs that lead them to the increasing use of cryptoassets and stablecoins? There are two seemingly contradictory perspectives that are at their core: central banks and consumers. For central banks (at least, for most), the only way to minimize the impacts of central bank issuing of the digital currency on financial stability and the transmission of monetary policy, and not to exclude private initiative from such a strategic and disruptive project, is to take these mechanisms into account. In turn, as the increasing use of cryptoassets demonstrates, the preferred instrumentas a means of paying in a virtual reality, is not necessarily what best serves as a reserve of value. Consumers will be receptive to the digital Euro, which will have reliability and no risk intrinsically guaranteed, if this currency provides them witha speed-free payment experience, fast and with low costs, whether in the real world or in the virtual world. Regardless of all the ongoing discussions on a possible digital Euro, there is something unquestionable: the most important condition for successful payment will beconsumer support.
text_original: Artigo do Administrador Hlder Rosalino no Expresso: "Moedas Digitais  a corrida espacial (monetria) do sculo XXI" 13 dez. 2021 O modo como realizamos pagamentos tem sofrido alteraes profundas nos ltimos anos, fruto do aparecimento e disseminao de novas tecnologias e da preferncia dos consumidores por meios de pagamentos mais convenientes, rpidos e baratos. Conceitos como distributed ledger technology/DLT, blockchain, criptoativos, bitcoins, stablecoins e Moeda Digital de Banco Central acentuam a ideia de que o ecossistema global de pagamentos e as tradicionais formas de emisso monetria esto a mudar rapidamente. Uma nova realidade est a emergir e poder colocar em confronto as moedas digitais emitidas pelos bancos centrais e as chamadas moedas virtuais privadas (criptoativos com funcionamento descentralizado). Quando, em 2008, apareceu a Bitcoin, o mais conhecido dos criptoativos, bancos centrais de vrios pases emitiram alertas aos consumidores, sublinhando os riscos associados  sua deteno e utilizao. Esses riscos, que persistem, podem envolver a perda parcial ou total de fundos (por ausncia de proteo legal que confira direitos de reembolso); resultar de atuao fraudulenta sobre as plataformas de negociao; ou simplesmente decorrer da sua elevada volatilidade e da impossibilidade de converso para moeda fiduciria com curso legal. Para os bancos centrais, os criptoativos no so verdadeiras moedas, porque no cumprem, em simultneo, as trs funes de uma moeda: reserva de valor, unidade de conta e meio de pagamento. Como no tm por trs uma obrigao legal ou uma entidade que os garanta so, por norma, muito volteis. Como forma de reduzir essa volatilidade, surgiram as stablecoins, assentes em solues oferecidas por grandes tecnolgicas que as publicitam como forma de superar alguns dos constrangimentos das solues de pagamento tradicionais, sobretudo em transaes internacionais. Este tipo de criptoativos procura garantir a estabilidade do seu valor atravs da associao a um cabaz de referncia composto por ativos ou moedas estveis. A utilizao crescente de criptoativos pode condicionar algumas das principais misses dos bancos centrais: a preservao da estabilidade financeira, a manuteno da estabilidade de preos e a promoo do bom funcionamento dos sistemas de pagamentos. Por isso, a partir de 2016, intensificou-se a discusso em torno das Moedas Digitais de Banco Central, como resposta das autoridades monetrias  crescente utilizao de criptoativos. O Banco Central Europeu (BCE) publicou, em outubro de 2020, um relatrio sobre a possvel emisso de uma moeda digital de banco central da rea do euro, em que assume que a emisso do Euro digital pode ser necessria, entre outros cenrios, pela ameaa do surgimento de outra forma de moeda que se torne uma alternativa credvel ao euro (como meio de troca e reserva de valor). A ameaa pode vir tanto de uma Moeda Digital de Banco Central de outra autoridade que se queira impor no espao monetrio (a China j iniciou testes em grande escala com o Yuan digital) como de uma iniciativa privada, do tipo stablecoin, que assuma dimenso global. Se vier a ser emitido, o Euro digital ser a moeda digital do Eurosistema, disponibilizada a particulares e empresas para utilizao nos pagamentos de retalho. A grande diferena face aos criptoativos  que ter curso legal, ou seja, ser aceite como meio de pagamento em toda a rea do euro. Ser uma forma de os cidados continuarem a ter acesso a moeda de banco central num ambiente em que existe uma crescente preferncia por meios de pagamento mais digitais. Paradoxalmente, os bancos centrais anseiam que as suas moedas digitais tenham sucesso, mas, em simultneo, admitem impedir o seu uso excessivo, na medida em que tal comportamento poderia levar a uma desintermediao financeira (dos bancos comerciais) e  substituio de solues privadas de pagamentos. Esto em discusso vrios mecanismos para mitigar o risco de desintermediao financeira, como a imposio de um limite de valor para pagamentos de retalho com moeda digital de banco central ou simplesmente para a sua deteno, ou a definio de um sistema de remunerao em escales. Podem ento colocar-se as seguintes questes. Se os bancos centrais limitarem a utilizao das suas moedas digitais como podero estas moedas serem consideradas, pelos consumidores, verdadeiras moedas? Conseguiro as moedas digitais de banco central, com funcionalidades mais restritas, ser suficientemente atrativas para os consumidores e responder s necessidades que os levam  crescente utilizao de criptoativos e stablecoins? Existem duas perspetivas, aparentemente contraditrias, que confluem na sua essncia: a dos bancos centrais e a dos consumidores. Para os bancos centrais (pelo menos, para a maioria), a nica forma de minimizar os impactos da emisso da moeda digital de banco central na estabilidade financeira e na transmisso da poltica monetria, e de no excluir a iniciativa privada de um projeto to estratgico e disruptivo,  ter esses mecanismos em considerao. Por sua vez, como demonstra a crescente utilizao de criptoativos, o instrumento preferido como meio de pagamento numa realidade virtual, no  necessariamente o que melhor serve como reserva de valor. Os consumidores sero recetivos ao Euro digital, que ter confiabilidade e ausncia de risco intrinsecamente garantidos, se esta moeda lhes propiciar uma experincia de pagamento sem frices, rpida e com baixos custos, seja no mundo real, seja no mundo virtual. Independentemente de todas as discusses em curso sobre um eventual Euro digital, existe algo inquestionvel: a condio mais importante para o sucesso deste novo instrumento de pagamento ser a adeso dos consumidores.

Title: Intervention of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, at the launch of the book "The Bank of Lisbon and the Liberal Revolution of 1820" by Jos Luis Cardoso
text: Compatible... Intervention of the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, at the launch of the book "The Bank of Lisbon and the Liberal Revolution of 1820" by Jose Luis Cardoso 13 Dec. 2021 Mr. Governor, Dear Colleagues of the Board of Directors, Senhor Professor Jose Luis Cardoso, Madam Professor Maria Eugenia Mata, Distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, This morning's session is the corollary of a project launched a few years ago by Professor Jose Luis Cardoso and his team from the Institute of Social Sciences of the University of Lisbon, a project that Banco de Portugal has associated with providing its Historical Archive and promoting and sponsoring the edition of the book that is presented today. It is a day of rejoicing, because I believe that we will all agree to consider that the final result of this research and editing project  the book "The Bank of Lisbon and the Liberal Revolution of 1820"  proved entirely achieved. I will not exactly talk about the work itself, because for this  in addition, of course, to its own author  we invited Professor Maria Eugenia Mata, who with her deep knowledge in the field of economic history and the history of economic thought will do so with greater benefit. I would, however, like to take thisopportunity to leave some reflections which i think are appropriate. Firstly, to stress that it is a huge pleasure for me to participate in this session, right from the outset because it is an event that goes beyond the typical activity as Deputy Governor of banco de Portugal, but that it does not fail to be part of one of the objectives of the Institution: to support the realization of studies that allow to keep alive the memory of the evolution of the Portuguese and the economic and financial life of the country in general. Like several other works that Banco de Portugal has already published, of which i would cite, by way of example, the Collection of Classic Works of Economic Thought Portuguese, then in partnership with the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation, also coordinated by Professor Jose Luis Cardoso, this book dixa a legacy and, like all good legacies, will certainly be an inspiring source for many other studies. Another point I would like to highlight is the fact that we are gathered here to participate in the launch of a book on a bank created noless than two hundred years ago, which was the first Portuguese bank in the modern sense of the term, and which is inextricably linked to the Liberal Revolution of 1820, which seems to demonstrate two things: (i) The emergence and importance of the banking sectoris inseparable from modernity economic; (ii) The link between banking and politics has existed since its inception. One of the most interesting aspects of the book is, moreover, that of bringing to light the debates in the Constituent Courts on theneed to create a bank (the author speaks even in "urgency") and about the different projects that have been presented for this purpose. The discussions in the Courts are very revealing of how the country was already struggling with some of the problems that, unfortunately, still plague it today, as is the case of public debt. And, more generally, how this was a very intense and defining time of what would become every nineteenth century, in which Portugal could not take the train of industrialization and set the pace with many of the main European countries. It also seems to me that the evocation of the creation of the Bank of Lisbon two hundred years ago and its significance in this historical context is only possible or, at least, only wins all the sense, because overthe course of two centuries as a national community we have been able to maintain our political independence translated into a sovereign state, internationally recognized, by the way of the oldest at European level. It wasn't that, and it's legitimate to ask: who would be interestedtoday for this event? Would he even have a seat? This idea of national continuity and political continuity also largein the fact that Banco de Lisboa is an integral part of Banco de Portugal, formally enshrined in Article 102 of theConstitution of the Republic of 1976 as "the national central bank". In fact, Banco de Lisboa merged on November 19, 1846, with Companhia Confianca Nacional (a financial company) gave rise to Banco de Portugal and, to that extent, is part of its history, even if the thesis supported by Damiao Peres is not shared according to which the date on which Banco de Portugal was founded is december 31, 1821 (date of the creation of the Bank of Lisbon), for the reason that the reform of 1846 would not have created a new banking institution, despite the change it determined in its designation. Another aspect I would like to point out is the fact that the emphasis that Banco de Portugal has given in its editions to matters relating to economic history and the history of economic thought is not the result of chance, but rather the recognition of theneed to encourage a scientific area which, at some point, saw his space in the gym reduce excessively. With the increasing and strict submission of economic science to mathematical models, the fact that the economy is asocial science was lost, anchored, therefore, in behaviors influenced by multiple factors that start from concrete realities. The inability to predict the global financial crisis of 2008 and the "mistakes" publicly assumed by some majorinternal organizations have generated some disenchantment with certain over-reductive views of economic science. In recent years, attention to the behavioural dimension of the economic phenomenon has been on the way, and this is an unequivocal sign ofrichard thaler's award ing of the Nobel Prize for economics in 2017. And for a long time too, the importance of the institutional dimension for economic science has been recovered in different ways by prestigious authors. The debates we see today being resumed in the European Union and the United States, debates and policies that were thought to be lost in time, have emerged because global geopolitics has changed profoundly and rapidly and to its detriment. When China joined the World Organization in 2001, very few predicted that China would makeprogress as extraordinary and rapid as it actually made from an economic point of view. No one was prepared for this, and in a short time the economic competition was transmuted into a strategic competition, a struggle for international influence, in short, in a power struggle. With protagonists exchanged in relation to periods of British and then American rule, behind topics such as the now-called "reindustrialization" or the recovery of the concept of "industrial policy", so criticized in the 80s and 90s of the twentieth century, what is at stake are very old themes in the economic debate, with arguments that make us familiar with the discussions that were made in the 19th century between free trade advocates and policy supporters and policy supporters. Protectionist. By admitting that the specialisation of production chains worldwide may have gone too far, what is meant is that economic logic cannot be takenso far as to generate a dependency that compromises the strategic autonomy of the European or United States, that is, that, after all, globalisation has even limits and that some "deglobalization" may be inevitable. Citing U.S. Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen at a recent financial times conference, "it is possible that policies that people will describe as protectionist may be needed in order to create the right incentives to produce more internal." In this context, the concept of "national economic security" has all the conditions to become quite elastic and expansive, with much work being given to international trade experts ininterpreting Article XXI of the G eral Agreement on Trade and Tariffs (GATT), which enshrines safety exceptions. It is therefore clear the importance of knowledge of economic history and the evolution of economic thinking so that we can further analyze theeco-nomic themes. For all this, I believe that this edition could not be more opportune: it marks the bicentenary of the Liberal Revolution and the Bank of Lisbon, it is part, as has already been said, in the plan of events commemorating the 175th anniversary of Banco de Portugal andreminds us how important this area of knowledge is. I would also like to stress that we will have an English edition of the book provided by a major UK publisher, thereby enhancing its international dissemination, and that another presentation session of the book will take place in the city of Porto on 11 January 2022. I end by congratulating Professor Jose Luis Cardoso for his work and also leaving a word of fair recognition and thanksto the various collaborators of Banco de Portugal, especially the Department of Support Services (DSA) and the Department of Communication and Museum (DCM), who contributed to make this edition a reality. Thank you so much for your attention.
text_original: Lu... Interveno do Vice-Governador, Lus Mximo dos Santos, no lanamento do livro O Banco de Lisboa e a Revoluo Liberal de 1820 de Jos Luis Cardoso 13 dez. 2021 Senhor Governador, Caros Colegas do Conselho de Administrao, Senhor Professor Jos Lus Cardoso, Senhora Professora Maria Eugnia Mata, Ilustres convidados, minhas Senhoras e meus Senhores, A sesso desta manh  o corolrio de um projeto lanado h alguns anos pelo Professor Jos Lus Cardoso e pela sua equipa do Instituto de Cincias Sociais da Universidade de Lisboa, projeto esse a que o Banco de Portugal se associou facultando o seu Arquivo Histrico e promovendo e patrocinando a edio do livro que hoje  apresentado.  um dia de regozijo, pois creio que todos estaremos de acordo em considerar que o resultado final desse projeto de investigao e edio  o livro O Banco de Lisboa e a Revoluo Liberal de 1820  se revelou inteiramente conseguido. No irei propriamente falar da obra em si, pois para isso  para alm, claro, do seu prprio autor  convidmos a Professora Maria Eugnia Mata, que com o seu profundo conhecimento no domnio da histria econmica e da historia do pensamento econmico o far com maior proveito. Gostaria, contudo, de aproveitar esta oportunidade para deixar algumas reflexes que se me afiguram oportunas. Em primeiro lugar, sublinhar que  um gosto enorme para mim participar nesta sesso, desde logo por se tratar de um evento que vai para alm da tpica atividade enquanto Vice-Governador do Banco de Portugal, mas que no deixa de se inserir num dos objetivos da Instituio: apoiar a realizao de estudos que permitam manter viva a memria da evoluo do sistema bancrio portugus e da vida econmica e financeira do Pas, em geral. Como vrias outras obras que o Banco de Portugal j editou, de que citaria, a ttulo de exemplo, a Coleo de Obras Clssicas do Pensamento Econmico Portugus, ento numa parceria com a Fundao Calouste Gulbenkian, tambm coordenada pelo Professor Jos Luis Cardoso, este livro deixa um legado e, como todos os bons legados, ser certamente uma fonte inspiradora para muitos outros estudos. Um outro ponto que gostaria de destacar  o facto de estarmos aqui reunidos a participar no lanamento de um livro relativo a um banco criado h nada menos do que duzentos anos, que foi o primeiro banco portugus no sentido moderno do termo, e que est indissociavelmente ligado  Revoluo Liberal de 1820, o que parece demonstrar duas coisas: (i) O surgimento e a importncia do setor bancrio so indissociveis da modernidade econmica; (ii) A ligao entre a banca e a poltica existe desde os primrdios sua criao. Um dos aspetos mais interessantes do livro , alis, o de trazer  luz do dia os debates nas Cortes Constituintes sobre a necessidade de criar um banco (o autor fala mesmo em urgncia) e sobre os diferentes projetos que foram apresentados para o efeito. As discusses nas Cortes so muito reveladoras de como j ento o Pas se debatia com alguns dos problemas que, infelizmente, ainda hoje o atormentam, como  o caso da dvida pblica. E, de uma forma mais geral, de como esse foi um tempo bastante intenso e definidor do que viria a ser todo sculo XIX, em que Portugal no conseguiu apanhar o comboio da industrializao e acertar o passo com muitos dos principais pases europeus. Afigura-se-me tambm que a evocao da criao, h duzentos anos, do Banco de Lisboa e do seu significado nesse contexto histrico s  possvel ou, pelo menos, s ganha todo o sentido, porque ao longo desses dois sculos enquanto comunidade nacional soubemos manter a nossa independncia poltica traduzida num Estado soberano, internacionalmente reconhecido, por sinal dos mais antigos a nvel europeu. No fora isso, e  legtimo perguntar: quem se interessaria hoje por este evento? Ser que ele teria sequer lugar? Essa ideia de continuidade nacional e poltica avulta tambm na circunstncia de o Banco de Lisboa ser parte integrante do Banco de Portugal, consagrado formalmente no artigo 102. da Constituio da Repblica de 1976 como o banco central nacional. Na verdade, o Banco de Lisboa ao fundir-se, em 19 de novembro de 1846, com a Companhia Confiana Nacional (uma sociedade financeira) deu origem ao Banco de Portugal e, nessa medida, faz parte da sua histria, mesmo que no se partilhe a tese sustentada por Damio Peres segundo a qual a data em que o Banco de Portugal foi fundado  a de 31 de dezembro de 1821 (data da criao do Banco de Lisboa), pela razo de que a reforma de 1846 no teria criado uma nova instituio bancaria, apesar da mudana que determinou na sua designao. Um outro aspeto que gostaria de assinalar  o facto de o relevo que o Banco de Portugal tem dado nas suas edies s matrias relativas  histria econmica e  histria do pensamento econmico no resultar de um acaso, mas sim do reconhecimento da necessidade de incentivar uma rea cientfica que, em dado momento, viu o seu espao na academia reduzir-se excessivamente. Com a crescente e estrita submisso da cincia econmica aos modelos matemticos foi-se perdendo de vista o facto de a economia ser uma cincia social, ancorada, portanto, em comportamentos influenciados por mltiplos fatores que arrancam de realidades concretas. A incapacidade para prever a crise financeira global de 2008 e os erros publicamente assumidos por algumas organizaes internacionais do maior relevo geraram algum desencanto com determinadas vises demasiado redutoras da cincia econmica. Nos ltimos anos, a ateno para a dimenso comportamental do fenmeno econmico tem vindo a fazer caminho, disso sendo sinal inequvoco a atribuio do Prmio Nobel da economia, em 2017, a Richard Thaler. E desde h muito que tambm a importncia da dimenso institucional para a cincia econmica tem sido recuperada, de formas diferentes, por autores de grande prestgio. Os debates que vemos hoje ser retomados na Unio Europeia e nos Estados Unidos, debates e polticas que se julgavam perdidos no tempo, emergiram porque a geopoltica mundial se alterou profunda e rapidamente e em seu prejuzo. Quando a China aderiu  Organizao Mundial do Comrcio, em 2001, muito poucos anteviram que esse pas fizesse progressos to extraordinrios e rpidos como aqueles que efetivamente fez do ponto de vista econmico. Ningum estava preparado para isso e, em pouco tempo, a competio econmica transmutou-se numa competio estratgica, numa luta pela influncia internacional, em suma, numa luta pelo poder. Com protagonistas trocados relativamente aos perodos de domnio britnico e, depois, americano, por detrs de temas como a agora denominada reindustrializao ou a recuperao do conceito de politica industrial, to criticado nos anos 80 e 90 do sculo XX, o que est em causa so temas bem antigos no debate econmico, com argumentos que nos tornam familiares as discusses havidas no sculo XIX entre os defensores do comrcio livre e os adeptos de polticas protecionistas. Ao admitir-se que a especializao das cadeias de produo a nvel mundial poder ter ido longe demais, o que se quer dizer  que a lgica econmica no pode ser levada to longe que gere uma dependncia que comprometa a autonomia estratgica do espao europeu ou dos Estados Unidos, ou seja, que, afinal, a globalizao tem mesmo limites e que alguma desglobalizao poder ser inevitvel. Citando a Secretria de Estado do Tesouro dos Estados Unidos, Janet Yellen, numa recente conferncia promovida pelo Financial Times,  possvel que sejam necessrias polticas que as pessoas descrevero como protecionistas, de maneira a criar os adequados incentivos para se produzir mais internamente. Neste contexto, o conceito de segurana econmica nacional tem todas as condies para se tornar bastante elstico e expansivo, antevendo-se muito trabalho para os especialistas em comrcio internacional na interpretao do Artigo XXI do Acordo Geral sobre Comrcio e Pautas Aduaneiras (GATT), que consagra as excees respeitantes  segurana. , pois, evidente a importncia do conhecimento da historia econmica e da evoluo do pensamento econmico para podermos aprofundar a anlise dos temas econmicos. Por tudo isto, creio que esta edio no poderia ser mais oportuna: assinala o bicentenrio da Revoluo Liberal e do Banco de Lisboa, inscreve-se, como j foi dito, no plano de eventos comemorativos dos 175 anos do Banco de Portugal e recorda-nos como  importante esta rea do conhecimento. Gostaria tambm de sublinhar que iremos ter uma edio em ingls do livro assegurada por uma grande editora do Reino Unido, desse modo potenciando a sua divulgao internacional, e que decorrer na cidade do Porto, no dia 11 de janeiro de 2022, uma outra sesso de apresentao do livro. Termino, felicitando o Senhor Professor Jos Lus Cardoso pelo trabalho realizado e deixando tambm uma palavra de justo reconhecimento e agradecimento aos diversos colaboradores do Banco de Portugal, em especial do Departamento de Servios Apoio (DSA) e do Departamento de Comunicao e Museu (DCM), que contriburam para tornar esta edio uma realidade. Muito obrigado pela vossa ateno.

Title: Article by the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, in the Jornal de Negcios: "In the 175 years of Banco de Portugal"
text: Article by the Deputy Governor, Luis Max... Article by the Deputy Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, in the Jornal de Negocios: "In the 175 years of Banco de Portugal" 21 Dec. 2021 On November 19, 1846, in an environment of profound economic, financial, social and political crisis, Banco de Portugal was created by royal decree, which resulted from the merger of Banco de Lisboa with Companhia Confianca Nacional, which was one of the measures taken to address the country's problems at the time. Banco de Lisboa was a commercial bank and issuer and was the first bank to Portuguese the modern sense of the term. Its creation, on December 31, 1821, is closely linked to the Liberal Revolution of 1820, as evidenced in a very interesting way in a book by Prof. Jose Luis Cardoso just edited by Banco de Portugal. The Companhia Confianca Nacional, founded in 1844, was a financial company specialized in financing public debt. Later, Banco de Portugal would gain the characteristics of central bank. Today the Constitution of the Republic refers to it, in Article 102, as "the national central bank", thus making it a constitutional body. As Prof. Jaime Reis points out [1], European central banks descend in direct line from banks with the privilege of issuing national credit systems during the 19th century and most emerged in the midst of severe monetary and financial crises, so the Portuguese route in this plan did not depart much from the European standard. On November 19 of this year, therefore, Banco de Portugal completed 175 years of existence. The history of Banco de Portugal is an important part of the economic, financial and political history of modern Portugal. This is a date with high symbolic charge, which has been marked with a set of events that will last until May 31, 2022. Institutions with this seniority are not very common, which gives the Bank of Portugal has a greater responsibility in the performance of its missions and in the expectations of the Portuguese. But antiquity, as they say, is not a post and alone solves nothing. It's supposed to bring a memory, a critical mass and an increased sense of responsibility. But it only becomes a real asset if in every historical moment it is up to the challenges that arise to it, to know how to evolve over time, in the organization and procedures, to demonstrate the dynamism indispensable to effectively and timely exercise its powers. There is vast economic and political literature that correlates the development of nations with the solidity and quality of their institutions. And many studies have pointed to the weakness of institutions in Portugal as a weakness of their development process. However, because of the importance of the tasks and powers that are assigned to it and that the legislator has been increasing in recent years (a fact that cannot be interpreted as a sign of the confidence it deserves), it is easy to conclude that banco de Portugal's performance is crucial for the country. Nationalized in 1974, Banco de Portugal was gaining in the following decades a growing role and accumulating functions: monetary and exchange rate authority, prudential supervision authority and behavioral supervision and fundamental entity for the economic and financial advice of governments, having played a key role in the two agreements with the International Monetary Fund. With the adoption of the euro in 1999, Banco de Portugal's functions changed but did not lose importance. Quite the contrary. In 2013, Banco de Portugal became a national macroprudential authority. From 2014, as the competent authority for prudential supervision (which had been since 1975), it became a member of the Single Supervisory Mechanism and, from 2016, as a national resolution authority, a member of the Single Resolution Mechanism. And how does the country see Banco de Portugal today? A Marktest study conducted in April 2021, based on 963 interviews conducted with a representative sample of the banked population residing in mainland Portugal, revealed that 63.8% of respondents consider the Bank a trusted institution; 60.3%, an institution with a positive impact on Portuguese society; 62.1%, which guarantees the stability of the financial system Portuguese; 60.1%, which deserves consideration; 58.8%, which has good leadership and 65.6%, which is endorsed with highly competent professionals. It should be noted that this study proves a very significant improvement in the appreciation of Banco de Portugal by the Portuguese in 2021 compared to 2017, since there is a positive evolution in all eleven reputation variables considered in the survey, and in some cases the variations in the order of 10.1 and 13.4 percentage points. The work resulting from the Strategic Plan resulting from the Strategic Plan has not been 20172020. Now, the Strategic Plan 2021-2025, which aims to "promote proximity, strengthen confidence", will certainly contribute to deepening this path of improvement. The 2021-2025 Strategic Plan is built around five guidelines: (i) a robust financial system capable of facing the post-pathamic period; (ii) a banking market which brings together the conditions necessary for the proper functioning of the economy; (iii) a recovered, resilient and convergent economy in the European context; (iv) an influential action, in Portugal and Europe, and of trust with Portuguese society; and (v) a Bank with an efficiency-inducing governance model, focused on employee appreciation and technological transformation. The traditional objectives of central banks, such as price stability and financial stability, remain. But there are new specificities that stem, for example, from the impact of the pandemic and the dynamics it has generated, the process of digital transformation and the responsibilities for sustainability and preservation of the environment or the possible creation of digital currencies by central banks. Therefore, in an accelerated changing world characterized by abnormal uncertainty, the mission of central banks has not only become even more important but also more problematic and complex. [1] Jaime Reis, The Bank of Portugal  from the origins to 1914 , Vol. I, pp. 17-18.
text_original: Artigo do Vice-Governador, Lus Mx... Artigo do Vice-Governador, Lus Mximo dos Santos, no Jornal de Negcios: "Nos 175 anos do Banco de Portugal" 21 dez. 2021 Em 19 de novembro de 1846, num ambiente de profunda crise econmica, financeira, social e poltica, foi criado, por decreto rgio, o Banco de Portugal, que resultou da fuso do Banco de Lisboa com a Companhia Confiana Nacional, sendo essa uma das medidas adotadas para enfrentar os problemas do Pas  poca. O Banco de Lisboa era um banco comercial e emissor e foi o primeiro banco portugus no sentido moderno do termo. A sua criao, em 31 de dezembro de 1821, est intimamente ligada  Revoluo Liberal de 1820, como se evidencia de forma muito interessante num livro do Prof. Jos Lus Cardoso acabado de editar pelo Banco de Portugal. A Companhia Confiana Nacional, fundada em 1844, era uma sociedade financeira especializada no financiamento da dvida pblica. Mais tarde, o Banco de Portugal ganharia as caractersticas de banco central. Hoje a Constituio da Repblica refere-se-lhe, no seu artigo 102., como o banco central nacional, tornando-o assim um rgo constitucional. Como o Prof. Jaime Reis assinala [1], os bancos centrais europeus descendem em linha direta dos bancos com o privilgio de emisso que caracterizavam os sistemas de crdito nacionais durante o sculo XIX e a maioria surgiu no meio de graves crises monetrias e financeiras, pelo que o trajeto portugus, neste plano, no se afastou muito do padro europeu. Em 19 de novembro deste ano, portanto, o Banco de Portugal completou 175 anos de existncia. A histria do Banco de Portugal  parte importante da histria econmica, financeira e politica do Portugal moderno. Trata-se de uma data com elevada carga simblica, que tem vindo a ser assinalada com um conjunto de eventos que se prolongaro at 31 de maio de 2022. No so muito comuns instituies com esta antiguidade, o que confere ao Banco de Portugal uma maior responsabilidade no desempenho das suas misses e nas expetativas dos Portugueses. Mas a antiguidade, como costuma dizer-se, no  um posto e s por si nada resolve.  suposto que traga uma memria, uma massa crtica e um sentido de responsabilidade acrescido. Mas s se torna uma verdadeira mais-valia se em cada momento histrico estiver  altura dos desafios que se lhe colocam, souber evoluir ao longo do tempo, na organizao e nos procedimentos, demonstrar o dinamismo indispensvel para exercer eficaz e tempestivamente os seus poderes.  vasta a literatura econmica e poltica que correlaciona o desenvolvimento das naes com a solidez e qualidade das suas instituies. E muito estudos tm apontado a debilidade das instituies em Portugal como um ponto fraco do seu processo de desenvolvimento. Ora, pela importncia das atribuies e competncias que lhe esto cometidas e que o legislador tem vindo a aumentar nos anos mais recentes (facto que no pode deixar de ser interpretado como um sinal da confiana que lhe merece),  fcil concluir que o desempenho do Banco de Portugal  crucial para o Pas. Nacionalizado em 1974, o Banco de Portugal foi ganhando nas dcadas seguintes crescente protagonismo e acumulando funes: autoridade monetria e cambial, autoridade de superviso prudencial e de superviso comportamental e entidade fundamental para o aconselhamento econmico e financeiro dos Governos, tendo desempenhado um papel fundamental nos dois acordos com o Fundo Monetrio Internacional. Com a adoo do euro, em 1999, as funes do Banco de Portugal transformaram-se, mas no perderam importncia. Muito pelo contrrio. Em 2013, o Banco de Portugal torna-se autoridade macroprudencial nacional. A partir de 2014, enquanto entidade competente para a superviso prudencial (que j era desde 1975), tornou-se membro do Mecanismo nico de Superviso e, a partir de 2016, enquanto autoridade nacional de resoluo, membro do Mecanismo nico de Resoluo. E como  que o Pas v o Banco de Portugal hoje? Um estudo da Marktest realizado em abril de 2021, baseado em 963 entrevistas realizadas a uma amostra representativa da populao bancarizada e residente em Portugal Continental, revelou que 63,8% dos inquiridos consideram o Banco uma instituio de confiana; 60,3%, uma instituio com impacto positivo na sociedade portuguesa; 62,1%, que garante a estabilidade do sistema financeiro portugus; 60,1%, que merece considerao; 58,8%, que tem uma boa liderana e 65,6%, que  dotada de profissionais altamente competentes. Importa sublinhar que este estudo comprova uma melhoria muito significativa da apreciao do Banco de Portugal pelos portugueses em 2021 face a 2017, j que se regista uma evoluo positiva em todas as onze varveis de reputao consideradas no inqurito, sendo, nalguns casos, as variaes na ordem dos 10,1 e 13,4 pontos percentuais. A essa evoluo positiva no foi alheio o trabalho resultante do Plano Estratgico 20172020. Agora, o Plano Estratgico 2021-2025, que tem como mote promover a proximidade, reforar a confiana, vai contribuir seguramente para aprofundar esse caminho de melhoria. O Plano Estratgico 2021-2025 est construdo em torno de cinco orientaes: (i) um sistema financeiro robusto, capaz de enfrentar o perodo ps pandmico; (ii) um mercado bancrio que rena as condies necessrias ao bom funcionamento da economia; (iii) uma economia recuperada, resiliente e convergente no contexto europeu; (iv) uma ao influente, em Portugal e na Europa, e de confiana junto da sociedade portuguesa; e (v) um Banco com um modelo de governao indutor de eficincia, centrado na valorizao dos colaboradores e na transformao tecnolgica. Os tradicionais objetivos dos bancos centrais, como a estabilidade de preos e a estabilidade financeira, mantm-se. Mas h novas especificidades que decorrem, por exemplo, do impacto da pandemia e das dinmicas que gerou, do processo de transformao digital e das responsabilidades em matria de sustentabilidade e preservao do ambiente ou da eventual criao de moedas digitais pelos bancos centrais. Por isso, num mundo em acelerada mutao e caracterizado por uma anormal incerteza, a misso dos bancos centrais no s se tornou ainda mais importante como mais problemtica e complexa. [1] Jaime Reis, O Banco de Portugal  das origens a 1914 , Vol. I, pp. 17-18.

Title: Interview of Governor Mario Centeno to the Saturday edition dedicated to the 20 years of the euro
text: Interview of Governor Mario Cent... Interview of Governor Mario Centeno to the Saturday edition dedicated to the 20 years of the euro 28 Dec. 2021 Here we are at the end of 2021 to talk about the euro we have had in our portfolio for 20 years. In 20 years we still have euros in the wallet? With a new design, but i'm sure we'll have euros in the wallet and bank account. A dystopia published in 2010, "Super Sad True Love Story", has the characters in the near future using euros from the South and Euros from the North. I suppose you say this scenario is fiction, but why are you away? Because the euro is a time of European and democratic integration, it is a european choice in 19 mature democracies. [The euro] has support among European citizens which is now the largest ever, i.e. it is not a backward summa. You're gaining support and growing understanding. We must ask ourselves why, not least because this is the first crisis in which this happens. In its short life story, the euro used to suffer from citizens in terms of the support it had. Why has it changed? Because in the period before the crisis we accumulated three dimensions of robustness, very significant. An institutional one with the banking union and the creation of the first budgetary instrument for euro area countries. And two of the results: the fact that we have a whole trajectory of reducing budgetary risk in the euro area; and the third, also risk reduction, which is to have a more capitalized banking system to meet the challenges. No one expected it to be a pandemic, but the accumulation of these episodes allowed the euro in 2020 to be the basis for a very muscular reaction to the crisis. And that people understood, unlike the reaction in 2008. People felt protected. They felt protected. This is what the currency offers them and this achievement was not created in 2020. Conditions have been created before. I was fortunate to be able to live that as president of the Eurogroup. I think it was perhaps the most decisive period for me to be able to answer the first question you asked me, if in 20 years we will have euros in our pockets. Europe is growing and integrating with integration leaps, it is not a completely continuous process. Jumps happen in crises. Often in crisis, but these developments I mentioned were all achieved in the longest period of growth in the euro area. It grew for more than 25 consecutive quarters, never before had it happened to this group of countries. To what extent does all this stabilisation and recovery fall almost entirely on top of the European Central Bank? To what extent is monetary policy being burdened at the expense of political advances in the euro? Perhaps 2020 was the first time monetary policy was not talking alone in responding to crises. We have succeeded in order to remove what have always existed in the euro area, of moral risk, that countries are behaviourous of a common currency. And we did it by taking another leap of integration, the issuance of ordinary debt, which seemed like an impossibility a few months earlier. It had to do with the sense of responsibility in the face of the crisis, but it would not have been possible, or it would not have been as effective, without the developments i mentioned. This integration leap, which funds the "Next Generation EU", has an integration value, maintained in due proportions, similar to the creation of the euro. Two years ago, maybe it was unthinkable. Two years ago the [Eurogroup] meetings ended rapidly as we approached this topic. Is Portugal's presence in the euro a success? Or is there a double side of blessing and curse? All transformations involve challenges. A rigorous evaluation needed to define what the alternative was. It was not that we got into the euro. I doubt that the experience before the convergence period for entry into the euro had been particularly happy. We had very close financial crises in the late 1970s and early 1980s. The country gained a lot from the entry into the then EEC and the natural path of this European integration was the adoption of the euro. But these processes have challenges. It took the country too long to understand institutionally [the implications] and to reap all the benefits of being in the euro. But it is also true that, fortunately, it was one of the great drivers of this latest risk reduction movement. The country's fiscal and financial results in the post-sovereign debt crisis prove that today we are fully aware of what we can benefit from being in the euro, and what we need to do. I remember the four years of convergence with the euro area average that preceded the pisemic crisis. They had never happened in the euro period. But they have happened in very specific circumstances: an extremely favourable monetary policy, low oil prices, all countries recovering simultaneously. For a small open economy like ours... In 2016 it is not necessarily true, the presence of monetary policy in the face of Portuguese debt began to be reduced as early as April 2016, by limits imposed on the debt purchase program. The country was able to take advantage of a period that was provided to it, also by the intervention of the national authorities following the adjustment program, and has achieved indicators that it cannot lose sight of. I'm talking to you and sometimes he's talking about you as finance minister, almost in a double hat. It's a natural double hat. I am talking about an experience of Portugal that leads to our debt today no longer being used in financial stress exercises between euro area countries and which leads the IMF, just to talk outside of that period that Bruno was saying, putting the Portuguese government debt ratio in 2026 below Belgium, France and Spain. This is a trend that the country cannot fail to pursue because it is the one that allows us to take away all the benefits of being in the euro. The ECB was part of the troika and Banco de Portugal defended the policies of the adjustment programme. Is Banco de Portugal re-united in this past? It is difficult to separate the years in which he was minister from the previous ones, there is a continuum. It is clear that there is a continuum and that there is a national perception about the challenges, many of which were indeferred, that were placed on the Portuguese economy. All the work of recovering what is the credibility of the Portuguese economy was and is a work that has had a lot of value and that has to be continued. That is why I was just telling him that indicators such as debt or the budget deficit are not from the past. There is no discontinuity in this process. There is the adaptation of [national] policies, which very naturally must be assumed, and some developments in European terms. If you make a collection of European leaders from the period between 2008 and 2012 who say they regretted it, or that they were not quite sure to impose coordinated austerity policies in Europe, you will see that almost everyone is there. Some were my colleagues in the Eurogroup. Before the sovereign debt crisis we experienced a stagnation that was attributed to the misadjustment between our economy and the euro. Then there was a bailout that to a large extent was also a reflection of the currency's problems. If we only look at this it seems that the euro has not done much for us. Should we look longer term? We have to focus on a transition process that the Portuguese economy and society have suffered in this period, which has not had at all to do with belonging to the euro, but which has allowed us to be in the euro today differently from what we were at the beginning of this century. The euro has evolved into a more robust monetary and economic area. The euro institution was not prepared to protect the countries that were part of it in 2008. That's almost consensual today. But now it is? It is clearly better now, but I never want to take part in this process that has to continue. For example, we do not yet have a European deposit protection system. There's a way to go. These results and the ECB's role eventually relegated the issue of public debt to the background, but the pandemic created additional pressure. The debt and deficits no longer matter? They wouldn't let me. All sectors leave this period with more debt. There is a very large understanding today about the debt in each country in the euro area debate. That's why we were able to make joint debt issues. One of the expressions I used most as president of the Eurogroup in dew the support mechanisms in spring 2020 was that we should build solutions that would smooth the cost of the pandemic over time and among economic actors. And the time portion is crucial in issuing joint debt. Sharing this risk is a huge achievement. I hope that 2022 and 2023 and the following years will be able to be [up to the same]. For that to happen we all have to do our part. What's our part? Having an understanding of what it means to have more debt and what public deficits mean, because that problem is with us, as with all the countries in the euro area. We need to maintain that attitude. But I just didn't tell you other national dimensions in which I believe that today we are different from what we were at the beginning of the century. I'm going to uniquemy qualifications. For the first time in 900 years  there is a certain risk in this phrase of mine [smile]  we have the generation between 20 and 24 years old with educational levels above the euro area. This was unthinkable for Portugal. This capacity building in the country is what allows me to say that if all other conditions of predictability of public policies and qualified employment are created, we now have the most important ingredient. We were light years away from Europe in this ingredient. One of the achievements of the euro has been low inflation, but it is rising. What can lead the ECB to abandon the strategy of waiting and seeing? The ECB has since the beginning of the pandemic adapted its measures to the reading of the risks of financial fragmentation and inflation indicators. The real increase in inflation rates occurred between October and November, we do not yet know the December data. We are taking the signs of the inflation rate very seriously, but we also have the perception that many of the factors justifying this price increase are associated with the pandemic. So we have to wait and be patient, the central banks are one of the few economic players who can have a very strong patience to let the whole pandamic process stabilise and normalise the economy. But we are not going to do it with our arms crossed, so we're going to adapt the pace of [debt] purchases to the new reality. We already did it at the December meeting and we will continue to do so. All institutions have an inverted U-shaped inflation forecast, peaking in late 2021 and early 2022, with a more or less slugr slowdown throughout 2022. We'll have time to react. We have experienced unprecedented times of zero interest rates, which the Portuguese seem to have incorporated as a new normal. Can this change? The deleveraging process of the Portuguese economy in the last 10 years has been unique in the world. We have reduced debt rates as a percentage of GDP in both the private sector in households and businesses and in the public. The Portuguese even before the crisis had realized the importance of reducing indebtedness and this process should be resumed quickly. I don't think before the crisis we were playing a little bit with this low interest rate, leveraging activity into more debt. The euro is changing. There will be a new design of the notes and there is the idea of dropping the 1 and 2 cent coins. How's that measure? It's in the hands of the European Commission. The figures are very interesting: there are currently 140 billion euro coins in circulation and half are 1 and 2 cent coins. These coins have a cost of production and treatment that goes far beyond their face cost. Some countries alone have already made this transition by removing the 1-cent coins. This is done by finding a formula for rounding, which causes all smas to be rounded to O or 5, the nearest value. It has a very small and transitory impact on inflation, in our daily life. Which countries have stopped using these currencies? The Netherlands and Finland. Was the launch of the digital euro project the ECB's response to the intention of private technology giants such as Facebook to launch competing currencies from central banks? Is there a power battle? There is something above this logic of battle, which is the need to maintain trust in a system that is essentially fiduciary. The only institution that can guarantee this at the moment is central banks. There is no question of wanting to impose rules out of predominance, but for the common good. One of the characteristics of a currency is the value reserve and an asset to be currency needs predictability in its value. That is why we care so much about inflation, the great factor of currency devaluation. When we transpose this into an asset that has dramatic fluctuations, sometimes intraday, we obviously don't work on a concept that approaches the paper of the currency. The idea of digitization is the answer to a challenge posed by society, and allowed by technology, to simplify transactions from the point of view of process, costs and time.
