However, this work would have to address tremendous challenges, such as the current differences in the legal regimes applicable to crisis resolution across Member States. I recall that the ECOFIN on 2 December 2009 invited the Economic and Financial Committee to continue its work on an EU policy coordination framework for crisis management, including the issue of burden sharing, and present concrete proposals to the Council in spring 2010. I am sure the Eurosystem will contribute to such discussions in order to define an approach to burden sharing that would contribute to reducing moral hazard. It would be crucial to set out a consensus about the objectives to be reached and a roadmap of actions to be undertaken to achieve them. Q29. How do you assess the current level of consolidation in financial services in the EU and what is your view on future prospects in this regard? According to latest available structural indicators for the EU banking sector (i.e. 2008 figures), consolidation in the banking sector is continuing. However, this has also meant that market concentration is increasing, with the smaller countries generally having more concentrated markets than the larger ones. Domestic credit institutions continued to dominate the EU banking landscape and even increased their market share at the expense of foreign branches. Significant differences between countries continued with regard to the importance of foreign entities, with subsidiaries having a euro area parent being prevalent in the new EU Member States. Merger and acquisition (M&A) activities increased in 2009 while remaining at low levels compared to the preceding ten years. Domestic and cross-border deals recorded the strongest increase. While in the past M&A deals were mainly driven by strategic considerations, such as realising economies of scale and entering new markets, many of the transactions completed in 2008 and in 2009 involved entities that had incurred significant losses or faced liquidity strains. At the same time, efforts to boost the capital position and cash reserves of certain credit institutions led to the spin-off of certain non-core activities, either in terms of business or geographical location. In terms of the total value of M&A transactions, acquisitions considerably declined in 2009, with only domestic deals recording an increase. It should also be noted that the participation of governments in credit institutions has constituted a significant shift in the ownership structure of some major credit institutions in the EU. However, due to the limited duration of government recapitalisation measures, it is expected that this shift in ownership will be temporary and that it will be reversed as the financial condition of these institutions, on a stand-alone basis, recovers. As to the assessment of consolidation patterns, this has to be viewed in terms of its impact on the efficiency and soundness of individual banks, on competition in the banking sector and on financial stability in the financial sector more generally. To the extent that recent consolidation activities in the banking sector have contributed to increasing the profitability of banks and strengthening their resilience to shocks, they can be viewed as positive. In assessing the future prospects for consolidation, an important consideration is the widespread consensus that the pre-crisis levels of banking sector leverage were excessive. Hence, it can be expected that as de-leveraging proceeds the profitability of the banking system (in terms of return on equity) will be lower return than in the recent past, at least at the medium term. Banks are therefore likely to look for new drivers of profitability. Consolidation may represent an attractive way to accomplish this objective for those banks which are emerging as the strongest players from the crisis, as acquisitions at relatively affordable prices will potentially be a way to achieve higher profitability in the long term  thanks to economies of scale. In that respect, M&A trends may be expected to continue after the crisis too. Mergers can also occur in the next few years as a rescue measure of troubled banks. As indicated, many of the reasons that validate the prediction that we will see further consolidation in the near future justify also the conclusion that this will lead to a more efficient and resilient banking system. On the other hand, the concentration of the sector may create more institutions too big to fail which makes it more pressing the need to implement the measures to address the problems that these institutions create. D. Functioning of the ECB and democratic accountability and transparency Q30: Shouldn't the different responsibilities of Board members change with time, in line with the changes occurred in the ECB's tasks and priorities? The Executive Board of the ECB is a collegiate decision-making body; its functioning is based on the principle of collective responsibility, i.e. the Executive Board in its entirety is collectively responsible for its decisions and the overall functioning of the ECB business areas. While, for practical reasons, business areas report to individual Executive Board members who oversee and guide their work, all work units are placed under the managing direction of the Executive Board as a whole. As has happened in the past the Executive Board may review, from time to time, the reporting lines to Executive Board members of work units and the preparation of its decisions. Such occasional adjustments in the individual responsibilities of Executive Board members contribute to strengthen the collegiate nature of the Executive Board. In this context, the composition of the portfolios of Executive Board members can change during their term of office. Any decision in this respect remains the sole responsibility of the Executive Board itself. I attach myself great value to the collective nature of the Executive Board as this best ensures that various perspectives are reflected and that all the available expertise, experience and wisdom are appropriately taken into account when making decisions. Q31. What system do you think is appropriate to ensure an equitable rotation of membership on the ECB-executive board also in terms of nationalities? The pre-requisites for appointees to the ECBs Executive Board are established by the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU (Art 283.2) and the Statute of the ESCB and the ECB (Art 11.2):  the members of the Executive Board shall be appointed among persons of recognised standing and professional experience in monetary or banking matters;  only nationals of [euro area] Member States may be members of the Executive Board. The Treaty thus establishes two requirements: competence and [euro area] nationality. No other specification can be found in the Treaty as a determinant for the composition of the Executive Board of the ECB. Appointments which would be based on considerations other than the above requirements may also conflict with the Treaty provisions on the ECBs independence. In the meetings of the ECBs decision making bodies all members participate in their personal capacity. The principle of independence entails that neither the ECB, nor a national central bank, nor any member of their decision-making bodies shall seek or take instructions from Community institutions or bodies, from any Government of a Member State or from any other body. (Art. 130 of the Treaty, Art. 7 of the Statute). This Treaty provision is incompatible with the principle of national representation. The final decision on appointments to the ECBs Executive Board is taken by the European Council (in which only euro area Members vote) upon a recommendation from the Council and following consultation of the European Parliament and the ECB. I trust that the above principles for the appointment of members to the Executive Board of the ECB are fully respected. Q32. What is your view on the need to increase the diversity of backgrounds represented in the ECB board rather than relying solely on central bankers? As mentioned in my reply to the previous question, the Treaty and the Statute are clear in stipulating that the members of the Executive Board shall be appointed among persons of recognised standing and professional experience in monetary or banking matters. It does not come as a surprise that central bankers fulfil this requirement. At the same time, this provision by no means excludes that appointment of candidates from outside the central banking community. As a matter of fact, in most central banks  and the ECB is no exception here - the background of members of the decision-making bodies is quite diverse and includes, for instance, professional experience in banking, academia and public administration. You have seen from my own curriculum vitae that this also applies to me. In my view, the diversity of backgrounds of members of a collegiate decision-making body is an asset for the governance of the institution. Q33. Could you elaborate on your views on the concept of democratic accountability with regards to the ECB and central banking in general? To retain legitimacy, an independent central bank must be accountable to democratic institutions and the general public for its actions in the pursuit of its mandate. With the increasing recognition, especially in the past few decades, that independence is crucial for a central bank to deliver on its mandate, the nature of democratic accountability has also become more important. In this context, the accountability of central banks around the world has taken a number of different forms. In the European Union, the ECB has a clear mandate and pursues it in an independent manner as provided for by the Treaty. Also foreseen in the Treaty is that this high degree of independence goes hand in hand with democratic accountability towards the European public and its directly elected representatives, that is, the European Parliament. A number of well defined ways have thus been established for holding the ECB accountable, not least with the regular appearances of the ECBs President before the Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (ECON), and further appearances by the ECB Vice-President and other members of the ECB Executive Board. It is notable that the latter hearings represent a closer form of cooperation between the ECB and the European Parliament than is foreseen in the Treaty and this established practice is, in my view, a very positive element and also welcome by the EP. The ECBs accountability also entails precise reporting obligations [Art. 15 of ECB Statute]. Beyond the Annual Report presented to Parliament (and Council, Commission and European Council), the ECB is required to publish quarterly reports on the activities of the Eurosystem. The ECB decided to go beyond these Treaty requirements and report more frequently in the form of the Monthly Bulletin. Finally, apart from the consolidated Weekly Financial Statement, the ECB publishes a range of other task-related publications, including its bi-annual Financial Stability Report and its annual Financial Integration Report. Q34. How do you judge the procedure used to replace ECB board members? Should ex ante democratic accountability and transparency not imply that the European Parliament at least be formally given the possibility to hear several potential candidates and give its opinion before Council makes the final decision about the nomination? The procedure to select members of the ECB Executive Board is set out in Article 283 of the Treaty and Article 11 of the ESCB and ECB Statute. It has been agreed by all signatories in the most recent Treaty revision and is effective European law. As a candidate for the ECB Executive Board I am subject to that procedure and do not consider it appropriate to comment on its suitability. Q35. What conclusions do you draw from the comparison between the transparency policies followed by the Federal Reserve Bank and by the ECB? Which alternative would you prefer: the publication of the minutes two weeks after monetary policy decisions were taken, such as practiced by the Fed and the Bank of England, or the press conference that immediately follows monetary policy decisions in addition to the instant publication on the internet of the reasoning behind the decision, such as done by the ECB? A comparison across different approaches is a complex undertaking. One of the reasons is that central banks may have different needs owing to their specific histories and cultures, their policy objectives and other elements in their institutional frameworks. As a robust conclusion from available research, it has emerged that the way in which central banks nowadays take monetary policy decisions is much clearer and more transparent than in previous decades. Thereby, effectiveness of monetary policy has been enhanced on a global scale. There are different ways of being transparent. For the following reasons I am convinced that the ECBs approach is one of the most advanced in the world. First, it is very transparent regarding the link between its monetary policy strategy and the reasons for its actions. Second, the Press Conference and the Introductory Statement are useful tools to disseminate important information to a heterogeneous audience. They provide interested parties (e.g. the general public, the media, and financial market observers) with a comprehensive set of relevant information on the ECBs monetary policy decisions. They aim at explaining the collective view of the Governing Council on the monetary policy stance. Third, the Introductory Statement and the Questions and Answers at the press conference are published in real-time. This feature would not be achievable with the publication of minutes. Overall, I regard the ECBs practice as demanding for all members of the Governing Council. I also believe that the ECBs approach is widely understood by now, and that the publication of minutes by other central banks makes perfect sense for them as well. Q36: Whats your opinion of the quarterly Monetary Dialogue between the European Parliament and the ECB President? Do you see any room for improvement in the Monetary Dialogue? Do the frequent discussions concerning the ECBs policies with other political actors harm the banks independence? The regular dialogue with the European Parliament is part of the democratic accountability of the European Central Bank to the European citizens and their directly elected representatives. In this context, the quarterly meetings between the President of the ECB and the Committee on Economic and Monetary Affairs represent a very important contribution to the public acceptance of the ECBs monetary policy. Together with additional appearances, also by other Executive Board Members, this interaction contributes to a deep and productive exchange of views. It also provides the ECB with a very valuable forum to explain its monetary policy and to receive feedback. This extends to the EP Plenary where, inter alia, the ECB President presents the Banks Annual Report. The quality of the dialogue between the ECB and the EP is of a very high standard. This has been acknowledged by both institutions on several occasions in the past. I consider the regular exchange of information with other policy actors as a very important element of our policy framework in EMU. In this context, the ECB interacts with a number of European institutions on a regular basis. For example, the ECB is invited to the meetings of the Eurogroup and the ECOFIN Council. It regularly participates in the meetings of the Macroeconomic Dialogue. Interaction at technical level with the Commission and national governments also take place, for example, in the Economic and Financial Committee and the Economic Policy Committee of the EU. All these exchanges of views take place according to the provisions of the Treaty, thereby ensuring and always respecting the full independence of the ECB while at the same time supporting the proper functioning of EMU. They are therefore necessary and desirable precisely because they recognise the independence of the ECB. Q37: Should the ECB be subject to a full scrutiny of the European Court of Auditors going beyond the concept of operational efficiency (Article 27.2 of the Statute of the ESCB and of the ECB) The ECBs corporate governance is subject to a comprehensive framework of external and internal controls most elements of which are statutory in nature. The examination of the operational efficiency of the management of the ECB by the Court of Auditors is one important element of this control framework. This framework is complemented by regular reporting obligation to the European Parliament and the general public as well as judicial control by the Court of Justice of the European Union. All these elements have been set up also in the light of the guarantee of central bank independence. The independence of the ECB extends also to its financial resources. From this it follows that there is no need to extend the control by the Court of Auditors beyond the concept of operational efficiency. E. General Q38. What do you see as the most important risks and challenges facing the ECB? As regards main challenges and risks facing the ECB, let me restrict myself here to three of them: The implementation of our exit strategy is an unprecedented challenge, with a need to ensure gradualism in the withdrawal of the ECB non-standard measures. Prevailing market uncertainty, however, means that determining the appropriate pace and scale of the exit continues to be a demanding task. I feel that the exit strategy measures taken to date by the ECB have been fully appropriate and justified by the assessment of economic and financial market conditions. Great care is needed going ahead, as the costs of errors can be very high, as the history of recovering from severe banking and economic crises has shown. Another challenge I would like to highlight is the establishment and operation of the ESRB, for which the ECB will offer support. Intellectually, this task is challenging as new tools need to be developed for the assessment of macro-prudential risk, while existing tools can also be used for this purpose. Furthermore, given overlaps between the ECBs General and Governing Councils and the new General Board of the ESRB as regards the composition of the both bodies, we need to ensure adequate and consistent communication. In particular, it needs to be emphasised that there is no trade-off between the objective of price stability and the support that the ECB can lend to other goals including financial stability. Finally, there are, for instance, organisational issues, such as how to embed the ESRB support function in the ECBs current organisation. Finally, let me mention the challenge stemming from the pressures created by the existing imbalances in several member countries. This a problem for the countries themselves and for all European institutions with responsibilities in the management of monetary union but must involve also an active role for the ECB. As I recalled before, there is only one monetary policy for the euro area as a whole, but there is also a mission for the ECB in contributing to the analysis of competitiveness and divergences within the area helping the countries themselves to device and implement the appropriate policies. Being member of the European Unioncreates benefits for the countries concerned but also obligations. For members of the euro area, this applies even more so. These responsibilities need to be respected by all, to benefit the most from economic and monetary union in Europe. Policy actions need to be in line with European requirements. By this, I do not only mean living up to the fiscal rules in the Stability and Growth Pact, but also conducting structural policies that make Europe more productive, and hence more flexible. Likewise, private agents need to observe balanced behaviour in their cost and wage-setting behaviour. Insufficient progress and convergence in these areas not only concerns me as an enthusiastic supporter of Europe, it also affects the environment in which the ECB operates, and therefore is also a concern to me as monetary policy-maker.

Title: Opinion article by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in the Economic Journal: "Future challenges of the banking system Portuguese"
text: Opinion article by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in the Economic Journal: Future challenges of the Portuguese banking system1 1 This article resumes the essential sum of the intervention at the Banking Forum on 23 November 2016. Where are we now? In recent years there has been a continuous and significant reduction in the indebtedness of individuals and non-financial corporations (Figure 1). However, debt levels remain very high and the deleveraging effort should continue to ensure resilience in the face of adverse developments affecting the ability to serve the debt. In contrast, the indebtedness of public administrations continued to increase and today represents an important vulnerability of the Portuguese economy to changes in market conditions. The continuation of a path of fiscal consolidation is essential for the sustained reduction of the level of public indebtedness and for creating favourable conditions for economic growth. A very positive fact of recent years, which should be noted, is the significant reduction in the leverage of the Portuguese banking system, with the transformation ratio falling from above 150% in 2010 to close to 100% in 2015. Currently, banks finance the economy only with client resources, when in 2011 about 40% of the financing was made on the basis of external resources. Figure 1 Source: Banco de Portugal As a result of the new regulatory requirements, but also the effort of their stakeholders, Portuguese banks are now more capitalized than in 2011 and with better quality own funds (Figure 2). At the end of the first half of 2016, the banking capital ratio stood at 12.1% (CET 1)2, up from 8.7% (CT1)3 in 2011. However, the banking sector Portuguese still has a CET 1 ratio below the average of European peers. 2 CET1  Common Equity Tier 1, after 2014. 3 CT1 - Core Tier 1, until 2013. In the context of the economic and financial crisis, the profitability of banks has fallen significantly and has fallen to negative values. In the most recent period there has been some recovery in profitability, although to still very low levels. Figure 2 Source: Banco de Portugal Banks' low levels of profitability strongly affect the strengthening of their capital in that they do not allow sufficient capital to be generated internally and restrict the ability to attract new investors by the low prospects for return on investment. The fall in bank income was accompanied by some efforts to rationalise their structures. Nevertheless, cost-to-income ratios remain high compared to the benchmarks of the most efficient European institutions. On the other hand, the high stock of non-yield-generating assets on banks' balance sheets, especially non-performing loans (NPL), as well as the need to recognize impairment losses associated with these exposures, significantly limit the generation of positive results. At the end of 2015, non-income-generating assets from all seven of the system's seven largest banks amounted to 53 billion and the costs to 21 billion. These oddities are mainly associated with credits granted before 2010. Compared to European peers, the national banking system is particularly penalised by higher levels of pay, as the gross operating result is similar to the European average (Figure 3). Figure 3 Results of the group of the seven largest banks of the banking system Portuguese Source: Banco de Portugal Calculations In a view, despite the challenges facing the banking system Portuguese some of which are global in nature, banks now have a much better liquidity and solvency situation than they had in 2010. It is therefore important to learn lessons from the past and to ensure that the same mistakes are not made in the future. Where did we come from? Six factors were at the origin of the weaknesses accumulated by the banking system Portuguese during the period of the so-called "great moderation": i. Shareholder structure of banks The absence of shareholders with "real money" (and in some cases the reluctance to open the capital to these shareholders) potentiated credit-granting phenomena that turned into shareholder holdings, which, in turn, were used to guarantee the credits granted. This practice began with the reprivatisation of financial groups in the early 1990s and continued in subsequent years. The financing of related parties through opaque mechanisms using non-cooperative jurisdictions was one of the strands of this phenomenon. When, in the context of the financial crisis, the banks' shares depreciated, many shareholders were no longer able to cope with the debt service of the loans they had contracted, which further aggravated the financial situation of banks through credit unparities. In addition, some of these shareholders to secure these holdings also committed assets they held in the real economy, which had increased destructive effects on the economy. ii. Financing for the acquisition of shareholdings The Portuguese banks also granted credit for the acquisition of shareholdings in companies in the non-financial sector, accepting them as a guarantee of their own credit. In the context of the crisis, and the use of guarantees for the settlement of financing, a large part of these holdings ended up being on the balance sheet of banks that became shareholders of companies of various business branches. In many cases the credit granted for this purpose replaced foreign capital previously invested in these companies. In macroeconomic terms this meant a decapitalisation of the economy and an increase in systemic risk by increasing the indebtedness of private national economic agents. iii. Underestimation of risk and maximisation of lending For several years the banking system was guided by an incentive scheme that promoted short-term results to the detriment of medium-term results, such as remuneration policies and dividend distribution. This system of incentives - based on business objectives and quarterly results - has led, in several institutions, to a policy of maximising the amount of credit granted, in many cases without an adequate assessment of the associated risk. Furthermore, as the registration of unevenness was not carried out on a preventive form (but only in the face of credit events justifying its recognition), risk coverage was transferred to the future and, therefore, the dividends distributed were higher than those that a conservative policy of setting up oddities would advise. iv. Financing to sectors dependent on domestic demand Much of the bank credit granted was concentrated in sectors that are heavily dependent on the indebtedness of their clients  such as construction and real estate activities  which eventually left financial institutions very vulnerable to the change in demand for these sectors of activity (Figure 4). There seemed to be an illusion that demand for these sectors and their financing would be unlimited. In this respect the responsibility of public servants is very great because they are the ones who give the signals on the basis of which private economic actors uphold their decisions. Economic policies with inconsistent temporal incentives generate situations of unsustainability. And it is not possible to have unsustainable policies without this being reflected in the banks. One of the lessons of this crisis was precisely the importance of reviewing the instruments for monitoring financial markets and safeguarding financial stability. Macroprudential policy has taken a prominent position in these reforms. Figure 4 Average risk in regular credit portfolio and contribution by sector to its variation Note: Note: The analysis uses only companies with all regular credit against the financial system (companies that default and their credit are withdrawn from the analysis). Risk estimation follows the methodology described in "Revisiting probabilities of non-compliance of companies" (Antunes, Homero, Prego, 2016). Source: Banco de Portugal When the economy began to reveal the first signs of the crisis, companies most sensitive to the economic cycle - such as construction and public works - began to find it difficult to repay debt. Thus, there was a significant increase in bank credit in default in these sectors, penalizing the results of credit institutions with significant time lags compared to the time of their concession (Figure 5). Figure 5 Stock of credit in a regular and non-compliance situation Source: Banco de Portugal v. Financing of companies with low levels of equity. Banks have financed companies with very low levels of equity, which are more vulnerable to possible changes in the macroeconomic context on their debt repayment capacity (Figure 6). In addition, many of these companies had great weaknesses in account transparency and poor internal government models. Figure 6 Private Companies: Equity as a percentage of total assets (weighted average) Source: Banco de Portugal vi. Financing for individuals with high exposure to the economic cycle. In 2010 almost 40% of indebted households had a debt of more than 300% of their income and for 17% of households the debt service exceeded 40% of their income (Figure 7). The high indebtedness of households has increased the sensitivity of their financial situation to income shocks, and this risk is exacerbated by the fact that a significant proportion of household income originates in the non-tradable sector which was most affected by the crisis. Figure 7 Indicators of the financial situation of households Sources: (a) INE and Banco de Portugal. (b) Costa, S., "Financial situation of households in Portugal: an analysis based on isff 2013 data", Journal of Economic Studies, vol. II, no. 4. Where should we go? Sustained economic recovery requires strong banks with the ability to increase credit to the economy as economic activity strengthens. In this context, it is essential that banks quickly overcome some of the remaining economic and financial crisis difficulties, and that at the same time they put in place strategies to enable them to respond to the opportunities and challenges associated with the digital technology revolution. The national banking system currently faces four major challenges, some of a more global nature: i. Sustainably improve its profitability ii. Adapt to new regulatory requirements and ensure compliance with iii. Introduce changes in the model of government and organizational culture that allow to regain the trust of stakeholders iv. Invest in innovation, both operationally and in terms of providing services to customers. In the immediate future, the strengthening of banks' profitability is the primary challenge, both to generate domestic capital and to attract foreign capital and thus to create conditions that allow the implementation of repositioning strategies in the face of the future. In this context, it is necessary to implement solutions that reduce the weight of unproductive assets in the balance sheet. This means that banks must adopt active strategies and implement measures to accelerate the decrease in this stock. The extension of the current situation has significant adverse consequences for the national banking sector, not only in terms of profitability and capital, but also in terms of the perception of markets about the soundness of institutions in a more demanding regulatory framework. In addition, the prospects for maintaining moderate economic growth and very low interest rates for a prolonged period require a comprehensive reassessment of the business models and cost structure of financial institutions. Although the efficiency ratio has improved in recent years, there is still a way to go to adjust the cost structure to turnover, and additional cost rationalisation measures are needed. The continuation of the process of adjusting business models should also take into account the demands and opportunities associated with the new paradigm of "digital banking". The introduction of digital technology has revolutionised the demand patterns of banking customers and the way proximity banking is done. Successful adaptation of the banking system requires a high initial investment in technological infrastructure and skills, but it also represents an opportunity to structurally reduce operating costs. Finally, it is very important that there is a change in the culture and behavior of organizations, demonstrating security, integrity, reliability and quality in the services provided to customers, as a way of recovering the trust of all stakeholders, contributing decisively to the stability of the national financial system.
text_original: Aro.wmf Artigo de opinio do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa no Jornal Econmico: Desafios futuros do sistema bancrio portugus1 Aro.wmf Aro.wmf Aro.wmf Aro.wmf Aro.wmf Aro.wmf Aro.wmf 1 Este artigo retoma o essencial da interveno no Frum Banca em 23 de novembro de 2016. Onde estamos? Nos ltimos anos verificou-se uma reduo contnua e significativa do endividamento dos particulares e das sociedades no financeiras (Figura 1). Os nveis de dvida permanecem, contudo, muito elevados e o esforo de desalavancagem dever prosseguir para garantir resilincia perante evolues adversas que afetem a capacidade de servir a dvida. Em contraste, o endividamento das administraes pblicas continuou a aumentar e representa hoje uma importante vulnerabilidade da economia portuguesa a alteraes nas condies de mercado. A continuao de uma trajetria de consolidao oramental  essencial para a reduo sustentada do nvel de endividamento pblico e para criar condies favorveis ao crescimento econmico. Um facto muito positivo dos ltimos anos, que importa salientar,  a reduo significativa da alavancagem do sistema bancrio portugus, tendo o rcio de transformao cado de valores superiores a 150% em 2010 para prximo de 100% em 2015. Atualmente, os bancos financiam a economia apenas com recursos dos clientes, quando em 2011 cerca de 40% do financiamento era feito com base em recursos externos. Figura 1 Fonte: Banco de Portugal Em consequncia dos novos requisitos regulatrios, mas tambm do esforo dos respetivos stakeholders, os bancos portugueses esto hoje mais capitalizados do que em 2011 e com fundos prprios de melhor qualidade (Figura 2). No final do primeiro semestre de 2016, o rcio de fundos prprios do setor bancrio situou-se em 12,1% (CET 1)2, superior aos 8,7% (CT1)3 em 2011. Contudo, o setor bancrio portugus continua a apresentar um rcio CET 1 inferior  mdia dos pares europeus. 2 CET1  Common Equity Tier 1, aps 2014. 3 CT1  Core Tier 1, at 2013. No quadro da crise econmica e financeira, a rendibilidade dos bancos sofreu uma reduo significativa e caiu para valores negativos. No perodo mais recente assistiu-se a alguma recuperao da rendibilidade, embora para nveis ainda muito reduzidos. Figura 2 Fonte: Banco de Portugal Os baixos nveis de rendibilidade dos bancos condicionam fortemente o reforo do seu capital na medida em que no permitem gerar capital prprio suficiente por via interna e restringem a capacidade de atrair novos investidores pelas baixas perspetivas de retorno do investimento. A queda dos proveitos dos bancos foi acompanhada de alguns esforos de racionalizao das suas estruturas. Apesar disso, os rcios cost-to-income permanecem elevados face aos valores de referncia das instituies europeias mais eficientes. Por outro lado, o elevado stock de ativos no geradores de rendimento nos balanos dos bancos, sobretudo os non-performing loans (NPL), bem como a necessidade de reconhecimento de perdas por imparidade associadas a estas exposies, limitam de forma determinante a gerao de resultados positivos. No final de 2015, os ativos no geradores de rendimento do conjunto dos sete maiores bancos do sistema ascendiam a 53 mil milhes de euros e as imparidades a 21 mil milhes de euros. Estas imparidades esto maioritariamente associadas a crditos concedidos antes de 2010. Na comparao com os pares europeus, o sistema bancrio nacional  particularmente penalizado pelos maiores nveis de imparidades, uma vez que o resultado bruto de explorao  semelhante  mdia europeia (Figura 3). Figura 3 Resultados do grupo dos sete maiores bancos do sistema bancrio portugus Fonte: Clculos do Banco de Portugal Em suma, apesar dos desafios que o sistema bancrio portugus atualmente enfrenta, alguns dos quais de natureza global, os bancos tm hoje uma situao de liquidez e solvabilidade muito melhor do que aquela que tinham em 2010. Importa por isso tirar lies do passado e assegurar que no futuro no so cometidos os mesmos erros. De onde vimos? Seis fatores estiveram na origem das fragilidades acumuladas pelo sistema bancrio portugus durante o perodo da chamada grande moderao: i. Estrutura acionista dos bancos A ausncia de acionistas com real money (e em alguns casos a relutncia em abrir o capital a estes acionistas) potenciou fenmenos de concesso de crdito que se transformavam em participaes acionistas, as quais, por sua vez, eram usadas em garantia dos crditos concedidos. Esta prtica iniciou-se com a reprivatizao dos grupos financeiros no incio dos anos 1990 e prosseguiu nos anos subsequentes. O financiamento de partes relacionadas atravs de mecanismos opacos usando jurisdies no cooperantes foi uma das vertentes deste fenmeno. Quando, no quadro da crise financeira, as aes dos bancos se desvalorizaram, muitos acionistas deixaram de conseguir fazer face ao servio da dvida dos crditos que tinham contrado, o que agravou ainda mais a situao financeira dos bancos por via das imparidades de crdito. Acresce que alguns destes acionistas para garantirem essas participaes, comprometeram tambm ativos que detinham na economia real, o que teve efeitos destrutivos acrescidos sobre a economia. ii. Financiamento para aquisio de participaes sociais Os bancos portugueses tambm concederam crdito para a aquisio de participaes sociais em empresas do setor no financeiro, aceitando as mesmas como garantia do prprio crdito. No contexto da crise, e da utilizao das garantias para liquidao dos financiamentos, grande parte dessas participaes acabaram por ficar no balano dos bancos que se tornaram acionistas de empresas de variados ramos de negcio. Em muitos casos o crdito concedido para esta finalidade substituiu capital estrangeiro anteriormente investido nessas empresas. Em termos macroeconmicos isto significou uma descapitalizao da economia e um aumento do risco sistmico por via do aumento do endividamento dos agentes econmicos nacionais privados. iii. Subestimao do risco e maximizao da concesso de crdito Durante vrios anos o sistema bancrio orientou-se por um regime de incentivos que promovia os resultados de curto prazo em detrimento dos resultados de mdio prazo, de que so exemplo as polticas de remunerao e a distribuio de dividendos. Este sistema de incentivos - assente em objetivos comerciais e resultados trimestrais - conduziu, em diversas instituies, a uma poltica de maximizao do montante de crdito concedido, em muitos casos sem uma avaliao adequada do risco associado. Para alm disso, como o registo de imparidades no era efetuado de forma preventiva (mas apenas perante eventos de crdito que justificassem o seu reconhecimento), a cobertura de riscos foi transferida para o futuro e, por conseguinte, os dividendos distribudos foram superiores aos que uma poltica conservadora de constituio de imparidades aconselharia. iv. Financiamento a setores dependentes da procura interna Grande parte do crdito bancrio concedido concentrou-se em setores muito dependentes da capacidade de endividamento dos respetivos clientes - como a construo e atividades imobilirias  o que acabou por deixar as instituies financeiras muito vulnerveis  alterao na procura destes setores de atividade (Figura 4). Parecia existir a iluso de que a procura dirigida a estes setores e o seu financiamento seriam ilimitados. Neste aspeto a responsabilidade dos agentes pblicos  muito grande porque so eles que do os sinais com base nos quais os agentes econmicos privados sustentam as suas decises. Polticas econmicas com incentivos inconsistentes do ponto de vista temporal geram situaes de insustentabilidade. E no  possvel ter polticas insustentveis sem que isso se venha a refletir nos bancos. Uma das lies desta crise foi precisamente a importncia de rever os instrumentos de acompanhamento dos mercados financeiros e de salvaguarda da estabilidade financeira. A poltica macroprudencial assumiu uma posio de destaque nestas reformas. Figura 4 Risco mdio na carteira de crdito regular e contributo por setor para a sua variao Nota: Nota: A anlise utiliza apenas empresas com a totalidade do crdito regular face ao sistema financeiro (empresas que entram em incumprimento e o seu respetivo crdito so retiradas da anlise). A estimao do risco segue a metodologia descrita em Revisitando probabilidades de incumprimento de empresas (Antunes, Homero, Prego, 2016). Fonte: Banco de Portugal Quando a economia comeou a revelar os primeiros sinais da crise, as empresas mais sensveis ao ciclo econmico - como a construo e obras pblicas - comearam a apresentar dificuldade em reembolsar a dvida. Assim, assistiu-se a um aumento significativo do crdito bancrio em incumprimento nestes setores, penalizando os resultados das instituies de crdito com desfasamentos temporais significativos face ao momento da sua concesso (Figura 5). Figura 5 Stock de crdito em situao regular e em incumprimento Fonte: Banco de Portugal v. Financiamento de empresas com reduzidos nveis de capitais prprios. Os bancos financiaram empresas com nveis muito reduzidos de capitais prprios, as quais so mais vulnerveis a possveis alteraes do contexto macroeconmico sobre a sua capacidade de reembolso da dvida (Figura 6). Acresce que muitas destas empresas apresentavam grandes debilidades na transparncia das contas e deficientes modelos de governo interno. Figura 6 Empresas Privadas: Capital Prprio em percentagem do total do ativo (mdia ponderada) Fonte: Banco de Portugal vi. Financiamento a particulares com elevada exposio ao ciclo econmico. Em 2010 quase 40% das famlias endividadas tinham uma dvida superior a 300% do seu rendimento e para 17% das famlias o servio da dvida excedia 40% do seu rendimento (Figura 7). O elevado endividamento das famlias aumentou a sensibilidade da sua situao financeira a choques sobre o rendimento, sendo este risco exacerbado pelo facto de uma proporo significativa do rendimento das famlias ter origem no setor dos no transacionveis que foi o mais afetado pela crise. Figura 7 Indicadores da situao financeira das famlias Fontes: (a) INE e Banco de Portugal. (b) Costa, S., "Situao financeira das famlias em Portugal: uma anlise com base nos dados do ISFF 2013", Revista de Estudos Econmicos, vol. II, n. 4. Para onde devemos ir? A recuperao econmica sustentada requer bancos fortes, com capacidade para aumentar o crdito  economia  medida que a atividade econmica se fortalea. Neste contexto  fundamental que os bancos ultrapassem com brevidade algumas das dificuldades associadas  crise econmica e financeira que ainda subsistem, e que, em simultneo, ponham em prtica estratgias que lhes permitam responder s oportunidades e desafios associados  revoluo da tecnologia digital. O sistema bancrio nacional defronta atualmente quatro grandes desafios, alguns de natureza mais global: i. Melhorar de forma sustentada a sua rendibilidade ii. Adaptar-se s novas exigncias regulatrias e assegurar a sua observncia iii. Introduzir alteraes no modelo de governo e na cultura organizacional que permitam recuperar a confiana dos stakeholders iv. Investir em inovao, quer em termos operacionais quer ao nvel da prestao de servios aos clientes. No imediato, o reforo da rendibilidade dos bancos  o desafio primordial, quer para gerar capital interno quer para atrair capital externo e, deste modo, criar condies que permitam pr em prtica estratgias de reposicionamento perante o futuro. Neste contexto,  necessrio implementar solues que reduzam o peso dos ativos improdutivos no balano. Isto significa que os bancos devem adotar estratgias ativas e implementar medidas que permitam acelerar a diminuio desse stock. O prolongamento da atual situao tem consequncias adversas significativas para o setor bancrio nacional, no s ao nvel da rendibilidade e capital, mas tambm em termos da perceo dos mercados acerca da solidez das instituies, num quadro regulamentar mais exigente. Adicionalmente, as perspetivas de manuteno de um crescimento econmico moderado e de taxas de juro muito baixas por um perodo prolongado impem uma reavaliao abrangente dos modelos de negcio e da estrutura de custos das instituies financeiras. Embora nos ltimos anos se tenha assistido a uma melhoria do rcio de eficincia, h ainda um caminho a percorrer para ajustar a estrutura de custos ao volume de negcios, sendo necessrias medidas adicionais de racionalizao de custos. A continuao do processo de ajustamento dos modelos de negcio dever tambm ter em conta as exigncias e as oportunidades associadas ao novo paradigma da banca digital. A introduo da tecnologia digital veio revolucionar os padres de procura dos clientes bancrios e a forma como a banca de proximidade se faz. A adaptao bem-sucedida do sistema bancrio requer um elevado investimento inicial em infraestruturas tecnolgicas e em competncias, mas representa tambm uma oportunidade para reduzir de forma estrutural os custos operacionais. Finalmente  muito importante que se verifique uma mudana da cultura e do comportamento das organizaes, demonstrando segurana, integridade, fiabilidade e qualidade nos servios prestados aos clientes, como forma de recuperao da confiana de todos os stakeholders, contribuindo de forma decisiva para a estabilidade do sistema financeiro nacional.

Title: Hearing of the Governor of Banco de Portugal by the Parliamentary Committees on Budget, Finance and Public Administration and Social Security and Work on the transfer of pension funds from bank workers to Social Security
text: Hearing of the Governor of Banco de Portugal by the Parliamentary Committees on Budget, Finance and Plica Administration and Social Security and Labour Transfer of funds from bank workers' penss to Social Security, January 30, 2012 Mr President, Gentlemen Last August, the Ministry of Finance asked Banco de Portugal to represent itself in a Working Group set up to analyze the technical aspects associated with the negotiation of the transfer to Social Security of part of the credit institutions' pension funds. Banco de Portugal's participation in the Working Group was framed in the twofold perspective: 1. On the one hand, technical advice to the Government 2. and, on the other hand, to safeguard the stability of the financial system. These two aspects are part of the description of functions of Banco de Portugal, as set out in points (c) and (d) of Article 12 of its Organic Law1. 1 Law No. 5/98 of 31 January, with amendments introduced by DecreesLaw neros 118/2001, of April 17, 50/2004, of March 10, and 39/2007, of February 20. As part of the technical advice, Banco de Portugal contributed to the formulation of the government's position in negotiations with the banks. By the nature of the advice, it would make no sense for me to explain here the suggestions given to the Government in the course of the negotiation, in the certainty, however, that they have always been in the sense of helping the Government to safeguard the interest. Focusing then on my intervention in the issues related to the impact of the transaction on banks, in accounting and prudential terms, I would like to begin by clarifying that banco de Portugal does not have the specific supervision of the funds of penss associated with the banks, in particular in the aspects of the solvency of the funds, the composition of their asset portfolios and the value of those assets. This responsibility for supervising the funds of penss is assigned to the Insurance Institute of Portugal, whose President will have the opportunity to hear soon. Banco de Portugal, as part of its banking supervision functions, assesses the impacts of penss funds on banks' accounts, with a view to identifying risks to their financial soundness. The penss funds that have been partially transfered of lideiresponsibilities cover defined benefit plans. This means that the rules for calculating the penss are fixed at the outset and do not depend on the valuation and profitability of the assets accumulated by the funds. In these types of plans, the responsibility for the payment of the penss lies with the fund associate (i.e. the bank promoting the benefit plan), who has to make financial contributions whenever this becomes necessary to ensure the adequate provision of the estimated current value of future benefits payable to the fund. According to the regulations in force2, at each time of clearance of accounts the assets of the penss funds must cover: 100% of the estimated current value of lideation for pensioners and pensioners; And at least 95% of the current value of the responsibilities related to participants still in the asset. Estimates of the current value of future payments provided for in the penss plans, as well as the evolution of the valuation of the assets of the funds, are calculated on the basis of a set of actuatory and financial assumptions, which are assessed not only by the ISP but also by statutory auditors/auditors and actuaries. Over time, differences are determined, classified as actualyr deviations, which result both from deviations between the assumptions adopted and the observed annual evolution or from reviews of the assumptions. International accounting standards (more specifically IAS 19  Employee Benefits) allow two alternatives for the accounting treatment of actuary deviations. In one of these alternatives, the so-called corridor method, accumulated actuary deviations do not immediately affect the results of banks. According to this method, a threshold is defined, designated as "corridor", which corresponds to 10% of the greater than two values: 2 Notice No. 12/2001 from Banco de Portugal of November 9. The value of responsibilities; Or the value of the assets of the penss fund. Accumulated deviations within the corridor boundary do not affect results. Only the accumulated deviations exceeding this limit are reflected in the results of the banks, through a repayment plan, the maximum period of which corresponds to the average working life expectancy of the workers participating in the penss fund (in the case of Portuguese banks, this corresponds to between 15 and 20 years). As can be seen, the corridor method allows to mitigate the effects of the volatility of actuary deviations on the results of banks. When the European Union adoption of international accounting standards IAS/IFRS, the corridor method was the accounting policy followed by the generality of Portuguese banks (which relates to historical reasons, which have to do with the similarity with the accounting rules that were previously in force and which had been established by banco de Portugal). In the past few years, the impact of the financial crisis on the valuation of fund assets has led Portuguese banks to record accumulated actuary deviations well above the corridor limit. As regards the operation of transfer of the funds of penss in question, it should be noted at the outset that, on the initiative of Banco de Portugal, the National Council of Financial Supervisors carried out a joint reflection on the accounting treatment of the operation, and for this purpose a technical report was prepared, which it submitted to the Ministry of Finance. This report clarifies that the operation of transfer of funds from penss to social security falls within the concept of "liquidation" contemplated by IAS 19, describing in some detail the resulting accounting impacts in the sphere of credit institutions. It also clarifies that, 1. The use of the so-called "corridor method" implies recognition in results of the impact of the operation of two plots: the first tranche corresponding to the fraction of actuatory deviations that were yet to be recognised in public capital (before the operation), and in proportion to the lishes transferred; The second tranche corresponding to the result of any revaluations of the liabilities to be transferred or the value of the financial assets held by the think-bottom fund. 2. Recourse to the method of direct recognition in capital itself of actuary deviations, a method also accepted by IAS 19, entails attributing the impact of the transaction directly to capital items, such as reserves/results carried over (with this alternative accounting policy, the volatility of actuary deviations from the penss funds does not affect results, but rather the capital resources themselves). However, regardless of the accounting policy adopted on the treatment of actuary deviations, banks will have to immediately recognise in results the difference between: On the one hand, the value they have considered for the responsibilities and assets of the plan (according to their actuators); And, on the other hand, the conditions laid down for the transfer. The decisions of the banks on the use of the options available in the accounting standards that determine the registration and accounting impacts of the transaction are not yet known. However, the available estimates point to a negative impact on the results of the banks that will be a function of the accounting policy followed: 1. Without accounting policy change, the negative impact on results in 2011 will be more than EUR 2 million; 2. With the accounting policy change mentioned above, there will continue to be a negative impact, but that impact will have a clearly lower order of magnitude. In any case, the impact of the transfer will be reflected in the accounting capitals at the end of 2011  the difference is whether it affects the results of the financial year more or less. Moving now from the accounting plan to the prudential plan, it should be noted that, although the "corridor method" leads to deferred recognition of actual deviations, prudential treatment has been more conservative. Banco de Portugal requires that the excess of negative deviations (actuary losses) from the corridor be deducted immediately from the financial funds, thus affecting the calculation of capital adequacy ratios. The volatility associated with the assumption of responsibilities with penss, translated into the prudential recognition of these deviations, constitutes a significant structural disadvantage of Portuguese banking vis-a-vis european counterparts. With the partial transfer of pension funds to Social Security, an opportunity was created to substantially reduce the size of the problem by reducing exposure of the bank to the volatility of the value of the assets that make up its thinkfunds. As regards the prudential implications of the partial transfer of funds from penss to social security, as foreseen in the second revision of the Econica and Financial Assistance Programme, Banco de Portugal will issue regulations to defer, by 30 June 2012, the impacts on capital adequacy ratios. It should be recalled that the date of 30 June also corresponds to the deadline set by the European Banking Authority (EBA) in order to comply with the Recommendation of 8 December for the strengthening of the capital levels of the banking system, which includes the establishment of a temporary capital buffer to expose sovereign debt and compliance with a Core Tier 1 capital ratio of 9%. Accordingly, it was considered appropriate to combine the deadline for meeting the overall needs for strengthening financial funds, pointing to this effect the date of 30 June 2012 set by the EBA. As the credit institutions may have a change in their accounting policy, which results in the adoption of the direct recognition in capital benefit method, Banco de Portugal will also issue regulations to ensure a neutral application of prudential standards on a continuity basis, i.e. to ensure that prudential treatment related to pension funds does not vary depending on the accounting policy adopted by the Banks. The available estimates point to a prudential impact resulting from the partial transfer to Social Security of the funds of penss which will be around 25% of the amount transferred (i.e. about 1500 million euros). According to the second revision of the Memorandum of Understanding for the Assistance Programme, it will be desirable that any additional capital needs be met through private sources. However, if this is not possible, state funding will be made available through participation in the capital of banks, using part of the money transferred from the pension funds. I must point out, on the very hand, that it was agreed with the European Union and the International Monetary Fund that part of the EUR 12 billion amount provided for in the Bank Recapitalisation Assistance Programme will not be used for this purpose. I am at your disposal to answer questions that you understand how to formulate about the operation in the areas of participation and responsibility of Banco de Portugal. As you will understand, I will refrain from answering questions outside the areas of participation and responsibility of Banco de Portugal, questions which will have to be addressed to the Government or the relevant entities. Carlos da Silva Costa
text_original: Audio do Governador do Banco de Portugal pelas Comisss Parlamentares de Oramento, Finanas e Administrao Plica e de Segurana Social e Trabalho Transferncia dos fundos de penss dos trabalhadores bancrios para a Segurana Social, 6 de Janeiro de 2012 Senhor Presidente, Senhores Deputados, No passado ms de Agosto, o Ministrio das Finanas solicitou ao Banco de Portugal que se fizesse representar num Grupo de Trabalho constitudo para a anlise dos aspectos tcnicos associados  negociao da transferncia para a Segurana Social de parte dos fundos de penss das instituis de crdito. A participao do Banco de Portugal no Grupo de Trabalho foi enquadrada na dupla perspectiva: 1. Por um lado, de aconselhamento tcnico ao Governo 2. e, por outro lado, de salvaguarda da estabilidade do sistema financeiro. Estas duas vertentes fazem parte da descrio de funs do Banco de Portugal, conforme estabelecido nas alneas (c) e (d) do Artigo 12 da sua Lei Orgnica1. 1 Lei n 5/98 de 31 de Janeiro, com alteras introduzidas pelos Decretoslei neros 118/2001, de 17 de Abril, 50/2004, de 10 de Maro, e 39/2007, de 20 de Fevereiro. No mbito do aconselhamento tcnico, o Banco de Portugal contribuiu para a formulao das posis do Governo nas negocias com os bancos. Pela natureza prria do aconselhamento, no faria sentido que eu explicitasse aqui as sugests dadas ao Governo no decurso da negociao, na certeza, porm, de que elas foram sempre no sentido de ajudar o Governo a salvaguardar o interesse plico. Centrando ento a minha interveno nas quests relacionadas com o impacto da operao para os bancos, em termos contabilsticos e prudenciais, gostaria de comear por esclarecer que no cabe ao Banco de Portugal a superviso especfica dos fundos de penss associados aos bancos, nomeadamente nos aspectos referentes  solvabilidade dos fundos,  composio das suas carteiras de activos e  valorimetria desses activos. Essa responsabilidade de superviso dos fundos de penss est atribuda ao Instituto de Seguros de Portugal, cujo Presidente tero a oportunidade de ouvir proximamente. O Banco de Portugal, no mbito das suas funs de superviso bancria, avalia os impactos dos fundos de penss nas contas dos bancos, numa perspectiva de identificao de riscos para a sua solidez financeira. Os fundos de penss que foram alvo de transferncia parcial de responsabilidades cobrem planos de benefcio definido. Tal significa que as regras de clculo das penss esto fixadas  partida e no dependem da valorizao e rendibilidade dos activos acumulados pelos fundos. Neste tipo de planos, a responsabilidade tima pelo pagamento das penss cabe ao associado do fundo (isto , ao banco promotor do plano de benefcios), que tem de realizar contribuis financeiras sempre que isso se torne necessrio para garantir o provisionamento adequado do valor actual estimado dos benefcios futuros a cargo do fundo. De acordo com a regulamentao em vigor2, em cada momento de apuramento de contas os activos dos fundos de penss tm de cobrir:  100% do valor actual estimado das responsabilidades para pensionistas e reformados;  E pelo menos 95% da estimativa do valor actual das responsabilidades relacionadas com participantes ainda no activo. As estimativas do valor actual dos pagamentos futuros previstos nos planos de penss, bem como da evoluo da valorizao dos activos dos fundos, so calculadas com base num conjunto de pressupostos actuariais e financeiros, que so objecto de avaliao no s pelo ISP mas tambm por revisores oficiais de contas/auditores e acturios. Ao longo do tempo so apuradas diferenas, classificadas como desvios actuariais, que resultam quer de afastamentos entre os pressupostos adoptados e a evoluo anual observada quer de revises dos pressupostos. As normas internacionais de contabilidade (mais especificamente o IAS 19  Employee Benefits) admitem duas alternativas para o tratamento contabilstico dos desvios actuariais. Numa dessas alternativas, o chamado mtodo do corredor, os desvios actuariais acumulados no afectam imediatamente os resultados dos bancos. De acordo com este mtodo,  definido um limiar, designado como corredor, que corresponde a 10% do maior de dois valores: 2 Aviso n 12/2001 do Banco de Portugal, de 9 de Novembro.  O valor das responsabilidades;  Ou do valor dos activos do fundo de penss. Os desvios acumulados dentro do limite do corredor no afectam resultados. Apenas os desvios acumulados que excedam esse limite so reflectidos nos resultados dos bancos, atravs de um plano de amortizao, cujo prazo mximo corresponde  esperana mdia de vida activa dos trabalhadores participantes do fundo de penss (no caso dos bancos portugueses, tal corresponde a entre 15 e 20 anos). Como se percebe, o mtodo do corredor permite atenuar os efeitos da volatilidade dos desvios actuariais sobre os resultados dos bancos. Aquando da adopo das normas internacionais de contabilidade IAS/IFRS pela Unio Europeia, o mtodo do corredor foi a poltica contabilstica seguida pela generalidade dos bancos portugueses (o que se prende com razs histicas, que tm a ver com a semelhana com as regras contabilsticas que estavam anteriormente em vigor e que tinham sido estabelecidas pelo Banco de Portugal). Nos timos anos, o impacto da crise financeira na valorizao dos activos dos fundos levou a que os bancos portugueses registassem desvios actuariais acumulados bastante superiores ao limite do corredor. No que respeita  operao de transferncia dos fundos de penss em questo, importa desde logo realar que, por iniciativa do Banco de Portugal, o Conselho Nacional de Supervisores Financeiros efectuou uma reflexo conjunta sobre o tratamento contabilstico da operao, tendo para o efeito sido elaborado um relatio tcnico, que submeteu ao Ministrio das Finanas. Este relatio esclarece que a operao de transferncia dos fundos de penss para a Segurana Social se enquadra no conceito de liquidao contemplado pelo IAS 19, descrevendose com algum detalhe os decorrentes impactos contabilsticos na esfera das instituis de crdito. E tambm clarifica que, 1. O recurso ao chamado mtodo do corredor implica o reconhecimento em resultados do impacto da operao de duas parcelas:  A primeira parcela correspondente  fraco dos desvios actuariais que estavam ainda por reconhecer em capitais prrios (antes da operao), e na proporo das responsabilidades transferidas;  A segunda parcela correspondente ao resultado de eventuais reavalias das responsabilidades a transferir ou do valor dos activos financeiros detidos pelo fundo de penses. 2. O recurso ao mtodo do reconhecimento directo em capital prprio dos desvios actuariais, mtodo tambm admitido pelo IAS 19, implicar imputar o impacto da operao directamente a rubricas dos capitais prrios, como sejam reservas/resultados transitados (com esta poltica contabilstica alternativa, a volatilidade dos desvios actuariais dos fundos de penss no afecta resultados, mas sim os capitais prrios). No entanto, e independentemente da poltica contabilstica adoptada quanto ao tratamento dos desvios actuariais, os bancos tero de reconhecer imediatamente em resultados a diferena entre:  Por um lado, o valor que tenham considerado para as responsabilidades e para os activos do plano (de acordo com os seus pressupostos actuariais);  E, por outro lado, as condis fixadas para a transferncia. Ainda no se conhecem as deciss dos bancos sobre o uso das ops disponveis nas normas contabilsticas que determinam o registo e os impactos contabilsticos da operao. No entanto, as estimativas disponveis apontam para um impacto negativo nos resultados dos bancos que ser funo da poltica contabilstica seguida: 1. Sem alterao de poltica contabilstica, o impacto negativo nos resultados, em 2011, ser superior a 2 mil milhs de euros; 2. Com a alterao de poltica contabilstica, antes mencionada, continuar a existir impacto negativo, mas esse impacto ter uma ordem de grandeza claramente inferior. Em qualquer caso, o impacto decorrente da transferncia ficar reflectido nos capitais prrios contabilsticos no final de 2011  a diferena  se afecta mais ou menos os resultados do exerccio. Passando agora do plano contabilstico para o plano prudencial, convm destacar que, apesar de o mtodo do corredor conduzir a um reconhecimento diferido dos desvios actuariais, o tratamento prudencial tem sido mais conservador. Com efeito, o Banco de Portugal requer que o excesso de desvios negativos (perdas actuariais) face ao corredor seja deduzido de imediato aos fundos prrios, afectando deste modo o clculo dos rcios de adequao de capital. A volatilidade associada  assuno de responsabilidades com penss, traduzida no reconhecimento prudencial daqueles desvios, constitui uma significativa desvantagem estrutural da banca portuguesa face s congneres europeias. Com a transferncia parcial dos fundos de penss para a Segurana Social, criouse uma oportunidade de reduzir substancialmente a dimenso do problema, diminuindo a exposio da banca  volatilidade do valor dos activos que integram os respectivos fundos de penses. No que respeita s implicas no plano prudencial da operao de transferncia parcial dos fundos de penss para a Segurana Social, tal como est previsto na segunda reviso do Programa de Assistncia Econica e Financeira, o Banco de Portugal ir emitir regulamentao para diferir, at 30 de Junho de 2012, os impactos nos rcios de adequao de capital. Deve ser lembrado que a data de 30 de Junho corresponde tambm  datalimite estabelecida pela Autoridade Bancria Europeia (European Banking Authority EBA), para se dar cumprimento  Recomendao de 8 de Dezembro para o reforo dos nveis de capital do sistema bancrio, na qual se inclui a constituio de um buffer temporrio de capital para exposis a dvida soberana e o cumprimento de um rcio de capital Core Tier 1 de 9%. Nestes termos, foi considerado adequado conjugar o prazo para o cumprimento da globalidade das necessidades de reforo de fundos prrios, apontando para o efeito a data de 30 de Junho de 2012 fixada pela EBA. Em virtude de poder vir a verificarse, por opo das instituis de crdito, uma alterao da sua poltica contabilstica que se traduza na adopo do mtodo do reconhecimento directo em capital prrio, o Banco de Portugal ir tambm emitir regulamentao para garantir uma aplicao neutral das normas prudenciais numa base de continuidade, isto , para assegurar que o tratamento prudencial relacionado com fundos de penss no varia em funo da poltica contabilstica adoptada pelos bancos. As estimativas disponveis apontam para um impacto prudencial resultante da operao de transferncia parcial para a Segurana Social dos fundos de penss que rondar 25% do valor transferido (isto , cerca de 1500 milhs de euros). De acordo com a segunda reviso do Memorando de Entendimento para o Programa de Assistncia, ser desejvel que as eventuais necessidades adicionais de capital sejam satisfeitas atravs de fontes privadas. No entanto, se tal no for possvel, ser disponibilizado financiamento do Estado atravs de participao no capital dos bancos, com recurso a parte da verba transferida dos fundos de penss. Devo salientar, a propito, que ficou acordado com a Unio Europeia e o Fundo Monetrio Internacional que no ser utilizada para o efeito parte da verba de 12 mil milhs de euros prevista no Programa de Assistncia para recapitalizao dos bancos. Fico  vossa disposio para responder a quests que entendam formular sobre a operao nos domnios de participao e de responsabilidade do Banco de Portugal. Como os senhores Deputados compreendero, abstermeei de responder a quests fora dos domnios de participao e de responsabilidade do Banco de Portugal, quests que tero de ser endereadas ao Governo ou s entidades relevantes. Carlos da Silva Costa

Title: Speech by Vice-Governor Clara Raposo at the Webinar "The challenges of climate regulation for banks" promoted by GRACE  Responsible Companies
text: GRACE  Responsible Companies Webinar: The challenges of climate regulation for banks December 7 (11:00-12:45) Keynote speech: The impact of climate risks on the financial system (11:05-11:30) Vice-Governor Clara Raposo Good morning everyone, I would like to begin by thanking GRACE and Dr. Margarida Couto for the kind invitation that was addressed to Banco de Portugal to develop some ideas on climate change at the opening of this timely event. I also greet the speakers in the following panel and the participants in this webinar, which is indeed particularly timely because the first week of COP28 in Dubai concluded yesterday and we are reaching the culmination of this key conference that every year (except at the peak of the pandemic) puts the climate crisis at the center of the attention of world public opinion. Unfortunately, we have not received good news from that region of the world in the last two months. But perhaps the climate issue can now convey a slightly more positive note. The first signs that are reaching us seem to give some hope, in matters such as the financial instrument for compensating for loss and damage associated with climate change (climatechange and damage) or the fight against methane emissions, that other gas less known than carbon dioxide, but with a greenhouse effect eighty times more powerful, although less durable in the atmosphere. Today I will start by recalling what is at stake with the climate crisis and what can  or should  be expected from public decision-makers in this matter. I will then share some considerations on the importance of the financial system in this context and on what the European authorities are doing to frame and enhance sustainable finance  in essence, this is the first major challenge that the climate crisis poses to the financial system: taking advantage of the financing opportunities provided by the climate transition. Finally, I will focus on how Banco de Portugal is dealing with climate and environmental risks in the banking sector, both from the perspective of financial stability and from the perspective of microprudential supervision  basically, this is the second major challenge posed to the financial system in this context: identifying and managing climate risks. What is at stake with climate change is well known: a sharp increase in the concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere since the beginning of the industrial era, which will have been decisive for an increase in the average global temperature already estimated at more than 1.1C. The consequences of this phenomenon seem increasingly visible, in the increasingly frequent occurrence of increasingly destructive extreme weather events. And the way forward  to respond to this real existential threat, which mainly affects the poorest  is a path that has also been mapped out for a long time: a global effort, because it is a global problem, which combines mitigation, adaptation and transition. It is important to bear in mind this notion of transition. The idea that we are facing a process of climate evolution, which implies a profound transformation of behaviour, but which is also, in essence, a process of energy transition. The idea, after all, that there is a way to go in order to achieve the famous goals of the Paris Agreement: to limit the increase in the global average temperature to no more than 1.5C  well below 2.0C  from the beginning of the industrial era. There is a way, but it will require decades of continued effort and the commitment of public decision-makers, private sector companies and society as a whole. What is called Mitigating the problem means reducing greenhouse gas emissions globally and possibly stabilising, or even decreasing, the volume of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. To this end, the two main instruments in terms of public policies are identified  those that can produce the most effective results in defining incentives and changing behaviour.  On the one hand, discouraging emissions by pricing carbon in line with the high social cost of emissions with its relatively low private cost  is the classic example of what economists call a negative externality. This can be done through emission allowances or taxes  but it does not necessarily have to mean an increase in the total tax burden. The IMF estimates that the average cost of carbon emissions is currently around 6 per tonne and that it will be necessary to reach 75 by 2030. Such a mechanism is important to drive the shift in the choice of carbon-emitting energy sources to cleaner ones, provided they are available.  On the other hand, to promote research and development initiatives in the area of climate, involving an effort by companies and academia, but also the granting of subsidies by public entities, in areas less suitable for private intervention. Such a policy is important, as scientific and technological progress is still needed if we are to be able to replace, on an appropriate scale, the current energy sources that are most harmful to the environment. In both cases, these are public interventions that clearly refer to the sphere of activity of governments. But this does not mean that financial institutions and their supervisors do not have a role to play in the global effort to respond to climate change. It is enough to recall the fact that this effort will have to be financial, involving amounts of investment  to finance the energy transition  which have been estimated by several reference institutions at close to one trillion dollars per year, or about 1% of world GDP, over the next few decades. And we are talking only about the investment that is not enough, that is, beyond what would always be necessary to make in order to replace the fixed capital. Considering the total investment, which will also tend to be implemented in a logic of energy transition, these are values that are clearly beyond the capacity of public budgets, which are already overburdened. They will thus be values that will require substantial and growing involvement of the private sector. And this means, of course, the involvement of the financial system  and above all the banking system  in the European Union, which, as we know, is the predominant segment in the financial universe; despite the commitment to promote initiatives  which are also very important - such as the development of capital markets and even their union. The commitment to financing the energy transition is, therefore, a first major challenge that climate change poses to the financial system. And it is also the most important and urgent challenge posed to the financial system by this whole ESG  environmental, social and governance institutions  which has been so much in focus in world public opinion and global financial markets, especially in the last decade. Not long ago, McKinsey reported that the number of internet searches for the term "ESG" had multiplied by five, since 2019 only. And this, despite all the events that have demanded our attention in these extraordinary years that we have been experiencing: such as the pandemic, Russia's invasion of Ukraine, the ebb and flow of inflationary pressures in advanced economies, the signs of a retreat from globalization, or the rise of artificial intelligence. The increasing attention given to ESG sustainability issues has been captured and reflected, to some extent, by global financial markets. It is a trend largely driven by the urgency of the climate crisis, but which goes beyond it, as it also reflects society's more general concerns, regarding issues such as increasing transparency in the management of institutions or reducing the various inequalities that we are identifying. A good synthetic indicator of this trend is the market value of the assets under management of investment funds considered sustainable  on a global scale. Despite the market fluctuations in the last two years, the trend is clear and markedly upward  although ESG funds still represent a small portion of total funds: around 6.2%. The European authorities have been very active in this matter of sustainability from an ESG perspective, reacting to market developments and, above all, seeking to frame and promote this evolution. This has resulted in a significant set of legislative and regulatory initiatives, which cover different aspects of the ESG universe and have placed the European Union at the forefront of regulatory developments on a global scale, also in this matter. The Portuguese Government participates in the definition of these initiatives, as is typical of the European process, and the Bank of Portugal has provided technical support to the Ministry of Finance in this context, as is its statutory obligation in matters of an economic and financial nature. I believe that the following panel will address in greater detail the dilemmas posed by this ambitious high tide of regulation, so I leave here only a synthetic preview of some of its main elements.
