Um dos produtos deste esfor<8d>o de investiga<8d><8b>o e an<87>lise <8e> o nosso primeiro relat<97>rio anual sobre a exposi<8d><8b>o do setor banc<87>rio ao risco clim<87>tico, que public<87>mos em julho passado, cumprindo uma obriga<8d><8b>o que decorre da Lei de Bases do Clima. O relat<97>rio abrange tamb<8e>m a segunda vertente, de supervis<8b>o microprudencial (de que falarei adiante), e <8e> particularmente original, no contexto internacional, por essa op<8d><8b>o abrangente. Entre os seus principais resultados est<87> a constata<8d><8b>o de que a transi<8d><8b>o clim<87>tica <d0> sobretudo se for <d2>ordeira<d3>, mas mesmo se for tardia <d0> <8e> prefer<92>vel <88> manuten<8d><8b>o das atuais pr<87>ticas, do ponto de vista do setor banc<87>rio. Apesar de um custo acrescido a curto prazo, esse processo de transi<8d><8b>o acaba por ser mais do que compensado a longo prazo. <83> igualmente interessante verificar que as empresas n<8b>o-financeiras com atividades mais intensivas em carbono s<8b>o as que mais se ressentem de uma transi<8d><8b>o tardia. Nesta mat<8e>ria, temos diversos outros estudos em curso. Por outro lado, a segunda vertente da nossa atua<8d><8b>o em mat<8e>ria de estabilidade financeira consiste em adaptar a nossa abordagem de supervis<8b>o por forma a incentivar os bancos <88> incorpora<8d><8b>o dos riscos clim<87>ticos e ambientais nas diversas <87>reas relevantes da sua atividade. Com esse intuito, adot<87>mos um guia onde comunicamos ao sistema as nossas expectativas de supervis<8b>o quanto <88> gest<8b>o dos riscos clim<87>ticos e ambientais, quer ao n<92>vel do Mecanismo <f2>nico de Supervis<8b>o quer na sua aplica<8d><8b>o aos bancos de menores dimens<9b>es, que est<8b>o sob a supervis<8b>o direta exclusiva do Banco de Portugal. E temos vindo a avaliar a forma como a banca est<87> a incorporar essas expectativas, que passar<8b>o a ser de cumprimento imperativo a partir de 2025. <83> um exerc<92>cio que se desenvolve tendo como base o quadro geral tradicionalmente estabele- cido para a supervis<8b>o prudencial e que assenta tamb<8e>m na materialidade dos riscos clim<87>ticos e ambientais. Nessa medida, as expectativas abarcam quatro dimens<9b>es cr<92>ticas da atividade banc<87>ria: as estrat<8e>gias de neg<97>cio, os modelos de governo interno, os procedimentos de ges- t<8b>o do risco e os sistemas para a divulga<8d><8b>o de informa<8d><8b>o relevante. Uma dificuldade adicional com que, no setor, todos nos deparamos <8e> a da qualidade da infor- ma<8d><8b>o que recolhemos. Os bancos t<90>m de nos reportar de que forma os seus clientes est<8b>o expostos a risco clim<87>ticos <d0> <8e> um mundo novo de dados, com metodologia ainda n<8b>o total- mente estabilizada e que depende da informa<8d><8b>o que as empresas disponibilizam. Ou seja, a natureza do exerc<92>cio <8e> ainda algo explorat<97>ria. Temos muito caminho a fazer. E concluo, agora que nos vamos aproximando da quadra festiva e da transi<8d><8b>o para um novo ano, fazendo votos de que o per<92>odo de Natal e o ano 2024 nos tragam boas prendas em ma- t<8e>ria de clima.

Title: Closing Remarks by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the ECB Youth Dialogue
text: Youth, innovation and productivity in Europe Closing Remarks by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa1 1 Version prepared for presentation. ISEG, 26 June 2017 Speaking points, It is with great pleasure and satisfaction that Banco de Portugal worked with the ECB and the Lisbon School of Economics and Management (ISEG) to organize the first ECB Youth Dialogue in Lisbon. This seminar provided an important opportunity for economics students to put questions to the ECB President, Mr. Mario Draghi, on issues that concern them. This initiative clearly demonstrates the ECBs endeavor to be an open institution that is close to society, in particular to the European youth. Turning now to the topic of this dialogue, Youth, Innovation and Productivity in Europe, I would like to start by pointing out that we live in a challenging world, both in social and economic terms, but that this should not be seen as a negative because, if prepared for and overcome, challenges lead to progress. The very fast pace of technological progress permanently challenges countries productive structures and firms. Indeed, products with high demand at one point in time may become outdated after a couple of years, as new goods offer new functionalities and higher quality. The Schumpeterian notion of creative destruction is nowadays more relevant than ever. Therefore, flexibility in the allocation of resources is key to minimizing the inevitable adjustment costs faced by the economies. Moreover, international competition is also very strong as firms struggle to offer cheaper and improved versions of recent innovations. Therefore, continuing innovation is the only way to create and maintain high value-added in the economy, which, in turn, is the basis of productivity and social welfare. The common ingredient to achieving flexibility and continuing innovation in the economy is human capital. That is why education and science policies have become a top policy priority in most countries. There is also a strong link between human capital, good management and entrepreneurship. The ability to restructure and sometimes reinvent a firm in the face of a negative shock asks for good management skills. Moreover, innovation in the production process is nourished by entrepreneurs and, in the event of radical innovation, they are the ones taking the risk of bringing new products or services to the test of the market. It should be noted that human capital is a necessary but insufficient condition to achieve flexibility and innovation in the economy. Entrepreneurship is also a key condition, which depends on a complex combination of a risk-taking culture, an adequate private and public institutional setup and financial mechanisms that promote the sharing of the risk that is intrinsic to the innovation process. Moreover, the importance of entrepreneurship and the difficulty in putting in place its underlying prerequisites is stronger for more radical innovations. Portugal has been catching up with EU levels in terms of human capital. Although it started from comparatively low education levels, the cohorts of Portuguese students that are now entering the labour market are perfectly comparable to those in other advanced economies. In addition, new Portuguese graduates have often had the chance to interact with foreign colleagues and institutions, which fosters a healthy critical attitude that also prompts entrepreneurship. In the cohort of 25- to 34-year-olds, the share of individuals that completed at least upper secondary education in Portugal increased from 30 per cent in 1995 to 70 per cent in 2016, while the shares in the EU are 70 per cent and 82 per cent, respectively. Moreover, the share of 25- to 34-year-old individuals with tertiary education in 2016 was 35 per cent in Portugal, against 39 per cent in the average for the EU countries (Chart 1 and 2). These very good developments are already bearing fruit in the economy and are part of the explanation for the good performance of Portuguese exports in the latest decade. There are many examples of new production processes being implemented by young managers in traditional sectors, for example, in textiles, clothing and agriculture, while radical innovation has been taking place in sectors like health and pharmaceuticals, engineering and software. Recent success in no way precludes the need for renewed efforts. There is plenty of untapped potential in the Portuguese innovation system. For example, the number of doctorates per thousand individuals in the 25- to 34-year-old cohort in Portugal is 70 per cent above that of the EU average. However, the share of innovative SMEs that engage in collaborations represents only 6.8 per cent of the total pool of SMEs in Portugal, against a figure of 10.3 per cent in the EU. Therefore, it is necessary to strengthen bridges between research centers, universities and firms. This overall picture is visible in the results of the European Innovation Scoreboard for Portugal (Chart 3 and 4). The Portuguese policies for research and development have been taking this direction, notably by putting in place specific programs that link the scientific system and firms (e.g. Programa Interface), leading to the creation of collaborative labs and to a visible increase in the take-up rates of available EU funds for science. Let me conclude with four ideas that run through much of what has been said. Firstly, innovation is a continuing process or even a state of mind. It should not be forgotten that sometimes innovation requires long research periods, reaching up to 10 or 15 years. Support for long-term research is necessary, it can hardly be provided by firms and is now an important item in the European research policy discussion. Secondly, the pool of startups is important because it constitutes the cradle of the successful firms of the future. Nevertheless, the early failure of most of these firms should not be taken as problematic. The high mortality rate of startups is, to a large extent, the result of a natural process of selection of good ideas and efficient firms by market forces. Therefore, public policies targeted at supporting startups that have not proven able to compete in the markets are expensive and clearly not efficient. Thirdly, as a follow-up to the previous point, the financing of radical innovation or startups is not the primary role of the banking system. The high levels of risk involved call for the intervention of specialized operators (for example venture capital or business angels). Unfortunately, in Portugal these operators are still not sufficiently developed, and the possibility of ventures with larger foreign players is limited. Fourthly, the challenge in Portugal is to speed up the pace of reform and further modernize its firms. Only high-performance firms can afford to pay the wages of those that make the difference in terms of innovation and entrepreneurship. Although foreign experience by young Portuguese highly skilled workers is beneficial, it should not turn into a mild form of brain drain. However, as initially said, challenges should be seen as opportunities to improve, not as problems. Thank you very much.

Title: Statement by the Governor, Carlos da Silva Costa, at the Hearing by the Committee on Budget, Finance and Administrative Modernization on the Novo Banco
text: Statement by the Governor of Banco de Portugal at Committee on Budget, Finance and Administrative Modernization in the context of the hearing held in May 2, 2019 Madam President, Ladies and gentlemen, 1. I present myself to this Commission following a request from the Parliamentary Group of the Socialist Party regarding the announcement by Novo Banco, S.A. ("Novo Banco"), that it was necessary to ask the Resolution Fund for a payment of EUR 1.149 million under the contingent capitalisation mechanism provided for in the contracts for the sale to Lone Star of a 75% stake in that bank. This request raises a set of questions about the resolution process of Banco Espirito Santo, S.A. ("Banco Espirito Santo" or "BES") and about the sale process of Novo Banco. In view of the values involved, I fully understand that it is necessary to recover the explanations on the resolution process and therefore I reiterate the full willingness of Banco de Portugal to provide all the clarifications that this Commission considers relevant. I would also like to begin by making it clear to this Commission that  even in view of the amounts that are being required of the Resolution Fund under the contingent capitalisation mechanism  Banco de Portugal maintains the full conviction that banco Espirito Santo's resolution has not only avoided serious losses to the financial system, for the national economy and also for the public office, as it was implemented in appropriate terms and in full compliance with the law. This conviction was, moreover, recently confirmed by the judgment of the Administrative Court of Circulo de Lisboa, delivered on 12 March in a pilot case in the context of the concentration of cases relating to the decision to apply the resolution measure to Banco Espirito Santo. 2. At this hearing I will therefore seek to address the main issues that have been raised in the work of this Commission, but also in the public space, and I will try to remove the doubts that still seem to exist. But I stress that, due to its unavoidable complexity and the values and interests affected, it is only possible to correctly understand the resolution process of Banco Espirito Santo if there is a frank willingness to know the reasons that are at the origin of the different decisions and to evaluate and scrutinize them without any motivation other than that of the defense of the public interest. 3. I will seek, more specifically, to address with objectivity and on the basis of concrete facts, certain judgments made regarding the process of resolution of the BES and the sale process of Novo Banco. In some cases, the judgments to which I refer show insufficient knowledge of the applicable regulatory framework or of the concrete circumstances in which the resolution of the BES and the chain of events that followed it took place, which is why It seems necessary to provide further explanations of banco de Portugal's action. To this end, it is useful to begin by stating some observations which, more or less frequently, appear in the public space or in the work of this Commission on the bes resolution process and which I summarise as this: I. "The resolution decision was inadequate and disproportionate and should have ensured the subsistence of BES"; II. "The assets responsible for Novo Banco's losses should not have been transferred to Novo Banco"; III. "The assets transferred to Novo Banco were misvalued at the time of the BES resolution"; IV. "Banco de Portugal did not endy the Novo Banco with sufficient capital at the time of its constitution"; V. "The New Bank should not have been sold" or "its sale should have been carried out with more time"; VI. "The sale of Novo Banco was not a competitive process"; VII. "In the sale of Novo Banco, the contingent capitalization mechanism should not have been foreseen." 4. On the first question  i.e. on the question of whether "the resolution decision was inadequate and disproportionate and should have ensured the subsistence of bes"  I will structure the explanations due on the basis of three facts: At the beginning of August 2014 Banco Espirito Santo was in a situation of irreparable financial imbalance. The events in late July and early August 2014 created a situation in which the bank was no longer able to engage in banking activity: losses in the first half of that year, or more rigorously the unexpected component of those losses (which was very substantial) caused a serious capital shortfall; liquidity difficulties have worsened to the point where the central bank's capacity to be recourse to emergency financing is exhausted; and the exclusion of the Eurosystem would require immediate reimbursement of the financing obtained there, without bes having any possibility of fulfilling that obligation. On the other hand, there was no alternative for the viability of Banco Espirito Santo; The only way available to Banco de Portugal to prevent BES from abruptly ceasing its activity in August 2014 and being subject to a sudden and disorderly liquidation, in those circumstances and in the short time available, was to create a new institution, from BES, to which it was possible to transfer most of the bes activity and which deserved the trust of the European Central Bank to be able to take the seat of BES as a eurosystem's party. 5. The need for a resolution measure to be a resolution has already been submitted to abundant explanations and all the grounds, in particular in previous hearings before this Commission and in a committee of inquiry. Nevertheless, it is important to recover briefly the facts that led to the resolution, not only because punctually there is still the suggestion that the subsistence of the BES would have been possible, but above all because the full awareness that the BES was in a situation of irreparable imbalance is fundamental to properly and fairly assess the resolution process. It is then worth recalling the most relevant facts: On July 30, 2014, Banco Espirito Santo reported a loss of 3,577 million euros for the first half of that year, far exceeding the forecast sums in light of the information available until the last two weeks of July. These losses, of an unexpected and exceptional size, reflected the effect of management acts seriously damaging the interests of the bank, known only to a restricted group of persons, which caused an additional loss of around EUR 1,500 million compared to previous estimates. In view of the size of the losses, the EUR 2.1 billion capital cushion available to BES to deal with exposure to the non-financial branch of the Espirito Santo Group was consumed and widely exceeded (according to the communication to the market by the bank itself on 10 July), and BES was placed in a situation of severe non-compliance with the minimum capital ratios in force. On 31 July 2014, Banco de Portugal was informed by the Executive Board of the ECB that, in view of the non-compliance with the minimum capital requirements and in the absence of a capitalisation plan by BES, it would propose to the governing council to suspend the status of bes as a counterparty to the Eurosystem's monetary policy. On 1 August 2014 the Governing Council decided to suspend bes's status as a subsidiary with effect on 4 August, determining that, on the same date, bes credit with the Eurosystem of around EUR 10 billion should be reimbursed in full. By the same time, BES was already in a situation of severe liquidity shortfall, which had forced it to resort to emergency liquidity-making operations, so the ECB's decision, caused by non-compliance with prudential ratios, made it clear that the bank was at serious and serious risk of short-term default of its obligations and, requirements for the maintenance of the authorisation for the exercise of banking. 6. It was, therefore, in this context of extreme gravity and urgency, and after it was also confirmed that there were no prospects for recovery of the bank, that the resolution measure was applied as a solution of last resort to avoid the disorderly liquidation of Banco Espirito Santo. All this has already been said by myself before this Commission and in a committee of inquiry, but today there are also judicial decisions that confirm it. The need to apply the resolution measure and its reasonableness and proportionality to the situation in which the BES was found were already assessed in court by the Administrative Court of Circulo de Lisboa in its unanimous judgment on the bes resolution measure (Proc. no. 2586/14.3 BELSB and Proc. no. 2808/14.0BELSB by appendage). In that regard, the Court expressly states the following: "given the concrete circumstances in which the BES was in, there was no alternative scenario [to the resolution] other than the settlement of BES, since it was not even in a position to maintain the authorisation to the exercise of its activity, being totally hypothetical and untraceable any scenario other than that" (fls. 213, 1) "it is clear that the resolution measure is reasonable, because of the weighting between the sacrifices that would occur in the event of liquidation  the only alternative scenario to the resolution  and those that occur in a resolution process, it is demonstrated that the benefits of this latter solution are greater than those of a liquidation, not only by pursuing the intended purposes, as well as the way in which it achieves these ends" (fls. 213, 2) "And the [resolution] measure, in the face of all the foregoing, cannot be said to have been adequate, since it ensured 'the continuity of the provision of essential financial services', has ensured the 'systemic risk', since otherwise there would have been, in the eyes of ordinary experience, a rush to deposit withdrawals, 'the interests of taxpayers and the public excarry' would have been safeguarded, rather than what would happen in any other scenario (...)" (fls. 212, 7). 7. On the other hand, the allegation that there would have been unexplored recapitalization routes of Banco Espirito Santo on the basis of private capital would still arise on time. In fact, there is no record of effective private investment proposals in the capitalization of BES after the disclosure of the bank's losses for the first half of 2014 and in the context of the new circumstances created by such disclosure. For the avoidance of doubt on this matter, it should be recalled that Banco de Portugal formally requested the Board of Directors of Banco Espirito Santo, on July 29, 2014, to submit, within the period required by the circumstances, a capitalization plan whose implementation would allow the reinforcement of own funds to adequate levels of solvency. It was banco Espirito Santo's own Board of Directors that confirmed, by letter of July 31, 2014, that it was not able to correspond to banco de Portugal's determination. 8. On this too there are today judicial decisions confirming what had already been explained by me on previous occasions. As stated by the Administrative Court of Circulo de Lisboa in its unanimous judgment on the bes resolution measure (Proc. no. 2586/14.3 BELSB): "(...) what is invoked in these cases is the violation [of the principle of impartiality, in its positive aspect] on the fact that Banco de Portugal did not consider in its decision the possibility of other alternatives the application of a resolution measure, no means private recapitalisation. However, as evidenced that it is evident, it is quite clear that such interest and possibility was taken into account by Banco de Portugal, in particular when it raised an effective recapitalisation plan before the decision, which was not viable in that short period. It is understood that, although it was invoked by BES itself, in its message in response to Banco de Portugal, that '[n]the last few weeks, the Bank has witnessed expressions of interest from current and potential shareholders in participating in the Capitalization Plan, some expressing even interest in taking significant stakes. This same information was transmitted to the management team by the financial advisor (Deutsche Bank) who, as recently reported, was hired by the Bank to advise on the optimization of the structure of its balance sheet, so it is expected that this capitalization will be materialisable', nothing concrete was presented, in the letter of the Board of Directors of BES, but mere expressions of interest that always refer to a period prior to the disclosure of results for the first half of 2014, that is, on July 30." (fls 230, 6 and 231, 1st). 9. The question of the hypothetical intervention of the State to enable the subsistence of Banco Espirito Santo is also raised on time, in particular through its nationalization. On this hypothesis, it should be stressed that it was not within banco de Portugal's reach: Banco de Portugal can only act within its framework of competences and the tasks conferred on it by the law and does not have the powers to nationalise credit institutions. But it is also said that the hypothetical use of state resources to allow the subsistence of BES  which was never within banco de Portugal's reach  would not meet the objective of minimizing costs for taxpayers, on the contrary. In fact, the losses that have been manifested since August 2014 reflect, for the most part, the quality of the existing assets in BES and would certainly have manifested themselves in any other case. It follows that only the resolution mechanism could allow, as was the case, that the losses were not fully assumed by the State and were shared, as indeed happened, with BES shareholders in the first place and also with creditors and, finally, with the Resolution Fund, even if financed by the State. Even if there had been the possibility of a nationalization, which was not the case, it is not seen how the loss-sharing that the resolution actually allowed could have occurred, and it is highly likely that all losses that have already been absorbed by creditors of Banco Espirito Santo would have been absorbed by the State. Moreover, the hypothetical nationalization would also not allow to obtain a shield in the face of responsibilities and contingencies arising from management acts carried out by previous administrations of the BES, and there is a risk that the nationalized bank may have to bear other responsibilities for which novo banco's balance sheet is isolated, as a result of the resolution measure. Finally, in the event of hypothetical nationalisation, the amounts borne by the Resolution Fund would have been borne directly by the State. Although the Fund is a public entity, its resources come from the contributions paid by the banking sector over the years, which will allow the Fund to pay the State  albeit over a long period  the loans it has obtained. This recovery would not occur in the event of nationalization. 10. The clarification that there was no alternative solution is a decisive factor in demonstrating that Banco de Portugal was confronted with a limit situation. The application of a resolution measure to Banco Espirito Santo was therefore a measure of last resort, in the absence of which that bank would have entered a disorderly liquidation process on August 3, 2014. The application of a resolution measure to Banco Espirito Santo on that date was not a choice of Banco de Portugal. As stated by the Administrative Court of Circulo de Lisboa in its unanimous judgment on the bes resolution measure (Proc. no. 2586/14.3 BELSB): "Having considered the facts that occurred in the 7 days preceding the application of the resolution measure, namely the knowledge on 28 July 2014 of the confirmation of the preliminary amounts of the accounts of the Banco Espirito Santo Group for the first half of 2014, in which it was concluded at a loss of EUR 3,577.3 million, which revealed a serious non-compliance with the minimum capital ratios in force, at individual and consolidated level, with the suspension of Banco Espirito Santo's status as a counterpartite for the purposes of monetary policy operations of the Eurosystem, which prevented the use of bes financing by Eurosystem funds and entailed the requirement for the immediate return of the entire approximately EUR 10 billion loan that BES had already obtained from that same European system, they are, without considering the other circumstances existing at the time in relation to the situation of the Bes, demonstrating the impossibility of, in the short term, recourse to any alternative other than that of a scenario of immediate liquidation of BES." (fls. 231, 2). 11. It is therefore demonstrated, without further doubt, that the resolution of Banco Espirito Santo avoided its disorderly liquidation and the losses of extraordinary magnitude that would result. No one can reasonably doubt that a hypothetical disorderly liquidation of BES in August 2014 would have incalculable impacts on the stability of the national financial system, but also on economic activity and social cohesion and the balance of public accounts. If a resolution measure had not been applied to Banco Espirito Santo, it would have become incapable of fulfilling its obligations, bank depositors, individuals and companies would have lost access to their funds and savings, customers would have lost access to means and payment services, companies would have seen their financing relationships interrupted, at a loss for the continuity of their operations, the bank's employees would have lost their jobs and large public resources would have to be mobilised to finance the repayment of guaranteed deposits, without avoiding losses for deposits not covered by collateral. Even without considering the effects on domestic companies by the interruption of financing provided by BES or the effects on economic activity by losses assumed by unprotected BES creditors, including depositors not covered by collateral, the estimate made in August 2014 for losses arising from the settlement of BES at that date amounted to EUR 20  EUR 25 billion. The amount to be paid by the Deposit Guarantee Fund  which is financed almost entirely by the State and with a direct impact on public accounts  amounted to about 13 - 14 billion euros. In turn, the estimate that was completed in 2016 by the independent evaluator provided for by the law  in this case, Deloitte  pointed to a reduction in the value of BES's assets in a liquidation scenario of around EUR 24 billion and estimated that the value of losses to be assumed by common creditors would amount to around EUR 17 billion, depositors, in the part not covered by the Deposit Guarantee Fund guarantee. On this subject, the European Commission has given its opinion in the following terms (translation of banco de Portugal)1: 1 Decision with the reference "State aid n SA.39250 (2014/N)  Portugal, Resolution of Banco Espirito Santo, S.A.", of August 3, 2014, available here: . "The Portuguese authorities estimate that the alternative scenario (i.e. immediate settlement) would increase the costs of the resolution. Considering the size of the institution, its market share, and the interconnections it presents, external and internal, as well as the degree of substitutability, Banco de Portugal estimates that the disorderly liquidation could generate losses of EUR 20 billion to EUR 25 billion. It would also involve disbursing around EUR 14 billion from the Deposit Guarantee Fund for the repayment of covered deposits. The Commission has no reason to question that assessment. Furthermore, the Commission notes that immediate liquidation as opposed to the resolution would entail an immediate sale of fire sale assets. However, no entity was available for an immediate purchase of BES assets and liabilities and considering the existing uncertainty this would hardly be an option. Therefore, the orderly resolution of BES through the creation of Novo Banco is the least costly option for Portugal." 12. Much has been said, and even written, about the impacts of the fall of Banco Espirito Santo. Banco de Portugal does not ignore the existence and significant impacts still persist. But there can no longer be any doubt that the fact that these impacts are the irreparable imbalance in which the BES stood and found itself at the end of July 2014, as a result of the large and unexpected losses found during that month. The resolution measure was not the cause of the impacts resulting from the fall of Banco Espirito Santo, it was a way  the only possible  of containing damage and preserving value. As such, the evaluation of the result obtained with the resolution measure can only be made by comparison with the only alternative scenario, which was the disorderly and sudden liquidation of a large banking group with a decisive role in financing the national economy and in raising savings from Portuguese companies and families, and not by reference to what the BES was before its collapse or by reference to other scenarios of subsistence of the bank, because such scenarios, objectively and demonstrably, did not exist. This awareness is of the utmost importance to properly and fairly assess the bes resolution process. This same principle was recognised and applied by the Administrative Court of Circulo de Lisboa in its unanimous judgment on the bes resolution measure (Proc. no. 2586/14.3 BELSB) in the context of the assessment of the claim that the resolution measure would have infringed the right of ownership of BES shareholders and subordinated creditors. The Court expressly states the following (emphasis added): "... it is not by reference to the ex ante period to the application of the resolution measure that the value of the [right of] credit is assessed, but by reference to the to the alternative liquidation scenario of the institution, in which shareholders and subordinated creditors would be the last to receive any payment of their claims. In other words, the compression of the property right will have to be analysed by reference to the alternative situation of the liquidation of the credit institution and not by reference to any other alternative scenario, so that the possible 'compression' of the right of ownership (...) will have to be examined by appeals to mechanisms of comparative weighting between the resolution measure and the liquidation, and not to other subsistence scenarios of the credit institution." (fls. 193, 1st and 2nd?) 13. It should be noted here, even before addressing the other issues, that the Administrative Court of The Circle of Lisbon, in its unanimous judgment on the bes resolution measure, ruled on the supervisory initiatives developed by Banco de Portugal and which preceded the application of that resolution measure. In particular, the judgment states that: "Since the end of 2013, Banco de Portugal has stepped up surveillance of BES, and within the scope of that same surveillance and supervisory powers, it has exercised, until the implementation of the resolution measure, a set of powers, namely the imposition of corrective measures and thus a high control of the management of BES (...) it cannot even be said that Banco de Portugal has not adopted a posture of diligence and vigilance in relation to the management of the BES" (p. 226, 1st?); "Banco de Portugal could not be required, within the framework of the regulation, to act differently from that which it had, since it established its action in full conviction of compliance with the special regulatory block that linked the BES and in the presumption of the veracity of the accounts presented by that, not being verified here, any "venire contra factum proprium", but rather a mistake in the face of the concealment or simulation of accounting data provided to it by the regulation" (p. 226, 2); "It cannot even be said that Banco de Portugal has not indicated an effective, permanent and consistent concern in its role as regulator with the situation of BES, in particular in view of the risk and exposure to GES" (p. 228, 3); "Any communication or externalization by Banco de Portugal, prior to 28 July [2014] is certain, correct and true, in view of the data available to them on those dates, and there is no action by such a public power, which has not been conveyed, in the pursuit of the public interests that it pursues, namely the sound regularity of the banking system" (p. 225, 5th); "It is important to remember that the supervision carried out by Banco de Portugal depends on other actors and actors in a regime of checks and balances, where, for example, internal and external auditors are told to the regulator itself" (p. 226, 4). 14. I then take back the list of the most frequently asked questions about the resolution process to address the issue I have indicated secondly, i.e. the claim that "the assets responsible for Novo Banco's losses should not have been transferred to Novo Banco". That is, moreover, one of the questions raised in the Application which is at the origin of that hearing. 15. First, it should be noted that Novo Banco's balance sheet actually resulted from Banco Espirito Santo's balance sheet. It could not be otherwise: under the law, Banco de Portugal, as a resolution authority, had the power to select bes assets to be transferred to Novo Banco, but this selection had as its exclusive source the portfolio of assets that was already part of bes' balance sheet. This unavoidable reality is, in itself, of the utmost importance because it confirms that, in fact, the losses that have been recognized by Novo Banco emerge from exposures generated in the moment prior to the resolution measure, still in the sphere of Banco Espirito Santo. But can it be concluded that the assets in question should not have been transferred to Novo Banco? The answer can only be no, you can't draw that conclusion. 16. According to the law that was in force at the time, only two alternatives were placed in relation to banco Espirito Santo's assets: either they were kept in BES or they were transferred to Novo Banco. The first hypothesis implied that the recovery of the assets would take place in the context of a judicial liquidation of the bank by its liquidator commission. It also implied that the proceeds of this recovery could be obtained by banco Espirito Santo shareholders and its creditors not transferred to Novo Banco. The second hypothesis allowed the recovery of assets to be made by Novo Banco, in the context of normal banking activity. It also allowed the product of this recovery to obtained by Novo Banco, of which the Resolution Fund held all of its share capital, and not by the insolvent mass of BES. It was based on this framework that banco Espirito Santo's assets were essentially purged the risks that had led the BES to the situation of imbalance in which it was, especially the risks emerging from exposure to the Espirito Santo Group and the risks and contingencies emerging from past management acts. The decision criteria were clear. On the one hand, the objective of ensuring the continuity of the banking activity provided by BES advised that not only exposures that did not fit the scope of normal banking activity should be transferred  this was the case with the exposure of BES to the Espirito Santo Group. The hypothetical non-transfer, for example, of a portfolio of loans to companies, just because they are defaulted credits and therefore with greater risk, would certainly compromise the continuity of financing relationships with the companies concerned. On the other hand, the objective of seeking to maximise the value of assets advised that recovery should be avoided as part of a liquidation process. Above all, it was important to ensure that the amount that was recovered from BES's assets was appropriated by Novo Banco, for the benefit of the transferred creditors and the Resolution Fund, and not of the insolvent mass of BES. For all this, assets whose recovery perspective, according to the information available at the time of the resolution, was "left behind", were "left behind", at Banco Espirito Santo, the assets whose recovery perspective, according to the information available at the time of the resolution, was really short and/or had the potential to generate new responsibilities and/or that were recognized as causing the financial imbalance in which the BES was. 17. In order to have no doubts in this regard, I propose that an exercise of abstraction be carried out, which, while simple, makes it possible to understand why it is wrong to argue that the assets which have caused losses should not have been transferred to the Novo Banco. It should be admitted, by chance, that the assets that are part of the contingent capitalization mechanism had not been transferred to Novo Banco or that were somehow purged from novo banco's balance sheet at the reference date of the contingent capitalization mechanism (30/06/2016). At that date, that portfolio had a nominal value of EUR 12.7 billion and the book value, net of default, was EUR 7.8 billion. Assuming that the book value of that portfolio was the same at the time of the application of the resolution measure (with great probability, the amount would be higher), then its non-transfer to Novo Banco would have meant that: (a) Novo Banco's assets would have been reduced by EUR 7.8 billion; (b) For this reason, such a reduction in the asset would have to be financed by a capital increase of the same amount by the Resolution Fund or would have to be borne by a very significant set of common creditors, in particular by the bank's clients, and it is certain that the absorption of losses by the bank's creditors has already been carried out to the extent permitted by the objective of preserving financial stability; c) All amounts recovered in this asset portfolio  to date, this represents 3.3 billion euros of actual receipts  would have been appropriated, not by Novo Banco, but by the insolvent mass of BES, which would potentially benefit bes shareholders and creditors who, under the law, must primarily absorb the bank's losses. That is, if this portfolio of assets had not been transferred to Novo Banco: i) the Resolution Fund would have to have capitalized the Novo Banco for the full book value of the assets, with inevitable massive recourse to public resources for its financing; (ii) such capitalization would have occurred regardless of the performance of the assets; (iii) the recovery of the assets would be made in the context of a liquidation procedure; iv) the recovered value would be appropriated by the insolvent mass of BES. In the current situation, what happens, by comparison, is as follows: i) the Resolution Fund capitalizes the Novo Banco only for the value of the losses recorded in the assets, or even less; ii) capitalization occurs only in the event of losses in assets; (iii) the recovery is made by Novo Banco as an active credit institution and not in the context of a liquidation; iv) the amount recovered is owned by Novo Banco. In practice, the hypothetical non-transfer of the assets concerned to Novo Banco would have in fact eliminated the inherent risk and prevented the losses from materialising later. But this security would have been achieved at a disproportionately higher cost to the Resolution Fund, for the benefit of bes's insolvent mass and impairing the ability to maximize asset value. 18. In that regard, I point out that the current legal framework offers more instruments and allows, in this regard, the transfer of assets to a vehicle created for that purpose. This instrument allows certain assets to be segregated from the activity that is intended to be preserved without this implying leaving them behind, to be recovered in a liquidation process and for the benefit of the insolvent mass of the resolved institution. The consecration of this instrument is proof that, even when the worst quality assets are at stake, it is not appropriate to allow them to remain in the sphere of the settled institution. This instrument was only provided for in the national regulatory framework from March 2015, with the publication of Law No. 23-A/2015, of March 26 and was used in the resolution of BANIF  Banco Internacional do Funchal, S.A., through the constitution of Oitante, S.A. 19. Return to the list of the most frequent doubts about the resolution process to address the third-place issue, i.e. the claim that "the assets transferred to Novo Banco were misassessed at the time of the BES resolution". This is also one of the questions raised in the Application which is at the origin of that hearing. 20. Due to its relevance, the question of the valuation of assets transferred to a transitional bank is the subject of express legal provision. Under the regime in force in August 2014, assets should be assessed at the time of transfer, carried out by an independent entity designated by Banco de Portugal (see Article 145h(4) of the General Regime of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations, in the version in force at the date of application of the resolution measure to bes). 21. Thus, the assets transferred to Novo Banco were the subject of an independent valuation, carried out for this purpose by determination of Banco de Portugal, in accordance with the law. The evaluation was carried out by PricewaterhouseCoopers & Associados  Sociedade de Revisores Auditors, Lda ("PwC"), between August and November 2014, with reference to the time of application of the resolution measure to BES, and from it resulted in adjustment needs, on a consolidated basis, in the aggregate value of 4,937 million euros, compared to the value at which the assets transferred to Novo Banco were measured by BES at the time of the resolution measure. On an individual basis, the adjustments made in that independent assessment amounted to EUR 4,920 million. That is, in the initial balance sheet of Novo Banco, adjustments were recorded in the value of assets corresponding to about 6% of the value by which the assets were recorded in the bes balance sheet, on a consolidated basis. Even disregarding the effect of the adjustment related to exposure to Banco Espirito Santo Angola, which represented 2,750 million euros, the losses recorded, in the initial balance sheet of Novo Banco, exceeded 2 billion euros, of which approximately 1,204 million euros of impairment reinforcement for the credit portfolio and 759 million euros to reduce the value of real estate assets. The independent evaluation then carried out aimed to determine the correct measurement of assets, liabilities, off-balance sheet elements and assets under management transferred to Novo Banco, in a perspective of continuity of the institution's activity, in accordance with the principles established in the International Financial Reporting Standards, as adopted in the European Union. 22. Furthermore, even before the implementation of the resolution measure, bes's balance sheet had been subject to the Asset Quality Review (AQR) exercise promoted by the European Central Bank, which, like the other European banks covered by the financial year, focused primarily on the revision of the credit portfolio. The results of this asset quality analysis promoted by the ECB were shared with the independent evaluator appointed by Banco de Portugal, the conclusions of which are therefore part of the results of the ecb's analysis. 23. Furthermore, Novo Banco was also the subject of the stress test conducted by the European Central Bank in 2015, with reference to 31 December 2014, in which the bank overcame the test in the baseline scenario, considered most likely, and capital shortfalls were found only in the adverse scenario. 24. These data are used to explain that Novo Banco's initial balance sheet was subject to successive scrutiny and that the value by which the assets were recorded was calculated on the basis of an independent assessment, carried out in the light of international accounting standards for a scenario of continuity of Novo Banco's activity, and also took into account the results of the asset quality analysis promoted by the European Central Bank. If this clarification has been made, the reality is that it has been seen from 2014 onwards that the assets in question have generated additional losses. Does this mean that the evaluations carried out in 2014 were incorrect? In order to answer this question, I use a technical standard published by the European Banking Authority, precisely on the valuation of assets in the context of the implementation of resolution measures2. In this technical standard, a distinction is made between the concepts of "economic value" and "book value": the first corresponds essentially to the 2 Regulatory Technical Standards on valuation for the purposes of resolution and on valuation to determine difference in treatment following resolution under Directive 2014/59/EU on recovery and resolution of credit institutions and investment firms, disponivel aqui: . current value of the financial flows that may be generated by the assets and is therefore a measure of the concrete recovery value (and therefore also of losses) associated with the assets; the concept of "book value" is the value that results from the application of accounting standards. In that technical standard it is noted that the two concepts do not lead to the same valuation and it is discussed precisely whether the relevant concept to be used in the valuation to ascertain the value to be attributed to assets following the application of a resolution measure (thereafter referred to as "Valuation 2") should be the concept of "economic value" or "book value". And it is in that technical standard that one concludes that (my translation): "On the basis of the comparison between the different policy options, the European Banking Authority decided that this technical note should aim to use an economic value-based approach in the case of 'assessment 2'". This technical standard of the European Banking Authority was published in May 2017, i.e. about three years after the resolution of Banco Espirito Santo. It is further explained in that the use of the concept of "economic value" is intended to ensure that losses are fully recognised at the time of resolution and that this is necessary to ensure prudent capitalisation. And it is clarified that this concept may imply a deviation from accounting and prudential standards (my translation): "For 'assessment 2', the technical note underlines the need to assess economic value in order to ensure that losses are fully recognised, even if this implies a deviation from accounting and prudential standards. This is necessary to ensure that the institutions concerned are capitalised on prudent terms and also because certain resolution actions (such as the divestment of the activity) imply that economic value is crystallised." 25. This foray into the more technical aspects of asset valuation seems necessary to me to demonstrate that: (a) As the European Banking Authority states, different approaches may be followed in carrying out asset valuation; (b) the assessment on the basis of the concept of "economic value" may result in values other than the assessment on the basis of accounting standards, without this meaning that this assessment  which is true to international accounting standards and is the assessment followed by credit institutions and their auditors in a situation of continuity of activity  is wrong; (c) the weighting between the two approaches and the European Banking Authority's technical standard forecast that the concept of "economic value" is more appropriate takes place during 2017, reflecting the regulatory regime based on Directive 2014/59/EU of the European Parliament and the Council of 15 May 2014, which establishes a framework for the recovery and resolution of credit institutions and investment firms ("Directive resolution), which was only partially transposed in Portugal at the time of banco Espirito Santo's resolution. Finally, it should always be said that, at the time of the resolution, there was no information available leading to the conclusion that the actual value of that portfolio of assets was much lower than its book value. 26. In view of the table I have described, I recognise the meaning of the comments that have been made more recently regarding the valuation of assets in the context of the resolution of the Bes. They reflect the paradigm currently in force and the maturity of the normative framework of the resolution, obtained over the last few years. But I would stress that Banco de Portugal acted in 2014 on the basis of the legal framework in force at that date, and with the information available, and that, in the context of resolution, there was a visible evolution, as evident in the technical standard of the European Banking Authority, dated 2017. 27. The fourth question which I wish to address concerns the claim that "Banco de Portugal did not endit with sufficient Capital At the time of its constitution". This question is also raised in the application which is at the origin of my hearing. 28. As it could not fail to be, Novo Banco's initial capitalization reflected the valuation of its assets, first on the basis of an interim valuation and then on the basis of the independent valuation I mentioned above, taking into account the capital requirements applicable at the time. Considering the valuation of assets transferred to Novo Banco, the initial capitalization allowed Novo Banco to present a common equity tier 1 (CET1) ratio of 9.2% on a consolidated basis. 29. In this regard, it is important to first note that, under the European State aid rules, to which the use of the Resolution Fund was linked, the use of public funds should be limited to the minimum amount required. This requirement is based on the "Commission Communication on the application, from 1 August 2013, of state aid rules to support measures to banks in the context of the financial crisis"3, which states that, in order to be compatible with the Treaty on the functioning of the European Union, the use of public funds should, among other requirements, be limited to the minimum necessary. The requirement was expressly verified by the European Commission, as can be confirmed in its decision of 3 August 2014, which states, with regard to novo banco's capital ratio at the time of its creation, that "[the] Commission considers that the resolution aid was limited to the minimum necessary"4. 3 Available here: . 4 Decision with the reference "State aid n SA.39250 (2014/N)  Portugal, Resolution of Banco Espirito Santo, S.A.", of August 3, 2014, available here: . 30. Considering the valuation of the assets resulting from the independent valuation and the capital requirements to which Novo Banco was subject, novo banco's capital allocation was not only adequate at that date, but banco de Portugal was therefore not even allowed to determine a capital allocation leading to a significant excess of capital in the face of the capital requirements required  in August 2014, these requirements were 8% for the total capital ratio. 31. It is certain that, since 2014, Novo Banco has faced situations of need for substantial capital reinforcement. But it is not legitimate to use the circumstances known in the meantime as to the evolution of the regulatory requirements applicable to Novo Banco, as well as the other European banks, and on the performance of their assets to make a judgment on the capitalization carried out in 2014. Indeed, the needs that have been registered by Novo Banco are essentially the result of the combination of two major factors: on the one hand, the recognition of impairments and losses, for which, however, it should be said that novo banco's accumulated registration has remained in line with what has been observed in the same period in other large national banks; on the other hand, the very substantial increase in regulatory requirements, by changing the regulatory framework. 32. The Novo Banco now faces capital requirements corresponding to a total capital ratio of 14%, which compared to the 8% requirements in August 2014, and which was (the latter) the relevant reference value for the bank's capitalisation, in the light of the legal requirements for the use of public funds for the minimum strictly necessary. The increase from 8% to 14% reflects the change in the regulatory framework, and more specifically the entry into force of the Single Supervisory Mechanism in November 2014, the provision for the possibility of setting capital requirements higher than the regulatory minimum  called the Pillar 2 requirement  and the new buffer maintenance obligations in the face of regulatory minimums, conservation reserve and the reserve for other institutions of systemic importance, subject to a transitional period of application of 4 years starting on 1 January 2016 and 1 January 2018 respectively. In concrete terms, the capital requirements imposed on Novo Banco therefore increased by 6 percentage points in the period between August 2014 and 1 January 2019. Considering novo banco's balance sheet at the time of the resolution, this increase alone would represent an estimated increase in capital resources needs of EUR 2.4 billion, all the rest constant. The increase in regulatory requirements resulting from changes in the regulatory framework has also added the transition effects to the new capital eligibility rules, which have involved, over the last few years, and gradually, deductions from own funds in an amount exceeding EUR 900 million. In summary: the change in the regulatory framework on capital requirements entailed an increase in capital resources needs in an amount that exceeded, in the case of Novo Banco, EUR 3 billion compared to the balance sheet at the time of its creation. 33. Almost five years after the creation of the Novo Banco, it is now known that the bank has faced capital-raising needs. But I would also reaffirm that in August 2014, based on the existing regulatory framework, based on the restrictions on the use of public funds, and on the basis of the information available, Novo Banco's capitalization level was adequate. Banco de Portugal cannot therefore accept the use of supervening facts to assess the sufficiency of the capital with which Novo Banco was constituted in 2014. 34. The fifth question which I have raised and which I want to ensure is definitively clarified refers to the suggestion that "the Novo Banco should not have been sold" or that "its sale should have been carried out with more time". 35. In fact, the sale of the Resolution Fund's stake in Novo Banco was a legal imperative to which Banco de Portugal was bound. In fact, it is expressly provided in the law that the transitional bank has a limited duration, unless it is the object of sale, and it was Banco de Portugal's legal obligation to promote the sale of Novo Banco. 36. For the avoidance of doubt, I would like to recall what was set out in Article 145g(12) of the General Regime of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations, as it was made at the time of the application of the resolution measure: "The transitional bank shall have a duration limited to two years, extendable for periods of one year on the basis of reasons of public interest, in particular if risks to financial stability remain or negotiations are pending with a view to the disposal of their assets, liabilities, off-balance sheet items and assets under their management and may not exceed the maximum duration of five years." Moreover, in the present case, the European Commission's decision on the resolution measure set the selling period at precisely two years, otherwise the Novo Banco would be liquidated5. 5 Decision with the reference "State aid n SA.39250 (2014/N)  Portugal, Resolution of Banco Espirito Santo, S.A.", of August 3, 2014, available here: . 37. The sale of the transitional bank is therefore not based on Banco de Portugal's discretion: Banco de Portugal acted on the basis of a very clear legal allocation, which it has complied with. 38. There is, on the other hand, another given of the greatest importance which is not always understood: the Novo Banco needed a capital injection to ensure compliance with the new capital requirements. The worsening of the minimum capital requirements by changing the regulatory framework, combined with the accumulation of losses, eventually led to a situation of insufficiency that could only be met by means of a capital injection  which came to occur with the capital increase of EUR 1 billion made by the buyer. 39. From the end of 2016, it became clear that novo banco's subsistence required a significant capital injection. And under the law, this requirement would have to be carried out on the basis of private capital. Indeed, under the Credit Institution Recovery and Resolution Directive, which was transposed into domestic law in 2015, the use of public funds to strengthen the capital of credit institutions in order to enable compliance with regulatory requirements has become, in itself  and unless certain exceptions have been found, which did not apply to the situation of the Novo Banco  a cause for the determination that that institution is at risk or in insolvency and, therefore, cause for the withdrawal of its authorisation or for the application of resolution measures. 40. That is, the sale of Novo Banco was not only a matter related to the ownership of its capital, i.e. with the transfer of ownership ofthe public sphere to the private sphere: there was a concrete need for capital injection to enable compliance with prudential requirements the which, under the law in force, required the entry of private capital, under penalty of the Novo Banco being liquidated or resolving. 41. That is also why I have no doubt that, in 2017, if the sale of Novo Banco had not been completed, the bank would have faced a liquidation or resolution procedure. This was not an academic hypothesis: the liquidation scenario of Novo Banco was studied under the Single Supervisory Mechanism and the Single Resolution Mechanism and, in 2017, there was very early work at the Banking Union level to prepare the liquidation or resolution of Novo Banco in case of failure to sell it. In the context of this work, it was agreed among all those involved, including the European authorities, that the contingency plans that were then prepared did not guarantee, unlike the sale solution, the preservation of financial stability, not guaranteed even the full protection of deposits and entailed very high risks and costs. 42. The sixth question I intend to address refers to the suggestion that arises in the public space that "the sale of Novo Banco was not a competitive process". Although these alleged doubts arise only episodically, I would like to also address this issue with a view to its full clarification. 43. I therefore think it is important to recall the facts: The relaunch of the novo banco sale process was the subject of public disclosure through a press release from Banco de Portugal of January 15, 2016. In order to maximise competition and obtain the best possible result in the face of prevailing market conditions, generally rather unfavorable, two routes were defined and pursued in parallel: a "Strategic Selling Procedure" and a "Market Sales Procedure". The "Market Sale Procedure" had a view to the possible placement of shares with institutional investors that met the eligibility criteria and, eventually, a public offering of novo banco shares. In turn, the "Strategic Selling Procedure" was addressed to strategic investors who were credit institutions, or insurance companies and/or entities that already directly own, or under management, qualifying shareholder holdings in credit institutions or insurance companies and that met their eligibility criteria. Throughout the sale process, Banco de Portugal disclosed information on the applicable conditions, in particular on the eligibility criteria of potential investors and on the criteria for evaluating the proposals: on 31 March 2016, Banco de Portugal disclosed information on the terms of the sale procedure and published the eligibility criteria of investors who could participate in each of the defined routes; 22 April 2016, the specifications relating to the "Strategic Sales Procedure" and the tender specifications relating to the "Market Sales Procedure" have been published Throughout the sale process, Banco de Portugal also released information on its progress: on June 30, 2016, Banco de Portugal disclosed the information that four proposals had been received for the acquisition of Novo Banco under the "Strategic Selling Procedure"; on 4 November 2016, information was disclosed that five proposals had been received under the two sales procedures. In view of the proposals received in November 2016, Banco de Portugal continued negotiations with all potential investors who were available for this purpose, without excluding any of them. Since the proposal submitted by Lone Star was the one that best met the valuation criteria set out in the tender specifications, on 4 January 2017, Banco de Portugal invited this investor to deepen the negotiations, but kept open the possibility for all other potential investors to improve their proposals. These negotiations eventually led to a final round of discussions and negotiations, under conditions of exclusivity, which resulted in the selection, on March 31, 2017, of the proposal presented by Lone Star for the completion of the sale of Novo Banco. 44. I would point out that all investors had the same conditions throughout the sale process and all had the opportunity to conduct complementary and confirmatory due diligence procedures and to improve their proposals on a level playing field. 45. In fact, Banco de Portugal does not know from any of the investors who participated in the sale process any complaint or complaint regarding the progress of the proceedings and its conditions of fairness and competitiveness. 46. Furthermore, the sale procedure has been scrutinised by the European Commission, which is precisely responsible for and in accordance with the 'Commission Communication on the application, from 1 August 2013, of state aid rules to support measures to banks in the context of the financial crisis', to examine whether: a) the sale process is opened, unconditional and non-discriminatory; b) the sale is carried out under market conditions; c) the selling price is maximized.
