The seventh and final question I wish to clarify concerns the idea that "in the sale of Novo Banco the quota capitalisation mechanism should not have been envisaged". 50. The contingent capitalisation mechanism is by its nature a source of contingent liabilities for the Resolution Fund. It is evident, therefore, that Banco de Portugal, as an entity that, in conjunction with the Government, promoted the sale of the Bank, would have also preferred that it had been carried out without the provision of such a mechanism. In fact, the attempt to avoid additional lideation for the Resolution Fund guided the entire sale process, but it was found that it would not have been possible to complete the sale of Novo Banco  which would have implied its liquidation or resolution, as I have already demonstrated  without the provision of a bank protection mechanism for certain assets. For this reason, the contingent capitalization mechanism was a structuring element of the sale of Novo Banco and was indispensable for its feasibility. As you have already explained before this Commission, the Deputy Governor and Chairman of the Resolution Fund's Directive Committee, Mr. Luis Maximo dos Santos, during the sale process, competitors have expressed doubts about the value or risk associated with certain assets that are part of what has been designated as the legacy of BES. At issue are unproductive assets, in many cases defaulted credits, or assets that are not considered strategic in the face of Novo Banco's central mission, as a commercial bank dedicated to the domestic retail market and to the financing of the national business fabric, especially small and medium-sized enterprises. The existence of a mechanism for the protection of Novo Banco in relation to certain assets, or its exclusion from the sale process, was therefore an essential condition of the generality of the proposals received in the novo banco's sale process. Moreover, in view of the large size of the portfolio of non-complied assets, the provision for such a mechanism was also a condition for the approval of the sale operation by the European Central Bank and the European Commission, since this was considered essential to ensure the viability of the institution. 51. It has been shown that the existence of an asset protection mechanism was essential for the completion of the sale, it should also be explained why the quota capitalisation mechanism model was followed. 52. The mechanism allows, as can be seen, to protect Novo Banco's capital from losses that are recorded in the assets covered. But this protection is ensured at the same time as it is ensured that settlement fund payments only occur when losses actually materialize and in the event that Novo Banco's capital becomes less than pre-defined targets, while also allowing potential savings for the Resolution Fund, i.e., resolution fund may pay less than the amount of losses actually recorded in the assets. The forecast of a condition associated with Novo Banco's capital ratios serves as a mechanism for sharing losses and reducing charges for the Resolution Fund. In the absence of such a condition, the effect would be that the Resolution Fund would pay the full amount corresponding to the losses that were to be recorded in the assets. But the condition associated with capital ratios determines that the Resolution Fund can pay less than losses on assets if the shortfall in capital ratios is less than the amount of losses, but in any case will not pay more than the losses on the assets. It is in this sense that the condition associated with Novo Banco's capital can allow savings against the value of emerging losses of assets and their management. This is confirmed by the actual implementation data of the mechanism, as has also been explained at a previous hearing before this Commission: According to what was announced by Novo Banco, the accumulated losses on the assets covered and their management, between the reference date of the mechanism (30/06/2016) and 31/12/2018, correspond to 2,662 million euros. Of that amount, the Resolution Fund paid around EUR 792 million in 2018, with around EUR 1,149 million expected to be paid in 2019, totaling around EUR 1,941 million  a figure that corresponds to about 73% of the losses of EUR 2,662 million accumulated in the assets. 53. The quota capitalisation mechanism therefore allows the protection granted to the assets covered to be limited to the minimum necessary for Novo Banco's capital ratios to remain in the pre-agreed targets, which may imply payments below the value of losses in the assets. In the worst case scenario, the resolution fund's liability will correspond to losses in assets, but without exceeding the amount of EUR 3,890 million. 54. The solution found is therefore the result of the balance between, on the one hand, the emerging need for the sale process and dialogue with the European authorities regarding the protection of Novo Banco's balance sheet in relation to losses associated with certain assets, and, on the other hand, the need to minimise costs for the Resolution Fund, and assurance that such costs only occur if strictly necessary. 55. In any event, what I think is essential to underline is that the proposal put forward by Lone Star was the least financially onerous proposal for the Resolution Fund, following a competitive sales process which ensured, as verified by the European Commission, that the selling price was maximised. That is, even if it resulted, in the final, at a negative price, given the payments that have been made by the Resolution Fund, what is observed is that the result obtained was objectively the best possible, in view of the circumstances, that is, in view of the quality of the assets, in view of the need for a capital increase, in view of the imperative need to complete the sale of Novo Banco, under penalty of the bank being liquidated or resolved, and in view of the implications and costs much higher of this alternative scenario. Ladies and gentlemen, 56. This exhibition is already long, as it could not fail to be faced with the complexity of the issues addressed. I would like to end by stressing the following key ideas, which I think I have presented here with clarity and factual support: a) The fact that is at the origin of the resolution process of Banco Espirito Santo and of the entire chain of events that followed it, until the conclusion of the contingent capitalization agreement, is the situation of irreparable financial imbalance in which the BES was and was: in August 2014, Banco Espirito Santo was no longer able to carry out the banking activity; b) There was no alternative for the viability of Banco Espirito Santo; c) If a resolution measure had not been applied, Banco Espirito Santo would have abruptly ceased its activity in August 2014 and there would have been a sudden and disorderly liquidation. d) The creation of Novo Banco allowed the continuity of the banking activity developed by BES, especially the full preservation of deposits and the continuity of credit provided to the economy, and also allowed that, as imposed by law, the losses had been absorbed, first, by the shareholders of the bank and, to the maximum extent possible, by its creditors. e) Novo Banco's balance sheet results, as it could not be, from Banco Espirito Santo's balance sheet and the losses that have materialized in the sphere of Novo Banco are mainly the result of exposures generated prior to the resolution measure. f) According to the law that was in force at the time of the resolution, only two alternatives were placed in relation to banco Espirito Santo's assets: either they were kept in BES or they were transferred to Novo Banco. The second hypothesis allowed the proceeds of the recovery of the assets to revert to Novo Banco, avoiding its recovery in the context of a liquidation lawsuit and avoiding its appropriation by the insolvent mass of BES. Thus, banco Espirito Santo's balance sheet essentially purged the risks that had led the bank to the situation of imbalance in which it was, especially the risks arising from exposure to the Espirito Santo Group and the risks and contingencies emerging from past management acts. g) The assets transferred to Novo Banco were the subject of an independent valuation, carried out by determination of Banco de Portugal, in accordance with the law, in addition to having been previously evaluated in the context of the exercise of asset quality analysis promoted by the European Central Bank. Based on the independent valuation, the valuation of assets transferred to Novo Banco was adjusted at the initial moment to an amount of more than EUR 4,900 million. (h) The independent assessment was carried out in a logic of continuity of the bank's activity, in accordance with international accounting standards, and not in a logic of economic value as currently recommended and has been foreseen by the European Banking Authority since 2017. On the other hand, after the independent assessment, previously unknown data and risks were revealed, reported to facts prior to August 3, which had an impact on the value of the assets. i) Novo Banco's initial capitalization reflected the valuation of its assets, according to the information available, in the light of the independent valuation, as well as the capital requirements applicable to the date. Under the applicable regulations, the use of the Resolution Fund would have to be limited to the minimum necessary for compliance with capital requirements. Since August 2014, the capital requirements for Novo Banco in terms of total capital ratio have increased from 8% in August 2014 to 14%. j) The sale of the resolution fund's stake in Novo Banco was a legal imperative, and it is expressly provided by law that the transitional bank has a limited duration, unless it is sold. k) If the sale of Novo Banco had not been completed, the bank would have faced a liquidation or resolution process. This scenario was studied under the Single Supervisory Mechanism and the Single Resolution Mechanism and, in 2017, there were very early work to prepare the liquidation or resolution of Novo Banco in case of failure in its sale. (l) In the context of such work, it was agreed among all those involved, including the European authorities, that the contingency plans which were then prepared did not guarantee, unlike the sale solution, the preservation of financial stability, did not guarantee full protection of deposits and entailed very high risks and costs. m) The sale of the Resolution Fund's stake in Novo Banco was carried out on the basis of an open, transparent and competitive process resulting in the selection of the most financially advantageous proposal for the Resolution Fund. This has been examined and confirmed by the European Commission as part of its legal tasks. n) The contingent capitalization mechanism was a structuring element of the sale of Novo Banco and was indispensable for its feasibility and, therefore, to avoid the liquidation or resolution of Novo Banco in 2017. 57. Having made this explanation, I would like to make it clear that Banco de Portugal is well aware of the impacts that have been manifested following the application of the resolution measure to Banco Espirito Santo. But I would like there to be no doubt in this Commission and in those who accompany us that these impacts have their origin and result from the collapse of one of the largest national banking groups, which played a nerve-racking role in financing the national economy and capturing tens of billions of euros in deposits. The collapse of a financial group with the size and relevance of Banco Espirito Santo in 2014 is invariably an extremely serious event in any economy. The resolution process of Banco Espirito Santo has certainly not avoided all the damage that has been generated by this event, but I remain firmly convinced  and I think there are abundant reasons for all to be firmly convinced  that the BES resolution allowed these damages to be more restrained and above all ensured that the objectives that the law attributes to the action of the resolution authority were achieved, in particular, the preservation of financial stability and the protection of depositors. Not concealing the severity of the collapse of BES, I remain sure that Banco de Portugal's action allowed us to achieve something that, of course, no one would imagine possible, if we go back to the period prior to the resolution: it ensured that, despite the collapse of BES and its entry into liquidation, the continuity of banking activity was ensured, all deposits and losses were supported, first, by the shareholders of the bank and, in legally permissible terms, by its creditors. Given the systemic nature of the Bank, it was not possible to prevent a substantial part of the losses from being borne by the Resolution Fund in need of public funding, but the use of the Resolution Fund will allow the public money involved to be recovered over time. 58. I would also like to conclude with the message that the regulatory framework for the resolution has evolved very significantly since the resolution of Banco Espirito Santo in August 2014. Some of the questions that are being raised today about this resolution, which I have just addressed here, now have a different legal and institutional framework, which offers a responsiveness that did not exist in Europe in 2014. On the one hand, the existing legal regime currently offers a wider range of instruments, which includes the possibility of creating asset management vehicles to concentrate the worst quality assets of the settled institution, with a view to maximising its value outside the framework of a liquidation for the benefit of the insolvent estate, but that also includes the bail-in measurement. On the other hand, resolution authorities are currently preparing resolution plans to define in advance the strategy to be defined in the event of the resolution of institutions. Currently there are resolution plans for all significant credit institutions in the Banking Union, which define, for example, what resolution measure to apply according to the characteristics of each institution and seeks to define how far assets can be purged from the balance sheet of institutions in the context of resolution. Moreover, the legal framework for the valuation of assets in the context of resolution is now significantly more densified, and the obligation to carry out assessments even before the implementation of resolution measures is now established and the principle of assessment based on economic value is now defined to ensure that losses are absorbed at the initial time, principle may differ from accounting standards. Finally, credit institutions are now subject to requirements relating to the maintenance of an adequate loss-absorbing capacity in the event of resolution, which means that they have to have sufficient liabilities to bear losses and thus avoid recourse to public funds. This requirement is so demanding that it is now one of the main challenges faced by the national banking system and may even raise questions of proportionality and efficiency, but there is no doubt that, from the strict perspective of the resolution function, it is a powerful mechanism to ensure that, in the future, the use of public funds is minimised in the event of resolution. All the instruments I have now announced are now considered decisive in ensuring that resolution measures are in place effectively and efficiently. They are also instruments that did not exist in 2014 and which are still, in some cases, under construction. For this reason, just as it seems illegitimate for the actions taken in 2014 to be assessed in the light of the current circumstances, I also believe that, in the present circumstances and, above all, those that will exist in the near future, there will be better conditions for resolution actions to be carried out even more effectively. Lisbon, 2 May 2019

(fls. 231, 2.). 11. Fica demonstrado, portanto, sem margem para mais dvidas, que a resoluo do Banco Esprito Santo evitou a sua liquidao desordenada e os prejuzos de extraordinria magnitude que da resultariam. Ningum pode razoavelmente duvidar de que uma hipottica liquidao desordenada do BES, em agosto de 2014, provocaria impactos incalculveis na estabilidade do sistema financeiro nacional, mas tambm na atividade econmica e na coeso social e no equilbrio das contas pblicas. Isso mesmo foi examinado e confirmado pela Comisso Europeia, no mbito das suas atribuies legais. n) O mecanismo de capitalizao contingente constituiu um elemento estruturante da venda do Novo Banco e foi indispensvel para a sua viabilizao e, portanto, para evitar a liquidao ou a resoluo do Novo Banco, em 2017. 57. Feita esta explanao, gostaria de deixar claro que o Banco de Portugal tem bem conscincia dos impactos que se tm vindo a manifestar-se na sequncia da aplicao da medida de resoluo ao Banco Esprito Santo. Mas gostaria que no houvesse dvidas nesta Comisso e em quem nos acompanha de que esses impactos tm a sua origem e resultam do colapso de um dos maiores grupos bancrios nacionais, que desempenhava um papel nevrlgico no financiamento da economia nacional e que captava dezenas de milhares de milhes de euros em depsitos. O colapso de um grupo financeiro com a dimenso e com a relevncia que tinha o Banco Esprito Santo, em 2014,  invariavelmente um acontecimento de extrema gravidade em qualquer economia. O processo de resoluo do Banco Esprito Santo no evitou, por certo, todos os danos que foram gerados por esse acontecimento, mas continuo firmemente convicto  e penso que h razes abundantes para todos estarmos firmemente convictos  que a resoluo do BES permitiu que esses danos fossem mais contidos e acima de tudo garantiu que fossem alcanados os objetivos que a lei atribui  ao da autoridade de resoluo, em especial, o de preservao da estabilidade financeira e de proteo dos depositantes. No escamoteando a gravidade do colapso do BES, continuo seguro de que a ao do Banco de Portugal permitiu alcanar algo que, por certo, ningum imaginaria possvel, se nos reconduzirmos ao perodo anterior  resoluo: garantiu que, apesar do colapso do BES e da sua entrada em liquidao fosse assegurada a continuidade da atividade bancria, fossem preservados todos os depsitos e as perdas fossem suportadas, em primeiro lugar, pelos acionistas do banco e, nos termos legalmente admissveis, pelos seus credores. Atendendo  natureza sistmica do Banco, no foi possvel evitar que tambm uma parte substancial das perdas tivessem sido suportadas pelo Fundo de Resoluo com necessidade de financiamento pblico, mas a utilizao do Fundo de Resoluo permitir que os dinheiros pblicos envolvidos venham a ser recuperados ao longo do tempo. 58. Gostaria tambm de concluir com a mensagem de que o quadro normativo da resoluo evoluiu muito significativamente desde a resoluo do Banco Esprito Santo, em agosto de 2014. Algumas das questes que hoje se colocam a propsito dessa resoluo, e que aqui acabo de abordar, tm hoje um quadro legal e institucional distinto, que oferece uma capacidade de resposta que, em 2014, no existia na Europa. Por um lado, o regime jurdico em vigor atualmente oferece um leque de instrumentos mais vasto, que inclui a possibilidade de criao de veculos de gesto de ativos para a concentrar os ativos de pior qualidade da instituio resolvida, com vista  maximizao do seu valor fora do quadro de uma liquidao judicial em benefcio da massa insolvente, mas que tambm inclui a medida do bail-in. Por outro lado, as autoridades de resoluo preparam atualmente planos de resoluo que permitem que seja definida, antecipadamente, a estratgia a seguir em caso de resoluo das instituies de crdito. Atualmente existem planos de resoluo para todas instituies de crdito significativas na Unio Bancria, em que se define, por exemplo, que medida de resoluo aplicar em funo das caractersticas de cada instituio e se procura definir at que ativos podem ser expurgados do balano das instituies em contexto de resoluo. Acresce que o quadro jurdico aplicvel  avaliao de ativos em contexto de resoluo est hoje significativamente mais densificado, tendo passado a estar consagrada a obrigatoriedade de realizao de avaliaes antes mesmo da aplicao de medidas de resoluo e passando a estar definido o princpio de avaliao com base no valor econmico para assegurar que as perdas so absorvidas no momento inicial, ainda que esse princpio possa divergir das normas de contabilidade. E, por fim, as instituies de crdito esto hoje sujeitas a requisitos relacionados com a manuteno de uma adequada capacidade de absoro de perdas em caso de resoluo, que leva a que tenham que dispor de passivos suficientes para suportar as perdas e assim evitar o recurso a fundos pblicos. Este requisito  de tal forma exigente que constitui hoje um dos principais desafios enfrentados pelo sistema bancrio nacional e pode at colocar questes de proporcionalidade e eficincia, mas no h dvida que, na perspetiva estrita da funo de resoluo,  um mecanismo poderoso para garantir que, no futuro,  minimizado o recurso a fundos pblicos em caso de resoluo. Todos os instrumentos que agora enunciei so considerados hoje decisivos para garantir que existem condies para que as medidas de resoluo sejam aplicadas com eficcia e com eficincia. So tambm instrumentos que no existiam em 2014 e que ainda esto, em alguns casos, em construo. Por essa razo, tal como me parece ilegtimo que as aes tomadas em 2014 sejam avaliadas  luz das circunstncias atuais, tambm penso que, nas circunstncias atuais e, sobretudo, naquelas que existiro num futuro prximo, haver melhores condies para que as aes de resoluo se executem ainda com maior eficcia. Lisboa, 2 de maio de 2019

Title: Statement by Deputy Governor Pedro Duarte Neves to the Committee of Inquiry on the Situation That Led to the Nationalization of LBW and On Inherent Banking Supervision - January 27, 2009
text: Initial statement by Deputy Governor Pedro Duarte Neves to the Committee of Inquiry on the Situation That Led to the Nationalization of LBW and on Inherent Banking Supervision January 27, 2009 Madam President of the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry, ladies and gentlemen, I thank you for addressing this Commission and providing all the clarifications that can contribute to a better understanding of what happened in the LBW case. The LBW  especially for its very rapid growth  has always deserved a very close monitoring of banking supervision in aspects such as credit to group companies, provision and internal control. The situations detected were resolved, following supervisory actions by Banco de Portugal, and the institution was strengthening its funds in a regular manner. However, at the same time, and by the willly attitude of the institution's management gons  which objectively omitted and provided false information to supervisory authorities  a parallel structure of unregistered operations, not available documentary and therefore not detectable by normal supervisory and audit methods, was developed. It is interesting to recall today that in March 2001, the then President of the LBW publicly stated that "Banco Insular is one of FINCOR's assets that are of no interest to SLN". The knowledge, in June 2008, of the instrumentalization of Banco Insular and the existence of the so-called 'Virtual Counter'  whose existence, even today, can not fail to create enormous perplexity  posed very serious and totally new problems to the solvency of the institution, which eventually became decisive in the outcome of this case. It should be stressed, however, that the admission and confession by the group's administration of the existence of this fraudulent situation was the corollary of a supervisory action of Banco de Portugal which - from the beginning of 2008 and triggered above all by an anima dencia - was obtaining elements increasingly been of the relationship of the group domain in relation to Banco Insular. I should mention here a meeting that took place in May 2008 with the members of the Board of Directors of SLN and which was convened by me to clarify the group's relationship with Banco Insular - drawing attention to the individual responsibilities of omission of answers or the provision of false information - and which proved decisive for the final confession, by Dr. Abdool Vakil, that the Group had the material domain of Banco Insular and, most surprisingly, of the existence of the so-called Virtual Counter. Before answering the questions of the members of this Parliamentary Committee, I would like to clarify three aspects that have been present in this work: the audit determined by Banco de Portugal in 2008, the requests for information in arrears and the correspondence with the Attorney General's Office of Replica on Banco Insular. On June 4, 2008  following the surprising revelation of the letter of 2 June  Banco de Portugal determined the presentation of consolidated accounts with the inclusion of previously omitted entities, duly certified by an authorized external entity, as well as the presentation of a report of environmental provisions relating to the assets to be integrated. At the time, Banco de Portugal did not specify which entity should carry out this work, because it was known that a new Administration was to be elected and Dr. Abdool Vakil had no conditions to advance the process in this transition phase. At the first meeting with Dr. Miguel Cadilhe, on 26 June, he expressed his intention to have an audit carried out  which had already been determined by Banco de Portugal on 4 June  and it was agreed that, in order not to be carried out two audits by two different companies, Banco de Portugal would accept the choice of the audit firm to be carried out by the new Board of Directors of SLN. It was also transmitted at that meeting that this audit should be carried out in the light of nero 2 of Art. 116 of the RGICSF, to allow Banco de Portugal to have access to the auditor and the monitoring of audit work. Later, Dr. Miguel Cadilhe informed Banco de Portugal of the audit ing company chosen and then Banco de Portugal confirmed in writing its determination, as agreed at the first meeting on 26 June. It is difficult to understand that, although these elements have been applied since the Governor's Hearing in the Parliamentary Committee on Budget and Finance on 11 November 2008, the determination of this audit by Banco de Portugal continues to question the determination of this audit. Let us now move on to the question of overdue requests for information, which Dr Abdool Vakil encountered when he took over the chairmanship of the BPN. As mentioned in that Commission by Dr Carlos Santos, a new inspection action on the LBW was scheduled for early February 2008. As is customary in these situations, a long list of requests for information was delivered at the end of January to various group institutions, which  added to clarifications already requested in the course of January 2008 and subsequent questions, some of which following responses from the bank, perfectly normal in supervisory processes  lead us to a nero of unanswered items of the order of magnitude of that referred to by Dr. Abdool Vakil. This, moreover, illustrates the great pressure that Banco de Portugal has exerted on lBW, in this regard as in other periods. In addition, it must be made clear that all the requests for information previously made by Banco de Portugal have followed, in some cases new requests for elements in order to make the responses to Banco de Portugal more complete and precise. It was, moreover, in the course of this case that, already in 2007, false information was provided to Banco de Portugal, which led, in 2008 and at the time of this finding, to the establishment of counter-ordination proceedings against the institutions and members of their social groups. A final comment on the correspondence exchanged between 2004 and 2007 with the Attorney General's Office of Replica. It was a set of extremely simple and direct questions such as "have authorization or request to operate in our country", participation in "occasional active operations" or "financing concessions for people and entities resident in Portugal" and which, consequently, had simple and direct answers. It should be stressed in this propitious that Banco Insular was obviously not under the supervision of Banco de Portugal and that none of the letters from the Attorney General's Office of Replica made any kind of reference to lBW or SLN. Moreover, the first reference to LBW appears in the January 2008 letter sent by Banco de Portugal. Surprisingly, this correspondence has been given great relevance, and the communication of Banco de Portugal to the PGR of August 2008 has been virtually forgotten, which, according to the Attorney General of Replica in hearing in the Parliamentary Committee on Budget and Finance, contributed, together with other documents transmitted, to a faster advance of investigations in the investigation of criminal responsibilities. In conclusion, Banco de Portugal acted throughout this process within the legal and regulatory standards that frame prudential supervision. There are no perfect or infallible organizations, but over the years, Banco de Portugal has shown that it is a serious and rigorous institution and that, therefore, it must continue to deserve the respect of the Portuguese. Pedro Duarte Neves
text_original: Declarao inicial do Vice-Governador Pedro Duarte Neves  Comisso de Inqurito sobre a Situao que Levou  Nacionalizao do BPN e sobre a Superviso Bancria Inerente 27 de Janeiro de 2009 Senhora Presidente da Comisso Parlamentar de Inqurito, Senhores Deputados, Agradeo a possibilidade de me dirigir a esta Comisso e de prestar todos os esclarecimentos que possam contribuir para uma melhor compreenso do que aconteceu no caso BPN. O BPN  sobretudo pelo seu crescimento muito rpido  mereceu sempre um acompanhamento muito primo da superviso bancria em aspectos como o crdito a empresas do grupo, constituio de proviss e controlo interno. As situas detectadas foram sendo resolvidas, na sequncia de acs de superviso do Banco de Portugal, e a instituio foi reforando os seus fundos prrios de uma forma regular. Contudo, paralelamente, e por atitude dolosa dos gos de administrao da instituio  que de uma forma objectiva omitiram e prestaram informao falsa s autoridades de superviso -foi-se desenvolvendo uma estrutura paralela de operas no registadas, no disponveis documentalmente e, por isso, no passveis de deteco pelos mtodos normais de superviso e de auditoria.  interessante recordar hoje que, em Maro de 2001, o ento Presidente do BPN afirmou publicamente que o Banco Insular  um dos activos da FINCOR que no interessam  SLN. O conhecimento, em Junho de 2008, da instrumentalizao do Banco Insular e da existncia do chamado Balco Virtual  cuja existncia, ainda hoje, no pode deixar de criar enorme perplexidade  colocaram problemas muito graves e totalmente novos  solvabilidade da instituio, que acabaram por ser determinantes no desfecho deste caso. Convm, contudo, sublinhar bem que a admisso e confisso pela administrao do grupo da existncia desta situao fraudulenta foi o corolrio de uma aco de superviso do Banco de Portugal que - a partir do incio de 2008 e desencadeada sobretudo por uma dencia anima - foi obtendo elementos cada vez mais sidos da relao do domnio de grupo em relao ao Banco Insular. Deverei referir aqui uma reunio que teve lugar, em Maio de 2008, com os membros do Conselho de Administrao da SLN e que foi convocada por mim para esclarecimento do relacionamento do grupo com o Banco Insular - chamando a ateno para as responsabilidades individuais de omisso de respostas ou de prestao de informas falsas  e que se mostrou decisiva para a confisso final, pelo Dr. Abdool Vakil, de que o Grupo tinha o domnio material do Banco Insular e, mais surpreendentemente ainda, da existncia do chamado Balco Virtual. Antes de responder s perguntas dos membros desta Comisso Parlamentar, gostaria de esclarecer trs aspectos que tm estado presentes nestes trabalhos: a auditoria determinada pelo Banco de Portugal em 2008, os pedidos de informao em atraso e a correspondncia com a Procuradoria-Geral da Replica sobre o Banco Insular. No dia 4 de Junho de 2008  em sequncia da surpreendente revelao da carta de 2 de Junho  o Banco de Portugal determinou a apresentao de contas consolidadas com incluso de entidades anteriormente omitidas, devidamente certificadas por entidade externa habilitada, bem como a apresentao de um relatio de proviss econicas referentes aos activos a integrar. Na altura, o Banco de Portugal no especificou qual a entidade que deveria proceder a esse trabalho, pois se sabia que ia ser eleita uma nova Administrao e o Dr. Abdool Vakil no tinha condis para fazer avanar o processo nessa fase de transio. Na primeira reunio com o Dr. Miguel Cadilhe, no dia 26 de Junho, ele manifestou a sua inteno de mandar proceder a uma auditoria  o que j tinha sido determinado pelo Banco de Portugal em 4 de Junho  tendo sido acordado que, para no serem feitas duas auditorias por duas empresas diferentes, o Banco de Portugal aceitaria a escolha da empresa de auditoria a efectuar pelo novo Conselho de Administrao da SLN. Foi tambm transmitido nessa reunio que essa auditoria deveria ser realizada  luz do nero 2 do art 116 do RGICSF, para permitir ao Banco de Portugal ter acesso ao auditor e ao acompanhamento dos trabalhos de auditoria. Posteriormente, o Dr. Miguel Cadilhe informou o Banco de Portugal da empresa de auditoria escolhida e sento o Banco de Portugal confirmou por escrito a sua determinao, conforme tinha ficado acordado na primeira reunio de 26 de Junho.  difcil compreender que, apesar destes elementos serem plicos desde a Audio do Senhor Governador na Comisso Parlamentar de Oramento e Finanas, a 11 de Novembro de 2008, se continue a questionar a determinao desta auditoria pelo Banco de Portugal. Passemos agora  questo dos pedidos de informao em atraso, que o Dr Abdool Vakil encontrou quando assumiu a presidncia do BPN. Conforme referido nesta mesma Comisso pelo Dr. Carlos Santos, estava agendada uma nova aco de inspeco ao BPN para o incio de Fevereiro de 2008. Como  habitual nestas situas, foi entregue, no final de Janeiro, uma longa lista de pedidos de informao, para vrias instituis do grupo, que  adicionado a esclarecimentos j solicitados no decurso do prrio ms de Janeiro de 2008 e de quests posteriores, algumas das quais na sequncia de respostas do banco, perfeitamente normais em processos de superviso  nos conduz a um nero de itens por responder da ordem de grandeza do referido pelo Dr. Abdool Vakil. Este aspecto, alis, silustra a presso grande que o Banco de Portugal exerceu sobre o BPN, neste como noutros perodos. Adicionalmente,  preciso que fique bem claro que todos os pedidos de informao anteriormente feitos pelo Banco de Portugal tiveram sequncia, suscitando-se nalguns casos novos pedidos de elementos de forma a tornar mais completas e precisas as respostas ao Banco de Portugal. Foi, alis, no decurso deste processo que, j em 2007, foram prestadas informas falsas ao Banco de Portugal, que levaram, em 2008 e no momento desta constatao,  instaurao de processos de contra-ordenao s instituis e aos membros dos seus gos sociais. Um comentrio final sobre a correspondncia trocada entre 2004 e 2007 com a Procuradoria-Geral da Replica. Tratou-se de um conjunto de perguntas extremamente simples e directas como tem autorizao ou pedido para operar no nosso pas, participao em operas activas ocasionais ou de concesss de financiamento a favor de pessoas e entidades residentes em Portugal e que, consequentemente, tiveram respostas simples e directas. Sublinhe-se, a este propito, que o Banco Insular no estava, obviamente, sob a superviso do Banco de Portugal e que nenhuma das cartas da Procuradoria-Geral da Replica fazia qualquer tipo de referncia ao BPN ou  SLN. Alis, a primeira referncia ao BPN aparece na carta de Janeiro de 2008 remetida pelo Banco de Portugal. Surpreendentemente tem sido dada grande relevncia a esta correspondncia, tendo sido praticamente esquecida a comunicao do Banco de Portugal  PGR de Agosto de 2008 que, de acordo com o Senhor Procurador-Geral da Replica em Audio na Comisso Parlamentar de Oramento e Finanas, contribuiu, juntamente com outros documentos transmitidos, para um avano mais rpido das investigas em sede de apuramento de responsabilidades criminais. Em concluso, o Banco de Portugal actuou ao longo deste processo dentro dos padrs legais e regulamentares que enquadram a superviso prudencial. No h organizas perfeitas nem infalveis, mas, ao longo dos anos, o Banco de Portugal tem demonstrado que  uma instituio sria e rigorosa e que, por isso, deve continuar a merecer o respeito dos portugueses. Pedro Duarte Neves

Title: Initial statement by the Governor of Banco de Portugal in the presentation of the Winter Economic Bulletin (2008)
text: Press Conference on 6 January 2009 INITIAL STATEMENT OF THE GOVERNOR OF BANCO DE PORTUGAL IN THE PRESENTATION OF THE WINTER ECONOMIC BULLETIN (2008) 1. As usual at this time of year, the Econico Bulletin includes projections for the Portuguese economy for two-year cousins. Prepared in the context of the Eurosystem projection exercise in October and November, however, some hipsses were updated and the latest information on economic developments was incorporated. Econic forecasts point to a 0.8 percent drop in econic activity in 2009 and growth of 0.3 percent in 2010. They are the most negative published so far on the Portuguese economy, although the raw updates to be published by international organizations are not yet known. The risk analysis we carry out points to possible alternative scenarios that are mostly descending. The estimate for growth in 2008 is also revised down, from 0.5 percent to just 0.3 percent. This change stems from the partial indicators already available pointing to a very negative performance of the economy in the fourth quarter. This also inevitably affects the forecast of average growth for 2009. All these negative perspectives occur in a context of marked recession in all developed countries and possibly in the framework of the world economy as a whole for the first time in decades. In fact, the current macro-ecological framework of the Portuguese economy is marked by a framework of interaction between an unprecedented crisis in international financial markets and an international recession. Despite measures by the authorities at global level to strengthen confidence and restore the smooth functioning of financial markets, there remains a high turbulence in these markets, with a significant revaluation of risk by investors and a deterioration in confidence in various segments of financial markets globally. In this context, it is worth noting the low liquidity in the interbank money markets of major advanced economies and in private debt markets, in particular in the wholesale financing markets of financial institutions. A small open economy fully integrated in eco-and financial terms as the Portuguese economy is strongly affected by that macro-econic environment. The slowdown in eco-activity and the reduction in global growth prospects, as well as the high uncertainty as to the magnitude and duration of the current down-stage of the econico cycle, tend to adversely affect external demand for domestic companies and the expectations of national econicos for future demand developments. 2. Following the recessionary phase of the international economy and the fall in commodity prices, in particular petreo, inflation will fall from 2.7 percent in 2008 to just 1 percent this year. This fall in inflation will contribute to a projected average increase in real disposable income of households by 1.1 percent. This implies, in turn, that, despite the decline in production, private consumption should have a positive growth of 0.4 percent, with the consumption of non-durable current goods knowing a variation of 1.2 percent. The already verified reduction in credit interest rates will also help to support consumer expenditure. On the other hand, the variation in consumption is negatively affected by an increase in the savings rate resulting from greater uncertainty about the future and an increase in unemployment. This thymus is the most negative point of the evolution of the economy, the human drama it entails, and the reduction in the income that originates in the segment of the affected population. The components of demand that explain the fall in domestic production are fundamentally investment and exports. The most recent estimates already point to a reduction in investment (FBCF) of 0.8 percent in 2008, aps a growth of 3.2 percent in 2007. Forecasts for this year and the cousin point to an investment contraction (FBCF) of 1.7 and 0.3 percent. This evolution essentially reflects a deterioration in the prospects for demand developments in the domestic and foreign markets and a drop in the expectations of eco-actors. As regards exports, they have already contributed significantly to the sharp slowdown in econica activity in 2008. Current estimates point to a volume export growth rate of 0.6 percent in 2008 (up from 7.6 percent in 2007). Forecasts indicate a drop in exports in 2009 (-3.6 percent) and growth of 1.8 percent in 2010, representing a prime evolution of the external demand indicator considered in the international framework underlying the current projection. This drop in exports in 2009 represents the maintenance of the trend already observed at the end of 2008 and affects both exports of goods and exports of tourism and other services. The economy's external financing needs will have increased from 8.2 percent in 2007 to 9.0 percent of nominal GDP in 2008. After the estimated deterioration for 2008, the deficit in the balance of goods and services as a percentage of GDP is expected to decline to 7.0 percent in 2009, subsequently increasing to 7.5 percent in 2010. This evolution is partly conditioned by the projection for the terms of exchange, which incorporate the impact of the evolution of the petreo price. It is assumed that this saw a sharp average decline in international markets in 2009, in a context of reducing global growth and demand prospects, and subsequently re-emerging. If we exclude energy goods, the deficit in the balance of goods and services is expected to stabilise between 2009 and 2010 at a level higher than that estimated for 2008 (3.6 per cent of GDP). This same deficit was around 8 per cent of GDP in 2000. Its reduction to 3.6 percent means a remarkable adjustment that included the transformation of the productive structure of the economy that in competitive terms promoted significant net exports of goods and services. The deterioration of the total balance of goods and services is due to the energy balance, which is aggravated in the total current account by increasing the deficit in the payment of interest and dividends abroad arising from the external indebtedness accumulated in the meantime. It should be pointed out that, although the level of indebtedness of companies and individuals is a source of vulnerability, there are some factors that mitigate this assessment. On the one hand, the trend of increased indebtedness of companies and individuals has largely translated the response of econic agents to the new regime in which the Portuguese economy began to operate with its participation in the euro area, characterized by lower and less volatile interest rates. This was reflected, despite the higher level of indebtedness, in a relative stability of interest paid by the non-financial private sector as a percentage of GDP. It should also be noted that this has occurred without developing speculative bubbles in the real estate market, unlike in other countries. In addition, it is important to highlight the absence of a sub-prime segment in housing credit in Portugal. In fact, the results of the previous Patrimio and Household Indebtedness Survey indicate that the share of the credit market, in particular housing credit, of lower income households is quite limited and, for indebted households, the value of their gross wealth (which includes the value of housing) exceeds that of their debts with a relatively comfortable margin. In another perspective, it should be stressed that the external financing needs for this year and the cousin represent a new and inevitable worsening of the GDP ratio of our indebtedness in a broad sense (International Investment Position). In the short term, containing more growth in external indebtedness would imply a worsening of the recession, which would not be acceptable in the face of the risks of unemployment and loss of income that entails. The priority of eco-policy in all countries now is to try to alleviate a recession that has become inevitable, but which must be contained in order to avoid scenarios of depression and deflation which, fortunately, seem to be off the horizon thanks to the determination of governments and central banks to adopt expansionist policies. 3. With regard to the major orientations of econic policy, I consider it important to highlight the following aspects: 3.1. First, in the current context of the global financial crisis, it is absolutely crucial to ensure the smooth functioning of the financial system. Stabilisation of the financial system is a prerequisite for resolving the econic crisis. In addition to the abundant supply of liquidity by central banks, the programmes to support the recapitalisation of banks and guarantees for their financing were essential to ensure financial stability, which was dangerously at risk after the bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers. It should be stressed that there is now a strong interaction between sovereign risk and risk from banks. This interaction reinforces the need to ensure both a sustainable situation of the finances and a strengthening of the balance sheet of banks. In this context, it is worth mentioning that the financing of banks in the framework of guarantees granted by the State has implied a cost for banks that depends directly on sovereign risk, also incorporating comissss calculated according to the risk of the banks. These guarantees do not therefore represent a subsidy to banks. Finally, in the current downside phase of the eco-cycle and the deterioration of the balance sheets of companies and households, a cyclical slowdown in the credit granted by the banking system, which must be distinguished from credit restriction situations associated with balance sheet difficulties of banks, should be expected. Moreover, in a recessive context there is a normal decrease in the demand for credit by individuals and companies, and it is not possible to distinguish in practice what in the credit slowdown is the result of the drop in demand or the restrictions of supply by banks. In any case, it is essential to ensure sound balance sheet of banks in order to ensure access to credit for eco-agents with appropriate balance sheet structures and profitable projects. 3.2. The international recession is caused by a widespread drop in demand and not by any real supply shocks. Measures to combat recessionary risks must therefore focus on having an effect on expanding demand in the shortest possible time. There are now no measures at stake to improve supply efficiency or the growth potential of the economy, although it was ideal to make everything compatible. Monetary policy has made its contribution and should continue to do so if inflation threatens to fall significantly below 2 per cent. In fact, the definition of stability we adopt in the Eurosystem points to inflation 'below, but close to 2 per cent'. Any risks of inflation consolidating well below this figure should be contained preemptively with interest rate declines. However, we must not forget that the effectiveness of monetary policy, always being less to respond to recessionary risks than to risks of high inflation, is now particularly limited in its transmission possibilities due to the situation of lack of confidence and liquidity in various segments of the money and credit markets. It has therefore become indispensable to make greater use of budgetary policy. 3.3. In accordance with the recent IMF text (IMF, Fiscal Policy for the Crisis, Office Memorandum 23 December), 'the budget package must be timely, large, durable, diversified, contingent, collective and sustainable'. This necessarily implies compromises depending on the concrete situation of each economy, since some of those characteristics are contradisitias each other. Ideally, fiscal stimulus programmes should comply with the following principles: - Focus on investment expenses of immediate realization and quick finishing, so as not to imply large future expenses. The government's recently announced programme for the construction and maintenance of schools is a good example. - Promote transfers to the most deprived segments of the population with a greater propensity for consumption (e.g. temporary improvements in the condition and duration of unemployment benefits). - Avoid general tax rate cuts that become difficult to reverse in the future, but may adopt specific temporary reductions or immediate tax returns for groups more prone to consumption (e.g. individual contributions of employees to social security). - Limit direct support for the maintenance of employment to clearly viable future companies and avoid discretionary support to entire sectors of activity. - Anticipate the future elimination of some of the measures now adopted or announce compensation measures in revenue or expenditure to reduce the deficit. This great aspect is concerned with providing guarantees of future sustainability of the finances, an important condition for maintaining without great increase in costs access to external financing. From this perspective, it is essential that Portugal seeks to respect in the announced programmes the terms and limits of the Stability Pact, which only admits in a recessionary period a deficit above three percent if it is limited and temporary. 4. This year and the cousin will not be easy for the Portuguese, but it is preferable to know what they can realistically count on and adjust as best they can to the recessive phase that the world goes through. This year, those who retain their jobs, and are the vast majority, will see their incomes increase and may slightly expand their consumption levels. We all have to be prudent in the current situation and prevent the future. The recession will pass and state intervention and policies around the world will be able to avoid the worst. The current phase of weak domestic spending growth has the effect of containing the expansion of indebtedness and pressuring companies to restructure, increasing productivity and reorienting the destinations of their production. Companies that remain viable should take advantage of this period to contain costs, reorganize and diversify production, build and consolidate brands, invest in training and think about recruiting quality staff that becomes available, carefully manage debt and treasury, look for new markets. The possibility of the economy containing the crisis and resuming a path of significant eco-growth depends heavily on the ability of companies to react appropriately to challenges and adopt innovation strategies. Responding to the crisis requires determination and effectiveness of the policies and dynamism of companies, in order to overcome the current phase of under-performing environment. Lisbon, 6 January 2009 Victor Constantius
text_original: Conferncia de Imprensa em 6 de Janeiro de 2009 DECLARAO INICIAL DO GOVERNADOR DO BANCO DE PORTUGAL NA APRESENTAO DO BOLETIM ECONMICO DE INVERNO (2008) 1. Como habitualmente nesta altura do ano, o Boletim Econico inclui as projecs para a economia portuguesa referentes aos primos dois anos. Preparadas no contexto do exerccio de projecs do Eurosistema que decorreu em Outubro e Novembro, procedeu-se, no entanto, a actualizas de algumas hipeses e  incorporao de informao mais recente sobre a evoluo econica. As previss econicas apontam para uma quebra da actividade econica de 0,8 por cento em 2009 e para um crescimento de +0,3 por cento em 2010. So as mais negativas at agora publicadas sobre a economia portuguesa, embora no se conheam ainda as primas actualizas a publicar por organismos internacionais. A anlise de riscos a que procedemos aponta para possveis cenrios alternativos maioritariamente descendentes. A estimativa para o crescimento em 2008  tambm revista em baixa, de 0,5 por cento para apenas 0,3 por cento. Esta alterao decorre de os indicadores parciais j disponveis apontarem para um desempenho muito negativo da economia no quarto trimestre. Esta circunstncia tambm afecta inevitavelmente a previso do crescimento mdio para 2009. Todas estas perspectivas negativas ocorrem num contexto de recesso marcada no conjunto dos pases desenvolvidos e, possivelmente, no quadro da economia mundial como um todo pela primeira vez em dcadas. Na verdade, o actual enquadramento macroeconico da economia portuguesa  marcado por um quadro de interaco entre uma crise sem precedentes nos mercados financeiros internacionais e uma recesso internacional. No obstante as medidas das autoridades a nvel global no sentido de reforar a confiana e restabelecer o regular funcionamento dos mercados financeiros, permanece uma elevada turbulncia nestes mercados, com uma significativa reavaliao em alta do risco por parte dos investidores e uma deteriorao da confiana em vrios segmentos dos mercados financeiros a nvel global. Neste contexto,  de destacar a reduzida liquidez nos mercados monetrios interbancrios das principais economias avanadas e nos mercados de dvida privada, em particular nos mercados de financiamento por grosso das instituis financeiras. Uma pequena economia aberta plenamente integrada em termos econicos e financeiros como a economia portuguesa  fortemente afectada por aquele enquadramento macroeconico. O abrandamento da actividade econica e a reduo das perspectivas de crescimento mundial, bem como a elevada incerteza quanto  magnitude e durao da actual fase descendente do ciclo econico, tendem a afectar negativamente a procura externa dirigida s empresas nacionais e as expectativas dos agentes econicos nacionais quanto  evoluo futura da procura. 2. Acompanhando a fase recessiva da economia internacional e a descida de preos das matrias-primas, em particular do petreo, a inflao ir reduzir-se de 2,7 por cento em 2008 para apenas 1 por cento este ano. Esta descida da inflao contribuir para um aumento mdio previsto do rendimento disponvel real das famlias em 1,1 por cento. Isto implica, por sua vez, que, apesar da descida da produo, o consumo privado deva ter um crescimento positivo de 0,4 por cento, com o consumo de bens correntes no-duradouros a conhecer uma variao de +1,2 por cento. A reduo j verificada das taxas de juro do crdito ajudar tambm a suportar as despesas de consumo. Por outro lado, a variao do consumo  afectada negativamente por um incremento da taxa de poupana decorrente da maior incerteza quanto ao futuro e por um aumento do desemprego. Este timo constitui o ponto mais negativo da evoluo da economia, pelo drama humano que implica, e pela reduo do rendimento que origina no segmento da populao afectada. As componentes da procura que explicam a queda da produo interna so fundamentalmente o investimento e as exportas. As estimativas mais recentes apontam j para uma reduo do investimento (FBCF) de 0,8 por cento em 2008, aps um crescimento de 3,2 por cento em 2007. As previss para este ano e o primo apontam para uma contraco do investimento (FBCF) de 1,7 e de 0,3 por cento. Esta evoluo traduz essencialmente uma deteriorao das perspectivas de evoluo da procura nos mercados interno e externo e uma quebra das expectativas dos agentes econicos. No que respeita s exportas, estas contriburam j significativamente para o forte abrandamento da actividade econica em 2008. As estimativas actuais apontam para uma taxa de crescimento das exportas em volume de 0,6 por cento em 2008 (contra 7,6 por cento em 2007). As previss indicam uma queda das exportas em 2009 (-3,6 por cento) e um crescimento de 1,8 por cento em 2010, o que representa uma evoluo prima do indicador de procura externa considerado no enquadramento internacional subjacente  actual projeco. Esta quebra das exportas em 2009 representa a manuteno da tendncia j observada no final de 2008 e afecta tanto as exportas de mercadorias como as exportas de turismo e outros servios. As necessidades de financiamento externo da economia tero aumentado de 8,2 por cento em 2007 para 9,0 por cento do PIB nominal em 2008. Ap a deteriorao estimada para 2008, o dfice da balana de bens e servios em percentagem do PIB dever reduzir-se para 7,0 por cento em 2009, aumentando posteriormente para 7,5 por cento em 2010. Esta evoluo est condicionada em parte pela projeco para os termos de troca, os quais incorporam o impacto da evoluo do preo do petreo. Assume-se que este registe uma forte queda em termos mdios nos mercados internacionais em 2009, num contexto de reduo das perspectivas de crescimento e procura mundiais, e que apresente posteriormente alguma recuperao. Se excluirmos os bens energticos, o dfice da balana de bens e servios dever estabilizar entre 2009 e 2010 num nvel primo do estimado para 2008 (3,6 por cento do PIB). Este mesmo dfice situava-se em cerca de 8 por cento do PIB em 2000. A sua reduo para 3,6 por cento significa um assinalvel ajustamento que incluiu a transformao da estrutura produtiva da economia que em termos competitivos promoveu exportas lquidas significativas de bens e servios. A deteriorao da balana total de bens e servios deve-se  balana energtica, o que  agravado na balana corrente total pelo acentuar do dfice de pagamento de juros e dividendos ao exterior decorrentes do endividamento externo entretanto acumulado. Assinale-se que, apesar de o nvel de endividamento das empresas e particulares constituir uma fonte de vulnerabilidade, existem alguns factores que atenuam esta avaliao. Por um lado, a tendncia de aumento do endividamento das empresas e dos particulares traduziu, em grande medida, a resposta endena dos agentes econicos ao novo regime em que a economia portuguesa passou a operar com a sua participao na rea do euro, caracterizado por taxas de juro mais baixas e menos volteis. Este facto reflectiu-se, apesar do maior nvel de endividamento, numa relativa estabilidade dos juros pagos pelo sector privado no financeiro em percentagem do PIB.  igualmente de referir que tal ocorreu sem que fossem desenvolvidas bolhas especulativas no mercado imobilirio, ao contrrio do observado em outros pases. Adicionalmente, importa sublinhar a ausncia de um segmento sub-prime no crdito  habitao em Portugal. De facto, os resultados do timo Inqurito ao Patrimio e Endividamento das Famlias indicam que a participao no mercado de crdito, em particular do crdito para habitao, das famlias de rendimentos mais baixos  bastante limitada e, para as famlias endividadas, o valor da sua riqueza bruta (que inclui o valor da habitao) ultrapassa o das respectivas dvidas com uma margem relativamente confortvel. Noutra perspectiva, sublinhe-se que as necessidades de financiamento externo para este ano e o primo representam um novo e inevitvel agravamento do rcio em relao ao PIB do nosso endividamento num sentido lato (Posio de Investimento Internacional). No curto prazo, conter mais o crescimento do endividamento externo implicaria o agravamento da recesso, que no seria aceitvel face aos riscos de desemprego e perda de rendimento que implica. A prioridade da poltica econica em todos os pases consiste agora em tentar minorar uma recesso que se tornou inevitvel, mas que h que conter para evitar cenrios de depresso e deflao que, felizmente, parecem afastados do horizonte graas  determinao de Governos e Bancos Centrais em adoptar polticas expansionistas. 3. No que concerne s grandes orientas da poltica econica, considero importante sublinhar os seguintes aspectos: 3.1. Primeiro, no actual contexto de crise financeira a nvel global,  absolutamente crucial garantir o funcionamento regular do sistema financeiro. A estabilizao do sistema financeiro constitui um pr-requisito para a resoluo da crise econica. Para alm do abundante fornecimento de liquidez pelos Bancos Centrais, os programas plicos de apoio  recapitalizao dos bancos e de garantias ao seu financiamento foram essenciais para garantir a estabilidade financeira, que foi posta perigosamente em risco ap a falncia do Lehman Brothers. Sublinhe-se que existe actualmente uma forte interaco entre o risco soberano e o risco dos bancos. Esta interaco refora a necessidade de assegurar simultaneamente uma situao sustentvel das finanas plicas e um reforo do balano dos bancos. Neste mbito, vale a pena referir que o financiamento dos bancos no quadro das garantias concedidas pelo Estado tem implcito um custo para os bancos que depende directamente do risco soberano, incorporando tambm comisss calculadas em funo do risco dos prrios bancos. Estas garantias no representam, assim, um subsdio aos bancos. Finalmente, na actual fase descendente do ciclo econico e de deteriorao dos balanos das empresas e das famlias, ser de esperar uma desacelerao cclica do crdito concedido pelo sistema bancrio, que importa distinguir de situas de restrio do crdito associadas a dificuldades de balano dos prrios bancos. Alis, num contexto recessivo existe uma normal diminuio da procura de crdito por particulares e empresas, no sendo possvel distinguir na prtica o que na desacelerao do crdito  o resultado da quebra da procura ou das restris da oferta pelos bancos. Em qualquer caso,  fundamental assegurar a solidez do balano dos bancos, de modo a garantir o acesso ao crdito dos agentes econicos com estruturas de balano adequadas e projectos rentveis. 3.2. A recesso internacional  causada por uma quebra generalizada da procura e no por quaisquer choques reais de oferta. As medidas para combater os riscos recessivos tm assim que se concentrar em produzir efeitos na expanso da procura no mais curto espao de tempo possvel. No esto agora em causa medidas para melhorar a eficincia da oferta ou o potencial de crescimento da economia, embora fosse ideal compatibilizar tudo. A poltica monetria tem dado o seu contributo e dever continuar a faz-lo se a inflao ameaar descer significativamente abaixo de 2 por cento. Na verdade, a definio de estabilidade que adoptamos no Eurosistema aponta para uma inflao abaixo, mas primo de 2 por cento. Quaisquer riscos de a inflao se consolidar muito abaixo desse valor devem ser contidos preventivamente com descidas das taxas de juro. No entanto, no podemos esquecer que a eficcia da poltica monetria, sendo sempre menor para responder a riscos recessivos do que a riscos de inflao alta, est neste momento particularmente limitada nas suas possibilidades de transmisso pela situao de falta de confiana e liquidez em vrios segmentos dos mercados monetrio e de crdito. Tornou-se, assim, indispensvel recorrer em maior escala  poltica oramental. 3.3. Nos termos do recente texto do FMI (IMF, Fiscal Policy for the Crisis, Office Memorandum 23 December), o pacote oramental timo deve ser atempado, grande, duradouro, diversificado, contingente, colectivo e sustentvel. Isto implica necessariamente compromissos consoante a situao concreta de cada economia, uma vez que algumas daquelas caractersticas so contraditias entre si. Idealmente, os programas de estmulo oramental deveriam obedecer aos seguintes princpios: - Concentrarem-se em despesas de investimento de imediata realizao e rpido acabamento, para no implicarem grandes despesas futuras. O programa recentemente anunciado pelo Governo de construo e manuteno de escolas constitui um bom exemplo. - Promoverem transferncias para segmentos mais carenciados da populao com maior propenso ao consumo (v.g. melhorias temporrias das condis e durao dos subsdios de desemprego). - Evitarem descidas gerais de taxas de impostos que se tornam difceis de reverter no futuro, podendo, porm, adoptar redus temporrias especficas ou devolus de impostos no imediato para grupos com maior propenso ao consumo (v.g. contribuis individuais de empregados por conta de outrem para a segurana social). - Limitarem os apoios directos  manuteno do emprego a empresas claramente com futuro vivel e evitarem apoios discricionrios a sectores inteiros de actividade. - Preverem desde j a eliminao futura de algumas das medidas agora adoptadas ou anunciar medidas de compensao em receita ou despesa para reduzir o dfice. Este timo aspecto obedece  preocupao de fornecer garantias de sustentabilidade futura das finanas plicas, condio importante para manter sem grande aumento de custos o acesso ao financiamento externo. Nesta perspectiva,  essencial que Portugal procure respeitar nos programas anunciados os termos e limites do Pacto de Estabilidade, que apenas admite em perodo recessivo um dfice acima de trs por cento se este for limitado e temporrio. 4. Este ano e o primo no sero fceis para os portugueses, mas  prefervel saber com o que podem contar realisticamente e ajustarem-se o melhor que for possvel  fase recessiva que o mundo atravessa. Este ano, os que conservam os seus empregos, e so a grande maioria, vero os seus rendimentos aumentarem e podero expandir ligeiramente os seus nveis de consumo. Todos temos, porm, que ser prudentes na actual situao e prevenir o futuro. A recesso passar e a interveno do Estado e as polticas plicas, um pouco por todo o mundo, conseguiro evitar o pior. A fase actual de dbil crescimento da despesa interna tem o efeito de conter a expanso do endividamento e de pressionar as empresas para se reestruturarem, aumentando a produtividade e reorientando os destinos das suas produs. As empresas que permanecem viveis devem aproveitar este perodo para conter custos, reorganizar e diversificar produs, construir e consolidar marcas, investir na formao e pensar em recrutar pessoal de qualidade que fique disponvel, gerir cuidadosamente o endividamento e a tesouraria, procurar novos mercados. A possibilidade de a economia conter a crise e retomar um caminho de crescimento econico significativo depende muito da capacidade das empresas para reagirem apropriadamente aos desafios e adoptarem estratgias de inovao. Responder  crise exige determinao e eficcia das polticas plicas e dinamismo das empresas, para mais rapidamente superarmos a actual fase de insuficiente desempenho econico. Lisboa, 6 de Janeiro de 2009 Vtor Constncio

Title: Initial statement by the Governor of Banco de Portugal in the presentation of the Spring Economic Bulletin (2009)
text: Press Conference on 14 April 2009 INITIAL STATEMENT OF THE GOVERNOR OF BANCO DE PORTUGAL IN THE PRESENTATION OF THE ECONOMIC BULLETIN OF SPRING (2009) In the context of the world's largest ecological crisis since the Great Depression of 1930, Portugal began in the second half of last year a recessionary period that is anticipated as the deepest and longest of decades. The Econic Bulletin that we publish today explains in detail the evolution of the Portuguese economy in 2008, marked by zero economic growth. Given the rapid and profound change in the information available in the past few months, we have also made a very significant revision of our projections for the current year. In fact, our current forecast for economic developments this year is for a recession of 3.5 percent, a figure that is expected to be marginally below the euro area average. This number is compared to the 0.8 per cent we published in January, although I had the opportunity to state publicly after that that the forecast for the beginning of the year would be revised down. In fact, this forecast had been made on the basis of data available for October last year and subsequent information on the 4th quarter radically changed the outlook for Portugal as well as for the rest of the world. World growth and trade sank at the end of the year and in the first quarter of this year. For Portugal, this represented in the fourth quarter a fall in GDP of 1.8 percent in the quarter and a reduction of 8.9% in exports and 8.4% of investment. This change made us review the forecast of external demand directed to the Portuguese economy in 2009 of a reduction from 2.5% to 13%. The recession of 2009 is thus mainly explained by the fall in exports (14.2%) and investment (14.4%). In the current situation of the world economy all forecasts are surrounded by enormous uncertainty. This is particularly true of the investment, but this time it also applies to the current forecast of a reduction in consumption by 0.9%. In fact, this decrease will be true even though we continue to predict a real increase of about 2 per cent in the average Disposable Income (RD) of Portuguese households. This means a sharp rise in the savings rate of individuals (from 6.2 to 9 per cent of rd) which may not occur, as it is very difficult to predict a reversal of behaviour of this order, despite the plausibility of an increase. This increase in savings will result from an attitude of fear and uncertainty about the future and will result in a postponement and sharp reduction in expenditure on durable consumer goods (17%) and there will continue to be a 1% increase in current consumer goods. The increase in real disposable income is mainly due to projected nominal wage growth and price cuts in 2009, which is expected to translate into an average inflation of 0.2 per cent. It is important to stress that this does not mean the start of a process of general price deflation. Most prices will continue to increase during the year and our forecast has implied the anticipation of a price index growth in the fourth quarter by 0.6%. As I mentioned earlier, the slight drop in prices on average annually is explained by the negative stock developments expected for the middle of the year. A relevant aspect of the ongoing disinflation is the gain in competitiveness compared to the other euro area countries, as since September 2007 Portugal has had a lower than average inflation rate. In 2009 the deficit in our balance of payments is expected to fall from 10.5% in 2008 to 7.9% of GDP and the deficit in the balance of goods and services (exports minus imports) will increase from 8.9% to 6.6%. One factor that contributes to depressing consumption is the rise in unemployment, social and eco-drama that the recession makes virtually inevitable. Unemployment is not expected to increase as much as the size of the recession would seem to indicate that the normal behaviour of companies is to try to keep their workers in the expectation of growth to be temporary. During 2008, when growth was already slowing, the number of unemployed decreased even by 5%. The prospect of a future increase, which began earlier this year, could not be too sharp if the recovery of the world economy begins at the end of this year or early 2010. Everything is, however, very uncertain at this time. Responding to the current crisis must therefore have as its main concern to try to reduce unemployment and its human and social effects. This is particularly important to avoid an increase in poverty in Portugal, since as shown in the study we publish in this Econic Bulletin on poverty, it is very much associated with the unemployment situation. A second element of response is related to the stabilisation of the situation of the banking system on which the flow of credit to the econic activity depends. Our banking system has essentially solved its liquidity problems for this year and this has allowed business credit to continue to grow above what is in the euro area and above nominal economic growth. Credit behaviour in our banking system cannot therefore be attributed to responsibilities in the unfolding of the recessionary climate we are experiencing. Moreover, the company surveys carried out by the INE and the European Commission clearly show how the main limiting factor in investment and expansion of production is the perspective of demand and sales (in about 60%), with factors showing the factors of access to credit or the level of interest rates with little relevance. The monetary policy response has been appropriate, in particular since the October decision to provide banks with liquidity at the central monetary rate without quantitative limitations, with the exception of collateral. This decision together with the successive declines in the central rate of monetary operations contributed to the significant fall in market interest rates, with Euribor at 3 months, for example, falling by more than 5% a few months ago to the current 1.4 %. The international recession is caused by a widespread drop in demand and measures to combat recessionary risks have to focus on having an effect on expanding demand in the shortest possible time. Despite the importance of monetary policy in this context, we know how from certain levels of interest rate it becomes less effective in combating recessive risks It has thus become evident to all countries that it was necessary to resort on a larger scale to fiscal policy. However, there is a high heterogeneity between the various countries as regards the margin of manoeuvre to implement more significant budgetary measures. In particular, in the current context of difficulties in accessing external financing and differentiating the costs of sovereign debt issuance, that margin of manoeuvre depends crucially on the assessment of the sustainability of the phasing finances. In Portugal, this dimension suggests the need for prudence and discretion in the implementation of any additional measures of a discretionary nature. In this perspective, it should be noted that according to estimates by Banco de Portugal, the structural deficit of the plicas administrations stood at 4.6 percent of trend GDP in 2008, with a further increase in 2009, in the context of the expansionary orientation already approved by fiscal policy in line with the latitude included in the Stability and Growth Pact. These high levels suggest the need to draw up a credible strategy in advance to ensure a return to a sustained fiscal consolidation path after the current period of strong contraction in econic activity. It is also important to ensure the efficient use of budgetary expansion measures. To that end, I have made a general outline of the general principles to which the budgetary programmes should be followed last January: 'Concentrate on investment expenses of immediate realization and quick finishing so as not to entail large future expenses. The government's recently announced programme for the construction and maintenance of schools is a good example. Promote transfers to the most deprived segments of the population with a greater propensity for consumption (e.g. temporary improvements in the condition and duration of unemployment benefits) Avoid general tax rate cuts that become difficult to reverse in the future, but may adopt specific temporary reductions or tax returns immediately for groups more likely to be used for consumption (e.g. individual employee contributions to social security) Limit direct support for the maintenance of employment to clearly viable future companies and avoid discretionary support to entire sectors of activity. .Provide for the future elimination of some of the measures now adopted or announce compensation measures in revenue or expenditure to reduce the deficit.' The economic policy measures adopted internationally have sought to respond to the crisis we are experiencing with the degree of urgency that the situation requires. However, they seem to be still insufficient, since, in several countries, the conditions for the reorganisation and restructuring of the financial system have not yet been fully clarified and the necessary commitments for reducing the heterogeneity of external balances in different regions of the world have not yet been fully clarified, which have contributed so much to the global financial instability. It appears to be particularly worrying for a small open economy such as the Portuguese one, the fact that the recession in Europe is more pronounced than in the United States, the country where the current financial and environmental crisis originated. According to IMF 1, European economic stimulus programs will only have an expansive effect of growth by 0.5 percent in 2009 and will even have a negative effect of 0.2 percent in 2010. The Portuguese economy is dependent to emerge from the recession of the European recovery. For an economy of our size and in the current context, recovery has to start with exports and proceed on the basis of investment. We have to have the exact understanding of the conditionings that the external framework puts us, we have to exercise to the limit solidarity with the Portuguese hardest hit by the crisis and we have to maintain the determination and rigor to implement the reforms that best prepare the country to more effectively take advantage of the international recovery when it comes. Lisbon, 14 April 2009 Victor Constantius 1 IMF The case for global fiscal stimulus, March 2009
text_original: Conferncia de Imprensa em 14 de Abril de 2009 DECLARAO INICIAL DO GOVERNADOR DO BANCO DE PORTUGAL NA APRESENTAO DO BOLETIM ECONMICO DA PRIMAVERA (2009) No contexto da maior crise econica mundial desde a Grande Depresso de 1930, Portugal iniciou no segundo semestre do ano passado um perodo recessivo que se antev como o mais profundo e prolongado das timas dcadas. O Boletim Econico que hoje publicamos explica detalhadamente a evoluo da economia portuguesa em 2008, marcada por um crescimento econmico nulo. Dada a alterao, rpida e profunda, da informao disponvel nos timos meses procedemos tambm a uma reviso muito significativa das nossas projecs para o ano corrente. Na verdade, a nossa previso actual para a evoluo da economia este ano  de uma recesso de 3,5 por cento, valor que dever situarse marginalmente abaixo da mdia da rea do euro. Este nmero compara com os 0,8 por cento que publicmos em Janeiro, embora eu tenha tido a ocasio de afirmar publicamente depois disso que a previso do princpio do ano seria revista em baixa. De facto, essa previso tinha sido feita com base em dados disponveis para Outubro do ano passado e a informao posterior sobre o 4 trimestre alterou radicalmente o panorama  para Portugal como para o resto do mundo. O crescimento e o comrcio mundial afundaram no final do ano e no primeiro trimestre deste ano. Para Portugal, isso representou no 4 trimestre uma queda do PIB de 1,8 por cento no trimestre e uma reduo de 8,9% das exportas e de 8,4 % do investimento. Esta alterao feznos rever a previso da procura externa dirigida  economia portuguesa em 2009 de uma reduo de 2,5% para 13%. A recesso de 2009 , assim, explicada essencialmente pela queda das exportas (14,2%) e do investimento (14,4%). Na situao actual da economia mundial todas as previss esto rodeadas de enorme incerteza. Isso  particularmente verdadeiro a propito do investimento, mas desta vez tambm se aplica  actual previso de reduo do consumo em 0,9%. Na verdade, esta diminuio registarse apesar de continuarmos a prever um aumento real de cerca de 2 por cento do Rendimento Disponvel (RD) mdio das famlias portuguesas.
