Isto supe uma forte subida da taxa de poupana dos particulares (de 6,2 para 9 por cento do RD) que poder no se verificar, uma vez que  muito difcil prever uma inverso de comportamento desta ordem, apesar da plausibilidade de se verificar um aumento. Este acrscimo da poupana resultar de um atitude de receio e incerteza face ao futuro e traduzirse num adiamento e forte reduo da despesa em bens de consumo duradouro (17%) continuando a registarse um incremento de 1% nos bens de consumo corrente. O aumento do Rendimento Disponvel real decorre fundamentalmente do crescimento previsto dos salrios nominais e da reduo dos preos em 2009 que dever traduzirse numa inflao mdia de 0,2 por cento.  importante sublinhar que isto no significa o incio de um processo de deflao geral dos preos. A maioria dos preos continuaro a aumentar durante o ano e a nossa previso tem implcita a antecipao de um crescimento do ndice de preos no 4 trimestre em +0,6%. Como referi anteriormente, a descida ligeira dos preos em mdia anual, explicase pela evoluo homloga negativa esperada para meados do ano. Um aspecto relevante da desinflao em curso  o ganho de competitividade relativamente aos restantes pases da rea do euro, uma vez que desde Setembro de 2007 Portugal regista uma taxa de inflao inferior  mdia. Em 2009 o dfice da nossa balana de pagamentos dever reduzirse de 10,5% em 2008para 7,9% do PIB e o dfice da balana de bens e servios (exportas menos importaes) passar de 8,9% para 6,6%. Um factor que contribui para deprimir o consumo  o aumento do desemprego, drama social e econico que a recesso torna praticamente inevitvel. O desemprego no dever aumentar tanto como a dimenso da recesso pareceria indicar uma vez que o comportamento normal das empresas  o de tentar conservar os seus trabalhadores na expectativa da quebra de crescimento ser temporria. Durante o ano de 2008, em que se verificou j uma desacelerao do crescimento, o nmero de desempregados diminuiu mesmo cerca de 5%. A perspectiva do aumento futuro, que se iniciou no princpio deste ano, no ser muito acentuado poder ser validada se a recuperao da economia mundial comear no final deste ano ou princpio de 2010. Tudo se apresenta, porm, muito incerto neste momento. Responder  crise actual deve ter, assim, como principal preocupao tentar minorar o desemprego e os seus efeitos humanos e sociais. Isso  particularmente importante para evitar um aumento da pobreza em Portugal, uma vez que conforme mostra o estudo que publicamos neste Boletim Econico sobre a pobreza esta aparece muito associada  situao de desemprego. Um segundo elemento de resposta est relacionado com a estabilizao conseguida da situao do sistema bancrio de que depende o fluir do crdito para a actividade econica. O nosso sistema bancrio tem globalmente resolvido no essencial os seus problemas de liquidez para este ano e isso tem permitido que o crdito s empresas tenha continuado a crescer acima do que se verifica na rea do euro e acima do crescimento nominal da actividade econmica. Ao comportamento do crdito no nosso sistema bancrio no podem, assim, ser atribudas responsabilidades no desenrolar do clima recessivo que atravessamos. Alis, os inquritos s empresas realizados pelo INE e pela Comisso Europeia revelam claramente como o principal factor limitativo do investimento e da expanso da produo  a perspectiva da procura e das vendas (em cerca de 60%), aparecendo os factores do acesso ao crdito ou do nvel das taxas de juro com escassa relevncia. A resposta da poltica monetria tem sido adequada, em particular desde a deciso de Outubro timo de passar a fornecer liquidez aos bancos  taxa monetria central sem limitaes quantitativas, com excepo das que decorrem da existncia de colateral. Essa deciso juntamente com as sucessivas descidas da taxa central das operas monetrias contriburam para a significativa baixa das taxas de juro de mercado, tendo a Euribor a 3 meses, por exemplo, descido de mais de 5% h poucos meses para os actuais 1,4 %. A recesso internacional  causada por uma quebra generalizada da procura e as medidas para combater os riscos recessivos tm que se concentrar em produzir efeitos na expanso da procura no mais curto espao de tempo possvel. Apesar da importncia da poltica monetria neste contexto, sabemos como a partir de certos nveis de taxa de juro ela se torna menos eficaz para combater riscos recessivos Tornouse, assim, evidente para todos os pases que era necessrio recorrer em maior escala  poltica oramental. Existe, porm, uma elevada heterogeneidade entre os vrios pases no que se refere  margem de manobra para implementar medidas oramentais mais significativas. Em particular, no actual contexto de dificuldades no acesso a financiamento externo e de diferenciao dos custos da emisso de dvida soberana, aquela margem de manobra depende crucialmente da avaliao da sustentabilidade das finanas plicas. Em Portugal, esta dimenso sugere a necessidade de prudncia e critrio na implementao de quaisquer medidas adicionais de carcter discricionrio. Nesta perspectiva, salientese que de acordo com estimativas do Banco de Portugal, o dfice estrutural das administras plicas situouse em 4.6 por cento do PIB tendencial em 2008, perspectivandose um novo aumento em 2009, no contexto da orientao expansionista j aprovada da poltica oramental em consonncia com a latitude inscrita no Pacto de Estabilidade e Crescimento. Estes nveis elevados sugerem a necessidade de traar antecipadamente uma estratgia credvel que assegure o retorno a uma trajectia de consolidao oramental sustentada aps o actual perodo de forte contraco da actividade econica. Importa tambm garantir o uso eficiente das medidas de expanso oramental. Nesse sentido, enumerei em Janeiro passado os princpios gerais a que deveriam obedecer os programas oramentais: Concentraremse em despesas de investimento de imediata realizao e rpido acabamento para no implicarem grandes despesas futuras. O programa recentemente anunciado pelo Governo de construo e manuteno de escolas constitui um bom exemplo. Promoverem transferncias para segmentos mais carenciados da populao com maior propenso ao consumo (v.g. melhorias temporrias das condies e durao dos subsdios de desemprego) Evitarem descidas gerais de taxas de impostos que se tornam difceis de reverter no futuro, podendo, porm, adoptar redus temporrias especificas ou devolus de impostos no imediato para grupos com maior propenso ao consumo (v.g. contribuis individuais de empregados por conta de outrem para a segurana social) Limitarem os apoios directos  manuteno do emprego a empresas claramente com futuro vivel e evitarem apoios discricionrios a sectores inteiros de actividade. .Preverem desde j a eliminao futura de algumas das medidas agora adoptadas ou anunciar medidas de compensao em receita ou despesa para reduzir o dfice. As medidas de poltica econmica adoptadas internacionalmente tm procurado responder  crise que atravessamos com o grau de urgncia que a situao requer. Parecem, porm, ainda insuficientes uma vez que, em vrios pases, no se clarificaram ainda completamente as condis de saneamento e reestruturao do sistema financeiro e ainda no se concretizaram os compromissos indispensveis para a reduo da heterogeneidade dos equilbrios externos em diferentes regis do globo que tanto contriburam para a instabilidade financeira mundial. Aparece como particularmente preocupante para uma pequena economia aberta como  a portuguesa, o facto da recesso na Europa se apresentar como mais acentuada que nos Estados Unidos, pas onde se originou a actual crise financeira e econica. De acordo com o FMI 1, os programas europeus de estmulo  economia apenas tero um efeito expansivo do crescimento em 0,5 por cento em 2009 e tero mesmo um efeito negativo de 0,2 por cento em 2010. A economia portuguesa est dependente para sair da recesso da retoma europeia. Para uma economia da nossa dimenso e no actual contexto, a recuperao tem que comear pelas exportas e prosseguir com base no investimento. Temos que ter a exacta compreenso dos condicionamentos que o enquadramento externo nos coloca, temos que exercer at ao limite a solidariedade para com os portugueses mais atingidos pela crise e temos que manter a determinao e o rigor para executar as reformas que melhor preparem o pas no sentido de mais eficazmente aproveitarmos a retoma internacional  quando vier. Lisboa, 14 de Abril de 2009 Vtor Constncio 1 IMF The case for global fiscal stimulus, March 2009

Title: Initial statement by the Governor in the presentation of the 2004 Annual Report and the Summer Economic Bulletin 2005
text: Bank of Portugal Press Conference on 12 July 2005 INITIAL STATEMENT OF THE GOVERNOR OF BANCO DE PORTUGAL ON THE PRESENTATION OF THE ANNUAL REPORT AND THE ECONOMIC BULLETIN OF THE SUMMER OF 2005 1. As usual at this time of year, today we present the Annual Report of Banco de Portugal, with the economic analysis of 2004 and the Econic Bulletin with the econic projections until 2006. 2004 was characterized as a year of weak economic growth, reduction of inflation, increase in unemployment and imbalances in the Portuguese economy. After the 2003 recession, the economy's recovery was only 1.1%, slowing throughout the year and was lower than growth in the European Union. The evolution of the economy was due to the dynamism of domestic demand, in particular private consumption, and the contribution of the external sector - exports less imports - was negative. The acceleration of consumption to 2.5% meant a drop in the savings of individuals and the continued use of indebtedness in values higher than the growth of the economy. This means that the adjustment to correct macro-economic imbalances was interrupted in 2004. However, it should be stressed that the dynamism of demand was associated with an increase in disposable income in real terms, with the reduction in the inflation rate from 3.3% to 2.5% contributed to this development. In short, the perception that the economic situation would be less unfavorable than expected and that the fiscal consolidation effort would not be particularly intense, will have contributed to stimulate private consumption in 2004. In addition, interest rates have fallen slightly again despite their very low levels and will have contributed to a reduction in liquidity constraints, facilitating the expansion of consumption. The total indebtedness of individuals, whose depreciation for many years, reached 118 % of their annual disposable income, but it should be stressed that the total patrimio held by individuals represents about 500% of that same income and that, on the other hand, interest charges have fallen to only about 5% of that same amount. 1 Bank of Portugal The dynamism of domestic demand was not reflected in an increase in production, but instead fuelled an acceleration of imports, which increased by more than 7% in volume, while exports progressed only 5.2%. The growth profile observed thus determined a worsening of the external imbalance of the economy, revealing a situation of loss of competitiveness that has tended to occur for some years. The rise in the price of petreo has also contributed to the increase in the deficit and the consequent external indebtedness. The banking system continued to play an important role in the necessary intermediation for the financing of the economy and continued to ensure conditions of robust financial stability. In fact, all institutions have noted an improvement in solvency, liquidity and credit quality indicators, with only profitability as a slight decrease compared to the previous year. In general, it can be said that the joint effect of macro-econic policies in 2004 was far from restrictive. In particular, monetary conditions continued to be favourable, with a prevalence of very low interest rates, especially in real terms. As far as fiscal policy is concerned, the total deficit was 5.2 % of GDP last year, if we exclude the extraordinary revenues, which consisted of transfers of funds from penss and thus had no restrictive effect on the economy because they did not affect the current income of the eco-agents. The need to achieve genuine fiscal consolidation has therefore continued to weigh on the Portuguese conjuncture. The persistent and rigorous implementation of the current Stability and Growth Programme recently presented to Brussels is therefore essential for the credibility of Portuguese fiscal policy. Ensuring conditions of macro-economic stability and reducing the ratio of plica debt is indispensable to create the foundations of an economic growth. That is the objective and, as I said last January, "the main problem of the Portuguese economy is the need to increase the growth rate of the potential product in the face of the challenges of globalisation and enlargement of the European Union." We have lost competitiveness over the past decade and we need structural reforms that improve the investment climate and stimulate innovation, increased productivity and the restructuring of the productive sector. 2 Bank of Portugal 2. The Economic Bulletin published today includes projections for the Portuguese economy for two-year cousins, according to the time horizon adopted by the Eurosystem for the euro area. As has been the case recently in several European countries, the current figures represent a bearish revision from our previous projections. Two orders of reasons justify this revision: the recent disclosure of the number for the first quarter, which have virtually zero homologous growth and, secondly, the consideration of the short-term restrictive effects of the fiscal consolidation measures presented in the meantime. We therefore now forecast economic growth of 0.5% for 2005 and 1.2% for 2006, which means that we will continue to diverge from average European growth. However, it should be noted that these forecasts include an increase of 2% and 1.3 % respectively in private consumption in real terms as a result of a positive evolution in Disposable Income in both years referred to. This is despite the expected acceleration of inflation from 2.3% this year to 3% in 2006. The dynamism of the business sector implicit in these forecasts is, moreover, moresignificant, since a mechanical exercise in considering GDP developments, excluding contributions from consumption and investment, would reveal a growth in private activity by around 0.5 percentage points higher than the economy average. It is assumed that Portuguese companies have sufficient productive capacity to take full advantage of the predictable increase in external demand. It is true that there are several risks associated with the hipeses of international evolution underlying the prepared forecasts that may make the scenario less favourable. However, there are sufficient reasons to support a positive development in the horizon of the forecasts we present today. In any case, and beyond the conjuncture, what matters is the persistence on the path of structural reforms with a view to ensuring increased productivity and the return to convergence of the Portuguese economy to European levels of development. Victor Constantius 3
text_original: Banco de Portugal Conferncia de Imprensa em 12 de Julho de 2005 DECLARAO INICIAL DO GOVERNADOR DO BANCO DE PORTUGAL NA APRESENTAO DO RELATRIO ANUAL E DO BOLETIM ECONMICO DO VERO DE 2005 1. Como habitualmente nesta altura do ano, apresentamos hoje o Relatio Anual do Banco de Portugal, com a anlise econmica de 2004 e o Boletim Econico com as projeces econicas at 2006. O ano de 2004 caracterizou-se como um ano de fraco crescimento econmico, de reduo da inflao, de aumento do desemprego e dos desequilbrios da economia portuguesa. Ap a recesso de 2003, a recuperao da economia foi de apenas 1,1%, esteve em desacelerao ao longo do ano e foi inferior ao crescimento verificado na Unio Europeia. A evoluo da economia ficou a dever-se ao dinamismo da procura interna, em particular do consumo privado, tendo sido negativo o contributo do sector externo  exportaes menos importaes. A acelerao do consumo para 2,5% significou uma quebra da poupana dos particulares e a continuao do recurso ao endividamento em valores superiores ao crescimento da economia. Isto significa que se interrompeu em 2004 o ajustamento no sentido da correco dos desequilbrios macroeconmicos. No entanto, deve sublinhar-se que o dinamismo da procura esteve associado a um aumento do rendimento disponvel em termos reais, tendo a reduo da taxa de inflao de 3,3% para 2,5% contribudo para essa evoluo. Em suma, a percepo de que a situao econmica seria menos desfavorvel do que o esperado e de que o esforo de consolidao oramental no seria particularmente intenso, ter contribudo para estimular o consumo privado em 2004. Alm disso, as taxas de juro voltaram a descer ligeiramente apesar dos nveis muito baixos em que se encontravam e tero contribudo para uma reduo das restries de liquidez, facilitando a expanso do consumo. O total do endividamento dos particulares, cujas amortizas se estendem por muitos anos, atingiu 118 % do seu rendimento disponvel anual, mas importa sublinhar que o conjunto do patrimio detido pelos particulares representa cerca de 500% desse mesmo rendimento e que, por outro lado, os encargos com juros desceram para apenas cerca de 5% desse mesmo valor. 1 Banco de Portugal O dinamismo da procura interna no se reflectiu num aumento da produo, mas antes alimentou uma acelerao das importas, que aumentaram mais de 7% em volume, enquanto as exportaes progrediram apenas 5,2%. O perfil do crescimento observado determinou, assim, um agravamento da desequilbrio externo da economia, revelando uma situao de perda de competitividade que tendencialmente se verifica j desde h alguns anos. A alta do preo do petreo contribuiu tambm para o aumento do dfice e do consequente endividamento externo. O sistema bancrio continuou a desempenhar um papel importante na intermediao necessria ao financiamento da economia e continuou a assegurar condis de robusta estabilidade financeira. Na verdade, o conjunto das instituis v oltou a denotar uma melhoria dos indicadores de solvabilidade, de liquidez e de qualidade de crdito, tendo apenas a rendibilidade revelado uma ligeira diminuio face ao ano anterior. Em geral, pode afirmar-se que o efeito conjunto das polticas macroeconicas em 2004 esteve longe de ser restritivo. Em particular, as condis monetrias continuaram a ser favorveis, com prevalncia de taxas de juro muito baixas, sobretudo em termos reais. No que respeita  poltica oramental, o dfice total situou-se o ano passado em 5,2 % do PIB, se excluirmos as receitas extraordinrias, que consistiram em transferncias de fundos de penss e no tiveram, assim, qualquer efeito restritivo sobre a economia porque no afectaram o rendimento corrente dos agentes econicos. A necessidade de conseguir uma autntica consolidao oramental continuou, portanto, a pesar sobre a conjuntura portuguesa. A aplicao persistente e rigorosa do actual Programa de Estabilidade e Crescimento apresentado recentemente a Bruxelas revela-se, pois, essencial para a credibilidade da poltica oramental portuguesa. Assegurar condis de estabilidade macroeconmica e reduzir o rcio da dvida plica  indispensvel para criar os fundamentos de um sido crescimento econico. Esse  o objectivo timo e, como afirmei em Janeiro passado, o problema principal da economia portuguesa reside na necessidade de aumentarmos a taxa de crescimento do produto potencial face aos desafios da globalizao e do alargamento da Unio Europeia. Temos perdido competitividade ao longo da tima dcada e precisamos de reformas estruturais que melhorem o clima de investimento e estimulem a inovao, o aumento da produtividade e a reestruturao do sector produtivo. 2 Banco de Portugal 2. Incluem-se no Boletim Econmico hoje divulgado as projeces para a economia portuguesa referentes aos primos dois anos, de acordo com o horizonte temporal adoptado pelo Eurosistema para a rea do euro.  semelhana do que tem acontecido recentemente em vrios pases europeus, os valores actuais representam uma reviso em baixa relativamente s nossas anteriores projecs. Duas ordens de razs justificam esta reviso: a recente divulgao dos nmeros relativos ao primeiro trimestre, que apresentam crescimento homlogo praticamente nulo e, em segundo lugar, a considerao dos efeitos restritivos no curto prazo das medidas de consolidao oramental entretanto apresentadas. Deste modo, prevemos agora um crescimento econmico de 0,5% para 2005 e de 1,2 % para 2006, o que significa que continuaremos a divergir do crescimento mdio europeu. No entanto, importa sublinhar que estas previss incluem um aumento de, respectivamente, 2% e 1,3 % do consumo privado em termos reais, em resultado de uma evoluo positiva do Rendimento Disponvel em ambos os anos referidos. Isto verifica-se apesar da acelerao prevista da inflao de 2,3 % este ano para 3% em 2006. O dinamismo do sector empresarial implcito nestas previss , alis, mais significativo, uma vez que um exerccio mecnico de considerar a evoluo do PIB, excluindo os contributos do consumo e investimento plicos, revelaria um crescimento da actividade privada cerca de 0,5 pontos percentuais superior  mdia da economia. Assume-se, assim, que as empresas portuguesas dispm de capacidade produtiva suficiente para aproveitar em pleno o aumento previsvel da procura externa.  certo que existem vrios riscos associados s hipeses de evoluo internacional subjacentes s previss elaboradas que podem tornar o cenrio menos favorvel. No entanto, existem suficientes razs para fundamentar uma evoluo positiva no horizonte das previss que hoje apresentamos. Em qualquer caso, e para alm da conjuntura, o que importa  a persistncia no caminho das reformas estruturais com vista a assegurar o aumento de produtividade e o regresso  convergncia da economia portuguesa para os nveis europeus de desenvolvimento. Vtor Constncio 3

Title: Introductory statement by the Governor to the European Parliament
text: Introductory Statement by Mr Vitor Constancio, candidate for Vice-President of the ECB, to the Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee of the European Parliament Brussels, 23d March 2010 I am honoured to appear before your Committee for this hearing which is part of the process of my nomination to the Vice-Presidency of the European Central Bank. On my recent appearance before your Committee for an informal exchange of views I had the occasion to summarize in my introductory statement my positions on some of the more important problems related to monetary policy. I expressed my views on the nature of the ECBs mandate; the meaning of the secondary objective as stated in the Treaty; the main points of our monetary strategy, the role of financial stability and asset prices in monetary policy and, finally, I discussed my assessment of inflationary risks in the present situation. It is not my intention to cover these subjects in my statement today but in view of their importance I want to suggest that my written introductory text to the previous informal session could be annexed to the present proceedings. Today I would like to concentrate my initial comments on matters of regulation and financial stability. As I mentioned last time,  the need to avoid disruption to the proper functioning of the financial system also confronts monetary policy. It is a problem that cannot be ignored by central banks as financial institutions are essential for the economy and for the transmission of monetary policy itself. The recent crisis is an example of the massive turbulence that the financial sector can create endogenously with devastating consequences to the economy. We must be aware of the main lessons to be drawn from the crisis: a) the financial sector is not self-equilibrating or self-correcting; b) an unfettered financial sector can generate crisis on its own; c) extended periods of high growth of credit and debt generate asset price booms that always end in a crisis; d) low inflation in the market of goods and services is not enough to guarantee financial stability. Human societies have learnt and forgotten these lessons several times throughout history. Misbehaviour of big financial institutions, deregulation and perverse incentives created this time the perfect storm that will continue for a protracted period of time to cause slow growth and severe unemployment. So, the question now is the following: can we devise the instruments and institutions necessary to tame the excesses of finance without jeopardizing its much needed role? An optimistic view about this possibility may rely on a positive assessment of all the solutions that have been put forward in several reports and proposals that have flooded our desks, many of which have been adopted in various legislative projects that are now being debated. Let me go through several of those proposals with brief comments as many of them are widely known. I just want to provide you with my own sense of their relative importance and later on I will dwell upon a few that I think have not been fully developed or considered. 1- Creation of a macro-prudential responsibility explicitly attributed to an existing or newly created institution. This is very important as the crisis showed that micro supervision is not sufficient when the risks come from the overall situation of the economy or the financial markets. Doubts remain about the exact competences to be given to the institutions in charge of this new role. 2- Introduction of new standards demanding more and better capital along the lines of the Basel Committee proposals (the increase in capital against trading book risks has already been the subject of legislation in Europe). 3- Reduction of the pro-cyclicality of the regulatory framework, through a system of capital buffers or dynamic provisions (or reserves) changeable with the economic cycle. In the first method, required capital would increase in good years, when loan losses are below long-run averages, creating capital buffers which would be drawn down in recession years as losses increase. Personally, I prefer dynamic provisions but any of the methods is preferable to the existing situation. 4- Correction of the pro-cyclical bias of present accounting standards, which allow profits to be increased with unrealized capital gains in periods of booming asset prices, and exaggerate declining profits in bad times through the effect of unrealized capital losses. Besides the changes in standards to permit a more flexible treatment of asset prices in periods of market stress and illiquidity, there is the need to introduce a concept of an Economic Cycle Reserve, along the lines proposed in the Turner Review, calculated with the same method used in the previous item (3), in order to set aside profit in good times to reduce losses in depressed economic cycles of the future. It is indeed necessary to affect the accounting reports in order to avoid that volatile unrealized gains influence share prices and consequent behaviour of financial institutions. 5- Introduction of a new maximum absolute leverage ratio (risk unweighted total assets over total capital) 6- Introduction of new regulations about liquidity ratios as proposed by the Basel Committee. 7- Prevention of the development of a shadow banking sector by enlarging the perimeter of regulated institutions, like hedge funds, and reinforcing consolidation accounting rules. 8- Tightening securitization regulations to avoid its misuse, its complexity, and opaqueness that prevented it from performing as predicted to diversify and dilute risk. What happened with subprime mortgage bonds, CDOs and Credit Default Swaps was appalling and should not happen again. 9- Reduction of the reliance for official regulatory purposes on Rating Agencies that have contributed to the pro-cyclicality of the financial sector and played a very negative role in the subprime crisis. The mere registration and monitoring of their activity and the elimination of conflicts of interest may not be sufficient to correct their performance. 10- Introduction of new principles regarding risk management and remuneration guidelines to correct prevailing perverse incentives with an excessive short-term perspective. With the exception of points 4 and 9, most of these aspects of a new regulatory environment are being developed by European Union institutions or the Basel Committee, subsequently to general guidelines prepared by the Financial Stability Board and approved by the G20. It would seem then that the work has been progressing in the right direction to create a more resilient and efficient financial system. Nevertheless, I want to make a few comments on aspects that I consider more important or are being insufficiently addressed. The first point refers to the assessment of whether the new rules are sufficient to prevent the excesses of finance and, in particular, whether the macro-prudential function is being implemented in a really efficient way for the same purpose. My answer tends to be positive because instruments like the gross leverage ratio, the capital buffers, the liquidity ratios and the discretionary use of Pillar II may be enough for the task. The remaining necessary instruments are related with the too big to fail problem that I address bellow. Regarding macro-prudential policy, it looks as if in all countries the institution in charge will be limited to making warnings and recommendations. In Europe, the proposed composition of the European Systemic Risk Board (ESRB) with the inclusion of the Commission and the 3 ESA representatives should ensure that this may not become a problem, guaranteeing at the same time the necessary coordination between the micro and macro levels. The whole setup may work well enough for us to hope that the macro-prudential function will not be reduced to warnings, sermons and regrets... I have been following with great interest the debate in your Committee about the ESRB and if you permit me I would like to stress two points that I consider very important for the efficient functioning of the new entity. The first regards the need for the Steering Committee to accurately reflect the composition of the General Board in order to avoid unnecessary tensions. The second refers to the importance of keeping the proposed composition of the Advisory Technical Committee since its main role will be to prepare the work of the General Board and it will be more efficient if composed of people who work in the institutions actually in charge of regulation and supervision. If you consider that a scientific committee is necessary it can always be added to the whole setup without eliminating a necessary component of the preparatory work for the General Board. The second point I wish to comment upon relates to the need to move trade in credit derivatives, especially trade in credit default swaps (CDSs), to organized exchanges. CDSs were at the centre of the crisis and were responsible for the demise of important institutions. They are obscure products, as they are transacted over the counter (OTC) and the premiums so widely quoted are not prices of actual transactions but mere quotations sent to a private firm that started to publish indexes in 2001. The exact way these indexes are built, the players sending the quotations are not publicly known and, finally, as they are quotations in a non-organized market, the institutions providing these quotations are not compelled to make transactions at these levels. Myron Scholes, the Chicago Professor and Nobel Prize of Economics, the co-author of the Black-Scholes formula for option pricing and a kind of godfather to derivatives, said last year: the solution is really to blow up or burn the OTC market, the CDSs and swaps and structured products and let us start over. Serious thought should also be given to the possibility of forbidding naked short selling of these instruments, allowing only market-maker institutions to do such transactions as hedging activity when they already have transactions with agents who possess a real insurable interest. The third aspect I want to address is the too big to fail problem. The existence of large and complex financial institutions (LCFI) whose bankruptcy is impossible to allow, creates a huge problem of moral hazard that may lead to unduly risky behaviour. Its an intricate question and there is still no international consensus on how to deal with it. The problem is even becoming potentially worse by the increase in size of surviving institutions a situation that is common after a crisis. Without dwelling upon the arguments, let me state that I do not believe that the problem can be solved by a policy of systematic break-up of big institutions or by adopting a solution of protecting only narrow banks and distinguishing between utility and investment banks. This means that I only believe in solutions that may contribute to transform the concerned entities in institutions too good to fail or that can organize, with special powers, an orderly resolution that avoids the more negative consequences of insolvency. The following proposals, not mutually exclusive, have been discussed or are already included in legislative projects: a) More intense and special supervision, including from a macro-prudential perspective. b) Higher capital requirements. This idea includes several possibilities: from a simple capital surcharge according to size and/or related to the banks contribution to systemic risk. In some schemes, these additional capital requirements can be in part satisfied through contingent capital securities (bonds automatically converted into equity when certain conditions are met). c) Insurance premiums. On top of higher capital, big institutions should pay insurance costs related to their size or contribution to systemic risk, with the proceeds of the insurance in case of insolvency reverting to the authorities in charge of the resolution of the crisis. A variant of these idea, already adopted in the US House of Representatives, consists in demanding from the banks contributions to a Resolution Fund to support the costs of insolvency problems in systemically important financial institutions (SIFIs). d) Living wills. This consists in compelling the SIFIs to have permanently prepared plans for a orderly resolution. e) Creation of a special resolution regime, giving an institution like the American FDIC (Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation) wide powers to take over a troubled institution and restructure and sell or liquidate it. In some proposals, the special powers should include the possibility of compulsory transformation of bonds into equity to recapitalize the institution. The institution responsible for this role will need to have access to a Restructuring or Resolution Fund. Elements of these five types of measures can be found in existing legislative proposals, although there is no international consensus to achieve a more harmonized regime that could be relevant for cross-border institutions. All these measures seem to be useful and complement the other instruments already mentioned to rein in excessive growth and unduly risky behaviour of major institutions. The fourth and final problem that is not yet completely solved refers to crisis resolution of cross-border institutions in the European Union. The creation of colleges of supervisors and the possible role of the ESAs in acting as mediators will make a contribution to find coordinated solutions to the problem. The main obstacle is related to the problem of burden-sharing of costs in dealing with crisis resolution. As I wrote in my answers to your questionnaire:  In my view, any potential move towards an even more integrated supervisory architecture in Europe will therefore have to be preceded by the establishment of a European safety net (including an ex-ante funded Resolution Fund)  The Commission has been doing good work in this area and the announcement made last Friday by Commissioner Barnier goes in that direction and is very important. Nevertheless, let me point out that a full solution and the operation of such a fund requires higher harmonization of national resolution regimes including bankruptcy laws, and this will prove to be difficult. Nevertheless, I believe that full European financial integration requires a common European resolution regime. A final thought about the overall impact of all the envisaged regulatory reforms. Some commentators make the criticism that all the measures at stake could amount to a sort of overkill that may possibly choke financial activity. In view of the extreme seriousness of the financial crisis engineered by the financial sector I think that there is no exaggeration in the re-regulating efforts being prepared even if they were fully implemented  something about which one may have doubts. There is nevertheless a risk to be avoided concerning the timing of the implementation. An immediate or quick implementation of all the measures, in particular those related with higher capital requirements, could generate credit supply restrictions detrimental to economic recovery. This implies that all authorities concerned should be as clear-headed and resolute regarding content of the reforms as they must be wise and prudent in timing their implementation.

Title: Inauguration speech of the Governor
text: Minister of State and Finance, Ladies and Gentlemen On behalf of me and my council colleagues, now sworn in, I thank the government for its confidence in n to ensure the management of Banco de Portugal. It is largely named a continuity team. It is therefore appropriate to recall some aspects that marked the tasks of the previous mandate. Started shortly after the creation of the euro, it coincided with the preparation of the major operation of introducing euro banknotes and coins which came to fruition with great success. However, given the powers of Banco de Portugal in our participation in the European Monetary Union, the key concerns of the mandate focused on the imbalances that were beginning to emerge in the economy and the banking system. We were still in 2000 in the phase of economic growth based on the explosion of domestic spending. However, we were beginning to see the signs of danger of a budget with a deficit that is not adjusted to a favourable situation and the signs of a growing loss of competitiveness. Clearly, eco-actors, including the State, had not internalised the fundamental rules of participation in a monetary union. As for the banking system, despite its high standards of efficiency, it fueled an exaggerated expansion of credit with a reduction in the solvency ratio and a deteriorating liquidity situation with excessive dependence on resources with maturity of less than one year raised in the international interbank market. It is understood that, in addition to the ever-demanding aspects of the management of our participation in the European System of Central Banks in order to ensure a dignified position for the country, the mandate has been marked by efforts to improve the behaviour of environmental agents in the context of monetary union and by the measures to regulate and supervise the banking system. Starting with the first aspect, I would remind you that already in my inaugural address in 2000, I stated that "... if private spending remains euficaus and growth is strong, the state has to maintain budgetary rigour. As no raw interest rate declines are expected, on the contrary, this implies that consumption expenditure scans cannot continue to grow at the same rate as in the last few years." And as for the real economy and the problems of competitiveness I said then that low financing and access costs of capital that facilitate modernising productive investment constitute "... the great opportunity created by the euro. This has to be used to operate an indispensable structural repositioning of the Portuguese economy. Companies now compete from a strong currency and cannot be deceived by short-term facilities. Trade unions also have the responsibility to grade their claims to the new competitive context in which we are, if they really want to defend employment. There will be no devaluations or subsidies to support companies that lose competitive position because they do not modernize, because they do not increase the technolic content of their processes or the quality of their productions. The path we have embarked on is what can best guarantee our future prosperity, but it is demanding and has no retreat." The situation of the Finances plicas worsened throughout 2000 and on the occasion of the Bank's Econic Bulletin of December of that year, I criticised fiscal policy, proposed the reform of the wage negotiation mechanism and set out four fundamental principles of macro-ecological management, indispensable to a successful participation in monetary union. In the situation at the time, anesthetized by the strong ecological growth that was verified, these themes were not present in the plico debate and caused some surprise and several criticisms. As I pointed out then, "These orientations may seem to some to be the expression of orthodox thinking, but they correspond, in addition, to the recognition of the fundamental reality in which the Portuguese economy is now moving." Nowadays they are principles trivialized in the plica discussion, which does not mean that they are properly internalized in behaviors. That is why Banco de Portugal continued in its publishing to insist on the pedagogy of the principles that allow us to grasp the new paradigm in which we live, that of an ecological regime in which European monetary policy ensures inflation control and national income policy must seek to protect employment in the context of an international system with strong competition. This conceptual reversal over past decades is further accentuated by the inevitable effects that globalisation has on economies. In macro-ecological terms, it can therefore be said that successful participation in monetary union requires the internalisation by econic agents of the need for the constant anti-cyclical use of budgetary policy and the control of unit labour costs in terms compatible with productivity developments and comparison as our Union partners. We have not fully recovered these principles, in terms and with consequences that I have examined many times. Given the importance of the budgetary issue, I have twice agreed to chair the Technical Commission to examine the problem of the budget deficit. The first time, because the European Commission had refused to validate the report submitted by Portugal and it was important that an independent Portuguese institution could clarify the outstanding problems. The second time, because the budgetary issue, which has faded the effect of the extraordinary measures, was particularly serious. In fact, we were last year in the presence of an unrealistic budget with significant under-budgeting so that without urgent and meaningful action, we were heading for a deficit of enormous proportions. This was a factor of extreme concern for those who were responsible for the Portuguese economy and the European Commission was preparing to put Portugal in excessive deficits on the basis of its forecasts only, as it had done earlier in the German case. I believe that the intervention of a new independent Commission to review the budget deficit forecast was important to convince all those involved and the opinion is that it was essential to adopt measures of genuine fiscal consolidation. In fact, although these measures were taken as a result of the Amending Budget, the deficit still came at 6%, the highest in all years. Although not unexpected, there were curious reactions to these two interventions. Despite the clear technical nature of the materials there were even those who could praise one and criticize the other, which proves the usefulness that has for a country the existence of some independent institutions that can be put at certain times outside the political sphere. I believe that in both occasions Banco de Portugal served the national interest in the context of what were clear service misss plico. What is really relevant, however, is that the important and courageous measures that the Government has been making indicate that we may be on the path to real fiscal consolidation. However, I have enough experience of the problem to say that success will still require you, Mr Minister, a great deal of determination. In particular, I advise that you exercise your rigorous magisterium in containing expenditure at the end of this year decisive for the implementation of the entire Stability Programme. You have my support for the measures you believe you are taking, as all the finance ministers who have taken effective deficit containment measures have had publicly. Despite the inevitable restrictive effect that fiscal consolidation has in the short term, the period of weak growth that the economy has been experiencing is not explained only by this fact. We have also been suffering the effect of the inevitable slowdown following the initial overheating resulting from the explosion of domestic spending related to the permanent shock of the new low interest rate regime. During this period, the imbalance between global demand and supply contributes to fueling a real appreciation associated with a differential in cost and price inflation compared to the other member countries. This inevitable real assessment, if it goes beyond a balance assessment, together with the limits on indebtedness imposed by the financial system, are the essential mechanisms for braking the initial boom and slowing domestic demand. The drop in investment was also accentuated by the reversal of the cycle of investment in housing, with particular emphasis on the 20% drop in 2003. The slowdown in domestic demand since 2001 has been the largest in the entire euro area, which cannot fail to be related to the drop in expectations that accompanied the outbreak of the fiscal crisis in 2002. In addition to these internal factors, some adverse external shocks have also contributed to the weaker recent performance of the economy. The effects of the enlargement and globalisation of trade on our export quotas on the central European markets or the consequences of the evolution of the petreo price are well known. Without several of the temporary factors affecting the economic environment, the economy would be more close to the European average this year. There are no economic policies that could immediately increase eco-growth. Some economists argue that it would be necessary to promote a kind of real devaluation resulting from putting our labour costs per unit produced to grow less than those of our European partners. I do not believe that the factor of relative costs is the fundamental explanation of our problem, so there would be no important solution at that point. The problem is not to compete with the same products and with the same countries with which we were in a balanced situation before. There is a change in the eco-regime resulting from enlargement and globalisation, so the problem is that of a structural shock resulting from the new international arbitration of labour costs. The answer is a real adjustment that changes the standard of specialization, which has been happening, but which is necessarily a slow process. The solution is consequently an overall increase in productivity in the framework of a process of product and process innovation that focuses on transactionable goods and services and alters our production structure. The concentration of efforts in the tradeable goods and services sectors should be a concern of all policies affecting investment decisions to avoid wasting resources and because it is in these sectors that the demand for high levels of productivity is greater. Structural reforms that improve the environment, eliminate bureaucracy and encourage innovation must be pursued. The essential, however, will depend on the response of the business initiative, Portuguese and foreign. Recent signs of the economy point to a slight recovery in economic activity, reflecting a positive evolution in the confidence levels of eco-scans. A faster recovery in private investment than that implied in existing forecasts could lead to higher-than-expected growth. We must wait, however, for the evolution of the second quarter to definitively assess whether growth could be noticeably above one percent. I believe that from 2008 on, we will be able to count on the dissipation of some of the latest negative effects, allowing the economy to grow at more normal rates in the European context. There will be no shortage of favourable financial conditions to support the eco-activity. Despite the recent rise in interest rates, the cost of financing, particularly in the medium term, remains historically low, which is an indisputable advantage of our participation in the euro. In this context, it is very important to ensure financial stability, i.e. the robust and effective functioning of financial institutions and markets in order to promote the proper channeling of savings to the best investment opportunities. Ensuring financial stability is one of Banco de Portugal's main responsibilities in the sector in which it exercises supervisory functions. Like other central banks, even those that do not have supervisory powers, we have started to publish a Financial Stability Report that analyses the main risks to which the banking system is subjected and is a reflection of the internal work of macro-prudential analysis. I think it is important to stress the particular importance that the banking system has in the Portuguese economy. As I said, the adjustment to a new level of intertemporal balance corresponding to a lower interest rate regime implied the rational expansion of the indebtedness of eco-actors, households and businesses. It was the expansion of private spending and indebtedness that fundamentally led banks to mediate external financing that allowed credit to increase credit well above that recorded by the pits. The International Investment Position (IIP) of the Portuguese economy, which includes debt instruments, shares and capital shares, went from a negative balance of 10% of GDP in 1996 to 65.9% last year and the banking system intermediated and assumed 60% of this total in the international monetary and financial markets. To maintain this role and ensure the financing of the economy, the banking system has to maintain a situation in terms of liquidity, solvency and profitability. That is why we acted at the beginning of the mandate to reduce the excessive dependence on short-term interbank financing by setting a new regulation on liquidity ratios. The coverage of short-term interbank liabilities by high liquidity assets increased from only 86.8% in 2000 to 132.1% in 2005, with regard to all domestic banks that are supervised by Banco de Portugal. For this same set, the solvency ratio reached only 8.9% in 2000 and has increased since then to 11.4% last year. We have also changed the provisioning rules, penalising high value/loan ratios in real estate operations and extending the concept of non-compliance credit subject to proviss. We have also prepared the introduction of new statistical or anti-cypress features that the slowdown in the economy has prevented us from applying, but which we have continued to calculate for analytical purposes. Provisions or rebates have also been introduced to the financial funds to cover the potential losses of stable financial holdings, previously recorded at historical cost. The Bank's interventions, the evolution of the economy and the improvement of risk management by banks have contributed to strengthen its robustness and also to the credit slowdown. From an average growth rate of 23% between 1996 and 2000, credit increased to an average growth of 8.3% between 2001 and 2005. The banking system, despite the slowdown in the economy, is currently in a position to be in a position of liquidity and solvency and maintain adequate levels of profitability. Other major regulatory changes have been introduced or had to be prepared in this period. The application of the International Accounting Standards imposed by the European Commission, the preparation of the transcription texts of several European Directives such as those relating to financial conglomerates, the reorganisation and liquidation of financial institutions, the prevention of money laundering or the distance marketing of financial services. In all these tasks, the role of the National Council of Financial Supervisors was important, a gon created in 2001 and which integrates Banco de Portugal, the Securities Market Commission and the Insurance Institute of Portugal, with the objective of coordinating its activity, keeping each institution fully its competences. The Council's work has been very il to harmonise position, coordinate interventions in European bodies and prepare legislation. It was also very important to coordinate the preparatory work of the Financial Sector Assesssment Program (FSAP) recently conducted by the International Monetary Fund to analyze the degree of compliance by Portugal with the international cigos and standards of supervision of the financial sector and to assess the situation, vulnerabilities and stability of monetary, financial and insurance institutions. The exercise involved the three Supervisors and the IMF's final report will be published shortly. The IMF considered that the current institutional supervisory structure in Portugal is appropriate, including the role of the Council, in addition to assessing positively the situation of the national financial system. We have a modern and efficient system that is the result of the prevailing degree of competition in the sector, the management capacity and the attraction of much of the best human capital in the country. It is important that the system's soundness is maintained in order to ensure the stability of the economy as a whole. That is why the main concern of the mandate that is now beginning will be to continue to improve the banking supervision system. A major modernisation effort will have to be carried out in the context of the implementation from the first year of the New Capital Agreement, known as Basel II, which will translate into new Directives to be published soon and to transcribe by December. The new regulation of the capital ratio is more sensitive to the rigorous assessment of the risks incurred by the Institutions, allows the use of sophisticated models to carry out this assessment, which the most important banks will adopt, and gives an increased role to the intervention of the Supervisor. The Supervision will have to know how to validate the entire system of risk control existing in the Institutions, have an overview of their strategy and vulnerabilities, evaluate the governance and internal control system, acquire a global and prospective view on their future evolution. In addition, the effort to adapt to the new regulatory framework that has been prepared implies an increased level of demand for credit institutions but also on Banco de Portugal. We will also have to monitor the evolution of the Payment System, as the start-up of the new European real-time wholesale payment system (Target 2) and the implementation of the Single PaymentS Area project in Europe (SEPA) will also entail major transformations in the use of cart and bank transfer systems, benefits for consumers in convenience and price matching. Anticipating these future tasks I want to ensure that Banco de Portugal has the technical staff, resources and sense of service plico to continue to be an institution of excellence capable of representing the country well in the institutions of the European Monetary Union and to perform effectively and independently the important functions for the Portuguese economy that are assigned to it. Lisbon 20 June 2006 Vitor Constancio
text_original: Senhor Ministro de Estado e das Finanas Senhores Secretrios de Estado Minhas Senhoras e meus Senhores Em meu nome e dos meus colegas de Conselho, agora empossados, agradeo a confiana que o Governo em n depositou para assegurar a gesto do Banco de Portugal. Em grande parte fica nomeada uma equipa de continuidade. , pois, apropriado recordar alguns aspectos que marcaram as tarefas do mandato anterior. Iniciado pouco tempo depois da criao do euro, coincidiu com a preparao da grande operao de introduo de notas e moedas em euros que veio a concretizar-se com elevado sucesso. No entanto, dadas as competncias do Banco de Portugal no mbito da nossa participao na Unio Monetria Europeia, as preocupas essenciais do mandato centraram-se nos desequilbrios que comeavam a emergir na economia e no prrio sistema bancrio. Estvamos ainda em 2000 na fase de crescimento econico eufico assente na exploso da despesa interna. Comeava-se, porm, a perceber os sinais de perigo de um oramento com dfice desajustado a uma fase de conjuntura favorvel e os indcios de uma crescente perda de competitividade. Claramente, os agentes econicos, incluindo o Estado, no tinham interiorizado as regras fundamentais da participao numa unio monetria. Quanto ao sistema bancrio, apesar dos seus elevados padrs de eficincia, alimentava uma exagerada expanso do crdito com reduo do rcio de solvabilidade e uma situao de liquidez em deteriorao com excessiva dependncia de recursos com maturidade inferior a um ano captados no mercado interbancrio internacional. Compreende-se, assim, que para alm dos aspectos, sempre exigentes, da gesto da nossa participao no Sistema Europeu de Bancos Centrais por forma a garantir uma posio dignificante para o pas, o mandato tenha ficado marcado pelos esforos para melhorar o comportamento dos agentes econicos no contexto da unio monetria e pelas medidas de regulao e superviso do sistema bancrio. Comeando pelo primeiro aspecto, recordo que j no meu discurso de posse em 2000, afirmei que  se as despesas privadas continuarem euficas e o crescimento for forte, o Estado tem que manter rigor oramental. Como no se prevem primas descidas dos juros, pelo contrrio, isto implica que as despesas de consumo plico no podero continuar a crescer ao mesmo ritmo dos timos anos. E quanto  economia real e aos problemas de competitividade referi ento que baixos custos de financiamento e de acesso ao capital que facilitam o investimento produtivo modernizador, constituem a grande oportunidade criada pelo euro. Isto tem que ser aproveitado para operar um indispensvel reposicionamento estrutural da economia portuguesa. As empresas concorrem agora a partir de uma moeda forte e no podem deixar-se iludir por facilidades de curto prazo. Aos sindicatos cabe tambm a responsabilidade de graduarem as suas reivindicas ao novo contexto competitivo em que estamos, se efectivamente querem defender o emprego. No haver desvalorizas nem subsdios para aguentar empresas que perderem posio competitiva por no se modernizarem, por no aumentarem o conteo tecnolico dos seus processos ou a qualidade das suas produs. O caminho em que embarcmos  o que melhor pode garantir a nossa prosperidade futura, mas  exigente e no tem recuo. A situao das Finanas plicas agravou-se ao longo de 2000 e por ocasio do Boletim Econico do Banco de Dezembro desse ano, critiquei a poltica oramental, propus a reforma do mecanismo das negocias salariais e enunciei quatro princpios fundamentais da gesto macroeconica, indispensveis a uma bem sucedida participao na unio monetria. Na situao da altura, anestesiada pelo forte crescimento econico que se verificava, estes temas no estavam presentes no debate plico e causaram alguma surpresa e vrias criticas. Como sublinhei ento, Estas orientas podero parecer a alguns a expresso de um pensamento ortodoxo, mas correspondem, singelamente ao reconhecimento da realidade fundamental em que se move agora a economia portuguesa. Hoje em dia so princpios banalizados na discusso plica, o que no significa que estejam devidamente interiorizados nos comportamentos. Por isso mesmo o Banco de Portugal continuou nas suas publicas a insistir na pedagogia dos princpios que permitem apreender o novo paradigma em que vivemos, o de um regime econico em que a poltica monetria europeia assegura o controle da inflao e a poltica de rendimentos nacional deve procurar proteger o emprego no contexto de um sistema internacional com forte concorrncia. Esta inverso conceptual relativamente a dcadas passadas  ainda acentuada pelos efeitos que a inevitvel globalizao exerce sobre as economias. Em termos macroeconicos pode, pois, dizer-se que a participao bem sucedida na unio monetria requer a interiorizao pelos agentes econicos da necessidade do permanente uso anti-cclico da poltica oramental e do controle dos custos unitrios do trabalho em termos compatveis com a evoluo da produtividade e a comparao como os nossos parceiros da Unio. No respeitmos inteiramente estes princpios, em termos e com consequncias que analisei muitas vezes. Dada a importncia da questo oramental, aceitei por duas vezes presidir a Comisss tcnicas para analisar o problema do dfice oramental. Da primeira vez, porque a Comisso Europeia tinha recusado validar o reporte apresentado por Portugal e era importante que uma instituio portuguesa independente pudesse esclarecer os problemas pendentes. Da segunda vez, porque a questo oramental, desvanecido o efeito das medidas extraordinrias, se apresentava com particular gravidade. Na verdade, estvamos o ano passado na presena de um oramento irrealista com significativa sub-oramentao pelo que, sem a tomada de medidas urgentes e significativas, nos encaminhvamos para um dfice de enormes propors. Isto constitua factor de extrema preocupao para quem analisasse responsavelmente a economia portuguesa e a Comisso Europeia preparava-se para colocar Portugal em situao de dfices excessivo com base apenas nas suas prrias previss, como tinha feito anteriormente no caso alemo. Creio que a interveno de uma nova Comisso independente para rever a previso do dfice oramental foi importante para convencer todos os intervenientes e a opinio plica que era fundamental aprovar medidas de autntica consolidao oramental. Na verdade, apesar dessas medidas terem sido tomadas na sequncia do Oramento Rectificativo o dfice mesmo assim veio a situarse em 6%, o mais elevado dos timos anos. Embora no inesperadas, verificaram-se curiosas reacs a estas duas intervens. Apesar da clara natureza tcnica das matrias houve mesmo quem conseguisse elogiar uma e criticar a outra, o que svem provar a utilidade que tem para um pas a existncia de algumas instituis independentes que se possam colocar em certos momentos fora da esfera poltica. Creio que em ambas as ocasis o Banco de Portugal serviu o interesse nacional no contexto do que eram claras misss de servio plico. O que  verdadeiramente relevante, porm,  que as importantes e corajosas medidas que o Governo tem vindo a tornar indiciam que podemos estar no caminho de uma verdadeira consolidao oramental. Tenho, porm, suficiente experincia do problema para afirmar que o sucesso vai ainda exigir de V. Exa., Senhor Ministro, muita determinao. Aconselho em particular que exera o seu rigoroso magistrio na conteno das despesas na parte final deste ano decisivo para a execuo de todo o Programa de Estabilidade. Tem V.Exa o meu apoio para as medidas que entender tomar, tal como o tiveram publicamente todos os Ministros das Finanas que adoptaram efectivas medidas de conteno do dfice plico. Apesar do inevitvel efeito restritivo que a consolidao oramental exerce no curto prazo, o perodo de fraco crescimento que a economia tem atravessado no  explicvel apenas por esse facto. Temos estado tambm a sofrer o efeito da inevitvel desacelerao que sucede ao sobreaquecimento inicial resultante da exploso da despesa interna relacionada com o choque permanente do novo regime de baixas taxas de juro. Nesse perodo, o desequilbrio que se gera entre procura e oferta globais contribui para alimentar uma apreciao real associada a um diferencial de inflao de custos e preos relativamente aos restantes pases membros. Essa apreciao real inevitvel, se for alm de uma apreciao de equilbrio, juntamente com os limites ao endividamento impostos pelo sistema financeiro, constituem os mecanismos essenciais de travagem do boom inicial e de desacelerao da procura interna. A quebra do investimento foi tambm acentuada pela inverso do ciclo do investimento em habitao, com particular relevo para a queda de 20% em 2003. A desacelerao da procura interna desde 2001 foi a maior de toda a rea do euro o que no pode deixar de estar relacionado com a quebra de expectativas que acompanhou o eclodir da crise oramental em 2002. Para alm destes factores internos, alguns choques externos adversos contriburam igualmente para o mais fraco desempenho recente da economia. So bem conhecidos os efeitos do alargamento e da globalizao das trocas nas nossas quotas de exportao nos mercados do centro da Europa ou as consequncias da evoluo do preo do petreo. Sem vrios dos factores temporrios que afectam a conjuntura o crescimento da economia estaria este ano mais primo da mdia europeia. No existem polticas plicas conjunturais que pudessem aumentar no imediato o crescimento econico. Alguns economistas defendem que seria necessrio promover uma espcie de desvalorizao real resultante de colocar os nossos custos de trabalho por unidade produzida a crescer menos que os dos nossos parceiros europeus. No creio que o factor dos custos relativos seja a explicao fundamental do nosso problema pelo que no residiria nesse ponto uma soluo importante. O problema no  o de concorrer com os mesmos produtos e com os mesmos pases com que anteriormente estivssemos em situao de equilbrio. H uma mudana de regime econico resultante do alargamento e da globalizao, pelo que o problema  o de um choque estrutural decorrente da nova arbitragem internacional de custos de trabalho. A ica resposta  de um ajustamento real que altere o padro de especializao, o que tem vindo alis a acontecer, mas que  necessariamente um processo lento. A soluo reside consequentemente num aumento geral de produtividade no quadro de um processo de inovao de produto e de processos que se concentre nos bens e servios transaccionveis e altere a nossa estrutura produtiva. A concentrao de esforos nos sectores dos bens e servios transaccionveis deve ser uma preocupao de todas as polticas que afectam as deciss de investimento para evitar o desperdcio de recursos e porque  nesses sectores que  maior a exigncia de elevados nveis de produtividade. H que prosseguir com as reformas estruturais que melhoram o enquadramento da actividade econica, eliminam burocracia e incentivam a inovao. O essencial, porm, depender da resposta da iniciativa empresarial, portuguesa e estrangeira. Os sinais recentes da economia apontam para uma ligeira recuperao da actividade econmica, o que reflecte uma evoluo positiva dos nveis de confiana dos agentes econicos. Uma recuperao mais rpida do investimento privado do que aquela que est implcita nas previss existentes poder conduzir a um crescimento superior ao esperado. Devemos aguardar, no entanto, pela evoluo do segundo trimestre para avaliar em definitivo se o crescimento poder situar-se visivelmente acima de um por cento. Creio que sa partir de 2008 poderemos contar a dissipao de alguns efeitos negativos mais recentes, permitindo que a economia possa crescer a taxas mais normais no contexto europeu. No faltaro condis financeiras favorveis para apoiar a actividade econica. Apesar da recente subida das taxas de juro, o custo do financiamento, em particular a mdio prazo, continua historicamente baixo, o que  uma indesmentvel vantagem da nossa participao no euro. Neste contexto,  muito importante assegurar a estabilidade financeira, ou seja, o funcionamento robusto e eficaz das instituies e mercados financeiros por forma a promover a adequada canalizao da poupana para as melhores oportunidades de investimento. Garantir a estabilidade financeira constitui uma das responsabilidades principais do Banco de Portugal no sector em que exerce funs de superviso.  semelhana de outros bancos centrais, mesmo os que no possuem competncias de superviso, comemos a publicar um Relatio de Estabilidade Financeira que analisa os principais riscos a que est submetido o sistema bancrio e  o reflexo dos trabalhos internos de anlise macro-prudencial. Creio ser importante sublinhar a particular importncia que o sistema bancrio tem na economia portuguesa. Como referi, o ajustamento a um novo nvel de equilbrio intertemporal correspondente a um regime de mais baixas taxas de juro implicou a expanso racional do endividamento dos agentes econicos, famlias e empresas. Foi a expanso da despesa e do endividamento privados que fundamentalmente determinaram um maior dfice externo e levaram os bancos a intermediar o financiamento externo que permitiu um aumento do crdito muito acima do registado pelos depitos. A Posio de Investimento Internacional (PII) da economia portuguesa, que inclui instrumentos de dvida, acs e partes de capital, passou de um saldo negativo de 10% do PIB em 1996 para 65,9% o ano passado e o sistema bancrio intermediou e assumiu 60 % deste total nos mercados monetrio e financeiro internacionais. Para manter este papel e assegurar o financiamento da economia o sistema bancrio tem que conservar uma situao sida em termos de liquidez, solvabilidade e rentabilidade. Por isso actumos no incio do mandato para reduzir a excessiva dependncia do financiamento interbancrio de curto prazo, definindo nova regulao sobre rcios de liquidez. A cobertura dos passivos interbancrios de curto prazo por activos de elevada liquidez passou de apenas 86,8% em 2000 para 132,1% em 2005, no que se refere ao conjunto dos bancos domsticos que so supervisionados pelo Banco de Portugal. Para este mesmo conjunto, o rcio de solvabilidade atingia apenas 8,9% em 2000 e aumentou desde ento at atingir 11,4% no ano transacto. Altermos tambm as regras de provisionamento, penalizando elevados rcios de valor/emprstimo nas operaes imobilirias e alargando o conceito de crdito em incumprimento sujeito a proviss. Preparmos tambm a introduo de novas proviss estatsticas ou anticiclicas que a desacelerao da economia nos impediu de aplicar, mas que continumos a calcular para fins analticos. Foram tambm introduzidas proviss ou abatimentos aos fundos prrios para cobrir as menos valias potenciais de participas financeiras estveis, antes registadas a custo histico. As intervens do Banco, a evoluo da economia e o aperfeioamento da gesto dos riscos por parte dos bancos, contriburam para reforar a sua robustez e tambm para a desacelerao do crdito. De uma taxa de crescimento mdia de 23% entre 1996 e 2000, o crdito passou para um crescimento mdio de 8,3% entre 2001 e 2005. O sistema bancrio, apesar da desacelerao da economia, encontra-se hoje em dia numa posio sida do ponto de vista da liquidez e da solvabilidade e pe manter nveis adequados de rentabilidade. Outras alteras regulamentares importantes foram introduzidas ou tiveram que ser preparadas neste perodo. A aplicao da Normas Internacionais de Contabilidade impostas pela Comisso Europeia, a preparao dos textos de transcrio de diversas Directivas europeias como as referentes aos conglomerados financeiros, ao saneamento e liquidao de instituis financeiras,  preveno do branqueamento de capitais ou  comercializao  distncia de servios financeiros. Em todas estas tarefas foi importante o papel do Conselho Nacional de Supervisores Financeiros, um go criado em 2001 e que integra o Banco de Portugal, a Comisso do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios e o Instituto de Seguros de Portugal, com o objectivo de coordenao da respectiva actividade, mantendo cada instituio inteiramente as suas competncias. O trabalho do Conselho tem sido muito il para harmonizar posis, coordenar intervens nas instncias europeias e preparar legislao. Foi tambm muito importante para coordenar os trabalhos preparatios do Financial Sector Assesssment Program (FSAP) recentemente conduzido pelo Fundo Monetrio Internacional para analisar o grau de cumprimento por Portugal dos cigos e padrs internacionais de superviso do sector financeiro e avaliar a situao, as vulnerabilidades e a estabilidade das Instituis Monetrias, Financeiras e Seguradores. O exerccio envolveu os trs Supervisores e o Relatio final do FMI ser publicado em breve. O FMI considerou que a actual estrutura institucional de Superviso em Portugal  adequada, incluindo o papel do Conselho, para alm de apreciar positivamente a situao do sistema financeiro nacional. Temos um sistema moderno e eficiente que  o resultado do grau de concorrncia prevalecente no sector, da capacidade de gesto e da atraco de boa parte do melhor capital humano existente no pas.  importante que a situao de solidez do sistema se mantenha a fim de garantir a estabilidade da economia em geral. Por isso mesmo a principal preocupao do mandato que agora se inicia ser o de continuar a aperfeioar o sistema de Superviso bancria. Um grande esforo de modernizao ter que ser realizado no contexto da aplicao a partir do primo ano do Novo Acordo de Capital, conhecido como Basileia II, que se traduzir em novas Directivas a publicar brevemente e a transcrever at Dezembro. A nova regulao do rcio de capital  mais sensvel  avaliao rigorosa dos riscos incorridos pelas Instituis, permite o uso de modelos sofisticados para realizar essa avaliao, que os Bancos mais importantes vo adoptar, e d um papel acrescido  interveno do Supervisor. A Superviso ter que saber validar todo o sistema de controle do risco existente nas Instituis, ter uma perspectiva geral sobre a sua estratgia e vulnerabilidades, avaliar o sistema de governance e de controle interno, adquirir uma viso global e prospectiva sobre a respectiva evoluo futura. Em suma, o esforo de adaptao ao novo quadro regulamentar que tem vindo a ser preparado implica um acrescido nvel de exigncia para as Instituis de Crdito mas tambm sobre o Banco de Portugal. Teremos tambm que monitorar a evoluo do Sistema de Pagamentos, uma vez que a entrada em funcionamento do novo sistema europeu de pagamentos por grosso em tempo real (Target 2) e a implementao do projecto da rea nica de Pagamentos no espao europeu (SEPA), vo tambm implicar importantes transformas na utilizao do sistemas de carts e transferncias bancrias, com benefcios para os consumidores em comodidade e harmonizao de preos. Antecipando essas tarefas futuras quero assegurar que o Banco de Portugal possui o corpo tcnico, os recursos e o sentido do servio plico para continuar a ser uma instituio de excelncia capaz de bem representar o pas nas instituis da Unio Monetria Europeia e de desempenhar com eficcia e independncia as importantes funs para a economia portuguesa que lhe esto atribudas. Lisboa 20 de Junho de 2006 Vtor Constncio

Title: Speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the presentation of the Conference and Workshop "For a comprehensive reform of the organization and management of the public sector"
text: Speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa presentation of the Conference and Workshop "For a comprehensive reform of the organization and management of the plico sector" Banco de Portugal, the Plicas Finance Council and the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation decided to promote a reflection in Portuguese society on the reform of the organization and management of the plico sector. To this end, they chose to organize a conference and a workshop on this topic, which will take place in Lisbon, in the installations of the Gulbenkian Foundation, from 28 to 30 January of the first year. The conference will take place on the 28th and 29th and will be open to plico, upon registration on the Internet, and the workshop will be on the 30th, with participation by invitation. In the current context of the ecological and financial crisis, it is natural that Portuguese society wants to revisit and reconsider the choice of the breadth of the functions of the State and the services it wants and which it is willing to pay, in a sustainable way, through fees of use and taxes. However, another plan is part of the joint initiative of Banco de Portugal, the Plicas Finance Council and the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation: the reflection on the organization and management of the sector so that it can fulfil its functions with the greatest effectiveness and efficiency possible. This is a fundamental reflection even if we want to take as a given the perimeter of the functions of the State. This is the perspective that has undered the sponsorship of the events we are announcing. I mentioned the two key words for the conceptual framework of the intended reflection: effectiveness and efficiency. A plico service (whether provided by plicas or private entities, in this case with contractualization by the plico sector) is all the more effective the greater the degree of satisfaction and confidence it can generate in the citizens to which the service is directed. In other words, a service is all the more effective the more its output fits the needs of citizens (and the objectives defined by the political power, which represents citizens). In turn, the efficiency of the services has to do with their productivity, that is, with the ability to produce a given volume of services with fewer resources and, therefore, with lower costs. The two strands  effectiveness and efficiency  have to be taken into account in the discussion on the reform of the Portuguese plica administration. The current budgetary situation makes the issue of the productivity of services and the costs involved in their production particularly relevant, but we must not forget the problems that exist in many services due to too long response times and/or insufficient quality. Political decisions on which goods and services the State guarantees access to, or on which market failures to regulate, are in a different sphere from decisions on the design of the institutions responsible for the supply of those goods and services and regulatory tasks. In this great sphere, of design of the institutions supplying goods and services, it is necessary to discuss the advantages and disadvantages of contractualization of plicas functions to non-plicas entities. But it is also crucial to discuss the desirable degree of specialisation of the functions and objectives of the plicas institutions. Should the first naturally smaller and the second largest be encouraged in the plico sector? Should the technical advice functions and the provision of the services themselves be separated into different institutions (and with different management models)? Two other issues that need to be addressed are: the type of coordination between different levels and natures of plicas institutions and the regulation of the provision of contracted services to private entities. The coordination and regulation of institutions and the regulation of the provision of services will be all the more critical the greater the degree of specialization of the institutions and the importance of contractualization to entities outside the plico sector. Another issue to be considered is the financial and human resources management of the plicas institutions. Traditional budgetary management does not establish a relationship between the allocation of financial resources and the performance of the plicas institutions.
