In addition, we all know the limitations and inefficiencies generated by the incremental approach to the institutions' budgets, which justify the allocation of resources mainly by the implementation of previous years. You must implement other practices that relate resources to policy priorities and the quality of performance in performing assigned tasks. The same type of paradigm shift is possible with regard to the management of human resources (in general, and of the most qualified managers and staff in particular). These and other issues will be addressed from a conceptual perspective in the first part of the conference, where three recognized international experts in plica administration will intervene (Christopher Pollitt and Geert Bouchaert of the Catica University of Lovaina, and Giovanni Valotti of the University of Bocconi), whose curricula vitae summaries can consult in the material distributed for this conference. The second part of the conference will be dedicated to the presentation and analysis of successful experiences in other countries that have faced complicated budgetary situations and which, through appropriate reforms, have been resolved in a lasting manner. None of the reform processes follows exactly a pure teic model and all tended, to a greater or lesser extent, to adapt the models to the realities of these countries. In this sense, the prospects behind the various successful reforms are different between countries. The experiences of Australia, Canada and Sweden were chosen to illustrate the plurality of cases. Each of these national experiences will be presented at the conference by an expert with recognised value in the international academic environment and with close links to the reform he describes, either because he has intervened directly in it or because he has extensive work to evaluate it. These are the cases of Professors John Halligan (University of Canberra, Australia), Evert Lindquist (University of Victoria, Canada) and Lars Jonung (University of Lund, Sweden). Each presentation of the invited foreign experts will be commented, from the perspective of the lessons that can be learned for the case Portuguese, by an eco-journalist and by a personality with relevant experience in the management of Portuguese institutions. The list of journalists includes Drs. Pedro Santos Guerreiro (Jornal de Negios), Francisco Sarsfield Cabral (Renaissance Group), Antio Costa (Diario Econico), Nicolau Santos (Expresso) and Teresa de Sousa (Plico). The list of national commentators includes Professor Antio Correia de Campos (European Parliament), Professor Diogo Lucena (Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation), Professor Rui Baleiras (Council of Plicas Finance), Dr. Isabel Mota (Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation) and Professor Luis Valadares Tavares (Instituto Superior Tecnico). Alongside the list of foreign guests, the quality of the speakers at the conference is unequivocally demonstrated. The third and last part of the conference will take the format of a round table, under the title "Lics para Portugal", moderated by Dr. Teodora Cardoso, President of the Council of Plicas Finance, and in which will participate Professor Luis Campos e Cunha (Nova SBE), Dr. Jose Leite Martins (Inspector General of Finance) and Professor Marco Cangiano (University of New York and IMF). This roundtable will discuss the main conclusions of the speeches and the comments made during the conference. In order to encourage participation in the conference, a website has been set up where, from the first week and until the date of the conference, the plico concerned can leave his questions, suggestions and comments on the reform of the Portuguese sector. Dr. Teodora Cardoso will select some questions and suggestions with more interest and introduce them for discussion at the round table. On the third day, Wednesday 30 January, the Workshop will take place under the theme "Fiscal Consolidation and Reform of the Organization and Management of the Plico Sector", which completes this joint initiative of Banco de Portugal, the Plicas Finance Council and the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation. The aim is to allow a more fruitful and informal technical discussion on possible models of reform in the case of Portuguese. Participation in the workshop will be by invitation, limited to experts, but seeking to cover a broad spectrum of political sensitivities. The aim of the conference and the workshop is to design and organise a space for debate and confrontation of ideas that are broad and not captured by any of the intervening groups, contributing to the formation of this consensus. It is desirable that the main elements of the future reform to be introduced into the management of the sector are as consensual as Portuguese possible, so that they remain relatively stable, in particular in the face of economic changes in government majorities. Banco de Portugal, 13 December 2012
text_original: Discurso do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa na apresentao da Conferncia e Workshop Para uma reforma abrangente da organizao e gesto do sector plico O Banco de Portugal, o Conselho de Finanas Plicas e a Fundao Calouste Gulbenkian decidiram promover uma reflexo na sociedade portuguesa sobre a reforma da organizao e gesto do sector plico. Para isso, escolheram organizar uma conferncia e um workshop sobre esta temtica, que tero lugar em Lisboa, nas instalas da Fundao Gulbenkian, de 28 a 30 de Janeiro do primo ano. A conferncia decorrer nos dias 28 e 29 e ser aberta ao plico, mediante inscrio na internet, e o workshop ser no dia 30, com participao por convite. No actual contexto de crise econica e financeira,  natural que a sociedade portuguesa queira revisitar e reequacionar a escolha sobre qual a amplitude das funs do Estado e dos servios plicos que pretende e que est disposta a pagar, de forma sustentvel, atravs de taxas de utilizao e de impostos. Todavia,  outro o plano em que se insere a iniciativa conjunta do Banco de Portugal, do Conselho de Finanas Plicas e da Fundao Calouste Gulbenkian: a reflexo sobre a organizao e a gesto do sector plico para que este cumpra as suas funs com a maior efectividade e eficincia possveis. Tratase de uma reflexo fundamental mesmo se quisermos tomar como dado o permetro das funs do Estado.  esta a perspectiva que norteou o patrocnio dos eventos que estamos a anunciar. Mencionei as duas palavraschave para o enquadramento conceptual da reflexo pretendida: efectividade e eficincia. Um servio plico (seja ele prestado por entidades plicas ou privadas, neste timo caso com contratualizao pelo sector plico)  tanto mais efectivo quanto maior for o grau de satisfao e confiana que consegue gerar nos cidados a que se dirige o servio. Por outras palavras, um servio  tanto mais efectivo quanto mais o seu output se ajusta s necessidades dos cidados (e aos objectivos definidos pelo poder poltico, que representa os cidados). Por sua vez, a eficincia dos servios plicos tem a ver com a sua produtividade, isto , com a capacidade de produzir um dado volume de servios com menos recursos e, por isso, com menores custos. As duas vertentes  efectividade e eficincia tm de ser tidas em conta na discusso sobre a reforma da administrao plica portuguesa. A situao oramental actual torna particularmente relevante a questo da produtividade dos servios plicos e os custos envolvidos na sua produo, mas no podemos esquecer os problemas que existem em muitos servios plicos devido a tempos de resposta demasiado longos e/ou de qualidade insuficiente. As deciss polticas sobre quais os bens e servios aos quais o Estado garante acesso, ou sobre quais as falhas de mercado a regular, esto numa esfera diferente das deciss sobre o desenho das instituis encarregadas do fornecimento desses bens e servios e das tarefas de regulao. Nesta tima esfera, de desenho das instituis fornecedoras de bens e servios,  necessrio discutir as vantagens e desvantagens da contratualizao de funs plicas a entidades no plicas. Mas  igualmente crucial discutir o grau de especializao desejvel das funs e objectivos das instituis plicas. Deverse favorecer uma organizao do sector plico assente em instituis uniobjectivo ou multiobjectivo, as primeiras naturalmente mais pequenas e as segundas maiores? Deverse separar em instituies diferentes (e com modelos de gesto diferentes) as funs de aconselhamento tcnico aos decisores polticos e a prestao de servios plicos propriamente ditos? Outros dois temas que tm de ser tratados so: o tipo de coordenao entre diferentes nveis e naturezas de instituis plicas e a regulao da prestao de servios plicos contratualizada a entidades privadas. A coordenao e regulao das instituis e a regulao da prestao de servios sero tanto mais crticas quanto maior for o grau de especializao das instituies e a importncia da contratualizao a entidades fora do sector plico. Outra questo sobre a qual importa reflectir  a gesto financeira e dos recursos humanos das instituis plicas. A gesto oramental tradicional no estabelece uma relao entre a alocao de recursos financeiros e o desempenho das instituis plicas. Alm disso, todos conhecemos as limitas e ineficincias geradas pela abordagem incremental aos oramentos das instituis, que justificam a atribuio de recursos sobretudo pela execuo verificada em exerccios anteriores.  preciso implementar outras prticas que relacionam recursos com prioridades polticas e com a qualidade do desempenho na execuo das tarefas atribudas. O mesmo tipo de mudana de paradigma  possvel no que respeita  gesto dos recursos humanos (em geral, e dos gestores e quadros mais qualificados, em particular). Estas e outras quests sero abordadas numa perspectiva conceptual na primeira parte da conferncia, onde interviro trs reconhecidos especialistas internacionais em administrao plica (Christopher Pollitt e Geert Bouchaert, da Universidade Catica de Lovaina, e Giovanni Valotti, da Universidade de Bocconi), cujos curricula vitae sumrios podem consultar no material distribudo para esta conferncia. A segunda parte da conferncia ser dedicada  apresentao e anlise de experincias bemsucedidas noutros pases que enfrentaram situas oramentais complicadas e que, atravs de reformas adequadas, foram resolvidas de forma duradoura. Nenhum dos processos de reforma segue exactamente um modelo teico puro e todos tenderam, em maior ou menor grau, a adaptar os modelos s realidades desses pases. Nesse sentido, as perspectivas subjacentes s vrias reformas bemsucedidas so diferentes entre os pases. Escolheramse as experincias da Austrlia, Canad e Sucia para ilustrar a pluralidade de casos. Cada uma destas experincias nacionais ser apresentada na conferncia por um especialista com valia reconhecida no meio acadmico internacional e com ligas estreitas  reforma que vem descrever, ou por nela ter intervindo directamente ou por ter vasta obra de avaliao da mesma. So os casos dos Professores John Halligan (Universidade de Canberra, Austrlia), Evert Lindquist (Universidade de Victoria, Canad) e Lars Jonung (Universidade de Lund, Sucia). Cada apresentao dos especialistas estrangeiros convidados ser comentada, na perspectiva dos ensinamentos que se possam retirar para o caso portugus, por um jornalista econico e por uma personalidade com experincia relevante em gesto de instituis plicas portuguesas. A lista de jornalistas inclui os Drs. Pedro Santos Guerreiro (Jornal de Negios), Francisco Sarsfield Cabral (Grupo Renascena), Antio Costa (Dirio Econico), Nicolau Santos (Expresso) e Teresa de Sousa (Plico).Da lista de comentadores nacionais fazem parte o Professor Antio Correia de Campos (Parlamento Europeu), o Professor Diogo Lucena (Fundao Calouste Gulbenkian), o Professor Rui Baleiras (Conselho de Finanas Plicas), a Dra. Isabel Mota (Fundao Calouste Gulbenkian) e o Professor Lus Valadares Tavares (Instituto Superior Tcnico). A par da lista de convidados estrangeiros, fica inequivocamente demonstrada a qualidade dos intervenientes na conferncia. A terceira e tima parte da conferncia assumir o formato de mesa redonda, sob o ttulo Lis para Portugal, moderada pela Dra. Teodora Cardoso, Presidente do Conselho de Finanas Plicas, e em que participaro o Professor Lus Campos e Cunha (Nova SBE), o Dr. Jos Leite Martins (InspectorGeral de Finanas) e o Professor Marco Cangiano (Universidade de Nova Iorque e FMI). Nesta mesa redonda discutirseo as principais concluss das intervens e os comentrios efectuados durante a conferncia. Com o objectivo de incentivar a participao na conferncia, criouse um stio na internet onde, a partir da prima semana e at  data da conferncia, o plico interessado poder deixar as suas perguntas, sugests e comentrios sobre a reforma do sector plico portugus. A Dra. Teodora Cardoso seleccionar algumas perguntas e sugests com mais interesse e introduzilas para discusso na mesa redonda. No terceiro dia, quartafeira 30 de Janeiro, ter lugar o Workshop sob o tema Consolidao Oramental e Reforma da Organizao e Gesto do Sector Plico, que completa esta iniciativa conjunta do Banco de Portugal, do Conselho de Finanas Plicas e da Fundao Calouste Gulbenkian. O objectivo  permitir uma discusso tcnica mais frutfera e informal sobre eventuais modelos de reforma para o caso portugus. A participao no workshop ser por convite, limitado a especialistas, mas procurando cobrir um espectro alargado de sensibilidades polticas. O objectivo da conferncia e do e workshop  conceber e organizar um espao de debate e de confronto de ideias amplo e no capturado por nenhum dos grupos intervenientes, contribuindo para a formao do referido consenso.  desejvel que os elementos principais da futura reforma a introduzir na gesto do sector plico portugus sejam o mais consensuais possvel, de forma a permanecerem relativamente estveis, nomeadamente perante mudanas conjunturais de maiorias governativas. Banco de Portugal, 13 de Dezembro de 2012

Title: Speech by the Governor of the Bank of Portugal on the occasion of the dinner in honour of the Council of the European Central Bank - Lisbon, 5 May 2010
text: SPEECH BY THE GOVERNOR OF BANCO DE PORTUGAL AT THE DINNER IN HONOUR OF THE GOVERNING COUNCIL OF THE EUROPEAN CENTRAL BANK LISBON, 5th OF MAY 2010 Prime Minister, Minister of State and Finance, President of the European Central Bank, Colleagues, Ladies and Gentlemen, It gives me great pleasure to welcome you all in this place full of history on the occasion of a meeting of the Governing Council of the European Central Bank. Look around. We are in a place that highlights two Portuguese adventures. Firstly, this monastery of Jerimos was built in the XVIth century to celebrate our maritime discoveries and secondly, here, in this very cloister, was signed our accession treaty into the European Union in 1985. A few yards from here is the shore from where set sail the ships to launch the discoveries. For almost a century Portugal kept a monopoly of the spice maritime trade with India and the Far East, where our ships arrived in 1498. In 1500 the fleet of alvares Cabral arrived in Brazil with all its riches. In 1501 the construction of this monastery began and was completed after several decades. As all major buildings of the time it was built to celebrate spiritual and earthly endeavours. On the northern side of this cloister we find symbols of the Passion of Christ. On the southern side we have the symbols of kingdom and Kings. The concept was that the history of Portugal and our monarchic dynasty interconnected with the history of Christianity. Appropriately, the King was called Manuel, from Emmanuel (meaning God with us) announced by Isaiah as the Saviour, and the Kings wife was named Maria like the mother of Christ. The Armillary Sphere is an instrument of navigation with the celestial orbits, used by the King as his symbol and combined with the Christian Cross it appears in different places. Empire, earthly power and religion come together. Politics also enters. The monastery was given to the Hermit Order of St. Hieronymus, a Spanish order of monks devoted to the perpetual service of the dynasty reigning in Castille. This is explained by the aim of our King of becoming the heir to the Castillian crown thus unifying the two kingdoms. He had after all just celebrated his second marriage to Maria of Castille, the sister of the great Queen Isabel. You see then how European history and politics are present in every stone. As this lengthy introduction shows it is difficult for me to resist the historic spell of the place. We are here in the cradle of the first globalization, the first adventure to articulate the unity of humanity. Denis de Rougemont, the great Swiss French European thinker defined Europe precisely by its globalizing mission. The Delphic oracle, when asked by Cadmon about the whereabouts of his sister Europe who had been kidnapped by the Great God of the Greeks, answered: You will never find her. From this answer and from the wanderings that Cadmon was advised to pursue until exhaustion, Rougemont concludes that ... it seems difficult to know where is Europe, if we understand by this bringing her, all ready and made by history: because it is the search itself that creates her. Seeking Europe, is to make her!  and that is what I call: Adventure. This tendency for universalism, for the globalizing of Europe, is what our greatest poet Fernando Pessoa characterizes as the main contribution of our country to civilization. Himself bilingual and with an English education, he wrote in the 1920s:  The Portuguese are essentially cosmopolitan. Never was a Portuguese only Portuguese: he was always everything . An expression very similar to the one used by a German philosopher Johann E. Erdman, a disciple of Hegel and Wilhelm von Humboldt, who wrote: Es ist undeutsch, bloss deutsch zu sein (It is not German to be only German) . Written in 1862, in the context of the debate about German nationality that occupied Germany during most of the XIXth century until its unification, the sentence reflects the caution of many participants to avoid any kind of nationalism. Another echo of this can be found in another expression by our Fernando Pessoa: To be Portuguese, in the decent sense of the word, is to be European without the bad manners of nationality. In the same vein, we may recall what Ortega y Gasset said in his Meditaci de Europa, delivered in 1949 in Berlin: ...Europe as a society precedes the existence of European nations. ... This historical space ...was created by the Roman Empire and the geographic configuration of the emergent nations coincides with the simple administrative definition of the dioceses in the Late Middle Ages. It is important to reflect upon this: before being a political project Europe is a memory, a key to understanding our own past. Nations are a construct of man, not a natural reality. They reflect the social a priori that implies that our consciousness and our knowledge are socially constituted. Many nations were even the product of the action of a State. There were Savoyards, Bretons, Gascons before there were French and Bavarians and Prussian before there were Germans. At the time of the French revolution half of the population did not speak French and only republican public schools completed the formation of Frenchmen. A form of civic community among strangers was somewhat artificially created to shape several European nation-states. Nothing proves that a similar process, certainly longer and more difficult, cannot occur at the European level. This does not imply that Europe could become a Nation, not even as Montesquieu pretended une Nation composee de plusieurs (a Nation composed of many). Europeans are too diverse and too self-critical for that to happen. We belong nevertheless to two societies, our own and the European one as the essential background for our rationalist, universal values. In his famous Vienna address in 1935 on the existential crisis of Europe , Edmund Husserl underlines the fact that philosophical reason is the original phenomenon that characterizes Europe. And his conclusion was: The existential crisis of Europe has only two outcomes: either Europe will disappear in becoming ever more distant from its own rational signification, that is its vital sense, and will sink in the hatred of the spirit and in barbarity; or Europe will be reborn from the philosophical spirit as a result of a heroism of reason that will overcome naturalism. We know very well what happened at those dramatic times and how we could never again trust reason the same way after the war. We live now in so-called postmodern times, which value more the sceptical side of reason. It is no surprise then that the greatest contemporary Portuguese thinker, Eduardo Lourenco, who has lived and taught in Germany, Brasil and mostly in France, a true good European, spoke in 1989 about European culture as a culture of inquietude, a culture of anguish and doubt, that is to say, a culture of radical defiance of the gods as figures of certainty. And above all a culture of defiance to the being never defined or pacified that we are as human beings This vision of Lourenco implies that our Faustian civilization that as he says has spread throughout the world its torment and insatiable curiosity, does not have a well defined identity. We could say that he theorizes our non-identitary identity. In this way, modern high culture has robbed us of any lofty spiritual goals behind our endeavours to build a unified Europe. It remains a fact that a truly united Europe can still be the mobilizing utopia of our times, but for most people committed to the idea we are talking now of a more prosaic utilitarian project. Even the original mission of maintaining peace in our continent seems to many an implausible or unnecessary goal after so many years of democratic normality. What quietly dominates is the target of achieving a better management of individual national interdependences to promote national self-interest, or even more prosaically to create the conditions to maximize GDP growth. Do not misinterpret me. These are important objectives and we all live and work to serve them. However, advanced European democracies face a difficult period ahead of slow growth, high unemployment and deep reforms of their social and economic model. I worry, consequently, that by lacking more elevated values deeply rooted in the core of our humanity as rational, forgiving beings we may lack the ramparts necessary to face any deeper crisis that may defy the very foundations of our institutions. And we all know what Georges Santayana said: Those who cannot remember the past, are condemned to repeat it... Even without considering long-term structural problems, we know how crises can emerge with threatening consequences. We are now going through one of the more acute episodes of turbulence in the short history of our monetary union. Investors in financial markets are trying to cast doubt on the capacity of the adjustment mechanisms within the monetary union to deal with the existence of macroeconomic imbalances in some member countries. They seem to forget that besides the functioning of the institutional framework that imposes corrective measures in any off-balance countries, there are endogenous mechanisms that in a currency area operate to restore a viable equilibrium between savings and investment. It has been known for quite a long time in economic theory that regions of a country with such an imbalance adjust, albeit through a recessionary process, to correct the disequilibrium. Imbalances that stem from private agents decisions have market-driven self-correcting mechanisms that operate through changes of competitiveness and the effect of budget constraints monitored by the financial sector. Naturally, countries must adopt policies that reinforce those spontaneous processes of adjustment by trying to prevent more serious problems to start with. As I wrote in 2000: It can be said that the macroeconomics of a successful monetary integration is about the interiorization by economic agents of new rules regarding fiscal policy and wage behaviour. Fiscal policy needs to keep a countercyclical role to act as a shock absorber. Wage behaviour should take as a reference wage cost developments in the euro area as a whole and should deviate from those only if there is a productivity growth differential. In reference to Portugal, our policies did not always follow these principles. But independently of it, the initial shock of interest rate reduction after joining the euro coming from a previous regime of higher rates, implied an unavoidable explosion of private expenditure and debt that no sensible fiscal policy could completely offset. As I remarked in 2004, the initial boom of private expenditure was as unavoidable as the subsequent fall and adjustment. After a mild recession in 2003 and a big budget slippage in 2005, we implemented what has been so far the biggest fiscal correction since the inception of the euro and initiated a broad process of adjustment. In mid 2007, we had achieved a budget deficit below 3% in a consistent way, the economy was growing again at around 2% and our inflation rate was below the euro area average. Our relative unit labour costs against our main trading partners (21 countries) increased from 2003 to 2009 by just 4.4% which is well below the increase of 10.9% for the euro area average, using the same concept of the real effective exchange rate. Since 1999 the figures are 9.1% for Portugal and 15.9% for the average of the euro area. On a par with this, our inflation rate since mid 2007 has been below the figure for the euro area. Our economy has been in a mode of competitive disinflation throughout this period. At the same time our productive structure continued to progress in the value chain and by 2008, for instance, our exports of services to business already had a higher weight than the traditional exports of textiles and clothing. Unfortunately, the improvement in our balance of goods and services was not sufficient, as our savings rate continued to be very low and our energy bill and the outflows of the income balance combined to keep a very high external deficit that has to be significantly reduced, namely through the mechanisms I have already described. We have lived beyond our means and, as Kenneth Rogoff recently said, Financial regulation has been appropriate, otherwise the situation would be much worse. The point is, that we needed time to continue the adjustment and in principle, monetary union was supposed to give us that time for a gradual process of rebalancing. The international financial crisis that started in 2007 interrupted the process and the more recent market attacks on euro area countries vulnerable in terms of sovereign debt implies that time became a luxury: we have now to make a more abrupt, quicker and more severe adjustment. As I warned already in 2001: Conceived for an infinite or very long horizon, the technical definition of external sustainability ends up not being truly operational because it only refers to the capacity of the economy to pay its debt within that time horizon. Operationally, what counts is the assessment made by investors about that capacity of repayment, which means that the possibility of financing depends on many factors, sometimes not fundamental ones. That is what we face now and so, we may need to ponder whether the recently approved Stability Programme should be reinforced by adopting upfront measures foreseen for later years. We must be resolute and clear-headed in recognizing the reality of how markets operate and, as captains of an embattled ship, we should not complain too much about the sea where we have to navigate. We have to take comfort from the fact that we are not alone in this. A monetary union is not a sort of multilateral currency board. All member countries have a common interest in the well being of our union and its currency. We all share the guilt related to the failure of governance in the preventive arm of the Stability Pact. We ourselves, have never tried to hamper the functioning of the Pact and, when caught at fault, we have abided by the rules. The recent events revealed indecisions and surprising misinterpretations of self-interest, but the system worked and deserves our trust. The need for reforms in surveillance and crisis management became nevertheless apparent, including the creation of an European Monetary Fund that had been foreseen in very early discussions about monetary union, and I am sure this episode will have consequences for future institutional arrangements. Everything must in fact be done to reinforce the euro area. We can all see how it was important to face the international financial crisis. From the beginning of the euro, the Eurosystem was able to consolidate a culture of stability that is so important to create the conditions for long-term economic growth. Since 1999, we have been able to deliver an average inflation rate of just 1.9%, an important achievement during an extended period of ten years. Very significant was also the way the euro and our common monetary policy helped Europe to face the financial crisis. The quick and bold decisions taken by the Eurosystem were instrumental in containing the risk of a deep recession or even a depression. Since May last year our monetary policy delivered an average overnight rate (EONIA) of just 0.4% and a three months Euribor of 0.8%. These low rates supported the income of indebted households and firms and were essential to shore up domestic demand. The unconventional measures taken in the area of liquidity provision were likewise fundamental to help the financial sector survive the test of a very serious market stress. In the end, academics and analysts had to agree that the ECB and the Eurosystem had performed well and strengthened its standing as a professional central bank. In this connection, I think it is of elementary justice to single out the role played by President Trichet in leading our team throughout the turmoil. His leadership qualities, his experience, his knowledge of the markets and his communication skills were essential to the overall performance of the system. I am therefore very glad that our President of the Republic has decided to decorate him tomorrow for his role in steering the euro area during this trying period. It is for me also a great honour to be able to work with him more closely in the near future in my new capacity and alongside all my colleagues on the Executive Board of the European Central Bank. There is much work to do to deal with the evolving predicament in capital markets and to implement the reforms stemming from the lessons that the financial crisis has compelled us to adopt. The crisis made clear that monetary policy focused on price stability had to be complemented with new instruments of macro-prudential policies to ensure financial stability and asset markets less prone to price bubbles. The creation of the European Systemic Risk Board, alongside the General Council of the ECB, is the European response to that requirement. At the same time, monetary policy will have to rely on a new vision of the transmission mechanisms and the economic models used to help the decision making will have to integrate in a relevant way the role of financial markets in our economies. A complete overhaul of regulation of the financial sector became necessary. We must be aware of the main lessons that must be drawn from the crisis: a) the financial sector is not self-equilibrating or self-correcting; b) an unfettered financial sector can generate crisis on its own; c) extended periods of high growth of credit and debt generate asset price booms that always end in a crisis; d) low inflation in the market of goods and services is not enough to guarantee financial stability. Human societies have learnt and forgotten these lessons several times throughout history. Misbehaviour by big financial institutions, deregulation and perverse incentives created this time the perfect storm that will continue for a long period of time to cause low growth and severe unemployment. New regulation will have to contribute to the taming of the sectors tendency to expand beyond proportion. Finally, a reform of the global monetary system is necessary to solve the recurrent problem of global macroeconomic imbalances that may lead to new crises in the future. Regarding Europe, besides the already mentioned changes in economic governance and crisis management, structural reforms are required to create new sources of economic growth that are necessary to survive in a very competitive world and to keep essential parts of our social model in the face of Europes collective demographic suicide. Deep down, we all know that Europe is again in a defining moment and is going through an existential crisis. Last year, the German philosopher Jurgen Habermas in his new book Europe, the faltering project wrote: For the first time in the process of European unification we face the danger of a regression behind the stage of integration already achieved. This sense of impending crisis is recurrent in European history. In his great book The Europeans, Luigi Barzini, in 1983, described Europe in a very apt way: It is pessimistic, prudent, practical, parsimonious, like an old-fashioned banker. ...It always prefers to wait and see. It enjoys delving into the complexity of things; the more complexities it can find the better. Europe looks for nuances, the bad side of anything good, the good side of anything bad. This does not mean that Europe is paralyzed. In moments of doubt we can always turn to the great man of action, one of Europes founders, Jean Monnet, who reminded us that Men only act in a state of need and only recognize the need in a state of crisis. In fact, we all know that Europe has progressed through the process of overcoming crises. Like the mythical bird, Europe has been reborn several times. I started with Rougemont talking about search and adventure. I conclude now that Europe as adventure continues. In this place, thinking about the men who set sail from these shores in such small ships to go into truly unchartered waters, it is perhaps easier to feel this sense of adventure. To face our own problems now, we must have their courage, their resolve and their hope. Lisbon 5th of May 2010. Vitor Constancio.

Title: Speech of the Governor at the 6th FIU-Banking Meeting on "The Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing"
text: VI MEETING UIF-BANCA "PREVENTING MONEY LAUNDERING AND TERRORIST FINANCING" Lisbon 12 March 2007 INTERVENTION OF THE GOVERNOR OF BANCO DE PORTUGAL I begin by congratulating the organizers of this 6th Meeting between the Financial Information Unit of the Judicial Police and the Banking Sector and for thanking the honorable invitation for Banco de Portugal to join the event. The issues to be addressed relate to serious threats to civilised society which must therefore be dealt with with determination. The fact of this Meeting bring together judicial entities, police, supervisors and financial institutions is revealing the dual objective of the activity against money laundering crimes. On the one hand, combating the crimes in which illicit money originates that seeks to enter the legal circuit and, on the other hand, defend the integrity of the financial system. This integrity is associated with the notion of trust that is fundamental to the exercise of financial activity. Without trust it is not possible to imagine the development of financial intermediaries that collect savings and distribute them for the best economic uses. The security in transactions that is essential to the proper functioning of financial markets implies more than legal certainty. As Durkheim reminded us , "the essence of a contract is not in the contract", that is, it lies in the mutual trust which can well assume the parties who conclude it as to its fulfilment. That is why financial crime undermines the fundamentals of market activity and is fought by all those responsible for the financial system. I do not forget, of course, that one of the specific interests in preventing money laundering is the need to combat the crimes associated with it. Initially, the motivation started from the fight against drug trafficking, but the range of underlying crimes gradually extended to the inclusion of terrorist financing. The degree of sophistication that criminal activity has achieved in the use of modern financial systems is enormous. The total freedom of movement of capital that currently prevails in the world makes the system more vulnerable to its illicit use. Despite the efforts of the authorities, the amounts of dubious capital that manage to enter the legal system are very large and it is estimated that they can currently reach annual amounts of almost EUR 1 billion. The best way to prevent misuse of the financial system is thus to prevent criminal money from going into the legal circuit. This is why the further development of legislative activity since the establishment of the Financial Action Action Group (FATF) in 1989, within the Framework of the OECD, is related to the preventive pillar of anti-money laundering activity. The full criminalisation of all forms of laundering, customer identification requirements, the development of internal control systems and the mandatory reporting of potentially suspicious transactions are fundamental aspects of this preventive pillar. Portugal was a founding country of FATF and since 1993 we have a money laundering prevention system involving all financial sector entities, which is monitored and monitored by the supervisory bodies of credit institutions and financial corporations, the insurance sector and the capital market, and finally that it implements the indispensable connection of financial entities to the competent authorities to receive and analyse suspicious communications of money laundering. Since 2004, a new law has been unifying the legal regime for the prevention of money laundering applicable to all sectors of the economy. In the context of our responsibilities, several Banco de Portugal Instructions regulate in greater detail the procedures that credit institutions have to comply with, including the preparation of an annual report on internal systems to prevent money laundering. We are therefore faced with a legal framework which is considered to be adapted to national requirements and international standards, both fatf, the Bank for International Payments or the European Union. The legislation has been the subject of constant improvement measures and is prepared to keep up with the challenges posed by the new typologies and trends in money laundering and, at present, also terrorist financing. As I mentioned earlier, the system combines with a classic repressive aspect of persecution and punishment of serious crime in general, a preventive aspect that results in the activity of the competent authorities to receive communications of suspicious transactions which, in case Portuguese, are the Attorney General's Office and the Financial Information Unit of the Judicial Police. It follows from the outset that the evaluation of the results of the implementation of the system should be carried out separately considering the results of the preventive and repressive aspects, only in this way can a complete assessment of the effectiveness of the system be made. This means, for example, that this effectiveness cannot be measured so only by the number of convictions for the crime of laundering and terrorist financing, which is actually quite low, but must be assessed by the results which, in the preventive aspect, the existing regulation determines as a means of deepening the integrity of the institutions and the financial system. In particular, measures to deepen customer knowledge and keep track of operations carried out and report potentially suspicious operations, it tends to remove the most serious crime from the institutions, in addition to facilitating any subsequent investigation of criminal activities. This preventive action requires the full cooperation of financial institutions which understand, of course, that this is also in their own interest. This is recognised in the anti-money laundering rules, as confirmed, for example, in the 3rd Community Directive on the prevention of money laundering of 26 October 2005, which in recital 2 states: "The soundness, integrity and stability of credit institutions and financial institutions, as well as confidence in the financial system as a whole, may be compromised by the efforts of criminals and their associates to conceal the origin of the proceeds of their activities." I believe that the ultimate purpose of a money laundering prevention scheme should never be lost in view of the purpose of preventing "criminals and their associates", often in an organised manner, from using financial entities as instruments for concealment, transformation and conversion of funds of criminal origin in a way that can help contaminate institutions and their employees, customers and economic activity in general. Understood in this way, it is understood that the preventive regime for laundering is also intended to avoid risks of an operational, reputational and image nature of institutions and customers, which may, for example, arise from the fraudulent use of their identities. They also seek to prevent the dangers to society and the economy in general, since both depend on the proper functioning of a financial system that has maximum integrity, is managed professionally and in accordance with strict ethical standards. It should also be considered that the recognition of the integrity of a financial system is a strategic asset, both internally and internationally, particularly if we consider the highly competitive landscape of economies in the global system in which we are located. This recognition of the benefits of money prevention systems leads institutions to consider bleaching prevention systems, despite the financial costs they entail, as instruments that can result in tangible benefits by protecting them from serious criminal action. In fact, properly designed preventive systems, driven by the regulatory intervention of supervisors in collaboration with supervised entities, in addition to constituting a protection of institutions against financial crime associated with money laundering, also advocate them for more common financial crime, such as forgery or theft of the identity of customers, or the use of false identity in distance transactions or the actions of dishonest employees in collusion with criminals seeking to abuse institutions. Another fundamental feature of a bleaching prevention system is the trust and understanding that must be established and maintained among all the authorities that collaborate in it, which must know perfectly the tasks and purposes of each and keep in mind that only by acting together can they build and operate a preventive system capable of producing effective results. It should be recognised that financial institutions play an important role in the system as they are the entry points into the financial circuit and that they are also responsible for the effort to know their clients well and, consequently, are the first agents to be able to realise who intends to abuse the system. In this way, in order for the system to function effectively, it is necessary for financial institutions to rely on the activity of the competent authorities and to understand the referral and sequence of their communications. In order to maintain trust among all the actors in the system, it is important that everyone acts with discretion and professionalism and that the results are achieved so that, ultimately, the repressive system has been established. From this perspective, it can be considered that to reinforce the possibilities of adequate final results the system still needs some improvements to become more robust and effective. On the other hand, it must always be held out that money laundering is a phenomenon of a clearly international nature, given the total freedom of movement of capital and the generalisation of new information technologies, the continued internationalisation of our financial sector creates new challenges that require the permanent action of all those involved and the vigilant attention of financial entities. It should be noted in this regard that international standards, in particular those of FATF, provide that institutions must apply the most stringent preventive standards also to their subsidiaries and branches abroad, in particular outside the European Communities and in the event that they fail to achieve this, have an obligation to inform the supervisory authorities of the country of their home office. In addition to being a mature system, the Portuguese system has already been tested by three rounds of international evaluations, the last of which was carried out in 2006 by an evaluation team composed of FATF experts who assessed not only the legal and regulatory framework that constitutes the system, but also how all its components operate. In the last international assessment, 33 authorities, institutions and private companies were visited only in the financial sector, and the level of application of the rules and regulations in force was examined in the financial sector alone, and the level of application of the rules and regulations in force in the financial sector was examined, as well as the procedures used in practice to disseminate and disseminate them and also assess the relations between the institutions and the supervisory authorities of the financial sector. The examination also included, of course, the fulfilment of the duty of reporting suspicious transactions by the supervised entities. In addition to Banco de Portugal, which coordinated the work, they participated from the outset in the preparation of the Portuguese position, the Attorney General's Office, the Securities And Exchange Commission, the Insurance Institute of Portugal, the Directorate-General for Customs and Excise Duties and the Financial Information Unit of the Judicial Police. They were also called to actively collaborate in the preparation of the evaluation, the Supreme Court of Justice, the Higher Agency for Economic Activities, the Directorate General of Registers and Notary, the Legislative Policy Office of the Ministry of Justice, the General Inspection of Games and the following private entities, Order of Lawyers, Chamber of Solicitors, Chamber of Statutory Auditors and Chamber of Accountants. In conclusion of the evaluation, the FATF Plenary considered in its Report, adopted in October 2006 and published, that the Portuguese system for the prevention of money laundering is generally complete and robust in all sectors. With regard in particular to the financial sector, it concludes that the existing supervisory structure, which includes the three supervisors and also the National Council of Financial Supervisors, is sound and has the necessary independence as well as the resources necessary for the pursuit of its tasks in this area. No sub-criticism is made in the FATF Report on the quality and level of supervision to which entities integrated in the banking, insurance and capital market sectors are subject in relation to the prevention of money laundering. The FATF Report also considers that the preventive measures to which financial entities comply with the prevention of money laundering constitute a broad and consistent set of customer identification and due diligence measures, in particular in relation to transactions which may present the greatest risk, such as remote operations, and relationships with bank correspondents. It also concluded that financial entities generally apply internal control schemes without significant deficiencies and that employees are provided regular and up-to-date training in this area, and information on the new typologies and trends of the most common bleaching practices is also disseminated. On the other hand, it also considered that the Portuguese system has a complete and clear legal framework that allows the indispensable international cooperation, which is essential in this area, to be provided. However, some criticisms are presented relating to the effectiveness of the system, as the number of suspicious laundering transactions reported by the general financial authorities to the competent authorities is still low, although these figures have been gradually increased in recent years. The overall results of the international assessment, which came to be included in the Financial Sector Assessment Program of the International Monetary Fund, also released at the end of last year, can thus be regarded as highly positive for Portugal, as of the 12 SYSTEMS assessed by FATF and for developed oecd countries, the Portuguese system was, following the Belgian system, the one in Europe presented a higher degree of compliance with international standards, presenting a higher degree of compliance than systems such as Spanish, Swiss, Italian, Irish, Norwegian, Danish or Swedish. As a result of this assessment, of the 13 OECD countries already assessed only Belgium and Portugal were not subject to fatf, a follow-up process, aimed at monitoring the improvement of the implementation of certain FATF Recommendations, such as paragraphs 1, 5, 10, 13, and Special II and IV. Recommendations that in the set of 49 General and Special Recommendations, are considered mischievous in the construction of an effective system for preventing money laundering and terrorist financing. In particular, it should be noted that only Belgium and Portugal were considered in broad compliance with General Recommendation 5, which is essential for preventing money laundering and terrorist financing in the financial sector and on the regime of identification, identity verification and due diligence to be applied to customers. It should therefore be stressed that, after the exhaustive and extremely rigorous analysis to which the system was subjected, both internally and externally, in the years 2005 and 2006, it should be considered that, although it needs improvements to contribute to the increase of its effectiveness, it does not present, in particular in the financial area, structural or functional deficiencies that require the change of its fundamental components and the way in which they relate to each other. Certain remaining shortcomings will be addressed with the adoption of community legislation, which is still under discussion, where it is considered appropriate to have a "level playing field" at Community level, such as the regulation of the identity of the payer in distance transactions. as regards other existing shortcomings, in particular as regards the prevention of terrorist financing, the notion and regime of politically exposed persons, as well as the more detailed consideration of the notion of risk derived from operations and the profile of customers, in order to modulate the measures to be taken to prevent the laundering and financing of terrorism, they will be matters to be considered in the transposition diploma of the 3rd Directive on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing in the financial sector, which is under preparation and should be published by the end of this year. Further improvements and solutions should also be enshrined in this legislation in order to update the legal regime for the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, placing it in full line with the Community Directives in this area and with the General and Special Recommendations of FATF, which as is known have decisively influenced Community legislation and have been delaying the most technically demanding solutions in this area. The transposition legislation of the 3rd Directive, which is in preparation and the solutions that are enshrined therein, will subsequently be supplemented in the regulations of the supervisory authorities, but radical changes that the system does not seem to need, as I said, is not expected. Improvements will be made in the financial sector, with the aim of increasing the effectiveness of the system, to guide it even more clearly to the modulation of solutions depending on the risk offered by customers and operations, in accordance with the new precepts of the 3rd Directive and in a way adapted to our financial system, which presents itself as an open system, flexible solutions but must continue to protect its integrity and the application of high ethical standards. Lisbon, 12 March 2007 Victor Constantius
text_original: VI ENCONTRO UIF-BANCA A PREVENO DO BRANQUEAMENTO DE CAPITAIS E DO FINANCIAMENTO DO TERRORISMO Lisboa 12 de Maro de 2007 INTERVENO DO GOVERNADOR DO BANCO DE PORTUGAL Comeo por felicitar os organizadores deste VI Encontro entre a Unidade de Informao Financeira da Polcia Judiciria e o Sector Bancrio e por agradecer o honroso convite para o Banco de Portugal se associar ao acontecimento. Os temas a tratar reportam-se a ameaas graves  sociedade civilizada que devem por isso ser combatidas com determinao. A circunstncia deste Encontro reunir entidades judiciais, policiais, supervisores e instituies financeiras  reveladora do duplo objectivo que preside  actividade contra os crimes de branqueamento de capitais. Por um lado, combater os delitos em que se origina o dinheiro ilcito que procura entrar no circuito legal e, por outro lado, defender a integridade do sistema financeiro. Essa integridade est associada  noo de confiana que  fundamental ao exerccio da actividade financeira. Sem confiana no  possvel imaginar o desenvolvimento de intermedirios financeiros que recolham poupanas e as distribuam para as melhores utilizaes econmicas. A segurana nas transaces que  essencial ao bom funcionamento dos mercados financeiros implica mais do que a segurana jurdica. Como nos lembrava Durkheim  o essencial de um contrato no se encontra no contrato, ou seja, reside na confiana mtua que podem fundadamente presumir as partes que o celebram quanto ao seu cumprimento.  por isso que a criminalidade financeira mina os fundamentos da actividade dos mercados e  combatida por todos os responsveis do sistema financeiro. No esqueo, naturalmente, que um dos interesses especficos em impedir o branqueamento de capitais assenta na necessidade de combater os crimes que lhe esto associados. Inicialmente, a motivao partiu do combate ao trfico de drogas, mas o leque de crimes subjacentes foi-se progressivamente alargando at  incluso do financiamento do terrorismo.  enorme o grau de sofisticao que a actividade criminosa atingiu na utilizao dos modernos meios dos sistemas financeiros. A total liberdade de movimento de capitais que actualmente prevalece no mundo torna o sistema mais vulnervel ao seu uso ilcito. Apesar dos esforos das autoridades os montantes de capitais duvidosos que conseguem entrar no sistema legal so muito vultuosos e estima-se que possam chegar actualmente a valores anuais de quase mil milhes de euros. A melhor forma de evitar a indevida utilizao do sistema financeiro consiste , assim, em impedir que o dinheiro criminoso entre no circuito legal. Da que o maior desenvolvimento da actividade legislativa desde a criao do Grupo de Aco Financeira (GAFI) em 1989, no mbito da OCDE, esteja relacionado com o pilar preventivo da actividade contra o branqueamento de capitais. A criminalizao plena de todas as formas de branqueamento, as exigncias de identificao de clientes, o desenvolvimento de sistemas de controle interno e a comunicao obrigatria de transaco potencialmente suspeitas, constituem aspectos fundamentais desse pilar preventivo. Portugal foi um pas fundador do GAFI e desde 1993 que possumos um sistema de preveno do branqueamento de capitais que envolve todas as entidades do sector financeiro, que  monitorizado e acompanhado pelas entidades de superviso das instituies de crdito e das sociedades financeiras, do sector segurador e do mercado de capitais e, finalmente, que concretiza a indispensvel ligao das entidades financeiras s autoridades competentes para receber e analisar as comunicaes suspeitas de branqueamento de capitais. Desde 2004 que uma nova lei veio unificar o regime jurdico de preveno do branqueamento de capitais aplicvel a todos os sectores da economia. No mbito das nossas responsabilidades, diversas Instrues do Banco de Portugal regulamentam em maior detalhe os procedimentos que as Instituies de Crdito tm que cumprir, incluindo a elaborao de um relatrio anual sobre os sistemas internos destinados a prevenir o branqueamento de capitais. Estamos, assim, perante um enquadramento legal que se considera adaptado s exigncias nacionais e s normas e padres internacionais, quer do GAFI, do Banco de Pagamentos Internacionais ou da Unio Europeia. A legislao tem sido objecto de medidas de aperfeioamento constante encontra-se preparada para acompanhar os desafios impostos pelas novas tipologias e tendncias do branqueamento de capitais e, actualmente, tambm do financiamento do terrorismo. Como referi anteriormente, o sistema alia a uma vertente repressiva clssica de perseguio e punio da grave criminalidade em geral, uma vertente de natureza preventiva que desemboca na actividade das autoridades competentes para receber as comunicaes de operaes suspeitas que, no caso Portugus, so a Procuradoria-Geral da Repblica e a Unidade de Informao Financeira da Polcia Judiciria. Daqui decorre, desde logo, que a avaliao dos resultados da aplicao do sistema dever ser feita considerando em separado os resultados da vertente preventiva e da vertente repressiva, s assim se podendo fazer uma apreciao completa da efectividade do sistema. Tal significa, por exemplo, que essa efectividade no se poder medir apenas pelo nmero de condenaes pela prtica do crime de branqueamento e de financiamento do terrorismo, que  na realidade bastante baixo, mas deve ser apreciado pelos resultados que na vertente preventiva a regulamentao existente determina como meio de aprofundamento da integridade das instituies e do sistema financeiro. Nomeadamente as medidas destinadas a aprofundar o conhecimento dos clientes e a manter o registo das operaes executadas e a comunicar as potencialmente suspeitas, tende a afastar a mais grave criminalidade das instituies, para alm de facilitar qualquer investigao posterior de actividades criminosas. Esta aco preventiva requer a plena colaborao das instituies financeiras que compreendem, naturalmente, que isso  tambm do seu prprio interesse. Esse facto  reconhecido nos normativos anti-branqueamento, como se confirma, por exemplo, na 3 Directiva Comunitria sobre preveno do branqueamento de capitais, de 26 de Outubro de 2005, que no seu 2 considerando refere o seguinte:  A solidez, a integridade e a estabilidade das instituies de crdito e das instituies financeiras, bem como a confiana no sistema financeiro no seu conjunto, podem ser comprometidas pelos esforos dos criminosos e dos seus associados para dissimular a origem do produto das suas actividades. Creio que nunca se dever perder de vista que o supremo propsito de um regime de preveno do branqueamento de capitais consiste em evitar que os criminosos e os seus associados, muitas vezes de modo organizado, utilizem as entidades financeiras como instrumentos de dissimulao, transformao e converso de fundos de origem criminosa de uma forma que pode contribuir para contaminar as instituies e os seus empregados, a clientela e a actividade econmica em geral. Entendido deste modo, compreende-se que o regime preventivo do branqueamento tenha tambm como finalidade evitar riscos de natureza operacional, de reputao e de imagem das instituies e dos clientes, que possam, por exemplo, advir da utilizao fraudulenta das suas identidades. Procuram-se tambm prevenir os perigos para a sociedade e para a economia em geral, uma vez que ambas dependem do bom funcionamento de um sistema financeiro que tenha a mxima integridade, seja gerido profissionalmente e de acordo com rigorosos padres ticos. Deve ainda considerar-se que o reconhecimento da integridade de um sistema financeiro se apresenta como um activo estratgico, quer a nvel interno, quer internacional, nomeadamente se considerarmos o panorama altamente competitivo das economias no sistema global em que nos inserimos. Esse reconhecimento dos benefcios dos sistemas de preveno do branqueamento conduz as instituies a considerar os sistemas de preveno do branqueamento, apesar dos custos financeiros que implicam, como instrumentos de que podem resultar benefcios tangveis ao proteg-las contra graves actuaes criminosas. Na verdade, sistemas preventivos adequadamente desenhados, impulsionados pela interveno normativa das entidades de superviso em colaborao com as entidades supervisionadas, para alm de constiturem uma proteco das instituies contra a criminalidade de natureza financeira associada ao branqueamento de capitais, tambm as defendem de um criminalidade financeira mais corrente, como a falsificao ou o roubo da identidade dos clientes, ou o uso de identidade falsa nas transaces  distncia ou ainda a actuao de empregados desonestos em conluio com criminosos que procurem abusar das instituies. Uma outra caracterstica fundamental de um sistema de preveno do branqueamento consiste na confiana e no entendimento que se deve estabelecer e manter entre todas as autoridades que nele colaboram, as quais devem conhecer perfeitamente as atribuies e os propsitos de cada uma e ter presente que s actuando conjugadamente podem construir e fazer funcionar um sistema preventivo capaz de produzir resultados efectivos. Deve reconhecer-se que as instituies financeiras tm uma funo importante no sistema uma vez que so os pontos de entrada no circuito financeiro e que lhes compete tambm o esforo de conhecer bem os seus clientes e, em consequncia, so os primeiros agentes a poder aperceber-se de quem pretende abusar do sistema. Deste modo, para que o sistema possa funcionar com eficcia, torna-se necessrio que as instituies financeiras confiem na actividade das autoridades competentes e compreendam o encaminhamento e a sequncia que tm as suas comunicaes. Para manter a confiana entre todos os intervenientes do sistema  relevante que todos actuem com discrio e profissionalismo e que se atinjam os resultados para que, em ltima anlise, o sistema repressivo foi institudo. Nesta perspectiva, pode considerar-se que para reforar as possibilidades de adequados resultados finais o sistema ainda necessita de alguns aperfeioamentos para se tornar mais robusto e eficaz. Por outro lado, h que ter sempre presente que sendo o branqueamento de capitais um fenmeno de natureza claramente internacional, dada a total liberdade de circulao de capitais e a generalizao das novas tecnologias de informao, a continuada internacionalizao do nosso sector financeiro faz surgir novos desafios que requerem a actuao permanente de todos os envolvidos e a ateno vigilante das entidades financeiras. Convir a este propsito salientar que as normas internacionais, designadamente as do GAFI, determinam que as instituies devam aplicar as normas preventivas mais exigentes tambm s suas filiais e sucursais no estrangeiro, nomeadamente situadas fora das Comunidades Europeias e em caso de no o conseguirem concretizar tm a obrigao de informar disso as autoridades de superviso do Pas da respectiva sede. Para alm de ser um sistema maduro, o sistema Portugus foi j testado por trs rondas de avaliaes internacionais, a ltima das quais realizada no ano de 2006, por uma equipa de avaliao constituda por peritos do GAFI que avaliaram no apenas o enquadramento legal e regulamentar que constitui o sistema, mas tambm o modo de funcionamento de todas as suas componentes. Nessa ltima avaliao internacional foram visitadas, s no sector financeiro, 33 autoridades, instituies e empresas privadas, tendo sido analisado, com rigor e detalhe, o nvel de aplicao das normas e regulamentos em vigor, bem como os procedimentos utilizados na prtica para os divulgar e fazer observar e ainda apreciadas as relaes entre as instituies e as autoridades de superviso do sector financeiro. O exame incluiu tambm, naturalmente, o cumprimento do dever de comunicao de operaes suspeitas pelas entidades supervisionadas. Para alm do Banco de Portugal, que coordenou os trabalhos, participaram desde o primeiro momento na preparao da posio portuguesa, a Procuradoria Geral da Repblica, a Comisso do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios, o Instituto de Seguros de Portugal, a Direco-Geral das Alfndegas e Impostos Especiais sobre o Consumo e a Unidade de Informao Financeira da Polcia Judiciria. Foram ainda chamados a colaborar activamente na preparao da avaliao, o Supremo Tribunal de Justia, a Agencia Superior das Actividades Econmicas, a Direco Geral dos Registos e Notariado, o Gabinete de Poltica Legislativa do Ministrio da Justia, a Inspeco Geral de Jogos e as seguintes entidades privadas, Ordem dos Advogadas, Cmara dos Solicitadores, Cmara dos Revisores Oficiais de Contas e Cmara dos Tcnicos Oficiais de Contas. Como concluso da avaliao, o Plenrio do GAFI considerou no seu Relatrio, aprovado em Outubro de 2006 e que se encontra publicado, que o sistema Portugus de preveno do branqueamento de capitais , em geral, completo e slido em todos os sectores. No que respeita em particular ao sector financeiro, conclui que a estrutura da superviso existente, que integra as trs autoridades de superviso e ainda o Conselho Nacional de Supervisores Financeiros,  slida e possui a independncia necessria bem como os recursos indispensveis  prossecuo das suas misses nesta rea. Nenhuma crtica de fundo  formulada no Relatrio do GAFI quanto  qualidade e ao nvel da superviso a que esto sujeitas as entidades integradas nos sectores bancrio, segurador e do mercado de capitais, relativamente  preveno do branqueamento de capitais. Considera igualmente o Relatrio do GAFI que as medidas preventivas a que obedecem as entidades financeiras no que respeita  preveno do branqueamento de capitais constituem um conjunto amplo e consistente de medidas de identificao dos clientes e de diligncia devida, designadamente em relao s operaes que podem apresentar maior risco, como acontece, por exemplo, com as operaes  distncia, e com as relaes com correspondentes bancrios. Concluiu ainda que as entidades financeiras aplicam, em geral, regimes de controlo interno sem deficincias significativas e que aos empregados  fornecida formao regular e actualizada nesta rea, sendo igualmente difundida informao sobre as novas tipologias e tendncias das prticas de branqueamento mais comuns. Por outro lado, considerou ainda que o sistema portugus possui um enquadramento legal completo e claro que permite fornecer a indispensvel cooperao internacional, fundamental nesta rea. No entanto, so apresentadas algumas crticas relacionadas com a efectividade do sistema, na medida em que se considera ainda baixo o nmero de operaes suspeitas de branqueamento comunicadas pela generalidade das entidades financeiras s autoridades competentes, embora se verifique um aumento gradual desses nmeros nos ltimos anos. Os resultados globais da avaliao internacional, que vieram a ser includos no Financial Sector Assessment Program do Fundo Monetrio Internacional, tambm divulgado em finais do ano passado, podem assim ser considerados como altamente positivos para Portugal, na medida em que dos 12 Sistemas avaliados pelo GAFI e relativos a pases desenvolvidos da OCDE, o sistema portugus foi, a seguir ao sistema Belga, aquele que na Europa apresentou um maior grau de conformidade com os padres internacionais, apresentando um maior grau de conformidade do que sistemas como o Espanhol, o Suo, o Italiano, o Irlands, o Noruegus, o Dinamarqus ou o Sueco. Em consequncia dessa apreciao, dos 13 Pases da OCDE j avaliados s a Blgica e Portugal no ficaram sujeitos pelo GAFI, a um processo de follow-up, tendente a monitorizar o aperfeioamento da aplicao de certas Recomendaes do GAFI, como as ns 1, 5, 10, 13, e Especiais II e IV. Recomendaes que no conjunto das 49 Recomendaes Gerais e Especiais, so consideradas traves mestras na construo de um sistema efectivo de preveno do branqueamento e de financiamento do terrorismo. Especialmente dever salientar-se que s a Blgica e Portugal foram considerados em largo cumprimento da Recomendao Geral n 5, essencial  preveno do branqueamento e do financiamento do terrorismo no sector financeiro e relativa ao regime de identificao, de verificao da identidade e de diligncia devida a aplicar  clientela. Convm frisar assim que, aps a anlise exaustiva e extremamente rigorosa, a que o sistema esteve submetido, quer a nvel interno quer externo, nos anos de 2005 e 2006, se deve considerar que embora necessite de aperfeioamentos destinados a contribuir para o aumento da sua efectividade no apresenta, nomeadamente na rea financeira, deficincias de natureza estrutural ou funcional que imponham a alterao dos seus componentes fundamentais e do modo como se relacionam entre si. Certas lacunas ainda existentes iro ser colmatadas com a aprovao de legislao de natureza comunitria, ainda em discusso, nos casos em que se considera apropriado dever existir um level playing field, a nvel Comunitrio, como acontece, por exemplo, com a regulamentao da identidade do ordenante nas transaces  distncia. Quanto a outras lacunas existentes, nomeadamente no que respeita  preveno do financiamento do terrorismo,  noo e regime das pessoas politicamente expostas, bem como  considerao mais detalhada da noo de risco derivado das operaes e do perfil dos clientes, para modular as medidas a instituir para prevenir o branqueamento e o financiamento do terrorismo, sero matrias a considerar no diploma de transposio da 3 Directiva de preveno do branqueamento e do financiamento do terrorismo no sector financeiro, que est em curso de preparao e dever estar publicado at ao final deste ano. Nesse diploma devero ser ainda consagrados outros aperfeioamentos e solues, de molde a actualizar o regime jurdico da preveno do branqueamento e do financiamento do terrorismo, colocando-o em plena consonncia com as Directivas Comunitrias nesta matria e com as Recomendaes Gerais e Especiais do GAFI, que como  sabido tm influenciado de modo determinante a legislao comunitria e vm consagrando as solues tecnicamente mais exigentes nesta matria. O diploma de transposio da 3 Directiva, que se encontra em preparao e as solues que nele se consagrarem sero posteriormente complementadas nos regulamentos das autoridades de superviso, no se prevendo, todavia, mudanas radicais de que, alis, o sistema no parece necessitar, como referi. No sector financeiro sero realizados aperfeioamentos, com o propsito de aumentar a eficcia do sistema, de o orientar ainda mais claramente para a modulao de solues consoante o risco oferecido pelos clientes e operaes, de acordo com os novos preceitos da 3 Directiva e de modo adaptado ao nosso sistema financeiro, que se apresenta como um sistema aberto, competitivo, dotado de solues flexveis mas que tem de continuar a proteger a sua integridade e a aplicao de elevados padres de natureza tica. Lisboa, 12 de Maro de 2007 Vtor Constncio

Title: Speech by the Governor, President of the Bureau of the 6th National Congress of Rail Transport - ADFER - Lisbon, 15-17 March 2005
text: Speech by Vitor Constancio, President of the Congressional Bureau, at the Opening Session Mr. President of Replica, Excellency Mr. President of the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation, Dr. Rui Vilar Sr. President of ADFER, Eng. Armenian Matias Sr. President of the Executive Committee of the Congress, Dr. Manuel Caetano My ladies and gentlemen I am honored to chair the Bureau of the 6th National Congress, an initiative of the Portuguese Association for the Development of Rail Transport that this year promotes the theme of Long-distance Passenger Transport, with reference to all modes of transport. I would like to express my appreciation to ADFER for another initiative that marks its commitment to the development of a modern and competitive model for the transport sector in Portugal. I thank you for your honorable presence, Mr President of Replica, in this opening ceremony which represents for all of us a clear sign of the importance it attaches to the transport sector as a decisive area for the ecological and social development of Portugal. I thank the President of the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation, Dr Rui Vilar, for the facilities granted to this Initiative of ADFER. Of course, I also want to thank the personalities who agreed to preside over the different technical sections  Dr. Manuela Ferreira Leite, Dr. Jorge Coelho, Dr. Elisa Ferreira and Eng. Ferreira do Amaral, as well as the players of these sesss - Prof. Paulino Pereira, Eng. Carlos Vicente, Dr. Ferreira de Lemos and Dr. Lidia Sequeira. I also thank Eng. Armenian Matias  President of ADFER, for the dedication and commitment that he has in holding this Congress and the respective Executive Committee, in the figures of its President, Dr. Manuel Caetano and its Secretary General, Eng. Campos Costa, as well as to all its collaborators. I would also like to express a word of appreciation to the prestigious guest speakers who greatly honour us and to the many congressmen who have presented theses and communications, because it is without dida, at the high level of communication and speech that the success of The Congress should be achieved. Finally, I thank the media for bringing to the opinion of information, ideas and proposals that interest everyone and especially the many users of the main modes of transport. This 6th National Congress takes place at a time of some expectation about the future of the national transport system and this gives added relevance to the debate between experts and leaders of the sector to which we will attend. The importance of the sector to the national economy is adequately reflected in the richness and diversity of the issues that will be addressed. from technological developments to the problems of charging, competition and regulation; from the European dimension to the definition of an integrated policy for the passenger transport sector as a whole, all these problems will be examined during the Congress. They impose enormous social demands on the passenger transport sector given the role it plays and the effects it has on eco-development and urban planning. In turn, passengers seeking transportation for work or leisure reasons require an effective and affordable service. For all these reasons, the passenger transport sector is considered at European level with a service of general eco-interest. Since the Treaty of Amsterdam, the fundamental text of the European Union, in Article 16, has enshrined such services as fundamental components of the values which the Union shares and as instruments of social and territorial cohesion. In the draft Constitutional Treaty, now in the process of ratification, Articles 96 and 122 repeat the wording of the current texts and establish, for the first time, the need for the adoption of a European Law on the subject. As stated in the White Paper published last year by the Commission 'services of general interest' have been 'at the heart of the debate on the European model of society'. Services of general ecological interest mean those who are subject to special obligations by the State given the importance of the collective interest. This concept therefore applies in particular to services provided by networked sectors such as transport, postal services, energy and communications. The White Paper lists a wide range of guidelines to be followed by services of general eco-interest which, in addition to acting in compliance with the provisions of the Treaties on competition law, must ensure principles of universal access, continuity, quality of service, affordable prices, protection and safety of users. In this context, the passenger transport sector has to respond to significant efficiency and equity requirements. Transport is sometimes referred to as a 'good of merit' because it is considered that access to a minimum of that service is part of the basic goods that make up the standard of living. This gives rise to a requirement of fairness in order to ensure equal terms in access to that minimum service. On the other hand, the consideration of the econic efficiency criterion implies that the provision of the service satisfies the demand for transport until it equalizes the social benefits of the activity with its social costs. This ideal criterion is impossible to apply, given the empirical difficulty of measuring benefits and costs for society as a whole. In both perspectives, benefits and costs, there are ineras externalities or effects of the service that are not traded in a market and therefore do not have an assigned price, but that are not difficult to measure are no less real. For example, the general benefits on the eco-development of a good transport system and its effect on the cohesion of the territory and the planning and balance of the country's urban network are benefits that the policies cannot ignore. On the other hand, in terms of costs, it is necessary to add to private costs those resulting from the effects of congestion, the risk of accidents and pollution. The existence of all these externalities, the indivisibility of large investments in infrastructure that creates conditions of almost natural monopio in some segments, as well as the importance of asymmetric information between operators and users, are factors that make it obliging the intervention of the powers plicos in the sector for reasons of mere econic efficiency. In fact, the existence of benefits and costs that are not assessed on the market mean that this is not sufficient to ensure total environmental efficiency. This is because of the need for State intervention, which should seek to avoid or overcome market failures and to ensure the interest of the market, including the concerns of equity that I have already mentioned. Such intervention normally takes the forms of direct service provision, regulation of the sector and the use of taxes and subsidies to internalise costs and benefits that the market does not consider. The evolution of the previous decades towards deregulation and privatisation has led to a reduction in direct provision by the State. It has been sought to separate, with variable success, the management of the basic network of infrastructures, predominantly delivered to a plica entity, and the operation of services assigned to private companies under competition and with the right of access and proper charging. In general, the regulatory function has been greatly evolving despite the specific difficulties it faces. With regard, for example, to the costs of road transport pollution which many estimates put between 20 and 30% of private costs, it is very difficult to regulate or fully internalise these effects in order to make those that actually cause them pay. Furthermore, the commitments arising from the Kyoto Agreement will require us to make an additional effort to comply with CO2 emission limits with the possible need to buy quotas that will increase the costs to be covered in the sector. As for the costs of congestion in motorized transport, to solve the problem properly, it would be necessary to know the marginal cost associated with different types of vehicles at different times.
