Existing taxes are generally referred to vehicle ownership and not to their actual use so they do not fulfil the function of internalising congestion costs. More modern solutions using electric ticketing and hourly or geographical modulation or the introduction of entrance fees to congested urban areas are possibilities that have been tried and should be considered. As can be seen from these brief examples, the problems of regulating the sector are complex, which Congress will certainly not fail to delve into. One conclusion that I have been able to draw from the analysis of what is happening in the sector is that a reform of the institutional organisation of regulation is justified, which seems to me to be insufficiently independent and too fragmented and cannot adequately address the problems of the intermodal dimension which is now so essential to the good performance of the transport service. I have also seen that there are now some consensus on the policies and guidelines that should preside over the creation of an efficient transport system that serves the most quality and safety. The first among them concerns precisely the need to achieve a better balance between modes of transport, especially by driving the railway sector, which implies High Speed, and generally developing intermodal operations. In the road sector, congestion and pollution costs need to be more internalised in addition to making the system more environmentally friendly. It is also necessary to ensure the ecological sustainability of the capital-summed sector and the modernisation of an aged fleet. This must be achieved first and foremost through normal levels of profitability of companies competing in the sector through realistic pricing. Social prices which have to be charged for justified reasons of fairness should give rise to compensation compensation correctly calculated. We cannot generalise and universalize the user-pays principle because it would imply admitting that there is no place for State intervention as an expression of solidarity between citizens on which good society is based. On another level, I must also stress the need for a firm policy to ensure competition in the sector to avoid dominance by some operators. In turn, urban and suburban transport policy should better stimulate the use of collective transport and promote the rational use of individual automel, as it is well known and permanently desired. This point is particularly sensitive in large metropolitan areas, and it is necessary to give effective powers to the Metropolitan Transport Authorities of Lisbon and Porto. Finally, from an international perspective, it is essential to ensure efficient connection to European networks with all interoperability standards. All these guidelines require a policy of structuring investments that currently pose sensitive financing problems. In fact, the budgetary crisis we have been going through is well known. If we exclude the necessarily temporary use of extraordinary measures, the deficit has been above 5% of GDP and if nothing were done there would be a risk of being even higher this year. The definition of a fiscal policy strategy for the prime years can be defined more precisely if the final terms of the revision of the Stability and Growth Pact, which is on the eve of being relaxed in some of its aspects, are known. However, as I said recently, the start of the inevitably gradual correction of our budgetary position 'will mean, even during the course of this year, the taking of new effective measures to increase revenue and contain expenditure'. Among the environmental and social reasons that point to this need, I mentioned the following: "The increasing weight of transfers relating to pension penss and the prospect of further population ageing in the future, oblige to build a budgetary situation that allows us to contemplate without fear the preservation of the essentials of our social security system. There will therefore be no healthy eco-growth without the financial stability provided by a smaller budget deficit and a restraint of the Ratio of Plica Debt to GDP." In this context, it is to be expected, for example, that taxes on vehicles and fuels will have to operate, in the present circumstances, as an alternative to tolls, as the road sector should pay a large part of the infrastructure it uses. The analysis has to be done as if the sector benefited from a kind of revenue consignment that contributes powerfully to ensuring its ecological balance. On the other hand, we know how the Structural Funds we receive from the European Union are gradually being reduced in the two years of the current Community Support Framework, an evolution that should continue in the first Framework for 2007-2013. Furthermore, we cannot ignore the competitiveness problems of our economy imply that we must concentrate resources on the internationally traded goods sectors, as well as on technological innovation projects. We must therefore be prepared that it is probably not possible, on the basis of investment only, to carry out at the same time all the major projects that have been talked about in the sector: completion of the Road Plan, launch of high-speed railway lines and a new international airport. Priorities should be established and private participation in infrastructure financing should be achieved. These partnerships will have to be surrounded by essential care to avoid future problems. In fact, so-called public/private partnerships must meet some fundamental criteria: -Participating private undertakings should be at genuine commercial risk, associated in particular with cost management, and thus not guaranteed a certain profitability. -The accounting of multiannual charges assumed by the State should be transparent and publicly known from the outset of projects -There should be overall limits on the amounts that the State may commit for the future as a percentage of total investment expenditure in order to preserve margin of freedom to future investment policy. With these conditions, it is therefore necessary to rely on the private capital tender for the sector although, in this perspective, the conclusions of a recent document of the European Conference of Transport Ministers of the OECD 1 countries are not encouraging, where it is possible to read the following: "The volume of private capital that has been possible to attract to transport infrastructure has remained relatively small in relation to the investment made in this type of equipment. In addition, contractual relations between governments and private infrastructure service providers have been less than stable. As a whole, deregulation and privatisation seem to have had limited success in reducing the need to allocate funds to finance transport infrastructure." What all this implies is that it will not be appropriate to start a wide range of major projects without ensuring the full level of their full funding. In any case, we cannot also ignore, as I have often said, that our main ecological problem is the need to increase our growth potential. From this perspective, I believe that the recovery of the economy requires the contribution of an intelligent investment programme in which there is a need to include the transport sector as an important part of our future economic growth. The country will have to make delicate choices in this area so structuring our future. I am sure that the work of the Congress that begins today will make a significant contribution to clarifying the technical perspectives to be considered in the decision-making process that leads to the efficient and modern transport system that the country needs. I therefore wish you all a good Congress. Lisbon, 15 March 2005 Victor Constantius 1 European Conference of Ministers of Transport (2004) The limits of (de-)regulation of transport infrastructure services , CEMT/CS(2004)32, September 2004
text_original: Discurso de Vtor Constncio, Presidente da Mesa do Congresso, na Sesso de Abertura Senhor Presidente da Replica, Excelncia Senhor Presidente da Fundao Calouste Gulbenkian, Dr. Rui Vilar Sr. Presidente da ADFER, Eng. Armnio Matias Sr. Presidente da Comisso Executiva do Congresso, Dr. Manuel Caetano Minhas senhoras e Meus senhores Cumpre-me a honra de presidir  Mesa do 6 Congresso Nacional, uma iniciativa da Associao Portuguesa para o Desenvolvimento do Transporte Ferrovirio que este ano promove a temtica do Transporte Interurbano de Passageiros, com referncia a todos os modos de transporte. Desejo manifestar o meu apreo  ADFER por mais uma iniciativa que marca o seu empenho no sentido do desenvolvimento de um modelo moderno e competitivo para o sector dos transportes em Portugal. Agradeo a honrosa presena de Vossa Excelncia, Senhor Presidente da Replica, nesta cerimia de abertura que representa para todos n um sinal claro da importncia que atribui ao sector dos transportes como rea decisiva para o desenvolvimento econico e social de Portugal. Agradeo ao Senhor Presidente da Fundao Calouste Gulbenkian, Dr. Rui Vilar, as facilidades concedidas a mais esta iniciativa da ADFER. Evidentemente, quero tambm agradecer s personalidades que aceitaram presidir as diferentes sesss tcnicas  Dr. Manuela Ferreira Leite, Dr. Jorge Coelho, Dr. Elisa Ferreira e Eng. Ferreira do Amaral, bem como aos dinamizadores dessas sesss - Prof. Paulino Pereira, Eng. Carlos Vicente, Dr. Ferreira de Lemos e Dra. Ldia Sequeira. Agradeo tambm ao Eng. Armnio Matias  Presidente da ADFER, pela dedicao e empenho que p na realizao deste Congresso e  respectiva Comisso Executiva, nas figuras do seu Presidente, Dr. Manuel Caetano e do seu Secretrio-Geral, Eng. Campos Costa, bem como a todos os seus colaboradores. Quero tambm expressar uma palavra de apreo aos prestigiados oradores convidados que muito nos honram e aos muitos congressistas que apresentaram teses e comunicas, pois  sem dida, ao elevado nvel das comunicas e intervens que se dever o xito do Congresso. Finalmente, agradeo a presena da Comunicao Social por levar  opinio plica informao, ideias e propostas que interessam a todos e em especial aos muitos utilizadores dos principais modos de transporte. Este 6 Congresso Nacional realiza-se num momento de alguma expectativa sobre o futuro do sistema nacional de transportes e isso confere relevncia acrescida ao debate entre especialistas e responsveis do sector a que vamos assistir. A importncia do sector para a economia nacional encontra-se adequadamente reflectida na riqueza e diversidade dos temas que sero abordados. Da evoluo tecnolica aos problemas da tarifao, da concorrncia e da regulao; da dimenso europeia  definio de uma poltica integrada para o conjunto do sector dos transportes de passageiros, todos estes problemas sero analisados no decurso do Congresso. Impendem sobre o sector dos transportes de passageiros enormes exigncias sociais dada a funo que desempenha e os efeitos que provoca no desenvolvimento econico e na ordenamento urbano. Por seu turno, os passageiros que procuram transporte por razs de trabalho ou de lazer requerem um servio eficaz e acessvel. Por todas estas razs, o sector dos transportes de passageiros  considerado no plano europeu com um servio de interesse econico geral. Desde o Tratado de Amsterdo que o texto fundamental da Unio Europeia, no seu Artigo 16, consagra esse tipo de servios como componentes fundamentais dos valores que a Unio partilha e como instrumentos da coeso social e territorial. No projecto de Tratado Constitucional, agora em processo de ratificao, os Artigos 96 e 122 repetem a formulao dos textos actuais e estabelecem, pela primeira vez, a necessidade de aprovao de uma Lei Europeia sobre a matria. Como se afirma no Livro Branco publicado o ano passado pela Comisso os servios de interesse geral tm estado no centro do debate sobre o modelo europeu de sociedade. Por servios de interesse econico geral entendem-se os que so sujeitos a obrigas especiais pelo Estado dada a importncia de que se revestem para a realizao do interesse colectivo. Este conceito aplica-se, pois, em particular a servios assegurados por sectores em rede como os transportes, os servios postais, a energia e as comunicas. O Livro Branco enumera um conjunto vasto de orientas a que devem obedecer os servios de interesse econico geral que, para alm de deverem actuar no respeito das disposis dos Tratados sobre direito da concorrncia, devem garantir princpios de acesso universal, continuidade, qualidade do servio, preos acessveis, proteco e segurana dos utentes. Neste enquadramento, o sector dos transportes de passageiros tem que responder a significativas exigncias de eficincia e equidade. O transporte  por vezes designado como um bem de mrito em virtude de se considerar que o acesso a um mnimo desse servio faz parte dos bens bsicos que integram o nvel de vida. Isto d origem a um requisito de equidade no sentido de assegurar condis de igualdade no acesso a esse servio mnimo. Por outro lado, a considerao do critrio de eficincia econica implica que a proviso do servio satisfaa a procura de transportes at igualar os benefcios sociais da actividade aos respectivos custos sociais. Este critrio ideal  de impossvel aplicao prtica dada a dificuldade emprica de medir benefcios e custos para o conjunto da sociedade. Em ambas as perspectivas, de benefcios e custos, existem ineras externalidades ou efeitos do servio que no so transaccionados num mercado e por isso no tm um preo atribudo, mas que nem por serem difceis de medir deixam de ser menos reais. Por exemplo, os benefcios gerais sobre o desenvolvimento econico de um bom sistema de transportes e o seu efeito sobre a coeso do territio e a ordenamento e equilbrio da rede urbana do pas, constituem benefcios que as polticas plicas no podem ignorar. Por outro lado, em termos dos custos, h que adicionar aos custos privados os que resultam dos efeitos de congestionamento, de riscos de acidentes e de poluio. A existncia de todas estas externalidades, a indivisibilidade dos grandes investimentos em infra-estruturas que cria condis de quase monopio natural nalguns segmentos, bem como a importncia da informao assimtrica entre operadores e utentes, constituem factores que tornam obrigatia a interveno dos poderes plicos no sector por razs de mera eficincia econica. Na verdade, a existncia de benefcios e custos que no so avaliados no mercado fazem com que este no seja suficiente para garantir a total eficincia econica. Daqui nasce a necessidade da interveno do Estado que deve procurar evitar ou ultrapassar as falhas do mercado e assegurar o interesse plico, incluindo as preocupas de equidade que j referi. Essa interveno assume normalmente as formas da oferta directa do servio, da regulao do sector e da utilizao de impostos e subsdios para internalizar custos e benefcios que o mercado no considera. A evoluo das timas dcadas no sentido da desregulamentao e privatizao tem conduzido no sector dos transportes a uma reduo da proviso directa por parte do Estado. Tem-se procurado separar, com sucesso varivel, a gesto da rede bsica de infra-estruturas, predominantemente entregue a uma entidade plica, e a operao dos servios atribuda a empresas privadas em regime de concorrncia e com direito de acesso e tarifao adequada. Em geral, a funo de regulao tem conhecido uma grande evoluo apesar das dificuldades especificas que defronta. No que se refere, por exemplo, aos custos de poluio dos transportes rodovirios que muitas estimativas colocam entre 20 a 30% dos custos privados, torna-se muito difcil regulamentar ou internalizar cabalmente esses efeitos por forma a fazer pagar os que efectivamente so os seus causadores. Acresce que os compromissos decorrentes do Acordo de Quioto nos iro obrigar a um esforo suplementar para respeitar os limites de emisso de CO2 com eventual necessidade de comprar quotas que agravaro os custos a cobrir no sector. Quanto aos custos de congestionamento no transporte motorizado, para resolver o problema adequadamente, seria necessrio conhecer o custo marginal associado a diferentes tipos de veculos em diferentes momentos. Os impostos existentes so em geral referenciados  propriedade de veculos e no ao seu uso efectivo pelo que no cumprem a funo de internalizar os custos de congestionamento. Solus mais modernas com recurso  bilhtica electrica e  modulao horria ou geogrfica ou ainda a introduo de taxas  entrada de zonas urbanas congestionadas, constituem possibilidades que tm vindo a ser experimentadas e que devem ser consideradas. Como se v por estes breves exemplos, so complexos os problemas da regulao do sector que o Congresso no deixar seguramente de aprofundar. Uma concluso que pude tirar da anlise do que se passa no sector  a de que se justifica uma reforma da organizao institucional da Regulao que me parece ser insuficientemente independente e estar demasiado fragmentada no podendo atender adequadamente aos problemas da dimenso intermodal que  hoje to essencial ao bom desempenho do servio de transportes. Verifiquei tambm que existem hoje alguns consensos quanto s polticas e orientas que devem presidir  criao de um sistema de transportes eficiente que sirva o plico com mais qualidade e segurana. O primeiro dentre eles diz precisamente respeito  necessidade de se alcanar um maior equilbrio entre modos de transporte, dinamizando nomeadamente o sector ferrovirio, o que implica a Alta Velocidade, e desenvolvendo em geral as operas intermodais. No sector rodovirio, h que procurar internalizar mais cabalmente os custos de congestionamento e de poluio para tornar o sistema mais amigo do ambiente. Torna-se tambm necessrio assegurar a sustentabilidade econica do sector, carecido de capitais e da modernizao de uma frota envelhecida. Isso deve ser conseguido em primeira linha atravs de nveis normais de rentabilidade das empresas que concorrem no sector atravs de uma tarifao realista. Os preos sociais que tenham que ser praticados por justificadas razs de equidade devero dar lugar a indemnizas compensatias correctamente calculadas. No podemos generalizar e universalizar o princpio do utilizador-pagador porque isso implicaria admitir que no existe lugar para a interveno do Estado como expresso da solidariedade entre cidados em que assenta a boa sociedade. Noutro plano, devo tambm sublinhar a necessidade de uma poltica firme para assegurar a concorrncia no sector para evitar situas domnio por parte de alguns operadores. Por seu turno, a poltica de transportes urbanos e suburbanos dever estimular melhor o uso dos transportes colectivos e promover o uso racional do automel individual, como  bem conhecido e permanentemente desejado. Este ponto  particularmente sensvel nas grandes reas metropolitanas, sendo necessrio atribuir poderes efectivos s Autoridades Metropolitanas de Transportes de Lisboa e Porto. Finalmente, na perspectiva internacional,  essencial garantir a ligao eficiente s redes europeias com todas as condis de interoperabilidade. Todas estas orientas requerem uma poltica de investimentos estruturantes que colocam neste momento problemas sensveis de financiamento. Na verdade,  conhecida a situao de crise oramental que temos vindo a atravessar. Se excluirmos o recurso, necessariamente temporrio, a medidas extraordinrias o dfice tem-se situado acima de 5% do PIB e se nada fosse feito existiria o risco de ser ainda mais elevado este ano. A definio de uma estratgia da poltica oramental para os primos anos spoder ser definida com maior preciso ap serem conhecidos os termos finais da reviso do Pacto de Estabilidade e Crescimento que est em vsperas de ser flexibilizado nalguns dos seus aspectos. No entanto, como afirmei recentemente, o incio da correco inevitavelmente gradual da nossa situao oramental implicar, ainda no decurso deste ano, a tomada de novas medidas efectivas de aumento de receitas e conteno de despesas. Entre as razs de ordem econica e social que apontam para essa necessidade, referi ento as seguintes: O peso crescente das transferncias relativas a penss de reforma e a perspectiva de maior envelhecimento populacional no futuro, obrigam a construir uma situao oramental sida que permita contemplar sem receios a preservao do essencial do nosso sistema de segurana social. No haver, pois, crescimento econico saudvel sem a estabilidade financeira proporcionada por um menor dfice oramental e uma conteno do rcio da Dvida Plica em relao ao PIB. Neste contexto,  de esperar, por exemplo, que os impostos sobre veculos e combustveis tenham que funcionar, nas presentes circunstncias, como alternativa a portagens, uma vez que o sector rodovirio dever pagar grande parte das infraestruturas que utiliza. A anlise tem que ser feita como se o sector beneficiasse de uma espcie de consignao de receitas que contribuam poderosamente para assegurar o seu equilbrio econico. Por outro lado, sabemos como os fundos estruturais que recebemos da Unio Europeia se encontram em fase de reduo gradual nos dois timos anos do actual Quadro Comunitrio de Apoio, evoluo que dever ter continuidade no primo Quadro para 2007-2013. Alm disso, no podemos ignorar que os problemas de competitividade da nossa economia implicam que devemos concentrar recursos nos sectores de bens transaccionveis internacionalmente, bem como nos projectos de inovao tecnolica. Temos, pois, que estar preparados para que provavelmente no seja possvel, com base apenas em investimento plico, realizar em simultneo todos os grandes projectos de que se tem falado para o sector: concluso do Plano Rodovirio, lanamento das linhas ferrovirias de alta velocidade e um novo aeroporto internacional. Haver que estabelecer prioridades e conseguir comparticipao privada para o financiamento das infra-estruturas. Estas parcerias tero que ser rodeadas de cuidados indispensveis para evitar problemas futuros. Com efeito, as denominadas parcerias publico/privado devem obedecer a alguns critrios fundamentais: -As empresas privadas participantes devem correr um genuno risco comercial, associado nomeadamente  gesto dos custos, no tendo assim garantida uma determinada rentabilidade. -A contabilidade dos encargos plurianuais assumidos pelo Estado deve ser transparente e conhecida publicamente desde o incio dos projectos -Devem existir limites globais aos montantes que o Estado pode comprometer para o futuro em percentagem das despesas totais de investimento, por forma preservar margem de liberdade  poltica de investimento futura. Com estas condies , pois, necessrio contar com o concurso de capitais privados para o sector embora, nesta perspectiva, no sejam encorajadoras as concluss de um recente documento da Conferncia Europeia dos Ministros de Transportes dos pases da OCDE 1, onde  possvel ler o seguinte:  O volume de capital privado que tem sido possvel atrair para infra-estruturas de transporte tem permanecido relativamente reduzido em relao ao investimento realizado nesse tipo de equipamentos. Alm disso, as relas contratuais entre Governos e os fornecedores privados de servios de infra-estruturas tm sido menos do que estveis. No seu conjunto, a desregulamentao e a privatizao parecem ter tido sucesso limitado na reduo da necessidade de afectar fundos plicos para financiar as infra-estruturas de transportes. O que tudo isto implica  que no ser apropriado iniciar um vasto conjunto de grandes projectos sem nos assegurarmos com rigor da viabilidade do seu integral financiamento. De qualquer forma, no podemos tambm ignorar, como tenho afirmado muitas vezes, que o nosso principal problema econico  a necessidade de aumentarmos o nosso potencial de crescimento. Nesta perspectiva, considero que a recuperao da economia requer o contributo de um programa inteligente de investimento plico em que h necessidade de incluir o sector de transportes como pea importante de que depende o nosso crescimento econico futuro. O pas ter que fazer escolhas delicadas neste domnio to estruturante do nosso futuro. Estou certo que os trabalhos do Congresso que hoje se inicia daro um significativo contributo para o esclarecimento das perspectivas tcnicas a considerar no processo de deciso que conduza ao sistema de transportes eficiente e moderno de que o pas precisa. Desejo, pois, a todos um bom Congresso. Title: State funding: what rules and what regulatory instruments? - Intervention of the Governor of Banco de Portugal Carlos da Silva Costa at the Commemorative Colloquium of the 35th Anniversary of the Constitution
text: State funding: what rules and what regulatory instruments? Intervention of the Governor of Banco de Portugal Carlos da Silva Costa at the Coluio Comemorativo dos 35 Anos da Constituicao Lisbon, 27 April 2011 "THE FAULT [FOR FISCAL IRRESPONSIBILITY] LIES NOT IN OURSELVES, AS PARTICIPANTS IN THE ORDINARY POLITICS OF MODERN MAJORITARIAN DEMOCRACY, BUT IN THE STRUCTURAL RULES WITH WHICH THIS POLITICS TAKES PLACE. (...) THAT WHICH MAKES THE EXISTING RULES GENERATE PATTERNS OF OUTCOMES THAT WE DEEM TO BE IRRESPONSIBLE IS THE POLITICAL AGENTS' AUTHORITY TO SPEND WITHOUT TAXING. LITTLE OR NO SOPHISTICATION IS REQUIRED TO RECOGNIZE HOW DIFFERENT THE DYNAMICS OF FISCAL CHOICE WOULD BE IN A CONSTITUTIONAL SETTING THAT FORCED POLITICIANS TO LEVY TAXES TO COVER OUTLAYS." (James Buchanan, "The balanced-budget amendment: Clarifying the arguments", Public Choice 90: 117-138, 1997) Introduction I would like to begin by thanking the invitation addressed to me to participate in this coluio commemorating the anniversary of the Constitution of the Portuguese Replica. The budgetary crisis that we are experiencing and which, to a greater or lesser extent, also affects other advanced economies, does not elaborate on the relevance and timeliness of the theme chosen for this session. The Current Budget Crisis Following the global crisis, phasing debt levels in advanced economies have increased significantly, reaching, in many cases, unprecedented values in peacetime. This trend was a consequence, on the one hand, of the stimulus measures adopted by governments to mitigate the effects of the financial crisis on environmental activity and, on the other hand, the state's large-scale taking on the responsibilities of the banking system motivated by financial stability concerns. As a result, plica debt already exceeds 200% of GDP in Japan, is expected to reach 100% of GDP in the United States this year and exceed80% of GDP in the euro area. The medium and long-term effects on plica expenditure resulting from ageing and population decline further aggravate this scenario. IMF estimates indicate that, in the absence of corrective measures, the debt ratio in the main advanced economies will increase by around 60 p.p. by 2030, the same value as projected by the European Commission for all euro area countries[1]. The global crisis has gone through several phases. It began in August 2007 as a financial crisis. In the second quarter of 2008, it became widespread and transformed into the Great Recession - the biggest drop in global econic activity since the Great Depression. And finally, since autumn 2009, it has manifested itself as a sovereign debt crisis in advanced economies, with a particular focus on the euro area. This is the stage we still find ourselves in. The so-called "budget space" - the difference between the levels of indebtedness reached and the "limit" or "critical point" from which the dynamics of a country's plica debt is considered unsustainable - has drastically reduced and is exhausted for several countries. The sovereign debt crisis in the euro area and the unfavourable evolution of credit risk in other parts of the globe are the visible face of this situation. In Portugal, the developments of the last few weeks showed, without scope for didas, that there is no budgetary space. The inability to refinance debt in financial markets has forced the Portuguese to use the existing European financial assistance mechanism. This assistance is conditional on an adjustment programme agreed with the International Monetary Fund and the European Commission in a process involving the European Central Bank. Portuguese p.A. debt has almost doubled in the last decade, currently surpassing 90% of GDP and maintaining an upward trajectory. The deterioration of the plicas accounts [1] SUSTAINABILITY REPORT 2009. reflects the persistence, in the last fifteen years, of disproportionate expenditure increases in relation to the growth dynamics of the Portuguese economy. In view of this unsustainable situation, there is no alternative but to implement a comprehensive fiscal consolidation programme, which promotes a rapid improvement of the budgetary balance, the short-term stabilisation of the debt ratio and the sustainability of the accounts in the medium and long term. It is important to remind those who may have alternatives that move away from immediate fiscal consolidation strategies, that Portugal has repeatedly violated the European Union's budgetary rules since joining the euro. In twelve years of participation in the euro area, the budget deficit was on average 4.5% of GDP. In just three years, in the initial period of euro support, the budget deficit was slightly less than 3% of GDP. Portugal is now, and for the third time since the adoption of the euro, subject to the excessive budget deficit procedure. In these past twelve years, persistent spending growth has always been made to the shiver of a rule of prudence that would ensure a prima fiscal position of balance or surplus (as required by the Stability and Growth Pact). The objective of achieving a balance-sounding budget balance has been systematically reiterated in the updates of the different stability programmes, but always postponed to the end of the horizon of the next programme update. The expansionist policy pursued in the context of the international crisis, in a starting situation where the margin of manoeuvre was already very limited, aggravated the vulnerability of the budgetary situation. Subsequent developments in terms of the sector's access to debt markets show that the risks associated with the need for debt refinancing have been largely underestimated. This disruption of state financing conditions is having profound repercussions on the financing of banks and, in this way, of Portuguese households and companies. We are entering a second period of econic contraction that is anticipated as prolonged and profound. The levels of debt achieved, and their inevitable growth to levels above 100% of GDP, represent a huge burden for future generations, who will have to affect an important part of the wealth they produce at the service of debt. The situation is aggravated by the fact that the level of indebtedness reached constitutes an obstacle to growth. A study by Carmen Reinhart and Keneth Rogoff, covering 200 years of histia and 44 countries with very different econic regimes and development levels, concludes that for debt ratios above 90%, GDP growth tends to [2] significantly lower. The evolution of the plicas accounts that I have been describing reveals the failure of the financial regime of our Plica Administration. This suggests institutional explanations. It is therefore not surprising that it is widely documented that Portugal compared unfavourably with most euro area countries (and the developed world) on budgetary rules and procedures aimed at ensuring budgetary discipline. This observation refers us to the citation of the Nobel Prize in Economics (in 1986), James Buchanan, who serves as the epigraph for this communication. Buchanan, responsible for reclaiming the tradition of econic constitutionalism associated, for example, with Swedish economist Knut Wicksell, teaches that budgetary decisions are the result of a complex network of interactions between individuals who act rationally on the basis of their individual interests and the rules to which they are subject. This interactive process, often very decentralised, tends, by its intrinsic nature, to generate excess expenditure, persistent deficits and too high debt. There are several factors that contribute to this situation, and that Buchanan masterfully sums up in the idea of "faculty to spend without tax"i. By being able to spend without tax, governments can considerably restrict the room for manoeuvre of future governments and impose intolerable costs on future generations. In this sense, the preservation of democracy and the principle of the rule of law justify the imposition of limits on the budget balance and the debt. It is therefore important to understand to what extent a profound reform of the Portuguese budgetary architecture could contribute to a lasting consolidation of the plicas accounts and to eliminating this "weight" on the growth capacity of the economy. Secondly, it is also important to see what are the advantages and disadvantages of constitutionalising budgetary principles and rules. My theme today is thus particularly adapted to a Coluio Commemorative of the 35th anniversary of the Constitution of the Portuguese Replica. [2] CARMEN M. REINHART / KENNETH S. ROGOFF, THIS TIME IS DIFFERENT: EIGHT CENTURIES OF FINANCIAL FOLLY, PRINCETON, 2009 What budgetary architecture for lasting financial discipline? The experience of countries with very different economic structures and political systems - we can mention, among others, the cases of the Netherlands, Sweden, Finland, Canada, Chile or New Zealand - shows that the definition of appropriate budgetary rules and procedures can counter the trend towards excessive indebtedness and contribute significantly to a lasting financial discipline. In the past, all these countries have experienced successful fiscal consolidation processes. These processes, based on reforms that have structurally reduced the growth of plica expenditure, have always been accompanied by profound reforms of the budgetary architecture. An analysis of success cases shows that there is no "ica revenue" with regard to the detailed design and weighting of the different instruments in the budgetary framework. In particular, the "ideal" characteristics of the budget model seem to depend critically on factors such as the institutional framework in its various aspects, and even on the ecological, political and social history of each country. In particular, factors such as the electoral system, the type of majorities generated by the political system, the ability of the judicial and political systems to apply the rules and the quality of information and the degree of sophistication of the debate in the "pblica sphere" are relevant. Despite the differences, we can list a set of fundamental principles that are present in all successful experiences. In particular, it would highlight the principles of stability, accountability and transparency. These principles complement long-established principles such as the principles of annuality, unity, universality, specification and balance of the budget (which, in this case Portuguese, are enshrined in the Constitution). The principle of stability reflects the need for a budgetary framework based on the following premises: -Promote intergenerational equity; -Anchor the expectations of eco-actors regarding the evolution of the tax burden, enabling them to optimise savings and investment decisions; and -Mitigate the fluctuations of econic activity, in particular through the operation of so-called automatic stabilisers. In a word, the budgetary framework should be designed in such a way as to ensure the sustainability of the plica accounts and, without prejudice to it, contribute to the stabilisation of the economy. Accountability in Anglo-Saxon terminology calls for a culture of evaluation, essential to the proper functioning of a democracy. It is crucial that policy makers and policy makers are accountable and held accountable for their use of the resources made available to them by taxpayers. By the heart of the matter, but not least, transparency appears as a principle transversal to the rest, more specifically as a necessary condition for achieving stability and accountability. This is to ensure that full, reliable, timely and easily accessible information is made available on the political decision-making and all the activities of the plico sector, as well as on its financial impacts. This requirement is essential to ensure the good information of the electorate, on the one hand, and to allow the situation to be rigorously checked on the part of the plica debt holders, on the other. For example, the information provided should provide a quick and clear response to questions such as: How many plico organisms are there? What governance and management rules apply to a particular plica entity? How many are the plicos employees and what is their binding regime? How has the expense of a particular Ministry evolved? What is the overall volume of guarantees granted by the State? What is the historical record of the guarantees triggered? What are the future burdens with the penss plicos systems or the Plico-Private Partnerships? The principles of stability, accountability and transparency have been explicitly enshrined in various legal orders, in particular in Budget Framework Laws, Budget Responsibility Laws or Conduct Management. In the Portuguese, they were enshrined in the revision of the recently adopted Budget Framework Act. The practical application of these principles has been reflected in a budgetary architecture built around five paradigmatic elements: (i) Budgetary rules; (ii) Multiannual budgetary framework; (iii) Programme budgeting; (iv) Equity accounting; (v) Independent budgetary institutions (tax councils or, as they are generally called, Plicas Finance Councils). In previous speeches, I have already had the opportunity to comment on these different sizes. Today I will only address the issue of budgetary rules because they represent the "roof" of the 'budget building' and also because this is the dimension that most directly may be related to the Constitution. Budgetary rules A budgetary rule consists of a numerical restriction imposed on a budget aggregate. The experiences of the countries are very varied with regard to the type of rules and their specific design. There are rules on plica debt, budget balance, plica expenditure and, less often, on the level of revenue. In several cases, there is a combination of different rules, or rules depending on the level of the plica administrations to which they apply. Extensive empirical evidence points to a relationship between budgetary rules and the performance of plica accounts. This association appears to be stronger in cases where the rules on the budget balance are supplemented by spending rules. There is also evidence that budgetary rules have contributed to successful budgetary consolidations. However, the existence of a budgetary rule is far from sufficient condition to ensure budgetary discipline. International experience suggests that there are four factors particularly relevant to assessing the degree of effectiveness of a budget rule. Firstly, it is important to take account of the formulation of the budgetary rule and, in particular, to take account of aspects such as its degree of scope and flexibility: The rule applies to all the plicas administration sector, or just the part of it? Does the rule cover all public revenues and expenses, or does it exclude certain items? Is the rule annual, or does it apply on average in an eco-cycle? Are exception mechanisms in place? What is the margin for accounting and/or statistical "manipulation"? Secondly, appropriate enforcement mechanisms should be put in place to ensure that reputational or other costs arising from non-compliance with the budgetary rule are high. Here too, international experience refers to a set of concerns, and it seems particularly promising to define automatic mechanisms for correcting deviations and the attribution to independent entities of responsibility for assessing compliance with the rule (this is a role increasingly assumed by the so-called Plicas Finance Councils). Thirdly, budgetary rules should be supported by operational procedures that contribute to the achievement of budgetary objectives, with particular relevance on instruments such as multiannual budgetary planning, programme budgeting and wealth accounting. By the tone, but not least, any institutional reform will bear lasting fruit if it is based on, or promote, a broad social consensus around its objectives. If the idea that financial discipline is a good that must be preserved is not widely shared, a "coalition" will easily emerge in favour of breaching the budget rule or amending it. As regards the nature of the legal instrument used to enshrine budgetary rules, different approaches have been followed. In some countries, such as the Netherlands and Sweden, budgetary rules are an integral part of political commitments (coalition agreements and/or government programmes). In other countries, the rules are inscribed in laws, with cases of rules defined in ordinary laws, laws of enhanced value and even in the Constitution. The most recent trend seems to be to integrate the rules into laws of enhanced value or in the Constitution. The debate on the constitutionalization of deficit and debt limits has intensified significantly with the adoption in Germany in 2009 of the constitutional ban on the federal deficit exceeding 0.35% of GDP from 2016 (rule commonly referred to as "debt brake"  Schuldenbremse) iii . This debate extended to other euro area countries, especially France, and even to countries that have not yet adopted the ica currency, such as polia and Hungary which, respectively, have approved or are in the process of approving constitutional limits on plico indebtedness (in the first case, 55%; in the second, 50% of GDP). Outside the European Union, Switzerland had already adopted in 2003 a constitutional rule on the budget balance not unlike that most recently approved in Germany. In the prime days, we will certainly see a deepening and generalization of this debate. This is, above all, due to the adoption at the European Council on 24 and 25 March last of the so-called Euro Plus Pact[3], in which Member States undertake to transpose the budgetary rules of the Stability and Growth Pact into national legal systems, leaving them to choose the legal form on condition that national rules are sufficiently binding and durable (e.g. constitution or framework law)[4]. The wording of the rule will also be left to the choice of each Member State, which may take the form of a "debt brake", a rule relating to the primary balance, or an expenditure rule. This debate raises two previous questions before we even consider the case Portuguese: first, the significance and relevance of the possible constitutionalisation of quantitative limits on deficit or indebtedness; second, the relationship of these possible national constitutional rules with the rules of the Stability and Growth Pact. [3] CO EUR 6, CONCL 3, ANEXO 1, PP. 13 SS. [4] IBID., P. 19. Meaning and relevance of the constitutionalization of deficit limits and indebtedness plicos With regard to the first question - meaning and relevance of the constitutionalisation of budgetary rules - it should be noted that the Constitution must be understood in dynamic terms. As the supreme law, it is not a mere normative text, but an expression of a state of cultural development [5], so its content must be permeable to the fundamental values and desiderates of the community in its various historical phases. Constitutionalization has the merit of p the fundamental values and principles of the community covered by conjunctural majorities, because the special rigidity that is, in general, associated with the norms of the Constitution makes it difficult to review it. Moreover, since the supreme normative document of a community is the supreme normative document of a community, the Constitution does not impose limits on the action of political power, thereby guaranteeing the rights and freedoms of citizens, as it guides political action towards the pursuit of constitutionally set values and objectives. In this sense, it is not hard to admit that the preservation of sustainable phasing finances constitutes a fundamental desideratum of a community and, as such, is part of constitutional axiology. It is, in essence, the expression of an intergenerational commitment that obliges the political decision-makers of the present not to transfer disproportionately burdensome burdens to future generations. However, does this fundamental value be densified in constitutional terms from the prediction of a set of quantitative limits? On the one hand, the setting of quantitative limits on deficit and plyo-indebtedness seems to be part of the function of negative self-tying of the Constitution: the early assessment of a series of restrictions on each person's conduct in the future becomes a means by which policy makers and environmental agents incorporate long-term assessments in their decisions at present[6]. Just as Ulysses tied himself to the masts to avoid the call of mermaids, the inclusion in the constitution of certain fundamental choices implies the acceptance by a community of a set of restrictions on political decision-making through its elected representatives and governments. On the other hand, constitutional self-tying should not serve as an instrument to regulate and decide more or less conjunctural political disputes. Regras oramentais Uma regra oramental consiste numa restrio de carcter numrico imposta sobre um agregado oramental. As experincias dos pases so muito variadas no que respeita ao tipo de regras e ao seu desenho em concreto. Existem regras sobre a dvida plica, o saldo oramental, a despesa plica e, menos frequentemente, sobre o nvel da receita. Em vrios casos, existe uma combinao de regras, ou regras diferentes consoante o nvel das administras plicas a que se aplicam. Uma vasta evidncia emprica aponta para uma relao entre regras oramentais e desempenho das contas plicas. Esta associao parece ser mais forte nos casos em que as regras sobre o saldo oramental so complementadas com regras de despesa. Existe igualmente evidncia de que as regras oramentais tm contribudo para consolidaes oramentais bem sucedidas. No entanto, a existncia de uma regra oramental est longe de ser condio suficiente para garantir a disciplina oramental. A experincia internacional sugere que h quatro factores particularmente relevantes para aferir do grau de eficcia de uma regra oramental. Em primeiro lugar, importa atender  formulao da regra oramental e, em particular, atender a aspectos como o seu grau de abrangncia e flexibilidade: A regra aplica-se a toda o sector das administras plicas, ou apenas a parte deste? A regra cobre todas as receitas e despesas pblicas, ou exclui determinados itens? A regra  anual, ou aplica-se em mdia num ciclo econico? Esto previstos mecanismos de excepo? Qual a margem para "manipulao" contabilstica e/ou estatstica? Em segundo lugar, h que prever mecanismos de enforcement adequados de forma a garantir que os custos de reputao, ou outros, decorrentes do no cumprimento da regra oramental so elevados. Tambm aqui a experincia internacional remete para um conjunto de solus, parecendo particularmente promissores a definio de mecanismos automticos de correco de desvios e a atribuio a entidades independentes da responsabilidade pela avaliao do cumprimento da regra (este  um papel crescentemente assumido pelos designados Conselhos de Finanas Plicas). Em terceiro lugar, as regras oramentais devem ser sustentadas em procedimentos operacionais que concorram para a concretizao dos objectivos oramentais, assumindo especial relevncia instrumentos como o planeamento oramental plurianual, a oramentao por programas e a contabilidade patrimonial. Por timo, mas no menos importante, qualquer reforma institucional strar frutos duradouros se assentar, ou promover, um consenso social alargado em torno dos seus objectivos.
