Title: Opening speech by Administrator Francisca Guedes de Oliveira at the ASFAC Annual Conference
text: Opening speech by Administrator Francisca Guedes de Oliveira at the ASFAC Annual Conference 22 March 2023 05 minutes Good morning I would first like to thank the Bank of Portugal for inviting us to participate in this event. I thank and greet in a special way Dr. Duarte Gomes Pereira and Dr. Pedro Alves for the kindness with which they welcomed me in this session.  In the current context, one of the main challenges facing the consumer credit market is related to the impact of the increase in inflation and the consequent rise in interest rates on the financial resilience of consumers, requiring institutions to be more rigorous and committed to assessing the credit risk of customers, ensuring that the granting of credit is based on robust procedures and criteria for assessing the credit of the solvency, and taking a proactive attitude in identifying and monitoring borrowers with difficulties in fulfilling their credit agreements.  Although the increase in interest rates has a more direct impact on home loan agreements, a market characterized by a large percentage of credit agreements subject to a variable interest rate regime, experience has shown that, in the event of financial difficulties, customers tend to default first on consumer loans and, only then, in housing credit contracts.  The significant and rapid increase in interest rates also has an impact on the adjustment of the maximum rates applicable to consumer credit, which I know is particularly dear to you. In fact, the evolution of maximum rates on consumer credit has not fully reflected the rapid and significant increase in market reference interest rates. In all credit segments, there is a reduction in the margin between the maximum rates and the market reference rates, a situation that is particularly critical in the car leasing segments, with the 12-month Euribor even exceeding the maximum rate defined for the new car leasing segment in the 1st quarter of 2023. Although it is not up to Banco de Portugal to define the methodology for calculating these rates, established in article 28 of Decree-Law No. 133/2009, of 2 June, it is, however, attentive and sensitive to this issue and has been reflecting, in dialogue with some industry associations (ASFAC and ALF) and financial institutions, on the current model.  In the current context, the procedures relating to the prevention and management of non-compliance, created in 2013, with the General Regime of Non-Compliance PARI/PERSI (Action Plan for the Risk of Non-Compliance and Extrajudicial Procedure for the Settlement of Situations of Default), and adjusted over time, are of particular importance.  The solutions provided for in this regime are in line with the best international practices, also meeting the Guidelines of the European Banking Authority on this matter (cf. EBA Guidelines on arrears and foreclosure - EBA/GL/2015/12 e EBA Guidelines on loan origination and monitoring - EBA/GL/2020/06). The national regime also seems to accommodate the a solution that is expected to be adopted in the context of the revision of the Consumer Credit Directive.  Particularly with regard to the monitoring of credit risk, institutions must have, and have had, an increasingly proactive attitude in monitoring the credit portfolio, in order to identify, at an early stage, bank customers at risk of default. It is recalled that, since 2021, permanent and systematic monitoring involves (i) monitoring credit agreements with a minimum monthly periodicity, (ii) creating individual processes for bank customers covered by the procedures provided for in the PARI that allows for more efficient action and (iii) monitoring the effectiveness of the solutions agreed with customers within the scope of the PARI, regularly assessing their adequacy to the financial capacity, objectives and needs of bank customers and proposing, whenever appropriate, other solutions.  In addition to the internal mechanisms for detecting situations of risk of default and monitoring the execution of credit agreements, it is extremely important to define and strengthen communication channels with customers that favour the awareness of risk alerts by customers, allowing for increasingly earlier action.  In addition to the challenges of the current context of monetary policy normalisation, there are also those faced by the consumer credit market, as a result of the growing digitalisation of retail banking products and services.  The digitalisation of the financial sector follows a general trend of change in consumption habits and the demand for products that meet the expectations of the consumers quickly and conveniently. This process has been greatly boosted by the COVID-19 pandemic. The health measures adopted at the time promoted a very significant increase in the use of digital channels, both in the use of digital payment instruments, or in the contracting of banking products and services.  The digital transformation we are witnessing is likely to bring benefits to the consumers and institutions, but also more risks. o The contracting of banking products and services through digital channels, as it is faster and does not involve physical contact between the bank customer and the institution, may, for example, make it difficult to identify the banking service provider and to read and understand pre-contractual and contractual information. On the other hand, it can allow access to successive credits (in a shopping around logic) that is more difficult to control, bringing dangers in the assessment of customers' credit risk. In this context, Banco de Portugal had the opportunity, already in 2020, to issue a set out in Circular Letter CC/2020/00000044 for the marketing of retail banking products and services (namely, bank deposits, credit products, payment services and electronic money), through digital channels (online or mobile), seeking to mitigate the risks arising from digitalisation. In addition, Banco de Portugal has the role of promoting the quality of demand, including through the development and implementation of a digital financial education strategy for Portugal (a theme of financial literacy that I know is also a pillar of action by ASFAC). I would like to take this opportunity to invite you to the event to disseminate the recommendations that will be part of the Sustainability Strategy. Digital Financial Literacy for Portugal, which will take place on May 10th, during the morning, at the Money Museum, in Lisbon.  As a result of the increasingly accelerated development of technology and the increase in new distribution channels, new products and services (e.g. buynow, paylater products) and new business models have emerged, involving third parties (e.g. market places) and new providers of products and services, sometimes operating from other Member States in the European Union.  The supervisor is called upon to respond, on an ongoing basis, to the challenges brought about by innovation in retail banking markets, ensuring compliance with the regulatory framework, ensuring that bank customers, regardless of the channel used to carry out banking operations (branch, telephone, homebanking, apps, etc.), benefit from identical rights, without thereby blocking innovation in the financial sector. The challenges are many, the evolution tends to be exponential, and the stability of the system with the proper protection of all stakeholders within a demanding and international regulatory framework can only be achieved with a collaborative attitude. We deeply believe that we all have an important role to play in the goal of having a robust, stable financial system that serves the economy, and therefore all of us, in the best possible way.
text_original: Interveno de abertura da Administradora Francisca Guedes de Oliveira na Conferncia Anual da ASFAC 22 maro 2023 05 minutos Bom dia, Gostava, em primeiro lugar, de agradecer o convite que foi dirigido ao Banco de Portugal para participarmos neste evento. Agradeo e cumprimento de forma especial o Dr. Duarte Gomes Pereira e o Dr. Pedro Alves pela amabilidade com que me acolheram nesta sesso.  No atual contexto, um dos principais desafios com que se confronta o mercado de crdito aos consumidores prende-se com o impacto do aumento da inflao e da consequente subida das taxas de juro na resilincia financeira dos consumidores, exigindo das instituies rigor e empenho acrescidos na avaliao do risco de crdito dos clientes, assegurando que a concesso de crdito assenta em procedimentos e critrios robustos de avaliao da solvabilidade, e assumindo uma atitude proativa na identificao e acompanhamento dos muturios com dificuldades no cumprimento dos seus contratos de crdito.  Embora o aumento das taxas de juro tenha impacto mais direto nos contratos de crdito  habitao, mercado caracterizado por uma larga percentagem de contratos de crdito sujeitos a um regime de taxa de juro varivel, a experincia tem vindo a demonstrar que, em caso de dificuldades financeiras, os clientes tendem a incumprir primeiro nos crditos ao consumo e, s depois, nos contratos de crditos  habitao.  O aumento significativo e rpido das taxas de juro tem tambm impacto no ajustamento das taxas mximas aplicveis ao crdito aos consumidores, assunto que, sei, vos  particularmente caro. Com efeito, a evoluo das taxas mximas no crdito aos consumidores no tem refletido integralmente o rpido e significativo aumento das taxas de juro de referncia do mercado. Em todos os segmentos de crdito verifica-se uma reduo da margem entre as taxas mximas e as taxas de referncia do mercado, situao que  particularmente crtica nos segmentos de locao financeira automvel, tendo a Euribor a 12 meses ultrapassado mesmo a taxa mxima definida para o segmento de locao financeira de automveis novos no 1. trimestre de 2023. No cabendo ao Banco de Portugal a definio da metodologia de clculo destas taxas, estabelecido no artigo 28 do Decreto-Lei n 133/2009, de 2 de junho, est, no entanto, atento e sensvel a esta questo e tem vindo a refletir, em dilogo com algumas associaes do setor (ASFAC e ALF) e instituies financeiras sobre o atual modelo.  No contexto atual, os procedimentos relativos  preveno e gesto do incumprimento, criados em 2013, com o Regime Geral do Incumprimento PARI/PERSI (Plano de Ao para o Risco de Incumprimento e Procedimento Extrajudicial de Regularizao de Situaes de Incumprimento), e ajustados ao longo do tempo, assumem especial importncia.  As solues previstas neste regime esto alinhadas com as melhores prticas internacionais, indo tambm ao encontro a Orientaes da Autoridade Bancria Europeia nesta matria (cf. EBA Guidelines on arrears and foreclosure - EBA/GL/2015/12 e EBA Guidelines on loan origination and monitoring - EBA/GL/2020/06). O regime nacional parece tambm acomodar a soluo que se perspetiva vir a ser adotada no contexto da reviso da Diretiva do Crdito aos Consumidores.  Em particular no que se refere  monitorizao do risco de crdito, as instituies devem ter, e tm tido, uma atitude cada vez mais proativa no acompanhamento da carteira de crdito, de forma a identificar, de forma precoce, os clientes bancrios em risco de incumprimento. Recorda-se que, desde 2021, o acompanhamento permanente e sistemtico passa por (i) realizar monitorizao, dos contratos de crdito com periodicidade mnima mensal, (ii) criar processos individuais para os clientes bancrios abrangidos pelos procedimentos previstos no PARI que permita uma atuao mais eficiente e (iii) acompanhar a eficcia das solues acordadas com os clientes no mbito do PARI, avaliando regularmente a sua adequao  capacidade financeira, objetivos e necessidades dos clientes bancrios e propondo, sempre que tal se revele adequado, outras solues.  Para alm dos mecanismos internos de deteo de situaes de risco de incumprimento e de acompanhamento da execuo dos contratos de crdito,  extremamente importante a definio e reforo de canais de comunicao com os clientes que favoream a tomada de conhecimento de alertas de risco por parte dos clientes, permitindo uma atuao cada vez mais precoce.  Aos desafios do atual contexto de normalizao da poltica monetria, acrescem os que se colocam ao mercado de crdito aos consumidores, fruto da crescente digitalizao dos produtos e servios bancrios de retalho.  A digitalizao do setor financeiro acompanha uma tendncia generalizada de alterao dos hbitos de consumo e a procura por produtos que satisfaam as pretenses dos consumidores de forma clere e conveniente. Este processo sofreu um grande impulso em virtude da pandemia de COVID-19. As medidas sanitrias ento adotadas promoveram um aumento muito significativo da utilizao dos canais digitais, quer na utilizao de instrumentos de pagamento digitais, quer na prpria contratao de produtos e servios bancrios.  A transformao digital a que se assiste  suscetvel de trazer benefcios para os consumidores e instituies, mas tambm mais riscos. o A contratao de produtos e servios bancrios atravs de canais digitais, por ser mais clere e por no implicar contacto fsico do cliente bancrio com a instituio, pode, por exemplo, dificultar a identificao do prestador do servio bancrio e a leitura e compreenso da informao pr-contratual e contratual. Por outro lado, pode permitir o acesso a crditos sucessivos (numa lgica de shoppingaround) mais difcil de controlar, trazendo perigos na avaliao do risco de crdito dos clientes. Neste mbito, o Banco de Portugal teve oportunidade, j em 2020, de emitir um conjunto de boas prticas, previstas na Carta Circular n. CC/2020/00000044, aplicveis  comercializao de produtos e servios bancrios de retalho (nomeadamente, depsitos bancrios, produtos de crdito, servios de pagamento e moeda eletrnica), atravs de canais digitais (online ou mobile), procurando mitigar os riscos decorrentes da digitalizao. Adicionalmente, o Banco de Portugal tem a funo de promover a qualidade da procura, nomeadamente atravs do desenvolvimento e implementao de uma estratgia de formao financeira digital para Portugal (tema da literacia financeira que sei tambm ser pilar de ao da ASFAC). Aproveito desde j para vos convidar para o evento de disseminao das recomendaes que faro parte da Estratgia de Literacia Financeira Digital para Portugal, o qual ter lugar no dia 10 de maio, durante a manh, no Museu do Dinheiro, em Lisboa.  Fruto do desenvolvimento cada vez mais acelerado da tecnologia e do incremento de novos canais de distribuio, surgiram novos produtos e servios (por exemplo, produtos buynow, paylater) e novos modelos de negcio, envolvendo terceiros (por exemplo, market places) e novos prestadores de produtos e servios, operando por vezes a partir de outros EM da Unio Europeia.  O supervisor  chamado a responder, de forma contnua, aos desafios trazidos pela inovao nos mercados bancrios de retalho, assegurando o cumprimento do quadro normativo, garantindo que os clientes bancrios, independentemente do canal utilizado para a realizao de operaes bancrias (balco, telefone, homebanking, apps, etc.), beneficiam de idnticos direitos, sem, com isto, bloquear a inovao no setor financeiro. Os desafios so muitos, a evoluo tende a ser exponencial, e a estabilidade do sistema com a devida proteo de todos os stakehoders dentro de um quadro normativo exigente e internacional s se consegue com uma atitude colaborativa. Acreditamos profundamente que todos temos um papel importante a cumprir no desgnio de ter um sistema financeiro robusto, estvel e que sirva a economia, e, portanto, a todos ns, da melhor forma possvel.

Title: Closing speech by Administrator Francisca Guedes de Oliveira at the ALF 2023 National Meeting: The Future of Environmental, Social and Governance Responsibilities
text: Closing speech by Administrator Francisca Guedes de Oliveira at the ALF 2023 National Meeting: The Future of Environmental, Social and Governance Responsibilities 23 MAY 2023 08 minutes Good afternoon everyone. I would like to begin by thanking the Bank of Portugal for the invitation to close this important and timely event. And I thank, in particular, Dr. Luis Augusto [President of ALF] and Dr. Vitor Graca [Secretary General of ALF] for the kindness with which they received me. I would also like to congratulate the previous speakers for the quality of their speeches. Throughout this day, we have already been able to benefit from varied and valuable perspectives on a reality - the ESG universe - that has been increasingly imposed on all of us. Just recently, McKinsey found that the number of internet searches for the term "ESG" had increased fivefold since 2019. Despite all the events that have demanded our attention in these truly exceptional years: the Covid-19 pandemic, the Russian invasion of Ukraine, the return of inflationary pressures in advanced economies, the signs of globalization's retreat - and a big etcetera. It is now up to me to bring the particular perspective of Banco de Portugal, from the outset as a public entity inserted in society and committed to capturing and reflecting its evolution, within the scope of the mandate entrusted to us. A mandate focused on safeguarding price stability and preserving the stability of the financial system. But it also covers aspects such as the oversight of the payment system, the promotion of financial literacy or advising the Government on economic and financial matters, to go no further. It follows that ESG sustainability issues, in their great diversity, intersect and affect the Bank's missions and activities in multiple ways. This is the case of the social aspect and what the Bank has done, for example, to reduce inequalities in the field of ethnicity or gender. This is also the case of the governance aspect - or governance, or governance, as you like - and what the Bank has done, for example, to promote transparency in the functioning of the institutions. This is also the case of several issues in the environmental sphere and what the Bank has done, for example, in the analysis of the implications arising from the loss of biodiversity. We have, in fact, sought to make contributions at various levels of the ESG universe - and we have deliberately chosen, in recent years, an integrated approach to this universe. An approach that combines the different dimensions of ESG sustainability and has resulted in a joint strategy of the various departments with a common institutional framework. With decentralized execution, but transversal coordination, reporting directly to the member of the Board of Directors responsible for sustainability. It is an integrated and comprehensive approach to sustainability. But also an approach that necessarily gives special prominence to what is one of the major global issues of our time  "a choice between collective action and collective suicide", in the words of the UN Secretary-General. I am talking, of course, about the challenge of climate change, which is also imposed on central banks - and the Bank of Portugal, in particular - because of the urgency and scale of what is at stake. We are now well aware of the roots and characteristics of the phenomenon, even if we cannot accurately predict the pace at which it will unfold and the extent it may reach. We are also getting to know more and more, and earlier than expected, the consequences associated with the problem, evident in the increasing frequency and magnitude of extreme weather events and the intensification of chronic events. We also know what is the most efficient way to respond to the climate crisis, which has at its origin "the biggest market failure the world has ever seen", in the words of Nicholas Stern. In other words, in good economese, a colossal negative externality, a gigantic difference between the social cost of global greenhouse gas emissions and the private cost that is assumed by the emitters of these gases. The response to the climate crisis, within the scope of government action, must necessarily combine an element of adaptation - since climate change is already a reality - and an element of mitigation. In this case, covering three critical aspects:  First, carbon taxation, through taxes or emission allowances - which does not necessarily have to mean an increase in the total tax burden, but may be achieved through a rebalancing of the tax system. The IMF estimates that the average cost of carbon emissions is currently around 6 per ton and that it will be necessary to reach 75 by 2030.  Second, the promotion of the so-called green L&D, involving an effort by companies and academia, but also the granting of subsidies by public entities in areas less conducive to private intervention.  Third, the mobilization of large financings, combining capital and debt. According to several leading international institutions, the annual investment needed to achieve climate neutrality by 2050 could amount to 8% of global GDP. If we consider only incremental investment, excluding what would be needed to replenish the capital stock, the annual bill would vary between 0.6 and 0.9% of global GDP. The public policies listed are within the scope of action of governments. So what is the role of Central Banks in the climate transition? For an institution like ours, part of the Eurosystem, there are two main tasks to perform in the context of climate action  two major contributions to make. The first - and most important - is to fulfil our core mission of promoting and ensuring price stability. Why? Essentially, because excessive levels of inflation distort relative prices and compromise an efficient allocation of resources. This tends to accentuate the uncertainty in what is already a complex and volatile environment, thus limiting and postponing the investment effort that is needed for the transformation of our economies. The second major contribution we can make in this matter is to deepen knowledge about the vulnerability of the financial system to climate risk and to foster an adequate integration of climate considerations in banks' strategies, governance models, risk management practices and reporting. In this way, we will be promoting financial stability - and also, ultimately, the ability of banks to finance the climate transition. In addition to these two critical aspects, a central bank with a mandate such as Banco de Portugal can also make some other relevant contributions to the response to the climate crisis. For example, by helping to overcome climate data gaps, which are a practical obstacle of great importance for the smooth development of the activities of various partners in this regard, from investors to researchers. Or, on the subject of researchers, directing part of our technical and analytical capacity to this area, which will thus be contributing to more informed decisions and more effective policies in the public sphere and in the economy, in general. It was with this framework in mind that we defined Banco de Portugal's strategy for ESG sustainability, with a particular emphasis on climate change. A strategy under the motto "Acting for sustainability", which succeeded an initial approach in place in 2020-21 and will now be in place until 2025, in close articulation with the Bank's overall strategic plan. Our action in favor of sustainability is developed in three main axes. First, integrate climate change into our mission , which unfolds in price stability, the financial system, and economic and financial support to the government. This integration into the mission is, objectively, the most important of the three and also the one in which we work most closely with the ECB and the other Eurosystem national central banks. In the mission of safeguarding price stability, a responsibility we share with the Eurosystem, we have been committed to incorporating climate issues into the conceptual framework and operational framework of monetary policy. These issues were integrated into the ECB's monetary policy strategy, which was revised about two years ago, at the same time as an action plan to develop such integration was approved. In the operational sphere, several climate-related innovations have been introduced in terms of asset purchase programmes, collateral and reporting requirements. Last March, the process of reporting the carbon footprint of these assets was also initiated. In the axis of safeguarding financial stability, two main aspects stand out.  On the one hand, assessing banks' exposure to climate-related risks and the resilience of the financial system in the face of them. To this end, we have developed our own technical capacity, prepared and published studies, invested in the acquisition and development of climate databases, and participated in Eurosystem-wide stress test exercises .  On the other hand, adapt our supervisory approach in order to encourage banks to incorporate climate and environmental risks in the various aspects relevant to your activity. To this end, we have adopted a guide with supervisory expectations regarding the management of climate and environmental risks, both at the level of the Single Supervisory Mechanism and in its application to smaller banks under our direct supervision. And we have been evaluating how banks are incorporating these expectations, which will become imperative from 2025 onwards. Finally, with regard to the mission to advise the Government on economic and financial matters, we have made numerous contributions to the debate on the EU's sustainability and sustainable financing agenda and have adopted climate and environmental issues as one of the main lines of work of our Study Agenda for 2022-25, already with several published papers . The second major axis of Banco de Portugal's sustainability strategy is to increase environmental, social and governance sustainability in our internal management. In this sense, and among several other initiatives, we have published a Responsible Investment Charter, which enshrines our climate and environmental commitment in the management of our own asset portfolios, we have started to disclose the carbon footprint of these assets and we are preparing a program for the development of our own assets. decarbonization of our activities, with a view to carbon neutrality by 2050. Finally, the third axis of our strategy is to strengthen the awareness of our fellow citizens on ESG sustainability issues. This is also part of numerous initiatives aimed at different stakeholders - including our employees, the banking system, the bank customer, large non-financial companies and colleagues from the central banks of Portuguese-speaking countries. I would particularly like to highlight the publication on our institutional website of a page dedicated to sustainability, which I invite everyone to know. And I conclude, if I may, quoting the Governor of the Bank of Portugal: "This is a topic that concerns everyone: political agents and political agents; financial institutions and non-financial companies; academia, non-governmental associations and citizens. No one can be separated from this debate. No one can resign from participating in the collective effort to adapt to climate change and decarbonize; of ecosystem preservation. In short, we cannot fail to integrate environmental considerations into our policies and decision-making frameworks in the fulfilment of our mandates. And this, in itself, is already a huge challenge!"
text_original: Interveno de encerramento da Administradora Francisca Guedes de Oliveira no Encontro Nacional ALF 2023: O Futuro das Responsabilidades Ambientais, Sociais e de Governana 23 MAI 2023 08 minutos Boa tarde a todos. Comeo por agradecer o convite que foi dirigido ao Banco de Portugal para encerrar este importante e oportuno evento. E agradeo, em especial, ao Dr. Lus Augusto [Presidente da ALF] e ao Dr. Vtor Graa [Secretrio-Geral da ALF] pela gentileza com que me receberam. Felicito ainda os participantes que me antecederam, pela qualidade das suas intervenes. Pudemos j beneficiar, ao longo deste dia, de variadas e valiosas perspetivas sobre uma realidade - o universo ESG - que se tem imposto cada vez mais a todos ns. Ainda recentemente, a McKinsey constatava que o nmero de pesquisas na internet pela expresso ESG tinha quintuplicado desde 2019. No obstante todos os acontecimentos que solicitaram a nossa ateno nestes anos verdadeiramente excecionais: a pandemia de Covid-19, a invaso russa da Ucrnia, o regresso das presses inflacionistas nas economias avanadas, os sinais de retrocesso da globalizao - e um grande etc. Cabe-me agora trazer a perspetiva particular do Banco de Portugal, desde logo enquanto entidade pblica inserida na sociedade e empenhada em captar e refletir a sua evoluo, no mbito do mandato que nos foi confiado. Um mandato centrado na salvaguarda da estabilidade de preos e na preservao da estabilidade do sistema financeiro. Mas que abrange tambm aspetos como a superintendncia do sistema de pagamentos, a promoo da literacia financeira ou o aconselhamento ao Governo em matria econmica e financeira, para no ir mais longe. Da decorre que as questes relativas  sustentabilidade ESG, na sua grande diversidade, intersetam e afetam de mltiplas formas as misses e as atividades do Banco.  o caso da vertente social e do que o Banco tem feito, por exemplo, para minorar as desigualdades no domnio da etnia ou do gnero.  tambm o caso da vertente de governo - ou governao, ou governana, como queiram - e do que o Banco tem feito, por exemplo, para fomentar a transparncia no funcionamento das instituies.  ainda o caso de diversas questes da esfera ambiental e do que o Banco tem feito, por exemplo, na anlise das implicaes decorrentes da perda de biodiversidade. Temos, de facto, procurado dar contributos a diversos nveis do universo ESG - e optmos deliberadamente, nos ltimos anos, por uma abordagem integrada a este universo. Uma abordagem que combina as diferentes dimenses da sustentabilidade ESG e que se traduziu numa estratgia conjunta dos vrios departamentos com um enquadramento institucional comum. Com execuo descentralizada, mas coordenao transversal, reportando diretamente ao membro do Conselho de Administrao responsvel pela sustentabilidade.  uma abordagem integrada e abrangente  sustentabilidade. Mas tambm uma abordagem que necessariamente confere especial destaque quela que  uma das principais questes globais do nosso tempo - uma escolha entre a ao coletiva e o suicdio coletivo, nas palavras do Secretrio- Geral da ONU. Falo, naturalmente, do desafio das alteraes climticas, que se impe, tambm aos bancos centrais - e ao Banco de Portugal, em particular - pela urgncia e pela dimenso do que est em causa. Conhecemos bem, atualmente, as razes e as caratersticas do fenmeno, mesmo se no podemos antever de forma rigorosa o ritmo a que ele se ir desenrolar e a extenso que poder vir a atingir. Vamos tambm conhecendo cada vez mais, e mais cedo do que se esperava, as consequncias associadas ao problema, patentes na crescente frequncia e magnitude dos eventos climticos extremos e na intensificao dos eventos crnicos. Sabemos ainda qual  o caminho mais eficiente para dar resposta  crise climtica, que tem na sua origem a maior falha de mercado que o mundo j viu, nas palavras de Nicholas Stern. Ou seja, em bom economs, uma externalidade negativa colossal, uma diferena gigantesca entre o custo social das emisses globais de gases com efeito de estufa e o custo privado que  assumido pelos emitentes desses gases. A resposta  crise climtica, no mbito da ao dos governos, deve necessariamente combinar um elemento de adaptao - uma vez que as alteraes climticas so j uma realidade - e um elemento de mitigao. Neste caso, abrangendo trs aspetos crticos:  Primeiro, a tributao do carbono, por via de impostos ou de licenas de emisso - o que no tem de significar necessariamente um aumento da carga tributria total, podendo ser conseguido atravs de um reequilbrio do sistema fiscal. O FMI estima que o custo mdio das emisses de carbono ronda atualmente os 6 dlares por tonelada e que ser necessrio atingir os 75 dlares at 2030.  Segundo, a promoo da chamada l&D verde, envolvendo um esforo das empresas e da academia, mas tambm a concesso de subsdios por entidades pblicas em domnios menos propcios  interveno privada.  Terceiro, a mobilizao de vultuosos financiamentos, combinando capital e dvida. De acordo com diversas instituies internacionais de referncia, o investimento anual necessrio para atingir a neutralidade climtica em 2050 pode ascender a 8% do PIB global. Se considerarmos apenas o investimento incremental, excluindo o que seria necessrio para repor o stock de capital, a fatura anual variaria entre os 0,6 e os 0,9% do PIB global. As polticas pblicas elencadas esto no escopo de ao dos governos. Qual  ento o papel dos Bancos Centrais na transio climtica? Para uma instituio como a nossa, integrada no Eurosistema, h duas tarefas principais a desempenhar no contexto da ao climtica - dois grandes contributos a prestar. O primeiro - e o mais importante -  cumprir a nossa misso principal de promover e assegurar a estabilidade de preos. Porqu? Essencialmente, porque nveis excessivos de inflao distorcem os preos relativos e comprometem uma afetao eficiente dos recursos. Isto tende a acentuar a incerteza no que  j um enquadramento complexo e voltil, podendo assim limitar e adiar o esforo de investimento que  necessrio para a transformao das nossas economias. O segundo grande contributo que podemos prestar nesta matria  aprofundar o conhecimento sobre a vulnerabilidade do sistema financeiro ao risco climtico e fomentar uma adequada integrao das consideraes climticas nas estratgias, nos modelos de governo, nas prticas de gesto do risco e nos reportes dos bancos. Desta maneira, estaremos a promover a estabilidade financeira - e tambm, em ltima instncia, a capacidade da banca para financiar a transio climtica. Para alm destes dois aspetos crticos, um banco central com um mandato como o do Banco de Portugal pode ainda dar alguns outros contributos relevantes para a resposta  crise climtica. Por exemplo, ajudando a ultrapassar as lacunas de dados climticos, que so um obstculo prtico de grande importncia para o bom desenvolvimento das atividades de vrios parceiros nesta matria, desde os investidores aos investigadores. Ou, a propsito de investigadores, orientando para esta rea uma parte da nossa capacidade tcnica e analtica, que assim estar a contribuir para decises mais informadas e polticas mais eficazes na esfera pblica e ao nvel da economia, em geral. Foi com este enquadramento que definimos a estratgia do Banco de Portugal para a sustentabilidade ESG, enfatizando sobretudo as alteraes climticas. Uma estratgia subordinada ao lema Agir pela sustentabilidade, que sucedeu a uma abordagem inicial vigente em 2020-21 e que vai agora vigorar at 2025, em estreita articulao com o plano estratgico geral do Banco. A nossa ao em prol da sustentabilidade desenvolve-se em trs grandes eixos. Primeiro, integraras alteraes climticas na nossa misso que se desdobra na estabilidade dos preos, do sistema financeiro e apoio econmico e financeiro ao governo. Esta integrao na misso , objetivamente, o mais importante dos trs e tambm aquele em que colaboramos mais de perto com o BCE e os outros bancos centrais nacionais do Eurosistema. Na misso de salvaguarda da estabilidade de preos, uma responsabilidade que partilhamos com o Eurosistema, temos estado empenhados em incorporar as questes climticas na estrutura conceptual e no enquadramento operacional da poltica monetria. Essas questes foram integradas na estratgia de poltica monetria do BCE, revista h cerca de dois anos, na mesma altura em que foi aprovado um plano de ao para desenvolver essa integrao. Na esfera operacional, tm sido introduzidas diversas inovaes relacionadas com a dimenso climtica, ao nvel dos programas de compra de ativos, dos colaterais e dos requisitos de reporte. Em maro passado, foi tambm iniciado o processo de reporte da pegada carbnica desses ativos. No eixo de salvaguarda da estabilidade financeira, destacam-se duas vertentes principais. i. Por um lado, avaliar a exposio dos bancos aos riscos climticos e a resilincia do sistema financeiro face aos mesmos. Para esse efeito, desenvolvemos capacidade tcnica prpria, elabormos e publicmos estudos, investimos na aquisio e desenvolvimento de bases de dados climticos e participmos nos exerccios de stress test ao nvel do Eurosistema. ii. Por outro lado, adaptar a nossa abordagem de superviso por forma a incentivar os bancos  incorporao dos riscos climticos e ambientais nas diversas vertentes relevantes da sua atividade. Com esse intuito, adotmos um guia com as expectativas de superviso quanto  gesto dos riscos climticos e ambientais, quer ao nvel do Mecanismo nico de Superviso quer na sua aplicao aos bancos de menores dimenses que esto sob a nossa superviso direta. E temos vindo a avaliar a forma como os bancos esto a incorporar essas expectativas, que passaro a ser imperativas a partir de 2025. Finalmente, no que diz respeito  misso de aconselhamento ao Governo em matria econmica e financeira, temos prestado numerosos contributos para o debate da agenda de sustentabilidade e financiamento sustentvel da UE e adotmos as questes climticas e ambientais como uma das grandes linhas de trabalho da nossa Agenda de Estudos para 2022-25, j com diversos papers publicados. O segundo grande eixo da estratgia de sustentabilidade do Banco de Portugal  incrementar a sustentabilidade ambiental, social e de governao na nossa gesto interna. Nesse sentido, e entre diversas outras iniciativas, publicmos uma Carta de Investimento Responsvel, que consagra o nosso compromisso climtico e ambiental na gesto das carteiras de ativos prprios, inicimos a divulgao da pegada carbnica destes ativos e estamos a elaborar um programa de descarbonizao das nossas atividades, tendo em vista a neutralidade carbnica em 2050. Por fim, o terceiro eixo da nossa estratgia  reforar a conscincia dos nossos concidados para os temas da sustentabilidade ESG. Tambm aqui se inserem numerosas iniciativas dirigidas a diferentes stakeholders - incluindo os nossos colaboradores, o sistema bancrio, o cliente bancrio, grandes empresas no financeiras e os colegas dos bancos centrais dos pases de lngua portuguesa. Destaco, em particular, a divulgao no nosso site institucional de uma pgina dedicada  sustentabilidade, que convido todos a conhecer. E concluo, se me permitem, citando o Governador do Banco de Portugal: Este  um tema que diz respeito a todos: agentes polticos e agentes de poltica; instituies financeiras e empresas no financeiras; academia, associaes no governamentais e cidados. Ningum se pode alhear deste debate. Ningum pode demitir-se de participar no esforo coletivo de adaptao s alteraes climticas e de descarbonizao; de preservao dos ecossistemas. Em suma, no podemos deixar de integrar consideraes ambientais nas nossas polticas e nos nossos quadros de deciso no cumprimento dos nossos mandatos. E isto, por si s,  j um enorme desafio!

Title: Opening speech by Administrator Hlder Rosalino at the Conference "The knowledge of the euro and the fight against counterfeiting"
text: Intervencao de abertura do Administrador Helder Rosalino na Conferencia "The knowledge of the euro and the fight against counterfeiting" (apenas em ingles) 20 junho 2022 07 minutos Good morning, everyone. And welcome to Lisbon! After the lift of restrictions on travei and face-to-face meetings, and more than two years after the original scheduled date (March 2020), I can finally welcome you all to the conferenceThe protection of the euro - the fight against counterfeiting. Special thanks are in order to the European entities here represented, in particular: the European Commission, the European Central Bank, the Europol, and, naturally, the Portuguese Criminal Police (Policia Judiciaria), our long-time privileged partner with whom the BdP has established a cooperation protocol in the fight against counterfeiting of cash and money laundering with great results. And, I would like to give a special greetings to our colleagues from the Portuguese-speaking countries [Central Banks and Criminal Investigation Authorities]. It is always a pleasure to welcome you to Banco de Portugal, to reinforcing our cooperation. A special word, too, for our colleagues who comes from our regional network. The COVID-19 pandemic forced the postponement of this conference because we considered that it only made sense in a face-to-face format. However, adversities can turn into opportunities, as proven by the online session of October 7,2021, not originally scheduled in the programme. That session allowed us to reach a wider audience, both in number of countries represented - with the participation of the countries here today, but also Croatia, which will soon join the Euro, and Turkey, which plays an important role in the fight against counterfeiting - and in number of participants. With this online session, we have minimized the time gap, kept the exchange of experiences with the benefits that come from it, and, as I have already mentioned, managed to gather a larger number of participants -130 specialists. This weekthe group is substantially smaller- around 40 participants - because not only is our goalto foster a fruitful and closer interaction between experts from Portuguese-speaking countries and the Euro Area, but also to share the best practices applied by each of the represented entities. Moreover, this programme will be enhanced with visits to the operational areas of the Issue and Treasury Department of the BdP in Carregado, Valora (Banco de Portugals Printing Work) and the scientific labs of the Portuguese Criminal Police, which would not be possible to achieve with a larger group. The conference is organized in partnership with the European Commission through the Pericles Programme, which aims to prevent and fight counterfeiting, therefore increasing the European Unions economic competitiveness and protecting the sustainability of public finances. I would like to take this opportunity to congratulatethe European Commission, not only for this specific programme, but also for the various initiatives it develops and supports in this area, and thankthe trust it has placed in Banco de Portugal to organize this conference. The goals of the Pericles Programme are aligned with the Strategic Plan of Banco de Portugal for the 2021-2025 timeframe, which has thefollowing motto: To promote proximity and strengthen trust, and with the EurosysterrTs strategy for cash. The strategic challenges we will face in the coming years include protecting the functioning of the banking system and the payment system, the deepening of the Economic and Monetary Union and the Banking Union. In addition, the response to the fast pace of digital transformation and the growing demands in matters of internai governance and sustainability, including environmental sustainability, in addition to having to share knowledge with society, listen to the concerns of the Portuguese people and be accountable for our actions. The Eurosystem accepts cash as a means of payment available to the public, which means ensuring that it remains widely available and accepted, both as a means of payment and as a store of value. The circulation of euro banknotes continues to grow faster than nominal GDP (around 6% on annual average in the last few years). However, the use of cash as a means of payment has been progressively declining, so that cash is increasingly becoming a store of value, reflecting a high degree of confidence from the majority of the population regarding this means of payment, which is easy to use and verifiable without resorting to sophisticated equipment. Although residual in relation to the number of banknotes in circulation, counterfeiting is a riskforthe States, due to the eventual loss of confidence in the currency and by the citizens and by damage created in the reputation of central banks. The volume of counterfeiting apprehended in circulation has diminished significantly, 2021 being, with the exception of 2002, the year in which the lowest number of counterfeit banknotes apprehended in circulation has been registered (around 347.000 globally). The apprehended volume corresponds to a minimal proportion of the banknotes in circulation: 12 counterfeits for every million genuine euro banknotes. 94,5% of counterfeits have been apprehended in euro area countries. Portugal has followed this trend of decreasing number of apprehended counterfeits, as well as a paradigm shift with the appearance of new typologies of counterfeit banknotes, as Movie Money, the replacement of offset by inkjet and the change in the origin of counterfeit banknotes, with the Naples group now less relevant than in the recent past. The use of the Darknet, and many times the Internet itself, and the appearance of non-conventional distribution channels has allowed a quick and at low cost spread of counterfeit security elements, originating the appearance of occasional counterfeiters. Both in the Eurosystem as in Portugal, the most counterfeited banknotes are the 20 and 50 denomination, with, however, a significant increase in the 10 counterfeit banknotes. It is important underline that coins and banknotes are the only form of public money that everyone can have direct access to. Thus, central banks from the Euro Area ensure the availability of Euro coins and banknotes, support access to cash Services for all, ensure that cash is accepted everywhere, design innovative and safe Euro banknotes and maintain banknotes safe and sustainable. From a Central Banks perspective, the fight against cash counterfeitingfocuses on four key pillars: production, cash recirculation, counterfeit analysis, and communication, training and police and judicial activity. Banco de Portugal has a very active intervention in the first three pillars, which follow the life cycle of cash. Regarding the production of Euro banknotes, I would like to highlight three aspects: the establishment of Valora in 1999, the stake in Europafi with a minority participation in 2017 and the establishment of EPIC in 2019. Valora was created with the purpose of producing the share of Euro banknotes allocated annually by the Eurosystem to Banco de Portugal. Currently, it is 100% owned by the BdP and produces euro banknotes for the BdP and not only, but also other currencies. To increase efficiency in the production of Euro banknotes, the BdP, the OeNB (central bank of austria) and the NBB (central bank of Belgium) have established an unmatched cooperation agreement in the Eurosystem (the aforementioned EPIC). The agreement foresees that the shares allocated to the three national central banks are aggregated and allocated equitably to the BdP and the OeNB and produced, respectively, by Valora and the OeBS (the Printing Works of central bank of austria). This cooperation allows scale economy, avoids task duplication, prevents disruptive production due to unforeseen situations, promotes the sharing of experience, safeguards, and consolidates specialized knowledge to a restricted group of professionals. The equity participation of the BdP at EuropafPs - the Paper Mill of Bank the France - allows the acquisition of fiduciary paper at favourable prices and a specialized and close technical support for the main raw material in banknote production. Banco de Portugal has also been a pioneer, in the Euro Area, by implementing (in 2007) the Common Frameworkfor Recirculation, with the preparation of the necessary legalframeworks and inspection teams. This frameworkforesees the recirculation of coins and banknotes whose genuineness and quality have been previously confirmed by professional cash handler entities - credit intermediaries, cash-in-transit companies and currency exchange offices - and is monitored onsite by the BdP inspection teams spread around the country. Regarding coin and banknotes counterfeit analysis: we have a unique organizational model in the Eurosystem, where responsibility is shared between Banco de Portugal and the Criminal Police, which is based on a cooperation agreement that now also covers money laundering. This conference is one of the many examples of the good cooperation between the two institutions, which you will have the opportunity to get to know better during this week. I therefore take this opportunity to acknowledge and thankthe Criminal Policeforthe unsurpassed contribution in organizingthis action. The commitment of Banco de Portugal with promoting the confidence of its citizens in the Euro is also connected to the production and transmission of knowledge, either by the development of studies on cash and its life cycle or by the preparation of materiais and training on the knowledge of Euro coins and banknotes. We are very proud of our e-learning tool that, in Portugal, is the basis of the training of professionals for cash recirculation, and has been adopted by the ECB, the European Commission and many national central banks of the Eurosystem. We also offerfree trainingfor all audiences eager to learn more about Euro coins and banknotes and we have the Museum of Money, which brings Banco de Portugal closer to its citizens and, in an attractive and relaxed way, makes its mission and functions known to the public. Another important aspect in the field of transfer of knowledge is the cooperation with other national central banks, especially those that are historically and culturally closer, such as the Portuguese- speaking countries. The most recent example is the protocol established between Banco de Portugal and Banco de Mozambique, aiming to share technical information and knowledge about Euro and Metical coins and banknotes. As is clear from my brief intervention, the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal values this mission field - Money Issuance - and has a very comprehensive understanding of how we can and must protect the Euro, the citizens and fight counterfeiting. A timely defined strategy for the protection of the Euro mitigates the impact of large-scale cash counterfeiting. And, being a central bank in a country of small dimensions, we are aware that only with an efficient use of the limited technical and human resources available we will succeed in fulfilling this mission, that is why, as you have probably noticed, we like partnerships, synergies and cooperation so much. This Pericles Programme action is a reflection of that Vision. I hope you have a great conference and a wonderful stay in Portugal.

Title: Speech by Administrator Hlder Rosalino at the Commemorative Session of the 15th Anniversary of the National Public Procurement System
text: Speech by Director Helder Rosalino at the Commemorative Session of the 15th Anniversary of the National Public Procurement System 19 October 2022 05 minutes Ladies and Gentlemen, Welcome to Banco de Portugal and the Money Museum. I begin by greeting: The Secretary of State for PCM, Dr. Andre Mos Caldas, The Vice-President of the Mission Structure Recover Portugal, Dr. Mario Tavares Silva, and The President of ESPAP, Dr. Cesar Pestana, and in his person the rest of the Board of Directors of ESPAP, as well as his collaborators. I also greet all the Leaders of the Public Administration present here. It is a pleasure to welcome you all here. It was with great satisfaction that we hosted, in the space of the Money Museum, the Annual Meeting of the European Public Procurement Centres, organised by the Public Administration Shared Services Entity (ESPAP IP). The same satisfaction is naturally extended to this evocative session of the 15th anniversary of the National Public Procurement System (SNCP), addressed to the Public Entities that make up the SNCP, its Directors and other guests. I congratulate ESPAP and its president, Dr. Cesar Pestana, for organizing the event and thank you for inviting me to participate in this session. I do so from two perspectives, which I highly value: The first, of course, on behalf of the Bank of Portugal, in the space of the Money Museum, which I believe demonstrates the Bank's attitude of openness to society. In its Strategic Plan 2021-2025, the Bank defined as a central objective the promotion of proximity and the strengthening of trust among the Portuguese. Openness and participation in initiatives such as this clearly goes in this direction. They demonstrate the Bank's interest and willingness to associate itself with events and themes that, although not at the center of its mission, are relevant in the context of public policies and the development of State functions. Being a Museum, this is the ideal space to connect the past to the future and, in this sense, to contextualize the intervention of the National Public Procurement System in the promotion of a more efficient State and also to envisage investments in the modernization of the Public Administration within the scope of the Recovery and Resilience Plan. The National Public Procurement System celebrates, in 2022, 15 years of existence and has a history of very relevant contributions to improving the efficiency and effectiveness of the Public Administration. It is an unquestionable fact that the modernisation of public procurement, centred on the National Public Procurement System, has assumed a crucial role in the strategy of reducing public expenditure through the centralised contracting of transversal goods and services. But the advantages are not limited to the reduction of spending. The possibility of optimizing and modernizing processes, strengthening specialization and knowledge sharing, creating synergies and scale in procurement processes, increasing bargaining power and transparency in the management of public resources are also very significant advantages that are widely captured by the SNCP. The results of this strategy are very clear for our Public Administration. Some numbers available on the ESPAP website are very illustrative of this:  About 400 million euros of savings obtained by the SNCP by 2021;  More than 2,200 entities linked to the system;  60 framework agreements already concluded;  More than 22 thousand prices on offer available in the shopping catalog. These indicators leave no room for doubt about the benefits already delivered by the SNCP. Looking at the past, albeit more recent, now from another perspective, I cannot fail to also refer to the birth of ESPAP at the time when I held government functions and had responsibilities for the creation and supervision of this Shared Services Entity for Public Administration. In 2012, in the midst of the Economic and Financial Assistance Programme for Portugal and within the scope of the Plan for the Reduction and Improvement of Central Administration, the Public Administration Shared Services Entity, I. P., was created by Decree-Law No. 117-A/2012, of 14 June, which I would like to take this opportunity to congratulate in the person of its president, in the year of his 10th birthday. To date and still today, the provision of shared services in the Public Administration promotes:  The use of common-use solutions and service capacities;  The reduction of administrative effort promoted by the standardization, integration and automation of processes;  The sharing of appropriate tools for the circulation of information and the decision-making process, In summary, it is aimed at:  A more efficient allocation of existing material and human resources;  A reinforcement of the rationality of public action;  A rationalization of the structures crucial in the process of modernization and optimization of the functioning of the State;  A reduction in expenditure, contributing to the balance of public accounts. It was with these objectives that ESPAP took over the mission and attributions of the Institute of Informatics, the Public Administration Shared Resources Management Company, E. P. E. (GeRAP), and the National Public Procurement Agency, E. P. E. (ANCP), all extinguished by merger. ESPAP thus began to ensure the development and provision of shared services within the scope of the Public Administration, as well as to design, manage and evaluate the National Public Procurement System and to ensure the management of the State's Vehicle Park. He was also responsible for defining and implementing strategic policies in the areas of information and communication technologies (ICT) of the Ministry of Finance. With the creation of ESPAP, the conditions were met for an improved and continuous evolution of the projects that had been developed, namely within the scope of the Shared Management of Resources in Public Administration Program, expanding and consolidating the adoption of common technological instruments and solutions in the areas of Financial and Budgetary Resources Management and Human Resources Management, in shared mode and extended to the entire AP. It is in this historical context that my modest contribution, as responsible for public policies in the past, to the evolution in continuity and respect for the evident merits of the National Public Procurement System, whose evocative session we are pleased to host and which I hope will be as fruitful as possible for all present. Thank you very much.

Em 2012, em pleno Programa de Assistncia Econmica e Financeira a Portugal e no mbito do Plano de Reduo e Melhoria da Administrao Central, foi criada pelo Decreto-Lei n. 117-A/2012, de 14 de junho, a Entidade de Servios Partilhados da Administrao Pblica, I. P., que aproveito, desde j, para felicitar na pessoa do seu presidente, no ano do seu 10. aniversrio.  data e ainda hoje a prestao de servios partilhados na Administrao Pblica promove: - O aproveitamento de solues e capacidades de servio de uso comum; - A reduo de esforo administrativo promovida pela uniformizao, integrao e automatizao dos processos; - A partilha de ferramentas adequadas  circulao de informao e ao processo de tomada de deciso, Em sntese, tem-se em vista: - Uma alocao mais eficiente dos recursos materiais e humanos existentes; - Um reforo da racionalidade da atuao pblica; - Uma racionalizao das estruturas crucial no processo de modernizao e de otimizao de funcionamento do Estado; - Uma reduo de despesa, contribuindo para o equilbrio das contas pblicas. Foi com estes objetivos que a ESPAP, assumiu a misso e atribuies do Instituto de Informtica, da Empresa de Gesto Partilhada de Recursos da Administrao Pblica, E. P. E. (GeRAP), e da Agncia Nacional de Compras Pblicas, E. P. E. (ANCP), todos extintos por fuso. A ESPAP passou, assim, a assegurar o desenvolvimento e a prestao de servios partilhados no mbito da Administrao Pblica, bem como a conceber, gerir e avaliar o Sistema Nacional de Compras Pblicas e a assegurar a gesto do Parque de Veculos do Estado. Ficou, ainda, com a responsabilidade pela definio e execuo de polticas estratgicas nas reas das tecnologias de informao e comunicao (TIC) do Ministrio das Finanas. Com a criao da ESPAP, reuniram-se as condies para uma evoluo aperfeioada e em continuidade dos projetos que vinham sendo desenvolvidos, designadamente no mbito do Programa de Gesto Partilhada de Recursos na Administrao Pblica, expandindo e consolidando a adoo de instrumentos e solues tecnolgicas comuns nas reas da Gesto de Recursos Financeiros e Oramentais e da Gesto de Recursos Humanos, em modo partilhado e alargado a toda a AP.  neste contexto histrico que se insere o meu modesto contributo, enquanto responsvel por polticas pblicas no passado, para a evoluo na continuidade e em respeito pelos mritos evidentes do Sistema Nacional de Compras Pblicas, cuja sesso evocativa temos o prazer de acolher e que espero que seja o mais proveitosa possvel para todos os presentes. text: Speech by the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Mario Centeno, at the closing of the Solemn Session of the Financial Education Week 2022 25 October 2022 04 minutes Very good morning, Minister of Education, dear Professor Joao Costa, Madam President of the Insurance and Pension Funds Supervisory Authority, dear Dr. Margarida Correa de Aguiar, Vice-Governor of the Bank of Portugal, dear Dr. Luis Maximo dos Santos, Madam Director of the Bank of Portugal, dear Professor Ana Paula Serra, Dear Director of the Portuguese Securities Market Commission, Mr. Rui Pinto, Dear members of the jury of the Todos Contam Contest, which I greet in the person of its President, Professor Isabel Alcada, Dear partners of the National Plan for Financial Education, Ladies and gentlemen, Financial literacy is an essential skill to achieve full financial citizenship. In times of change in the economic cycle and high inflation, the ability to understand the evolution of the economic and financial situation is even more important; Citizens are better able to mitigate any adverse impacts on their personal finances, becoming more financially resilient. In times of crisis, economies tend to disproportionately penalize the most vulnerable groups. The absence of financial literacy exacerbates the impact by increasing their financial vulnerability. Therefore, financial education is important to promote a more inclusive and less unequal society. But the promotion of financial literacy does not only bring benefits to citizens in their personal sphere. The benefits are also for the economy and society in general. Citizens with greater financial literacy contribute to a more resilient economy. The financial system benefits from consumers who are aware of the characteristics and risks of different financial products and who make choices that are appropriate to their needs, contributing to the development of more efficient and stable financial markets. For the National Council of Financial Supervisors, promoting financial education has been a priority for more than a decade. The National Plan for Financial Education has always sought to empower consumers to better understand financial products and to adopt appropriate financial behaviors. In this area, Portugal is fully aligned with international best practice guidelines. The National Council of Financial Supervisors is committed to the implementation of the financial skills framework for the adult population of the European Union, which the European Commission published in January, in which it was also involved. To date, we are working on the development of a European framework for financial skills for children and young people. In fact, for the National Plan for Financial Education, the financial education of children and young people in schools is an essential and strategic pillar and, therefore, financial supervisors have maintained an active collaboration with the Ministry of Education. Financial education in schools allows you to transmit knowledge and develop in children and young people the most appropriate financial attitudes and behaviors, preparing them for the financial decisions they will make throughout their lives. The first stage of this partnership was the publication, in 2013, of the Financial Education Framework, a guiding document for the implementation of financial education in schools, from pre-school to primary and secondary education. The process of reviewing and updating content, which began this year, was the subject of this morning's panel. This review takes place in parallel with the work of the European Commission, benefiting financial supervisors and the Ministry of Education from the international reflection in which they participate. This year the preparation of a guide to support the pre-school educator also began, when young children begin to distinguish needs and desires and to get to know the concept of saving. With the publication of this notebook, didactic-pedagogical resources will be available for all levels and cycles of education, completing the series of 4 Financial Education Notebooks. All this work is enhanced with the commitment of teachers and schools that assume the promotion of financial education among their activities. Joining the Todos Contam Contest is testimony to this. This year, we received 60 applications for "School Awards", involving 96 schools and more than 9500 students. We award the continuity award aimed at schools with a consistent performance in promoting financial education. And also the award that highlights the importance of the teacher in boosting financial education. The adhesion of schools to the invitation to join the Financial Education Week is proof of how schools recognize, not only the importance of financial education, but also the quality of the materials and training proposals that have been continuously made available through the Todos Contam portal. Ladies and gentlemen, The National Council of Financial Supervisors assigns the National Plan for Financial Education as a strategic priority. But this path is only possible with the active and committed collaboration of our partners. Only with them do financial education initiatives reach multiple population groups. Financial Education Week is a great example of this collaboration. This year we have the involvement of 27 entities and about 400 schools, which will develop more than 500 activities and 8 awareness campaigns for audiences of all ages, through social networks and public and school libraries. As president of the National Council of Financial Supervisors, I reaffirm my commitment to promoting the financial education of the Portuguese through the National Plan for Financial Education. Thank you very much.

Title: Closing speech by Administrator Hlder Rosalino, at the 5th edition of the Fintech meeting: Virtual Assets  Prevention of Money Laundering/Terrorist Financing and MiCA Regulation (on markets in crypto-assets)
text: Closing speech by Director Helder Rosalino, at 5th edition of the Fintech meeting: Virtual Assets - Prevention of money laundering/terrorist financing and MiCA Regulation (on Markets in Crypto-assets) 04 MAY 2023 02 minutes Good afternoon everyone. It was with great interest that I attended the speeches of this FinTech Meeting. In fact, the topic of crypto-assets is on the agenda and has very relevant implications for the financial sector and for the competences of Banco de Portugal. In the current legal framework, the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing in relation to entities carrying out these activities is particularly relevant. But, as we heard here today, in the near future, with the implementation of the MiCA Regulation, we will have changes in the rules applicable to crypto-asset activities and the entities that issue them, across Europe. With this Regulation, we will have a harmonised performance of supervisory authorities at European level. Because if there is an area of the financial sector that clearly goes beyond the country's borders, it is the area of activities with cryptoassets, whether for investment purposes or for payment purposes. And it is this aspect of the potential use of crypto-assets as a payment instrument, even if they are an instrument without legal tender or mandatory acceptance, that is the most sensitive for Central Banks, due to the impact that this use, if generalized on a global scale, can have on their own functions, such as promoting the correct functioning of payment systems, the appropriate transmission of monetary policy or the maintenance of financial stability. Cryptoassets are an area of the financial sector that is undergoing profound transformation, which neither innovators, nor incumbents, nor regulators can ignore. But they are not the only one, quite the contrary. We are in a context of accelerated technological evolution, the implications of which are being felt at various levels and to which all actors in the financial system are adapting. First of all, users, who increasingly demand digital, agile and convenient solutions, both to make payments and in other areas of their financial life. Market agents also have to adapt to this evolution, evolving their systems, offering new services and even changing their own business models, namely to better cope with the increased competition they face. Central banks, legislators and regulators also need to adapt the applicable legal framework, and their supervisory practices, in order to promote innovation, while ensuring adequate levels of security and the appropriate leading field. More than regulating and supervising entities, it is increasingly urgent to regulate and properly supervise activities. And this is, without a doubt, the ultimate objective of the framework applicable to crypto-assets, both with regard to the entities that issue them and the related activities that are provided with these crypto-assets. On the part of Banco de Portugal, we are committed to working to collaborate with supervised entities, other economic agents and society as a whole, in promoting understanding, and consequent compliance, with the applicable legal framework. We will, as before, monitor ongoing market developments with a view to identifying potential areas where changes to the existing framework are necessary. This Fintech Meeting is part of this line of action, of proximity, dialogue and cooperation, in this case, with a focus on cryptoassets. I hope you found this sharing useful. I conclude by thanking you for your presence and wishing you all a good rest of the day.

Title: Opening speech by Administrator Hlder Rosalino at the Conference "The rise of AI and its implications for Cybersecurity"
text: Opening speech by Director Helder Rosalino at Conferencia "The rise of Al and its implications for Cybersecurity" 26 October 2023 04 minutes Good afternoon, welcome to Banco de Portugal A greeting to all those present, and in particular to the external speakers:  Luis Rato, National Security Officer da Microsoft Portugal, e  Prof. Miguel Pupo Correia, President of the Department of Computer Engineering at Instituto Superior Tecnico Special thanks also to Pedro Rodrigues for the initiative of organizing this conference and, by the way, for the quality of the work he has been developing as Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) of Banco de Portugal. This event takes place as part of Banco de Portugal's initiatives to mark the European Cybersecurity Month, a programme developed since 2012 by the European Cybersecurity Agency. Among the various activities that we have been developing in this area, involving several departments, this event is especially relevant. Not only because of the presence of renowned speakers from academia and industry, but also because it aims to give a clearer view of how Banco de Portugal sees the impact of Artificial Intelligence on its Cybersecurity strategy. It is a commonplace to say that Artificial Intelligence is a technology that is increasingly integrated into our daily lives. It is no longer so common to mention that Artificial Intelligence is also increasingly used, by criminal agents, to seek to overcome the defense mechanisms of organizations in the face of cyberattacks, with a special focus on the financial sector. In recent times, we have witnessed the democratization of the use of very powerful Artificial Intelligence solutions, which provide a giant leap in the reach and results of this technology. This democratization has allowed the use of artificial intelligence in multiple dimensions. However, these dimensions are not always the most virtuous, as we will see throughout this session. In the context of Cybersecurity (what interests us today), Artificial Intelligence presents a set of challenges, but also positive impacts that we can take advantage of. On the challenge side, it is essential to identify the risks associated with the use of Artificial Intelligence in our systems, with special emphasis on data processing and inherent protection of both personal data and confidential information. In addition, the risks of over-reliance on the use of Artificial Intelligence must be considered, with the impact that may arise in terms of loss of internal knowledge and lack of transparency or errors in the automatic processing of information. By being a "black box", an Artificial Intelligence system may not be able to justify decision-making, creating potential situations of injustice and discrimination. But perhaps the biggest challenge that we can already identify in the use of Artificial Intelligence is the universal availability of this technology (that is, its democratization). This phrase may seem paradoxical, since we usually associate the universality of a new technology with a positive aspect. What this statement means is that Artificial Intelligence solutions will not only be available to organizations that want to increase their efficiency, but also to all malicious actors that aim to carry out cyberattacks against those organizations. In the same way that Artificial Intelligence platforms allow Banco de Portugal to improve its processes (ALYA), they will also allow these external actors to collect information on possible technological or procedural weaknesses that they can exploit to achieve their ends. The financial sector is beginning to face increasingly advanced and targeted fraud attempts, which require prior knowledge of information that until now would take a long time to collect. Currently, using Artificial Intelligence, access to this information becomes almost immediate. Using traditional methods (i.e., in the past), with a high manual effort, attackers directed their efforts to targets with high potential, for example boards of large companies, where, in case of success, their return would be high. With the use of Artificial Intelligence (i.e., in the present) attackers can easily collect public information from multiple sources and combine it to conduct targeted cyberattacks in a much more cost-effective way. Using financial terminology, Artificial Intelligence has significantly increased the ROI of cybercriminals! This development requires central banks and financial institutions to respond quickly in anti-fraud capacities. And it is at this point that it makes sense to address the enormous potential that Artificial Intelligence also brings to organizations' cybersecurity teams, which we can call "the good side of the force". Being aware of the use of Artificial Intelligence platforms by attackers, it is essential that the teams in charge of protecting organizations also have access to this type of tools. It will be impossible to detect and respond to attacks that use Artificial Intelligence using only manual procedures or technology with an efficiency that is well below that of attackers. At today's event, we will have the opportunity to learn, through Pedro Rodrigues, a little better about how Banco de Portugal's Cybersecurity and IT Compliance area is monitoring the impacts of Artificial Intelligence on Cybersecurity, both from the point of view of threats and opportunities to improve its teams and platforms. We will also hear from Prof. Miguel Pupo Correia to give an overview of how academia has been developing research work in this area. On the part of the head of the Cybersecurity area at Microsoft Portugal, Luis Rato, will come the vision of how Artificial Intelligence can enhance the products of this technological partner of the Bank of Portugal, especially Cybersecurity products. We will continue with a round table with the presence of the two guest speakers, as well as the Data Protection Office of Banco de Portugal, where we will seek to explore the compliance, privacy and data protection issues that are essential in the strategy for adopting Artificial Intelligence in our institution. The session will be closed by Carlos Moura, Director of the DSI of the BdP. Thank you
text_original: Interveno de abertura do Administrador Hlder Rosalino na Conferncia "The rise of Al and its implications for Cybersecurity" 26 outubro 2023 04 minutos Boa tarde, bem-vindos ao Banco de Portugal Uma saudao a todos os presentes, e em particular aos oradores externos:  Lus Rato, National Security Officer da Microsoft Portugal, e  Prof. Miguel Pupo Correia, Presidente do Departamento de Engenharia Informtica do Instituto Superior Tcnico Um agradecimento especial tambm ao Pedro Rodrigues pela iniciativa da organizao desta conferncia e, j agora, pela qualidade do trabalho que tem vindo a desenvolver como Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) do Banco de Portugal. Este evento decorre no mbito das iniciativas do Banco de Portugal para assinalar o ms Europeu da Cibersegurana, um programa desenvolvido, desde 2012, pela Agncia Europeia para a Cibersegurana. De entre as diversas atividades que temos vindo a desenvolver neste mbito, envolvendo vrios departamentos, este evento assume especial relevncia. No s pela presena de reputados oradores da academia e da indstria, mas tambm porque pretende dar uma viso mais clara sobre a forma como o Banco de Portugal encara o impacto da Inteligncia Artificial na sua estratgia de Cibersegurana.  um lugar-comum dizer que Inteligncia Artificial  uma tecnologia cada vez mais integrada no nosso dia-a-dia. Nos ltimos tempos, assistimos  democratizao da utilizao de solues de Inteligncia Artificial muito poderosas, que proporcionam um salto gigante no alcance e resultados desta tecnologia. No contexto da Cibersegurana (o que nos interessa hoje), a Inteligncia Artificial apresenta um conjunto de desafios, mas tambm de impactos positivos dos quais podemos tirar partido. Do lado dos desafios,  essencial identificar os riscos associados  utilizao de Inteligncia Artificial nos nossos sistemas, com especial destaque para o tratamento dos dados e inerente proteo quer dos dados pessoais, quer da informao confidencial. Adicionalmente, devem ser considerados os riscos de dependncia excessiva da utilizao de Inteligncia Artificial, com o impacto que da poder advir ao nvel da perda de conhecimento interno e da falta de transparncia ou erros no processamento automtico de informao. Ao ser uma caixa negra, um sistema de Inteligncia Artificial poder no conseguir justificar a tomada de decises, criando potenciais situaes de injustia e discriminao. Mas talvez o maior desafio que podemos, desde j, identificar na utilizao de Inteligncia Artificial seja a disponibilidade universal desta tecnologia (ou seja, a sua democratizao).
