BANKING GROUPS Special inspections focused on the eight largest domestic groups, which represent around 80% of the banking system: Banco Comercial Portugues (BCP), Banco BPI (BPI), Caixa Geral de Depositos (CGD), Espirito Santo Financial Group (ESFG), Caixa Economica Montepio Geral (CEMG), Santander Totta (BST), Rentipar Financeira (BANIF) and Sistema Integrado do Credito Agricola Mutuo (SICAM, Integrated Mutual Agricultural Credit Scheme). ORGANISATION Given the defined objectives, scope and timeline, both the credit portfolio valuation and the assessment of the adequacy of the methodologies and tools used in stress test exercises were carried out with recourse to specialised outsourcing, in strict cooperation with Banco de Portugal. Credit portfolios were valuated by Ernst & Young Audit & Associados  SROC, S.A. and PricewaterhouseCoopers & Associados  Sociedade de Revisores Oficiais de Contas, Lda. Four banking groups were allocated to each audit firm, taking into account the need to ensure a balanced workload as well as the minimisation of any conflicts of interest. As regards stress test exercises, Oliver Wyman provided the specialised outsourced services. Valuation of credit portfolios, capital requirements and tools and methodologies of the stress test exercises involved auditors, consultants and Banco de Portugal staff, totalling around 350. STEERING COMMITTEE To monitor implementation of the programme, a Steering Committee was set up, chaired by Banco de Portugal and composed of representatives of the International Monetary Fund, the European Commission, the European Central Bank and three European Union supervisors  Banco de Espana, Autorite de Controle Prudentiel (France) and Banque Nationale de Belgique  as well as Banco de Portugal. In July 2011 the Steering Committee approved the Terms of Reference for the work to be carried out, which defined the scope, methodological approach, implementation timelines, and monitoring and control mechanisms to be adopted. RESULTS The Special On-site Inspections Programme results on the credit portfolios of the eight main Portuguese banking groups as at 30 June 2011 essentially validate data used to support their solvency assessment, confirming the resilience and financial soundness of the Portuguese banking system as at that date. The overall impact of SIP results on the aggregate Tier 1 ratio of the eight banking groups as a whole would imply a minor revision of this ratio at the end of June 2011, from 9.1% to 8.8%, remaining above the minimum 8% required on that date. Impairment Audit firms have analysed individual impairment levels of a judgmental sample, covering for each banking group the 50 economic groups with the highest credit exposures, as well as other groups and entities whose exposures were selected on the basis of a comprehensive set of credit risk indicators. For some credits updated valuations performed by independent experts were considered for a few assets pledged as collateral. In total, 5,516 borrowers and 61,531 credit files were assessed on an individual basis, covering more than 50% of the credit portfolio under inspection. As regards collective impairment, there was an assessment of the assumptions, methodology and the historical information incorporated in the model supporting the respective calculation in each banking group. Also, sensitivity analyses were performed on the main parameters and on the estimated impact of the main areas for improvement identified. In addition, credit risk management policies were analysed, including the main control procedures, with emphasis on the valuation of collateral and problem assets. The work done led to the conclusion that credit risk management policies and their control procedures are generally suitable, although there are areas for improvement. As at 30 June 2011 estimates pointed to a need to reinforce the value of impairment recorded for the credit portfolio analysed by 838 million (not considering impairment buffers existing on that date), so as to achieve robust provisioning levels. This amount corresponded to 9.1% of total impairment recognised for credits within the scope of the SIP and 0.3% of the total amount of such credits. The impact on total impairments of the eight banking groups was nevertheless smaller, given that the above reinforcement needs were partly offset (by 242 million) by the reallocation of impairments identified as available on 30 June 2011  regarding the overall credit portfolios amounting to 339 million. Additionally, in the third quarter of 2011, the eight banking groups recorded an impairment reinforcement of 208 million for some of the exposures where the need to reinforce impairment was identified. Capital requirements The validation of the capital calculations involved the collection and validation of relevant data for each of the eight banking groups and a recalculation of the requirements through a specially developed tool. Work related to this SIP workstream was carried out by teams from Banco de Portugal and included revising credit risk capital requirements calculations (which accounted for about 90% of capital requirements for the eight banking groups). Banco de Portugal has processed around 16.6 million contracts/exposures relating to nearly 7.7 million debtors and incorporating the effect of 2.3 million risk mitigation techniques. With regard to the assessment of credit risk capital requirements calculations, the work has identified a need for one-off corrections. As at 30 June 2011, this totals, in the eight banking groups as a whole, around 0.6% of total estimated capital requirements. Banco de Portugal also assessed risk control and management procedures underlying the calculation of risk-weighted assets and concluded that these are generally adequate. Stress test methodologies and tools Under the Economic and Financial Assistance Programme, Banco de Portugal was tasked with conducting regular stress test exercises, in order to evaluate the resilience of the largest Portuguese banking groups should the identified risks materialise in an adverse scenario. Workstream 3 of the SIP was forward-looking, with the purpose of gauging the adequacy of the tools and methodologies used by banks in financial forecasts supporting the assessment of their future solvency. The work carried out led to the following classification of banking groups: Institutions that have used clearly adequate tools and methodologies: two banking groups Institutions that have used adequate tools and methodologies: one banking group Institutions that have used adequate tools and methodologies in most aspects analysed, but need to improve a number of areas: four banking groups, and Institutions that need improvement in a series of specific areas so that the tools and methodologies used may be considered adequate: one banking group FOLLOW UP Once the aspects marked for improvement were identified for all banking groups, Banco de Portugal required the adoption of adequate corrective measures, with clearly defined priorities and implementation timelines. Banco de Portugal has adopted procedures for the regular monitoring of implementation of the corrective measures, based on a timeline agreed with banking groups.

Title: Opening speech by Administrator Luis Maximo dos Santos at the III Meeting on Inclusion and Financial Training of central banks of Portuguese-speaking countries (BCPLP)
text: III Meeting on The Inclusion and Financial Training of Central Banks of Portuguese-speaking Countries (BCPLP) July 6, 2017 Opening speech of Administrator Luis Maximo dos Santos 1 1 Prepared for presentation. 1. Welcome to Portugal, Lisbon and Banco de Portugal. Welcome to this III Meeting on Inclusion and Financial Training. I greet the Central Bank of S. Tome and Principe, the Central Bank of Timor-Leste, the Central Bank of Brazil, the Central Bank of West African States, the Bank of Cape Verde, the Bank of Mozambique, the National Bank of Angola, as well as all the distinguished members of their delegations, whose presence I thank and greatly honor us. I also greet all the other participants in this Meeting, which for the first time this year is attended by The Alliance for Financial Inclusion, to whom I also greet and welcome, in the person of its Executive Director. 2. In good time, in 2013, these Meetings began, which continued in 2015, and the one that we continue today with the third edition. Organizing this Meeting is an honorable responsibility for us but also a great pleasure. In fact, the issue of inclusion and financial training has been increasingly recognised as a priority issue on the international agenda for its implications for promoting financial stability and economic development. The BCPLP Meetings on inclusion and financial training highlight the importance that the central banks of the Lusophone space attach to the sharing of knowledge and experiences on initiatives to promote inclusion and financial training. The richness of the sharing of experiences and good practices that took place in the first two meetings led to the publication of reports on inclusion and financial training initiatives in Portuguese-speaking countries. I am sure that the developments of the last two years in this area, in the various countries, and which will be presented and analysed today and tomorrow, will justify the preparation of a new report with the conclusions of this THIRD Meeting. Throughout these Meetings, the following subjects have been densified: (i) The 1st Meeting in 2013 reflected on the role of central banks and international best practices in promoting inclusion and financial training; (ii) The Second Meeting in 2015 addressed the themes of financial education in schools, the means of distance learning and the importance of partnerships for the success and sustainability of inclusion and financial training policies. In this III Meeting, in addition to deepening the areas of financial education in schools, a strategic pillar of the formation of the whole population and in particular of the youngest, new topics will be addressed, including the evaluation of financial training initiatives and training for the proper use of financial products and services through digital channels. I would like to stress that a great added value of sharing experiences in these Meetings is the diversity of approaches. While we all have a common goal, to increase the levels of inclusion and financial literacy of the population and, ultimately, the well-being of citizens, the ways of achieving that can be - and certainly are - different. It is therefore important that we get to know the various approaches better, take advantage of the diversity of experiences and adapt them to the economic, financial and institutional context of each country. The discussion of these matters is very stimulating because of the complexity they are in, but it also has a particularly gratifying dimension because of the implications that we know they can have on improving the lives of concrete people. These reasons would already be more than enough for us to provide for two excellent working and sharing days. But there is an additional reason for it to become an added pleasure: to do all this in Portuguese, a language that instantly brings us closer together and reminds us of the fact that our countries are actors of a globalization that also expresses itself and feels in the enriching diversity of the changing of a language that is common to us. 3. Financial inclusion is an essential component of social inclusion, as by creating conditions for better management of the family budget, greater efficiency in the use of means of payment and, as well as the application of savings in appropriate products and the more secure contracting of credit, provides more efficient management of personal finances. It cannot be lost in fact that financial inclusion also helps to combat inequality, a major problem in contemporary economies. As European Central Bank President Mario Draghi pointed out a day ago at a Meeting in Lisbon with young university students, "inequality is a highly destabilizing phenomenon for all areas of our society, including financial stability." Traditionally, the main barriers to financial inclusion are related to factors of geographical proximity, such as the low density of branches of credit institutions, which hinders access to the formal financial sector. Such barriers provide for an informal sector that provides competing financial products and services, not subject to financial regulation, but to which citizens access more easily. Other exclusion factors are the high costs of financial services in the formal sector or the non-availability by credit institutions of products with characteristics appropriate to the needs of consumers with low incomes and/or low levels of education. However, the increasing digitisation of financial services brings new opportunities to promote financial inclusion, allowing some of these obstacles to be overcome, as digital channels make access easier and lower costs. The commercialization of financial products and services through digital channels allows the population to access, even in the absence of proximity to service providers, to financial products made available through these channels, which are generally simpler and more standardized. However, digital channels have also associated new risks. First of all, the risks related to the security of access and use of digital channels and the need to take appropriate fraud prevention behaviour. But also the risk of less weighted acquisition of financial products and services, including recourse to credit without adequate clarification of the associated financial conditions and the consequences of non-compliance. On the other hand, digital channels are not the solution for the inclusion of more vulnerable population groups, such as older people, who generally have greater difficulty in dealing with technology. Therefore, despite the new opportunities brought by digital channels, new risks must be addressed. And also recognise that many of the traditional challenges of promoting financial inclusion remain. As the need for the financial inclusion strategy based on three pillars also remains: (i) policies promoting financial inclusion; (ii) proper regulation of financial products and services; and (iii) Population financial training initiatives. 4. Financial training is essential for the proper financial inclusion of persons who currently do not have access to the financial system and, in particular, to a bank account. Through financial training, basic knowledge is transmitted, but also becomes aware of the need for prudent behaviour in the access and use of banking products. A challenge of training that aims at financial inclusion is to reach this training to the audiences that need it, which are usually the most vulnerable population groups. An example that we have in Portugal is the challenge of the dissemination of minimum banking services, consisting of a bank account and basic payment services. Institutions are obliged to make these minimum banking services available at a reduced cost, but they are not known to the general population and, even less, to those excluded from the financial system and who could benefit most from their use. But of course financial training is not only important to the population excluded from the financial system. Financial training is important for the general population, as it promotes the responsible and efficient use of financial products and services, alerting to the advantages and risks associated with financial products and services made available by credit institutions and the rights and duties of financial consumers. A greater understanding of products and the financial system empowers citizens to make financial decisions and make choices that are more appropriate to their needs. The promotion of financial training faces important challenges, in particular, as has already been said, to cover the entire population, which is not necessarily homogeneous, has diverse characteristics and needs. Therefore, it is important to define the appropriate themes and means to reach each population group, choose messages that are properly perceited by the target audience and find the partners indicated to work with these audiences. Another factor that cannot be ignored is the cost of financial training initiatives, which leads to the need for a gradual approach and an evaluation that allows us to know the effectiveness of the action and direct the commitment of training to the initiatives with better results. 5. Banco de Portugal has been committed to promoting financial training for several years. A few years ago, in international forums, the importance of central banks and financial regulators to be involved in financial training initiatives. This is the question of this issue today, because it is common place that it should be, as citizens with higher levels of financial literacy choose financial products more appropriately and therefore contribute to financial stability and more sustained economic growth. Nine years ago, Banco de Portugal launched the Banking Client Portal, an initiative that marked the beginning of a more structured strategy to promote financial training. Since then, it has published brochures and leaflets of information and training on banking products and services and has deduring numerous financial training actions, which have the support of the Bank's Regional Network. On the other hand, in partnership with the other financial supervisors, since 2011 it has streamlined the National Financial Training Plan, which includes several initiatives that will certainly be the subject of specific reference throughout the work. Such initiatives are carried out in partnership with public and private entities, involving schools, companies and local authorities, among others. 6. We want to make these two days the guarantee that the interest for the IV Meeting is already launched. On the part of Banco de Portugal, in addition to sharing our experience, we are very interested in knowing the recent developments of inclusion and financial training initiatives in your countries, so that we can all make the best use of the experiences that will be presented here. We have always believed that together, in reflection and cooperation, we have achieved our goals better. Allow me a final word, more focused on the institution to which I belong, to thank the commitment of all those in Banco de Portugal worked to make this THIRD Meeting a reality. And among them, allow me, in the person of your Director, Mrs. Lucia Leitao, to thank, in particular, the Department of Behavioral Supervision, which gave herself heart and soul to the initiative.
text_original: III Encontro sobre Incluso e Formao Financeira dos Bancos Centrais dos Pases de Lngua Portuguesa (BCPLP) 6 de julho de 2017 Interveno de abertura do Administrador Lus Mximo dos Santos 1 1 Preparado para apresentao. 1. Sejam muito bem-vindos a Portugal, a Lisboa e ao Banco de Portugal. Sejam muito bem-vindos a este III Encontro sobre Incluso e Formao Financeira. Sado o Banco Central de S. Tom e Prncipe, o Banco Central de Timor-Leste, o Banco Central do Brasil, o Banco Central dos Estados da frica Ocidental, o Banco de Cabo Verde, o Banco de Moambique, o Banco Nacional de Angola, bem como todos os ilustres membros das respetivas delegaes, cuja presena agradeo e muito nos honra. Cumprimento tambm todos os demais participantes neste Encontro, que pela primeira vez este ano conta com a presena da AFI  Alliance for Financial Inclusion, a quem igualmente sado e apresento as boas vindas, na pessoa do seu Diretor Executivo. 2. Em boa hora, em 2013, se deu incio a estes Encontros, que tiveram continuidade em 2015, e a que hoje damos sequncia com a terceira edio. Organizar este Encontro  para ns uma honrosa responsabilidade mas tambm enorme prazer. De facto, o tema da incluso e da formao financeira tem sido cada vez mais reconhecido como uma matria prioritria da agenda internacional pelas suas implicaes na promoo da estabilidade financeira e do desenvolvimento econmico. Os Encontros dos BCPLP sobre incluso e formao financeira evidenciam a importncia que os bancos centrais do espao lusfono atribuem  partilha de conhecimentos e experincias sobre iniciativas de promoo da incluso e da formao financeira. A riqueza da partilha de experincias e boas prticas que teve lugar nos dois primeiros encontros levou  publicao de relatrios sobre as iniciativas de incluso e formao financeira nos pases de lngua portuguesa. Estou certo que os desenvolvimentos dos dois ltimos anos nesta rea, nos vrios pases, e que hoje e amanh sero apresentados e analisados, vo justificar a elaborao de um novo relatrio com as concluses deste III Encontro. Ao longo destes Encontros tm-se densificado as matrias em anlise: (i) No I Encontro, em 2013, refletiu-se sobre o papel dos bancos centrais e as melhores prticas internacionais de promoo da incluso e da formao financeira; (ii) No II Encontro, em 2015, abordaram-se os temas da educao financeira nas escolas, dos meios de formao  distncia e da importncia das parcerias para o sucesso e sustentabilidade das polticas de incluso e formao financeira. Neste III Encontro, alm de se aprofundarem as matrias de educao financeira nas escolas, pilar estratgico da formao de toda a populao e em particular dos mais jovens, sero abordados novos temas, nomeadamente a avaliao das iniciativas de formao financeira e a formao para a utilizao adequada de produtos e servios financeiros atravs de canais digitais. Gostaria de realar que uma grande mais-valia da partilha de experincias nestes Encontros  a diversidade de abordagens. Ainda que todos tenhamos um objetivo comum, o de aumentar os nveis de incluso e de literacia financeira da populao e, em ltima anlise, o bem-estar dos cidados, as formas de alcanar esse objetivo podem ser - e so certamente - diferentes. Por isso,  importante conhecermos melhor as vrias abordagens, tirar proveito da diversidade de experincias e adapt-las ao contexto econmico, financeiro e institucional de cada pas. A discusso destas matrias  bastante estimulante pela complexidade de que se revestem mas comporta tambm uma dimenso especialmente gratificante pelas implicaes que sabemos que podem ter na melhoria da vida de pessoas concretas. Estas razes j seriam mais do que suficientes para que possamos prever dois excelentes dias de trabalho e de partilha. Mas h uma razo a adicional para que se torne um prazer acrescido: o fazermos tudo isto em portugus, lngua que instantaneamente nos aproxima e nos lembra o facto de que os nossos pases so atores de uma globalizao que tambm se exprime e sente na diversidade enriquecedora dos cambiantes duma lngua que nos  comum. 3. A incluso financeira  uma componente essencial da incluso social, na medida em que ao criar condies para uma melhor gesto do oramento familiar, uma maior eficincia na utilizao dos meios de pagamento e, bem assim, a aplicao de poupanas em produtos adequados e a contratao de crdito de forma mais segura, proporciona uma gesto mais eficiente das finanas pessoais. No pode perder-se de vista, de facto, que a incluso financeira ajuda tambm a combater a desigualdade, problema maior das economias contemporneas. Como bem assinalou h dias o Presidente do Banco Central Europeu, Mario Draghi, num Encontro em Lisboa com jovens universitrios, a desigualdade  um fenmeno altamente desestabilizador para todas as reas da nossa sociedade, incluindo a estabilidade financeira. Tradicionalmente, as principais barreiras  incluso financeira esto relacionadas com fatores de proximidade geogrfica, como a fraca densidade de balces das instituies de crdito, que dificulta o acesso ao setor financeiro formal. Tais barreiras proporcionam a existncia de um setor informal que disponibiliza produtos e servios financeiros concorrentes, no sujeitos  regulao financeira, mas a que os cidados acedem com mais facilidade. Outros fatores de excluso so os custos elevados dos servios financeiros no setor formal ou a no disponibilizao pelas instituies de crdito de produtos com caractersticas adequadas s necessidades de consumidores com baixos rendimentos e/ou baixos nveis de escolaridade. Todavia, a crescente digitalizao dos servios financeiros traz novas oportunidades de promoo da incluso financeira, permitindo ultrapassar alguns destes obstculos, na medida em que os canais digitais tornam o acesso mais fcil e com menores custos. A comercializao de produtos e servios financeiros atravs de canais digitais permite o acesso da populao, mesmo na ausncia de proximidade com os prestadores dos servios, aos produtos financeiros disponibilizados atravs destes canais, que so geralmente mais simples e padronizados. Contudo, os canais digitais tm tambm associados novos riscos. Desde logo, os riscos relacionados com a segurana do acesso e utilizao dos canais digitais e a necessidade de adoo de comportamentos adequados de preveno da fraude. Mas tambm o risco de aquisio menos ponderada de produtos e servios financeiros, nomeadamente de recurso ao crdito sem o adequado esclarecimento das condies financeiras associadas e das consequncias do incumprimento. Por outro lado, os canais digitais no so a soluo para a incluso de grupos populacionais mais vulnerveis, como as pessoas mais idosas, que tm geralmente maior dificuldade em lidar com a tecnologia. Por isso, apesar das novas oportunidades trazidas pelos canais digitais, h que atender aos novos riscos. E reconhecer, igualmente, que muitos dos tradicionais desafios de promoo da incluso financeira se mantm. Como se mantm tambm a necessidade da estratgia de incluso financeira assentar em 3 pilares: (i) Polticas de promoo da incluso financeira; (ii) Regulao adequada dos produtos e servios financeiros; e (iii) Iniciativas de formao financeira da populao. 4. A formao financeira  essencial para uma incluso financeira adequada das pessoas que atualmente no tm acesso ao sistema financeiro e, em particular, a uma conta bancria. Atravs da formao financeira transmitem-se conhecimentos bsicos, mas tambm se sensibiliza para a necessidade da adoo de comportamentos prudentes no acesso e utilizao de produtos bancrios. Um desafio da formao que tem por objetivo a incluso financeira  o de fazer chegar essa formao aos pblicos que dela precisam, que so geralmente grupos populacionais mais vulnerveis. Um exemplo que temos em Portugal  o desafio da divulgao dos servios mnimos bancrios, constitudos por uma conta bancria e por servios de pagamento bsicos. As instituies so obrigadas a disponibilizar estes servios mnimos bancrios a um custo reduzido, mas eles no so conhecidos pela generalidade da populao e, ainda menos, pelos que esto excludos do sistema financeiro e que mais poderiam beneficiar da sua utilizao. Mas naturalmente que a formao financeira no  apenas importante para a populao excluda do sistema financeiro. A formao financeira  importante para a generalidade da populao, pois promove a utilizao responsvel e eficiente dos produtos e servios financeiros, alertando para as vantagens e riscos associados aos produtos e servios financeiros disponibilizados pelas instituies de crdito e para os direitos e deveres dos consumidores financeiros. Uma maior compreenso dos produtos e do sistema financeiro capacita os cidados para tomarem decises financeiras e fazerem escolhas mais adequadas s suas necessidades. A promoo da formao financeira enfrenta importantes desafios, nomeadamente, como j se referiu, o de abranger toda a populao, a qual, necessariamente, no  homognea, tem caractersticas e necessidades diversificadas. Por isso,  desde logo importante definir os temas e meios adequados para chegar a cada grupo populacional, escolher mensagens que sejam devidamente percecionadas pelo pblico-alvo e encontrar os parceiros indicados para trabalhar com esses pblicos. Outro fator que no pode ser ignorado  o do custo das iniciativas de formao financeira, o que leva  necessidade de uma abordagem gradual e de uma avaliao que permita conhecer a eficcia da ao e direcionar a aposta da formao para as iniciativas com melhores resultados. 5. O Banco de Portugal est h vrios anos empenhado na promoo da formao financeira. H alguns anos atrs, nos fruns internacionais, discutia-se a importncia dos bancos centrais e dos reguladores financeiros estarem envolvidos em iniciativas de formao financeira. Tal questo hoje em dia a questo no se coloca, pois  ponto assente que assim deve ser, uma vez que cidados com maiores nveis de literacia financeira escolhem produtos financeiros de forma mais adequadas e contribuem, por isso, para a estabilidade financeira e um crescimento econmico mais sustentado. H nove anos, o Banco de Portugal lanou o Portal do Cliente Bancrio, uma iniciativa que marcou o incio de uma estratgia mais estruturada de promoo da formao financeira. Desde a, publicou brochuras e desdobrveis de informao e formao sobre produtos e servios bancrios e dinamizou inmeras aes de formao financeira, que contam com o apoio da Rede Regional do Banco. Por outro lado, em parceria com os outros supervisores financeiros, dinamiza desde 2011 o Plano Nacional de Formao Financeira, que contempla diversas iniciativas que ao longo dos trabalhos sero certamente objeto de referncia especfica. Tais iniciativas so efetuadas em parceria com entidades pblicas e privadas, envolvendo escolas, empresas e autarquias locais, entre outras. 6. Queremos fazer destes dois dias a garantia de que fica j lanado o interesse para o IV Encontro. Da parte do Banco de Portugal, alm da partilha da nossa experincia, estamos muito interessados em conhecer os desenvolvimentos recentes das iniciativas de incluso e formao financeira nos vossos pases, para que possamos todos aproveitar da melhor forma as experincias que vo ser aqui apresentadas. Sempre acreditmos que juntos, na reflexo e na cooperao, atingimos melhor os nossos objetivos. Permitam-me uma palavra final, mais virada para a instituio a que perteno, para agradecer o empenho de todos quantos no Banco de Portugal trabalharam para que este III Encontro seja uma realidade. E de entre eles, permita-me que, na pessoa da sua Diretora, a Senhora Dra. Lcia Leito, agradea, em particular, ao Departamento de Superviso Comportamental, que se entregou de alma e corao  iniciativa.

Title: Opening speech by the Director of the Department of Statistics Joo Cadete de Matos at the 2nd Session of the 6th Conference of the Balance Sheet Center
text: BP logo.jpg Opening speech of the Director of the Department of Statistics Joao Cadete de Matos in the 2nd Session of the 6th Conference of the Central Balance Sheet evora, Auditorium of the Eugenio de Almeida Foundation, March 29, 2017 Modernization of the Corporate Fabric Portuguese Panel on the wine and wine tourism sector Banco de Portugal's Balance Sheet Center Banco de Portugal's Balance Sheet Center is a database with annual and quarterly economic and financial information on non-financial corporations in Portugal. This database has existed in Banco de Portugal since 1983 and serves several functions of Banco de Portugal, namely those associated with the supervision and stability of the financial system, the analysis of the national economic situation and the compilation of statistics. Since 2007, Banco de Portugal's Balance Sheet Center has been the main source of annual information for IES  Simplified Business Information, thus covering practically the entire universe of non-financial corporations in Portugal, or about 400,000. The main statistical series obtained from this database (Statistics of Non-Financial Companies and Industry Tables) can be found at BPStat Online statistics, the statistical dissemination portal of Banco de Portugal. One of the products of the Balance Sheet Center that is made available every year by Banco de Portugal to companies corresponds to the Company and Sector Framework, which allows each company to compare its economic and financial situation with the other companies in the same sector of activity, thus constituting a very useful tool for business management. The information from the Balance Sheet Centre is also available to the general public, in particular to researchers, who can access a wide range of indicators on Portuguese companies, with a high degree of detail per sector of activity. Participation in the European Committee of Central Balance Sheets Since its foundation in 1987, Banco de Portugal has been part of the European Committee of Central Balance-Sheet Data Offices (ECCBSO), whose objective is the development of balance sheet centers as a privileged source of information on non-financial corporations in the various countries, as well as the promotion of their use in the functions of central banks, not only in the dissemination of statistics or studies, but also in terms of macroprudential functions and financial stability, and Banco de Portugal has assumed the chairmanship of that Committee during the last three years. Banco de Portugal regularly contributes information to BACH (Bank for the Accounts of Companies Harmonized), a European economic and financial information database for non-financial companies in several countries. The Studies of the Balance Sheet Center In order to promote greater and better use of the information disclosed by the various categories of users, Banco de Portugal began in 2010 the publication of the Studies of the Central Balance Sheet, and so far 27 studies have been published. The Studies of the Balance Sheet Center are an important tool for reading the statistical information of the Balance Sheet Center. These studies may take on a methodological nature, functioning as explanatory manuals of the information of the Central Balance Sheets, or may have a more generic nature, being dedicated to a general analysis of the situation of non-financial companies in Portugal. These studies have been updated annually since 2010, presenting an in-depth analysis of the Portuguese business fabric based on a wide range of economic and financial indicators. On the other hand, the Studies of the Balance Sheet Center include the dissemination of sector analyses, dedicated to specific sectors of activity. Sectors as varied as textiles and clothing, footwear, food industries or accommodation and catering are among the sectors already studied, in addition to the beverage industry (the target of the most recently published study), sectors as varied as textiles and clothing, footwear, food industries or accommodation and catering, including sectors such as construction, information and communication activities, the agricultural sector, tourism, the metal-industry or the pharmaceutical sector, to name just a few cases. Banco de Portugal has sought to monitor the evolution of the most dynamic sectors, also reflecting on their regional importance and their contribution to exports, and in this regard carried out a specific analysis of the sector of exporting companies. The sector studies of the Balance Sheet Center carried out so far have allowed to cover about half of the non-financial companies in activity in Portugal, portraying sectors that generate two-thirds of turnover and employ about 60 percent of the people at the service. The Balance Sheet Center Conferences The Conferences of the Central Balance Sheet, which also began in 2010, followed the publication of the above-mentioned sectoral studies, constituting an initiative of Banco de Portugal that aims not only to disseminate the statistical data made available, but also an in-depth characterization of the business Portuguese. These Conferences have covered a diverse set of specific topics, such as the role of statistical and economic information in the decision-making of economic agents or the internationalization of the Portuguese economy, with the collaboration of several experts in the various topics addressed. Banco de Portugal has simultaneously sought to promote closer interaction with business associations, universities and public entities at national and regional level, promoting meetings to discuss economic and financial indicators published and for the preparation of the Central Balance Sheet Conferences. Banco de Portugal has also privileged the organization of these Conferences throughout the national territory, seeking that the dissemination of sectoral studies take place in the districts where their activities are most relevant. It was with this purpose that the Conferences, which addressed sectors such as accommodation and catering, textiles and clothing and footwear, took place in Loule, Braga and Aveiro, respectively. Or that the discussion about the agricultural sector took place in Santarem, or about the tourism sector in Funchal, or about the sectors of wood, cork and paper in Coimbra. The 6th Conference of the Central Balance Sheet already had a first session in Vila Real, held on January 27, where the contribution of the beverage industry to the modernization of the Portuguese business fabric was addressed, and continues today, here in evora, with a second session dedicated to the specific contribution of the wine and wine tourism sector. The relevance of the theme of this 6th Conference of the Central Balance Sheet The definition of the theme underlying this session stems from the recognition of the fundamental role that the modernization of the more traditional sectors of the Portuguese economy, which take on a very significant weight in our business fabric, has had in the development of the Portuguese economy and in contributing to the correction of macroeconomic imbalances, in particular through the creation of added value and greater internationalization. In the previous editions of the Conferences of the Central Balance Sheet, we have already focused our attention on several successful cases, fully justifying that this time we focus our analysis on the study of the wine and wine tourism sector, as well as on its contribution to the development of the Alentejo region. And there would be no better option for this purpose than to hold this conference in evora, one of Portugal's most recognized sites of world importance in the preservation of historical heritage, as evidenced to have been classified 31 years ago as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. As we will have the opportunity to see in the following presentations and in the main panel of this Conference, the wine sector has demonstrated, over the last few years, a very positive performance, visible both in terms of the evolution of its invoicing and in terms of its profitability, and it is also worth noting the important contribution of the external market to these levels of performance. The development of this sector has benefited from the growth of tourism in Portugal, but it has also contributed to this growth. In fact, tourism has been an important channel for the dissemination of Portuguese wine in the world, but at the same time foreign tourists are attracted to Portugal for the opportunity to visit and get to know the regions in which the wine is produced Portuguese. For this reason, wine tourism has shown an important dynamic effect on local communities, especially some regions in the interior of the country. These dynamics have proved very important for the development of the Portuguese economy and will therefore be the subject matter of deepening and debate at this 6th Conference of the Central Balance Sheet.
text_original: Logotipo BP.jpg Interveno de abertura do Diretor do Departamento de Estatstica Joo Cadete de Matos na 2 Sesso da 6 Conferncia da Central de Balanos vora, Auditrio da Fundao Eugnio de Almeida, 29 de maro de 2017 Modernizao do Tecido Empresarial Portugus | Painel sobre o setor do vinho e o enoturismo A Central de Balanos do Banco de Portugal A Central de Balanos do Banco de Portugal  uma base de dados com informao econmica e financeira, anual e trimestral, sobre as sociedades no financeiras em Portugal. Esta base de dados existe no Banco de Portugal desde 1983 e serve vrias funes do Banco de Portugal, nomeadamente as associadas  superviso e estabilidade do sistema financeiro,  anlise da situao econmica nacional e  compilao de estatsticas. A Central de Balanos do Banco de Portugal tem, desde 2007, como principal fonte de informao anual a IES  Informao Empresarial Simplificada, cobrindo assim praticamente todo o universo das sociedades no financeiras existentes em Portugal, ou seja cerca de 400 mil. As principais sries estatsticas obtidas a partir desta base de dados (Estatsticas das Empresas No Financeiras e Quadros do Setor) podem ser consultadas no BPStat | Estatsticas online, o portal de disseminao estatstica do Banco de Portugal. Um dos produtos da Central de Balanos que  disponibilizado, todos os anos, pelo Banco de Portugal s empresas corresponde ao Quadro da Empresa e do Setor, o qual permite a cada empresa comparar a respetiva situao econmica e financeira com a das restantes empresas do mesmo setor de atividade, constituindo assim um instrumento muito til  gesto empresarial. A informao da Central de Balanos est, igualmente, disponvel para o pblico em geral, nomeadamente para os investigadores, que podem aceder a um vasto conjunto de indicadores sobre as empresas portuguesas, com um elevado grau de detalhe por setor de atividade. Participao no Comit Europeu de Centrais de Balanos O Banco de Portugal integra, desde a respetiva fundao em 1987, o Comit Europeu de Centrais de Balanos (ECCBSO - European Committee of Central Balance-Sheet Data Offices), cujo objetivo  o desenvolvimento das centrais de balanos como fonte privilegiada de informao sobre as sociedades no financeiras nos diversos pases, assim como a promoo da sua utilizao no mbito das funes dos bancos centrais, no s na divulgao de estatsticas ou de estudos, mas tambm ao nvel das funes macroprudencial e de estabilidade financeira, tendo o Banco de Portugal assumido a presidncia desse Comit durante os ltimos trs anos. O Banco de Portugal contribui regularmente com informao para a BACH (Bank for the Accounts of Companies Harmonized), base de dados europeia de informao econmica e financeira das empresas no financeiras de diversos pases. Os Estudos da Central de Balanos Com o objetivo de promover uma maior e melhor utilizao da informao divulgada por parte das diversa categorias de utilizadores, o Banco de Portugal iniciou em 2010 a publicao dos Estudos da Central de Balanos, tendo sido at ao momento publicados 27 estudos. Os Estudos da Central de Balanos constituem uma importante ferramenta para a leitura da informao estatstica da Central de Balanos. Estes estudos podem assumir uma natureza metodolgica, funcionando como manuais explicativos da informao da Central de Balanos, ou podem ter uma natureza mais genrica, sendo dedicados a uma anlise geral da situao das empresas no financeiras em Portugal. Estes estudos de mbito geral tm sido atualizados anualmente, desde 2010, apresentando uma anlise aprofundada do tecido empresarial portugus com base num vasto conjunto de indicadores econmicos e financeiros. Por outro lado, os Estudos da Central de Balanos contemplam a divulgao de anlises setoriais, dedicadas a setores de atividade especficos. Entre os setores j estudados constam, para alm da indstria das bebidas (alvo do estudo publicado mais recentemente), setores to variados como os txteis e vesturio, o calado, as indstrias alimentares ou o alojamento e restaurao, abrangendo ainda setores como a construo, as atividades de informao e comunicao, o setor agrcola, o turismo, a indstria metalomecnica ou o setor farmacutico, para citar apenas alguns casos. O Banco de Portugal tem procurado acompanhar a evoluo dos setores mais dinmicos, refletindo igualmente sobre a sua importncia regional e o seu contributo para as exportaes, tendo a este propsito efetuado uma anlise especfica do setor das empresas exportadoras. Os estudos setoriais da Central de Balanos efetuados at ao momento permitiram cobrir cerca de metade das empresas no financeiras em atividade em Portugal, retratando setores que geram dois teros do volume de negcios e empregam cerca de 60 por cento das pessoas ao servio. As Conferncias da Central de Balanos As Conferncias da Central de Balanos, que tiveram tambm o seu incio em 2010, acompanharam a publicao dos atrs referidos estudos setoriais, constituindo uma iniciativa do Banco de Portugal que tem como objetivo, no s a divulgao dos dados estatsticos disponibilizados, como tambm uma caracterizao aprofundada do tecido empresarial portugus. Estas Conferncias tm versado um conjunto diversificado de temas especficos, como sejam o papel da informao estatstica e econmica na tomada de deciso dos agentes econmicos ou a internacionalizao da economia portuguesa, contando com a colaborao de vrios especialistas nas diversas temticas abordadas. O Banco de Portugal tem, simultaneamente, procurado promover uma interao mais prxima com as associaes empresariais, com as Universidades e com as entidades pblicas de mbito nacional e regional, promovendo reunies para debater os indicadores econmicos e financeiros publicados e para preparao das Conferncias da Central de Balanos. O Banco de Portugal tem igualmente privilegiado a organizao destas Conferncias em todo o territrio nacional, procurando que a divulgao dos estudos setoriais ocorra nos distritos onde as respetivas atividades assumem maior relevncia. Foi com esse intuito que as Conferncias, que abordaram setores como o alojamento e restaurao, os txteis e o vesturio e o calado, tiveram lugar em Loul, Braga e Aveiro, respetivamente. Ou que a discusso sobre o setor agrcola teve lugar em Santarm, ou sobre o setor do turismo no Funchal, ou ainda sobre os setores da madeira, da cortia e do papel em Coimbra. A 6 Conferncia da Central de Balanos contou j com uma primeira sesso em Vila Real, ocorrida no passado dia 27 de janeiro, onde se abordou o contributo da indstria das bebidas para a modernizao do tecido empresarial portugus, e prossegue hoje, aqui em vora, com uma segunda sesso dedicada ao contributo especfico do setor do vinho e do enoturismo. A relevncia da temtica desta 6 Conferncia da Central de Balanos A definio da temtica subjacente a esta sesso decorre do reconhecimento do papel fundamental que a modernizao dos setores mais tradicionais da economia portuguesa, que assumem um peso muito significativo no nosso tecido empresarial, tem tido no desenvolvimento da economia portuguesa e no contributo para a correo de desequilbrios macroeconmicos, nomeadamente atravs da criao de valor acrescentado e de uma maior internacionalizao. Nas anteriores edies das Conferncias da Central de Balanos focmos j a nossa ateno em diversos casos de sucesso, justificando-se plenamente que desta vez centremos a nossa anlise no estudo do setor do vinho e do enoturismo, bem como no respetivo contributo para o desenvolvimento da regio do Alentejo. E no haveria melhor opo para o efeito do que realizar esta conferncia em vora, um dos mais reconhecidos locais de Portugal de importncia mundial na preservao do patrimnio histrico, como o comprova ter sido classificado h 31 anos atrs como Patrimnio Mundial da UNESCO. Como teremos oportunidade de comprovar nas apresentaes seguintes e no painel principal desta Conferncia, o setor do vinho tem demonstrado, ao longo dos ltimos anos, um desempenho muito positivo, visvel tanto ao nvel da evoluo da sua faturao, como ao nvel das suas rendibilidades, sendo de destacar igualmente o contributo importante do mercado externo para estes nveis de desempenho. O desenvolvimento deste setor tem beneficiado do crescimento do turismo em Portugal, mas tambm tem contribudo para esse crescimento. De facto, o turismo tem constitudo um importante canal de divulgao do vinho portugus no Mundo, mas simultaneamente os turistas estrangeiros so atrados a Portugal pela oportunidade de visitar e conhecer as regies em que se produz o vinho portugus. Por isso mesmo, o enoturismo tem revelado um importante efeito dinamizador sobre as comunidades locais, com destaque para algumas regies no interior do pas. Estas dinmicas tem-se revelado muito importantes para o desenvolvimento da economia portuguesa e sero, por esse motivo, a matria objeto de aprofundamento e debate nesta 6 Conferncia da Central de Balanos.

Title: Opening speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the "Paychallenge'17: The Future of Payments and Fintech" Conference
text: CONFERENCE THE FUTURE OF PAYMENTS AND FINTECH NOVEMBER 6, 2017 Money Museum Governor of Banco de Portugal, Carlos da Silva Costa It is with great pleasure and satisfaction that Banco de Portugal hosts this event dedicated to the theme "The Future of Payments and FinTech", aiming at the creation of innovative technological solutions in the payment market under the new Payment Services Directive (DSP2), which will enter into force in early 2018. I congratulate CIONET1 and Portugal FinTech2 on this organization. 1 The world's largest community of information technology managers. 2 Association that has the mission to create the best conditions for the development of Fintech, Insurtech and Cybersecurity Startups in Portugal. When we look at the future of payments, there's nothing better than doing it in a place full of history, like the Money Museum. Introduction The phenomenon of the digitisation of economies and societies is irreversibly changing the behaviour and expectations of economic operators in various contexts. The way they make payments is no exception. Bank customers are increasingly looking for payment services tailored to their real needs. To meet these expectations, providers (incumbents or FinTechs) will have to develop faster payment services, with greater availability and increased ease of use, based on innovative solutions in the field of information technologies and meeting the necessary security conditions. For incumbent providers, this response represents a huge challenge but also an opportunity. Information technologies and partnerships with other entities can be instrumental in helping to overcome the constraints associated with low activity growth, low profitability and to restore high levels of trust and reputation. For its part, FinTech should not only be seen as competitors of traditional providers, but also, in many circumstances, as complementary institutions or partners. This wave of innovation and digital transformation promises a technological revolution that will in the long run have benefits in the lives of all of us. Initiatives developed by Banco de Portugal in the context of monitoring the digital evolution of the financial sector Over the years, the Portuguese has been recognized internationally as one of the most efficient, the result of the capacity revealed by the financial system to cooperate in the development of national infrastructures. Banco de Portugal has been an active party to this process. It plays a catalyst role in the cooperation and development of payment systems. It thus seeks to ensure the efficiency of the systems and the confidence in payment services, both on the supply side and on the demand side of these services. Along with other European regulators, Banco de Portugal has highlighted in several years the importance of the financial system being able to respond adequately to the new challenges posed by the growing digitization of society. In October 2016, Banco de Portugal organized an important international conference dedicated to the theme of Digital Banking and FinTech. The challenges and threats to the banking system in these areas were discussed, with the presence of speakers from other central banks in Europe, the EDF, the IMF and also international consultants. Subsequently, the Bank welcomed on its premises a very significant set of representatives of the financial system and other entities for the discussion of innovation and digital transformation in banking, within the framework of the conference "Finance Innovation Day". And today, the Bank is the host of this challenge "PayChallenge: Rethinking Payment Services" that aims to discuss the creation of innovative technological solutions in the payment market under DSP2. Internally, Banco de Portugal has set up a multidisciplinary think tank with the aim of studying the evolution of Digital Banking and FinTech and to look at, in 2020, the challenges presented to it in the broader context of its mission, from the outset in the field of regulation and supervision, but also in the dimension of financial stability, systems and means of payments, cybersecurity, and even reserve management and the conduct of monetary policy. The DSP2 Payment Services Directive as an opportunity for innovation DSP2 aims to contribute to the creation of a single market for payment services, which is both safe, efficient, innovative and competition-promoting. And it is especially in relation to this last objective, that I note the greatest novelty of the Directive, and the one that most affects the discussions on FinTech: the creation of account information services3 and payment initiation services4. 3 They consist of providing users with aggregate information on accounts held in several banks and enabling dynamic business budget management or cash management services. 4 They consist of initiating payments on behalf of the user, in a convenient and expeditious manner, without having to leave the website of the merchant on which he is purchasing a product or service. These services will be provided to users online by providers who consider themselves 'third parties' in the relationship between you and your bank. These third parties will have, with the consent of users, access to the account data. The Directive allows these payment services to be provided by a bank or other entities. To that end, those entities benefit from a scheme to enable the provision of lighter payment services. In addition, the Directive establishes a set of security requirements for electronic payment services. Payment service providers will have to start authenticating their customers using strong authentication mechanisms, with special requirements for remote operations. This is where fintech's intervention space arises. They will be able to position themselves in the market as entities specialized in the provision of certain services directly to users and banks. European payment service providers seek to position themselves in this new paradigm. If, on the one hand, they must ensure timely compliance with the new regulatory requirements, on the other hand they see in the Directive an incentive to change, in search of new business opportunities, in an increasingly innovative and competitive market. Final considerations Digitisation provides opportunities for providers and challenges for central banks and regulators. The new architecture and new business models followed by payment service providers require a multidisciplinary response from central banks and regulators, require new approaches, resources and skills in order to maximize opportunities and minimize risks to society. The best way to anticipate and know the challenges and impacts that the new reality poses to them is to be close to or even within technological innovation, to understand and guide it towards the proper functioning, efficiency, security, trust and resilience, in payment systems and for financial stability. In this context, it is very important that the competent authorities ensure, in particular:  The neutrality of regulation, eliminating the inhibitory factors of the adoption of technologies (safe and efficient) in the development of financial activity.  Fair and balanced treatment between incumbents and new entrants, as well as between jurisdictions.  The identification of new risks and challenges posed by the provision of technology-based financial services and the adoption of appropriate regulatory and supervisory initiatives.  Coordinated action between regulators and supervisors at national and European level. It is with a posture of monitoring, and especially of collaboration and sharing, that Banco de Portugal intends to work with all stakeholders in the analysis and development of solutions in this area, promoting innovation and safeguarding risk and security conditions. I end by appealing that this event contribute to a closer proximity between Banco de Portugal and all potential providers of new payment solutions, whether more traditional or FinTechs. Many thanks to all and I hope that it will be a very fruitful session for those present.
text_original: CONFERNCIA THE FUTURE OF PAYMENTS AND FINTECH 6 DE NOVEMBRO 2017 Museu do Dinheiro Governador do Banco de Portugal, Carlos da Silva Costa  com enorme gosto e satisfao que o Banco de Portugal acolhe este evento dedicado ao tema The Future of Payments and FinTech, visando a criao de solues tecnolgicas inovadoras no mercado de pagamentos no mbito da nova Diretiva de Servios de Pagamento (DSP2), que entrar em vigor no incio de 2018. Felicito a CIONET1 e a Portugal FinTech2 por esta organizao. 1 A maior comunidade mundial de gestores de tecnologias da informao. 2 Associao que tem por misso criar as melhores condies para o desenvolvimento de Startups Fintech, Insurtech e Cybersecurity em Portugal. Quando perspetivamos o futuro dos pagamentos, nada melhor do que faz-lo num local cheio de histria, como o Museu do Dinheiro. Introduo O fenmeno da digitalizao das economias e das sociedades est a alterar, de forma irreversvel, os comportamentos e as expetativas dos agentes econmicos em vrios contextos. A forma como realizam pagamentos no  exceo. Os clientes bancrios procuram cada vez mais servios de pagamento customizados s suas reais necessidades. Para responder a estas expetativas, os prestadores (incumbentes ou FinTechs) tero de desenvolver servios de pagamento mais rpidos, com maior disponibilidade e com facilidade de utilizao acrescida, assentes em solues inovadoras no domnio das tecnologias de informao e cumprindo as necessrias condies de segurana. Para os prestadores incumbentes, esta resposta representa um enorme desafio mas tambm uma oportunidade. As tecnologias de informao e as parcerias com outras entidades podem ser instrumentais para ajudar a ultrapassar as condicionantes associadas ao baixo crescimento da atividade, baixa rentabilidade e para restabelecer nveis elevados de confiana e de reputao. Por seu lado, as FinTech no devem ser vistas apenas como concorrentes dos prestadores tradicionais, mas tambm, em muitas circunstncias, como instituies complementares ou parceiras. Esta onda de inovao e transformao digital promete uma revoluo tecnolgica que ir a prazo ter benefcios na vida de todos ns. Iniciativas desenvolvidas pelo Banco de Portugal no mbito do acompanhamento da evoluo digital do setor financeiro Ao longo dos anos, o sistema de pagamentos portugus tem sido reconhecido a nvel internacional como um dos mais eficientes, fruto da capacidade revelada pelo sistema financeiro para cooperar no desenvolvimento das infraestruturas nacionais. O Banco de Portugal tem sido parte ativa neste processo. Assume um papel catalisador da cooperao e do desenvolvimento dos sistemas de pagamentos. Procura, desta forma, assegurar a eficincia dos sistemas e a confiana nos servios de pagamento, tanto no lado da oferta como no lado da procura destes servios. A par de outros reguladores europeus, o Banco de Portugal tem destacado em diversos fora a importncia do sistema financeiro conseguir responder adequadamente aos novos desafios colocados pela crescente digitalizao da sociedade. Em outubro de 2016, o Banco de Portugal organizou uma importante Conferncia internacional dedicada ao tema da Banca Digital e das FinTech. Foram debatidos os desafios e as ameaas que se colocam ao sistema bancrio nestes domnios, com a presena de oradores de outros bancos centrais da Europa, do FED, do FMI e tambm de consultoras internacionais. Posteriormente, o Banco acolheu nas suas instalaes um conjunto muito significativo de representantes do sistema financeiro e de outras entidades para a discusso da inovao e da transformao digital na banca, no mbito da conferncia "Finance Innovation Day". E hoje, o Banco  o anfitrio deste desafio "PayChallenge: Rethinking Payment Services" que visa debater a criao de solues tecnolgicas inovadoras no mercado de pagamentos no mbito da DSP2. A nvel interno, o Banco de Portugal criou um grupo de reflexo multidisciplinar, com o objetivo de estudar a evoluo da Banca Digital e das FinTech e de perspetivar, no horizonte 2020, os desafios que se lhe apresentam no contexto alargado da sua misso, desde logo no domnio da regulao e superviso, mas tambm na dimenso da estabilidade financeira, dos sistemas e meios de pagamentos, da cibersegurana, e at da gesto de reservas e da conduo da poltica monetria. A Diretiva dos Servios de Pagamento DSP2 enquanto oportunidade para a inovao A DSP2 pretende contribuir para a criao de um mercado nico para os servios de pagamento, que seja simultaneamente seguro, eficiente, inovador e promotor da concorrncia. E  especialmente em relao a este ltimo objetivo, que destaco a maior novidade da Diretiva, e aquela que mais afeta as discusses sobre FinTech: a criao dos servios de informao sobre contas3 e dos servios de iniciao de pagamentos4. 3 Consistem em fornecer, aos utilizadores, informao agregada sobre contas detidas em vrios bancos e possibilitar servios dinmicos de gesto do oramento familiar ou de tesouraria das empresas. 4 Consistem em iniciar pagamentos em nome do utilizador, de forma cmoda e clere, sem que este tenha de sair do site do comerciante no qual est a adquirir um produto ou servio. Estes servios sero prestados aos utilizadores, online, por prestadores que se consideram terceiros na relao entre o utilizador e o seu banco. Estes terceiros tero, mediante o consentimento dos utilizadores, acesso aos dados das contas. A Diretiva permite que estes servios de pagamento sejam prestados por um banco ou por outras entidades. Para esse efeito, essas entidades beneficiam de um regime de habilitao para a prestao de servios de pagamento mais aligeirado. Adicionalmente, a Diretiva estabelece um conjunto de requisitos de segurana para os servios de pagamento fornecidos por via eletrnica. Os prestadores de servios de pagamento tero de passar a autenticar os seus clientes com recurso a mecanismos de autenticao forte, com especiais requisitos para as operaes remotas.  aqui que surge o espao para interveno das FinTech. Podero posicionar-se no mercado como entidades especializadas na prestao de determinados servios diretamente aos utilizadores e aos bancos. Os prestadores de servios de pagamento europeus procuram posicionar-se neste novo paradigma. Se, por um lado, tm de assegurar o cumprimento atempado dos novos requisitos regulamentares, por outro, veem na Diretiva um incentivo  mudana, em busca de novas oportunidades de negcio, num mercado cada vez mais inovador e concorrencial. Consideraes finais A digitalizao aporta oportunidades para os prestadores e desafios para os bancos centrais e reguladores. A nova arquitetura e os novos modelos de negcios seguidos pelos prestadores de servios de pagamento obrigam a uma resposta multidisciplinar dos bancos centrais e reguladores, exigem novas abordagens, recursos e competncias, de forma a maximizar as oportunidades e a minimizar os riscos para a sociedade. A melhor forma de antecipar e conhecer os desafios e impactos que a nova realidade lhes coloca  estar perto ou mesmo dentro da inovao tecnolgica, para a compreender e orientar no sentido do bom funcionamento, eficincia, segurana, confiana e resilincia, nos sistemas de pagamentos e em prol da estabilidade financeira. Neste enquadramento,  muito importante que as autoridades competentes assegurem, nomeadamente:  A neutralidade da regulao, eliminando os fatores inibidores da adoo de tecnologias (seguras e eficientes) no desenvolvimento da atividade financeira.  O tratamento justo e equilibrado entre incumbentes e novos entrantes, bem como entre jurisdies.  A identificao de novos riscos e desafios colocados pela disponibilizao de servios financeiros de base tecnolgica e a adoo de iniciativas regulatrias e de superviso adequadas.  Uma atuao coordenada entre reguladores e supervisores a nvel nacional e europeu.  com uma postura de acompanhamento, e principalmente de colaborao e partilha, que o Banco de Portugal pretende trabalhar com todas as partes interessadas na anlise e no desenvolvimento de solues neste domnio, promovendo a inovao e salvaguardando as condies de risco e de segurana. Termino apelando para que este evento contribua para uma maior proximidade entre o Banco de Portugal e todos os potenciais prestadores de novas solues de pagamentos, sejam mais tradicionais ou FinTechs. Muito obrigado a todos e fao votos de que seja uma sesso muito proveitosa para os presentes.

Title: Interveno de Vitor Gaspar no painel How to regain confidence in the euro area? - Conferncia The Euro Area and the Financial Crisis, Banco Nacional da Eslovaquia, Bratislava, 6-8 Setembro 2010
text: How to regain confidence in the euro area? contribution by Vitor Gaspar 1to a panel discussion at the Conference The Euro Area and the Financial Crisis, 6-8 September, Bratislava, hosted by the National Bank of Slovakia. I thank the organizers, especially Ludovit odor, for inviting me for this Conference and for giving me the opportunity to participate in this panel to discuss How to regain confidence in the euro area? As Athanasios Orphanides said, in his opening keynote address, the Global Crisis revealed fault lines in the governance of the euro area. He focused on the new architecture for financial stability in Europe. In my brief introduction to this panel I want to focus on public finances; specifically I want to focus on budget discipline. 1 Special Adviser Banco de Portugal. I am grateful to Isabel Gameiro and Paul Hiebert for comments and corrections. The remaining errors are my responsibility. The views expressed are my own and do not necessarily reflect those of the Banco de Portugal or the Eurosystems. 2 An authoritative source is provided by United Nations, 2009. 3 In 1950 the relevant percentage was 14.8%. 1. Demographic transition, the global crisis and debt levels. Before focusing on the specific case of the euro area I want to very briefly comment on a crucial evolutionary trend that shapes the context in which budgetary policy will be conducted in the next decades: demographics. Developments are the more surprising as the world is experiencing a fundamental demographic transition. According to the latest demographic projections, made available by the United Nations2, World Population will stop growing by 2050, when it will have reached about 9 billion people (compared to almost 7 billion in 2010). This will interrupt a trend of pronounced population growth recorded for centuries. This constitutes an epochal transition with profound impacts on economic, political and social balances. The transition will happen first in advanced countries. For example for the 27 Member States of the European Union the population is projected to decline slightly in the four decades from 2010 to 2050 (notwithstanding significant migration flows). The share of EU27 in World population is projected to decline from 7.2% to 5.4%3. The transition has far-reaching implications for social, political and economic trends. It has, in particular, strong influence on the sustainability of public finances. All other things equal, a slowdown in population growth increases the implicit public debt burden associated with the operation of health and pension systems. At the same time demographic transition raises very difficult issues of equity across generations. Public debts in OECD countries have doubled since the mid-seventies. The Global Crisis accelerated the trend. The evolution was marked by the functioning of automatic stabilizers, discretionary expansion and the costs of intervention to stabilize the financial system4. Such accumulation of public debt is unprecedented in peace time. Therefore, sustainability of Public Finances is a central challenge that the Global Crisis has made even more pressing. 4 As Trichet stressed, in his address to the 2010 Jackson Hole Conference, in the euro area, public debt to GDP shot up by more than 20 percentage points in a period of just four years starting in 2007 (see Trichet, 2010). 5 The point is made by Marzinotto, Pisani-Ferry and Sapir (2010). 6 Empirical evidence and further discussion are provided in Restoy (1996) and Bernoth et al. (2006) and Schuknecht et al (2008). 2. Budgetary rules and procedures in the euro area. The economic constitution of the euro area reflects the view that stability-oriented macroeconomic policies provide the groundwork for the proper functioning of a market economy with unfettered competition leading to sustainable growth. The primary goal of monetary policy is price stability and the conduct of monetary policy was entrusted to the independent European Central Bank. The Lisbon Treaty includes provisions protecting the central bank from encroachment from the fiscal authorities. Article 123 prohibits monetary financing and Article 124 rules out privileged access to financial institutions. Moreover, Article 125 excludes the responsibility of the Union or of other Member States for financial commitments assumed by one Member State; and Article 122 limits financial assistance for cases in which a Member State is in difficulties or is seriously threatened with severe difficulties caused by natural disasters or exceptional occurrences beyond its control  Notoriously, article 143 of the Treaty does not foresee mutual assistance for the case of members of the euro area5. A fundamental question is whether, given the prohibition of monetary financing, privileged access and bail out, market discipline can be expected to be sufficient to ensure fiscal discipline. The question was addressed more than twenty years ago in the Delors Report (page 24): To some extent market forces can exert a disciplinary influence  However, experience suggests that market perceptions do not necessarily provide strong and compelling signals and that access to a large capital market may for some time facilitate the financing of economic imbalances  The constraints imposed by market forces might either be too slow and weak or too sudden and disruptive. In a companion piece, Lamfalussy (1989) argues that there is indeed reason to be skeptical about the effectiveness of market-imposed discipline for countries participating in a monetary union6. The conclusion in the Delors Report was that participation in the single market and in the single currency implied that Member States had to accept corresponding policy constraints. This view is reflected in relevant provisions in the Lisbon Treaty. Specifically Articles 120 and 121 prescribe that Member States conduct their economic policies as a matter of common concern and with a view to achieve the objectives of the Union. In case a Member State does not behave in conformity with the Broad Economic Policy Guidelines or risks jeopardizing the smooth functioning of economic and monetary union, it is subject to the possibility of warnings from the European Commission and recommendations from the EUs Council. Moreover, Article 126 imposes on Member States participating in the euro area, the legal obligation to avoid excessive deficits. The Treaty provisions were completed by the Stability and Growth Pact7. The Pact made clear a distinction between the preventive arm, based on the surveillance of budgetary positions, and the corrective arm, based on the excessive deficit procedure. The preventive arm is covered by Regulation EC 1466/97 (amended by Regulation EC 1055/2005). The corrective arm, in turn, is covered by Regulation EC 1467/97 (amended by Regulation EC 1056/2005)8. Paragraph 11, of article 126 of the TFEU foresees the possibility of sanctions in the case of non-compliance. 7 For the genesis of the Stability and Growth Pact see Stark (2001) and Costello (2001). 8 A very useful source for the relevant secondary legislation texts is . 9 As documented by, for example, Gerlach, Schulz and Wolff (2010). 3. Sovereign Debt Market Behavior. The creation of the euro area has been associated with the emergence of an integrated market for sovereign debt. Capiello, Engle and Shephard (2006) find that correlation between bond returns issued by governments participating in the euro area approached unity shortly after the start of the euro area in 1999. In most of the first decade of the euro area sovereign spreads have been low (rarely exceeding 30 basis points and averaging much lower)9. The situation changed dramatically with the Global Crisis. Spreads widened slowly and gradually and the process paced up after the bankruptcy of Lehman, in September 2008. In 2009 there was a period when the situation seemed on a path of gradual easing. However, from the autumn onwards spreads widened again and CDS premiums increased reflecting bond market tensions, driven, to a large extent, by idiosyncratic factors. Euro area bond markets were in turmoil in early May 2010 and stabilized only after the announcement of strong collective action at the European level. At the current time (September 2010) tensions persist in bond markets. Schuknecht, von Hagen and Wolswijk (2008, 2010) importantly show that bond yield spreads can be largely explained on the basis of economic fundamentals before and after financial market turmoil and the crisis. They are able to relate differentials to benchmark (the German bunds for the euro area) with deficit and debt differentials. However, after September 2009, the coefficient on deficit differentials has been multiplied by a factor between 3 and 4 and the coefficient on debt differentials by a factor of 7-8. At the same time spreads have also increased as a response to shifts in general risk aversion, with German ten-year bonds assuming a safe haven role. The ability of these authors to find a systematic relation between spreads and fundamentals before and after market turmoil and the crisis has important policy implications. In particular market discipline has been present throughout the whole period, albeit in a much stronger way in the recent past. The evidence shows a clear pattern in which market discipline was too slow and weak before the Global Crisis and became, more recently, too sudden and disruptive. The Stability and Growth Pact and the other provisions in the Treaty and secondary legislation failed to prevent the very pattern of market behavior they were designed to avoid. Such failure requires major adjustments in the governance of the euro area. The issue is central for macroeconomic stability, in general, and for financial stability, in particular. 4. The work of the van Rompuy Task Force. The problem identified above was already clear in March 2010. On 26 March the European Council gave a mandate to the van Rompuy Task Force to examine the relevant issues and proposed specific actions aiming at reinforcing economic governance in the euro area. The approach of the Task Force includes three elements: First, strong surveillance over national fiscal policies and more effective prevention and correction of excessive levels of public deficits and public debt; Second, effective monitoring countries competitiveness positions aiming at the correction of macroeconomic imbalances; Third, a crisis management framework. In their contribution to the work of the van Rompuy Task Force, the Governing Council of the ECB, stresses the importance of mechanism design to contain moral hazard associated with the crisis management framework. As Jean Tirole said: in crisis, policy-makers often have their options narrowed to choosing between the bad and the ugly. The only way around is to design ex ante institutions to shape incentives to ensure prudent behavior. To do so it is necessary to ensure that financial support will be made available only at penalty rates and under strict conditionality. The rules that apply in extreme crisis situations are crucial to shape incentives at all times. The Task Force has met for the fourth time on Monday, September 6 and Van Rompuy will report to the 16 September European Council. The Task force is due to complete its work and to make concrete proposals before the end of October. Progress is being reported. Nevertheless, it is important not to underestimate difficulties. The work of the Task Force is made harder because we already have an extensive framework of rules and procedures (described above in section 2) that failed to deliver as intended (as discussed in section 3). The Global Crisis has demonstrated an unprecedented degree of international interdependence. Nowhere are linkages stronger than in the euro area. An institutional response is required, consistent with this increased interdependence. The construction of the euro area is work in progress. If we are successful we will lay the stability-oriented economic policy framework of the euro area on stronger institutional foundations.
