Title: Intervention of Administrator Hlder Rosalino at the opening session of the ASFAC Conference 2017: Challenges and Opportunities of Fintech
text: ASFAC CONFERENCE 2017 FINTECH IN SPECIALIZED CREDIT, OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES OCTOBER 23, 2017 ISEG - Higher Institute of Economics and Management FinTechs Challenges and Opportunities Elder Rosalino I would like to begin by thanking, on behalf of the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal, the invitation to be present at the opening of the ASFAC - 2017 Annual Conference and also for the opportunity to participate by the Directors of the prudential and behavioral supervision departments in the following sessions. I would also like to congratulate ASFAC, in the person of its President: Dr. Antonio Menezes Rodrigues and all the other members of the governing bodies, for the relevant services it has provided to the sector of specialized consumer financing, an area that Banco de Portugal naturally monitors very closely within the framework of its regulatory and supervisory powers. The theme of this conference [AS FINTECH] is very current and timely, discussing itself in all contexts and geographies. 1. Framing Earlier this year, Mark Carney, Governor of the Bank of England and Chairman of the Financial Stability Board, said FinTech could represent the end of the traditional banking model. More recently Cristine Lagarde, Managing Director of the IMF, in an intervention she called "Central Banking and Fintech - A Brave New World" said: "In the FinTech paradigm, regulators will have to shift their focus, evolving from the supervision of financial entities to the supervision of financial activities, and should also specialise in assessing the soundness and security of financial transaction algorithms themselves." In China, FinTech already has as many customers as the largest banks, and in the rest of the world it is estimated that around 40% of loans are granted by non-bank entities, notably through shadow banking. These figures and findings lead many to say that the FinTech sector has imposed a "disruptive innovation", which is changing the status quo and the balances of the financial system itself. However, this is only a starting point. It seems that we are still at the beginning of a long cycle of structural digital changes, which will lead to increased competition between FinTech and financial institutions, which will surely lead to the transformation of the financial system as we know it today. In this regard, an ECB supervisory officer recently said that: "Whichever direction we go, there's one thing supervisors should take for granted: there's a growing and not yet clearly identified risk now that FinTech has come to stay and they often operate outside the regulated banking sector" This means that: the risk to financial stability that arises from this new reality cannot be overlooked and is currently of particular concern on the part of national and European regulators and supervisors. Due to the diversity and scope of FinTech's impacts, the performance at the level of its regulation and supervision is necessarily complex, implying that the theme is analyzed and discussed in different entities and international forums, and is monitored by Banco de Portugal through different departments, within the framework of their different competences. Banco de Portugal will have the opportunity at this conference to develop its vision, especially in the areas of prudential and behavioural supervision, so I will not address these aspects in particular. It should be recalled that the term FinTech, an acronym often used to combine financial services and technology, seeks to cover a wide range of technological innovations with potentially transformative implications for the financial system, but also for its intermediaries and, above all, for end-users of financial services. The main services that the FinTech industry provides are as vast and diverse as payments and transfers of currencies, consulting platforms, robot-advising and trading, new models of lending (crowdfunding and Peer to Peer lending - P2P), personal finance management or even fraud detection or creation of enterprise software to help manage and streamline the very compliance process of credit institutions. However, the majority of FinTech (almost 75%) focuses on commercial banking (more traditional), providing money lending, asset management and, above all, payment services. In this area, FinTech has traditionally addressed end customers directly, without the help of the banking sector, which has contributed to being considered innovative and disruptive, as they alter established business models. However, more recent information also shows that fintech's share of business to business offers has increased to almost 50% of total companies launched annually. These companies establish partnerships and provide services to incumbent banks, which maintain their normal relationship with customers. It is indisputable that FinTech has played an active role in increasing the digital experience and financial innovation, outline with many of the technological solutions that support the functioning of the digital financial market. They have often been responsible for the development of new technology platforms, which allow the distribution of products and the provision of financial services in a faster, more convenient way, adapted to the needs of customers, more intuitive and often with lower costs. For its promoters, this wave of innovation and digital transformation promises a technological revolution that will democratize financial services, with the following immediate benefits: 1. Consumers will have more options, services more targeted to their needs and more attractive prices. 2. Small and medium-sized enterprises shall have access to new credit facilities and better market conditions. 3. Banks will become more productive, with lower transaction costs, greater capital efficiency and greater operational resilience. 4. The financial system itself will become more resilient, with greater diversity, redundancy and depth. 5. And, above all, financial services will be more inclusive, with people better connected, more informed and increasingly empowered. It is therefore indisputable that the use of technology is already significantly changing the way financial services are provided and perceived by bank customers. But it is also certain and certain that this transformation will be increasingly accentuated with the arrival in the financial market of millennials - the generation of the Internet - (which is about to happen) and with the growing emergence of several startups with high technological expertise and strongly innovative. These startups (or "emerging companies") operate in the financial market providing services to "traditional" financial institutions or competing with them, proving to be, as a general rule, more competitive, because their structures are considerably less "heavy" in operational and regulatory costs. In this context of growing "disruptive innovation" in the financial sector, FinTech is a ubiquitous theme in various general or structural policy and legislative initiatives. These include, for example, the strategy for the creation of a digital single market, the capital market union plan, or even the General Data Protection Regulation, which will enter into force throughout the Union in May 2018, and which introduces new figures dictated by technology, such as profiling, automated decisions or the right to data portability. FinTech is also a theme present in initiatives on specific areas, as is the case in the revision of the Payment Services Directive (PSD2), of which I will talk later, in the revision of the Financial Markets Directive (MIFII), or even in the national regulation of crowdfunding. 2. Banco de Portugal's position Banco de Portugal has been paying increasing attention to this theme, seeking to support and stimulate, at the national level, the debate around the great challenges that digital innovation poses to the financial system and its regulation. Banco de Portugal organized, in October last year, an important international conference dedicated to the theme of Digital Banking and FinTech, which allowed us to discuss the challenges and threats posed to the banking system in these areas, and which was attended by speakers from other central banks in Europe, the EDF, the IMF and also international consultants. More recently, the Bank has hosted a very significant set of representatives of the financial system and other entities in its facilities for the discussion of innovation and digital transformation in banking, within the framework of the "Finance Innovation Day" conference. Early next month, Banco de Portugal will host a challenge launched by CIONET, the world's largest community of information technology managers, to create innovative technological solutions in the payments market. The "PayChallenge: Rethinking Payment Services" challenge is addressed to the banking system, startups and universities and aims to develop innovative solutions for the payments market under the new Payment Services Directive (PSD2), which will come into force in January 2018. Internally, Banco de Portugal has set up a multidisciplinary think tank, with the aim of studying the evolution of Digital Banking and FinTech and to look at, in 2020, the challenges that arise in the broader context of its mission and in the specific framework of its regulatory and supervisory responsibilities. 3. Provision of payment services: evolution of the regulatory framework as an opportunity for innovation As I have already mentioned, one of the areas in which FinTech has operated innovations of greatest impact is the provision of payment services, which I will try to address more carefully. While the focus of this conference focuses on fintech's challenges and opportunities in the context of the consumer finance sector, the truth is that this sector is composed of various types of institutions, some of which are also dedicated to the provision of payment services. In fact, there is often a very large interconnection between the granting of credit and the provision of payment services, as these activities are increasingly integrated into the customer's shopping experience. We are currently living challenging days within payment systems and services in Portugal, to which it is not unrelated, on the one hand, to the publication of a new Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and, on the other hand, the initiatives that foster innovation in payments, taking advantage of the advancement of technology. In this context, I stress the adoption of immediate payment solutions, which has been fostered at European level, and will soon be a reality in Portugal. In view of this framework, challenges arise for traditional operators  typically banks  and opportunities for new players, especially those from the FinTech industry, who have had, in the area of retail payments and lending, attractive ground for establishing and presenting innovative offers.  The Revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2) At the level of the regulation stemins the provision of payment services, it is essential to address the main impacts associated with the entry into force of the Revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2), many of which are disruptive to the provision of payment services at European level. In fact, this Directive follows the first Payment Services Directive, published in 2009, to address the increasing digitisation in financial services, which has resulted in the emergence of new payment service providers, innovative payment solutions, more demanding users and new challenges for payment security. The new Directive aims to contribute to the creation of a single market for payment services, which is both secure (for payment service providers and users), efficient, innovative and competition-promoting. And it is especially with regard to this last objective  that of promoting competition  that it is important to mention the one that is the biggest novelty of the Directive, and the one that interests us most today, in the context of the discussions on FinTech: The Directive regulates two payment services which have so far not benefited from a regulatory framework  account information services and payment initiation services. These services will be provided to users online by providers who consider themselves 'third parties' in the relationship between you and your bank. These third parties will have, with the consent of users, access to the account data of bank customers and may, for example, in the case of account information services, provide users with aggregate information about accounts held in various banks and enable dynamic services for the management of household budgets or the treasury of companies. In the case of payment initiation services, they may initiate payments on behalf of the user, conveniently and quickly, without having to leave the website of the merchant to whom you are purchasing a product or service. Although the Directive allows such payment services to be provided by a bank, it is true that it enables other entities to form payment service providers only for the provision of one of those two types of services, in which case they benefit from a system of enabling the provision of lighter services. However, the Directive does not indemend concerns about payment security, which is why it establishes a set of security requirements for electronic payment services, implying that, with their entry into force, payment service providers will have to authenticate their customers using strong authentication mechanisms, with special requirements for remote operations. This is where the space for FinTech's intervention arises, which will be able to position themselves in the market as entities specialized in providing certain services directly to users, but also to banks. Banco de Portugal is actively involved in the preparation of the preliminary draft transposition of psd2 into the national legal system, and even promoted, in June 2017, a public consultation on the legislative options that the Directive allows the State Portuguese exercise. ASFAC responded to this consultation, with contributions that I thank very much, and which reveal the industry's interest in payment service issues. It is in this context of change that national and European banks have been trying to position themselves: if, on the one hand, they have to ensure timely compliance with the new regulatory requirements, on the other hand, they seek not to see PSD2 only as an exercise in compliance, but also as an incentive to change, in search of new business opportunities, increasingly innovative and competitive market.  Immediate payments: innovation at the service of speedy payments As I have already mentioned, the implementation of immediate payment solutions has been a hotly debated topic with a central role in the coming evolution of the European payments market. Since 2014, the Eurosystem, in which Banco de Portugal operates, has been promoting interoperable solutions for immediate payments at European level since 2014. In fact, immediate payment solutions developed in recent years in European countries, based on payment cards and/or credit transfers are not, as a rule, interoperable with each other and therefore do not allow cross-border use, frustrating the objectives of the single payment market. In this context, in December 2014, the European Retail Payments Board (ERPB) agreed on the need to create at least one pan-European immediate payment solution (through the use of credit transfers) in euro, accessible to any payment service provider operating in the European Union, thus resulting in a process that has merited the commitment of multiple actors. The solution created, which will be available for effective adoption by payment service providers from November 21, 2017, profoundly changes the payment execution paradigm, as it establishes that:  Funds should be available in the beneficiary's account within an indicative maximum time of ten seconds;  The payee's payment service provider is obliged to accept all transactions of eur 15,000 or less;  Operations can be ordered at any time of the day and any day of the year, i.e. with an availability of 24/7/365; and  Payer and payee payment service providers may be established in any of the 34 countries that are part of SEPA. In this context, several banking communities will launch immediate payment solutions in the coming months. Also in Portugal is being prepared a national cooperative solution of immediate payments, compatible with the principles and harmonised technical requirements defined at European level, and framed under the Interbank Compensation System managed by Banco de Portugal. Here too, fintech's intervention potential is notorious: in a context where, for example, the provision of psd2-regulated payment initiation services can be enhanced in the effective use of immediate payment solutions made available at an infrastructure level, placing FinTech in a situation where they can provide services that provide flexibility, speed and confidence of users. 4. Conclusion In this context, I can only conclude that we are witnessing today a number of technological, sociological and, above all, regulatory developments, which will give rise to a market for the provision of retail payment services almost transfigured from what has been the predominant practice in recent decades. It is important that both traditional operators and FinTech are able to position themselves in the market, combining the need to observe new regulatory requirements with the possibility of taking advantage of the new reality, increasingly dynamic and interoperable, striving to ensure that the efficiency and safety of the services provided are the determining factors of their success. Of course, the increasing digitisation of financial services will have to correspond to an equally growing concern about digital security in carrying out operations and the protection of clients' personal data from such operations. These are central issues in the ongoing debate and will certainly be widely addressed throughout this conference. Banco de Portugal, as part of its insertion in the Eurosystem, has taken an active role in supporting this evolutionary process and fostering new European solutions and initiatives. It is therefore of every interest not to lose sight of these trends, focusing on efficiency and freedom of choice that, in competition and transparency, provide better services, based on the trust of all the actors involved. The growth dynamics of FinTech and the emergence of new service providers requires an organized, agile, timely and transparent response, involving all actors. In this regard, I hope that this conference will become a valuable contribution to helping build as much as possible a shared vision of the challenges and benefits that digital transformation and FinTech can bring to the functioning of the entire financial system and its regulation. Thank you very much 23/10/2017

O prprio sistema financeiro tornar-se- mais resiliente, com maior diversidade, redundncia e profundidade. 5. E, principalmente, os servios financeiros sero mais inclusivos, com pessoas melhor conectadas, mais informadas e cada vez mais capacitadas. , pois, indiscutvel que a utilizao da tecnologia est j a modificar significativamente o modo como os servios financeiros so prestados e percecionados pelos clientes bancrios. Mas  tambm certo e seguro que essa transformao ser cada vez mais acentuada com a chegada ao mercado financeiro dos millennials - a gerao da Internet - (o que est prestes a acontecer) e com o crescente aparecimento de diversas startups com elevada especializao tecnolgica e fortemente inovadoras. Estas startups (ou emerging companies) atuam no mercado financeiro prestando servios s instituies financeiras tradicionais ou competindo com estas, provando ser, regra geral, mais competitivas, pois as suas estruturas so consideravelmente menos pesadas em custos operacionais e regulatrios. Nesse contexto de crescente inovao disruptiva no setor financeiro, as FinTech so um tema omnipresente em diversas iniciativas polticas e legislativas de natureza geral ou estrutural. Entre estas podemos referir, por exemplo, a estratgia para a criao de um mercado nico digital, o plano para a unio do mercado de capitais, ou mesmo o Regulamento Geral de Proteo de Dados, que entrar em vigor em todo o espao da Unio em maio de 2018, e que introduz figuras novas ditadas pela tecnologia, como a formulao de perfis, as decises automatizadas ou o direito  portabilidade dos dados. As FinTech so tambm um tema presente em iniciativas sobre reas especficas, como acontece na reviso da Diretiva de Servios de Pagamentos (PSD2), de que falarei mais  frente, na reviso da Diretiva dos mercados financeiros (DMIFII), ou mesmo na regulao nacional do financiamento colaborativo. 2. O posicionamento do Banco de Portugal O Banco de Portugal tem vindo a dedicar uma crescente ateno a este tema, procurando apoiar e dinamizar, ao nvel nacional, o debate em torno dos grandes desafios que a inovao digital coloca ao sistema financeiro e  sua regulao. O Banco de Portugal organizou, em outubro do ano passado, uma importante Conferncia internacional dedicada ao tema da Banca Digital e das FinTech, que permitiu debater os desafios e as ameaas que se colocam ao sistema bancrio nestes domnios, e que contou com a presena de oradores de outros bancos centrais da Europa, do FED, do FMI e tambm de consultoras internacionais. Mais recentemente, o Banco acolheu nas suas instalaes um conjunto muito significativo de representantes do sistema financeiro e de outras entidades para a discusso da inovao e da transformao digital na banca, no mbito da conferncia "Finance Innovation Day". No incio do prximo ms, o Banco de Portugal ser o anfitrio de um desafio lanado pela CIONET, a maior comunidade mundial de gestores de tecnologias da informao, para a criao de solues tecnolgicas inovadoras no mercado de pagamentos. O desafio "PayChallenge: Rethinking Payment Services"  dirigido ao sistema bancrio, startups e universidades e tem como objetivo o desenvolvimento de solues inovadoras para o mercado dos pagamentos no mbito da nova Diretiva de Servios de Pagamento (PSD2), que entrar em vigor em janeiro de 2018. A nvel interno, o Banco de Portugal criou um grupo de reflexo multidisciplinar, com o objetivo de estudar a evoluo da Banca Digital e das FinTech e de perspetivar, no horizonte 2020, os desafios que se lhe colocam no contexto alargado da sua misso e no quadro especfico das suas responsabilidades de regulao e superviso. 3. Prestao de servios de pagamento: evoluo do quadro regulatrio como oportunidade para a inovao Como j referi, uma das reas em que as FinTech tm operado inovaes de maior impacto  a da prestao de servios de pagamento, que procurarei abordar de seguida com maior ateno. Embora o foco desta conferncia se centre nos desafios e nas oportunidades das FinTech no contexto do sector do financiamento especializado ao consumo, a verdade  que este setor  composto por diversos tipos de instituies, algumas das quais se dedicam tambm  prestao de servios de pagamento. Na realidade,  frequente a existncia de uma interconexo muito grande entre a concesso de crdito e a prestao de servios de pagamento, na medida em que estas atividades esto cada vez mais integradas na experincia de compra do cliente. Estamos, neste momento, a viver dias desafiantes no mbito dos sistemas e servios de pagamento em Portugal, aos quais no  alheia, por um lado, a publicao de uma nova Diretiva dos Servios de Pagamento (PSD2) e, por outro, as iniciativas que fomentam a inovao nos pagamentos, tirando partido do avano da tecnologia. Neste mbito, saliento a adoo de solues de pagamentos imediatos, que tem sido fomentada a nvel europeu, e em breve ser uma realidade em Portugal. Face a este quadro, colocam-se desafios aos operadores tradicionais  tipicamente, os bancos  e oportunidades para novos intervenientes, especialmente os oriundos da indstria das FinTech, que tm tido, na rea dos pagamentos de retalho e da concesso de crdito, um terreno atrativo para se estabelecerem e apresentarem ofertas inovadoras.  A Diretiva dos Servios de Pagamento revista (PSD2) Ao nvel da regulamentao que enquadra a prestao de servios de pagamento,  fundamental abordar os principais impactos associados  entrada em vigor da Diretiva dos Servios de Pagamento revista (PSD2), muitos deles disruptivos para a prestao de servios de pagamento a nvel europeu. De facto, esta Diretiva vem, no seguimento da primeira Diretiva dos Servios de Pagamento, publicada em 2009, procurar fazer face  crescente digitalizao ao nvel dos servios financeiros, que se traduziu no surgimento de novos prestadores de servios de pagamento, solues de pagamento inovadoras, utilizadores mais exigentes e novos desafios para a segurana dos pagamentos. A nova Diretiva pretende contribuir para a criao de um mercado nico para os servios de pagamento, que seja simultaneamente seguro (para prestadores de servios de pagamentos e utilizadores), eficiente, inovador e promotor da concorrncia. E  especialmente em relao a este ltimo objetivo  o da promoo da concorrncia - que importa referir aquela que  a maior novidade da Diretiva, e aquela que mais nos interessa hoje, no contexto das discusses sobre FinTech: A Diretiva vem regular dois servios de pagamento que, at  data, no beneficiavam de enquadramento regulamentar  os servios de informao sobre contas e os servios de iniciao de pagamentos. Estes servios sero prestados aos utilizadores, online, por prestadores que se consideram terceiros na relao entre o utilizador e o seu banco. Estes terceiros tero, mediante o consentimento dos utilizadores, acesso aos dados das contas dos clientes bancrios e podero, por exemplo, no caso dos servios de informao sobre contas, fornecer aos utilizadores informao agregada sobre contas detidas em vrios bancos e possibilitar servios dinmicos de gesto dos oramentos das famlias ou da tesouraria das empresas. No caso dos servios de iniciao de pagamentos, podero iniciar pagamentos em nome do utilizador, de forma cmoda e clere, sem que este tenha de sair do site do comerciante ao qual est a adquirir um produto ou servio. Embora a Diretiva permita que estes servios de pagamento sejam prestados por um banco, a verdade  que possibilita a outras entidades constiturem-se como prestadores de servios de pagamento apenas para a prestao de um daqueles dois tipos de servios, caso em que beneficiam de um regime de habilitao para a prestao de servios mais aligeirado. No obstante, a Diretiva no desconsidera as preocupaes com a segurana nos pagamentos, razo pela qual estabelece um conjunto de requisitos de segurana para os servios de pagamento fornecidos por via eletrnica, implicando que, com a sua entrada em vigor, os prestadores de servios de pagamento tero de passar a autenticar os seus clientes com recurso a mecanismos de autenticao forte, com especiais requisitos para as operaes remotas.  aqui que surge o espao para interveno das FinTech, que podero posicionar-se no mercado como entidades especializadas na prestao de determinados servios diretamente aos utilizadores, mas, tambm, aos bancos. O Banco de Portugal est ativamente envolvido na preparao do anteprojeto de transposio da PSD2 para o ordenamento jurdico nacional, tendo mesmo promovido, em junho de 2017, uma consulta pblica s opes legislativas que a Diretiva permite ao Estado Portugus exercer. A ASFAC respondeu a esta consulta, com contributos que muito agradeo, e que revelam o interesse do setor nas temticas relacionadas com os servios de pagamento.  neste contexto de mudana que os bancos nacionais e europeus tm vindo a procurar posicionar-se: se, por um lado, tm de assegurar o cumprimento atempado dos novos requisitos regulamentares, por outro, procuram no ver a PSD2 apenas como um exerccio de compliance, mas, tambm, como um incentivo  mudana, em busca de novas oportunidades de negcio, num mercado cada vez mais inovador e concorrencial.  Os Pagamentos imediatos: a inovao ao servio da celeridade nos pagamentos Como tambm j referi, a implementao de solues de pagamentos imediatos tem sido um tpico muito debatido e com papel central na evoluo vindoura do mercado de pagamentos europeu. O Eurosistema, em que o Banco de Portugal se insere, tem vindo a promover, desde 2014, a adoo de solues interoperveis de pagamentos imediatos a nvel europeu. De facto, as solues de pagamentos imediatos desenvolvidas nos ltimos anos nos pases europeus, baseadas em cartes de pagamento e/ou em transferncias a crdito no so, por norma, interoperveis entre si, pelo que no possibilitam uma utilizao transfronteiria, frustrando os objetivos do mercado nico de pagamentos. Neste quadro, em dezembro de 2014, o European Retail Payments Board (ERPB) concordou na necessidade de ser criada, pelo menos, uma soluo pan-europeia de pagamentos imediatos (atravs do recurso a transferncias a crdito) em euros, acessvel a qualquer prestador de servios de pagamento a operar na Unio Europeia, originando-se assim um processo que tem merecido o empenho de mltiplos atores. A soluo criada, que estar disponvel para adoo efetiva pelos prestadores de servios de pagamento a partir de 21 de novembro de 2017, vem alterar profundamente o paradigma de execuo de pagamentos, uma vez que estabelece que:  Os fundos devero estar disponveis na conta do beneficirio num tempo mximo indicativo de dez segundos;  O prestador de servios de pagamento do beneficirio  obrigado a aceitar todas as transaes de valor igual ou inferior a 15 mil euros;  As operaes podem ser ordenadas a qualquer momento do dia e em qualquer dia do ano, isto , com uma disponibilidade de 24/7/365; e,  Os prestadores de servios de pagamento do ordenante e do beneficirio podem estar estabelecidos em qualquer um dos 34 pases que integram a SEPA. Neste mbito, diversas comunidades bancrias vo lanar nos prximos meses solues de pagamentos imediatos. Tambm em Portugal est a ser preparada uma soluo cooperativa nacional de pagamentos imediatos, compatvel com os princpios e requisitos tcnicos harmonizados definidos a nvel europeu, e enquadrada no mbito do Sistema de Compensao Interbancria gerido pelo Banco de Portugal. Tambm aqui  notrio o potencial de interveno das FinTech: num contexto em que, por exemplo, a prestao de servios de iniciao de pagamentos regulamentada pela PSD2 pode ser potenciada numa utilizao efetiva das solues de pagamentos imediatos disponibilizadas a um nvel infraestrutural, colocando as FinTech numa situao em que podero prestar servios que proporcionem flexibilidade, rapidez e confiana dos utilizadores. 4. Concluso Neste quadro, no posso seno concluir que assistimos hoje a um conjunto de desenvolvimentos tecnolgicos, sociolgicos e, acima de tudo, regulamentares, que daro origem a um mercado de prestao de servios de pagamento de retalho quase transfigurado face ao que foi a prtica predominante nas ltimas dcadas.  importante que tanto os operadores tradicionais, como as FinTech saibam posicionar-se no mercado, combinando a necessidade de observar as novas exigncias regulamentares com a possibilidade de tirarem partido da nova realidade, crescentemente dinmica e interopervel, pugnando para que a eficincia e a segurana dos servios prestados sejam os fatores determinantes do seu sucesso. Naturalmente, a uma crescente digitalizao dos servios financeiros ter de corresponder uma igualmente crescente preocupao com a segurana digital na realizao das operaes e com a proteo de dados pessoais dos clientes dessas operaes. Estes so temas centrais no debate em curso e que seguramente sero amplamente tratados ao longo desta conferncia. O Banco de Portugal, no quadro da sua insero no Eurosistema, tem assumido um papel ativo de apoio a este processo evolutivo e de fomento das novas solues e iniciativas europeias.  pois de todo o interesse no perder de vista estas tendncias, com foco na eficincia e na liberdade de escolha que, em concorrncia e com transparncia, propiciem melhores servios, assentes na confiana de todos os agentes envolvidos. A dinmica de crescimento das FinTech e de aparecimento de novos prestadores de servios exige uma resposta organizada, gil, tempestiva e transparente, envolvendo todos os atores. Nesse sentido, espero que esta conferncia se transforme num valioso contributo para ajudar  construo de uma viso tanto quanto possvel partilhada sobre os desafios e os benefcios que a transformao digital e as FinTech podem introduzir no funcionamento de todo o sistema financeiro e na sua regulao. Muito obrigado 23/10/2017

Title: Intervention of Administrator Hlder Rosalino at the opening session of the Conference "Cybersecurity in the financial system: risks, cooperation and governance"
text: Cybersecurity in the financial system: risks, cooperation and governance June 30, 2017 Intervention in the opening session of Administrator Helder Rosalino 1 1 Prepared for presentation. Welcome to Banco de Portugal and the conference we have organized on "Cybersecurity in the financial system: risks, cooperation and governance". I thank, on behalf of the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal and the organizing departments, the high interest shown in the participation in this Conference, both of entities of the banking system widely represented here, and of many other entities that have joined this initiative. While the issue of cybersecurity is transversal to all types of organizations and sectors of activity, this conference focuses primarily on the financial system and addresses some of the dimensions of cybersecurity that arise in this sector.  We have a first panel on the impact of cyber-risk on the Financial System and business continuity:  We have a second panel that focuses on Cybersecurity Cooperation and Governance in the context of the Financial System: The theme of Cybersecurity It is a topic of great relevance, to all titles, as evidenced by the computer attack recorded last Tuesday (known as NotPetya) and that had impacts on a global scale. As had already happened with the cyber-attack in May, known as WannaCry, which put cybersecurity at the heart of public debate and the concerns of all public and private organisations. However, these attacks have also shown that we are not yet sufficiently prepared to face this new threat and that we have no clear collective awareness of what it represents. What we know is that the current context in this context is characterized:  The increasing complexity and volume of cyberattacks;  The existence of increasingly sophisticated cybercrime networks, possibly supported by States whose economy may be based in part on this activity, given the financial return it can generate;  The lack of adequate legal framework, or still embryonic development, creating a sense of impunity in the realization of malicious acts in cyberspace;  By the permanent and unpredictable nature of the attacks: no specific time to happen and can come geographically from any side, which requires continuous and increasingly complex surveillance to implement;  By increasing the risk to the functioning of organizations, with progressively more destructive cyberattacks and with effective capacity to interrupt sectors and business vital to the functioning of the economy. This is the case with the latest attacks (WannaCry and NotPetya), which have caused damage globally and across the board, affecting sectors such as banking, healthcare, communications service operators, among others. We certainly live in an environment of high complexity in terms of cybersecurity, enhanced by a set of risks and threats that calls for reflection and above all to action. The context The use of technologies and information systems has allowed, in recent decades, a complete transformation of the way companies operate. In a short period of time, we have started to communicate globally at very low costs, build new forms of relationships between people and between companies, learn to take advantage of the large volume of data and information we produce, automate processes, control at a distance, among many other technological-based developments. In a few years, we completely reorganize our lives around technologies. And when we look forward we realize that the potential for evolution and application of these technologies is enormous and will inevitably accelerate. In the financial system evolution was parallel and Portugal has been at the forefront in some areas of innovation. We can recall, as a pioneering and always mentioned example, the "ATM system" which allows a large number of networked banking operations and outside the branches, along side the recent massification of digital banking and the extraordinary evolution of the electronic payment systems to which we have assisted. All these developments have allowed significant gains in efficiency and effectiveness. Dependency However, the advantages were so great and developments were so rapid that, without realizing it, the whole society became dependent on information technologies. In such a way that we can no longer imagine how we can function without them. By not, of course, calling into question the enormous benefits of information technologies, the truth is that the dependency created is of great concern. The vulnerabilities generated by this dependency take on several facets, which have produced some recently known examples:  One respects the relative ease and impunity with which individuals or groups are able to carry out thefts and cause harm to third parties, as happened in the case of the theft to the Bangladesh Central Bank, which resulted in losses of around EUR 84 million, but whose damage could have exceeded EUR 1 billion;  Another example is the system failures themselves, either automatic or manually caused, the impacts of which can be extremely high, as happened recently when a power failure in the British Airways Data Center led to the cancellation of numerous flights and extremely high financial impacts;  We also have the growing interconnection of the Cyber and physical worlds, which led, for example, to a cyberattack shut down power plants in Ukraine at the end of last year. Or that hackers could turn off the video surveillance cameras at the inauguration of the President of the United States.  And we naturally have the massive spread of malicious software that can lead to total or partial disruption of information systems, such as attacks that have occurred recently. It is in this context of almost permanent threat, under different facets, that cybersecurity is of increasing and fundamental importance. This importance brings us to the issues of Governance and Cooperation in the field of cybersecurity. Good cybersecurity government is an unavoidable challenge at the moment and will be even more so in the future. That's a conscience we're now assuming, maybe a little late. This good government must be embodied in a Global Cybersecurity Strategy, based on a 360 organizational vision and associated with a corporate security culture, recovering the concept of Corporate Security. This concept is based on an integrated approach to information security, systems and technologies and physical security. This Global Strategy should be based on the three essential pillars of cybersecurity [people, processes and technology], but also on a culture of institutional cooperation that promotes the sharing of information and, above all, develops networks of trust and joint work between similar entities and peers. It is necessary, more than ever, to promote strong collaboration and organisation in the cybercrime field to address the growing threats. Individuals and organizations must create sufficient conditions to promote their self-protection, and on the other hand, participate as an integral part of a defence system that has to involve everyone. This issue will be discussed in depth in the Panel on Cybersecurity Cooperation and Governance in the second part of this conference. Likewise, it is extremely important to focus on the training and awareness of people (and with this of the whole organization), as a central and first-line pillar in the defense of cyber-attacks. There is still a long work to be done in this area. The role of Banco de Portugal Banco de Portugal is naturally attentive and concerned about this reality. It should be noted that Since 2011 Banco de Portugal has been developing a consistent strategy in the field of cybersecurity, with important and recognized results at national and international level. At home, Banco de Portugal has highly specialised cybersecurity resources and has in recent times been developing and strengthening its skills and expanding its cooperation networks in the field of cybercrime prevention. As regulator and supervisor of the financial system, Banco de Portugal has also more recently developed a set of initiatives and actions aimed at integrating and functioning the entire system in the field of cybersecurity. This has happened:  Through the creation of a specialized team in the soc (Security Operations Center) and CSIRT ( Computer Security Incident Response Team ) and CSIRT ( Computer Security Incident Response Team), with human resources dedicated to cybersecurity management from the internal and sectoral perspective;  Through the promotion of strategic partnerships in this area, namely with the National Cybersecurity Center and the Judicial Police, in the figure of its National Cybercrime Unit; and in general terms  Through the promotion of a culture of knowledge sharing, experiences and methodologies of defense and mitigation, both at eSCB level and at national level in the relationship with various entities linked to the financial system. Recently, taking into account its obligations as a central bank, Banco de Portugal has begun a process of strengthening its competences and organisation the creation of a CSIRT for the banking sector, focusing on the following aspects:  Establishment of communication channels for the exchange of relevant information with all financial sector entities;  Development of intelligence processes aimed at the timely prediction of planned attacks;  Strengthening the automatic detection capacity of cyberattacks by creating technological controls of various order. This development should position Banco de Portugal, of course, as the centralising entity and aggregator of the banking sector for the cybersecurity aspect, functioning as a responsible entity at the sectoral level. In this role, the Bank will encourage cooperation and collaboration within the banking sector, in a close and integrated manner with the national authority, the National Cybersecurity Center. Along these lines, an internal working group was set up to support the National Cybersecurity Centre in transposition of the Network and Information System Security Directive (NIS). Work that's already underway. These actions are representative of the importance that cybersecurity assumes for Banco de Portugal, from its own perspective and the financial sector. The organization of this conference is a reflection of this importance. It is also a way of fostering knowledge sharing and presenting the role of Banco de Portugal in promoting cybersecurity, especially in view of its sectoral role. Concluding We must begin by recognizing that cybersecurity currently plays a key role in defending some of our basic principles of citizenship and even defending some of the fundamental foundations on which our current life model is built. Because of its role in our economic and social organization, the banking sector is especially targeted by cybercrime activities, both because of the relevance of its functions, or by the openness and natural vulnerabilities of the technological systems that support its activity. The management of these risks is increasingly important, mainly due to the challenges facing financial institutions today in the areas of digital transformation and the evolution of related regulatory frameworks, which tend to create increasingly open and competitive environments in the banking sector. In this context, it is assumed that the financial system should be equipped in a particular way for the promotion of cybersecurity. For its part, Banco de Portugal will clearly and committedly assume its responsibilities in this area. Both as an active agent in the creation and promotion of an integrated cyber-defense system for the banking sector, and as a supervisor, naturally requiring banks to implement strategies and mechanisms for the protection, sharing and reporting of necessary information. I hope that this conference will become a valuable contribution to help build a shared vision on the challenges we face in the field of cybersecurity and on the best forms of cooperation to combat the new and growing threat of cybercrime. Thank you very much Elder Rosalino Glossary of terms: Cyberattack [Definition]  Attack carried out through information technologies in cyberspace directed against one or more systems, with the aim of harming the security of information and communication technologies (confidentiality, integrity and availability), in part or totally. [Source] - Austrian Cyber Security Strategy (2013), cited in NATO CCDCOE. CyberCrime [Definition]  Criminal acts committed online using electronic communication networks and information systems. [Source] - European Commission. Cyber defense [Definition]  The term "cyber defense" refers to all measures used to defend cyberspace with military means and appropriate to achieve military strategic objectives. Cyber defense is an integrated system comprising the implementation of all ICT and information security measures, milCERT and CNO (computer network operations) resources, as well as the support of the army's physical resources. [Source] - Austrian Cyber Security Strategy (2013), cited in NATO CCDCOE. Cyberspace [Definition]  Metaphor used to describe the non-physical space created by computer networks, namely the Internet, where people can communicate in different ways, for example, through electronic messages, in chat rooms or in discussion forums. [Source] - Association for the Promotion and Development of the Information Society. Csirt National Network [Definition]  The National Network of CSIRTs is a forum for the sharing of operational information. Its main objectives are:  Establish bonds of trust between elements responsible for IT security in order to create an environment of cooperation and mutual assistance in the handling of incidents and the sharing of good security practices;  Create national statistical indicators and information on security incidents with a view to better identifying proactive and reactive countermeasures;  Create the tools needed for prevention and rapid response in a large incident scenario;  Promote a culture of security in Portugal. [Source] - National Cybersecurity Center Portugal Network and Information Systems Security [Definition]  the ability of networks and information systems to resist, with a given level of trust, actions that compromise the availability, authenticity, integrity or confidentiality of data stored, transmitted or processed, or related services offered by such networks or information systems, accessible through them. [Source]  Directive (EU) No 2016/1148 of the European Parliament and the Council of 6 July 2016 on measures to ensure a high common level of network and information security across the Union.
text_original: Cibersegurana no sistema financeiro: riscos, cooperao e governao 30 de junho de 2017 Interveno na sesso de abertura do Administrador Hlder Rosalino 1 1 Preparado para apresentao. Bem-vindos ao Banco de Portugal e  conferncia que organizamos sobre Cibersegurana no sistema financeiro: riscos, cooperao e governao. Agradeo, em nome do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Portugal e dos departamentos organizadores, o elevado interesse demonstrado na participao nesta Conferncia, tanto de entidades do sistema bancrio aqui amplamente representadas, como de muitas outras entidades que se associaram a esta iniciativa. No obstante o tema da cibersegurana ser transversal a todo o tipo de organizaes e setores de atividade, esta conferncia foca-se essencialmente no sistema financeiro e aborda algumas das dimenses da cibersegurana que se colocam a este setor.  Temos um primeiro painel sobre o impacto do ciber-risco no Sistema Financeiro e na continuidade de negcio:  Temos um segundo painel que se foca na Cooperao e Governao de Cibersegurana no contexto do Sistema Financeiro: O tema da Cibersegurana  um tema de grande atualidade, a todos os ttulos, como o comprova o ataque informtico registado na passada tera-feira (conhecido como NotPetya) e que teve impactos  escala global. Como, alis, j tinha acontecido com o ciberataque registado em maio, conhecido como WannaCry, que colocou a cibersegurana no centro do debate pblico e das preocupaes de todas as organizaes pblicas e privadas. No entanto, esses ataques tambm vieram demonstrar que ainda no estamos suficientemente preparados para enfrentar esta nova ameaa e que, to pouco, temos uma conscincia coletiva apurada sobre o que a mesma representa. O que sabemos  que o contexto atual, neste mbito, se carateriza:  Pela crescente complexidade e volumetria dos ciberataques;  Pela existncia de redes de cibercrime cada vez mais sofisticadas, eventualmente suportadas por Estados cuja economia se pode basear, em parte, nesta atividade, dado o retorno financeiro que pode gerar;  Pela falta de enquadramento legal adequado, ou em desenvolvimento ainda embrionrio, criando um sentimento de impunidade na concretizao de atos maliciosos no ciberespao;  Pelo carter permanente e imprevisvel dos ataques: sem hora especfica para acontecer e podendo vir geograficamente de qualquer lado, o que obriga a uma vigilncia contnua e cada vez mais complexa de implementar;  Pelo aumento do risco para o funcionamento das organizaes, com ciberataques progressivamente mais destrutivos e com capacidade efetiva de interrupo de setores e negcio vitais para o funcionamento da economia. Foi, alis, o que aconteceu com os mais recentes ataques (WannaCry e o NotPetya), que causaram danos a nvel mundial e de forma transversal, afetando setores como a banca, a sade, os operadores de servios de comunicaes, entre outros. Vivemos, sem dvida, num ambiente de elevada complexidade em termos de cibersegurana, potenciado por um conjunto de riscos e ameaas que a todos convoca para a reflexo e sobretudo para a ao. O contexto A utilizao de tecnologias e de sistemas de informao permitiu, nas ltimas dcadas, uma completa transformao da forma de funcionamento das sociedades. Num curto espao de tempo, passmos a comunicar globalmente a custos muito baixos, construmos novas formas de relaes entre as pessoas e entre as empresas, aprendemos a tirar partido do grande volume de dados e de informao que produzimos, automatizmos processos, passmos a controlar  distncia, entre muitas outras evolues de base tecnolgica. Em suma, reorganizamos completamente a nossa vida em torno das tecnologias. E quando olhamos para a frente percebemos que o potencial de evoluo e de aplicao destas tecnologias  enorme e tender inevitavelmente a acelerar. No sistema financeiro a evoluo foi paralela e Portugal tem estado na linha da frente em algumas reas de inovao. Podemos recordar, como exemplo pioneiro e sempre citado, o sistema multibanco que permite a realizao de um grande nmero de operaes bancrias em rede e fora dos balces, a par da recente massificao da banca digital e da extraordinria evoluo dos sistemas de pagamentos eletrnicos a que temos assistido. Todas estas evolues permitiram significativos ganhos de eficincia e de eficcia. A dependncia Porm, as vantagens foram to grandes e a evoluo foi to rpida que, sem nos apercebermos disso, toda a sociedade ficou dependente das tecnologias de informao. De tal forma que j no conseguimos imaginar como poderemos funcionar sem elas. No pondo, naturalmente, em causa os enormes benefcios das tecnologias de informao, a verdade  que a dependncia criada  motivo de enorme preocupao. As vulnerabilidades geradas por esta dependncia assumem vrias facetas, que produziram alguns exemplos recentemente conhecidos:  Um respeita  relativa facilidade e impunidade com que indivduos ou grupos conseguem realizar roubos e causar danos a terceiros, como aconteceu no caso do roubo ao Banco Central do Bangladeche, que se traduziu em perdas na ordem dos 84 milhes de euros, mas cujos danos podiam ter ultrapassado os mil milhes de euros;  Outro exemplo, so as prprias falhas nos sistemas, ou automticas ou provocadas manualmente, cujos impactos podem ser extremamente elevados, como aconteceu recentemente quando uma falha de energia no Data Center da British Airways levou ao cancelamento de inmeros voos e a impactos financeiros extremamente elevados;  Temos ainda a crescente interligao dos mundos Ciber e fsico, que levaram, por exemplo, a que um ciberataque desligasse centrais eltricas na Ucrnia, no final do ano passado. Ou que hackers conseguissem desligar as cmaras de videovigilncia na tomada de posse do Presidente dos Estados Unidos.  E temos naturalmente a disseminao massiva de software malicioso que pode levar  disrupo total ou parcial dos sistemas de informao, como so exemplo os ataques que ocorreram recentemente.  neste contexto de ameaa quase permanente, sob diferentes facetas, que a cibersegurana assume uma crescente e fundamental importncia. Essa importncia remete-nos para os temas da Governao e da Cooperao no domnio da cibersegurana. O bom governo da cibersegurana  um desafio incontornvel no momento atual e s-lo- ainda mais no futuro. Essa  uma conscincia que estamos agora a assumir, talvez um pouco tarde. Esse bom governo deve estar consubstanciado numa Estratgia Global de cibersegurana, baseada numa viso organizacional a 360 e associada a uma cultura de segurana corporativa, recuperando o conceito de Corporate Security. Este conceito assenta numa abordagem integrada da segurana da informao, dos sistemas e tecnologias e da segurana fsica. Esta Estratgia Global dever assentar sobre os trs pilares essenciais da cibersegurana [pessoas, processos e tecnologia], mas tambm sobre uma cultura de cooperao institucional que promova a partilha de informao e, sobretudo, que desenvolva a criao de redes de confiana e de trabalho conjunto entre entidades congneres e pares.  necessrio, mais do que nunca, promover uma forte colaborao e organizao no domnio ciber-crime para enfrentar as crescentes ameaas. Os indivduos e as organizaes tm de criar condies suficientes para, por um lado, promoverem a sua autoproteo, e por outro, participar como parte integrante de um sistema de defesa que tem que envolver todos. Esta questo ser aprofundadamente debatida no painel sobre a Cooperao e Governao de Cibersegurana, na segunda parte desta conferncia. Do mesmo modo,  de extrema importncia apostar na formao e na consciencializao das pessoas (e com isso de toda a organizao), como pilar fulcral e de primeira linha na defesa a ciber-ataques. Neste domnio h ainda um longo trabalho a fazer. O papel do Banco de Portugal O Banco de Portugal est naturalmente atento e preocupado com esta realidade. Importa referir que o Banco de Portugal desenvolve, desde 2011, uma estratgia consistente no domnio da cibersegurana, com resultados importantes e reconhecidos ao nvel nacional e internacional. Internamente, o Banco de Portugal dispe de recursos altamente especializados em cibersegurana e tem vindo, nos ltimos tempos, a desenvolver e reforar as suas competncias e a alargar as suas redes de cooperao no domnio da preveno do cibercrime. Enquanto regulador e supervisor do sistema financeiro, o Banco de Portugal tem igualmente desenvolvido, mais recentemente, um conjunto de iniciativas e aes orientadas para a integrao e o bom funcionamento de todo o sistema no domnio da cibersegurana. Isso tem acontecido:  Atravs da criao de uma equipa especializada na vertente de SOC (Security Operations Center) e de CSIRT  Computer Security Incident Response Team, com recursos humanos dedicados  gesto da Cibersegurana na perspetiva interna e sectorial;  Atravs da promoo de parcerias estratgias nesta rea, nomeadamente com o Centro Nacional de Cibersegurana e com a Polcia Judiciria, na figura da sua Unidade Nacional de Combate ao Cibercrime; e em termos gerais  Atravs da promoo de uma cultura de partilha de conhecimento, experincias e metodologias de defesa e mitigao, tanto ao nvel do SEBC, como ao nvel nacional na relao com vrias entidades ligadas ao sistema financeiro. Recentemente, tendo em considerao as suas obrigaes enquanto banco central, o Banco de Portugal iniciou um processo de reforo das suas competncias e organizao no sentido da criao de um CSIRT para o setor bancrio, com enfoque nas seguintes vertentes:  Estabelecimento de canais de comunicao para troca de informaes relevantes com todas as entidades do setor financeiro;  Desenvolvimento de processos de intelligence, que visem a previso atempada de ataques planeados;  Reforo da capacidade de deteo automtica de ciberataques, mediante a criao de controlos tecnolgicos de vria ordem. Esta evoluo dever posicionar o Banco de Portugal, naturalmente, como a entidade centralizadora e agregadora do setor bancrio para a vertente da cibersegurana, funcionando como entidade responsvel ao nvel sectorial. Nesse papel, o Banco incentivar a cooperao e a colaborao dentro do sector bancrio, de forma prxima e integrada com a autoridade nacional, o Centro Nacional de Cibersegurana. Nessa linha, foi criado um grupo de trabalho interno para apoio ao Centro Nacional de Cibersegurana na transposio da Diretiva relativa  Segurana das Redes e dos Sistema de Informao (SRI/NIS). Trabalho que j est em curso. Estas aes so representativas da importncia que a cibersegurana assume para o Banco de Portugal, na perspetiva prpria e do sector financeiro. A organizao desta conferncia  o reflexo dessa importncia.  tambm uma forma de fomentar a partilha de conhecimento e de apresentar o papel do Banco de Portugal na promoo da cibersegurana, sobretudo na perspetiva do seu papel sectorial. Concluindo Temos que comear por reconhecer que a cibersegurana tem atualmente um papel fundamental na defesa de alguns dos nossos princpios bsicos de cidadania e mesmo na defesa de alguns dos alicerces fundamentais em que est construdo o nosso modelo de vida atual. Pelo papel que desempenha na nossa organizao econmica e social, o setor bancrio  especialmente visado pelas atividades do cibercrime, quer pela relevncia das suas funes, quer pela abertura e vulnerabilidades naturais dos sistemas tecnolgicos que suportam a sua atividade. A gesto destes riscos  cada vez mais importante, sobretudo devido aos desafios que as instituies financeiras enfrentam atualmente nos domnios da transformao digital e da evoluo dos quadros regulamentares conexos, que tendem a criar ambientes cada vez mais abertos e competitivos no sector bancrio. Neste contexto,  assumido que o sistema financeiro se deve apetrechar de modo particular para a promoo da cibersegurana. Pela sua parte, o Banco de Portugal assumir de forma clara e empenhada as suas responsabilidades nesta rea. Quer como agente ativo na criao e promoo de um sistema integrado de ciber-defesa para o setor bancrio, quer como supervisor exigindo naturalmente que os Bancos implementem estratgias e mecanismos de proteo, partilha e reporte de informao necessrios. Espero que esta conferncia se transforme num valioso contributo para ajudar  construo de uma viso partilhada sobre os desafios que enfrentamos no domnio da cibersegurana e sobre as melhores formas de cooperao para combater a nova e crescente ameaa do cibercrime. [Fonte] - Austrian Cyber Security Strategy (2013), citado em NATO CCDCOE. CiberCrime [Definio]  Atos criminosos cometidos cometidos on-line utilizando redes de comunicao eletrnicas e sistemas de informao. [Fonte]  Comisso Europeia. Ciberdefesa [Definio]  O termo "ciber defesa" refere-se a todas as medidas utilizadas para defender o espao ciberntico com os meios militares e apropriados para alcanar objetivos estratgico militares. A ciber defesa  um sistema integrado, que compreende a implementao de todas as medidas relacionadas com as TIC e a segurana da informao, os recursos milCERT e CNO (operaes de rede do computador), bem como o apoio dos recursos fsicos do exrcito. [Fonte] - Austrian Cyber Security Strategy (2013), citado em NATO CCDCOE. Ciberespao [Definio]  Metfora usada para descrever o espao no fsico criado por redes de computadores, nomeadamente pela Internet, onde as pessoas podem comunicar de diferentes maneiras, por exemplo, atravs de mensagens eletrnicas, em salas de conversa ou em fruns de discusso. [Fonte] - Associao para a Promoo e Desenvolvimento da Sociedade de Informao. Tem como principais objetivos:  Estabelecer laos de confiana entre elementos responsveis pela segurana informtica de forma a criar um ambiente de cooperao e assistncia mtua no tratamento de incidentes e na partilha de boas prticas de segurana;  Criar indicadores e informao estatstica nacional sobre incidentes de segurana com vista  melhor identificao de contra-medidas pr-ativas e reativas;  Criar os instrumentos necessrios  preveno e resposta rpida num cenrio de incidente de grande dimenso;  Promover uma cultura de segurana em Portugal. [Fonte] - Centro Nacional de Cibersegurana Portugal Segurana das Redes e dos Sistemas de Informao [Definio]  a capacidade das redes e dos sistemas de informao para resistir, com um dado nvel de confiana, a aes que comprometam a disponibilidade, a autenticidade, a integridade ou a confidencialidade dos dados armazenados, transmitidos ou tratados, ou dos servios conexos oferecidos por essas redes ou por esses sistemas de informao, ou acessveis atravs deles. Title: Intervention of Administrator Jos Silveira Godinho at the APB Conference on the Payment System Portuguese "The Challenges of SEPA"
text: SEMINAR ON PAYMENT SYSTEMS (promoted by APB) Lisbon, December 4, 2013 SEPA's challenges Intervention of the Administrator of Banco de Portugal Jose da Silveira Godinho Framing Payment systems are a central component of the financial system, alongside markets and institutions. From this perspective, the existence of efficient and reliable payment, clearing and settlement systems is essential for economic and financial transactions, as well as for the implementation of monetary policy and for preserving the stability of the financial system, thus constituting a key element for the functioning of the economy as a whole. As a general rule, the fact that payment systems are not talked about is a sign of their well-functioning and resilience, based on efficient infrastructure. In recent years, developments in the field of payments have been determined by the implementation of SEPA  Single Euro Payments Area  implying the dedication of resources by banks and companies, and  not least  by regulators, including Banco de Portugal. 1. SEPA: a European project The implementation of SEPA is a project approaching a crucial stage, as from 1 February 2014 all payments deputed in euro in an enlarged geographical area will have to comply with a set of common rules and standards in its implementation, in particular when it comes to credit transfer or direct debit transactions. This initiative covers a total of 33 countries whose national systems have their own characteristics and diverse starting points in view of the harmonisation objectives set for the full scope of a single euro payment area. From the outset, the countries that currently make up the euro zone will be the most immediately affected by the implementation of SEPA, with some obligations that the rest will need to meet only after 31 October 2016. Overall, SEPA covers the 28 countries of the European Union, as well as Iceland, Norway and Liechtenstein (integrated into the European Economic Area), as well as Monaco and Switzerland. 1.1. Objectives and brief project history The establishment of these objectives stems from the intention expressed since 2001 by the European Commission to equate the conditions applicable to retail payment transactions carried out in a national context with a set of harmonised rules at pan-European level. To this end, the publication of Regulation (EC) No 2560/2001 of 19 December set out the first concrete step on this path, which, in essence, is a natural consequence of the introduction of the euro as a single currency. In fact, in addition to the harmonisation achieved at cash level, the execution and processing of book-entry payments was based on fragmented infrastructure, operating the market from a purely national perspective. The path taken to date has identified a multitude of obstacles, often associated with national specificities of several countries, to which the European payments industry  in particular banks  has sought to respond by finding the most appropriate solutions within the applicable regulatory framework, which it has also gradually built during this period. 1.2. SEPA governance: the role of authorities and the market The entire implementation of the SEPA project has been framed by the actions of the authorities and the fact that it involves a wide range of stakeholders has involved the establishment of an appropriate governance structure, co-led by the European Commission and the European Central Bank and bringing together representatives from the retail payment services side  namely the European Payments Council ( composed of European banks)  and on the demand side  through European associations representative of public administration bodies, treasurers of large companies, as well as SMEs and consumers. Thus, in mid-2010, the SEPA Council entered into operation, following up on the publication of the Ecofin conclusions of 2 December 2009, materialised in an agreement between the European Commission and the ECB reached in March 2010. Its primary objective, as established, was to promote the realisation of the SEPA vision, with a strategic orientation towards the evolution of retail payments in euro within the EU, ensuring the involvement of all relevant players in this area. To date, Ecofin encouraged the European Commission and the ECB to improve the existing framework for SEPA governance, pointing to a new structure starting by the end of the first half of 2010. The first sepa council meeting took place in Brussels on 7 June 2010. More recently, as part of the evolution of the regulatory framework for retail payments, this model has been re-equated, with the prospect that, with the consolidation of SEPA, the SEPA Council will be succeeded by a permanent structure, focused on the constant evolution of this market, the Euro Retail Payments Board (ERPB). The definition of the contours of the new forum is still being finalised and should be part of the ECB's intervention, which will chair and boost the work, with the participation of the European Commission and maintaining a representative composition. A more visible balance should be promoted compared to what is currently happening in SEPA Council, between payment service providers (supply side) and their users (demand side), by enhancing their involvement, which should be strengthened. There is an expectation that the first ERPB meeting could take place by the end of Q1 2014, and this new structure should have a 2-level operating model, a strategic and a technical one, possibly using ad hoc groups. At the same time, the Eurosystem has held regular meetings of the SEPA High Level Group, composed of elements at the level of the Governing Councils of the ECB and the NCBs, preparing to take a position on the topics under consideration by the SEPA Council. This group should remain active after the creation of the ERPB, and will occasionally hold high-level meetings with market representatives to assess ongoing developments and share information and concerns on the part of the Eurosystem. The next meeting of this ECB's High Level Group will take place on 19 December, attended by representatives of euro zone credit institutions, and will focus on the final phase of the migration period. 2. The challenges that SEPA entails for Portugal, whether current or future, The context of sepa implementation naturally entails challenges for the payment system Portuguese, one of the most advanced at European level. If, on the one hand, it was necessary to adopt various adjustments in order to be in line with sepa requirements, it is also true that there are a number of services developed over the years by the national community, which have created payment habits among users; in this new phase, it is important to ensure such services in the most appropriate way, without contradicting the grounds and the progressive explanation of the SEPA framework. In fact, the Portuguese payment system has in recent years shown a trend towards the increasing use of electronic instruments to the detriment of paper-based instruments. Since then, while the cheque has seen a marked decrease in its use  corresponding in 2012 to just over 5% of the total book keeping transactions (excluding cash) recorded in Portugal, when in 2000 this indicator was 33%  the use of electronic payment instruments has been significantly increased. In this case, card payments predominate, which represented in 2012 about 68% of the same universe of transactions, compared to 50% in 2000. In the instruments covered by SEPA in its current phase  credit transfers (TC) and direct debits (DD)  the evolution of its indicators between 2000 and 2012 was, respectively, from 5% to 12% (in CT) and from 12% to 14% (in DDs). In this process of migration to SEPA, Banco de Portugal has been playing a catalyst role, promoting debate, sharing and dissemination of relevant information to the various stakeholders and market players. The publication of the National Migration Plan for SEPA at the end of 2012 made it possible to clarify a set of objectives that contribute to the achievement of full migration to the SEPA format of credit transfer and direct debit transactions in the national community. In addition to establishing the expectation that the various actors will ensure their contribution, the Plan also points out a list of actions that several entities, namely Banco de Portugal, have committed to implement. In this context, it is worth mentioning the holding, in June and July 2013, of a cycle of 10 regional seminars aimed primarily at SMEs and public administration bodies at local level, often identified as being among the most vulnerable groups with regard to access to relevant information on such a project. These seminars, organized by Banco de Portugal in several cities in the country, with the collaboration of banks and SIBS, proved of great use to those entities. In addition, a number of other communication initiatives have been taken, namely those aimed at entities that collect through direct debits in Portugal, drawing attention to the effort required to complete the migration process in a timely manner, in an area where it is essential that the companies themselves make adaptations to their systems, in partnership with the banks providing payment services and the software providers with which they relate. Also in order to inform the general public about SEPA, Banco de Portugal published in October a leaflet, making available 200,000 copies to the banking system, aiming at dissemination through its customer base. In addition, the newsletter SEPA.pt has maintained the publication of 2 editions per year since 2011, highlighting developments in the project, and its no. 6 dated last October. It is also expected to soon publish a set of FAQs on the Internet, based on the requests for clarification that have been put to Banco de Portugal over the last few months. 2.1. Banco de Portugal's tasks in the field of Payment Systems In the framework of this action, the tasks of Banco de Portugal should be taken into account with regard to its intervention in payment systems, in which it performs four functions: (i) regulator; (ii) supervisory authority; (iii) operator and provider of settlement services in central bank currency; and (iv) catalyst and promoter of the efficiency and development of payment systems. As a general framework, the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, which establishes, in article 127(2) of its article, that the fundamental tasks conferred on the ESCB should be considered, among others, to promote the proper functioning of payment systems. This follows the provisions of the Statute of the ESCB and the ECB, which in paragraph 1 of Article 3 of article 3 reflect precisely this task and, in addition, state in Article 22 that "The ECB and the national central banks may grant facilities and the ECB may adopt regulations in order to ensure the efficiency and soundness of clearing and payment systems within the Union and with third countries". From this regulatory framework, it follows that the Organic Law of Banco de Portugal states, in article 14, that it is for the Bank to regulate, monitor and promote the proper functioning of payment systems, in particular in the context of its participation in the ESCB. It should be noted that Banco de Portugal has maintained, as an advisory body of its Board of Directors, the Interbank Commission for Payment Systems (CISP), created in 1997, and whose structure of working groups dedicated to these matters has enabled us to achieve cooperative solutions in the national community, pursuing and deepening good practices and introducing new solutions within payment systems and instruments. On the other hand, also as an advisory body of the Bank, the Forum for Payment Systems was created in 2009, which allowed the establishment of a regular dialogue with entities using these services, among the most prominent at national level, such as large distribution companies, telecommunications, insurance, among others, alongside public administration bodies (e.g. the IGCP or Social Security), also including the National Association of Portuguese Municipalities, as well as representatives of consumers. 2.2. Regulation 260/2012: a crucial trigger At SEPA's regulatory framework level, the publication on 30 March 2012 of Regulation (EU) No 260/2012 set up a key part of the process as it made it possible to clarify a number of aspects that until then lacked due framework by the authorities, giving guidance and constituting a change factor for the market. It should be noted that the initial expectation, in the foresight of a single area of payments in euro, would be that, in view of the objectives outlined by the authorities, there would be a self-regulation by the market in order to materialise this desideratum. This would be the gradual discontinuation of the use of legacy solutions, centered on national characteristics, being replaced by SEPA-compatible solutions, following the definition of operational rules at the initiative of the industry itself. However, this commitment effort has not been brought to a successful point, leading to the need to establish, by legislative means, the rules to be observed and their implementation schedule. Regulation (EU) No 260/2012 thus established the technical and business requirements applicable to euro credit transfer and direct debit transactions, as well as setting the deadline for the migration process: 1 February 2014. The publication of this diploma with an extended advance advance over the migration deadline (slightly less than 2 years) sought to provide conditions for market players  banks, companies and public administration bodies  to position themselves in good time in terms of preparing the necessary adaptations. In addition, the Regulation gave Member States the prerogative to adopt a set of derogations, as well as to designate competent authorities to ensure compliance with them, and to establish the applicable sanctioning regime. It should be noted that the European Commission may, in such cases (involving compliance with deadlines), trigger a subsequent verification procedure, some 3 months after the date in question, through requests for information from the competent authorities designated in each Member State, which in this particular case will be Banco de Portugal, which may have an "impact" on Portuguese payment service providers. 2.3. Decree-Law 141/2013 and its derogatory and sanctioning aspects In this context, the Portuguese has adopted 3 of the possible 5 derogations identified in Article. 16 of Regulation (EU) No. 260/2012, through the publication of Decree-Law No. 141/2013 of 18 October, which has desecrate the national measures necessary for the implementation of the provisions of that diploma, allowing until 1 February 2016: (i) NIB can continue to be used in domestic transactions by consumers, without payment service providers being able to charge charges for any conversion into IBAN; (ii) the requirement to use ISO 20022 XML in communication between users and payment service providers for batch transactions is waived; (iii) BIC is used in national operations if necessary. The remaining 2 derogations considered in the Regulation would not be applicable in Portugal: one is associated with "niche products", with its own definition, not existing in our community; the other focuses on the specificity of the German and Austrian markets of originating one-off direct debits from a card transaction. This decree-law also assigned To Banco de Portugal, in its Article 7, the function of authority responsible for monitoring compliance with the Regulation and defined the sanctioning framework applicable in this area. In this respect, it will be necessary to retain that the diploma establishes, in Article 8, that the fines to be imposed for non-compliance with the Regulation may be between 1 000 to 3 500 and from 3 000 to 44 000 , depending on whether the natural person or collective person is applied, allocated a multiplicity of possible infringements. 2.4. Current point of the state of migration in Portugal and Europe With regard, specifically, to the migration process to SEPA, it should be noted at this time that, in Portugal, the index of credit transfers processed in SEPA format reached 81.28% of the total at the end of November. From the known information, it will be expected to continue the growth of this index, allowing an optimistic perspective of compliance with the established schedule. At the global level of the euro area, this indicator stood at around 60% at the end of October, although it is the result of a heterogeneous picture between countries. However, the information gathered at ESCB level points to a timely migration completion scenario. With regard to direct debits, the situation is substantially more worrying: while on the euro area average the indicator at the end of October stood at 11.5%, within the national community this same indicator was still at worrying levels (6.42%). Still, there are evidences that this index will be significantly increased from now on. Banco de Portugal has issued alerts to this situation, since failure to comply with the requirements from 1 February next may have undesirable consequences for creditor entities, that is, the inability to make charges. This call for attention is, moreover, in line with other warnings about the increased risks of the option for a big bang migration, concentrated near the deadline of the migration period.
