Title: Intervention of Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the CMVM International Conference  "Flexibility and proportionality in corporate governance - The promotion of the capital market (Portuguese) through corporate governance"
text: CMVM International Conference  "Flexibility and proportionality in corporate governance - The promotion of the capital market (Portuguese) through corporate governance" June 20, 2017 Intervention of the Governor of Banco de Portugal Carlos da Silva Costa 1 1 Prepared for presentation. "The role of banks in corporate governance and capital market promotion" I begin by welcoming the CMVM by organizing a Conference on corporate governance. Weaknesses in this area are one of the main obstacles to economic development Portuguese and are not always the subject of the necessary attention. I would like to stress from the outset that the problem of governance is much wider than the mere issue of representing and defending the interests of shareholders in corporate governance. In fact, the governance framework and practices condition and determine the sustainability of the development process itself. The focus on the dissemination of good governance models and practices to all sectors of activity is a key element in fostering confidence and more robust and sustainable economic growth. Indeed, when we talk about governance, it is important to be in mind that what is at stake is not only the existence of an appropriate set of rules  the regulatory framework of the institution  but also the institutional framework, practices, values and behaviours. The existence of a good formal governance framework does not guarantee the existence of a practice in agreement with this framework, since the practice does not always follow the principles, particularly for reasons related to the current incentive system or the organizational culture itself. That is, it does not matter to have a good "governance manual" if in practice it is not followed. Therefore, in addition to the existence of rules, it is essential to ensure compliance. If this does not happen, it is not only the institution that is compromised but also the general interest. Institutions are complex bodies and involve multiple stakeholders (owners, managers, employees, creditors, customers, suppliers, public entities, etc.) whose interests must be taken into account. The sustainability dimension must be integrated, particularly in view of the time that there are stakeholders who cannot even be represented. Future generations have the right to benefit from the share capital that the company has accumulated. The question is the reproduction of the ways of doing and interacting and the ethics of behaviors. The governance model, in a broad sense, is the way in which the framework of rules and practices of the institution integrate and reconcile internal and external interests that converge or diverge within the institution. This model must clearly express how it organises these interests and ensure balance in the distribution of benefits. What is fundamentally at stake is whether the institution produces the results to which it has proposed, if it shows them in a transparent way and whether it distributes them according to the "contractor" with its stakeholders. This is the question of how the company organizes itself to achieve its objective, as well as its efficiency, its effectiveness, its resilience and its sustainability. This means that governance is not a balance problem between capital owners/shareholders, or between them and managers, but of all stakeholders. The involvement of stakeholders is fundamental: it is necessary to ensure inclusion, participation, motivation and commitment and generate confidence in the resilience of the institution. Governance is not static and should be viewed from a perspective of anticipation and response to the institution's challenges. At the same time, there will have to be adequate communication to all stakeholders about what these challenges are and how to overcome them. We must always keep in mind that governance models are not indifferent to society: governance is not a private matter, it is a matter of public interest. There is a general interest that overlaps with the particular interests, which is that of the continuity of the institutions. When a company dislikes, it's a set of expectations that it's undone. Institutions have a social capital that, when it is undone, has a negative impact on the economy, has a cost for economic and social development. There are governance models of certain entities that condition the governance practices of other institutions. This is particularly the case with general government entities and financial institutions. In the case of public administrations, the orientation of the governance model can determine the most productive direction of the economy and development models. When the governance model of public administrations is predominantly of "extractive" reasoning, the economy will also have a predominance of companies that are oriented in this direction. For its part, the role played by the banking sector provides a unique opportunity to dissemine good governance practices and encourage the production of complete, timely, reliable and properly scrutinized information. The confidence of the agents and the optimisation of economic decisions depend critically on the quality and relevance of the information provided. A breach of trust implies a risk premium, i.e. an additional cost in terms of resource consumption. The role of banks in this area is critical in that: (i) they may require information; (ii) they must ensure that the information is complete, reliable and unique (and not different depending on recipients); and (iii) should contribute to the resilience of institutions. In this context, the risk approach made by banks must undergo a profound change: risk assessment must move away from the analysis of personal or equity guarantees and focus on the assessment of business models and governance and the viability of projects. In other words, banks should finance on the merits and resilience of companies and projects and not the owner's guarantees. This means that the allocation made by the banks of the savings society must move from a logic of redistribution of wealth to a logic of wealth creation. Matter keep in mind that whenever the allocation of savings is not adequate there is a loss for society as a whole and, at the limit, a destruction of capital. Of course, banks are not designed to finance all kinds of projects and companies. Therefore, diversification of sources of financing is not only desirable but indispensable in any economy. In this regard, I would like to stress that I believe that the development of the capital market and alternative forms of financing that will complement bank credit is necessary. Increased use of financing through the capital market also contributes to increasing the level of demand in terms of the quality of information and governance of institutions. In this context, it is important to consider some issues that are at the origin of the traditional standard of financing of companies, such as those relating to taxation, so that relative advantages of financing through indebtedness do not persist. In addition, the existence of robust corporate governance models and scrutinized by stakeholders, with appropriate incentive schemes, with appropriate control mechanisms and good practices of production and reporting of information, enhances the efficiency of institutions and better management and mitigation of risks. In addition, the existence of a more diverse range of sources of financing, as well as the possibility of access to innovative financial instruments benefit companies and investment and contribute to the financial stability and more sustainable and balanced growth of the Portuguese economy.
text_original: Conferncia Internacional da CMVM  Flexibilidade e proporcionalidade em corporate governance - A promoo do mercado de capitais (portugus) atravs do corporate governance 20 de junho de 2017 Interveno do Governador do Banco de Portugal Carlos da Silva Costa 1 1 Preparado para apresentao. O papel dos bancos no corporate governance e na promoo do mercado de capitais Comeo por saudar a CMVM pela organizao de uma Conferncia sobre corporate governance. As fragilidades neste domnio constituem um dos principais obstculos ao desenvolvimento econmico portugus e nem sempre so objeto da necessria ateno. Gostaria de sublinhar, desde logo, que o problema da governance  bastante mais vasto do que a mera questo da representao e defesa dos interesses dos acionistas no quadro de governo societrio. De facto, o quadro e as prticas de governance condicionam e determinam a sustentabilidade do prprio processo de desenvolvimento. A aposta na disseminao, a todos os setores de atividade, de modelos e prticas de boa governao  um elemento-chave no fomento da confiana e de um crescimento econmico mais robusto e sustentvel. Efetivamente, quando falamos de governance, importa ter presente que o que est em causa no  apenas a existncia de um adequado conjunto de regras  o quadro normativo da instituio  mas tambm o quadro institucional, as prticas, os valores e os comportamentos. A existncia de um bom quadro formal de governance, no garante a existncia de uma prtica concordante com esse quadro, j que a prtica nem sempre segue os princpios, nomeadamente por razes ligadas ao sistema de incentivos vigente ou  prpria cultura organizacional. Ou seja, no importa ter um bom manual de governance se na prtica ele no for seguido. Por conseguinte, para alm da existncia das regras,  indispensvel garantir a sua observncia. Se isso no acontecer, no  apenas a instituio que est comprometida mas tambm o interesse geral. As instituies so organismos complexos e envolvem mltiplos stakeholders (proprietrios, gestores, colaboradores, credores, clientes, fornecedores, entidades pblicas, etc.) cujos interesses devem ser tidos em conta. H que integrar a dimenso sustentabilidade, designadamente tendo em conta que h stakeholders que nem sequer se podem fazer representar. Com efeito, as geraes futuras tm o direito de beneficiar do capital social que a empresa acumulou. Est em causa a reproduo dos modos de fazer e de interagir e a tica dos comportamentos. O modelo de governance, em sentido lato,  a forma como o quadro de regras e as prticas da instituio integram e conciliam interesses internos e externos que convergem ou divergem no seio da instituio. Esse modelo tem de exprimir claramente como organiza estes interesses e assegurar equilbrio na distribuio dos benefcios. O que est fundamentalmente em causa  saber se a instituio produz os resultados a que se props, se os evidencia de forma transparente e se os distribui de acordo com o contratado com os seus stakeholders. Est em causa a forma como a empresa se organiza para atingir o seu objetivo, bem como a sua eficincia, a sua eficcia, a sua resilincia e a sua sustentabilidade. Isto significa que a governance no  um problema de equilbrio entre proprietrios de capital/acionistas, ou entre estes e os gestores, mas sim de todos os stakeholders. O envolvimento dos stakeholders  fundamental:  necessrio assegurar incluso, participao, motivao e compromisso e gerar confiana na resilincia da instituio. A governance no  esttica e deve ser encarada numa perspetiva de capacidade de antecipao e de resposta aos desafios da instituio. Paralelamente, ter de existir uma adequada comunicao a todas as partes interessadas sobre quais so esses desafios e como os superar. Devemos ter sempre presente que os modelos de governance no so indiferentes para a sociedade: a governance no  um assunto privado,  uma questo de interesse pblico. H um interesse geral que se sobrepe aos interesses particulares, que  o da continuidade das instituies. Quando uma empresa se desfaz,  um conjunto de expectativas que se desfaz. As instituies tm um capital social que, quando  desfeito, tem impacto negativo sobre a economia, tem um custo para o desenvolvimento econmico e social. H modelos de governance de determinadas entidades que condicionam as prticas de governo das outras instituies. Isto sucede, nomeadamente, com as entidades das administraes pblicas e com as instituies financeiras. No caso das administraes pblicas, a orientao do modelo de governance pode determinar o pendor mais produtivo da economia e os modelos de desenvolvimento. Quando o modelo de governance das administraes pblicas  predominantemente de raciocnio extrativo, a economia ter tambm predominncia de empresas que se orientam nesse sentido. Por seu turno, a funo desempenhada pelo setor bancrio proporciona uma oportunidade singular de difuso de boas prticas de governance e de incentivo  produo de informao completa, tempestiva, fivel e devidamente escrutinada. A confiana dos agentes e a otimizao das decises econmicas dependem criticamente da qualidade e pertinncia da informao disponibilizada. Uma quebra de confiana implica um prmio de risco, ou seja, um custo adicional em termos de consumo de recursos. O papel dos bancos neste domnio  crtico, na medida em que: (i) podem exigir informao; (ii) tm de garantir que a informao  completa, fivel e nica (e no diferente consoante destinatrios); e (iii) devem contribuir para a resilincia das instituies. Neste contexto, a abordagem ao risco feita pelos bancos deve sofrer uma profunda alterao: a avaliao do risco tem de afastar-se da anlise de garantias pessoais ou patrimoniais e passar a centrar-se na avaliao dos modelos de negcio e de governance e da viabilidade dos projetos. Ou seja, os bancos devem financiar em funo do mrito e da resilincia das empresas e dos projetos e no das garantias do proprietrio. Isto significa que a afetao feita pelos bancos da poupana da sociedade deve passar de uma lgica de redistribuio de riqueza para uma lgica de criao de riqueza. Importa ter presente que sempre que a afetao da poupana no  adequada h uma perda para a sociedade no seu conjunto e, no limite, uma destruio de capital. Naturalmente, os bancos no esto vocacionados para financiar todo o tipo de projetos e de empresas. Por isso, a diversificao de fontes de financiamento no s  desejvel como indispensvel em qualquer economia. Neste sentido, gostaria de realar que considero necessrio o desenvolvimento do mercado de capitais e de formas de financiamento alternativas que venham complementar o crdito bancrio. Um maior recurso a financiamento atravs do mercado de capitais contribui tambm para o aumento do nvel de exigncia em termos de qualidade da informao e da governance das instituies. Neste mbito, importa contemplar algumas questes que esto na gnese do padro tradicional de financiamento das empresas, como sejam as relativas  fiscalidade, de modo a que no persistam vantagens relativas do financiamento atravs de endividamento. Em suma, a existncia de modelos de corporate governance robustos e escrutinados pelos stakeholders, com esquemas de incentivos apropriados, com mecanismos de controlo adequados e boas prticas de produo e de reporte de informao, potencia a eficincia das instituies e uma melhor gesto e mitigao dos riscos. Adicionalmente, a existncia de um leque mais diversificado de fontes de financiamento, bem como a possibilidade de acesso a instrumentos financeiros inovadores beneficiam as empresas e o investimento e contribuem para a estabilidade financeira e um crescimento mais sustentvel e equilibrado da economia portuguesa.

Title: Intervention of Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the Investment and Investment Finance Conference
text: Investment and investment finance conference: financing economic recovery and growth - challenges for Portugal in the European context Porto, December 4, 2017 Intervention of the Governor of Banco de Portugal Carlos da Silva Costa1 1 Prepared for presentation. Good morning. I am delighted to welcome the presence of all at this Conference on investment and investment financing. This is a theme of the utmost relevance, since it is through investment, innovation and the improvement of the management of our companies that the conditions for productivity growth can be created, indispensable to economic growth in the long term. It is indeed a pleasure to open this Conference for two orders of reasons:  Firstly, because the Conference takes place in Porto, in the northern region of the country, where a substantial part of the companies that make up the business fabric of the Portuguese. Companies that play a key role in the country's economy and which need not only to regenerate but also equip and prepare for the challenges of the future, particularly those that arise from technological developments, automation and the digital economy; it is essential to support the development of skills, new organisation and management models and the development or introduction of new products, processes and services;  Secondly, because the Conference is organised together with the European Investment Bank (EIB) whose role has been and remains of the greatest importance for the economic development of our country. In the last 40 years  since the first loans in 1976  the EIB has supported multiple projects in Portugal, in the most varied sectors (from the most traditional to the most innovative), with emphasis on supporting small and medium-sized enterprises and medium-sized enterprises. In 2016 alone, the EIB group's support for projects in Portugal accounted for around 1% of Portuguese GDP (EUR 1 780 million). It is essential that the productive Portuguese evolves towards higher levels of the value chain, the incorporation of knowledge and the use and profiting of the benefits arising from technological evolution. In order to continue the regeneration and modernization of Portuguese companies, it is important to reduce the remaining barriers to investment, diversify financing and promote entrepreneurship. Portuguese companies are among the most leveraged in Europe and are heavily dependent on bank financing. Of course, however, banks are not designed to finance all types of projects and companies, particularly in the field of radical innovation. Increased use of self-financing, the existence of a more diverse range of funding sources and the possibility of access to innovative financial instruments benefit businesses and investment and contribute to the financial stability and more sustainable and balanced growth of the Portuguese economy. I am sure that today's Conference:  It will give us a general picture of the investment activities of Portuguese companies, their financing needs and the difficulties they face;  It will enable an enriching debate on the challenges and opportunities of the future to promote productivity growth and improve Portugal's position in Europe. Thank you very much
