Title: Speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the Platform for Sustainable Growth Conference "What World Do We Live In?"
text: Intervention of Dr. Carlos da Silva Costa Governor of Banco de Portugal PLATFORM CONFERENCE FOR SUSTAINABLE GROWTH "What World Do We Live In?" Lisbon December 13, 2011 1st Round Table: European Political Project1 How to relaunch the European political project? What model of econic governance for the EU? What agenda for growth and jobs in the EU? Ladies and gentlemen, I begin by thanking you for the invitation you have been addressed to me to attend this conference. I would like to begin my speech by conveying a very simple message which is at the same time revealing the importance i attach to this kind of initiative: it is not possible to build the European Union without informed and aware of the root of the problems, because only in this way do we legitimise the project of European construction. The relationship we live with the European Union is, in a way, the relationship that the Portuguese citizen lives with the State: "ns and the others", as if the citizen were not part of the State. This remoteness is one of the fundamental reasons for many of the difficulties we are facing and which tend to be difficult to tolerate by the people of the different Member States. In this speech I would like to examine the process of European construction taking into account three aspects which seem fundamental to me: i) the European Union is a project under construction; ii) the European project cannot be dissociated from its Member States; and, strongly linked to it, iii) the Econica Union project must be developed alongside that of monetary union. The great challenge we face today is to ensure the balance of European construction, in this dual perspective, in a balanced and sustainable way. The European Union is a project under construction Firstly, we must keep in mind that the European Union is the typical case of a 'project that is being done by doing it'. As the Spanish writer said, "the path that is made walking". And like any "project you do doing", every time a problem arises, you have to find an answer, which will be the solution until the moment a new problem arises. Problems are not solved before they arise, in anticipation, nor in a manner anatia; they resolve after they have emerged and emerge as the integration process deepens. In other words, the problems arise according to a sequence that is the reflection of the very process of European construction. We could not have an eco-and monetary union before we had the ico market, as we would not have the ico market before we had built an area with common borders at international level. This situation was evident from the outset in the monetary and financial field, with a construction based on a process of increasing integration which, at some point, faced a difficulty: the existence of national currencies, which constituted an obstacle to the construction of a common market. The monetary snake on the tel was a first response to this difficulty and was initially a success; later it became a problem and then a failure. This monetary system gave way to the exchange rate mechanism, which was also a great success but which, subsequently, when it reached its limits as a solution, failed, leading, in turn, to the ica currency. A monetary union followed, which was dubbed the "Econic and Monetary Union" (EMU). But in practice, we build a monetary union with a uppercase U, an E minsculo, and an M maiculo. In other words, we have a full monetary union, but we do not have a full ecological union, which causes a new imbalance. In this sense, we live in a climate of some dramatism, which is not new to all those who have experienced this process of European construction. What is new is the fact that response times are much shorter. This imbalance between the two pillars of EMU is the problem that we are facing today and which has only just emerged. Indeed, as I have already said, the search for the solution only begins when the problem is identified. The fact that the eco-and monetary union was built in a particularly favourable context from an international point of view has enabled it, for ten years, to conceal the shortcomings and shortcomings of its eco-pillar. The abundance of liquidity and low interest rates have enabled Member States not to prepare for the reality of the new context: for the need to safeguard competitiveness, on the one hand, and to safeguard the sustainability of finances and external position, on the other. A large number of countries in the European Union have accumulated imbalances in phasing-up finances and external accounts, reaching unsustainable levels of public or private debt and losing competitiveness during this period. These imbalances were hidden and would manifest itself one day, regardless of the international crisis. But it was precisely the international crisis that has highlighted these imbalances and, in the current context, we only have two problems: either we directly attack the fragility of the econica union within this two-pillar construction that is EMU, or we recognize that the construction is not balanced. So today we are asked to continue the work we started when we decided to build a monetary union. This means that we need to know whether or not we are prepared to live in a context of monetary currency and monetary policy. This implies knowing whether we can manage imbalances at national level, bearing in mind that we no longer have the exchange rate 'cane' that we used whenever necessary. In the past, whenever the econica part failed, it was the exchange rate "cane" that directly allowed the external competitiveness to be re-achieved and, indirectly, a real depreciation of public and private debts, through inflation that resulted from the exchange rate devaluation. The European dimension and the national dimension of EMU This question brings me to the second point I would like to stress: we must be aware that the problem of EMU has two dimensions: a dimension of integration and a national dimension, that is, a dimension of solidarity of the group and a dimension of individual responsibility. These are, of course, two associated dimenses, because it is not possible to count on the dimension of integration if the national dimension is not properly taken care of. In the internal construction of EMU, the insufficiency of the econic pillar creates a problem of trust between partners. It is natural for such a problem to be solved by the establishment of rules. These rules lie in the area of environmental policy and, above all, budgetary policy. It turns out that the rules that had so far existed were not sufficiently disciplinary, since they were not sufficiently explicit and were not shaped in institutional mechanisms capable of ensuring their compliance. It follows that the solution to the crisis we are facing involves, at European level, a strengthening of these institutional rules and mechanisms and necessarily involves, at national level, fiscal consolidation, a strengthening of the stability of the financial system and a rebalancing of external accounts, based on structural reforms that enhance the flexibility and efficiency of the productive fabric and, competitiveness of the national economy in a context of globalisation. These three dimenss are a necessary condition for the rebalancing of the econic and monetary pillars of EMU. To conceal them would be to make the solution unfeasible and, in any case, it would be a way of creating difficulties and difficulties for those who, through participation in financial assistance mechanisms, have to be part of the solution and which, if they do not participate, make it impossible to respond to the problems facing Europe. We must be aware that any response  which must be adjusted and proportionate to the nature and size of the risk  has as a counterpart a very strong commitment at the national level of the Member States receiving assistance; a commitment that, in itself, minimizes the moral risk of the group. To this end, it is important to recall some principles which underptook place in the construction of EMU: the principle that there would be no-default by the Member States, the principle that there would be no bailout (nobailout), the principle that each would retain its budgetary sovereignty and, finally, the principle that there would be no exit from the ica currency (noexit). These principles are internally incompatible. This is because someone who uses his budgetary sovereignty or his green policy in such a way as not to converge with the whole accumulates imbalances that, of course, at a certain time, either imply redemption or imply exit. The interest of the whole is always that of safeguarding the group and, therefore, the rescue , but involves a moral hazard. An unconditional rescue necessarily implies contemporizing with irresponsible behavior in the past and, consequently, legitimizing irresponsible behavior in the future. This means that the group's financial assistance to some of its members is not combined with the maintenance of all degrees of freedom of these members in environmental policy or budgetary policy. The stability of EMU does not require that the situation of the federal state be arrived, but it is necessary, and imperative, to bring together conditions, in terms of discipline and rules in relation to each of the members, capable of giving confidence to the group. This is an issue which I would like to highlight the conclusions of the summit of heads of state and government of the euro area countries on 9 December. The final declaration is aimed at strengthening the architecture of EMU, in particular the eco-pillar, through two lines of action: (i) strengthening budgetary rules and coordinating national economic policies, and (ii) the development of financial stabilisation mechanisms to address short-term challenges. These summit conclusions correspond, using an image of the sports area, to a two-way eliminatria: the first is to create rules that generate trust and the second is to take advantage of the confidence generated to introduce the assistance mechanisms, I would say assistance, that promote the stability of the group and each of its members. The decisions of this summit are the necessary step towards limiting moral hazard through the introduction of budgetary rules. The second step will be to complement these rules with the necessary financial mechanisms inherent to the stability of the system. To admit that it would be possible to have these financial mechanisms before the rules minimise moral hazard and divergence of behavioural preferences within EMU would be to admit that those in a position to decide the "luck of the game" would agree to submit to the moral risk of bearing the devious behaviour of one or more members of the group. Bearing this in mind, we must have a positive perspective on the conclusions of the last European summit, knowing, however, that it is not the end of the journey, but rather the first stage. The second stage will arrive, depending on the speed and conviction with which the first one will take place. In particular, it will depend a lot on what will happen in the prime three months, in particular on the implementation of rules and budgetary discipline. It will also depend on how these measures will be transposed into the public and internal plan of each Member State and on the notion that the rules do not result from an external dictat, but are inherent in group life. It is necessary to strengthen the convergence of environmental policies, as well as the constitutionalization of these objectives, as a way of ensuring that the national ownership of these same objectives continues in the next stage. If we are able to achieve this objective , and it is out of the question not to be able to fulfil it , the second part is missing, which naturally involves developing what is embryonically present in the conclusions of the summit of 9 December, in particular in terms of the financial mechanisms necessary to ensure the stability of EMU. At this point, as Professor DeGrawe pointed out, we must be aware that this EMU was not only created with an internal inconsistency  by providing for national sovereignty in budgetary and environmental policy matters and, at the same time, the other three principles (nodefault, nobailout and noexit)  but was also created with another gap: the lack of liquidity support mechanisms for a sovereign or, at the limit, solvency support. A State that finances itself in its own currency, endowed with its own central bank and which has no sovereign monetary financing limits that is, that is, that functions as a lender in the last instance, issuing currency and acquiring pblica debt in the primary market  can respond to the temporary difficulties of debt placement through monetary issuance. In addition to the problem of insufficient construction in the economic pillar, EMU, because it is not a federal state, has a specificity in the monetary pillar characterized by the absence of a lender in the last instance. An econic and monetary union is an agreement between partners with monetary histrias and with very different national preferences. In view of this, it is clear that EMU had to align itself with the preference that would allow the cohesion of the group, which was not conflicting and which, in essence, was structurally more sida: a preference for nominal stability. The preference for nominal stability had consequences. The entire configuration of the European Central Bank was made according to a model that excluded monetary financing from the budget deficit, as it was included in the Treaty, and excluded the financial ity of a lender in the past. This difficulty in building EMU is not resolved immediately, because the European Union is also not an ico state immediately. This implies that the European Union must find supplementary mechanisms to solve the problem without creating further internal conflict. In the absence of a monetary financing mechanism by the Eurosystem, euro area states finance themselves as if they did so in "foreign" currency and are subject to a liquidity trap. Therefore, a State that is part of an economic and monetary union must have, at group level, the capacity to solve the problem without the group suffering the moral risk associated with the behavior of that State. In a way, the euro area Member States are now faced with two types of problems: one national and one European. The solution to the national problem is to address existing imbalances. The solution to the European problem is to create the stability mechanisms of EMU by strengthening the econic pillar  which has a competitiveness dimension and a fiscal policy dimension  and at the same time to create the mechanisms that will stabilise this union. Strengthening the EMU's eco-pillar At this point, it is necessary to be aware of how important it is to generate more than mere nominal stability or mere currency sharing. It has to generate growth and jobs. This problem is not on the side of the monetary pillar, but on the side of the eco-pillar. Coordination of environmental policies needs to be strengthened in order to ensure that there is an overall view of the impacts of national policies on the group, as is also included in the Treaty. It is also foreseen that Member States must regard their economic policy as being of common interest  and the crisis has reinforced the sense of that common responsibility. We will have to further strengthen the economic pillar, clearly understanding that it is not possible to adjust all the pieces of this puzzle if only part of the pieces are moving. Peer pressure can act favorably in this context and not only for individual interest. The movement must be joint within an econic policy framework, which means that we will have to move from a discussion that focuses on fiscal policies and financial policies to a broader discussion, which will have to be focused on the growth policies of the European Union. There is no stable European Union without a stable monetary arm, without an eco-arm that generates confidence and without a financial instrument that reintroduces feedback mechanisms capable of restoring stability. But there is also no stable economic and monetary union if it is not innovative and does not generate growth. Because if it does not generate economic growth and does not recover in terms of employment, the economic and monetary union will always be subject to national budgetary policy and the legitimacy of the European constitution. European construction is only legitimised if it favours eco-growth, employment and well-being. We have a two-step challenge here as well. Firstly, to consolidate and stabilise EMU by strengthening the econic arm of econic and monetary union. Second, design EMU as a global growth space. It is not enough to have good indicators as an area if we keep large asymmetries inside. It is necessary to combine the management of asymmetries  whether development or financial in nature  with the projection of this European area. In conclusion, the reform of the model of econic governance in the European Union necessarily goes through three levels. At the first level, of an institutional nature, the mechanisms relating to economic union must accompany the strength of the mechanisms of monetary union. What needs to be corrected is not the monetary pillar, because it is strong, but the econic component, which is relatively weak. The second level is that of a strengthening of democratic legitimacy, which has to be found to realize that the citizen plays on two "boards": the national board and the European board (some that are in federated states still play on the regional board). And, by the way, the third level is to implement the principle of the Treaty that the policy of each Member State is in the interests of all  it is therefore in the interests of all that it has to be exercised. It is a game that is either of a positive sum and everyone win, or is of negative sum and everyone loses. Thank you very much.
text_original: Interveno do Dr. Carlos da Silva Costa Governador do Banco de Portugal CONFERNCIA PLATAFORMA PARA O CRESCIMENTO SUSTENTVEL Em Que Mundo Vivemos? Lisboa 13 de dezembro de 2011 1 Mesa Redonda: Projeto Poltico Europeu1 Como relanar o projeto poltico europeu? Que modelo de governao econica para a UE? Que agenda para o crescimento e emprego na UE? Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, Comeo por agradecer o convite que me foi endereado para participar nesta conferncia. Gostaria de iniciar esta minha interveno veiculando uma mensagem muito simples e que , ao mesmo tempo, reveladora da importncia que atribuo a este tipo de iniciativa: no  possvel construir a Unio Europeia sem opinies plicas informadas e conscientes da raiz dos problemas, porque s desta forma legitimamos o projeto da construo europeia. A relao que vivemos com a Unio Europeia , de certa forma, a relao que o cidado portugus vive com o Estado: ns e os outros, como se o cidado no fosse parte do Estado. Este afastamento constitui uma das razes fundamentais de muitas das dificuldades com que estamos confrontados e que tendem a ser dificilmente toleradas pelas populas dos diferentes EstadosMembros. Nesta interveno gostaria de analisar o processo de construo europeia tendo em conta trs aspetos que me parecem fundamentais: i) a Unio Europeia  um projeto em construo; ii) o projeto europeu no pode ser dissociado dos respetivos EstadosMembros; e, fortemente interligado com este, iii) o projeto da Unio Econica tem de ser desenvolvido a par do da Unio Monetria. O grande desafio que enfrentamos hoje  assegurar o equilbrio da construo europeia, nesta dupla perspetiva, de forma sida e sustentvel. A Unio Europeia  um projeto em construo Em primeiro lugar, temos de ter presente que a Unio Europeia  o caso tpico de um projeto que se faz, fazendo. Como disse o escritor espanhol, o caminho que se faz caminhando. E como qualquer projeto que se faz fazendo, sempre que surge um problema h que encontrar uma resposta, que ser a soluo at ao momento em que surja um novo problema. Os problemas no se resolvem antes de se colocarem, por antecipao, nem de forma aleatia; resolvemse aps terem surgido e emergem  medida que o processo de integrao se aprofunda. Ou seja, os problemas colocamse segundo uma sequncia que  o reflexo do prrio processo de construo europeia. No poderamos ter uma unio econica e monetria antes de termos o mercado ico, como no teramos o mercado ico antes de termos construdo um espao com fronteiras comuns no plano internacional. Esta situao foi evidente, desde o incio, no campo monetrio e financeiro, com uma construo baseada num processo de crescente integrao que, em dado momento, se deparou com uma dificuldade: a existncia de moedas nacionais, que constituam um obstculo  construo de um mercado comum. A serpente monetria no tel foi uma primeira resposta a esta dificuldade e foi inicialmente um sucesso; mais tarde transformouse num problema e, depois, num fracasso. Este sistema monetrio deu lugar ao mecanismo de taxas de cmbio, que foi tambm um grande sucesso mas que, posteriormente, quando atingiu os seus limites enquanto soluo, fracassou, conduzindo, por sua vez,  moeda ica. Seguiuse ento uma unio monetria, que foi batizada de Unio Econica e Monetria (UEM). Mas, na prtica, construmos uma unio monetria com um U maiculo, um E minsculo e um M maiculo. Ou seja, temos uma unio monetria plena, mas no temos uma unio econica plena, o que causa um novo desequilbrio. Neste sentido, vivemos num clima de alguma dramatismo, que no  novo para todos os que viveram este processo de construo europeia. Aquilo que  novo  o facto de os tempos de resposta serem muito mais curtos. Este desequilbrio entre os dois pilares da UEM  o problema com que hoje estamos confrontados e que s agora emergiu. Com efeito, como j referi, a procura da soluo s se inicia quando o problema  identificado. O facto de a unio econica e monetria ter sido construda num contexto particularmente favorvel do ponto de vista internacional permitiu, durante dez anos, dissimular as falhas e as insuficincias do seu pilar econico. A abundncia de liquidez e as reduzidas taxas de juro permitiram que os EstadosMembros no se preparassem para a realidade do novo contexto: para a necessidade de salvaguarda da competitividade, por um lado, e de salvaguarda da sustentabilidade das finanas plicas e da posio externa, por outro lado. Um grande nmero de pases na Unio Europeia acumulou desequilbrios nas finanas plicas e nas contas externas, atingindo nveis insustentveis de dvida pblica ou privada e perdeu competitividade durante este perodo. Estes desequilbrios estavam dissimulados e iriam manifestarse um dia, independentemente da crise internacional. Mas foi precisamente a crise internacional que veio evidenciar estes desequilbrios e, no contexto atual, s temos duas solues: ou atacamos diretamente a fragilidade da unio econica dentro desta construo em dois pilares que  a UEM, ou reconhecemos que a prria construo no  equilibrada. Assim, somos interpelados hoje a continuar o trabalho que inicimos quando decidimos construir uma unio monetria. Isto significa que temos de saber se estamos preparados ou no para viver num contexto de moeda ica e de poltica monetria nica. Isto implica saber se conseguimos gerir os desequilbrios a nvel nacional, tendo presente que j no dispomos da bengala cambial a que recorramos sempre que era necessrio. No passado, sempre que a parte econica falhava, era a bengala cambial que permitia, de forma direta, repor a competitividade externa e, de forma indireta, uma depreciao real das dvidas pblicas e privadas, atravs da inflao que resultava da desvalorizao cambial. A dimenso europeia e a dimenso nacional da UEM Esta questo levame ao segundo aspeto que gostaria de salientar: temos de ter conscincia de que o problema da UEM tem duas dimenses: uma dimenso de integrao e uma dimenso nacional, ou seja, uma dimenso de solidariedade do grupo e uma dimenso de responsabilidade individual. Tratase, naturalmente, de duas dimenses associadas, porque no  possvel contar com a dimenso de integrao se a dimenso nacional no estiver devidamente acautelada. Na construo interna da UEM, a insuficincia do pilar econico gera um problema de confiana entre parceiros.  natural que um problema deste tipo se resolva pelo estabelecimento de regras. Essas regras residem na rea da poltica econica e, sobretudo, de poltica oramental. Acontece que as regras at agora existentes no eram suficientemente disciplinadoras, dado que no eram suficientemente explcitas nem estavam plasmadas em mecanismos institucionais capazes de assegurar a sua observncia. Daqui decorre que a soluo para a crise com que estamos confrontados passa, no plano europeu, por um reforo dessas regras e mecanismos institucionais e passa necessariamente, no plano nacional, por uma consolidao oramental, um reforo da estabilidade do sistema financeiro e um reequilbrio das contas externas, assente em reformas estruturais que reforcem a flexibilidade e a eficincia do tecido produtivo e, por consequncia, a competitividade da economia nacional num contexto de globalizao. Estas trs dimenss so uma condio necessria do reequilbrio dos pilares econico e monetrio da UEM. Escamotelas seria inviabilizar a soluo e, em qualquer caso, seria uma forma de criar dvidas e dificuldades queles que, atravs da participao nos mecanismos de assistncia financeira, tm de ser parte da soluo e que, caso no participem, inviabilizam a prria resposta aos problemas com que est confrontada a Europa. Temos de ter conscincia de que qualquer resposta  que deve ser ajustada e proporcional  natureza e  dimenso do risco  tem como contrapartida um compromisso muito forte no plano nacional dos EstadosMembros que beneficiam de assistncia; um compromisso que, em si mesmo, minimize o risco moral do grupo. Para o efeito, importa recordar alguns princpios que estiveram na base da construo da UEM: o princpio de que no haveria incumprimento dos EstadosMembros (nodefault),o princpio de que no haveria resgate (nobailout), o princpio de que cada um conservaria a sua soberania oramental e, finalmente, o princpio de que no haveria sada da moeda ica (noexit). Estes princpios so internamente incompatveis. Isto porque algum que use a sua soberania oramental ou a sua poltica econica de forma a no convergir com o todo acumula desequilbrios que, naturalmente, em determinado momento, ou implicam resgate ou implicam sada. O interesse do todo  sempre o da salvaguarda do grupo e, portanto, o resgate , mas envolve um risco moral. Um resgate incondicional implica necessariamente contemporizar com um comportamento irresponsvel no passado e, em consequncia, legitimar um comportamento irresponsvel no futuro. Isto significa que a assistncia financeira do grupo a alguns dos seus membros no se conjuga com a manuteno de todos os graus de liberdade desses membros em matria de poltica econica ou de poltica oramental . A estabilidade da UEM no requer que se chegue  situao de Estado federal, mas  necessrio, e imperioso, reunir condis, em termos de disciplina e de regras relativamente a cada um dos membros, capazes de dar confiana ao grupo. Esta  uma questo que gostaria de pr em evidncia a propito das concluss da cimeira dos chefes de Estado e de Governo dos pases da rea do euro, que teve lugar a 9 de dezembro. A declarao final est orientada para o reforo da arquitetura da UEM, em particular do pilar econico, atravs de duas linhas de ao: i) o reforo das regras oramentais e da coordenao das polticas econmicas nacionais, e ii) o desenvolvimento dos mecanismos de estabilizao financeira para fazer face aos desafios de curto prazo. Estas concluses da cimeira correspondem, utilizando uma imagem da rea desportiva, a uma eliminatria em duas mos: a primeira consiste em criar regras que gerem confiana e a segunda consiste em tirar partido da confiana gerada para introduzir os mecanismos de assistncia, diria de entreajuda, que promovam a estabilidade do grupo e de cada um dos respetivos membros. As deciss desta cimeira so o passo necessrio para a limitao do risco moral atravs da introduo de regras de natureza oramental. O segundo passo consistir em complementar estas regras com os mecanismos financeiros necessrios e inerentes  estabilidade do sistema. Admitir que seria possvel dispor destes mecanismos financeiros antes de terem sido estabelecidas as regras que minimizem o risco moral e a divergncia de preferncias comportamentais no seio da UEM seria admitir que quem estava na posio de decidir a sorte do jogo aceitaria submeterse ao risco moral de suportar os comportamentos desviantes de um ou vrios membros do grupo. Tendo presente este enquadramento, devemos ter uma perspetiva positiva sobre as concluss da tima cimeira europeia, sabendo, no entanto, que no  o fim do percurso,  antes a primeira etapa. A segunda etapa chegar, dependendo muito da rapidez e da convico com que decorrer a primeira. Em particular, vai depender muito do que se ir passar nos primos trs meses, nomeadamente em matria de concretizao de regras e de disciplina oramental. Depender tambm da forma como estas aes sero transpostas para o plano pblico e interno de cada um dos EstadosMembros e da noo de que as regras no resultam de um dictat exterior, mas so inerentes  vida em grupo.  necessrio um reforo da convergncia das polticas econicas, bem como a constitucionalizao destes objetivos, como forma de assegurar que a apropriao nacional destes mesmos objetivos tenha continuidade na etapa seguinte. Se conseguirmos cumprir este objetivo , e est fora de questo no conseguir cumprilo , fica a faltar a segunda parte, que passa naturalmente por desenvolver aquilo que est embrionariamente presente nas concluss da cimeira de 9 de dezembro, nomeadamente em termos dos mecanismos financeiros necessrios para garantir a estabilidade da UEM. Nesse ponto, como foi referido pelo professor DeGrawe, temos de ter conscincia de que esta UEM no s foi criada com uma inconsistncia interna  ao prever soberania nacional em matria oramental e de poltica econica e, simultaneamente, os outros trs princpios (nodefault, nobailout e noexit)  mas tambm foi criada com outra lacuna: a falta de mecanismos de suporte  liquidez de um soberano ou, no limite, de suporte  solvabilidade. Um Estado que se financie na sua prria moeda, dotado de um banco central prprio e que no tenha limites de financiamento monetrio soberano isto , que exera a funo de prestamista em tima instncia, emitindo moeda e adquirindo dvida pblica no mercado primrio pode responder s dificuldades temporrias de colocao de dvida atravs da emisso monetria. Alm do problema de insuficincia de construo no pilar econmico, a UEM, por no se tratar de um Estado federal, tem uma especificidade no pilar monetrio caracterizada pela ausncia de um prestamista em tima instncia. Uma unio econica e monetria  um acordo entre parceiros com histrias monetrias e com preferncias nacionais muito diferentes. Face a isto,  vio que a UEM tinha de se alinhar pela preferncia que permitiria manter a coeso do grupo, que no era conflituosa e que, no fundo, era estruturalmente mais sida: uma preferncia pela estabilidade nominal. A preferncia pela estabilidade nominal teve consequncias. Toda a configurao do Banco Central Europeu foi feita segundo um modelo que exclua o financiamento monetrio do dfice oramental, como ficou inscrito no Tratado, e exclua a lica de prestamista em tima instncia. Esta dificuldade na construo da UEM no se resolve de forma imediata, porque a Unio Europeia tambm no passa a ser um Estado ico de forma imediata. Isto implica que a Unio Europeia tem de encontrar mecanismos supletivos que resolvam o problema sem criar maior conflitualidade interna. Na falta de um mecanismo de financiamento monetrio por parte do Eurosistema, os Estados da rea do euro financiamse como se o fizessem em moeda estrangeira e ficam sujeitos a uma armadilha de liquidez. Por isso, um Estado que faz parte de uma unio econmica e monetria tem de ter, ao nvel do grupo, capacidade para resolver o problema sem que o grupo sofra o risco moral associado ao comportamento desse Estado. Em suma, os EstadosMembros da rea do euro esto hoje confrontados com dois tipos de problemas: um nacional e outro europeu. A soluo para o problema nacional  resolver os desequilbrios existentes. A soluo para o problema europeu  criar os mecanismos de estabilidade da UEM, reforando o pilar econico  que tem uma dimenso de competitividade e uma dimenso poltica oramental  e, simultaneamente, criar os mecanismos que iro estabilizar esta unio. O reforo do pilar econico da UEM Neste ponto,  necessrio ter conscincia de quo importante  a UEM gerar mais do que mera estabilidade nominal ou mera partilha de moeda. Tem de gerar crescimento e emprego. Este problema no se coloca do lado do pilar monetrio, mas do lado do pilar econico. A coordenao das polticas econicas tem de ser reforada, de forma a assegurar que existe uma viso de conjunto dos impactos das polticas nacionais sobre o grupo, como alis est inscrito no Tratado. Est inclusivamente previsto que os EstadosMembros tm de considerar a sua poltica econmica como sendo de interesse comum e a crise veio reforar o sentido dessa responsabilidade comum. Teremos de reforar ainda mais o pilar econmico, compreendendo claramente que no  possvel o ajustamento de todas as peas deste puzzle se s uma parte das peas estiver a moverse. A presso dos pares pode atuar favoravelmente neste contexto e no apenas visando o interesse individual. O movimento tem de ser conjunto dentro de um quadro de poltica econica, o que significa que teremos de passar de uma discusso que est centrada sobre as polticas oramentais e as polticas financeiras para uma discusso mais vasta, que ter de estar centrada sobre as polticas de crescimento da prria Unio Europeia. No h Unio Europeia estvel sem um brao monetrio estvel, sem um brao econico que gere confiana e sem um instrumento financeiro que reintroduza os mecanismos de feedback, capazes de restabelecer a estabilidade. Mas tambm no h unio econica e monetria estvel se esta no for inovadora e no gerar crescimento. Porque, caso no gere crescimento econmico e no recupere em termos de emprego, a unio econica e monetria vai estar sempre sujeita s tentas nacionais em matria de poltica oramental e de legitimidade da constituio europeia. A construo europeia s se legitima se favorecer o crescimento econico, o emprego e o bemestar. Temos aqui um desafio em duas etapas tambm. Em primeiro lugar, consolidar e estabilizar a UEM, reforando o brao econico da unio econica e monetria. Em segundo lugar, projetar a UEM como um espao de crescimento  escala global. No basta termos bons indicadores enquanto rea se mantivermos grandes assimetrias no nosso interior.  preciso conjugar a gesto das assimetrias  sejam elas de desenvolvimento ou de natureza financeira  com a projeo desse espao europeu. Em concluso, a reforma do modelo de governao econica na Unio Europeia passa, necessariamente, por trs nveis. No primeiro nvel, de natureza institucional, ser preciso que os mecanismos relativos  unio econmica acompanhem a fora dos mecanismos da unio monetria. O que tem de ser corrigido no  o pilar monetrio, por ser forte, mas sim a componente econica, que est relativamente fraca. O segundo nvel  o de um reforo de legitimidade democrtica, que tem de ser encontrada para que se perceba que o cidado joga em dois tabuleiros: o tabuleiro nacional e o tabuleiro europeu (alguns que esto em Estados federados jogam ainda no tabuleiro regional). E, por timo, o terceiro nvel consiste em pr em prtica o princpio do Tratado segundo o qual a poltica de cada um dos EstadosMembros  do interesse de todos , portanto, no interesse de todos que ela tem de ser exercida. Tratase de um jogo que ou  de soma positiva e todos vencem, ou  de soma negativa e todos perdem. Muito obrigado.

Title: Speech by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the 20th Meeting of SaeR
text: 20th SAER Meeting Museum of the East, June 25, 2014 Intervention of the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Carlos da Silva Costa Where are we and where are we going?1 1 Prepared for presentation. I thank Dr. Francisco Murteira Nabo and Dr. Jose Pocas Esteves for the invitation to participate in the opening of the 20th SAER Meeting and to join the tribute to Professor Ernani Lopes. I would like to begin by highlighting two distinctive characteristics of Prof. Ernani Lopes who guided his work in the various positions and fields in which he worked. The first characteristic is determination. This determination was decisive in the 2nd Adjustment Programme with the IMF, in preparing Portugal's participation in the European Economic Comunidades and in the creation of SAER in a context where few the ability to launch a rating agency in Portugal. The second characteristic I point out is the medium-term view. Professor Ernani Lopes has always favored a medium-term perspective, being immune to the small intrigue that is naturally present when horizons are limited. In his vision for the future, the concern was always present to ensure the growth and economic independence of Portugal, which he considered vital for the country's affirmation in the European and global context. In this way, and in honor of Professor Ernani Lopes, I decided to focus my presentation today on the future challenges of Portugal, giving it the title: "Where are we and where are we going?" 1. Where are we? The completion of the Economic and Financial Assistance Programme is an important milestone in the adjustment process of the Portuguese economy. In the programme's implementation period, significant progress has been made in correcting the main macroeconomic imbalances, financial stability has been preserved and the sovereign has regained access to international debt markets. With regard to macroeconomic imbalances, it should be noted that external accounts are rebalancing, with the current and capital accounts moving from a deficit of 9.5% of GDP in 2010 to a surplus of 2.6% in 2013. Economic operators reacted quickly to the change in incentives. Individuals significantly reduced expenditure and companies reoriented the production of goods and services to the foreign market. Exports grew more than external demand, with significant gains in market shares. This is very important from the perspective of economic and monetary union, because it shows that it is possible to correct imbalances in external accounts in a single currency framework. It is also worth noting the significant adjustment of the budgetary balance. The general government deficit fell from 9.8% of GDP in 2010 to 4.9% in 2013 and the primary balance recorded an improvement of 6.4 p.p. of GDP, reaching a near-equilibrium figure in 2013. The soundness of the financial system has strengthened. Today, the banking system Portuguese is more capitalized, has a more favorable liquidity position and is more transparent. We benefit from better supervision and a more robust regulatory framework. This development is the result of the strategy developed by Banco de Portugal since 2010, which was based on three fundamental objectives: stability of the financial system, soundness of each of the institutions and public confidence. Achieving these objectives requires banks to have adequate levels of capital, rigour and transparency in balance sheets, ability to anticipate problems, strengthen government models, assess, manage and control risk, audit and compliance, and strengthen supervision of external auditors. This strategy continued within the framework of the Adjustment Programme, but with a higher degree of demand than the programme. In fact, the cross-sectional inspection exercises for the largest national banking groups  On-site Inspections Programme (OIP) in 2012, The Transverse Exercise for The Review of Credit Portfolio Oddities (ETRICC) in 2013 and ETRICC2 in 2013/2014 - were the initiative of Banco de Portugal2. Banco de Portugal also took cross-cutting action to verify the management and recovery capacity of problematic credits of the eight largest banking groups. This whole process forced a great effort by Banco de Portugal and the financial institutions involved, which cooperated and responded to all the demands made to them. In this context, the Bank has carried out a significant reorganisation of the internal structure and a strengthening of the number of human resources assising supervisory activities and their respective competences3. 2For more information on Banco de Portugal's inspection actions, please refer to the framework document available on the Banco de Portugal website at: . 3 For more details see "Report of the Board of Directors of Activity and Accounts 2013" of Banco de Portugal, available at: . The economic adjustment of the last three years has enabled us  the State, but also non-financial companies and financial institutions  to regain the credibility and confidence of international investors and return to financing in international financial markets. Despite the progress made, there remain a number of weaknesses, which need to be addressed in order to ensure the sustainability of such progress and real convergence with our European partners. In my view, the main challenges are: the indebtedness of economic operators; Structural unemployment; Investment and modernisation of the economy; Institutional reform. Although I refer to them separately and in this order, I must stress that these challenges are naturally interlinked. In order to intervene and attack the weaknesses of the Portuguese economy consistently and adequately, it is crucial to know them. We urgently need to increase knowledge about the Portuguese economy. Here I call on all organizations that have the capacity to deepen and base their knowledge of the Portuguese economy, such as SAER, to contribute to this mission, in particular through micro-economic studies and analyses. Knowledge is essential to avoid policy errors and public incentive systems with perverse effects. 2. The indebtedness of economic operators The Portuguese economy is currently conditioned by the high indebtedness of all institutional sectors: public administrations, companies and families. This imposes significant restrictions on public expenditure, domestic demand and the allocation of available savings, and is a focus of vulnerability in the recovery of economic activity. Despite progress in the evolution of the budget balance, government debt increased by 35 p.p. of GDP between 2010 and 2013 to 129% in 2013 (Table 1). The most important contribution to this increase is due to deficit-debt adjustments. In cumulative terms, the value of these adjustments increased to around 15% of GDP, with the accumulation of government deposits (which amounted to 12.6% of GDP at the end of 2013) and the impact of the issue of contingent capital instruments in the context of the capitalisation processes of national banks. The second most relevant contribution to the increase in debt was interest expenditure (12.6% of GDP in the three-year period). Finally, the effects of the primary deficit and the change in nominal GDP have also contributed, even to a lesser extent, to the increase in the debt ratio. Picture 1 Key budget indicators As a percentage of GDP Source: Banco de Portugal and INE Notes: (a) Transactions which adversely affect the general government deficit are considered special factors, but which, according to the Definition of the Eurosystem, cannot be treated as temporary measures. (b) structural values are adjusted for the cycle and the effects of temporary measures and special factors. The cyclical components and temporary measures are determined by Banco de Portugal, according to the methodologies used in the Eurosystem. The level of Portuguese government debt makes us particularly vulnerable to adverse economic shocks and abrupt changes in risk perception in international financial markets. In this context, and first of all, it is important to make it important to make it important for international investors that debt repayment will not be called into question at any time. This means that in the coming years we need permanent surveillance of our ability to repay. In addition, it is crucial to ensure strict compliance with our European budgetary commitments. Strict European budgetary commitments are in our best interests, for two orders of reason. Firstly, because it guarantees the consistency of the countries belonging to economic and monetary union, enabling mutual trust to be sustained and moral hazard minimised. Secondly, because the adoption of additional fiscal consolidation measures that meet European commitments ensures a sustainable path to public debt, even in a conservative macroeconomic scenario. With the figures we have today of the government debt ratio, if we admit a nominal GDP growth rate of between 2.5% and 3%, we will need an overall budgetary balance around the equilibrium point (Table 2). Of course, if we achieve greater product growth, we will have more room for manoeuvre in public finances. This exercise illustrates well the confluence between sustainable public finance and economic growth objectives. However, the budgetary effort required is still significant and the temporary measures that have had to be taken in an emergency situation should give way to permanent measures. Framework 2 Budget balance needed to reduce debt ratio twenty of the difference from the reference value Source Calculations of Banco de Portugal. Note: The shaded cells indicate the different combinations of nominal GDP growth rate and government debt ratio where the total balance meeting the debt ratio reduction criterion is higher than the MTO. Another challenge we have to face is the excessive indebtedness of non-financial companies. According to data from Banco de Portugal's Balance Sheet Center, in 2012, the level of financial autonomy of non-financial companies (excluding SGPS) was, on average, 30%. More than half had levels below 24% (Chart 3). The ratio of financial autonomy was low in all business size classes and in all sectors of activity, but especially in construction and trade (Table 4). Moreover, in 2012, the weight of interest in terms of cash flow was, on average, more than 50% and the financial debt was almost 9.5 times higher than EBITDA. Framework 3 Indicators of the financial situation of non-financial undertakings (excluding SGPS) Source: Banco de Portugal (Central Balance Sheet) Note: Financial AutonomyEquity/Total Assets Framework 4 Financial autonomy by sector of activity and size (excluding SGPS) Source: Banco de Portugal (Central Balance Sheet) The high leverage ratios of Portuguese companies, when compared to those of companies in most European countries, reflect a double fragility of our business fabric: Financial fragility, because companies are particularly vulnerable to changes in financing conditions, both in terms of volume and cost; Strategic fragility, because the high leverage ratios of Portuguese companies are not consistent with a bet on the sustained growth of the company. Moreover, when financial pressure reaches a point where it decisively conditions the future life of companies, there is a "divorce" between the interests of entrepreneurs and the interests of companies. The commitment of entrepreneurs to the strategic orientation of the company is broken. Indeed, the high level of shareholder/partner loans and intragroup loans of Portuguese companies suggests some resistance from their owners to strengthen equity (Graph 1). This phenomenon is partly associated with the tax system, which favors indebtedness over capital. It is therefore essential to develop financial instruments to strengthen the financial autonomy of companies and to define an economic policy framework, in particular tax, which favours interest in opening up and increasing the share capital of enterprises. Graph 1 Indicators of financial autonomy of private companies Source: Banco de Portugal Calculations Notes: Traditional concept Equity/Total Asset; Alternative 1 (Equity Financing obtained from shareholders &partners and group companies)/Total Asset; Alternative 2 (Equity Net financing of shareholders&partners and group companies)/(Total Asset-Loans granted to group companies) In the immediate future, we must reduce the mortality rate of economically viable or viable companies, as they represent an important share capital. When a company disappears, the capital invested by the owners and the capital borrowed by the banks is destroyed, but, more importantly, the share capital that represents, for example, the routines and tacit knowledge that existing. It is therefore necessary to ensure the continuity of viable companies that today are under financial stress and, in this way, preserve the capital of technological and market knowledge that they incorporate. In addition, it is necessary to ensure a sustainable and more efficient financial structure, and in particular that there are procedures that ensure the effectiveness and opportunity of the restructuring process itself. It is therefore important to act on two fronts: in the conversion of debt into capital or near-capital, in particular by the correct allocation of Community resources in the next EMP and by the sale of bank credits to funds specialised in risk-taking in the so-called mid-caps; and, secondly, the strengthening of equity by current owners or third parties. Any recapitalisation solution requires transparent accounts, audited by certified entities, an appropriate governance model, which provides, inter alia, for professional management of the enterprise and, in the case of medium-sized enterprises, the opening up of third parties' share of capital and the separation of ownership and management. 3. Structural unemployment The significant increase in unemployment is one of the most striking and negative phenomena of the recent adjustment of the Portuguese economy. The sharp contraction in domestic demand, the perception that this contraction was persistent and the adjustment of the previous production structure (the non-tradable sector was oversized relative to the tradable sector) resulted in a very significant increase in unemployment. In 2013, the average unemployment rate stood at 16.3%. The increase in unemployment affected all age groups, but was particularly pronounced in young people. Recent developments in unemployment are part of an upward trend seen since 2000, suggesting structural dysfunctions and misadjustments between supply and demand for work. Estimates from Banco de Portugal point to a very high structural unemployment rate of around 11%. The difficulty of resorption of unemployment is also manifested in the significant rise in long-term unemployment, which reached around 60% in 2013. The high duration of unemployment creates serious economic and social problems and creates increased difficulties in employability. Long-term unemployment in the age groups over 40, which typically have lower levels of education and qualifications than would be desirable for reallocation between sectors, is of particular concern. The duration of unemployment also has an effect on productivity and future labour market developments, as human capital tends to depreciate. Stigmas are often created that can severely affect links to the labour market and culminate in discouragement and the transition to inactivity. This phenomenon is particularly serious in view of demographic change. In recent years, there has been a reduction in portugal in both the total population and the working population (Graph 2). The reduction in the total population will have been associated with the intensification of emigration flows and the trend reduction in fertility rates, which in recent years have remained very low. The evolution of migration flows, with the departure of immigrants and the emigration of nationals, had a very important impact on the evolution of the active population, which fell by 1.9% in 2013 (after falls of 0.2 and 0.9% in 2011 and 2012). The interaction between reduction of the working population and the decrease in the activity rate has a negative impact on gdp growth potential. It is thus more difficult to achieve the sustainability of both public debt and the social model, with harmful effects on intergenerational equity mechanisms, on the security "network" against the risks of exclusion and on equal opportunities in access to education. Graph 2 Total population, working population and employment (index 1999 100) Source: INE The increase in youth unemployment is closely related to the organization of the labor market in Portugal, namely the segmentation between workers with fixed-term contracts and workers with permanent contracts. In the period 2008-2012, fixed-term contracts accounted for about 18% of employees, with mainly young people with higher education than the population average. These workers have high rotation between jobs, frequent unemployment and receive lower wages. In contrast, workers with permanent contracts have very low employment rates and higher wages. In addition, according to the available estimates, only about 12% of fixed-term contracts are converted into permanent contracts, a very low value both in absolute terms and compared to other European countries. In this context, the relationship established between the employer and the employee is not deepened, resulting in frequent separatements and investment in human resources less than desirable. Companies do not have incentives to bet on the professional training of workers with temporary ties, since the return of this training is not guaranteed. As a consequence, specific knowledge and, in particular, the tacit knowledge associated with the production processes of companies tends to be limited to the group of workers hired without term, a group that, with the passage of time, tends to suffer loss and obsolescence of skills, both in terms of the capacity to revitalize the organization and nature of the productive processes and in terms of the number of workers. On the other hand, the high rotation associated with the low conversion rate into fixed-term contracts and the low remuneration of human capital discourage the investment of young people in formal education and, later, when they reach the labor market, investment in the acquisition of specific professional skills related to the job they occupy. This situation also promotes the emigration of the most skilled workers. If we do not change it, we will be wasting a new generation of human resources  highly skilled and able to compete at European and global level  which is essential to increase the growth potential of the economy. In this context, the resorption of structural unemployment is a major challenge for the Portuguese economy. Such resorption will have to be based on the correction of labour market dysfunctions and investment in the tradable sector. However, part of this investment in the tradable sector will result in increased productivity, without creation or even with further destruction of employment. This means that the size of the investment needed to absorb structural unemployment will have to be very significant and greater than that which would result from a normal cycle of Shumpeterian-type creative destruction. This predicts a slow process of resorption of structural unemployment. For this reason, it is necessary to create and strengthen mechanisms that mitiguate the effects of adjustment on the cohesion of Portuguese society. This means that you will need: Income support mechanisms that avoid social exclusion due to lack of income, bearing in mind that income support mechanisms cannot discourage the beneficiary from returning to the labour market. Mechanisms to support the requalification of the long-term unemployed, to prevent them from going to inactivity due to obsolescence of knowledge. It is necessary to ensure that the requalification mechanisms of workers are efficient and that the employment created is not artificial but economically sustainable. Desirfully, the requalification and acquisition of new qualifications should be managed with companies. Mechanisms that enable the advance of the transition to retirement of workers with very long contributory careers and their replacement by younger and more qualified resources, with a neutral impact on public finances. In some industries, there is a limitation to productivity because they keep workers with very long contributory careers (about 50 years) who are not able to meet the demands of new technologies and who are unmotivated. These companies will be available to negotiate with the worker a complement to the reform due for the contributory career using the savings they will get from hiring a young person  more qualified and cheaper  without impact on public finances. This is a possible way of reconciling the renewal of human capital of companies with the preservation of intergenerational cohesion. This solution already exists in other European countries, such as this is the case in Germany, which has recently introduced the possibility for long contributory careers to give way to reforms based on the amount of contributions negotiated with the employer. 4. Investment and modernization of the economy To ensure a path of sustained growth we must have productive investment that promotes a structural transformation of the Portuguese business fabric and leads the economy to a standard of specialization that ensures the balance of external accounts. It is necessary to strengthen the productive fabric of tradable goods and services and improve the standard of specialization of the Portuguese economy, both in sectoral terms and product ranges. The infrastructure and support services are available, we need to monetize them. The strategy to be adopted should be based on four pillars: (i) on optimising installed production capacity; ii) in the evolution to higher segments of the value chain in the sectors where we are already installed; (iii) sectoral diversification by endogenous means; and iv) in attracting foreign investment. First, it is necessary to optimize the use of installed productive capacity, taking advantage of the investment already made, increasing production and looking for new markets and new customers. Today we benefit from a remarkable response from the tradable goods sector, which has moved from the domestic market to the export market and increased its market shares there. It is essential to continue to redirect the production of tradable sectors to foreign markets, which requires increased installed capacity. In the services sector, the use of installed capacity must be increased. There is also scope for production and, consequently, the absorption of unemployment in the area of services and, in particular, in tourism-related services. It is necessary to take advantage of a number of equipment that is currently underused, either because they have been in insolvency or for the absence of capacity or lack of market ability. It is potential for job creation and production that, because they do not materialize, means a waste of capital. The endogenous improvement of the intrasectoral specialization standard should be promoted, inducing a sustained process of incremental innovation. This process will have a significant impact on the added value generated by each sector and, consequently, on the ability to pay salaries compatible with the country's development stage. To implement this strategy, it is crucial that companies have the capacity to increase their production scale and take advantage of new knowledge and qualifications on products and production processes. The production scale must enable an organization with strategic functions to be supported, with a market approach and capable of absorbing knowledge and innovation. This strategy presupposes investment and financing capacity and, last but not least, management capacity. These are the elements that need to be scrutinised in the business Portuguese. The development of Portuguese companies is now conditioned by several factors, namely high indebtedness, poor management quality and insufficient production scale, which translate into a lack of strategy and functional limitations of organization, namely lack of endogenous capacity to keep up with markets and innovation. The development of a dynamic of scale implies a professionalized management, clearly separated from the property, which is able to provide transparent and reliable information to the different stakeholders. It is not always true that the owner of the company's capital has management capacity. In family businesses, the quality of management tends to degrade, first, in the transition from the management of the founder to the second generation and from the second to the third generations; secondly, when they have an accelerated process of growth and reach a scale that requires an organisation model, a definition of functions and a delegation of competences and responsibilities that are not compatible with the centralised management model; and, thirdly, when the balance of the financing structure requires a volume of equity that exceeds the financing capacity of the owners. The intergenerational transmission of family businesses is one of the biggest challenges we face in the short term. Mechanisms must be found to speed up the transmission of companies between heirs or to third parties, for example through Management Buy-Out Operations (MBO). In this sense, correct incentives should be established in the transparency of accounts, in the tolerance of banks in relation to the mismanagement of companies and, in particular, in taxation, defining a fiscal framework that does not pre-embehe indebtedness. We must also improve intersectoral specialisation, with new production sectors, by using radical innovation. In today's knowledge-based economies, innovation is the key to productivity gains, economic growth and long-term well-being. Finally, we must create the conditions for mobile production factors at international level to move to our country, namely foreign direct investment. And at the same time, we have to retain our own mobile production factors. It must, however, be taken into account that the change in the productive structure of the Portuguese economy will have to be made from existing companies, giving room for the emergence of new companies. In this process of transformation, the dialogue between the national innovation system  composed of education, vocational training and research  and businesses is crucial. Portugal has a great lack in this area, right from the outstart because there are deficiencies in the articulation between education, vocational training and research that make the national innovation system less efficient. In turn, there are also deficiencies in the articulation  or even lack of articulation  between the national innovation system and the business sector, for example difficulties inherent to the national innovation system itself and due to the lack of qualified interlocutors on the business side. The evidence that the greater the link between the three vertices, the greater the impact on productivity and growth of economies is widely documented by the OECD. The success of the footwear, moulding and metalworking sectors in Portugal is an excellent example of the advantages of the articulation between the innovation system, national or regional, and the business fabric, in clearly delimited areas and based on well-organized projects. As far as public investment is concerned, a cost-benefit assessment needs to be introduced. Projects should be scrutinised and hierarchised according to their economic and social return. One cannot make a public investment just because there is an unmet need or aspiration; social and economic return must be demonstrated and justified by the priority assigned to investment. This is an essential point on which we must agree, because the savings that will be available to promote Portuguese development will naturally be scarce and has to be used more efficiently than in the past. An international comparison of competitiveness factors allows us to have an idea of where we are in the global panorama (Graph 3). Our main weaknesses come, on the one hand, from factors related to companies  namely innovation, business sophistication and market size  and, on the other hand, from the macroeconomic situation, i.e. stop and resume growth cycles ( "stop and go"). The recurrence of these cycles demonstrates the inadequacy of policies to ensure the sustainability of the development trajectory of the economy and the persistent lack of institutional frameworks that promote the quality of these policies. As noted in Graph 3, institutions are one of our main weaknesses in international competitiveness indicators. In fact, institutional reform is one of our major challenges for the coming years and that is what I will reflect on next. Graph 3 Competitiveness indicator Fonte: Global Competitiveness Report 2013-2014 5. Institutional reform It is widely documented that the quality of institutions is closely related to countries' results in terms of growth and economic development. In fact, the framework of values, standards and institutions has a central place in economic development, enhancing the productive impact of physical capital, the qualification of the working population and the accumulation of technical and organizational knowledge. This framework includes laws that uphold the rule of law and guarantee property rights, but also those that define political institutions and interaction between the social partners. The framework of values, standards and institutions influences the confidence with which economic agents interact and security in the relationship with third parties. This means that this framework conditions the functioningof how the economy works and incentives that motivate individuals. The results of a study by Julio, Alves and Tavares (2013)4 indicate that improvements in institutional performance in Portugal, in the sense of convergence towards European best practices, can increase the EI directed to Portugal by about 60%. 4 Julio, P., Alves, R.P., Tavares, J. (2013), "Foreign investment and institutional reform: Portugal in the European Context", Banco de Portugal Economic Bulletin, Primavera. In Portugal, three types of institutional reforms are needed: (i) Appropriation of the presuppositions of a socio-economic development process supported by political and social actors; (ii) Reform of the budgetary procedure by the State; (iii) Response to the process of globalization of the world economy by financial, non-financial companies and regulators of monolotrack/oligopolistic sectors. (i) Appropriation of the assumptions of a socio-economic development process supported by political and social actors The absence of a broader public policy time perspective is a persistent feature of our history and has been at the root of the recurring economic and financial crises we have faced. In fact, there seems to be a chronic inability of Portuguese society to adopt policies and to bind itself to rules that continuously ensure the sustainability of public accounts and external accounts and the levels of competitiveness compatible with the safeguarding of employment. The macroeconomic costs of unsustainable policies are very high and well known, resulting in cycles of stopping and resuming growth that condition the pace and sustainability of the economic development process. But bad economic policies also have high micro-economic costs because they generate a poor allocation of resources  capital and work  and give rise to the insolvency of economic actors who have been moved by the wrong signals. Indeed, economic policies with inconsistent incentives or inconsistent economic policies from a temporal point of view lead to inconsistent responses, particularly in terms of investment, culminating in costs, for individuals and society, which are very high and often irreversible. This means that political actors need to consider in decisions the future implications of the various options, not only at macro level but also at the micro-economic level. Thus, and in order to break the pattern of recurrent crises once and for all, it is essential to reach a broad consensus on the need to ensure the balance of public accounts, external accounts. It is also necessary to establish an income distribution policy based on credible rules ensuring social mobility and the competitiveness of the economy. Finally, it is necessary to agree on collective rules that anchor incentives for the long-term sustainability of immediate options  the social responsibility of economic policy makers. (ii) Reform of the budgetary procedure Progress needs to be made in reforming the budgetary process and in the capacity building of public administration. The characteristics of the budgetary procedure are crucial for the performance of public accounts. Currently, the scale and complexity of this process, including organic fragmentation in budget implementation, pose important challenges of coordination and accountability of the different actors. In this context, it is particularly important to adopt mechanisms for the control and accountability of public authorities for strict compliance with approved budgets and the implementation of corrective measures in the event of deviation. Sectoral intermediation mechanisms are needed between the State Budget, centrally controlled by the Ministry of Finance, and the executing bodies, to ensure an overview of the financial situation of each ministry and each of the policies. Concentrating budgetary responsibility on a single entity in each ministry, which would become the sole interlocutor of the Ministry of Finance, is essential. At the same time, measures need to be taken to attract and maintain qualified and motivated public administration leaders, an essential requirement for implementing reforms that will enable the development of a more efficient and modern state. (iii) Responding to the process of globalization of the world economy The structure and institutional model of Portuguese companies must be changed so that they can respond to the challenges of competition and innovation in the global market. In particular, and as I have already mentioned, it is necessary to ensure: The clear separation between ownership and management of the company; The professionalization of management; Strengthening the internal organization; Strengthening the absorption capacity of knowledge. At the same time, the banking system needs to ensure efficient intermediation between savings and investment. Specifically, it is important to ensure the minimum of friction, so that the price is adequate, the maximum safety, for the comfort of the aphors, and the maximum efficiency, so that the financing is adequate for the economic agents and for the economy as a whole. To this end, banks' government and risk management models need to be significantly strengthened. Banks should consider that some of the risks they have on their balance sheets is endogenous, depending on their follow-up of customers. They shall make a careful assessment of financing projects, monitor and manage the risk of the companies they finance, detecting any moments of non-compliance and taking corrective action in a timely manner so that the financial pressure does not result in the company's unviability. Finally, an institutional change in the regulatory approach to monopolistic/oligopolistic sectors (utilities) is necessary, whose supply and price conditions significantly affect the competitiveness of the tradable sectors. This reform involves the introduction of a new concept of regulators in the monopolistic/oligopolistic sectors. They must be actors in defining the conditions of relationship between these sectors and their customers, which means that they must be able to define: i) efficiency bechmarks for production, i.e. the level of services they have to provide; (ii) cost bechmarks, i.e. what costs should be taken as a reference in company policy; and iii) margin-setting benchmarks. Otherwise, weaknesses in efficiency and supply of unjustified services, margins and investments are easily transferred to the end customer. But in order to perform these functions well, a modern regulator must be endowed with power, independence, capacity to attract competences and there must be vigilance from society in relation to the way in which it carries out its functions.

Programa de Ajustamento com o FMI, na preparao da adeso de Portugal s Comunidades Econmicas Europeias e na criao da SAER num contexto em que poucos acreditavam na capacidade de lanar uma agncia de rating em Portugal. Deste modo, e em homenagem ao Professor Ernni Lopes, decidi centrar a minha apresentao de hoje nos desafios futuros de Portugal, dando-lhe o ttulo: Onde estamos e para onde vamos? 1. Onde estamos? A concluso do Programa de Assistncia Econmica e Financeira constitui um marco importante no processo de ajustamento da economia portuguesa. No perodo de execuo do Programa, registaram-se progressos assinalveis na correo dos principais desequilbrios macroeconmicos, foi preservada a estabilidade financeira e o soberano recuperou o acesso aos mercados de dvida internacionais. Relativamente aos desequilbrios macroeconmicos,  de assinalar o reequilbrio das contas externas, com a balana corrente e de capital a transitar de um dfice de 9,5% do PIB em 2010 para um excedente de 2,6% em 2013. As exportaes cresceram mais do que a procura externa, tendo-se registado ganhos significativos de quotas de mercado. Este facto  muito importante na perspetiva da Unio Econmica e Monetria, porque evidencia que  possvel corrigir desequilbrios das contas externas num quadro de moeda nica.  tambm de realar o significativo ajustamento do saldo oramental. O dfice das administraes pblicas reduziu-se de 9,8% do PIB em 2010 para 4,9% em 2013 e o saldo primrio registou uma melhoria de 6,4 p.p. do PIB, tendo, em 2013, atingido um valor prximo do equilbrio. A solidez do sistema financeiro reforou-se. Hoje, o sistema bancrio portugus encontra-se mais capitalizado, tem uma posio de liquidez mais favorvel e  mais transparente. Beneficiamos de melhor superviso e de um quadro regulamentar mais robusto. Esta evoluo  resultado da estratgia desenvolvida pelo Banco de Portugal desde 2010, que assentou em trs objetivos fundamentais: estabilidade do sistema financeiro, solidez de cada uma das instituies e confiana do pblico. A concretizao destes objetivos exige aos bancos nveis adequados de capital, rigor e transparncia nos balanos, capacidade de antecipao de problemas, reforo dos modelos de governo, de avaliao, gesto e controlo de risco, de auditoria e de compliance e reforo da superviso dos auditores externos. Esta estratgia prosseguiu no quadro do Programa de Ajustamento, mas com um grau de exigncia superior ao que resultava do Programa. Com efeito, os exerccios de inspeo transversais aos maiores grupos bancrios nacionais  Programa de Inspees On-site (OIP, On-site Inspections Programme) em 2012, Exerccio Transversal de Reviso das Imparidades das Carteiras de Crdito (ETRICC) em 2013 e ETRICC2 em 2013/2014 - foram da iniciativa do Banco de Portugal2. Foi tambm da iniciativa do Banco de Portugal a ao transversal desenvolvida para verificar a capacidade de gesto e de recuperao de crditos problemticos dos oito maiores grupos bancrios. Todo este processo obrigou a um grande esforo do Banco de Portugal e das instituies financeiras envolvidas, que cooperaram e responderam a todas as exigncias que lhes foram feitas. Neste contexto, o Banco procedeu a uma significativa reorganizao da estrutura interna e a um reforo do nmero dos recursos humanos afetos s atividades de superviso e das respetivas competncias3. 2Para mais informaes sobre as aes de inspeo do Banco de Portugal, pode consultar-se o documento de enquadramento disponvel no stio do Banco de Portugal, em: http://www.bportugal.pt/pt-PT/OBancoeoEurosistema/ComunicadoseNotasdeInformacao/Documents/combp20140328.pdf. 3 Para mais detalhes veja-se Relatrio do Conselho de Administrao de Atividade e Contas 2013 do Banco de Portugal, disponvel em: https://www.bportugal.pt/pt-PT/PublicacoeseIntervencoes/Banco/RelatConselhoAdministracao/Paginas/default.aspx. O ajustamento econmico destes ltimos trs anos permitiu-nos  ao Estado, mas tambm s empresas no financeiras e s instituies financeiras  recuperar a credibilidade e a confiana dos investidores internacionais e regressar ao financiamento nos mercados financeiros internacionais. Apesar dos progressos alcanados, permanecem diversas fragilidades, que tm de ser resolvidas para assegurarmos a sustentabilidade desses progressos e retomarmos a convergncia real com os nossos parceiros europeus. A meu ver, os principais desafios so: O endividamento dos agentes econmicos; O desemprego estrutural; O investimento e a modernizao da economia; A reforma institucional. Apesar de os referir separadamente e por esta ordem, devo sublinhar que estes desafios esto, naturalmente, interligados. Para intervir e atacar as fragilidades da economia portuguesa de forma consistente e adequada,  crucial conhec-las. Necessitamos de urgentemente aumentar o conhecimento sobre a economia portuguesa. Lano aqui um convite a todas as organizaes que tm capacidade para aprofundar e fundamentar o conhecimento da economia portuguesa, como a SAER, para que contribuam para esta misso, nomeadamente atravs da realizao de estudos e anlises microeconmicos. O conhecimento  fundamental para evitarmos erros de poltica e sistemas de incentivos pblicos com efeitos perversos. 2. O endividamento dos agentes econmicos A economia portuguesa encontra-se atualmente condicionada pelo elevado endividamento de todos setores institucionais: administraes pblicas, empresas e famlias. Esta situao impe restries significativas  despesa pblica,  procura interna e  afetao da poupana disponvel, constituindo um foco de vulnerabilidade na recuperao da atividade econmica. Apesar dos progressos registados na evoluo do saldo oramental, a dvida pblica aumentou 35 p.p. do PIB entre 2010 e 2013, situando-se em 129% em 2013 (Quadro 1). O segundo contributo mais relevante para o aumento da dvida foi a despesa com juros (12,6% do PIB no conjunto dos trs anos). Finalmente, os efeitos do dfice primrio e da variao do PIB nominal tambm contriburam, ainda que em menor medida, para o aumento do rcio da dvida.
