Esta reforma passa pela introduo de um novo conceito de reguladores dos setores monopolistas/oligopolistas. Tm de ser entidades intervenientes na definio das condies de relacionamento entre estes setores e os seus clientes, o que significa que tm de ter capacidade para definir: i) bechmarks de eficincia para a produo, ou seja, o nvel de servios que tm de prestar; ii) bechmarks de custos, isto , quais os custos que devem ser tidos como referncia na poltica da empresa; e iii) benchmarks de fixao de margens. Caso contrrio, facilmente se transfere para o cliente final insuficincias de eficincia e de fornecimento de servios, margens e investimentos no justificados. Mas, para exercer bem estas funes, um regulador moderno tem de estar dotado de poder, independncia, capacidade de atrao de competncias e tem de existir vigilncia da sociedade em relao  forma como exerce as suas funes.

Title: Intervention by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the American Club
text: The immediate and medium-term challenges of the Portuguese economy Intervention by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the American Club 24 November 2011 Good afternoon, everyone. First of all, let me thank the American Club's invitation to the person of your President. Since I only have twenty minutes, please excuse me from addressing a greeting to all the friends and people I admire and who are present in the room, to enter directly into the theme of my intervention: "the immediate and medium-term challenges of the Portuguese economy". The question at the outset is whether we must first consider the immediate challenges, to leave for the medium-term ones, or whether, on the contrary, we must start from the medium-term challenges and then reflect on the immediate ones. Baltic sailors say there are no storms for sailors who know the ports they are headed for; there are only storms for those who don't know where they're going. Likewise, caught up in the middle of a crisis, we need to know what our medium-term challenge is so that we can address the immediate challenges. Otherwise, we will not be able to prioritise the immediate challenges and, consequently, we may be ill-prepared to meet the medium-term challenges. Our medium-term challenge is to create a more productive and job-creating country The great challenge in the medium term is to make Portugal a more productive and job-generating country. A country capable of providing its population with a per capita income and well-being higher than it has today and a level of employment compatible with its aspirations. I refer to these two realities separately, because it may happen that a country has an increase in per capita income due to a significant increase in productivity and, at the same time, there is an increase in structural unemployment. The countries in which this happens are not necessarily in balance, because, from the point of view of social cohesion, structural unemployment is a corrosive factor. When we want to position a country, we have to look at the two variables: increased per capita income  which implies increased productivity  and job creation for those who are reaching the labour market and who obviously cannot see their expectations frustrated. So the country we're going to build will have to be more productive and generate more jobs. The sustainability of public finances and external debt are part of the medium-term challenge On the other hand, the country must be able to ensure the sustainability of this well-being. This means that the sustainability of public finances and external debt are part of the medium-term challenge, but it is a short-term challenge. It is not possible to ensure a sustainable path of growth and well-being for the Portuguese population if, at the same time, we incur cycles of "to-start" in terms of public finances and external debt. Which means, from the outside  and using the image of baltic sailors  that not all engines serve to return this boat to the port where we want to get. For a country like Portugal, where there is a large imbalance between the non-tradable goods sector and the tradable goods sector, the engine of non-tradables is not an engine that can guarantee this arrival at the port of destination. Therefore, we must look at the external rebalancing of the Portuguese economy as a rebalancing based on the development of tradable goods, the development of exports and, consequently, on job creation in this sector of the economy. But it is also important to realise that creating jobs only through the expansion of public spending is, at the outset, a process of limited duration, because at some point the problem of the sustainability of public debt will necessarily be raised and, as such, funding will have to be stopped. It is, by the way, what we are living today. Whatever our political and social position, we must keep in mind that, if the goal is well-being, employment and sustainability, sustainable public finances and a sustainable external position must be assumed as necessary conditions, along side increased productivity. As increased productivity, by definition, destroys employment  because when productivity is increasing, it is producing more with less  we necessarily have to expand our production system, have more companies, new sectors. In other words, the challenge of the tradable sector is both a challenge to expand the productive apparatus of the Portuguese economy. More investment is needed which, on the one hand, increases productivity and, on the other hand, generates jobs to absorb those that will be dispensed with by increased productivity. The economic dynamics of any country is a dynamic of permanent metabolism: there are units that die and units that are born and there are jobs that end up and jobs that are created. The employment structure in Portugal 100 years ago was not today's, because from the technological point of view, demand and our insertion in the international division of labor, the situation is different. Someone who is convinced that it is possible to think about the future by blocking social and economic metabolism is making a mistake. This permanent metabolism is inherent to development and all the mechanisms that seek to mitigate it, although they may seem beneficial in the short term, end up proving to be strongly penalizing in the long term. This premise has to be taken into account when we look at the Portuguese reality. Access to the "new normal" The first immediate challenge of the Portuguese economy is to be able to return to the market at the end of the Economic and Financial Assistance Programme negotiated with the European Union and the IMF. To return to the market, Portugal must meet the minimum requirements of what is market admissibility. And the lows aren't the same as five years ago or seven years ago. The minimums in terms of capacity and cost of financing, financial soundness requirements and leverage levels of companies and banks will be completely different. Banco de Portugal was, moreover, a precursor in a series of measures successively seconded at international level: we ask for more capital and now, at international level, they are asking for even more than we ask for; leverage and the market is demanding even more deleveraging. What is happening under the Assistance Programme is therefore not different from what is and will happen at international level. On the contrary, it is convergent. We can discuss the pace or even the lucidity of the markets, but in this matter it is not worth thinking that someone, and especially a small country, can condition the rules of the game. Precisely because we are a small country, we have to respect the "Olympic minimums" to participate in that "championship". If we don't, we're out. And being out of this championship is very serious for an economy like the Portuguese, because we will reach the end of the program with high levels of indebtedness, which means that we will have to arrive with a credibility that leads the market to want to renew credit to the economy. Renewing credit to the economy means believing in us. As Portugal will reach the end of the programme with a high public debt, public finances will have to be credible. If they are not, at the end of the programme we will find ourselves again in the middle of a "no man's land", because we will not be in the market and we will not be in the program. It would be the worst of situations. The conditions under which we reach the end of the assistance program will determine our access to a new level playing field that is slowly and consistently organizing internationally. That is why we need a budgetary adjustment programme that re-enhances the credibility of public finances and a deleveraging programme and strengthening the soundness of the financial system  which, be aware, is sound. We are not talking about recapitalizing the financial system. This is, moreover, a mistake that I systematically confront when I read the Portuguese press, because talking about recapitalization means "resuming something that has been missing". We are not talking about recapitalisation, we are talking about capital strengthening, which is a different thing: it is "adding to what exists" and not "making up for what is missing". This question of semantics must be clearly understood so that we do not induce our fellow citizens to think that the problem is of another nature. Portugal needs to reach the end of the process stronger and less dependent on external funding. But this will only be possible with the commitment of the State, businesses and individuals. Families will have to increase the savings rate, because without this increase the external rebalancing process will necessarily be conditioned. Companies will also have to "change their lives". In fact, today I was misquoted by a newspaper, which wrote that I had attacked SMEs. We have a fabric of SMEs that is very important and decisive for the Portuguese economy. And we must ensure that the metabolism of these companies continues in such a way that they do not have a life curve very connected to their founder. It is necessary, on the one hand, to ensure the vitality of the company, even when the vitality of the initial entrepreneur or his successors disappears. On the other hand, it is necessary to assume that companies make profits to reinvest, to strengthen themselves, and not to deviate. Otherwise, Portuguese SMEs will not be able to pass beyond a given tier. When comparator, for example, the average echelon of companies in Portugal with the middle tier in Spain, there is a resistance ceiling in the Portuguese that is one third of the Spanish. Portuguese companies are at a level of invoicing that is almost a third of that of The Spanish ones. And it is necessary to understand what is the socio-economic dynamics, which has to do with the way the company is seen by the one who owns it. This issue is obviously related to the management capacities of companies, the quality of the organisation and a factor which, in my opinion, is very important: there must be a clear distinction between the management function and the capital holding function. It is good that the capital is remunerated and that, in to be remunerated, do not necessarily need to occupy the chair of the administration. The two functions are different. Not always who has the capital is the best administrator or the best strategist and, therefore, it is natural that there is division of functions, especially when companies grow. What is very often the case in Portugal is the "inorganicity" of companies, because all command functions are confused and, automatically, the management capacity is impoverished. Attention needs to be paid to this. There are certainly roots in the tax system Portuguese and the legal system that induce non-separation, non-segregation of functions. I can't get enough of quoting one of the model companies I know that is Spanish. A family has owned this company for four generations, the company has continued to grow and is the largest company in the sector at European level. But it was based on a basic principle: being a company owner does not give you the right to be an administrator, because the risk, at some point, is that management skills fail, especially when you move from one generation to the next. Therefore, it is important to look at the business fabric Portuguese. There are no miracles, no business sectors that arise from nothing. The business sector in ten years will be the one that results from the current, plus the shoots that are emerging over time, which will be the new phenomena of entrepreneurship. There must be a legal context that favours this development. Job creation depends on the legal framework Job creation depends on the context  and in Portugal there are high context costs. One cost of context that should be mentioned is the legal system. It is necessary to ensure that an undertaking's financial difficulties do not become economic difficulties and that disputes relating to the resolution of problems between creditor and debtor do not compromise the continuity of the undertaking. As long as the company has a positive cash flow, it should continue its activity, because a company is more than an individual possession of an entrepreneur. The company is a share capital and this share capital is intangible. If the company disappears, it's not an answer the next day. They are routines, ways of being, forms of relationship with the market and notoriety in the market that disappear on the same day that a company disappears and that, therefore, it is important to preserve. Therefore, if an economically viable undertaking is in financial difficulties, it is necessary to clearly separate the economic dimension from the financial dimension, resolving financial problems as soon as possible, so as not to jeopardise economic viability. Otherwise, we commit the share capital, in addition to the associated employment. The revision of insolvency law is essential, as is it essential to expeditious the process and to protect economic unity. For me, this is a very important aspect. Another aspect of greater importance, from a legal point of view, is the certainty of contracts and the relationship between economic actors. A legal framework and a dispute resolution framework that does not guarantee certainty produce uncertainty; uncertainty means costs; costs mean disincentives to enter the process. It is necessary to minimise costs in order to increase efficiency and to prevent the resolution of the financial part from dangerously dangerous from an economically viable undertaking. If a large American car company, which had to appeal to Article 11 of the law, had been dealt with at the time by Portuguese insolvency law, it would have been sold to the junkyard and the workers would have been unemployed. If we look at the current quote of this company, we find that it goes "from wind to stern". Why? Because the resolution of the financial conflict has been separated from the economic issue. It is not natural for the economic issue to be dependent  if the company is viable  on the resolution of the financial conflict. The two issues have to be resolved, but at their own times. A small country needs strong public administration Another issue that worries me is public administration. It is not fashionable to talk about it, but one must be aware that a small state does not work without a strong and capable public administration. This does not mean a large public administration, but rather a highly skilled and stable public administration, with the ability to think organically, to ensure continuity and certainty in the relationship with economic agents and  this is a very important aspect  that guarantees not to be captured. A small country needs values and institutions and public administration is a fundamental pillar for its development. However, let us not confuse the size of the State with the strength of public administration. We need a smaller, lighter and more economical state; but we certainly need a much stronger state from the point of view of the administration, which means that  and this idea goes against the mainstream  we must overcome some demagoguery with regard to senior management remuneration. Otherwise, it will not be possible to recruit people with quality and, above all, to ensure their permanence, which is essential for us to have a modern state. The essential function of a modern state is regulatory Another important dimension concerns the functions of regulation. A State has areas of natural monopoly and, when it is small, has other areas that, not being natural monopolies, are areas of oligopoly that, consequently, tax the areas that are downstream, through the prices they set. In these areas, it is essential to have a strong regulatory system. It's a matter of want and competence. The essential function of a modern State is not to produce, but to ensure that the production and provision of goods and services are made in the most efficient conditions and at the lowest price. If this function is not the most important and is not assumed as such, a rent problem is generated. It moves from a modern state to a state of the eighteenth or nineteenth century, a state that serves to distribute rents to those who are directly or indirectly involved in its activity. A new social contract is needed for those outside the labour market One last concern concerns the labour market. The Portuguese labour market is clearly divided into two: those who are "inside"  the legacy market, which are less than 50 per cent  and those who are "out" (who are, so to speak, in "no man's land"). It is necessary that those outside the legacy market benefit from modern employment contracts, which simultaneously contemplate the protection of the worker  which is the protection of the citizen  and the need for economic metabolism, which implies the possibility of reviewing the permanence of the job. In Portugal, the worker is often protected, crystallizing the job. It's a bit like Ulysses tying himself to the mast: the worker has the income assured, because he does not leave the job. As the job depends on the market, technology, demand, one day the job disappears and protection for workers disappears. It is important to distinguish between the two aspects, because the faster we do so, the easier it will be to reallocation of human resources and the readjustment of the productive tissue. But that means a new social contract, a new way of being. It's not about "opening a war" with those in the legacy market  it will go down over time. The new contract (and the new type of protection) has to be given to a younger workforce in which it is necessary to invest. Not forgetting that companies also only invest if they are able to stay. If the workers go in and out, no one invests: he does not invest the worker, because he does not know if he will continue; nor invests the company, because it does not know if it can continue. At the moment we are facing a process of usury of a human capital that, on top of that, is better than that which existed in the past. It is necessary to "reinvent" this social contract, creating an employment contract in which the protection of the citizen does not translate into the crystallization of the productive structure, because otherwise it will be a vain goal. The importance of the national innovation system To create jobs and to evolve the economy there is another great theme that is important to discuss: the functioning of the so-called "national innovation system". There is no innovation without education, without vocational training and without research. But education, research and vocational training do not guarantee development if a clear bridge is not established between the productive fabric, the needs of the economy and the system innovation. How many companies know what's going on on the lab side? How many companies pass on their needs to the vocational training system? Where are we, for example, comparing the vocational training model Portuguese with the Swiss, with that of Singapore or with the German? We're in league. How many laboratories care about what practical use they do? When the Spanish minister of research and innovation two years ago decided  and she came from research  that there would be no public participation in research projects if there were no associated Spanish companies, "Carmo and Trindade" fell, because the "sacrosanct" autonomy of the research sector was called into question. But this is the only way to ensure that the system has a purpose compatible with the interests of those who pay. And it's the taxpayer who pays. Thank you very much.
text_original: Os desafios imediatos e de mdio prazo da economia portuguesa Interveno do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa no American Club 24 de novembro de 2011 Boa tarde a todos. Permitam-me, antes de mais, que agradea o convite do American Club na pessoa do seu Presidente. Dado que s disponho de vinte minutos, dispensem-me, por favor, de dirigir um cumprimento a todos os amigos e pessoas que admiro e que esto presentes na sala, para entrar diretamente no tema da minha interveno: os desafios imediatos e de mdio prazo da economia portuguesa. A questo que se coloca  partida  saber se devemos equacionar primeiro os desafios imediatos, para partirmos para os de mdio prazo, ou se, pelo contrrio, devemos partir dos desafios de mdio prazo para depois refletirmos sobre os imediatos. Segundo se conta, os marinheiros do Bltico dizem que no h tempestades para os marinheiros que conhecem os portos para onde se dirigem; s h tempestades para aqueles que no sabem para onde vo. Do mesmo modo, apanhados no meio de uma crise, temos de saber qual o nosso desafio de mdio prazo para que possamos equacionar os desafios imediatos. Caso contrrio, no saberemos hierarquizar os desafios imediatos e, em consequncia, poderemos estar mal preparados para fazer face aos desafios de mdio prazo. O nosso desafio de mdio prazo  criar um pas mais produtivo e gerador de emprego O grande desafio de mdio prazo  conseguir tornar Portugal num pas mais produtivo e gerador de emprego. Um pas capaz de proporcionar  sua populao um rendimento per capita e um bem-estar superiores aos que tem hoje e um nvel de emprego compatvel com as suas aspiraes. Refiro estas duas realidades em separado, pois pode acontecer que um pas tenha um aumento do rendimento per capita por fora de um aumento significativo da produtividade e, ao mesmo tempo, registe um aumento do desemprego estrutural. Os pases em que isso acontece no esto necessariamente em equilbrio, porque, do ponto de vista da coeso social, o desemprego estrutural  um fator corrosivo. Quando queremos posicionar um pas, temos de olhar para as duas variveis: aumento do rendimento per capita  o que implica aumento da produtividade  e criao de emprego para aqueles que esto a chegar ao mercado de trabalho e que, obviamente, no podem ver frustradas as suas expectativas. Portanto, o pas que vamos construir ter de ser mais produtivo e gerar mais emprego. A sustentabilidade das finanas pblicas e da dvida externa so parte do desafio de mdio prazo Por outro lado, o pas tem de ser capaz de garantir a sustentabilidade desse bem-estar. Isto significa que a sustentabilidade das finanas pblicas e da dvida externa so parte do desafio de mdio prazo, constituindo, no entanto, um desafio de curto prazo. No  possvel assegurar um trajeto sustentvel de crescimento e de bem-estar para a populao portuguesa se, ao mesmo tempo, incorrermos em ciclos de para-arranca em matria de finanas pblicas e de dvida externa. O que significa, desde logo  e utilizando a imagem dos marinheiros do Bltico  que nem todos os motores servem para reconduzir este barco ao porto aonde queremos chegar. Para um pas como Portugal, onde existe um grande desequilbrio entre o setor dos bens no transacionveis e o setor dos bens transacionveis, o motor dos no transacionveis no  um motor que possa garantir esta chegada ao porto de destino. Portanto, temos de olhar para o reequilbrio externo da economia portuguesa como um reequilbrio assente no desenvolvimento dos bens transacionveis, no desenvolvimento das exportaes e, consequentemente, na criao de emprego nesse setor da economia. Mas  tambm importante perceber que criar emprego apenas atravs da expanso da despesa pblica ,  partida, um processo com durao limitada, porque, em dado momento, colocar-se-, necessariamente, o problema da sustentabilidade da dvida pblica e, como tal, o financiamento ter de ser forosamente interrompido. , alis, o que estamos hoje a viver. Qualquer que seja o nosso posicionamento em termos polticos e sociais,  preciso que tenhamos presente que, se o objetivo  bem-estar, emprego e sustentabilidade, finanas pblicas sustentveis e uma posio externa sustentvel tm de ser assumidas como condies necessrias, a par do incremento da produtividade. Como o aumento da produtividade, por definio, destri emprego  porque, quando se aumenta a produtividade est a produzir-se mais com menos  temos, necessariamente, de expandir o nosso aparelho produtivo, ter mais empresas, novos setores. Ou seja, o desafio do setor dos transacionveis  simultaneamente um desafio de expanso do aparelho produtivo da economia portuguesa.  necessrio mais investimento que, por um lado, aumente a produtividade e que, por outro, gere emprego para absorver aqueles que vo ser dispensados pelo aumento da produtividade. A dinmica econmica de qualquer pas  uma dinmica de metabolismo permanente: h unidades que morrem e unidades que nascem e h empregos que acabam e empregos que se criam. A estrutura de emprego em Portugal h 100 anos no era a de hoje, porque do ponto de vista tecnolgico, da procura e da nossa insero na diviso internacional do trabalho, a situao  diferente. Algum que esteja convencido de que  possvel pensar o futuro, bloqueando o metabolismo social e econmico, est a cometer um erro. Este metabolismo permanente  inerente ao desenvolvimento e todos os mecanismos que o procurem mitigar, embora possam parecer benficos no curto prazo, acabam por revelar-se fortemente penalizadores no longo prazo. Esta premissa tem de ser tida em conta quando olhamos para a realidade portuguesa. O acesso  nova normalidade O primeiro desafio imediato da economia portuguesa  conseguir regressar ao mercado no final do Programa de Assistncia Econmica e Financeira negociado com a Unio Europeia e o FMI. Para regressar ao mercado, Portugal tem de cumprir os requisitos mnimos daquilo que  a admissibilidade pelo mercado. E os mnimos no so os mesmos de h cinco anos ou de h sete anos. Os mnimos em termos de capacidade e de custo de financiamento, de requisitos de solidez financeira e de nveis de alavancagem de empresas e bancos sero completamente diferentes. O Banco de Portugal foi, alis, precursor numa srie de medidas sucessivamente secundadas no plano internacional: pedimos mais capital e agora, no plano internacional, solicitam ainda mais do que pedimos; pedimos desalavancagem e o mercado est a exigir ainda mais desalavancagem. O que est a fazer-se no quadro do Programa de Assistncia no , portanto, divergente daquilo que est e vai passar-se no plano internacional. Pelo contrrio,  convergente. Podemos discutir o ritmo ou at a lucidez dos mercados, mas, nesta matria, no vale a pena pensar que algum, e sobretudo um pequeno pas, consegue condicionar as regras do jogo. Precisamente porque somos um pequeno pas, temos de respeitar os mnimos olmpicos para participarmos naquele campeonato. Se no o fizermos, estaremos fora. E estar fora deste campeonato  muito grave para uma economia como a portuguesa, porque chegaremos ao fim do programa com nveis de endividamento altos, o que significa que teremos de chegar com uma credibilidade que leve o mercado a querer renovar o crdito  economia. Renovar o crdito  economia significa acreditarem em ns. Uma vez que Portugal chegar ao fim do programa com uma dvida pblica elevada, as finanas pblicas tero de ser credveis. Se o no forem, no fim do programa encontrar-nos-emos novamente no meio de uma "terra de ningum", porque no estaremos no mercado nem estaremos no programa. Seria a pior das situaes. As condies em que chegarmos ao fim do programa de assistncia determinaro o nosso acesso a um novo level playing field que est a organizar-se lenta e consistentemente no plano internacional. Por esse motivo,  necessrio que tenhamos um programa de ajustamento oramental que reponha a credibilidade das finanas pblicas e um programa de desalavancagem e de reforo da solidez do sistema financeiro  que, ateno,  slido. No estamos a falar de recapitalizao do sistema financeiro. Este , alis, um erro com que me confronto sistematicamente quando leio a imprensa portuguesa, porque falar de recapitalizao significa repor alguma coisa que faltou. Ns no estamos a falar de recapitalizao, estamos a falar de reforo de capital, que  uma coisa diferente:  acrescentar ao que existe e no compensar o que falta.  preciso que esta questo de semntica seja claramente entendida, para no induzirmos os nossos concidados a pensar que o problema  de outra natureza. Portugal precisa de chegar ao fim do processo mais forte e menos dependente do financiamento externo. Mas isso s ser possvel com o empenho do Estado, das empresas e dos particulares. As famlias tero de aumentar a taxa de poupana, porque sem esse aumento o processo de reequilbrio externo estar necessariamente condicionado. As empresas tambm tero de mudar de vida. Alis, hoje fui mal citado por um jornal, que escreveu que eu tinha atacado as PME. Temos um tecido de PME que  importantssimo e decisivo para a economia portuguesa. E temos de assegurar que o metabolismo dessas empresas prossiga de tal forma que elas no tenham uma curva de vida muito ligada ao seu fundador.  necessrio, por um lado, assegurar a vitalidade da empresa, mesmo quando a vitalidade do empreendedor inicial ou dos seus sucessores desaparece. Por outro lado,  preciso partir do princpio de que as empresas fazem lucros para reinvestir, para se reforar, e no para desviar. Caso contrrio, as PME portuguesas no conseguiro passar alm de um dado escalo. Quando se compara, por exemplo, o escalo mdio das empresas em Portugal com o escalo mdio em Espanha, h um teto de resistncia nas portuguesas que fica a um tero do das espanholas. As empresas portuguesas ficam num nvel de faturao que  quase um tero do das espanholas. E  preciso perceber qual  a dinmica socioeconmica, que tem a ver com a forma como  encarada a empresa por quem a detm. Esta questo est, obviamente, relacionada com as capacidades de gesto das empresas, com a qualidade da organizao e com um fator que, na minha opinio,  importantssimo: deve existir uma clara distino entre a funo de administrao e a funo de deteno de capital.  bom que o capital seja remunerado e que, para ser remunerado, no precise necessariamente de ocupar a cadeira da administrao. As duas funes so diferentes. Nem sempre quem tem o capital  o melhor administrador ou o melhor estratega e, portanto,  natural que haja diviso de funes, sobretudo quando as empresas crescem. O que se verifica em Portugal com muita frequncia  a inorganicidade das empresas, pois confundem-se todas as funes de comando e, automaticamente, empobrece-se a capacidade de gesto.  necessrio prestar ateno a este aspeto. H, seguramente, razes no sistema fiscal portugus e no sistema jurdico que induzem a no separao, a no segregao de funes. No me canso de citar uma das empresas-modelo que conheo e que  espanhola. Uma famlia detm essa empresa h quatro geraes, a empresa continuou a crescer e  a maior empresa do setor a nvel europeu. Mas assentou num princpio bsico: ser dono da empresa no d direito a ser administrador, porque o risco, em determinado momento,  que falhem as competncias de administrao, sobretudo quando se passa de uma gerao para a outra. Por conseguinte,  importante olhar para o tecido empresarial portugus. No h milagres, no h setores empresariais que surjam a partir do nada. O setor empresarial daqui a dez anos h de ser aquele que resulta do atual, acrescido dos rebentos que vo surgindo ao longo do tempo, que sero os novos fenmenos de empreendedorismo. Tem de existir um contexto legal que favorea essa evoluo. A criao de emprego depende do quadro jurdico A criao de emprego depende do contexto  e em Portugal existem custos de contexto elevados. text: Intervention of the Governor of Banco de Portugal at the Meeting of Economists "Portugal in the post-troika period"1 July 30, 2013 Thank you very much, Mr President. In my speech I would like to address the situation of Portugal in the post-troika period, starting by analyzing the conditions in which we arrived there, that is "the eve". In fact, the situation on the eve of the end of the Economic and Financial Assistance Programme is as important as the next day, as it conditions what will happen in the subsequent period. I. The eve of the end of the Adjustment Programme Taking into account the currently available economic projections, and using as a reference the colours of a traffic light, we will arrive at the time of the transition with the indicators of external accounts to "green", indicators of economic activity and some budgetary indicators to "yellow" and unemployment and public debt in "red" (Table 1). Significant adjustment of external accounts (green) The external rebalancing of the Portuguese economy is remarkable, having been faster and stronger than that observed in the previous two adjustment programmes, when we had the exchange rate as an adjustment instrument. The current and capital account and the balance of goods and services - which in 2012 recorded positive values for the first time in decades - are expected to remain in surplus. This adjustment reflects both the impact on imports of domestic demand contraction and the increase in market shares of Portuguese exports. In fact, in a particularly unfavorable international environment, Portuguese companies have made a remarkable effort to increase penetration and diversify export markets. 1 Version for presentation. In fact, economic activity contracted more than originally projected and the current outlook points to a tenuous recovery in 2014. The budgetary adjustment, although it fell short of what had originally been planned, is very substantial. The primary budget balance, which excludes interest expenditure, has improved significantly. The adjustment is also very significant if we look at the evolution of the structural balance of public finances. However, the fiscal consolidation process has been slower than expected and it is necessary to ensure its sustainability with structural measures to cut public expenditure. Page 2 of 12 Unemployment and public debt at very high levels and still growing (red) The level of unemployment is of course worrying, particularly as it is largely structural unemployment. This requires the implementation of a safety net that safeguards social cohesion and allows the requalification of the long-term unemployed and avoids their passage into inactivity. Public debt has reached very high levels and is still growing. It is imperative that its evolution ensures a sustainable trajectory. This is the main restriction of economic policy in the future. I would like to draw attention here to a point which I consider very important and which deserves particular reflection. As pointed out in the intervention by Marco Buti, our adjustment programme has been implemented rigorously. Nevertheless, the perception of failure was created in the Portuguese population, social agents and political agents, namely the perception that we have failed the goals of the programme. This perception is not correct. I therefore believe that it is not only necessary to demystify this idea, noting that:  first, international economic developments were much more unfavourable than originally envisaged, which had very negative consequences on exports, investment, economic activity and, consequently, budgetary revenue and expenditure and public debt. Thus, for example, if external demand had evolved according to what had originally been envisaged in the Programme, the budgetary adjustment effort made so far would have already induced a downward trajectory of the government debt ratio (line-to-line figure 1). Page 3 of 12 Figure 1 Public Debt as a percentage of GDP 130 120 110 100 90 80 70 60 50 40 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 2013 2014 "Observed Program goals" "Scenario with external search of the initial program" Source: Banco de Portugal  secondly, the Programme's projections were based on budgetary multipliers that turned out to be lower than the estimated ex-post. The added uncertainty for economic operators that resulted from the prolongation of the weakness of the external environment of the Portuguese economy and, in particular, the simultaneity of the budgetary consolidation processes underway in these same economies, led economic operators to foresee a further fall in permanent income. As a result, the impact of fiscal consolidation measures on GDP - multipliers - has been underestimated. The combination of these two orders of adverse factors with the setting of the Programme's targets as a percentage of GDP has determined a need to revise the targets, under penalty of triggering and fueling a vicious cycle between fiscal consolidation and economic activity developments. This justifies rethinking the setting of the targets of the adjustment programmes in order to avoid the return effect of GDP developments on the achievement of budgetary targets - via tax revenues and social expenditure - and on debt targets - via tax revenues, social expenditure and "denominator effect". This is a message I address in particular to Marco Buti: the budgetary objectives of future programmes should not be set as a percentage of GDP, but rather in the form of limits on nominal public expenditure as they are targets Page 4 of 12 controllable by fiscal policy makers and therefore allow a real assessment of the results achieved and the consequent accountability for failures. Also in the chapter on the eve of the post-troika period, it is important to keep in mind the degree of access of the sovereign issuer to the financial markets. If we do not restore access to markets in a credible and sustained way over time, on the day we conclude the programme we will start a very painful process. For this reason, the issues of 5- and 10-Portuguese-year Treasury bonds, respectively in January and May, are relevant milestones. They were very important to measure the "temperature" of the market and to create a process of progressive credibility of portuguese public debt. It should be in mind that even after balancing public accounts, we will continue to depend on financial markets, given the substantial need for refinancing already contracted public debt (Figures 2 and 3). That is, we will continue to need financial markets to be available to renew the financing of our debt. To this end, investors need to be comfortable with the level of public debt, its path of evolution and the consistency and credibility of the budgetary process. In short: creditors have to consider that our debt is affordable, that our budgetary policy allows us to accommodate their service, that their reduction is consistent in the medium term and that political actors ensure that the obligations that result from it are complied with. In the current state of public finances, the margin we have and with which we can play is at the pace of adjustment of public debt. This means that, in a context of return to economic growth, meeting the medium-term commitments under the Fiscal Compact would lead to a sustainability trajectory in Portuguese public debt in the medium-long term. My preference goes to a smoother debt adjustment path, compatible with a parallel reduction in the tax burden. Figure 5 presents a scenario of a gradual reduction in the tax burden over time resulting from an effort to freeze nominal expenditure, within a framework of strict compliance with budgetary commitments. This scenario would induce a slower reduction in public debt, but on a sustainable trajectory, having the advantage of allowing the reduction of the tax burden. As it is public, I have argued that we need to share the "bonus" that will result from economic growth between the decline in public debt and the reduction of taxation. Debt reduction is essential to credibility with our position with financial markets and thereby ensure refinancing. On the other hand, reducing the tax burden is very important to unlock the growth potential and absorb the Page 7 of 12 1998 2000 2002 2004 2006 2008 2010 2012 2014 2016 2018 2020 2022 2024 2026 2028 2030 2032 2034 2036 2038 2040 structural unemployment of the Portuguese economy. It would be good if we reached a broad political consensus, accompanied by a broad consensus between the social partners, in which it was accepted that the future economic growth bonus would be used to reduce public debt and taxation. To this end, one option would be to reach a commitment to maintain the level of nominal public expenditure constant from 2015 on, which means a decrease in real terms equivalent to the inflation rate that is recorded in that period. The post-Program period The challenges that arise in the period following the end of the Economic and Financial Assistance Programme are not less than those of the Programme period. In particular, we need to be able to answer the questions: How to ensure that the return to financial markets is not reversed? How can we ensure the sustained and balanced economic growth of the Portuguese economy in the euro area? The answers to these questions require, as mentioned by the President of the Republic and Marco Buti, that certain conditions be ensured, both internally and externally (Figure 6). Figure 6 Conditions for a successful exit from the Program POST-ECONOMIC AND FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAMME How to ensure that Portugal's return to the markets is not reversed? Countercyclical fiscal policy?  Break banks-sovereign bank ing union link Change in financial regulation  Accommodative monetary conditions  Promote credit to SMEs  Deepen the internal market  Greater ambition reforms Structural CONTINUATION OF ADJUSTMENT  Consolidation of public accounts Multiannual budgetary framework Capacity creation on AP  Profitability banking system Reducing operating costs Dealing with "legacy" assets  Adjustment balance sheets private sector NF Strengthening financial autonomy of companies  Dealing with structural unemployment Social support network; Requalification  Promote potential growth Tax reform; national innovation system, product market competition; functioning justice; and so on NEW "SOCIAL CONTRACT" New institutional framework that fosters behaviour compatible with preservation of nominal stability / competitiveness by  Political actors / public sector Reform of the budget process Public Finance Council Reform governance model AP  Social partners Income sharing mechanisms SOCIAL AND POLITICAL CONSENSUS MUTUAL TRUST BETWEEN MEMBER STATES Based on the restrictions / limits on economic policy Integrate individual perspectives into a whole view (positive sum game logic) Short-medium term Medium-long term Page 9 of 12 Internally, and in the short term, it is necessary to continue with the process of adjusting the Portuguese economy. This means, in particular, continuing with the consolidation of public accounts, improving the profitability of the banking system, continuing with the adjustment of the balance sheet of businesses and households, creating a social safety net for the long-term unemployed and creating conditions that favour the increase in the potential product of the Portuguese economy. In a broader time horizon, it is essential to establish a new institutional framework, based on a broad consensus, which fosters behaviour compatible with the preservation of fundamental macroeconomic balances and the competitiveness of the economy. In this context, a first aspect to be taken into account is that of social cohesion. The ongoing sectoral recomposition in the Portuguese economy suggests that unemployment rates should remain high over a prolonged period of time. Safeguarding social cohesion is crucial if we are to manage the unemployment situation in a way that is compatible with its structural nature. In fact, a mechanical exercise conducted at Banco de Portugal shows that an annual growth in external demand of 8 percent by 2020 would have a cumulative impact of 7 p.p. on reducing the unemployment rate (to about 11 percent), which is worth noting that it is not on the demand side that solves the problem of our unemployment. We must be able to free up and generate entrepreneurial capacity, attract foreign direct investment and increase the extent of our productive fabric. At the same time, it is necessary to set up mechanisms to support the requalification of the long-term unemployed to support their employability. In addition to social cohesion, there are still two other conditions that are important to me. The first is the creation of a political consensus on the degrees of autonomy of Portuguese economic policy. This political consensus does not mean unanimity, it means recognition of the limits of economic policy and circumscribing political discussion to the limits resulting from our restriction of external funding and our public indebtedness. The second condition is consensus among social partners. We need to enrich the dialogue between the social partners in order to ensure realistic negotiation on income distribution, i.e. taking into account the productivity gains of the economy. The experiences of countries such as Belgium or Finland are inspiring to this end. These countries have in place systems that, in situations that jeopardise competitiveness, make wage negotiation subject to the imperative of preserving competitiveness and employment. In parallel, it is necessary to create external conditions that support our adjustment. These external conditions require the solidarity of our European partners, which Page 10 of 12 it is only possible if on our side there is a sense of responsibility and ability to respect our commitments. The key word of this whole process is "trust". The creation of the internal conditions I mentioned above are important to strengthen our partners' confidence in fulfilling our obligations over time and to achieve their solidarity. With regard to the short-term external conditions for a successful exit from the adjustment programme, I believe that it is essential that European mechanisms are available to deal with contingent situations. In order to deal with possible situations of excessive volatility of financial markets and to prevent investors from departing from Portuguese debt, it is imperative to operationalise european intervention mechanisms in the primary and secondary market for public debt, which presupposes, in return, the adoption of a Precautionary Programme. A Precautionary Programme will act as an instrument for enhancing the credibility of the macroeconomic adjustment process in the period immediately following the end of the Programme. The conditionality associated with it is, on the one hand, the counterpart of the solidarity of our European partners and, on the other hand, a decisive element in consolidating market confidence in the country's economic policies. In terms of medium-term conditions, it is very important that the European Union implements mechanisms for coordinating economic policies and is to move towards the creation of a cooperative process of growth at European level. In this context, European countries with favourable economic situations should use the margin they have to expand their domestic demand, contributing to a more balanced and sustainable adjustment of the whole. The creation of the Banking Union is a key pillar for solving the problem of financial fragmentation in the euro area and for cutting the link between sovereign risk and bank risk today. This is a very important step in strengthening competitiveness because it will allow identical companies, in terms of profitability and risk, to have similar financing conditions, regardless of geographical location. In addition, structural reforms should be carried out to boost potential product growth at European level (e.g. deregulation of product markets and tax system reforms). All in all:  For a successful adjustment of the Portuguese economy and to ensure its prosperity in the framework of monetary union, it is necessary to meet certain internal and external conditions. The demonstration that internal conditions are created is what will drag and reinforce the creation of external conditions. Page 11 of 12  At the level of internal conditions it is essential to ensure social cohesion and to reach consensus between social partners and a broad consensus among political actors.  The necessary political consensus is not aimed at the policies to be implemented but only the limits and restrictions that are required for their definition and implementation (as I have said, although we may have different ideas on how to furthest the room space, we must recognize that the walls of the room constitute our limit and our restriction; in economic policy the walls of the exercise are the external restrictions that arise to any country). Thank you very much. Page 12 of 12

O ajustamento oramental, apesar de ter ficado aqum do que tinha sido inicialmente programado,  muito substancial. Contudo, o processo de consolidao oramental foi mais lento do que o esperado e  necessrio assegurar a sua sustentabilidade com medidas estruturais de corte de despesa pblica. Esta situao exige a implementao de uma rede de segurana que salvaguarde a coeso social e que permita a requalificao dos desempregados de longa durao e evite a sua passagem  inatividade. A dvida pblica atingiu nveis muito elevados e est ainda a crescer.  imperativo que a sua evoluo garanta uma trajetria sustentvel. Esta constitui a principal restrio da poltica econmica no futuro. Gostaria aqui de chamar a ateno para um ponto que considero muito importante e que merece uma reflexo particular. Como foi salientado na interveno pelo Marco Buti, o nosso programa de ajustamento foi executado de forma rigorosa. Apesar disso, criou-se na populao portuguesa, nos agentes sociais e nos agentes polticos a perceo de fracasso, designadamente a perceo de que falhmos as metas do programa. Esta perceo no  correta. Por isso, considero que  no s necessrio como importante desmistificar tal ideia, salientando que:  em primeiro lugar, a evoluo econmica internacional foi muito mais desfavorvel do que o inicialmente previsto, o que teve consequncias muito negativas nas exportaes, no investimento, na atividade econmica e, consequentemente, nas receitas e despesas oramentais e na dvida pblica. O acrscimo de incerteza para os agentes econmicos que resultou do prolongamento da fraqueza do enquadramento externo da economia portuguesa e, em particular, da simultaneidade dos processos de consolidao oramental em curso nessas mesmas economias, levou os agentes econmicos a anteverem uma maior queda do rendimento permanente. Como consequncia, o impacto das medidas de consolidao oramental no PIB - os multiplicadores - foi subestimado. A conjugao destas duas ordens de fatores adversos com a fixao das metas do Programa em percentagem do PIB determinou uma necessidade de reviso das metas, sob pena de se desencadear e alimentar um ciclo vicioso entre consolidao oramental e evoluo da atividade econmica. Este facto, justifica que se repense a configurao das metas dos programas de ajustamento de forma a evitar o efeito de regresso da evoluo do PIB sobre o cumprimento das metas oramentais - via receitas fiscais e despesas sociais - e sobre as metas da dvida - via receitas fiscais, despesas sociais e "efeito denominador". Esta  uma mensagem que dirijo em particular ao Marco Buti: os objetivos oramentais de programas futuros no devem ser fixados em percentagem do PIB, mas antes sob a forma de limites  despesa pblica nominal dado que so metas Pgina 4 de 12 controlveis pelos decisores de poltica oramental e, por isso, permitem uma real avaliao dos resultados alcanados e a consequente responsabilizao pelos fracassos. Ainda no captulo da vspera do perodo ps-troika, importa ter presente o grau de acesso do emissor soberano aos mercados financeiros. Se no restabelecermos ao longo do tempo o acesso aos mercados de forma credvel e sustentada, no dia em que concluirmos o programa iniciaremos um processo muito penoso. Por esta razo, as emisses de obrigaes do Tesouro portugus a 5 e 10 anos, respetivamente em Janeiro e Maio, constituem marcos relevantes. Foram muito importantes para aferir a temperatura do mercado e para criar um processo de credibilizao progressiva da dvida pblica portuguesa. Para tal,  necessrio que os investidores se sintam confortveis com o nvel da dvida pblica, com a sua trajetria de evoluo e com a consistncia e credibilidade do processo oramental. Em suma: os credores tm que considerar que a nossa dvida  comportvel, que a nossa poltica oramental permite acomodar o respetivo servio, que a sua reduo  consistente a mdio prazo e que os agentes polticos garantem o cumprimento das obrigaes que dela resultam. O perodo ps-Programa Os desafios que se colocam o perodo posterior ao final do Programa de Assistncia Econmica e Financeira no so menores do que os do perodo do Programa. Em particular temos de saber responder s questes: Como assegurar que o retorno aos mercados financeiros no  revertido? Como assegurar o crescimento econmico sustentado e equilibrado da economia portuguesa na rea do euro? As respostas a estas questes exigem, como referido pelo Senhor Presidente da Repblica e pelo Marco Buti, que sejam asseguradas determinadas condies, quer no plano interno quer o plano externo (Figura 6). Isto significa, nomeadamente, continuar com a consolidao das contas pblicas, melhorar a rendibilidade do sistema bancrio, prosseguir com o ajustamento do balano das empresas e das famlias, criar uma rede de segurana social para os desempregados de longa durao e criar condies que favoream o aumento do produto potencial da economia portuguesa. Num horizonte temporal mais alargado,  essencial estabelecer um novo quadro institucional, baseado num consenso alargado, que fomente comportamento compatveis com a preservao dos equilbrios macroeconmicos fundamentais e da competitiva da economia. Neste contexto, um primeiro aspeto a ter em considerao  o da coeso social. A recomposio setorial em curso na economia portuguesa sugere que as taxas de desemprego devero permanecer elevadas durante um perodo prolongado de tempo. A salvaguarda da coeso social  crucial para conseguirmos gerir a situao do desemprego de forma compatvel com a sua natureza estrutural. De facto, um exerccio mecnico conduzido no Banco de Portugal mostra que um crescimento anual da procura externa de 8 por cento at 2020 teria um impacto acumulado de 7 p.p. na reduo da taxa de desemprego (para cerca de 11 por cento), o que vale por dizer que no  pelo lado da procura que se resolve o problema do nosso desemprego. Temos de ser capazes de libertar e gerar capacidade empreendedora, atrair investimento direto estrangeiro e aumentar a extenso do nosso tecido produtivo. Paralelamente  necessrio criar mecanismos de apoio  requalificao dos desempregados de longo prazo para apoiar a sua empregabilidade. Alm da coeso social, h ainda duas outras condies que para mim so importantes. A primeira consiste na criao de um consenso poltico sobre os graus de autonomia da poltica econmica portuguesa. Este consenso poltico no significa unanimidade, significa reconhecimento dos limites da poltica econmica e circunscrio da discusso poltica aos limites que resultam da nossa restrio de financiamento externo e do nosso endividamento pblico. A segunda condio  o consenso entre parceiros sociais. Temos de enriquecer o dilogo entre parceiros sociais, de forma a garantir uma negociao realista sobre a distribuio do rendimento, isto  que tenha em conta os ganhos de produtividade da economia. As experincias de pases como a Blgica ou a Finlndia so inspiradoras para este efeito. Estes pases tm em prtica sistemas que, em situaes que pem em risco a competitividade, subordinam a negociao salarial ao imperativo da preservao da competitividade e do emprego. Em paralelo,  preciso criar condies externas que suportem o nosso ajustamento. Essas condies externas exigem a solidariedade dos nossos parceiros europeus, o que Pgina 10 de 12 s  possvel se do nosso lado existir sentido de responsabilidade e capacidade para respeitar os nossos compromissos. A palavra-chave de todo este processo  confiana. A criao das condies internas que acima referi so importantes para reforar a confiana dos nossos parceiros no cumprimento das nossas obrigaes ao longo do tempo e conseguir a sua solidariedade. No que se refere s condies externas de curto prazo para uma sada bem-sucedida do programa de ajustamento, considero que  essencial que estejam disponveis mecanismos europeus que permitam fazer face a situaes contingentes. Para lidar com eventuais situaes de volatilidade excessiva dos mercados financeiros e evitar que, em consequncia destes, os investidores se afastem da dvida portuguesa,  imperioso operacionalizar os mecanismos europeus de interveno no mercado primrio e secundrio da dvida pblica, o que pressupe, como contrapartida, a adoo de um Programa Cautelar. Um Programa Cautelar funcionar como um instrumento de reforo da credibilidade do processo de ajustamento macroeconmico no perodo imediatamente a seguir ao final do Programa. A condicionalidade que lhe est associada , por um lado, a contrapartida da solidariedade dos nossos parceiros europeus e, por outro, um elemento determinante da consolidao da confiana dos mercados nas polticas econmicas do pas. Em termos de condies de mdio prazo,  muito importante que a Unio Europeia ponha em prtica os mecanismos de coordenao das polticas econmicas e que se oriente para a criao de um processo cooperativo de crescimento  escala europeia. Neste contexto, os pases europeus com situaes econmicas favorveis, devem usar a margem que tm para expandir a sua procura interna, contribuindo para um ajustamento mais equilibrado e sustentvel do todo. A criao da Unio Bancria  um pilar fundamental para resolver o problema da fragmentao financeira na rea do euro e para cortar a ligao que hoje se regista entre o risco soberano e o risco dos bancos. Trata-se de um passo muito importante no reforo da competitividade porque permitir que empresas idnticas, em termos de rendibilidade e de risco, passem a dispor de condies de financiamento semelhantes, independentemente da localizao geogrfica. Adicionalmente, devero ser levadas a cabo reformas estruturais que favoream o aumento do crescimento do produto potencial a nvel europeu (por exemplo, desregulamentao dos mercados de produto e reformas do sistemas fiscais). Em suma:  Para um ajustamento bem sucedido da economia portuguesa e para assegurar a sua prosperidade no quadro da unio monetria  necessrio que se verifiquem determinadas condies internas e externas. A demonstrao de que esto criadas as condies internas  o que vai arrastar e reforar a criao das condies externas. Pgina 11 de 12  Ao nvel das condies internas  essencial garantir a coeso social e alcanar um consenso entre parceiros sociais e um consenso alargado entre agentes polticos.  O consenso poltico necessrio no visa as polticas a implementar mas to s os limites e as restries que se impem  respetiva definio e implementao (como tenho dito, embora possamos ter ideias diferentes sobre o modo de mobilar o espao da sala, temos de reconhecer que as paredes da sala constituem o nosso limite e a nossa restrio; na poltica econmica as paredes do exerccio so as restries externas que se colocam a qualquer pas).
