Title: Speech of the Governor at the opening of the 15th Lisbon Meeting with the Delegations of portuguese and Timor-leste african countries to the IMF/BM Annual Assembly
text: INTERVENTION OF THE GOVERNOR OF BANCO DE PORTUGAL AT THE OPENING OF THE 15th MEETING OF CENTRAL BANKS OF THE PALOP, PORTUGAL AND TIMOR-LESTE September 20, 2005 Ambassadors, Governors, ladies and gentlemen I begin by thanking everyone for their presence at this 15th Meeting of Central Banks of PALOP, Portugal and Timor-Leste. We thus continue a tradition that has served to strengthen ties of cooperation between our institutions. The cooperation actions developed throughout 2005 mainly reflect the consolidation of major reforms in the central banks of the PALOP and Timor-Leste, in particular with regard to the development of monetary and foreign exchange markets and the strengthening of the banking system's supervisory activity. Bilateral cooperation during the current year covered virtually all the main areas of activity of a central bank, in particular those referring to the organisation and functioning of the interbank money market, the payment system, statistics or accounting. However, this year there has been a growing weight of regional or multilateral actions, i.e. seminars and round tables that brought together technicians from all our Central Banks in meetings that were good examples of an il exchange of experiences. I would also like to point out the importance of the 2nd Meeting of Governors of the Central Banks of the CPLP, held in Maputo on the occasion of the 30th Anniversary of the Bank of Mozambique and which addressed issues related to the application of international accounting standards and the challenges of regional integration. It is also worth mentioning the development of two exercises in support of the International Monetary Fund's monitoring activity on the dissemination of statistical data, with a view to increasing transparency and the adoption of universal standards of good conduct. During 2006 we will continue the cooperation efforts that have been developed in the areas already mentioned, through technical misses, training internships or thematic seminars. 2. As usual, this Lisbon Meeting takes place on the eve of the annual meeting of the IMF and the World Bank, which means that at the working meeting of our delegations, yesterday, the problems that are on the international agenda will be analyzed. This year attention focuses on the need for a strategic review of IMF action, the problems of the least developed countries and the achievement of the Millennium Goals and, finally, the international ecological situation and the risks resulting from major international macro-ecological imbalances. After the strong expansion in 2004 of more than 5%, the world economy has evolved favorably this year, although with a slight reduction in the growth rate. On the other hand, inflation also appears to be contained, despite the latest risks, medium-term interest rates are low and the financial environment calm, given the improvement in the balance sheet situation of financial and non-financial companies. Financial stability has continued to be ensured and even strengthened as a result of the institutions' good performance in risk management and the strengthening of the supervisory and regulatory framework. In general, financial conditions remain favourable, with abundant liquidity, minute risk premiums and low-slope yield curves. For its part, private financial flows to emerging countries expanded in 2004 as a result of foreign direct investment, and this development continued this year, although mitigated in net terms by the reverse effect resulting from the recycling of the surpluses of the petreo-producing countries. In normal conditions, growth in the world economy is expected to remain favourable in the first year, and yet we know how enormous risk factors persist that appear to be reflected with concern in all published analyses of the international situation. The first risk relates to the sharp rise in petreo prices, which reached more than 100% in the first 18 months. Figures of this size were supposed until recently to have significant consequences for inflation and growth prospects. When comeming, however, the current situation with the previous oil shocks, two major differences are identified: on the one hand, the gains in efficiency and energy conservation have reduced the energy content of production and, moreover, this time the evolution of prices reflects not a shock of supply, but rather a dynamism of energy demand that is associated with a period of strong growth of the world economy. Even though, of course, the increase in the cost of energy has contributed to a slight reduction in growth, this has not prevented the recording of a significant expansion of econic activity in this period. The low effect on other prices has resulted from the positive consequences of globalisation on the containment and even reduction of various industrial prices and the effects of the credibility of monetary policies in achieving low inflation expectations. However, part of these results is due to the fact that eco-agents have so far interpreted the rise in crude oil prices as temporary, which has contributed to postponing price adjustments and reductions in consumption of other goods and services. The most recent tensions on inflation in several countries show that we cannot be complacent based so much on what has been so far in the reactions to rising oil prices. Behaviour may change if prices remain at high levels or if they re-decline. This poses delicate problems to the management of monetary policy, which cannot allow the generalisation of second-order effects of petreo prices on other costs and prices, and is not to be allowed to lose control over inflation expectations. The importance of this control is manifested in the fact that it is one of the key factors in explaining the current low level of medium-term interest rates. The ability of monetary policy to maintain sufficient room for manoeuvre to promote growth without compromising the objective of price stability depends crucially on maintaining credibility with economic actors, in the sense that it manages to maintain inflation at the levels set as an objective in the long term. Recent pressures on inflation levels in several countries thus create increasing problems with their monetary policies and pose the threat of simultaneously giving rise to inflationary pressures and recessionary trends. Monetary policy responses must be prudent, without compromising, however, firmly control of future inflation expectations. While short-term developments in petreo prices are the most immediate threat to global economic growth, the potentially most disturbing problems stem from the strong external imbalances in various parts of the world. The significant Us external deficit and the accumulation of external reserves by Asian countries indicate difficult-to-be-sustainable situations in the long term and their correction can trigger significant disruption snares in the international economic and financial situation. While it is true that there is a broad consensus on the long-term unsustainability of such imbalances, the same is not the case for their causes or the mechanisms for their correction. There is also consensus on the consequences of these differences between savings and investment on the scale currently verified, with the US absorbing around 75% of the world's savings annually. In fact, these effects are reflected in distortions in exchange rates, artificially maintained by massive interventions in the foreign exchange market, which creates excess liquidity and low interest rates. This has fueled the price of financial and real estate assets, which in turn has contributed to stimulating consumption and reducing savings in the United States. The bubble in the asset market has successively passed from actions to bonds and, finally, to real estate, which, according to Robert Shiller, the inventor of the term 'irrational exuberance', may turn out to be 'the biggest bubble in American history'. As the recent period shows, the current situation can still remain for a considerable period. This reality has allowed us to confer some verisiion to several relatively benign interpretations of the conjuncture we are going through. The first refers to the theory that we would be facing a new Bretton-Woods fixed exchange regime now reduced to the Pacific area, spontaneously formed by the interests of the parties and, consequently, stable for many years. Asian countries, and China in particular, would exchange financial losses from interventions to maintain a competitive exchange rate by building a more modern and job-creating production apparatus as a result of strong ecogrowth. The United States would thus find the financing of its deficits and its excess expenditure on domestic product. The analogies that theory tries to establish with what happened between Europe and the United States after the Second World War do not entirely reap and powerful ecological and geopolitical reasons undermine the possibility of such a regime being stable in the long term. The second relatively benign view of the current imbalances points to the existence of a spontaneous excess of savings on investment in the rest of the world and its application in American assets, for security reasons or greater return. This influx of capital would sustain the giving in high values, which would explain, in turn, the current account deficit. Moreover, in view of the behaviour of the private sector, the US budget deficit, easily financed from abroad, would have become the counterpoint of the external deficit and a way of sustaining global demand and growth. Given the depth and efficiency of international financial markets that globalisation has made possible, the financing of strong deficits has become easy and their correction could be quite gradual. The problems with this vision stem mainly from the fact that in the last two years the financing of the American balance is ensured mainly by foreign central banks and not as a result of the external private sector putting their savings in the United States. Private flows of direct investment and portfolio investment have even been negative. On the other hand, if we look at the evolution of savings and investment, we see that since the 1970s the savings rate and the investment rate have decreased simultaneously in the world economy. In particular, instead of talking about excess savings one can speak before insufficient investment, especially since the financial crises of 1997-98. This means that an important part of the explanation for the current situation has to be found in the large reduction in savings, private and public, in the United States, which means that the correction of current imbalances necessarily has to be the increase in American savings. In fact, it would not be sufficient for the solution to result primarily from exchange rate adjustments, particularly between the United States and Asian countries. Let us not forget, for example, that of the worsening us current deficit between 1997 and 2004, of 529 million dares, only 7% is explained by the relationship with China. On the other hand, putting the tica in the exchange rate mechanism could contribute to making more likely an abrupt correction scenario that would be quite disruptive to the international economy. It is true that some recent studies published by the Federal Reserve point to the relatively benign nature that significant exchange rate adjustments between developed countries have had in the early 20s. This would be particularly true of the fact that there have been no sensitive interest rate rises accompanying currency depreciation, thus avoiding recessionary consequences and crises in the asset markets. 1 However, it should be stressed that monetary policy can certainly influence short-term rates, but the present circumstances are different from other previous esdiities, since dependence on domestic capital markets of foreign investors is greater. It is therefore necessary to be prudent and avoid any developments that could jeopardise a gradual correction in the foreign exchange markets. While the resolution of imbalances requires demand-shifting behaviour stemming from exchange rate adjustments, it is, however, unquestionable that any resolution of the problem has to be addressed by reductions in domestic spending in countries with the largest external deficits. It is clear that the effects and reactions to Hurricane Katrina have made it more difficult, at least in the short term, to absorb existing imbalances. However, it is also clear that the longer the inevitable adjustments are postponed, the greater the risks of uncontrolled the situation. It is no wonder, therefore, that more recently international institutions and leading experts in the international economy have called for effective coordinated action by the main countries to tackle this problem. In addition to the OECD and imf, the Institute of International Finance, which is associated with large private financial institutions, also called for joint action by world leaders to reduce "growing worrying" global imbalances. Overcoming this phase of macro-econic imbalances can be well achieved if there is 1 Joseph Gagnon (2005),  Currency crashes and bond yields in industrial countries, Federal Reserve Board immediate and coordinated action between the main countries. In addition to the adjustment in the US economy, it is important to recover investment in emerging countries (excluding China here), greater exchange rate flexibility in Asian countries and an effective recovery in growth in Japan and Europe. Europe has had difficulty fulfilling its part of this programme. After the recovery in the second half of last year, growth has weakened again this year as a result of the oil shock, political uncertainties and the prudence of consumers and businesses that has halted the expansion of domestic demand. The structural reforms tested to address the problems arising from the challenges of competitiveness and population ageing seem to have a short-term negative effect on the expectations of eco-actors and affect the recovery of domestic expenditure. However, the decline of the working-age population in the raw decades makes it inevitable to increase the number of working hours throughout life, in addition to requiring productivity increases that enable the sustainability of the European social model. 3. The European situation is not entirely in favour of a significant recoveryin the Portuguese economy. Despite the increased risks arising from the evolution of petreo prices, we have not yet changed the forecast that the Bank published in July of growth of 0.5% this year and 1.2% in the first year. Since 2001 we have been going through a period of weak econational growth which is explained by a number of factors First, external shocks, such as the drop in demand directed at the Portuguese economy in 2001 and 2002, the structural change in the conditions of international competition associated with the enlargement of the European Union and the globalisation and the evolution of the price of the oil, which affects one country that is more dependent on this form of energy than most European countries. The second factor refers to the prciclique budgetary policy made necessary after the outbreak of an unsustainable deficit. Finally, we have the effect of the inevitable slowdown in domestic demand as a result of the previous excessive expansion, based on increasing indebtedness. We cannot, in fact, continue an evolution that has passed the country from an international creditor situation of around 7,000 million euros in 1996 to an external debt position of more than 55,000 million at the end of last year. We must not burden future generations of Portuguese. The current phase of weak domestic expenditure growth has the effect of containing debt expansion and pressuring companies to restructure, increasing productivity and reorienting their production destinations on a larger scale to foreign markets. The possibility of the economy resuming a path of significant eco-growth depends essentially on the ability of companies to react appropriately to the challenges of competition in the liberalised framework in which we move. The best contribution that the policies plicas can make at this stage is to put order in the accounts and reduce bureaucracy, to free the strength of the initiative of the economic agents who can not count on more financial aid from the State. As in other difficult situations that the Portuguese economy has experienced in the past, I am sure that eco-actors will be able to react appropriately. We are not facing a permanent crisis in our economy, which could, moreover, come out stronger at the end of a phase of adjustment to the new conditions of international framework in which it has to work. The greater the determination and rigour of the pblica action and the dynamism of the companies, the faster we will overcome the current phase of restructuring. Hesitations or excessive gradualism would create uncertainty and remove effectiveness from the ecological policy, whose strategic meaning must be that of financial realism and that of supporting everything that decisively alters the medium-term comparative advantages of Portuguese companies. 4. Growth prospects in sub-Saharan Africa have recently proved more favourable. After a steady growth of 5.3% in 2004, it is estimated some attenuation of the pace of activity this year, but a further acceleration in 2006. The dynamism of the region is based on the robustness of external demand, progress in macro-econic stability and structural reforms in large countries. Petreo exporting countries continue to benefit from price increases, but unlike 2004, prices for other primary goods evolved negatively in 2005, which combined with higher energy import costs has hurt many countries in this area. Success in the Doha Agenda negotiations, together with increased support for the development of the trade capacity of the countries in this region, is important to promote Africa's integration into world markets. However, the immediate benefits of the liberalisation process may be limited. In a 2003 UNCTAD study, it was concluded that a generalised 50% cut in these customs tariffs on agricultural goods would have an almost nil effect in terms of welfare for sub-Saharan Africa, as losses in terms of exchange would absorb gains from increased access to export markets. Other studies point to moderate gains (from 0.5 to 1.3% of GDP), depending on the specific characteristics that trade liberalisation will assume. In fact, it should be worth noting that many of these African countries, despite being exporters of agricultural products, are, however, net importers of food agricultural goods, in many cases from the rich countries of the north. It follows that a liberalisation process eliminating the export subsidy policy of certain European and American products could lead to an increase in the international prices of these goods and harm their importers. Of course, for African countries exporting products that compete with those heavily subsidized by developed countries, the end of these subsidies and tariff disarmament on imports would significantly benefit African exporters. The overall effect would be positive, but despite the medium and long-term advantages of further integration of all the least developed countries into the world economy, the benefits are far from being considered sufficient for the millennium goals to be achieved within the predicted time horizon. Effective development aid policies are therefore indispensable, with increased transfers for the benefit of developing countries. As regards external aid to achieve the Millennium Goals, estimates range from an additional amount, compared to present levels, from US50,000 million (value calculated by the UN High-Panel on Financing for Development) to 75,000 million (estimated by the UN Millennium Project). It is worth taking into account that these neros - despite their high size in absolute terms - are entirely within the commitments made by the international community, since in Monterrey these same countries have committed themselves to reaching by 2015 the minimum threshold of 0.7% of their income in international aid. It should be stressed that the European Union has committed itself at the Brussels European Council in June this year to effectively meet the collective target of 0.7% of GDP by 2015, with an intermediate target of 0.56% in 2010. Assuming that the transfer of financial resources is one of the key elements in the pursuit of the Millennium Goals, one of the ways in which this transfer is to achieve this is the cancellation of the debt of the poorest countries, since the resources thus freed up can be effectively used in the fight against poverty and the promotion of development. To that extent, a proposal for the full cancellation of the multilateral debt of the highly indebted countries was approved at the last G-8 meeting in Gleneagles, which will be presented at the annual world bank and international monetary fund. This proposal provides for a differentiated debt treatment to the IMF (which would be absorbed by the institution's own resources), IDA and the African Development Fund. For this cancellation to result in effectively additional aid resources for the least developed countries, it is necessary that their funding be provided by the developments. In addition, many other technical aspects remain to be addressed so that the measures to be implemented correspond to what was announced at the end of the G-8 summit as corresponding to a historic milestone in the international development aid process. Let us hope that, during the Bretton-Woods Annual Meeting of Institutions this week, all these problems will find a solution. The Millennium Goals now seem difficult to achieve, but the effort and resources mobilised to meet them are, in addition to a moral requirement, the expression of interest well understood by developed countries. In an increasingly globalised and interdependent world, stability and security depend not only on overcoming eco-financial imbalances, but also on social imbalances that contradict peoples' sense of justice. Lisbon, 20 September 2005
text_original: INTERVENO DO GOVERNADOR DO BANCO DE PORTUGAL NA ABERTURA DO 15 ENCONTRO DE BANCOS CENTRAIS DOS PALOP, DE PORTUGAL E DE TIMOR-LESTE 20 de Setembro de 2005 Senhores Embaixadores Senhores Governadores Minhas Senhoras e meus Senhores Comeo por agradecer a presena de todos neste 15 Encontro de Bancos Centrais dos PALOP, de Portugal e de Timor-Leste. Continuamos assim uma tradio que tem servido para reforar laos de cooperao entre as nossas instituis. As acs de cooperao desenvolvidas ao longo de 2005 reflectem essencialmente a consolidao de importantes reformas nos bancos centrais dos PALOP e de Timor-Leste, nomeadamente no que se refere ao desenvolvimento dos mercados monetrios e cambiais e ao reforo da actividade de superviso do sistema bancrio. A cooperao bilateral durante o ano em curso abrangeu praticamente todas as reas principais de actividade de um banco central, em particular as que se referem  organizao e funcionamento do mercado monetrio interbancrio, ao sistema de pagamentos, s estatsticas ou  contabilidade. No entanto, verificou-se neste ano um peso tendencialmente crescente das acs regionais ou multilaterais, ou seja, de Seminrios e mesas redondas que reuniram tcnicos de todos os nossos Bancos Centrais em encontros que constituram bons exemplos de uma il troca de experincias. Quero tambm assinalar a importncia de que se revestiu o 2 Encontro de Governadores dos Bancos Centrais da CPLP, realizado na cidade de Maputo por ocasio do 30 Aniversrio do Banco de Moambique e que abordou temas relacionados com a aplicao das Normas Internacionais de Contabilidade e com os desafios da Integrao Regional.  igualmente de destacar o desenvolvimento de dois exerccios de apoio  actividade de monitorizao do Fundo Monetrio Internacional em matria de disseminao de dados estatsticos, com vista ao aumento de transparncia e da adopo de cigos e padrs universais de boa conduta. Durante 2006 continuaremos os esforos de cooperao que tm sido desenvolvidos nas reas j referidas, atravs de misses tcnicas, estgios de formao ou seminrios temticos. 2. Como habitualmente, este Encontro de Lisboa ocorre nas vsperas da reunio anual do FMI e do Banco Mundial, o que proporciona que na reunio de trabalho das nossas Delegas, ontem ocorrida, se analisem os problemas que constam neste momento da agenda internacional. Este ano as atenes concentram-se na necessidade de reviso estratgica da aco do FMI, nos problemas dos pases menos desenvolvidos e no cumprimento dos Objectivos do Milnio e, finalmente, na situao econica internacional e nos riscos resultantes dos grandes desequilbrios macroeconicos internacionais. Ap a forte expanso verificada em 2004, de mais de 5%, a economia mundial tem evoludo de forma favorvel este ano, embora com ligeira reduo da taxa de crescimento. Por outro lado, a inflao parece tambm estar contida, apesar dos riscos mais recentes, as taxas de juro de mdio prazo esto baixas e o ambiente financeiro calmo, face  melhoria da situao de balano de empresas financeiras e no financeiras. A estabilidade financeira tem continuado a ser assegurada e mesmo reforada em resultado do bom desempenho das instituis na gesto do risco e do reforo do enquadramento de superviso e regulao. Em geral, as condis financeiras continuam favorveis, com liquidez abundante, diminutos prmios de risco e curvas de rendimentos com inclinao reduzida. Por seu turno, os fluxos financeiros privados para os pases emergentes expandiram-se em 2004, em resultado fundamentalmente do investimento directo estrangeiro, e esta evoluo prosseguiu no corrente ano, embora atenuada em termos lquidos pelo efeito de sentido inverso resultante da reciclagem dos excedentes dos pases produtores de petreo. Em condis normais,  previsvel que o crescimento da economia mundial continue favorvel no primo ano e, no entanto, sabemos como persistem enormes factores de risco que aparecem reflectidos com preocupao em todas as anlises publicadas sobre a situao internacional. O primeiro risco refere-se  forte subida dos preos do petreo, que atingiu mais de 100% nos timos 18 meses. Valores desta dimenso eram supostos at h pouco tempo provocar consequncias significativas na inflao e nas perspectivas do crescimento. Quando se compara, porm, a actual situao com os anteriores choques petrolferos, identificam-se duas grandes diferenas: por um lado, os ganhos de eficincia e de conservao de energia fizeram diminuir o conteo energtico da produo e, alm disso, desta vez a evoluo dos preos reflecte no um choque de oferta, mas antes um dinamismo da procura de energia que est associado a um perodo de forte crescimento da economia mundial. Mesmo que, naturalmente, o aumento do custo da energia tenha contribudo para uma ligeira reduo do crescimento, isso no impediu o registo de uma significativa expanso da actividade econica neste perodo. O reduzido efeito sobre os restantes preos tem resultado das consequncias positivas da globalizao sobre a conteno e mesmo reduo de diversos preos industriais e dos efeitos da credibilidade das polticas monetrias ao conseguirem fixar baixas expectativas de inflao. No entanto, parte destes resultados deve-se ao facto de os agentes econicos terem at agora interpretado a progresso dos preos do crude como sendo temporria, o que tem contribudo para adiarem ajustamentos de preos e redues de consumo de outros bens e servios. As tenss mais recentes sobre a inflao em diversos pases vem demonstrar que no podemos ser complacentes com base apenas no ocorrido at agora nas reaces  subida dos preos do petrleo. Os comportamentos podero alterar-se se os preos se mantiverem em nveis elevados ou se voltarem a recrudescer. Isto coloca delicados problemas  gesto da poltica monetria, que no pode permitir a generalizao de efeitos de segunda ordem dos preos de petreo sobre outros custos e preos, sob pena de consentir na perda de controlo sobre as expectativas da inflao. A importncia deste controle manifesta-se no facto do mesmo ser um dos factores essenciais para explicar o actual baixo nvel das taxas de juro de mdio prazo. A capacidade da poltica monetria manter uma margem de manobra suficiente para favorecer o crescimento sem comprometer o objectivo da estabilidade dos preos depende crucialmente da manuteno da credibilidade junto dos agentes econmicos, no sentido de que consegue a prazo manter a inflao nos nveis definidos como objectivo. As recentes presses sobre os nveis de inflao em vrios pases criam, assim, problemas crescentes s respectivas polticas monetrias e perfilam a ameaa de originar simultaneamente presss inflacionistas e tendncias recessivas. As respostas da poltica monetria tm de ser prudentes, sem comprometer, no entanto, o firme controlo das expectativas de inflao futura. Embora a evoluo a curto prazo dos preos do petreo seja a ameaa mais imediata ao crescimento econico mundial, os problemas potencialmente mais perturbadores decorrem dos fortes desequilbrios externos que se verificam em diversas zonas do mundo. O significativo dfice externo americano e a acumulao de reservas externas pelos pases asiticos indiciam situaes dificilmente sustentveis a prazo e a sua correco pode desencadear perturbaes significativas na situao econica e financeira internacional. Se  verdade que existe um amplo consenso sobre a insustentabilidade a prazo de tais desequilbrios, j o mesmo se no verifica a propito das suas causas ou dos mecanismos da sua correco.  tambm consensual a anlise das consequncias dessas diferenas entre poupana e investimento na escala actualmente verificada, com os EUA a absorverem anualmente cerca de 75% da poupana mundial. Na verdade, esses efeitos reflectem-se em distors nas taxas de cmbio, artificialmente mantidas por intervens macias no mercado cambial, o que cria excesso de liquidez e taxas de juro baixas. Isso tem alimentado o empolamento do preo dos activos financeiros e imobilirios, o que, por sua vez, tem contribudo para estimular o consumo e reduzir a poupana nos Estados Unidos. A bolha no mercado de activos tem passado sucessivamente das aces para as obrigaes e, finalmente, para o imobilirio, que, de acordo com Robert Shiller, o inventor da expresso exuberncia irracional, pode vir a ser a maior bolha da histia americana. Como o perodo recente demonstra, a actual situao pode manter-se ainda durante um perodo considervel. Esta realidade tem permitido conferir alguma verosimilhana a diversas interpretas relativamente benignas da conjuntura que atravessamos. A primeira refere-se  teoria de que estaramos perante novo regime de Bretton-Woods de cmbios fixos agora reduzido  zona do Pacifico, espontaneamente formado pelo interesse das partes e, consequentemente, estvel para muitos anos. Os pases asiticos, e a China em particular, trocariam as perdas financeiras decorrentes das intervens para manter uma taxa de cmbio competitiva pela construo de um aparelho produtivo mais moderno e criador de empregos em resultado do forte crescimento econico. Os Estados Unidos encontrariam, assim, o financiamento dos seus dfices e do seu excesso de despesa sobre o produto interno. As analogias que a teoria tenta estabelecer com o que se passou entre a Europa e os Estados Unidos a seguir  segunda guerra mundial no colhem inteiramente e poderosas razs econicas e geopolticas minam a possibilidade de um tal regime ser estvel a prazo. A segunda viso relativamente benigna dos actuais desequilbrios aponta para a existncia de um espontneo excesso de poupana sobre o investimento no resto do mundo e a sua aplicao em activos americanos, por razs de segurana ou maior retorno. Este afluxo de capitais sustentaria o dar em valores elevados, que explicariam, por sua vez, o dfice da balana corrente. Alm disso, face ao comportamento do sector privado, o dfice oramental americano, facilmente financiado do exterior, ter-se-ia tornado no contraponto do dfice externo e uma forma de sustentar a procura e o crescimento mundiais. Face  profundidade e eficincia dos mercados financeiros internacionais que a globalizao tornou possveis, o financiamento de fortes dfices tornou-se fcil e a sua correco poderia ser bastante gradual. Os problemas com esta viso decorrem sobretudo do facto de nos timos dois anos o financiamento da balana americana ser assegurado sobretudo por bancos centrais estrangeiros e no em resultado do sector privado externo colocar as suas poupanas nos Estados Unidos. Os fluxos privados de investimento directo e de investimento de carteira tm mesmo sido negativos. Por outro lado, se olharmos para a evoluo da poupana e do investimento, verificamos que desde os anos 70 tm diminudo simultaneamente na economia mundial a taxa de poupana e a taxa de investimento. Em particular, em vez de se falar de excesso de poupana pode-se falar antes de insuficincia de investimento, sobretudo desde as crises financeiras de 1997-98. Isto significa que uma parte importante da explicao para a situao actual tem que se encontrar na grande reduo da poupana, privada e pblica, nos Estados Unidos, o que implica que a correco dos actuais desequilbrios tenha que passar necessariamente pelo aumento da poupana americana. Na verdade, no seria suficiente que a soluo resultasse sobretudo de ajustamentos das taxas de cmbio, nomeadamente entre os Estados Unidos e os pases asiticos. No esqueamos, por exemplo, que do agravamento do dfice corrente americano entre 1997 e 2004, de 529 mil milhs de dares, apenas 7%  explicado pela relao com a China. Por outro lado, colocar a tica no mecanismo das taxas de cmbio poderia contribuir para tornar mais provvel um cenrio de correco abrupta que seria bastante perturbador da economia internacional.  verdade que alguns estudos recentes publicados pela Federal Reserve apontam para o carcter relativamente benigno que ajustamentos significativos das taxas de cmbio entre pases desenvolvidos tiveram nos timos vinte anos. Isso seria particularmente verdadeiro a propito do facto de no se terem verificado subidas sensveis das taxas de juro a acompanhar as depreciaes cambiais, evitando assim consequncias recessivas e crises nos mercados de activos. 1 No entanto, importa sublinhar que a poltica monetria pode certamente influenciar as taxas de curto prazo, mas as presentes circunstncias so diferentes de outros episdios precedentes, uma vez que  maior a dependncia dos mercados de capitais domsticos de investidores estrangeiros. H, pois, que ser prudente e evitar qualquer evoluo que possa comprometer uma correco gradual nos mercados cambiais. Sendo certo que a resoluo dos desequilbrios requer comportamentos de desvio de procura que os ajustamentos cambiais provocam, , porm, inquestionvel que qualquer resoluo do problema tem de passar por redus de despesa interna nos pases com maiores dfices externos.  manifesto que os efeitos e as reacs ao furaco Katrina tornaram mais difcil, pelo menos no curto prazo, a absoro dos desequilbrios existentes. No entanto,  tambm evidente que quanto mais tempo se adiar os inevitveis ajustamentos maiores sero os riscos de descontrole da situao. No admira, por isso, que mais recentemente as instituis internacionais e os grandes especialistas da economia internacional tenham lanado apelos a uma efectiva aco coordenada dos principais pases para fazer face a este problema. Alm da OCDE e do FMI, igualmente o Institute of Internacional Finance, associado a grandes instituies financeiras privadas, apelou  actuao conjunta dos lderes mundiais para reduzirem os crescentemente preocupantes desequilbrios globais. A superao desta fase de desequilbrios macroeconicos poder ser bem conseguida se houver 1 Joseph Gagnon (2005),  Currency crashes and bond yields in industrial countries, Federal Reserve Board uma actuao imediata e coordenada entre os principais pases. Com efeito, para alm do ajustamento na economia americana  importante a recuperao do investimento nos pases emergentes (excluindo aqui a China), maior flexibilidade cambial nos pases asiticos e uma efectiva retoma do crescimento no Japo e na Europa. A Europa tem tido dificuldade em cumprir a sua parte deste programa. Ap a retoma na segunda metade do ano passado, o crescimento voltou a fraquejar este ano, em consequncia do choque petrolfero, das incertezas polticas e da prudncia de consumidores e empresas que tem travado a expanso da procura interna. As reformas estruturais ensaiadas para fazer aos problemas decorrentes dos desafios da competitividade e do envelhecimento populacional parecem provocar efeitos negativos de curto prazo sobre as expectativas dos agentes econicos e afectar a recuperao da despesa interna. No entanto, o declnio da populao em idade de trabalhar nas primas dcadas torna inevitvel aumentar o nmero de horas de trabalho ao longo da vida, para alm de exigir aumentos de produtividade que viabilizem a sustentabilidade do modelo social europeu. 3. A situao europeia no  inteiramente favorvel a uma retoma significativa da economia portuguesa. Apesar dos riscos acrescidos decorrentes da evoluo dos preos do petreo, no altermos ainda a previso que o Banco publicou em Julho de um crescimento de 0,5% este ano e de 1,2% no primo ano. Desde 2001 temos atravessado um perodo de fraco crescimento econico que se explica por um conjunto de vrios factores Em primeiro lugar, choques externos, como a quebra de procura dirigida  economia portuguesa em 2001 e 2002, a alterao estrutural das condies de concorrncia internacional associada ao alargamento da Unio Europeia e  globalizao e a evoluo do preo do petrleo, que afecta mais um pas extremamente dependente dessa forma de energia que a generalidade dos pases europeus. O segundo factor refere-se  poltica oramental prciclica tornada necessria ap a ecloso de um dfice plico insustentvel. Finalmente, temos o efeito da inevitvel desacelerao da procura interna, em consequncia da excessiva expanso anterior, assente num endividamento crescente. No podemos, na verdade, continuar uma evoluo que fez passar o pas de uma situao credora internacional em cerca de 7 mil milhes de euros, em 1996, para uma posio de dvida externa de mais de 55 mil milhs no final do ano passado. No devemos sobrecarregar as futuras geraes de portugueses. A fase actual de dbil crescimento da despesa interna tem o efeito de conter a expanso do endividamento e de pressionar as empresas para se reestruturarem, aumentando a produtividade e reorientando os destinos das suas produs em maior escala para os mercados externos. A possibilidade de a economia retomar um caminho de crescimento econico significativo depende essencialmente da capacidade das empresas reagirem apropriadamente aos desafios da concorrncia no quadro liberalizado em que nos movemos. A melhor contribuio que as polticas plicas podem dar nesta fase  porem ordem nas contas pblicas e diminuir a burocracia, para libertar a fora da iniciativa dos agentes econmicos que no podem contar com mais ajudas financeiras do Estado. Como aconteceu noutras situas difceis que a economia portuguesa atravessou no passado, estou certo de que os agentes econicos sabero reagir adequadamente. No estamos perante uma crise permanente da nossa economia, que poder, alis, sair mais forte no fim de uma fase de ajustamento s novas condies de enquadramento internacional em que tem que funcionar. Quanto maior for a determinao e o rigor da aco pblica e o dinamismo das empresas mais rapidamente superaremos a actual fase de reestruturao. Hesitaes ou excessivo gradualismo scriariam incerteza e retirariam eficcia  poltica econica, cujo sentido estratgico tem de ser o do realismo financeiro e o do apoio a tudo o que altere decisivamente as vantagens comparativas de mdio prazo das empresas portuguesas. 4. As perspectivas de crescimento na frica sub-sahariana tm-se revelado recentemente mais favorveis. Ap um firme crescimento de 5.3% em 2004, estima-se alguma atenuao do ritmo da actividade no corrente ano, mas uma nova acelerao em 2006. O dinamismo da regio assenta na robustez da procura externa, nos progressos na estabilidade macroeconica e nas reformas estruturais verificadas em grande nmero de pases. Os pases exportadores de petreo continuam a beneficiar dos aumentos de preos, mas, contrariamente a 2004, os preos de outros bens primrios evoluram negativamente em 2005, o que conjugado com os maiores custos de importao de energia prejudicou muitos pases desta zona. O sucesso nas negocias da Agenda de Doha, em conjunto com um acrescido apoio para o desenvolvimento da capacidade de comrcio dos pases desta regio,  importante para promover a integrao de frica nos mercados mundiais. No entanto, os benefcios imediatos do processo de liberalizao podero ser limitados. Num estudo da UNCTAD de 2003, concluiu-se que um corte generalizado de 50% nas presentes tarifas aduaneiras aplicveis aos bens agrcolas teria um efeito quase nulo em termos de bem-estar para a frica sub-sahariana, dado que as perdas nos termos de troca absorveriam os ganhos decorrentes do maior acesso a mercados de exportao. Outros estudos apontam para ganhos moderados (de 0.5 a 1.3% do PIB), dependendo das caractersticas especficas que a liberalizao do comrcio venha a assumir. Na verdade, convm ter presente que muitos destes pases africanos, no obstante serem exportadores de produtos agrcolas, so, no entanto, importadores lquidos de bens agrcolas alimentares, em muitos casos provenientes dos pases ricos do norte. Decorre daqui que um processo de liberalizao que elimine a poltica de subsdios  exportao de certos produtos europeus e americanos poderia provocar um aumento dos preos internacionais destes bens e prejudicar os respectivos importadores. Naturalmente que para os pases africanos exportadores de produtos que concorrem com os que so fortemente subsidiados pelos pases desenvolvidos, o fim desses subsdios e o desarmamento pautal nas importas beneficiaria significativamente os exportadores africanos. O efeito global seria positivo, mas apesar das vias vantagens numa perspectiva de mdio e longo prazo de uma maior insero do conjunto dos pases menos desenvolvidos na economia mundial, os benefcios esto longe de se poderem considerar como suficientes para o propito de serem alcanados os Objectivos do Milnio no horizonte temporal previsto. So, por isso, indispensveis polticas eficazes de ajuda ao desenvolvimento, com aumento das transferncias em benefcio dos pases em desenvolvimento. No que se refere  ajuda externa para alcanar os Objectivos do Milnio, as estimativas variam entre um montante adicional, face aos nveis presentes, de 50 mil milhs de dlares (valor calculado pelo UN High-Panel on Financing for Development) a 75 mil milhs (estimados pelo UN Millennium Project). Vale a pena ter em conta que estes neros - apesar da sua elevada dimenso em termos absolutos - esto inteiramente dentro dos compromissos assumidos pela comunidade internacional, uma vez que em Monterrey estes mesmos pases assumiram o compromisso de atingirem at 2015 o limiar mnimo de 0.7% do seu rendimento em ajuda internacional. A este propito deve sublinhar-se que a Unio Europeia comprometeu-se no Conselho Europeu de Bruxelas de Junho deste ano a cumprir efectivamente at 2015 a meta colectiva de 0.7% do PIB, com um objectivo intermdio de 0.56% em 2010. Assumindo que a transferncia de recursos financeiros  um dos elementos fundamentais para a prossecuo dos Objectivos do Milnio, uma das formas de concretizar essa transferncia  o cancelamento da dvida dos pases mais pobres, na medida em que os recursos assim libertos podem ser efectivamente utilizados no combate  pobreza e  promoo do desenvolvimento. Nessa medida, foi aprovada na tima reunio do G-8 de Gleneagles uma proposta de cancelamento integral da dvida multilateral dos pases altamente endividados, a qual ser apresentada nas primas reunies anuais do Banco Mundial e do Fundo Monetrio Internacional. Essa proposta prev um tratamento diferenciado da dvida ao FMI (que seria absorvida pelos recursos prprios da instituio),  AID e ao Fundo Africano de Desenvolvimento. Para que este cancelamento resulte em recursos efectivamente adicionais de ajuda aos pases menos desenvolvidos  necessrio que o seu financiamento seja assegurado pelas naes desenvolvidas. Subsistem para alm disso muitos outros aspectos tcnicos a resolver para que as medidas a concretizar correspondam ao que foi anunciado no final da cimeira do G-8 como correspondendo a um marco histico no processo de ajuda internacional ao desenvolvimento. Esperemos que, no decurso da Reunio Anual das Instituis de Bretton-Woods que se realiza esta semana, todos esses problemas encontrem soluo. Os Objectivos do Milnio parecem hoje difceis de alcanar, mas o esforo e os recursos mobilizados para os cumprir so, alm de uma exigncia moral, a expresso de interesse prrio bem compreendido por parte dos pases desenvolvidos. Num mundo cada vez mais globalizado e interdependente, a estabilidade e a segurana no dependem apenas da superao de desequilbrios econico-financeiros, mas tambm de desequilbrios sociais que contradizem o sentido de justia dos povos. Lisboa, 20 de Setembro de 2005

Title: Intervention of the Governor at the opening of the 16th meeting of Central Banks of PALOP, Portugal and Timor-Leste
text: INTERVENTION OF THE GOVERNOR OF BANCO DE PORTUGAL AT THE OPENING OF THE 16th MEETING OF CENTRAL BANKS OF THE PALOP, PORTUGAL AND TIMOR-LESTE September 12, 2006 Ambassadors Governors Ladies and gentlemen I thank you all for your presence at this 16th Meeting of Central Banks of PALOP and Timor-Leste. Once again we continue a tradition that has strengthened the bonds of cooperation between our institutions. The actions carried out throughout 2006 by our central banks and monetary authorities directly reflect the needs and challenges arising from the consolidation of new areas and processes of action in each of the institutions, in particular with regard to the development of money and exchange markets, the deepening of the banking system's supervisory activity and the strengthening of its human and organisational structures, contribute to the development of their financial systems. The cooperation during the current year essentially covered all the main areas of action that characterize the activity of central banks, having involved, in our case, virtually all the main Departments of the Bank. Of course, there is a significant continuity of projects initiated in previous years, given the complex and evolving nature of the challenges facing these institutions. As in the previous year, there was an increase in the relative weight of actions of a regional and multilateral nature, embodied in particular in Meetings and Seminars, the emphasis of which consists essentially on the exchange of information and experiences and the joint reflection on topics which, although they may present different expressions according to the size and degree of development of each central bank, evidence the similitude of propitious and the analogy of the objectives that preside over the activity of the participating institutions. This reflects the maturity already achieved by the generality of our institutions, which in turn implies that we all have to gain from the experience of other monetary authorities. During 2007 we will continue the cooperation efforts that have been developed in the areas already mentioned, through technical misss, training courses and thematic seminars, in particular in the areas of Information and Issuance and Treasury Systems. 2. As usual, this Lisbon Meeting takes place on the eve of the annual meeting of the IMF and the World Bank, which means that at the working meeting of our delegations, which took place yesterday, the problems that are on the agenda of the two international institutions will be analyzed. This year attention focuses on the risks that threaten the evolution of the world economy and the strategic reform of the IMF, including the start of the review of member countries' quotas and the implementation of the new process of multilateral monitoring of macro-econic and exchange-rate policies responsible for major global imbalances. Despite the various types of risks it has faced, the world economy has continued to show growth of about 5 percent in 2006, similar to that achieved in the first three years. Monetary and financial conditions have remained growth-friendly, despite the process of standardising interest rates carried out by the general monetary authorities and the review of risk premiums, which caused some volatility in the financial markets in the second quarter. Medium- and long-term interest rates, as well as credit rate spreads to companies or emerging countries, generally remain at reduced levels. An important aspect to be highlighted is that growth has been more widespread and well distributed, as Europe and Japan have been at a higher pace of growth that has made it possible to compensate for slowdown in the U.S. economy in the second quarter. This has seen full confirmation of the central scenario envisaged by the European Central Bank in relation to the euro area economy. The standardisation of the interest rates we have been doing since last December has not prevented the ongoing econica recovery. In addition to the results of the first quarter revealing a significant growth momentum, it is also important to stress that as a result of recent statistical reviews of past growth, the increase in income per inhabitant was on average equal in the first ten years in the European Union and the United States. It is also confirmed that the level and productivity growth per hour worked has been higher in several European countries than in the US economy. Finally, the employment growth rate in the first ten years has also been higher in Europe. I recall these results because they should make them reflect those who have hastily expressed definitive conclusions about the so-called European inefficiencies and the supposed prevalence of the American paradigm in all aspects of ecological and social life. Europe has undertaken many structural reforms in the past few years and, in addition to maintaining the essence of its social model, it is beginning to see some positive results in terms of eco-growth, although the enormous uncertainties of the current international situation do not allow us to have reliable guarantees about future developments. In fact, it is possible that the world economy will experience some slowdown in the first year in a dimension that is difficult to predict and on which there are, as always, very different positions. The most consensual view so far is that the reduction in growth will be very slight and will have beneficial effects on the evolution of global eco-imbalances. Everything, however, is dependent on the extent of the fall of the real estate sector in the United States and the size of its effects on the American economy. It is known as the price increase in the asset markets has successively passed from shares to bonds and, finally, to real estate, which, according to Robert Shiller, the inventor of the expression 'irrational exuberance', could turn out to be "the biggest speculative bubble of American history". The drop in production and prices threatens to be the largest in many decades with a negative wealth effect on consumption behavior in the United States. Analysts are divided, however, on the size of this wealth effect and on its eventual contagion effect on the rest of the American economy. There is a minority of economists who even predict a recession in the first year and others fear that the problem of housing collapse could add an abrupt adjustment in foreign exchange markets associated with global external imbalances. The purpose of the Us deficit requires around 800,000 million funding and absorbs more than 70% of the world's savings, Kenneth Rogoff, former chief economist at the IMF, recently said the need for "difficult measures if a global eco-collapse is to be avoided." The maintenance of so-called "global imbalances" translates, as is well known, into a huge US external deficit and a very substantial accumulation of foreign exchange reserves by several countries, notably the major exporters of petreo and China. One of the most feared effects that these imbalances could cause  an abrupt drop in the exchange value of the give  has not occurred so far and, on the contrary, we have seen a gradual evolution in the foreign exchange markets. On the other hand, it has apparently been easy to secure the financing of the American deficit. In fact, given the depth and efficiency of international financial markets, which globalisation has made possible, the financing of strong deficits has become simple, which makes it possible for them to be very gradual. This is, moreover, the basis of a benign view of current imbalances, which points to the existence of a spontaneous excess of savings on investment in the rest of the world and its application in American assets, for security reasons or greater return. This influx of capital would sustain the giving in high values, which would explain, in turn, the current account deficit. The problems with this interpretation stem mainly from the fact that in the last few years the financing of the American balance has been significantly secured by foreign monetary authorities and not only as a consequence of the private sector put their savings in the United States. (a) the important role played by the Asian monetary authorities now has the contribution of several oil-producing countries which have accumulated, on average, external surpluses of around 18% of their GDP. The orderly and gradual correction of existing imbalances thus necessarily involves an increase in savings in the United States and a slowdown in its growth in the immediate future; secondly, for greater exchange rate flexibility in Asian countries and petreo-producing countries and, finally, for an increase in their investment expenditure. Europe, for its part, is now fulfilling its share of the indispensable global adjustment by accelerating its growth based also on the dynamics of its domestic demand. Europe, which has no responsibility for accumulating global imbalances, given its ongoing concern for stability and macro-ecological balances, is now contributing to its gradual resolution. In the immediate future, emerging countries have also helped offset the slowdown in the U.S. economy, with very significant growth rates, particularly in the cases of China, India and several petreo-producing countries that have benefited from high crude oil prices. In Africa too, there has been a support of economic activity clearly above the historical trend, reflecting in the general ity of these countries the progress made in macro-economic and structural policies. It is very positive to welcome that this also applies to the African countries present here, which have estimated growth rates for this year between 4 and 15%, as appropriate, while achieving success in controlling inflation, thus showing significant progress in the conduct of their macro-econic policies and in carrying out some structural reforms. In sub-Saharan Africa as a whole, growth will exceed 5% for the third consecutive year, even though this figure is even more pronounced in 2007, thanks to the expected increases in petreo production in Angola and Equatorial Guinea. The general increase in commodity prices (petreo, metals, coffee) has also benefited significantly from some of these economies, although for other African countries, notably those whose main export goods are cotton or cocoa, the rise in the import price of petreo is prevailing and, therefore, the evolution of their terms of trade is clearly negative. For countries facing this, the strengthening of international aid flows are of fundamental importance to counterbalance the adverse effects of the deterioration of their terms of trade. In this perspective, it would also be important that the recently created Shock Response Facility for low-income countries within the IMF had greater flexibility and automatism of use, as was the case with the former Compensatia Facility (CFF). This rise in the price of petreo and, in general, of raw materials, as well as its prolonged maintenance at high levels, if it has positive effects for some countries, cannot but be an element of concern, since it significantly conditions the evolution and behaviour of the world economy. However, despite these increases, inflation has remained reasonably contained, both in the most developed economies and in most emerging and low-income economies, which is inseparable from the credibility gained by central banks in the last two decades and the effects of international competition enhanced by globalisation and the contribution of the entry into international trade of industrial production stems from countries with lower production costs. The recent slowdown in growth has also contributed to a reduction in commodity prices and to easing tensions and reducing the risk of second-order effects on rising inflation. As I mentioned earlier, the main incnita of the current situation refers to the degree of slowdown that the American economy may suffer and its possible effect on the world economy. It is in the context of this uncertainty that the OECD's recent reference to the need for the normalisation of interest rates in Europe to continue to be gradual. In fact, I think that the essential thing is that monetary policy remains vigilant, but dependent on the concrete data of the evolution of the European economy and the analysis of the risks present in the current situation. We should therefore not speculate on the basis of hypothetical scenarios for the most prime future of the coming year, all the more so since there is no anticipated commitment to an accurate trajectory for the evolution of interest rates. 3. As is natural for a small open economy such as the Portuguese one, the European recovery has had very positive effects on our ecological evolution this year. In particular, export behaviour led to higher-than-expected second-quarter growth. This development confirmed the basis of the forecast that Banco de Portugal released in July of an annual growth of 1.2%, against the opinion of those who found this number too optimistic. It is possible that the dynamics of the second quarter will justify a further rerevision of our forecasts. We must, however, wait prudently for more information, in particular that for August, a month of usual drop in activity, before we proceed to any revision, especially since the growth of 0.9% of the first quarter exceeds only by 0.2 percentage points the growth that was implied for that quarter in our annual forecasts of 1.2%. An important aspect of the growth pattern is the same result only from net exports while reducing domestic demand. This means achieving an inevitable adjustment after years of growth based on the growing indebtedness of econic agents, including the state. We could not, in fact, continue down a path that passed the country from an international creditor situation of around 7,000 million in 1996 to an external debt position of around 65,000 million at the end of last year. The current phase of internal expenditure adjustment has the effect of containing debt expansion and pressuring companies to restructure and seek to target their production on a larger scale to foreign markets. The fall in public consumption also foretells that it now seems likely that the State will be able to meet the target set for the budget deficit as a result of favourable revenue developments, but also the control of phasing expenditure. This is a positive development, as deficit control is an important factor of credibility and a condition of increased domestic savings and future eco-growth. The path of economic recovery is essentially the dynamics of exports and business investment in transactional goods and services, given the limitations of investment expenditure and the inevitably less active phase of investment in housing. The recent ancios by foreign companies for new investments in Portugal are based on the expectation that we are facing a phase of some change in the production structure and composition of Portuguese exports. As I said here last year, "The best contribution that the implementing policies can make at this stage is to put order in the plicas accounts and reduce bureaucracy to free up the strength of the initiative of the eco-actors". The improvements made in these areas are to be noted, but the path of real adjustment necessary to overcome the challenges of new international competition will be long and difficult. Determination and rigour in the policies and dynamism of companies are therefore essential for us to return to a path of convergence with our European partners more quickly. Lisbon 12 September 2006
text_original: INTERVENO DO GOVERNADOR DO BANCO DE PORTUGAL NA ABERTURA DO 16 ENCONTRO DE BANCOS CENTRAIS DOS PALOP, DE PORTUGAL E DE TIMOR-LESTE 12 de Setembro de 2006 Senhores Embaixadores Senhores Governadores Minhas Senhoras e meus Senhores Agradeo a presena de todos neste 16 Encontro de Bancos Centrais dos PALOP e Timor-leste. Uma vez mais damos continuidade a uma tradio que tem reforado os laos de cooperao entre as nossas instituis. As acs desenvolvidas ao longo de 2006 pelos nossos bancos centrais e autoridades monetrias reflectem de forma directa as necessidades e os desafios decorrentes da consolidao de novas reas e processos de actuao em cada uma das instituis, nomeadamente no que se refere ao desenvolvimento dos mercados monetrios e cambiais, ao aprofundamento da actividade de superviso do sistema bancrio e ao reforo das suas estruturas humanas e organizativas, de forma a poderem contribuir activamente para o desenvolvimento dos respectivos sistemas financeiros. A cooperao durante o ano em curso abrangeu no essencial todas as principais reas de actuao que caracterizam a actividade dos bancos centrais, tendo envolvido, no nosso caso, praticamente todos os principais Departamentos do Banco. Naturalmente que se regista uma significativa continuidade dos projectos iniciados em anos anteriores, dada a natureza complexa e evolutiva dos desafios com que estas instituis so confrontadas.  semelhana do ano anterior, verificou-se um acrscimo do peso relativo das acs de natureza regional e multilateral, consubstanciadas nomeadamente em Encontros e Seminrios, cuja nfase consiste essencialmente na troca de informas e experincias e na reflexo conjunta sobre temas que, embora possam apresentar expresses diferentes conforme a dimenso e o grau de desenvolvimento de cada banco central, evidenciam a similitude de propitos e a analogia dos objectivos que presidem  actividade das instituis participantes. Esta circunstncia reflecte a maturidade j atingida pela generalidade das nossas instituis, que implica, por sua vez, que todos tenhamos a ganhar com a experincia de outras autoridades monetrias. Durante 2007 continuaremos os esforos de cooperao que tm sido desenvolvidos nas reas j referidas, atravs de misss tcnicas, estgios de formao e seminrios temticos, nomeadamente nos domnios dos Sistemas de Informao e de Emisso e Tesouraria. 2. Como habitualmente, este Encontro de Lisboa ocorre nas vsperas da reunio anual do FMI e do Banco Mundial, o que proporciona que na reunio de trabalho das nossas Delegas, ontem ocorrida, se analisem os problemas que constam neste momento da agenda das duas Instituis internacionais. Este ano as atens concentram-se nos riscos que ameaam a evoluo da economia mundial e na reforma estratgica do FMI, nomeadamente o incio da reviso das quotas dos pases membros e a concretizao do novo processo de monitorizao multilateral das polticas macroeconicas e cambiais responsveis pelos grandes desequilbrios mundiais. Apesar dos vrios tipos de riscos que tem enfrentado, a economia mundial tem continuado a apresentar em 2006 um crescimento de cerca de 5 por cento, semelhante ao alcanado nos timos trs anos. As condis monetrias e financeiras tm permanecido favorveis ao crescimento, apesar do processo de normalizao das taxas de juro levada a cabo pela generalidade das autoridades monetrias e da reviso dos prmios de risco, que causou alguma volatilidade nos mercados financeiros no segundo trimestre. As taxas de juro de mdio e longo prazo, bem como os spreads das taxas do crdito a empresas ou a pases emergentes, continuam em geral em nveis reduzidos. Um aspecto importante a sublinhar  a circunstncia do crescimento ter sido mais generalizado e bem distribudo, uma vez que a Europa e o Japo tm vindo a apresentar um maior ritmo de crescimento que permitiu compensar a desacelerao da economia norte-americana no segundo trimestre. Verificou-se, assim, a plena confirmao do cenrio central previsto pelo Banco Central Europeu relativamente  economia da rea do euro. A normalizao das taxas de juro a que temos procedido desde Dezembro passado no impediu a recuperao econica em curso. Para alm dos resultados do timo trimestre revelarem uma assinalvel dinmica de crescimento,  importante sublinhar tambm que em resultado de recentes revises estatsticas do crescimento passado, o aumento do Rendimento por habitante foi em mdia igual nos timos dez anos na Unio Europeia e nos Estados Unidos. Confirma-se tambm que o nvel e o crescimento da produtividade por hora trabalhada tm sido superiores em vrios pases europeus aos verificados na economia norte-americana. Finalmente, a taxa de crescimento do emprego nos timos dez anos tem tambm sido superior na Europa. Recordo estes resultados porque eles deveriam fazer reflectir os que apressadamente tm enunciado concluss definitivas sobre as chamadas ineficincias europeias e a suposta prevalncia do paradigma americano em todos os aspectos da vida econica e social. A Europa realizou nos timos anos bastantes reformas estruturais e, para alm de manter o essencial do seu modelo social, comea a ver alguns resultados positivos no plano do crescimento econico, apesar de as enormes incertezas da actual situao internacional no nos permitirem ter garantias seguras sobre a evoluo futura. Na verdade,  possvel que a economia mundial conhea alguma desacelerao no primo ano numa dimenso que  difcil de prever e sobre a qual existem, como sempre, posies muito diferentes. A perspectiva mais consensual at ao momento  a de que a reduo do crescimento ser muito ligeira e ter efeitos benficos sobre a evoluo dos desequilbrios econicos globais. Tudo, porm, est dependente da extenso da queda do sector imobilirio nos Estados Unidos e da dimenso dos seus efeitos na economia americana.  conhecido como o empolamento dos preos nos mercados de activos tem passado sucessivamente das acs para as obrigas e, finalmente, para o imobilirio, que, de acordo com Robert Shiller, o inventor da expresso exuberncia irracional, poderia vir a ser a maior bolha especulativa da histia americana. A quebra da produo e dos preos ameaa vir a ser a maior em muitas dcadas com um efeito-riqueza negativo sobre o comportamento do consumo nos Estados Unidos. Os analistas dividem-se, porm, sobre a dimenso desse efeito-riqueza e sobre o seu eventual efeito de contgio ao resto da economia americana. Existe uma minoria de economistas que prev mesmo uma recesso no primo ano e outros temem que ao problema da quebra do imobilirio se possa juntar um ajustamento abrupto nos mercados cambiais associado aos desequilbrios externos globais. A propito de o dfice americano requerer cerca de 800 mil milhs de dares de financiamento e absorver mais de 70 % da poupana mundial, Kenneth Rogoff, ex-economista chefe do FMI, referiu recentemente a necessidade de medidas difceis se se pretender evitar um colapso econico global. A manuteno dos denominados desequilbrios globais traduz-se, como  bem conhecido, num enorme dfice externo norte-americano e numa muito substancial acumulao de reservas cambiais por diversos pases, nomeadamente os grandes exportadores de petreo e a China. Um dos mais temidos efeitos que esses desequilbrios poderiam provocar  uma quebra abrupta do valor cambial do dar  no se verificou at ao presente e, pelo contrrio, temos assistido a uma evoluo gradual nos mercados cambiais. Por outro lado, tem sido aparentemente fcil assegurar o financiamento do dfice americano. Na verdade, face  profundidade e eficincia dos mercados financeiros internacionais, que a globalizao tornou possvel, o financiamento de fortes dfices tornou-se simples, o que possibilita que a sua correco possa ser bastante gradual. Esta , alis, a base de uma viso benigna dos actuais desequilbrios, a que aponta para a existncia de um espontneo excesso de poupana sobre o investimento no resto do mundo e a sua aplicao em activos americanos, por razs de segurana ou maior retorno. Este afluxo de capitais sustentaria o dar em valores elevados, que explicariam, por sua vez, o dfice da balana corrente. Os problemas com esta interpretao decorrem sobretudo do facto de nos timos anos o financiamento da balana americana ter sido assegurado de forma significativa por autoridades monetrias estrangeiras e no apenas como consequncia do sector privado externo colocar as suas poupanas nos Estados Unidos. Ap o papel importante desempenhado pelas autoridades monetrias asiticas temos agora o contributo de vrios pases produtores de petrleo que acumularam, em mdia, excedentes externos de cerca de 18% do respectivo PIB. A correco ordenada e gradual dos desequilbrios existentes passa, assim, necessariamente por um aumento da poupana nos Estados Unidos e uma desacelerao do seu crescimento no imediato; em segundo lugar, por uma maior flexibilidade cambial nos pases asiticos e nos pases produtores de petreo e, finalmente, por uma aumento das despesas de investimento destes timos. A Europa, por sua vez, est agora a cumprir a parte que lhe competia no indispensvel ajustamento mundial ao acelerar o seu crescimento assente tambm na dinmica da sua procura interna. A Europa, que no tem responsabilidade no acumular dos desequilbrios mundiais, dada a sua permanente preocupao com a estabilidade e os equilbrios macroeconicos, est agora a contribuir para a sua gradual resoluo. No imediato, tambm os pases emergentes tm contribudo para compensar a desacelerao da economia americana, apresentando taxas de crescimento muito assinalveis, nomeadamente nos casos da China, da ndia e de vrios pases produtores de petreo que tm beneficiado dos elevados preos do crude. Igualmente em frica tem-se verificado uma sustentao da actividade econmica claramente acima da tendncia histica, o que reflecte na generalidade destes pases os progressos alcanados nas polticas macroeconmicas e estruturais. Importa saudar como muito positivo que isso tambm se aplica aos pases africanos aqui presentes, que apresentam taxas de crescimento estimadas para este ano entre 4 a 15%, consoante os casos, ao mesmo tempo que tm alcanado sucesso no controle da inflao, revelando, assim, assinalveis progressos na conduo das suas polticas macroeconicas e na realizao de algumas reformas estruturais. No conjunto da frica Sub-Saariana o crescimento ir pelo terceiro ano consecutivo exceder 5%, prevendo-se mesmo que esse valor seja ainda mais acentuado em 2007, graas aos acrscimos previstos da produo de petreo em Angola e na Guin Equatorial. O aumento generalizado dos preos das matrias primas (petreo, metais, caf) tambm tem beneficiado significativamente algumas destas economias, embora, para outros pases africanos, nomeadamente aqueles cujos principais bens de exportao so o algodo ou o cacau, a subida do preo de importao do petreo seja prevalecente e, portanto, a evoluo dos seus termos de troca seja de sentido claramente negativo. Para os pases que enfrentam esta circunstncia, o reforo dos fluxos de ajuda internacional so de fundamental importncia para contrabalanar os efeitos adversos da deteriorao dos seus termos de troca. Nesta perspectiva seria tambm importante que a recentemente criada Facilidade de Resposta a Choques para pases de baixo rendimento, no mbito do FMI, tivesse maior flexibilidade e automatismo de utilizao, como acontecia com a antiga Facilidade Compensatia (CFF). A referida subida do preo do petreo e, em geral, das matrias-primas, bem como a sua manuteno prolongada em patamares elevados, se tem efeitos positivos para alguns pases, no pode deixar de constituir um elemento de preocupao, na medida em que condiciona de forma relevante a evoluo e o comportamento da economia mundial. No entanto, apesar destas subidas, a inflao temse mantido razoavelmente contida, quer nas economias mais desenvolvidas quer na generalidade das economias emergentes e nas de baixo rendimento, o que  indissocivel da credibilidade ganha pelos bancos centrais nas timas duas dcadas e dos efeitos da concorrncia internacional potenciada pela globalizao e pelo contributo da entrada no comrcio internacional de produs industriais com origem em pases de mais baixos custos de produo. A recente desacelerao do crescimento tambm contribuiu para uma reduo dos preos das matrias-primas e para aliviar as tenss e reduzir o risco de efeitos de segunda ordem na subida da inflao. Como referi anteriormente, a principal incnita da actual situao refere-se ao grau de desacelerao que poder sofrer a economia americana e seu possvel efeito na economia mundial.  no contexto desta incerteza que se compreende a recente referncia da OCDE  necessidade de a normalizao das taxas de juro na Europa continuar a ser gradual. Na verdade, penso que o essencial  que a poltica monetria continue vigilante, mas dependente dos dados concretos da evoluo da economia europeia e da anlise dos riscos presentes na actual conjuntura. No devemos, pois, especular com base em cenrios hipotticos para o futuro mais primo do ano que se aproxima, tanto mais que no existe qualquer compromisso antecipado com uma trajectia precisa para a evoluo das taxas de juro. 3. Como  natural para uma pequena economia aberta como  a portuguesa, a recuperao europeia tem tido efeitos muito positivos na nossa evoluo econica este ano. Em particular, o comportamento das exportas conduziu a um crescimento no segundo trimestre acima do esperado. Este desenvolvimento veio confirmar o fundamento da previso que o Banco de Portugal divulgou em Julho de um crescimento anual de 1,2%, contra a opinio dos que acharam esse nmero demasiado optimista.  possvel que a dinmica do segundo trimestre venha a justificar uma nova reviso em alta das nossas previses. Devemos, no entanto, aguardar prudentemente por mais informao, nomeadamente a relativa a Agosto, um ms de habitual quebra de actividade, antes de procedermos a qualquer reviso, tanto mais que o crescimento de 0,9% do timo trimestre excede apenas em 0,2 pontos percentuais o crescimento que estava implcito para esse trimestre nas nossas previses anuais de 1,2%. Um aspecto importante do padro de crescimento verificado  o mesmo resultar apenas das exportas lquidas ao mesmo tempo que se reduzia a procura interna. Isto significa a concretizao de um ajustamento inevitvel ap anos de crescimento assente no endividamento crescente dos agentes econicos, incluindo o Estado. No poderamos, na verdade, continuar por um caminho que fez passar o pas de uma situao credora internacional em cerca de 7 mil milhs de euros em 1996 para uma posio de dvida externa de cerca de 65 mil milhes no final do ano passado. A fase actual de ajustamento da despesa interna tem o efeito de conter a expanso do endividamento e de pressionar as empresas para se reestruturarem e procurarem orientar as suas produs em maior escala para os mercados externos. A quebra do consumo pblico em termos reais prenuncia tambm que parece agora provvel que o Estado consiga cumprir o objectivo definido para o dfice oramental, em consequncia da evoluo favorvel das receitas, mas tambm do controle da despesa plica. Tratase de um desenvolvimento positivo, uma vez que o controle do dfice  um importante factor de credibilidade e uma condio do aumento da poupana interna e crescimento econico futuro. O caminho da recuperao sida da economia passa essencialmente pela dinmica das exportas e do investimento empresarial em bens e servios transaccionveis, dadas as limitas das despesas de investimento plico e a fase inevitavelmente menos activa do investimento em habitao. Os recentes ancios por parte de empresas estrangeiras de novos investimentos em Portugal fundamentam a expectativa de que estamos perante uma fase de alguma alterao da estrutura produtiva e da composio das exportas portuguesas. Como afirmei aqui o ano passado, A melhor contribuio que as polticas plicas podem dar nesta fase  a de porem ordem nas contas plicas e diminuir a burocracia para libertar a fora da iniciativa dos agentes econicos. As melhorias conseguidas nestes domnios so de assinalar, mas o caminho do ajustamento real necessrio para vencermos os desafios da nova concorrncia internacional ser longo e difcil. Determinao e rigor nas polticas plicas e dinamismo das empresas so, assim, essenciais para mais rapidamente regressarmos a uma percurso de convergncia com os nossos parceiros europeus. Lisboa 12 de Setembro de 2006

Title: Intervention of the Governor in the public presentation of the Simplified Business Information project
text: Intervention of the Governor of Banco de Portugal in the implementation of the Simplified Business Information project Lisbon, 30 April 2007 Ladies and gentlemen, Ministers, Ladies and Gentlemen Banco de Portugal welcomes the creation of simplified business information (HEIs) and the fact that it can join the launch of this project. In view of its objectives of statistical production, analysis of the evolution of the economy and aid for the management of credit risk by the banking system, Banco de Portugal has always been interested in the knowledge of the economic and patrimonial situation of non-financial companies. For this reason, Banco de Portugal has long maintained and disclosed data from a Balance Sheet Center containing annual and quarterly information, obtained through the response to two questionnaires: the annual questionnaire of the Banco de Portugal Balance Sheet Center and the quarterly survey of non-financial companies, conducted in partnership with the National Statistical Institute (INE). In addition to the use made by the Bank, the Central Balance Sheet provides the collaborating companies and the banking system with a set of sectoral indicators for the management and framework in their econic sector. On average, the database of our Central Balance Sheet ree annual information of about 17 500 companies, of which there are usually about 15 000 common with the previous year. These account for about 5% of the total number of companies, 37% of total people in the service and 58% of the gross added value of total non-financial companies. In the field of quarterly information, the Balance Sheet Centre contains data from approximately 3 300 companies per year, of which there are typically around 2,300 common with the previous year. These are representing about 1% of the total number of companies, 22% of total people in service and 41% of the gross added value of total non-financial companies. Despite the manifest quantitative representativeness of the samples mentioned, the truth is that they focus on the responses of large companies.
