The sample nature of the financial documents sent annually by companies naturally limits the scope of the results obtained, although we should highlight the excellent collaboration that companies provide to us. However, we have long considered that there would be interest, as in some other countries, in taking advantage of the so-called official account ability by non-financial companies to improve the information and usefulness that we have already taken from our Balance Sheet Centre today. In this context, the IES project represents the culmination of a long process, started more intensely five years ago. The contacts since then maintained with the Ministry of Justice have always been based on the conviction that, constituting this information a good plico, it was up to the plicas entities to proceed with their treatment and making available in order to meet the needs of users efficiently and without excessive burdens for the information providers. Thus, Banco de Portugal sought to boost the computerization of the account system of non-financial companies, with a view to improving the quality of this system, so far carried out only on paper with the Conservatias of the Commercial Register, in a very incomplete and with a reduced use. Banco de Portugal is thus willing to contribute to the financing of the project in the form of the purchase of a permanent service for the provision of data subject to a quality control system of the reported information and providing the use of the project for statistical purposes. It is therefore with satisfaction that we see that the initial objectives of Banco de Portugal have been fully contemplated in the legislation establishing Simplified Business Information (HEIs). These same objectives are also enshrined in the Protocol concluded in March between the Directorate-General for Registers and Notary (DGRN), the Institute of Information Technologies in Justice (ITIJ) and Banco de Portugal, which defined the general framework for cooperation between these three entities within the framework of the information system developed for the statistical treatment of THEIs. We are, without dida, faced with a very innovative solution in several plans:  First, because it reflects an efficient articulation, based on good institutional cooperation, between different plicas entities (Ministry of Justice, Ministry of Finance, National Institute of Statistics and Banco de Portugal);  Second, because it guarantees the satisfaction of information needs in an integrated manner for very different purposes: in particular, the commercial register and the practice of notary acts, the accounting and tax declaration, statistical production, the economic analysis of undertakings and sectors of activity;  Third, because it results in significant cost savings, both for the companies reporting and for the plicae entities involved;  And finally, because this project is an excellent example of the use of information from administrative acts for statistical purposes, thus satisfying important needs of the National Statistical System, in this case both the INE and Banco de Portugal. Access to the basic accounting data of all Portuguese companies will allow Banco de Portugal to reinforce the set of information it has and which it considers indispensable for the fulfilment of the mission conferred on it through its Organic Law. Thus, among the functions carried out by Banco de Portugal that will benefit from the creation of the HEI, I highlight the following:  the production of statistics;  the analysis of the ecological and financial situation of companies and sectors of activity;  supervision of the stability of the financial system;  and, in all these areas, the contribution of Banco de Portugal in supranational terms, especially with regard to compliance with the requirements arising from our participation in the European System of Central Banks. The statistical function, due to its relevance in monitoring the quality of the data and preparing the information necessary for the proper performance of the other functions of the Bank that use it, deserves special attention. Thus, in the field of its statistical competences, the Bank may draw direct benefits from the HEI to:  more accurately assess the ecological and financial situation of Portuguese companies;  improve the quality of existing statistics by crossing, for example, with securities emisss statistics or reports of foreign operations carried out to the Bank by companies in the context of the preparation of the Balance of Payments;  to determine and correctly characterize the universe of Portuguese companies and thus improve the selection of samples for the conduct of other surveys.  determine final statistics directly from the HEI, as the universe becomes known. By way of example, I cite some cases where this information proves to be a privileged source and, in some cases, ica: for example, in the assessment of the amounts of commercial credits, for the purposes of financial account statistics, balance of payments and international investment position; or in the assessment of the capital of companies that are not animated companies for the purposes of financial accounts; or, finally, in direct contributions to international databases, such as the BACH database, managed by the European Commission All this means that it is possible to identify immediate benefits in the use of HEI within the scope of Banco de Portugal's functions, which are quite significant compared to the results that were possible so far from the annual survey of the Central Balance Sheet. The services that it has been able to provide are, however, noteable and I therefore take this opportunity to thank the excellent collaboration that we have obtained over many years from the companies surveyed and their Official Account Technicians, providing a very significant response rate to this survey. I would also like to congratulate the team of technicians who have been working more closely on the new IES project and to stress, in conclusion, that the entities represented here can rightly congratulate themselves on another initiative of administrative simplification that improves the efficiency and quality of the services that the country so badly needs to consolidate its modernisation process. Lisbon, 30 April 2007 Victor Constancio
text_original: Interveno do Governador do Banco de Portugal na apresentao plica do projecto de Informao Empresarial Simplificada Lisboa, 30 de Abril de 2007 Exmos Senhores Ministros Exmos Senhores Secretrios de Estado Minhas Senhoras e meus Senhores O Banco de Portugal congratula-se com a criao da Informao Empresarial Simplificada (IES) e com a circunstncia de poder associar-se ao lanamento plico deste projecto. Na perspectiva dos seus objectivos de produo estatstica, de anlise da evoluo da economia e de ajuda  gesto do risco de crdito pelo sistema bancrio, o Banco de Portugal sempre se interessou pelo conhecimento da situao econmica e patrimonial das empresas no financeiras. Por essa razo desde h muito que o Banco de Portugal mantm e divulga os dados de uma Central de Balanos que contm informao de base anual e trimestral, obtida atravs da resposta a dois questionrios: o questionrio anual da Central de Balanos do Banco de Portugal e o inqurito trimestral s empresas no financeiras, realizado em parceria com o Instituto Nacional de Estatstica (INE). Para alm da utilizao feita pelo Banco, a Central de Balanos proporciona s empresas colaboradoras e ao sistema bancrio um conjunto de indicadores sectoriais eis para a gesto e enquadramento no respectivo sector de actividade econica. Em mdia, a base de dados da nossa Central de Balanos ree informao anual de cerca de 17 500 empresas, das quais h normalmente cerca de 15 000 comuns com o ano anterior. Estas correspondem a cerca de 5% do nero total de empresas, 37% do total de pessoas ao servio e 58% do valor acrescentado bruto do total das empresas no financeiras. No domnio da informao trimestral, a Central de Balanos contm dados de aproximadamente 3 300 empresas por ano, das quais h normalmente cerca de 2 300 comuns com o ano anterior. Estas so representativas de cerca de 1% do nero total de empresas, 22% do total de pessoas ao servio e 41% do valor acrescentado bruto do total das empresas no financeiras. Apesar da manifesta representatividade quantitativa das amostras referidas, a verdade  que as mesmas se concentram nas respostas das grandes empresas. O carcter amostral dos documentos financeiros enviados anualmente pelas empresas limita naturalmente o mbito dos resultados obtidos, apesar de devermos realar a excelente colaborao que as empresas nos prestam. No entanto, desde h muito consideramos que haveria interesse, como acontece nalguns outros pases, em aproveitarmos o chamado depito oficial de contas por parte das empresas no financeiras para melhorarmos a informao e a utilidade que hoje j retiramos da nossa Central de Balanos. Neste contexto, o projecto da IES representa o culminar de um longo processo, iniciado de forma mais intensa h cinco anos atrs. Os contactos desde ento mantidos com o Ministrio da Justia assentaram sempre na convico de que, constituindo esta informao um bem plico, competia s entidades plicas proceder ao seu tratamento e disponibilizao de forma a satisfazer as necessidades dos utilizadores de forma eficiente e sem sobrecargas excessivas para os fornecedores da informao. Assim, o Banco de Portugal procurou impulsionar a informatizao do depito de contas das empresas no financeiras, com vista a melhorar a qualidade desse sistema, at agora efectuado apenas em suporte de papel junto das Conservatias do Registo Comercial, de forma muito incompleta e com um aproveitamento reduzido. O Banco de Portugal disp-se, assim a contribuir para o financiamento do projecto sob a forma da compra de um servio permanente de disponibilizao de dados sujeitos a um sistema de controlo de qualidade da informao reportada e proporcionando a utilizao da mesma para fins estatsticos. , portanto, com satisfao que verificamos que os objectivos iniciais do Banco de Portugal foram plenamente contemplados na legislao que cria a Informao Empresarial Simplificada (IES). Esses mesmos objectivos so tambm consagrados no Protocolo celebrado em Maro entre a Direco-Geral dos Registos e do Notariado (DGRN), o Instituto das Tecnologias de Informao na Justia (ITIJ) e o Banco de Portugal, que definiu o quadro geral da cooperao entre estas trs entidades no mbito do sistema de informao desenvolvido com vista ao tratamento estatstico da IES. Estamos, sem dida, perante uma soluo bastante inovadora em diversos planos:  Primeiro, porque reflecte uma articulao eficiente, assente na boa cooperao institucional, entre diferentes entidades plicas (Ministrio da Justia, Ministrio das Finanas, Instituto Nacional de Estatstica e Banco de Portugal);  Segundo, porque garante a satisfao de forma integrada de necessidades de informao para finalidades bem distintas: nomeadamente, o registo comercial e a prtica de actos notariais, a declarao contabilstica e fiscal, a produo estatstica, a anlise econmica das empresas e dos sectores de actividade;  Terceiro, porque resulta numa significativa economia de custos, quer para as empresas que reportam, quer para as entidades plicas envolvidas;  E, finalmente, porque este projecto constitui um excelente exemplo da utilizao da informao de actos administrativos para fins estatsticos, satisfazendo desta forma necessidades importantes do Sistema Estatstico Nacional, neste caso quer do INE, quer do Banco de Portugal. O acesso aos dados de base contabilstica de todas as empresas Portuguesas permitir ao Banco de Portugal reforar o conjunto de informao de que disp e que considera indispensvel para o cumprimento da misso que lhe  conferida atravs da sua Lei Orgnica. Assim, de entre as funs exercidas pelo Banco de Portugal que iro beneficiar com a criao da IES, destaco as seguintes:  a produo de estatsticas;  a anlise da situao econica e financeira das empresas e dos sectores de actividade;  a superviso da estabilidade do sistema financeiro;  e, em todos estes domnios, o contributo do Banco de Portugal no plano supranacional, sobretudo no que respeita ao cumprimento dos requisitos decorrentes da nossa participao no Sistema Europeu de Bancos Centrais. A funo estatstica, pela relevncia que assume no controlo da qualidade dos dados e na preparao da informao necessria ao desempenho adequado das outras funs do Banco que a ela recorrem, merece um especial destaque. Assim, no domnio das suas competncias estatsticas, o Banco poder retirar benefcios directos da IES para:  avaliar com mais rigor a situao econica e financeira das empresas portuguesas;  melhorar a qualidade das estatsticas j existentes, efectuando cruzamentos, por exemplo, com as estatsticas de emisss de ttulos ou os reportes de operas com o exterior efectuados ao Banco pelas empresas no mbito da elaborao da Balana de Pagamentos;  apurar e caracterizar correctamente o universo das empresas portuguesas e assim melhorar a seleco de amostras para a realizao de outros inquritos.  apurar estatsticas finais directamente da IES, na medida em que o universo passa a ser conhecido. A ttulo exemplificativo, cito alguns casos em que esta informao se revela fonte privilegiada e, nalguns casos, ica: por exemplo, na avaliao dos montantes de crditos comerciais, para efeitos das estatsticas das Contas Financeiras, da Balana de Pagamentos e da Posio de Investimento Internacional; ou ainda, na avaliao do capital das empresas que no so sociedades animas para efeitos das Contas Financeiras; ou, finalmente, nos contributos directos para bases de dados internacionais, como por exemplo a base de dados BACH, gerida pela Comisso Europeia Tudo isto significa que  possvel identificar benefcios imediatos na utilizao da IES no mbito das funs do Banco de Portugal, bastante significativos em comparao com os resultados que era possvel at agora obter com o inqurito anual da Central de Balanos. Os servios que esta tem podido prestar so, porm, assinalveis e aproveito, por isso, para agradecer a colaborao excelente que ao longo de muitos anos obtivemos da parte das empresas inquiridas e dos respectivos Tcnicos Oficiais de Contas, proporcionando uma taxa de resposta muito significativa a esse inqurito. Desejo tambm felicitar a equipa de tcnicos que mais de perto tem trabalhado no novo projecto da IES e sublinhar, em concluso, que as entidades aqui representadas se podem justamente congratular por mais uma iniciativa de simplificao administrativa que melhora a eficincia e a qualidade dos servios plicos de que o pas tanto carece para consolidar o seu processo de modernizao. Lisboa, 30 de Abril de 2007 Vtor Constancio

Title: Speech of the Governor at the 19th Lisbon Meeting with the DELEGATIONS OF THE PALOP and Timor-Leste
text: INTERVENTION OF THE GOVERNOR OF BANCO DE PORTUGAL AT THE OPENING OF THE 19th MEETING OF CENTRAL BANKS OF THE PALOP, PORTUGAL AND TIMOR-LESTE September 29, 2009 Ambassadors Governors Ladies and gentlemen I thank you all for your presence at this 19th Lisbon Meeting, between the delegations of Portugal, the PALOP and Timor-Leste to the IMF/World Bank Annual Assembly. Once again we continue a tradition that allows us to strengthen the bonds of cooperation between our institutions. This meeting is also an opportunity for us to discuss the recent international economic and financial developments and how they affect our countries together. As everyone is aware, we have gone through (and are still going through) a complex period of environmental crisis, during which the risks of disruption of the functioning of financial systems have reached an extremely serious expression. This required forms of intervention by central banks and monetary and financial authorities which, before the crisis, many of them would think to be outside the scope of action of institutions such as ours. Despite the attention and effort that the international situation requires by our institutions, it was possible to intensify the activity cooperation. We are pleased to say that it will see a significant increase in 2009, expressed in the number of actions carried out between our central banks. As had been the norm in previous years, the cooperation activity developed throughout this year essentially covered all the main areas of action of central banks, thus implying the mobilization of virtually all major units of structure of Banco de Portugal. On the one hand, projects that had already been started in previous years, but which maintain their timeliness and importance, have continued, and, on the other hand, new initiatives have been introduced or other initiatives have been introduced in their content and form, with the aim of more adequately addressing the challenges facing central banks and monetary authorities in the current complex situation. Bilateral cooperation actions covered areas as varied and relevant as, for example, eco-studies, human resources, accounting, banking supervision, legal affairs or management of penss funds. Among the bilateral cooperation actions in 2009, it is also worth mentioning the joint work carried out throughout the year by the Central Bank of Sao Tome and Principe and Banco de Portugal, which contributed to the conclusion of the Econica Cooperation Agreement between the governments of the two countries, which will allow a nominal anchor conducive to greater macroeconomic stability in Sao Tome, the country's option for a exchange rate regime more linked to the euro. As with Cape Verde, the follow-up to this project will determine the regular and periic implementation of the Commission's meeting of the Econica Cooperation Agreement and the Macro-Economic Monitoring Unit, in which the two central banks participate. At the request of the IMF, Banco de Portugal participated in February 2009 in a new fsap (Financial Sector Assessment Program) exercise on mozambique's financial system. Although bilateral actions continue to play an important role in the field of cooperation, there continued to be a growing increase in the importance of multilateral and regional actions, reflecting a progressive greater similarity to the concerns and objectives of the different central banks, which find in these initiatives a privileged frum to discuss their experiences and seek to find solutions similar to their common problems. These initiatives are reflected in particular in the various Meetings held, both the Lisbon Meeting and the sectoral meetings that focused on areas such as issuance and treasury, information systems and technologies and human resources. As a result of the decisions of one of these meetings - the 2nd Meeting of Issuance and Treasury - it was agreed to organize on a regular basis a Technical Course on Issuance and Treasury, the first edition of which will take place as early as 2010. In 2009 there were also Meetings on Information Technologies, in S. Tome and Principe, and on Human Resources in Macao, which has been associated with our community of Central Banks and which today has an outstanding participation in the program of our 19th Meeting with the presentation of Dr. Anselmo Teng to whom I take this opportunity to give a warm welcome. These Lisbon Meetings, if, on the one hand, serve to discuss and view the activity of our institutions in the field of cooperation, also aim to allow a joint reflection on the international ecological environment and the topics that will most strongly mark the agenda of the annual raw meetings of international financial institutions, in particular the International Monetary Fund. The dominant theme of these meetings' agenda is, as it should be, the global financial crisis. This crisis, which was feared to have consequences as serious and lasting as the great depression of the 1930s, now shows some signs of slowing down. Some people are trying to take advantage of this to try to devalue the crisis we are going through and to try to argue that the rules of the game and environmental policies should go back to what they were. I am referring to economists and interests who tend to devalue the role of monetary shocks and, above all, financial shocks. It is therefore appropriate to highlight four aspects: The first is that the smaller ecological effects of the crisis have been made possible by unprecedented levels of monetary and budgetary policy intervention, accompanied by high international coordination. The lessons of the 1930s were well learned by the current officials. A second aspect stems from the current greater weight of the state in the economy when compared to what happened during the Great Depression period, which contributes to a balancing effect that is reflected in more substantial automatic stabilisers. As I said here last year, 'The State is again the manager of the risk of the last instance in modern economies'. In fact, the crisis has shown that both in the financial sphere and in the real sphere, markets are not self-balancing and need plica intervention to return to an acceptable balance. The third point I would like to stress is the scale of the crisis in the financial sector which has been very substantial and has significant future consequences. Between 1980 and 2007 total financial assets (shares, bonds and pits) quadrupled as a percentage of world GDP. In 2008, almost 9%, or about 16 trilis of American dares, fell. This nero must add a drop of about 3 trillion in the value of real estate assets to get an idea of the loss of wealth by econic agents who will seek to repla, in whole or in part, saving more and consuming less. We are facing the biggest decline in wealth in a year. At the stock market level the decline was even greater, with a loss of value of about 29 trillion U.S. dares from January 2008 to June this year, on all world stock exchanges. In 2008 the stock markets recorded the biggest annual drop since the Great Depression. It was above all the increase in pits and plica debt that contributed to a reduction in the total number of global financial assets. On the other hand, cross-border financial flows (direct investment, portfolio, loans and pits) decreased in 2008 by 82 percent, from about 11 to about just 2 trillion. The greatest contribution to this decrease came mainly from bank loans. This very strong reduction has caused ineras liquidity crises and currency tensions in many parts of the globe. All these changes reveal the extraordinary scale of the financial crisis that has caused enormous displacement in the world economy. The future of financial globalisation has been shaken and it is now uncertain whether and when it will return to similar to those before the crisis. One thing seems certain: the financial sector in developed economies has been reduced relative to GDP and will not return to growth at least in the first few decades, because the authorities now seem to be committed to containing and taming the financial excesses that periodically generate serious economic crises. Finally, the fourth point I would like to highlight, in order to owe those who seek to devalue the importance of the crisis, refers to the fact that it can be said that the crisis is not over yet. In fact, there is still great uncertainty about the depth and sustainability of a global recovery, which has led some analysts to predict that it may be slower than would be desirable. Several factors contribute to underpouring this fear, above all in developed countries. The replacement of the net balance sheet position of econic agents, which leads individuals to save more, contributes, together with uncertainty about the future, to the contained growth of consumption. This will also be affected by the increase in unemployment which will continue until the end of the first year. In turn, the negative product gap and the low degree of utilization of installed production capacity discourage the dynamics of investment. The small cycle of stock variation that has animated industrial production in the last months has come to an end and will no longer liven up demand. The supply of credit may remain contained given the weakness of the banks' balance sheet and the need to continue to increase their capital to cope with unrecorded losses. On the other hand, high fiscal stimulus has contributed to increasing budget deficits and raising the level of debt in a large number of countries to worrying levels, which will strongly condition the margin of fiscal policy in those countries in the most important years. Moreover, one of the risks to growth is precisely the result of a possible premature withdrawal of any fiscal stimulus with the start of significant fiscal consolidation efforts which, although necessary in several countries, should not start before 2011, as I mentioned last January and was recently stated by the European Commission. The same risks of withdrawal of exceptional measures to support the economy could, moreover, occur in the field of monetary policy. Central banks reacted by seeking to ease restrictions on the financing capacity of the financial system through large liquidity injections, significant declines in interest rates and less conventional actions, such as the widening of collateral and eligible counterparts, which has contributed to increasing the burden of central banks in financial intermediation and to the significant increase in their balance sheets and the monetary base which, for example, it has risen almost 100% in the American case and about 40% in the euro area since the beginning of the crisis. There are those who see this as a threat or a certainty of future inflation and worry about the exit from this monetary situation. It should be recalled, however, that despite the growth of the monetary base, the responsibility of central banks, credit growth and the monetary mass have been substantially reduced. In the euro area, in July the M3 aggregate was growing by only 3% and credit to companies and individuals only 1.8 %. The explanation is that there is a drop in credit demand and the balance sheet and capital difficulties of banks contribute greatly to reducing the monetary and credit multiplier. Furthermore, it should be stressed that, especially in the euro area, the withdrawal of exceptional liquidity support measures is easy to do and is technically prepared for implementation at the appropriate time. For now, inflation forecasts show figures for 2009 and 2010 well below the definition of price stability that we have adopted in the euro area and, above all, the medium and long-term expectations for inflation are well anchored within the limits of our definition. This contributes without the credibility of the Eurosystem and the fact that the negative product gap, the low degree of use of productive capacity and the wage moderation that occurs, put the European economy very far from an overheating situation that could rekindle inflationary tensions. In a way, the exit from the econic growth crisis will be slow and prolonged Although it is premature to talk about the end of the crisis, the statistical indicators released in the last few weeks show that, on a global scale, econic growth has returned to positive values, if not compared to the levels of the previous year, at least in relation to the previous quarters. This recovery also has the characteristic of being widespread, i.e. being biased simultaneously and covering both the most developed economies and emerging and developing economies. This development will not prevent, however, that for the year 2009 and for the world economy as a whole, the real rate of change will be negative. However, this negative value is essentially the result of the deep contraction in the first quarter of the year, because, as we mentioned above, the majority of economies showed positive signs of recovery, reacting to the strong monetary and fiscal stimulus implemented by the respective authorities. International trade, which will contract unprecedentedly in 2009, could also show a recovery in 2010, albeit at a much lower rate than it had been in the years before the crisis. Emerging and developing economies as a whole will be able to show a positive product change in 2009 (as opposed to what will happen in developed economies). Of course, among these, there will be countries that, either because they rely heavily on petreo or have suffered in particular the effects of the collapse of world trade or their banking systems, will still contract in 2009 and more modest recoveries in 2010. The African economies have experienced a performance worthy of highlighting in this crisis. In a way it can be said that, in several countries in this region, the crisis came before the international collapse caused by the sub-prime market, because the price increases of food and fuel occurred at the beginning of 2007 generated econic and social tenss in the countries net importing of food and energy goods than the good performance of gross domestic product growth (annual average of 6% in real terms for the period 2004-08) succeeded in softening. However, the most serious consequences are now being experienced as the sharp reduction in the price of primary goods (of which several African countries are net exporters), alongside the massive contraction of international trade, reduced foreign investment flows and emigrant remittances will lead to a marked slowdown in product growth in 2009, which may even see negative variations in some African countries, particularly those most heavily dependent on the exploitation of energy goods. The prospects for recovery of these economies for 2010 depend critically on the behaviour of the world economy and, in particular, on the recovery of international trade to levels similar to those before the crisis. The signals transmitted by the statistical data for the end of the 2nd and this quarter feed the hope that already in 2010 the world economy and, more particularly, all African countries can present a pace of growth more compatible with the ecological potential and social needs of the region. The eco-growth predicted for Africa as a whole in 2010 is thus more in line with the levels observed until 2008, thus representing a clear recovery from the very modest variation that is estimated to be recorded in 2009, despite all positive. No less important is the expectation that this growth dynamics in 2010 will extend to the majority of the countries and subregions of the continent. As far as the Portuguese economy is concerned, it should be noted that there is also an improvement in the situation compared to the forecasts of a few months ago. In the forecast published by Banco de Portugal last April, we predicted a recession of -3.5% this year and a negative growth of -0.6% n first year. At the moment, the outlook points to a lower recession this year and slightly positive growth in 2010. The performance of the Portuguese economy should therefore be slightly higher than expected for the euro area. In addition to the measures already taken to contain the effects of the crisis, it is of fundamental importance to create the necessary mechanisms to prevent new crises of this nature in the future. To this extent, efforts should be made to create a more resilient regulatory and supervisory framework that avoids the re-emergence of the weaknesses that led to the outbreak of this crisis. This effort will be truly successful if there is deep coordination at international level and, to that extent, the role of international financial institutions is key. The financial crisis revealed ineras vulnerabilities in the functioning of the international financial system, which the strong growth of the years preceding it contributed to camouflage. Optimism associated with high eco-growth and prolonged maintenance of interest rates at a historically low level have encouraged investors to seek more profitable and risk-risk financial applications. The complexity of the new financial instruments, based on particularly opaque securitisation structures, has helped to disguise the fact that the inherent risk is more concentrated than initially assumed. On the other hand, the segmentation of financial regulation and deregulation in some countries, notably in the United States, has contributed to the expansion of the unregulated financial sector (which includes investment banks, investment funds, hedge funds, etc.), leaving out the universe of regulation and supervision the market segments with higher risk and which have proved to have a much greater systemic impact than previously thought. If the crisis shows us weaknesses in the system and dogmas that we take for sure, it also creates the opportunity to reflect on a new order and new principles that should exist in the future. This is particularly noteable in this crisis and, after interventions aimed at resolving the immediate problems of the financial crisis, several initiatives have demonstrated the concern of the international community, whether at the G-20, European Union, or international organisations, to take measures aimed at reforming the international financial system and minimising the emergency hipese of future crises, at least with the characteristics it has assumed. The guidelines adopted at the g20 meeting are significant in this perspective and include: the regulation of the so-called shadow banking system; the imposition of a maximum leverage ratio between banks' capital and the balance sheet total without any risk weight; reducing the prciclic character of capital regulation and accounting rules; the transfer to organised markets of credit derivatives such as CSDs; the correction of the wrong incentives in the remuneration of grestores and traders. The most striking features of this action are, on the one hand, its high degree of coordination  which is normal in the case of a global crisis  but also the recognition of the role that international organisations, in particular the IMF, should play in its prevention and resolution and in the architecture of a new international financial system. It is important to recall here that this role has not always been recognised in previous crises. Indeed, the IMF's action in the financial crises of the 1990s was often criticised on the grounds that the large financial packages that characterised it could give rise to 'moral hazard' (i.e. adverse incentives from both debtor countries and international creditors, and may even contribute to the worsening effects of the crisis) and that the range of financial facilities at its disposal is poorly targeted at resolving balance crises capital, which became more relevant from then on. Thus, with its role redefined, there are several reforms under discussion at the IMF that aim to make the institution more suitable for the prevention and resolution of financial crises. These reforms cover all areas of their activities: the financial resources available to them, governance, financial facilities to support the crisis and the surveillance of the international monetary and financial system. Indeed, the decision of the G-20 countries at the April Summit in London, now confirmed in Pittsburg, to increase the resources available to the IMF by 750 million dares, is an indication of the role that the institution should play in resolving the crisis. The ongoing reforms in the field of governance (covering the two-year anticipation of the planned quota review, the configuration of the Executive Board, the possible transformation of the IMFC into a more active and decision-making gon), contribute to increasing the voice and representation of emerging and low-income countries, and will make the organisation more representative at the level of the global economy and, consequently more effective. Within the FRAMEWORK of imf financing facilities, several initiatives clearly reflect a concern to make the Fund's financial facilities more targeted at the individual problems and circumstances of member countries. This is reflected in the initiatives to increase member countries' access to the Fund's resources, to make such access more flexible, for example, through the new Flexible Credit Line which has replaced the need for ex-post conditionality with ex ante eligibility criteria, or to redefine cross-compliance and eliminate some elements that may contribute to the stigma sometimes associated with the Fund's programmes, such as the elimination of structural performance criteria, the non-compliance of which would have to entail a formal abdicating of the criterion or non-compliance with the IMF programme. The provision of a higher amount of resources and the reform of facilities to support low-income countries, particularly vulnerable to the financial crisis, also reflect this concern. This is illustrated by the consolidation in the Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust of the various previously existing trusts, under which three new facilities are created: the Extended Credit Facility, the Standby Credit Facility and the Rapid Gredit Facility, which replace previously existing instruments As regards the surveillance of the international financial system, the ongoing reforms are to place greater emphasis on macro-prudential and multilateral surveillance. The aim of these reforms is to better integrate macro-econic policy analysis with that of financial systems, as well as between bilateral and multilateral surveillance, thereby seeking to better identify risks, contagion problems and spillovers that led to the current crisis. While any comment on the effectiveness of all these reforms is still premature, they reflect an effort to respond to most of the problems identified as the causes of the current financial crisis and seem to reveal an unprecedented willingness to cooperate on the part of the international community. This will be put to the test in the prime times in relation to a fundamental problem not yet solved, that of so-called global macro-econic imbalances. The existence of several countries with huge external deficits in counterpoint with others with significant surpluses will not allow for balanced growth in the world economy and can easily lead to new crises in the future. The coordination of adjustment policies that solve this problem will require a degree of international cooperation that has no historical precedent. The new geopolitical reality resulting from the consecration of the G20 as the main body of global governance is a positive factor. Let us just hope that the lucidity of world leaders is up to their responsibilities. Lisbon 29 de Setembro 2009
