Em 23 de junho de 2016  trs dias depois de ter iniciado funes  os cidados do Reino Unido votaram livre e democraticamente pela sada do seu pas da Unio Europeia, tendo sido j acionado pelo governo britnico o mecanismo previsto no artigo 50. do Tratado da Unio Europeia. Trata-se de um acontecimento de enormes implicaes a todos os nveis, muito em particular para Portugal, que viu a balana europeia pender ainda mais para a Europa central, aumentando assim a nossa periferia no contexto da Unio. Fao meno a este acontecimento  cujas consequncias transcendem em muito a esfera do Banco de Portugal -, apenas para sublinhar que vivemos uma poca caracterizada no s por grandes mutaes econmicas, tecnolgicas e sociais mas tambm por profundas mudanas polticas. Perante as incertezas e indefinies estratgicas de um tempo que talvez seja demasiado novo para o que neste momento conseguimos percecionar ou queremos admitir, a ao de instituies como o Banco de Portugal  ainda mais importante para o Pas. Os desafios so, pois, imensos, quaisquer que sejam os domnios considerados. Pela minha parte, estou confiante que o Banco de Portugal se continuar a afirmar e alcanar os seus objetivos nas duras misses em que est investido a nvel nacional e no contexto europeu. 5. Num belo e curto poema, Fernando Pessoa escreveu, sob o heternimo Ricardo Reis: para ser grande, s inteiro; pe quanto s no mnimo que fazes. A grandeza de que fala o genial poeta -me seguramente inacessvel. Mas feita essa ressalva, posso prometer s Senhoras e Senhores Deputados que serei inteiro no exerccio das funes de Vice-Governador do Banco de Portugal, caso seja esse o desfecho deste processo de nomeao. Muito obrigado pela vossa ateno.

Title: Initial intervention by the Director of the Department of Prudential Supervision, Carlos Antnio Torroaes Albuquerque, in the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry into the process that led to the sale and resolution of BANIF
text: Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry into the process leading to the sale and resolution of BANIF April 28, 2016 Initial intervention by Carlos Antonio Torroaes Albuquerque Director of the Department of Prudential Supervision Mr Chairman of the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry Ladies and gentlemen Good afternoon 1. Introduction It is with great honour that I am in the presence of the Honourable Members to seek to provide the clarifications they most understand regarding Banif, in the context of my duties at Banco de Portugal. I understand it is useful to frame my performance and the performance of the Department of Prudential Supervision, which I direct throughout this process and be able to give note of the main activities that have been carried out since I started my duties at the central bank at the end of November 2014, not having sufficient knowledge about events prior to that date. I also believe it is important to note that Banco de Portugal has been part of the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM) since November 4, 2014. All supervisory actions carried out by Banco de Portugal teams are part of this new supervisory process and are monitored by the teams of the European Central Bank, in particular by confirming that the mechanisms, processes, techniques and supervisory actions comply in their respective times and to the extent that they are adapted to the rules, regulations and procedure manuals of the Single Supervisory Mechanism. Thus, in the field of supervision, Banco de Portugal and the European Central Bank, to the extent that they are integral parts of the SSM, observe the same principles and methodologies and act in a coordinated manner with information sharing in relation to the entities they supervise. 2. Prudential supervision At Banco de Portugal there is a segregation of functions between the supervisory area and the resolution area, so that the events, decisions and facts relating to the specific resolution process had no other direct participation of the Department of Prudential Supervision other than, in some parts of the process, the provision of supervisory elements to support resolution teams, functional control of this area. Prudential (micro) supervision aims to ensure that financial institutions hold sufficient capital and liquidity to withstand shocks that could affect any of these variables and that institutions are managed in a sound and secure manner. Prudential supervision monitors the position of solvency, liquidity and the internal government of the institutions in order to ensure sound and prudent management of the institutions. This is a function specifically aimed at assessing the risks that institutions incur and the capital levels needed to cover those risks and the monitoring of government and control mechanisms. In summary, the supervisory function is directed towards monitoring the fundamental balances of the banking activity of each of the institutions with a perspective of continuity of operations (going concern). 3. Banif in a financial crisis environment A financial crisis usually has three very different times. A first time of credit growth more or less sharply. A second time of disupation, with rapid stop of this growth. And a third phase of correction of previous asymmetries. In this last phase, profitability is severely degraded, with reduced business and increased unevenness. The accumulation of non-productive assets and the necessary deleveraging process increase the weight of the most risky assets on the balance sheets. In a recovery phase from the economic crisis, four factors are absolutely fundamental for banking institutions: i. the economic climate (inflation rates, economic growth levels and reference interest rates); ii. the management of the institution, in particular the ability to restructure and resize the institution according to the new characteristics of the markets and customers; iii. The ability to generate capital to absorb process losses and sustain recovery; and iv. The ability to manage the liquidity situation, in particular by maintaining sufficient clearances to ensure the continuity of financial operations. At the beginning of 2015, the economic situation was very unfavorable to the banking business (low inflation rate, low economic growth and low interest rates). The challenges were therefore great and difficult. On the other hand, the Economic and Financial Assistance Programme had set deleveraging targets for financial institutions that meant reaching a loan to deposits ratio of 120%, and credit should focus on the sectors producing tradable goods for export. In certain sectors of activity there has been a high number of insolvencies and, consequently, an increase in overdue credit. Given the country's budgetary constraints, in particular the high levels of public debt, it was not possible to make available to the financial system instruments used in other countries to improve banks' balance sheets by putting additional pressure on supervisory activity. 4. Supervisory lines of action in 2015 Supervision is not exercised in the abstract. Supervision is carried out taking into account the objectives that are to be achieved and the circumstances of each institution. Bearing these constraints in sight, the supervisory actions outlined for Banif focused on four key areas: i. First, in the permanent monitoring of capital levels and their capital ratios. On December 30, 2014, Banif submitted to Banco de Portugal a letter requesting reimbursement from the State of the last tranche of hybrid instruments of 125 M. (better known as CoCo's). However, in view of the time being made by the request under the information necessary, Banco de Portugal forwarded to Banif, by letter dated 31 December 2014, that it would not be considered. This situation constituted a breach of a structural objective of the commitments made at the time of recapitalisation, as reported in due course to the Ministry of Finance in the report monitoring the specific commitments for the 4th quarter of 2014 (submitted in March 2015), as well as in the following quarterly reports and in several communications sent to the Ministry of Finance. With reference to December 31, 2014, Banif reported, in February 2015, capital ratios close to the minimum limits (CET1 ratio and total capital of 8.4%, without repayment of CoCo's), showing a capital gap of only 34 M., well below the projected ratios in the latest version of the Restructuring Plan, dated 8 October 2014 (CET1 ratio of 8.8% and total capital ratio of 10.6%, already estimated considering the reimbursement of the last tranche of hybrid instruments of 125 M.). At the same time, the results of the stress tests conducted by Banco de Portugal in early 2015, in accordance with the guidelines of the European Banking Authority (EBA), with reference to 31 December 2013, showed an insufficient degree of capitalization of the bank to cope with adverse macroeconomic scenarios. Thus, Banco de Portugal: the. On 22 May 2015, it referred to the European Central Bank - DGMS-III, a Former Ante Notification of Financial Deterioration (Template E), noting, inter alia, the deterioration of the financial situation given the results of 2014, the results of the stress test exercise, the liquidity position and the non-payment of the CoCo's; b. On 27 May 2015, it requested banif's Board of Directors to submit a plan to strengthen capital measures, and forwarded that the institution was unable to repay the last tranche of hybrid instruments, as reported to the Ministry of Finance, by letter of 4 June 2015; c. On 6 July and 25 August 2015, Banco de Portugal reiterated to Banif its position that the plan submitted by the Bank on 16 June remained insufficient. In response, Banif requested, on 11 September 2015, that the presentation of capital enhancement measures was framed in the new draft Restructuring Plan which was in the final stages of preparation for DG-COMP (which had to be sent by 18 September). On 6 July 2015, Banco de Portugal informed Banif that it did not authorize the inclusion of the provisional positive result on June 30, 2015 in individual and consolidated own funds, as requested by Banif on June 18, 2015, taking into account that: (i) the net result achieved in the first half of 2015 resulted, essentially, from a set of non-recurring transactions and (ii) according to Banif's financial projections, the net result obtained in the first half of 2015 would be progressively consumed in the second half of the year, becoming negative at the end of the 2015 financial year, in the amount of -24.6 M. In parallel with the assessment of the capital shortfall reported to Banif on May 27, 2015, Banco Portugal also identified weaknesses in the provision of various credit holdings, real estate assets, financial holdings and deferred tax assets, as well as in the calculation of capital requirements that were generally transmitted and discussed in due course with Banif's managers, at various times of 2015. On 17 November 2015, Banco de Portugal reported to banif's Board of Directors the final results of a set of analyses carried out (of which the Ministry of Finance was reported on the same day), having determined the reinforcement of 177 M., on a consolidated basis, and the minimum reinforcement of risk-weighted assets (RWA) of 258 M., 30 November 2015. Given that the reflection of these situations would lead to a default of the estimated total consolidated capital ratio, based on the situation of 30 September 2015, Banco de Portugal determined that it would be submission, under Article 116(1c) of the General Regime of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations, within 10 days, of a capital plan to reset capital ratios above regulatory minimums, as well as demonstrate the viability and sustainability of the institution in the long term. In addition, Banif was told that it should also refrain from carrying out operations involving a deterioration of the bank's solvency position, without the prior authorization of Banco de Portugal. For other analyses carried out at the level of the capital position, Banco de Portugal reported the results of the Risk Assessment exercises of the Banif Group, with reference to 31 December 2013 (updated on 31 March 2014) and 31 December 2014 on 6 March 2015 and 30 September 2015, identifying an expressive set of deficiencies/weaknesses, having requested an action plan to regularize them. In addition, given the potential relevant impact on capital, Banco de Portugal monitored developments in the Group's real estate asset portfolio and its valuation, including portfolio valuation methodologies, and in this context determined in August 2015 the implementation of a special audit of valuation of these properties through an independent entity, which was ongoing at the time of the resolution. In addition, Banco de Portugal monitored the sales processes of subsidiaries in Malta, Brazil and Cape Verde, requesting regular points of situation and establishing contacts with the supervisory authorities of the host countries. ii. Secondly, in the daily monitoring of liquidity levels and deposit flows On a daily basis, Banco de Portugal monitored Banif's liquidity situation and projections, as well as the evolution of client deposits and the pool of collateral for eurosystem credit operations, with daily contact with Banif's treasury department. In this sense, Banif himself considered that it should maintain a liquidity buffer equal to or greater than 10% of deposits. This regular monitoring was intensified at times when the Bank's liquidity situation showed greater fragility, notably through the request for sensitivity analyses and liquidity contingency plans, in order to address the possibility of early demobilization of deposits or additional liquidity needs. As of 16 October 2015, following public references to banif's situation, the bank's liquidity situation deteriorated. Banco de Portugal reiterated to Banif the need to prepare a formal and complete Liquidity Contingency Plan. At the beginning of November, the liquidity buffer fell below 10% and requests for the indication of concrete, timed liquidity measures and their impacts intensified. Monitoring of the bank's liquidity situation was strengthened throughout November and December, and the need for liquidity retention as a priority measure by the Bank was always stressed. In December, after the known television news, the position of deposits and liquidity deteriorated very quickly and sharply. The bank no longer has collateral to access the Eurosystem and initiated the use of emergency financing (ELA). At the end of this week, Banif had virtually no collateral available, even for emergency liquidity-disingation operations (ALS) and would certainly no longer be able to survive Monday morning. iii. Thirdly, in the monitoring of restructuring plans and possible sale of the bank, including negotiations on the response process to the requirements of the EU Directorate General for Competition (DG-Comp). With regard to the restructuring plans, as has already been clarified in due course to this Commission, taking into account that their preparation was the responsibility of the Banif Board of Directors and the Ministry of Finance, Banco de Portugal's role has focused on making suggestions and comments to the plans submitted by Banif, with a view to ensuring that financial and prudential information was accurate, and in issuing opinions on specific matters, when requested by DG-COMP and the Ministry of Finance. As part of its supervisory action, Banco de Portugal monitored and monitored banif's implementation of the main measures of the different aspects of the Capitalization Plan and critically analyzed the financial projections, within the scope of the Financing and Capital Plans, identifying their execution risks and reporting timely and in detail to the Ministry of Finance possible deviations. As for the role of Banco de Portugal in the presentation by Banif of the response to the formal in-depth investigation process of DG-COMP, in line with the action followed since the beginning of the negotiation of the Restructuring Plan, Banco de Portugal followed, without directly interfering, the relationship between Banif and the Portuguese State with DG-COMP, having participated in the Steering meetings of the new restructuring plan project prepared jointly with external consultants N1, always seeking to meet the established response deadlines, a situation that has been the case. Additionally, in early 2015, Banco de Portugal issued a specific determination to implement the government model of the core and non-core units, reinforced in March of the same year. Banif was subsequently advised to speed up the voluntary sale process it had underway. This accelerated sale process of "Clean Bank" was conducted by banif's Board of Directors. Banco de Portugal also participated in steering meetings to keep track of the development of the process, having no involvement on the conditions of a possible transaction. In the end, there was no intervention by the supervisory area in the reception or analysis of the proposals that will have been addressed to Banif. iv. Fourth, the monitoring of the preparation of contingency strategies that could respond to disruptive events of the bank's activity. In the first half of 2015, alternative scenarios were considered that could be triggered due to specific contingency events. Subsequently, in September 2015, a task force was set up, coordinated by the resolution area, in which contingency scenarios were studied to address the risks of a deterioration in banif's prudential situation. With greater or lesser intensity, these were the determining lines of the monitoring of Banif by the Department of Prudential Supervision of Banco de Portugal in 2015. Despite the rigorous and diligent monitoring carried out, the specific circumstances of the bank and the constraints of the moment, including the absence of a restructuring plan approved by the Directorate General for Competition, together with the constraints resulting from the institutional framework and European regulations, the rapid and marked deterioration of the liquidity position from 13 December 2015 and the non-implementation of the voluntary sale process, led to the deliberation of the Banif resolution measure. 5. The relationship with the General Directorate of Competition It is important to clarify a little more contacts with the European Union's Directorate-General for Competition in 2015. With regard to prudential supervision, in this period, in addition to a telephone conference attended by members of the Department of Prudential Supervision, related to the issue of confidentiality regarding the causes of the investigation by the Directorate-General for Competition, I must highlight, for their importance, two face-to-face contacts with that entity that I had, on behalf of the Department. The first face-to-face contact took place on October 8, when I accompanied the delegation of the Ministry of Finance and Banif (an administrator and an N1 representative) to present the restructuring plan for the contours paper of the Directorate General of Competition. The second contact took place on November 17, at a meeting in which I asked several questions to the Directorate General for Competition to better understand the follow-up of the Banif process in the near future. At the first meeting, my presence was as an observer, both of the presentation by the elements of Banif and n1 of the restructuring plan prepared by this entity, or of the technical discussion of the same by the members of the Directorate General for Competition, who had received the document in advance. As a result, the Directorate General for Competition said that it would immediately request an additional set of information and details of the project in order to be able to analyze, line by line (an expression used by the technicians of the General Directorate of Competition), the evolution of the business and the support of the project to ensure that the "clean" bank would be viable. At this meeting, which had fundamentally technical contours, my only intervention happened at the end, when I mentioned that Banco de Portugal understood that, at that time, this seemed to be the best solution, bearing in mind the need to preserve financial stability in the country. It was clear that Banif should work to clarify and explain to the Directorate-General for Competition some key aspects of the proposal. The second meeting took place on November 17, 2015 and was attended by other members of Banco de Portugal and the participation by telephone of a representative of the Ministry of Finance. At this meeting, I tried, in particular, to obtain an indication of the perception of the Directorate-General for Competition on the possible developments in the Banif case and of the adjustments which it considered to be important so that the restructuring process to be presented, following the questions which DG-Comp itself had sent at the end of October, could be accepted. At this meeting, the representatives of the Directorate General for Competition clearly said: With regard to Banif, which was not worth continuing with the discussion of a restructuring plan, even with amendments, as it should not be approved by the Directorate General for Competition; Banif would have to be put into resolution before the end of the year, which is the only solution they understood possible; Who, alternatively and in response to a question of mine, did not see public recapitalisation very viable, even though they did not denied it at all; As for the possibility of moving forward with the sale of the "good" part of Banif, noting a number of entities that had already expressed interest in the institution, they said, in short, that it would be necessary to know the more specific contours of this possibility, that it would be necessary to prove the feasibility of the solution, that the sale would have to involve some cash payment, even if low, that the sale process should be very simple and straightforward and that Banif should disappear before the end of the year. These were the key messages that immediately led banif to be informed that the sale process that had already begun should be accelerated and completed by 18 December, in order to avoid the consequences of a potential resolution in 2016, with the bail in necessarily involving the absorption of losses by ordinary creditors (integrating depositors not guaranteed by the Guarantee Fund in this capacity Deposits). This sales process was fully led by Banif, its directors and the n1 consultant and accompanied by Banco de Portugal, mainly with the objectives of ensuring compliance with the deadlines established and the fundamental steps for it to develop in the terms mentioned above. 6. Conclusion These are, in general terms, the aspects that seem to me most important in the activity of prudential supervision in the Banif case, specifically in 2015. I would like to end by reinforcing the following aspects of this process: Banif had special recovery difficulties because there were deviations in the economic assumptions of the recapitalisation plan, given its banking business portfolio, with liquidity, profitability and solvency positions to be degraded successively; Banif did not show the capacity to strengthen equity through its private shareholders and suffered from numerous constraints on the additional use of public capital; and The Bank's overall reputation has deteriorated in a context of progressively less positive public perception of its soundness, significantly increasing the risk of disruptive events to its liquidity position; In this context, the work of supervision had as fundamental objectives (i) to monitor the solvency position, (ii) to continuously monitor the liquidity position, (iii) to boost the restructuring and negotiation process with the Directorate General for Competition and (iv) to monitor the work of the team that, at the same time, was preparing the contingency plans for responding to the risks that Banif faced. It should also be noted that all the activities carried out by the supervision of the Banif situation were made known to all relevant stakeholders: Ministry of Finance, ECB-SSM, international and national supervisory authorities and state representatives in the administration of Banif. Analyses and due diligence of various natures were carried out (several capital and liquidity contingency plans were requested and scrutinized and specific recommendations and determinations were issued), bearing in mind the defense of the public money involved, the protection of depositors and the defense of financial stability in the country, within the functional, property and legal and regulatory restrictions of the institution. And it is very important to note that all the action of supervision was carried out within the framework of the delegated powers and with the aim of safeguarding the stability of the financial system. I am naturally at the disposal of the Commission and the ladies and gentlemen on the issues they deem to be. Thank you very much.
text_original: Comisso Parlamentar de Inqurito ao processo que conduziu  venda e resoluo do BANIF 28 de abril de 2016 Interveno inicial de Carlos Antnio Torroaes Albuquerque Diretor do Departamento de Superviso Prudencial Senhor Presidente da Comisso Parlamentar de Inqurito Senhoras e Senhores Deputados Boa Tarde, 1. Introduo  com muita honra que estou na presena dos Senhores Deputados para procurar prestar os esclarecimentos que melhor entenderem relativamente ao Banif, no mbito das minhas funes no Banco de Portugal. Entendo ser til enquadrar a minha atuao e a atuao do Departamento de Superviso Prudencial, que dirijo, em todo este processo e poder dar nota das principais atividades que foram sendo executadas desde que iniciei as minhas funes no banco central no final de novembro de 2014, no tendo conhecimento suficiente sobre acontecimentos anteriores quela data. Entendo ainda ser importante dar nota de que o Banco de Portugal integra o Mecanismo nico de Superviso (MUS) desde o dia 4 de novembro de 2014. Todas as aes de superviso executadas pelas equipas do Banco de Portugal se inserem neste novo processo de superviso e so acompanhadas pelas equipas do Banco Central Europeu, nomeadamente atravs da confirmao de que os mecanismos, processos, tcnicas e aes de superviso obedecem nos respetivos tempos e na medida da sua adequao s normas, regulamentos e manuais de procedimentos do Mecanismo nico de Superviso. Desta forma, no domnio da superviso, o Banco de Portugal e o Banco Central Europeu, na medida em que so partes integrantes do MUS, observam os mesmos princpios e metodologias e atuam de forma coordenada com partilha de informaes relativamente s entidades por si supervisionadas. 2. Superviso prudencial No Banco de Portugal existe uma segregao de funes entre a rea de superviso e a rea de resoluo, pelo que os acontecimentos, as decises e os factos relativos ao processo especfico de resoluo no tiveram outra participao direta do Departamento de Superviso Prudencial que no fosse, em algumas partes do processo, a disponibilizao de elementos da superviso para apoio s equipas de resoluo, com controlo funcional desta rea. A superviso (micro) prudencial tem como objetivo assegurar que as instituies financeiras detm capital e liquidez suficientes para resistir a choques que possam afetar alguma destas variveis e que as instituies sejam geridas de forma slida e segura. A superviso prudencial acompanha a posio de solvabilidade, de liquidez e o governo interno das instituies por forma a assegurar uma gesto s e prudente das mesmas. Trata-se de uma funo especialmente dirigida  avaliao dos riscos que as instituies incorrem e dos nveis de capital necessrios para cobrir esses riscos e  monitorizao dos mecanismos de governo e controlo. Em resumo, a funo de superviso  dirigida para o acompanhamento dos equilbrios fundamentais da atividade bancria de cada uma das instituies numa perspetiva de continuidade das operaes (going concern). 3. O Banif num ambiente de crise financeira Uma crise financeira tem normalmente trs tempos muito distintos. Um primeiro tempo de crescimento do crdito de forma mais ou menos acentuada. Um segundo tempo de disrupo, com paragem rpida desse crescimento. E uma terceira fase de correo das assimetrias anteriores. Nesta ltima fase, a rendibilidade degrada-se de forma acentuada, com reduo do negcio e aumento das imparidades. A acumulao de ativos no produtivos e o necessrio processo de desalavancagem fazem crescer o peso dos ativos de maior risco nos balanos. Numa fase de recuperao da crise econmica, quatro fatores so absolutamente fundamentais para as instituies bancrias: i. A conjuntura econmica (taxas de inflao, nveis de crescimento econmico e taxas de juro de referncia); ii. A gesto da instituio, nomeadamente a capacidade de restruturar e redimensionar a instituio em funo das novas caractersticas dos mercados e dos clientes; iii. A capacidade de gerar capital para absorver as perdas do processo e sustentar a recuperao; e iv. A capacidade de gerir a situao de liquidez, designadamente atravs da manuteno de folgas suficientes para assegurar a continuidade das operaes financeiras. No incio de 2015, a conjuntura econmica apresentava-se com caractersticas muito desfavorveis ao negcio bancrio (baixa taxa de inflao, baixo crescimento econmico e baixas taxas de juro). Os desafios eram, por isso, grandes e difceis. Por outro lado, o Programa de Assistncia Econmica e Financeira tinha estabelecido objetivos de desalavancagem s instituies financeiras que implicavam atingir um rcio crdito/depsitos (loan to deposits) de 120%, devendo o crdito concentrar-se nos setores produtores de bens transacionveis dirigidos  exportao. Em determinados setores de atividade assistiu-se a um nmero elevado de insolvncias e, consequentemente, a um aumento do crdito vencido. Dadas as restries oramentais do pas, nomeadamente os elevados nveis de dvida pblica, no foi possvel colocar  disposio do sistema financeiro instrumentos utilizados noutros pases que permitissem melhorar os balanos dos bancos, colocando uma presso adicional sobre a atividade de superviso. 4. Linhas de ao da superviso em 2015 A superviso no se exerce no abstrato. A superviso  exercida tendo em conta os objetivos que se querem alcanar e as circunstncias prprias de cada instituio. Tendo presentes estes condicionalismos, as aes de superviso delineadas para o Banif concentraram-se em quatro domnios fundamentais: i. Em primeiro lugar, no acompanhamento permanente dos nveis de capital e dos respetivos rcios de fundos prprios. O Banif apresentou ao Banco de Portugal, no dia 30 de dezembro de 2014, uma carta a solicitar o reembolso ao Estado da ltima tranche de instrumentos hbridos de 125 M. (mais conhecidos por CoCos) . Contudo, tendo em conta que o pedido em apreo no se encontrava instrudo com a informao necessria, o Banco de Portugal transmitiu ao Banif, por carta datada de 31 de dezembro de 2014, que o mesmo no seria considerado. Esta situao constitua um incumprimento de um objetivo estrutural dos compromissos assumidos aquando da recapitalizao, conforme oportunamente reportado ao Ministrio das Finanas no relatrio de acompanhamento dos compromissos especficos, referente ao 4. trimestre de 2014 (submetido em maro de 2015), bem como nos relatrios trimestrais seguintes e em diversas comunicaes enviadas ao Ministrio das Finanas. Com referncia a 31 de dezembro de 2014, o Banif reportou, em fevereiro de 2015, rcios de capital prximos dos limites mnimos (rcio CET1 e capital total de 8,4%, sem reembolso dos CoCos), evidenciando uma folga de capital de apenas 34 M., bastante abaixo dos rcios projetados na ltima verso do Plano de Reestruturao, datada de 8 de outubro de 2014 (rcio CET1 de 8,8% e rcio de capital total de 10,6%, j estimados considerando o reembolso da ltima parcela dos instrumentos hbridos de 125 M.). Paralelamente, os resultados dos testes de esforo conduzidos pelo Banco de Portugal, no incio de 2015, de acordo com as orientaes (guidelines) da Autoridade Bancria Europeia (EBA), com referncia a 31 de dezembro de 2013, evidenciaram um grau de capitalizao do banco insuficiente para fazer face a cenrios macroeconmicos adversos. Assim, o Banco de Portugal: a. Em 22 de maio de 2015, remeteu ao Banco Central Europeu - DGMS-III, uma Ex-ante Notification of Financial Deterioration (Template E), dando nota, designadamente, da deteriorao da situao financeira dados os resultados de 2014, os resultados do exerccio de stress test, a posio de liquidez e o no pagamento dos CoCos; b. Em 27 de maio de 2015, solicitou ao Conselho de Administrao do Banif a apresentao de um plano de reforo de medidas de capital, tendo transmitido que a instituio no se encontrava em condies de reembolsar a ltima tranche de instrumentos hbridos, conforme foi dado conhecimento ao Ministrio das Finanas, por carta de 4 de junho de 2015; c. Em 6 de julho e 25 de agosto de 2015, o Banco de Portugal reiterou ao Banif a sua posio de que o plano apresentado pelo Banco em 16 de junho continuava a ser insuficiente. Em resposta, o Banif solicitou, a 11 de setembro de 2015, que a apresentao das medidas de reforo de capital fosse enquadrada no novo projeto de Plano de Reestruturao que se encontrava em fase final de preparao para a DG-COMP (que tinha de ser enviado at 18 de setembro). Em 6 de julho de 2015, o Banco de Portugal informou o Banif de que no autorizava a incluso do resultado positivo provisrio a 30 de junho de 2015 nos fundos prprios individuais e consolidados, conforme solicitado pelo Banif a 18 de junho de 2015, tendo em conta que: (i) o resultado lquido atingido no primeiro semestre 2015 resultava, essencialmente, de um conjunto de operaes no recorrentes e (ii) de acordo com as projees financeiras do Banif, o resultado lquido obtido no primeiro semestre de 2015 seria progressivamente consumido no segundo semestre, tornando-se negativo no final do exerccio de 2015, no montante de -24,6 M. Em paralelo com a avaliao da insuficincia de capital, comunicada ao Banif em 27 de maio de 2015, o Banco Portugal identificou tambm insuficincias no provisionamento de diversas exposies creditcias, ativos imobilirios, participaes financeiras e ativos por impostos diferidos, bem como no clculo de requisitos de capital que, de um modo geral, foram oportunamente transmitidas e discutidas com os responsveis do Banif, em diversos momentos de 2015. Em 17 de novembro de 2015, o Banco de Portugal comunicou ao Conselho de Administrao do Banif os resultados finais de um conjunto de anlises efetuadas (dos quais foi dado conhecimento, no mesmo dia, ao Ministrio das Finanas), tendo determinado o reforo de imparidades de 177 M., em base consolidada, e o reforo mnimo de ativos ponderados pelo risco (RWA) de 258 M., com referncia a 30 de novembro de 2015. Tendo em conta que o reflexo destas situaes conduziria a um incumprimento do rcio de capital total consolidado estimado, com base na situao de 30 de setembro de 2015, o Banco de Portugal determinou a apresentao, ao abrigo do artigo 116. 1 c) do Regime Geral das Instituies de Crdito e das Sociedades Financeiras, no prazo de 10 dias, de um plano de capital para repor os rcios de capital acima dos mnimos regulamentares, bem como demonstrar a viabilidade e sustentabilidade da instituio no longo prazo. Alm disso, foi comunicado ao Banif que deveria ainda abster-se de realizar operaes que implicassem uma deteriorao da posio de solvabilidade do banco, sem a prvia autorizao do Banco de Portugal. Relativamente a outras anlises efetuadas ao nvel da posio de capital, o Banco de Portugal comunicou os resultados dos exerccios de avaliao de risco (Risk Assessment) do Grupo Banif, com referncia a 31 de dezembro de 2013 (atualizado a 31 de maro de 2014) e a 31 de dezembro de 2014, em 6 de maro de 2015 e 30 de setembro de 2015, identificando um conjunto expressivo de deficincias/fragilidades, tendo solicitado um plano de ao para as regularizar. Alm disso, dado o potencial impacto relevante no capital, o Banco de Portugal acompanhou a evoluo da carteira de ativos imobilirios do Grupo e a respetiva valorizao, incluindo as metodologias de avaliao dos imveis em carteira, tendo, neste mbito, determinado, em agosto de 2015, a execuo de uma auditoria especial de avaliao destes imveis atravs de uma entidade independente, que estava em curso no momento da deliberao de resoluo. Adicionalmente, o Banco de Portugal acompanhou os processos de venda das filiais em Malta, Brasil e Cabo Verde, solicitando pontos de situao regulares e estabelecendo contactos com as autoridades de superviso dos pases de acolhimento. ii. Em segundo lugar, no acompanhamento dirio dos nveis de liquidez e dos fluxos de depsitos Numa base diria, o Banco de Portugal monitorizava a situao e projees de liquidez do Banif, bem como a evoluo dos depsitos de clientes e da pool de ativos de garantia para as operaes de crdito do Eurosistema, existindo um contacto dirio com a rea de tesouraria do Banif. Neste sentido, o prprio Banif considerou que deveria manter um buffer de liquidez igual ou superior a 10% dos depsitos. Este acompanhamento regular era intensificado em momentos em que a situao de liquidez do Banco evidenciava maior fragilidade, nomeadamente atravs do pedido de anlises de sensibilidade e planos de contingncia de liquidez, para fazer face  eventualidade de desmobilizao antecipada de depsitos ou a necessidades adicionais de liquidez. A partir de 16 de outubro de 2015, na sequncia de referncias pblicas  situao do Banif, verificou-se uma deteriorao da situao de liquidez do banco. O Banco de Portugal reiterou ao Banif a necessidade de preparao de um Plano de Contingncia de Liquidez formal e completo. No incio do ms de novembro, o buffer de liquidez desceu abaixo dos 10% e intensificaram-se os pedidos de indicao de medidas de liquidez concretas, calendarizadas e respetivos impactos. O acompanhamento da situao de liquidez do banco foi reforado ao longo dos meses de novembro e dezembro, tendo sido sempre salientada a necessidade de reteno da liquidez como medida prioritria por parte do Banco. Em dezembro, aps as notcias televisivas conhecidas, a posio de depsitos e de liquidez deteriorou-se de forma muito rpida e acentuada. O banco deixou de dispor de colaterais para aceder ao Eurosistema e iniciou o recurso aos financiamentos de emergncia (ELA). No final dessa semana, o Banif praticamente no possua colaterais disponveis, mesmo para operaes de cedncia de liquidez de emergncia (ELA) e, seguramente, j no teria possibilidade de sobreviver  manh de segunda-feira. iii. Em terceiro lugar, no acompanhamento dos planos de restruturao e de possvel venda do banco, incluindo as negociaes do processo de resposta aos requisitos da Direo Geral da Concorrncia da eu (DG-Comp). Relativamente aos planos de reestruturao, conforme j foi oportunamente clarificado a esta Comisso, tendo em conta que a respetiva elaborao era da responsabilidade do Conselho de Administrao do Banif e do Ministrio das Finanas, o papel do Banco de Portugal centrou-se na apresentao de sugestes e comentrios aos planos submetidos pelo Banif, tendo em vista assegurar que a informao financeira e prudencial era exata, e na emisso de opinies sobre matrias especficas, quando solicitado pela DG-COMP e pelo Ministrio das Finanas. No mbito da sua ao de superviso, o Banco de Portugal acompanhou e fiscalizou a execuo pelo Banif das principais medidas das diferentes vertentes do Plano de Capitalizao e analisou criticamente as projees financeiras, no mbito dos Planos de Financiamento e de Capital, identificando os respetivos riscos de execuo e reportando tempestivamente e de uma forma detalhada ao Ministrio das Finanas eventuais desvios. Quanto ao papel do Banco de Portugal na apresentao pelo Banif da resposta ao processo formal de investigao aprofundada da DG-COMP, em linha com a atuao seguida desde o incio da negociao do Plano de Reestruturao, o Banco de Portugal acompanhou, sem interferir diretamente, o relacionamento do Banif e do Estado Portugus com a DG-COMP, tendo participado nas reunies de Steering do novo projeto de Plano de Reestruturao elaborado em conjunto com os consultores externos N+1, procurando sempre que fossem respeitados os prazos de resposta estabelecidos, situao que se veio a verificar. Adicionalmente, no incio de 2015, o Banco de Portugal emitiu uma determinao especfica para implementar o modelo de governo das unidades core e no core, reforado em maro deste mesmo ano. Posteriormente, o Banif foi aconselhado a acelerar o processo de venda voluntria que tinha em curso. Este processo de venda acelerada do Clean Bank foi conduzido pelo Conselho de Administrao do Banif. O Banco de Portugal participou tambm nas reunies de Steering para se manter informado sobre o desenvolvimento do processo, no tendo qualquer envolvimento sobre as condies de uma eventual transao. No houve, no final, qualquer interveno da rea de superviso na receo ou na anlise das propostas que tero sido endereadas ao Banif. iv. Em quarto lugar, o acompanhamento da preparao de estratgias de contingncia que pudessem responder a eventos disruptivos da atividade do banco. No primeiro semestre de 2015, foram equacionados cenrios alternativos que pudessem ser acionados em funo de eventos especficos de contingncia. Posteriormente, em setembro de 2015, foi constituda uma task force, coordenada pela rea de resoluo, no mbito da qual foram estudados cenrios de contingncia para fazer face aos riscos de uma deteriorao da situao prudencial do Banif. Com maior ou menor intensidade, foram estas as linhas determinantes do acompanhamento do Banif pelo Departamento de Superviso Prudencial do Banco de Portugal no ano de 2015. Apesar do acompanhamento rigoroso e diligente efetuado, as circunstncias especficas do banco e os condicionalismos do momento, nomeadamente a ausncia de um plano de restruturao aprovado pela Direo Geral da Concorrncia, juntamente com os constrangimentos resultantes do enquadramento institucional e da regulamentao europeia, a deteriorao rpida e acentuada da posio de liquidez a partir de 13 de dezembro de 2015 e a no concretizao do processo de venda voluntria, conduziram  deliberao da medida de resoluo do Banif. 5. O relacionamento com a Direo Geral da Concorrncia Importa clarificar um pouco mais os contactos com a Direo Geral da Concorrncia da Unio Europeia no ano de 2015. No que diz respeito  superviso prudencial, neste perodo, alm de uma conferncia telefnica a que assistiram elementos do Departamento de Superviso Prudencial, relacionada com a questo da confidencialidade relativa s causas da investigao aprofundada pela Direo Geral da Concorrncia, cumpre-me destacar, pela sua importncia, dois contactos presenciais com aquela entidade que eu tive, em representao do Departamento. O primeiro contacto presencial teve lugar no dia 8 de outubro, quando acompanhei a delegao do Ministrio das Finanas e do Banif (um administrador e um representante da N+1) para apresentao do plano de restruturao de resposta ao contours paper da Direo Geral da Concorrncia. O segundo contacto teve lugar no dia 17 de novembro, numa reunio em que coloquei vrias questes  Direo Geral da Concorrncia para melhor entender o seguimento do processo do Banif nos tempos mais prximos. Na primeira reunio, a minha presena foi de observador, quer da apresentao por parte dos elementos do Banif e da N+1 do plano de restruturao preparado por esta entidade, quer da discusso tcnica do mesmo pelos elementos da Direo Geral da Concorrncia, que tinham recebido por antecipao o documento. Como resultado, a Direo Geral da Concorrncia referiu que iria solicitar de imediato um conjunto adicional de informao e de detalhes do projeto de forma a poder analisar, linha a linha (expresso utilizada pelos tcnicos da Direo Geral da Concorrncia), a evoluo do negcio e o suporte ao projeto para garantir que o banco limpo seria vivel. Nesta reunio, que teve contornos fundamentalmente tcnicos, a minha nica interveno aconteceu no final, quando referi que o Banco de Portugal entendia que, naquele momento, aquela parecia ser a melhor soluo, tendo presente a necessidade de preservao da estabilidade financeira no pas. Ficou claro que o Banif deveria trabalhar no sentido de clarificar e explicar  Direo Geral da Concorrncia alguns aspetos fundamentais da proposta. A segunda reunio teve lugar no dia 17 de novembro de 2015 e contou com a participao de outros elementos do Banco de Portugal e com a participao por telefone de representante do Ministrio das Finanas. Nesta reunio, procurei, fundamentalmente, obter indicao da perceo da Direo Geral da Concorrncia sobre a possvel evoluo do caso Banif e dos ajustamentos que esta entidade entendia serem importantes para que o processo de restruturao a apresentar, na sequncia das questes que a prpria DG-Comp enviara no final de outubro, pudesse ser aceite. Nesta reunio, os representantes da Direo Geral da Concorrncia referiram, com toda a clareza: Relativamente ao Banif, que no valia a pena continuar com a discusso de um plano de restruturao, mesmo com alteraes, pois no deveria ser aprovado pela Direo Geral da Concorrncia; O Banif teria de ser colocado em resoluo antes do final do ano, sendo esta a nica soluo que entendiam possvel; Que, em alternativa e em resposta a uma pergunta minha, no viam com muita viabilidade a recapitalizao pblica, apesar de no a terem negado em absoluto; Quanto  possibilidade de se avanar com a venda da parte boa do Banif, dando nota de um conjunto de entidades que j haviam manifestado interesse na instituio, referiram, em resumo, que haveria que conhecer os contornos mais especficos desta possibilidade, que haveria que provar a viabilidade da soluo, que a venda teria de envolver algum pagamento em dinheiro, ainda que baixo, que o processo de venda deveria ser muito simples e direto e que o Banif deveria desaparecer antes do final do ano. Foram estas as mensagens fundamentais que levaram a que, de imediato, se tenha informado o Banif de que o processo de venda que j tinha sido iniciado deveria ser acelerado e concludo at ao dia 18 de dezembro, de forma a evitar as consequncias de uma potencial resoluo em 2016, com o bail in que envolveria necessariamente a absoro de perdas pelos credores comuns (integrando-se nesta qualidade os depositantes no garantidos pelo Fundo de Garantia de Depsitos). Este processo de venda foi integralmente liderado pelo Banif, seus administradores e pela consultora N+1 e acompanhado pelo Banco de Portugal, fundamentalmente com objetivos de garantia de cumprimento dos prazos estabelecidos e dos passos fundamentais para que o mesmo se desenvolvesse nos termos antes referidos. 6. Concluso Estes so, em termos gerais, os aspetos que me parecem mais importantes na atividade da superviso prudencial no processo Banif, especificamente no ano de 2015. Gostava de terminar reforando, os seguintes aspetos sobre este processo: O Banif apresentava especiais dificuldades de recuperao, por ter havido desvios nos pressupostos econmicos do plano de recapitalizao, dada a sua carteira de negcio bancrio, com as posies de liquidez, de rendibilidade e de solvabilidade a degradarem-se sucessivamente; O Banif no evidenciava capacidade de reforo dos capitais prprios com recurso aos seus acionistas privados e sofria de inmeros constrangimentos ao recurso adicional a capitais pblicos; e A reputao geral do Banco foi-se deteriorando num contexto de perceo pblica progressivamente menos positiva face  sua solidez, aumentando significativamente o risco de manifestao de eventos disruptivos para a sua posio de liquidez; Neste contexto, o trabalho da superviso teve como objetivos fundamentais (i) acompanhar a posio de solvabilidade, (ii) monitorar em permanncia a posio de liquidez, (iii) dinamizar o processo de restruturao e de negociao com a Direo Geral da Concorrncia e (iv) acompanhar o trabalho da equipa que, paralelamente, se encontrava a preparar os planos de contingncia de resposta aos riscos que o Banif enfrentava. De realar ainda que de toda a atividade desenvolvida pela superviso sobre a situao do Banif foi dado conhecimento a todas as partes interessadas relevantes: Ministrio das Finanas, BCE-MUS, autoridades de superviso congneres internacionais e nacionais e representantes do Estado na administrao do Banif. Foram efetuadas anlises e diligncias de vria natureza (foram pedidos e escrutinados diversos planos de capital e de contingncia de liquidez e foram emitidas recomendaes e determinaes especficas), tendo presente a defesa dos dinheiros pblicos envolvidos, a proteo dos depositantes e a defesa da estabilidade financeira no pas, dentro das restries funcionais, patrimoniais e legais e regulamentares da instituio. E  muito importante referir que toda a atuao da superviso foi efetuada no quadro dos poderes delegados e com o objetivo da salvaguarda da estabilidade do sistema financeiro. Fico naturalmente  disposio da Comisso e das Senhoras e dos Senhores Deputados para as questes que entenderem colocar. Muito obrigado.

Title: Initial intervention of Governor Carlos da Silva Costa at the Annual Hearing of the Governor of Banco de Portugal by the Committee on Budget, Finance and Public Administration
text: Annual Hearing of the Governor of Banco de Portugal by the Committee on Budget, Finance and Public Administration May 30, 2014 Initial Intervention of Governor Carlos da Silva Costa Mr President, Ladies and gentlemen, At the beginning of the month, Banco de Portugal released its annual activity and accounts report for 2013. This document assumes particular relevance in that it marks the end of the implementation period of the Strategic Plan adopted by the Bank for 2011-2013 and the beginning of a new strategic cycle. The report therefore contains, in addition, the usual accountability for the reference year, an assessment of the work carried out in the last three years. On the occasion of this hearing, Banco de Portugal released a statement this morning highlighting the main points of this report. In addition, the annual report of the Board of Directors on the Portuguese Economy was released last Wednesday. At the time of the conclusion of the Economic and Financial Adjustment Programme, which began in mid-2011, and given that the detailed analysis of 2013 had already been the subject of previous publications, the annual report presents a medium-term analysis of the Portuguese economy and the ongoing adjustment process. In the same vein, I also chose to focus this initial intervention on the ongoing adjustment process. I will begin by taking a, necessarily not exhaustive, assessment of the results obtained in the framework of the implementation of the Programme. Secondly, I will set out the issues which I consider to be priorities for the coming years, in view of the path we still have to follow. Finally, I will address an issue that underlies the recurrent crises of the Portuguese economy  the absence of an intertemporal perspective of economic policies  which needs to be resolved in order to definitively break the cycles of progress and setbacks in our economic development. I will end with a very brief reference to the accounts of Banco de Portugal, which I will have the opportunity to develop in response to the questions that you agree to ask. I would also like to mention that the reports of the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal  on the activity and accounts and on the Portuguese economy  were delivered this morning to the Shareholders' Assembly of the Republic, with a request for distribution to the members of COFAP. The latest editions of the financial stability and behavioral supervision reports produced by Banco de Portugal were also distributed. This initial intervention will, as usual, be made available on the Banco de Portugal website. 1. The adjustment of the Portuguese economy The interruption of market financing has made it unfeasible to correct the macroeconomic imbalances accumulated in the Portuguese economy since the mid-1990s. This correction could be done in two ways: or abruptly, in a scenario of forced cessation of payments, with extremely burdensome economic and social costs; or in a gradual and orderly manner, with the financing needs provided by international creditors, through conditionality. The Economic and Financial Adjustment Programme, negotiated with the European Union and the International Monetary Fund, has ensured the predictability of financing over the past three years, as part of a strategy to restore the balance of external accounts and regain the confidence of international investors, thereby ensuring the return to market financing on regular terms. The adjustment strategy was based on three pillars: (i) the structural correction of the imbalance in public finances; (ii) the deleveraging of the economy in a framework of financial stability; (iii) The preparation and implementation of a wide range of structural reforms to remove the main barriers to economic growth. At the end of the Program, it is worth taking stock of the results of its implementation. In this regard, I'd leave three notes. The first note is to highlight the remarkable progress in correcting the main macroeconomic imbalances in the Portuguese economy. We are witnessing the rebalancing of external accounts. The current and capital account rose from a deficit of 9.5% of GDP in 2010 to a surplus of 2.6% in 2013. This adjustment was overall similar to that observed in the previous stabilisation agreements with the IMF of 1977 and 1983, despite the absence of the exchange rate instrument and much lower growth in external demand (Figure 1). Economic operators reacted quickly to the change in incentives. Individuals have significantly reduced consumption and increased the savings rate. In turn, companies reoriented the production of goods and services to the foreign market. Although exports have not grown as much as in previous adjustment episodes, there has been an increase in market shares. The accumulated gains in market share between 2011 and 2013 amounted to about 12 p.p. when increasing their exports above external demand, Portuguese companies showed a remarkable capacity to react to adverse changes and demonstrated the fundamental role of non-price competitiveness factors. This is very important from the perspective of economic and monetary union, because it shows that it is possible to correct imbalances in external accounts in a single currency framework. A frequent question is to the extent to which, in a context of recovery of domestic demand, there will not be a reversal of the share gains recorded in recent years. In that regard, it should be in mind that an export decision requires undertakings to invest resources. Empirical evidence suggests that, when the return on this investment is favorable, companies tend not to abandon their export activity, even in a context of recovery of domestic demand. However, it is essential to pursue the structural reforms necessary to strengthen and support the transition to an export-oriented sustainable economic growth model (Figure 2). In addition, the significant adjustment of the budgetary balance should be highlighted. The general government deficit fell from 9.8% of GDP in 2010 to 4.9% in 2013 and the primary balance recorded an improvement of 6.4 p.p. of GDP, with a value close to balance (-0.6% of GDP) (Table 1) in 2013. The accumulated revenue and expenditure contributions to fiscal consolidation in this period were of similar magnitude. This adjustment is remarkable if we make an international comparison and also compare well with what happened in 1983-1985 (Figure 3). Despite progress in the evolution of the budget balance, government debt increased by 35 p.p. of GDP between 2010 and 2013 to 129% in 2013. The most important contribution to this increase is the result of adjustments to the stock of gross debt without counterpart in the deficit, mainly related to the accumulation of financial assets. In cumulative terms, the value of these deficit-debt adjustments amounted to about 15 per cent of GDP, highlighting the accumulation of government deposits and the impact of the issue of contingent capital instruments in the capitalisation processes of a number of national banks. A second very relevant contribution to the increase in debt was interest expenditure, 12.6 percent of GDP over the three-year period. Finally, the effects of the primary deficit and the change in nominal GDP have also contributed, even to a lesser extent, to the increase in the debt ratio. The second note I would highlight is that the adjustment occurred in a particularly adverse macroeconomic framework which aggravated the already high level of unemployment. The significant reduction in household spending reflected the contraction in disposable income  which in three years fell to the level observed in 2004/2005  and the impact of restrictive conditions of access to credit and the high level of indebtedness on the ability to smooth consumption (Figure 4). In fact, domestic expenditure contracted more than in previous programmes, with the most noticeable difference in the behavior of private consumption (Graph 5). In contrast to previous adjustments, the savings rate of households has increased, reaching highs since the beginning of the euro area. This evolution suggests that the shock over disposable income was perceived as permanent. Indeed, the absence of the phenomenon of monetary illusion has contributed to a lower revision of the expectations of permanent income of private actors, which has accelerated and increased the impact of policy measures on domestic spending. In the previous adjustments, the monetary illusion allowed a large redistribution of wealth silently: holders of monetary assets and those with fixed incomes lost purchasing power, but, as nominal yields increased, they did not immediately notice  let alone anticipate  the loss in real terms. In an "anesthetic" process of this type, the reaction of private demand tends to be less intense and immediate than in a process in which citizens find that their income is falling (Graph 6). The sharp contraction in domestic demand, the perception that this contraction was persistent and the adjustment of the previous production structure  a sector not oversized tradable relative to the tradable sector  resulted in a very significant increase in unemployment. In 2013, the average unemployment rate stood at 16.3 percent. The increase in unemployment affected all age groups, but was particularly pronounced in young people. It should be noted that recent developments in unemployment are part of a trend of increased unemployment since 2000, which shows structural dysfunctions and misadjustments between supply and demand for work. Estimates from Banco de Portugal point to a very high structural unemployment rate of around 11%. The third note is that, despite very demanding internal and external conditions, the stability of the financial system has been preserved. The strategy that Banco de Portugal had been pursuing since 2010 to ensure stability and strengthen the resilience of the financial system was incorporated and deepened under the Adjustment Programme. The objectives of this strategy were: strengthening the solvency of banks, protecting the liquidity of the system, strengthening monitoring and supervision of the banking system and improving the regulatory framework. As a result of its implementation, the Portuguese banking system is currently more capitalized, has a more favorable liquidity position and is more transparent. We currently benefit from better supervision and a more robust regulatory framework. 2. The way to go It is clear that in the last three years much progress has been made. But it is also clear that there remain a number of weaknesses that need to be addressed. In my view, the priorities of action in the coming years are as follows:  Absorption of structural unemployment. The solution to this serious problem necessarily depends on the restructuring of the economy and the additional transfer of resources from the non-tradable sector to the tradable sector. The transfer of human capital is not instantaneous: it requires economically viable investments and the adequacy of workers who are currently unemployed to the qualification requirements of those same investments. That is, this process will take time, certainly much more than desirable in view of the impact of unemployment on individuals and on society. For this reason, mechanisms need to be strengthened to mitiguate the effects of adjustment on the cohesion of Portuguese society and mechanisms to support the requalification of the long-term unemployed.  Improving the financial autonomy of non-financial companies. Portuguese companies have very high leverage ratios. In 2012, the level of financial autonomy of non-financial companies was, on average, 30% and the weight of interest on the cash flow generated was more than 50% (Table 2). High levels of corporate indebtedness are an obstacle to investment. It is therefore essential to develop financial instruments to strengthen the financial autonomy of undertakings, in particular through the conversion of debt into capital, and to define an economic policy framework, in particular tax, which favours the interest in opening up and increasing the share capital of enterprises.  Improved bank profitability. In a context of prolonged recession in economic activity and low short-term interest rates, banks' profitability has been under great pressure. Improving profitability requires banks to act on several fronts. On the one hand, they must find ways to reduce the proportion of old assets with low interest rate differentials (mortgage credit), thereby freeing up liquidity for new activity. On the other hand, rationalisation efforts to reduce operating costs should be pursued with determination. Finally, they should actively seek strategic investors who can bring new capital to institutions.  Continuation of the fiscal consolidation process. To this end, an agreement between the main political forces on the trajectory of public finances is critical. The level of Portuguese government debt makes us particularly vulnerable to adverse economic shocks and abrupt changes in risk perception in international financial markets. Therefore, there is no room for complacency in the continuation of the budgetary adjustment. As I have already mentioned in previous public interventions, strict compliance with our European budgetary commitments ensures a sustainable path to public debt, even in a conservative macroeconomic scenario. However, the budgetary effort still required is significant and the temporary measures that have had to be taken as a matter of urgency must give way to permanent measures. To this end, it is necessary, on the one hand, a concertation of political actors around effective reform of the State and the budgetary procedure and, on the other hand, in order for the measures to be socially accepted, they must be transparent and fair and it is important to explain them well to the Portuguese. 3. The need for an intertemporal perspective of public policies The absence of an intertemporal perspective of public policy is a persistent feature of our history and has been at the root of the recurring economic and financial crises we have faced. In fact, there seems to be a chronic inability of Portuguese society to adopt policies and to bind itself to rules that continuously ensure the sustainability of public accounts and external accounts and levels of competitiveness compatible with the safeguarding of employment. The macroeconomic costs of unsustainable policies are very high and well known, resulting in cycles of stops and growth resumes that condition the pace and sustainability of the economic development process. But bad economic policies also have high micro-economic costs because they generate a poor allocation of resources - capital and labour - and give rise to the insolvency of economic agents who have been led by the wrong signals. The economic policy options taken by public decision-makers show signals to economic actors and significantly influence their decisions, in particular investment decisions. The conduct of unsustainable economic policies induces decisions of economic actors who, although supported by micro-economic rationality, are compromised in the long term by the absence of macroeconomic rationality. This is the case for many investments that were made before the current crisis in the non-tradable sector  for example, construction and trade  which were based on an unsustainable policy of continued expansion of credit-financed domestic demand. It should be made in mind that the individual and social costs that arise from this, although less visible, are very high and often not reversible. This clearly illustrates the importance of the social responsibility of economic policy makers. Political actors should consider in decisions the future implications of the various options, not only at macro level but also at a micro-economic level. This means that, in the wake of the pattern of recurrent crises, it is essential to agree collective rules that anchor incentives towards the long-term sustainability of immediate options. And it is necessary to integrate these rules into an institutional framework that promotes and ensures the political and social mediation necessary for their continued observance. * As I mentioned initially, and since I would not like to exceed the time allocated to me for this initial intervention, I will leave detailed comments on banco de Portugal's activity and accounts to the question and answers session. However, I cannot fail to make a very brief reference to the financial results of 2013. At the end of 2013, Banco de Portugal's total balance sheet was 111,592 million. The decrease of around 7.8 billion compared to 2012 was mainly due to the significant decrease in the market price of gold and the sharp decrease in the amount of liquidity in monetary policy operations at Banco de Portugal level, the overall amount of which fell to 47 864 million (52 784 million in 2012), reflecting lower refinancing needs of the national banking system with the Eurosystem. Net income for the 2013 financial year was 253 million (449 million in 2012), following a 130 million transfer to the general risk provision. The decrease in the result compared to 2012 was mainly due to the decrease in the interest margin (resulting from the reduction in average annual income rates and average balances of monetary policy assets) and the increase in unrealised losses (mainly resulting from negative exchange rate revaluation differences and the devaluation of the price of euro trading portfolio securities). The result obtained allowed a distribution of dividends to the State of 202 million. It should be noted that, in the last six years, Banco de Portugal has transferred to the State, in taxes and dividends, an average annual value of 287 million euros.
