Verificaram-se, no entanto, alteraes nos riscos de balano do Banco, resultantes da variao da dimenso da carteira, da sua composio e dos riscos dos ativos subjacentes. Antes da deciso do Conselho do BCE de criao do PSPP, em 2015, o Banco de Portugal assegurava a cobertura integral dos riscos financeiros determinados pela referida metodologia harmonizada. Em 2015, o Banco manteve o objetivo de cobertura integral dos riscos financeiros do seu balano, excluindo o PSPP. Considerando as especificidades do novo programa de poltica monetria, o Banco de Portugal definiu um objetivo de cobertura mnima dos riscos deste programa. Em 2016, o volume da carteira do PSPP no balano do Banco de Portugal aumentou em 11 253 milhes, ascendendo a 21 357 milhes. No entanto, o risco associado, decorrente da aplicao da metodologia harmonizada do Eurosistema, no aumentou proporcionalmente, permitindo que o reforo da proviso fosse de apenas 200 milhs. O valor acumulado da proviso associado a este programa representava em 2016 cerca de 16% do valor total da proviso para riscos gerais e menos de 3% do volume total do PSPP, na componente de ttulos governamentais. De referir que o risco de mercado subjacente ao PSPP, na componente de ttulos governamentais, ganha relevncia dada a sua natureza de instrumento de poltica monetria, decidida pelo Conselho de Governadores do BCE. Esta especificidade implica que as aquisis e eventuais vendas de ttulos estejam associadas  orientao da poltica monetria, sendo efetuadas independentemente das condies de mercado. Assinale-se, a este propito, que, no final de 2016, o valor latente das menos valias relacionadas com esta carteira, valorizada a preos de mercado, era de 1092 milhs. De referir ainda que, na medida em estes ativos de longo prazo foram financiados com as responsabilidades TARGET, remuneradas com taxas de curto prazo, a margem financeira gerada tender a reduzirse ou mesmo a tornar-se negativa,  medida que ocorra a normalizao da poltica monetria. O resultado antes do reforo da proviso para riscos gerais e de impostos aumentou 46 milhes relativamente a 2015, ascendendo a 850 milhes. Este aumento deveuse, essencialmente:  Ao incremento da margem de juros (+223 milhes de euros), devido, em grande parte, ao aumento do valor dos juros dos ttulos detidos para fins de poltica monetria (em particular do PSPP na componente de ttulos governamentais), que mais que compensou a reduo generalizada das taxas de juro mdias anuais;  Ao aumento do resultado lquido da repartio do rendimento monetrio (+88 milhs de euros). Estes efeitos foram parcialmente compensados pela reduo dos resultados realizados em operaes financeiras. O resultado apurado em 2016 possibilitou uma distribuio de dividendos ao Estado de 352 milhes (186 milhes em 2015). O valor total de dividendos e impostos referentes a 2016 ascende a 527 milhes (277 milhes, em 2015). Muito obrigado. Estou  disposio dos Senhores Deputados para responder s quests que considerem pertinentes.

Title: Initial intervention by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in the Committee on Budget and Finance and Administrative Modernization
text: Committee on Budget and Finance and Administrative Modernization (COFMA) April 27, 2016 Initial intervention by Governor Carlos da Silva Costa1 1 Prepared for presentation. Madam President of COFMA, Ladies and gentlemen, 0 Banco de Portugal was invited, on March 25, to submit its comments to the Bills: No. 52/XIII/1st - CFP: Prohibits banks from unilaterally changing interest rates and other contractual conditions; No. 90/XIII/1  BE: Establishes the obligation for banking institutions to fully reflect euribor's decline in housing and consumer credit agreements; No. 83/XIII/1st - BE: Ensures the gratuity of the base account; No. 92/XIII/1  CFP: Determines the obligation of credit institutions to provide a standard ispitude account, called the "base account", and prohibits the collection of commissions, expenses or other charges for the services provided under that account. Following the hearing of March 29, in which the directors of the Departments of Prudential and Behavioral Supervision were present, Banco de Portugal explained in writing its position, in a letter addressed to the Minister of Finance on April 5 and also transmitted to COFMA. In addition, in response to the request made on 12 April by this Commission, Banco de Portugal yesterday provided information on the possible effects on the financial system arising from the legislative changes under discussion, in particular those relating to the use of negative interest rates. My initial intervention will be short, as Banco de Portugal's position on this matter is already well known. The credit market Portuguese, based predominantly on variable rate contracts, was put in a new situation from the moment euribor rates became consistently negative. 3-month interest rates have become negative as of April 2015. Rates at 6 months  the main indexing  became negative from November 2015, while negative 12-month rates only took place from February this year. This situation threatened the sustainability of the financial intermediation function and jeopardised the onerous nature of the market loan, as provided for in Article 395 of the Commercial Code. The impact of the level of interest rates on banks' financial margins is a complex issue that is being considered in several international institutions and banco de Portugal. Despite the complexity of the theme, one aspect that seems indisputable is that the fall in market interest rates further harms the financial margins of banks than, like the Portuguese: Have a higher weight of credits with indexed rate in total loans to individuals (more than 90 percent in the case Portuguese); Deposits are more important in the financing structure (the ratio of credit to deposits is around 102 per cent, significantly lower than the 158 per cent recorded in 2010). It is important to note that deposit rates are more resistance to the decline than credit interest rates. On the one hand, the deposit fees are only updated during the period of their maturity. On the other hand, the fall in deposit interest rates is limited by the proximity of the so-called zero lower bound. In fact, Portuguese legislation does not cover the application of negative interest rates to bank deposits, so there is an asymmetry between the formation of active and passive rates which calls into question the sustainability of the financial intermediation function. Furthermore, changing the legal limitation of deposit rates would not be advisable, given the present levels of savings of households and the need to ensure the financing of the economy through the banking intermediation of savings. The decline of indexers to negative values also brought about an apparent regulatory conflict. In the absence of legislative changes, interest rates are framed by two normative principles. On the one hand, the provisions of Article 3 of Decree-Law No. 240/2006 and Articles 1 and 3 of Decree-Law No. 171/2007 implies the need to comply with the conditions laid down for determining the interest rate in credit and financing contracts, in particular with regard to the use of agreed indexers. Moreover, the possible practice of negative interest calls into question the abovementioned principle of the costof the market loan. In the current context, it is for the legislator to consider the different interests in the present and to clarify the doubts that have been raised, in particular as to the admissibility of negative remuneration of credit agreements, bearing in mind that easier solutions to implement in the short term can sometimes generate irreversible costs in the medium and long term. Seeking a solution that promotes the balance between the sustainability of the financial intermediation function and the existing legal framework, Banco de Portugal suggested to the Minister of Finance, in the letter of April 5, that the consecration of legal provision be considered that distinguish between existing contracts and new contracts. Like this: (a) for ongoing credit and financing contracts, an obligation should be laid down for credit institutions to apply an interest rate of zero where the sum of the indexing to the contractually fixed margin or spread results in a negative interest rate; (b) For credit and financing contracts to be concluded in the future, contractual freedom should continue to be favoured, and it is worth considering the possibility of legislation requiring the use of an indexvalue of zero in cases where that indexer is negative (thus ensuring that the interest rate of these transactions will be, at least equal to the spread). Also in relation to credit agreements to be concluded in the future, the possibility of constructing an alternative indexer, representative of the average remuneration of deposits in the banking system of the Portuguese. In fact, in the current context, Euribor is not a good indicator of the financing cost of Portuguese banks, since, as mentioned, this financing is predominantly based on the collection of deposits. I end by reiterating the willingness of Banco de Portugal to collaborate in the discussion of these or other legislative changes that may be decided and that have an impact on the financial system. Thank you very much. Lisbon, 27 April 2016
text_original: Aro.wmf Aro.wmf Aro.wmf Comisso de Oramento e Finanas e Modernizao Administrativa (COFMA) 27 de abril de 2016 Interveno inicial do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa1 1 Preparado para apresentao. Senhora Presidente da COFMA, Senhoras e Senhores Deputados, 0 Banco de Portugal foi convidado, no passado dia 25 de maro, a apresentar os seus comentrios aos Projetos de Lei:  N. 52/XIII/1  PCP: Probe os bancos de alterarem unilateralmente taxas de juro e outras condies contratuais;  N. 90/XIII/1.  BE: Institui a obrigatoriedade de as instituies bancrias refletirem totalmente a descida da Euribor nos contratos de crdito  habitao e ao consumo;  N. 83/XIII/1.  BE: Assegura a gratuitidade da conta base;  N. 92/XIII/1  PCP: Determina a obrigatoriedade de as instituies de crdito disponibilizarem uma conta de depsito  ordem padronizada, designada de conta base, e probe a cobrana de comisses, despesas ou outros encargos pelos servios prestados no mbito dessa conta. Dando seguimento  audio de 29 de maro, na qual estiveram presentes os diretores dos Departamentos de Superviso Prudencial e Comportamental, o Banco de Portugal explicitou por escrito a sua posio, em carta dirigida ao Senhor Ministro das Finanas no passado dia 5 de abril e tambm transmitida  COFMA. Adicionalmente, em resposta ao pedido efetuado em 12 de abril por esta Comisso, o Banco de Portugal remeteu ontem informao relativa aos eventuais efeitos sobre o sistema financeiro decorrentes das alteraes legislativas em discusso, em particular das relacionadas com a utilizao de taxas de juro negativas. A minha interveno inicial ser curta, uma vez que a posio do Banco de Portugal nesta matria  j conhecida. O mercado do crdito portugus, assente predominantemente em contratos de taxa varivel, foi colocado perante uma situao nova a partir do momento em que as taxas Euribor passaram a ser consistentemente negativas. As taxas de juro a 3 meses tornaram-se negativas a partir de abril de 2015. As taxas a 6 meses  principal indexante  tornaram-se negativas a partir de novembro de 2015, enquanto taxas a 12 meses negativas apenas se verificaram a partir de fevereiro deste ano. Esta situao veio ameaar a sustentabilidade da funo de intermediao financeira e pr em causa o carter de onerosidade do mtuo mercantil, conforme disposto no artigo 395. do Cdigo Comercial. O impacto do nvel das taxas de juro na margem financeira dos bancos  um assunto complexo, que est a ser objeto de estudo em vrias instituies internacionais e no Banco de Portugal. Apesar da complexidade do tema, um aspeto que parece indiscutvel  o de que a descida das taxas de juro de mercado prejudica mais as margens financeiras dos bancos que, como os portugueses:  Apresentam um maior peso dos crditos com taxa indexada no total dos crditos a particulares (superior a 90 por cento no caso portugus);  Apresentam uma maior importncia dos depsitos na estrutura de financiamento (o rcio entre crdito e depsitos situa-se em cerca de 102 por cento, significativamente inferior aos 158 por cento registados em 2010).  importante notar que as taxas dos depsitos tm mais resistncia  descida do que as taxas de juro do crdito. Por um lado, a atualizao das taxas dos depsitos apenas  efetuada no perodo do seu vencimento. Por outro, a descida das taxas de juro dos depsitos est limitada pela proximidade do designado zero lower bound. De facto, a legislao portuguesa no contempla a aplicao de taxas de juro negativas aos depsitos bancrios, pelo que h uma assimetria entre a formao de taxas ativas e passivas que pe em causa a sustentabilidade da funo de intermediao financeira. Acresce que a alterao da limitao legal das taxas dos depsitos no seria recomendvel, dados os presentes nveis de poupana das famlias e a necessidade de garantir o financiamento da economia atravs da intermediao bancria da poupana. A descida dos indexantes para valores negativos fez tambm emergir um aparente conflito normativo. Na ausncia de alteraes legislativas, as taxas de juro so enquadradas por dois princpios normativos. Por um lado, o disposto no artigo 3. do Decreto-Lei n. 240/2006 e nos artigos 1. e 3. do Decreto-Lei n. 171/2007 implica a necessidade de cumprimento das condies estabelecidas para a determinao da taxa de juro nos contratos de crdito e de financiamento, nomeadamente no que se refere  utilizao dos indexantes acordados. Por outro lado, a eventual prtica de juros negativos coloca em causa o j referido princpio da onerosidade do mtuo mercantil. No atual contexto, cabe ao legislador ponderar os diferentes interesses em presena e clarificar as dvidas que tm sido suscitadas, em particular quanto  admissibilidade de remunerao negativa dos contratos de crdito, tendo presente que solues mais fceis de implementar no curto prazo podem, por vezes, gerar custos irreversveis a mdio e longo prazos. Procurando uma soluo que promova o equilbrio entre a sustentabilidade da funo de intermediao financeira e o quadro legal existente, o Banco de Portugal sugeriu ao Senhor Ministro das Finanas, na carta do dia 5 de abril, que fosse ponderada a consagrao de disposio legal que distinguisse entre contratos existentes e novos contratos. Assim: (a) Para os contratos de crdito e de financiamento em curso, deveria estabelecer-se a obrigao de as instituies de crdito aplicarem uma taxa de juro igual a zero sempre que da soma do indexante  margem ou spread contratualmente fixado resulte uma taxa de juro negativa; (b) Relativamente aos contratos de crdito e de financiamento a celebrar no futuro, deve continuar a privilegiar-se a liberdade contratual, valendo a pena equacionar a possibilidade de legislao que exija a utilizao de um valor de indexante igual a zero nos casos em que esse indexante assuma valores negativos (assegurando-se, assim, que a taxa de juro destas operaes ser, pelo menos, igual ao spread). Ainda em relao aos contratos de crdito a celebrar no futuro, poderia tambm equacionar-se a possibilidade de construo de um indexante alternativo, representativo da remunerao mdia dos depsitos no sistema bancrio portugus. De facto, no contexto atual, a Euribor no  um bom indicador do custo do financiamento dos bancos portugueses, uma vez que, como referido, esse financiamento assenta predominantemente na captao de depsitos. Termino reiterando toda a disponibilidade do Banco de Portugal em colaborar na discusso destas ou de outras alteraes legislativas que venham a ser decididas e que tenham impacto no sistema financeiro. Muito obrigado. Lisboa, 27 de abril 2016

Title: Initial intervention of Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in the Eventual Commission of Parliamentary Inquiry to the performance of the XXI Constitutional Government in relation to the appointment and resignation of the Administration of Dr. Antnio Domingues
text: Eventual Committee of Parliamentary Inquiry to the performance of the XXI Constitutional Government in relation to the appointment and resignation of the Administration of Dr. Antonio Domingues June 5, 2017 Initial Intervention of Governor Carlos da Silva Costa1 1 Prepared for presentation. Mr President Ladies and gentlemen In this brief initial intervention I would like to leave four notes clarifying the role of Banco de Portugal in the process that is the subject of this Committee of Inquiry, 1. The first note concerns the appointment of the Administration of Dr. Antonio Domingues The proposal to appoint the members of the corporate bodies of Caixa Geral de Depositos (CGD) is the responsibility of its shareholder  the State. And the authorisation for the performance of functions has been, since the entry into operation of the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM) on 4 November 2014, under the responsibility of the European Central Bank (ECB). In this process, Banco de Portugal's participation corresponds, generally, to the following:  Banco de Portugal is the entry point of notifications of credit institutions to inform about the appointment or renewal of a member of the management body;  Banco de Portugal collaborates with the ECB in collecting all the information and documentation necessary for the process;  The Bank also collaborates with the Joint Supervisory Team in assessing the suitability of members of the governing bodies (such as the analysis of the documents received, the consultation of local registers and contact with other national authorities);  Finally, through participation in the joint supervisory team, the Bank supports the SSM services in the preparation of a proposal for a decision which is subsequently subject to consideration by the SSM Supervisory Board and approval by the Governing Council. The ECB very recently published (last May) a document entitled "Guide to adequacy and suitability assessments" which provides a detailed description of the whole process and which you can consult2. 2 . From what I have just mentioned, it is clear that Banco de Portugal does not play any decision-making role in the process of appointing cgd's management bodies. This function belongs to the ECB, as well as all related documents and information. Also within this point, I take the opportunity to provide some chronological data:  On April 19, 2016, Dr. Antonio Domingues informed me that he had been invited to the position of Chairman of the Board of Directors of CGD, but did not provide additional information on the subject;  Formal notification for the purpose of authorisation with a view to the commencing of duties by candidates for members of cgd's governing bodies was entered into the BdP on 22 July 2016;  On 17 August 2016 (4 weeks later), the ECB communicated its decision to CGD and Banco de Portugal. 2. My second note of clarification is about the hiring process of Dr. Antonio Domingues Banco de Portugal was not involved, nor did it have, within the framework of its legal powers, any intervention in the process of hiring Dr. Antonio Domingues and his team, nor in the negotiations that led to it. This is a matter of the exclusive sphere of competence of the Portuguese, CGD and the members of its Administration. 3. My third note refers to cgd's strategic and recapitalisation plan Cgd's strategic and recapitalisation plan agreed between the Portuguese State and the European Commission is not covered by the State aid scheme and therefore did not call for an opinion from Banco de Portugal (as with other cases in the past). Banco de Portugal was informed about the plan in question:  In some face-to-face meetings with Dr. Antonio Domingues (as listed already sent to this Commission);  And through their participation in the SSM; 4. The fourth and final note relates to the provision of information by Banco de Portugal to this Commission On this issue I would like to reinforce some points already transmitted in the correspondence exchanged with this Commission, namely that the provision of information by Banco de Portugal on CGD is conditioned by the following factors:  First, CGD is a bank in full activity, so Banco de Portugal is bound by the duty of professional secrecy established in Article 80 of the General Regime of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations. The duty of secrecy of supervision subjects everyone as they perform or have exercised functions at Banco de Portugal to the duty not to disclose or use information whose knowledge comes exclusively from the performance of those functions. It should be noted that the secrecy of supervision is not intended to protect private interests, but rather a public interest linked to the exercise of the supervisory function, and is enshrined in the European Directives on the exercise of this function in the banking sector. Banco de Portugal is therefore obliged not to disclose the documents in its possession and relate to the assessment of the suitability of the members of cgd's management. Personal data collected in the context of the authorisation process for the performance of duties may only be transmitted to third parties with the authorisation of their holders.  Secondly, since the prudential supervision of CGD is carried out directly by the SSM (and Banco de Portugal is reserved for the exercise of ecb's co-adivetion functions), the information collected under the institution's supervision and the supervisory measures taken are the responsibility of the ECB. Thus, regardless of whether Banco de Portugal can keep in its archives documentation relating to CGD after November 2014, that documentation relates to decisions of the ECB and their access is governed by European standards. In those rules governing access to ECB documents, it is expressly stated that: "the ECB shall have the right to protect the documents exchanged in the framework of its cooperation with national central banks, competent national authorities, designated national authorities and other relevant authorities and bodies" [Decision ECB/2015/1] Only the ECB can assess the conditions under which any access to the required documentation may be provided.  Finally, with regard to the suggestion made by this Commission to consult in terms that preserve the confidentiality of the documentation, Banco de Portugal considers that, in certain specific and exceptional situations, duly justified, there may be grounds for such consultation (as I suggested at the cofma hearing, concerning a situation of serious public disinformation on the content of certain documents prior to the SSM). In the specific case of CGD, and for the reasons I have mentioned, the consultation of confidential information and the conditions thereof will depend on an assessment by the ECB. Thank you very much.
text_original: Comisso Eventual de Inqurito Parlamentar  atuao do XXI Governo Constitucional no que se relaciona com a nomeao e a demisso da Administrao do Dr. Antnio Domingues 5 de junho de 2017 Interveno Inicial do Governador Carlos da Silva Costa1 1 Preparado para apresentao. Senhor Presidente Senhoras e Senhores Deputados Nesta breve interveno inicial gostaria de deixar quatro notas de clarificao do papel do Banco de Portugal no processo que  objeto desta Comisso de Inqurito, 1. A primeira nota diz respeito  nomeao da Administrao do Dr. Antnio Domingues A proposta de designao dos membros dos rgos sociais da Caixa Geral de Depsitos (CGD)  da responsabilidade do seu acionista  o Estado. E a autorizao para o exerccio de funes , desde a entrada em funcionamento do Mecanismo nico de Superviso (MUS), em 4 de novembro de 2014, da responsabilidade do Banco Central Europeu (BCE). Neste processo, a participao do Banco de Portugal corresponde, genericamente, ao seguinte:  O Banco de Portugal  o ponto de entrada das notificaes das instituies de crdito a informar sobre a designao ou reconduo de um membro do rgo de administrao;  O Banco de Portugal colabora com o BCE na recolha de toda a informao e documentao necessria ao processo;  O Banco colabora ainda com a equipa conjunta de superviso (Joint Supervisory Team) na avaliao da adequao dos membros dos rgos sociais (o que envolve, por exemplo, a anlise dos documentos recebidos, a consulta dos registos locais e o contacto com outras autoridades nacionais);  Finalmente, por via da participao na equipa conjunta de superviso, o Banco apoia os servios do MUS na preparao de uma proposta de deciso que , subsequentemente, sujeita  apreciao pelo Conselho de Superviso do MUS e  aprovao pelo Conselho do BCE. O BCE publicou muito recentemente (em maio passado) um documento intitulado Guia para as avaliaes da adequao e idoneidade que apresenta uma descrio detalhada de todo o processo e que os Senhores Deputados podero consultar2. 2 https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/ecb/pub/pdf/ssm.fap_guide_201705.pt.pdf. Do que acabei de referir, resulta claro que o Banco de Portugal no desempenha qualquer funo decisria no processo de designao dos rgos de administrao da CGD. Essa funo pertence ao BCE, assim como todos os documentos e informao relacionados. Ainda no mbito deste ponto, aproveito para fornecer alguns dados cronolgicos:  No dia 19 de abril de 2016, o Dr. Antnio Domingues informou-me que tinha sido convidado para o cargo de Presidente do Conselho de Administrao da CGD, no tendo no entanto prestado informao adicional sobre o assunto;  A notificao formal para efeitos de autorizao com vista ao incio de funes por parte dos candidatos a membros dos rgos sociais da CGD deu entrada no BdP no dia 22 de julho de 2016;  No dia 17 de agosto de 2016 (4 semanas depois), o BCE comunicou a sua deciso  CGD e ao Banco de Portugal. 2. A minha segunda nota de clarificao  sobre o processo de contratao do Dr. Antnio Domingues O Banco de Portugal no esteve envolvido, nem teve, no quadro das suas competncias legais, qualquer interveno no processo da contratao do Dr. Antnio Domingues e da sua equipa, nem nas negociaes que conduziram  mesma. Trata-se de uma matria da exclusiva esfera de competncia do Estado Portugus, da CGD e dos membros da respetiva Administrao. 3. A minha terceira nota refere-se ao plano estratgico e de recapitalizao da CGD O plano estratgico e de recapitalizao da CGD acordado entre o Estado portugus e a Comisso Europeia, no est coberto pelo regime das ajudas de estado, no tendo, por conseguinte, exigido a emisso de um parecer do Banco de Portugal (como aconteceu com outros casos no passado). O Banco de Portugal foi sendo informado sobre o plano em causa:  Em algumas reunies presenciais com o Dr. Antnio Domingues (conforme lista j remetida a esta Comisso);  E atravs da sua participao no MUS; 4. A quarta e ltima nota prende-se com a prestao de informao pelo Banco de Portugal a esta Comisso Sobre esta questo pretendo reforar alguns pontos j transmitidos na correspondncia trocada com esta Comisso, designadamente que a prestao de informao pelo Banco de Portugal sobre a CGD se encontra condicionada pelos seguintes fatores:  Em primeiro lugar, a CGD  uma instituio bancria em plena atividade, pelo que o Banco de Portugal se encontra vinculado pelo dever de segredo profissional estabelecido no artigo 80. do Regime Geral das Instituies de Crdito e Sociedades Financeiras. O dever de segredo de superviso sujeita todos quanto exeram ou tenham exercido funes no Banco de Portugal ao dever de no divulgarem nem utilizarem informaes cujo conhecimento lhes advenha exclusivamente do exerccio dessas funes. Note-se que o segredo de superviso no tem por objetivo proteger interesses privados, mas sim um interesse publico ligado ao exerccio da funo de superviso, e encontra-se consagrado nas diretivas europeias relativas ao exerccio desta funo no setor bancrio. O Banco de Portugal est assim obrigado a no divulgar os documentos que estejam na sua posse e digam respeito  apreciao da idoneidade dos membros da administrao da CGD. Os dados pessoais recolhidos no mbito do processo de autorizao para o exerccio de funes apenas podem ser transmitidos a terceiros com autorizao dos seus titulares.  Em segundo lugar, sendo a superviso prudencial da CGD efetuada diretamente pelo MUS (ficando reservado ao Banco de Portugal o exerccio de funes de coadjuvao do BCE), as informaes recolhidas no mbito da superviso da instituio e as medidas de superviso tomadas so da responsabilidade do BCE. Assim, e independentemente de o Banco de Portugal poder conservar nos seus arquivos documentao respeitante  CGD posterior a novembro de 2014, essa documentao diz respeito a decises do BCE e o respetivo acesso rege-se por normas europeias. Nestas normas, que regulam o acesso aos documentos do BCE,  expressamente referido que: "o BCE deve ter o direito de proteger os documentos trocados no mbito da sua cooperao com os bancos centrais nacionais, as autoridades nacionais competentes, as autoridades nacionais designadas e outras autoridades e organismos relevantes" [Deciso BCE/2015/1] S o BCE pode avaliar as condies em que um eventual acesso  documentao requerida pode ser facultado.  Por ltimo, relativamente  sugesto feita por esta Comisso de realizao de uma consulta em termos que preservem a confidencialidade da documentao, o Banco de Portugal considera que, em determinadas situaes especficas e excecionais, devidamente justificadas, poder existir fundamento para tal consulta (como sugeri na audio na COFMA, a propsito de uma situao de grave desinformao pblica sobre o contedo de certos documentos anteriores ao MUS). No caso concreto da CGD, e pelas razes que referi, a consulta de informao confidencial e as condies da mesma depender de uma apreciao do BCE. Muito obrigado.

Title: Initial intervention of Governor Carlos da Silva Costa in the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry into the process that led to the sale and resolution of BANIF
text: Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry into the process leading to the sale and resolution of BANIF April 5, 2016 Initial Intervention of Governor Carlos da Silva Costa1 1 Prepared for presentation. Mr President Ladies and gentlemen On December 20, 2015 Banco de Portugal applied a resolution measure to BANIF in accordance with Article 145e of the RGICSF. This measure consisted of: - In the sale of most of its assets and liabilities to Banco Santander Totta (BST); - In the transfer of a set of assets to Oitante, asset management vehicle created for this purpose; - On the stay in BANIF (which will be the subject of future liquidation) of a very restricted set of assets, shareholder positions and subordinated credits and related parties. The resolution measure was taken in an environment of urgency and the absence of viable alternative solutions that would ensure the continuity of the provision of essential financial services by BANIF, protect the savings entrusted to the bank through its retail network and preserve the stability of the financial system Portuguese. In order to understand the option of resolution vis-up to the only available alternative, settlement, it will be necessary to take into account not only the higher settlement cost but, above all, the systemic importance of BANIF. In fact, BANIF was the seventh largest banking group Portuguese, with a consolidated net asset of 12 billion euros (about 7% of GDP), customer deposits of 6.8 billion euros and 2 224 employees (September 2015 data). BANIF's activity was mainly focused on the provision of retail banking services in the domestic market, in the small and medium-sized enterprises segment and in private customers. Despite having a share of only 3.2% of total assets in the Portuguese banking market, it was a leader in the autonomous regions of the Azores and Madeira, with market shares of about 45% and 28% in deposits and credit, respectively. Banif thus had a unique role in financing the island economy, which is why a possible interruption of the services provided by it would necessarily have serious impacts in those regions. In order to frame this resolution decision, I think it is important to take note of the main developments related to BANIF from its capitalisation with public funds to the implementation of the resolution measure: I will begin by explaining what led to the need for public capitalization of BANIF; I will then discuss the main developments in the period following capitalisation with public funds, with a particular focus on the monitoring carried out by Banco de Portugal as a prudential supervisory authority; I will explain the resolution process later; And I will conclude by sharing with the Commission some reflections and concerns raised by experience with this process. I. What led to the recapitalisation of BANIF with public funds Throughout 2011 and 2012, the financial situation of the BANIF Group deteriorated sharply, and the Group did not reach the required core tier 1 ratio on a consolidated basis, with reference to 31 December 2011. The deterioration of BANIF's financial situation resulted from the combination of several factors: (i) Rapid credit growth in the years prior to the crisis, without adequate risk management and concentrating on real estate assets and SME credits (in 2012, banif's deposit credit ratio was 134%, compared with a banking system average of 128%); (ii) a very heavy operating cost structure compared to the activity carried out, which was not unrelated to the policy of expansion of branches and overseas holdings pursued by BANIF (in 2012 BANIF had a cost-to-income ratio of 178%, which compared with about 60% in the banking system as a whole); (iii) the recognition of a very significant volume of comparities (approximately EUR 500 million), following, first, the cross-sectional inspection exercises conducted in 2011 and 2012 (SIP  Special Inspections Program and OIP - On-Site Inspections Program) and, secondly, the special audit to BANIF carried out in 2012; (iv) The highest capital requirements imposed by Banco de Portugal on the banking system, with the setting of minimum Core Tier 1 ratios of 9% for the end of 2011 and 10% for the end of 2012 (anticipating the implementation of some of the main basel III recommendations); (v) and the deterioration of the country's economic and financial situation, with an impact on the volume and quality of the business, as well as on the risk of the credit portfolio. In view of this capital shortfall, Banco de Portugal determined in May and June 2012: - The submission by BANIF of a restructuring plan aimed at re-resuming prudential ratios above the required minimum, with a significant participation of private investors; - The adoption of measures to reorganize the group, including simplification of the structure and reduction of entities and activities not essential to the banking business; - The implementation by BANIF of corrective measures, with emphasis on limiting exposure to group entities, shareholders and related entities. Faced with the incapacity revealed by private shareholders to ensure the strengthening of the necessary capital or to attract other private investors, Banco de Portugal began to consider different alternative scenarios to deal with the situation of BANIF. Thus, capitalization scenarios using public funds, resolution and settlement were analyzed. According to the calculations made at the time, the liquidation of BANIF would lead to the payment of deposits covered by the Deposit Guarantee Fund (in the amount of EUR 4500 million) and to a significant risk of loss of uncovered deposits (amounting to EUR 2700 million). For its part, the resolution scenario, which was based on the creation of a transitional bank, would require a total financial effort of between EUR 2 500 million and EUR 4 600 million, depending on whether a more or less conservative estimate of the valuation of the transferred assets was considered. It was, on the other hand, a solution that had not yet been tested and involved significant operational risks, as well as risks of litigation by shareholders and other unprotected creditors, as is the case in any resolution process. Moreover, and more importantly, in the recessionary and uncertain economic environment in which we were, any of the options would imply a disruption in the confidence of depositors that could have devastating effects on the stability of the national financial system and on the adjustment of the portuguese economy in progress. Safeguarding financial stability discouraged these options. In the consideration of the solution to be adopted, the existence of EUR 1175 million of bonds issued by BANIF and guaranteed by the State was also taken into account. In a scenario of capitalisation with public funds, the increase in the State's exposure to BANIF would be partially offset by the immediate reduction of contingent state liabilities for guarantees provided (by EUR 300 million). From the evaluation of the various alternatives, Banco de Portugal concluded that the option of public recapitalization of BANIF was, in the prevailing circumstances, the one that best ensured financial stability and also that which entailed lower costs for the State. Since BANIF opted for access to the public capitalization line, and to meet the requirements of the Law for this purpose, at the end of December 2012, it submitted the Recapitalization Plan to Banco de Portugal. The plan included a statement by the BANIF Board of Directors ensuring that it was empowered to meet the resulting commitments. This plan included the financial and prudential projections for the public investment period, taking into account the macroeconomic scenario that had been defined by Banco de Portugal in the context of the regular updating of the capital and financing plans of national banks. The capitalisation plan provided for a capital increase of EUR 1400 million to be achieved in two phases: - The first phase was an injection of EUR 1100 million of public funds and was intended to exceed in a short period of the (700 million by the subscription of special shares and 400 million hybrid instruments); - The second phase corresponded to the use of private investment amounting to EUR 450 million, to be implemented by the end of June 2013  an amount intended to constitute a capital cushion of EUR 300 million to address the risks of implementing the capitalisation plan identified in banco de Portugal's assessment, and to repay EUR 150 million for hybrid instruments. Banco de Portugal considered that the proposed capitalization structure was adequate and that BANIF was viable at the end of the public investment period. Under the recapitalization plan, BANIF would present sufficient results at the end of this period to attract the interest of private investors, which would allow public disinvestment to be achieved in 2017. Banco de Portugal noted in its opinion that the viability of a credit institution is largely endogenous, depending largely on the capacity of its management. Thus, on December 28, 2012, Banco de Portugal sent the Ministry of Finance an opinion proposing the approval of BANIF's access to public investment as provided for in the capitalization plan. This opinion was issued on condition that a series of measures were adopted to ensure ownership of the Plan by the shareholders and the BOARD of DIRECTORS of BANIF, namely: The approval of the Recapitalization Plan by the Shareholders' General Meeting; The appointment of new members to the Bank's governing bodies that had deserved the prior agreement of the State; The granting to the management body of a mandate to make commitments and take the necessary measures for the implementation of the Recapitalisation Plan. These measures have all been adopted. According to European rules, the involvement of public funds implies that capitalisation must be approved by the European Commission. The public recapitalisation of BANIF was temporarily approved by the European Commission on 21 January 2013. However, as is apparent from the applicable rules, final approval was dependent on the approval of a restructuring plan by DGComp. The capitalisation operation with public funds was approved by the Government on January 24, 2013, and the State was empowered to appoint a non-executive member to the Board of Directors and a member to the BANIF Supervisory Board. It should be kept in mind that Banco de Portugal's opinion, as has been expressly mentioned, was based on a business plan which was successively altered in the interactions with DGComp, which prompted multiple warnings from Banco de Portugal to the Ministry of Finance and the European institutions. On 7 January 2013, Banco de Portugal expressed serious concerns about the inconsistency between the measures that were being required by DGComp to Portuguese banks, in particular BANIF, and the policies, objectives and measures that were part of the agreement underlying the Adjustment Programme. On 10 January 2013, Banco de Portugal sent an email to the President of the European Commission and the ECB, with knowledge to the Minister of State and Finance, warning that the requirements for reduction and geographical delimitation of BANIF's activity constituted a material change in the assumptions of the business plan underlying the Recapitalisation Plan, impact on banco de Portugal's opinion. It should be made in mind that the approval of a new business plan by DGComp presupposed the long-term viability of the institution, i.e. the ability to repay or remunerated public capital under normal market conditions. Therefore, in a letter of 30 April 2013 to the Minister of Finance, Banco de Portugal stressed: That the final decision [of DGComp] "on the restructuring plan will not cease to constitute a materially important change in relation to the recapitalisation plan assessed by Banco de Portugal, given the discontinuation of a broader set of non-strategic assets than originally considered." And that "As soon as the outcome of the negotiations is known, Banco de Portugal will carry out a new assessment in order to update its opinion sabre the conditions of viability of the institution with a view to informing the Ministry of Finance." II. Monitoring of BANIF by Banco de Portugal after recapitalization Follow-up procedures by Banco de Portugal Following the public recapitalisation operation, Banco de Portugal, as a prudential supervisory authority, bearing in mind the relevance of monitoring very close to the implementation risks inherent in the Recapitalisation Plan, defined specific follow-up procedures for BANIF. These procedures included sending periodic reports on: - The corporate reorganization process; - The sale of subsidiaries; - Real estate disinvestment; - Changes in the Bank's information systems and database; - And exposure to group entities, shareholders and related parties. At the same time, Banco de Portugal, in compliance with the applicable legal framework, has always kept the Ministry of Finance informed of compliance with the conditions and commitments legally made by BANIF, as well as relevant deviations from the Recapitalisation Plan and the achievement of its structural targets. Under the State aid procedure, it was up to the Board of Directors and the shareholders of BANIF to be responsible for submitting a restructuring plan to DGComp, which was responsible for its approval. The lack of a Restructuring Plan approved by DGComp has always been a prudential concern for Banco de Portugal, given the risks that adid to the stability of BANIF's capital position. Therefore, Banco de Portugal, in the context of cooperation with the Ministry of Finance, followed the preparation of the different versions of the plan and contributed with technical opinions and suggestions for amendment. However, this did not mean, nor could it mean, taking responsibility for its approval and implementation. I would remind you that the approval was up to DGComp and that the responsibility for implementing the plan fell to the shareholders and the BOARD of DIRECTORS of BANIF. Developments in the prudential situation of BANIF Between recapitalisation with public funds and the end of 2015, BANIF has always reported prudential ratios above legal lows. It should be noted that, although in a split manner and in a revised timetable, BANIF has achieved a capital increase of EUR 450 million from private investors, in a particularly unfavorable economic environment and although it does not yet have a restructuring plan approved by DGComp. BANIF reimbursed the State 275 million for hybrid instruments (of which EUR 150 million in August 2013 and EUR 125 million in April 2014). Positively, it would also highlight the reduction of structural costs (mainly through the closure of branches and the reduction of the staff) and, by the end of 2014, the improvement of the liquidity position with the diversification of the sources of stability of the depositor base and the release of state liability for the guarantees previously provided. However, there were significant deviations from the assumptions assumed in the BANIF Recapitalisation Plan, and the bank did not disclose the capacity to adopt countervailing measures. In particular, banif results were systematically and significantly below projected reflecting three main factors: (i) the compression of the financial margin, in a context of sharp fall in interest rates (which contrasted with the expected increase prevailing when the recapitalisation plan was approved); (ii) Impairments in the credit portfolio and losses associated with the real estate portfolio, much higher than expected; (iii) and the inability to realise the sale of a significant set of assets, including subsidiaries abroad and real estate assets. The accounts for the end of 2014, released in May 2015, revealed a high and unexpected loss, which drove capital ratios to levels very close to the minimum limits: the total consolidated capital ratio fell to 8.4%, from a regulatory low of 8%. The erosion of the capital cushion led Banco de Portugal not to authorize the reimbursement to the State of the last tranche of hybrid instruments subscribed by BANIF, in the amount of 125 million euros that expired on December 31, 2014. This resulted in the failure to fulfil a structural objective of the commitments made at the time of recapitalisation. Therefore, as early as May 2015, the BANIF Board of Directors was asked to submit a capital plan for capital reinforcement. As is well known, on 24 July 2015 the European Commission decided to open an in-depth investigation process into State aid to BANIF. This decision reinforced Banco de Portugal's concern about the stability of the bank's capitalisation levels, given the possibility of declared illegal the State aid granted and, consequently, required for its refund, with a very material impact on their solvency ratios. Following this decision, the shareholders and the BOARD of DIRECTORS of BANIF prepared a new version of the Restructuring Plan, which they submitted to the European Commission in September 2015 and initiated a process of voluntary sale of the institution. The conduct of the voluntary sale process was a matter of the responsibility of the shareholders and the Board of Directors. Given its relevance from the point of view of the stability of BANIF's capital, Banco de Portugal sought to monitor developments as an observer. In parallel with this voluntary sale process, the process continued with a view to dgcomp's approval of the restructuring plan. Banco de Portugal monitored the interactions between the BANIF Board of Directors, the Portuguese Government and the European Commission, having participated in the steering meetings of the new plan and submitted comments and suggestions to the documents. As it is for you, it has also provided all relevant information to the ECB. In addition, during the transition period between the 20th and 21st Governments, Banco de Portugal was called by DGComp to temporarily assume a more intervening role in this dialogue process. For this reason, in the second half of November, he participated in face-to-face meetings with that authority on the Restructuring Plan, having involved and informed the Ministry of Finance of all developments. It should also be stressed that in the context of normal prudential supervision activity, Banco de Portugal identified several weaknesses throughout 2015, both in terms of accounting for credit and real estate, as well as in the calculation of capital requirements - situations that increased the pressure on BANIF's capital ratios. These situations were repeatedly transmitted and discussed with BANIF throughout 2015, as confirmed by the documentation that was sent to this Commission, and there was no adequate response or solution from BANIF. In the absence of response, and in the exercise of its supervisory responsibilities, in November 2015, Banco de Portugal ordered BANIF to take amending measures to increase its assets and urgently send a plan containing additional capital strengthening measures to address the situations identified. It should be noted that the shortcomings and weaknesses identified, in the absence of compensatory measures, implied a capital ratio below the legal minimums. Contingency plans In parallel with the prudential supervision of BANIF, and as a national macroprudential authority and resolution authority, Banco de Portugal has developed, since 2012, as was its obligation, contingency plans to address the risks of a deterioration of the prudential situation of BANIF. As of October 2015, in view of the growing risk of failure of the voluntary sale process and a declaration by DGComp of illegality of the aid provided in 2013, Banco de Portugal intensified the work of preparing contingency plans. It should be noted in this regard that, from 1 January 2016, any intervention in BANIF would be conducted within the framework of the Single European Resolution Mechanism. At the end of November 2015, the Single Resolution Board alerted Banco de Portugal that, in the absence of a solution to BANIF by the end of the year, it is likely that an intervention in the subsequent period would take the form of settlement or resolution with extensive bail-in, covering deposits not guaranteed by the Deposit Guarantee Fund. Such a situation would entail damage of unpredictable scope to national financial stability, given the high risks of loss of confidence of depositors, with subsequent contagion to other credit institutions. Five intervention scenarios were studied in BANIF: Mandatory capitalisation using public investment; Internal recapitalisation (bail-in); Resolution with partial transfer of BANIF activity to a transitional bank; Resolution with immediate sale of BANIF's activity; Liquidation. These scenarios were discussed with the Ministry of Finance and the various relevant European institutions, including DGComp, the Single Supervisory Mechanism and the Single Resolution Board. Among the contingency scenarios, Banco de Portugal considered that carrying out a mandatory capitalization operation using public investment and sale of BANIF within 2 years was the least serious solution for BANIF and for the stability of the financial system, so it recommended it to the Ministry of Finance. This naturally involved the submission of a restructuring plan which was accepted by DGComp. Why, in the case of BANIF, did Banco de Portugal not favour the application of a resolution measure similar to that of BES? For two reasons: i. First, because the share capital of BANIF is majority owned by the State, this bank could be perceived as a public bank. The resolution of a bank perceived as public and the corresponding creation of a transitional bank could significantly affect the confidence of depositors and have a contagion effect on the system of proportions that are difficult to foresee; ii. Secondly, because the option of mandatory capitalisation using public investment would not burden the Resolution Fund. As is well known, following the BES resolution, significant contingent liabilities resulting from the high level of indebtedness of the Resolution Fund hang over the national banking system. A possible aggravation responsibilities also entailed risks to financial stability. It should be noted that, with the change in the legal regime for public recapitalisation in 2013/2014, compulsory capitalisation using public investment became possible only if the withdrawal of the authorisation or the resolution of the institution did not constitute appropriate measures to ensure the stability of the financial system; and also had to be preceded by burden-sharing measures. Furthermore, under State aid rules, burden-sharing between shareholders, holders of other own funds instruments and subordinated creditors would have to ensure that they would bear losses of not less than 8% of liabilities. Banif's total own funds and subordinated claims were sufficient to comply with this requirement, which gave the State the possibility for the State to recapitalise the institution with public funds. The decision to carry out this operation and the decision on burden-sharing measures was solely for the Ministry of Finance. It would, however, have to be preceded by a reasoned proposal from Banco de Portugal, stating the reasons why the application of a resolution measure would not ensure the pursuit of its objectives, in particular the safeguarding of financial stability. In addition, since public investment consisted of State aid, prior authorisation from the European Commission was required. Following banco de Portugal's recommendation in early December, the Ministry of Finance proposed to DGComp the public recapitalization solution combined with the subsequent integration of BANIF into caixa Geral de Depositos (CGD), a solution that Banco de Portugal evaluated favourably from the perspective of financial stability. However, the European Commission has blocked this solution, arguing in particular: - THAT CGD is under going into restructuring and subject to a ban on acquisitions; - And that this solution could be regarded as state aid to CGD because it needs capital, forcing, for that purpose, the resolution of that institution alone. In this context, this mandatory capitalization option has been abandoned. The scenario of internal recapitalisation has been removed by Banco de Portugal as it would jeopardise financial stability. In fact, given the structure of BANIF's liabilities, the absorption of all losses would inevitably require a contribution from depositors. Finally, the possibility of resolution with the creation of a transition bank was not made possible in a timely manner by the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM). The SSM expressed serious reservations about this alternative, making it, in practice, unfeasible, even as a redress solution that would strengthen the negotiating capacity in a resolution process with immediate sale. As a result of these constraints, in the event of failure of the voluntary sale option of BANIF, the Portuguese authorities had only two options: Apply a resolution measure with immediate sale of BANIF's activity; Or proceed to the bank's liquidation. The liquidation of BANIF would entail the imputation of losses to all senior creditors, including small retail investors, and to deposits not protected by the Deposit Guarantee Fund, in addition to implying the activation of this Fund. This would mean a very high funding effort for the repayment of deposits covered by the Deposit Guarantee Fund and its consequent decapitalisation. But more importantly, the liquidation of a financial institution with the systemic importance of BANIF would constitute an unprecedented event in the financial system Portuguese, with high risks of contagion and potentially very significant overall costs for the financial system and economy, in particular autonomous regions. I stress that the voluntary sale process - which was banco de Portugal's preferred solution (Plan A) - was still ongoing and that, if successful, it would dispense with any contingency plan. III. Resolution and sale When, on Friday, December 18, Banco de Portugal was confronted with the failure of the voluntary sale process, in which the shareholders and the BOARD of Directors of BANIF were working, it became evident that the application of a resolution measure with immediate sale of most of its assets was imperative and urgent. It is worth remembering in some detail the sequence of events that led to the resolution measure: On December 16, 2015 (Wednesday before the weekend of the resolution), the Ministry of Finance informed Banco de Portugal that if the voluntary sale was not successful, there was no alternative left that did not pass the BANIF resolution. On the same day, the Single Supervisory Board expressed serious reservations about the creation of a transitional bank and the Governing Council of the ECB decided to suspend banif's monetary policy counter-party status from 21 December (following Monday) in the event that the bank has not been sold in the meantime or has not entered into resolution. On 17 December 2015 (Thursday before the resolution), the Ministry of Finance made the European Commission aware to Banco de Portugal of the European Commission's position, according to which, in view of the notorious and very accelerated worsening of the BANIF situation and the repeated doubts about the bank's viability in the event of the failure of the sale of BANIF, the divestment of its activity under a resolution measure should take place. In the same letter, the Ministry of Finance informed Banco de Portugal that, when the alternatives were analyzed, the said divestment of the activity seemed to correspond to the least costly solution for the public treasury. On 18 December 2015 (Friday before the resolution), the European Commission clarified to Banco de Portugal and the Ministry of Finance that voluntary disposal could not take place if it entailed the granting of State aid, which was the case with the acquisition proposals known to it up to that time. He also informed that, in his view, the divestiture solutions that were being analyzed could only take place in a resolution scenario. On the same day, the Ministry of Finance reported that the voluntary sale did not appear to have materialized. On the morning of 19 December 2015 (Saturday), the Ministry of Finance confirmed that, on the basis of information provided to it by the BANIF Board of Directors, it had not been possible to implement the sale of the bank in the context of the voluntary disposal process because all tenders submitted by potential buyers involved additional State assistance, which was not accepted by DGComp. Meanwhile, BANIF's liquidity situation had suffered a notorious and very accelerated deterioration, particularly after the news reported by the media about the bank's imminent closure. This degradation resulted from a drastic decrease in customer deposits (which fell by 960 million euros between 14 and 21 December), which led BANIF to ask Banco de Portugal for access to emergency liquidity (ELA) to cope with the withdrawals. By December 18, the ELA operation had already reached 1 billion euros, virtually exhausting the BANIF collateral available for these operations. On that date, banif's collateral cushion to increase ELA operations was reduced to 124 million euros. In view of these facts, on 19 December 2015, Banco de Portugal declared that BANIF was "at risk or in insolvency" (failing or likely to fail). This decision was based on the risk of creating an unrecoverable capital shortfall through the likely obligation to refund State aid and on the notorious and accelerated degradation of the liquidity situation, which put BANIF at serious and serious risk of imminent non-compliance with obligations and the provision of essential financial services. All this would imply that BANIF would be led to a situation of effective incapacity for the continuation of the activity. In this regard, I note that in the days following the resolution, and despite the public announcement that BANIF deposits were secured and that they had all been transferred to Banco Santander Totta, significant outflows of deposits continued (almost EUR 300 million between 21 and 23 December, companies and institutions). Also on December 19, 2015, Banco de Portugal decided to trigger the institution's urgent resolution process in part or total disposal of its activity and invite Banco Santander Totta and Banco Popular Espanol to submit proposals for acquisition in a resolution context. Why were Banco Popular Espanol and Banco Santander Totta only invited to submit proposals to acquire BANIF? First, the urgency of the process - the proposals had to be submitted by the morning of the following day, Sunday, and the transaction concluded that same day - recommended that candidates be chosen from among the participants in the voluntary sale process, because they were already aware of banif's financial and patrimonial situation. Secondly, because of this universe, these two institutions were the only ones that cumulatively met the following mandatory requirements: (i) The model of sale in the context of resolution, which was jointly articulated with the European authorities, provided for the sale of assets and liabilities to the acquiring institution. According to the law (Article 145M of the RGICSF), the sale of assets and liabilities requires the buyer to be a credit institution authorized to develop the activity in question, or an entity that has requested authorisation for the exercise of that activity. (ii) In accordance with the commitments made by the Portuguese State to the European Commission in the context of State aid in terms of the profile of the acquiring institution, it would have to be a credit institution with a significant presence in Portugal and a total balance sheet 3 times higher than that of BANIF in Portugal or 5 times higher than that of BANIF overall. In the early hours of 20 December, only Banco Santander Totta submitted a binding proposal. Based on it, immediately negotiations to obtain an agreement that would allow the operation to be concluded on the same day (before the reopening of the banks the following day). The resolution operation with sale of banif activity The model of the resolution operation with sale of BANIF's activity resulted from intense interactions between Banco de Portugal, as the resolution authority, the Government, the European Commission and the European Central Bank, resulting in various constraints. The operation involved the breakdown of the BANIF balance sheet into three components: Transfer to Banco Santander Totta of the vast majority of assets and the generality of senior and guaranteed liabilities; Transfer of a set of problematic or unwanted assets by the buyer to a vehicle specifically created for this purpose, Oitante; Permanence in the BANIF of residual assets, mainly related to some subsidiaries abroad, as well as equity and subordinated liabilities. The assets transferred to Oitante were essentially real estate assets, defaulted credits and financial holdings. These assets as a whole had a net book value of unevenness in BANIF of EUR 2190 million. However, these assets were subject ed to a heavy haircut required by DGComp (about 66% on the balance sheet net value) so their value was reduced to EUR 746 million. The haircut applied was determined according to the Community regulations contained in the Commission Communication on the Treatment of Depreciated Assets in the Community banking sector, known as "Impaired Assets Communication". The acquisition of these assets by Oitante was financed through bonds issued for the same amount, guaranteed by the Resolution Fund and counter-guaranteed by the Portuguese, which were subsequently transferred to Banco Santander Totta. Banco Santander Totta also received an amount of EUR 2 255 million to bridge the difference that resulted from its valuation between the assets and liabilities transferred and also ensure: - a positive difference between assets and liabilities of EUR 750 million, resulting in a minimum amount of CET1 fully loaded own funds of EUR 500 million; - And the coverage of credit, commercial, operational and legal risks. For the operation, BST paid EUR 150 million. The cost of the operation and its financing In aggregate terms, the operation cost EUR 3.3 billion which resulted from the combination of the following factors: (i) dgcomp's above-mentioned imposition of very high haircuts on assets transferred to Oitante (resulting in a reduction in value of around EUR 1.4 billion compared to the amount by which the assets were accounted for); (ii) the valuation attributed to banif's activity by the acquirer in the circumstances of rapid sale and lack of alternatives to retreat by national authorities (EUR 1.6 billion, which includes EUR 1.1 billion of value reduction for coverage of various risks and restructuring costs and approximately EUR 650 million to meet the purchaser's requirements for balance sheet balance, amount on which it also deducts the price of EUR 150 million). This amount is influenced by the decisions taken by the authorities on the involvement of BANIF creditors in the effort to absorption of losses, which protected all depositors and senior creditors; (iii) the residual assets that remained in BANIF in the amount of approximately EUR 300 million. The financing of the operation involved three components: - the absorption of losses by banif's shareholders and subordinated creditors in an amount slightly exceeding EUR 1 billion; - financial support provided by the Resolution Fund (EUR 489 million, financed using a State loan); - Financial support granted directly by the State (EUR 1766 million). For the amounts involved in the transaction, it should be noted: - On the one hand, final validation procedures and closing of the operation are still in progress (even if material changes are not expected the above values); - And, secondly, that the final overall cost of the resolution measure applied to BANIF depends on what will be recovered from the disposal of the assets transferred to Oitante and, to a lesser extent, on any costs in the context of banif's liquidation court proceedings. IV. Final considerations The experience gained from the BANIF case has raised a number of issues and concerns that I have been passing on to the European and national authorities and which I consider important to share with this Commission: Firstly, in the current European institutional framework in which we have an incomplete Banking Union, there is an asymmetry between those who have decision-making power over a banking institution and who have responsibility for financial stability. National authorities remain responsible for financial stability, but their action is conditional on decisions on supervision, resolution and enforcement of competition rules that are taken at European level. This limitation of powers and instruments of national authorities weakens their ability to ensure the stability of the financial system and, given that it is not perceptible by the ordinary citizen, gives them a responsibility which has no correspondence in terms of competences; on the other hand, it swipes at European decision-makers for scrutiny (accountability) of public opinion in countries where their decisions have an impact. This means that the European conditioning of the action of national authorities, in a context where risk sharing at European level is incomplete, hinders the role of safeguarding financial stability and, by affecting the confidence of agents in the financial system, accentuates the underlying risks. Secondly, we currently have in Europe a multitude of entities to define and implement policies with material impact on sectoral and national developments in the financial system - the Single Supervisory Mechanism, the Single Resolution Mechanism and the European Commission - whose action is neither adequately coordinated nor consistent, despite the obvious negative externalities that result. This problem is aggravated by the lack of decision-making mechanisms at European level that ensure agility, speed and confidentiality, which are indispensable for effective banking resolution. Thirdly, the current regulatory framework prevents viable but incapable banks from financing themselves through private investors from being able to benefit from public financial support, even if temporary, without being in the framework of the resolution. The application of a resolution measure typically involves an assessment of the institution's assets at a very significant discount, thereby leading to the materialisation of losses for the institution's creditors and/or taxpayers. It is the banking systems of the countries with the most fragile financial situation, where the legacy of the economic crisis is more relevant, which present greater vulnerabilities. This could be costly in terms of financial stability, given the risk of repeated and widespread implementation of resolution measures, exacerbating fragmentation in the euro area. The challenges facing the national banking system are not unique to our country and find parallel, albeit to different degrees, in several other euro area countries. The current European institutional and regulatory framework imposes strong limitations on the design of national solutions, posing risks to financial stability in the euro area. In this context, I have been advocating the need for urgent reflection and action at European level and for close collaboration and coordination of the position of national authorities in the various European outlaws in which they participate. Thank you very much. Lisbon, 5 April 2016

Senhor Presidente Senhoras e Senhores Deputados No dia 20 de dezembro de 2015 o Banco de Portugal aplicou uma medida de resoluo ao BANIF de acordo com o artigo 145E do RGICSF. Esta medida consistiu: - Na venda da maior parte dos seus ativos e passivos ao Banco Santander Totta (BST); - Na transferncia de um conjunto de ativos para a Oitante, veculo de gesto de ativos criado para o efeito; - Na permanncia no BANIF (que ser objeto de futura liquidao) de um conjunto muito restrito de ativos, das posies acionistas e dos crditos subordinados e de partes relacionadas. A medida de resoluo foi tomada num ambiente de urgncia e de ausncia de solues alternativas viveis que permitissem assegurar a continuidade da prestao dos servios financeiros essenciais pelo BANIF, proteger as poupanas confiadas ao banco atravs da sua rede de retalho e preservar a estabilidade do sistema financeiro portugus. Para compreender a opo de resoluo perante a nica alternativa disponvel, a liquidao, ser necessrio ter em conta no s o maior custo de liquidao como, sobretudo, a importncia sistmica do BANIF. De facto, o BANIF era o stimo maior grupo bancrio portugus, com um ativo lquido consolidado de 12 mil milhes de euros (cerca de 7% do PIB), depsitos de clientes de 6,8 mil milhes de euros e 2 224 trabalhadores (dados de setembro de 2015). A atividade do BANIF estava essencialmente focada na prestao de servios de banca de retalho no mercado domstico, no segmento de pequenas e mdias empresas e nos clientes particulares. Apesar de ter uma quota de apenas 3,2% no total de ativos do mercado bancrio portugus, era lder nas regies autnomas dos Aores e da Madeira, com quotas de mercado de cerca de 45% e de 28% nos depsitos e no crdito, respetivamente. O BANIF tinha, assim, um papel singular no financiamento da economia das ilhas, razo pela qual uma eventual interrupo dos servios por si prestados teria impactos necessariamente graves nessas regies. A fim de enquadrar esta deciso de resoluo, penso que importa ter presentes os principais desenvolvimentos relacionados com o BANIF desde a sua capitalizao com fundos pblicos at  aplicao da medida de resoluo:  Comearei por explicar o que levou  necessidade de capitalizao pblica do BANIF;  De seguida abordarei os principais desenvolvimentos no perodo subsequente  capitalizao com fundos pblicos, com particular enfoque no acompanhamento efetuado pelo Banco de Portugal enquanto autoridade de superviso prudencial;  Explicarei depois o processo de resoluo;  E concluirei partilhando com a Comisso algumas reflexes e preocupaes suscitadas pela experincia com este processo. I. O que levou  recapitalizao do BANIF com fundos pblicos Ao longo de 2011 e 2012, a situao financeira do Grupo BANIF registou uma deteriorao acentuada, no tendo o Grupo atingido o rcio exigvel de Core Tier 1, em base consolidada, com referncia a 31 de dezembro de 2011. A deteriorao da situao financeira do BANIF resultou da conjugao de vrios fatores: (i) Um rpido crescimento do crdito nos anos anteriores  crise, sem uma adequada gesto do risco e com concentrao em ativos imobilirios e crditos a PME (em 2012, o rcio de crdito sobre depsitos do BANIF era 134%, o que compara com uma mdia do sistema bancrio de 128%); (ii) Uma estrutura de custos operacionais muito pesada face  atividade desenvolvida, a que no foi alheia a poltica de expanso de agncias e de participaes no exterior prosseguida pelo BANIF (em 2012 o BANIF tinha um rcio cost to income de 178%, que compara com cerca de 60% no conjunto do sistema bancrio); (iii) O reconhecimento de um volume muito significativo de imparidades (cerca de 500 milhes de euros), na sequncia, primeiro, dos exerccios de inspeo transversal conduzidos em 2011 e em 2012 (SIP  Special Inspections Program e OIP  On-Site Inspections Program) e, em segundo lugar, da auditoria especial ao BANIF realizada em 2012; (iv) As maiores exigncias de capital impostas pelo Banco de Portugal ao sistema bancrio, com a fixao de rcios mnimos de Core Tier 1 de 9% para o final de 2011 e de 10% para o final de 2012 (antecipando a aplicao de algumas das principais recomendaes de Basileia III); (v) E a deteriorao da situao econmica e financeira do pas, com impacto no volume e na qualidade do negcio, assim como no risco da carteira de crdito. Em face desta insuficincia de capital, o Banco de Portugal determinou, em maio e junho de 2012: - A apresentao pelo BANIF de um plano de reestruturao visando repor os rcios prudenciais acima do mnimo exigido, com uma participao significativa de investidores privados; - A adoo de medidas de reorganizao do grupo, nomeadamente de simplificao da estrutura e de reduo de entidades e atividades no essenciais ao negcio bancrio; - A implementao pelo BANIF de medidas corretivas, com destaque para a limitao da exposio a entidades do grupo, acionistas e entidades relacionadas. Perante a incapacidade revelada pelos acionistas privados para assegurarem o reforo do capital necessrio ou para atrarem outros investidores privados, o Banco de Portugal passou a equacionar diferentes cenrios alternativos para fazer face  situao do BANIF. Assim, foram analisados os cenrios de capitalizao com recurso a fundos pblicos, de resoluo e de liquidao. De acordo com os clculos efetuados na altura, a liquidao do BANIF conduziria ao pagamento dos depsitos cobertos pelo Fundo de Garantia de Depsitos (no montante de 4500 milhes de euros) e a um risco de perda significativo dos depsitos no cobertos (que ascendiam a 2700 milhes de euros). Por seu turno, o cenrio de resoluo, que assentava na criao de um banco de transio, requereria um esforo financeiro total entre 2500 milhes de euros e 4600 milhes de euros, consoante se considerasse uma estimativa mais ou menos conservadora de valorizao dos ativos transferidos. Tratava-se, por outro lado, de uma soluo que no tinha sido ainda testada e que envolvia riscos operacionais significativos, bem como riscos de litigncia pelos acionistas e outros credores no protegidos, como acontece em qualquer processo de resoluo. Para alm disso, e mais importante, na conjuntura econmica recessiva e incerta em que nos encontrvamos, qualquer uma das opes implicaria uma perturbao na confiana dos depositantes que poderia ter efeitos devastadores na estabilidade do sistema financeiro nacional e no ajustamento da economia portuguesa em curso. A salvaguarda da estabilidade financeira desaconselhava estas opes. Na ponderao sobre a soluo a adotar, foi ainda levada em considerao a existncia de 1175 milhes de euros de obrigaes emitidas pelo BANIF e garantidas pelo Estado. Num cenrio de capitalizao com fundos pblicos, o aumento da exposio do Estado ao BANIF seria parcialmente compensado pela reduo imediata das responsabilidades contingentes do Estado por garantias prestadas (em 300 milhes de euros). Da avaliao das vrias alternativas, o Banco de Portugal concluiu que a opo de recapitalizao pblica do BANIF era, nas circunstncias prevalecentes, a que melhor assegurava a estabilidade financeira e tambm a que implicava menores custos para o Estado. Tendo o BANIF optado pelo acesso  linha de capitalizao pblica, e para satisfazer os requisitos previstos na Lei para tal efeito, em finais de dezembro de 2012, submeteu ao Banco de Portugal o Plano de Recapitalizao. O plano inclua uma declarao do Conselho de Administrao do BANIF garantindo que se encontrava habilitado para cumprir os compromissos dele resultantes. Este plano contemplava as projees financeiras e prudenciais para o perodo de investimento pblico, tendo em conta o cenrio macroeconmico que tinha sido definido pelo Banco de Portugal no mbito da atualizao regular dos planos de capital e de financiamento dos bancos nacionais. O plano de capitalizao previa um aumento de capital de 1400 milhes de euros a concretizar em duas fases: - A primeira fase correspondia a uma injeo de 1100 milhes de euros de fundos pblicos e destinava-se a ultrapassar num prazo curto a insuficincia de capitais prprios (700 milhes por via da subscrio de aes especiais e 400 milhes de instrumentos hbridos); - A segunda fase correspondia ao recurso a investimento privado no montante de 450 milhes de euros, a concretizar at ao final de junho de 2013  montante que se destinava a constituir uma almofada de capital de 300 milhes de euros para fazer face a riscos de execuo do plano de capitalizao, identificados na avaliao do Banco de Portugal, e a reembolsar 150 milhes de euros de instrumentos hbridos. O Banco de Portugal considerou que a estrutura de capitalizao proposta era adequada e que o BANIF apresentava viabilidade no final do perodo do investimento pblico. De acordo com o plano de recapitalizao, o BANIF apresentaria no final desse perodo resultados suficientes para atrair o interesse de investidores privados, o que permitiria concretizar o desinvestimento pblico em 2017. O Banco de Portugal no seu parecer fez notar que a viabilidade de uma instituio de crdito , em grande parte, endgena, dependendo muito da capacidade da sua gesto. Assim, no dia 28 de dezembro de 2012, o Banco de Portugal enviou ao Ministrio das Finanas um parecer propondo a aprovao do acesso do BANIF ao investimento pblico como previsto no plano de capitalizao. Este parecer foi emitido sob a condio de serem adotadas uma srie de medidas que visavam assegurar a apropriao (ownership) do Plano pelos acionistas e pelo Conselho de Administrao do BANIF, designadamente:  A aprovao do Plano de Recapitalizao pela Assembleia Geral de acionistas;  A designao de novos membros para os rgos sociais do Banco que tivessem merecido o acordo prvio do Estado;  A atribuio ao rgo de administrao de um mandato para assumir os compromissos e adotar as medidas necessrias  implementao do Plano de Recapitalizao.
