Ao longo da semana, os depitos do Banif sofreram uma reduo de quase 1000 milhs de euros, pelo que, no final da semana, mesmo o colateral disponvel para as operas ELA estava praticamente exaurido (o buffer existente era apenas de 124 milhs de euros). A dinmica negativa em curso, que por certo se acentuaria com a divulgao do insucesso da venda voluntria, iria com muito elevada probabilidade impedir o banco de cumprir as suas obrigas para com os clientes e de manter fluxos regulares de pagamentos na abertura da semana seguinte (21 de dezembro). Desencadeamento e fundamentao da resoluo Na sequncia do progressivo estreitamento do leque de alternativas que descrevi atrs, o Banco de Portugal e o Ministrio das Finanas concordaram que, no sendo a venda voluntria bem sucedida, a venda da atividade em resoluo era a soluo menos gravosa para a estabilidade financeira e para a proteo dos depositantes e do errio pblico, em face da alternativa disponvel, que era apenas a da liquidao. O Banco de Portugal solicitou ao Ministrio das Finanas que confirmasse a impossibilidade de concretizar a venda voluntria e, uma vez que esta soluo requeria envolvimento ativo do Ministrio na definio do permetro, repartio de perdas, prestao de garantias e apoio financeiro do Estado, solicitou tambm ao Ministrio a nomeao dum interlocutor com capacidade de deciso para acompanhar as negocias de venda em resoluo. O Ministrio designou o Secretrio de Estado Adjunto, do Tesouro e das Finanas e um seu assessor. Em 18 de dezembro, o Ministrio informou que a venda voluntria parecia no se ter concretizado, e confirmou esta informao no dia seguinte, com base em comunicao recebida do Conselho de Administrao do Banif. A Direo Geral de Concorrncia clarificou, a 18 de dezembro, que a venda voluntria no poderia prosseguir se envolvesse ajuda de Estado  o que acontecia em todas as propostas que eram do seu conhecimento , situao que implicaria a necessidade de resoluo. Neste contexto, no dia 19 de dezembro, o Banco de Portugal deliberou declarar que o Banif se encontrava em risco ou situao de insolvncia (failing or likely to fail). A deliberao (publicada) recorda o historial, invoca as comunicas recebidas do Ministrio das Finanas e da Direo Geral da Concorrncia, e fundamenta a deciso com base no risco de criao de uma irrecupervel insuficincia de capital (por obrigao de restituio da ajuda de Estado) e na degradao notia e acelerada da situao de liquidez do Banif, que o colocava em risco srio e grave de incumprimento das suas obrigaes e da prestao dos servios financeiros essenciais, o que seria ainda agravado pela frustrao das expectativas de venda voluntria. A deliberao conclui que tudo isto implicaria que o Banif seria conduzido a uma situao de incumprimento dos requisitos para a manuteno da autorizao para o exerccio da sua atividade, pelo que se encontrava em risco ou em situao de insolvncia. Nas circunstncias descritas, o Banco de Portugal deliberou, assim, iniciar o processo de aplicao da medida de resoluo de venda total ou parcial da atividade do Banif. Seleo dos candidatos A seleo dos candidatos  compra em resoluo foi condicionada pela extrema urgncia do processo (na medida em que as propostas tinham que ser apresentadas at ao dia seguinte e a transao concluda tambm nesse dia), pelo projeto de compromissos acordados com a Direo Geral de Concorrncia sobre o perfil do adquirente e pelos requisitos legais associados a uma venda de atividade bancria. A urgncia do processo limitava o nmero possvel de candidatos (seria muito difcil gerir um processo com mais do que um pequeno nmero de concorrentes num to curto espao de tempo) e, na prtica, exigia que estes fossem escolhidos de entre os participantes no processo de venda voluntria (para beneficiar da manifestao de interesse destes e do conhecimento que tinham adquirido do Banif). Por seu turno, os requisitos do projeto da carta de compromissos do Estado quanto ao perfil do adquirente restringiam a elegibilidade a um banco comercial com presena significativa em Portugal ou uma certa dimenso global e capacidade financeira. A estes requisitos acrescia a necessidade legal de o comprador ter uma licena bancria, uma vez que no se tratava da venda duma participao acionista mas da venda da atividade. As duas nicas instituies que se perfilavam como satisfazendo os vrios requisitos eram o Banco Santander Totta e o Banco Popular Espaol. Acresce que, no mbito do processo de venda voluntria, as propostas destes dois candidatos eram precisamente aquelas que tinham sido selecionadas pelo assessor desse concurso (a empresa N+1) como as propostas mais interessantes. Nesse contexto, o Banco de Portugal, o Ministrio das Finanas e os respetivos assessores iniciaram reunis exploratias com os dois candidatos, a que se seguiram teleconferncias s quais se juntou a Direo Geral de Concorrncia da Comisso Europeia. Nestas condies, na mesma deliberao de 19 de dezembro em que foi decidido iniciar o processo de resoluo com venda, o Banco de Portugal selecionou o Banco Santander Totta e o Banco Popular Espaol para concurso e aprovou os documentos deste concurso. Terceira Parte: Aplicao da medida de resoluo Processo O processo de aplicao da medida de resoluo decorreu no fim de semana de 19 e 20 de dezembro. A medida aplicada consistiu na alienao da atividade do Banif, conjugada com a prvia segregao de parte dos ativos para um veculo de gesto de ativos. Aos dois potenciais adquirentes foram entregues cadernos de encargos contendo, designadamente, uma descrio sumria da medida, incluindo o permetro de transferncia para o veculo de gesto de ativos. Era expressamente indicado que as propostas deviam ser entregues at s 8h00 de dia 20, com vista  imperativa concluso do processo at s 23h59 do mesmo dia. O processo de aplicao da medida envolveu numerosas reunis e teleconferncias (com os concorrentes, o Banco de Portugal e respetivos assessores, o Ministrio das Finanas e respetivos assessores, a Direo Geral de Concorrncia da Comisso Europeia e tambm o Mecanismo nico de Superviso do BCE) para discusso das propostas, acerto da carta de compromissos das autoridades e preparao dos aspetos tcnicos. Dos dois concorrentes apenas o Banco Santander Totta apresentou proposta vinculativa, pelo que as negocias e discusses no domingo concentraram-se na proposta desta instituio. O processo envolveu tambm uma estreita interao e troca de correspondncia entre o Banco de Portugal e o Ministrio das Finanas no que se refere ao financiamento da transao, designadamente a repartio de encargos entre acionistas e credores, Fundo de Resoluo e Estado. Descrio da transao A transao aprovada, de acordo com a deliberao do Banco de Portugal de 20 de dezembro, envolveu a desagregao do balano do Banif em trs componentes: (i) A grande maioria dos ativos (cerca de 9,7 mil milhs de euros1) e a generalidade dos passivos seniores e garantidos (cerca de 11,2 mil milhes de euros) foram transferidas para o Banco Santander Totta; (ii) Um conjunto de ativos problemticos ou indesejados pelo comprador (em especial ativos imobilirios, crditos em incumprimento e participas financeiras, totalizando 2,2 mil milhes de euros) foi transferido para o veculo de gesto de ativos Oitante, detido pelo Fundo de Resoluo; (iii) E um conjunto residual de ativos permaneceu no Banif, que ser liquidado dentro de pouco tempo. Os ativos transferidos para o veculo foram sujeitos a um pesado haircut determinado pela Direo Geral da Concorrncia (cerca de 66% sobre o valor lquido de balano), pelo que o seu valor foi reduzido para 746 milhs de euros; a aquisio destes ativos pelo veculo foi financiada pela emisso de obrigas, garantidas pelo Fundo de Resoluo e contragarantidas pelo Estado, que foram entregues ao Banco Santander Totta. O Banco Santander Totta recebeu ainda um montante de 2255 milhs de euros (489 milhs do Fundo de Resoluo e 1766 milhs do Estado) para colmatar a diferena entre ativos e passivos, assegurar uma diferena positiva de 750 milhes de euros (resultante num montante mnimo de fundos prprios CET1 fully loaded de 500 milhs de euros) e cobrir riscos de crdito, comerciais, operacionais e legais. Foram ainda feitos pequenos acertos remanescentes e o Banco Santander Totta pagou um montante de 150 milhes de euros, j tido em conta no montante acima referido. Em termos agregados, a operao envolveu um custo de cerca de 3,3 mil milhs de euros, dos quais 1,4 mil milhs decorrentes do haircut aplicado aos ativos transferidos para o veculo e cerca de 1,8 mil milhs decorrentes dos ajustes de valor requeridos pelo Banco Santander Totta e, residualmente, dos ativos deixados no Banif. 1 No inclui ttulos de dvida da Oitante (746 milhes de euros) nem o montante do apoio pblico pelo Estado e Fundo de Resoluo (totalizando 2255 milhes de euros). O financiamento deste custo envolveu trs componentes:  Em primeiro lugar, a imputao de perdas aos acionistas e credores subordinados do Banif, num montante ligeiramente superior a 1000 milhs de euros;  Em segundo lugar, a prestao de apoio financeiro pelo Fundo de Resoluo (489 milhs de euros), feito at ao limite mximo permitido pela BRRD e pela lei, e financiado atravs dum emprstimo do Estado ao Fundo de Resoluo;  E, finalmente, o apoio financeiro direto do Estado (1766 milhes de euros). Note-se que o custo total atingido (3,3 mil milhs de euros) ficou relativamente prximo do previsto no cenrio de contingncia preparado pelo Banco de Portugal com base na avaliao em exit value num horizonte muito curto (2,9 mil milhs de euros); a diferena resulta da combinao de diversos fatores, com destaque para o maior haircut aplicado pela Direo Geral de Concorrncia na transferncia de ativos para o veculo (diferencial de cerca de 0,4 mil milhs de euros). O envolvimento do Fundo de Resoluo na operao incluiu basicamente trs componentes: (i) o apoio financeiro direto de 489 milhs de euros, para absoro de prejuzos, financiado por um emprstimo do Estado (em contrapartida deste apoio o Fundo de Resoluo ficou com um crdito sobre o Banif residual, cujo valor expectvel, no entanto,  primo de zero); (ii) a prestao duma garantia s obrigaes emitidas pela Oitante, no montante de 746 milhes de euros, com uma contragarantia do Estado; e (iii) a subscrio e realizao do capital social da Oitante (50 mil euros). O envolvimento do Estado na operao incluiu tambm basicamente trs componentes: (i) o apoio financeiro direto de 1766 milhs de euros; (ii) o emprstimo ao Fundo de Resoluo, no montante de 489 milhs de euros; (iii) e a prestao duma contragarantia s obrigas emitidas pelo Oitante, no montante de 746 milhs de euros. Quarta Parte: Breve avaliao dos resultados e algumas lies Quando um banco atinge uma situao de irreparvel desequilbrio financeiro, no h solus sem custos. As quests que se colocam so, em primeiro lugar, a da dimenso destes custos comparativamente a solus alternativas, que apenas podemos estimar porque no existe um contrafactual observado, e, em segundo lugar, a da distribuio dos custos entre os diversos credores do banco resolvido, os outros bancos, e os contribuintes. A aplicao da medida de resoluo ao Banif atingiu o objetivo principal de preservao da estabilidade financeira. A medida assegurou a proteo de todos os depitos, bem como dos credores seniores. Assegurou igualmente a continuidade do financiamento da economia (designadamente nas ilhas, onde o Banif era lder de mercado) e a prestao de servios financeiros pelo banco, sem disrupo. No se observaram sinais de contgio significativos para o sistema financeiro ou para a economia. Tudo isto so aspetos positivos fundamentais que no so demais realar, porque a ateno pblica tende a focar-se nos custos e a menosprezar o facto de se ter salvaguardado aquilo que era essencial. E saliento que a preservao do essencial  um resultado que no estava garantido  partida e que, ou no teria sido conseguido com a soluo alternativa  a liquidao  ou s-lo-ia certamente com custos, disrupo e riscos muito mais elevados, inclusivamente para os contribuintes. Dito isto,  indiscutvel que a resoluo do Banif implicou um custo absoluto muito elevado para os contribuintes portugueses, que nos penaliza a todos. H vrias razs para este elevado custo para os contribuintes. Em primeiro lugar, o mbito da absoro de perdas pelos credores, basicamente restringido aos acionistas e credores subordinados. Esta deciso foi tomada pelo Banco de Portugal, em estreita articulao com o Ministrio das Finanas, e teve em conta a necessidade de no p em risco a estabilidade financeira, face a uma estrutura de passivos do Banif em que um maior mbito de absoro de perdas atingiria os credores de retalho e os depositantes no garantidos. Uma segunda razo do elevado custo para os contribuintes foi o pesado haircut aplicado pela Direo Geral de Concorrncia aos ativos transferidos para o veculo (embora parte deste valor possa vir a ser recuperado). Finalmente, e no menos importante, o elevado custo para os contribuintes resultou tambm em larga medida das condies de venda, num prazo extremamente curto e numa posio negocial muito enfraquecida pela ausncia duma soluo de recurso que no fosse a liquidao. A experincia recolhida desta resoluo levanta uma srie de quests e lis. Em particular, destacaria trs reflexes muito breves. Em primeiro lugar, este caso ilustra a necessidade de voltar a refletir sobre o tratamento de bancos em dificuldades, comparativamente a empresas de outros setores, sobre os instrumentos disponveis para lidar com essas situas e sobre a adequada repartio de custos entre credores, outros bancos e contribuintes, quando um banco  objeto de resoluo e os fundos prrios no so suficientes para absorver a totalidade das perdas. Em segundo lugar, impe-se uma reflexo sobre se o enquadramento regulatio na Europa pondera devidamente os objetivos, por vezes conflituantes, de preservao da estabilidade financeira, minimizao dos custos para o contribuinte e manuteno da concorrncia. Em especial, parece profundamente questionvel o papel predominante que as consideras sobre a concorrncia assumem nestes processos, em detrimento das consideras que deveriam ser prioritrias, que so a preservao da estabilidade financeira e a proteo do errio pblico. Acresce que as preocupas com a concorrncia neste contexto so consideradas na perspetiva limitada de evitar distores da concorrncia resultantes de ajudas de Estado, desconsiderando (ou sconsiderando de forma secundria) o potencial de distoro mais geral  concorrncia que resulta do processo de concentrao bancria. Finalmente, importa avaliar se o movimento de constituio da Unio Bancria poder contribuir para uma reponderao das prioridades nos processos de resolus bancrias, ou se ir tornar o processo ainda mais complexo, ao introduzir novos intervenientes (o Mecanismo nico de Superviso, o Conselho nico de Resoluo, para alm da j existente Direo Geral da Concorrncia), cada um focado num mandato especfico, sem que esteja  partida assegurado um quadro eficiente de coordenao entre eles, e sem que nenhum deles tenha como preocupao central a preservao da estabilidade financeira. Muito obrigado.

Title: Initial intervention of Deputy Governor Pedro Duarte Neves in the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry to the process that led to the sale and resolution of BANIF
text: Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry into the process leading to the sale and resolution of BANIF April 21, 2016 Initial Intervention of Deputy Governor Pedro Duarte Neves Mr Chairman of the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry, Ladies and gentlemen, I thank you for addressing this Commission and providing all the information that can contribute to a better understanding of the process that led to the sale and resolution of BANIF. My speech will have four parts A. Monitoring of prudential supervision of BANIF in the period prior to reca-pitalization with public funds; B. Factors that led to recapitalization with public funds; C. The opinion of Banco de Portugal of 28 December 2012; D. Monitoring of Banco de Portugal after the recapitalization of BANIF. A. Monitoring of prudential supervision of BANIF in the period prior to recapitalisation with public funds 1. BANIF was, at the beginning of this decade, a commercial bank which specialises essentially in small and medium-sized enterprises and entrepreneurs on their own behalf (representing about 60 per cent of its credit portfolio) and in loan to retail customers. BANIF was the seventh most relevant financial group in terms of credit granted and the eighth in terms of customer resources. 2. BANIF has always had a strong presence in the autonomous regions of Madeira and the Azores, with a share of about 30 percent in the granting of credit and deposit collection, thus constituting a fundamental support of the econo-mia of those regions. On the continent, the bank was running with the main banks in the main regions of the country, namely In Lisbon, Porto and Faro, where it con-focused about 38 percent of the total of its credit portfolio. 3. It is also worth noting the relevant role of BANIF in the collection of deposits from Portuguese migrant communities. 4. Compared to the Portuguese banking system, BANIF was characterised at the beginning of this decade by (i) a higher credit-at-risk ratio, (ii) a higher transformation ratio (credit/deposits), (iii) lower levels of profitability, reflecting a higher cost structure, and (iv) until 2009, lower levels of better quality capital (Core Tier 1). 5. Taking into account the risk profile presented by BANIF, Banco de Portugal focused its prudential supervision activity - in addition to re-monitoring compliance with the applicable prudential standards - into 4 main dimensions: (i) strengthening the bank's own funds position; (ii) verification of the levels of the institution's or notforant; (iii) monitoring the liquidity situation; and (iv) redefinition of the group's strategic positioning. 6. As regards the capital position, it is important to begin by recalling that, from 2008 on, Banco de Portugal issued a set of recommendations and determinations that increased the requirements for the minimum capital values of the Portuguese banking system, anticipating the additive capital requirements arising from Basel III. a number of operations were carried out with the aim of strengthening own funds, highlighting the integration of the Tecnicredito Group (later Banif) in BANIF  announced in July 2009 and implemented in September 2009  to which an increase in better quality capital ratios (Tier 1 and Core Tier 1) by about 200-250 basis points was to be achieved. In addition, this integration has made a positive contribution to the group's financial margin over the past few years. 7. From 2011, however, it became progressively clear that the bank's then shareholders were not in a position to strengthen their own funds in line with the new capital requirements and, if-gundo, that no new shareholders would be entered. 8. At the same time, Banco de Portugal, in view of the higher credit at-risk ratios, paid particular attention to the quality of BANIF's credit portfolio with the purpose of ensuring a correct valuation of assets. Thus, in 2010 and 2011, for example, specific inspections were carried out on credit-related parsand and credit renegotiation procedures. Subsequently, banif's credit portfolio was again evaluated in the context of the exercises across the banking system Portuguese which took place in 2011 and 2012 (SIP - Special Inspection program and OIP-On-Site InspectionS Program). In addition, and already at a near stage of the recapitalisation, a special audit was developed on the BANIF, by PwC, which, in addition to updating the analysis of the higher risk credits covered by the SIP, also evaluated the portfolio of credits of subsidiaries in the es-trangeiro, the real estate portfolio, the portfolio of securities and the participations in socie-dades excluded from the consolidation perimeter. This complete set of credit portfolio tours has led to a very significant recognition of impairment losses in these two years (around EUR 500 million). 9. As regards the liquidity position, it is important to recall the difficulties in obtaining liquidity that have been generally the case for Portuguese banks since 2009. In this context, Banco de Portugal strengthened the monitoring of the liquidity situation, first through the establishing of regular meetings with the banks and then with the introduction of new reports on the liquidity position and the requirement to present pre-visionary treasury plans. In the specific case of BANIF, this follow-up was particularly close from 2009, involving daily liquidity reports and the holding of telephone meetings and conferences  in some periods on a weekly basis  with the bank's managers. 10. In 2008-2009, the BANIF transformation ratio was slightly above the average values of the banking Portuguese and therefore required enhanced monitoring. During the implementation of the Economic and Financial Assistance Programme to the Portuguese economy, banif's situation was more vulnerable, becoming especially serious in early 2012, in a context of closing financial markets for the por-tuguesfinancial institutions, the successive downgrades of the banks' ratings and the consequent devaluation of assets that served as collateral for Eurosystem financing operations, as well as the set of reimbursements scheduled for the second quarter of 2012 in the case of BANIF. Under monitoring the liquidity situation of BANIF, Banco de Portugal exerted continuous pressure on the bank's management to develop solutions to overcome this situation. 11. In order to cope with the difficult liquidity situation, BANIF has carried out a policy of re-holding deposits by paying high interest rates. At the end of 2011, Banco de Portugal introduced a deduction for own funds - in the case of high interest rates - which, in the case of BANIF, reached around 100 million euros (about 100 basis points of the bank's capital), which reduced the institution's own funds. 12. Finally, from 2011 onand at a stage in which the bank's difficulties began to be revealed more clearly, Banco de Portugal acted with the management and shareholders of the group to redefine its strategic positioning, through the hiring of consultants to present and de-re-translate cost rationalization programs, in particular through the pair of services dispersed by the units of the group, the development of operations for the sale of units located abroad and the search for strategic partners. Since they did not deliver immediate results, these initiatives eventually contributed to the establishment of the recapitalisation plan by the institution. B. Factors that led to recapitalisation with public funds 13. Throughout 2011 and 2012, Banif's financial situation saw a sharp deterioration, which resulted in significant losses, in a context where the institution's shareholders have not shown the capacity to strengthen the group's solvency level or attract private investors. The worsening of banif's financial situation resulted from the combination of several factors. 14. In terms of higher capital requirements, it is notelike the setting by Banco de Portugal of Core Tier 1 capital targets of 9 % by the end of 2011 and 10 % by the end of 2012, anticipating the implementation of some of the main recommendations of Basel III. such as the above-mentioned penalty associated with the practice of very high interest rates. 15. In addition, the institution's results were very negative from 2011 on, worsening in a very marked way in 2012, which reflected two main factors: (i) the reduction in the financial margin resulting from the low interest rate environment; and (ii) in a much more significant way, the increase in the oddities of the credit portfolio, which was successively reinforced in the sequen-cia of the various independent audits on the quality of assets determined by Banco de Portugal. 16. The significant increase in oddities reflects two contributions of a sea-each different nature. 17. First, BANIF's credit portfolio was affected by the reces-sivo context of the Portuguese economy, with the resulting impact on the volume and quality of credit, which was amplified by the high concentration of credit in small-sized enterprises and in the real estate sector, sectors in which the impact of the economic crisis was felt more strongly. 18. Secondly, this significant increase in oddages is also a reflection of an inadequate credit risk management by BANIF. In fact, it was possible to identify, following banco de Portugal's supervisory activity, a set of management practices that highlight the existence of a negligent approach to the credit risk of BANIF's activity. 19. In particular, irregular situations have been identified in proceedings for the renegotiation of claims, the undue recognition of damaged portfolios and the provision of false or late information to Banco de Portugal which led to the initiation of several counter-national proceedings. These cases have all been completed, with fines of approximately EUR 1.8 million being imposed on the institutions of the BANIF Group and about a dozen directors of the same group. 20. Additionally, Banco de Portugal identified - through an analysis of the credit allocation processes in the exposures that came to present higher im-parities in the inspections of 2011 and 2012 - a set of deficient management practices, such as: (i) about half of the exposures analyzed were approved by the Executive Committee and/or Board of Directors-traction despite the unfavorable opinion of the Bank's Global Risk Directorate and without a rationale appropriate; (ii) lack of risk analysis in some pro-posts; (iii) the constitution of mortgages for an amount higher than that of the valuation of the properties; and (iv) approval of some financing knowing the client's financial inability to repay the debt. 21. Banco de Portugal, following these findings, has ordered a forensic audit of the processes for granting those claims and, after the conclusion of that audit, has ordered the opening of new procedures for the determination of their individual and collective responsibilities. These processes are ongoing. 22. Finally, it should be noted that BANIF developed an agency expansion policy which, in a context of contraction of credit volumes, contributed to a heavy operating cost structure which in 2012 was about one third above the Portuguese banking sector average. 23. In addition, the need to recapitalise BANIF reflects four main factors: (i) the inability of shareholders to strengthen the group's capital or attract new strategic partners; (ii) the effects on credit quality of the deep economic downturn of the Portuguese economy; (iii) the existence of deficient management practices; (iv) and the adoption of a policy of expansion of action that has shown to be unadjusted. C. The opinion of Banco de Portugal of 28 December 2012 24. It was in this context that the capitalisation of BANIF was considered through public inves-timento, under Law No. 63-A/2008 of 24 November, with a view to supporting banks which, although viable, were unable to meet the required levels of capital because they did not have access to the markets. 25. It is important to mention, in this context, some important events throughout 2012. 26. As early as 6 March 2012, in its opinion on the feasibility study heard by Rentipar SGPS, Banco de Portugal considered that the group should to deal with additional measures to increase capital effectively, with the need for the group to have to use the Public Capitalisation Fund for an amount of EUR 440 million to be expected. 27. On 15 May 2012, Banco de Portugal ordered an extraordinary audit of BANIF  which was carried out by PwC  to establish the correct valuation of the assets recorded in the Group's consolidated balance sheet, in particular assets not included in the SIP, regardless of its geographical location and having as reference date the end of the first quarter of 2012. 28. On May 25, 2012, Banco de Portugal determined the formal sending by BA-NIF of a capitalization plan in accordance with and for the purposes provided for in Law No. 63-A/2008, as set out in Ordinance No. 150-A/2012 published on May 17, 2012; 29. On 5 June 2012, Banco de Portugal determined, under Articles 141 and 142 of the GSF, the presentation of a restructuring plan covering: (i) measures to reset capital ratios above the legally required minimum, which should include a significant participation of private investors; and (ii) group reorganization measures. To acompa-nhar the evolution of this plan came to be designated a financial advisor (Citi). 30. On September 21, 2012, Banco de Portugal determined, under arti-gos 141 and 142 of the RGICSF, a set of corrective measures for the preservation of own funds and the submission of certain operations to the prior approval of Banco de Portugal; 31. During this period, the Board of Directors of BANIF submitted to Banco de Portugal, in accordance with the provisions of the law, several versions of the Recapitalization Plan, the last of which on December 28, 2012. This plan included, in the legally defined terms, a statement by the Board of Directors that it was empowered to meet its commitments. 32. On 28 December 2012, Banco de Portugal sent the Ministry of Finance a proposal for a decision proposing the approval of BANIF's access to public investment as provided for in the capitalisation plan, which is a result of a public investment of EUR 1 100 million. 33. In the period preceding this proposal, and in view of the high amount of capital ne-cessions, Banco de Portugal considered alternative solutions to ca-pitalisation, in particular the resolution and liquidation of the Bank, concluding that the option proposed in the Recapitalisation Plan was that, in the circumstances concerned, and taking into account the risks and impacts of the available alternatives, better safeguarded financial stability and the interests of the State and taxpayers by facilitating the return to normal market conditions within an acceptable period, in terms that did not distort competition, without prejudice of course to the risk factors associated with the implementation of the Plan to be identified below. These alternative solutions have been intensively discussed with the Troika and the Government, as is clear from the information sent by Banco de Portugal to this Commission. 34. Banco de Portugal also considered that BANIF presented a systemic risk, and this risk was particularly enhanced by the macro-economic environment of great uncertainty and the still weak recovery of external perception of national risk, in a context where the confidence of depositors was a critical element in the ongoing adjustment process and the disruption of which could have unpredictable effects. 35. In its opinion of 28 December 2012, Banco de Portugal concluded that, in view of the basic macroeconomic scenario and the expected evolution of profitability levels, the institution was able to bear the remuneration and repayment of a significant part of public investment, as well as the projected developments for capital ratios above the applicable regulatory minimums. Thus, the proposed capitalization structure was adequate and the institution was looking forward to viability at the end of the public investment period, with a view to achieving levels of profitability capable of attracting the interest of investors, through which public disinvestment would take place at the end of 2017. 36. In its opinion, Banco de Portugal clearly assumed that the repayment of part of the public investment would not be ensured by generating internal resources within the horizon considered. The repayment would be guaranteed by means of a market sale solution of the shares subscribed by the State, since it was anticipated that the bank would, at the time of that sale, have rentable conditions capable of attracting private capital. 37. Banco de Portugal also noted in its opinion that the viability of an institution is largely endogenous depending heeding much on the capacity of its management. It also noted that there were execution risks associated with macroeconomic development, capital increase, projected levels of profitability and disinvestment. 38. The conclusion on the viability of the institution was duly based on: (i) in the assessment of the starting point, by carrying out several assessment activities by entities independent of the value of the bank's assets; (ii) in the assessment of the institution's capital and financing plans, baseline and in adverse situations; and (iii) In an opinion independent of an investment bank. 39. In the assessment of the starting point, Banco de Portugal determined that several audit work was carried out, which covered extensively and comprehensively the consolidated balance sheet of the group with the aim of establishing, in the name of the existence of losses already incurred and not yet reflected in the consolidated financial statements. 40. The value of the banif group's capital enhancement needs, with reference to 31 December 2012, to meet the minimum core tier 1 solvabili-dade ratio of 10 per cent plus a safety margin of 50 basis points amounted to EUR 1100 million. In view of the situation immediately prior to the end of 2011, about 60 per cent of these capital needs corresponded to higher specific prudential requirements already reflected. The remaining capital requirements sat from ne-gativos results of the bank's activity as a result of increased levels of unevenness and, albeit to a lesser extent, the reduction in the bank's financial margin in a context of low interest rates. 41. It should also be reported that the increase in capital needs compared to what had been anticipated by Banco de Portugal in March (from EUR 440 million to EUR 1100 million) was primarily due to the revision, in relation to initial forecasts, of net results for 2011 and 2012. By way of comparison, it should be noted that, for all eight largest banking groups, the increase in pay and the reduction in financial margin have negatively impacted, in more than 3 billion, the 2012 results account, compared to the figures projected at the beginning of the year. 42. Banco de Portugal also examined the projections and assumptions included in the Financing and Capital Plan with the aim of assessing the bank's ability to generate sufficient results to remunerate public investment at the end of the term of the capitalisation operation and thus conclude by the bank's financial development. In this context, a critical analysis of the reasonableness of the variables and assumptions of the Financing and Capital Plan (such as credit evolution, deposits, financial margin, commissions, operating-onal costs, results in financial operations, other operating results and credit imparity) was performed. From this critical analysis it was concluded that the Financing and Capital Plan presented an insufficient degree of conservatism in some of its projections and that there were material risks, aggravated by a macroeconomic con-juntura of great uncertainty, of execution of the sales values assumed for the disposal of subsidiaries of BANIF and the real estate portfolio, as well as in the respective timing. A sensitivity analysis was carried out with additional degrees of conservatism for the variables and assumptions of the Plan, and it was concluded that an additional capital increase of EUR 300 million was necessary to address a scenario of materialization of the risks of execution anticipated for the period 2013-2014. 43. At the same time, Banco de Portugal considered requesting an independent assessment of the adequacy and exequibili-dade of the measures contemplated in banif's Financing and Capital Plan, in particular the assumptions and results of the associated financial and prudential projections, with a view to confirming the bank's future viability. The opinion expressed by Citi, in the final report sent to Banco de Portugal on November 19, was consistent with Banco de Portugal's assessment, both in the overall reasonableness and credibility of the Financing and Capital Plan presented, as well as the underlying execution risks. In these conditions, Banco de Portugal formally requested BANIF to review the Financing and Capital Plan and submit a re-visa Recapitalization Plan, with a view to issuing an opinion under the Law. 44. In summary, taking into account the capitalisation of BANIF in the above mentioned terms, in particular the projections presented and the macroeconomic scenario defined for the Financing and Capital Plans of the various banks, it was found that the minimum levels of own funds required under the regulations in force of Banco de Portugal were met over the time horizon of the Plan. Additionally, the financial projections presented by BANIF, with an adverse scenario, pointed to an evolution of the Core Tier 1 ratio over the investment period that always placed it above the 6% reference threshold defined in the Economic and Financial Assistance Program for stress-test exercises. 45. The BANIF Recapitalization Plan was approved on January 16 in banif's General Shareholder Office. On 21 January 2013, the European Commission temporarily approved the recapitalisation of BANIF using public functions. Finally, the Portuguese State, through Order No. 1527-B/2013 of January 24, approved, on a proposal from Banco de Portugal, the operation of capitalization of BANIF through the subscription of 400 million euros of hybrid instruments "Core Tier 1" and 700 million euros of special shares of BANIF. D. Monitoring of BANIF by Banco de Portugal after recapitalization 46. Following the public recapitalisation operation, Banco de Portugal, as the prudential supervisory authority, defined enhanced implementation procedures for BANIF which were intended to verify that bank's compliance with a set of conditions and commitments legally covered by the institution and the risks of implementing the recapitalisation plan. Thus, Banco de Portugal: (i) ordered BANIF to carry out, on a regular basis, a set of information resets covering the various strands of the Recapitalisation Plan; (ii) Subjected BANIF to duties of communication and prior authorization of ope-rations within the scope of the commitments entered into; (iii) Kept the Ministry of Finance permanently informed  through regular meetings and correspondence exchange  on compliance with the conditions and commitments legally made, as well as on even-current relevant deviations from the estimates contained in the Recapita-lization Plan and the fulfillment of structural goals, information complemented by the quarterly delivery of Follow-up Reports. 47. In the context of the State aid procedure, it was for the Board of Directors and the shareholders of BANIF to be responsible for submitting and implementing a restructuring plan to DGCOMP, which was responsible for the respetive approval. The non-approval of a Restructuring Plan by DGCOMP has always been a prudential concern for Banco de Portugal. For this reason, Banco de Portugal, in the framework of cooperation with the Ministry of Finance, followed the preparation of the different versions of the plan, having con-tribuido with comments, suggestions for amendment and technical opinions on specific methods. 48. Despite the efforts made by the various actors in this process, it was not possible to achieve a solution that would allow BANIF to continue to develop its activity. Thus, a situation has been reached in which a resolution measure has become necessary  the only one in which Banco de Portugal can replace its shareholders in structural decisions  which, by its very nature, is a measure of last resort, to preserve the safety of savings and public confidence. 49. I conclude by stating that Banco de Portugal is fully aware of having taken action throughout the process in a serious and rigorous manner  at every moment and on the basis of the information available  with the fundamental concern of pro-teger the interests entrusted to it by law: the stability of the financial system, the security of deposits and the preservation of public trust. Thank you very much.
