Estas solues alternativas foram intensamente discutidas com a Troika e com o Governo, como  evidente da informao enviada pelo Banco de Portugal a esta Comisso. 34. O Banco de Portugal considerou tambm que o BANIF apresentava um risco sist-mico, sendo este risco especialmente potenciado pela conjuntura macroecon-mica de grande incerteza e pela ainda dbil recuperao da perceo externa sobre o risco nacional, num contexto em que a confiana dos depositantes constitua um elemento crtico no processo de ajustamento em curso e cuja perturbao poderia ter efeitos imprevisveis. 35. No parecer de 28 de dezembro de 2012, o Banco de Portugal concluiu que, tendo em conta o cenrio macroeconmico de base e a evoluo prevista dos nveis de rendibilidade, a instituio era capaz de suportar a remunerao e o reembolso de parte significativa do investimento pblico, bem como a evoluo projetada para os rcios de capital acima dos mnimos regulamentares aplicveis. Assim, a estrutura de capitalizao proposta mostrava-se adequada e a instituio apre-sentava viabilidade no final do perodo do investimento pblico, tendo em vista atingir nveis de rendibilidade capazes de atrair o interesse de investidores pri-vados, mediante o qual se concretizaria o desinvestimento pblico no final de 2017. 36. No parecer, o Banco de Portugal assumiu, claramente, que o reembolso de uma parte do investimento pblico no seria assegurado com a gerao de recursos internos no horizonte considerado. O reembolso seria garantido atravs de uma soluo de venda em mercado das aes subscritas pelo Estado, na medida em que se antecipava que o banco teria, na altura dessa venda, condies de renta-bilidade suscetveis de atrair capital privado. 37. O Banco de Portugal fez notar tambm no seu parecer que a viabilidade de uma instituio , em grande parte, endgena dependendo muito da capacidade da sua gesto. Fez notar ainda que existiam riscos de execuo associados  evolu-o macroeconmica,  concretizao do aumento de capital, aos nveis de rendi-bilidade e de desinvestimento projetados. 38. A concluso sobre a viabilidade da instituio foi devidamente alicerada: (i) Na avaliao do ponto de partida, atravs da realizao de vrios exerc-cios de avaliao por entidades independentes do valor dos ativos do banco; (ii) Na avaliao dos planos de capital e de financiamento da instituio, em baseline e em situao adversa; e (iii) Num parecer independente de um banco de investimento. 39. Na avaliao do ponto de partida, o Banco de Portugal determinou a realizao de vrios trabalhos de auditoria, j referidos, que cobriram de forma extensiva e abrangente o balano consolidado do grupo com o objetivo de apurar, nomeada-mente, a existncia de perdas j incorridas e ainda no refletidas nas demonstra-es financeiras consolidadas. 40. O valor das necessidades de reforo do capital do grupo BANIF, com referncia a 31 de dezembro de 2012, para dar cumprimento ao rcio mnimo de solvabili-dade Core Tier 1 de 10 por cento acrescido de uma margem de segurana de 50 pontos base ascendia a 1100 milhes de euros. Face  situao imediatamente anterior do final de 2011, cerca de 60 por cento destas necessidades de capital correspondiam a maiores exigncias de natureza prudencial especficas j refe-ridas. As restantes necessidades de fundos prprios decorriam de resultados ne-gativos da atividade do banco, em resultado do reforo dos nveis de imparidade e, embora em menor grau, da reduo da margem financeira do banco, num contexto de taxas de juro baixas. 41. Refira-se, ainda, que o acrscimo das necessidades de capital face ao que tinha sido antecipado pelo Banco de Portugal em maro (de 440 para 1100 milhes de euros) deveu-se, fundamentalmente,  reviso, em relao s previses iniciais, dos resultados lquidos para 2011 e 2012. A ttulo de comparao, importa ter presente que, para o conjunto dos oito maiores grupos bancrios, o aumento de imparidades e a reduo da margem financeira impactaram negativamente, em mais de 3 mil milhes de euros, a conta de resultados de 2012, em relao aos valores projetados no incio do ano. 42. O Banco de Portugal analisou igualmente as projees e os pressupostos inclu-dos no Plano de Financiamento e Capital com o objetivo de aferir a capacidade do banco para gerar resultados suficientes para remunerar o investimento pblico no final do prazo da operao de capitalizao e, deste modo, concluir pela viabi-lidade da instituio. Nesse mbito, foi realizada uma anlise crtica da razoabili-dade das variveis e dos pressupostos do Plano de Financiamento e Capital (como da evoluo do crdito, depsitos, margem financeira, comisses, custos operaci-onais, resultados em operaes financeiras, outros resultados operacionais e im-paridade no crdito). Dessa anlise crtica concluiu-se que o Plano de Financia-mento e Capital apresentava um grau de conservadorismo insuficiente em algu-mas das suas projees e que existiam riscos materiais, agravados por uma con-juntura macroeconmica de grande incerteza, de execuo dos valores de vendas assumidos para a alienao de filiais do BANIF e da carteira de imveis, bem como na respetiva calendarizao. Foi realizada uma anlise de sensibilidade com graus adicionais de conservadorismo para as variveis e pressupostos do Plano, tendo-se concludo ser necessrio um aumento de capital adicional no montante de 300 milhes de euros, para fazer face a um cenrio de materializao dos riscos de execuo antecipados para o perodo 2013-2014. 43. Em paralelo, o Banco de Portugal entendeu solicitar a uma entidade externa es-pecializada, o Citi, uma avaliao independente da adequao e da exequibili-dade das medidas contempladas no Plano de Financiamento e Capital do BANIF, em particular dos pressupostos e resultados das projees financeiras e pruden-ciais associadas, com vista a confirmar a viabilidade futura do banco. A opinio expressa pelo Citi, no relatrio final enviado ao Banco de Portugal no dia 19 de novembro, foi consistente com a avaliao do Banco de Portugal, tanto no que se refere  razoabilidade global e  credibilidade do Plano de Financiamento e Capital apresentado, como aos riscos de execuo subjacentes. Nestas condi-es, o Banco de Portugal solicitou formalmente ao BANIF a reviso do Plano de Financiamento e Capital e a apresentao de um Plano de Recapitalizao re-visto, com vista  emisso de parecer nos termos da Lei. 44. Em sntese, tendo em conta a capitalizao do BANIF nos termos acima referidos, designadamente as projees apresentadas e o cenrio macroeconmico definido para os Planos de Financiamento e Capital dos diversos bancos, verificava-se que os nveis mnimos de fundos prprios exigidos nos termos da regulamentao em vigor do Banco de Portugal eram cumpridos ao longo do horizonte temporal do Plano. Adicionalmente, as projees financeiras apresentadas pelo BANIF, con-siderando um cenrio adverso, apontavam para uma evoluo do rcio Core Tier 1 ao longo do perodo de investimento que o posicionava sempre acima do limiar de referncia de 6% definido no Programa de Assistncia Econmica e Financeira para os exerccios de stress-test. 45. O Plano de Recapitalizao do BANIF foi aprovado, em 16 de janeiro, em Assem-bleia Geral de Acionistas do BANIF. Em 21 de janeiro de 2013, a Comisso Euro-peia aprovou, temporariamente, a recapitalizao do BANIF com recurso a fun-dos pblicos. Finalmente, o Estado Portugus, mediante o Despacho n. 1527-B/2013, de 24 de janeiro, aprovou, sob proposta do Banco de Portugal, a opera-o de capitalizao do BANIF atravs da subscrio de 400 milhes de euros de instrumentos hbridos Core Tier 1 e de 700 milhes de euros de aes especiais do BANIF. D. Acompanhamento do BANIF pelo Banco de Portugal aps a recapitalizao 46. No seguimento da operao de recapitalizao pblica, o Banco de Portugal, en-quanto autoridade de superviso prudencial, definiu procedimentos de acompa-nhamento reforados para o BANIF que se destinavam a verificar o cumprimento por aquele banco de um conjunto de condies e compromissos legalmente assu-midos pela instituio e os riscos de execuo do plano de recapitalizao. Assim, o Banco de Portugal: (i) Determinou que o BANIF realizasse, numa base regular, um conjunto de repor-tes de informao abrangendo as diversas vertentes do Plano de Recapitaliza-o; (ii) Sujeitou o BANIF a deveres de comunicao e de autorizao prvios de ope-raes enquadradas no mbito dos compromissos assumidos; (iii) Manteve o Ministrio das Finanas permanentemente informado  atravs de reunies regulares e de troca de correspondncia - sobre o cumprimento das condies e dos compromissos legalmente assumidos, bem como sobre even-tuais desvios relevantes face s estimativas constantes do Plano de Recapita-lizao e ao cumprimento das metas estruturais, informao complementada pela entrega trimestral de Relatrios de Acompanhamento. 47. No mbito do procedimento de auxlios de Estado, cabia ao Conselho de Admi-nistrao e aos acionistas do BANIF a responsabilidade pela apresentao e pela execuo de um plano de reestruturao  DGCOMP, a quem competia a respe-tiva aprovao. A no aprovao de um Plano de Reestruturao pela DGCOMP constituiu sempre uma preocupao prudencial para o Banco de Portugal. Por esse motivo, o Banco de Portugal, no mbito da cooperao com o Ministrio das Finanas, acompanhou a elaborao das diferentes verses do plano, tendo con-tribudo com comentrios, sugestes de alterao e opinies tcnicas sobre ma-trias especficas. 48. Apesar dos esforos desenvolvidos pelos vrios agentes neste processo, no foi possvel conseguir uma soluo que permitisse ao BANIF continuar a desenvolver a sua atividade. Atingiu-se, assim, uma situao em que se tornou necessria uma medida de resoluo  nica em que o Banco de Portugal se pode substituir aos acionistas em decises estruturais - que, pela sua prpria natureza,  uma medida de ltimo recurso, para preservao da segurana das poupanas e da confiana do pblico. 49. Concluo, afirmando que o Banco de Portugal tem a plena conscincia de ter atu-ado ao longo de todo o processo de forma sria e rigorosa  em cada momento e com base na informao disponvel  com a preocupao fundamental de pro-teger os interesses que lhe esto confiados por lei: a estabilidade do sistema financeiro, a segurana dos depsitos e a preservao da confiana pblica. Muito obrigado.

Title: Interview of Director Luis Laginha de Sousa to Network for Greening the Financial System: "In conversation with..."
text: In Conversation with Mr. Luis Laginha de Sousa Member of the Board of Directors, Banco de Portugal (September 2020) 1. When and why did your institution join the NGFS? The Banco de Portugal joined the NGFS on 11 December, 2018  about one year after it had been launched by its eight founding members. As for why we joined our peers from all over the world in this endeavour, it comes down to a simple fact: we acknowledged that the journey towards a low-carbon economy and, more broadly, towards higher levels of ESG sustainability is one of those, very few, make-or-break issues that are shaping our times and will shape our common future for decades to come. The Banco de Portugal, as part of the Portuguese, European and global communities  but, above all, in its role as a public authority with a diversified set of responsibilities  could not simply stand aside. I am actually quite fond of something very accurately put by a few eminent people, on this issue, a couple of years ago1: the primary responsibility for managing the transition to a low carbon economy rests with the elected governments. However, if it is true that climate change is indeed the greatest and widest ranging market failure ever seen, a smooth low-carbon transition will require the imple-mentation of a comprehensive set of policies, some of which might involve the collaboration of central banks and financial regulators. I would only add that the implementation of policies like these is in-deed very hard to conceive without a significant involvement and collaboration of central banks and financial regulators. 1 Campiglio, E. et al (2018), Climate change challenges for central banks and financial regulators, in Perspec-tive, Nature Climate Change, Vol 8, June 2018, pp. 462-468. In fact, at the root of the sustainability issues and the pressing need to address them is, in all likelihood, the largest global mispricing phenomenon in living memory, to the extent that its negative externali-ties, stemming from the impact of multiple activities, have not yet been correctly incorporated into the prices of products and services charged by the various economic agents. This means all those who carry out such activities, those who incorporate them as intermediate products or services, and those who act as final consumers, but also those who fund such activities. If we believe that this is the main problem, then its solution must entail the adjustment of relative prices, which means making some prices more expensive against others. Clearly, such matters fall mostly within the remit of whoever makes economic and tax-related choices. Nevertheless, in this path of adjustments to the prices of products and services, there is surely a major role to be played also by the financial sector. And, therefore, by the supervisors and regulators both of the financial sector, in general, and of the banking sector, in particular  acting in line with their mandates. Although we are still at what can be considered as an initial stage of involvement with the NGFS, there is no doubt of how relevant such involvement has become. At the end of 2018, when the Bank became a member, we were already 25 central banks and financial supervisors working together, alongside 4 observers. Today, by late September 2020, total membership adds up to 72 institutions and 13 observ-ers. This is a truly amazing pace of expansion, which speaks volumes of how relevant ESG factors and climate change have become for financial systems, in general, and the global community of central banks and financial supervisors, in particular. 2. Can you share with us the key elements of the Banco de Portugals climate strategy and how it fits into the broader national strategy in your jurisdiction? Beginning with the second part of your question, when the Banco de Portugal started to engage more forcefully with sustainability and sustainable finance issues  a couple of years ago  we decided that it would be necessary to get involved in the ongoing or planned national efforts in this field. Apart from some outreach initiatives put forward in partnership with national players of key relevance to the en-ergy transition, the Banco de Portugal thus joined the Government, the two other financial supervisors  for markets and the insurance sector  a few financial industry representatives and several financial institutions in creating a think tank focused on promoting sustainable finance in Portugal. Functioning in both high-level and technical compositions, this new body has been instrumental in advancing awareness of the issues and launching several initiatives, notably a masterplan and a Letter of Com-mitment undersigned by all participants. Our own internal efforts at the Banco de Portugal have matured into a cross-cutting strategy, encom-passing all the different dimensions of the Banks activities which are meaningfully challenged by ESG issues. Released last March, "Banco de Portugal's Commitment to Sustainability and Sustainable Fi-nancing"2 frames the Bank's response to such sustainability challenges  with a special focus on those arising from climate change and sets out action plans in four key areas: 2 the identification and assessment of climate-related risks; the adoption of internal sustainability practices; participation in national and international fora; communication and collaboration with other entities. Going into more detail in each of these action plans: first, we have integrated the identification and assessment of climate-related risks into our research agenda, and a number of research projects are being implemented. In this context, I would like to highlight two studies, which are being completed and we hope to release soon: The first study seeks to assess the Portuguese banking system's exposures to non-financial corporations in relevant sectors from the standpoint of climate change, with the aim of iden-tifying the banking sector's vulnerabilities to the transition towards a low-carbon economy. We believe that it is critical to be well aware of the risks already present in the balance sheets of financial institutions, in view of their exposure to the sectors most likely to be severely im-pacted by the energy transition. The second study addresses the geophysical, technological, and economic aspects of climate change, with a focus on Portugal, and discusses economic policies aimed at dealing with its effects. We hope and trust that these studies will make a positive contribution to "fact based decisions" and hopefully "good fact based decisions". Our second action plan is the implementation of internal sustainability practices, namely in the man-agement of the Bank's asset portfolio and the reduction of its ecological footprint as an organisation. About a year ago, we incorporated the ESG principles into our own asset management guidelines, and implementation is currently underway. Given the size of the Banco de Portugals balance sheet, it is clear how important these guidelines can be for resource allocation in the investment portfolio. Among other initiatives, by the end of January this year, we joined the Lisbon Green Capital 2020 Commitment, an initiative of Lisbon City Council, through which the Bank has committed to take 10 actions, by 2030, in four key areas to tackle climate change -- i.e., energy, water, the circular economy, and citizenship. The third priority action plan we have set out concerns the Bank's intervention in national and inter-national fora where measures that may also have a potential impact on the Portuguese financial sys-tem are discussed. This is a field where much has happened, and on different "stages". At the national level, our involvement with the abovementioned think tank, which brings together financial supervi-sors, Government and industry, is the most relevant reference. At the international level, the Banco de Portugal currently takes part in 12 working groups, committees and other bodies specifically fo-cused on this issue, within the European Central Bank, the European Systemic Risk Board, the European Banking Authority, the Bank for International Settlements and, of course, the NGFS. Our concept of "integrating working groups" is not just about being there and listening to what other people have to say -- although this is also important. A key element of our participation is trying to provide an active contribution aimed at including in the discussion a number of issues that are relevant to our economy and our financial system. We must bear in mind that it is in many of these working groups that guidelines are prepared to be incorporated into the rules established at European level and applied to each of the EU member states. In a context where the rules under which we operate are increasingly set at European rather than national level, we need to be able to follow-up and mon-itor everything that can impact us through a supranational regulatory approach, aiming to avoid neg-ative impacts and, if possible, influence decisions so that they can be positive for the economy and for the country as a whole. Finally, the Banco de Portugals fourth and last action plan to address sustainability challenges is com-munication and cooperation with external entities, which covers the establishment of contacts, net-working, and the implementation of disclosure and other initiatives. In this field, the Bank has so far mostly participated in various conferences and seminars, published articles in specialised journals and cooperated with the media. 3. To what extent did the Banco de Portugal leverage the work of the NGFS in its own domestic journey? Any concrete examples? The Banco de Portugal regards its engagement with the NGFS as particularly strategic to our own po-sitioning in the area of sustainability and sustainable finance. Indeed, its specific focus on greening the financial system, the fact that it is a coalition of the willing, its global range  bringing together experiences, best practices and, increasingly, a common will to act, involving peers from all over the world  are features that set the NGFS apart. The Bank is committed to sharing its own experience, while benefitting from close access to the expe-rience of our peers, participating in the early discussion around issues of relevance to the Portuguese financial system and also trying to contribute towards the advancement of international efforts in this field. Indeed, since we began taking part in the networks activities  notably, joining the various work streams established within it  our approach has been largely focused on providing inputs, as signifi-cant as possible, to the work undertaken by those bodies. Conversely, the awareness to specific issues within the realm of sustainability and sustainable finance that was gained through our participation in the NGFS has actually spilt over to several areas of our activity in this field, be it through our participation in other national and international bodies or our own internal initiatives. That was the case in shaping our cross-cutting roadmap, the abovementioned Commitment, and many of the initiatives to be carried out under it. But also, for instance, in terms of such concrete NGFS outputs as the work on scenario analysis3 or the guide for portfolio managers4, which were and are important inputs to what the Banco de Portugal has been doing. 3 4 4. One last word? It is only appropriate to go back to where we started  the involvement of Banco de Portugal with the NGFS. Having formerly been connected to the business world, where competition is the name of the game  therefore resulting in winners and losers  it is indeed a privilege to witness the remarkable ability shown by the global community of central banks and financial supervisors to share information and to cooperate in such an open and committed manner  thus creating only winners. Against this background, the importance of contributing to a healthy technical debate within the NGFS and other fora cannot be understated. That is the path to follow if we seek to enjoy the fruits that come from having the force of reason, and not to endure the bitterness derived from being struck by the reason of force.

Title: Intervention of Administrator Hlder Rosalino at the opening session of the Interbank Meeting on Payment Systems
text: Interbank Meeting on Payment Systems September 28, 2017 Opening intervention - Helder Rosalino I would like to begin by thanking everyone for being present at this very participatory interbank meeting, which I assume is the result of the importance and timeliness of the issues we have on the agenda. I think we all share the idea that the Portuguese payment system has been recognised internationally over the years as one of the most outlawed and efficient. Just as we agree that this positioning greatly contributed to the capacity of our banking system to cooperate in the development of national payment infrastructures, particularly in the framework of the operation of the Interbank Clearing System (SICOI), but not only in this system. It is in this framework and aware of the responsibility that assumes in this area that Banco de Portugal, taking into account the operational and regulatory developments that have been anactioned in the short term, some of them of disruptive nature, considered to hold this Interbank Meeting on Payment Systems, inviting all credit institutions to operate in Portugal, which covers topics of greatest relevance to the national banking community. I In the first topic of the agenda we will deal with "immediate payment" solutions that are under development at national and European level. The phenomenon of the digitisation of economies and societies is irreversibly changing the expectations of economic operators in various contexts. The way they make payments is no exception. Following this trend and the market dynamics itself, banks have sought to develop faster payment solutions, with greater availability and with added ease of use. It should be said in this regard that this development has been supported by the European authorities, both by the European Commission and by the ECB. Immediate payment solutions developed in recent decades in European countries (based on payment cards and credit transfers) are not, as a rule, interoperable with each other. It thus means that its use is restricted to a limited number of adhering payment service providers  usually from the same national banking community, a situation that enhances a new scenario of fragmentation of the payment market at European level. This scenario is contrary to the integration ideal that has supported the development of the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA). In this context, the implementation of interoperable immediate payment solutions at European level is one of the main challenges facing banks in the short term. With the aim of ensuring the development of interoperable immediate payment solutions at European level, in December 2014 the European Retail Payments Board (ERPB) agreed on the need to create at least one pan-European euro immediate payment solution accessible to any Payment Service Provider (PSP) operating in the European Union. The definition of harmonised technical procedures and requirements has been developed by the European Payments Council (EPC). And following these works was created the SCHEME SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCTInst), which will be available for effective adoption by Payment Service Providers from November 21, 2017. The solution created states that: (i) the funds should be available in the beneficiary's account within an indicative maximum time of ten seconds; (ii) the payee's Payment Service Provider is obliged to accept all transactions of eur 15,000 or less; (iii) operations may be ordered at any time of the day and on any day of the year (24/7/365); and (iv) the payer's and payee's Payment Service Providers may be established in any of the 34 SEPA countries. In this context, several banking communities will launch immediate payment solutions in the coming months. In Portugal too, it is being developed by SIBS and a national cooperative immediate payment solution will be made available within sICOI, in line with the harmonised technical requirements defined at European level. This new SICOI subsystem is expected to start operating in April 2018. SIBS will present in detail the evolution of this project, as well as the challenges and opportunities it poses to the national banking community. In addition, with the aim of ensuring interoperable immediate payment solutions at European level, the Governing Council of the ECB approved on 22 June 2017 the development of a new settlement service at TARGET2 exclusively dedicated to the processing of immediate payments. This new service called TARGET Instant Payment Settlement (TIPS) is expected to start operating in November 2018 and is already under development. TIPS is a solution to ensure the full interoperability and accessibility of all European Payment Service Providers, complementing the offer provided by European clearing rooms with a central bank currency settlement service for immediate payments. Banco de Portugal will present the state of play of the development of this project and its objectives. II As a second topic we have the "changes to SICOI's risk management mechanisms and the processes associated with compensation reform." Following the international reformulation of the requirements that payment systems must meet in order to be resilient and contribute to preserving financial stability, SICOI, as a prominently important retail payment system, has undergone an evaluation process. Following this evaluation, the need to optimize risk management mechanisms and procedures to be adopted in a participant suspension/exclusion event was identified. With regard to the procedures for the urgent suspension or exclusion of sicoi participants, it should be resemable that this is a measure that will gradually extend to all SICOI subsystems and which has been worked on at the level of the different interbank groups existing in the cisp structure, taking into account the specificities of each instrument covered. This initiative originated in 2015, in a then-carried sicoi assessment of the 12 Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (PFMIs) applicable to prominently important retail payment systems, in which the need to optimise the procedures to be developed in an urgent suspension/exclusion event of a participant was identified. The SICOI Regulation provides that Banco de Portugal, in the course of its duties, may suspend or exclude a participant from a clearing subsystem. In addition, the SICOI Regulation provides that, in the event of a lack or insufficiency of provision in the settlement account opened in TARGET2 and after analysis of the specific situation, Banco de Portugal may determine the recalculation of balances excluding the defaulting participant and their debit and credit operations. However, in the event of an event of exclusion, suspension or failure of liquidation, the remaining participants do not currently receive detailed information about the operations that, in that specific case, have not been completed, requiring administrative work to identify these operations and, where possible, reverted to customers. In order to accommodate these recommendations, Banco de Portugal, in collaboration with the interbank working groups, has defined a set of amendments to the SICOI, which are expected to be implemented in a phased manner by the end of 2018. III Thirdly, we will also address the main impacts associated with the entry into force of the new Payment Services Directive (PSD2), many of which are disruptive to the provision of payment services at European level. Since the entry into force of the first Payment Services Directive (PSD) in 2009, there has been a growing digitisation of financial services, embodied in the emergence of new payment service providers, innovative payment solutions, more demanding users and new challenges for payment security. In this context, the European legislature decided to update the regulatory framework through the publication of the PSD2. This Directive seeks to contribute to the creation of a single market for payment services that is both secure (both for payment service providers and for users), efficient, innovative and competitive. PSD2 maintains, in essence, the regulatory framework adopted with the entry into force of PSD1. However, the scope is wider, and the payment transactions where at least one of the payment service providers is located in the European Union, regardless of the currency used in the transaction. The rules set out in PSD2 shall apply in the relationship between the paying customer and his payment service provider (but only for the parts of the payment transaction carried out in the Union), for example, when the former orders a dollar credit transfer to an account opened in a bank located in any country outside the Union. PSD2 creates and regulates new types of payment services, defines a set of security requirements to be respected in the execution of payment transactions, and imposes greater responsibilities on payment service providers in the execution of unauthorized payment transactions.  New payment services  PSD2 has established and regulated two new activities related to access to payment accounts and the execution of online payments, designated, respectively, by account information services and payment initiation services  Security requirements in the execution of payment transactions - PSD2 establishes a set of security requirements for payment services provided electronically. With the entry into force of the Directive, payment service providers will have to start authenticating their customers using strong authentication mechanisms.  Unauthorized payment transactions - PSD2 also reinforces the safeguards of the payment service user in the performance of unauthorized payment transactions. This Directive will certainly be a central element in the provision of payment services in Europe, especially as it includes the action of new types of payment service providers, but also because it introduces new security requirements for non-face-to-face transactions. It is in this framework that national banks have to position themselves. Ensuring, on the one hand, timely compliance with the new regulatory requirements and, on the other hand, preparing to operate in an increasingly innovative and competitive market. Banco de Portugal is preparing the preliminary draft transposition of PSD2 into the internal legal system, having promoted in June 2017 a public consultation on the options that the Portuguese State may exercise in the context of the transposition process. The aim is to finalise the legislative process in time for the new legal framework to enter into force in January 2018. Banco de Portugal will make a presentation of the main changes resulting from the entry into force of the new DSP2 and the current state of the work transposition of this Directive. In a way, the themes prepared for this session take on a wide range and will have implications for the forthcoming evolution of retail payment services. Banco de Portugal reiterates the advantages of the strong cooperation that has supported the evolution of national payment systems, largely based on the work of existing interbank groups within the framework of the Interbank Commission for Payment Systems, reinforcing the importance of each institution of the banking system preparing in time for the new challenges that currently arise. I thank you once again for your presence and interest in the topics proposed for our working session, which naturally provides for the opportunity for some debate around the presentations that will be made. Elder Rosalino
text_original: Reunio interbancria sobre Sistemas de Pagamentos 28 de setembro de 2017 Interveno de abertura  Hlder Rosalino Gostaria de comear por agradecer a presena de todos nesta reunio interbancria, bastante participada, o que presumo resulta da importncia e da atualidade dos temas que temos em agenda. Julgo que todos partilhamos a ideia de que o Sistema de Pagamentos portugus tem sido, ao longo dos anos, reconhecido a nvel internacional como um dos mais evoludos e eficientes. Do mesmo modo que concordamos que para este posicionamento muito contribuiu a capacidade do nosso sistema bancrio em cooperar no desenvolvimento das infraestruturas de pagamento nacionais, designadamente no mbito do funcionamento do Sistema de Compensao Interbancria (SICOI), mas no s neste sistema.  neste enquadramento e ciente da responsabilidade que assume nesta rea, que o Banco de Portugal, tendo em considerao as evolues operacionais e regulamentares que se anteveem no curto prazo, algumas delas de carter disruptivo, entendeu realizar a presente Reunio Interbancria sobre Sistemas de Pagamentos, convidando todas as Instituies de Crdito a operar em Portugal, que cobre tpicos da maior relevncia para a comunidade bancria nacional. I No primeiro tpico da agenda iremos tratar as solues de pagamentos imediatos que esto em fase de desenvolvimento ao nvel nacional e europeu. O fenmeno da digitalizao das economias e das sociedades est a alterar, de forma irreversvel, as expetativas dos agentes econmicos em vrios contextos. A forma como realizam pagamentos no  exceo. Seguindo esta tendncia e a prpria dinmica do mercado, os bancos tm procurado desenvolver solues de pagamento mais rpidas, com maior disponibilidade e com facilidade de utilizao acrescida. Diga-se, a este propsito, que esta evoluo tem vindo a ser suportada pelas autoridades europeias, tanto pela Comisso Europeia, como pelo BCE. As solues de pagamentos imediatos desenvolvidas nas ltimas dcadas nos pases europeus (baseadas em cartes de pagamento e em transferncias a crdito) no so, por norma, interoperveis entre si. Significa, assim, que a sua utilizao se encontra restringida a um nmero limitado de prestadores de servios de pagamentos aderentes  habitualmente de uma mesma comunidade bancria nacional, situao que potencia um novo cenrio de fragmentao do mercado de pagamentos a nvel europeu. Este cenrio  contrrio ao ideal de integrao que tem suportado o desenvolvimento da rea nica de Pagamentos em Euros (SEPA). Neste quadro, a implementao de solues de pagamentos imediatos interoperveis a nvel europeu  um dos principais desafios que se colocam aos bancos no curto prazo. Com o objetivo de assegurar o desenvolvimento de solues de pagamentos imediatos interoperveis a nvel europeu, em dezembro de 2014 o European Retail Payments Board (ERPB) concordou na necessidade de ser criada, pelo menos, uma soluo pan-europeia de pagamentos imediatos em euros, acessvel a qualquer Prestador de Servios de Pagamento (PSP) a operar na Unio Europeia. A definio dos procedimentos e requisitos tcnicos harmonizados foi desenvolvida pelo European Payments Council (EPC). E na sequncia destes trabalhos foi criado o scheme SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCTInst), que estar disponvel para adoo efetiva pelos Prestadores de Servios de Pagamento a partir de 21 de novembro de 2017. A soluo criada estabelece que: (i) os fundos devero estar disponveis na conta do beneficirio num tempo mximo indicativo de dez segundos; (ii) o Prestador de Servios de Pagamento do beneficirio  obrigado a aceitar todas as transaes de valor igual ou inferior a 15 mil euros; (iii) as operaes podem ser ordenadas a qualquer momento do dia e em qualquer dia do ano (24/7/365); e (iv) os Prestador de Servios de Pagamento do ordenante e do beneficirio podem estar estabelecidos em qualquer um dos 34 pases da SEPA. Neste mbito, diversas comunidades bancrias vo lanar nos prximos meses solues de pagamentos imediatos. Tambm em Portugal est a ser desenvolvida pela SIBS e ser, no mbito do SICOI, disponibilizada uma soluo cooperativa nacional de pagamentos imediatos, em linha com os requisitos tcnicos harmonizados definidos a nvel europeu. Este novo subsistema do SICOI deve iniciar o seu funcionamento em abril de 2018. A SIBS ir apresentar detalhadamente a evoluo deste projeto, bem como os desafios e oportunidades que o mesmo coloca  comunidade bancria nacional. Complementarmente, com o objetivo de assegurar a existncia de solues de pagamentos imediatos interoperveis a nvel europeu, o Conselho de Governadores do BCE aprovou, em 22 de junho de 2017, o desenvolvimento de um novo servio de liquidao no TARGET2 exclusivamente dedicado ao processamento de pagamentos imediatos. Este novo servio designado de TARGET Instant Payment Settlement (TIPS) deve iniciar o seu funcionamento em novembro de 2018 e est j em fase de desenvolvimento. O TIPS assume-se como uma soluo que visa garantir a plena interoperabilidade e acessibilidade de todos os Prestadores de Servios de Pagamentos europeus, complementando a oferta disponibilizada pelas cmaras de compensao europeias com um servio de liquidao em moeda de banco central para pagamentos imediatos. O Banco de Portugal far uma apresentao do ponto de situao do desenvolvimento deste projeto e dos seus objetivos. II Como segundo tpico temos as alteraes aos mecanismos de gesto do risco do SICOI e aos processos associados  reforma da compensao. Na sequncia da reformulao, a nvel internacional, dos requisitos que os sistemas de pagamento devem respeitar para que sejam resilientes e contribuam para preservar a estabilidade financeira, o SICOI, enquanto sistema de pagamentos de retalho proeminentemente importante, foi alvo de um processo de avaliao. Na sequncia desta avaliao foi identificada a necessidade de se otimizarem os mecanismos de gesto do risco e os procedimentos a adotar num evento de suspenso / excluso de um participante. Relativamente aos procedimentos de suspenso ou excluso urgente de participantes no SICOI, haver a reter que se trata de uma medida que se estender gradualmente a todos os subsistemas do SICOI e que tem sido trabalhada ao nvel dos diferentes grupos interbancrios existentes na estrutura da CISP, atendendo s especificidades de cada instrumento abrangido. Esta iniciativa teve origem em 2015, numa avaliao ento realizada do SICOI face aos 12 Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (PFMIs) aplicveis aos sistemas de pagamento de retalho proeminentemente importantes, em que foi identificada a necessidade de se otimizar os procedimentos a desenvolver num evento de suspenso / excluso urgente de um participante. O Regulamento do SICOI prev que o Banco de Portugal, no mbito do exerccio das suas funes, possa suspender ou excluir um participante de um subsistema de compensao. Adicionalmente, o Regulamento do SICOI prev que, no caso de falta ou insuficincia de proviso na conta de liquidao aberta no TARGET2 e aps anlise da situao concreta, o Banco de Portugal possa determinar o reclculo dos saldos multilaterais, excluindo-se o participante em incumprimento e as respetivas operaes a dbito e a crdito. No entanto, caso ocorra um evento de excluso, suspenso ou falha de liquidao, os restantes participantes no recebem atualmente informao detalhada sobre as operaes que, naquele caso concreto, no foram concludas, obrigando a um trabalho administrativo para que essas operaes sejam identificadas e, quando possvel, revertidas junto dos clientes. Com o intuito de acomodar as referidas recomendaes, o Banco de Portugal, em colaborao com os grupos de trabalho interbancrios, definiu um conjunto de alteraes ao SICOI, as quais se esperam implementadas de forma faseada at ao final de 2018. III Como terceiro tpico, iremos ainda abordar os principais impactos associados  entrada em vigor da nova Diretiva dos Servios de Pagamento (PSD2), muitos deles disruptivos para a prestao de servios de pagamento a nvel europeu. Desde a entrada em vigor da primeira Diretiva dos Servios de Pagamento (PSD), em 2009, verificou-se uma crescente digitalizao dos servios financeiros, consubstanciada no surgimento de novos prestadores de servios de pagamentos, de solues de pagamento inovadoras, de utilizadores mais exigentes e de novos desafios para a segurana dos pagamentos. Neste contexto, o legislador europeu decidiu atualizar o enquadramento regulamentar atravs da publicao da PSD2. Esta Diretiva procura contribuir para a criao de um mercado nico para os servios de pagamento que seja simultaneamente seguro (quer para os prestadores de servios de pagamentos, quer para os utilizadores), eficiente, inovador e concorrencial. A PSD2 mantm, na sua essncia, o quadro normativo adotado com a entrada em vigor da PSD1. No entanto, o mbito de aplicao  mais alargado, passando a regular as operaes de pagamento sempre que pelo menos um dos prestadores de servios de pagamento esteja situado na Unio Europeia, independentemente da moeda utilizada na operao. As regras definidas na PSD2 aplicar-se-o na relao entre o cliente ordenante e o seu prestador de servios de pagamento (mas apenas quanto s partes da operao de pagamento efetuadas na Unio), por exemplo, quando o primeiro ordenar uma transferncia a crdito em dlares para uma conta aberta num banco situado em qualquer pas fora do espao da Unio. A PSD2 cria e regula novos tipos de servios de pagamento, define um conjunto de requisitos de segurana a respeitar na execuo de operaes de pagamento e impe aos prestadores de servios de pagamento maiores responsabilidades na execuo de operaes de pagamento no autorizadas.  Novos servios de pagamento  A PSD2 veio estabelecer e regular duas novas atividades relacionadas com o acesso s contas de pagamento e com a execuo de pagamentos online, designados, respetivamente, por servios de informao sobre contas e servios de iniciao de pagamentos  Requisitos de segurana na execuo de operaes de pagamento - A PSD2 estabelece um conjunto de requisitos de segurana para os servios de pagamento fornecidos por via eletrnica. Com a entrada em vigor da diretiva, os prestadores de servios de pagamento tero de passar a autenticar os seus clientes com recurso a mecanismos de autenticao forte.  Operaes de pagamento no autorizadas - A PSD2 refora tambm as salvaguardas do utilizador de servios de pagamento perante a execuo de operaes de pagamento no autorizadas. Esta diretiva ser certamente um elemento central na prestao de servios de pagamento no espao europeu, especialmente porque contempla a atuao de novos tipos de prestadores de servios de pagamento, mas tambm porque introduz novos requisitos de segurana para as transaes no presenciais.  neste enquadramento que os bancos nacionais se tm de posicionar. Assegurando, por um lado, o cumprimento atempado dos novos requisitos regulamentares e, por outro, preparando-se para operar num mercado cada vez mais inovador e concorrencial. O Banco de Portugal encontra-se a preparar o anteprojeto de transposio da PSD2 para o ordenamento jurdico interno, tendo promovido em junho de 2017 uma consulta pblica s opes que o Estado Portugus pode exercer no mbito do processo de transposio. O objetivo passa por finalizar o processo legislativo a tempo da entrada em vigor do novo quadro legal em janeiro de 2018. O Banco de Portugal far uma apresentao das principais alteraes que resultam da entrada em vigor da nova DSP2 e do estado atual dos trabalhos de transposio desta diretiva. Em suma, os temas preparados para esta sesso assumem uma grande abrangncia e tero implicaes na evoluo prxima dos servios de pagamento de retalho. O Banco de Portugal reitera as vantagens da forte cooperao que tem suportado a evoluo dos sistemas de pagamentos nacionais, em grande medida assente no trabalho dos grupos interbancrios existentes no quadro da Comisso Interbancria para os Sistemas de Pagamentos, reforando a importncia de cada instituio do sistema bancrio se preparar atempadamente para os novos desafios que atualmente se colocam. Agradeo mais uma vez a vossa presena e o interesse nos temas propostos para a nossa sesso de trabalho, que naturalmente prev a oportunidade de algum debate em torno das apresentaes que iro ser efetuadas. Hlder Rosalino

Title: Introduction of the Governor to the Report of the Commission for the Analysis of budgetary situation
text: COMMISSION REPORT FOR THE ANALYSIS OF THE BUDGETARY SITUATION INTRODUCTION BY THE GOVERNOR OF BANCO DE PORTUGAL May 2005 INTRODUCTION BY THE GOVERNOR OF BANCO DE PORTUGAL 1. For the second time I was asked by the Government to chair a Commission to examine the state of public finances. In 2002, it was a question of reassessing the accounts of the previous year and this time an estimate of the expected deficit for 2005. As I wrote in the introduction to the 2002 Report: "Although the matter does not fall under the normal competences of Banco de Portugal, the government's advisory functions which its Organic Law specifies justify the acceptance of the mission in question." In fact, the Bank has a duty to cooperate with the Government and has done so, now as in 2002, with the same sense of responsibility and with the independence generally recognized to the work of the technicians who integrate it. It is also the Bank's obligation to regularly disclose objective analyses of the country's economic situation, warning of macroeconomic problems that may affect stability and growth. The Bank has fulfilled this duty even at the risk of misunderstandings by opinion segments that vary naturally with conjunctures. Since 2000 I have been drawing attention to the need for a member country of a monetary union to have to use fiscal policy in an anti-cyclical manner, looking for surpluses in the phases of strong growth in order to be able to withstand deficits in the depressed periods. Unfortunately, like other European countries, Portugal did not take advantage of the favourable phase of the cycle to consolidate public finances. Thus, when the international economic situation suddenly suffered a sharp slowdown, the budget deficit worsened substantially. That is why I classified the situation as a 'fiscal crisis' in 2001 and supported the measures taken since 2002 to reduce the deficit. Consolidation was, however, insufficient and compliance with the Stability Pact was largely based on temporary measures that reached 1.5; 2.5 and 2.3 percent of GDP in 2002, 2003 and 2004, respectively. Although legitimate in order to formally comply with the Pact, extraordinary revenues are by nature incapable of being repeated indefinitely, so the Bank has always analysed the budgetary situation also taking into account the budget deficit that excludes them. In January of this year, in the Presentation Note of the Bank's Economic Bulletin, I stated: '... the use of extraordinary revenues helped to create the illusion that the budgetary problem was in the process of being solved or that time would eventually be solved without further effective measures. However, if we exclude the extraordinary measures, the deficits of 2003 to 2005 point to figures of around 5 per cent of GDP. It is therefore strange that one might think that it would be possible to continue to find temporary revenues of more than 2 per cent of GDP (around EUR 3 billion) every year. The events of 2004 surrounding this issue clearly reveal that this has become increasingly difficult. The time has therefore come for the real reduction of the budget deficit over the next two years." What was implicit in this statement was the forecast, carried out internally at the end of 2004, of a deficit without extraordinary measures slightly above 5 percent of GDP. A new forecast made in March this year already gave a slightly higher result and this has worsened with the consideration of the additional information to which the Commission has now had access. 2. The main part of the Commission's mandate was to draw up a review of the budget deficit forecast in 2005, without considering further policy measures, and to re-include the Road Institute of Portugal within the public administrations perimeter. The work carried out was based on models of forecasting and information directly requested and received from some public services. In fact, a detailed analysis of relevant areas of budgetary implementation was carried out on the basis of information requested from various public administration bodies and services. As stated in the Report: "In assessing this information, the figures included in the OE-2005-based account are systematically compared with the estimates drawn up by the Commission with a view to quantifying the likely effects on the PA deficit. The selected areas were: the tax revenue of the PAs; state dividends; the primary expenditure of the State; the National Health Service; the Roads of Portugal; Social Security; the General Retirement Box; financial contribution to the EU; public investment; capital increases, debt adjustments by the Treasury and privatisation revenue used in debt amortization; and the stock of the debt and the expenses in interest.' 3. The conclusion reached by the Commission points to a deficit of 6.8 per cent of domestic product Bruto if further budgetary consolidation measures are not adopted 1. This corresponds to a significant increase from the deficit in 2004 which, without extraordinary revenues, stood at 5.2 per cent of GDP and represents an even greater deviation from the deficit foreseen in the 2005 Budget Report (about 4.3 per cent without temporary revenues). It is also above the internal forecasts that Banco de Portugal had drawn up and were implicit in the macroeconomic projections published in last December's Economic Bulletin. Picture 1 Budget Deficit Forecasts (as % of GDP) Year Deficit with Extraordinary Revenues Deficit without Extraordinary Revenues Deficit verified 2004 -2,9 % -5,2 % OE Report for 2005 2005 -2,9 % -4,3 % BP's internal forecast on Dec 04 2005 -3,9 % -5,1 % Commission forecast 2005 --- -6,8 % Commission forecast with GDP higher at 5% (1) 2005 --- -6,5% To better understand what is underlying the estimate now made, it is necessary to analyze the following points: 3.1.) reasons for the exclusion of extraordinary revenues; 3.2.) explanation of the deviation of the current forecast from the budgeted figures; 3.3.) fundamentals of the difference in the current estimate from the deficit value in 2004. 1 Assuming that the imminent revision of the GDP series, as in several other European countries, will lead to an increase of around 5%, the estimated deficit would rise to 6.5 per cent (see Table 7.1). Let's look at each of these aspects. 3.1.) The estimate carried out excluded the consideration of the extraordinary or temporary revenues that were foreseen in the Budget, mainly because they no longer sem viable. The four sources of temporary revenue considered in the Budget were the following: GALP dividends ( 548 million); Sale of Assets used by the State ( 500 million); Transfer of Pension Funds ( 422 million); Sale of concessions ( 500 million). As is well known, the first two were disapproved by Eurostat already after the budget was adopted. The transfer of budgeted Pension Funds (from Caixa Geral de Depositos e outros) corresponded to the forecast that part of the amounts of funds transferred at the end of 2004 could be realised as early as 2005 because it was not necessary last year to meet the deficit target to be below 3 per cent of GDP. It happened, however, that it was necessary after all to make full use in 2004 of all the amounts involved in those Pension Funds. Finally, as far as the sale of concessions' heading has not been fully established and, in any event, nothing specific was now provided for in the services on this subject. 3.2.) As to the deviation from the Commission's forecast for the budgeted balance, the following table (which is a summary of Table 4.19 of the Report) reveals the key aspects: Framework 2 Revised Budget Balance The first point to be highlighted is that the forecast of revenues is only slightly below budgeted. This is due to the 2004 starting point being higher than expected at the time of budgeting and assuming that the efficiency gains of the tax administration will continue this year. The evolution of total revenues hides, however, differentiated progress from various taxes as analyzed in detail in the text of the Report (pages 24 to 29). The main loss of revenue, however, refers to dividends to be received by the State from public companies and other equity interests (less 740.3 million). As regards differences in expenditure or additional negative balances for some services, the main points to be highlighted are related to budgeting weaknesses in several headings. The most relevant is the National Health Service for which a deficit is estimated to be higher than that reported in the Budget at EUR 1512.8 million. As in this part for years, but in an increasing way, budgets do not correctly provide for the evolution of revenue and expenditure, giving rise to the need for further adjustments. For 2005, budgeted expenditure was lower than in 2004, as can be seen in the following table (see Table 4.11 of the Report): Framework 3 National Health Service As in the previous two years, the 2005 State Budget determines a high amount of expenditure captives. In 2004 it was that a significant percentage of these captives had to be cancelled in return for unavoidable expenditure. For 2005, after a detailed analysis, it was accepted that the execution rate of the captives would be similar to that of the previous year, implying an estimated more expenditure amounting to EUR 614.1 million. It should be noted that the hypothesis of maintaining a final percentage of captivated appropriations equal to that of the previous year is a demanding objective to be met. As regards the provisional allocation, an amount entered in the budget of the Ministry of Finance to meet current and unplanned capital expenditure, the need for an increase in the amount of eur 180 million was estimated. This is the result of a 180 million cut in the allocation for capital expenditure that is not necessary and a 360 million increase needed to meet the remuneration costs of civil servants, as the budgeted amount would represent a decrease of 0.8 per cent compared to 2004, when it is true that there has been an increase of 2.25 per cent and that there would be a significant effect of progression in the ranks of non-higher education teachers. As it is known, the Budget for 2005 excluded the Institute of Roads of Portugal after its transformation into a public business entity. However, as their own revenues are far from the 50 percent of the costs necessary for, according to national accounting rules, a public entity not being considered in public administrations (see Annex 1 to the Report), it was necessary to re-include that body in the budget deficit estimate, which resulted in an increase of EUR 458.3 million. As regards the Social Security Budget, the Commission took on one of the scenarios for reviewing budget implementation drawn up by the Social Security Financial Management Institute (IGFSS). This new forecast implies a worsening of its deficit by EUR 598.8 million, 497.5 million revision sums of revenues and a 101.2 million increase in expenditure, including 50.3 million for unemployment benefit. The estimated implementation of the Budget of the General Retirement Fund implies a worsening of the deficit by EUR 228.3 million resulting primarily from a higher revision of pension expenditure by 216.5 million, as the budget did not consider the updating of pensions which, as usual, was equal to the updating of the salary scale of active civil servants. All these budget deficit changes associated with such significant budgeting weaknesses should lead to in-depth reflection followed by the indispensable decision-making that changes the rules and institutional framework for drawing up and presenting the Budget so that such situations no longer occur in the future. As regards Investment Expenditure, the Commission assumed a much more moderate evolution of public investment in 2005 (nominal change of -0.7 per cent), in line with the expected developments in EU transfers and a chance of non-variation in non-participating investment. This change has resulted in a decrease in the PA deficit of 796.2 million and is close to the behaviour that has occurred in recent years with substantial differences between budgeted figures and final implementation (-319 million in 2001, -778 million in 2002, 1290.6 million in 2003 and - 485.2 million in 2004). 3.3.) To explain the evolution of the deficit in 2004, excluding temporary revenues (5.2 per cent of GDP) and the one now estimated by the Commission for 2005 (6.8 per cent of GDP), the Commission decommins that difference between what can be attributed to developments in the economic environment, the effects of discretionary measures and waste (Table 4 and Table 5.2) of the Report). Framework 4 A the budget balance, as economic growth will mean that the difference for potential product will increase only slightly. Thus, the change in the deficit from 2004 to 2005 is explained by the impact of discretionary fiscal policy measures (-0.7 p.p. of GDP) and by other factors (-0.8 p.p. of GDP). The justification for the increase in the deficit from 2004 to 2005 by 1.6 percentage points of GDP can be summed up by the following essential aspects: reduction of tax revenue through discretionary changes in taxes (-0.48 p.p. of the fall in the IRC rate, -0.13 p.p. of the IRS and 0.07 of the ISP); decrease in dividends received by the State (-0.4 p.p. of GDP); strong growth of some headings of primary current expenditure, including intermediate consumption (0.2 p.p. of GDP), staff expenditure (0.2 p.p. of GDP) and expenditure on pensions (0.5 p.p. of GDP). 4 Of. Even if it were possible to find other extraordinary revenues that partially replaced those that were planned, this would only be legitimate, as I recalled last January "if they are significantly reduced and used in the context of a programme that solves the budgetary problem over the next three years. This will also involve taking further effective measures to increase revenue and contain expenditure. This is a programme that has both difficult and inexorable." This makes it possible to stress once again that the Commission's work boils down to a forecast of this year's budget deficit, in the event that no new policies will be adopted in the meantime. The worsening of the situation that the new estimate shows certainly reinforces the need for measures to reduce the deficit as early as this year. The conditional provision that has been drawn up should therefore be desired ly invalidated. As is often the case in economics, the best predictions are those that do not occur, given the reactions they trigger. As with all forecasts there are several risks of for the 2005 PA deficit produced by the Commission, and the Report groups (see page 51) into five areas: (i) the forecast of tax revenue; (ii) the degree of implementation of the captives in State expenditure and the budgetary implementation of autonomous services and funds, excluding the SNS; (iii) the amount of the financial contribution to the EU on the basis of GNP; (iv) the budgetary results of the regional and local administration, which have not been reviewed by the Commission; and, finally, (v) the eventual realization of capital increases and regularizations of past situations by the Treasury, which should be classified as above-the-line expenditure, in National Accounting. The truth is, in any case, and this justifies the insistence on the need for budgetary discipline under the Stability and Growth Pact which remains fully valid with the recently introduced amendments. Regardless of what one thinks of the Pact from the perspective of monetary union as a whole, it must be distinguished from the need for a country like Portugal to continue to respect the rules that are defined. Moreover, budgetary discipline is also at its very disposal when one thinks of the long-term interests of the Portuguese economy which involve the recovery of the anti-cyclical role of budgetary policy which can only be fully exercised after we have reached a more balanced position. On the other hand, the growing burden of pension transfers and the prospect of further population ageing in the future require us to build a sound budgetary position that allows us to contemplate without fear the preservation of the essentials of our social security system. In addition to these aspects, it should also be stressed that the persistence of high budget deficits has a long-term negative effect on national wealth and income. More balanced public finances are a condition of stability indispensable to future economic growth. We should not minimize the difficulties but we cannot ignore the view that many other countries made even more stringent adjustments, such as Denmark and Ireland in the 1980s and Sweden and Finland in the 1990s. A recent IMF study analyses budgetary adjustments of more than 5 percent of GDP that have been 260 times in 165 countries in the last 30 years. Some of the conclusions of the study are particularly relevant: - Macroeconomic conditions at the beginning of the Adverse. Programs expenditure, current and capital expenditure, although there are also successful cases of revenue adjustments when the programmes have been significantly gradual. More expressive adjustments I have had positive than small fiscal consolidation efforts. Institutional reforms in the budgetary process are in particular those relating to expenditure control systems and greater transparency and monitoring of the macroeconomic stance of fiscal policy. In our case, as if af the most grown years ago to this part are also the ones that have the greatest weight in the percentage structure of expenses (Graph 2.6). Both aspects show how fiscal consolidation on the expenditure side has both difficult and inevitable." However, one of the obstacles to fiscal consolidation carried out by the expenditure side is that it refers to its high degree of rigidity, which this year reaches 82.4 per cent of total primary expenditure (see Table 2.7). On the other hand, structural or legislative changes in the main programmes that condition public expenditure take time to take effect and it is necessary to start reducing the deficit as early as this year, so it is perhaps inevitable to take measures also on the revenue side. We may perhaps find some hope of this being possible in the fact that in January 2003 the Assembly of the Republic adopted by a large majority a Resolution on the objectives of the Stability Programme and in which it could be read: "Consider that .... a balanced structure of public finances should be achieved by requalifying expenditure, ensuring efficiency in revenue collection and reducing the deficit in a structural and consolidated manner."
