Mas surgiro com o tempo, se as estratgias forem corretas. O Banco de Portugal, tanto no contexto da sua participao no Conselho Nacional de Supervisores Financeiros como por iniciativa prpria, tem feito da promoo da formao e da incluso financeiras uma prioridade, acolhida, alis, no seu Plano Estratgico para 2021-2025. Todos os esforos que trilhem esse rduo caminho so, por isso, muito bem-vindos. Muito obrigado pela vossa ateno.

Title: Speech by Vice-Governor Lus Mximo dos Santos at the Colloquium "New Cycle of the Angolan Economy" organized by the Portugal-Angola Chamber of Commerce and Industry
text: Speech by Vice-Governor Luis Maximo dos Santos at the Colloquium "New Cycle of the Angolan Economy" organized by the Chamber of Portugal-Angola Trade and Industry 08 June 2022 08 minutes PANEL "THE FINANCIAL REFORMS CARRIED OUT AND THEIR IMPACT" NOVA SBE CAMPUS - JUNE 8, 2022 Professor Miguel Ferreira of the Faculty of Economics of the New University of Lisbon, Mr. President of the Board of the Portugal-Angola Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Dr. Joao Luis Traca, Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Dr. Jose de Lima Massano, Distinguished speakers and participants, I would like to begin by greeting our hosts - the Faculty of Economics of the New University of Lisbon - in the person of Professor Miguel Ferreira, as well as all the speakers and participants in this conference. It is always a special pleasure to speak in these inspiring facilities of the Nova SBE Campus. Allow me to extend a special greeting to the Ambassador of the Republic of Angola and to the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Dr Jose de Lima Massano, whom I have had the pleasure of meeting for several years in the context of their professional activities. I am grateful for the invitation that the Portugal-Angola Chamber of Commerce and Industry addressed to the Bank of Portugal to participate in this event, which we accepted with great pleasure. International chambers of commerce have a long tradition and are a classic example of the great importance that business associations can achieve. The existence of a strong and dynamic business associative movement is an important institutional asset for the creation of favorable conditions for economic development. This is even more true of associations focused on economic relations between different countries. Bringing entrepreneurs together, contributing to a rigorous knowledge of the characteristics of different economies and their regional specificities, making the behaviour and culture of other peoples better known - even in countries with a long common history, as is the case of Portugal and Angola - is very important to stimulate economic relations and reciprocal investment. Sometimes, like old acquaintances, we take mutual knowledge for granted, but we neglect the effects of the passage of time and the inherent changes in each one. It happens to people and it happens to nations and peoples. Now, chambers of commerce are entities that are especially well placed to account for changes and help overcome the barrier of stereotypes, to understand new realities and facilitate their visibility and recognition, thus helping to identify new investment opportunities. Created in July 1987, the Portugal-Angola Chamber of Commerce and Industry is to be congratulated on its 35th anniversary. Historically, it will not be a very long period, but the political, economic, social, technological and lifestyle changes that have taken place in such a period could not be more profound. The financial sector is essential for economic development. It is a commonplace, but it must be repeated. In fact, a stable, well-capitalized and well-managed financial sector promotes the efficient allocation of savings, induces confidence in citizens and economic agents and, in this way, becomes a fundamental lever of economic activity. On the contrary, as recent history clearly shows, crises in the financial system have very pernicious, sometimes even devastating, effects on economic growth, employment and social stability. The panel in which I say these words is entitled 'The financial reforms carried out and their impact'. The reform effort in the financial sector must be a continuous effort. In Portugal, for example, and with regard to the regulatory framework, it is important to create conditions for the Preliminary Draft of the Banking Activity Code to replace the General Regime of Credit Institutions and Financial Companies, already very outdated and with its historical time exhausted, with a view to simplifying and improving the regulatory framework overall. In his previous speech, the Governor of the National Bank of Angola impressively highlighted the reform effort in Angola in recent years, both in the financial and non-financial sectors. This is a remarkable path for the extension and transversality of the reforms undertaken, several of them focusing on the institutional dimension, which is fundamental for a process of lasting economic development. This set of reforms is important not only for the Angolan economy and population, but also for Portugal. In fact, Portugal and Angola present, in addition to everything else, a very significant level of economic and financial relationship. Portugal has systematically remained among the top three suppliers of goods to Angola. Portugal's exports to Angola have followed the dynamics of the Angolan economy. In certain years, Angola's imports from Portugal have been higher than those of any other country. In terms of bilateral investment, the sustained increase in Angolan direct investment in Portugal is notorious. And the largest share of this investment, as well as Portuguese investment in Angola, corresponds to the financial sector. This relationship also justifies Banco de Portugal being particularly attentive to developments in the Angolan financial sector and its regulatory and institutional framework. It is not surprising, therefore, that the Bank of Portugal and the National Bank of Angola have deepened their technical and institutional cooperation relations in the various areas of their competences. We are very pleased that the National Bank of Angola continues to rely on the openness, availability and experience of the Bank of Portugal in cooperation activities. The National Bank of Angola is one of the most active participants in this dialogue and in the initiatives promoted, both bilaterally and multilaterally. Last year, and at bilateral level alone, we carried out eighteen cooperation actions, which mobilised sixteen departments of Banco de Portugal (from prudential and behavioural supervision, to financial stability and monetary policy or payment systems, to mention just a few areas in which we worked and worked together). This year, we have already carried out fifteen actions - and we are still at the beginning of June - and nine more actions are scheduled by the end of the year. These figures demonstrate the broad scope of cooperation between the two central banks, its permanent nature and the clear awareness of its advantages for both institutions. As mentioned by Governor Lima Massano, the new legislation that regulates the Angolan central bank, among other elements, enshrines its independence and establishes the mandate to maintain price stability, now based on the Constitution of the Republic of Angola, a fact that is a very clear signal to the markets. Legislative initiatives in areas such as the prudential framework for financial institutions or the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing are also key steps towards modernising the governance framework of the banking and financial sector, with impacts on the entire economy and on economic and financial relations with third countries. On the other hand, it is expected that Angola's successful conclusion of the Memorandum of Understanding with the International Monetary Fund will have a lasting impact on the country's macroeconomic and financial stability, also in the field of public finances. Although it is less known to the general public, Banco de Portugal has long been carrying out extensive and fruitful cooperation activities, namely with the central banks of Portuguese-speaking countries. The Cooperation Activity Report for 2021 reflects very well the importance we attach to it. In that year, Banco de Portugal carried out 174 cooperation actions, the highest number on record, and there was also an increase in the number of participants: 1100 people from 38 partner institutions. Of these 174 actions, 93% took place remotely, which shows that the pandemic has not overcome our determination or that of our partners to pursue the common goals in this regard. Of these 174 actions, 116 took place with the central banks of the Portuguese-speaking countries. But we have also cooperated with other geographies: countries neighbouring the European Union, particularly in the Balkans, countries in Latin America and the Caribbean. Within the framework of cooperation with Portuguese-speaking central banks, two multilateral initiatives deserve special mention: the XXXI Lisbon Meeting, held in October 2021, dedicated to the theme of climate change and sustainable finance, and the X Meeting of Governors, last year promoted precisely by the National Bank of Angola, which had the pandemic crisis as its central theme. In short, at Banco de Portugal, international cooperation, in particular with the central banks of Portuguese-speaking countries, is today a strategic, consolidated and growing option. Close to completing the first quarter of the twenty-first century, perhaps we did not imagine, at its beginning, how difficult these initial years would be: terrorism of unprecedented dimensions, which began with the attacks of September 11, 2001, the outbreak of several wars on different continents, of which Iraq was just one more example, natural disasters of enormous proportions, the global financial crisis of 2008-2012, the Covid-19 pandemic and, since February 24 of this year, the war between the Russian Federation and Ukraine, generating consequences that are felt all over the world. Until the war is over, it is not possible to fully assess its consequences. It is already known that there are many and some deeply tragic. After the pandemic crisis, the current conflict in Ukraine - with disruptive impacts on the global economy - brings many uncertainties to the macroeconomic scenario of all economies and poses added challenges to the pursuit of macroeconomic policy objectives and the definition of structural policies. The geopolitical framework will certainly be different from what we had before the war, which may provide a new look at the economic relations between Portugal and Angola and the advantages that they can bring to both countries and their respective peoples. Entities such as the Portugal-Angola Chamber of Commerce and Industry can and should have a role to play in this reflection. In any case, cooperation between Banco de Portugal and Banco Nacional de Angola, both bilaterally and multilaterally, will continue to be driven by the desire to try to contribute to a better world. Thank you very much for your attention.
text_original: Interveno do Vice-Governador Lus Mximo dos Santos no Colquio "Novo Ciclo da Economia Angolana" organizado pela Cmara de Comrcio e Indstria Portugal-Angola 08 junho 2022 08 minutos PAINEL "AS REFORMAS FINANCEIRAS REALIZADAS E O SEU IMPACTO" CAMPUS DA NOVA SBE - 8 DE JUNHO DE 2022 Senhor Professor Doutor Miguel Ferreira da Faculdade de Economia da Universidade Nova de Lisboa, Senhor Presidente da Direo da Cmara de Comrcio e Indstria Portugal - Angola, Dr. Joo Lus Traa, Senhor Governador do Banco Nacional de Angola, Dr. Jos de Lima Massano, Ilustres oradores e participantes, Comeo por cumprimentar os nossos anfitries - a Faculdade de Economia da Universidade Nova de Lisboa - na pessoa do Senhor Professor Miguel Ferreira, bem como todos os oradores e participantes nesta conferncia.  sempre um gosto especial usar da palavra nestas inspiradoras instalaes do Campus da Nova SBE. Permitam-me uma saudao especial ao Senhor Embaixador da Repblica de Angola e ao Senhor Governador do Banco Nacional de Angola, Dr. Jos de Lima Massano, que tenho o gosto conhecer, h j vrios anos, no contexto das respetivas atividades profissionais. Agradeo o convite que a Cmara de Comrcio e Indstria Portugal-Angola dirigiu ao Banco de Portugal para participar neste evento, que aceitmos com o maior gosto. As cmaras de comrcio internacional tm uma longa tradio e so um exemplo clssico do grande relevo que o associativismo empresarial pode alcanar. A existncia de um movimento associativo empresarial forte e dinmico  uma mais-valia institucional importante para a criao de condies favorveis ao desenvolvimento econmico. Isso  ainda mais verdadeiro relativamente s associaes centradas nas relaes econmicas entre diferentes pases. Aproximar empresrios, contribuir para o conhecimento rigoroso das caractersticas das diferentes economias e das suas especificidades regionais, tornar melhor conhecidos os comportamentos e a cultura dos outros povos - mesmo em pases com uma longa histria comum, como  o caso de Portugal e Angola -,  algo muito importante para estimular as relaes econmicas e o investimento recproco. Por vezes, como os velhos conhecidos, damos por adquirido o conhecimento mtuo, mas negligenciamos os efeitos da passagem do tempo e as inerentes mudanas em cada um. Sucede com as pessoas e sucede com as naes e os povos. Ora, as cmaras de comrcio so entidades especialmente bem colocadas para dar conta das mudanas e ajudar a vencer a barreira dos esteretipos, para compreender novas realidades e facilitar a sua visibilidade e reconhecimento, assim ajudando  identificao de novas oportunidades de investimento. Criada em julho de 1987, a Cmara de Comrcio e Indstria Portugal-Angola est de parabns pelos seus 35 anos. Em termos histricos, no ser um perodo muito longo, mas as mutaes polticas, econmicas, sociais, tecnolgicas e de modo de vida ocorridas em tal perodo no poderiam ser mais profundas. O setor financeiro  essencial para o desenvolvimento econmico.  um lugar comum, mas importa ser repetido. De facto, um setor financeiro estvel, bem capitalizado e bem gerido promove a alocao eficiente da poupana, induz confiana nos cidados e nos agentes econmicos e, desse modo, torna-se uma alavanca fundamental da atividade econmica. Ao contrrio, como a histria recente bem o demostra, as crises do sistema financeiro tm efeitos muito perniciosos, por vezes mesmo devastadores, sobre o crescimento econmico, o emprego e a estabilidade social. O painel em que profiro estas palavras tem por ttulo "As reformas financeiras realizadas e o seu impacto". O esforo das reformas no setor financeiro tem de ser um esforo continuado. Em Portugal, por exemplo, e no que ao quadro regulatrio diz respeito,  importante que se criem condies para que o Anteprojeto de Cdigo da Atividade Bancria venha a substituir o Regime Geral das Instituies de Crdito e Sociedades Financeiras, j muito desatualizado e com o seu tempo histrico esgotado, tendo em vista a simplificao e a melhoria global do quadro regulatrio. Na interveno anterior, o Senhor Governador do Banco Nacional de Angola salientou, de forma impressiva, o esforo reformista em Angola nos ltimos anos, tanto no setor financeiro como no setor no financeiro. Trata-se de um caminho notvel pela extenso e transversalidade das reformas empreendidas, vrias delas incidindo na dimenso institucional, que  fundamental para um processo de desenvolvimento econmico duradouro. Esse conjunto de reformas  importante no s para a economia e a populao angolanas, mas tambm para Portugal. Com efeito, Portugal e Angola apresentam, alm de tudo o mais, um nvel de relacionamento econmico e financeiro muito significativo. Portugal tem-se sistematicamente mantido entre os trs principais fornecedores de bens a Angola. As exportaes de Portugal para Angola tm acompanhado a dinmica da economia angolana. Em determinados anos, as importaes de Angola com origem em Portugal tm sido maiores do que as de qualquer outro pas. No plano do investimento bilateral,  notrio o aumento sustentado do investimento direto angolano em Portugal. E a parcela maior deste investimento, bem como do investimento portugus em Angola, corresponde ao setor financeiro. Este relacionamento justifica tambm que o Banco de Portugal esteja particularmente atento aos desenvolvimentos do setor financeiro angolano e do respetivo enquadramento regulatrio e institucional. No espanta, pois, que o Banco de Portugal e o Banco Nacional de Angola tenham aprofundado as suas relaes de cooperao tcnica e institucional nos diversos domnios das suas atribuies. Muito nos satisfaz que o Banco Nacional de Angola continue a confiar na abertura, disponibilidade e experincia do Banco de Portugal na atividade de cooperao. O Banco Nacional de Angola  um dos participantes mais ativos nesse dilogo e nas iniciativas dinamizadas, tanto no plano bilateral como no plano multilateral. No ano passado, e s no plano bilateral, realizmos dezoito aes de cooperao, as quais mobilizaram dezasseis departamentos do Banco de Portugal (desde a superviso prudencial e comportamental,  estabilidade financeira e  poltica monetria ou aos sistemas de pagamentos, para mencionar apenas alguns domnios em que trabalhmos e trabalhamos em conjunto). No corrente ano, j realizmos quinze aes - e ainda vamos no incio de junho -, estando programadas ainda mais nove aes at ao final do ano. Estes nmeros demonstram o alargado mbito da cooperao entre os dois bancos centrais, o seu carter permanente e a clara conscincia das vantagens da mesma para as duas instituies. Conforme foi referido pelo Senhor Governador Lima Massano, a nova legislao que regula o banco central angolano, entre outros elementos, consagra a sua independncia e estabelece o mandato da manuteno da estabilidade de preos, agora com assento na prpria Constituio da Repblica de Angola, facto que constitui um sinal muito claro para os mercados. As iniciativas legislativas em reas como a do quadro prudencial das instituies financeiras ou da preveno do branqueamento de capitais e do financiamento do terrorismo so tambm passos fundamentais para a modernizao do enquadramento de governao do setor bancrio e financeiro, com impactos sobre toda a economia e sobre as relaes econmicas e financeiras com pases terceiros. Por outro lado,  expectvel que a concluso com sucesso por parte de Angola do Memorando de Entendimento com o Fundo Monetrio Internacional venha a ter um impacto duradouro na estabilidade macroeconmica e financeira do pas, tambm no domnio das finanas pblicas. Embora seja menos conhecida do grande pblico, o Banco de Portugal h muito que desenvolve uma extensa e frutuosa atividade de cooperao, designadamente com os bancos centrais dos pases de lngua oficial portuguesa. O Relatrio da Atividade de Cooperao referente a 2021 espelha muito bem a importncia que lhe conferimos. Nesse ano, o Banco de Portugal realizou 174 aes de cooperao, o nmero mais elevado de que h registo, verificando-se tambm o crescimento do nmero de participantes: 1100 pessoas provenientes de 38 instituies parceiras. Dessas 174 aes, 93% tiveram lugar por via remota, o que demonstra que a pandemia no venceu nem a nossa determinao nem a dos nossos parceiros em prosseguir os objetivos comuns nesta matria. Dessas 174 aes, 116 tiveram lugar com os bancos centrais dos pases de lngua portuguesa. Mas coopermos igualmente com outras geografias: pases vizinhos da Unio Europeia, designadamente dos Balcs, pases da Amrica Latina e das Carabas. No quadro da cooperao com os bancos centrais de lngua oficial portuguesa, duas iniciativas multilaterais merecem um destaque especial: o XXXI Encontro de Lisboa, realizado em outubro de 2021, dedicado  temtica das alteraes climticas e do financiamento sustentvel, e o X Encontro de Governadores, o ano passado promovido precisamente pelo Banco Nacional de Angola, que teve como tema central a crise pandmica. Em suma, no Banco de Portugal a cooperao internacional, em particular com os bancos centrais dos pases de lngua oficial portuguesa,  hoje uma opo estratgica, consolidada e em crescimento. Perto de completarmos o primeiro quartel do sculo XXI, talvez no imaginssemos, no seu incio, como seriam to difceis estes anos iniciais: o terrorismo de dimenses nunca vistas, iniciado com os atentados de 11 de setembro de 2001, a ecloso de vrias guerras em diferentes continentes, de que a do Iraque foi s mais um exemplo, calamidades naturais de enormes propores, a crise financeira global de 2008-2012, a pandemia da Covid-19 e, desde 24 de fevereiro deste ano, a guerra entre a Federao Russa e a Ucrnia, geradora de consequncias que se fazem sentir em todo o mundo. At a guerra terminar, no  possvel avaliar em toda a extenso as suas consequncias. J se sabe que so muitas e algumas profundamente trgicas. Aps a crise pandmica, o atual conflito na Ucrnia - com impactos disruptivos na economia global - traz muitas incertezas ao cenrio macroeconmico de todas as economias e coloca desafios acrescidos  prossecuo dos objetivos de poltica macroeconmica e  definio das polticas estruturais. O quadro geopoltico ficar seguramente diferente do que tnhamos antes da guerra, o que poder propiciar um novo olhar sobre as relaes econmicas entre Portugal e Angola e as vantagens que as mesmas podem trazer aos dois pases e aos respetivos povos. Entidades como a Cmara de Comrcio e Indstria Portugal-Angola podero e devero ter um papel a desempenhar nessa reflexo. Em qualquer caso, a cooperao entre o Banco de Portugal e o Banco Nacional de Angola, tanto no plano bilateral como multilateral, continuar animada pelo desejo de tentar contribuir para um mundo melhor. Muito obrigado pela vossa ateno.

Title: Closing speech by Vice-Governor Lus Mximo dos Santos at the Launch Session of the Report of the 1st Survey on the Financial Literacy of Micro and Small Business Entrepreneurs and the Challenges of COVID-19 in Portugal 2021
text: Opening speech by Director Ana Paula Serra at the launch session of the Report of the 1st survey on the financial literacy of micro and small enterprise entrepreneurs and the challenges of COVID-19 in Portugal 2021 18 July 2022 06 minutes Minister of Economy and the Sea, Eng. Antonio Costa Silva, Madam President of the Insurance and Pension Fund Supervisory Authority, Dr. Margarida Correa de Aguiar, Mr. Director of the Portuguese Securities Market Commission, Dr. Rui Pinto, Vice-Governor of the Bank of Portugal, Dear colleagues on the Board of Directors, Ladies and gentlemen, Very good morning. It is with great pleasure that I participate in this launch session - Report of the 1st survey on the financial literacy of micro and small business entrepreneurs and the challenges of COVID-19 in Portugal 2021. Introduction My main purpose of my intervention is to highlight the importance of initiatives to promote financial literacy for micro and small enterprises as well as all the work that has been developed, at an international level, by the G20 and the OECD's International Financial Education Network, and at the national level, the initiatives of the National Plan for Financial Education by the three financial supervisors with their wide network of partners, under the aegis of the CNSF. In this context, the 1st survey on the financial literacy of micro and small enterprise entrepreneurs is an initiative of enormous merit, allowing a diagnosis, from the outset, of the attitudes, behaviors and financial knowledge of micro and small enterprise entrepreneurs, which will be the basis for the definition of a coherent strategy for the Financial Education Plan with the business public in the coming years. Promptly, the National Council of Financial Supervisors, in partnership with the Ministry of Economy and the Sea, accepted the challenge of the G20 and the OECD/INFE to join this international diagnostic and comparison exercise that had the participation of 14 countries. The management of a company requires a diverse set of skills, including those related to the financial management of the company. In micro and small companies, by their nature, these skills are often concentrated in the entrepreneur himself. The training of entrepreneurs in the area of financial management is a critical factor for the success and financial sustainability of companies. Financial knowledge is essential for the day-to-day management of businesses, but also for mitigating risks in adverse situations such as those resulting from the recent exogenous shocks of the COVID-19 pandemic, or more recently, those related to the war in Ukraine. G20 and OECD/INFE work The G20 and OECD/INFE have for some years chosen the issue of financial skills for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises as a priority in their work. I would like to highlight the publication of the Principles on Financing Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (G20/OECD High-Level Principles on SME Financing) in 2015. Principle 7 of this document refers to the need to promote the financial literacy of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) to be able to develop a strategic approach to their long-term financing, which can contribute to sustaining and improving their businesses. The OECD/INFE has meanwhile set up a working group dedicated to promoting the financial education of MSMEs. This group began by promoting an international survey of financial education initiatives aimed at entrepreneurs, owners and managers of these companies and to be defined. I would also like to highlight the work on defining financial literacy frameworks and measuring the financial literacy levels of MSME entrepreneurs, which gave rise in 2018 to the OECD/INFE's dissemination of an international benchmark on financial literacy skills for MSMEs (OECD/INFE). The international benchmark of financial literacy skills for MSMEs has defined a set of financial knowledge, attitudes and behaviours considered essential for potential entrepreneurs and for MSME owners and managers to start and manage their business. It should be noted that this benchmark benefited greatly from Portugal's experience in this field, which at the time was one of the few countries that had already published a financial education benchmark dedicated to MSMEs 2016, a work developed within the scope of the National Plan for Financial Education, in collaboration between financial supervisors and the Ministry of Economy. In turn, the OECD/INFE questionnaire for measuring financial literacy was developed based on the international framework of financial literacy skills for MSMEs and on the surveys previously used to characterize the levels of financial literacy of the adult population. Also in this chapter, Portugal played a very active role in this regard, having been one of the seven countries131 that participated, in 2019, in a pilot test to assess the relevance and appropriateness of the questions. In Portugal, this pilot exercise was conducted by the Strategy and Studies Office and the General Directorate of Economic Activities of the Ministry of Economy. In 2020, the OECD/INFE published the final version of the OECD/INFE survey instrument to measure the financial literacy of MSMEs141, the version used in the survey carried out in 2021, and whose results for Portugal are presented today. With this survey, the G20 and OECD/INFE aimed to measure the financial literacy of micro and small enterprise entrepreneurs, namely with regard to the ownership and choice of financial products and the planning and management of company finances, but took the opportunity to ask questions related to the consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic, the level of digitalization of companies and the use of government measures adopted to mitigate the effects of the pandemic. Survey results Without wishing to anticipate the presentation that will follow, I must mention that we consider the results of the survey of Portuguese companies to be generally positive and encouraging. The answers of the entrepreneurs surveyed reveal that there are disparities between companies and the values of the aggregate indicators of financial literacy, in terms of financial knowledge, attitudes and behaviours, vary naturally depending on the educational qualifications of the entrepreneurs, and also with the size of the company, namely with its number of employees and turnover. There is also heterogeneity in the values of the aggregate digitization indicator, as a function, once again, of educational qualifications and company size. The survey results also confirmed, as already evidenced by other analyses, that the COVID-19 pandemic had a negative impact on the activity of most companies, in particular in terms of liquidity, results and turnover. Greater financial and digital literacy will also have helped companies to adopt procedures to better cope with the negative effects of the pandemic crisis. In the results of this survey, the companies that presented a higher level of digitalization were the ones that most reported having resorted to public support measures in the context of COVID-19. The results published by the OECD for the participating countries show Portugal with above-average values in the global indicator of financial literacy and in its components of attitudes, behaviors and financial knowledge. The digitization indicator of the Portuguese companies that participated in this survey is also above average. The international comparison further confirms that, as expected, the impact of the COVID-19 crisis was uneven across countries. As I mentioned at the beginning of my speech, this diagnosis brings new challenges to the performance of the National Plan for Financial Education, namely within the scope of the protocol signed between the National Council of Financial Supervisors and the Ministry of Economy, through IAPMEI, which has made it possible to promote training actions for trainers with content based on the Financial Education Framework defined in 2016. With this diagnosis, we are better equipped to proceed, in an informed way, to review the training content of the Financial Education Framework for the future. I would like to conclude by thanking all those who worked on this project, on the side of the Ministry of Economy and the Sea and on the side of the Financial Supervisors, and highlighting the fruitful collaboration with the OECD/INFE. text_original: Interveno de abertura da Administradora Ana Paula Serra na Sesso de lanamento do Relatrio do 1. inqurito sobre a literacia financeira de empresrios de micro e pequenas empresas e os desafios da COVID-19 em Portugal 2021 18 julho 2022 06 minutos Senhor Ministro da Economia e do Mar, Eng. Antnio Costa Silva, Senhora Presidente da Autoridade de Superviso de Seguros e Fundo de Penses, Dra. Margarida Corra de Aguiar, Senhor Administrador da Comisso do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios, Dr. Rui Pinto, Senhor Vice-Governador do Banco de Portugal, Caros colegas do Conselho de Administrao, Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, Muito bom dia.  com muito agrado que participo nesta sesso de lanamento - Relatrio do 1. inqurito sobre a literacia financeira de empresrios de micro e pequenas empresas e os desafios da COVID-19 em Portugal 2021. Introduo A minha interveno tem como principal propsito salientar a importncia das iniciativas de promoo de literacia financeira para as micro e pequenas empresas bem como todo o trabalho que tem vindo a ser desenvolvido, a nvel internacional, pelo G20 e Rede Internacional de Educao Financeira da OCDE, e a nvel nacional, as iniciativas do Plano Nacional de Formao Financeira pelos trs supervisores financeiros com a sua rede alargada de parceiros, sob a gide da CNSF. Neste contexto, o 1. inqurito sobre a literacia financeira de empresrios de micro e pequenas empresas  uma iniciativa de enorme mrito, permitindo fazer um diagnstico, de partida, das atitudes, comportamentos e conhecimentos financeiros dos empresrios das micro e pequenas empresas, que sero a base para a definio de uma estratgia coerente de atuao do Plano de Formao Financeira junto do pblico empresarial nos prximos anos. Prontamente, o Conselho Nacional de Supervisores Financeiros, em parceria com o Ministrio da Economia e do Mar, aceitou o repto do G20 e da OCDE/INFE para se associar a este exerccio de diagnstico e comparao internacional que contou com a participao de 14 pases. A gesto de uma empresa requer um conjunto diversificado de competncias em que se inclui as relacionadas com a gesto financeira da empresa. Nas micro e pequenas empresas, pela sua natureza, estas competncias esto muitas vezes concentradas no prprio empresrio. A formao dos empresrios na rea da gesto financeira  um fator crtico para o sucesso e sustentabilidade financeira das empresas. Os conhecimentos financeiros so essenciais para a gesto dos negcios no dia a dia, mas tambm na mitigao dos riscos em conjunturas adversas como as resultantes dos recentes choques exgenos da pandemia de COVID-19, ou mais recentemente, os relacionados com a guerra na Ucrnia. Trabalhos no mbito do G20 e OCDE /INFE O G20 e OCDE/INFE elegeram, desde h alguns anos, o tema das competncias financeiras para as micro, pequenas e mdias empresas como uma prioridade nos seus trabalhos. Destaco, desde logo, a publicao dos Princpios sobre financiamento de pequenas e mdias empresas (G20/OECD High-Level Principies on SME Financingm), em 2015. O princpio 7 deste documento refere a necessidade de promover a literacia financeira das micro, pequenas e mdias empresas (MPME) para serem capazes de desenvolver uma abordagem estratgica em relao ao seu financiamento de longo prazo, que possa contribuir para sustentar e melhorar os seus negcios. A OCDE/INFE constituiu entretanto um grupo de trabalho dedicado  promoo da formao financeira das MPME. Este grupo comeou por promover um levantamento internacional das iniciativas de formao financeira dirigidas a empreendedores, proprietrios e gestores destas empresas e por definir. Destaco ainda os trabalhos de definio de referenciais de competncias financeiras e de medio dos nveis de literacia financeira dos empresrios de MPME que deram origem em 2018,  divulgao pela OCDE/INFE, de um referencial internacional de competncias de literacia financeira para MPME (OECD/INFE Core competencies framework on financial literacy for MSMEs e de um questionrio para medio da literacia financeira. O referencial internacional de competncias de literacia financeira para MPME definiu um conjunto de conhecimentos, atitudes e comportamentos financeiros considerados essenciais para potenciais empreendedores e para proprietrios e gestores de MPME iniciarem e gerirem o seu negcio. Refira-se que este referencial beneficiou muito da experincia de Portugal neste domnio, que  data era dos poucos pases que tinha j publicado um referencial de formao financeira dedicado s MPME 2016 trabalho desenvolvido no mbito do Plano Nacional de Formao Financeira, numa colaborao entre os supervisores financeiros e o Ministrio da Economia. Por seu turno, o questionrio da OCDE/INFE para medio da literacia financeira foi desenvolvido com base no referencial internacional de competncias de literacia financeira para MPME e nos inquritos anteriormente utilizados para a caracterizao dos nveis de literacia financeira da populao adulta. Tambm neste captulo, Portugal teve um papel muito ativo em relao, tendo sido um dos sete pases131 que participaram, em 2019, num teste piloto para aferir a relevncia e adequabilidade das perguntas. Em Portugal, este exerccio piloto foi conduzido pelo Gabinete de Estratgia e Estudos e pela Direo Geral das Atividades Econmicas do Ministrio da Economia. Em 2020, a OCDE/INFE publicou a verso final do questionrio sobre a literacia financeira das MPME (OECD/INFE survey instrument to measure the financial literacy of MSMEs141), verso usada no inqurito efectuado em 2021, e cujos resultados para Portugal so apresentados hoje. Com este inqurito, o G20 e a OCDE/INFE tiveram por objetivo medir a literacia financeira dos empresrios de micro e pequenas empresas, nomeadamente no que toca  deteno e escolha de produtos financeiros e ao planeamento e gesto das finanas da empresa, mas aproveitaram para colocar questes relacionadas com as consequncias da pandemia de COVID-19, o nvel de digitalizao das empresas e o recurso s medidas governamentais adotadas para mitigar os efeitos da pandemia. Resultados do inqurito Sem querer antecipar a apresentao que se seguir, devo referir que consideramos os resultados do inqurito s empresas portuguesas globalmente positivos e encorajadores. As respostas dos empresrios inquiridos revelam que existem disparidades entre empresas e os valores dos indicadores agregados de literacia financeira, nas vertentes de conhecimentos, atitudes e comportamentos financeiros, variam em funo, naturalmente, das habilitaes literrias dos empresrios, e tambm com a dimenso da empresa, nomeadamente com o seu nmero de trabalhadores e volume de negcios. Existe tambm heterogeneidade nos valores do indicador agregado de digitalizao, em funo, mais uma vez, das habilitaes literrias e dimenso da empresa. Os resultados do inqurito confirmaram ainda, tal como j evidenciado por outras anlises, que a pandemia de COVID-19 teve um impacto negativo na atividade da maioria das empresas, nomeadamente em termos de liquidez, resultados e volume de negcios. Uma maior literacia financeira e digital ter tambm ajudado as empresas a adotarem procedimentos para melhor fazerem face aos efeitos negativos da crise pandmica. Nos resultados deste inqurito, as empresas que apresentaram um maior nvel de digitalizao foram as que mais referem ter recorrido a medidas de apoio pblico no mbito da COVID-19. Os resultados publicados pela OCDE para os pases participantes apresentam Portugal com valores acima da mdia no indicador global de literacia financeira e nas suas componentes de atitudes, comportamentos e conhecimentos financeiros. O indicador de digitalizao das empresas portuguesas que participaram neste inqurito surge tambm acima da mdia. A comparao internacional confirma ainda que, como esperado, o impacto da crise de COVID-19 foi desigual entre os pases. Como referi no incio da minha interveno, este diagnstico vem trazer novos desafios  atuao do Plano Nacional de Formao Financeira, designadamente no mbito do protocolo celebrado entre o Conselho Nacional de Supervisores Financeiros e o Ministrio da Economia, atravs do IAPMEI, que tem permitido dinamizar aes de formao de formadores com contedos assentes no Referencial de Formao Financeira definido em 2016. Com este diagnstico, estamos mais equipados para proceder, de forma informada,  reviso dos contedos formativos do Referencial de Formao Financeira para o futuro. Termino agradecendo a todos aqueles que trabalharam neste projecto, do lado do Ministrio da Economia e do Mar e do lado dos Supervisores Financeiros, e realando a frutuosa colaborao com a OCDE/INFE. Title: Opening speech by the Vice-Governor, Lus Mximo dos Santos, at the tenth meeting of the Monitoring Committee of the National Plan for Financial Education
text: Opening speech by the Vice-Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, at the tenth meeting of the Monitoring Committee of the National Plan for Financial Education 03 April 2023 06 minutes Madam Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Insurance and Pension Funds Supervisory Authority, dear Dr. Margarida Correa de Aguiar, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Portuguese Securities Market Commission, dear Dr. Luis Laginha de Sousa, Mr. Director of the Bank of Portugal, my dear colleague Dr. Rui Pinto, Distinguished Representatives of the Partners of the National Plan for Financial Education, Dear members of the Todos Contam jury, which I greet in the person of its President, Professor Isabel Alcada, Ladies and Gentlemen, I am delighted to address all of you - whom I greet and welcome - on behalf of the Chairman of the National Council of Financial and Financial Supervisors Governor of Banco de Portugal, Prof. Mario Centeno, opening the work of the Tenth Annual Meeting of the Monitoring Committee of the National Plan for Financial Education (PNFF). Today's meeting is the first face-to-face meeting of the PNFF Monitoring Committee for the post-pandemic period. In fact, in 2020 and 2021 this event did not take place and, in 2022, the annual meeting took place via videoconference. Also for this reason, it has a particular meaning. PNFF partners are absolutely indispensable for the fulfillment of the Plan's objectives. They are the ones who make it reach society. The Monitoring Committee is made up of all PNFF partners. Many of these partners develop joint initiatives with financial supervisors, in the framework of Cooperation Protocols, while other partners develop their initiatives autonomously. The function of this Commission is, on the one hand, to contribute to identifying priorities and training needs, so it integrates partners such as the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Economy, the Ministry of Labour, Solidarity and Social Security and the High Commission for Migration, which help to identify training needs and how to reach many of the priority target audiences of the PNFF, namely, teachers and students, entrepreneurs and managers of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, most vulnerable sectors of the population, including low-income families, the elderly, the unemployed and migrants. On the other hand, this Commission also has the function of providing means to boost financial education projects, thus relying on the main associations of the financial sector, such as the Portuguese Association of Banks (APB), the Portuguese Association of Insurers (APS), the Portuguese Association of Investment Funds, Pensions and Assets (APFIPP) or the Association of Specialized Credit Institutions (ASFAC), which have financially supported, for example, the publication of the Financial Education Notebooks, but also with some of the main employers' confederations, such as the Business Confederation of Portugal, the Confederation of Commerce and Services of Portugal (CCP) and the National Association of Young Entrepreneurs (ANJE). This annual meeting is, in itself, a form of reiteration of the commitment of all financial supervisors with the National Plan for Financial Education and the strengthening of the involvement of the Plan's partners. In addition to the reference to the main activities carried out in 2022, an accountability exercise that is always fundamental, the PNFF program of activities for 2023 will be presented. In 2023, financial supervisors will continue to implement the strategic guidelines of the National Plan for Financial Education for the period 2021-2025, maintaining the focus on strengthening strategic partnerships and investing in digital, to reach an increasingly diverse set of target audiences and reach the general population more quickly and broadly. In pursuing these objectives, priority will continue to be given to promoting the financial resilience of households and businesses, digital financial education and contributing to a more sustainable economy. The strategic guidelines are divided into eight priority lines of action for the period 2021-2025, each with several initiatives planned for 2023. I will not, of course, refer in detail to these initiatives, not least because other colleagues from the CNSF will certainly refer to and contextualize them, but I would still like to mention some of the ones that seem to me to be most important, namely:  The revision of the Financial Education Framework, a guiding document for the implementation of financial education in an educational context, published in 2013, has therefore been ten years since then;  The continuity of the work of preparing didactic-pedagogical materials dedicated to pre-school education, in partnership with the Ministry of Education, through the Directorate-General of Education, and with the four main associations of the financial sector - the APB, the APS, the APFIPP and the ASFAC;  The continuity of the teacher training programme to support teachers in addressing the financial education content provided for in the Financial Education Framework, and it is important to highlight that, at the end of February, the first teacher training course of this year took place in Funchal, promoted in partnership with the Regional Secretariat for Education, Science and Technology of the Autonomous Region of Madeira;  The holding of training sessions within the framework of the Financial Capacity Plan for the Northern Region, within the scope of the protocol signed with the Northern Regional Coordination and Development Commission (CCDR-N);  Several initiatives - some of them already carried out in the first quarter - aimed at strengthening financial education in the Autonomous Region of Madeira, together with the Regional Secretariat for Social Inclusion and Citizenship;  Various actions aimed at technicians from the Bank Customer Support Network (RACE), as part of the partnership with the Directorate-General for Consumers, and also at technicians from migrant support associations, within the scope of the partnership with the High Commission for Migration (ACM).  Partnerships with other entities that provide support to vulnerable audiences, such as the Portuguese Association for Victim Support (APAV), and it should be noted that on March 9, the first training action aimed at APAV employees who provide advice to victims of online financial fraud took place. On another level, a remarkable event in 2023 will be the publication and presentation of the report of the 4th survey on the financial literacy of the Portuguese population, as part of the international comparison exercise of the levels of financial literacy of the adult population, promoted by the OECD/INFE. This new international comparison exercise will make it possible to assess aspects related to financial resilience, digital finance and sustainable finance, which are highlighted in the strategic guidelines of the Plan for 2021-2025. In view of this assistance, I do not need to justify the advantages that we can obtain from the promotion of financial education and the progressive improvement in the level of literacy of the Portuguese population. But I must emphasise that we all have a duty to devise effective strategies, mobilise resources and define the appropriate instruments and actions for this purpose. We know that it is a work that requires many and combined efforts and that the results are not immediate. But they must be visible, at least in the medium term. Some recent events in the international financial system have shown how behaviors incompatible with financial literacy sometimes appear where one would least expect them: according to the news we have had, it seems appropriate to conclude, for example, that Silicon Valley Bank depositors have not considered the basic principle of risk dispersion. On the other hand, the acceleration of inflation, from the end of 2021, significantly changed the macroeconomic picture, after a long period of stability. This change was accompanied by a change in monetary policy materialized in a rapid and sharp rise in interest rates. These are events that have a major impact on the lives of citizens and businesses and that make it even more important that their financial decisions are the most appropriate to this new context that has so suddenly emerged. Everything, therefore, new challenges for the promotion of financial education, an objective that brings us all together here, which we know is difficult, but which we are determined to achieve together. Thank you very much for your attention.
text_original: Interveno de abertura do Vice-Governador, Lus Mximo dos Santos, na dcima reunio da Comisso de Acompanhamento do Plano Nacional de Formao Financeira 03 abril 2023 06 minutos Senhora Presidente do Conselho de Administrao da Autoridade de Superviso de Seguros e Fundos de Penses, cara Dra. Margarida Corra de Aguiar, Senhor Presidente do Conselho de Administrao da Comisso do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios, caro Dr. Lus Laginha de Sousa, Senhor Administrador do Banco de Portugal, meu caro colega Dr. Rui Pinto, Ilustres Representantes dos Parceiros do Plano Nacional de Formao Financeira, Caros membros do jri Todos Contam, que sado na pessoa da sua Presidente, a Professora Isabel Alada, Minhas Senhoras e meus Senhores,  com o maior gosto que me dirijo a todos vs - a quem sado e dou as boas-vindas -, em representao do Senhor Presidente do Conselho Nacional de Supervisores Financeiros e Governador do Banco de Portugal, Prof. Mrio Centeno, abrindo os trabalhos da Dcima Reunio Anual da Comisso de Acompanhamento do Plano Nacional de Formao Financeira (PNFF). Este nosso encontro de hoje  a primeira reunio presencial da Comisso de Acompanhamento do PNFF do perodo ps-pandemia. Com efeito, em 2020 e 2021 este evento no teve lugar e, em 2022, a reunio anual realizou-se por videoconferncia. Tambm por isso, tem um significado particular. Os parceiros do PNFF so absolutamente indispensveis para o cumprimento dos objetivos do Plano. So eles que o fazem chegar  sociedade. A Comisso de Acompanhamento  constituda por todos os parceiros do PNFF. Muitos destes parceiros desenvolvem iniciativas conjuntas com os supervisores financeiros, no quadro de Protocolos de Cooperao, enquanto outros parceiros desenvolvem as suas iniciativas de forma autnoma. Afuno desta Comisso , por um lado, contribuir para identificar prioridades e necessidades de formao, por isso integra parceiros como o Ministrio da Educao, o Ministrio da Economia, o Ministrio do Trabalho, Solidariedade e Segurana Social e o Alto Comissariado para as Migraes, que ajudam a identificar as necessidades de formao e a forma de chegar a muitos dos pblicos- alvo prioritrios do PNFF, nomeadamente, professores e alunos, empreendedores e gestores de micro, pequenas e mdias empresas, setores da populao mais vulnerveis, incluindo famlias de baixo rendimento, idosos, desempregados e migrantes. Por outro lado, esta Comisso tem igualmente a funo de disponibilizar meios para dinamizar projetos de formao financeira, contando por isso com as principais associaes do setor financeiro, como a Associao Portuguesa de Bancos (APB), a Associao Portuguesa de Seguradores (APS), a Associao Portuguesa de Fundos de Investimento, Penses e Patrimnios (APFIPP) ou a Associao de Instituies de Crdito Especializado (ASFAC), que tm apoiado financeiramente, por exemplo, a publicao dos Cadernos de Educao Financeira, mas tambm com algumas das principais confederaes patronais, como a Confederao Empresarial de Portugal, a Confederao de Comrcio e Servios de Portugal (CCP) e a Associao Nacional de Jovens Empresrios (ANJE). Esta reunio anual , em si mesma, uma forma de reiterao do compromisso de todos os supervisores financeiros com o Plano Nacional de Formao Financeira e o reforo do envolvimento dos parceiros do Plano. Alm da referncia s principais atividades realizadas em 2022, um exerccio de prestao de contas que  sempre fundamental, ser apresentado o programa de atividades do PNFF para 2023. Em 2023, os supervisores financeiros iro dar continuidade  implementao das orientaes estratgicas do Plano Nacional de Formao Financeira para o perodo 2021 -2025, mantendo o foco no reforo das parcerias estratgicas e na aposta no digital, para atingir um conjunto cada vez mais diversificado de pblicos-alvo e chegar de forma mais clere e ampla  populao em geral. Na prossecuo desses objetivos, continuar a ser dada prioridade  promoo da resilincia financeira das famlias e empresas,  formao financeira digital e  contribuio para uma economia mais sustentvel. As orientaes estratgicas esto divididas em oito linhas de ao prioritrias para o perodo 2021- 2025, cada uma com diversas iniciativas previstas para 2023. No vou, naturalmente, referir-me em detalhe a essas iniciativas, at porque outros colegas do CNSF certamente as referiro e contextualizaro, mas ainda assim gostaria de mencionar algumas das que me parecem mais importantes, a saber: a) A reviso do Referencial de Educao Financeira, documento orientador para a implementao da educao financeira em contexto educativo, publicado em 2013, j l vo, portanto, dez anos; b) A continuidade dos trabalhos de elaborao de materiais didtico-pedaggicos dedicados  educao pr-escolar, em parceria com o Ministrio da Educao, atravs da Direo-Geral da Educao, e com as quatro principais associaes do setor financeiro - a APB, a APS, a APFIPP e a ASFAC; c) A continuidade ao programa de formao de professores para apoiar os docentes na abordagem aos contedos de educao financeira previstos no Referencial de Educao Financeira, sendo importante destacar que, no final de fevereiro, teve lugar o primeiro curso de formao de professores deste ano, no Funchal, dinamizado em parceira com a Secretaria Regional de Educao, Cincia e Tecnologia da Regio Autnoma da Madeira; d) A realizao de sesses formativas enquadradas no Plano de Capacitao Financeira da Regio Norte, no mbito do protocolo celebrado com a Comisso de Coordenao e Desenvolvimento Regional do Norte (CCDR-N); e) Iniciativas vrias - algumas delas j realizadas no primeiro trimestre - visando o reforo da formao financeira na Regio Autnoma da Madeira, em conjunto com a Secretaria Regional de Incluso Social e Cidadania; f) Aes diversas dirigidas a tcnicos da Rede de Apoio ao Cliente Bancrio (RACE), enquadradas na parceria com a Direo-Geral do Consumidor, e tambm a tcnicos de associaes de apoio aos migrantes, no mbito da parceria com o Alto Comissariado para as Migraes (ACM). g) Parcerias com outras entidades que prestam apoio a pblicos vulnerveis, como a Associao Portuguesa de Apoio  Vtima (APAV), sendo de sublinhar que no dia 9 de maro teve lugar a primeira ao de formao dirigida a colaboradores da APAV que prestam aconselhamento a vtimas de fraude financeira online. Noutro plano, um acontecimento marcante em 2023 ser a publicao e apresentao do relatrio do 4. inqurito  literacia financeira da populao portuguesa, enquadrado no exerccio de comparao internacional dos nveis de literacia financeira da populao adulta, promovido pela OCDE/INFE. Este novo exerccio de comparao internacional permitir avaliar aspetos relacionados com a resilincia financeira, as finanas digitais e as finanas sustentveis, temas em destaque nas linhas de orientao estratgicas do Plano para 2021-2025. Perante esta assistncia, no preciso justificar as vantagens que podemos obter da promoo da formao financeira e da progressiva melhoria do nvel de literacia da populao portuguesa. Mas devo sublinhar que temos todos o dever de gizar estratgias eficazes, mobilizar meios e definir os instrumentos e aes adequados para o efeito. Sabemos que  um trabalho que requer muitos e conjugados esforos e que os resultados no so imediatos. Mas tm de ser visveis, pelo menos, a mdio prazo. Alguns acontecimentos recentes no sistema financeiro internacional, demonstraram como comportamentos incompatveis com a literacia financeira surgem, por vezes, onde menos se esperaria: segundo as notcias que tivemos, parece adequado concluir, por exemplo, que os depositantes do Silicon Valley Bank no tero ponderado o princpio bsico da disperso do risco. Por outro lado, acelerao da inflao, a partir de finais de 2021, veio alterar de forma significativa o quadro macroeconmico, aps um longo perodo de estabilidade. Esta alterao foi acompanhada por uma mudana na poltica monetria materializada numa rpida e acentuada subida das taxas de juro. Trata-se de acontecimentos de grande impacto na vida dos cidados e das empresas e que tornam ainda mais importante que as respetivas decises financeiras sejam as mais adequadas a este novo contexto que to repentinamente emergiu. Tudo, portanto, novos desafios para a promoo da formao financeira, objetivo que aqui a todos nos congrega, que sabemos difcil, mas que estamos determinados a alcanar em conjunto. Muito obrigado pela vossa ateno.

Title: Speech by the Vice-Governor, Lus Mximo dos Santos, at the Jacques Delors Award Ceremony
text: Speech by the Vice-Governor, Luis Maximo dos Santos, at Jacques Delors Prize Award Ceremony 13 April 2023 03 minutes Secretary of State for European Affairs, Professor Tiago Antunes, Director of the Jacques Delors European Information Centre, Dr Regina Quelhas Lima, Members of the Jacques Delors Prize jury, Dear speakers and dear winners. Ladies and gentlemen, It is with great pleasure that, on behalf of Banco de Portugal, I participate in this ceremony to award the Jacques Delors Prize for the 2020 and 2022 editions. Being at the Money Museum of the Bank of Portugal for the presentation of these awards is of special symbolism, for several reasons. Firstly, because Jacques Delors is rightly and commonly called the 'father' of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), which was both the most profound change in the process of European integration and an act of great political voluntarism. Regardless of the judgments and evaluations that may be made on the subject, it is undeniable that EMU has profoundly transformed the European Union and brought with it a new economic regime for all members of the euro area, which Portugal joined, along with ten other member states, on 1 January 1999, a number that today stands at twenty member states. with Croatia's accession in January this year. The impact on Banco de Portugal resulting from Portugal's participation in EMU and the adoption of the euro was enormous, as it radically changed the framework of its operation. On another level, it is worth noting that Jacques Delors was someone from the central banking community, since he began his career at the Bank of France, where he worked for 17 years. Finally, this year marks twenty years of partnership with the Jacques Delors European Information Centre, with Banco de Portugal being responsible for the cash prize awarded to the author of the winning work. I would like to take this opportunity to congratulate the Jacques Delors European Information Centre for this very worthy initiative, a true public service that it provides, at various levels, which has contributed greatly to an enlightened debate on European issues and the construction of European citizenship. In fact, the Jacques Delors Prize was established in 1996 with the aim of encouraging the appearance of research works, in Portuguese, on current and innovative topics in the European Union. Over the years, many award-winning works have contributed to enriching knowledge and strengthening critical thinking not only in the areas of economics and European law, but also in social and geopolitical issues. The Bank of Portugal could not remain indifferent to this initiative, first of all because of its role in the construction of EMU: firstly, in the technical negotiations of the Maastricht Treaty; secondly, in the implementation of the three stages of EMU and, today, in the daily performance of the tasks assigned to it by the European treaties, by European Union law and by national law. The promotion of knowledge and public debate on European integration, especially in areas related to its missions, is a priority assumed in Banco de Portugal's strategic plan for the 2021-2025 horizon, whose motto is "Promoting proximity and strengthening confidence". Encouraging and supporting studies such as those that will be presented and awarded here today is, therefore, for us, more than an honour, an institutional duty. Ladies and gentlemen, We live in times that, more than ever, push us to debate and, above all, to action. But at the moment the action of decision-makers is, at all levels, particularly complex and difficult. Profound geopolitical and geoeconomic changes are underway, the dynamics of which have been underway for some time, all in a context of permanent technological revolution. The meaning and results of these changes are far from being anticipated. However, with today's data, it is not easy to foresee that such changes could lead to the strengthening of Europe's role in the world, which, it is worth remembering, has always been one of the main objectives of the European integration process. Will we be able to focus on the essentials, contrary to what has been done so many times? Will we be able to preserve our values and maintain political, economic and social cohesion? Will we be able to contribute so that the world is not cornered in painful divisions of civilization? In addition to these, many other questions could be asked. It is important to keep in mind that improving the world has always required an arduous and strenuous effort, but making it worse is something very easy to do, as we are seeing with the invasion of Ukraine by the Russian Federation. There is therefore no shortage of themes for future works that are candidates for the Jacques Delors Prize. But today what really matters here is to celebrate the winning works of the 2020 and 2022 editions. I therefore end by addressing my congratulations to the awardees and their supervisors for their excellent academic work on such interesting and current research topics. Thank you very much for your attention.

Title: Opening speech by Vice-Governor Lus Mximo dos Santos, at the 5th edition of the Fintech meeting: Virtual Assets  Prevention of Money Laundering/Terrorist Financing and MiCA Regulation (on Markets in Crypto-Assets)
text: Opening speech by Vice-Governor Luis Maximo dos Santos, on the 5th.the edition of the Fintech meeting: Virtual Assets - Prevention of money laundering/terrorist financing and MiCA Regulation (on Markets in Crypto-assets) 04 MAY 2023 04 minutes I would like to start by greeting and welcoming the participants in the 5.the edition of the Fintech Meeting of Banco de Portugal and to thank all those at the Bank who contributed to the organization of this event, especially colleagues from DAS and DPG. Promoting proximity and strengthening trust is the motto of Banco de Portugal's Strategic Plan for 2021-2025. We intend to be an institution close to the regulated, the stakeholders of the different areas in which we intervene and society in general. This proximity is important for the good performance of our missions. It is an attitude and a method that helps to enhance the effectiveness of our action. Listening to market agents and dialoguing with them is not an end in itself, but it is a fundamental instrument for Banco de Portugal, as a regulator, supervisor and supervisory entity for compliance with the regulatory framework, to take the best decisions. This event is one of many that the Bank has promoted - in all its mission areas - in order to promote the objectives I have just mentioned. I would welcome the fact that today we have a very large number of participants - more than 400 - from credit institutions, payment institutions, fintechs, entities registered for the exercise of activities with virtual assets, business associations, consultants, lawyers and, of course, colleagues from the Bank of Portugal. This large number of participants undoubtedly reflects the importance of the topics that will be addressed here, but it is also an implicit recognition of the validity of our methodology of dialogue and proximity that we want to carry out. This edition of the Fintech Meeting is dedicated to the opportunities and challenges that virtual assets contain and the respective regulatory context, present and future, from a double perspective:  The first, the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing within the scope of activities with virtual assets;  The second, regulation of the virtual asset market, including its issuers and service providers. The choice of the topic is particularly important at the present time, marked by the impetus of European and international initiatives on the regulation and supervision of the market and activities with virtual assets, as well as by national legal and regulatory instruments, which incorporate, in the national legal order, the recommendations, guidelines and supranational standards in this matter. In turn, all these developments are a reflection of the relevance that virtual assets have assumed. Even among experts in the financial world, the topic of virtual assets raises very diverse opinions, some totally contradictory and sometimes even somewhat passionate, which is not usual in this type of subject. The approach to virtual assets that began to prevail some time ago is pragmatic in nature and can perhaps be summed up as follows: if you can't stop them, it's better to regulate them. And it is, I believe, a correct view. If we look at history, this is what has usually happened with all potentially more disruptive innovations compared to the status quo. If they gain traction in the market, clear and proportionate rules must be created, which are as effective as possible, namely in mitigating the greatest risks. In this context, the European Union's impulses deserve special relevance, with emphasis on two important legislative packages:  ) The package on preventing and combating money laundering and terrorist financing - globally referred to as the "AML Package". This package, published in July 2021, defined, among several priorities, the effective application of the current European Union framework on combating money laundering and terrorist financing to service providers with virtual assets, as well as the creation of a single set of European Union rules on this matter, which integrates the activities developed with virtual assets. The solutions contained in this package undoubtedly materialize a profound reform in the institutional and legal framework applicable in this area, as we will have the opportunity to see at today's Fintech Meeting.  ) The Digital Finance Package on the new European Union strategy on digital finance for the financial sector, which culminated in the publication of the Proposal for a Regulation on Markets in Crypto-assets (known as the "MiCA" Regulation). This Regulation marks the current position of the European Union and the Member States in regulating the risks for consumers related to crypto-assets, including the so-called "stablecoins", taking into account, in particular, the recent events in the markets associated with this category of assets. As stated by the President of the European Commission, Mrs von der Leyen, it is necessary to establish "a common approach with Member States towards cryptocurrencies to ensure that we understand how to make the most of the opportunities they create and manage the new risks they may pose"1. The identification and mitigation of these risks are inseparable from the construction of robust beacons, based on a regulatory framework that does not hinder innovation, but promotes safety. Banco de Portugal's activities have been attentive and diversified, from the point of view of the instruments used. By way of example, I would underline: - The regulation, by means of Notice of the Bank of Portugal No. 3/2021, of the registration process with the Bank of Portugal of entities that intend to carry out, in national territory, activities with virtual assets subject to registration, as well as the subsequent changes to the elements to be registered; -The regulation, through Notice No. 1/2023, of the aspects necessary to ensure compliance with the preventive duties of money laundering and terrorist financing, within the scope of the activity of entities that carry out activities with virtual assets;  The publication of answers to frequently asked questions about virtual assets, including, inter alia, the main risks associated with transactions with these assets, in line with the alerts of the European Supervisory Authorities and the National Council of Financial Supervisors2;  The publication of reports summarizing the analysis of the contributions received under the public consultations promoted. I conclude by expressing the certainty that this 5th edition ofthe Fintech Meeting will be a very good time spent for all participants who, within the scope of their respective activities, deal with the theme of virtual assets and their regulation and want to learn more about the vision of Banco de Portugal. Thank you very much for your attention. Separator  Mission letter from President-elect von der Leyen to Vice-President Dombrovskis of 10 September 2019  /FAQs/8196

Essa proximidade  importante para o bom desempenho das nossas misses.  uma atitude e um mtodo que ajuda a potenciar a eficcia da nossa ao. Ouvir os agentes de mercado e dialogar com eles no  um fim em si mesmo, mas  um instrumento fundamental para que, enquanto regulador, supervisor e entidade fiscalizadora do cumprimento do quadro regulatrio, o Banco de Portugal tome as melhores decises. Saudaria o facto de contarmos hoje com um nmero muito elevado de participantes - mais de 400 - provenientes de instituies de crdito, instituies de pagamento, fintechs, entidades registadas para o exerccio de atividades com ativos virtuais, associaes empresariais, consultores, advogados e, claro, colegas do Banco de Portugal. Este elevado nmero de participantes reflete, sem dvida, a importncia dos temas que aqui vo ser tratados, mas  tambm um reconhecimento implcito da validade dessa nossa metodologia de dilogo e proximidade que queremos levar a cabo. Esta edio do Fintech Meeting  dedicada s oportunidades e desafios que os ativos virtuais contm e ao respetivo contexto regulatrio, presente e futuro, numa dupla perspetiva: - A primeira, de preveno do branqueamento de capitais e financiamento do terrorismo no mbito das atividades com ativos virtuais; - A segunda, de regulao do mercado dos ativos virtuais, incluindo os respetivos emitentes e prestadores de servios. A escolha do tema  particularmente importante no momento atual, marcado pelo impulso de iniciativas europeias e internacionais sobre a regulao e superviso do mercado e das atividades com ativos virtuais, bem como por instrumentos legais e regulatrios nacionais, que incorporam, na ordem jurdica nacional, as recomendaes, orientaes e normas supranacionais nesta matria. Por sua vez, todos esses desenvolvimentos so um reflexo da relevncia que os ativos virtuais assumiram. Mesmo entre especialistas do mundo financeiro, o tema dos ativos virtuais suscita opinies muito diversas, algumas totalmente contraditrias e, por vezes, at algo apaixonadas, o que no  habitual neste tipo de assuntos. A abordagem em relao aos ativos virtuais que comeou a prevalecer h algum tempo  de ndole pragmtica e talvez se possa resumir do seguinte modo: se no os consegues travar,  melhor regul- los. E , creio, uma viso correta. Se olharmos para a histria,  o que normalmente tem acontecido com todas as inovaes potencialmente mais disruptivas face ao status quo. Se ganham trao no mercado, h que criar regras claras e proporcionadas, que sejam to eficazes quanto possvel, designadamente na mitigao dos maiores riscos. Neste contexto, merecem especial relevncia os impulsos da Unio Europeia, com destaque para dois importantes pacotes legislativos: 1. ) O pacote em matria de preveno e combate ao branqueamento de capitais e ao financiamento do terrorismo - globalmente denominado AML Package. Este pacote, publicado em julho de 2021, definiu, entre vrias prioridades, a aplicao efetiva do atual quadro da Unio Europeia em matria de combate ao branqueamento de capitais e ao financiamento do terrorismo aos prestadores de servios com ativos virtuais, assim como a criao de um conjunto nico de regras da Unio Europeia nesta matria, que integre as atividades desenvolvidas com ativos virtuais. As solues contidas no referido pacote materializam, sem dvida, uma profunda reforma no quadro institucional e legal aplicvel neste domnio, como teremos ocasio de ver no Fintech Meeting de hoje. 2. ) O Pacote do Financiamento Digital sobre a nova estratgia da Unio Europeia em matria de financiamento digital para o setor financeiro, que culminou com a publicao da Proposta de Regulamento relativo aos Mercados de Criptoativos (conhecido por Regulamento MiCA). Este Regulamento marca o atual posicionamento da Unio Europeia e dos Estados-membros na regulao dos riscos para os consumidores relacionados com os criptoativos, incluindo as designadas "criptomoedas estveis", tendo em conta, designadamente, os recentes acontecimentos nos mercados associados a esta categoria de ativos. Conforme foi afirmado pela Presidente da Comisso Europeia, a Senhora Von der Leyen,  necessrio estabelecer uma abordagem comum com os Estados-Membros em relao s criptomoedas para assegurar que compreendemos como tirar o mximo partido das oportunidades que criam e gerir os novos riscos que possam representar1. A identificao e a mitigao destes riscos so indissociveis da construo de robustas balizas, aliceradas num quadro regulamentar que no entrave a inovao, mas promova a segurana. A atuao do Banco de Portugal tem sido atenta e diversificada, do ponto de vista dos instrumentos usados. A ttulo de exemplo, sublinharia: - A regulao, por via do Aviso do Banco de Portugal n. 3/2021, do processo de registo junto do Banco de Portugal das entidades que pretendam exercer, em territrio nacional, atividades com ativos virtuais sujeitas a registo, bem como as alteraes subsequentes aos elementos a registar; -A regulao, atravs do Aviso n. 1/2023, dos aspetos necessrios a assegurar o cumprimento dos deveres preventivos do branqueamento de capitais e do financiamento do terrorismo, no mbito da atividade das entidades que exercem atividades com ativos virtuais; - A publicao de respostas s perguntas frequentes sobre ativos virtuais, incluindo, nomeadamente, os principais riscos associados s operaes com estes ativos, na linha dos alertas das Autoridades de Superviso Europeias e do Conselho Nacional de Supervisores Financeiros2; - A publicao de relatrios que sintetizam a anlise dos contributos recebidos ao abrigo das consultas pblicas promovidas. Termino, exprimindo a certeza de que esta 5a edio do Fintech Meeting vai ser tempo muito bem empregue para todos os participantes que, no mbito das respetivas atividades, lidam com o tema dos ativos virtuais e da sua regulao e pretendem conhecer melhor a viso do Banco de Portugal. Muito obrigado pela vossa ateno. Separator 1 Carta de misso da Presidente eleita Von der Leyen ao Vice-presidente Dombrovskis, de 10 de setembro de 2019 2 /perguntas-frequentes/8196

Title: Opening speech by Vice-Governor Lus Mximo dos Santos at Banco de Portugal's Legal Conference
text: Opening speech by Vice-Governor Luis Maximo dos Santos at the Banco de Portugal's Legal Seminars 07 December 2023 03 minutes Dean of the Faculty of Law of the University of Porto, Professor Doutor Paulo de Tarso Domingues, Madam Administrator, Professor Francisca Guedes de Oliveira, Distinguished Professors, Dear colleagues of Banco de Portugal, Dear students, Ladies and Gentlemen, It is a great pleasure for me and for all of us at the Bank to welcome you and, above all, to organize these Legal Conferences in collaboration with the Faculty of Law of the University of Porto (FDUP). A special word is due to Professor Paulo de Tarso Domingues, whom I thank for the willingness he has shown in hosting this initiative, which is part of the broader framework of a Cooperation Protocol between Banco de Portugal and the Faculty of Law, which we have just signed and which, in itself, is a reason for us to be deeply satisfied with the institutions. but also personal. In fact, although my alma mater is the Faculty of Law of the University of Lisbon, I have a very special affection for the Faculty of Law of the University of Porto, where, in 1997 and 1998, in the first years of my law degree, I was a lecturer in the discipline of International Economics. Curiously, also under a protocol, in this case with FDUL, which provided some teachers in that initial period, a mission that I embraced with great pleasure. It was a fantastic experience, in which I shared with the students and teachers of the time the enthusiasm of building an institution of which, inexplicably, the city of Porto and the country itself were deprived for many years. These Days are already being held within the framework of the Protocol that we signed this morning. We are sure that they will be the first of several other study and reflection initiatives to be carried out in partnership with FDUP on matters related to the missions and functions entrusted to Banco de Portugal. I would also like to underline that the motto of Banco de Portugal's Strategic Plan for the 2021-2025 time horizon is precisely to promote proximity and strengthen confidence. Now, it is also in this context that we must understand the Days that bring us together here today. Its purpose is to strengthen the dialogue between Banco de Portugal and the Portuguese university - in this case, through the University of Porto - thus bringing it closer to the society it is supposed to serve and also facilitating a more complete understanding of the public purposes it pursues. I also want to express my congratulations on the programme of the Conferences, in which topics of the greatest relevance in the field of Banking Law and financial law in general will be considered and discussed. Economic and technological developments have profoundly changed the exercise of banking activity. Therefore, an updated legal framework is indispensable, which responds to the needs of this evolution. When it emerged, in 1992, the General Regime of Credit Institutions and Financial Companies (RGICSF) materialized a profound legal renewal of the Portuguese banking and financial sector, which accompanied its economic and financial evolution. However, after more than thirty years, the RGICSF is today a legal instrument that is largely obsolete - from the outset in its system - and confusing, having lost, as a result of several changes, the legal quality that initially characterized it. Aware of this, the Bank of Portugal submitted to public scrutiny, three years ago, the Preliminary Draft Code of Banking Activity, better known by its acronym "CAB". The CAB aroused great interest in the legal community and the public consultation to which it was subjected, despite having revealed natural opportunities for improvement and even aspects of some critical debate, especially with the industry, confirmed that Banco de Portugal was right to propose to the political power the adoption of this ambitious legislative reform, since the overall reception was very positive. I hope that the Government that will result from the legislative elections scheduled for March 10, 2024 will resume the work on the CAB Draft and materialize it in a legislative initiative, as it is a legislative reform that the country needs. It is a challenge that is imposed, not only on the next Government, but also on the political forces represented in the future Assembly of the Republic. These Banco de Portugal Legal Conferences will, in fact, allow the participants in the different panels to address some of the issues that the CAB Draft intended to respond to and justify the indispensability of this legislative reform. I would like to conclude by thanking the scientific committee and organiser of the Conference, in the persons of Professor Manuel Carneiro da Frada and Professor Luis Bigotte Chorao, as well as the services of the Bank of Portugal who participated in its organisation - with justified emphasis on the Department of Legal Services and its Board of Directors - for all the dedication and work that allowed them to be carried out. Thank you very much for your attention.
