Title: Speech by the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Mrio Centeno, at the Vamos l Portugal Conference
text: Speech by the Governor of the Bank of Portugal, Mario Centeno, at the Vamos La Portugal Conference 09 February 2022 14 minutes Today we face several transitions - of which climate and digital are the most debated. But perhaps we could use a more far-reaching word, and borrow it from the writer Lidia Jorge, who described them as being "more than a transition, a metamorphosis". If it is true that the pandemic was a brutal interregnum in the process of development and convergence, which brought to light doubts and weaknesses, it will not mark our near future. The crisis has enhanced the conditions for change. But he did not create them. In the challenges we face, nothing is new. Nothing is post-pandemic. The pandemic crisis was temporary, not structural and we are recovering in a short period of time, which did not happen in previous crises. We have to take advantage of the much we have done before and during the crisis, to envision how much we have to do. In the structural changes we are facing, we must remain supportive and pro-European. Solidarity, because we cannot leave anyone behind. Europeanists, because it was in the euro, our common home, that we found, as early as March 2020, answers to the crisis. Let's go, then. I will divide my intervention into two parts, in the first I analyze the Opportunities we have, in the second the necessary Action. The opportunities. For the first time, Portugal faces a challenge of structural transformation with the homework done, and with distinction:  first, with a strong reduction in risk, both public and private;  secondly, with an improvement in the indicators of qualifications and participation in the labour market;  and finally with an active involvement in the construction of Europe. The Economist recognized this week: correct accounts and stability are the hallmark of Portugal. The opportunities were and will be endogenous to the effort and policies adopted by the Portuguese. Let's look first at risk reduction. At the time of the crisis, Portugal had balanced public accounts, with a budget surplus; A metamorphosis after 45 years of democracy. In 2019, the public debt ratio was high and today it remains high, but it had fallen by 15 pp in the previous four years, standing at 116% of GDP. In what is the biggest challenge we face, we already know the way to go, we have already started it, we cannot hesitate. In 2021, the budget deficit will be very close to 3%, perhaps even if it already complies with the fiscal treaties, that is, it will probably be less than 3%. Public debt fell in 2021 to 127% of GDP and, in nominal terms, is expected to fall, which is happening for the first time since 1948. Who does not remember the threats of sanctions and the constraints of the Excessive Deficit Procedure? Today, fortunately we have left these moorings, and so we must continue. With these budgetary results, it is the first time that Portugal faces a crisis without going into excessive deficits. Completing the article already cited: Portugal is no longer part of the PIGS. But it was not only the State that contributed to the reduction of risk. The financial system, households and companies have made a contribution, and what a contribution. In the years leading up to the pandemic crisis, the reduction of private debt in Portugal was unparalleled in Europe. The figures are instructive: a reduction of 78 pp in the private debt ratio and an approximation to euro area indicators not seen in the last 50 years. The differential between the private debt burden between Portugal and the euro area, which was 74pp in 2012, has been cancelled out in just 7 years. In this period, we grew more than the euro area, starting from high debt and deleveraging. Remarkable. And what did the banking sector do? It reduced costs, reduced risks and capitalized. Banks' results grew and, in 2021, returned to pre-pandemic values. The Return on Equity of the largest banks is close to 5%, with an aggregate net profit of 1.2 billion euros. The standardization of NB. In recent years, the two banks with public recapitalizations compatible with State Aid have successfully fulfilled the restructuring plans. How many newspaper covers have been made with these successes? The gross NPL ratio fell to close to 4%, net of impairments is below 2%. They are, respectively, 14pp and 9pp less than in June 2016. If we focus on non-financial corporations, the ratio is around 8%, a more favourable evolution, with a reduction of 22pp. Today, Portuguese banks have lower cost-to-income ratios than euro area banks, and in 2021, the ratio decreased by 2pp to 52%. We are a country with less risk. The second chance: participation in the labour market and qualifications. The labour market participation rate had never reached 77%. Between 2011 and 2021, the participation rate of the Portuguese aged 55 to 64 rose 20 pp, to two-thirds and, today, they are the largest demographic group in the market. The Portuguese over 45 years old in the labor market are half a million more than in 2011. The intensive margin of labour supply has been very well used: longer working lives and starting later, with more training. Because the job offer is mainly worth your qualifications. Schooling is the most universal determinant of economic growth. Portugal has accumulated decades, which add up to centuries, of insufficiencies in qualifications, which distanced us from all European countries and gave us a competitive disadvantage when the European Union opened up to the East and China entered the World Trade Organization. But the country responded to this delay. The response was extraordinary and unique. In the last two decades, we have overtaken the euro area and spread the gap with Eastern Europe. The percentage of young people (20-24 years old) with at least secondary education increased from 43% to 86%. The euro area had 74% and went to 84%. In the East they were 84% and 89%. The increase in schooling in the Portuguese population has a clear impact on the quality of the labour supply. A real structural change in our economy. The signs coming from the economy - the qualitative leap in supply - are already beginning to reflect this reality. We must continue to take advantage of this. And Europe? This is the third opportunity I have mentioned. In Europe, the crisis has been marked by an unprecedented policy response: immediate, robust and coordinated. A Europe of solidarity has avoided repeating the mistakes of the sovereign debt crisis. Portugal was part of this reversal of the cycle. From a bad student he became a cardinal in the resumption of a single European project. We were there, on our own merit. This new cycle of European policies that began in 2019/2020 cannot be missed. Because credibility is a scarce commodity. Europe has made AAA debt issues available to all countries. In fact, between 2021 and 2023 the European Commission will be the largest issuer of AAA debt in Europe. This was a quantum leap in European integration, one of those that deserved the verse of our Sophia de Mello Breyner, "the dawn I waited". We cannot waste it, because tomorrow is always too far away. Before we go to tomorrow, allow me to briefly remind you of Banco de Portugal's perspective for the period from 2022 to 2024. Activity in the first quarter of 2022 will return to 2019 values and grows 5.8% in the year (after 4.9% in 2021), supported, as since 2015, by investment and exports, with emphasis on services. Portugal can complete a full decade of growth based on exports and investment! In an environment of geopolitical tensions, pressure on energy and demand growth and conditional expansion of supply, we have higher inflation. Still, core inflation - which excludes energy and food - is 2.3%, and fell in January. Inflation expectations want to be anchored. One of the most used indicators to measure them, 5-year swaps, is at 1.8%. We can say that for the first time in many years inflation is anchored. Second-round effects on wages are not yet being felt, at least for now, despite the fact that the limitation of labour supply poses an upside risk to inflation. After the temporary effects and the resumption of labour mobility in Europe, inflation is expected to decline, which is expected to converge in 2024 to values consistent with the monetary policy objective. We are going to enter a new cycle for monetary policy. The interest rate period generally low, some even negative, should be followed by normalization, a desired process. Monetary policy, a macro policy, aims to control prices. But it will not be able to cope with geopolitical pressures, nor with decarbonization. These are processes with temporary effects, but whose impact is not negligible. At this stage, monetary policy must keep all flexibility and all options open. It would be a mistake, comparable to those of the recent past, to attribute to monetary policy the function of going after Mr. Putin. The credibility of a monetary policy that responds to supply shocks and political tensions does not survive the first clash. On the contrary, in Europe, coordination with fiscal policy should maintain the spirit of 2020 and increase its effectiveness. At times when policies are turning, restlessness usually takes hold of analysts. But it is worth remembering: in 2017 we financed ourselves at 5% and Germany at 1% (at a maturity of 10 years). Today, financing costs are much lower. The interest rate differential with Germany is about 80 basis points, it was more than 400 basis points. The budget balance was still lurking at the limit of excess, the demand today is clearly within our reach. The ECB's purchase programs have already had a halt in the net purchase phase at the end of 2018. At that time, 10-year rates were at 1.70%, a value well above what we have today. In other words, we are now in a better starting position in this too. Interest expense fell by 1100 million euros between 2019 and 2021. No one should have been convinced that interest rates would remain at 2020/21 values (was it?). But we have to stay focused on our responsibilities and bring the debt quickly to values close to 120% in 2022 and improve the values of 2019 the following year. And it is possible. Let's go, then, to the Action. Debt and public finances. It is essential to resume the path of reducing the public debt ratio, underpinned by a credible fiscal consolidation plan. In 2022, the budget balance meets the conditions (arithmetic) to be below 1%. The end of the pandemic, with the elimination of extraordinary expenditure, and the increase in economic activity to pre-pandemic levels, contributes to this. At all remarkable levels and, I am sure, increasing the self-esteem of the majority of Portuguese, the country is in a position to recover, between 2022 and 2023, the budget balance prior to the pandemic crisis. This evolution represents nothing other than economic activity: in January, year-on-year VAT revenue grew by close to 40%; Stamp Duty grew by around 20%; and ISP by 18%. Tax relief must be selective and with clear objectives. Figures from the Bank of Portugal show that since 2015 the structural tax burden (the one resulting from fiscal policy decisions) has been reduced by 1.2 pp of GDP, in a context of fiscal consolidation. Above-forecast growth in tax revenue should be channelled into deficit and debt reduction. This remains the best way to invest in the future in a context of uncertainty. Maintaining this path will allow the credit rating of public (and private) debt to continue to progress and the interest rate differential not to widen against benchmark securities in the European Union. In a country where public and private debt has been over 300% of GDP since 2007 (it is expected to be so in 2022), this is the best public policy to support growth. In the analysis of debt sustainability, carried out by international organizations, Portugal left behind countries such as Spain, France, Belgium and Italy. He did it on his own merit. We cannot lose this momentum. Balancing the budget and reducing public debt are not incompatible with the challenges of Public Administration, where I highlight Justice and Health. In doing so, we must give priority to efficiency criteria. To put the question, perhaps too simplistically: we live in a paradox, Portugal, per inhabitant, has the fourth highest number of doctors in Europe, but the fourth lowest number of consultations. Public expenditure reached 42% of GDP in 2019, coming from 52% in 2010 and ... 2014. That's 10 pp less, and the room for tax reduction is gained in the efficiency of spending, which allows this trend to continue. As a second priority for action, I identify education, talent and demography. The sustainability of growth and confidence condition the ability to retain talent, which families and schools make available to the economy. This continues to be the investment with the highest economic and social return. We have made a quantum leap in the last twenty years, but this is a battle that is never won. Intergenerational transmission and family financial constraints are the biggest obstacles to investment in education. Indicators have improved in Portugal, but public policy must continue to respond to this challenge. To retain talent, investment is needed, which should benefit from more attractive tax conditions, when it is associated with qualified human capital. In an adverse demographic context, the ability to attract qualified human capital is a key factor for sustained growth. Portugal must open up to immigration to prevent low fertility rates. Precariousness, measured by the weight of fixed-term contracts and excessive job rotation, has fallen in recent years in all age groups. I highlight the number of young people with open-ended contracts: it increased by 54% between 2015 and 2019, 42 thousand more. This trend must be strengthened and measures to achieve this must be implemented. Europe and Portugal: a design of integration is the third dimension of action. In 2022, we face a new challenge: to continue the moment of European integration launched in 2020 by Next Generation EU and the coordination of monetary and fiscal policies. An efficient implementation of the RRP projects and reforms is not only essential for the economic design - increasing productivity, competitiveness and sustainable growth - but also for the European political design. We are advancing the climate and digital transition with very low-rate and risk-sharing financing. If we squander this opportunity, we will go back to the endless and sterile discussions on risk reduction. Discussions in which mistrust blocked effective advances. The short window for implementation of the RRP is a challenge in itself. All hesitations and complacency will have a high price for a successful metamorphosis. Public investment in Portugal in recent years has been financed essentially by the State Budget. In the years of the RRP this situation should change. Public investment must be exclusively, or close to it, financed by European funds. Only then will we be able to implement these funds. If public investment is not "Anita goes shopping", in recent years Anita's portfolio has rarely been from Brussels. The clearest and most evident priority for the coming years is: to implement the RRP and the funds of the new budget cycle. Public investment is a small part of total investment, but it must catalyze private investment, avoiding unsustainable maintenance burdens on investments that do not generate the necessary resources to sustain themselves. The past knows this reality all too well. With the financing assumptions underlying the RRP, we will be able to simultaneously increase investment and reduce indebtedness. Finally, the banking system. In the banking system, the progress made in the decade after the sovereign debt crisis was preponderant in increasing the resilience of the sector, so important during the pandemic crisis. However, structural challenges remain. The digitisation process should be a lever. But the consolidation of the sector and the climate transition are no less challenging. It is a huge responsibility for the sector to change the page of bank resolutions, of inexplicable and unexplained credits. The requirement cannot, and should not, be reduced. This will be the case on the side of banking supervision. The sector has to work with society to give back to the country everything that the country has granted it in a collective effort. We must not be stuck in images of the past. In recent years, the contribution to the public accounts of the banking sector has been positive. Whether for the dividends paid, as a result of the strong investments made by the State shareholder; or for the IRC revenue, which results from a profitable sector, or even for the support to the productive sectors and families, the banking sector has ceased to be a burden on the State Budget in recent years. Let me conclude. The concertation of these actions is the key to growth. Growth is not a speed race. It is not supply OR demand. Growth, to be inclusive and sustained, must be supply AND demand. There is no production without demand. There is no investment without savings. In all countries with sustained growth over the last 100 years (already dubbed the century of education) the supply shock resulting from the increase in schooling was followed by the response in demand for these qualifications; That's how it's been and there are many success stories. We have a duty to make Portugal another success story. The challenges we face must result in the metamorphosis of the economy, in a reformist impetus that increases productivity and competitiveness, but above all that prepares Portugal to face the climate and digital transitions, with an opportunity to show its best and to reinvent itself. In the process of deciding economic policies, the most difficult thing is to define the counterfactual, but in this case it is defined by what we can lose, if we do the unforgivable, which is to waste financial stability, investment, financing conditions in a Europe of solidarity and an educated population to match the best in Europe and in the world. Let's go. Thank you very much.

Mas no foi apenas o Estado a contribuir para a reduo do risco. O sistema financeiro, as famlias e as empresas deram um contributo, e que contributo. Os nmeros so elucidativos: uma reduo de 78 pp do rcio da dvida privada e uma aproximao aos indicadores da rea do euro como no se via nos ltimos 50 anos. O diferencial entre o peso da dvida privada entre Portugal e a rea do euro, que era de 74pp em 2012, anulou-se em apenas 7 anos. Portugal pode cumprir uma dcada completa a crescer tendo como base as exportaes e o investimento! Title: Opening speech by Governor Mrio Centeno at the Meeting of the Monitoring Committee of the National Plan for Financial Education
text: Opening speech by Governor Mario Centeno at the Meeting of the Monitoring Committee of the National Plan for Financial Education 21 February 2022 04 minutes  Aperture It is with great pleasure that I begin the meeting of the Monitoring Committee of the National Plan for Financial Education. On behalf of the National Council of Financial Supervisors, I thank the participation in this meeting of the Plan's partners and the members of the Jury of the Todos Contam Contest. The National Plan for Financial Education completed ten years of existence in 2021, but its mission is not complete. The National Council of Financial Supervisors reiterates the commitment of ten years ago: to promote financial education for the entire population. The strategic guidelines of the Plan for 2021-2025 reflect this ambition, assuming the urgency of the massification of the initiatives and the need to adapt them to the diversity of target audiences, objectives that will be achievable with the support of a network of entities, strategically close two different audiences.  Growing importance of financial education on the international agenda The revision of the Plan's guidelines takes place in a context marked by the restrictions associated with the pandemic, which have brought new challenges to financial education and led it to assume increasing importance on the international agenda, recognizing the urgency of it being assumed as a public policy. At the end of 2020, the OECD issued a recommendation on financial literacy, which was endorsed in 2021 by the G20, and which recognizes financial literacy as essential to face societal transformations In January of this year, the European Commission and the OECD's International Financial Education Network published a benchmark of financial literacy skills for the adult population of the European Union. In it, they identify the financial knowledge, attitudes and behaviors necessary for informed decision-making in money management. These skills are key to empowering citizens in financial decision-making and facing adverse financial shocks. The promotion of financial resilience, digital financial education and sustainable finance are highlighted themes in this framework.  National Plan for Financial Education 2021 -2025 The National Plan for Financial Education 2021-2025, whose final version we present today, is aligned with the objectives of the framework proposed by the European Union. It identifies as three strategic dimensions of action: strengthening financial resilience; the promotion of digital financial education; and the contribution to sustainability. To achieve the objectives set by 2025, the financial supervisors intend to establish new partnerships and strengthen the current ones, with a view to extending the Plan's activities to more target audiences. The Plan's strategy will continue to be based on the experience and knowledge of its partners, which allow the design and implementation of cohesive financial education programs that are appropriate to different segments of the population. Benefiting from the learning in the use of digital channels, which resulted from the pandemic, the Plan aims to strengthen the commitment to digital platforms, as a channel to transmit financial education messages to more target audiences. However, we must not forget the importance of face-to-face financial education initiatives. "Strengthening partnerships, investing in digital" is, therefore, the vision that guides the strategy of the National Plan for Financial Education for 2021-2025. It is through it that the CNSF proposes to lead the ambitious work program, counting on the valuable contribution of all the Plan's partners.  Priority lines of action for 2022 To achieve the new priorities, the Plan presents lines of action to be implemented. In 2022, the implementation of these lines of action involves densifying the work carried out in structuring projects such as:  Financial education in schools, with the support of the Ministry of Education, through the Directorate-General for Education, ANQEP and the School Library Network;  The financial training of employed or unemployed assets, with the support of the Institute of Employment and Vocational Training;  Financial training for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, with the support of IAPMEI and Turismo de Portugal. During this year, it is also intended to extend the financial education in the workplace project , recently started with the General Secretariat of the Ministry of Labour, Solidarity and Social Security, to other public sector entities. This project will also be extended to private sector entities. Financial training through local authorities has proven to be important to promote regional capillarity initiatives. In 2022, we will strengthen the work with the municipalities with the support of the Coordination and Development Commission of the Northern Region and with the National Library Network. The Plan has also strengthened this year the partnership with the Directorate-General for Consumers for the financial training of citizen support institutions, which work with vulnerable audiences, namely at risk of over-indebtedness. Awareness campaigns such as Global Money Week or Financial Education Week will continue to be important milestones in drawing the population's attention to the importance of financial education.  Final notes I conclude by thanking once again the partners present here, the members of the Jury of the Todos Contam Contest and all those who have accompanied us over these ten years The commitment of the partners is crucial for the success of this new stage of the Plan. Only with the collaboration of all will it be possible to achieve the objectives of this ambitious project... Because in financial education, Everyone Counts!
text_original: Interveno de abertura do Governador Mrio Centeno na Reunio da Comisso de Acompanhamento do Plano Nacional de Formao Financeira 21 fevereiro 2022 04 minutos 1. Abertura  com muito gosto que dou incio  reunio da Comisso de Acompanhamento do Plano Nacional de Formao Financeira. Em nome do Conselho Nacional de Supervisores Financeiros, agradeo a participao nesta reunio dos parceiros do Plano e dos membros do Jri do Concurso Todos Contam. O Plano Nacional de Formao Financeira completou, em 2021, dez anos de existncia, mas a sua misso no est concluda. O Conselho Nacional de Supervisores Financeiros reitera o compromisso de h dez anos: o de promover a formao financeira de toda a populao. As linhas de orientao estratgicas do Plano para 2021-2025 refletem esta ambio, assumindo a urgncia da massificao das iniciativas e a necessidade de adequao das mesmas  diversidade de pblicos alvo, objetivos que sero alcanveis com o apoio de uma rede de entidades, estrategicamente prximas dos diferentes pblicos. 2. Importncia crescente da formao financeira na agenda internacional A reviso das linhas de orientao do Plano ocorre num contexto marcado pelas restries associadas  pandemia, que trouxeram novos desafios para a educao financeira e levaram a que esta assumisse uma importncia crescente na agenda internacional, reconhecendo a urgncia de que seja assumida como uma poltica pblica. No final de 2020, a OCDE emitiu uma recomendao sobre literacia financeira, que foi endossada em 2021 pelo G20, e que reconhece a literacia financeira como essencial para enfrentar as transformaes da sociedade Em janeiro deste ano, a Comisso Europeia e a Rede Internacional de Educao Financeira da OCDE publicaram um referencial de competncias de literacia financeira para a populao adulta da Unio Europeia. Nele identificam os conhecimentos, as atitudes e os comportamentos financeiros necessrios para a tomada de decises informadas na gesto do dinheiro. Estas competncias so fundamentais para capacitar os cidados na tomada de decises financeiras e a enfrentar choques financeiros adversos. A promoo da resilincia financeira, a formao financeira digital e as finanas sustentveis so temas em destaque neste referencial. 3. Plano Nacional de Formao Financeira 2021 -2025 O Plano Nacional de Formao Financeira 2021 -2025, cuja verso final hoje apresentamos, est alinhado com os objetivos do referencial proposto pela Unio Europeia. Identifica como trs dimenses estratgicas de atuao: o reforo da resilincia financeira; a promoo da formao financeira digital; e o contributo para a sustentabilidade. Para alcanar os objetivos traados at 2025, os supervisores financeiros pretendem estabelecer novas parceiras e reforar as atuais, tendo em vista alargar a atuao do Plano a mais pblicos- alvo. A estratgia do Plano continuar a ser alicerada na experincia e conhecimento dos seus parceiros, que permitem desenhar e implementar programas de formao financeira coesos e adequados aos diferentes segmentos da populao. Beneficiando da aprendizagem na utilizao dos canais digitais, que resultou da pandemia, o Plano pretende reforar a aposta nas plataformas digitais, como canal para transmitir mensagens de formao financeira a mais pblicos-alvo. Contudo, no devemos esquecer a importncia das iniciativas de formao financeira presenciais. Reforar parcerias, apostar no digital , por isso, a viso que orienta a estratgia do Plano Nacional de Formao Financeira para 2021 -2025.  atravs dela que o CNSF se prope liderar o ambicioso programa de trabalhos, contando com o valioso contributo de todos os parceiros do Plano. 4. Linhas de ao prioritrias para 2022 Para concretizar as novas prioridades, o Plano apresenta linhas de ao a implementar. Em 2022, a implementao dessas linhas de ao passa por densificar o trabalho realizado em projetos estruturantes como:  A educao financeira nas escolas, com o apoio do Ministrio da Educao, atravs da Direo-Geral da Educao, da ANQEP e da Rede de Bibliotecas Escolares;  A formao financeira de ativos empregados ou desempregados, com o apoio do Instituto do Emprego e Formao Profissional;  A formao financeira para micro, pequenas e mdias empresas, com o apoio do IAPMEI e do Turismo de Portugal. Durante este ano, pretende-se tambm alargar o projeto da formao financeira no local de trabalho, recentemente iniciado com a Secretaria Geral do Ministrio do Trabalho, Solidariedade e Segurana Social, a outras entidades do setor pblico. Este projeto ser tambm estendido a entidades do setor privado. A formao financeira atravs das autarquias locais tem-se revelado importante para promover iniciativas de capilaridade regional. Em 2022, iremos reforar o trabalho com as autarquias com o apoio da Comisso de Coordenao e Desenvolvimento da Regio Norte e com a Rede Nacional de Bibliotecas. O Plano reforou tambm j este ano a parceria com a Direo-Geral do Consumidor para a formao financeira de instituies de apoio aos cidados, que trabalham junto de pblicos vulnerveis, nomeadamente em risco de sobre-endividamento. As campanhas de sensibilizao como a Global Money Week ou a Semana da Formao Financeira, continuaro a ser marcos importantes para chamar a ateno da populao para a importncia da formao financeira. 5. Notas finais Concluo, agradecendo uma vez mais aos parceiros aqui presentes, aos membros do Jri do Concurso Todos Contam e a todos os que nos acompanharam ao longo destes dez anos O compromisso dos parceiros  crucial para o sucesso desta nova etapa do Plano. S com a colaborao de todos ser possvel atingir os objetivos deste ambicioso projeto... Porque na formao financeira, Todos Contam!

Title: Speech by Governor Mrio Centeno at the Conference "Portugal: objective growth"
text: Speech by Governor Mario Centeno at the Conference "Portugal: Objective Growth" 11 March 2022 07 minutes Economic growth in Portugal For the first time, certainly in the last 80 years, economies are facing two exogenous shocks simultaneously. None of them change our priorities. What we have to do, to achieve economic growth, only accelerates in some dimensions. Today I would like to talk to you about three essential ideas: the ingredients of growth; monetary policy; economic policy priorities. What are the ingredients of sustainable growth?  Qualifications  Debt reduction  Climate transition None of these dimensions is new and Portugal has in each of them a difficult past, but remarkable progress. In qualifications. In the last two decades, we have bypassed the euro area and spread the gap with Eastern Europe. The percentage of young people (20-24 years old) with at least secondary education increased from 43% to 86%. The euro area had 74% and went to 84%. In the East they were 84% and 89%. In debt. In 2019, the public debt ratio was high and today it remains high, but it had fallen by 15 pp in the previous four years, standing at 116% of GDP. In what is the biggest challenge we face, we already know the way to go. We have already started it and we cannot hesitate. In 2021, the ratio is 127% of GDP. In energy dependence. Portugal has a high dependency ratio (percentage of imported energy). In recent years it has values slightly above 80%, which compares with 90% in the mid-2000s. On a positive side, the weight of renewables and biofuels was 27% in 2019, compared to only 16% in the euro area. Even given that the use of nuclear power explains part of this difference, the Portuguese leadership in the sustainable component of the use of renewable energy is still remarkable. To respond to these priorities, we need instruments: policy and market. To the question "do we have these instruments today?", the answer is yes, and we do not depend on anyone to use them. Only ourselves. The instrument for qualifications is the RRP, in the dimensions:  Digitalization of the economy and  Public policies for training and schooling, which should be associated with the reduction of liquidity difficulties for families. In 2015, in an initiative of the Presidency of the Republic, I had the opportunity to draw attention to the impact of liquidity restrictions on the decisions of Portuguese families about their children's schooling. This is a dimension that deserves all the attention of public policies. For debt reduction , given the circumstances, the starting point for 2022 could not be more positive. We are leading Europe in resuming the path of deleveraging the economy and finance, both public and private. I will speak in a moment about monetary policy, but the path is clear and has already been traveled in the past. We know how to do it. Growth, with investment and deleveraging, is a rare phenomenon in economics. We made this route. The biggest constraint that the market places on these processes is their financing. But this restriction does not exist today. We must value the advantageous conditions that the market grants us at the moment and always try to improve them. Finally, for energy dependence, we return to the European mechanisms, already defined and being defined, to reduce our dependence on fossil fuels, which are not sustainable and which the conflict in Ukraine has only underlined. But the issue is not dependence on Russian gas or oil, it is dependence on unsustainable energy sources. The market has alternatives. The transition should accelerate the use of these alternatives. Monetary policy is changing cycles in a gradual and measured manner, in line with the economic and financial challenges of the euro area. Economic, because inflation is a concern and growth is still recovering compared to the pre-pandemic period. Financial, because the stability and financial integration of the euro area are inalienable objectives for us. This means that monetary policy should seek a more neutral and less accommodative stance. For this to be achieved, fiscal integration in Europe must move forward, in the wake of the decisions taken in December 2019 and then already in the pandemic period in April and July 2020. In this context, there are three words to memorize: proportionality, which has a legal dimension, crucial in the context of the European Treaties, but which only says that the size and intensity of our interventions must balance instruments and objectives; optionality, creating space for decisions that should always be guided by the principle of doing whatever is necessary, as President Draghi put it in 2012; and flexibility, the principle behind the enormous success of the policy adopted in March 2020. Yesterday's decision, March 10, did not change the medium-term perspective. Standardisation is important, in a context where non-standard measures have already represented, since 2015, a value of more than 5 trillion euros. Of these, a significant component is available for reinvestment to tackle the financial fragmentation of the euro area. The projections, perhaps benign in the baseline scenario, predict growth of 3.7% for GDP and 5.1% for prices in 2022. However, the growth figures are positively affected by the carry-over effect of 2021. If GDP grows at 0% in all quarters of 2022, the annual GDP growth rate will still be 2.1%. In the adverse scenario of the ECB staff, released yesterday, annual growth is 2.5%, that is, it essentially corresponds to the carry over effect. Quarterly growth will be virtually nil, with a negative impact on the second and third quarters as a whole, recovering at the end of the year. This scenario, the likelihood of which will depend on the duration of the conflict, does not exclude a period of stagflation. We must all remember that the definition of stagflation, in the economics books and the historical experience of this phenomenon, also implies an impact on the labor market that I do not anticipate may happen. But a period of zero growth and high inflation seems inescapable. Changes in interest rates by the ECB are conditional on the conditions set out in its forwardguidance. These conditions are not yet met. Core inflation , which excludes the most volatile components, is still dominated by external factors, rather than supported by domestic factors such as wages. Labour markets in the euro area show no signs of second-round effects, in fact the ECB's wage forecasts have been successively revised downwards. Finally, the ECB adjusted one of the dimensions of the forward guidance, replacing the expression "shortlyafter" with "after some time" in defining how we move from the phase of net asset purchases to the phase of rate hikes. We have gained time and explicitly say that we should analyse the data and the economic and financial outlook when moving from one stage to the next. How can economic policy help in Portugal? Priority number 1: Effective, efficient and transversal use of European funds. This time, it is really different and I am not sure that the Public Administration is aware of this. Looking at the meager 17% of public investment financed by European funds in 2021, I would say that you are not aware of this at all. Priority number 2: Fiscal predictability. This predictability was an achievement of recent years, which according to the Bank of Portugal's calculations have reduced the structural weight of taxes by 1.2 pp of GDP since 2015. Fiscal predictability means reducing uncertainty about the future, without jeopardizing the imperative consolidation of public accounts. Priority number 3: Creating the conditions so that the increase in the quality and quantity of the labour supply is followed by the increase in the demand for labour. All countries, which in the last century and a half have had progressions similar to those of Portugal, have seen in the last decade an increase in the demand for work for these qualifications and an unparalleled acceleration in economic growth. Stability and competitive conditions are essential for this to happen. Priority number 4: Reduce risks in the banking system, consolidating the market and maintaining a trajectory that has allowed the banking system, as a whole, to make a positive contribution to the State Budget since 2021. And, step by step, but with sure steps, the trust that we all place (literally) in the banking system can translate into a feeling of "battle won" in the face of the storms of the not too distant past. One last word of optimism: few, very few, predicted the evolution of our economy between 2015 and 2022. The disasters committed in the forecasts during that period were sometimes epic, sometimes too anchored in a past of default, sometimes a a priori epistemological that proved to be profoundly wrong. We learn, sometimes at excessive cost. That must really belong to the past. And for this to be so, we only depend on ourselves. How many times have we been able to say this in our recent history? Not often. We must take advantage of this unique moment, in a difficult context, in which the word solidarity gains new contours every day. Thank you very much
text_original: Interveno do Governador Mrio Centeno na Conferncia Portugal: objetivo crescimento 11 maro 2022 07 minutos O crescimento econmico em Portugal Pela primeira vez, certamente nos ltimos 80 anos, as economias enfrentam em simultneo dois choques exgenos. Nenhum deles altera as nossas prioridades. O que temos que fazer, para alcanar crescimento econmico, apenas acelera nalgumas dimenses. Gostaria hoje de vos falar de trs ideias essenciais: os ingredientes do crescimento; a poltica monetria; as prioridades da poltica econmica. Quais so os ingredientes de um crescimento sustentvel? 1. Qualificaes 2. Reduo da dvida 3. Transio climtica Nenhuma destas dimenses  nova e Portugal tem em cada uma delas um passado difcil, mas um progresso notvel. Nas qualificaes. Nas duas ltimas dcadas, ultrapassmos a rea do euro e pulverizmos a diferena para com o Leste Europeu. A percentagem de jovens (20-24 anos) com pelo menos o ensino secundrio passou de 43% para 86%. A rea do euro tinha 74% e passou para 84%. No Leste eram 84% e 89%. Na dvida. Em 2019, o rcio da dvida pblica era alto e, hoje, permanece elevado, mas tinha cado 15 pp nos quatro anos anteriores, fixando-se nos 116% do PIB. Naquele que  o maior desafio que enfrentamos, j sabemos o caminho a percorrer. J o inicimos e no podemos hesitar. Em 2021, o rcio  de 127% do PIB. Na dependncia energtica. Portugal apresenta um rcio de dependncia (percentagem de energia importada) elevado. Nos ltimos anos tem valores ligeiramente superiores a 80%, o que compara com 90% em meados dos anos 2000. Numa dimenso positiva, o peso das energias renovveis e biocombustveis era 27% em 2019, quando na rea do euro era de apenas 16%. Mesmo atendendo a que o recurso ao nuclear explica parte desta diferena, no deixa de ser notvel a liderana portuguesa na componente sustentvel da utilizao de energia renovvel. Para responder a estas prioridades, necessitamos de instrumentos: de poltica e de mercado.  pergunta temos esses instrumentos hoje em dia?, a resposta  sim, e no dependemos de ningum para os utilizar. S de ns mesmos. O instrumento para as qualificaes  o PRR, nas dimenses: 1. Digitalizao da economia e 2. Polticas pblicas de formao e escolaridade, que devem estar associadas  reduo das dificuldades de liquidez para as famlias. Em 2015, numa iniciativa da Presidncia da Republica, tive oportunidade de chamar a ateno para o impacto das restries de liquidez nas decises das famlias portuguesas acerca da escolaridade dos seus filhos. Esta  uma dimenso que merece toda a ateno das polticas pblicas. Para a reduo da dvida, atendendo s circunstncias, o ponto de partida para 2022 no poderia ser mais positivo. Lideramos a Europa na retoma da trajetria de desalavancagem da economia e das finanas, pblicas e privadas. Falarei j a seguir da poltica monetria, mas o caminho  claro e j foi percorrido no passado. Sabemos faz-lo. Crescimento, com investimento e desalavancagem,  um fenmeno raro em economia. Ns fizemos esse trajeto. A maior restrio que o mercado coloca nestes processos  o seu financiamento. Mas essa restrio no existe hoje. Devemos valorizar as condies vantajosas que o mercado nos concede neste momento e tentar sempre melhor-las. Finalmente, para a dependncia energtica, voltamos aos mecanismos europeus, j definidos e em definio, para reduzir a nossa dependncia de combustveis fsseis, que no so sustentveis e que o conflito na Ucrnia apenas veio sublinhar. Mas a questo no  a dependncia do gs ou do petrleo russo,  a dependncia de fontes de energia no sustentveis. O mercado tem alternativas. A transio deve acelerar a utilizao dessas alternativas. A poltica monetria est a mudar de ciclo, de forma gradual e ponderada, acompanhando os desafios econmicos e financeiros da rea do euro. Econmicos, porque a inflao  uma preocupao e o crescimento ainda est a recuperar face ao perodo pr-pandemia. Financeiros, porque a estabilidade e a integrao financeira da rea do euro so objetivos inalienveis para ns. Isto quer dizer que a poltica monetria deve procurar uma posio mais neutra e menos acomodatcia. Para que isto seja conseguido, a integrao oramental na Europa deve avanar, na senda das decises tomadas em dezembro de 2019 e depois j no perodo pandmico em abril e julho de 2020. Neste contexto h trs palavras a memorizar: proporcionalidade, que tem uma dimenso jurdica, crucial no contexto dos Tratados Europeus, mas que apenas diz que a dimenso e intensidade das nossas intervenes devem equilibrar instrumentos e objetivos; opcionalidade, criando espao para decises que devem ser sempre guiadas pelo principio do fazer tudo o que for necessrio, como colocou o Presidente Draghi em 2012; e flexibilidade, o principio que est por detrs do enorme sucesso da poltica adotada em maro de 2020. A deciso de ontem, dia 10 de maro, no alterou a perspetiva de mdio-prazo. A normalizao  importante, num contexto em que as medidas no convencionais j representam, desde 2015, um valor superior a 5 bilies de euros. Destes, uma componente significativa est disponvel para reinvestimento para combater a fragmentao financeira da rea do euro. As projees, talvez benignas no cenrio de base, preveem um crescimento de 3,7% para o PIB e 5,1% para os preos, em 2022. No entanto, os nmeros do crescimento esto positivamente afetados pelo efeito de carry-over de 2021. Se o PIB crescer em cadeia 0% em todos os trimestres de 2022, ainda assim, a taxa de crescimento anual do PIB ser de 2,1 %. No cenrio adverso do staff do BCE, divulgado ontem, o crescimento anual  de 2,5%, ou seja, corresponde essencialmente ao efeito carry over. O crescimento trimestral ser virtualmente nulo, com um impacto negativo no conjunto dos segundo e terceiro trimestres, recuperando no final do ano. Este cenrio, cuja verosimilhana depender da durao do conflito, no permite excluir um perodo de estagflao. Devemos todos recordar que a definio de estagflao, nos livros de economia e a experiencia histrica deste fenmeno, implica tambm um impacto no mercado de trabalho que eu no antecipo que possa acontecer. Mas parece inescapvel um perodo de crescimento nulo e inflao elevada. As alteraes de taxas de juro pelo BCE esto dependentes de que se verifiquem as condies estabelecidas na sua forwardguidance. Essas condies ainda no esto cumpridas. A inflao core, que exclui as componentes mais volteis,  ainda dominada por fatores externos, e no sustentada por fatores domsticos, tais como os salrios. Os mercados de trabalho na rea do euro no mostram sinais de efeitos de segunda ordem, alis as previses do BCE para os salrios tm sucessivamente sido revistas em baixa. Finalmente, o BCE ajustou uma das dimenses da forwardguidance, substituindo a expresso shortlyafter por after some time na definio de como passamos da fase de compras liquidas de ativos para a fase de subidas de taxas. Ganhamos tempo e explicitamente dizemos que devemos analisar os dados e as perspetivas econmicas e financeiras ao passar de uma fase para a seguinte. Como pode a poltica econmica ajudar em Portugal? Prioridade nmero 1: Utilizao efetiva, eficaz e transversal dos fundos europeus. Desta vez,  mesmo diferente e no estou certo de que a Administrao Pblica esteja ciente disto. Ao olhar para os parcos 17% de investimento pblico financiado por fundos europeus em 2021, eu diria que no est mesmo nada ciente disto. Prioridade nmero 2: Previsibilidade fiscal. Esta previsibilidade foi uma conquista dos ltimos anos, que segundo os clculos do Banco de Portugal reduziram o peso estrutural dos impostos em 1,2 pp do PIB desde 2015. Previsibilidade fiscal significa reduzir a incerteza face ao futuro, sem por em causa a imperiosa consolidao das contas pblicas. Prioridade nmero 3: Criando as condies para que ao aumento da qualidade e da quantidade da oferta de trabalho, se siga o aumento da procura de trabalho. Todos os pases, que no ltimo sculo e meio tiveram progresses semelhantes s de Portugal, assistiram na ltima dcada a um aumento da procura de trabalho por essas qualificaes e a uma acelerao sem paralelo no crescimento econmico. Estabilidade e condies concorrenciais so essenciais para que isso acontea. Prioridade nmero 4: Reduzir os riscos no sistema bancrio, consolidando o mercado e mantendo uma trajetria que permitiu que desde 2021 o sistema bancrio, como um todo, tenha um contributo positivo para o Oramento de Estado. E, passo a passo, mas com passos seguros, a confiana que todos depositamos (literalmente) no sistema bancrio se possa traduzir num sentimento de batalha ganha face s tormentas de um passado no muito distante. Uma ltima palavra de otimismo: poucos, muito poucos, previram a evoluo da nossa economia entre 2015 e 2022. Os desastres cometidos nas previses durante esse perodo foram por vezes picos, por vezes demasiado ancorados num passado de incumprimento, por vezes um a priori epistemolgico que provou estar profundamente errado. Aprendemos, por vezes com um custo excessivo. Isso deve mesmo pertencer ao passado. E para que assim seja, s dependemos de ns mesmo. Quantas vezes pudemos dizer isso na nossa histria recente? No muitas vezes. Devemos aproveitar este momento nico, num quadro difcil, em que a palavra solidariedade ganha novos contornos a cada dia. Muito obrigado

Title: Opening speech by Governor Mrio Centeno at the Banking Forum
text: Opening speech by Governor Mario Centeno at the Banking Forum 13MAY2022 13 minutes Very good morning. First of all, I thank Jornal Economico for inviting me to open this debate on the prospects for the Portuguese banking system. We are living in a moment in European history that we did not anticipate. When the post-pandemic economic recovery was beginning to be a given, Russia's invasion of Ukraine created an economic, social and geopolitical framework of unpredictability. As a result, the European economy is simultaneously facing two large-scale and unprecedented exogenous shocks, which condition the outlook for economic growth and introduce inflationary pressures. While inflation is expected to remain high during 2022, there is no structural reason why it should not converge towards the medium-term objective as imbalances are gradually resolved and uncertainty dissipates. There are, for now, no structuring signs of de-anchoring. However, the balance of risks around inflation projections is skewed upwards due to the possibility of a longer conflict and the imposition of additional economic sanctions on Russia, including on energy imports. A possible de-anchoring of inflation expectations and the second-round effects on wage pressures pose additional risks that require close and continued monitoring. As I have been saying, the normalisation of monetary policy is necessary and desirable. But the conditions for doing it and the way in which it will be implemented deserve our attention. Patience and gradualism in monetary policy are necessary and must be proportionate to the shocks we face. Monetary policy should not overreact, in a sign of unwarranted nervousness that would create instability and fragmentation. An untimely reaction will also penalise economic growth. In a recent survey of business leaders around the world, the biggest fear raised about the ECB's monetary policy was that there could be an overreaction that would penalize the economic recovery. The costs of aggressive monetary policy or even very rapid normalization outweigh the benefits. A reaction that is too strong, through a rapid and sharp increase in interest rates, can have destabilising effects or even trigger a recession when the euro area has barely recovered from the previous crisis. On the other hand, the absence of a reaction, or the perception that there is not a sufficiently vigorous response, may require aggressive monetary policy tightening later on to control inflation, with increased costs in terms of activity and employment. Complicating the analysis, it is also conceivable that the absence of a reaction, or a very slow normalisation, favours expectations of low inflation in the long run, as it reinforces the idea that the monetary regime remains one of relatively low interest rates and low inflation. At the present time, the definition of optimal monetary policy is conditioned by the succession and size of recent shocks. Gone are the times of autopilot. In any case, the high degree of uncertainty calls for a gradual, data-driven response on the evolution of the economy now and in the future. In other words, maintaining optionality in monetary policy decisions is crucial at the present time. Central banks are aware of the risks and, therefore, have adopted a gradual response depending on the information that becomes available. In the case of the euro area, the end of net asset purchases should occur during the third quarter of this year and "some time later" the ECB should raise interest rates. At the moment it is anticipated that all this could happen in the first weeks of the third quarter, but that is not the most important debate now. The focus should be on the process, on its duration, on its magnitude. Because the truth is that normalization has already started from the moment net purchases began to reduce, still in 2021 and continuing in 2022. It is in this context that Portuguese banking will have to assert itself in the near future. This macroeconomic framework, national and international, will condition the balance of vulnerabilities and risks in the sector. But it is important to remember that the progress made by the Portuguese banking system in the last decade has prepared it to absorb potential losses, resulting from the effects that may persist from the pandemic crisis and the indirect impacts of Russia's military aggression against Ukraine. During the pandemic, the Portuguese banking sector proved its resilience. The global regulatory and supervisory reforms initiated after the global financial crisis and the risk reduction that occurred in the 5 years prior to the pandemic crisis contributed to increasing the resilience of our banks. The gross NPL and net impairment ratios maintained the downward trajectory started in June 2016, standing at 3.6% and 1.7%, respectively, in December 2021, reflecting compliance with the objectives outlined in the non-performing asset reduction plans. Because we sometimes diminish our efforts and successes, I recall that in June 2016, 17.9% of the banking sector's loan portfolio was classified as non-performing. The more than 38 billion euros of reduction speak well of the extraordinary, but difficult, path that the banks have traveled. And even during the pandemic. However, this risk reduction effort should remain for institutions that still have high ratios, and for the rest it is essential to maintain prudent credit granting criteria that avoid the accumulation of excessive risk on the balance sheet. Along with the support measures aimed at maintaining employment, the moratoria and the credit lines with public guarantee, made it possible to mitigate the materialization of credit risk and maintain the liquidity of households and companies. During the pandemic, the change in the support factor applied to exposures to SMEs under the CRR quickfix also contributed to the resilience of the banking sector , allowing for a lower risk weight in these exposures. Monetary policy liquidity support was also crucial for maintaining the financing structure of the banking system. The significant use of banks to TLTRO operations contributed to the reduction of the cost and risk of financing. As well as the recommendation not to distribute dividends to strengthen solvency. In the post-pandemic period, the way in which these measures were gradually lifted, plus European support for the recovery, has made it possible to preserve value and economic relations without preventing the necessary adjustment of the business fabric, without introducing increased risks into the banking system. The measures implemented in Portugal, national or European, and their combined effect, as well as their timing of implementation and extinction, allowed the Portuguese economy to be overcoming the challenges of the pandemic and the post-pandemic with distinction. The figures for the position of the Portuguese banking system at the end of 2021 are revealing of this process. The system's Total Capital ratio stood at 18% in 2021, compared to 16.9% in 2019. The liquidity profile also strengthened, with the transformation ratio, measured by credit to deposits, decreasing from 87.1% in 2019 to 81.2% in 2021, supported by a liquidity coverage ratio that currently stands at around 260%, compared to 218.5% in 2019. The level of capital has allowed the reduction of the amount of non-performing assets, which I have already mentioned. The profitability of the system has also seen a positive evolution. The return on assets increased by 0.41 p.p. compared to the previous year, standing at 0.46%, slightly above pre-pandemic values. This evolution reflected the decrease in credit impairments and, to a lesser extent, the increase in results from financial operations. Portuguese banks are more efficient than their European counterparts. The cost-to-income ratio maintained the downward trend started in 2019, standing at 53.4% in 2021, 4.4 pp less than in 2020 and about 8 pp less than the European average. The increase in banking income and the reduction in operating costs contributed to this reduction. Despite positive developments, challenges remain. With the increase in market interest rates, gross margin will tend to improve, given the concentration of variable rate loans. We expect the net impact on banks' balance sheets to be positive, as the economic recovery may contain the negative effects of the increased materialisation of credit risk. In addition, the NPL coverage ratio of around 52% for the total portfolio and 86% in the sectors most affected by the pandemic, will shield the sector from the effects of credit risk. On the other hand, the increase in long-term interest rates may have a negative impact on the valuation of financial assets in the portfolio, especially public debt. However, the relative reduction in exposure to national government debt and the increase in the proportion of exposure to public debt at amortised cost mitigates these effects. The banking sector's exposure to residential real estate is also monitored, but the current situation is not comparable to that of the previous financial crisis. The risk profile of borrowers has improved following the macroprudential recommendation and around 90% of the mortgage loan portfolio has a loan-to-value ratio below 80%. Good indicators of the resilience of Portuguese banks in this area. The challenge of digitalization continues . In the last two years, Portuguese banking has made a significant investment in information technology infrastructures. The programs of The digital transformation implemented has made it possible to adjust the operational structure to the new digital reality, enhance the offer of products and services and obtain efficiency gains. But digitalization has led to an increase in the entry points of cyberattacks - in digital channels for customers, in teleworking and by the greater use of service providers in the areas of information technology. This concern also extends to supply-chain attacks. The geopolitical context in which we live has also enhanced cyber risk. Resilience Cybernetics is thus a critical element in banking. Given the existing interlinkages between institutions and the use of common technology service providers, the possibility of systemic risks is also not negligible. The assessment of banks' ability to defend themselves in the face of a potential materialisation of cybersecurity risks is one of the supervisory priorities of the SSM and Banco de Portugal. Finally, a word for the challenges of the climate transition, now more conditioned by the need to reduce energy dependence. European mechanisms, already defined and being defined, will play a crucial role in reducing our dependence on fossil fuels, which are not sustainable and which Russia's aggression has only underlined. But beyond dependence on Russian gas or oil, the issue is related to dependence on unsustainable energy sources. The market has alternatives. The transition should accelerate the use of these alternatives. The commitment to carbon neutrality and a circular economy implies a profound transformation of our economic system. A transformation that covers all sectors of activity and forces companies and financial institutions to change business models. The task of reconverting the economy is cyclopean (as it could only be in the face of the threat we are facing). It has already been demonstrated by several reference entities that the energy transition is a behavioural and financial challenge of an absolutely exceptional dimension. The European Investment Bank has estimated that in order to achieve the target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 55% by 2030, the European Union will need additional investments equivalent to 2.1% of GDP per year. The International Monetary Fund has presented estimates, which it even considered conservative, according to which achieving the global target of net zero greenhouse gas emissions in 2050 requires additional investments of 0.6 to 1% of global GDP each year. The McKinsey Global Institute, for its part, has calculated that this same goal of netzero in 2050 will require an effort that should peak between 2026 and 2035, with additional investments that will then be equivalent to 1.6% of global GDP. Faced with figures of this order of magnitude, there is an incontrovertible conclusion: public investment will have to be accompanied by an even greater volume of private investment. Especially taking into account that:  we are faced with additional investment values, that is, in addition to gross investments to replace productive capital, also redirected to the transition, but which would have to be carried out anyway;  whereas this is an effort to be sustained for decades;  and, finally, that the effort will be uneven between countries and sectors; I have already said it: public policies will be decisive for the transition - and, therefore, they are also decisive for private investment. But the involvement of the financial sector will also be crucial. The information asymmetry is unfavorable to governments and the monitoring capacity is on the side of the financial sector. This responsibility, which can and should be seen as an opportunity, has several implications. I will highlight two. The first is that the types of investment will have to be adjusted. Sustainable investment projects typically involve innovative technologies, entail considerable research and development costs, incorporate a high capital intensity and have very long realisation horizons, measured in decades. These features require equity, quasi-equity, venture capital and other less common modalities, in addition to the traditional bank credit and bond markets. A second implication has to do with the quality of the information underlying these investments. A good assessment of risks and opportunities related to environmental sustainability requires that information is available, of good quality and comparable, and does not entail excessive costs. Several reference entities have studied this issue, which can be seen as the foundations of the building. I am talking, for example, about the International Monetary Fund, the Financial Stability Board, NetWork for Greening the Financial System and the International Financial Reporting Standards Foundation. Banco de Portugal has accompanied and contributed to these efforts. In fact, we need data that:  allow supervisors to monitor risks to financial stability from environmental sources;  provide investors with the information they need to assess companies and projects that are actually "green";  inform the various stakeholders about the plans for the transition of companies to more sustainable ways of operating. We must all be aware that the energy transition is already happening and will tend to intensify. National financial institutions, in particular, need to internalize this reality. The cost of delaying this adaptation process, waiting for the regulatory and reporting frameworks to be complete, is likely to be higher than the cost of acting now, even with the limitations and data gaps that we all recognize. The economic consequences and financial risks of a climate crisis will be profound for the sector. It is therefore essential that banks develop ways to address these risks by incorporating them into their business models, governance structures and risk management. At the same time, prudential regulation and supervision are undergoing profound transformation. The three pillars of the microprudential framework are being adapted to ESG risks; SSM's supervisory expectations on the management of climate risks by banks have been extended to banking institutions operating in Portugal; and the ECB launched a climate risk stress test to assess banks' preparedness. The results, expected in June, will be considered from a qualitative perspective in the supervisory review and evaluation (SREP) process. Due to the indirect impact on P2G capital requirements (via the assigned ratings), this exercise is therefore a key step in this transformation process. To conclude. The Portuguese banking sector is once again facing an increased uncertainty. However, in the years ahead, I am sure that it will continue its process of de-risking and market consolidation. The Portuguese banking system has the capital and liquidity to develop, without constraints, its role as a financial intermediary, contributing to the resilience and sustainability of the Portuguese economy. Thank you very much.
text_original: Interveno de abertura do Governador Mrio Centeno no Frum Banca 13MAI2022 13 minutos Muito bom dia. Em primeiro lugar, agradeo o convite do Jornal Econmico para abrir este debate sobre as perspetivas do sistema bancrio portugus. Vivemos num momento da histria Europeia que no antecipvamos. Quando a recuperao econmica no ps-pandemia comeava a ser um dado, a invaso da Ucrnia pela Rssia veio criar um quadro econmico, social e geopoltico de imprevisibilidade. Com isto, a economia europeia enfrenta em simultneo dois choques exgenos de grande dimenso e sem precedentes, que condicionam as perspetivas de crescimento econmico e introduzem presses inflacionistas. Embora a inflao deva permanecer alta durante 2022, no h razes estruturais para que no convirja para o objetivo de mdio prazo  medida que os desequilbrios sejam gradualmente resolvidos e a incerteza dissipada. No h por ora, sinais estruturantes de desancoragem. Contudo, o balano de riscos em torno das projees da inflao est enviesado em alta devido  possibilidade de um conflito mais longo e  imposio de sanes econmicas adicionais sobre a Rssia, nomeadamente sobre a importao de energia. Uma eventual desancoragem das expetativas de inflao e os efeitos de segunda ordem originrios nas presses salariais constituem riscos adicionais que exigem uma monitorizao atenta e continuada. Como tenho vindo a referir, a normalizao da poltica monetria  necessria e desejvel. Mas as condies para a fazer e o modo como ser concretizada merecem a nossa ateno. A pacincia e o gradualismo na poltica monetria so necessrios e devem ser proporcionais aos choques que enfrentamos. A poltica monetria no deve sobrerreagir, num sinal de nervosismo injustificado que criaria instabilidade e fragmentao. Uma reao intempestiva penalizar tambm o crescimento econmico. Num recente inqurito a responsveis empresariais de todo o mundo o maior receio levantado sobre a poltica monetria do BCE foi o de poder existir uma sobrereao que penalizasse a recuperao econmica. Os custos de uma poltica monetria agressiva ou mesmo de uma normalizao muito rpida superam os benefcios. Uma reao demasiado forte, atravs de um aumento rpido e acentuado das taxas de juro, pode ter efeitos desestabilizadores ou mesmo desencadear uma recesso quando a rea do euro mal recuperou da anterior crise. Por outro lado, a ausncia de reao, ou a perceo de que no h uma resposta suficientemente vigorosa, poder exigir um aperto agressivo da poltica monetria mais  frente para controlar a inflao, com custos acrescidos em termos da atividade e de emprego. Para complicar a anlise,  tambm concebvel que a ausncia de reao, ou uma normalizao muito lenta, favorea expectativas de inflao baixa no longo prazo, uma vez que refora a ideia de que o regime monetrio continua a ser um de taxas de juro relativamente baixas e inflao baixa. No momento atual, a definio da poltica monetria tima  condicionada pela sucesso e dimenso dos choques recentes. Longe vo os tempos do piloto automtico. Em qualquer caso, o elevado grau de incerteza aconselha a uma resposta gradual e baseada nos dados sobre a evoluo da economia agora e no futuro. Por outras palavras, manter a opcionalidade nas decises de poltica monetria  crucial no momento atual. Os bancos centrais esto cientes dos riscos e, por isso, tm adotado uma resposta gradual em funo da informao que vai ficando disponvel. No caso na rea do euro, o fim das compras lquidas de ativos dever ocorrer durante o terceiro trimestre deste ano e algum tempo depois o BCE dever aumentar as taxas de juro. Neste momento antecipa-se que tudo isto possa acontecer nas primeiras semanas do terceiro trimestre, mas esse no  o debate mais importante agora. O foco deve ser no processo, na sua durao, na sua magnitude. Porque a verdade  que a normalizao j se iniciou a partir do momento em as compras liquidas comearam a reduzir-se, ainda em 2021 e continuando em 2022.  com este contexto que a banca portuguesa ter de se afirmar no futuro prximo. Este enquadramento macroeconmico, nacional e internacional, ir condicionar o balano das vulnerabilidades e riscos do setor. Mas  importante relembrar que o progresso desenvolvido pelo sistema bancrio portugus na ltima dcada, preparou-o para absorver potenciais perdas, resultantes dos efeitos que podero persistir da crise pandmica e dos impactos indiretos da agresso blica da Rssia  Ucrnia. Durante a pandemia, o setor bancrio portugus provou a sua resilincia. As reformas regulatrias e de superviso globais iniciadas aps a crise financeira global e a reduo de risco que ocorreu nos 5 anos anteriores  crise da pandemia contriburam para aumentar a resilincia dos nossos bancos. Os rcios de NPL bruto e lquido de imparidades mantiveram a trajetria de reduo iniciada em junho de 2016, situando-se em 3,6% e 1,7%, respetivamente, em dezembro de 2021, refletindo o cumprimento dos objetivos delineados nos planos de reduo de ativos no produtivos. Porque s vezes minoramos os nossos esforos e sucessos, recordo que, em junho de 2016,17,9% da carteira de emprstimos do setor bancrio estava classificada como non-performing. Os mais de 38 mil milhes de euros de reduo dizem bem do extraordinrio, mas difcil, caminho que os bancos percorreram. E mesmo durante a pandemia. Todavia, este esforo de reduo de risco deve permanecer para as instituies que ainda registam rcios elevados, sendo que para as restantes  essencial manter critrios de concesso de crdito prudentes e que evitem a acumulao de risco excessivo no balano. A par das medidas de apoio dirigidas  manuteno do emprego, as moratrias e as linhas de crdito com garantia pblica, permitiram mitigar a materializao do risco de crdito e manter a liquidez das famlias e das empresas. Durante a pandemia, contribuiu ainda para a resilincia do setor bancrio, a alterao do fator de apoio aplicado s exposies a PME no mbito do CRR quickfix, permitindo um menor ponderador de risco nestas exposies. Tambm o suporte  liquidez da poltica monetria foi crucial para a manuteno da estrutura de financiamento do sistema bancrio. O recurso significativo dos bancos s operaes TLTRO contribuiu para a reduo do custo e risco de financiamento. Bem como a recomendao para a no distribuio de dividendos para o reforo da solvabilidade. No ps-pandemia, a forma como essas medidas foram gradualmente levantadas, acrescido do apoio europeu para a recuperao, tem permitido preservar valor e relaes econmicas sem impedir o necessrio ajustamento do tecido empresarial, no introduzindo riscos acrescidos no sistema bancrio. As medidas implementadas em Portugal, nacionais ou europeias, e o seu efeito conjugado, bem como o seu timing de execuo e de extino, permitiu que a economia portuguesa fosse ultrapassando com distino os desafios da pandemia e do ps-pandemia. Os nmeros da posio do sistema bancrio portugus no final de 2021 so reveladores deste processo. O rcio de Fundos Prprios Totais do sistema cifrou-se em 18% em 2021, face a 16,9% em 2019. O perfil de liquidez tambm se reforou, com o rcio de transformao, medido pelo crdito em funo dos depsitos a reduzir-se de 87,1% em 2019 para 81,2% em 2021, suportados por um rcio de cobertura de liquidez que se situa atualmente em cerca de 260%, face a 218,5% em 2019. O nvel de capital tem permitido a reduo do montante de ativos no produtivos, de que j falei. Tambm a rendibilidade do sistema tem observado uma evoluo positiva. A rendibilidade do ativo aumentou 0,41 p.p. face ao ano anterior, tendo-se fixado em 0,46%, ligeiramente acima dos valores pr-pandmicos. Esta evoluo refletiu a diminuio das imparidades para crdito e, em menor grau, o aumento dos resultados com operaes financeiras. Os bancos portugueses so mais eficientes do que os seus congneres europeus. O rcio cost-to- income manteve a tendncia de reduo iniciada em 2019, situando-se, em 2021, em 53,4%, menos 4,4 pp face a 2020 e cerca de menos 8 pp face  mdia europeia. Para esta reduo contribuiu o aumento do produto bancrio e a reduo dos custos operacionais. Apesar dos desenvolvimentos positivos, os desafios permanecem. Com o aumento das taxas de juro de mercado, a margem bruta tender a melhorar, dada a concentrao de emprstimos a taxa varivel. Perspetivamos que o impacto lquido no balano dos bancos possa vir a ser positivo, uma vez que a recuperao econmica poder conter os efeitos negativos da materializao acrescida do risco de crdito. Adicionalmente, o rcio de cobertura de NPLs, de cerca de 52% para o total da carteira e de 86% nos setores mais afetados pela pandemia, escudar o setor de efeitos do risco de crdito. Por outro lado, o aumento das taxas de juro de longo prazo poder ter um impacto negativo na valorizao dos ativos financeiros em carteira, com destaque para a dvida pblica. Contudo, a reduo relativa da exposio  dvida pblica nacional e o aumento da proporo da exposio a dvida pblica a custo amortizado minora estes efeitos. A exposio do setor bancrio ao imobilirio residencial tambm  monitorizada, mas a situao atual no  comparvel com a da anterior crise financeira. O perfil de risco dos muturios melhorou na sequncia da recomendao macroprudencial e cerca de 90% da carteira de crdito  habitao apresenta um rcio de loan-to-value inferior a 80%. Bons indicadores da resilincia dos bancos portugueses neste domnio. O desafio da digitalizao continua. Nos ltimos dois anos a banca portuguesa realizou um investimento significativo em infraestruturas de tecnologias de informao. Os programas de transformao digital implementados tm permitido ajustar a estrutura operacional  nova realidade digital, potenciar a oferta de produtos e servios e obter ganhos de eficincia. Mas a digitalizao levou a um aumento dos pontos de entrada dos ciberataques - nos canais digitais para clientes, nos de teletrabalho e pela maior utilizao de prestadores de servios nas reas de tecnologia de informao. Esta preocupao estende-se ainda aos ataques a prestadores de servios (supply-chain attacks). O contexto geopoltico em que vivemos tambm tem potenciado o ciber-risco. A resilincia ciberntica,  assim, um elemento crtico na atividade bancria. Dadas as interligaes existentes entre as instituies e o recurso a prestadores de servios tecnolgicos comuns, a possibilidade de riscos sistmicos tambm no  negligencivel. A avaliao da capacidade de os bancos se defenderem perante uma potencial materializao de riscos de cibersegurana  uma das prioridades de superviso do SSM e do Banco de Portugal. Finalmente, uma palavra para os desafios da transio climtica, agora mais condicionados pela necessidade da reduo da dependncia energtica. Os mecanismos europeus, j definidos e em definio, tero um papel crucial para reduzir a nossa dependncia de combustveis fsseis, que no so sustentveis e que a agresso da Rssia apenas veio sublinhar. Mas para alm da dependncia do gs ou do petrleo russo, a questo prende-se com a dependncia de fontes de energia no sustentveis. O mercado tem alternativas. A transio deve acelerar a utilizao dessas alternativas. A aposta na neutralidade carbnica e numa economia circular implica uma transformao profunda do nosso sistema econmico. Uma transformao que abarca todos os setores de atividade e obriga as empresas e as instituies financeiras a alterarem os modelos de negcio. Atarefa de reconverso da economia  ciclpica (como s poderia ser perante a ameaa com que estamos confrontados). Foi j demonstrado por vrias entidades de referncia que a transio energtica constitui um desafio comportamental e financeiro de uma dimenso absolutamente excecional. O Banco Europeu de Investimento estimou que, para atingir o objetivo de reduzir em 55% as emisses de gases com efeito de estufa at 2030, a Unio Europeia vai necessitar de investimentos adicionais equivalentes a 2,1 % do PIB por ano. O Fundo Monetrio Internacional apresentou estimativas, que at considerou conservadoras, segundo as quais atingir a meta global de emisso nula lquida - netzero - de gases com efeito de estufa em 2050 requer investimentos adicionais de 0,6 a 1 % do PIB global em cada ano. O McKinsey Global Institute, por seu turno, calculou que essa mesma meta de netzero em 2050 vai exigir um esforo cujo pico dever acontecer entre 2026 e 2035, com investimentos adicionais que sero, nessa altura, equivalentes a 1,6% do PIB global. Perante valores desta ordem de grandeza, h uma concluso incontroversa: o investimento pblico ter de ser acompanhado por um volume ainda maior de investimento privado. Sobretudo tendo em conta que:  estamos perante valores adicionais de investimento, ou seja, a acrescer aos investimentos brutos para substituir o capital produtivo, tambm reorientados para a transio, mas que teriam de ser realizados de qualquer forma;  que se trata de um esforo a sustentar ao longo de dcadas;  e, finalmente, que o esforo ser desigual entre pases e setores; j o disse: as polticas pblicas sero determinantes para a transio - e, portanto, so tambm determinantes para o investimento privado. Mas o envolvimento do setor financeiro tambm ser crucial. A assimetria de informao  desfavorvel aos governos e a capacidade de monitorizao est do lado do setor financeiro. Esta responsabilidade, que pode e deve ser encarada como uma oportunidade, tem vrias implicaes. Vou destacar duas. A primeira  que as tipologias de investimento tero de ser ajustadas. Os projetos de investimento sustentvel tipicamente envolvem tecnologias inovadoras, acarretam custos considerveis em investigao e desenvolvimento, incorporam uma forte intensidade de capital e tm horizontes de concretizao muito longos, medidos em dcadas. Estas caratersticas requerem instrumentos de capital, quase-capital, capital de risco e outras modalidades menos comuns, alm dos tradicionais mercados de crdito bancrio e de obrigaes. Uma segunda implicao tem que ver com a qualidade da informao subjacente a estes investimentos. A boa avaliao dos riscos e das oportunidades relacionados com a sustentabilidade ambiental exige que a informao esteja disponvel, seja de boa qualidade e comparvel e no comporte custos excessivos. Vrias entidades de referncia tm estudado esta questo, que pode ser vista como os alicerces do edifcio.
