Falo, por exemplo, do Fundo Monetrio Internacional, do Financial Stability Board, da NetWork for Greening the Financial System e da International Financial Reporting Standards Foundation. O Banco de Portugal tem acompanhado e contribudo para estes esforos. De facto, necessitamos de dados que:  permitam aos supervisores monitorizarem os riscos para a estabilidade financeira de origem ambiental;  forneam aos investidores a informao necessria para avaliarem as empresas e os projetos efetivamente verdes;  informem as diversas partes envolvidas quanto aos planos de transio das empresas para formas de funcionamento mais sustentveis. Todos devemos estar conscientes de que a transio energtica est j a acontecer e tender a intensificar-se. As instituies financeiras nacionais, em particular, necessitam de interiorizar essa realidade. O custo de adiar este processo de adaptao, aguardando que os quadros de regulao e de reporte estejam completos, ser provavelmente superior ao custo de agir j, mesmo com as limitaes e as lacunas de dados que todos reconhecemos. As consequncias econmicas e os riscos financeiros de uma crise climtica sero profundas para o setor. , assim, essencial que os bancos desenvolvam formas de lidar com esses riscos, incorporando-os nos seus modelos de negcio, nas suas estruturas de governo e na gesto de risco. Paralelamente, a regulao e superviso prudencial esto em profunda transformao. Os trs pilares do enquadramento microprudencial esto a ser adaptados aos riscos ESG; as expectativas de superviso do SSM sobre a gesto dos riscos climticos pela banca foram alargadas s instituies bancrias a operar em Portugal; e o BCE lanou um teste de esforo centrado nos riscos climticos para avaliar o grau de preparao dos bancos. Os resultados, previstos para junho, sero considerados numa perspetiva qualitativa no processo de anlise e avaliao para fins de superviso (SREP). Pelo impacto indireto nos requisitos de fundos prprios do Pilar 2 (por via das notaes atribudas), este exerccio revela-se, assim, um passo determinante neste processo de transformao. Para concluir. O setor bancrio portugus enfrenta mais uma vez um quadro de incerteza acrescido. Contudo, nos anos que tem pela frente, estou certo que continuar o seu processo de reduo do risco e consolidao de mercado. O sistema bancrio portugus possui capital e liquidez para desenvolver, sem condicionantes, o seu papel de intermedirio financeiro, contribuindo para a resilincia e sustentabilidade da economia portuguesa. Muito obrigado.

Title: Opening speech by Governor Mrio Centeno at the XXXII Lisbon Meeting between Portuguese-speaking Central Banks
text: Opening speech by Governor Mario Centeno at the XXXII Lisbon Meeting between the Portuguese-speaking Central Banks 10 October 2022 06 minutes Ambassadors, Governors and Vice-Governors, Dear Guests, It is with great pleasure that I welcome you at the beginning of the work of this 32nd Lisbon Meeting. Once the worst phase of the pandemic is over and the reopening of economies resumes, which allows us to be here, we hoped to be able to witness more robust economic growth, less affected by economic or geopolitical uncertainties. But an unprecedented second exogenous shock  Russia's unjustifiable invasion of Ukraine  has severely disrupted this panorama. Cooperation gains with this new context another sense of urgency. The outlook for the global economy has deteriorated. The projections for economic activity, international trade and inflation are worse than those we had a year ago. Since the beginning of the invasion, there has been a sharp outflow of capital from emerging and developing economies, with the consequent deterioration of financial conditions for the most vulnerable debtors and importers of raw materials. Exchange rate depreciation, with the reinforcement of inflationary pressures, has also been affecting external debts. The role of central banks in this framework - in particular in defending price stability - and the cooperation required depend very much on the nature of the shocks. The rise in inflation mainly reflects an increase in energy and food prices, initially as a result of supply disruptions and the post-pandemic recovery in global demand, but has been exacerbated more recently by the invasion of Ukraine. We know that the effectiveness of monetary policy is limited in the face of supply shocks such as: disruptions in the energy market, shortages of raw materials, increases in shipping costs and supplier delivery times, temporarily closed factories. The increase in prices caused by these disruptions in global supply chains recommends caution in our actions. I have repeated that the normalisation of monetary policy is necessary and desirable. At the same time, monetary policy decisions should be gradual and guided by flexibility and proportionality. The costs of an aggressive monetary policy have outweighed the benefits: untimely reactions are likely to become an overshooting , adding to the various overreactions that have characterized economies in the post-pandemic period. A decision-maker cannot himself be a factor of instability. It will be worse if the decisions have to be reversed shortly after, affecting the credibility of central banks. Signs of de-anchoring inflation expectations and second-round effects (including wage formation) require timely interventions, as it is necessary to avoid a transition to a monetary regime of high inflation and high interest rates. In that case, the costs of acting late are clearly higher. Ultimately, it is important to try to understand whether price increases and volatility remain limited to some categories of goods and services or whether, on the contrary, they have contagion effects. In any case, clear and timely communication of decisions and statistical information to enable economic agents to make informed decisions remains crucial. Let me also insist on the issues of macroeconomic stability and the role of fiscal policy. It is true that fiscal policies in several countries and regions of the world are under severe pressure. In 2021, several countries continued to use expansionary fiscal policies to address the pandemic situation. With historically high public debt, the scope to accommodate the impacts of the war on their economies in 2022 is, in many cases, quite small. In addition, rising interest rates in advanced economies will have an additional impact on the external public debt of emerging and developing economies. In this context, any attempt to mitigate the impact of the reduction in purchasing power on populations should be very cautious, so that it does not generate even more inflation. It will be crucial that budget support is temporary and focused on population groups affected by the pandemic and on lower-income households. On the central bank side, we continue to monitor fiscal policy, given the implications for safeguarding price stability. The agenda of the International Financial Institutions also continues to focus on the issue of cooperation between economic policies. They have also been reminding that a rules-based global system is essential for a strong recovery, while considering responses to cyclical and structural challenges. In addition to monetary policy decisions, let me focus on the importance of the role of central banks in promoting financial stability. From a more structural perspective, continued efforts to reform regulation and supervision were also decisive in maintaining the robustness of monetary and financial systems during and after the pandemic. The delivery and visibility of these reform efforts will remain the most important tool for addressing uncertainty and system challenges. Improving the responsiveness of central banks and thus their role in building more robust economies and societies is the objective of Banco de Portugal's cooperation. Cooperation activity - bilateral, regional and international - is not limited to Official Development Assistance. It is much more than that. I am referring to the joint benefit of debating solutions to problems that go beyond our borders. It is this notion that moves us in the realization of the Lisbon Meeting and the various initiatives that take place on its margins. In this way, we bring to the annual meetings of the IMF/WBG a rich perspective and mutual knowledge, which are a unique capital and an effective contribution to the performance of our role as central banks. In 2021, Banco de Portugal participated in an unprecedented number of cooperation actions (174), involving more than a thousand external participants from almost 40 institutions. These figures demonstrate the rapid adaptation of the "business model" of cooperation. Cooperation has been extended to new themes and needs. We have put climate change and the digital transition on our agenda and exploited the full potential of remote technology to scale up our action. With the pandemic we did not reduce cooperation, we increased cooperation in terms of topics, partners, and number of actions. We have continued to contribute to the fundamental issues of central bank mandates, such as financial supervision and stability, payment systems, economic analysis or statistics. We are well aware of how fundamental the quality of governance is, and we therefore devote great attention to it. We continued to be available to our traditional partners in Portuguese-speaking countries, but also to other latitudes. We work with other institutions, namely European, also convened by the effort that the invasion of Ukraine required. These will also be the pillars of the debate in Washington, where multilateral cooperation takes on renewed urgency. Supporting the most vulnerable economies, rising public debt, climate change and the digital transition are shared challenges, requiring global action. The IMF, as the institution at the heart of the global financial safety net, has shown readiness, calibrating its advice and tools for an effective response. We will thus have the opportunity to assess the progress of cooperative action in the voluntary channelling of Special Drawing Rights, following the historic general allocation of August 2021 - a process in which Portugal, with the involvement of Banco de Portugal, remains firmly committed. I also highlight the recent creation of a window for food shocks in emergency financial assistance facilities and the expected entry into operation of the new Resilience and Sustainability Trust. The diversity is evident, but also the convergence of concerns and responses in cooperation between central banks and in terms of participation in International Financial Institutions. That is why, throughout the day, it is important to listen to each other on the future of technical cooperation, but also on the major themes of international financial institutions, so that we can contribute with knowledge of each other's perspectives. Ladies and Gentlemen, In a context of particular uncertainty about the immediate future, but also the medium and long term, the challenges facing central banks are extremely complex. To talk to us about these challenges, we have with us Dr. Vitor Constancio, who more than anyone needs no introduction, so I give him the floor. Thank you very much.
text_original: Interveno de abertura do Governador Mrio Centeno no XXXII Encontro de Lisboa entre os Bancos Centrais de Lngua Portuguesa 10 outubro 2022 06 minutos Senhores Embaixadores, Senhores Governadores e Vice-Governadores, Caros Convidados,  com muito gosto que vos dou as boas-vindas no incio dos trabalhos deste 32 Encontro de Lisboa. Ultrapassada a pior fase da pandemia e retomada a reabertura das economias, que nos permite estar aqui, espervamos puder testemunhar crescimento econmico mais robusto, menos afetados por incertezas econmicas ou geopolticas. Mas um segundo choque exgeno sem precedentes-a injustificvel invaso da Ucrnia pela Rssia - veio perturbar severamente esse panorama. A cooperao ganha com este novo contexto outro sentido de urgncia. As perspetivas para a economia mundial deterioraram-se. As projees para a atividade econmica, o comrcio internacional e a inflao so piores do que aquelas que tnhamos h um ano atrs. Desde o incio da invaso tem-se observado uma sada acentuada de capitais das economias emergentes e em desenvolvimento, com a consequente degradao das condies financeiras para os devedores mais vulnerveis e para os importadores de matrias-primas. As depreciaes cambiais, com reforo das presses inflacionistas, tem vindo a afetar tambm as dvidas externas. O papel dos bancos centrais neste quadro - em especial na defesa da estabilidade dos preos - e a cooperao exigida dependem muito da natureza dos choques. A subida da inflao reflete maioritariamente um aumento dos preos dos bens energticos e alimentares, inicialmente em resultado das disrupes na oferta e da recuperao ps-pandmica da procura global, mas foi, mais recentemente, exacerbada pela invaso da Ucrnia. Ora, sabemos que a eficcia da poltica monetria  limitada perante choques da oferta como: disrupes no mercado da energia, escassez de matrias-primas, aumentos dos custos de transporte martimo e dos prazos de entrega dos fornecedores, fbricas temporariamente encerradas. O aumento dos preos originado por estas perturbaes nas cadeias de abastecimento globais recomenda prudncia nas nossas aes. Tenho repetido que a normalizao da poltica monetria  necessria e desejvel. Ao mesmo tempo, as decises de poltica monetria devero ser graduais e pautar-se pela flexibilidade e pela proporcionalidade. Os custos de uma poltica monetria agressiva superaram os benefcios: reaes intempestivas so suscetveis de se tornarem uma sobre-reao (overshooting), acrescendo s vrias sobre-reaes que muito tem caracterizado as economias na ps-pandemia. Um decisor no pode ele prprio ser um factor de instabilidade. Pior ser se as decises tiverem de ser revertidas pouco depois, afetando a credibilidade dos bancos centrais. Sinais de desancoragem das expetativas de inflao e de efeitos de segunda ordem (inclusive na formao dos salrios) exigem intervenes atempadas pois torna-se necessrio evitar que se transite para um regime monetrio de inflao elevada e de taxas de juro elevadas. Nesse caso, os custos de agir tardiamente so claramente superiores. Em ltima anlise, importa procurar compreender se os aumentos e a volatilidade de preos permanecem circunscritos a algumas categorias de bens e de servios ou se, pelo contrrio, tm efeitos de contgio. Em qualquer caso, permanece crucial uma comunicao clara e atempada das decises, bem como da informao estatstica que permita aos agentes econmicos tomar decises fundamentadas. Permitam-me ainda insistir nas questes de estabilidade macroeconmica e sobre o papel da poltica oramental.  certo que as polticas oramentais em vrios pases e regies do mundo esto sob forte presso. Em 2021, vrios pases continuaram a recorrer a polticas oramentais expansionistas para fazer face  situao de pandemia. Com a dvida pblica historicamente elevada, a margem para acomodar os impactos da guerra sobre as respetivas economias em 2022 , em muitos casos, bastante reduzida. Acresce que o aumento das taxas de juro nas economias avanadas ter um impacto adicional sobre a dvida pblica externa das economias emergentes e em desenvolvimento. Neste quadro, qualquer tentativa de mitigao do impacto da reduo do poder de compra nas populaes dever ser muito cautelosa, para que no gere ainda mais inflao. Ser fulcral que o apoio oramental seja temporrio e focalizado nos grupos populacionais afetados pela pandemia e nas famlias de menor rendimento. Do lado dos bancos centrais, continuamos a acompanhar a poltica oramental, dadas as implicaes para a salvaguarda da estabilidade de preos. A agenda das Instituies Financeiras Internacionais continua igualmente a dar destaque  questo da cooperao entre as polticas econmicas. Tm vindo tambm a relembrar que um sistema mundial assente em regras  essencial para uma retoma slida, enquanto equacionam respostas aos desafios conjunturais e estruturais. Alm das decises de poltica monetria, permitam-me que me foque na importncia do papel dos bancos centrais na promoo da estabilidade financeira. Numa perspetiva mais estrutural, os esforos continuados de reforma na regulao e superviso foram tambm decisivos para manter a robustez dos sistemas monetrios e financeiros durante e aps a pandemia. A concretizao e visibilidade destes esforos de reforma permanecer a mais importante ferramenta para fazermos face  incerteza e aos desafios dos sistemas. A melhoria da capacidade de resposta dos bancos centrais e, deste modo, do seu papel na construo de economias e sociedades mais robustas,  o objetivo da cooperao do Banco de Portugal. A atividade de cooperao - bilateral, regional e internacional - no se resume  Ajuda Pblica ao Desenvolvimento.  muito mais do que isso. Refiro-me ao benefcio conjunto sobre o debate de solues para problemas que extravasam as nossas fronteiras.  essa noo que nos move na realizao do Encontro de Lisboa e das vrias iniciativas que  sua margem decorrem. Levamos, desta forma, para as reunies anuais do FMI/GBM uma perspetiva rica e um conhecimento mtuo, que so um capital nico e um efetivo contributo para o desempenho do nosso papel de bancos centrais. Em 2021, o Banco de Portugal participou num nmero sem precedentes de aes de cooperao (174), envolvendo mais de mil participantes externos provenientes de quase 40 instituies. Estes nmeros demonstram a rpida adaptao do modelo de negcio da cooperao. A cooperao tem vindo a alargar-se a novos temas e necessidades. Colocmos as alteraes climticas e a transio digital na nossa agenda e explormos todas as potencialidades da tecnologia remota para alargar a nossa ao. Com a pandemia no reduzimos a cooperao, aumentmos a cooperao em abrangncia de temas, em parceiros, em nmero de aes. Mantivemos o contributo nas questes fundamentais dos mandatos dos bancos centrais, como a superviso e estabilidade financeira, os sistemas de pagamentos, a anlise econmica ou as estatsticas. Sabemos bem como a qualidade da governao  fundamental e, assim, dedicamos-lhe grande ateno. Continumos disponveis para os nossos tradicionais parceiros da lusofonia, mas tambm para outras latitudes. Trabalhamos com outras instituies, nomeadamente europeias, convocados tambm pelo esforo que a invaso da Ucrnia exigiu. Sero tambm estes os pilares do debate em Washington, em que a cooperao multilateral assume renovada urgncia. O apoio s economias mais vulnerveis, a dvida pblica crescente, as alteraes climticas e a transio digital so desafios partilhados, exigindo ao global. O FMI, enquanto instituio no centro da rede de segurana financeira global, tem mostrado prontido, calibrando o seu aconselhamento e instrumentos para uma resposta eficaz. Teremos, assim, oportunidade de avaliar os progressos da ao cooperativa na canalizao voluntria de Direitos de Saque Especiais, na sequncia da histrica atribuio geral de agosto de 2021 - processo no qual Portugal, com o envolvimento do Banco de Portugal, permanece firmemente comprometido. Destaco, tambm, a recente criao de uma janela para choques alimentares nas facilidades de assistncia financeira de emergncia e a esperada entrada em operao do novo Resilience and Sustainability Trust.  patente a diversidade, mas tambm a convergncia de preocupaes e de respostas na cooperao entre bancos centrais e no plano da participao nas Instituies Financeiras Internacionais.  por isso que, ao longo do dia,  relevante auscultarmo-nos sobre o futuro da cooperao tcnica, mas tambm sobre os grandes temas das instituies financeiras internacionais, para que possamos contribuir com conhecimento das perspetivas uns dos outros. Senhoras e Senhores, Num quadro de particular incerteza quanto ao futuro imediato, mas tambm de mdio e longo prazo, os desafios que os bancos centrais enfrentam revestem-se de enorme complexidade. Para nos falar destes desafios, temos connosco o Dr. Vtor Constncio, que mais do que ningum dispensa apresentaes, pelo que lhe passo a palavra. Muito obrigado.

Title: Speech by the Governor of Banco de Portugal, Mrio Centeno, at the closing ceremony of the Financial Education Week 2022
text: Speech by Governor Mario Centeno at the Order of Economists - State Budget 2023 09 November 2022 05 minutes Good afternoon. It is with great regret that I cannot participate in person in the debate promoted by the Order of Economists on the 2023 State Budget. By the time you are listening to me, I will be on the Governing Council of the ECB, taking care of the normalisation of monetary policy, with the aim of reducing inflation while seeking to ensure economic and financial stability. The current macroeconomic picture is full of uncertainties, associated with the prolongation of the atrocious invasion of Ukraine and Europe's energy dependence, where high inflation inflicts destabilizing pressure. If this inflation scenario continues, it will bring uncertainty, loss of confidence of economic agents and an inevitable recession. As we know, inflation started out as a phenomenon originating in supply, but it has extended to demand, although not yet generalized. Widespread, frequent and large price increases have become the norm rather than the exception. Although inflation expectations remain anchored in the medium term, it is urgent to act, collectively, towards a common goal: to bring inflation to 2% as soon as possible. Inflation is just a symptom, which has underlying causes. Without attacking its sources, it will erode the foundations of our economic system, which in recent decades has benefited from price stability. If we do not control inflation, the behavior of economic agents will bring a recession. Inflation will wipe out the very significant gains in wages, employment, and savings of recent years. Just one example, between 2015 and 2021 the minimum wage grew by more than 40% in real terms. That is why monetary policy "has to", "is" and "will" act. The role of the European Central Bank is very clear in this area. The goal is to bring inflation to 2% in the medium term. Monetary policy plays a key role in managing expectations. By acting on interest rates, it is reflected in consumption and investment decisions, often acting on past decisions made using credit with variable interest rates. The effects will tend to be staggered and spaced out in time, but will allow the medium-term objective to be achieved. All agents - consumers, companies and the State - understand the ECB's commitment to this new monetary policy cycle as long as the inflation rate in the medium term is not controlled. Failure to act would have a greater recessionary cost than the increase in interest rates causes. This is the challenging scenario that the Portuguese are facing for 2023, and also, of course, the State Budget. Compared to Europe, the most recent data show that Portugal is one of the fastest growing countries, in year-on-year terms we were even the country that grew the most compared to 2021. The data surprise us positively, since the third quarter of 2020.0 unemployment remains low and employment has responded positively together with wages. In the short term, the news is good. Its dynamism is not behaving as clearly and sustainably as it has in recent years, especially since 2015, including in 2020 during the peak of the pandemic crisis. The increase in production and financing costs burdens investment and the increase in uncertainty undermines decision-making processes. As a result, the process of economic recovery suffers. The statistics that tell us what percentage of investment is financed by European funds are still dramatically low. Less than 20% of total public investment is financed by European funds, which means that more than 80% is financed with taxes paid by the Portuguese. The execution rate of the RRP has been much lower than expected, also hampered by the inflation of the cost of projects. For 2023, the continuation of reforms under the RRP is expected to accelerate the effective and efficient use of funds and boost investment. But to return to inflation, let me say a word about the second-round effects on prices. The focus cannot be on wage pressures alone; It is equally important to pay attention to the role of profit margins in this inflationary process. One euro of wages paid above what is compatible with price stability causes equal pressure on inflation as one euro more on corporate profit margins. A wage increase compatible with price stability would be equal to the sum of the ECB's inflation target, 2%, with the productivity gain, divided between wages and return on capital. It is here, at this point, that the problem of inflation becomes a collective issue. Which will only be overcome at the lowest cost if we have the ability to act in a coordinated and collective manner on inflationary pressures. In 2020, the net deposit debt of households and companies in Portugal decreased. This was the extraordinary result of the awareness we all had of the need to respond to a unique crisis. Today, in the face of inflation, these financial cushions respond in a first phase, creating the conditions to cushion the recessive effects of inflation, but paradoxically they can be factors of resistance to the reduction of inflation. However, we know that rising and prolonging inflation will erode these cushions and have far worse consequences than would result from coordinated action in the markets to contain wage pressures and profit margins on prices. The loss of real income from the economy translates into a social cost that must be shared by all. The productivity gains resulting from the post-pandemic recovery should be used to reverse the inflationary cycle. On the fiscal policy side, any attempt to mitigate the impact of the reduction in purchasing power on populations must be very meticulous. It should be focused on those who suffer the most, avoiding transversal measures that can themselves be factors that sustain price increases and prolong this state of accelerating inflation. Budgetary policy must be guided by sustainability, with future generations in mind. The reduction of public debt is equitable; it benefits everyone today and protects the future. I will close my speech with a message that I have reiterated. It is necessary to maintain the European spirit of 2020, guided by effective coordination between monetary and fiscal policy, a sense of solidarity, translated into the issuance of common debt by the European Commission, a decades-old European dream made a reality by the decisions of the Eurogroup in spring 2020. I wish you a productive discussion. Thank you very much.

Title: Speech by Governor Mrio Centeno at the Order of Economists - State Budget 2023
text: Speech by Governor Mario Centeno at the Launch of the Book "The Legacy of Manuela Silva" 11 November 2022 04 minutes Mr. President of the Republic, Senhora Presidente do ISEG Ladies and gentlemen, It is with great pleasure that I join in the tribute to the pioneering work of Professor Manuela Silva in the study of inequality and poverty in Portugal. As a full professor at my Higher Institute of Economics between 1970 and 1991, the same school where she graduated in Economics and became a researcher, Manuela Silva was the source of many teachings and enormous inspiration. The launch of this book is a tribute of incomparable value. It brings together testimonies from many of those who crossed paths with her and worked with her during her 87 years of life. He publishes articles about his career, his thought and his work. And it makes known the work of several of his disciples on the themes that marked his academic, professional and personal path. Due to the importance of his career for students and colleagues, but also for future generations, Banco de Portugal is very pleased to be associated with the publication and launch of this book. As a public service institution operating in the economic and financial area, Banco de Portugal aims to promote research and knowledge in the area of economic sciences. In the pursuit of the public interest, we always seek to contribute to the reflection and informed public discussion of topics relevant to the economy and society. Professor Manuela Silva defended and taught us that the economy must be at the service of people, contribute to the preservation of the planet we inhabit and promote inclusive community development. It was the defense of the common good that he always had in mind. By appealing to the need to "put poverty in the foreground", he did not intend only to care for the poor. His concern was to take care of everyone. Because, as he argued, "poverty affects the poor, but also the quality of democracy". A lesson that today, at a time of enormous economic and geopolitical uncertainty, is even more important. This is the main legacy of Professor Manuela Silva: to show us that studying and caring for those on the margins of society and the economy is to know, care for and promote the common good. In economics, after many decades of meandering intellectually motivated attempts, we realize that it is not possible to distribute without growing, and it is not possible to grow without distributing. It took us many decades to assume this result that today seems obvious. Science is just like that. As Professor Manuela Silva knew so well, the best strategy to fight inequality in a structural way is, without a doubt, education. Education is a key factor for economic and social inclusion. It is the universal solution to achieve long-term economic growth. It is up to us to continue their work. In a study recently published by Banco de Portugal, we concluded that the intergenerational transmission of education, reinforced by the interaction with the financial situation of families, has important implications for the individual's educational paths, and with that, for social inclusion and the potential for economic growth. In Portugal, 73% of individuals whose parents have higher education have also completed a higher education course. However, more than half of individuals with less than secondary education (56%) come from families that have a lower level of education. The family's ability to finance their children's education is a very relevant factor in the intergenerational transmission of education. This study concludes that the family's financial situation when young people are 14 years old is critical for the duration of their school career. The combination of the two factors - education and financial condition of the parents - results in an even more decisive effect. Individuals who come from families whose parents have less than secondary education and who, at the time of their educational choice, the family's financial situation was poor, the graduate rate is very low. Of these, only one in ten individuals completed higher education. At the opposite extreme, parents with degrees and good financial situation, the proportion is 60%. This reality shows how much Banco de Portugal should pay attention to and encourage studies such as the ones we are honouring here today. Today, half of the workers between the ages of 25 and 34 have a degree. It is less than 20% in the most advanced generations. The net debt of households is at multi-year lows, and has reduced in the last two years, despite the state of crisis in which many say we live. I also recall that, in 2021 in Portugal, the at-risk-of-poverty rate for adults whose parents have less than secondary education was 17.1%, which contrasts with 6.8% for adults whose parents had higher education. This evidence reinforces the importance of the need to design public policies that enhance opportunities for all. Investment in education, starting with families, is critical to the development process of the economy. As a result of the effort made in recent decades, today, the human resources that our schools place in the job market are more and of higher quality. We have surpassed the European countries to whom we have looked for centuries from a lower position. The increase in the quality of the labour supply is already felt in our productivity, which represents a real structural change in our economy. But being a long-term journey, this path is never finished; We cannot leave it incomplete. The legacy of Manuela Silva, present in this book, allows us not to forget this very important mission, which as researchers or political decision-makers, or in both functions at the same time, we have in our hands. As Governor, an alumnus, but not a former student - we are always students - of ISEG, it is a privilege to participate in this tribute. ISEG is an institution, the Bank of Portugal is an institution. We do not reduce poverty and inequality in democracy if we do not respect institutions, either when we serve them or after we stop serving them. This appeal also remains today. Thank you very much.

Levou- nos muitas dcadas at assumir este resultado que hoje parece bvio. A cincia  mesmo assim. Como to bem sabia a Professora Manuela Silva, a melhor estratgia para combater a desigualdade de uma forma estrutural , sem dvida, a educao. A educao  um fator chave para a incluso econmica e social.  a soluo universal para alcanar o crescimento econmico a longo prazo. Cabe-nos a ns continuar o seu trabalho. Title: Closing speech by Governor Mrio Centeno at the 11th Banco de Portugal Conference - Economic Portuguese development in Europe
text: Closing speech by Governor Mario Centeno on the 11th .the Conference of the Bank of Portugal - Portuguese Economic Development in the European Area 14 November 2022 04 minutes Good afternoon, I would like to thank everyone for their presence at 11 .the Conference of the Bank of Portugal - Portuguese Economic Development in the European Area. And to express my sincere thanks to Professor Clara Raposo, Professor Luis Cabral and the other speakers, for having accepted the invitation of the Bank of Portugal. Your contributions were fundamental to enrich the discussion on the importance of public policies in the development of the Portuguese economy. But allow me a special word for the young people we have just awarded, in partnership with the Francisco Manuel dos Santos Foundation, for their excellent academic work. I do so, not only because of the intrinsic merit of the work they have developed, but also because they illustrate the importance of public policies, in particular, education policy. Education is a key driver for inclusive economic growth and social development. Over time, the supply of qualified labor has always been associated with economic development processes. It is therefore a universal solution for achieving long-term economic growth. We know how in the short term, the generalized increase in the quantity and quality of the supply of qualifications can bring individual anxiety about the return for these qualifications. For example, increasing the number of years of schooling in a short period of time may not immediately generate an increase in demand that would allow wages to be maintained. But we also know that over a sufficiently long period of time demand will add to this increased supply, provided that the institutional context allows it. The winning theses do justice to the importance of education as an institution that catalyzes economic growth. Both contribute to understanding how Portuguese companies react to uncertainty and crises. Although the two analyses are based on theoretical developments of a different nature, both theses conclude that the Portuguese business fabric is resilient. Martim Leitao studied the effect of crises on employment and productivity. Productivity is almost synonymous with growth. It was the productivity gains brought about by the industrial revolution that made possible the gains in quality of life that we have observed in the last two and a half centuries, after living millennia in Malthusian survival economies. These gains were based on multiple innovations, which Sofia Canada exploits to illustrate the role they play in the competitiveness of companies in uncertain environments. It is these advances in literature that will also help us to overcome more effectively the current moment of economic uncertainty. These are living examples of the importance of education in Portugal today. Unfortunately, education has not always been a priority of our public policies, which has had consequences not only for the country's productivity capacity, but also for distributive and non-inclusive policies. A study recently published by the Bank of Portugal, already mentioned today by Prof. Clara Raposo, shows that the intergenerational transmission of education, reinforced by the interaction with the financial situation of families, has important implications for the individual's educational paths, and with that, for social inclusion and the potential for economic growth. If the concern about the financial situation of families is at the heart of our mandate, adding to it the themes of education, access and results, is an addition that we consider not only natural, but providential for the success of our mission. Portugal was finally able to change the face of the success of its education system, and this also had to do largely with improving the financial situation of our families. If today half of the workers between 25 and 34 years old have a degree, 10 years ago it was only 20%. If today 85% of our young people leave school with at least secondary education, 20 years ago it was just over 40%. The net debt of households is at multi-year lows, a drop of more than 44 billion euros in real terms compared to 2009. In the last two years, despite the state of crisis and overlapping shocks in which we have been living, debt has fallen by 3.2 billion euros. These numbers reinforce the importance of the need to design public policies that enhance opportunities for all. In fact, the study presented by Lara Wemans gives us a concrete example of this importance. The policy instruments analysed in the study are decisive for strengthening the incomes of the most needy families and fundamental for reducing child poverty in Portugal. In redistributive terms, in the absence of this support, disposable income in the first decile of the income distribution would fall by almost 15%. Investment in education is thus critical to the development process of the economy, both in aggregate and individual terms. We cannot continue to look at the Portuguese economy and society with the same lenses that brought us to the sovereign debt crisis. Either we make an F5 in the data we use or we will bump into the ambition and will of the generation that is effectively better prepared ever. As a result of the effort made in recent decades, today, the human resources that our schools place in the job market are more and of higher quality. We have surpassed the European countries to whom we have looked for centuries from a lower position. The increase in the quality of the labour offer is already felt in our productivity, in the companies we attract to Portugal, and in those that we have been able to develop endogenously. This is the origin of the real structural change in our economy. But being a long-term journey, this path is never finished; We cannot leave it incomplete. We cannot, either, think that education is the elixir of growth. As an institutionalist, I cannot fail to mention the role that other institutions play in this complex process of growth, which is relatively recent in the history of humanity. We need to reflect on our social, political and judicial institutions in a European context and improve their functioning. The geopolitical moment we are experiencing should make us reflect on the importance of strengthening democratic institutions. We cannot take them for granted, we owe them the greatest respect and the obligation to preserve them as political decision-makers, but also as citizens. Thank you very much.

Title: Opening speech by Governor Mrio Centeno at the Great Banking of the Future Meeting 2022
text: Opening speech by Governor Mario Centeno at the Great Meeting Banking of the Future 2022 16 November 2022 07 minutes Good morning. As we know, the current macroeconomic picture is full of uncertainties, associated with the prolongation of the atrocious invasion of Ukraine and Europe's energy dependence, where high inflation inflicts destabilizing pressure. A prolonged inflation scenario will bring uncertainty, loss of confidence of economic agents and an inevitable recession. Therefore, inaction is not an option. The role of the European Central Bank is very clear in this area. The goal is to bring inflation to 2% in the medium term. The effects of monetary policy tend to be time-staggered, but I am sure that in the medium term the objective will be achieved. If we do not control inflation, the behavior of economic agents will induce a recession and inflation will wipe out the significant gains in wages, employment and savings of recent years. As I have been saying, not acting would have a recessionary cost greater than that which rising interest rates can cause. It is in this context of economic uncertainty and higher interest rates that Portuguese banks will have to face the challenges of the future. But we cannot continue to think about the future without knowing the present. And we cannot perceive the present if we continue to think about how it is in the past. The Portuguese banking system is very different. The steps he has taken in recent years have been decisive for a successful future. At the end of 2015, three-quarters of the assets and deposits of Portuguese banks were in institutions with their future compromised. There is no modern society that can grow in this environment. This is not a task for the central bank or the government. It is, and was, a collective task. That took the country out of the garbage, the excessive deficit procedures and the uncertainty of what would be the rating of a single Canadian rating agency. Which accelerated the cleaning of the more than 17% of non-performing, non-performing loans with which the Portuguese banks were living at that time. Which attracted to Portuguese banking capital from the four corners of the world. Today we live the fruits of this inversion, today we live the future. The interest premiums we paid, we stopped paying. The chronic budget deficits we had, we no longer have. The debt, public and private, which did not stop growing, fell. Between families and companies, there are 70 billion euros less, in real terms, in the last decade. There is only one dimension in which we still maintain the same old habit, rewriting history, with the data censored. And what we like about it. The evolution of the Portuguese banking sector over the last few years has been characterised by a strengthening of the capital position, liquidity levels, improved credit quality and increased profitability. This evolution has allowed the system to absorb the shocks resulting from the pandemic crisis and the emergence of the conflict between Russia and Ukraine, without a material impact on the financial situation of credit institutions. Allow me to give you a few figures to illustrate this development. The Total Capital ratio stood at 17.6% in June 2022, compared to 15.2% at the end of 2018, the first year in which the system recorded a positive net profit after the financial crisis. The liquidity profile has also been strengthened, greatly benefiting from the stability of the deposit base, which increased by more than 25% between 2012 and June 2022. At the same time, the reduction in the size of the loan portfolio by around 18% in the same period resulted in the evolution of the transformation ratio from 122% to 79% in the last 10 years. The asset quality of institutions has improved as banks have invested in reducing the legacy of NPLs, with emphasis on the sale and write-off of these assets. In 2015, NPLs amounted to almost 50 billion, representing 17% of total credit. One of the worst records in Europe. More than three times the amount that is considered the limit for risk-taking in a given banking system. In June this year, it represented only 3.4% of the total loan portfolio. Currently, the position of the Portuguese banking system compared to European peers is already much more similar than a few years ago, reflecting the improvement recorded since 2015. Today, due to the solution found for the seven plagues that the banking system suffered from in 2015, the RoE, liquidity and transformation ratio and the CET1 ratio are at the same level or even higher than the average of the Single European Mechanism. Portuguese banking is therefore aware of the European banking system. And the risks it faces in the future are also common. It is not surprising that the main risk factors for the banking system are high and persistent inflation, the abrupt increase in interest rates and the strong slowdown in economic activity. In the short and medium term, structurally higher interest rates are expected to have a favourable effect on net interest income. They will enhance a greater diversification of the public debt portfolio, but may also result in the devaluation of the asset portfolio. Nor should the additional pressure on net interest income that higher interest rates put on banks' market funding costs be overlooked. In particular, as part of the fulfilment of the minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities. On the other hand, the rise in financing costs, in a context of deteriorating economic expectations, may result in a lower demand for credit and a reduction in debtors' ability to meet contractual obligations. Materializing in an increase in credit risk for the banking system and reflected in an increase in impairments. However, an abrupt increase in the materialisation of credit risk is not expected to jeopardise the stability of the financial system. Institutions should take a proactive approach in assessing their customers' ability to pay and in adapting the terms of their loans to any difficulties in their lives. At the same time, they should follow appropriate provisioning and capital conservation practices, promoting the ability to absorb possible losses and the financing of the economy. Allow me to say a word about another risk, which is also not specific to the Portuguese banking sector, but should be at the center of our attention: cyber risk. With the increasing use of technology, the risks associated with operational failures and external attacks on banks have increased. The identification, definition and implementation of measures to mitigate this risk is fundamental. In this area, cooperation between all market players plays an essential role, so I could not fail to publicly acknowledge the sector's involvement in the Forum with Industry for Cybersecurity and Operational Resilience, promoted by Banco de Portugal since 2020. The regulatory changes underway in Portugal and Europe will be challenging, both for the Portuguese banking system and for the Bank of Portugal itself. But they will also be fundamental for us to build our "Banca de Futuro" together. I could not fail to refer, albeit briefly, to climate change. These are also a major source of financial risk for financial institutions. European banks, including the Portuguese ones, have made progress in incorporating climate and environmental risks into their activity in order to ensure compliance with supervisory expectations on this matter. This path is still at an early stage, so the effort to identify the materiality of these risks and adapt risk management models to this new paradigm should continue. Banking does not live dissociated from the country and the market it is supposed to serve. Banking has surpassed obstacles with the help of the country. Just as, in the last two years, the country has overcome challenges, with the help of the banks. A sign of this development is the strict compliance with the financing plans of the Cohesion Fund. Resolution. In 2022, the contribution of the Resolution Fund to public accounts amounts to around 260 million euros. This amount corresponds to the balance - finally positive - between the Resolution Fund's revenues, resulting from contributions paid by the banking sector, and its expenses. This has taken another step in a strategy to stabilise the banking system, which is as difficult as it is crucial for the country. Today the challenges are different. The reflection of interest rate hikes must be felt in deposits, so that savings take on another meaning. The normalisation of monetary policy has led to a considerable increase in interest rates. We cannot remain indifferent to it. It will require a collective response. Similar to what we gave in the recent past. In defense of the country's financial stability and sustainable growth. Thank you very much.

Esta evoluo tem permitido ao sistema absorver os choques decorrentes da crise pandmica e do emergir do conflito entre a Rssia e a Ucrnia, sem impacto material na situao financeira das instituies de crdito. Permitam-me alguns nmeros para ilustrar esta evoluo. O rcio de Fundos Prprios Totais cifrou-se em 17,6% em junho de 2022, face a 15,2% no final de 2018, o primeiro ano em que o sistema registou um resultado lquido positivo aps a crise financeira. O perfil de liquidez tambm se tem reforado, em muito beneficiando da estabilidade da base de depsitos que apresentaram um aumento de mais de 25% entre 2012 e junho de 2022. Ao mesmo tempo, a reduo da dimenso da carteira de crdito em cerca de 18% no mesmo perodo, resultou na evoluo do rcio de transformao de 122% para 79% nos ltimos 10 anos. A qualidade do ativo das instituies foi melhorando  medida em que os bancos investiram na reduo do legado de NPLs, com destaque para a venda e o abate desses ativos. Em 2015 os NPLs cifravam-se em quase 50 mil milhes de euros, representando 17% do crdito total. Um dos piores registos da Europa. Mais de trs vezes o valor que  considerado limite para a tomada de risco num determinado sistema bancrio. Em junho deste ano representava apenas 3,4% do total da carteira de crdito. Atualmente, a posio do sistema bancrio portugus face aos pares europeus  j bem mais similar do que h poucos anos atrs, reflexo da melhoria registada desde 2015. Hoje, tributria da soluo encontrada para as sete pragas de que o sistema bancrio sofria em 2015, o RoE, a liquidez e o rcio de transformao e o rcio CET1 esto ao mesmo nvel ou so mesmo superiores aos da mdia do Mecanismo nico Europeu. A banca portuguesa est, pois, a par do sistema bancrio europeu. E os riscos que enfrenta no futuro so tambm eles comuns. No  surpreendente que os principais fatores de risco do sistema bancrio passem pela inflao elevada e persistente, pelo aumento abrupto das taxas de juro e pelo abrandamento forte da atividade econmica. No curto e mdio prazo, as taxas de juro estruturalmente mais elevadas devero ter um efeito favorvel sobre a margem financeira. Potenciaro uma maior diversificao da carteira de dvida pblica, mas tambm podero resultar na desvalorizao da carteira de ativos. No deve ser tambm descurada a presso adicional sobre a margem financeira que as taxas de juro mais elevadas colocam nos custos de financiamento de mercado dos bancos. Em particular, no mbito do cumprimento do requisito mnimo de fundos prprios e passivos elegveis. Por outro lado, a subida dos custos de financiamento, num quadro de deteriorao das expectativas econmicas, poder resultar numa menor procura por crdito e numa reduo na capacidade de cumprimento das obrigaes contratuais por parte dos devedores. Materializando-se num aumento do risco de crdito para o sistema bancrio e refletindo-se num aumento das imparidades. No se espera, contudo, um aumento abrupto na materializao do risco de crdito que ponha em causa a estabilidade do sistema financeiro. As instituies devem adotar uma abordagem proactiva na avaliao da capacidade de pagamento dos seus clientes e na adequao das condies dos emprstimos face a eventuais dificuldades dos mesmos. Paralelamente, devem seguir prticas de provisionamento adequadas e de conservao do capital, promovendo a capacidade de absoro de eventuais perdas e o financiamento da economia. Permitam-me uma palavra para um outro risco, que tambm no sendo especfico ao setor bancrio portugus, deve estar no centro das nossas atenes: o ciber-risco. Com o aumento crescente da utilizao da tecnologia, aumentaram os riscos associados a falhas operacionais e a ataques externos s instituies de crdito. A identificao, definio e implementao de medidas que permitam mitigar este risco  fundamental. Neste domnio, a cooperao entre todos os intervenientes de mercado assume um papel essencial, pelo que no poderia deixar de reconhecer publicamente o envolvimento do setor no Frum com a Indstria para a Cibersegurana e Resilincia Operacional, promovido pelo Banco de Portugal desde 2020. As alteraes regulamentares em curso em Portugal e na Europa sero desafiantes, quer para o sistema bancrio portugus, quer para o prprio Banco de Portugal. Mas sero tambm fundamentais para construirmos em conjunto a nossa Banca de Futuro. No poderia deixar de me referir, ainda que brevemente s alteraes climticas. Estas so tambm uma importante fonte de risco financeiro para as instituies financeiras. Os bancos europeus, incluindo os portugueses, tm apresentado um progresso na incorporao dos riscos climticos e ambientais dentro da sua atividade de modo a garantir com o cumprimento das expetativas de superviso sobre esta matria. Este caminho est ainda numa fase inicial pelo que deve continuar o esforo de identificao da materialidade destes riscos e adaptao dos modelos de gesto do risco a este novo paradigma. A banca no vive dissociada do pas e do mercado que  suposto servir. A banca ultrapassou obstculos com a ajuda do pas. Tal como, nos ltimos dois anos, o pas ultrapassou desafios, com a ajuda da banca. Um sinal desta evoluo  o cumprimento rigoroso dos planos de financiamento do Fundo de Resoluo. Em 2022, o contributo da Fundo de Resoluo para as contas pblicas ascende a cerca de 260 milhes de euros. Esse montante corresponde ao saldo - finalmente positivo - entre as receitas do Fundo de Resoluo, resultantes de contribuies pagas pelo setor bancrio, e as suas despesas. Deu-se assim mais um passo numa estratgia de estabilizao do sistema bancrio, to difcil como crucial para o pas. Hoje os desafios so outros. O reflexo das subidas das taxas de juro deve fazer-se sentir nos depsitos, para que a poupana passe a ter outro significado. A normalizao da poltica monetria provocou um aumento das taxas de juro de uma magnitude considervel. No lhe podemos ficar indiferente. Vai requerer uma resposta coletiva. Semelhante  que demos no passado recente. Na defesa da estabilidade financeira e do crescimento sustentvel do pas. Muito obrigado.

Title: Speech by Governor Mrio Centeno at the swearing-in ceremony of the new members of the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal
text: Speech by Governor Mario Centeno at the swearing-in ceremony of the new members of the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal 29 November 2022 06 minutes Ex.mo Minister of Finance, Dear Secretaries of State, Ladies and Gentlemen, Institutions define much of the wealth of nations. Nor was Adam Smith's wealth of nations limited to the invisible hand, itself an institution. Today, for economic science, it is unequivocal that a solid, democratic institutional model in which an effective system of checks and balances is in force is fundamental for the socio-economic development of countries. Banco de Portugal is an inseparable part of our collective development. Today, a renewed and expanded Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal takes office. I would even venture to say that it is, in many years, the most qualified Board of Directors of the Bank of Portugal. In the image of the country. A Council with gender parity, the likes of which has never existed at the Bank. This Council comes at the best time. The moment of the challenge of fighting inflation, which today is once again in the spotlight of decision-makers. The independence of central banks, formally enshrined over the past few decades, is seen as the key to success in controlling inflation. While there is no one-size-fits-all model  as some central banks have more than one goal  there is a common denominator: keeping inflation over the medium term at 2%. This dimension must be preserved. In order for it to be so, its exercise is understood at Banco de Portugal as a duty. A duty before the Republic, not a prerogative, nor a right. Banco de Portugal recognises its position in Portuguese society, a position of leadership, a sense of responsibility and sharing, based on the qualifications of its staff, without which no Board of Directors would be able to perform its function. But independence, beyond what is legislated, is justified by the actions of the institutions, at all times. It is the Bank's decisions that qualify and justify independence. It is useless to appeal to a concept if the actions, and the results of these acts, do not achieve the objectives that can justify it. The new Board of Directors will exercise the position responsibly, open to society and public scrutiny, preserving the integrity of the privileged information entrusted to it. We will do so with and for the independence of the Bank of Portugal, which celebrated its 176th anniversary in November! Only in this way can we aspire to endure in the Portuguese institutional framework for at least another 176 years. No one owns qualified information, shared under the motto of trust, the cornerstone of the entire financial system. The breach of this principle calls into question the work of almost two centuries of the Bank. That is not our DNA. Significantly, the motto of the Strategic Plan 2021 -2025 is "proximity and trust". Quite the opposite of a closed and non-dialoguing Bank. Independence is built on collective action, it is not an antonym of cooperation. That is why the Bank leads the National Council of Financial Supervisors. Assuming institutional cooperation as the supreme form of independence. The institutional model in Portugal places the Minister of Finance at the top of the pyramid of preserving financial stability. We know how financial stability is a concept of general equilibrium. It needs everyone. It passes through families, companies and the State. No regulator, no supervisor, no Government, achieves this desideratum alone in a liberal, market and democratic economy like ours. There is a role for everyone and therefore there is an extraordinarily important role for the Bank of Portugal. In the European institutional framework, where we fit in, this is exactly how the monetary, supervisory and budgetary authorities relate to each other. If in this room or in this country, anyone still believes that it would have been possible, without strong institutional cooperation, between 2015 and 2018 to have capitalized the largest national banks, started the reduction of non-performing loans, resumed levels of profitability prior to the financial and sovereign debt crises, in a sign of demand never seen before in Portugal, he will have to urgently review everything he has not read about the financial system. In finances, as in life, there is no bad luck, there is procrastination. As I have already mentioned, the structure of highly trained and specialised human resources, as well as the knowledge of the financial sector accumulated by the Bank of Portugal, are fundamental for the preservation of financial stability and, consequently, for purposefully informing political decision-makers. This Board of Directors is tributary, collectively and collegially, of this unique mission. No pressure. With the full filling of the seven seats on the Board of Directors, provided for in Banco de Portugal's governance model, another firm step towards the success of the institutional model that the country has adopted. The team in office is now joined by the Vice-Governor, Professor Clara Raposo, and the members Dr. Helena Adegas, Professor Francisca Oliveira and Dr. Rui Pinto. It also counts on the renewal of the mandate of Dr. Luis Maximo dos Santos, as Vice-Governor, which is a sign of confidence in the work of the Bank of Portugal. Allow me to highlight the responsibilities of the Resolution Authority, a reflection of the enormous difficulties experienced in the past by the Portuguese banking system. This is the translation of the quality of the Bank's work. Today the Resolution Fund releases funds for the State Budget, in 2022 there were more than 200 million euros, a sign that we have overcome the storms that devastated us less than ten years ago, but which seem to have dissipated from the memory of some. Thank you, in the person of Luis, to all those who have promoted financial stability through bank resolution at the Bank of Portugal. We have two new contributions from academia and the business world. Professor Clara Raposo brings to the Board of Directors her training in the area of finance in one of the best schools in the world and her own vision that will allow her to challenge the Bank's structures with new ideas. Ideas that he brings from a school environment that I know well, ISEG, which he has led in recent years and has taken to maximum international recognition. He adds to this the participation in the Boards of Directors of some of the most dynamic national companies. Similarly, Professor Francisca Oliveira will put at the service of the Bank the combination of her academic experience at the Catolica Porto Business School of the Catholic University of Portugal combined with her business experience at AICEP, in a context of internationalization of the Portuguese economy. The approach to society is also made by the diversity of experiences with the business world, which dictates much of the country's economic success. A business sector that now has the added responsibility of being part of the fight against inflation. Assigning responsibility to the ECB alone will have a higher cost than is strictly necessary to achieve the same objective. Dr. Helena Adegas and Dr. Rui Pinto are two members of the house, who accumulate with experiences outside the Bank of Portugal. They know the ins and outs of the Bank of Portugal and the national and European regulatory environment. They also represent for current workers an example of successful internal careers. Helena, as director of the Markets Department, managed for many years the assets of the Bank of Portugal, which today exceed two hundred billion euros. I am sure that the responsibility that such a task entailed is an extraordinary business card. Rui also brings an outside view, of another regulator, which we should use to build bridges between regulators - continuously reinforcing independence from the regulated, so that we can face the growing challenges of regulation, supervision and financial markets in Europe. Rui Pinto's supervision experience is a guarantee for the future. A word of thanks, as Governor, to the two outgoing members of the Board of Directors of Banco de Portugal, Professor Ana Paula Serra and Dr. Luis Laginha de Sousa. The work carried out in their respective intense mandates in crucial areas of micro and macro-prudential supervision is testimony to the dedication, rectitude and solidarity that I have been able to witness for more than two years, in challenging and sometimes difficult times for our financial system. To all of you, those who enter and those who leave, I wish you every success in the performance of your duties, which in this case will also be those of the country. A Portugal that today is a model of success and overcoming challenges in Europe and in the world. Thank you very much.

Helena Adegas, Professora Francisca Oliveira e Dr. Rui Pinto. Title: Speech by Governor Mrio Centeno at the award of the Professor Jacinto Nunes Award 2022
text: Speech by Governor Mario Centeno at the award of the Professor Jacinto Nunes Award 2022 10 January 2023 03 minutes Dear award-winners, Respectful parents, family members and guests, Your Excellencies, Ladies and gentlemen, First of all, my congratulations to the winners! It is a privilege to recognize and reward nine students of exceptional academic performance. They are certainly a source of pride for family, friends and the institutions in which they graduated. And, of course, for the Bank of Portugal. I even dare to say, for the country. The Jacinto Nunes Award annually distinguishes students with the best final average of the degree in Economics. With it, the Bank intends to value the merit and individual performance of students, in what is the main area of study for the mission of a central bank. But it is also a way of distinguishing the educational establishments of which the selected ones are part. It was in 1987, almost 36 years ago, that the Bank of Portugal decided to award this prize, then called the "Bank of Portugal Award", for the first time. More recently, in 2016, the prize was renamed in honor of Professor Manuel Jacinto Nunes, one of the most distinguished economists of the second half of the twentieth century in Portugal. In addition to having been deputy governor (1960-1974) and governor (1974-75 and 1980-85) in this "house", he was also deputy prime minister and minister of finance in the IV Constitutional Government (1978-79). A convinced Europeanist and author of several economic and financial studies, his name is deeply associated with the dissemination of Keynesian principles in Portugal. Professor Manuel Jacinto Nunes was responsible, at the Ministry of Economy, for the negotiations of the Marshall Plan, Portuguese representative on the Economic Policy Committee of the OECD (1959 to 1965) and participated in important negotiations for Portugal, such as accession to the International Monetary Fund. This award should be seen not only as a form of recognition of your merit and effort in this, so far, demanding journey, marked by a pandemic, but should mark, above all, an incentive. A motivation to continue studying, researching, creating and sharing knowledge. And, why not, to one day come to work at the Bank of Portugal. In your academic and intellectual path, at a certain point you will stop being students, but never stop being students. Education is the key to achieving long-term sustainable economic growth. Investment in education is critical for your development, but also for that of the economy and society in which you operate. As a result of the effort made in recent decades, the human resources that our schools provide to the labour market are now more and of higher quality. The Bank of Portugal, by receiving more than a hundred of these human resources every year, witnesses and values this collective investment. Today, half of the workers between the ages of 25 and 34 have a degree; 10 years ago it was only 20%. Today, 85% of our young people leave school with at least secondary education; 20 years ago it was just over 40%. The increase in the quality of the job offer is already being felt in our productivity, in the companies we attract to Portugal and in those we create. And this, indeed, represents a real structural change in our economy and in our society. Higher schooling is always associated with greater civic, economic and social demand. Economists refer to these aspects as "general equilibrium effects". We must not allow the positive effects to be mitigated by impediments in the transmission mechanisms: the labour market must function in such a way as to absorb all these new resources. Finally, I would like to express a word of recognition to the deans and directors of the schools of Economics and Management, who have played an important role in this process. And through them to the teachers who have contributed in a remarkable way to allow this transformation to happen. Like the best companies, higher education institutions have become internationalized and are today poles of talent attraction and examples of positioning and differentiation in international rankings. Finally, I would like to say a word to the families of the winners. May they celebrate this award with pride and see it as confirmation that education is the right path, the path that opens doors to a more prosperous and more inclusive future. Once again, congratulations to the winners. And, I hope, see you soon.
text_original: Interveno do Governador Mrio Centeno na atribuio do Prmio Professor Jacinto Nunes 2022 10 janeiro 2023 03 minutos Carssimos premiados, Respeitosos pais, familiares e convidados, Excelentssimos reitores e vice-reitores, Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, Em primeiro lugar, os meus parabns aos premiados!  um privilgio reconhecer e premiar nove alunos de excecional desempenho acadmico. So certamente motivo de orgulho para a famlia, amigos e as instituies nas quais se formaram. E, claro, para o Banco de Portugal. Arrisco mesmo dizer, para o pas. O Prmio Jacinto Nunes distingue anualmente os alunos com a melhor mdia final da licenciatura em Economia. Com ele o Banco pretende valorizar o mrito e o desempenho individual dos alunos, naquela que  a principal rea de estudos para a misso de um banco central. Mas  tambm uma forma de distinguir os estabelecimentos de ensino de que fazem parte os selecionados. Foi em 1987, j l vo quase 36 anos, que o Banco de Portugal decidiu atribuir pela primeira vez este prmio, ento designado Prmio Banco de Portugal. Mais recentemente, em 2016, o prmio foi renomeado em homenagem ao professor Manuel Jacinto Nunes, um dos economistas mais ilustres da segunda metade do sculo XX em Portugal. Alm de ter sido vice-governador (1960-1974) e governador (1974-75 e 1980-85) nesta casa, foi tambm vice-primeiro ministro e ministro das Finanas no IV Governo Constitucional (1978-79). Europesta convicto e autor de diversos estudos econmico-financeiros, o seu nome est profundamente associado  divulgao dos princpios keynesianos em Portugal. O professor Manuel Jacinto Nunes foi o responsvel, no Ministrio da Economia, pelas negociaes do Plano Marshall, representante portugus no Comit de Poltica Econmica da OCDE (1959 a 1965) e participou em negociaes importantes para Portugal, como a da adeso ao Fundo Monetrio Internacional. Title: Opening speech by Governor Mrio Centeno at the Digital First Conference
text: Opening speech by Governor Mario Centeno at the Digital First Conference 18 April 2023 04 minutes Very good morning, I begin by welcoming the Secretary of State for Digitalization and Administrative Modernization (Eng. Mario Campolargo), to the Secretary of State for Justice (Dr. Pedro Tavares), to MUDA (in the person of its Executive Director, Dr. Alexandre Nilo da Fonseca) and to all those present. It is with great pleasure that Banco de Portugal hosts this conference promoted by the initiative of the Movement for Active Digital Use - MUDA. The rapid evolution of technology, and its widespread availability to consumers and other economic agents, has introduced changes in the way we work, communicate, and carry out our daily activities. The pandemic has further accelerated this trend. As a movement that brings together companies, universities and associations and the Portuguese State itself, MUDA has played a leading role in promoting greater participation of the Portuguese in the digital space and in preparing society to face these changes. Banco de Portugal has been associated, as an institutional partner, with some of the actions developed by MUDA. I highlight the dissemination of informative content on the use of payment instruments and on the precautions to be taken in the prevention of fraud, especially in e-commerce. The motto of today's conference is "how organizations, people and technology can change Portugal". I believe that, in this rapidly changing world, Banco de Portugal will make a relevant contribution. On the one hand, as a reference institution and example in the adoption of technology and in the training of people for the development of the country and, on the other hand, supporting the efforts that the financial system and economic agents make in this regard. This is one of those purposes in which the gains will be greater for all parties if there is coordinated action. Banco de Portugal's Strategic Plan 21-25, whose motto is proximity and trust, reflects this contribution that we must make. Internally, we intend to adapt our governance and organization model to the most efficient pursuit of our mission, namely:  prioritizing the development and training of its people and investing in the integration of new necessary profiles;  taking advantage of technological innovation to achieve a digital transformation, with process automation, efficiency gains and the provision of innovative services to society; and  investing in integrated information management and a modern data architecture. We recognise, therefore, that technological innovation has an impact on the way we carry out our mission. For example, today, we have an ongoing research project for the possible issuance of the Digital Euro - the Eurosystem's central bank digital currency. If it is issued, the Digital Euro will be able to combine the security and universality of cash with the benefits of electronic payments, adapting central bank money to the needs of more digital users. The Digital Euro will increase the range of payment options and enhance the resilience of payment systems. Let me also highlight another dimension of our Strategic Plan with an impact on innovation. I am referring to the close monitoring of the new business models of institutions, whether incumbents or new operators, favouring innovation and safeguarding risk and security conditions. The Bank will also continue its work to contribute to increasing the accessibility of safer, more efficient and innovative payment solutions for consumers and businesses. Solutions that facilitate the growth of economic activity and income. A relevant example is the National Strategy for Retail Payments developed under the Payment Systems Forum, a structure that brings together the main national players in the supply and demand of payment services, including representatives of the Public Administration. The first National Strategy for Retail Payments, whose implementation was completed in December 2022, was designed with the objectives of  promote a more informed society;  enhancing the benefits of digital transformation;  contribute to a regulatory environment that would favour innovation and efficiency; and  encourage the adoption of more secure payment solutions. A new Strategy is currently being prepared, which will build on the previous one and include new dimensions such as resilience and sustainability. In order for everyone to benefit from technological innovation, it is necessary to ensure inclusive, appropriate and secure use of digital financial services. To this end, we will promote a medium/long-term digital financial literacy strategy for Portugal. Financial services will be more inclusive, with people who are better connected, more informed, and increasingly empowered. I believe, as is the motto of this conference, that "organizations, people and technology can change Portugal" and that we have a duty to join our efforts. Let me conclude this opening remarks with a broader perspective, underlining three main ideas: First, the role of technology has evolved over time. It is no longer just a tool, nor a channel, it is a product in itself. It must be put at the service of people and organizations, to improve decision-making, increase the efficiency of processes and improve the quality and safety of the services offered. Second, the pace of technological innovation is not expected to slow down. Digital transformation should not be seen as a transition path, but rather as a process of continuous creation and adaptation, which requires permanent monitoring of technology and consistent investment in people. Third, to change Portugal, it is necessary for each organization to embark on its own transformational process, but also to make a contribution to collective effort and change. This is how we also see Banco de Portugal, as an active part of this collective change. Thank you very much and enjoy the conference.
